title: Cua Driver install fails on Intel macOS because x86_64 release asset is missing
body:
## Summary

The Cua Driver docs say Intel Macs are supported, but the current installer fails on an Intel Mac because it tries to download a `darwin-x86_64` asset that does not exist.

## Environment

- Mac: Intel MacBook Pro
- Architecture: `x86_64`
- macOS: `15.7.5`
- Cua Driver release resolved by installer: `cua-driver-v0.1.6`

## Steps to reproduce

Run:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh)"
```

or via Hermes:

```bash
hermes computer-use install
```

## Actual behavior

The installer resolves the latest release correctly:

```text
latest release: cua-driver-v0.1.6
```

Then attempts to download:

```text
https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/download/cua-driver-v0.1.6/cua-driver-0.1.6-darwin-x86_64.tar.gz
```

That URL returns `404`.

Hermes reports:

```text
curl: (56) The requested URL returned error: 404
error: download failed; try CUA_DRIVER_VERSION=<version> to pin a specific release
```

## Expected behavior

Either:

1. publish a `cua-driver-0.1.6-darwin-x86_64.tar.gz` asset, or
2. publish a universal macOS binary, or
3. update the docs/install script if Intel is no longer supported.

## Additional verification

I downloaded the generic `cua-driver.tar.gz` from `cua-driver-v0.1.6` and inspected the bundled binary:

```text
CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64
```

`lipo` reports:

```text
Non-fat file ... is architecture: arm64
```

So the generic tarball does not appear to be a universal or Intel-compatible build.

## Relevant docs

The Cua Driver installation docs currently list `Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) or Intel Mac` under requirements:

https://cua.ai/docs/cua-driver/guide/getting-started/installation

title: fix(cd): pass universal binary to notarization script (fixes #1493)
body:
## Problem

The CD workflow correctly built arm64 + x86\_64 and combined them with `lipo` into a universal binary, but then called `build-release-notarized.sh` **without** `CUA_DRIVER_PREBUILT_BINARY`. The script would:

1. Rebuild from source (arm64 only via `swift build -c release`)
2. Package the arm64 binary into `.app` and then into the tarball
3. The workflow's post-hoc `cp .build/cua-driver-universal` only updated the `.app` on disk — the tarball was already sealed

Result: **every released tarball** (`-arm64`, `-x86_64`, `-universal`) contained an arm64-only binary. Intel users got `zsh: bad CPU type in executable` (#1493 / reported by @jakechism).

## Fix

- Export `CUA_DRIVER_PREBUILT_BINARY="$(pwd)/.build/cua-driver-universal"` **before** calling the notarization script so it uses the fat binary when assembling the `.app` and creating tarballs
- Add `CUA_DRIVER_PREBUILT_BINARY` support to `build-release-notarized.sh` (skips `swift build`, uses the provided binary path)
- Replace the post-hoc binary injection block with a `lipo -info` verification so it's clear from CI logs whether the packaged binary is actually universal
- Backward-compatible: running the script locally without the env var still builds from source as before

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger CD workflow for a new `cua-driver-v*` tag
- [ ] In the "Build arm64 + x86_64" step logs, confirm `lipo -info` reports `Architectures in the fat file: arm64 x86_64`
- [ ] Download the released `-x86_64.tar.gz` and run `file cua-driver` — expect `Mach-O universal binary with 2 architectures`
- [ ] Install on an Intel Mac and confirm `cua-driver --version` works

Fixes #1493

title: Clarify Cua Driver support for Intel MacBookPro14,3 on macOS Ventura 13.7.8
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver-v0.1.9` fixes the Intel/x86_64 release artifact packaging issue from #1493 / #1494, but it still cannot run on an Intel MacBook Pro model whose latest officially offered macOS appears to be Ventura 13.7.8.

The current docs say:

- `macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later`
- `Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) or Intel Mac (x86_64)`

That is technically accurate for Intel Macs that can run macOS 14+, but it is easy to read as broad Intel Mac support. Some Intel MacBook Pro models are x86_64 but do not receive a macOS 14+ installer through Software Update.

## Environment

```text
Mac: MacBook Pro
Model Identifier: MacBookPro14,3
Architecture: x86_64
Current macOS: 13.7.8 (22H730)
Cua Driver: 0.1.9
Installed binary: Mach-O universal binary with x86_64 + arm64 slices
CuaDriver.app LSMinimumSystemVersion: 14.0
```

`softwareupdate --list-full-installers` on this machine lists Ventura 13.7.8 and older installers, but not Sonoma or later:

```text
macOS Ventura 13.7.8 (22H730)
macOS Monterey 12.7.6 / 12.7.4
macOS Big Sur 11.7.x
macOS Catalina / Mojave / High Sierra
```

## Actual behavior

The `v0.1.9` installer can install a universal binary, but executing it fails before any TCC permission checks:

```text
dyld: Library not loaded: /usr/lib/swift/libswiftObservation.dylib
Referenced from: /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver (built for macOS 14.0 which is newer than running OS)
```

Local inspection also shows:

```text
/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/Info.plist: LSMinimumSystemVersion = 14.0
libs/cua-driver/Package.swift: .macOS(.v14)
```

## Expected clarification

Please clarify one of these paths:

1. **Cua Driver intentionally supports only macOS 14+**, even on Intel, in which case the docs and installer should say something like: `Intel Macs are supported only if they can run macOS 14 Sonoma or later` and fail fast on macOS 13 with a clear message.
2. **Ventura support is desired**, in which case the code/build needs a macOS 13 deployment target and removal or back-deployment of macOS-14-only dependencies such as `Observation`.

## Related upstream context

- #1493 fixed the missing/mislabeled Intel artifact path for `v0.1.9`.
- #1494 merged the packaging fix.
- #1469 scoped Intel support to x86_64 builds and stated the frameworks are available on Intel macOS 14+.

This issue is not a duplicate of #1493: the architecture packaging is fixed locally. The remaining blocker is the supported macOS floor for Intel MacBook Pro hardware that cannot install macOS 14+ through Software Update.

title: Allow Cua Driver to target macOS Ventura
body:
## Summary

This attempts to make Cua Driver build and launch on macOS 13 Ventura, including Intel Macs such as `MacBookPro14,3` whose latest Software Update offering is Ventura 13.7.8.

Changes:

- lower the Swift package platform from `.macOS(.v14)` to `.macOS(.v13)`
- lower `CuaDriver.app` `LSMinimumSystemVersion` from `14.0` to `13.0`
- remove the macOS-14-only `Observation` framework usage from the agent cursor overlay
- keep the cursor overlay rendering through `TimelineView`, which already samples renderer state every frame
- add installer preflight for macOS version detection so unsupported pre-Ventura systems fail clearly
- update Cua Driver docs and the bundled skill README to describe macOS 13+ support

## Why

`cua-driver-v0.1.9` fixed the Intel/x86_64 release artifact issue from #1493 / #1494. On an Intel `MacBookPro14,3` running macOS `13.7.8`, the installed `v0.1.9` binary is now correctly universal, but it fails before permission checks:

```text
dyld: Library not loaded: /usr/lib/swift/libswiftObservation.dylib
Referenced from: /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver (built for macOS 14.0 which is newer than running OS)
```

Local machine context:

```text
Mac: MacBook Pro
Model Identifier: MacBookPro14,3
Architecture: x86_64
macOS: 13.7.8 (22H730)
Installed Cua Driver: 0.1.9
Installed binary: Mach-O universal binary with x86_64 + arm64 slices
```

`softwareupdate --list-full-installers` on that machine only lists Ventura 13.7.8 and older installers, not Sonoma or later.

## Related context

- Refs #1497
- #1493 fixed the missing/mislabeled Intel artifact path for `v0.1.9`
- #1494 merged the universal packaging fix
- #1469 discussed x86_64 release builds and scoped the existing source to Intel macOS 14+

## Validation

Ran locally on the Ventura Intel host:

```text
git diff --check
bash -n libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh
plutil -lint libs/cua-driver/App/CuaDriver/Info.plist
```

All passed.

I could not run a local Swift build on this host because it only has Command Line Tools / Swift 5.8.1, and `swift build` fails before package resolution with:

```text
xcrun: error: unable to lookup item 'PlatformPath' from command line tools installation
```

title: TypeScript computer tests fail for file byte transport and reconnect after disconnect
body:
Closed in favor of a replacement issue created via local `gh` from the intended contributor account (`iqdoctor`).

Original body:

## Summary

`libs/typescript/computer` currently has failing Vitest coverage on `main` after installing the workspace and building `@trycua/core`/`@trycua/computer`.

## Repro

```bash
cd libs/typescript
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm --filter @trycua/computer test --run
```

Observed result before the fix:

- 50 tests pass
- 5 tests fail in `tests/interface/macos.test.ts`

## Root cause

There are two separate issues:

1. The file-operation tests are stale. `MacOSComputerInterface.readText()` and `writeText()` intentionally go through `readBytes()` / `writeBytes()` so they share the byte transport path used by the Python generic interface. That byte transport carries `offset: 0` and `append: false` defaults, but the tests still expect direct `read_text` / `write_text` commands.
2. `BaseComputerInterface.connect()` mishandles reconnect after an explicit `disconnect()`. When the socket is closed, it creates a new `WebSocket` and immediately returns after `authenticate()`, without waiting for the new socket's `open` event. The next command can then call `send()` while the socket is still `CONNECTING`.

## Expected

- Tests should assert the byte transport contract used by the current TS and Python generic interfaces.
- Reconnect should wait until the recreated WebSocket is open before command dispatch.

I have a small patch ready that updates the stale test expectations and fixes `connect()` to wait for `open` on recreated sockets.

title: cua-driver crashes on macOS 14 (Sonoma) — unrecognized selector SLSEventAuthenticationMessage
body:
cua-driver v0.1.9 (and v0.1.6) crashes when calling hotkey, press_key, or scroll on macOS 14.8.7 (Sonoma, arm64).

## Crash
```
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInvalidArgumentException',
reason: '+[SLSEventAuthenticationMessage messageWithEventRecord:pid:version:]:
unrecognized selector sent to class'
```

## Root cause
`SLSEventAuthenticationMessage` exists on macOS 14 but the `messageWithEventRecord:pid:version:` selector was added in macOS 15 (Sequoia). Keyboard/scroll tools that use SkyLight's `SLEventPostToPid` with auth message crash at runtime.

`type_text` (Accessibility API) works fine. `capture` and `click` also work.

## To reproduce
```bash
cua-driver call hotkey '{"pid": 747, "keys": ["cmd", "a"]}'
```

## Environment
- macOS 14.8.7 (Sonoma)
- Apple M1 Pro
- cua-driver 0.1.9

## Suggested fix
Detect macOS version and skip SLSEventAuthenticationMessage on < macOS 15, falling back to CGEventPostToPid without auth.

title: 🐛 CuaDriver v0.1.9 缺少 AppIcon.icns 导致图标显示为无图标占位符
body:
## 问题描述

安装官方 CuaDriver v0.1.9 后，应用图标显示为 **"无图标的占位符"**（系统默认的灰色文档图标），而非 Cua 的官方 Logo。

```xml
<!-- Contents/Info.plist -->
<key>CFBundleIconFile</key>
<string>AppIcon</string>
<key>CFBundleIconName</key>
<string>AppIcon</string>
<key>LSUIElement</key>
<true/>
```

**注意**: `LSUIElement=true` 表示这是一个后台应用，不会显示在 Dock 栏或 Cmd+Tab 中。图标问题主要体现在系统设置、启动器（Launchpad）、Finder 等需要显示应用图标的地方。

### 根因

检查安装包内容：

```bash
tar -tzf cua-driver-0.1.9-darwin-arm64.tar.gz | grep -i icon
# 输出: 无 (Resources 目录只有 Skills/ 子目录)

ls -la /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/Resources/
# 输出: 只有 Skills/ 子目录，没有 AppIcon.icns
```

`Info.plist` 声明了图标文件，但原始安装包中 **Resources 目录没有 AppIcon.icns 文件**。

---

## 修复尝试与经验

### 尝试 1: 手动添加图标文件

**方法**: 从 GitHub 下载官方 Cua Logo SVG，转换为 PNG 后创建 icns 文件，手动复制到 `Contents/Resources/AppIcon.icns`

**结果**: ❌ 失败

**具体现象**:
- SVG 转换后的 PNG 图标显示为 **纯黑色方块**（根元素 `fill="none"` 覆盖子元素 `fill="black"`）
- 修复 SVG 后重新生成 icns，图标正确显示考拉图案
- 但替换后应用无法正常工作，功能异常

**经验**: 
- 官方 SVG 存在 `fill` 属性冲突，需移除根元素的 `fill="none"`
- 手动添加图标文件后，应用签名状态改变，可能导致功能异常

---

### 尝试 2: 封装图标后重新安装

**方法**: 将修复后的 `AppIcon.icns` 直接封装进官方安装包，重新解压安装

**结果**: ❌ 失败

**具体现象**:
- 安装后图标显示正常（考拉图案）
- **每次重启电脑，系统都会弹出权限授权提示**，要求重新授予 Accessibility 和 Screen Recording 权限
- 系统设置中 CUA 的权限开关消失

**根因**: 
- 原始安装包中 `CodeResources` 密封资源规则为 `^Resources/` => `true`（要求 Resources 下所有文件必须注册）
- 添加 `AppIcon.icns` 后，文件存在但不在密封资源列表中，签名验证失败
- 重新签名后变成 adhoc 签名，丢失 Developer ID，导致 TCC 权限记录失效

**经验**:
- 修改 notarized 应用前，必须先检查密封资源规则
- `^Resources/` => `true` 是"所有文件必须注册"模式，添加新文件会导致签名验证失败
- 重新签名会丢失 Developer ID 和公证状态，导致权限记录失效

---

## 建议

### 给官方的建议

1. **发布包含图标的版本**: 在 `Resources/` 目录中添加 `AppIcon.icns` 文件，并更新 `CodeResources` 密封资源

2. **提供官方图标源文件**: 在 GitHub Releases 或仓库中提供：
   - `CuaDriver.icns` 源文件
   - `CuaDriver-iconset/` 目录（包含所有尺寸的 PNG）

3. **提供修复指南文档**: 在 README 或 Wiki 中添加自定义图标指南，说明：
   - 如何检查密封资源规则
   - 如何安全修改图标（替换 vs 添加）
   - 重新签名的后果和注意事项

### 给用户的建议

**不要尝试手动修改图标文件**，除非你了解以下风险：

1. **签名验证失败**: 添加新文件到密封资源区域会导致 `codesign -v` 报错
2. **权限记录失效**: 重新签名后，系统会认为这是"新应用"，原有权限记录失效
3. **功能异常**: 签名状态改变可能导致应用功能异常

**如果必须修改图标**：

```bash
# 1. 检查密封资源规则
plutil -p /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/_CodeSignature/CodeResources

# 2. 如果规则是 "^Resources/" => true，不要添加新文件
#    可以考虑替换现有文件（但 Resources 下只有 Skills/ 子目录）

# 3. 如果必须添加，接受重新签名的后果
codesign --sign - --force /Applications/CuaDriver.app
# ⚠️ 警告：这会丢失 Developer ID 和公证状态
```

---

## 总结

| 方案 | 结果 | 原因 |
|------|------|------|
| 官方安装 | ⚠️ 图标显示"无图标占位符" | Resources 目录缺少 AppIcon.icns |
| 手动添加图标 | ❌ 功能异常 | 签名状态改变导致应用异常 |
| 封装后重新安装 | ❌ 权限提示 | 密封资源验证失败，重新签名后权限记录失效 |

**唯一可行的方案是官方发布包含图标的版本**。其他方法都会导致签名问题或权限问题。

---

## 环境信息

- **CuaDriver 版本**: v0.1.9
- **平台**: macOS 26.2 (ARM64)
- **安装包**: `cua-driver-0.1.9-darwin-arm64.tar.gz`

---

希望这份经验对官方和其他用户有帮助！🙏

title: Windows + Linux support for cua-driver via cua-driver-rs (Rust port)
body:
## Summary

Introduces **Windows and Linux support** to cua-driver through `libs/cua-driver-rs/` — a Rust port of the Swift `cua-driver` that runs on all three desktop OSes and ships the same MCP tool surface.

- **Windows** and **Linux**: feature-complete background-automation backends. Windows uses `PostMessage` + UIA; Linux uses X11 + AT-SPI. Both reach background windows without stealing focus from the user's foreground app.
- **macOS**: builds as a universal binary (arm64 + x86_64 via `lipo -create`). Parity with the Swift `cua-driver` is in progress — the Swift binary remains the recommended production macOS driver; the Rust port is BETA on macOS.

The Rust port lives entirely in a new `libs/cua-driver-rs/` directory and publishes to GitHub Releases under the **`cua-driver-rs-v*`** tag prefix. The Swift `cua-driver` keeps its existing `cua-driver-v*` prefix and `libs/cua-driver/` location — no overlap, both installers are pinned to their own prefix.

## What's in the diff

- `libs/cua-driver-rs/` — new Rust workspace (~46 commits squashed into this PR):
  - `crates/cua-driver/` — the binary + CLI front-end (mcp, list-tools, describe, call, serve/stop/status, recording, update, mcp-config, doctor, diagnose, config, dump-docs, --version, --help).
  - `crates/mcp-server/` — shared MCP server + tool registry, recording session, daemon transport.
  - `crates/platform-{macos,windows,linux}/` — platform-specific backends. Every MCP tool lands in the same registered shape across platforms; platform-specific transport differences (CGEvent vs PostMessage vs XSendEvent) are isolated below the tool layer.
  - `crates/cursor-overlay/` — the animated agent-cursor overlay rendered via `tiny-skia` (cross-platform). 16-color palette, Bezier-arc + spring-settle motion, click pulse, idle hide.
  - `tests/integration/` — 111-test parametrized parity suite (`test_api_parity.py`) that runs the **identical test set** against the Swift and Rust binaries to surface drift. Run `./run_tests.sh --parity` for side-by-side comparison.
- `.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml` — release workflow that builds 3 platforms (linux-x86_64, windows-x86_64, darwin-universal via `lipo`) plus bare-binary variants for curlable installers. Marks the GitHub Release as `prerelease: true` with a BETA banner.
- `.github/workflows/release-bump-version.yml` — adds `cua-driver-rs` as a bumpable service and a `target_branch` input.
- `libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/install.sh` — sudo-free installer hard-pinned to the `cua-driver-rs-v*` release prefix.
- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh` — adds a `grep -v cua-driver-rs` defense-in-depth so the Swift installer is provably isolated from the Rust port's releases.
- `libs/cua-driver-rs/PARITY.md` — surface-by-surface audit log of every MCP tool / CLI command / daemon-protocol comparison between the Rust port and the Swift reference, including the deterministic test pattern (`crates/platform-windows/examples/*_parity.rs`) used to lock parity in.

## What this enables for users

- Customers running **Windows** workflows (Sandbox, native, RDP) can now drive backgrounded apps via cua-driver without porting their Swift-only integrations.
- Customers running **Linux** automation (CI containers, Wayland-X11 bridges) get the same MCP tool surface.
- macOS users see no change in the recommended install path — the Swift `install.sh` still resolves to `cua-driver-v*` and the existing CuaDriver.app workflow is untouched.

## Compatibility & isolation

- Tag prefixes are **disjoint**: `cua-driver-v*` (Swift) vs `cua-driver-rs-v*` (Rust). Neither installer's grep regex matches the other's tags; `cua-driver/scripts/install.sh` also has an explicit `grep -v cua-driver-rs` for defense in depth.
- The two binaries publish independently with their own bump-version workflow paths.
- MCP tool names match (same `tools/list` output modulo a few Rust-only extras like `type_text_chars` deprecated alias, `browser_eval`, `get_accessibility_tree`).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green: `linux-x86_64`, `windows-x86_64`, `darwin-universal` builds + release job all pass on the existing v0.1.2 tag (already green on `trycua/cua-staging`).
- [ ] On macOS: `./run_tests.sh --parity` to run the 222-test side-by-side suite against both binaries.
- [ ] On Windows: `cargo build -p cua-driver && cargo run --example list_tools_parity -p platform-windows` (and the other `*_parity.rs` examples) to verify per-tool behavior.
- [ ] Confirm `cua-driver/scripts/install.sh` still resolves the latest `cua-driver-v*` Swift release after the `grep -v cua-driver-rs` addition.
- [ ] Confirm `cua-driver-rs/scripts/install.sh` resolves the latest `cua-driver-rs-v*` release and installs `~/.local/bin/cua-driver`.

title: lume ssh corrupts binary stdout (UTF-8 coercion, ~1.77x expansion on random data)
body:
## Summary

`lume ssh <vm> "<cmd>"` decodes the guest's stdout as UTF-8 before re-emitting it to the host, replacing invalid bytes with U+FFFD (`0xEF 0xBF 0xBD`). Binary streams (gzip, tar, archives, encrypted blobs) are silently corrupted with no error. For uniform-random input, output is ~1.77x larger than the source and unrecoverable. Any host-side pipeline that relies on `lume ssh` for binary transport — e.g. `lume ssh vm 'tar -cf - $d | gzip' | ...` — produces garbage.

## Environment

- lume 0.3.9 (Homebrew)
- Host: macOS 15.x, Apple Silicon
- Guest: `ghcr.io/trycua/macos-tahoe-vanilla:latest`

## Reproduction Steps

```sh
# Inside-VM wc -c: source bytes before they leave the guest.
lume ssh <vm> 'dd if=/dev/urandom bs=1M count=10 2>/dev/null | wc -c'
# 10485760

# Host-side wc -c: what lume ssh actually wrote to the host pipe.
lume ssh <vm> 'dd if=/dev/urandom bs=1M count=10 2>/dev/null' | wc -c
# ~18531371  (≈1.77x expansion)
```

## Root Cause

`SSHResult.output` is typed `String`, forcing stdout through UTF-8 decoding in both SSH backends:

1. **NIO SSH path** — [`libs/lume/src/SSH/SSHClient.swift`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/lume/src/SSH/SSHClient.swift), `CommandExecHandler.checkCompletion`:

   ```swift
   let output = outputBuffer.readString(length: outputBuffer.readableBytes) ?? ""
   ```

   `ByteBuffer.readString(length:)` uses `String(decoding:as: UTF8.self)`, which substitutes invalid bytes with U+FFFD. For uniform-random bytes, ~half don't start a valid UTF-8 sequence and each gets replaced with the 3-byte U+FFFD encoding: `0.5*3 + 0.5*1 ≈ 1.77x`. Matches the observed ratio.

2. **System SSH fallback** — [`libs/lume/src/SSH/SystemSSHClient.swift`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/lume/src/SSH/SystemSSHClient.swift):

   ```swift
   let output = String(data: stdoutData, encoding: .utf8) ?? ""
   ```

   Strict decoder. Returns nil on invalid UTF-8, so binary stdout is silently replaced with the empty string. Different symptom, same root cause.

SSH's connection protocol treats channel data as opaque bytes (RFC 4254 §5.2); there is no encoding contract on stdout. Comparable tools — `tart` (no wrapper; users invoke `ssh` directly), `limactl shell` (execs `/usr/bin/ssh` with inherited stdio) — preserve bytes by never materializing stdout as a `String`.

## Suggested Fix

Change `SSHResult.output` from `String` to `Data` (or `ByteBuffer`). In [`Commands/SSH.swift`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/lume/src/Commands/SSH.swift), write raw bytes to stdout via `FileHandle.standardOutput.write(_:)` instead of `print(result.output)`. Interactive use already bypasses `SSHResult` via PTY, so this preserves it while making non-interactive `lume ssh <vm> <cmd>` a transparent byte conduit.

## Workaround

Base64-wrap inside the VM:

```sh
lume ssh <vm> '<cmd> | base64' | base64 -d
```

Base64 output is ASCII (already valid UTF-8) and survives the coercion intact. ~33% transport overhead.

title: fix(agent): use is not None check in predict_click for zero coordinates
body:
## Summary

`AnthropicHostedToolsConfig.predict_click` uses a Python truthiness check to validate click coordinates:

```python
if action.get("x") and action.get("y"):
```

This silently returns `None` when either coordinate is `0` (falsy in Python). Valid edge-of-screen clicks at `x=0` or `y=0` are incorrectly discarded.

## Changes

Replace the truthiness check with an explicit `None` check in `libs/python/agent/cua_agent/loops/anthropic.py`:

```python
# Before (buggy)
if action.get("x") and action.get("y"):

# After (fixed)
if action.get("x") is not None and action.get("y") is not None:
```

This matches the pattern already used in the OpenAI loop (`openai.py:401`).

## Testing

Added `libs/python/agent/tests/test_predict_click_zero_coords.py` with 6 tests:

- Confirm the old truthiness check drops `x=0`, `y=0`, and `(0, 0)` (regression proof)
- Confirm the fix returns correct coordinates for all three cases
- Non-zero coordinates still work
- Returns `None` when no `computer_call` in response
- Source file contains the `is not None` check (not the old buggy pattern)

Run with:
```bash
pytest libs/python/agent/tests/test_predict_click_zero_coords.py -v
```

title: cd(cua-driver): bake latest version into install.sh after each release
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `BAKED_VERSION` sentinel block to `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh` that the CD workflow updates automatically after every `cua-driver-v*` release
- Version resolution is now: env var override → baked version (no API call) → GitHub API fallback
- Fixes 403 errors seen by `hermes computer-use install` users on shared NAT/VPN IPs that exhaust the 60 req/hr GitHub unauthenticated rate limit
- Also bumps `per_page` from 40 → 100 on the API fallback path so future releases never fall off the page

## How it works

**`install.sh`** gains a sentinel block kept in sync by CI:
```bash
# ~~~ BAKED_VERSION: auto-updated by CD workflow after each release — do not edit ~~~
CUA_DRIVER_BAKED_VERSION="0.1.9"
# ~~~ END_BAKED_VERSION ~~~
```

The tag resolution block now tries the baked version before falling back to the API:
```bash
if   [[ -n "${CUA_DRIVER_VERSION:-}" ]];       then TAG=...  # env pin
elif [[ -n "${CUA_DRIVER_BAKED_VERSION:-}" ]]; then TAG=...  # baked (no API)
else                                                TAG=$(curl api.github.com ...)  # fallback
fi
```

**`cd-swift-cua-driver.yml`** gains a post-release step:
```yaml
- name: Bake version into install.sh
  # fetches main, sed-replaces CUA_DRIVER_BAKED_VERSION, commits, pushes main
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger a `cua-driver-v*` release and confirm the CD step commits an updated `CUA_DRIVER_BAKED_VERSION` line to main
- [ ] Run `install.sh` and confirm it prints `latest release: cua-driver-vX.Y.Z` without making any GitHub API calls (check with `tcpdump` or network proxy if needed)
- [ ] Confirm `CUA_DRIVER_VERSION=0.1.8 ./install.sh` still overrides the baked version correctly

title: cua-driver daemon crash on launch_app when urls contains non-ASCII (CJK) path
body:
Summary
launch_app with urls containing non-ASCII characters (tested with Chinese / CJK paths) causes the daemon to disconnect mid-request. Every retry reproduces. ASCII paths work fine.

Environment
cua-driver v0.1.9
macOS 26.5 (build 25F71), arm64
Daemon started via open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve, verified via cua-driver status
Reproducer

mkdir -p "/Users/me/Desktop/器材控/templates"
cp /path/to/any.key "/Users/me/Desktop/器材控/templates/master_template.key"
cua-driver launch_app '{"bundle_id":"com.apple.Keynote","urls":["/Users/me/Desktop/器材控/templates/master_template.key"]}'
Expected
JSON response with pid and windows array.

Actual

daemon closed connection before responding
Daemon dies; cua-driver status shows not running. CLI auto-relaunches it on next call, same input crashes it again.

Workaround
Copy target file to ASCII path first (e.g. /tmp/).

Probably
Path encoding / NSURL construction inside application(_:open:) not preserving UTF-8 bytes when handing the URL to LaunchServices. launch_app without urls works fine for the same bundle id.

Why this matters
CJK / Cyrillic / accented filenames are common on translator and creator machines. The current behaviour silently breaks any agent flow opening files by path on those systems.

title: cua-driver: kill focus-handle leak class via 4-layer scope binding
body:
## Summary

A leaked `SuppressionHandle` in `SystemFocusStealPreventer` turns the wildcard observer into a process-lifetime focus trap: every `NSWorkspace` activation notification re-routes back to whatever was frontmost at the leak point, so the user can't switch to other apps. CPU spikes because every OS-level focus change fires `Task.detached → MainActor → activate()`. Recovery is only by killing the cua-driver process. I hit this on macOS 14 with v0.1.9 and traced it back to the `WindowChangeDetector.snapshot()` / `detectChanges()` pair.

The root cause is **not** a missing `defer`. It's the API shape: `beginSuppression(...) → handle / endSuppression(handle)` couples acquire and release across module boundaries, async boundaries, and error boundaries. `ClickTool` has 6+ early-return paths between `WindowChangeDetector.snapshot()` (begin) and `detectChanges()` (end); `LaunchAppTool` has a multi-phase placeholder→pid swap with `endSuppression` calls in three branches. Any future copy-paste of either pattern, plus a forgotten cleanup branch, reproduces the leak. Singleton + no deadline + global observer = self-amplifying.

This PR replaces the API surface with **four overlapping leak-prevention layers**, ranked by depth, so the bug class becomes structurally impossible.

## The four layers

| Layer | Mechanism | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Closure scope (preferred)** | `withSuppression { … }` pairs begin/end with a `defer` the caller can't skip | Forgotten release on every exit path the compiler can see (return, throw) |
| **2. ARC scope** | `SuppressionLease` reference type with `deinit` cleanup | Lifetime spanning function boundaries (the snapshot/detect pattern); thrown errors *between* begin and end; future copy-paste regressions |
| **3. Wall-clock deadline** | 5s monotonic deadline per entry; reaper fires on every NSWorkspace observer fire + on a 1s janitor | Every imaginable leak — worst-case duration is bounded regardless of higher-layer correctness |
| **4. Observability** | Origin tags (`#function` default), `os.Logger` warnings on > 4 active entries, `.error` logs on deadline reap | Loud failure mode — future regressions surface in `log show --process cua-driver` instead of silently stealing focus |

Layer 3 is the structural guarantee that the v0.1.9 regression class is impossible — even when a caller uses the deprecated raw API, throws away the handle, and never calls `endSuppression`, the entry is still evicted within `maxLifetimeNs`.

## Migration

`beginSuppression` / `endSuppression` are kept and marked `@available(*, deprecated)`. All internal call sites switched to the scoped APIs:

- `WindowChangeDetector.Snapshot` now holds a `SuppressionLease`. **Dropping the snapshot without calling `detectChanges` is now safe** — the lease's `deinit` releases. This is the structural fix for the `ClickTool` early-return paths.
- `LaunchAppTool` placeholder phase uses `SuppressionLease`, post-launch re-arm uses `withSuppression { … }`.
- `FocusGuard.withFocusSuppressed` migrated to `SuppressionLease` (do/catch with two manual end calls is exactly the pattern this PR makes safe).

External callers continue to compile against the deprecated API and now also benefit from the deadline safety net.

## Implementation details

- `OSAllocatedUnfairLock<Bool>` (not `NSLock`) for the lease's released-flag — Swift 6 bans `NSLock.lock()` from async contexts. macOS 13+, fits our `.macOS(.v14)` target.
- `clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW)` for entry deadlines — wall-time jumps (sleep, NTP slew) can't accidentally expire entries early or extend leaks.
- Reaper runs on every observer fire (so a leaked wildcard stops hijacking activations *before* the next user app-switch) and on a 1s janitor (so idle leaks recover without needing an activation event).
- Janitor is started lazily on first add and stops itself when the dispatcher idles to zero entries — no permanent background task.
- `SuppressionLease.deinit` schedules a `Task.detached` for the actor hop. Pending reactivation tasks are orphaned (harmless idempotent `activate(options: [])` calls), and the deadline safety net catches the same case in bounded time even if that Task is never scheduled.

## Test coverage

8 new tests in `Tests/FocusStealPreventerTests/`, all green in 0.7 s total:

- `testWithSuppressionReleasesOnReturn` — closure scope, normal path
- `testWithSuppressionReleasesOnThrow` — closure scope, error path
- `testLeaseReleasesOnExplicitCall` — ARC, explicit `release()`
- `testLeaseReleaseIsIdempotent` — ARC, double release
- `testLeaseReleasesOnDeinit` — ARC contract (the language guarantee)
- `testDeadlineReapsLeakedManualEntry` — **the v0.1.9 regression test** (deprecated API + leaked handle still recovers)
- `testDeadlineReapsOnlyExpiredEntries` — precision (still-live entries survive a reap pass)
- `testEndSuppressionAfterDeadlineIsNoOp` — idempotency of late end calls

The deadline test uses a 200 ms `maxLifetimeNs` via a public init seam — production keeps the 5 s default. `_forceReapForTesting()` exposes the reap path so tests don't have to fire `NSWorkspace` notifications from a unit-test context.

## Risk

Low — the deprecated API is preserved, all existing call sites are migrated and tested, and `swift build` + `swift test` are clean. The 0 ms `suppressionDelayNs` and the wildcard observer behavior are unchanged. The only behavioral difference for callers on the old API is that a forgotten `endSuppression` now self-recovers in ≤ 5 s instead of leaking forever — strictly better.

Happy to split into smaller PRs if reviewers prefer (preventer + tests, then per-tool migration). Kept it as one because the migration depends on the new APIs.

title: CI: re-run cua-driver docs generator on release-bump to prevent stale-version drift
body:
## Summary

The cua-driver docs generator (`scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver.ts`) is not currently re-run on release bumps, so the generated docs (`docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/cli-reference.mdx`, `mcp-tools.mdx`) carry stale version strings until the next PR that happens to trip the `Check Documentation Sync` CI gate.

## Evidence

Discovered while unblocking PR #1492. Three accumulated sources of drift in that PR's docs-sync failure:

1. **Version bump never regenerated docs.** Docs were stamped `Version: 0.1.6` but the binary now reports `0.1.7` (commit `81baebe8` "Bump cua-driver to v0.1.7" didn't re-run the generator).
2. **Upstream docstring edits never regenerated docs** — three tool docstrings (`get_window_state`, `launch_app`) were updated in Swift sources between merges without running the generator.
3. The PR that finally tripped the check (#1492) had nothing to do with the drift — its own diff (`AppLauncher.locate()` internals) didn't change any public CLI/MCP surface. It was just the unlucky next-PR-to-touch-cua-driver.

This creates a bad pattern: the next person to open a cua-driver PR inherits the accumulated docs drift and has to do unrelated regen work.

## Proposed fix

Two complementary changes, either alone would solve it:

**Option A — bake into release-bump workflow**

Add a step to `.github/workflows/release-bump-version.yml` (or wherever the version-bump PR is created) that runs `npx tsx scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver.ts` after the version change, so the generated docs land in the same PR as the version bump.

**Option B — bake into the release-build workflow**

Have `.github/workflows/cd-swift-cua-driver.yml` run the generator with `--check` as a release gate, so a release can't ship without docs matching source.

Option A is preferred — it shifts the cost to the PR that introduces the drift (the version bump), not the next unrelated cua-driver PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- A version bump PR (`Bump cua-driver to vX.Y.Z`) includes the regenerated `cli-reference.mdx` / `mcp-tools.mdx` in the same diff.
- A standalone PR touching only Swift source docstrings still has to re-run the generator (this issue doesn't change that — it just covers the version-bump case).
- Same treatment applied to cua-driver-rs (`scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver-rs.ts` or whatever the Rust generator is named) since the same pattern will apply there.

title: parity(launch_app): port Swift #1492 bundle-ID + locale fallbacks to Rust
body:
## Summary

Ports Dylan's just-merged Swift fix from PR #1492 (`3b5c372d`) to the Rust port. `launch_app` on macOS now accepts the same three input shapes the Swift binary does — bundle identifiers as `name`, locale-specific display names, and case-insensitive variants — not just the exact on-disk bundle filename.

The Rust resolver `apps::locate_app_by_name` mirrors Swift `AppLauncher.locate(bundleId:name:)` with the same three-pass chain:

1. **Filesystem `<name>.app` lookup** in the canonical roots (`/Applications`, `/System/Applications[/Utilities]`, `~/Applications`, `~/Applications/Chrome Apps.localized`). Fast, locale-independent.
2. **LaunchServices bundle-ID lookup** via `NSWorkspace.URLForApplicationWithBundleIdentifier:` (objc2). Lets `name="com.apple.calculator"` resolve without switching to the `bundle_id` parameter.
3. **Fuzzy scan, case-insensitive:**
   - Locale-aware `localizedName` from `NSRunningApplication` (covers e.g. `計算機` on JP macOS for Calculator).
   - `CFBundleDisplayName` → `CFBundleName` from each candidate bundle's Info.plist (via `plutil -extract`, matching the existing `scan_installed_apps` pattern in this file).
   - Bundle URL stem (filename minus `.app`).

When a match resolves to a bundle ID, `launch_app_by_name` and `launch_with_urls_by_name` delegate to the bundle-ID launch path (`open -g -b`) — unambiguous, avoids a second LaunchServices lookup inside `open`. Falls back to `open <path>` when no bundle ID is recovered, and finally to a raw `open -g -a <name>` if the resolver misses (preserves the pre-fix behavior for unusual installs LaunchServices already knows about).

## Scope

Only `crates/platform-macos/` and the parity test/doc files. Linux and Windows backends are untouched — bundle ID / locale display name is a macOS concept (the Windows port already documents `name` as a path/bundle alias).

## Before / After

```
# Before this PR (Rust binary)
launch_app name="com.apple.calculator" → "Could not locate app"
launch_app name="CALCULATOR"           → "Could not locate app"

# After this PR (Rust binary)
launch_app name="com.apple.calculator" → pid=…, bundle_id=com.apple.calculator
launch_app name="CALCULATOR"           → pid=…, bundle_id=com.apple.calculator
launch_app name="Calculator"           → pid=…, (regression guard)
launch_app name="no_such_app_xyzzy"    → MCP error
```

## Files touched

- `libs/cua-driver-rs/crates/platform-macos/src/apps.rs` — new `locate_app_by_name` + `ResolvedApp` and supporting helpers (`url_for_application_with_bundle_identifier`, `find_running_app_by_localized_name`, `read_bundle_metadata`, `app_search_roots`).
- `libs/cua-driver-rs/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/launch_app.rs` — `launch_with_urls_by_name` now runs the resolver first; raw `open -g -a` remains as a fallback.
- `libs/cua-driver-rs/tests/integration/test_api_parity.py` — three new parametrized parity tests:
  - `test_mcp_launch_app_by_name_accepts_bundle_id`
  - `test_mcp_launch_app_by_name_case_insensitive`
  - `test_mcp_launch_app_unknown_name_raises_error`
- `libs/cua-driver-rs/PARITY.md` — `launch_app` macOS row flipped from `OPEN` → `VERIFIED` with cross-reference to Swift `AppLauncher.locate` (PR #1492). Notes block ported.
- `libs/cua-driver-rs/Cargo.lock` — workspace version bumps (cua-driver 0.1.2→0.1.3, cursor-overlay, mcp-server, focus-monitor-win) refreshed during build; matches the version numbers already committed in `Cargo.toml` files since commit `c1731734`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build -p platform-macos --release` clean (no new warnings).
- [x] `cargo build --release` (full workspace) clean.
- [x] All 5 launch_app parity tests pass on the Rust binary:
  - `test_mcp_launch_app_by_bundle_id`
  - `test_mcp_launch_app_by_name`
  - `test_mcp_launch_app_by_name_accepts_bundle_id` (new)
  - `test_mcp_launch_app_by_name_case_insensitive` (new)
  - `test_mcp_launch_app_unknown_name_raises_error` (new)
- [x] Full Rust parity suite still green (114/114).
- [ ] Re-run the new tests against a freshly-built Swift binary (local Swift binary at `~/cua/libs/cua-driver/.build/release/cua-driver` is from before `3b5c372d`, so `test_mcp_launch_app_by_name_accepts_bundle_id` currently fails on it pre-rebuild — expected, the Swift fix already landed on `main`).
- [ ] CI to run both binaries via `./run_tests.sh --parity` once Swift binary in CI cache rebuilds against `3b5c372d`.

## References

- Swift fix: PR #1492 (commit `3b5c372d`)
- Swift implementation: `libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverCore/Apps/AppLauncher.swift::AppLauncher.locate(bundleId:name:)`

title: cua-driver-rs: missing TCC auto-relaunch (#1479 equivalent) — mcp from IDE terminals fails
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver-rs mcp` lacks the TCC auto-relaunch behavior that Swift PR #1479 added to the original `cua-driver` binary. When invoked from an IDE terminal (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Warp), macOS TCC attributes the subprocess to the parent terminal — not to `CuaDriver.app` — so AX accessibility probes fail silently against the wrong bundle id.

## Context

- **Issue #1465** identified the TCC attribution problem on macOS.
- **PR #1479** fixed it for the Swift binary via:
  - Detection heuristic: `Bundle.main.bundlePath` + `realpath` checks for `/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/` presence, plus ppid != launchd (shell-spawned context).
  - Auto-relaunch: When wrong TCC context detected, spawn daemon via `open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve`.
  - Proxy: Run in-process MCP stdio server that forwards every ListTools/CallTool request through the daemon's Unix socket (`~/Library/Caches/cua-driver/cua-driver.sock`).
  - Tool semantics identical to in-process path; MCP client sees ordinary stdio server.
  - Escape hatch: `--no-daemon-relaunch` flag + `CUA_DRIVER_MCP_NO_RELAUNCH=1` env var.

## What Swift does

See **libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverCLI/**:
- **BundleHelpers.swift**: `isExecutableInsideCuaDriverApp()` — realpath-based detection of bare binary inside an installed .app bundle.
- **CuaDriverCommand.swift** (lines ~342–450): `MCPCommand` struct with:
  - `shouldUseDaemonProxy()` (lines ~459–472): detects shell-spawned context via `Bundle.main.bundlePath.hasSuffix(".app")`, `isExecutableInsideCuaDriverApp()`, and ppid check.
  - `runViaDaemonProxy()` (lines ~475–508): ensures daemon via `open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve`, waits up to 10s, then runs proxy MCP server forwarding to the daemon socket.
  - `launchDaemonViaOpen()` (lines ~510–529): spawns the daemon via Process + /usr/bin/open.

## What Rust lacks

**libs/cua-driver-rs/crates/cua-driver/src/main.rs** (lines 147, 308):
- `cli::Command::Mcp => {} // fall through to MCP server startup below` (line 147)
- No TCC context detection before MCP server startup.
- No daemon relaunch logic.
- No MCP proxy mode.

**libs/cua-driver-rs/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs** (lines 20–21):
- Command enum has no `--no-daemon-relaunch` or `--socket` flags.
- `parse_command()` does not recognize these flags.

**libs/cua-driver-rs/crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs**:
- Plain stdio MCP server; no proxy logic or daemon socket integration.

The Rust `call` command (cli.rs lines 287–363) has daemon forwarding — it checks if a daemon is listening and proxies requests through the socket if one is reachable. **MCP does not have this logic.**

## Packaging implications

The Swift binary ships as part of **CuaDriver.app** (a macOS application bundle). The `open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve` command can relaunch it directly from the bundle.

The Rust binary is installed bare at `~/.local/bin/cua-driver` (or similar) via **libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/install.sh**. There is no .app bundle wrapping the Rust binary today.

**Question: what should the Rust fix relaunch into?**

Two options:
1. **Create a .app bundle for cua-driver-rs** (like the Swift version) and use the same `open -a` relaunch path. This would match the Swift architecture exactly.
2. **Use an alternative relaunch strategy** — e.g. spawn the binary directly with elevated TCC context via a helper process, or rely on a separate .app bundle created by the installer, or find a macOS API that grants TCC context without needing a bundle.

Option 1 is simplest and mirrors the Swift fix exactly. It would also allow the installer to register the Rust binary inside `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` (alongside or instead of the Swift binary for the macOS GA flip).

## Scope estimate

**Minimal (option 1 — relaunch into a Rust-specific .app bundle):**
- ~200–400 LOC: TCC detection heuristic (Rust equivalent of `isExecutableInsideCuaDriverApp()` + ppid check).
- ~100–150 LOC: daemon launch logic (Process-based equivalent of `launchDaemonViaOpen`).
- ~150–200 LOC: proxy MCP server (forward ListTools/CallTool to daemon socket).
- ~50 LOC: CLI flag + env var support (`--no-daemon-relaunch`, `CUA_DRIVER_MCP_NO_RELAUNCH`).
- ~100 LOC: .app bundle packaging (Cargo.toml build script, or separate macOS build step).
- **Total: ~600–900 LOC** (moderate complexity, mostly straightforward porting of the Swift code to Rust).

**Complexity: medium.**
- Requires understanding of macOS TCC, NSWorkspace/LaunchServices (or Rust equivalents), Process spawning, realpath.
- Requires .app bundle creation and packaging (may need new build step or CI changes).
- Cross-platform concerns: the feature is macOS-only, so conditional compilation is required.

## Why this matters for macOS GA flip

The Rust port is aimed at macOS parity with the Swift cua-driver before the macOS GA flip. AX permission failures due to wrong TCC context are a critical blocker: users on IDE terminals (the most common macOS IDE scenario) would see silent AX failures or get spurious permission-denied messages.

Without this fix, the Rust port cannot be recommended for production macOS automation when invoked from an IDE. This breaks the "feature-complete Rust port" narrative and delays the macOS GA flip.

## Acceptance criteria

1. TCC detection heuristic (realpath + ppid check) implemented in Rust.
2. Auto-relaunch into a macOS .app bundle (either a Rust-specific one or the existing CuaDriver.app).
3. MCP proxy mode: stdio server forwards ListTools/CallTool requests to daemon socket.
4. Escape hatch: `--no-daemon-relaunch` flag + `CUA_DRIVER_MCP_NO_RELAUNCH=1` env var work.
5. `cua-driver mcp` from an IDE terminal transparently uses the proxy path and succeeds at AX probes.
6. No change to tool semantics or MCP protocol — the client sees the same stdio server.
7. Documentation: add a macOS-specific section to the mcp-config docs explaining the auto-relaunch behavior and how to opt out.
8. Tests: verify TCC context detection and daemon launch/proxy logic on macOS CI.

---

**Related:**
- #1465 (original TCC attribution issue)
- PR #1479 (Swift fix)
- cd-rust-cua-driver.yml (.github/workflows/ — Rust packaging; may need .app bundle step)

title: cua-driver-rs: port WindowChangeDetector + FocusGuard per-action focus suppression
body:
## Context

PR #1524 ported `SystemFocusStealPreventer` from Swift to Rust, enabling the **launch-time focus-suppression** path. The reactive focus-suppression machinery that prevents **per-action side-effect activations** (clicking a button that opens a dialog, typing into a field that triggers autocomplete, etc.) remains unported.

The Swift `cua-driver` has two cross-cutting helpers that wrap individual AX actions with focus suppression:

1. **WindowChangeDetector** (`libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverServer/Tools/WindowChangeDetector.swift:20-212`) — captures window/foreground state before an action, detects changes after, and emits a summary of any opened windows or app-switch side-effects. Arms a **wildcard** suppression entry covering the snapshot→detect cycle.

2. **FocusGuard** (`libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverCore/Focus/FocusGuard.swift:27-157`) — wraps individual AX-action calls with per-**targeted** focus-suppression and synthetic focus manipulation. Used inside ClickTool, TypeTextTool, SetValueTool, etc. to catch self-activations triggered by clicking or typing on focus-grabbing UI.

## What these do

**WindowChangeDetector** (line 20-212):
- `snapshot()` captures `(window_ids: Set<Int>, frontPid: Int32?, suppressionHandle)` before the action, arms a wildcard focus-steal suppressor (targetPid=0).
- `detectChanges(snapshot)` polls for up to 1.3s for new windows or foreground changes, returns `Changes { newWindows: [WindowEvent], foregroundChanged: Bool }` and yields a `resultSuffix` describing what happened (e.g., "opened new window(s): Chrome").
- `reRaiseForeground(pid)` re-activates the prior frontmost app if needed.
- The wildcard suppressor stays armed for the full snapshot→action→detect cycle, blocking any app from stealing focus before we notice it in the poll loop.

**FocusGuard** (line 27-157):
- `withFocusSuppressed(pid, element, body)` wraps an AX action call with three layers of protection:
  1. Enablement — set `AXManualAccessibility` / `AXEnhancedUserInterface` on the app root (no-op on native Cocoa, required for Chromium/Electron).
  2. Synthetic focus — write `AXFocused` / `AXMain` on the enclosing window + element before the action, restore after. Makes AppKit's state machine behave as if the action came from a focused process, preventing reflexive self-activation.
  3. Reactive — arms `SystemFocusStealPreventer` with a targeted entry if the target isn't already frontmost.
- Includes special case: skips synthetic focus on minimized windows (writing AXFocused=true on a minimized window deminiaturizes apps like Chrome).
- All cleanup is RAII (even on error).

## Rust gap (confirmed)

`crates/platform-macos/src/` has **no**:
- `window_change_detector.rs`
- `focus_guard.rs`
- Calls to these from the action tools (`click.rs`, `type_text.rs`, `hotkey.rs`, `press_key.rs`, `drag.rs`, `scroll.rs`, `set_value.rs`)

Verified by:
```bash
grep -r "WindowChangeDetector\|FocusGuard\|snapshot_windows\|with_focus_suppressed" \
  crates/platform-macos/src/ 2>/dev/null
# Returns nothing
```

## Infrastructure already shipped

- `crates/platform-macos/src/focus_steal.rs` (PR #1524):
  - `FocusStealPreventer::shared()` singleton
  - `begin_suppression(target_pid, restore_to, origin)` → `SuppressionLease` (RAII Drop)
  - `with_suppression(target, restore_to, origin, f)` closure API
  - Wildcard support (targetPid=None matches any activation)
  - 5s deadline + 1s janitor (prevents stale leak)
  - NSWorkspace observer subscribed to `didActivateApplicationNotification`

- `crates/platform-macos/src/windows.rs`:
  - `visible_windows() → Vec<WindowInfo>` (layer 0 only)
  - Fields: `window_id`, `pid`, `app_name`, `title`, `bounds`, `layer`, etc.
  - Thread-safe per CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo docs

## Scope estimate

**Lines of code (rough):**
- WindowChangeDetector struct + snapshot/detect/snapshot_windows: ~120–150 LOC
- FocusGuard + AXEnablementAssertion wrapper + synthetic focus manipulation: ~180–220 LOC
- Integration into each tool:
  - Per-tool wrapper around AX action block: ~15–25 LOC
  - 7 tools × ~20 LOC avg = 140 LOC
  - click.rs + double_click (or refactor as click(count=2)): ~30 LOC
  - type_text.rs: ~20 LOC
  - hotkey.rs: ~15 LOC
  - press_key.rs: ~15 LOC
  - drag.rs: ~20 LOC
  - scroll.rs: ~20 LOC
  - set_value.rs: ~20 LOC
- Tests (parity with Swift): ~150–200 LOC

**Total: ~600–750 LOC in a single PR**. Likely 2–3 days elapsed time (review, iteration on AX edge cases).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `WindowChangeDetector` module in `crates/platform-macos/src/` with:
  - `snapshot() → Snapshot { window_ids, front_pid, suppression_handle }`
  - `detect_changes(snapshot) → Changes { new_windows, foreground_changed, result_suffix }`
  - Thread-safe window enumeration (no main-thread hop)
  - Wildcard suppressor integration
- [ ] `FocusGuard` in same module with:
  - `with_focus_suppressed(pid, element, body)` async closure wrapper
  - Enablement layer (AXManualAccessibility / AXEnhancedUserInterface)
  - Synthetic focus layer (AXFocused / AXMain write + restore)
  - Minimized-window skip logic
  - Targeted suppressor integration
- [ ] Integration into 7 tools:
  - ClickTool (AX path): snapshot → click → detectChanges → re-raise if needed
  - ClickTool (pixel path): skip (pure CGEvent, no AX side-effects)
  - TypeTextTool: withFocusSuppressed around AXSelectedText write + fallback
  - SetValueTool: withFocusSuppressed around AXValue write
  - PressKeyTool: skip (CGEvent only, no AX)
  - HotKeyTool: skip (CGEvent only, no AX)
  - DragTool: skip or wrap (mostly CGEvent, some AX setup)
  - ScrollTool: skip (AXScroll via DOMContentLoaded AX element)
- [ ] Tests:
  - WindowChangeDetector snapshot/detect roundtrip
  - FocusGuard synthetic-focus and enablement layers
  - Real-world regression tests: click on button that opens dialog, type into Chrome web input, click Safari link that opens new tab
- [ ] Result suffix appended to tool output (matching Swift verbatim)

## Why it matters

Without this, agent actions on backgrounded apps can:
1. Trigger involuntary context switches (clicking an element that launches Finder, typing into a field that opens a search result autocomplete, etc.)
2. Leave no trace of the side-effect in the tool result (agent has no signal that something unexpected happened)
3. Surprise the user with their window stack reshuffled mid-task

The wildcard + targeted dual-layer design is empirically necessary:
- Wildcard (during snapshot→action→detect) catches fast self-activations before the poll loop observes them
- Targeted (during individual AX calls) catches slower ones (WebKit, Safari link handling)
- Together they close the ~200ms window during which a side-effect app can activate, yielding ~99% suppression on real-world workflows

---

**Related:**
- PR #1524 (SystemFocusStealPreventer Rust port)
- Swift originals: `libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverServer/Tools/WindowChangeDetector.swift`, `libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverCore/Focus/FocusGuard.swift`, `libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverCore/Focus/FocusGuard.swift`

title: cua-driver-rs: missing interactive PermissionsGate (first-launch UX)
body:
## Summary

Swift **cua-driver** has an interactive permissions-grant flow (`PermissionsGate`) that Rust **cua-driver-rs** completely lacks. This is a real first-launch UX gap.

### What Swift has

- **PermissionsGate** class: friendly SwiftUI panel shown on `serve` startup
  - Location: `libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverCore/Permissions/PermissionsGate.swift`
  - Shows missing Accessibility + Screen Recording permissions with "Open System Settings" buttons
  - Auto-chains between Settings panes (grant one, Settings auto-opens to the other)
  - Polls TCC state every second and auto-dismisses when all granted
  - Prevents daemon startup until permissions are confirmed

### What Rust has

- **check_permissions** MCP tool: read-only status check + optional system prompts
  - Calls `AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions` and `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess` (raw macOS dialogs, not branded UI)
  - No interactive panel, no chaining, no auto-dismiss
  - Requires explicit tool call (not automatic on startup)

### Impact

**Rust users get worse first-launch experience:** system-native permission dialogs are terse and don't explain what the permissions are for. They don't chain between Accessibility and Screen Recording the way the Swift gate does.

### Notes

- The check_permissions tool itself is correctly implemented (parity verified in PARITY.md)
- The gap is the **absence of startup-time interactive gate**, not the tool itself
- Similar logic already in Rust for daemon relaunch detection + TCC context fixes; adding a UI panel is incremental

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Port PermissionsGate equivalent to Rust (blocking serve startup, shows window, auto-dismisses)
2. Call it automatically before daemon socket bind
3. Verify first-launch UX matches Swift (interactive panel, chaining, auto-dismiss)

title: cua-driver-rs: missing telemetry (PostHog integration)
body:
## Summary

Swift **cua-driver** ships with **TelemetryClient** (PostHog integration) that Rust **cua-driver-rs** completely lacks. This is an analytics gap that makes it hard to understand Rust user behavior.

### What Swift has

- **TelemetryClient** class
  - Location: `libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverCore/Telemetry/TelemetryClient.swift`
  - Posts to `https://eu.i.posthog.com/capture/` with API key
  - Sends: version, OS, OS version, CPU architecture, CI-detection flag, stable per-install UUID
  - Does NOT send: usernames, file paths, command arguments, anything user-typed
  - Records events: `cua_driver_install` (one-time, bypasses opt-out), `cua_driver_mcp`, `cua_driver_serve`, `cua_driver_call`, etc.
  - Opt-out via `CUA_DRIVER_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` or persisted config flag
  - Respects env overrides `CUA_DRIVER_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` and `CUA_DRIVER_TELEMETRY_DEBUG`

### What Rust has

- **Nothing** — no telemetry, no analytics, no usage insights
- Rust telemetry ID path documented in `diagnose` output but never used

### Impact

**Can't measure Rust adoption or usage patterns.** Swift has usage insights that are important for:
- Understanding which features users actually exercise
- Detecting regressions (if a command suddenly has 0 traffic)
- Measuring Windows / Linux adoption separately
- Justifying continued investment in Rust port

### Decision points

1. **Should we port it?** Yes, telemetry is valuable for platform decisions
2. **Same endpoint + API key?** Or separate tracking for Rust vs Swift?
3. **Same config flag structure?** Or separate `CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`?
4. **Windows / Linux?** Yes — the Rust port targets all three, so telemetry should too

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Port TelemetryClient to Rust (or equivalent minimal PostHog client)
2. Hook it into CLI entry points (mcp, serve, call, etc.)
3. Verify opt-out flag is respected (`CUA_DRIVER_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false`)
4. Test on macOS, Windows, Linux
5. Document privacy posture (same as Swift — non-identifying)

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): port TelemetryClient PostHog integration (#1528)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1528. Ports Swift's `TelemetryClient` (anonymous usage telemetry to PostHog) to the Rust port `cua-driver-rs`. Same endpoint, same event names, same payload shape, same opt-out semantics as Swift — so dashboards aggregate cleanly.

## What lands

- **`crates/cua-driver/src/telemetry.rs`** — new module with `capture(event, properties)`, `capture_install()`, `is_enabled()`, and canonical event-name constants mirrored 1:1 from Swift's `TelemetryEvent`.
- **HTTP client**: `ureq` v3 (rustls + json features). Fire-and-forget with 3 s timeout; runs on `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` when a runtime is live, else on a short-lived OS thread.
- **Call-site wiring**: every CLI dispatch in `main.rs` calls `emit_entry_telemetry(&command)` once after parsing, before doing work. `call <tool>` reports as `cua_driver_api_<tool>` so per-tool adoption is visible without ever recording args.
- **Hidden `cua-driver telemetry install-event` subcommand** — used by `scripts/install.sh` post-install to fire the one-shot `cua_driver_install` ping. Guarded by `~/.cua-driver-rs/.installation_recorded` marker so it only fires once per install.
- **`scripts/install.sh`** — backgrounded post-install call so the install ping never delays the user-facing "installed" log line.
- **`PARITY.md`** — new "Telemetry (PostHog)" section documenting endpoint, event names, payload shape, privacy posture, opt-out env var, HTTP client choice, and intentional divergences from Swift.

## Privacy posture

Identical to Swift. Each event sends: driver version, OS name, OS version, CPU arch, CI-environment flag, and a stable per-install UUID. The payload **never** contains usernames, file paths, command arguments, tool args, screenshot paths, window titles, application names, or coordinates. Asserted by a unit test that serializes the payload and greps for `$user`/`username`/`home_dir`/`cwd`/`argv`.

## Independence from Swift install (deliberate)

The Rust install ID lives at `~/.cua-driver-rs/.telemetry_id` and is opted out via `CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` — both intentionally distinct from Swift's `~/.cua-driver/.telemetry_id` + `CUA_DRIVER_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`. This means:

- A machine with both ports installed shows up as two distinct adoption events (we can count Rust adoption separately from Swift).
- A user who opts out of one port stays opted-in for the other unless they set both env vars.
- The Rust port can ship telemetry changes without invalidating Swift's install UUID (no shared on-disk state).

Documented in `PARITY.md` under "Independence from Swift install".

## Opt-out

`CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` (or `0` / `no` / `off`) disables ALL telemetry from the binary. The **only** path that bypasses the check is `capture_install()` (one-shot adoption ping fired by `install.sh`) — every subsequent event respects the flag normally. Verified locally and in unit tests.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build -p cua-driver --release` — clean build green on macOS arm64.
- [x] `cargo test -p cua-driver --release telemetry` — 8 unit tests pass (env parsing, opt-out default, CI detection, payload shape, payload-key collision, install-id idempotent persistence, ISO-8601 format, arch mapping).
- [x] Manual: `cua-driver list-tools` with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` silently skips the POST.
- [x] Manual: `cua-driver list-tools` with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=true` prints `[telemetry] sending event: cua_driver_list_tools`.
- [x] Manual: `cua-driver telemetry install-event` returns PostHog HTTP 200 on first call; second call is silent (marker file present).
- [x] Manual: `cua-driver --version` exits cleanly without firing telemetry.
- [ ] CI: verify Linux and Windows builds (cross-platform `ureq + rustls` build).
- [ ] Manual on Linux: `cua-driver list-tools` with debug — confirm POST works.
- [ ] Manual on Windows: same.

## Commits (4)

1. `feat(telemetry): TelemetryClient with PostHog integration + opt-out` — module + unit tests, no call-site wiring.
2. `feat(cli): emit telemetry events from mcp/serve/call subcommands` — wire `capture(...)` at dispatch + add `telemetry install-event` hidden subcommand.
3. `feat(install.sh): emit cua_driver_install event post-install` — installer hook.
4. `docs(PARITY.md): document telemetry parity + opt-out` — new section.

title: cua-driver-rs: notarize + sign CuaDriverRs.app for Gatekeeper-clean installs
body:
## Summary

PR #1530 introduced the `CuaDriverRs.app` bundle (required for TCC attribution per #1525). The current `.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml` builds the bundle but **does not sign or notarize it**. End users installing via `install.sh` will hit a Gatekeeper warning on first launch ("can't be opened because Apple cannot check it for malicious software") and have to right-click → Open. That's a non-starter for production rollout.

## Context

The Swift `cua-driver` already signs + notarizes via `libs/cua-driver/scripts/build/build-release-notarized.sh` + `.github/workflows/cd-swift-cua-driver.yml`. Same Apple Developer ID Application cert, same notarytool API key — the secrets are already in the repo.

## Proposed scope

**Split into a separate workflow** (or add as an opt-in step on the existing one) so we can iterate on the signing/notarization plumbing without risking the main Rust release pipeline.

Concretely:

1. New workflow `cd-rust-cua-driver-notarize.yml` (or add a step to the existing CD), triggered on `workflow_dispatch` initially, later promoted to run on every release.
2. Steps:
   - Build `CuaDriverRs.app` as today
   - Import Developer ID Application cert from secret into a temporary keychain
   - `codesign --deep --options runtime --timestamp --sign "Developer ID Application: ..." /path/to/CuaDriverRs.app`
   - Zip the .app and submit to notarytool: `xcrun notarytool submit ./CuaDriverRs.app.zip --wait --key ... --key-id ... --issuer ...`
   - `xcrun stapler staple /path/to/CuaDriverRs.app`
   - Verify: `spctl -a -v /path/to/CuaDriverRs.app` should report `accepted` `source=Notarized Developer ID`
   - Repackage signed+stapled .app into the release tarball

## Acceptance criteria

- A signed, notarized, stapled `CuaDriverRs.app` ships in every Rust release tarball
- `spctl -a -v CuaDriverRs.app` reports `accepted` after install
- First-launch from `/Applications/CuaDriverRs.app` produces no Gatekeeper warning
- The notarization step is isolated enough that a failure doesn't block the un-notarized build (so we can still ship dev artifacts during iteration)

## Dependencies

- PR #1530 must merge first (introduces the `.app` bundle the workflow signs).

## References

- Swift signing/notarization workflow for reference: `.github/workflows/cd-swift-cua-driver.yml`
- Swift build script: `libs/cua-driver/scripts/build/build-release-notarized.sh`

title: cua-driver: add `--experimental-rust` install flag to opt into cua-driver-rs backend
body:
## Summary

Add a `--experimental-rust` flag to the canonical `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh` that delegates to `libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/install.sh`, so early adopters can opt into the Rust binary without us flipping the default switch on everyone at once.

## Context

cua-driver-rs is approaching feature parity with cua-driver Swift on macOS (PRs #1524, #1529, #1530, #1531, #1532 cover the GA-blocker stack). Before promoting Rust to default — and before deprecating Swift — we want a soak period where early adopters can opt in via a single flag, hit any remaining edge cases in real use, and report back. Same pattern other tools use (`--use-experimental-backend`, `--track=beta`, etc.).

## Proposed scope

1. Modify `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh`:
   - Parse a new `--experimental-rust` flag (also accept `--backend=rust` for explicitness)
   - When set: print a one-line "Installing experimental Rust backend. The Swift binary won't be touched." note and `exec` into `libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/install.sh` with the rest of the argv passed through
   - Otherwise: existing Swift install path, unchanged

2. Document the flag in `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guide/getting-started/installation.mdx` under a "Try the Rust backend (experimental)" callout that explains:
   - What the Rust port is (port of the same MCP tool surface, Windows/Linux support, macOS BETA today)
   - That it installs to `/Applications/CuaDriverRs.app` (separate from Swift's `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`)
   - That both binaries can coexist (different TCC grants, different telemetry IDs)
   - That `~/.local/bin/cua-driver` will point to the Rust binary after this install, but the Swift binary stays installed and reusable via its bundle path

3. Same flag on the `install.sh` one-liner in the README / docs ("curl ... | bash -s -- --experimental-rust").

4. After this lands, communicate to Hermes (and other downstream wrappers) that they can recommend the flag to users who want to try Rust ahead of GA.

## Acceptance criteria

- `curl -fsSL .../install.sh | bash` works as before (Swift install).
- `curl -fsSL .../install.sh | bash -s -- --experimental-rust` installs the Rust binary into `/Applications/CuaDriverRs.app` + `~/.local/bin/cua-driver` symlink.
- Both can be installed on the same machine without conflict (verified by running both `--version` calls after).
- Docs page updated with the experimental callout and a "how to switch back" note (`rm /Applications/CuaDriverRs.app && cua-driver` falls back to whichever bundle the symlink points at).

## Dependencies

- Should land **after** #(notarization issue) so the experimental install pulls a Gatekeeper-clean artifact.
- Independent of the individual GA-blocker PRs (#1530, #1531) — they can land in any order; the flag just delegates to whatever the current cua-driver-rs install.sh does.

## Non-goals

- Not flipping the default. That's a separate, later decision once we have soak data.
- Not removing the Swift binary or its install path.
- Not changing Hermes' upstream installer reference — that stays on Swift until GA.

title: cua-driver-rs: surface 'new version available' banner with one-line update instructions
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver-rs` already has the `update` subcommand for performing the update; what it lacks is **proactive surfacing** that an update is available. Users running an outdated version today won't know unless they manually check the GitHub releases page. Other modern CLI tools display a small "new version available" hint at startup with a single command to upgrade — adopt that pattern here.

## Desired behavior

When the user invokes an interactive entry point (`cua-driver mcp`, `cua-driver serve`, possibly `cua-driver doctor`), if a newer release exists, print a small banner like:

```
✨ cua-driver v0.1.4 is available (you have v0.1.3).
   Update with: cua-driver update
   Release notes: https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.1.4
```

Specifically:

1. **Check is asynchronous and non-blocking.** Spawn the version check in the background at startup so the MCP server / daemon spin-up is never delayed by network latency. If the check completes before the first tool call, the banner gets included in the next stderr line; otherwise it appears next launch.

2. **Cache on disk to avoid hammering GitHub.** Store the last-check timestamp + latest-version string in `~/.cua-driver-rs/version_check.json`. Refresh only if older than ~20 hours.

3. **Version source = `https://api.github.com/repos/trycua/cua/releases/latest` filtered to the `cua-driver-rs-v*` tag prefix** (same source the `update` subcommand already uses — share the code path).

4. **Persistent "skip until next version" dismissal.** Three actions when banner fires interactively: update now, skip this run, skip until next version. The "skip until next" choice writes the version string to a dismissed-versions list on disk so we don't nag.

5. **Disable via env var + config flag.** `CUA_DRIVER_RS_UPDATE_CHECK=false` to disable for a single invocation, plus a persisted `update_check_enabled = false` option in the config file for users who want it off permanently. Also auto-skip for source-builds where `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` doesn't correspond to a published release.

6. **Network failures are silent.** Log via `tracing::debug!` only — never surface a "couldn't check for updates" warning to the user. The next launch will try again.

7. **Skip in non-interactive contexts:** `cua-driver --version`, `cua-driver list-tools`, `cua-driver describe <tool>`, `cua-driver call <tool>` — these are commonly invoked from scripts where banner output would pollute parseable stdout/stderr. Limit the banner to the long-running entry points (`mcp`, `serve`, `doctor`).

## Architecture

Suggested file layout in `crates/cua-driver/src/`:

- `version_check.rs` — public API: `pub fn maybe_announce_update()` (sync, non-blocking — spawns the background task and immediately returns); `fn fetch_latest_version()` (HTTP GET against GitHub releases); `fn read_cache() / write_cache()`; `fn dismissed_versions()`; `fn is_newer(latest, current) -> bool` (semver compare).
- `main.rs` — call `version_check::maybe_announce_update()` at the top of `Mcp`, `Serve`, `Doctor` arms, after argv parsing but before any blocking work.

Reuse:
- HTTP client = `ureq` (already a dep after #1532's telemetry).
- Semver comparison crate (`semver = "1"` — add to `Cargo.toml` if not present).
- Config home discovery (already used by telemetry — `~/.cua-driver-rs/`).

## Acceptance criteria

- First launch on an outdated install prints the banner; subsequent launches within 20h reuse the cached result without a network call.
- `CUA_DRIVER_RS_UPDATE_CHECK=false cua-driver serve` skips the check entirely (verifiable via `tracing::debug!` log absence).
- Scripted call: `cua-driver list-tools | jq …` produces no banner pollution.
- Network outage during the background check leaves the user's command untouched (no error message, no exit-code change).
- A user who clicks "skip until next version" doesn't see the same banner again until a strictly-newer version appears.

## Out of scope

- Auto-installing the update without user consent (the banner instructs how to update; it doesn't run `update` automatically).
- TUI prompt UX. We don't have a TUI; this is a one-shot stderr banner.
- Telemetry on update events — that's already covered by the `cua_driver_update` event (#1528) when the user runs the `update` subcommand.

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): announce new versions at startup (#1535)
body:
Closes #1535.

## Summary

Adds a non-blocking "new version available" banner to the long-running interactive entry points of `cua-driver-rs` (`mcp`, `serve`, `doctor`). The check runs on a background task at startup, hits the GitHub releases API once per ~20 hours (cached on disk), and prints a small two-line banner to stderr if a newer `cua-driver-rs-v*` release exists and the user hasn't dismissed it.

Banner format:
```
✨ cua-driver v0.1.4 is available (you have v0.1.3).
   Update with: cua-driver update
   Release notes: https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.1.4
```

## What's in this PR

- `crates/cua-driver/src/version_check.rs` — new module:
  - `pub fn maybe_announce_update()` — sync, returns instantly; spawns the network check on `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (or a short-lived OS thread for sync entry points)
  - `pub(crate) fn fetch_latest_version()` — `ureq`-based GitHub releases call, filtered to the `cua-driver-rs-v*` tag prefix, drafts + pre-releases excluded
  - `read_cache` / `write_cache` against `~/.cua-driver-rs/version_check.json` with a 20-hour refresh threshold
  - `pub fn is_newer(latest, current) -> bool` — strict semver compare; pre-release sorts below release
  - `pub fn dismiss_version(version: &str)` — appends to `dismissed_versions` for the future interactive "skip until next version" path
- `crates/cua-driver/src/main.rs` — wires `maybe_announce_update()` into the `Mcp`, `Serve`, and `Doctor` arms on both the macOS and non-macOS `main()` paths
- `crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs` — `run_update_cmd` now delegates to the shared `version_check::fetch_latest_version()` / `version_check::is_newer()` instead of shelling out to `curl` with its own JSON-walking code path
- `crates/cua-driver/Cargo.toml` — adds `semver = "1"` and `tempfile` (dev-dep)
- `libs/cua-driver-rs/PARITY.md` — new "Startup flow: update-available banner" section covering behavior, cache shape, opt-out layers, HTTP client, and shared release-fetch with `cua-driver update`
- `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guide/getting-started/installation.mdx` + `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/cli-reference.mdx` — user-facing docs for the banner, the cache, the scripted-context skip list, and the env / config opt-out paths

## Opt-out (three layers, any one disables the check)

1. Env var `CUA_DRIVER_RS_UPDATE_CHECK=false` (also `0`, `no`, `off`; case-insensitive) — single invocation
2. Config flag `update_check_enabled = false` in `~/.cua-driver/config.json` — permanent (set via `cua-driver config set update_check_enabled false`)
3. `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` with a pre-release suffix (`-dev`, `-rc.1`, `-beta`, …) — auto-skips for source / dev builds

## Skipped entry points

`--version`, `list-tools`, `describe`, `call`, `dump-docs`, `mcp-config`, `update`, `stop`, `status`, `recording`, `config`, `diagnose`, `telemetry install-event` — these are routinely piped from scripts and a banner would corrupt their parseable output.

## Tests

22 new unit tests in `version_check::tests`, all passing:

- `is_newer` semver edge cases (`0.2.0 > 0.1.99`, `0.1.3 > 0.1.3-dev`, equal / older returns false, unparseable returns false)
- pre-release detection (`-dev`, `-rc.1`, `-beta`, garbage input)
- cache round-trip through `tempfile::tempdir()`
- `dismissed_versions` persistence (append, idempotent re-dismissal)
- 20h refresh threshold (stale cache → fetch; fresh cache → no fetch, uses cached value)
- dismissed-latest suppresses the banner
- env-var opt-out short-circuits `is_enabled`
- persisted `update_check_enabled = false` config flag disables; `true` / missing leaves on
- banner format contains all required lines + the correct release-tag URL
- `pick_latest_release` filters out Swift-port tags, drafts, and pre-releases
- ISO-8601 timestamp round-trips against a known unix epoch

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --release -p cua-driver` — clean build (1 pre-existing unrelated warning)
- [x] `cargo test -p cua-driver version_check::` — 22 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `cua-driver --version` — no banner pollution, prints `cua-driver 0.1.3`
- [x] `CUA_DRIVER_RS_UPDATE_CHECK=false cua-driver list-tools` — clean machine-readable output, no banner
- [ ] Manual: run `cua-driver mcp` from an outdated install (e.g. `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` patched to `0.1.0`) and verify the banner lands on stderr within ~5s
- [ ] Manual: re-run `cua-driver mcp` within 20h and verify the cache file is reused (`~/.cua-driver-rs/version_check.json` mtime unchanged, no HTTP request in `tracing::debug!` output with `CUA_LOG=debug`)
- [ ] Manual: write `~/.cua-driver/config.json` with `{"update_check_enabled": false}` and verify the check is skipped (no banner, no debug-log fetch line)
