title: macOS: replace ffmpeg+avfoundation video recorder with ScreenCaptureKit binding
body:
## Background

#1720 fixes the immediate regression where `recording.mp4` was never finalized on macOS because the ffmpeg subprocess silently blocked forever waiting on a Screen Recording TCC prompt that couldn't be surfaced from a daemon. The fix is **defensive only** — it detects the hang within ~2 s, kills the subprocess, and returns an actionable error telling the user to manually add ffmpeg to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording.

That works around the symptom; this issue tracks the actual fix.

## Why ffmpeg+avfoundation will never be zero-config on macOS

TCC (Apple's privacy framework) gates Screen Recording **per-binary**, not per-process-tree. Even when `cua-driver` itself has Screen Recording permission, the `ffmpeg` subprocess does NOT inherit that grant — and when ffmpeg is spawned by a daemon (which is the normal cua-driver mode), there's no UI thread to display the consent dialog. So:

- First-time users see the per-turn JSON+screenshot capture work fine (cua-driver has TCC) but their `recording.mp4` is 0 bytes.
- They have to manually find their ffmpeg binary (Homebrew puts it at `/opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg`, MacPorts elsewhere, vendored builds elsewhere) and grant it Screen Recording.
- They have to restart cua-driver after granting.

That's three steps too many for a "video on by default" feature.

## What needs to happen

Replace the `Command::new("ffmpeg") -f avfoundation -i 1:` shell-out in `cua-driver-core/src/video.rs` with a native ScreenCaptureKit binding on macOS. ScreenCaptureKit (`SCStream`) runs in-process under cua-driver's TCC attribution, so the existing Screen Recording grant covers it. No subprocess, no per-binary TCC, no consent dialog deadlock.

### Reference implementation

The Swift reference impl is at:
- `libs/cua-driver/swift/Sources/CuaDriverCore/Recording/VideoRecorder.swift` — `SCStream` config, frame callback, `AVAssetWriter` encode path.

Port the same pattern to Rust. Options for the bindings:
- `objc2` + the `screencapturekit` crate (community Rust binding around SCK).
- Hand-rolled `objc2` + framework headers (more control, more boilerplate).
- A `swift-bridge`-generated FFI to call straight into a small Swift helper (highest fidelity, biggest build-system change).

### Stays the same

- `recording.rs` interaction (`VideoRecorder::start(path)` → `recorder.stop() -> VideoMetadata`) is platform-agnostic — only the macOS arm of `platform_input_args` + the start/stop body changes.
- Windows + Linux keep the ffmpeg shell-out (TCC is a macOS concept; gdigrab and x11grab work fine from subprocesses).

### Bonus

The Swift impl writes raw frames into `AVAssetWriter` rather than re-encoding via x264, which produces smaller and faster files. Worth mirroring.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `start_recording {output_dir, record_video: true}` on a fresh macOS install (cua-driver has Screen Recording grant, nothing else does) produces a valid playable `recording.mp4`.
- [ ] No ffmpeg dependency on macOS for video recording (ffmpeg is still fine for users who explicitly want it via a config flag, but it's no longer the default).
- [ ] `session.json` `video.finalized: true` post-stop.
- [ ] The defensive TCC-hang detector added in #1720 stays in place for users who opt back into ffmpeg, and for the install/upgrade transition window.

## Related

- #1720 — defensive fast-fail introduced for the immediate regression
- #1718 — the original cross-platform Rust recording refactor that picked ffmpeg as the macOS path

title: uninstall.sh fails under macOS /bin/bash (bash 3.2): "unexpected EOF while looking for matching )"
body:
### Description

The cua-driver uninstaller `libs/cua-driver/scripts/uninstall.sh` fails to run under **bash 3.2** — the `/bin/bash` that ships on macOS, and the exact shell the documented uninstall/install one-liner invokes (`/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL …/uninstall.sh)"`). The script aborts immediately with a syntax error and removes nothing.

### Steps to reproduce

On macOS (system bash is `3.2.57`):

```bash
# the documented one-liner — or just syntax-check it:
bash -n libs/cua-driver/scripts/uninstall.sh
```

### Expected behavior

The script parses and runs the uninstall.

### Actual behavior

```
uninstall.sh: line 324: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `)'
uninstall.sh: line 694: syntax error: unexpected end of file
```

### Environment

- macOS (Darwin), `/bin/bash` → `GNU bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release`
- Works fine under bash 4+/5+ (e.g. Homebrew bash), so it only bites users running the documented `/bin/bash` one-liner.

### Root cause

bash 3.2 has a parser bug where a here-document inside a `$( … )` command substitution is **not** skipped while scanning for the closing `)`. The Rust-branch Python here-doc (`python3 <<'PY'` at line 325) contains three apostrophes in comments — `Swift's` (L364), `it's` (L365), `shouldn't` (L366), an **odd** count. bash 3.2 treats the first as the start of a single-quoted string, never finds the closing `)` of the command substitution, and runs to EOF. The Swift branch's equivalent here-doc is apostrophe-free, which is why only the Rust branch trips.

The reported "line 324" is where the `$(` opens, not where the real problem is.

### Fix

Reword the three comment lines to drop the contractions/possessives so the here-doc carries no unbalanced single quotes. PR incoming.

title: `cua-driver mcp` SIGABRTs during AppKit registration on macOS 15.7.7
body:
# `cua-driver mcp` SIGABRTs during AppKit registration on macOS 15.7.7

## Summary

`cua-driver mcp` aborts before the MCP handshake on macOS 15.7.7 arm64 when
the binary is launched directly as a stdio child. The process exits within
~500 ms with return code `-6` (`SIGABRT`), no stdout, and no stderr.

CrashReporter shows the abort occurs while AppKit is registering the process:

```text
abort
_RegisterApplication
GetCurrentProcess
-[NSMenuBarPresentationInstance _getAggregateUIMode:withOptions:]
_NSGetAggregateUIMode
-[NSMenuBarPresentationInstance _isVisible]
+[NSMenuBarPresentationInstance _isMenuBarVisible]
_NSInitializeAppContext
-[NSApplication init]
+[NSApplication sharedApplication]
```

This prevents any MCP client from using `cua-driver mcp`; Python MCP clients
surface it only as `McpError: Connection closed`.

## Environment

- macOS: 15.7.7 (24G720)
- Architecture: arm64
- SIP: enabled
- Repo release installed by upstream installer: `cua-driver-v0.2.0`

Two app bundles are present on the machine:

### Current user-local bundle

- Path: `~/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver`
- `--version`: `0.2.0`
- Bundle identifier: `com.trycua.driver`
- Format: `app bundle with Mach-O universal (x86_64 arm64)`
- TeamIdentifier: `YCK386LBJ7`

### Older root-owned bundle

- Path: `/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver`
- `--version`: `0.0.13`
- CrashReporter `app_version`: `0.1.0`
- Bundle identifier: `com.trycua.driver`
- Format: `app bundle with Mach-O thin (arm64)`
- TeamIdentifier: `LH7NH6SPDB`

## Repro

With the user-local `0.2.0` bundle:

```bash
"$HOME/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver" --version
"$HOME/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver" list-tools
"$HOME/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver" mcp-config
```

All three succeed.

Raw MCP startup fails before handshake:

```bash
python - <<'PY'
import json, subprocess, time
cmd = [f"{__import__('os').path.expanduser('~')}/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver", "mcp"]
init = {
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 1,
    "method": "initialize",
    "params": {
        "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
        "capabilities": {},
        "clientInfo": {"name": "manual", "version": "0.0.1"},
    },
}
proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
time.sleep(0.5)
print("alive_after_500ms", proc.poll() is None)
out, err = proc.communicate(json.dumps(init) + "\n", timeout=3)
print("returncode", proc.returncode)
print("stdout", repr(out))
print("stderr", repr(err))
PY
```

Observed:

```text
alive_after_500ms False
returncode -6
stdout ''
stderr ''
```

The same raw MCP startup failure occurs with the older `/Applications`
bundle.

## Direct call matrix

### User-local 0.2.0

```bash
~/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver call list_apps --compact
~/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver call list_windows '{"on_screen_only":true}' --compact
~/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver call get_screen_size --compact
```

Observed: each exits `-1` with no stdout/stderr.

This command does reach CLI/schema validation:

```bash
~/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver call screenshot --compact
```

Observed:

```text
Missing required field(s) for screenshot: window_id
```

### Older /Applications bundle

```bash
/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver call list_apps --compact
```

Observed: succeeds.

```bash
/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver call list_windows '{"on_screen_only":true}' --compact
```

Observed: succeeds, returns an empty `windows` array.

```bash
/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver mcp
```

Observed: exits `-6` before handshake, same AppKit registration crash shape.

## CrashReporter details

For user-local 0.2.0, repeated crash reports show:

```text
Exception Type: EXC_CRASH
Signal: SIGABRT
Termination: Abort trap: 6
Process path: ~/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver
Parent: python or codex
TeamIdentifier: YCK386LBJ7
Top frames:
  __pthread_kill
  pthread_kill
  abort
  _RegisterApplication
  GetCurrentProcess
  -[NSMenuBarPresentationInstance _getAggregateUIMode:withOptions:]
  _NSGetAggregateUIMode
  -[NSMenuBarPresentationInstance _isVisible]
  +[NSMenuBarPresentationInstance _isMenuBarVisible]
  _NSInitializeAppContext
  -[NSApplication init]
  +[NSApplication sharedApplication]
```

For the older `/Applications` bundle, raw `mcp` also crashes with the same
`SIGABRT` / `_RegisterApplication` / `NSApplication sharedApplication` shape.

## Notes

- This is not just a Python MCP client issue: raw `cua-driver mcp` crashes
  before any client handshake.
- This is not just PATH/LaunchServices ambiguity: explicit full binary paths
  reproduce the failure.
- The user-local 0.2.0 bundle appears to regress direct `call list_apps` /
  `call list_windows` relative to the older bundle, while both bundles fail
  for `mcp`.
- TCC database inspection was not available from the invoking terminal
  (`authorization denied`), so permissions should still be sanity-checked in
  System Settings, but the `mcp` crash happens before any useful error is
  reported to stderr.

## Question

Should `cua-driver mcp` be launchable as a normal stdio child process by
directly executing `CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver`, or must it be
started via LaunchServices/`launchctl`/a daemon?

If direct stdio execution is supported, it looks like the `mcp` subcommand is
initializing AppKit in a way that calls `NSApplication.sharedApplication` and
aborts during process registration.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): trajectory recorder writes no click.png for element_index clicks (only pixel-clicks get the marker)
body:
## Summary

On the Rust cua-driver (Windows), the trajectory recorder does **not** produce `click.png` (the screenshot with a red marker at the click point) for `element_index`-based clicks. Only pixel-addressed clicks (`click({pid, x, y})`) get a `click.png`. Since the canonical Windows workflow is element_index clicks (UIA Invoke on `{pid, window_id, element_index}`), real recordings end up with **zero** click markers.

macOS (Swift impl) just fixed the equivalent gap — "Fix #2: click.png for element_index — all turns produced click.png (previously zero)". This issue tracks the same fix on the Rust/Windows side.

## Reproduction

Record a calculator 5+7 session driving the buttons by `element_index` (the normal path), then inspect the turn folders:

```
turn-00001: action.json screenshot.png
turn-00002: action.json screenshot.png
turn-00003: action.json screenshot.png
turn-00004: action.json screenshot.png
turn-00005: action.json screenshot.png
```

`find <rec-dir> -name click.png` → 0 results. Every click was element_index-based.

## Root cause

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/recording.rs` (`write_turn`), ~line 335:

```rust
let click_point: Option<(f64, f64)> = if matches!(
    tool_name, "click" | "double_click" | "right_click"
) {
    match (args.opt_f64("x"), args.opt_f64("y")) {  // only pixel-clicks have x/y
        (Some(x), Some(y)) => Some((x, y)),
        _ => None,                                    // element_index clicks → None
    }
} else { None };
```

`click_point` is `None` for element_index clicks (their `arguments` carry `element_index`, not `x`/`y`), so the `click.png` write branch is skipped entirely. The drawing infrastructure is otherwise fully wired (`set_screenshot_fn` + `set_click_marker_fn` registered in `cua-driver/src/main.rs`; `screenshot.png` proves the path runs).

## The coordinates already exist

For element_index clicks the screen coords are in `result_summary`:

```json
{
  "tool": "click",
  "arguments": { "element_index": 28, "pid": 9072, "window_id": 1312138 },
  "result_summary": "✅ Performed UIA Invoke on [28] (screen (745,679))."
}
```

A `parse_screen_from_summary` that pulls `(screen (X,Y))` already exists in `cua-driver-core/src/recording_loader.rs` (added for the zoom renderer's click-event recovery). The recorder can reuse the same parse.

## Proposed fix

In `write_turn`, when `args.x/y` are absent, recover the click point from `result_summary`'s `(screen (X,Y))`:

```rust
let click_point = pixel_click_point(args)
    .or_else(|| parse_screen_from_summary(result_text));
```

### ⚠️ Coordinate-space gotcha (the non-obvious part)

`result_summary`'s `(screen (X,Y))` is in **screen-absolute** pixels, but `screenshot.png` is a **per-window** capture (window-local pixels). The click-marker function (`CLICK_MARKER_FN`) draws in screenshot-pixel space, so the screen point must be converted to window-local before drawing:

```
local_x = screen_x - window_bounds.left  (× any DWM/DPI scale)
local_y = screen_y - window_bounds.top
```

Use `DwmGetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS)` (same mapping `bitmap_to_screen` already uses in `platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`, inverted). Without this conversion the marker lands offset by the window's top-left.

The cleaner long-term fix is for the `click` tool itself to write the resolved screen point into a structured field (rather than parsing it back out of the human-readable result text), so both the recorder and the renderer's loader can stop string-scraping. That'd also benefit `double_click` / `right_click`.

## Acceptance

- Element_index click recording produces a `click.png` per click turn whose red marker lands on the actual clicked control.
- Existing pixel-click `click.png` behavior unchanged.
- Marker uses window-local coordinates (correctly offset on multi-monitor / non-origin windows).

title: [codex] Add embedded cua-driver MCP SDK
body:
## Summary

Adds an in-process embedded SDK for the Rust cua-driver so host apps can handle MCP requests without spawning `cua-driver mcp`, `cua-driver serve`, or `CuaDriver.app` for protected AX / screen-capture work.

## What Changed

- Adds a new Rust workspace crate, `cua-driver-embedded`, with direct Rust calls and JSON-RPC MCP request handling.
- Exposes a C ABI (`cua_driver_embedded_*`) for Swift, Objective-C, Electron/native-node, and other non-Rust hosts.
- Adds a `CuaDriverEmbedded` Swift Package product and wrapper API around the C ABI.
- Exposes the core MCP request dispatcher from `cua-driver-core::server` so embedded transports reuse the stdio server's method handling.
- Adds a macOS `.app` smoke harness that links the embedded dylib, launches via LaunchServices, and verifies bundle-attributed permission status without prompting.
- Adds embedded MCP docs and marks the old Swift integration page as legacy.

## Why

The standalone CLI/daemon path gives macOS TCC attribution to `CuaDriver.app`, the helper process, or the spawning terminal. Embedded hosts need protected calls to happen in their own process so Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions attach to the host app bundle.

## Notes

The Swift package wrapper intentionally does not build Rust by itself. Apps using `CuaDriverEmbedded` still need to link `libcua_driver_embedded.a`, `libcua_driver_embedded.dylib`, or a future packaged xcframework.

The docs call out a current caveat: macOS `list_apps` still goes through `osascript` / System Events, so that tool can require Automation permission separately until it is replaced with a fully native implementation.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/lib/swift-5.5/macosx cargo test -p cua-driver-embedded`
  - Passes; emits Swift runtime duplicate-class warnings from the current ScreenCaptureKit bridge environment.
- `swift build --target CuaDriverEmbedded`
- `crates/cua-driver-embedded/examples/macos-app-smoke/run.sh`
- Temporary downstream Swift package importing `CuaDriverEmbedded`, linking the Rust release dylib, and calling MCP `tools/list`

title: refactor(cua-driver)(test-harness): per-OS layout + cross-platform/shared signposting
body:
## Why

The previous flat layout under `libs/cua-driver/test-harness/` mixed
host-OS apps, shared fixtures, build scripts, and CLI smoke runners
side-by-side with no signal that some assets are cross-OS reusable.
`scripts/mac-smoke.sh` and its baseline also lived outside the harness
tree entirely. This PR makes the directory tree itself encode which
apps run where and which assets are shared.

## New layout

```text
libs/cua-driver/test-harness/
├── shared/                      # cross-OS reusable
│   ├── scenarios.json
│   └── web/index.html           # WebView2 + Electron load the same file
├── apps/
│   ├── cross-platform/
│   │   └── electron/            # CuaTestHarness.Electron (any OS)
│   ├── macos/
│   │   ├── appkit/
│   │   └── swiftui/
│   └── windows/
│       ├── wpf/
│       ├── winui3/
│       └── webview2/
├── build/                       # host-OS build scripts
│   ├── macos.sh                 # appkit + swiftui
│   └── windows.ps1              # wpf + winui3 + webview2 + electron
└── smoke/                       # host-OS per-tool CLI smoke runners
    ├── macos.sh
    └── results/macos.txt        # checked-in baseline
```

## Moves (`git mv` so blame follows)

- `scenarios/scenarios.json`         → `shared/scenarios.json`
- `shared-web/index.html`            → `shared/web/index.html`
- `CuaTestHarness.Electron/`         → `apps/cross-platform/electron/`
- `CuaTestHarness.AppKit/`           → `apps/macos/appkit/`
- `CuaTestHarness.SwiftUI/`          → `apps/macos/swiftui/`
- `CuaTestHarness.Wpf/`              → `apps/windows/wpf/`
- `CuaTestHarness.WinUI3/`           → `apps/windows/winui3/`
- `CuaTestHarness.WebView/`          → `apps/windows/webview2/`
- `build.sh`                         → `build/macos.sh`
- `build.ps1`                        → `build/windows.ps1`
- `scripts/mac-smoke.sh`             → `libs/cua-driver/test-harness/smoke/macos.sh`
- `scripts/mac-smoke-RESULTS.txt`    → `libs/cua-driver/test-harness/smoke/results/macos.txt`

## Reference fixups

- `build/macos.sh` + `build/windows.ps1` recompute their paths from the
  new depth.
- `apps/cross-platform/electron/build.ps1` reaches `shared/web/` via the
  new relative path.
- `apps/windows/webview2/CuaTestHarness.WebView.csproj` links `shared/web/index.html`.
- `CuaTestHarness.sln` updated to the new `apps/windows/*` project paths.
- `rust/sandbox/run-tests-in-sandbox.ps1` points at `..\test-harness\build\windows.ps1`.
- `smoke/macos.sh` `ROOT="$(...)/../../../.."` resolves to the repo root from the new location.
- Integration-test doc comments under `rust/crates/cua-driver/tests/harness_*.rs` updated.
- `.gitignore` excepts `libs/cua-driver/test-harness/build/` (the repo's
  root `build/` ignore was masking the new subdir).

## Non-goals

- Integration test trees (`rust/tests/integration/*`,
  `swift/Tests/integration/*`) — out of scope.
- Pre-built `rust/test-apps/` bundles — those are build outputs, cleanup
  is a separate concern.
- No new tests, no new platforms, no build-logic changes. Move +
  path-fixup + README only.

## JOURNAL.md

Left untouched on purpose — it's a historical journal of past commits,
and the path references in it are accurate as of when they were
written.

## Test plan

Local (macOS):
- [x] `cargo build --release -p cua-driver` clean
- [x] `cargo test --release --no-run -p cua-driver` — all `harness_*.rs` compile
- [x] `bash libs/cua-driver/test-harness/build/macos.sh` — builds AppKit + SwiftUI `.app` bundles into `rust/test-apps/harness-{appkit,swiftui}/`
- [x] `bash libs/cua-driver/test-harness/smoke/macos.sh` — runs end-to-end against the AppKit harness, PASSes the same tool set

Still to validate on the Windows VM:

- [ ] `rust\sandbox\run-tests-in-sandbox.ps1 harness_wpf` picks up the new build path
- [ ] WebView2 csproj `..\..\..\shared\web\index.html` Link resolves correctly under `dotnet publish`

title: PiP preview (experimental): native Windows + Linux backends
body:
Follow-up to the macOS PiP preview that landed in #TBD.

`pip-preview` + `cua_driver_core::pip_hook` already expose the cross-platform
contract (`PipBackend`, `PipFrame`, `PipBackendFactory`); the macOS impl
lives in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/pip/mod.rs`. The
Windows and Linux factories ship as compile-clean stubs whose `start()`
returns "not yet implemented".

## Windows
- `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE | WS_EX_TOPMOST | WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW` HWND created via
  `CreateWindowExW`.
- Child `STATIC` with `SS_BITMAP` for the screenshot; `SetWindowPos`
  (`SWP_NOACTIVATE`) on every frame.
- PNG → HBITMAP via `WIC` (`IWICImagingFactory::CreateDecoderFromMemory`).
- One UI thread per process; tool dispatcher posts a `WM_USER+1` with a
  boxed `PipFrame` payload, message handler unboxes + repaints.
- Survives Session 0 by no-oping when `current_session_id()` is 0
  (same gate as `platform-windows::diagnostics`).

## Linux
- Two backends, chosen at runtime by detecting `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`:
  - X11 / XWayland: `xcb` window with `_NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE_UTILITY` +
    `_NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE`, PNG decoded to `xcb_image` and pushed via
    `xcb_put_image`.
  - Wayland-native: `wlr-layer-shell` `LAYER_TOP` surface where the
    compositor supports it; otherwise fall back to a regular xdg_toplevel
    + `_NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE` hint (no-op under most compositors but
    harmless).

## Validation
For each backend, the existing macOS smoke test transposes 1:1:

```
cua-driver serve --experimental-pip &
cua-driver call launch_app '{"name":"calc"}'   # or platform equivalent
# → window appears, label updates each call
```

Tracking issue intentionally split out so the macOS drop can ship
behind the experimental flag without blocking on Win/Linux UI bring-up.

title: feat(cua-driver-rs)(experimental): picture-in-picture agent preview (macOS native; Win/Linux stubs)
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `--experimental-pip` flag that opens a small always-on-top window showing what the cua-driver agent is doing in real time: the post-action screenshot of the target window plus a one-line label describing the tool call (`click element_index=2`, `type_text "hello world"`, etc.).

Frames are pushed for every non-read-only tool call — the same set the recording pipeline writes a `turn-NNNNN/screenshot.png` for. The PNG bytes come from the existing `SCREENSHOT_FN` callback, so the live view matches what a replay would show. No continuous capture: PiP follows tool calls, not a frame rate.

**Experimental, default OFF.** Cross-platform from day 1 via a trait, with macOS as the first working backend; Windows and Linux ship as compile-clean stubs whose `start()` returns a clear "not yet implemented" notice so the daemon keeps running without a window. Win + Linux native impls tracked in #1729.

## How to try it locally (macOS)

```bash
~/.local/bin/cua-driver serve --experimental-pip &
~/.local/bin/cua-driver call launch_app '{"bundle_id":"com.apple.calculator"}'
# → PiP window appears top-right; label updates with each call
```

Geometry override (X11 `WxH[+X+Y]` form, default `480x360` top-right):

```bash
cua-driver serve --experimental-pip --experimental-pip-geometry 640x480+24+24
```

## Architecture (mirror of cursor-overlay + video.rs)

- **`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/pip-preview/`** — `PipConfig`, `PipFrame`, `PipBackend` trait, `PipBackendFactory`, `PIP_FACTORY: OnceLock` registry. Same shape as `cua_driver_core::video`.
- **`cua-driver-core/src/pip_hook.rs`** — per-process push callback the tool dispatcher (`tool.rs::invoke`) calls after a successful action tool lands. Synthesises the action label from `(tool_name, args)`; pulls screenshot bytes via the existing `recording::screenshot_for(window_id, pid)` shim.
- **`platform-macos/src/pip/mod.rs`** — `MacosPipBackend` using NSWindow + NSImageView + NSTextField. Frame push → `dispatch_async_f(main_queue, ...)` (AppKit must run on main).
- **`platform-{windows,linux}/src/pip/mod.rs`** — stubs returning `Err("not yet implemented")`. Tracked in #1729.
- **`cua-driver/src/main.rs::maybe_init_pip`** — registers the platform factory, starts the backend, bridges the live `Box<dyn PipBackend>` to `pip_hook::set_pip_push_fn`. Wired into `Serve` and `Mcp` on macOS plus `Serve` and `async_main` on non-macOS.

### macOS Serve mode quirk (worth a closer review eye)

`dispatch_async_f` → main queue only fires while NSRunLoop is pumping. The cursor overlay's `run_on_main_thread()` provides that loop in MCP mode, but Serve mode normally blocks its tokio runtime on main. When `--experimental-pip` is on, the macOS Serve arm now moves the tokio runtime onto a background thread and parks main in `NSApplication.run()` (via `platform_macos::pip::run_appkit_main_loop`). Without this, frames queue forever and the window stays blank.

The non-PiP Serve path keeps its original run-on-main semantics so existing users are unaffected.

## Window properties (macOS)

- `NSFloatingWindowLevel` — above normal apps, below menus / accessibility overlays.
- `CanJoinAllSpaces | FullScreenAuxiliary | Stationary | Transient | IgnoresCycle` — visible across spaces and full-screen apps; never the main / key window.
- `orderFrontRegardless` instead of `makeKeyAndOrderFront` — never steals keyboard focus.
- Closeable via the red traffic-light button (decouples from the session per spec).

`becomesKeyOnlyIfNeeded:` is NSPanel-only and crashes when sent to NSWindow — using collection-behavior flags + `orderFrontRegardless` achieves the same passive-window contract.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --release -p cua-driver` on macOS — passes
- [x] `cargo check --workspace` — passes (only pre-existing warnings)
- [x] CLI `--help` lists the new `--experimental-pip` / `--experimental-pip-geometry` flags
- [x] `cua-driver serve --experimental-pip --no-permissions-gate` starts; PiP window appears top-right at 480x360 with placeholder "waiting for first action…"
- [x] `cua-driver call launch_app '{"bundle_id":"com.apple.calculator"}'` → window updates with screenshot + label `launch_app: com.apple.calculator` (verified via `screencapture`)
- [ ] Manual: confirm window stays passive when clicked (doesn't steal focus from frontmost app)
- [ ] Manual: confirm window survives space-switch + full-screen-app transitions
- [ ] Windows / Linux smoke (deferred — stubs only today; tracked in #1729)

## Files touched

- New crate: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/pip-preview/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs}`
- New module: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/pip_hook.rs`
- New module: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-{macos,windows,linux}/src/pip/mod.rs`
- Wire-up: `cua-driver/src/{main.rs,cli.rs}`, `cua-driver/Cargo.toml`, `platform-*/Cargo.toml`, `platform-*/src/lib.rs`, `cua-driver-core/src/{tool.rs,recording.rs,lib.rs}`, workspace `Cargo.toml`
- Docs: `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guide/getting-started/pip-preview.mdx` + meta.json entry

## Follow-ups

- #1729 — native Windows + Linux backends
- Consider exposing the action label as part of the `tools/call` response metadata so HTTP clients (not just the local PiP window) can show what the driver just did

title: feat(cua-driver-rs)(platform-windows,platform-linux): glide agent cursor to the field on set_value/type_text
body:
## What

The agent-cursor overlay previously only glided to **click** targets. During `set_value` and `type_text` the cursor never moved to the field, so recordings showed fields filling with no indication of *where* the agent was acting.

This moves the agent cursor onto the target element before the write — reusing the same overlay helpers the click path already uses — whenever an `element_index` is supplied.

## Changes

- **Windows** (`platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`): `SetValueTool` and `TypeTextTool` now `pin_overlay_above` + `overlay_glide_to(center)` + `ClickPulse` before writing.
- **Linux** (`platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`): `SetValueTool` and `TypeTextTool` resolve `atspi::get_element_bounds` and `ClickPulse` at the element center (mirrors the existing click path).
- **macOS**: already animated the cursor (`AgentCursor.animateAndWait`) in both tools — no change.

The glide only fires when an `element_index` is provided (where a position is resolvable); the "type into the focused element" path is unchanged.

## Testing

- Windows: `cargo build -p cua-driver` ✅
- Linux / macOS not built on the authoring host (Windows). Linux change mirrors the existing click pattern; macOS was already correct.

title: ci(cua-driver): add SPDX header check workflow (warn-only)
body:
## Summary

- Adds `scripts/spdx-headers.py` — idempotent applier/checker for `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` + `// Copyright (c) 2026 Cua AI, Inc.` headers on every `.swift` / `.rs` file under `libs/cua-driver/`
- Adds `.github/workflows/ci-spdx-headers.yml` — warn-only CI gate (`continue-on-error: true`) that runs the checker on PRs touching cua-driver sources
- **Does NOT stamp the existing tree.** That's a follow-up sweep PR. Today, 297 source files would be flagged; the warning lands on every relevant PR until we sweep.

## Why now

[EYHN/kwwk-computer-use-core#6](https://github.com/EYHN/kwwk-computer-use-core/issues/6) — a downstream Swift repo ported substantial code from `cua-driver`'s `AppState.swift` and `SkyLightEventPost.swift` without preserving the MIT copyright notice. Three days later, zero engagement on the issue.

Per-file SPDX headers:
- Make attribution stripping mechanically obvious (it stops being "we missed the LICENSE file" and becomes "they deleted the header")
- Give us stronger, file-by-file evidence in any future GitHub DMCA filing
- Are the standard convention across Rust ecosystem, Linux kernel, and modern OSS — low friction for contributors

## Sequencing

1. **This PR** — script + warn-only CI. Zero conflicts with in-flight PRs (only adds new files). ← *you are here*
2. **Follow-up sweep PR** — runs `scripts/spdx-headers.py --apply libs/cua-driver` once. Single mechanical commit touching ~297 files. Timed for a quiet merge window to minimize rebase pain on the ~9 currently-open PRs that touch cua-driver sources.
3. **Enforcement flip PR** — removes `continue-on-error: true` from the workflow. One-line diff.

## Script usage

```bash
# Preview what would change without writing
python3 scripts/spdx-headers.py --dry-run libs/cua-driver

# Stamp files that lack headers
python3 scripts/spdx-headers.py --apply libs/cua-driver

# CI-mode: exit 1 if anything is missing
python3 scripts/spdx-headers.py --check libs/cua-driver
```

The script is idempotent — it skips any file that already contains an `SPDX-License-Identifier` marker in its first 2 KiB. Safe to re-run on partially stamped trees, safe to run in `--apply` mode locally before opening a PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `--dry-run` reports 297 files would receive headers, 0 already have them
- [x] `--check` exits 1 with file list when headers are missing
- [x] YAML workflow validates cleanly (parsed via `ruby -ryaml`)
- [ ] CI workflow runs on this PR and emits the warn-only output (will verify after push)
- [ ] Workflow message renders correctly in the GitHub Actions UI

## Out of scope

- Stamping existing files (separate sweep PR)
- Flipping CI to enforcing (separate one-line PR after sweep lands)
- Trademark policy + DMCA runbook (separate work tracks)
- Extending headers to TypeScript / Python source — happy to follow up if the team agrees, but cua-driver is the highest-priority surface given the kwwk incident specifically involved Swift code derived from it

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): check-update CLI verb + check_for_update MCP tool
body:
## Summary

Add a focused, machine-readable update-check surface so both humans and Hermes-style agents can ask *"is there a newer cua-driver?"* without scraping `cua-driver update` text output.

Three new surfaces, all reading from the same primitive (`version_check::check_update_state`) so the CLI, MCP, and launch-time banner never disagree on which release is *latest*:

- **`cua-driver check-update [--json] [--no-cache]`** — pure check verb, never installs. Default text output for humans; `--json` emits the same payload as the MCP tool; `--no-cache` forces a fresh GitHub round-trip (bypasses the existing 20h cache).
- **`cua-driver update --json`** — same JSON payload from the existing apply verb. The text behaviour of `cua-driver update` (no `--json`) is byte-for-byte unchanged for backward compat.
- **`check_for_update` MCP tool** — read-only, idempotent, empty input schema. Mirror of `check-update --json`. Registered from `main.rs` via a small `register_into(&mut ToolRegistry)` shim so the `ureq` + rustls + ring dep tree stays in `cua-driver` and never reaches `cua-driver-core` (which would break cross-target Windows builds from macOS host).

## How Hermes (and any MCP client) will consume this

```bash
# Direct CLI — for shell scripts:
if cua-driver check-update --json | jq -e .update_available > /dev/null; then
  cua-driver update --apply
fi
```

```jsonc
// MCP — for agents:
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"check_for_update","arguments":{}}}
// Returns structuredContent with the full UpdateState schema documented
// in docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guide/getting-started/updating.mdx
```

JSON schema (same shape on both paths):

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `current_version` | string | Running binary's `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`. |
| `latest_version` | string \| null | Highest non-draft non-prerelease `cua-driver-rs-v*` tag. `null` on fetch failure with no cache. |
| `update_available` | bool | Strict semver compare. |
| `source` | string | `"github_releases"` today. |
| `checked_at` | string | ISO-8601 UTC. |
| `cache_hit` | bool | Whether we short-circuited via the 20h on-disk cache. |
| `install_command` | string \| null | Shell one-liner. `null` when up-to-date. |
| `release_notes_url` | string \| null | GitHub release URL. `null` when up-to-date. |
| `error` | string \| null | Human-readable failure reason. |

## What was NOT done (intentional)

- No `--apply` on `check-update` — separation of intent. Apply lives on `update`.
- No `apply` variant of the MCP tool — installing over MCP forces self-replacement of the running MCP server.
- No auto-update / background-apply behaviour.
- Launch-time banner code (`maybe_announce_update`) untouched.

## Verification run locally

- `cargo build --release -p cua-driver` (macOS) — clean.
- `cargo check -p platform-windows --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` — clean.
- `cargo check -p platform-linux` — clean (existing warnings only).
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver version_check` — 22/22 pass.
- `~/.local/bin/cua-driver check-update` — text path.
- `~/.local/bin/cua-driver check-update --json | jq .update_available` — parseable, branches cleanly.
- `~/.local/bin/cua-driver check-update --no-cache --json` — fresh fetch (cache bypassed).
- `~/.local/bin/cua-driver call check_for_update '{}'` — MCP path returns the same JSON shape via `structuredContent`.
- `~/.local/bin/cua-driver update` — text output byte-for-byte identical to pre-change behaviour.
- `~/.local/bin/cua-driver update --json` — structured payload, no text noise.
- `~/.local/bin/cua-driver list-tools | grep check_for_update` — tool registered on macOS.

The existing `cua-driver-rs-v*` releases on `trycua/cua` are all marked `prerelease=true` on GitHub today, which the canonical filter (`pick_latest_release`) strips — so live runs currently surface `"no matching cua-driver-rs-v* release in response"` in the `error` field. This is pre-existing behaviour shared with `cua-driver update`; the JSON path still returns a well-formed payload and exits with the documented code, so consumers can detect and report it.

## Test plan

- [ ] Land a non-prerelease `cua-driver-rs-v*` tag and re-verify `update_available: true`/`false` flips correctly across the version boundary.
- [ ] Verify `--no-cache` triggers a fresh fetch (delete `~/.cua-driver-rs/version_check.json` and observe re-write).
- [ ] Confirm Hermes can consume the JSON via its existing tool-call wrapper.
- [ ] Smoke-test on Windows + Linux that `check_for_update` is listed in `cua-driver list-tools` and returns the same shape.

title: cua-computer-server (Python): screenshot ↔ click coordinate space mismatch on macOS Retina/AVF
body:
## Summary

`cua-computer-server`'s macOS handler ships three coordinate spaces that disagree on Retina (and on Apple Virtualization Framework virtual displays, which always report Retina-ish behavior). An agent that picks click targets off a screenshot will miss them by exactly the Retina scale factor.

Same family of bug as #1592 (which is about `cua-driver`'s Swift `ScreenshotTool` / `ClickTool`). This issue is about the **Python `computer_server.handlers.macos.MacOSAutomationHandler`** in `libs/python/computer-server`.

## The three spaces

In `libs/python/computer-server/computer_server/handlers/macos.py`:

| Method | Coord space | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `screenshot()` | physical pixels, **resized to max_width=1920** | The body explicitly downsamples for size: `screenshot.resize((max_width, new_height), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)` |
| `get_screen_size()` | **physical pixels, pre-resize** | Calls `ImageGrab.grab()` and returns `img.width × img.height` |
| `left_click(x, y)` (and right/middle/double_click, move_cursor) | **logical points** | Uses `self.mouse.position = (x, y)` from pynput, which uses CoreGraphics in display points |

On a Retina 2× display (1024×768 points, 2048×1536 pixels), an agent doing:

```python
shot = await screenshot()   # returns 1920×1440 PNG
size = await get_screen_size()  # returns 2048×1536
# model decides to click the bottom-right corner from the 1920×1440 image
await left_click(1500, 1100)
# pynput interprets (1500, 1100) as POINTS, off the 1024×768 display, clamped to the bottom-right corner
```

The click misses every visual target.

## The AVF wrinkle (Lume / Trycua VMs)

On Lume macOS guests (AVF), `CGDisplayPixelsWide(displayID)` returns the same value as `CGDisplayBounds(displayID).size.width` — both are **points**, not pixels. So even code that tried to derive the scale from `CGDisplayPixelsWide / CGDisplayBoundsWidth` would get `1.0` and miss the 2× scale.

Trace from a live Lume VM (macOS 26.5 guest):

```python
from Quartz import CGDisplayBounds, CGDisplayPixelsWide, CGMainDisplayID
from PIL import ImageGrab
did = CGMainDisplayID()
print("CGDisplayBounds.size.width  =", CGDisplayBounds(did).size.width)   # 1024.0
print("CGDisplayPixelsWide         =", CGDisplayPixelsWide(did))           # 1024  ← LIES
print("ImageGrab.grab().size       =", ImageGrab.grab().size)              # (2048, 1536)  ← truth
```

So the only reliable way to know the scale **on this codepath** is `ImageGrab.grab().size / CGDisplayBounds.size`.

## Reproduction

On a Lume macOS 26.5 guest with cua-computer-server installed and the LaunchAgent running:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/cmd -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"command":"move_cursor","params":{"x":1024,"y":768}}'   # intends "center of 2048×1536 screenshot"
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/cmd -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"command":"get_cursor_position","params":{}}'           # returns (1023, 767) — bottom-right of 1024×768 point display
```

The expected center would be `(512, 384)` in point space.

## Proposed fix

Three edits to `libs/python/computer-server/computer_server/handlers/macos.py`:

1. **Compute the scale once, cached.** Derive from `ImageGrab` and `CGDisplayBounds` (since `CGDisplayPixelsWide` lies on AVF):
   ```python
   def _pt_scale(self) -> float:
       cached = getattr(type(self), "_pt_scale_cache", None)
       if cached is not None:
           return cached
       try:
           from Quartz import CGDisplayBounds, CGMainDisplayID
           from PIL import ImageGrab as _IG
           pw = float(CGDisplayBounds(CGMainDisplayID()).size.width)
           px = float(_IG.grab().size[0])
           scale = (px / pw) if pw else 1.0
       except Exception:
           scale = 1.0
       type(self)._pt_scale_cache = scale
       return scale
   ```

2. **Scale incoming click coords to points** before delegating to pynput, in every coord-taking method (`left_click`, `right_click`, `middle_click`, `double_click`, `move_cursor`, and likely `drag_to`):
   ```python
   if x is not None and y is not None:
       s = self._pt_scale()
       if s != 1.0:
           x, y = x / s, y / s
   ```

3. **Drop the screenshot `max_width=1920` resize** so `screenshot()` and `get_screen_size()` agree, AND so the model sees native pixels (more detail). The resize "saved size" but at the cost of a third coordinate space. With (1) + (2) in place the screenshot can be returned at native and clicks still work — coordinates from the model live in pixel space, and we silently convert.

## What we shipped locally

While we wait for an upstream fix, we patch the installed `macos.py` in-place via a marker-guarded script:

- Adds `_geyserlabs_pt_scale()` helper (uses ImageGrab+CGDisplayBounds, as above).
- Wraps `left_click` / `right_click` / `middle_click` / `double_click` / `move_cursor` with the `x, y = x/s, y/s` transform at the top.
- Disables the screenshot `max_width=1920` resize.

Patch script: https://github.com/geyserlabs/a2a-claude-agent/blob/main/scripts/cua-bootstrap/apply-cua-hidpi-patch.py — happy to convert it into a proper PR against this repo if you'd like. Discovered while running cua-computer-server in Lume macOS VMs driven by [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) workers.

## Environment

- `cua-computer-server` 0.3.39
- macOS 26.5 (Tahoe) guest under AVF, via Lume
- Lume host: macOS 15.x (Sequoia) on Apple Silicon
- Display: 1024×768 points / 2048×1536 pixels (2.0× Retina-style scale)
- Python 3.12 (Homebrew)

title: cua-mcp-server on Windows hangs because Computer backend config is not exposed
body:
# Summary

On Windows, `cua-mcp-server` starts successfully and exposes its MCP tools, but `run_cua_task` hangs when asked to do a simple GUI task such as launching Calculator and computing `1+1`.

The underlying Windows host computer server works when used directly, so this appears to be an MCP wrapper/configuration issue: `cua-mcp-server` does not expose enough configuration to pass `os_type`, `api_host`, `api_port`, or `provider_type` into `Computer(...)`.

---

# Environment

- OS: Windows build 26200
- Python in uv tool env: 3.12.11
- `cua-mcp-server`: 0.1.16
- `cua-agent`: 0.4.53
- `cua-computer`: 0.4.19
- `cua-computer-server`: 0.3.39 (installed separately)
- MCP client: Codex CLI / stdio MCP

---

# Steps To Reproduce

1. Install the MCP server:

```bash
uv tool install cua-mcp-server
```

2. Add it to an MCP client as a stdio server:

```bash
cua-mcp-server
```

3. Call `run_cua_task` with a simple task:

```text
Launch Windows Calculator, compute 1 + 1, and report the visible result.
```

---

# Actual Behavior

- The MCP server initializes successfully.
- `list_tools` returns:

```text
screenshot_cua
run_cua_task
run_multi_cua_tasks
get_session_stats
cleanup_session
```

- Calling `run_cua_task` did not return after 6 minutes.
- Isolating `Computer.run()` with defaults shows it waiting on the Lume/macOS path:

```text
Failed to pull VM macos-sequoia-cua_latest
curl: (7) Failed to connect to localhost port 7777
```

---

# Direct Host Computer Server Works

As a control test, I installed and started the host computer server on a free port:

```bash
uv tool install cua-computer-server

cua-computer-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765
```

Then this direct Python usage worked:

```python
from computer import Computer

computer = Computer(
    os_type="windows",
    use_host_computer_server=True,
    api_port=8765,
)

await computer.run()
```

Using the resulting Windows interface, I was able to:

- Launch Calculator
- Focus the window
- Type `1+1`
- Press Enter
- Verify the visible result was `2`

So the Windows host-control path works correctly.

The issue is that `cua-mcp-server` does not appear to let the MCP user configure the `Computer(...)` instance to use that working host server.

---

# Likely Cause

In the installed package, `mcp_server/session_manager.py` creates the computer roughly like this:

```python
use_host = os.getenv(
    "CUA_USE_HOST_COMPUTER_SERVER",
    "false"
).lower() in ("true", "1", "yes")

computer = Computer(
    verbosity=logging.INFO,
    use_host_computer_server=use_host,
)
```

That leaves important values at defaults:

- `os_type` defaults to `macos`
- `provider_type` defaults to `lume`
- `api_port` defaults to `8000`
- `api_host` defaults to `localhost`

There is `CUA_MODEL_NAME` for agent model selection, but I could not find equivalent MCP environment variables for the computer backend.

---

# Expected Behavior

For MCP usage on Windows, one of these should work:

## Option 1: Configurable Environment Variables

`cua-mcp-server` should allow env/config values such as:

```env
CUA_COMPUTER_OS_TYPE=windows
CUA_USE_HOST_COMPUTER_SERVER=true
CUA_COMPUTER_API_HOST=127.0.0.1
CUA_COMPUTER_API_PORT=8765
CUA_COMPUTER_PROVIDER_TYPE=...
CUA_COMPUTER_DISPLAY=...
CUA_COMPUTER_IMAGE=...
```

## Option 2: Fail Fast

The MCP server should fail fast with an actionable error if the default Lume backend is unavailable, instead of hanging indefinitely.

## Option 3: Documentation

The docs should clearly explain how to use `cua-mcp-server` with `cua-computer-server` on Windows.

---

# Suggested Fix

Expose the `Computer(...)` backend settings through MCP server environment variables and pass them through in `session_manager.py`, for example:

```python
computer = Computer(
    os_type=os.getenv("CUA_COMPUTER_OS_TYPE", "macos"),
    provider_type=os.getenv("CUA_COMPUTER_PROVIDER_TYPE", "lume"),
    use_host_computer_server=use_host,
    api_host=os.getenv("CUA_COMPUTER_API_HOST") or None,
    api_port=int(os.getenv("CUA_COMPUTER_API_PORT", "8000")),
    display=os.getenv("CUA_COMPUTER_DISPLAY", "1024x768"),
    verbosity=logging.INFO,
)
```

title: docs(cua-driver): sync to cua-driver-rs 0.3.2
body:
## Why

The cua-driver fumadocs were auto-generated from the **Swift driver (~v0.2.0)** and badly drifted from the shipping **Rust port `cua-driver-rs` 0.3.2**. Concrete examples surfaced in an audit:

- Reference docs claimed **29 MCP tools** — the live binary exposes **34**. Seven Rust tools (`bring_to_front`, `check_for_update`, `debug_window_info`, `get_accessibility_tree`, `kill_app`, `start_recording`, `stop_recording`) were undocumented; two documented tools (`screenshot`, `set_recording`) don't exist on the Rust port.
- `cli-reference.mdx` had `doctor` documented as "Clean up stale install bits" — it's actually a structured health report (`doctor --json`). It also omitted real verbs: `autostart`, `check-update`, `skills`.
- Every quickstart / faq / installation example invoked tools as bare `cua-driver <tool> '{...}'`, which **hangs** on the Rust binary (the real form is `cua-driver call <tool>`).
- `introduction.mdx` framed cua-driver as macOS-only ("Requires macOS 14") while the same getting-started section ships dedicated Windows and Linux pages and the binary self-describes as "cross-platform."
- Windows install paths in the env-var table and the autostart manual block still pointed at the legacy `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin` + `%USERPROFILE%\.cua-driver-rs`, but the actual install lives at `Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin` + `.cua-driver` (verified against `cua-driver mcp-config` output).
- Version strings ranged from `0.1.0` → `0.2.1` → `0.2.9` within a single file.

## What changed

**Reference docs** rewritten from ground truth (`cua-driver list-tools` + `describe <tool>` + `--help`):

- `reference/mcp-tools.mdx` — all 34 tools documented; added a **Dispatch modes** section (`background`/`foreground`/`auto`) that was missing entirely; fixed behavior drift (`move_cursor` is the overlay not the real cursor; `set_value` requires `window_id`; `set_agent_cursor_motion` defaults updated); replaced the junk auto-generated examples (`set_config {"key":"return"}`, zero-area `drag`/`zoom`); fixed `type_text_in`/`scroll_in` → `type_text`/`scroll`.
- `reference/cli-reference.mdx` — rebuilt at verb level from `--help`; `doctor` description inverted to the correct "health probe"; added `autostart`, `check-update`, `skills`, `mcp-config`; added the PowerShell-5.1 JSON-quoting gotcha the binary itself surfaces.

title: feat(cua-driver): macOS lock-state observer + display-sleep guard for background agent sessions
body:
# feat(cua-driver): macOS lock-state observer + display-sleep guard for background agent sessions

## Motivation

cua-driver's background-mode pitch — "agent and user co-work on the same machine" — degrades the moment the user steps away. Two failure modes:

1. **The display goes to sleep** while the agent is mid-task. ScreenCaptureKit returns black frames; `capture(mode="vision")` and SOM screenshots break. AX-only mode survives but vision-capable models lose grounding.
2. **The user locks the screen** and the agent has no way to know. It keeps clicking against a UI it can no longer see, can no longer be approved against, and is increasingly likely to be operating against the loginwindow's AX tree instead of the intended app.

There is no current way for an agent driving cua-driver to (a) detect that the session has locked, (b) prevent the display from sleeping during an active session, or (c) get notified when the user comes back. Filling those three gaps unblocks longer-running autonomous sessions — overnight batches, scheduled tasks, "leave it running while I'm in a meeting" workflows — without the agent silently working blind.

This issue covers the **sudo-free MVP**. A follow-up issue (see "Related work" below) covers the SecurityAgentPlugin path needed for actual lock-screen UI interaction.

## Proposed mechanism

A small Swift helper inside the existing `CuaDriver.app` bundle — modeled on the same architecture 1Password and Yubico use for their lock-aware integrations. No new daemons, no privilege escalation at install time, no system-wide changes.

### Lock-state observer

Subscribe to the canonical macOS distributed notifications via `DistributedNotificationCenter.default`:

| Notification | Fires when |
|---|---|
| `com.apple.screenIsLocked` | Screen lock engages (screensaver or `Cmd+Ctrl+Q`) |
| `com.apple.screenIsUnlocked` | User successfully unlocks |
| `com.apple.screenLockUIIsShown` | Lock UI rendered (precedes auth) |
| `com.apple.sessionagent.screenIsLocked` | Session-agent confirmation of lock |
| `com.apple.sessionagent.screenIsUnlocked` | Session-agent confirmation of unlock |

Cross-check against the private SkyLight `CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` key for direct session state — cua-driver already depends on SkyLight SPIs for event posting, so this stays within the existing private-API surface.

Lock-state can also be detected without private API by checking whether the loginwindow process owns the active AX tree — cua-driver already has the AX walker needed.

### Display-sleep guard

Hold an `IOPMAssertion` of type `kIOPMAssertPreventUserIdleDisplaySleep` (constant string `"PreventUserIdleDisplaySleep"`) for the duration of an active agent session. Released when the session ends or no MCP tool has been invoked for a configurable idle window. Equivalent to running `caffeinate -d` for the session lifetime, but scoped to the driver's process and cleaned up automatically.

This is the right assertion type for the use case: it keeps the display awake (so ScreenCaptureKit + SOM stays functional) without preventing actual user-initiated sleep via the Apple menu, and without preventing the system from sleeping when no agent is active.

### Inter-process channel

Expose the observer + guard to the existing MCP/CLI surface so agents can reason about session state and opt in/out of the guard explicitly.

## Proposed API surface

Three new MCP tools and two new CLI subcommands. All run inside the existing `cua-driver` process — no new binary, no new daemon.

### MCP tools

```
get_session_state         → { "locked": bool, "lock_ui_shown": bool,
                              "display_asleep": bool,
                              "since_ms": int }

acquire_sleep_guard       → { "held": true, "assertion_id": <int>,
                              "expires_at_ms": <int|null> }
  args: { "ttl_ms": int? (default unlimited, max 86_400_000) }

release_sleep_guard       → { "held": false }
  args: { "assertion_id": int? (optional — releases all guards held by this session if omitted) }
```

The TTL cap is a safety floor — a misbehaving agent that crashes mid-task shouldn't pin the display awake indefinitely.

### MCP server-sent notifications

Emit a server-to-client notification on every lock-state transition so a connected agent (or harness) can react without polling:

```
method: notifications/session_state_changed
params: { "locked": bool, "lock_ui_shown": bool, "transition": "lock"|"unlock"|"lock_ui_shown" }
```

Agents that don't subscribe pay zero overhead.

### CLI

```
cua-driver session-state               # one-shot read of get_session_state, exit 0
cua-driver sleep-guard --hold [--ttl 3600]
cua-driver sleep-guard --release
```

### Configuration

One new key in the persistent config, sensible default:

```
auto_sleep_guard: true     # when true, cua-driver auto-acquires the guard
                           #   for the duration of any MCP session and releases
                           #   when the session ends.
```

Defaults to `true` so the headline UX ("agent stays alive while you're away") works without explicit opt-in, but can be turned off for users who prefer manual control.

## Acceptance criteria

- Running `cua-driver session-state` returns valid JSON with the four documented fields and exits 0, both when the screen is locked and when it isn't.
- With `auto_sleep_guard: true`, an active MCP session prevents `pmset -g assertions` from showing the display going idle. Verified by leaving an idle agent session attached for 30 minutes with display-sleep set to 1 minute — display stays on for the duration of the session, sleeps within 1 minute after `cua-driver mcp` exits.
- Locking the screen during an active session fires a `notifications/session_state_changed` MCP notification with `transition: "lock"` within 500ms of the macOS `com.apple.screenIsLocked` notification firing.
- `acquire_sleep_guard` with a TTL strictly enforces release — no `IOPMAssertion` outlives its declared TTL by more than 1 second.
- All assertions cleaned up on `cua-driver mcp` exit (SIGTERM, SIGINT, normal shutdown). No orphan assertions visible in `pmset -g assertions` after process exit.
- `pmset -g assertions` shows the assertion owner as `cua-driver` (or `CuaDriver`) for attribution.

## Out of scope (for this issue)

- **Unlocking the screen on the user's behalf.** That requires a `SecurityAgentPlugin` running inside the privileged loginwindow context. Tracked separately — see "Related work" below.
- **Cross-platform parity.** Windows needs `WTSRegisterSessionNotification` + `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED | ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED)`. Linux session-lock handling is desktop-environment-dependent (logind D-Bus on systemd hosts, X11 idle hooks elsewhere). Both should land as separate per-platform issues once the macOS API surface here is stable enough to mirror.
- **Acting on lock state from inside cua-driver itself** (auto-pausing actions, auto-resuming on unlock, etc.). The API surface above gives agents and harnesses enough information to implement their own policy; cua-driver stays mechanism, not policy.

## Related work

- The deeper "drive the actual unlock UI" capability is a SecurityAgentPlugin job — separate issue, bigger lift, needs sudo installer and a security review pass. Filing that as a sibling so this MVP can ship independently.
- Issue #794 (closed) — "The computer-server cannot execute the operation on the Windows login page" — same shape of problem on Windows, different APIs. The macOS observer here is the precondition for a clean cross-platform story; without it, the Windows-side parity work has nothing to mirror.

## References

- Apple, `IOPMLib` — [IOPMAssertion documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/iopmlib_h)
- Apple, `DistributedNotificationCenter` — [public docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/distributednotificationcenter)
- The `com.apple.screenIsLocked` / `com.apple.screenIsUnlocked` distributed notifications are observable by any sandboxed-or-not app; reading them does not require entitlements. They have been stable across every macOS major since 10.9.
- 1Password and Yubico Authenticator both use the same notification pattern for their lock-aware unlock prompts — long-standing precedent for the approach.

title: feat(cua-driver): SecurityAgentPlugin for lock-screen interaction and unlock flow
body:
# feat(cua-driver): SecurityAgentPlugin for lock-screen interaction and unlock flow

## Motivation

Once cua-driver knows the screen is locked (tracked in the sibling lock-observer issue), the natural next question is: can the agent unlock it on behalf of the user?

The honest answer today is "no, and there is no userspace API that lets it." The lock-screen UI is rendered by `loginwindow` inside the privileged SecurityAgent context. Normal apps — even with full Accessibility + Screen Recording grants — cannot inject events into that context or read its UI in a way that survives Apple's sandbox boundaries. Trying to drive it via SkyLight private SPIs against `loginwindow`'s pid hits the same wall: the loginwindow refuses synthesized input events from a non-privileged source.

The sanctioned macOS escape hatch is a **`SecurityAgentPlugin`** — a bundle installed under `/Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins/` and registered against the system authorization database. Plugins are loaded by `authd` inside the SecurityAgent process, where they can interact with the lock-screen UI, present custom prompts, and complete authentication on the user's behalf. This is the same mechanism 1Password's Touch ID unlock, Yubico Authenticator's smart-card unlock, and most enterprise MFA agents use to integrate with the macOS lock screen.

Building this lets cua-driver complete a full background co-work session: the agent can finish a task, hit a lock-out, and (with explicit user consent) resume after unlock — without the user ever needing to physically return to the machine. Pair with the lock-state observer to drive a real "leave it running overnight" workflow.

## Proposed mechanism

A new bundle product in the cua repo, separate from `cua-driver` itself:

```
libs/cua-driver/plugins/CuaDriverAuthorizationPlugin.bundle
```

Loaded by `authd` into the SecurityAgent process when a request for a custom authorization right (proposed: `com.trycua.cua-driver.unlock`) is evaluated. The right is registered into `/etc/authorization` (the modern path: `/var/db/auth.db` via `security authorizationdb write`) at install time, with a rule like:

```
mechanisms = [ "CuaDriverAuthorizationPlugin:unlock-via-driver,privileged" ]
class      = "evaluate-mechanisms"
```

The plugin's responsibilities, when invoked:

1. Listen on the existing cua-driver socket (or a new, scoped one — see "Inter-process channel" below) for unlock requests from the running `cua-driver` MCP server.
2. Present a system-modal SecurityAgent prompt confirming the unlock with the user. The prompt is non-bypassable and rendered by the OS, not by cua-driver — this is the right safety story for "an agent is about to type your password".
3. On approval, complete the auth via the standard `AuthorizationCopyRights` flow. Reuses macOS keychain credentials; cua-driver never sees the user's password in plaintext.
4. Signal back to the running cua-driver MCP session that the unlock completed (or was denied), so the agent can resume its task or back off cleanly.

The plugin also reuses cua-driver's existing AX walker to inspect the loginwindow's UI — already implemented and exercised by the lock-observer issue. Inside SecurityAgent context, that walker now sees the actual lock-screen UI, not just its outer chrome.

## Inter-process channel

`SecurityAgentPlugin`s and userspace processes can't share memory or open files in the obvious way — SecurityAgent runs as a different user (`_securityagent`) in its own session. The standard pattern is a Unix-domain socket in `/var/run/` or `/tmp/<reverse-dns>/`, owned by root and accessible to both:

```
/var/run/com.trycua.cua-driver/lock-auth.sock
```

Permissions: `0600`, owner `root`, group `_securityagent`, with cua-driver's MCP server having a small helper (sudo-installed) that proxies to it. Lifetime: created at plugin install time, cleaned up by the uninstaller.

## Installer surface

A separate signed-and-notarized installer .app, distinct from the existing sudo-free `install.sh`:

```
CuaDriverAuthorizationPluginInstaller.app
```

Required because:

- Writing to `/Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins/` needs root.
- Registering the authorization right via `security authorizationdb write` needs root.
- Creating the socket directory under `/var/run/` needs root.

The existing `cua-driver install.sh` stays untouched and sudo-free. The auth-plugin installer is **opt-in only**, advertised in `cua-driver computer-use status` output and in the docs as a follow-up step for users who need the unlock capability. Users who don't install it never see any prompts and the lock-observer MVP keeps working as-is.

The installer is also responsible for its own uninstaller — `CuaDriverAuthorizationPluginUninstaller.app` or a documented `cua-driver computer-use uninstall-plugin` subcommand — so users can cleanly remove the plugin without touching the OS authorization database by hand.

## Proposed API surface

One new MCP tool, gated on the plugin being installed:

```
unlock_screen     → { "ok": bool, "denied": bool, "reason": str? }
  args: { "reason": str (shown verbatim in the SecurityAgent prompt) }
```

When the plugin isn't installed, the tool returns:

```
{ "ok": false, "denied": false,
  "reason": "auth plugin not installed; run CuaDriverAuthorizationPluginInstaller.app" }
```

CLI:

```
cua-driver unlock-screen --reason "agent X needs to resume task Y"
cua-driver computer-use plugin status        # installed / not installed / version
cua-driver computer-use plugin uninstall     # opens uninstaller
```

## Acceptance criteria

- A fresh install of the auth-plugin installer drops the bundle into `/Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins/`, registers `com.trycua.cua-driver.unlock` into the auth database, and creates the socket directory — all in a single sudo prompt.
- After install, calling `unlock_screen` from a connected MCP session, while the screen is locked, presents a system-modal SecurityAgent confirmation prompt with the agent-supplied reason string. Cancelling the prompt returns `denied: true`; confirming completes the unlock and returns `ok: true`.
- Calling `unlock_screen` when the screen is NOT locked returns `ok: true` immediately as a no-op.
- The uninstaller fully reverses the install: bundle removed, auth right removed via `security authorizationdb remove`, socket directory cleaned up. `pluginkit -m` shows no residual entries.
- The plugin is code-signed and notarized; Gatekeeper accepts the installer on a fresh macOS without quarantine workarounds.
- No keychain credentials are ever read or transmitted by cua-driver outside the SecurityAgent context. The plugin uses only `AuthorizationCopyRights` and never reads the in-memory password buffer.

## Out of scope

- **Driving 2FA / hardware-key prompts.** If the user's unlock requires Touch ID or a YubiKey, the plugin should pass through to the OS-native flow — not attempt to fake the second factor. Out of scope to add 2FA-bypass capabilities; in scope to make sure the existing flow works alongside one.
- **Storing the user's password.** Never. The plugin uses standard auth APIs that consume credentials in protected memory; cua-driver itself never sees the password.
- **Cross-platform parity.** Windows has no direct equivalent — the closest analog is a service running as SYSTEM in the winlogon context. Different security review story, different installer model, different issue.

## Security considerations

- The plugin's authorization right has its own audit trail (`log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.apple.authd"'`) — every invocation is logged by the OS.
- The system-modal SecurityAgent prompt is non-bypassable by the agent. cua-driver cannot programmatically dismiss it, type into it, or work around it — that's the entire point of routing through SecurityAgent.
- The plugin bundle is code-signed by the cua-driver team; tampering breaks the signature and `authd` refuses to load it.
- The socket is root-owned + `_securityagent` group + 0600, so no third party can MITM the unlock requests on a multi-user box.

## References

- Apple, [Authorization Services Programming Guide](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/Security/Conceptual/AuthorizationServices/Introduction/Introduction.html)
- Apple, [Security framework — Authorization](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/authorization_services)
- `man 8 authd`, `man 1 security` — runtime and CLI for the authorization database
- 1Password and Yubico Authenticator both ship SecurityAgentPlugin bundles via signed installers — long-standing reference implementations of this pattern.

## Related work

- This issue assumes the lock-state observer MVP (sibling issue) is landed first. Without the observer, this plugin has no clean way to know when to offer the unlock flow.
- Issue #794 (closed) — Windows login-page operation — is the conceptual sibling on the Windows side. The plugin pattern here doesn't apply there directly, but the cross-platform "unlock the device" capability lines up.

title: feat(nix): screenshot test using cua-driver's own MCP tools
body:
## Summary

Uses cua-driver's own `get_window_state` MCP tool with `capture_mode: "vision"` to take a screenshot of an xterm window running on Xvfb inside a NixOS VM. This proves the driver can:

1. Connect to X11 via Xvfb
2. Enumerate windows via `list_windows`
3. Capture pixels via `get_window_state` (vision mode)
4. Return the screenshot as base64 image data over MCP

### How it works

The test script:
1. Starts Xvfb + xterm with a test banner
2. Initiates MCP handshake with cua-driver
3. Calls `list_windows` to discover the xterm window (pid + window_id)
4. Calls `get_window_state` with `capture_mode: "vision"` to capture the window
5. Decodes the base64 image from the MCP response and saves it as PNG
6. Copies the PNG out of the VM via `copy_from_machine`

### Trigger

Add the `cua-driver-screenshot` label to any PR. The workflow:
- Runs the screenshot test
- Uploads the screenshot as a GitHub artifact
- Comments on the PR with a download link
- Removes the label

- The documented one-liner `irm <url>/scripts/uninstall.ps1 | iex` crashes at parse time with `Unexpected attribute 'CmdletBinding'` because `[CmdletBinding()] param([switch]$Force)` is only legal at the start of a script-file, function, or scriptblock — **not** inside an `Invoke-Expression`'d string.
- Replace the formal param block with an env var (`$env:CUA_DRIVER_RS_UNINSTALL_FORCE`). Env vars inherit across `Start-Process … -Verb RunAs`, so the `-Force` argument-forwarding plumbing in the self-elevation re-exec collapses too.
- Doc block updated to show the new force-mode usage and explain *why* it's an env var (so a future contributor doesn't reintroduce the param block).

## Repro (before this PR)

```
PS> irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/uninstall.ps1 | iex
iex : At line:67 char:1
+ [CmdletBinding()]
+ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Unexpected attribute 'CmdletBinding'.
At line:68 char:1
+ param(
+ ~~~~~
Unexpected token 'param' in expression or statement.
```

## After

```
# Interactive (asks before each major delete):
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/uninstall.ps1 | iex

# Force (skip all prompts):
$env:CUA_DRIVER_RS_UNINSTALL_FORCE = '1'
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/uninstall.ps1 | iex
```

Force flag survives the self-elevation re-exec (env inherits into the elevated child via `Start-Process`), so no `-ArgumentList` forwarding needed.

## Test plan

- [x] Parser-level: `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile` on the patched file → 0 errors.
- [x] iex-level: piped the patched script through `Invoke-Expression` up to the elevation pre-check.
  - env unset → `$Force = False` ✓
  - `$env:CUA_DRIVER_RS_UNINSTALL_FORCE = '1'` → `$Force = True` ✓
- [ ] End-to-end on a fresh box: install via `install.ps1` then run the new one-liner.
- [ ] End-to-end force path: same as above with the env var set, confirm no prompts.

## Follow-up — `install.ps1` has the same bug

`scripts/install.ps1` opens with the same `[CmdletBinding()] param(...)` block (L76-88) and reproduces the same parser error under `iex`:

```
PS> irm <url>/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
At line:78 char:33
+     [string]$Release = "latest",
+                                 ~
Missing expression after ','.
Missing ')' in function parameter list.
```

Three params there (`-Release`, `-AutoStart`/`-NoAutoStart`, `-NoPathUpdate`) → more API surface to translate, so deliberately left for a separate PR. Tracking issue worth opening if not already.

title: [Feature]: Add 'cua info' CLI diagnostic command
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?
When users report issues in the repository or Discord, maintainers frequently have to ask them for their OS, Python version, and cua-cli version. This causes unnecessary back-and-forth and slows down the debugging process.

### Describe the solution you'd like
Add a simple `cua info` command to the CLI that prints out all the necessary environment diagnostics (Platform, OS, Python version, CLI version) in a formatted list. This way, users can just run the command and paste the output when filing an issue.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
Currently, users have to run `python --version`, `uname -a`, and `cua --version` separately, which is error-prone.

title: cua-driver (macOS): extend launch_app preflight pattern to focus_app
body:
Follow-up from #1712 / PR #1719.

#1719 landed the preflight existence-check pattern for `launch_app` (`urls`, `bundle_id`, `name`) — missing targets now return structured `FILE_NOT_FOUND` / `APP_NOT_INSTALLED` errors instead of letting macOS pop a persistent Finder dialog.

The same gap exists in `focus_app`:

- `focus_app(app="ThisAppIsNotInstalled")` doesn't pre-check existence
- `NSWorkspace.urlForApplication(...)` / `NSRunningApplication` activation paths can still surface a "could not be opened" modal

## What to do

Extend the same preflight pattern from `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/launch_app.rs` (and the lookup helpers in `platform-macos/src/apps/mod.rs`) into `focus_app`. Return `APP_NOT_INSTALLED` with the same shape `launch_app` now returns, so MCP callers get a uniform contract.

Spec for the new error path matches LexClaw's original request in #1712: structured `{"error": "APP_NOT_INSTALLED", "app": "..."}` from the tool, no system dialog.

## Test plan

- Unit test: `focus_app({"app": "DoesNotExist"})` returns the structured error without spawning any macOS UI
- Mirror the test in `launch_app.rs` for parity

Good first issue if a contributor wants to follow up — the launch_app PR diff is a clean template.

title: cua-driver-rs (macOS): audit WindowChangeDetector + type_text for Bugs 2 + 3 from #1592
body:
Follow-up from #1592 (xronocode) after retiring the Swift backend.

The 3 candidate Swift fixes (#1593, #1691, #1700) won't land — cua-driver-rs is now the default backend after #1738. Bug 1 (Retina coord mismatch) doesn't exist in the Rust port because there's no standalone `screenshot` tool; capture is unified into `get_window_state` which already applies `max_image_dimension`.

But **Bugs 2 + 3 might still exist in the Rust port** and need verification.

## Bug 2 — daemon's own cursor-overlay window shown as "new window" in click responses

Swift fix (PR #1700) filtered `newEvents` by `ProcessInfo.processInfo.processIdentifier`. Rust equivalent lives in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/window_change_detector.rs`. Check whether the `snapshot` / `detect_changes` path filters out windows owned by the daemon's own pid (`std::process::id()`). If not, port the filter.

Symptom in agent traces: every `click` response includes a spurious "🪟 Action opened new window(s): Cua Driver" suffix.

## Bug 3 — `type_text` writes to stale focused element in modal-sheet context

Swift fix (PR #1700) guards `TypeTextTool` against stale `AXFocused` element when a macOS modal sheet (e.g. Open File dialog) is the actual focus owner.

Rust equivalent: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs` calls `focused_element_of_pid` on line 207. Audit whether it re-queries on every invocation or caches across modal sheet open/close. If the cached focus can go stale, port the Swift guard.

Symptom: `type_text` inserts into the AX element behind the modal instead of the modal's own text field.

## Verification

- Hard one for Bug 2: confirm via a recording, check that `action.json` no longer reports the overlay.
- Hard one for Bug 3: trigger a macOS Open File dialog, `type_text` into the sheet's path field, confirm characters land in the sheet.

Original report: https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/1592

title: fix(cua-driver-rs)(get_window_state): 30s timeout + 2000-node cap for heavy webview apps
body:
## Summary

Closes #1537. Cherry-picked from #1609 (@hippoley) — same fix concept, ported to the post-#1674 path layout (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/`).

When `get_window_state` walks the AX tree of a pathologically large app (Arc, Safari with many tabs, Electron), `AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue` can block indefinitely via XPC. There's no built-in deadline, so the MCP server just hangs forever — reported by @obaid on macOS 26.

Two changes, both Rust-only:

- **`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs`** — `MAX_ELEMENTS = 2000` cap on total nodes visited in a single walk. `walk_element` now threads a shared `visited_count` + `truncated` flag; when the cap is hit the walk stops early and `TreeWalkResult.truncated = true`. The renderer appends a warning line to `tree_markdown` so the agent knows the partial tree is intentional and existing element indices remain valid.
- **`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs`** — wraps the `spawn_blocking` AX walk in `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))`. On expiry returns a descriptive `ToolResult::error` suggesting `capture_mode=vision` or a `query` filter rather than hanging.

## Notes

- Swift backend changes from #1609 (`libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverCore/AppState/AppState.swift`) **deliberately dropped** — that path is being deprecated per #1738.
- `TreeWalkResult` gains a new public field (`truncated: bool`); additive, doesn't break existing callers.
- Credit to @hippoley — the 30s timeout + 2000-node cap shape is verbatim from their PR. Co-authored.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --release -p cua-driver` on macOS — green
- [x] `cargo check -p platform-windows --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` — green (additive struct field doesn't touch Windows code)
- [ ] Live repro on Arc / Safari w/ many tabs (the issue #1537 repro): verify `get_window_state` returns a truncation warning rather than hanging
- [ ] Verify the 30s timeout fires with a clear error message on a known-bad target

cc @obaid for the original repro, @hippoley for the original fix.

title: fix(cua-driver-rs)(macos): per-element AX messaging timeout + cycle/time guards for heavy webview walks
body:
## Problem

`get_window_state` can hang indefinitely on apps with large or busy accessibility trees (heavy webviews). Reading an AX attribute is a synchronous XPC round-trip into the target app; while a renderer is materializing its tree, that round-trip can stay pending forever and wedge the entire walk. The outer thread-level timeout then just tears down a stuck walk rather than letting it make progress.

## Fix

Set a per-element messaging timeout once, on the application element, right after `AXUIElementCreateApplication`:

- `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout(app_elem, 1.5)` — the ceiling is inherited by every descendant element vended through the app element, so a single wedged element fails fast with `kAXErrorCannotComplete` in ~1.5s instead of blocking the whole traversal. This is the real anti-hang fix.

Two layered backstops in `walk_element`:

- **Cycle dedup** — a `visited: HashSet<usize>` keyed on the element pointer address. AX is a graph, not a strict tree; a malformed hierarchy can re-vend an element already walked, and this stops that from inflating the walk.
- **5s per-walk wall-clock budget** — bails between AX calls the same way the depth guard does. It cannot abort an in-flight call (that is the messaging timeout's job); it caps cumulative time across many slow-but-completing calls.

These complement, not replace, the existing outer thread-level timeout and the `MAX_DEPTH` guard.

## Scope

- `platform-macos` only; `platform-windows` / `platform-linux` unaffected.
- `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout` is a stable HIServices symbol (since 10.4); declared alongside the other `AXUIElement*` FFI bindings.

## Validation

- `cargo build --release -p cua-driver` passes.
- `cargo test --no-run -p platform-macos` compiles (the pre-existing `libswift_Concurrency.dylib` rpath issue is at the test-binary link step, not introduced here).
- Live VM validation against heavy webview apps still recommended before un-drafting.

Refs #1537
