title: perf(cua-driver-rs)(macos): batch AX attribute fetch + ranged children to cut walk IPC ~3x
body:
## What

Each AX attribute read is a synchronous IPC round-trip to the target app. The macOS tree walker previously issued **~7 round-trips per node** (AXRole, AXTitle, AXValue, AXPlaceholderValue, AXDescription, AXIdentifier, AXHelp). This coalesces them into **one batched fetch per node (~7→1)** and bounds how many children of any single node we materialize.

## Changes

**`bindings.rs`**
- Declare the batched / ranged / count attribute FFI (`AXUIElementCopyMultipleAttributeValues`, `AXUIElementCopyAttributeValues`, `AXUIElementGetAttributeValueCount`) plus `AXValueGetTypeID`.
- `copy_multiple_attrs(element, &[&str]) -> Vec<Option<String>>`: one round-trip for N attributes. **`options = 0` (NOT stop-on-error)** so a single unsupported attribute does not abort the whole batch — that slot comes back as an AXValue error placeholder and is filtered out **by position and type**. One `Option<String>` per requested attribute, in request order.
- `copy_children_ranged(element, max) -> (Vec<…>, clipped)`: fetch up to `max` children in one round-trip and report whether the child list was clipped.

**`tree.rs`**
- `walk_element` now issues one `copy_multiple_attrs` batch indexed by position instead of ~7 separate calls. Action names stay a separate call (different AX API).
- Per-node child fetches use `copy_children_ranged` with a **200-child cap**; a per-node `… (children clipped at 200)` note is appended when a node exceeds it.

## None-vs-empty semantics (preserved)

A **present-but-empty** attribute stays `Some("")` and an **absent** attribute stays `None`. So a node whose AXTitle is `""` but whose AXDescription carries the real label still renders the description in parens — the digit-button case the click harness depends on is unaffected by batching.

## Coexistence with the total-walk cap

The per-node child cap (`MAX_CHILDREN = 200`) is a **different concern** from the existing total-walk node cap (`MAX_ELEMENTS = 2000`): the child cap bounds one pathological node (a virtualized list/grid), the total cap bounds the walk as a whole. They layer cleanly.

## Notes

- Build passes (`cargo build --release -p cua-driver`); tests compile (`cargo test --no-run -p platform-macos`).
- Recommend merging **after** #1755 (per-element messaging timeout) so the batched calls inherit the bounded XPC timeout.

Refs #1537

title: cua-driver (macOS): serve launched via `open -n -g -a CuaDriver` lags/fails socket creation on first launch (permissions-gate re-exec)
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver serve` creates its Unix socket **instantly** when run foreground from a terminal, but when launched via LaunchServices (`open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve` — the path that gives correct TCC attribution) the socket lags many seconds or doesn't appear in a reasonable window on first launch.

## Why it matters

This is the blessed launch for correct TCC attribution (the daemon's prompts attribute to `com.trycua.driver` instead of the calling terminal — see #1491, PR #1760). But because the socket lags:
- `launch_daemon_and_wait(socket, 10)` times out → callers fall back / re-launch.
- An auto-spawn-from-`call` approach piled up zombie daemons re-prompting in a loop (abandoned in PR #1760 for this reason).

## Observed

```
# foreground from terminal — instant
$ /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver serve
Cua Driver daemon listening on ~/Library/Caches/cua-driver/cua-driver.sock   # <1s

# via LaunchServices — daemon is alive (ppid=1) but socket absent for >4-10s
$ open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve
$ ps -o pid,ppid,command -ax | grep CuaDriver.app.*serve
  19800  1  /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver serve
$ ls ~/Library/Caches/cua-driver/cua-driver.sock
  (absent)
```

The daemon process is alive but hasn't bound the socket.

## Hypothesis

The macOS permissions gate (`platform-macos/src/permissions/gate.rs`) runs **before** the socket is created in `run_serve_cmd`. On first launch its initial `AXIsProcessTrusted()` / screen-recording check can return a stale `false` (per-process TCC cache), triggering the `wait_for_grants` re-exec cycle (`reexec_self` every ~5 polls). Under LaunchServices the re-exec/attribution interaction seems to delay reaching the socket-bind step. Foreground from a terminal (which already has the grant in its responsible chain) passes the gate immediately.

Possibly compounded by a stale TCC cache after `tccutil reset` (#1561).

## Suggested directions

- Create + bind the socket **before** entering the blocking permissions gate, so callers can connect (and the daemon reports "permissions pending" over the socket) rather than waiting on the gate.
- Or: skip/short-circuit the gate when a fast read already shows grants present.
- Or: have the gate's first check use a fresh (non-cached) TCC query so the re-exec cycle isn't entered when grants exist.

## Refs
- #1491 (mcp/call LaunchServices attribution), #1561 (stale TCC cache after reset), PR #1758 (the .app bundle), PR #1760 (call report-only fix)

title: fix(cua-driver): default install.sh backend back to Swift
body:
The Rust implementation has issues with the macOS TCC permission system, so this flips the default backend in `install.sh` back to the Swift macOS implementation.

## Changes (scoped to `install.sh` only)

- **Default flipped**: `USE_RUST_BACKEND=0`. With no flags on macOS, the installer now uses the Swift implementation, sidestepping the Rust TCC permission issues.
- **Rust is now opt-in**: `--backend=rust` and the legacy `--experimental-rust` opt into Rust; `--backend=swift` is the explicit no-op default.
- **Non-macOS safety net**: Swift is macOS-only, so on any non-Darwin host the script transparently promotes to the Rust implementation (the only one that builds there) with a `note:`. This avoids breaking Linux/Windows installs.
- Updated header flag docs and two-pass parsing comments to match the inverted default.

## Verification

- `bash -n` passes.
- Backend selection verified across platforms/flags: macOS defaults to Swift, `--backend=rust`/`--experimental-rust` select Rust, and non-macOS hosts fall back to Rust.

title: cua-driver-rs 0.3.2: serve daemon RSS grows unbounded (~1GB/h) + ~15% idle CPU after computer-use session on Apple M4 / macOS 26
body:
## Summary

On macOS (Apple M4), the `cua-driver-rs` 0.3.2 `serve` daemon grows **unbounded (~1 GB/hour)** and holds **~15% CPU at idle** after a computer-use session, persisting until killed. In one incident it reached **~4.8 GB RSS over ~1h13m** and contributed to a host memory-thrash that forced a hard reboot.

We run `cua-driver-rs` as the documented M4 workaround for #1671 (the Swift driver hangs on M4), driving it from a long-lived MCP stdio client.

## Environment

- Hardware: Apple M4 Mac mini (Mac16,10), 16 GB
- macOS: 26.x (Tahoe), arm64
- cua-driver: **cua-driver-rs 0.3.2** (`/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, teamID YCK386LBJ7), running as the LaunchServices daemon spawned by `cua-driver mcp` (default daemon-relaunch), Accessibility + Screen Recording granted.
- Client: long-lived MCP stdio client, `args: [mcp]`.

## What we observed

- **A fresh `serve` with no client connected is healthy**: flat ~16 MB RSS, **0% CPU**. `sample` shows every thread (main + `tokio-rt-worker`s) parked in `parking_lot::Condvar::wait_until_internal` -> `_pthread_cond_wait`. No spin.
- **After a persistent MCP session that performed captures**, `serve` begins growing (~1 GB/h) and spins ~15% CPU, and **does not release after the agent goes idle** — the connection stays open and a background loop keeps running until the daemon is killed.
- The growth is **not** driven by client polling — capture tools are called on-demand only; there is no heartbeat/poll loop on the client side.
- `strings` on the binary shows `Timeout waiting for shareable content` (ScreenCaptureKit `SCShareableContent`) and a WindowChangeDetector (cf. #1526). Suspected: a continuous ScreenCaptureKit / window-change-detection loop (or a retained `SCStream`/frame buffer) started on first capture and **not torn down when the session goes idle or disconnects**.
- Possibly related: the daemon proxy intermittently returns **`Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)`** when forwarding larger tool responses (e.g. `get_accessibility_tree`), then falls back to in-process with a warning. Small calls (`check_permissions`) proxy fine.

## Repro

1. Launch `serve` via `cua-driver mcp` daemon-relaunch (TCC granted).
2. Hold an MCP session open; issue a few `get_window_state` (capture_mode `som`) calls, then leave the session connected but idle.
3. Watch `ps -o rss,%cpu` of the `serve` pid climb (~1 GB/h) and CPU sit ~15% while no further tool calls are made.

## Expected

After a session goes idle (or the client disconnects), the daemon should release capture resources and return to the parked ~16 MB / 0% CPU baseline; RSS should stay bounded under sustained sessions.

## Asks

1. Tear down the capture pipeline / `SCStream` / WindowChangeDetector when a session goes idle or the MCP client disconnects.
2. Consider an idle TTL for the daemon (auto-exit after N seconds with no active session), since `cua-driver mcp` re-execs it on demand.
3. Investigate the `os error 35` (EAGAIN) on larger daemon-proxy frames.

Happy to provide full `sample` thread backtraces or test a patch. Thanks for the great tool — otherwise `cua-driver-rs` + a long-lived MCP client is working well on M4.

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): daemon session identity — own + clean up session-scoped recording & config
body:
## The multi-tenant problem

The cua-driver daemon (`serve.rs`) is **one shared process**: every `cua-driver mcp` proxy connects to it and shares its `ToolState`. Any "set once, affects later calls" daemon state is therefore multi-tenant and gets clobbered across concurrent MCP sessions:

- **Recording** — `ToolRegistry.recording` is a singleton. Session A's disconnect could stop session B's recording.
- **Config** — `set_config` does `config.write()` AND persists to `~/.cua-driver/config.json`. A sets `vision`, B sets `som` → clobber, and the on-disk default flips under everyone.

The daemon drives **one** physical machine, so this is a **state ownership + cleanup** problem, not safe concurrent screen/input control (two sessions clicking at once still contend for one desktop — out of scope, kept honest).

## The session_id model

A **proxy-minted session identity** (one per `cua-driver mcp` process) carried in the daemon request envelope, used to OWN and CLEAN UP session-scoped state.

- **Envelope** — `DaemonRequest` gains an optional `session_id` (`skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none`, so the absent case is byte-identical on the wire; serde defaults a missing field to `None`). A new `session_end` lifecycle method reuses the same envelope. The daemon injects `_session_id` into the tool args right before `invoke` (Unix + Windows mirrors); tools read it via the existing `ArgsExt`, exactly like `cursor_id` — **no `Tool` trait change**, no schema whitelist (the daemon never validates args against `input_schema`).
- **Recording ownership** — `RecordingSession` gains `owner: Option<String>`; `start()` stamps it from `_session_id`; `stop_owner(requester)` is `None` = unconditional (manual/CLI/idle-TTL), `Some==owner` = stop, `Some!=owner` = no-op. **Supersedes the #1775 generation token wholesale** — a stable owner identity that doubles as the config key, instead of a monotonic counter.
- **Config-per-session (macOS)** — `SessionConfigRegistry` holds in-memory overrides keyed by `session_id`, layered over the global. A named MCP session's `set_config` writes only its override (no global write, no disk); the anonymous CLI / one-shot path keeps writing + persisting the global default. `get_config` / `get_window_state` / `click` resolve effective = call-arg > session > global.
- **Cleanup** — the proxy mints the id once (dep-free `pid+nanos`, **no `uuid` crate**) and sends one best-effort `session_end` on stdin EOF; the daemon drops that session's recording (`stop_owner`) + config overrides (platform session-end hooks). `_session_id` and any `_`-prefixed key are stripped before a turn is recorded, so the UUID never lands in `action.json`.

## In scope vs deferred

**In:** the envelope + `session_end`, daemon-side `_session_id` injection (both platforms), proxy minting/teardown, recording ownership (replacing the #1775 token), and config-per-session for macOS.

**Deferred (design-noted TODOs):**
- **Cursor** session-scoping — pure-additive, rides this envelope; `CursorRegistry` needs a `remove`/overlay-disable that doesn't exist yet.
- **PiP** — process-global by design (one experimental preview for the one machine); no session change ever.
- **Generic per-session idle reaper** for SIGKILLed proxies (`session_end` only fires on graceful EOF). The daemon-global recording idle-TTL is an acceptable interim backstop; there is no merged config TTL yet, so a SIGKILLed session's config overrides linger until daemon restart — a small bounded in-memory leak.
- **Windows/Linux `set_config` parity** — they have their own `DriverConfig`; this PR scopes the config split to macOS.
- The clean `invoke_with_session` trait/context API — YAGNI; inject-via-args avoids touching every Tool impl across 3 platform crates.

## Verification (live, isolated socket, two real `cua-driver mcp` proxies)

- **Config isolation** — A `set_config capture_mode=vision`, B `set_config capture_mode=som`; A's `get_config` → **vision**, B's → **som**, concurrently, no clobber. `~/.cua-driver/config.json` capture_mode stayed **ax** (neither named-session write touched disk). ✅
- **Recording ownership + disconnect** — A `start_recording`, B `start_recording` (clobbers the singleton); close A → recording still enabled, `owner` = B's id; close B → stops. A-only start + disconnect → stops. ✅
- **Manual / CLI stop unconditional** — a recording owned by a session is torn down by an anonymous direct-socket `recording stop` (`session_id=None` → `stop_owner(None)`). ✅
- **Backward-compat** — one-shot `cua-driver call get_config` (no session) returns the global; `call set_config capture_mode=vision` writes the persisted global default (survives a daemon reboot via `load_driver_config()`). ✅
- **Args non-pollution** — a recorded `move_cursor` turn's `action.json` carries only `{x, y}`; `_session_id` was injected, used, and stripped. ✅
- `cargo build -p cua-driver` clean; `cargo test -p cua-driver -p cua-driver-core` introduces **no new failures** beyond the 5 pre-existing `mcp_protocol_test` ones (verified identical set on the base branch).

## Notes

- Supersedes the **#1775 generation token** (this branch inherits the #1764 recording-teardown leak fix and replaces its generation guard with session ownership) and fixes the **daemon-restart race** on the persisted config default (named sessions no longer race it — only the anonymous CLI / one-shot writes it).
- Warrants a **MINOR (0.4.0)** bump: new wire field + `session_end` method, new public `core::session` hook surface, and `get_config`-from-a-named-session now reports effective-per-session values rather than the raw global.

title: fix(cua-driver-rs): wire/guide per-session cursors through the real mcp path + skills/docs
body:
## The user report

A user ran the documented Claude Code install — `cua-driver mcp-config --client claude` → `claude mcp add-json cua-computer-use ... args:["mcp","--claude-code-computer-use-compat"]` — then drove Claude Code: launch Calculator, AX-press `3 1 =`, screenshot. It worked, and `check_permissions` standalone correctly showed `attribution:"driver-daemon"`, `responsible_ppid:1` (the bundle daemon). But:

1. **No agent cursor was visible**, even on the AX actions.
2. *"I do not see any notion of session in the mcp calls"* — is the session actually wired through the real mcp path?
3. Did we forget to update the CLI / MCP / skills?

## Bug vs working-as-designed

### Working as designed: the session IS wired on the path the user ran
The `mcp --claude-code-computer-use-compat` proxy mints one `session_id` per MCP connection (`proxy.rs`), opens a control connection (`session_begin`), and stamps `session_id` on every forwarded request. The daemon injects it as `_session_id` into tool args (`serve.rs:498`) and **strips it from the user-visible wire envelope by design** — that's why the user "sees no session in the mcp calls." `resolve_cursor_key` reads `cursor_id > _session_id > "default"`, and `session_end` fires on control-connection EOF. Per-session cursor / config / recording are **live** on this exact path, not inert.

**Verified headless** (against the installed bundle): in one MCP session, `set_agent_cursor_enabled{enabled:false}` followed by `get_config{}` returns `agent_cursor.enabled:false`. That round-trip only works if `_session_id` reached the daemon and `resolve_cursor_key` read **this session's** cursor (a broken path would read the always-on `"default"`). ✅

### BUG 1 (user-visible): no glide on a pure-AX run
A brand-new session cursor sits at the off-screen sentinel `(-200,-200)`. `animate_cursor_to` early-returned at the sentinel, so the **first** AX action only snapped a static arrow via `ClickPulse` — no motion, easy to miss in a recording. **Fix:** `seed_start_if_sentinel` seeds the cursor on-screen (offset up-left of the target, clamped to the screen) before animating, so the first action glides. Get-or-create + `ended`-tombstone guard so it never resurrects a reaped session. Unit-tested (3 tests).

### BUG 2 (latent wiring): `--claude-code-computer-use-compat` dropped on the proxy path
The flag only flipped *in-process* registration; the proxy-spawned daemon (`Serve` arm) hardcoded `build_macos_registry()` → `compat=false`, so the flag was **silently dropped on the exact path users run**. **Fix:** thread it end-to-end — the proxy forwards `serve --claude-code-computer-use-compat`, and the `Serve` arm honours it via `build_macos_registry_with_compat`. **Honest caveat:** the compat *screenshot* tool was removed in #1692, so today the served tool surface is identical either way (confirmed by diffing tools/list with/without the flag). The value here is that the flag now **travels** — the moment any compat-gated tool returns, the proxy path will honour it instead of dropping it.

### BUG 3 (nondeterministic): get_config cursor state
`get_config` reported `agent_cursor.enabled` from `cursor_registry.all_states().first()` — a nondeterministic `HashMap.first()`. **Fix:** resolve the calling session's cursor by key (`resolve_cursor_key`), falling back to `"default"`. Unit-tested with two sessions reading opposite flags.

## Skills / docs updated
- **SKILL.md** — kept "Default: enabled"; added the per-session model + `session_end` removal + the AX no-glide/snap caveat; **corrected the false claim** that the AX path "skips the agent-cursor overlay" (it doesn't — it seeds/pulses the session cursor and draws a focus rect).
- **cursor_tools.rs** — `set_agent_cursor_enabled` description now says the overlay is default-ON and each session owns its own cursor (does NOT claim OFF-by-default).
- **protocol.rs** — server-instructions "Agent cursor:" line: per-session + AX-snap caveat.
- **cli.rs** — `print_help` now documents `--no-overlay` / `--cursor-id` / `--cursor-icon` / `--cursor-palette` / `--claude-code-computer-use-compat` and the "needs serve/mcp runloop" note.
- **mcp-tools.mdx** (per MEMORY: docs touched in the same PR) — AX snap-not-glide caveat near `set_agent_cursor_enabled`.

## Cursor-default RECOMMENDATION (your call — not implemented here)
There is a spec-vs-code divergence: the task framing assumed #1657 shipped the agent cursor as **opt-in / default-OFF**, but the current code has **no such gate** — a lazily-created per-session cursor inherits `visible=true` and the paint gate checks only `core.visible`, so the cursor is effectively **default-ON**. `set_agent_cursor_enabled` is NOT required to make it draw.

**My recommendation: keep default-ON** (it matches the code, matches mcp-tools.mdx, and means a demo/recording "just works" without an extra enable call) and instead fix the real visibility gap — which this PR does (BUG 1: seed-then-glide on AX). If you instead want true opt-in/default-OFF per #1657, that gate is **currently unimplemented** and needs building (a session-scoped enabled flag read by the paint/animate path + deterministic get_config), plus all docs flipped to "OFF by default." I did **not** change the default — flagging the divergence for you to decide.

## Verification
- `cargo build -p cua-driver` ✅; `cargo check -p platform-windows -p platform-linux` ✅
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core` 46 passed ✅; `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` 72 passed (incl. 5 new) ✅
- The 5 `tests/mcp_protocol_test.rs` failures are the **pre-existing** stale-name (`"cua-driver"` vs `"cua-driver-rs"`) failures, already red on origin/main — no NEW failures.
- **Headless (a) session injected on compat path:** PASS — `mcp --claude-code-computer-use-compat` → `_session_id` reaches the daemon; per-session cursor active.
- **Headless (b) cursor keying:** PASS — `set_agent_cursor_enabled` + an AX click in the same session resolve the SAME session key (unit test) so the enabled cursor renders at the AX-pressed element.
- **Installed local** (authorized): uninstall + `install-local.sh --release`; `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` is this build, `~/.local/bin/cua-driver` points at it, and `permissions status` shows `attribution:"driver-daemon"`, `responsible_ppid:1`.

### Manual VM eyeball (REQUIRED — cannot be headless)
On the macOS VM with the bundle daemon launched `-g`:
1. Grant Accessibility + Screen Recording: `cua-driver permissions grant`.
2. Re-run the Calculator AX task (launch Calculator, AX-press `3 1 =`).
3. **Expect:** the agent cursor now **glides** to the first AX target (not a silent snap), pulses, and draws a focus rect. For an even more obvious glide, do a pixel `click({pid,x,y})` or `move_agent_cursor` first.

title: feat(cua-driver-rs)(install-local): stable self-signed identity so TCC grants survive rebuilds
body:
## Problem
`install-local` ad-hoc-signs the bundle, so the TCC grant is pinned to the binary's **cdhash** — which changes on **every rebuild**. Each `install-local` silently invalidates Accessibility/Screen Recording (Settings still shows granted; the live check fails), and the daemon re-prompts. The exact "I granted it but it keeps asking" loop.

## Fix
Create a self-signed code-signing cert **once** (idempotent, login keychain) and sign the bundle with it. TCC then keys the grant on the **certificate leaf** (stable across rebuilds):

```
designated => identifier "com.trycua.driver" and certificate leaf = H"c5a1743…"   # was: cdhash H"…"
```

Grant once; future `install-local`s keep it. Verified locally (DR is now cert-based; signs + launches fine — local bundles have no quarantine so Gatekeeper doesn't object).

Fail-soft: openssl 3.x needs `-legacy` + a p12 password for Apple's `security import`; falls back to non-legacy (LibreSSL) and ultimately to **ad-hoc + a note** if the cert can't be made (CI, locked keychain). Local-dev only; releases are CI-signed.

title: fix(cua-driver-rs)(install-local): reset a TCC grant pinned to a previous signing identity
body:
## Problem

A user on the local dev loop hit this exact dead end (debugged live this session):

```
$ cua-driver permissions status
Accessibility:    ❌ not granted
Screen Recording: ❌ not granted
```

…yet **System Settings showed CuaDriver toggled ON**, and the TCC rows were `auth_value=2` (allowed). Decoding the stored requirement:

```
kTCCServiceAccessibility | com.trycua.driver | 2 | csreq = cdhash H"388846d5…"   ← granted on an older (ad-hoc) build
                                                    current build cdhash = 50f6b910…   ← doesn't match → "not granted"
```

#1792 made `install-local` sign `CuaDriver.app` with a stable self-signed cert so grants survive rebuilds — **but only for grants created while cert-signed**. A grant made earlier on an *ad-hoc* build is pinned to that build's per-rebuild `cdhash`. It survives reinstall as `allowed` but stops matching the new binary, and because the row already records a decision, **re-toggling the switch never re-fires the prompt**. The user is stuck.

## Fix

Record the signing identity (cert leaf, or `adhoc`) in `~/.cua-driver/.tcc-signing-identity`. When `install-local` signs with a cert identity that **differs from the last install**, run `tccutil reset` for Accessibility + ScreenCapture once, so the next `cua-driver permissions grant` prompts cleanly and re-pins to the stable cert. From then on, grants survive every rebuild.

- `tccutil reset` needs no sudo / Full Disk Access; it's a no-op when nothing was granted.
- Only resets when moving **to** a cert identity — an ad-hoc build churns its cdhash every rebuild regardless, so resetting it would add friction with no durable fix.

Transition matrix (verified):

| last install | this install | action |
|---|---|---|
| _(none)_ / ad-hoc | cert | **reset** (clears stale ad-hoc grant) |
| cert X | cert X | no reset (stable rebuild — the whole point) |
| cert X | cert Y | reset (cert rotated) |
| cert | ad-hoc | no reset (no durable fix anyway) |

## Docs

- FAQ: new entry "After a rebuild, the driver reports `NOT granted` but System Settings still shows CuaDriver toggled ON" with the manual `tccutil reset` recovery.
- Changelog: Unreleased entry (this script lives in `libs/cua-driver/scripts/`, outside the `libs/cua-driver/rust` path the release changelog auto-scans, so it needs a manual line).

## Test

- `bash -n` clean.
- Identity extraction verified against the live signed bundle → `cert:c5a1743942b4777b6819288447730db37f1663d9` (matches the bundle DR leaf).
- Reset decision simulated across all six transitions above.

Local dev path only — release builds are CI-signed with a stable identity and unaffected.

title: docs(cua-driver-rs)(launch_app): surface creates_new_application_instance for concurrent multi-agent isolation
body:
## Why

Follow-up to the concurrent-sessions discussion (and the UAF fix in #1796). When two agents drive the **same** app, `launch_app`'s idempotency hands them the **same** instance — and on single-instance apps (Calculator, many utilities) the **same window** — so they clobber each other.

The capability to avoid this **already exists**: the `creates_new_application_instance` param maps to AppKit's `NSWorkspaceOpenConfiguration.createsNewApplicationInstance` (the programmatic `open -n`). My earlier "possible follow-up" note was wrong — it's been there. The real gap was **discoverability**: nothing in the agent-facing surfaces told an agent to reach for it in the concurrent case.

## What

Pure docs/description — **no behavior change**:
- `launch_app` tool description (the agent-facing schema) now explains the concurrent-session use.
- `creates_new_application_instance` property description spells out the isolation rationale.
- `mcp-tools.mdx` reference entry updated to match.
- `SKILL.md` action-loop section gains a "Concurrent sessions" note: pass `creates_new_application_instance: true` so each session gets its own `(pid, window_id)` — which also keeps the element cache and per-session cursor cleanly separated.

The verbose name is kept deliberately (self-documenting); no terse alias added.

## Verified

Two `launch_app(name="Calculator", creates_new_application_instance=true)` calls through the daemon return distinct pids + distinct `window_id`s. `cargo build -p cua-driver` clean; `4/4` launch_app tests pass.

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): caller-declared session identity + Streamable-HTTP transport for multi-agent parallelism
body:
**DRAFT — needs VM eyeball (macOS cursor visual + Windows `cua demo use`) before ready.**

## Why

A "session" (which owns the agent cursor + per-session state) was minted **per MCP connection**, so it (a) couldn't be set from the CLI, (b) couldn't span a run that touches multiple apps, and (c) made subagents on one connection share a cursor. Per the design discussion, a session should be a **caller-declared identity**, orthogonal to both the transport and the target window.

Spec: `drafts/session-identity-redesign-2026-05-31.md` (local).

## What

- **Explicit `session` identity.** Pass a `session` id (or call new `start_session`/`end_session` tools). The daemon mirrors it into the reserved `_session_id` at the boundary (`apply_session_identity`), so cursor + per-session config + recording all key on it. Same id over MCP, CLI (`cua-driver call <tool> '{"session":"x"}'`), or raw socket; follows the run across apps/windows.
- **Cursor is explicit-required.** `resolve_cursor_key` reads only the explicit `session`/`cursor_id` (no connection fallback, no seeded `"default"`). No `session` → `NO_CURSOR` (`""`); overlay + registry short-circuit the empty key. The action still executes — just cursor-less.
- **Lifecycle = `end_session` + idle-TTL.** `session::{touch_session, end_session, evict_idle}`; a 30s daemon sweep ends sessions idle past the TTL (default 300s, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_SESSION_IDLE_TTL_SECS`). Per-session config + recording keep connection-EOF cleanup as the fallback when no session is declared (low-risk; unchanged for that path).
- **Tools:** `start_session` / `end_session` (core, registered on all 3 platforms). `session` property added to action-tool schemas.
- **Docs/instructions:** MCP server instructions + SKILL.md now tell agents to `start_session` first; mcp-tools + changelog updated. **Breaking** (cursor opt-in).

## Tested (so far)

- `cargo build -p cua-driver` clean.
- `74/74` platform-macos lib tests, `50/50` cua-driver-core tests (incl. new session registry/TTL + session_tools + rewritten cursor-key tests).

- [ ] macOS: install-local, eyeball — start_session → action shows a colored cursor; two sessions = two cursors; end_session removes; anonymous call = no cursor; idle-TTL reclaims.
- [ ] **Windows VM: `cua demo use` smoke** — daemon runs, start/end_session work, no regressions (no overlay on Windows; identity scopes config/recording).
- [ ] Consider `--session` CLI flag + `session start/end` verbs (works via `call` today).

title: fix(cua-driver-rs)(windows): per-session agent cursors (port macOS #1779)
body:
## The problem

On Windows the agent cursor overlay was a **process-wide singleton** — one `RenderState` behind the single layered window. Every cursor op (`move_cursor`, the `ClickPulse` of click/double_click/right_click/drag, `set_agent_cursor_*`) drove that one state with **no session discriminator**, so concurrent MCP sessions clobbered each other last-writer-wins → **one shared cursor for all sessions**.

**#1779** fixed exactly this on macOS but scoped itself macOS-only: *"Windows (`platform-windows/src/overlay.rs`) and Linux compile and behave exactly as before (single cursor; the key concept never reaches them)."* The 0.4.x daemon already mints per-session identity (caller-declared `session`, `session_end` hook, idle-TTL) — this PR uses it to give each Windows session its own cursor, mirroring the macOS data model 1:1.

## What changed

**`platform-windows/src/overlay.rs`** — the keyed render collection:
- `static RENDER: Mutex<Option<RenderState>>` → `Mutex<Option<RenderMap>>` where `RenderMap { cursors: IndexMap<CursorKey, RenderState>, … }`. `IndexMap` = deterministic insertion-ordered iteration = stable per-session z-order frame to frame.
- `send_command(key, cmd)` carries a `CursorKey`; the `WM_TIMER` tick drains keyed `OverlayMsg`s via get-or-create, ticks every cursor, fires per-key arrival oneshots, and **composites all cursors into the ONE layered window** via `paint_cursor` (alpha-over, insertion order = paint order). Idle/hidden cursors early-return.
- Lazy per-key creation with `Palette::for_instance(key)` → **each session a distinct colour automatically**.
- `remove_cursor` + render-side `ended` tombstone (resurrection guard); `"default"` guarded against removal so the anonymous / one-shot `cua-driver call` path is unchanged. Per-key arrival `HashMap` so concurrent sessions don't cross-cancel glide-waits. Sentinel-seed so a session's first AX action glides instead of snapping.

**`platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`**:
- `resolve_cursor_key` — precedence `session` > `cursor_id` > `NO_CURSOR` (never the connection-injected `_session_id`), identical to `platform_macos::tools::cursor_tools::resolve_cursor_key`.
- Threaded the key through `pin_overlay_above`, `overlay_glide_to`, every `ClickPulse` callsite, and the 5 cursor tools (`move_cursor`, `set_agent_cursor_enabled` / `_motion` / `_style`, `get_agent_cursor_state`).
- Registered a once-guarded `session_end` hook → `overlay::remove_cursor` (+ `cursor_registry.remove`), so explicit `end_session`, the CLI verb, and the idle-TTL sweep all drop a session's cursor.
- `get_config`'s `cursor_enabled` is now session-scoped + deterministic (was `all_states().first()` over a HashMap — macOS BUG 3).

**`cursor-overlay/src/lib.rs`** — `CursorRegistry::remove` (guards `"default"`). **`Cargo.toml`** — `indexmap`. **`page.rs` / `stubs.rs`** — updated to the keyed API.

### Known limitation (follow-up)
`page.click_element` drives the seeded `"default"` cursor: the cross-platform `PageBackend` trait carries no caller `session`. Threading session through the trait is a separate cross-platform change (macOS doesn't implement `click_element` at all today).

## Verification
- `cargo build -p platform-windows` + `-p cua-driver` — clean, **zero warnings**.
- `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib` — **49 passed** (15 new: two-session isolation, `session_end` removal, default-guard, resurrection tombstone, sentinel seed, key-resolution precedence, two-parallel-session distinct keys).
- **Live on Windows 11** (after `install-local`, daemon restarted): launched two Calculator instances, drove `2+1` and `5+6` from two declared sessions interleaved → **two distinct-coloured cursors gliding/pulsing in parallel** (confirmed by eye); results 3 and 11; `end_session` removed each cursor.

Advances #1777 (the Win/Linux half of the cursor session-scoping). Linux (`platform-linux/src/overlay.rs`) is still single-cursor — a natural follow-up using the same shared `cursor_overlay::{CursorKey, KeyedOverlayCommand, OverlayMsg}` types.

title: fix(cua-driver-rs): release installer unifies home on ~/.cua-driver + cleans up prior local install
body:
## Problem

Two related install bugs in the macOS/Linux **release** installer (`libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh` → `_install-rust.sh`):

1. **Two-homes collision (root cause).** The release installer still defaulted its package home to the legacy `~/.cua-driver-rs`, while the local installer (`_install-local-rust.sh`) and the runtime already use `~/.cua-driver` (renamed in v0.2.16 / PR #1644 — this script was missed in that rename). So the release install wrote to one home and install-local + the runtime used the other.

2. **No cleanup of a prior local install.** When a user ran `install-local` and then ran the release `install.sh`, the release path did **not** clean up the pre-existing local install, leaving two conflicting installs (the local build's `*-local-*` release dirs and its `.tcc-signing-identity` marker dangling).

## Fix (`_install-rust.sh`)

- **Unify the home:** default `HOME_DIR` to `~/.cua-driver` (still honoring the `CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME` override for back-compat), matching install-local + the runtime.
- **Clean up a prior install-local build** before staging the new release: `cleanup_prior_local_install()` stops the daemon (reusing the shared `stop_cua_driver_daemons` helper), then removes the `*-local-*` release dirs and the `~/.cua-driver/.tcc-signing-identity` marker. Marker-gated and conservative — it never touches a real release dir, the `current` symlink, or unrelated user state; best-effort + idempotent (a clean machine is a no-op).
- **Sweep a stale `~/.cua-driver-rs`** left by an older release, after the new install is fully staged — mirroring the belt-and-braces legacy-home sweep `_install-local-rust.sh` already does.
- **TCC preserved:** `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` is replaced in place by the existing release `ditto` (grants key on the shared `com.trycua.driver` bundle id). No `tccutil reset`, so cert-pinned grants are not gratuitously churned.

`install.ps1` (Windows) already defaults to `~/.cua-driver` and migrates the legacy home (`$LegacyHomeDir` sweep) — **verified unchanged**.

## Why conservative

- Only `*-local-*` dirs (the unambiguous `install-local` signature — `VERSION_TAG="0.0.0-local-<config>"`) and the local-only signing-identity marker are removed.
- The `current` symlink is owned by the release branch, which re-creates it immediately after; a transient dangling link is harmless.
- The legacy-home sweep runs **after** staging, so we never delete state before the replacement exists, and is skipped if the user pinned `CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME` to the legacy path.

## Docs

- Reconciled `~/.cua-driver-rs` → `~/.cua-driver` home references across `installation.mdx` and `linux.mdx` (install paths, env-var table default, doctor/lockfile/version-check examples, uninstall table).
- Documented the local/legacy cleanup behavior in a new install callout.
- Added an `## Unreleased` changelog entry.

## Testing

- `bash -n` passes on `_install-rust.sh` and `install.sh`.
- Functional test in a sandboxed `$HOME`: a prior local build (`0.0.0-local-debug-*` dir + `.tcc-signing-identity` marker), a real release dir, an intact `current` symlink, and a stale `~/.cua-driver-rs`. After cleanup + sweep: local build dir removed, **real release dir preserved**, marker removed, `current` symlink intact, legacy home swept.
- No-op cases verified under bash (the script's interpreter): fresh machine and release-only reinstall both no-op (unmatched `*-local-*` glob expands to the literal and is filtered by `[[ -d ]]`); no daemon stop fires.
- `shellcheck` not available in this environment; verified array/glob handling is bash-3.2-safe and `set -u`-safe by hand.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): agent-cursor overlay stops rendering on a long-lived daemon
body:
## Summary

On Windows, the agent-cursor overlay **stops rendering on a long-lived `cua-driver` daemon**. After extended use (many cursor operations / sessions over time), cursors no longer paint on screen even though the daemon reports them as enabled and positioned. **Restarting the daemon reliably restores rendering.** A freshly started daemon renders cursors correctly *even while the stale daemon's overlay is still present*, which rules out z-order/DPI/screen-size as the cause and points at per-daemon overlay render-state degradation.

## Environment

- `cua-driver-rs` 0.4.3 (local `--release` build), Windows 11, single 2560×1440 display.
- Long-running `cua-driver serve` daemon driven over the HTTP/JSON-RPC transport.

## Symptoms

- Cursor visible early in the daemon's life; after a while it silently disappears and never comes back for that daemon.
- `get_agent_cursor_state` shows the session cursor with `enabled=true` and a valid `(x, y)` and color — i.e. the registry state looks correct.
- `move_cursor` returns success ("Agent cursor 'X' moved to (…)") but **nothing repaints**.
- The overlay window still exists and still spans the full virtual screen (`0,0 2560×1440`, `on_screen=true`), so it is not a stale-size / DPI-coverage problem.

## What rules things out

- **Not screen size / DPI:** overlay window bounds match the live virtual screen; a separate `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE` fix already keeps the overlay sized correctly.
- **Not z-order vs. app windows:** the overlay sits above the target windows (verified via z-index).
- **Not multi-overlay competition:** even with two other daemons' overlays present (two registered MCP servers each spawn a full-screen overlay), a *fresh* daemon's cursor renders fine — so the issue is internal to the degraded daemon.

## Suspected cause (needs investigation)

Something in the long-lived overlay's render path stops producing frames for the affected cursor. Candidates:
- The STA `WM_TIMER` render-loop thread wedging / stopping over time.
- `overlay::send_command`'s `try_send` dropping commands once the channel backs up (so `MoveTo`/`ClickPulse` never reach the render map) — would explain "move reports success but no repaint."
- A cursor that has idle-hidden (`idle_hide_ms`) failing to revive on a subsequent `MoveTo` (idle_alpha not restored), so it stays at alpha 0.

(Relevant: `platform-windows/src/overlay.rs` render thread + `apply_msg`/`send_command`; `cursor-overlay` `render_state` idle/fade logic.)

## Workarounds (current)

- Restart the daemon before a session — reliably restores rendering.
- Set `idle_hide_ms: 0` ("never hide") so cursors never fade.

## Repro sketch

1. Start `cua-driver serve` with the HTTP transport.
2. Drive many cursor operations / multiple sessions over an extended period.
3. Observe cursors eventually stop rendering; `get_agent_cursor_state` still reports them enabled/positioned; `move_cursor` succeeds but nothing shows.
4. Start a fresh daemon → cursors render again.

title: fix(platform-linux): focus-free GTK3 write + assert gtk in background-GUI test
body:
## Summary

Gives the **gtk (zenity / GTK3)** background-GUI matrix job a working, **focus-free WRITE** path and asserts it. gtk was the only GUI matrix entry left read-only (no typed-text assertion); this lands the write and proves focus never moves.

## Root cause

GTK3 accessibility goes through `libatk-bridge`, which reads the in-process accessibility flag — GSettings `org.gnome.desktop.interface toolkit-accessibility` (mirrored by `org.a11y.Status IsEnabled`) — essentially **once at startup**. In this hand-rolled headless session the runtime `dbus-send ... Set IsEnabled true` raced zenity's process start, so atk-bridge frequently **never registered** zenity's accessible tree. The driver's AT-SPI walk then found only the top window node (no `GtkEntry` child), so the existing GTK3 write fallback had nothing to target — hence gtk stayed read-only.

## What changed

**Test (`nix/cua-driver/tests/linux-background-gui.nix`)**
- **Pre-seed the GSettings keyfile** with `org.gnome.desktop.interface toolkit-accessibility=true` *before any app launches* (keyfile backend, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/cua-cfg`). This is the in-process flag atk-bridge actually consults at startup, so it is true the instant zenity starts — no dependence on a runtime D-Bus race. The existing `org.a11y.Status IsEnabled` set + read-back is kept.
- Add a short, deterministic settle after the zenity window maps (gtk only) for the bridge's async tree-registration handshake.
- Add `gtk` to the typed-text readback assertion list (now `["qt", "qt6", "gtk4", "gtk"]`), with comments. The existing **"Focus stayed on the control terminal"** assertion is unchanged and must still pass — proving the write is focus-free.

**Driver (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs`)**
- Make the GTK3 fallback genuinely **focus-free**. It previously XSendEvent-**clicked** the entry center to give it widget focus; under openbox a synthetic button press on a *background* window raises/activates it, which would move X focus off the control terminal and break the focus assertion. 
- New mechanism: AT-SPI `Component.GrabFocus` on the GtkEntry (**widget** focus only, no window activation) followed by XSendEvent typing — **no pointer click**, so the background window is never raised or activated. 
- Removed the now-unused `screen_to_window_coords` helper.

Run on macOS (the nixos VM tests only run on `x86_64-linux`, so the real gtk VM test runs in CI on this PR):
- `cargo check -p platform-linux --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` — clean, no new warnings (9 pre-existing warnings live in `mod.rs`/`overlay.rs`, untouched).

- `nix-instantiate --parse nix/cua-driver/tests/linux-background-gui.nix` — OK.
- The actual gtk nixos VM test cannot run locally; it executes in CI on this PR.

## Summary
Fixes the version desynchronization between `.bumpversion.cfg` (0.4.3) and workspace `Cargo.toml` (0.5.1) that was causing incorrect "new version available" warnings.

## Problem
Users reported that `cua-driver` always shows update notifications even after updating. Root cause: `.bumpversion.cfg` was 2 versions behind the actual codebase version.

1. `.bumpversion.cfg` thinks current version is 0.4.3

## Verification
All crates inherit version from workspace via `version.workspace = true`, so this single change restores proper version bump behavior.

Next bump workflow run will correctly tag from 0.5.1 → 0.5.2 (or 0.6.0/1.0.0 as appropriate).

title: fix(lume): verify pulled layers against their sha256 digest (#296)
body:
## Problem

Fixes #296 — `lume pull` for the `macos-sequoia` images stalls around 30–40% and then enters an endless "Retrying download" loop with failing sha256 checksums.

## Root cause

Two issues in `downloadLayer` (`libs/lume/src/ContainerRegistry/ImageContainerRegistry.swift`):

1. **No integrity check.** Downloaded blobs were never verified against their content-addressed digest, so corrupt/truncated bytes were silently accepted, **written to the layer cache**, and reused on every subsequent pull — which is what makes the failure persist across re-pulls and "loop".

2. **Transport compression on content-addressed blobs.** The request sent `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate`. OCI/Docker digests are computed over the exact stored bytes (already gzip/lz4-compressed), so when the CDN applied transport gzip, `URLSession` *transparently decompressed* the response before writing the file. The bytes on disk no longer matched the digest, and `expectedContentLength` became unreliable (chunked/`-1`), which is why progress appeared to freeze around 30%.

## Fix

- Request `Accept-Encoding: identity` so content-addressed blobs are never transparently decompressed.
- Stream-hash each downloaded layer (4 MiB chunks, so multi-GB disk layers aren't loaded into memory) and compare it to the expected `sha256:` digest **before** accepting it. On mismatch, delete the bad bytes (cache is never poisoned), route back through the existing bounded retry loop, and on persistent failure throw a clear, actionable `PullError.layerVerificationFailed` instead of producing a corrupt VM.
- Add a distinct log line for a real checksum mismatch so it's no longer indistinguishable from a generic network retry.

## Tests

- Added `tests/SHA256FileTests.swift` covering the streaming file-hash helper (known vectors, cross-chunk-boundary equivalence with the in-memory hash, and distinctness).
- `swift build` succeeds; the new tests pass:

```
✔ Suite SHA256FileTests passed after 0.033 seconds.
✔ Test run with 4 tests in 1 suite passed.
```

## Notes

This makes corruption (server-side or in-transit) **fail loudly and boundedly** rather than silently caching bad layers. If the registry blobs themselves are corrupt, users now get an explicit checksum error naming the expected vs. actual digest instead of an opaque infinite loop.

title: capture() returns 0x0 empty screenshots (width=0, height=0)
body:
# `capture()` returns 0x0 empty screenshots (width=0, height=0)

## Description

`cua-driver capture` returns PNG data with **width=0, height=0** — the screenshot is effectively empty. The AX accessibility tree and element detection work correctly, but the actual pixel data is missing.

This affects both `som` and `vision` capture modes.

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS 26.5 (25F71) — Apple Silicon (M4)
- **cua-driver version:** 0.2.0 (also reproduced on 0.5.1)
- **Binary:** Universal (x86_64 + arm64)
- **Install method:** GitHub release tarball

## Steps to Reproduce

```python
from tools.computer_use.cua_backend import CuaDriverBackend
import base64

backend = CuaDriverBackend()
backend._session.start()

for mode in ['som', 'vision']:
    result = backend.capture(mode=mode)
    print(f'Mode: {mode}')
    print(f'  Width: {result.width}, Height: {result.height}')
    print(f'  Elements: {len(result.elements) if result.elements else 0}')
    if result.png_b64:
        img = base64.b64decode(result.png_b64)
        print(f'  PNG size: {len(img)} bytes')
```

## Actual Output

```
Mode: som
  Width: 0, Height: 0
  App: BetterDisplay
  Elements: 31
  PNG size: 4127 bytes

Mode: vision
  Width: 0, Height: 0
  App: BetterDisplay
  Elements: 0
  PNG size: 4127 bytes
```

## Expected Output

Width and Height should match the actual screen resolution (e.g., 2560x1440 for a built-in display or external monitor). The PNG data should contain the actual screenshot pixels.

## Additional Context

- **AX tree works fine:** `list_windows` and element detection return valid data (31–119 elements depending on the active app).
- **osascript screencapture works:** Using `screencapture -x` via osascript produces a valid 2560x1440 PNG (~4MB), confirming the screen is accessible.
- **PNG data is small:** The returned PNG is only ~4KB, suggesting it contains a 1x1 or empty image rather than a full screenshot.
- **Multiple apps tested:** Issue persists regardless of which app is in the foreground.
- **cua-driver process is healthy:** Socket connection works, daemon starts without errors.

## Workaround

For screenshot-only use cases, `screencapture -x` via osascript works as a fallback. However, this doesn't integrate with cua-driver's SOM overlay or element indexing.

```bash
osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to do script "screencapture -x /tmp/screenshot.png; exit"'
```

---

**Possibly related:** The `capture()` call returns `CaptureResult` with valid `elements` and `app` fields, but `width=0, height=0`. This suggests the screen capture call itself is failing silently while the AX tree query succeeds.

## Summary

When `get_window_state` is called through the `cua-driver mcp` stdio server and forwarded to the `cua-driver serve` daemon over the Unix socket, the daemon proxy can fail with `os error 35` / `EAGAIN`:

```text
mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError: daemon transport error forwarding `get_window_state`:
Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)
```

The same `get_window_state` call succeeds when run in-process with `cua-driver call`, which makes quick CLI testing look healthy while MCP daemon usage fails.

## Environment

- OS: macOS Darwin 25.5.0, Apple Silicon / aarch64
- `cua-driver`: 0.5.1
- App: `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, Developer ID signed
- MCP path: downstream MCP client -> `cua-driver mcp` over stdio -> `cua-driver serve` daemon over `~/Library/Caches/cua-driver/cua-driver.sock`
- macOS permissions: Accessibility and Screen Recording granted for the driver app

## Behavior Observed

Two independent triggers reproduce the proxy failure:

1. Large `get_window_state` response
   - `capture_mode=som` can include a multi-MB base64 screenshot.
   - Smaller calls such as `list_windows`, `click`, and `type_text` forward successfully.

2. Slow accessibility traversal
   - Apple Notes produced a small response of roughly 35 KB, but `capture_mode=som` and `capture_mode=ax` still failed through the MCP -> daemon proxy.
   - `capture_mode=vision` succeeds on the same window, so this does not appear to be purely response-size related.

This looks like the proxy may be treating non-blocking socket `EAGAIN` as a fatal transport error instead of waiting for readiness and retrying. Client-side retry did not help: 5/5 repeated attempts failed. Restarting the daemon also did not help.

## Minimal Repro Shape

This succeeds in-process:

```bash
cua-driver call get_window_state '{"pid":<PID>,"window_id":<WID>,"capture_mode":"som"}'
```

The equivalent call through the MCP stdio server, where `cua-driver mcp` forwards to the daemon socket, fails on large responses or slow accessibility walks:

```text
McpError: daemon transport error forwarding `get_window_state`:
Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)
```

Apple Notes reproduces reliably in this environment. `capture_mode=vision` on the same window succeeds.

## Downstream Workarounds Tried

A downstream wrapper was patched locally to reduce impact:

- Use `screenshot_out_file` so screenshots are written to a temp PNG and the MCP response carries the smaller accessibility tree instead of a multi-MB base64 screenshot.
- Fall back to `capture_mode=vision` when `som` / `ax` fails with the daemon transport error.

This avoids hard failures for some workflows, but it does not fix the daemon proxy behavior.

## Related Upstream Questions

- Is `os error 35` / `EAGAIN` in the MCP -> daemon proxy known? Can the proxy wait for socket readiness or retry on `EAGAIN` instead of returning an MCP error?
- Is `screenshot_out_file` the recommended way to keep MCP payloads small? Is there a plan to default screenshots to files or chunk large responses?
- Apple Notes main window can produce an empty or unusable AX tree in this setup. Is that a known limitation, or is there an alternate traversal flag/path?
- For coordinate clicks on scaled HiDPI displays, what coordinate space should `x,y` use when `get_screen_size.scale_factor` reports `1.0` but screenshot scale appears higher? Could the coordinate click path accept `window_id` to disambiguate multi-window apps?
- Idle CPU for the driver process was observed around 52-54% in this setup. Is there a known mitigation or tracking issue?
- Please confirm whether the removed screenshot tool is intentionally replaced by `get_window_state(capture_mode=vision)`.

title: cuabot shell execution still loses exit status on current main
body:
## Summary

Current main still loses structured shell execution status for cuabot bash commands and still marks computer-server run_command() as successful even when the process exits non-zero.

This was previously addressed in stale PR #1404 for issue #1403, but that PR has not been merged for months and current upstream main no longer contains the fix.

## Current behavior on main

- libs/cuabot/src/cuabotd.ts returns only { stdout, stderr, pid? } from execInContainer().
- Failed docker exec calls are compressed into { stdout, stderr }, losing err.code, timeout, and signal metadata.
- libs/cuabot/src/cuabot.tsx exits cuabot --bash with 0 regardless of remote command status.
- libs/python/computer-server/computer_server/handlers/base.py returns success: True for run_command() even when process.returncode != 0.

## Expected behavior

Shell execution should return structured status with stdout, stderr, exit_code, success, timed_out, signal, and pid where applicable.

The local CLI should propagate non-zero remote exits and timeouts.

## Reproduction examples

- cuabot --bash "exit 42" should exit 42 or at least non-zero, but current main exits 0.
- cuabot --bash "sleep 65; echo after" should expose structured timeout metadata and exit non-zero.

## Proposed fix

I opened a fresh PR against current main with the minimal contract fix and regression tests. It supersedes stale PR #1404 while preserving the same intent from #1403.

title: Migrate NixOS integration tests from VMs to containers
body:
## Summary
This PR migrates the CUA driver integration tests from NixOS VM-based tests (using QEMU) to container-based tests (using systemd-nspawn). This change improves CI performance and reduces resource requirements while maintaining test coverage.

## Key Changes

- **Test Infrastructure Migration**: Converted all `pkgs.testers.nixosTest` configurations from `nodes.machine` (VM-based) to `containers.machine` (container-based)
  - Updated test files: `linux-background-gui.nix`, `integration.nix`, `screenshot.nix`, `linux-background-terminal-gif.nix`, `linux-cursor-click-gif.nix`, `set-config.nix`

- **Removed VM-Specific Configuration**: Eliminated `virtualisation` blocks that specified:
  - `cores = 2`
  - `memorySize` settings (2048 MB, 4096 MB, 6144 MB variants)
  - `diskSize = 8192`
  - These are no longer needed as containers run at native speed without QEMU emulation overhead

- **Removed Per-App Memory Overrides**: Deleted `memoryMB` parameter from `mkSkeleton` function and individual app configurations (electron-zettlr, electron-joplin, electron-logseq, chromium, tk) since containers don't require memory pre-allocation

- **Updated Documentation**: Changed references from "VM" to "container" throughout comments and docstrings to reflect the new test infrastructure

- **Updated Nixpkgs Pin**: Changed `flake.nix` nixpkgs input from `nixos-unstable` to `nixos-26.05` to ensure compatibility with container-based tests

- **CI Configuration**: Added required Nix experimental features to GitHub Actions workflows:
  - `auto-allocate-uids` and `cgroups` for systemd-nspawn UID/cgroup support
  - `extra-system-features = uid-range` to advertise UID range capability

- **Updated Comments**: Clarified Firefox test status and GTK3 app timeout issues, noting that container tests run at native speed and may resolve previous emulation-related timeouts

- **Migrated `set-config.nix` too**: the `cua-driver-set-config` regression check (#1923/#1928) only needs Xvfb + the driver over MCP stdio — no kernel modules, seat, or DRM — so it moves to a `containers.machine` the same way `integration.nix`/`screenshot.nix` did. It runs in the same `nix-checks` matrix that already advertises the `auto-allocate-uids`/`cgroups`/`uid-range` features, so no extra workflow change was needed.

### Tests intentionally kept on VMs

These cannot run under `systemd-nspawn` and remain `nodes.machine` by design — containers can't load kernel modules (`modprobe uinput` needs `CAP_SYS_MODULE`), expose `/dev/uinput`, allocate a logind seat/VT, or provide DRM:

- `linux-parallel-drag-gif.nix` and `linux-parallel-drag-xserver.nix` — real Xorg + `boot.kernelModules = [ "uinput" ]`; the xserver variant also needs a display-manager seat.
- `nix/cua-driver/tests/wayland/*` — `boot.kernelModules = [ "uinput" ]` + `hardware.graphics`/DRM for the headless compositors.

## Implementation Details

The migration leverages NixOS's native container support via systemd-nspawn, which provides:
- Faster test execution (no QEMU emulation)
- Lower resource consumption (no VM memory overhead)
- Simpler configuration (no virtualization parameters needed)
- Native-speed execution that may resolve previous timeout issues in emulated environments

title: Release cua-driver-rs-v0.5.2 contains stale binary (0.5.1 instead of 0.5.2)
body:
## Description

Release `cua-driver-rs-v0.5.2` Info.plist reports version `0.5.2` but the actual binary reports `0.5.1`:

```
$ ./CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver --version
cua-driver 0.5.1
```

The binary inside both tarballs (`cua-driver-rs-0.5.2-darwin-universal.tar.gz` and `cua-driver-rs-0.5.2-darwin-universal-binary.tar.gz`) has a build date of Jun 4 and SHA256 that does not match the checksums listed in the release:

**Expected (from release notes):**
```
45bfd3244c4943fb677c83250d8c4323d1c8d0b8ea55045a65bf584bba24cb21  cua-driver-rs-0.5.2-darwin-universal.tar.gz
```

**Actual:**
```
c7c79bb1738439411fa5c975348d18d55cf6e6661667f635f8f5b892b5c7dfae  cua-driver-rs-0.5.2-darwin-universal-binary.tar.gz
```

The SHA mismatch confirms the CDN is serving a cached Jun 4 build of the 0.5.1 binary.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Download either tarball from https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.5.2
2. Extract and run `./cua-driver --version`
3. Observe output: `cua-driver 0.5.1`

## Expected Behavior

Binary should report version `0.5.2` and match the published checksums.

## Environment

- macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel universal binary)
- Version from Info.plist: `0.5.2`
- Version from binary: `0.5.1`
- Binary build date: Jun 4 23:12 (pre-release date)

title: chore(packaging): add license metadata to Python distributions
body:
Fixes #1868

## Missing metadata evidence

Before this change, I built and inspected the wheel/sdist metadata for the Python packages under `libs/`.

- `cua-agent`, `cua-core`, `cua-computer`, `cua-mcp-server`, `cua-bench-ui`, and `cua-sandbox-apps` had no `License` metadata, no license classifier, and no LICENSE entry in the built archives.
- `cua-computer-server` had `License: MIT`, but no license classifier and no LICENSE entry in the built archives.
- `cua-auto`, `cua-cli`, `cua-sandbox`, and `cua-driver` had an MIT classifier but no LICENSE entry in wheel/sdist archives.
- `cua`, `cua-bench`, and `cua-som` already produced license file entries, so this PR leaves their existing license behavior intact.

I also checked for duplicates with:

```bash
gh pr list -R trycua/cua --state open --search "1868" --json number,title,state,headRefName,author,url,updatedAt
gh search prs --repo trycua/cua --state open "license metadata" --json number,title,state,url,author,updatedAt --limit 20
```

Both returned no open PRs.

## Changes

- Add MIT license metadata and MIT license classifiers to the affected Python package `pyproject.toml` files.
- Add package-local `LICENSE` files for the MIT-licensed Python distributions that did not include one.
- Add PDM `source-includes` entries where needed so sdists include the license file.
- Keep the change scoped to packaging metadata and license inclusion; no runtime code changes.

## Verification

I ran a metadata build inspection over these packages:

- `libs/python/agent`
- `libs/python/core`
- `libs/python/computer`
- `libs/python/computer-server`
- `libs/python/som`
- `libs/python/mcp-server`
- `libs/python/bench-ui`
- `libs/python/cua`
- `libs/python/cua-auto`
- `libs/python/cua-cli`
- `libs/python/cua-sandbox`
- `libs/python/cua-sandbox-apps`
- `libs/cua-driver/python`
- `libs/cua-bench`

Command pattern:

```bash
uv build --no-progress --color never --out-dir build/license-green <package-dir>
```

Then I inspected each wheel `METADATA` and each sdist `PKG-INFO` plus archive contents. Result:

```text
All checked distributions include license metadata and a LICENSE file entry.
```

Additional checks:

```bash
python - <<'PY'
import pathlib, tomllib
for path in sorted(pathlib.Path('.').glob('libs/**/pyproject.toml')) + [pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml')]:
    tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
print('parsed pyproject.toml files successfully')
PY

git diff --check
git diff --cached --check
```

Both diff checks exited 0, and all `pyproject.toml` files parsed successfully.

## Not run

I did not run runtime pytest/mypy suites because this PR only changes package metadata and LICENSE files, with no Python runtime source changes. The direct risk is package build metadata, covered by the wheel/sdist inspection above.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): PMv2 DPI manifest from #1821 is never applied - RT_MANIFEST embedded as string-typed resource
body:
## Summary

PR #1821 (v0.5.2) embeds a Per-Monitor V2 DPI manifest to fix pixel-click offsets under
display scaling. The manifest XML is in the binary, but not as a loadable resource:
`cua-driver.rc` declares the type as the identifier `RT_MANIFEST`, which the resource
compiler emits as a *custom string-named type*. The loader only applies manifests under
integer type `24`, ID `1` — so the daemon still starts **DPI-unaware** and the offset
bug #1821 targeted is presumably still present on the raw-injection paths.

## Evidence (installed 0.5.2, Windows 11 build 26200, 3840×2160 @ 125%)

- `GetProcessDpiAwareness` on the running `cua-driver.exe` → `0` (DPI_UNAWARE).
- `get_screen_size` → `3072x1728 points @ 1x` (virtualized; PMv2 would report 3840×2160 @ 1.25x).
- Resource enumeration shows one type: the string `"RT_MANIFEST"`. No integer type 24 / ID 1.
- Pixel clicks on UIA-exposed elements still land correctly (UIA hit-test + Invoke is
  coordinate-space agnostic), which masks the regression in everyday use.

## Root cause and fix

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/cua-driver.rc`:

```rc
1 RT_MANIFEST "cua-driver.manifest"   // RT_MANIFEST is not an .rc keyword
1 24 "cua-driver.manifest"            // fix: 24 = RT_MANIFEST
```

## Must fix together: capture paths double-scale once PMv2 is active

The same PR added `GetDpiForWindow / 96` scaling to capture paths in
`platform-windows/src/capture.rs`, premised on `GetWindowRect` / `GetSystemMetrics`
returning logical pixels under PMv2. Per Microsoft docs it's the opposite: PMv2 processes
get **physical** pixels (virtualization only applies to unaware/system-aware processes).
Today the code accidentally runs in the unaware regime it assumes; once the manifest
loads, three spots multiply physical coordinates by `DPI / 96` again:

1. `screenshot_via_screen_region` (~139–150): BitBlt source rect shifted/oversized by
   25% — wrong screen region for UWP / WinUI3 / DirectComposition targets.
2. `screenshot_window_bytes_with_occlusion_unsafe` (~288–303): buffer 25% too large;
   only masked while the unscaled `DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS` crop (~380–397) passes
   its bounds check.
3. `screenshot_display_bytes` (~478–489): same pattern via `GetDpiForSystem()`.

The click-side transform (`bitmap_to_screen` in `tools/impl_.rs`, no scaling) is correct
under PMv2 — fixing the manifest alone would break captures while clicks keep working.

## Verification (at 125% scaling)

- `get_screen_size` must report physical resolution @ 1.25x; `GetProcessDpiAwareness` → 2.
- With both fixes: capturing a UWP app (e.g. Calculator) positioned away from (0,0)
  must show the window, not a region shifted by ~25% of the window origin.

Side note: `--version` / `get_config` still report `0.5.1` on the 0.5.2 release.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): Windows zoom uses resized-image coordinates as native capture coordinates
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `zoom` documents `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, and `y2` as coordinates in the same pixel space as the screenshot returned by `get_window_state`. If `max_image_dimension` downscales that screenshot, callers therefore pass resized-image coordinates.

The implementation appears to apply those values directly to a fresh native-resolution screenshot. When downscaling is active, `zoom` crops the wrong region. The stored zoom context is then based on that wrong crop, so later `click(..., from_zoom=true)` calls are translated to the wrong window position.

## Reproduction

Tested locally on Windows with `cua-driver` reporting version `0.5.1` (but it is 0.5.2!).

1. Set `max_image_dimension` low enough to force downscaling, for example `400`.
2. Open a large window and call `get_window_state(..., capture_mode: vision)`.
3. Use a region from the returned downscaled screenshot, for example `x1=300, y1=0, x2=395, y2=70` on a 400 px wide screenshot.
4. Call `zoom` with that region.

In my repro, `get_window_state` returned a 400 px wide image while a native capture of the same window was 1981 px wide. The zoom for `x=300..395` should therefore have cropped roughly `x=1486..1956` in native pixels. Instead, the returned zoom image matched a native crop at `x=300..395`.

## Why this seems to happen

`get_window_state` records a resize ratio for the pid, and normal pixel clicks use it before converting screenshot coordinates to screen coordinates.

`ZoomTool::invoke` captures a new native-resolution screenshot and passes the caller's coordinates straight into the crop function:

```rust
let png = crate::capture::screenshot_window_bytes(hwnd)?;
cursor_overlay::capture_utils::crop_png_to_jpeg(&png, x1, y1, x2, y2, 500)
```

That means the documented resized-image coordinate space is skipped for `zoom`.

## Expected behavior

`zoom` should interpret `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, and `y2` in the screenshot coordinate space returned by the last `get_window_state` call, as documented.

A likely fix is to multiply the region coordinates by the stored resize ratio for the pid before cropping the native screenshot. The 500 px max-width validation should still apply to the caller-provided resized-image width.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): a single BuildUpdatedCache failure (0x80004005) returns elements=0 - no retry, no partial tree
body:
## Summary

When the UIA bulk cache build fails for a window, `get_window_state` returns an empty tree (`elements=0`) instead of a partial result. One misbehaving accessibility provider in the target app takes down the entire snapshot, which makes all `element_index`-based tools (click, type_text, ...) unusable for that window — the agent is forced to fall back to pixel clicks.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (build 26200), 125% display scaling
- cua-driver-rs 0.5.2 (also observed on 0.5.1)

## Symptom

```
window_id=2884078 pid=13116 elements=0
BuildUpdatedCache failed: Unbekannter Fehler (0x80004005)
```

The same `get_window_state` call returned 14 elements moments earlier. The failure surfaced while automating an app whose automation peers are replaced at runtime (a rich-text control that rebuilds its document tree on load). Any target with transient/unstable UIA providers can trigger it — the trigger isn't specific to one app. On 0.5.2 the error is rarer but still occurs (e.g. right after Ctrl+A in such a control).

## Where it happens

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/uia/mod.rs` — the tree walk does a single `BuildUpdatedCache(TreeScope_Subtree)` on the window root and hard-fails on any error:

```rust
let root_elem = match uncached.BuildUpdatedCache(&cache_req) {
    Ok(e) => e,
    Err(e) => return UiaTreeResult {
        tree_markdown: format!("BuildUpdatedCache failed: {e}"),
        nodes: Vec::new(),
    },
};
```

There is no retry and no fallback walk, so a transient `E_FAIL` from one provider yields a total outage for the whole window. (A similar resilience problem was already solved for SAL/VCL windows via the MSAA walker fallback — but that path is class-name-gated and doesn't help here.)

## Why it matters

`element_index` interaction is the most reliable mode the driver offers (works on background windows, exact hits). Losing the whole tree because one subtree is momentarily broken degrades the agent to pixel coordinates, which is precisely the mode with the weakest guarantees.

## Suggested improvements

1. **Retry with a short backoff** — the error is often transient (a second call right after frequently succeeds).
2. **Partial-tree fallback** — if the bulk Subtree cache build fails, fall back to a per-node walk (e.g. `ControlViewWalker` with per-element property reads), skipping nodes that error, and return `elements=N` with a warning instead of `elements=0`.
3. **Better diagnostics** — include which stage failed (root cache build vs. a specific child) so callers can tell a dead provider from a transient hiccup.

## Reproduction

The failure needs a UIA provider that errors mid-walk, which is timing-dependent in real apps. Two practical options:

1. **Real-world shape:** any control that swaps out its automation subtree while the snapshot is taken — e.g. a rich-text editor that rebuilds its document model on load, or a virtualized list re-realizing items. Call `get_window_state` repeatedly while the subtree is being replaced.
2. **Deterministic harness:** a small test app hosting a custom `IRawElementProviderFragment` that returns `E_FAIL` from one child's property fetch reproduces the total outage deterministically — and would double as a regression test for the partial-tree fallback.

title: fix: extend daemon proxy read timeout
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1864.

This PR fixes the MCP -> daemon proxy timeout described in the issue. It does not make `get_window_state` smaller or bypass AX traversal; it makes the daemon transport wait long enough for legitimate tool execution and return a clearer transport timeout if the daemon still does not respond.

## Issue Behavior Addressed

The issue reports that this path can fail:

```text
MCP client -> cua-driver mcp stdio server -> cua-driver serve daemon over Unix socket -> get_window_state
```

The same `get_window_state` operation can look healthy through `cua-driver call`, while the MCP proxy path fails with:

```text
Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)
```

The root cause fixed here is the proxy client read timeout: `send_request` used a hardcoded 10-second socket read timeout. Slow but valid daemon calls, especially `get_window_state`, could exceed that transport timeout before the tool returned its own result or timeout. On macOS, that timed-out socket read appears as `WouldBlock` / `EAGAIN` / os error 35.

## What Changed

- Replaced the inline daemon socket timeout with named daemon write/read timeout constants.
- Raised the daemon read timeout from 10 seconds to 60 seconds.
- Kept the write timeout short at 5 seconds.
- Mapped `WouldBlock` / `TimedOut` while reading the daemon response into a clear error:

```text
daemon timed out waiting for response after 60s
```

The 60-second transport budget is intentionally above the macOS `get_window_state` AX walk timeout of 30 seconds, leaving room for screenshot capture, resizing/encoding or `screenshot_out_file`, and JSON response serialization.

This PR intentionally does not blindly retry on `EAGAIN`. In this code path, `EAGAIN` is the socket read timeout firing, not a transient readiness event from a nonblocking socket loop. Retrying would hide the timeout policy instead of fixing the proxy deadline.

## Relation To The Issue's Upstream Questions

Resolved by this PR:

- `os error 35` / `EAGAIN` in the MCP -> daemon proxy no longer leaks as the primary failure for slow-but-valid daemon responses below the transport budget.
- The proxy now waits longer than the old 10-second transport timeout and longer than the macOS `get_window_state` AX timeout.
- If the daemon still does not respond inside the transport budget, the user gets a daemon timeout message instead of raw macOS `EAGAIN`.

Not changed by this PR and still follow-up scope:

- Whether `screenshot_out_file` should be the recommended long-term payload-size strategy.
- Whether large screenshot payloads should default to files or be chunked.
- Whether Apple Notes empty/unusable AX trees are a known platform limitation or need an alternate traversal path.
- Coordinate click semantics on HiDPI displays, including whether coordinate click should accept `window_id` for multi-window disambiguation.
- Idle CPU around 52-54% in the driver process.
- Whether the removed `screenshot` tool is intentionally replaced by `get_window_state(capture_mode=vision)`.

`screenshot_out_file` remains useful as an optional payload-size mitigation, but it is not the primary fix for this bug. The transport timeout/backpressure behavior is the bug addressed here.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p cua-driver daemon_response_read_tests`
- `git diff --check`
- local `install-local.sh` rebuild and CuaDriver daemon restart
- forced MCP proxy reproduction with a fake daemon delaying `get_window_state` for 12 seconds; the call succeeds instead of failing at the old ~10-second transport timeout

title: fix(computer-server): serve MCP at both /mcp and /mcp/
body:
## Problem

The MCP app is mounted at `/mcp` with its internal route at `/`, and the outer FastAPI app sets `redirect_slashes=False`. Starlette's `Mount` only matches `/mcp/...`, so a bare `POST /mcp` resolves to inner path `""` → 404, with no 307 rescue. Most MCP clients (claude.ai connectors included) POST to the bare path — for them the MCP server is unreachable even though `/status` advertises the `mcp` feature and the StreamableHTTP session manager is running.

Observed live on a Windows KubeVirt guest running `cua-computer-server`: `POST /mcp` → `404 {"detail":"Not Found"}` while `POST /mcp/` → `200` + `Mcp-Session-Id` from the same process.

## Fix

A small pure-ASGI middleware rewrites bare `/mcp` → `/mcp/` before routing, so both literal forms answer directly:

- **rewrite, not redirect** — POSTed initialize bodies and SSE streams survive; some MCP clients don't follow 307s on POST
- **plain ASGI, not `BaseHTTPMiddleware`** — no response buffering on the MCP event stream
- all other paths pass through untouched

Includes standalone unit tests for the shim (no server deps needed, following the existing skip-on-missing-import style).

title: cua-driver 0.5.3 missing com.apple.security.device.screen-capture entitlement on macOS 15
body:
## Problem

cua-driver 0.5.3 vision capture returns 0x0 screenshots on macOS 15 Sequoia despite:
- Binary being properly signed with Developer ID (Cua AI, Inc.)
- TCC Screen Recording permission granted
- ScreenCaptureKit code path existing in the binary

## Root Cause

The binary is signed with a Developer ID but **lacks the `com.apple.security.device.screen-capture` entitlement**. On macOS 15, ScreenCaptureKit requires both:
1. A valid Developer ID signature (✅ present)
2. The `com.apple.security.device.screen-capture` entitlement (❌ missing)

Without the entitlement, `SCStream::start_capture` fails with "Missing entitlements" even though TCC is granted.

## Verification

```
$ codesign -d --entitlements - /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver
# No entitlements output
```

## Fix

Add `com.apple.security.device.screen-capture` to the entitlements in the build/release pipeline.

## Impact

All macOS 15 users cannot use vision capture mode. SOM/AX tree works but screenshots are 0x0.

## References

- Related: #1862 (0x0 screenshots)

title: fix(computer-server): tolerate any Accept header on /mcp (claude.ai connector)
body:
## Problem

claude.ai's MCP connector fails to connect to the computer-server's `/mcp`
endpoint with `Your account was authorized, but ... returned an error when
connecting`. Hitting `/mcp` returns:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"server-error","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Not Acceptable: Client must accept both application/json and text/event-stream"}}
```

The MCP Python SDK's StreamableHTTP transport rejects a request unless its
`Accept` header advertises **both** `application/json` and `text/event-stream`
(POST path), or `text/event-stream` (GET SSE path). Some MCP clients (incl.
claude.ai's connector) don't send both, so the handshake POST is rejected
before reaching any tool. supergateway-fronted servers (e.g. cua-driver) are
lenient here and work; the FastMCP-native computer-server does not.

This is distinct from the bare-`/mcp` 404 fixed in #1887 — that fix is intact.

## Fix

Add `McpAcceptHeaderShim`, a pure-ASGI middleware scoped to `/mcp` that
normalizes the inbound `Accept` header to `application/json, text/event-stream`.
It rewrites only the **request** header — it does not set `json_response` or
touch any response semantics, so SSE-vs-JSON negotiation and existing clients
(Claude Code, SDK) are unaffected. Mounted inside the existing
`McpBarePathRewrite` (kept intact); middleware ordering documented in-code.

`json_response=True` was deliberately *not* used: it only relaxes the POST path
(the GET SSE path still hard-requires `text/event-stream`) and would change
response framing for other clients.

## Tests

- `tests/test_server.py::TestMcpAcceptHeaderShim` — normalizes json-only Accept
  on `/mcp`, `/mcp/`, `/mcp/...`; adds a missing Accept; leaves non-mcp paths
  (`/status`, `/`, `/mcpx`, `/ws`) untouched.
- Verified by in-process integration test against the real FastMCP/MCP SDK
  (fastmcp 2.14.x): json-only `Accept` POST `initialize` returns `406 / -32600`
  **without** the shim and `200 + mcp-session-id` **with** it, on both `/mcp`
  and `/mcp/`.
