title: feat(cua-driver): add experimental MCP OAuth front door
body:
## What changed

Adds an experimental `cua-driver mcp-oauth` subcommand that serves as an OAuth/DCR front door for an existing local MCP HTTP endpoint.

The new entry point:
- exposes OAuth protected-resource and authorization-server discovery metadata
- supports Dynamic Client Registration, authorization code + PKCE, and token exchange
- stores OAuth clients/codes/tokens in a local JSON store with atomic writes
- validates Bearer tokens and binds token audience/resource to `<public-url>/mcp`
- forwards authenticated `/mcp` requests to a loopback-only upstream such as `http://127.0.0.1:7677/mcp`
- preserves streaming proxy behavior for non-`tools/list` responses
- returns a connector-friendly `tools/list` descriptor view while leaving `tools/call` and other MCP JSON-RPC methods untouched

This does not change the existing `cua-driver mcp`, `serve`, or `mcp_http` behavior.

## Why

Some OAuth-only MCP clients require OAuth discovery and Dynamic Client Registration before they will call an MCP endpoint. This keeps that compatibility layer opt-in and isolated from the existing local stdio/HTTP MCP transports.

## Safety notes

- `--public-url` must be HTTPS.
- `--mcp-upstream` is restricted to loopback HTTP hosts.
- The proxy forwards only selected MCP request headers to the upstream and strips the front-door Bearer token.
- Clients should be configured with the full MCP endpoint, e.g. `https://your-tunnel.example/mcp`.

## Testing

- `cargo check --offline -p cua-driver`
- `cargo test --offline -p cua-driver mcp_oauth -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test --offline -p cua-driver parse_positive_u64_accepts_positive_and_rejects_zero_or_invalid -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test --offline -p cua-driver manifest_has_documented_top_level_shape -- --nocapture`
- `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check crates/cua-driver/src/mcp_oauth.rs`
- `git diff --check`

Manual acceptance:
- Started local MCP upstream on `127.0.0.1:7677`.
- Exposed `mcp-oauth` through a Tailscale HTTPS URL.
- Connected ChatGPT web to the `/mcp` URL.

title: test-harness: cross-toolkit control parity + macOS/Windows driver fixes
body:
## Summary

Brings the cross-platform test harnesses to **control parity with the WPF baseline** so the same 8-action matrix (click, double-click, right-click, drag, scroll, set_value, type, press-key) over 6 controls is exercisable on every surface, plus a set of **driver fixes** the per-action verifier surfaced.

`shared/scenarios.json` + `shared/web/index.html` are the single source of truth; each toolkit's harness was extended to match.

## Driver fixes

- **macOS `set_value` writes a CFNumber for numeric `AXValue` controls** (NSSlider/NSStepper reject a CFString write — `-25200`/`-25201`); falls back to CFString for text fields. *Verified live on an AppKit NSSlider: `slider_value` 0 → 50.*
- **macOS `set_value` steps `AXIncrement`/`AXDecrement` when `AXValue` is unsettable** (SwiftUI's `AXSlider` exposes a readable-but-unsettable value plus increment/decrement actions). Bounded loop (cap 500), stops within half the observed step, breaks if a step doesn't move the value. *Compile-verified; runtime verification pending a daemon reinstall.*
- **Windows off-screen click guard** (`point_in_window_bounds`): refuses a coordinate click that resolves outside its window (previously misfired onto the taskbar at the 556px reflow), applied to the coordinate-delivery paths only so background UIA Invoke still opens off-screen modals.
- **WinUI3 dispatch finding documented**: the WPF-style synthetic-input arm does not fix WinUI3 double/right-click and regresses the no-foreground contract — recorded in `dispatch.rs` rather than shipped.

## Harness parity

- **GTK3, WinUI3, shared web (WebView2/Electron/WKWebView), macOS AppKit + SwiftUI** extended with the full control set (checkbox, click-target L/R/double, slider, scroll-target, text-input, context-menu).
- New **WKWebView** macOS harness (Apple-WebKit analogue of WebView2) + macOS build script.
- New **Electron** build glue (Linux + macOS) reusing the shared web DOM.

## Findings (per-action verifier)

`modality-recordings/FINDINGS.md` documents what actually lands per surface and whether the no-foreground contract holds — including the headline that Windows Electron/Chromium self-foregrounds (contract violated) while macOS WKWebView and Linux Electron hold it, and the synthetic-input limits (GTK ignores XSendEvent; nested web overflow-divs don't scroll via keystrokes).

## Verification status (honest)

- macOS CFNumber set_value fix: **verified live** (AppKit slider).
- macOS increment/decrement fallback: **compile-verified**, runtime pending reinstall.
- Windows off-screen guard, harness parity, recordings: verified on the respective VMs/host; frame-checked.
- No user-facing MCP tool / installation / API surface changed, so no `/docs` update is required.

title: feat(examples): add Router Learning System — self-improving task routing with multi-tier fallback for Cua agents
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a Router Learning System as a reference example for building production-grade computer-use agents with Cua Driver.

## Problem

Current Cua examples show single-tool usage, but real agents need to gracefully handle failures. When CDP is unavailable, an agent should fall back to Cua pixel automation. When that fails, it should try Vision AI. Current examples don't address this escalation pattern.

## Solution

A compact (~700 lines), self-contained task routing engine with:

- Dynamic path sorting — reorders tiers by historical success_rate / execution_time
- Self-learning — SQLite-backed history that improves after 5+ samples
- Consecutive failure skip — skips paths with 3+ failures
- 10 pre-configured tasks — git_commit, git_push, browser_navigate, browser_fill_input, browser_click_button, app_hotkey, app_type, app_click, app_screenshot, create_github_token

## Why This Matters for Cua

Computer-use agents are entering production. The key challenge is orchestration — which tool to use, what to do when it fails, how to get smarter over time. This router demonstrates the architectural pattern we use at scale, battle-tested across 100+ real desktop automation sessions.

## Files Changed

- examples/router-learning-system/router.py — Main routing engine
- examples/router-learning-system/README.md — Usage documentation

## Testing

python3 examples/router-learning-system/router.py stats
python3 examples/router-learning-system/router.py git_commit

title: Test infra: add NixOS-based desktop base images for cua-driver testing
body:
## Context

cua-driver's Linux desktop validation currently runs against **Ubuntu-based** desktop containers on Azure Container Instances:

- `trycua/cua-xfce` — Ubuntu 22.04 + XFCE + TigerVNC/noVNC
- `trycua/cua-ubuntu` (Kasm) — Ubuntu 22.04 + XFCE + KasmVNC
- `linuxserver/webtop:ubuntu-kde` — Ubuntu + KDE Plasma (KasmVNC)
- GNOME (in progress)

These all share a Debian/Ubuntu filesystem layout (FHS paths, apt, `/run/user/<uid>/bus`, standard systemd/dbus session wiring). That means our coverage is biased toward one distro family.

## Ask

We need **NixOS-based desktop base image(s)** for testing, so cua-driver is exercised against NixOS's non-FHS layout and different session/dbus/AT-SPI wiring. Notably relevant to recent work:

- **Session-bus discovery** (`platform-linux/src/session_bus.rs`) currently scans `/run/user/<uid>/bus` and session-process `/proc/<pid>/environ` — NixOS lays out the user bus and session leaders differently; worth confirming the discovery still lands.
- **`XAUTHORITY` / X server discovery**, the AT-SPI bus launcher path (`/usr/libexec/at-spi-bus-launcher` doesn't exist on NixOS), and binary/library resolution all differ on NixOS.
- The install path (`install-local` / prebuilt binary) and any hardcoded FHS assumptions.

## Suggested scope

- A NixOS desktop image (X11; XFCE or GNOME) reachable over VNC/web for the same modality-matrix + recording harness we use for the Ubuntu lanes (see `libs/cua-driver/test-harness/linux-container/`).
- Bonus: a Wayland NixOS variant once the X11 one is green.

cc @r33drichards

title: Computer-use support for the macOS iPhone Mirroring app (AX vs pixel)
body:
## Context

External report on X from **Bora Turan (@_boraturan)**, 2026-06-29, directed at @francedot:

> "@NousResearch hermes computer-use doesn't seem to drive iPhone ui via iPhone Mirroring app on Mac, but Codex computer-use does it well, @francedot any views on this?"

Observation: agent/model results differ a lot when driving the **iPhone Mirroring** app UI on macOS — Hermes (Nous) struggles, Codex does it well.

## Why this likely happens / what to investigate

- **How does cua-driver surface the iPhone Mirroring window today?** The mirrored iPhone UI is remote-rendered by the iPhone Mirroring app, so its contents are almost certainly **not exposed as a macOS AX tree** — `get_window_state` would see an opaque surface with no actionable elements (likely `degraded`/empty), forcing agents onto **pixel/vision** input.
- If that's the case, it explains the model gap: a stronger vision-grounding model (Codex) can localize and click from screenshots, while a weaker one (Hermes) flails without an accessibility tree to anchor to.

## Action

- Test cua-driver against the iPhone Mirroring app on macOS: capture whether AX is available at all, what `get_window_state` returns, and confirm pixel-click delivery lands on the mirrored surface.
- Document the supported modality (expect: vision/pixel only) and add agent-facing guidance.
- Decide whether anything on the driver side can improve it (e.g. better pixel-click targeting / cursor visibility on that surface).

cc @ddupont808

title: fix(cua-driver/windows): reject stale element-cache snapshots
body:
## What changed

This adds a freshness guard to the Windows UIA/MSAA element cache so cached element centers and rects are no longer reused after the target window moves or resizes.

Instead of silently dispatching a click with stale screen coordinates, click-family tools now fail fast with a stale snapshot error and ask the caller to rerun `get_window_state`.

## Related issue

Fixes #1984

## Approach

- Store the top-level window rect alongside each cached Windows element snapshot.
- Treat cached centers/rects as stale when the current `GetWindowRect` no longer matches the captured rect.
- Surface a specific stale-snapshot error from `click`, `double_click`, and `right_click` instead of the old generic cache-miss message.
- Add regression tests for both center and rect lookups when the window rect changes.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p platform-windows`

## Notes

This is the smaller fail-fast variant discussed in #1984. It does not try to auto-refresh the snapshot or hook window-move events yet.

title: Linux: list_windows does not populate app_name or is_on_screen fields

## Description

On Linux (X11, Artix Linux), `list_windows` returns window entries that are missing the `app_name` and `is_on_screen` fields. This breaks Hermes Agent ability to filter windows by application name and correctly identify on-screen windows.

## Actual response from cua-driver 0.6.8

```json
{"windows":[
  {"height":688, "pid":11381, "title":"~", "window_id":23068686, "x":12, "y":40},
  {"height":1056,"pid":840, "title":"hermes ~", "window_id":20971534, "x":1378,"y":12},
  {"height":688, "pid":10454, "title":"YouTube Music \u2014 LibreWolf", "window_id":14680067, "x":12, "y":40}
]}
```

Each entry is missing `app_name` and `is_on_screen`. On macOS these fields are populated correctly.

## Expected

Each window entry should include:
- `app_name`: the application name (e.g. "LibreWolf", "kitty")
- `is_on_screen`: boolean

## Impact

Without `app_name`, consumers cannot filter windows by application, making `capture(app="SomeApp")` return "no on-screen window matched".

- OS: Artix Linux (X11, i3 WM)
- Display: :0

title: cua-driver: unify the windowless desktop-scope knob (per-call `scope` vs `capture_scope` config)
body:
Follow-up from #2077 (cross-platform tool-schema consistency).

### Problem
All three platforms support **windowless screen-absolute (desktop-scope) clicks/scrolls**, but they expose the opt-in differently:

- **macOS** — a **per-call** `scope:"desktop"` parameter on the pointer tools (`click`, etc.).
- **Windows & Linux** — gated on the **persisted** `capture_scope:"desktop"` config (`set_config capture_scope=desktop`); there is no per-call `scope` param.

So a per-call `scope` param appears only on macOS, and the same capability is reached via different mechanisms elsewhere. This is a real cross-platform inconsistency in how the knob is surfaced (the capability itself exists everywhere).

### Proposal
Pick one canonical surface and apply it on all three platforms — most likely **promote `scope` to a per-call param everywhere** (add it to the Windows/Linux pointer tools and have it override/short-circuit the `capture_scope` config for that call), since a per-call frame is more predictable than a sticky global setting. Then add `scope` to the shared `cua-driver-core::tool_schema` canon so the consistency gate enforces it.

### References
- macOS per-call `scope`: `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs` (schema enum `["window","desktop"]`)
- Windows/Linux config gate: `crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs` (`is_windowless_desktop_action`, `capture_scope`), `crates/platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`
- Gate: `crates/cua-driver-core/src/tool_schema.rs`, `crates/cua-driver/tests/schema_consistency_test.rs`

title: cua-driver: expose `delivery_mode` on macOS `press_key`/`hotkey` for parity with Windows
body:
Follow-up from #2077 (cross-platform tool-schema consistency).

### Problem
`delivery_mode` (`background`/`foreground`) is now uniform across the **pointer** family on all platforms, but for the **keyboard** tools it is asymmetric:

- **Windows** exposes `delivery_mode` on `press_key` and `hotkey`.
- **macOS** does **not** — macOS routes key dispatch through a different mechanism (the NSMenu / `with_menu_shortcut_activation` activation path), so `press_key`/`hotkey` there don't take a `delivery_mode` param.

A cross-platform client that sends `delivery_mode` to `press_key`/`hotkey` works on Windows but is schema-rejected on macOS.

### Proposal
Add `delivery_mode` to macOS `press_key`/`hotkey` schemas (via `cua_driver_core::tool_schema::delivery_mode_schema()`) and map `foreground` onto the existing `with_menu_shortcut_activation` / `with_foreground_assist` activation path that the NSMenu key route already uses, so the param is honored rather than accepted-and-ignored. Then the keyboard family matches the pointer family's uniform `delivery_mode` surface.

### References
- macOS key activation path: `crates/platform-macos/src/input/skylight.rs` (`with_menu_shortcut_activation`, `with_foreground_assist`), `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/hotkey.rs`, `press_key.rs`
- Windows `delivery_mode` on keys: `crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`
- Fragment: `crates/cua-driver-core/src/tool_schema.rs::delivery_mode_schema`

title: cua-driver: wire `session` cursor glide on Windows `scroll` (schema-accepted but not glided)
body:
Follow-up from #2077 (cross-platform tool-schema consistency).

### Problem
After #2077, `session` is accepted on every Windows action/cursor tool (it was previously rejected via `additionalProperties:false`). On most tools the Windows invoke already calls `resolve_cursor_key` and glides the per-session agent cursor. **`scroll` is the exception**: the Windows `scroll` invoke does not call `resolve_cursor_key` at all, so it has no overlay glide.

Net: a `session` passed to Windows `scroll` is now *accepted* (no longer rejected), but the agent cursor does not move/pulse for that scroll the way it does on the other Windows tools and on macOS `scroll`.

### Proposal
Thread `session` through the Windows `scroll` invoke the same way the other Windows pointer tools do — resolve the cursor key and drive the overlay glide/pulse to the scroll point — so the per-session cursor behavior is consistent.

### References
- Windows `scroll` invoke: `crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`
- Reference (already-wired) pattern: Windows `click`/`double_click` `resolve_cursor_key` + overlay usage in the same file; macOS `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/scroll.rs`

Flagged by the implementation agent during #2077 as the one Windows tool where `session` is schema-only rather than fully cursor-wired.

title: cua-driver: AX setValue/type_text false-confirms on Electron (read-back echoes the written attribute)
body:
Surfaced by a live session (Codex.app, an Electron app) and related to the modality-ladder audit. Companion to the structured-`value` fix in #2077 (commit 03168580).

### Problem
`type_text` via `element_index` (and `set_value`) on an Electron AXTextArea returns `effect:"confirmed"` / `verified:true` while the field is actually **still empty**.

Root cause: the AX rung's read-back **reads back the same `AXValue` attribute it just wrote**. On Electron the `AXValue` attribute is settable but disconnected from the React/DOM input, so:
1. We `AXUIElementSetAttributeValue(AXValue, "hey there")` → succeeds, sets the AX attribute.
2. We read `AXValue` back → returns `"hey there"` (the attribute we just set).
3. `verify_typed` sees the text present → reports `verified:true` / `effect:"confirmed"`.
4. …but the visible web input never received it.

So the "post-condition" is tautological — it confirms the *write* took, not that the *UI changed*. This is the residual the audit flags as fundamentally driver-unverifiable for the AX rung on disconnected-AX surfaces, and here it produces an actively misleading `confirmed`.

Observed inversion: on this app the real keystroke rung (`key_events`, no element_index) returned only `unverifiable` + an escalation hint, yet that's the path that actually worked — opposite of the AX verdict.

### Possible directions (none trivial)
- Detect the echo case: if `after == exactly what we wrote` AND nothing else in the field changed (e.g. caret/selection/length deltas unchanged), downgrade `confirmed` → `unverifiable` rather than asserting success.
- On Chromium/Electron targets (already detectable — see the degraded/Chromium heuristics), distrust AX setValue read-back and prefer the keystroke rung up front.
- Cross-check against a second signal (e.g. the structured `value` now emitted by #2077, read from a fresh snapshot rather than the just-written handle).

### References
- `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs` (`verify_typed`, `is_silent_accept`)
- `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/set_value.rs`
- Related: structured `value` field added in #2077 (03168580); modality-ladder audit `CUA_DRIVER_MODALITY_LADDER_AUDIT.md`

title: cua-driver: type_text drops keystrokes in RDP clients (Windows App) — needs scancode-based background typing
body:
## Summary

`type_text` currently relies on Unicode-based CGEvent keystroke synthesis. This works for most macOS-native and Electron/Catalyst apps, but fails silently against RDP clients (tested with Microsoft's "Windows App" / Remote Desktop client) because the RDP client's input handling is scancode-based, not Unicode-based.

## Repro

1. Launch an RDP session to a Windows host via the macOS "Windows App" client.
2. Open the Windows Start menu / search box (via a backgrounded pixel click — this part works fine).
3. Call `type_text({pid, window_id, x, y, text: "bing"})` (or the element-indexed form) targeting the search field.
4. Re-snapshot: the search field still shows placeholder text. Nothing was typed, and the call returns `verified:false` with no clear signal that the text was dropped.

## What actually works (validated live)

Two things had to change together:

1. **Real foreground activation, not the `delivery_mode:"foreground"` flash-and-restore.** The existing foreground rung fronts the window, acts, and immediately restores the prior frontmost — that's too fast for the RDP client to register real keyboard focus before the keystroke lands. A genuine `activate` (e.g. `osascript -e 'tell application "Windows App" to activate'`) that leaves the window frontmost long enough was required.
2. **Per-character `press_key` instead of `type_text`.** Once the window was genuinely focused, sending each character as its own `press_key` call landed correctly. The batched Unicode path `type_text` uses does not.

## Ask

Add scancode-based / per-character keystroke delivery as a rung `type_text` can escalate to automatically when it detects an RDP-style client (or more generally, a surface where Unicode CGEvent synthesis is dropped), instead of requiring the caller to manually fall back to a loop of `press_key` calls plus a real (non-flash) foreground activation. Ideally this stays backgroundable — right now the only known working path requires genuinely stealing foreground focus, which breaks the no-foreground contract cua-driver otherwise guarantees for every other surface.

Environment: macOS "Windows App" (Microsoft Remote Desktop successor) connected to an Azure Windows VM. Likely affects any RDP/VNC-style client where keyboard input is scancode-driven rather than IME/Unicode-driven.

title: cua-driver: port insert_text / type_keystrokes CDP typing to Windows and Linux
body:
## Context

The \`page\` tool's \`insert_text\` and \`type_keystrokes\` actions (CDP-native typing for rich-text contenteditable editors that discard one-shot \`execCommand\`/\`innerText =\` writes) currently only work on macOS. On Windows and Linux, \`PageBackend::insert_text\`/\`type_keystrokes\` fall through to the default trait implementation and return a clean "not implemented" error — confirmed via live testing on both platforms (no crash/hang, shared dispatch code unaffected).

## What exists today

- **macOS** (\`crates/platform-macos/src/browser/cdp_client.rs\`): full implementation —
  - \`Input.insertText\` (single call) and \`Input.dispatchKeyEvent\` (per-character keyDown/char/keyUp) rungs
  - \`CdpSessionCache\`: reuses one open CDP connection per port across calls instead of reconnecting every time
  - Browser-endpoint fallback (\`ws://host:port/devtools/browser\` + \`Target.getTargets\`/\`Target.attachToTarget{flatten:true}\`) for CDP ports that don't serve the classic \`/json\` HTTP discovery — needed for Chrome's \`chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging\` toggle on a user's real/default profile
  - \`target_url_contains\` param to disambiguate which tab to act on in a multi-tab browser
  - Automatic CDP-port discovery from a pid via \`lsof\`

- **Windows/Linux** (\`crates/cua-driver-core/src/cdp.rs\`, shared): only implements \`Runtime.evaluate\`, used solely by \`execute_javascript\`. No \`Input\` domain support, no session reuse (reconnects fresh every call — see "Why this matters" below), no browser-endpoint/\`Target.attachToTarget\` fallback, and CDP port discovery is a manual \`CUA_DRIVER_CDP_PORT\` env var rather than automatic pid→port lookup.

## Scope of work

1. Add \`Input.insertText\` and \`Input.dispatchKeyEvent\` support to the shared \`cua-driver-core/src/cdp.rs\` client (or a Windows/Linux-specific extension of it).
2. Port the session-reuse pattern (\`CdpSessionCache\` equivalent) — **this isn't optional polish**: reconnecting fresh on every call means re-triggering Chrome's live "Allow remote debugging?" confirmation popup on every single action when driving a user's real profile via the \`chrome://inspect\` toggle path. Confirmed live on macOS: naive reconnect-per-call got prompted 3-for-3; caching one connection across calls got prompted once, then silent for repeated calls into the same session.
3. Add the browser-endpoint (\`Target.getTargets\`/\`attachToTarget\`) fallback for CDP ports that don't serve \`/json\` — needed for the same real-profile-toggle scenario on Windows/Linux browsers, if applicable there.
4. Add \`target_url_contains\`-style tab disambiguation for multi-tab browsers.
5. Consider automatic CDP-port discovery from a pid (Windows: enumerate the process's TCP endpoints, e.g. via \`GetExtendedTcpTable\`; Linux: \`/proc/<pid>/net/tcp\` or similar) to match macOS's \`lsof\`-based \`find_port_for_pid\`, instead of requiring the \`CUA_DRIVER_CDP_PORT\` env var.
6. Wire the above into \`WindowsPageBackend\`/\`LinuxPageBackend\`'s \`insert_text\`/\`type_keystrokes\` trait methods, update \`crates/platform-*/src/tools/page.rs\`.
7. Update docs (\`docs/content/docs/how-to-guides/driver/drive-a-web-page.mdx\`, \`docs/content/docs/reference/cua-driver/mcp-tools.mdx\`) once implemented — they currently correctly scope this as macOS-only.

## Reference

macOS implementation: \`crates/platform-macos/src/browser/cdp_client.rs\`, \`crates/platform-macos/src/tools/page.rs\`. Skill doc with the full escalation-ladder rationale: \`Skills/cua-driver/WEB_APPS.md\` (search "insert_text" / "type_keystrokes" / "CdpSessionCache").

title: Linux launch_app should return structured PID for direct executable launches
body:
## Summary

On Linux, `launch_app` direct executable launches expose the child PID only in the human text response. macOS and Windows expose launch identity through MCP `structuredContent`, so typed clients can read `pid` without parsing prose.

## Minimal reproduction

On Linux, start the CUA driver MCP server and call `launch_app` with a direct executable:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "launch_app",
    "arguments": { "name": "sleep 30" }
  }
}
```

Before the fix, the response text included the PID, for example:

```text
Launched 'sleep 30' with pid 12345.
```

but `result.structuredContent` did not include that PID.

## Expected

For direct executable launches, Linux should return structured launch identity, matching the shape macOS and Windows already expose:

```json
{
  "pid": 12345,
  "bundle_id": null,
  "name": "sleep 30",
  "running": true,
  "active": false,
  "windows": []
}
```

`windows` can be empty immediately after launch, especially for commands without UI.

## Why this matters

Typed MCP clients should not need to parse a PID out of prose. In our downstream CUA driver integration probes, Linux app launch normalized to `pid=null` even though the child process had launched, because the transport intentionally reads `structuredContent` rather than human text.

title: cua-driver: drive Windows apps from an agent running in WSL (Hermes/WSL → Windows daemon)
body:
## Use case

A user runs **Hermes inside WSL (Linux)** and wants to drive **Windows 11 GUI apps** from there. They'd prefer to keep the agent in WSL and have it reach a driver on the Windows side (a daemon on Windows that the WSL agent connects to), rather than installing the whole agent stack on Windows.

## What happens today

Running `cua-driver` *inside WSL* runs the Linux build against a headless Linux environment with no Windows desktop, so it can't see or drive Windows apps. On older builds this surfaced in Hermes as a cryptic crash:

```
capture failed: int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a real number, not 'NoneType'
```

That's a null screen size (no usable display in WSL) reaching Hermes' Python wrapper. #2006 already replaced it with a typed "no usable display" error on WSL/WSLg, so 0.7.0 fails clearly instead of crashing — but it still doesn't let the user actually drive Windows.

## Why the SSH path doesn't cover this

We already support driving a Windows session from a *remote* shell: run `cua-driver serve` in the interactive session (Session 1+) via an autostart Scheduled Task, and `cua-driver mcp` detects that daemon and proxies over its **named pipe** (see the "Drive a Windows app over SSH" how-to). That path assumes the agent runs a *Windows* `cua-driver.exe`. In the WSL case the agent runs a *Linux* binary that can't open the Windows named pipe.

## The path that should work (to validate)

WSL2 interop lets a Linux process exec a Windows `.exe` with stdio bridged across the boundary. So the intended architecture mirrors the SSH story, with interop instead of SSH:

1. Install cua-driver on **Windows**, start the `cua-driver serve` daemon in the interactive session (Session 1+, autostart Scheduled Task).
2. The WSL agent spawns the **Windows** `cua-driver.exe mcp` (via interop, e.g. `cua-driver.exe` on PATH or `/mnt/c/.../cua-driver.exe`), not the Linux binary. That Windows process connects to the Session-1 daemon's named pipe locally and drives the apps; MCP stdio crosses the WSL↔Windows boundary through interop pipes.

## What's needed

**cua-driver**
- [ ] Validate that `cua-driver.exe mcp` launched from WSL interop connects to the Session-1 named-pipe daemon and drives Windows apps end to end (session detection, named pipe, stdio over interop).
- [ ] Make the WSL "no usable display" error actionable: point the user at the Windows `.exe` path instead of leaving them stuck ("You're in WSL — to drive Windows apps, run the Windows cua-driver.exe against a Session 1+ daemon; see <docs>").
- [ ] Decide whether the Linux binary, when it detects WSL (`is_wsl()` already exists), should auto-hand off to the Windows `.exe` or just guide.

**Hermes** (cross-repo, `tools/computer_use/cua_backend.py`)
- [ ] Teach the backend to launch the Windows `cua-driver.exe` (via interop) when running under WSL and targeting Windows, rather than the in-WSL Linux binary. A config toggle or a WSL+`.exe`-present auto-detect.

**Docs**
- [ ] A "Drive Windows apps from WSL" how-to, parallel to the SSH one: install on Windows, start the Session-1 daemon, point the WSL agent at `cua-driver.exe`.

## Alternative

If interop-stdio proves insufficient, add a **TCP transport** for the daemon (WSL2 can reach the Windows host over TCP), so the Linux `cua-driver mcp` can connect to a Windows daemon directly.

## Acceptance

- A Hermes run inside WSL can `list_windows` and drive Windows 11 GUI apps through a Windows-side cua-driver daemon.
- The WSL null-screen-size crash is gone (done via #2006) and replaced with a clear route to the working setup.
- The WSL→Windows setup is documented.

_Filed from a user report (Hermes on WSL, wants to control Windows 11). Related: #2006 (typed WSL error), the "Drive a Windows app over SSH" how-to (named-pipe daemon), and the Hermes 0.7.0 integration audit._

title: feat(cua-driver): embedded mode — inherit the host app's TCC grants, never prompt
body:
Adds an explicit **embedded mode** to cua-driver-rs so a host macOS app (an agent harness) can run the driver as a child process and have it inherit the host's Accessibility + Screen Recording grants — one permission prompt total, one entry in System Settings, no `com.trycua.driver` dialogs. Activated via `CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1` or `cua-driver mcp --embedded [--host-bundle-id <id>]`.

## Why

Standalone cua-driver deliberately makes itself its own TCC *responsible process* (disclaim re-exec + `open -a CuaDriver` relaunch) so grants attach to a stable bundle identity. That's right for standalone, wrong for embedding: a harness that already holds both grants ships a second app identity and its users hit a second set of permission prompts. macOS attributes TCC to the responsible process, so a directly-spawned child inherits the host's grants *for free* — the driver just has to stop opting out.

## What changed

**Behavior (~25 lines, all gated on the flag; standalone is unchanged when it's off):**
- `responsibility.rs` — skip the disclaim re-exec (stay in the host's chain). Decision factored into a pure `should_skip_disclaim()` seam for testability.
- `cli.rs` `should_use_daemon_proxy` — never auto-relaunch via the `CuaDriver.app` bundle (both platform branches; an embedded driver answers in-process).
- Permissions gate (`gate.rs`) — embedded mode opts out; the driver never raises its own prompts or panel.
- `check_permissions` — `prompt:true` is ignored (this + the gate are the only two `request_*` call sites, so prompts are unreachable), and `permission_source()` reports `attribution: "host"` with the advisory host bundle id and a `disclaim_env` debug field. The live `SCShareableContent` capture probe is untouched.

**Docs + example:**
- `Skills/cua-driver/EMBEDDING.md` — integration guide: TCC responsibility model, launch contract, standalone-vs-embedded table, `check_permissions` attribution semantics, copy-paste host example, troubleshooting (second prompt / black screenshot / empty AX / re-sign), Windows/Linux notes. Ships in the skill pack, so it links by repo path, not relative links.
- `examples/embedded-host-macos/` — `ExampleAgentHarness.swift`, a 122-line no-UI reference host mirrored **verbatim** in the guide (grants → embedded spawn → attribution check → background screenshot → background AX read → agent-cursor glide), plus a self-verifying `demo.sh` (build + sign + `tccutil reset` + tail-until-`DEMO COMPLETE: PASS`).
- `--embedded` / `--host-bundle-id` added to `--help`, `manifest`, and `dump-docs`; `cli-reference.mdx` regenerated via `scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver.ts` (no hand edits to generated docs).

## Security notes

- **The env var is caller-controlled, and that is safe by construction**: embedded mode only ever *removes* capability claims (suppresses prompting, downgrades attribution to `host`). It never feeds the `driver-daemon` attribution decision, which stays keyed on the non-spoofable bundle-path signal. New tests pin this, including embedded + disclaim env set together never yielding `driver-daemon`.
- Only the exact value `1` enables the mode (fail-safe); `--host-bundle-id` is an advisory label, not a trust signal — trust comes from the OS responsibility chain.
- The host must spawn the driver directly (`Process`/`posix_spawn`); launching via `open(1)`/`NSWorkspace` breaks inheritance. Documented, with the TCC `AttributionChain` log-stream command for debugging.

## Testing

- 20/20 unit tests pass (release profile): gate opt-out incl. exact-value rule, host attribution, fail-closed spoofing cases, disclaim truth table. Env-mutating tests across `gate` and `check_permissions` now share one crate-wide lock (they race under separate per-module mutexes).
- Example host + the guide's copy-paste block both compile with `swiftc`; verified byte-identical to each other.
- **End-to-end one-grant demo verified on a real Mac** (macOS Darwin 25.5, TCC reset via `tccutil`): host granted once, embedded driver started with zero driver-side prompts, `check_permissions` reported `attribution: host` with the live capture probe true, background Finder AX tree + window screenshot returned, agent-cursor overlay glided, `DEMO COMPLETE: PASS`. Settings listed only the harness — no CuaDriver entry. Still not CI-able (needs interactive grants).
- The manual run surfaced and fixed real issues: macOS 26 only registers an app in the Screen Recording pane after an actual ScreenCaptureKit attempt (the embedded driver's live probe is that attempt, attributed to the host — so the demo registers both rows in one pass); ad-hoc re-signing orphans grant rows (demo.sh now reuses the built bundle and skips `tccutil reset` on re-runs); `get_window_state` needs `pid`+`window_id` via `launch_app`; stock macOS has no `timeout(1)`.

## Not in this PR

- Nothing further is needed for Windows/Linux (X11) embedding: those platforms have no per-app permission grants, so a directly-spawned driver child inherits everything by plain process inheritance, and the flag already keeps it in-process. Two documented exceptions remain out of scope: driving elevated/UWP windows from an embedded host on Windows (embedded mode does not route through the uiAccess `cua-driver-uia` worker — the host must manage it), and Wayland capture (XDG portals prompt per-session and cannot be pre-granted; X11 is the supported path).
- CI automation of the TCC demo (requires interactive grant).

title: install.ps1: Add-Type fails on Windows with non-ASCII system locale (zh-CN, ja-JP, etc.) — csc.exe can't find temp .cs file
body:
## Summary

`install.ps1` fails to complete on Windows systems with a non-ASCII system locale (e.g. `zh-CN`, codepage 936/GBK). The `Add-Type` call that compiles the `Win32` P/Invoke helper (junction resolution) fails with `CS2001: Source file not found`, causing the installer to abort before it can refresh/upgrade cua-driver.

This makes `hermes update` (which calls `install.ps1` for the cua-driver refresh) fail every time on such systems, even when cua-driver is already on the latest version.

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10, system locale `zh-CN` (ACP = GB2312 / codepage 936)
- **PowerShell**: 5.1.26100.8655 (Desktop edition, CLR 4.0.30319.42000)
- **csc.exe**: v4.8.9221.0 at `C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe`
- **cua-driver**: 0.7.0 (already installed, latest at time of writing)

## Reproduction

Run the installer on a `zh-CN` Windows system:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1 | iex"
```

Output (error messages localized, translated here):

```
==> cua-driver-rs installer (Windows)
==>   install dir : ...\AppData\Local\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin
==>   package home: ...\.cua-driver
==>   target      : x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
==> using baked release: cua-driver-rs-v0.7.0
==> release 0.7.0 is already on disk (skipping download)
Add-Type : (0) : Cannot find source file 'C:\Windows\TEMP\xxxxxxxx.0.cs'
(1) : using System;
At line:463 char:5
+     Add-Type -TypeDefinition $source -Language CSharp
+     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    + CategoryInfo : InvalidData: (AddTypeCompilerError) [Add-Type], Exception
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : SOURCE_CODE_ERROR
```

Even a minimal `Add-Type` reproduces the failure:

```powershell
PS> Add-Type -TypeDefinition 'public class TestClass { }' -Language CSharp
Add-Type : (0) : Cannot find source file 'C:\Windows\TEMP\cxj5ga5u.0.cs'
```

## Root cause

This is a **known PowerShell 5.1 bug** on systems where the ANSI code page is not ASCII (codepage 936/GBK, 932/Shift-JIS, 949/EUC-KR, etc.):

1. `Add-Type` writes the C# source to a temp `.cs` file via `CodeDomProvider`.
2. It then invokes `csc.exe` with the temp file path as an argument.
3. On non-ASCII codepage systems, the path encoding gets mangled when passed to `csc.exe` — `csc.exe` receives a garbled path and reports `CS2001: Source file not found`.

`csc.exe` itself works fine when invoked directly with an explicit `/codepage` parameter or when the source file path is pure ASCII. The bug is in PowerShell's `Add-Type` wrapper, not in csc.exe.

Reference: [MicrosoftDocs/PowerShell-Docs#7684](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/PowerShell-Docs/issues/7684) and various reports of `Add-Type` failing on Chinese/Japanese/Korean Windows.

## Impact

- `install.ps1` cannot complete on `zh-CN` (and likely `ja-JP`, `ko-KR`) Windows systems.
- Downstream tools that call `install.ps1` for upgrades/refreshes (e.g. `hermes update`) report a spurious failure every time, even though cua-driver is already installed and up to date.
- The `check-update --json` command also hits GitHub API rate limits (unauthenticated, 60 req/hour per IP), which causes callers to fall back to `install.ps1` — compounding the problem.

## Suggested fixes

Any of these would resolve the issue:

1. **Replace `Add-Type` with a pre-compiled assembly** or a different junction-resolution method that doesn't require runtime C# compilation (e.g. `cmd /c mklink /J`, or calling `CreateSymbolicLink` via `DllImport` through a different mechanism).
2. **Use `pwsh` (PowerShell 7+) if available** — it doesn't use `csc.exe` for `Add-Type` and isn't affected.
3. **Pass `/codepage:65001` (UTF-8) to csc.exe** via `CodeDomProvider` compiler parameters, or set `PYTHONUTF8=1` equivalent for PowerShell.
4. **Detect the failure and fall back gracefully** — if `Add-Type` fails, skip junction creation and use `cmd /c mklink /J` directly.
5. **Support `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `check-update`** so authenticated requests (5000/hour) are used instead of unauthenticated (60/hour), reducing the need to fall back to `install.ps1` for version checks.

## Workaround

For anyone hitting this: cua-driver is likely already installed and working. The `Add-Type` failure only affects the junction/refresh path in the installer. The binary itself at `...\Cua\cua-driver\bin\cua-driver.exe` continues to work normally.

title: fix(agent): recognize cua_sandbox Localhost as a computer
body:
## Summary

Closes #1897

Passing a `cua_sandbox` `Localhost` to an agent as a tool fails with `Warning: Unknown tool type: Localhost()`, even though `Localhost.connect()` is documented as a no-VM alternative to `Sandbox`. The agent's tool resolution (`is_agent_computer` / `make_computer_handler` in `cua_agent/computers/__init__.py`) only recognizes `Computer`, `Sandbox`, `AsyncComputerHandler` and dicts, so a `Localhost` instance falls through to the "unknown tool" branch and is never wired up.

`Localhost` exposes the same interface as `Sandbox` (this is already relied on inside `cua_sandbox`, whose `LocalhostHandler` subclasses `SandboxHandler` and just swaps the object), so this recognizes it the same way and reuses `SandboxComputerHandler`.

## Changes

`libs/python/agent/cua_agent/computers/__init__.py`:

- import `Localhost` from `cua_sandbox` in a `try/except`, mirroring the existing optional `Sandbox` import (stays `None` when `cua_sandbox` is not installed, so nothing changes for installs without it)
- `is_agent_computer` returns `True` for a `Localhost`
- `make_computer_handler` builds a `SandboxComputerHandler` for a `Localhost`, matching how `Sandbox` is handled

## Tests

`libs/python/agent/tests/test_localhost_resolution.py`:

- `is_agent_computer` returns `False` for an object before it is a known type and `True` once `Localhost` is recognized
- `make_computer_handler` wraps a `Localhost` in a `SandboxComputerHandler` around the same instance

Both pass; the existing `tests/test_tool_resolution.py` suite still passes unchanged. Fail-before / pass-after verified (removing the new `make_computer_handler` branch fails the handler test).

title: fix(cua-driver/linux): surface native Wayland windows in list_windows on GNOME/KDE (#1978)
body:
## Summary
`list_windows` returned no real application windows on GNOME/Mutter (and KDE/KWin) — only XWayland infrastructure. Native Wayland apps were invisible (#1978). This surfaces them via the AT-SPI registry.

## Root cause
`list_windows_dispatch` gates the native-Wayland enumeration on `is_wayland()`, which requires `DISPLAY` unset. GNOME/KDE always run XWayland → `DISPLAY` set → `is_wayland()` false → it goes straight to X11 enumeration, which only sees XWayland apps. Native Wayland apps have no X11 XID, so they never appear.

## Change
On an opted-in Wayland session (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1` + `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`), merge the AT-SPI registry (keyed by pid — the same tree `get_window_state` walks) into the X11 results:
- X11 entries keep priority (real XID + geometry).
- AT-SPI adds windows for pids X11 didn't report (native Wayland apps that expose accessibility).

No change on pure-wlroots sessions (the existing `is_wayland()` path) or non-opted-in sessions.

## Validation (Ubuntu 26.04, Mutter, Wayland)
- **Before:** `list_windows` returns only `mutter guard window`, `GNOME Shell`, `mutter-x11-frames`, `ibus-*` — no real apps.
- **After:** a native `gnome-text-editor` (no X11 XID) appears with its pid + title (`New Document (Draft) - Text Editor`), alongside the XWayland windows.

## Limitations
Only apps that expose an AT-SPI accessibility tree are enumerable this way (the same constraint as `get_window_state`). AT-SPI windows carry a stable synthetic xid + pid but no geometry (x/y/size are 0), consistent with the existing AT-SPI fallback used on wlroots. Full native-Wayland geometry needs a compositor-side helper (out of scope).

## Refs
Part of the #1922 native-Wayland follow-ups. Complements #2112 (input) — you can now both enumerate and drive native Wayland apps on GNOME/KDE.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved window listing on Wayland by combining information from multiple sources when available.
  * Reduced missing or duplicate windows in mixed Wayland/X11 sessions by merging results more intelligently.

title: Fix cross-platform CUA driver GUI verification
body:
## Summary

This PR hardens the CUA driver GUI verification path across Windows, macOS, and Linux. It fixes cases where platform GUI tests skipped the real assertion path, could not address native controls exposed by app frameworks, relied on stale accessibility-tree assumptions, or depended on downloaded fixture apps that drifted away from repo-owned harnesses.

The latest Windows pass also addresses partner-reported 0.7.1 findings around background keyboard false-success reporting, Chrome/background click refusal diagnostics, packaged Notepad launch verification, and the RDP-backed runner needed for real cursor/focus assertions.

## What This Fixes

### Windows interactive desktop detection and RDP guard runner

- Keeps Windows Session 0 as a clear non-interactive runner signal for SSH and service-launched processes.
- Replaces the named `OpenWindowStationW("WinSta0")` probe with the process's attached window station, active input desktop, thread desktop, and foreground HWND diagnostics.
- Distinguishes a locked/non-Default desktop from an unlocked idle `Default` desktop that simply has no foreground window yet.
- Lets GUI tests seed the foreground with `focus-monitor-win` when the desktop is otherwise valid.
- Adds `CUA_REQUIRE_GUI=1` so dedicated GUI runners fail closed instead of skip-passing when the desktop is unsuitable.
- Updates Windows `doctor` output with the same desktop-state summary.

### Windows guard UX and launch behavior

- Reorders guard tests so the target harness launches first, then `focus-monitor-win` becomes the measured foreground sentinel.
- Adds stronger cleanup for leftover focus monitor, Electron harness, and driver processes.
- Makes the cursor pixel assertion deterministic by using an explicit cursor id and motion settings.
- Updates the repo-local Electron harness to show main and child windows inactive, allowing launch/background assertions without stealing focus.
- Adds a shared web child-window control so background click can assert a real window-open side effect.
- Verifies `launch_app({"name":"Notepad","start_minimized":true})` resolves packaged Notepad through its AUMID and returns usable pid/window metadata on the Azure Windows RDP VM.

### Windows W1/W8 reporting hardening

- Changes background `type_text` on the unreadable PostMessage path from a checked success to “sent, not verified” with structured `verified:false`, `verify:"unreadable"`, and foreground escalation guidance.
- Changes background `press_key` PostMessage success to the same unverified reporting shape, so callers no longer see a confirmed keypress when the driver cannot prove it landed.
- Preserves coordinate-injection failure causes for click, double-click, and right-click instead of collapsing them into a generic class-level `background_unavailable` message.
- Adds structured refusal codes for `background_occluded`, `background_uipi_blocked`, and generic `background_unavailable`.
- Adds unit/guard coverage for these reporting contracts.

### Windows WPF and WinUI3 harness coverage

- Updates UIA walking so enabled actionable elements can be indexed even when the framework reports them as offscreen.
- Adds a narrow fallback for WPF menu items that are visible and enabled but do not expose the expected cached action pattern.
- Restores the WPF scroll test to the background `WM_VSCROLL` path and narrows the silent-drop guard so scroll messages are not rejected with pointer click/move cases.
- Uses explicit foreground delivery where WPF text input requires it.
- Reorders the WinUI3 fixture so radio, flyout, popup, and related controls are discoverable before the long scroll region dominates the UIA walk.

### Shared Electron and Tauri harnesses

- Removes the old macOS pytest Electron fixture that downloaded a prebuilt `.app` release zip.
- Adds a repo-local Tauri harness under `libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures/apps/cross-platform/tauri` that embeds the shared web DOM.
- Adds the Windows Tauri ICO asset required by `tauri-build` so the harness builds on both macOS and Windows.
- Builds Electron and Tauri from repo-local source and stages deterministic `harness-electron` / `harness-tauri` outputs for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
- Updates Windows guard/modality tests and sandbox staging to use the repo-local harness executables instead of downloaded desktop-test-app binaries.
- Removes the tracked downloaded Tauri macOS binary from the Python fixture assets.

### macOS harness and capture verification

- Updates macOS GUI harness tests to use the daemon proxy path where needed.
- Covers the capture and desktop-scope paths that require local GUI permissions and daemon-backed execution.
- Includes build/runtime adjustments for the Swift-linked driver pieces so local test and install flows can find the required runtime consistently.

### Linux harness and accessibility behavior

- Updates Linux GUI verification around AT-SPI, capture, input, overlay, and Wayland/X11 support paths exercised by the ignored GUI suites.
- Fixes the GTK popover test assumption: GTK/AT-SPI can expose the popover content in the tree before it is shown, so the test now asserts an explicit `popover_open=False` to `popover_open=True` state transition.
- Keeps the headless GUI test flow compatible with Xvfb, DBus, AT-SPI, and a lightweight window manager.

### Test organization and contributor docs

- Removes the legacy Python e2e suite so Rust integration tests are the source of truth for driver behavioral coverage.
- Rehomes repo-local fixture apps and build helpers from `libs/cua-driver/test-harness` to `libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures`, giving Rust harness tests one neutral fixture root.
- Keeps generated staged apps under ignored `libs/cua-driver/rust/test-apps` and keeps Electron/Tauri build products out of the PR.
- Moves the legacy Windows Sandbox runner out of `libs/cua-driver/rust/sandbox` into `libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/windows-sandbox` and marks it as a non-canonical smoke runner.
- Adds a canonical Rust-only Windows runner at `libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/windows/run-all.ps1` for repo-local fixture suites; optional external-app suites are excluded.
- Ports TextEdit launch-focus coverage into ignored Rust macOS coverage in `modality_launch_focus_macos_test.rs`, and marks LibreOffice as optional explicit-run coverage.
- Adds focused contributor READMEs for the Rust workspace, Rust test matrix, scripts, and fixture app/build folders.
- Adds a small Fumadocs contributor page at `reference/cua-driver/development` that points to repo-local READMEs instead of duplicating implementation detail.
- Removes an uncertain checked-in macOS smoke result file and stale download-era ignore/docs entries.

### Testkit and verification workflow

- Adds small testkit helpers for reading structured tool responses and tree text in the platform harnesses.
- Makes guard-style tests report why they skipped when the runner is not interactive instead of failing with ambiguous platform API errors.
- Adds `libs/cua-driver/scripts/sync-vm-worktree.sh`, a generic helper for syncing the host checkout to verification machines and pulling artifacts back while keeping source commits host-owned.
- Makes touched Windows PowerShell scripts parse cleanly under Windows PowerShell 5.1, which can read UTF-8-without-BOM files as ANSI.

## Validation

- Local host checks passed:
  - `node --check libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures/apps/cross-platform/electron/main.js`
  - `cargo test --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p cua-driver --test modality_launch_focus_macos_test --no-run`
  - `cargo check --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p cua-driver --test guard_ux_test`
  - `cargo test --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p platform-windows input::delivery::tests::background_unavailable_with_cause_preserves_actuator_failure --no-run`
- Azure Windows VM compile passed: `cargo check -p platform-windows -p cua-driver --tests`.
- Azure Windows VM focused W8 unit passed: `cargo test -p platform-windows input::delivery::tests::background_unavailable_with_cause_preserves_actuator_failure -- --nocapture`.
- Azure Windows VM RDP/scheduled-task GUI run with `CUA_REQUIRE_GUI=1` passed: `cargo test -p cua-driver --test guard_ux_test -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`, 6/6 passed.
- Azure Windows VM packaged Notepad launch check passed via `cua-driver call launch_app`, returning the Notepad AUMID, pid, inactive state, and visible window metadata.
- Azure Windows VM PowerShell 5.1 parser check passed for the touched harness/sandbox scripts, including the moved `tests/runners/windows-sandbox` scripts and `tests/runners/windows/run-all.ps1`.
- Azure Windows VM full harness build passed and staged WPF, WinUI3, WebView2, Electron, and Tauri executables from repo-local sources.
- Azure Windows VM Rust no-run checks passed: `cargo test -p cua-driver --test guard_ux_test --no-run` and `cargo test -p cua-driver --test modality_input_e2e_test --no-run`.
- Windows WPF ignored harness suite passed, 18/18.
- Windows WinUI3 ignored harness suite passed, 7/7.
- Windows SSH/default pass: `cargo test -p cua-driver -p platform-windows -- --nocapture` passed; GUI-only assertions skip explicitly when run outside an interactive desktop.
- Linux default pass: `cargo test -p cua-driver -p platform-linux -- --nocapture` passed.
- Linux ignored GUI suites passed under Xvfb/DBus/AT-SPI for GTK3, capture mode, and desktop scope.
- macOS default and ignored GUI harness passes were verified locally with the daemon proxy path.
- Shared Electron/Tauri harness checks: `bash -n` for build scripts, `git diff --check`, staged-output ignore checks, and targeted sensitive/stale-reference scans passed.
- macOS aggregate harness build passed and staged AppKit, SwiftUI, WKWebView, `CuaTestHarness.Electron.app`, and `CuaTestHarness.Tauri.app` from repo-local sources.
- Tauri harness build passed directly and the staged app plist reports `CuaTestHarness.Tauri`, `com.trycua.harness.tauri`, and executable `CuaTestHarness.Tauri`.

## Latest Cross-Platform Behavioral Matrix

The Rust-owned `cross_platform_behavior_test` now exercises the same classes of
background/foreground, AX, and pixel workflows through repo-local Electron and
Tauri fixtures. Every action is checked against a fresh application-state
oracle; a successful driver response without a state change is a failure.

Latest validation after the driver fixes:

- Linux Electron under Xvfb, xfwm4, DBus, and AT-SPI: **5/5 passed**.
- Windows Electron + Tauri in the active RDP user session: **5/5 passed**.
- Windows guard UX in the active RDP user session: **6/6 passed**.
- Windows background modifier hotkeys: both fixture families now return honest structured refusal rather than a false success.
- macOS Electron + Tauri: AX calculator, background pixel calculator, keyboard, and child-window + foreground drag rows pass; the nested scroll row remains a strict known capability gap.

The underlying fixes include Linux AT-SPI element focus and directional scroll actions, Windows UIA element focus, focused-child key retargeting for WebView2/Tauri, UIA `ScrollPattern` delivery, and stricter Windows background hotkey capability reporting. The private machine journal is intentionally excluded from this PR.

## Notes

- The Windows GUI guard path now has a verified RDP/scheduled-task runner with a real foreground desktop; SSH/service runs still self-skip GUI-only assertions by design.
- Background keyboard delivery on partner GH-hosted Windows still needs environment comparison if their fixture continues to see dropped input. This PR prevents false confirmed success and gives structured escalation, but does not claim every GH-hosted keyboard target now accepts background PostMessage input.
- Background Chrome click refusals now preserve the concrete actuator cause. Restoring any 0.6.8-era apparent no-foreground Chrome click behavior under fully occluded GH-hosted conditions remains separate follow-up work.
- macOS background Chromium pixel click and foreground drag are now fixed in this branch using focus-without-raise plus an explicit active HID gesture. Nested non-focusable web scrolling remains separate follow-up work.
- This PR intentionally omits local verification journals and machine-specific details.

## Verification Update

- macOS local daemon, after `install-local.sh`: Electron and Tauri background pixel calculator **2/2 passed**.
- macOS local daemon, after `install-local.sh`: Electron and Tauri foreground drag/drop **2/2 passed**.
- macOS full Rust matrix: AX, pixel, keyboard, and drag rows pass for both fixtures; editor/save passes, while the nested `overflow:auto` scroll oracle remains at `scroll_offset=0`. A follow-up explicit foreground global-HID wheel experiment also remained unchanged, so this is documented as a renderer/scroll-surface capability gap rather than an assertion relaxation.
- The private cross-platform fix journal is maintained locally and is intentionally not staged or published.

## Verification Update: Linux AT-SPI and Background Keyboard

- Linux WebKitGTK AT-SPI traversal now preserves raw `(bus name, object path)` references for WebProcess descendants, while ordinary unique-name references retain the `atspi` P2P connection path used by Electron/Chromium.
- Linux default Rust matrix under Xvfb, xfwm4, DBus, and AT-SPI: **5/5 passed** with external application-state oracles.
- Linux unit suites: `cua-driver` **67/67** and `platform-linux` **48/48** passed; active protocol/schema checks also passed.
- Linux Chromium/Electron background hotkey behavior is now an explicit structured `background_unavailable` refusal when no EIS backend is available. The X11 probe showed that claiming success for an unfocused renderer was a silent no-op; foreground is the explicit escalation.
- Linux Tauri/WebKitGTK tree readiness is fixed and exposes the full web tree, but the optional strict Tauri input lane remains failing under headless Xvfb (0/5 external input-oracle rows). It is still opt-in via `CUA_INCLUDE_TAURI_LINUX=1` until a principled WebKitGTK input route is implemented.
- The VM sync helper now preserves platform-specific VM-built `rust/test-apps` artifacts during host-to-VM `rsync --delete` syncs.
- macOS was rebuilt with `install-local.sh`; TCC grants remained intact. The known nested web `overflow:auto` scroll gap remains strict and unchanged.
- The Linux interactive CI workflow now installs the Tauri/WebKitGTK build prerequisites required for the repo-local harness; the replacement workflow passed its build and Xvfb/AT-SPI modality job.## CI Architecture Foundation (2026-07-10)

- Adds OS-scoped Rust unit workflows: Linux runs the Linux platform set; Windows runs the Windows platform/UIA set. Shared Rust/testkit and fixture changes trigger both appropriate lanes.

- Adds strict fixture preflight for the canonical Rust matrix, preventing missing apps from becoming silent skips in CI or VM runs.

title: Support OpenAI GPT-5.5 built-in computer tool (`computer_call.actions[]`)
body:
Hi Cua team,

I’m evaluating Cua as the execution/runtime layer for a Linux computer-use demo, and I’d like to clarify the roadmap for OpenAI’s newer built-in computer tool flow.

From the public docs/blog posts and the current agent loop, it looks like Cua already covers two OpenAI-style paths:

1. The older preview path:
   - model: `gpt-5.5`
   - tool: `computer_use_preview`
   - `computer_call.action` with a single action
   - `computer_call_output` for screenshots

2. The newer-model function-call harness path, for example GPT-5.4 support:
   - Responses API
   - a custom `computer` function tool schema
   - model output handled as `function_call`

OpenAI’s current GA computer-use docs now describe a different built-in tool flow:

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "tools": [{ "type": "computer" }]
}
```

The response uses `computer_call`, with batched `actions[]`, rather than the old single `action` shape.

Do you have plans to support this GPT-5.5 built-in computer tool flow directly in `cua-agent`? In particular:

- selecting the OpenAI loop for `gpt-5.5` / `openai/gpt-5.5`
- sending `tools: [{ "type": "computer" }]` instead of the old `computer_use_preview` schema or a custom function tool
- handling `computer_call.actions[]`
- emitting the correct screenshot output shape expected by the new GA flow

This would make it much easier to use Cua with OpenAI-compatible Responses gateways that already support `gpt-5.5` and the new built-in computer tool, without relying on the deprecated preview protocol or a custom function-call harness.

Thanks!

title: test(cua-driver): converge Rust desktop E2E contracts
body:
## Why

The desktop suites mixed unit checks, shell-generated summaries, one-off guards, and GUI behavior tests. Missing cells could disappear, setup failures could produce reduced green runs, and a successful tool response could be mistaken for input delivery.

This PR makes the Rust harnesses the source of truth for desktop behavior. Repo-local applications expose observable state, and every action must prove either its external effect or an exact structured refusal. Background actions also prove that they did not steal focus, raise the target, move the real cursor, or leak input.

## Canonical test model

- Unit and protocol tests stay desktop-independent and video-free.
- Electron and Tauri share one 36-cell catalog per app. macOS also runs a native WKWebView host.
- Native harness owners use the same typed result and evidence contract.
- AX/PX targeting and foreground/background delivery are dimensions of each action.
- Focus, z-order, cursor, leaked-input, capture, and desktop-scope checks attach to the actions that need them.
- Contributors run `all`; CI partitions shared, native, and capture work only as internal jobs.

Each result records platform, display server, harness, action, targeting, delivery, scope, backend route, expected and observed behavior, independent oracles, duration, and evidence. The reporter rejects missing, duplicate, undeclared, contradictory, or evidence-less rows.

## Driver and harness fixes

### Evidence and reporting

- Added source, fixture, accessibility, capture, GUI-session, and playable-video preflights.
- Resolves one immutable source SHA per workflow and records it in every summary and environment record.
- Added a physically foreground, fully occluding sentinel for background actions.
- Requires an allowed structured refusal plus clean desktop-side-effect observations.
- Records a full-desktop MP4 for each canonical cell and before/after evidence for targeted actions.
- Added a compact coverage grid and artifact-linked row for each cell.
- Isolated process-global recording hook phases so parallel unit tests cannot consume another test's before/after capture.

### Linux

- Replaced X11 false-success paths with foreground XTest delivery, semantic background delivery where proven, and exact refusals elsewhere.
- Added generic `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` discovery, native wlroots capture and recording, stable window identity, compositor-aware geometry, and strict session preflights.
- Added GNOME WinRects geometry and activation plus persistent portal/libei input with revocable grants.
- Preserves 64-bit Wayland identities, resolves connection-local toplevel IDs by stable process and title data, and reconstructs renderer origins for targeted PX input.
- Packages `libxkbcommon`, portal/libei support, the nested compositor, and source-owned Rust tests through Nix.
- Restored the optional `cua-compositor` as a separate experimental environment with a versioned acknowledged protocol, PID targeting, exact resource errors, focus and z-order observation, scene geometry queries, direct pointer and keyboard routes, and typed evidence.
- Makes nested pointer hit-testing target-subtree-local so an occluding sentinel cannot intercept a background action. Renderer child surfaces reuse their bound pointer resource or fall back to the owning root.
- Keeps standard Wayland and the private nested route separate in result metadata and public documentation.

### Windows

- Restored occluded Electron AX/PX single-left clicks through the proven background-safe `PostMessage` route.
- Proved occluded Electron child-window delivery; unsupported Chromium gestures retain exact refusals.
- Corrected foreground PX activation and renderer keyboard targeting.
- Added canonical WPF and WebView2 PX background-left-click rows with fixture-owned state and desktop-side-effect oracles.
- Added WPF background combo selection and an exact WPF background-drag refusal.
- Made `start_minimized` fail closed before spawning when Windows cannot guarantee no activation.
- Reports minimized windows truthfully, filters them from `on_screen_only`, and restores them through the existing `bring_to_front` tool.

### macOS

- Restored PX background left-click delivery through AX hit-testing for Electron, Tauri, and AppKit without focus changes.
- Fixed the first-character loss in foreground PX typing.
- Converts silent background scroll and drag no-effects into exact `background_unavailable` refusals.
- Added the native WKWebView host to the complete shared catalog.
- Added AppKit scroll, right/double click, slider drag, and background-drag contracts.
- Added SwiftUI background AX click/value rows and foreground popover state verification.
- Fixed desktop-scope HID delivery, fixture stability, per-connection daemon sessions, and structured refusal propagation.
- Preserves the installed app's TCC identity during local installation.

## Cleanup

- Removed the synthetic calculator fixture and duplicate calculator tests.
- Removed old guard, modality, delivery, and legacy shared owners after mapping useful assertions into typed action rows.
- Removed shell and PowerShell behavioral inference from Cargo output.
- Keeps software-dependent checks such as LibreOffice outside canonical `all`.
- Added `libs/cua-driver/docs/action-support.md`, an evidence journal, and the public [Platform Support](https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/platform-support) reference.\n- Split the validation model into [How Cua Driver Is Validated](https://cua.ai/docs/concepts/how-cua-driver-is-validated), covering source-built harnesses, independent oracles, retained evidence, and maintainer-triggered release validation.\n- Added a cross-OS [Platform Roadmap](https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/platform-roadmap) that separates evidence gaps, engineering work, experimental environments, and hard OS boundaries without promising dates.

## Validation

- **Linux X11:** [run 29194456173](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29194456173) passed all **108** declared outcomes: **71 delivered, 37 exact refusals, 0 failures, 0 skips**.
- **Linux Sway native and capture:** [run 29195551765](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29195551765) passed native GTK **31/31** and capture/scope **5/5**, with playable per-cell video.
- **Linux Sway shared:** [run 29199656600](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29199656600) passed **29/36** Electron rows, up from 23/36. [Focused run 29200827296](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29200827296) then passed all **9/9 Electron PX-background** rows at the replacement source. The same 9 Tauri rows remained environment-limited by the hosted DRM/EGL setup.
- **Nested compositor:** [run 29197643541](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29197643541) passed native GTK **31/31**; [run 29197887387](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29197887387) passed capture/scope **5/5** with exact `LinuxCuaCompositorInject` metadata. Full shared run [29199596935](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29199596935) passed **26/36** Electron rows before focused repairs. [Run 29200462634](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29200462634) then passed **7/9** occluded PX-background rows. Dedicated scroll run [29200854535](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29200854535) remained red, so the environment stays experimental.
- **GNOME:** a representative GNOME 46 session passed **31** native GTK rows, **3** capture contracts, and **2** desktop-scope contracts.
- **KDE:** Plasma 6 reached session startup, GTK AT-SPI discovery, generic discovery, and portal-interface preflight. No KDE behavioral matrix is accepted.
- **Packaging and unit gates:** [Nix source run 29200852035](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29200852035) passed at `a78f525a`. Linux unit, distribution, docs, script, Windows compile, and the local 35-test testkit suite are green.
- **Windows:** [run 29166454913](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29166454913) passed all **113** typed rows: **92 delivered, 21 exact refusals, 0 failures, 0 skips**.
- **macOS:** the complete local matrix passed all **130** declared rows: **124 delivered, 6 exact refusals, 0 failures, 0 skips**.

## Remaining explicit gaps

- Standard Wayland cannot route arbitrary raw focus-bound pointer or keyboard input to an occluded, unfocused surface. Unsupported paths return exact structured refusals.
- Sway Electron still lacks foreground AX right click, foreground AX double click, and foreground AX/PX hotkey delivery.
- Hosted Sway cannot expose a representative Tauri/WebKitGTK renderer accessibility tree without DRM/EGL. The native frame can exist while the renderer tree is absent.
- The nested `cua-compositor` remains experimental. Renderer left/double click, one AX right-click timeout, and renderer scroll are not stable across focused runs. Unicode text and a canonical parallel-drag row remain unproven.
- KDE lacks a target-addressable KWin activation adapter and an accepted behavioral matrix.
- GNOME and KDE portal-backed MP4 parity, representative shared renderer runs, and real-Xorg MPX/uinput evidence remain open.
- SwiftUI transient-panel AX enumeration, Windows elevated-integrity refusal coverage, and several native control combinations remain unproven.

title: feat(cua-bench,agent): enable Claude Fable 5 and Meta Muse Spark 1.1 computer-use
body:
Enables benchmarking **Claude Fable 5** (Amazon Bedrock) and **Meta Muse Spark 1.1** (Meta Model API) as function-calling computer-use agents through the cua-agent loop and cua-bench harness. All model-specific behavior is keyed off model-name substrings, so **existing models are unaffected**.

## Agent — `cua_agent/loops/anthropic.py`
The anthropic loop is a generic litellm tool-calling computer-use loop; this widens it to two new families:
- Register for `muse-spark*` in addition to `claude-*`.
- **Function-tool fallback** for models without Anthropic's hosted `computer_*` tool (Fable 5, Mythos 5, Muse Spark).
- Use `role:"tool"` (not the invalid `role:"function"`) for tool-result messages.
- **Parallel-tool-call dedup** to the first action + `parallel_tool_calls=False` — avoids Bedrock `Expected toolResult blocks ... for the following Ids` pairing errors when a model emits two tool calls in one turn.
- **Muse Spark specifics**: deliver screenshots in a following `user` message (its strict OpenAI-Chat endpoint rejects images in tool messages), and a **1000×1000 coordinate adapter** — Muse grounds in a normalized square (Qwen-style), so raw-pixel interpretation put clicks ~30% off; the adapter maps them back to within ~1px.
- Optional `CUA_DEBUG_IMAGES` instrumentation for diagnosing image delivery (off by default).

## cua-bench
- **agents/cua_agent**: raise per-step retries to 6 (via the ComputerAgent `max_retries` arg — library default is unchanged) so long benchmark runs ride out sustained provider throttling (e.g. Bedrock 503s) instead of dropping a task mid-run.
- **task_runner**: pass `AWS_*` (Bedrock), `OPENAI_BASE_URL`/`OPENAI_API_BASE` (OpenAI-compatible endpoints like the Meta Model API), and `CUA_DEBUG_IMAGES` through to the agent container; when `--with` mounts a local agent, re-sync the litellm version it pins — the baked image shipped an older litellm that **silently dropped Bedrock screenshots** (agent ran blind).
- **run**: forward `--with` dev paths to the dataset detached subprocess (previously only the single-task path forwarded them).
- **solver**: still evaluate partial work when the agent hits max steps, instead of exiting before grading.

## Validation
- Fable 5: cua-bench-basic 10/13; full KiCad set graded (mean 0.267).
- Muse Spark 1.1: cua-bench-basic 10/13; full KiCad set graded (mean 0.246 over 23 tasks).
- Lint (isort/black/ruff) and the agent test suite pass locally.

title: fix(cua-driver): target page JavaScript exactly
body:
## Summary

- allow `page.execute_javascript` to accept explicit `cdp_port` and `target_url_contains`
- require an explicit target hint to match exactly one CDP page
- reject invalid CDP ports instead of truncating them

## Why

Multi-window Electron processes expose multiple page targets on one CDP port. `execute_javascript` previously discarded the caller's resolved page identity and selected the first page target. An explicit URL hint also fell back to the first page when no target matched, so a successful RPC could execute against the wrong renderer.

The lower-level CDP session code already supported selecting a target by URL. This change threads that identity through the `page` tool and makes explicit hints fail closed when absent or ambiguous.

## Validation on latest upstream main

Rebased without conflict onto `trycua/cua@8c921b2b3bf13494724ead4f0a814d80c56a7e8b`.

```text
cargo test -p cua-driver-core page::tests
  3 passed

cargo test -p platform-macos browser::cdp_client::tests
  6 passed

cargo test -p cua-driver-core cdp::tests
  2 passed

cargo check -p cua-driver --release
  passed

cargo check -p platform-windows --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
  passed

cargo check -p platform-linux  # Debian bookworm / Rust 1.92
  passed
```

The targeted-page commit is `68a42c06bf3fdfa429d65e9c011efa13c2414548`; review feedback is addressed by `5c2b402d`, which reuses the existing CDP session cache, and `0e9a8294`, which prevents replay after a script has been sent. `35fa5658` completes explicit targeted routing on Windows and Linux. `git range-diff` reports it equivalent to the originally tested patch commit `adef3e87405986cc82df52ae59aef4c32e08a082`.

## Real multi-window downstream validation

Maka uses cua-driver as the sole page executor. Its real-machine harness runs two independent Electron `BrowserWindow` pages on one CDP port and passes the exact port + unique URL hint through cua-driver for pointer actions, element inspection, `Input.insertText`, and post-action readback.

Final batch `semantic-targeting-v5`:

- 10/10 complete runs passed
- 39/39 checks passed in every run
- two-window click/type routing and text isolation passed in every run
- zero fallback, wrong-target, no-op, or duplicate-effect cases
- frontmost application and real pointer remained unchanged

Per-action results:

| Action | Pass | Route | p50 / p90 / max |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| left click | 10/10 | targeted `page.execute_javascript` | 84 / 87 / 102 ms |
| checkbox click | 10/10 | targeted `page.execute_javascript` | 70 / 77 / 77 ms |
| range drag | 10/10 | targeted `page.execute_javascript` | 96 / 102 / 127 ms |
| right click | 10/10 | targeted `page.execute_javascript` | 74 / 80 / 85 ms |
| double click | 10/10 | targeted `page.execute_javascript` | 74 / 78 / 98 ms |

The downstream repo also passed its full typecheck, build, tests, bundle provenance gate, and final 39/39 real-machine E2E after integrating the patched driver.

## Compatibility

- Repeated targeted evaluations reuse the existing per-port CDP session cache, avoiding repeated Chrome remote-debugging confirmation prompts.
- Retry is limited to retarget failures before `Runtime.evaluate`; a sent script is never replayed after timeout or disconnect.
- Windows and Linux consume explicit `cdp_port` and unique URL hints through the shared CDP helper; calls without explicit targeting retain the existing backend behavior.
- Backends that do not implement targeted execution fail closed only when the caller supplies an explicit target.
- `insert_text` and `type_keystrokes` now share the checked CDP port parser, eliminating the previous `u16` truncation behavior.
