title: CuaDriver type_text can silently truncate long Chrome textarea input
body:
### Summary

When `type_text` targets a textarea in Chrome and falls back to synthesized key events, a long insertion can stop before all characters are delivered. The call may end without a useful failure payload, while the page retains only a prefix.

### Reproduction

1. Open any ordinary web form in Chrome with a textarea.
2. Call `get_window_state`.
3. Call `type_text` on the textarea with roughly 800–1,000 characters and `delay_ms: 0`.
4. Read the field back with `get_window_state`.

### Expected

The call should return only after all characters are present, or return a clear partial-write error containing the requested and delivered character counts.

### Actual

Only a prefix is present. The caller can mistake process completion for a successful full write.

### Suggested safeguards

- Serialize and await the underlying key-event delivery.
- Return requested versus delivered counts.
- Verify the final DOM/AX value length when feasible.
- On partial write, return a structured retryable error.

title: CuaDriver allows overlapping background text operations to interleave across Chrome fields
body:
### Summary

If a long background `type_text` operation is still delivering synthesized key events and another text operation starts for a different Chrome field, characters from both inputs can interleave and land in the wrong field.

### Reproduction

1. Start a long `type_text` call against one Chrome textarea.
2. Before delivery is fully complete, start `type_text` against a second input.
3. Read both fields back.

### Expected

Text operations for a browser process or session should be serialized, or the second call should fail fast while the first remains active.

### Actual

Characters from the two payloads can interleave, corrupting the second field and leaving both inputs unreliable.

### Suggested safeguards

- Add a per-session or per-PID input queue or mutex.
- Do not report a long write complete until the key-event worker exits.
- Reject concurrent text injection with a structured busy error.
- Include target element identity and delivered character count in results.

title: feat(cua-driver): add capability-aware browser tools
body:
## Summary

- add five typed browser tools: `get_browser_state`, `browser_prepare`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, and `browser_type`
- bind every browser mutation to the caller's exact native `pid` and `window_id` through session-scoped, expiring capabilities; ambiguous, stale, or unsupported targets return structured refusals
- discover only owner-verified loopback CDP endpoints, support isolated prepared profiles with explicit approval, and resolve shadow-DOM, same-process iframe, and out-of-process iframe references over a shared event-capable CDP transport
- keep the legacy `page` surface compatible while moving it onto the shared transport
- document the browser workflow, action-selection ladder, platform boundaries, migration path, and release-validation process; update bundled skills and MCP schemas
- add repository-owned standalone Chrome/Edge and embedded Electron, Tauri, WebView2, WKWebView, and WebKitGTK acceptance rows with fixture-state, focus, z-order, cursor, leaked-input, protocol, screenshot, and video evidence

## Why

Native accessibility and pixel delivery remain useful for ordinary desktop interaction, but they cannot provide reliable full-background browser automation on every Chromium surface. The browser tools add a trusted protocol route while preserving the native window identity selected by the caller. This makes browser work deterministic without silently changing tabs, profiles, processes, or windows.

## Safety and compatibility

- `get_browser_state` is read-only and never prepares or restarts a browser implicitly
- `browser_prepare` requires explicit approval and uses an isolated profile; it does not copy, restart, or attach to an existing user profile
- endpoint ownership and native-window correlation are revalidated before each mutation
- split-process or otherwise ambiguous embedded views fail closed instead of falling back to a different window
- browser logs and artifacts exclude cookies, authorization data, storage, page secrets, and authenticated endpoint URLs
- legacy `page` callers retain their public behavior
- macOS Electron JavaScript probes only CDP listeners owned by the requested process; it never falls through to an unrelated browser on a conventional debug port

## Embedded fixtures

Electron and Tauri use the same checked-in web fixture. The Tauri harness serves that fixture from an ephemeral loopback HTTP server and opens it in a programmatically created webview, so all platforms exercise the same DOM and external oracle rather than a downloaded app or platform-specific substitute.

## Supported and refused routes

- standalone Chromium browsers: exact, owner-verified CDP mutation after preparation or an already verifiable endpoint
- Electron and same-process Chromium webviews: exact correlated route where the native window and protocol target can be proven
- WebView2 split-process ambiguity: structured refusal until an exact native-window-to-webview route exists
- Safari, WKWebView, and WebKitGTK mutation: structured refusal until an exact trusted WebKit route exists
- Firefox mutation: structured refusal until a verified BiDi route is implemented
- generic Wayland targets without exact PID and geometry correlation: structured refusal

## Validation

The final source commit is `3722465181e62e70a2c634411b51179e43f86983`.

- [x] parent-head ordinary PR CI: Rust Linux/Windows unit and compile, docs and links, distro compatibility, SPDX, release reminder, and all Nix jobs
- [x] [parent-head Windows hosted interactive matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29519279172): 100 delivered, 25 correctly refused, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- [x] [parent-head Linux X11 hosted interactive matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29519280619): 76 delivered, 42 correctly refused, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- [x] [parent-head Linux native Wayland/Sway matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29519281986): 76 delivered, 42 correctly refused, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- [x] [parent-head standalone Chrome/Edge on hosted Windows and Linux X11](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29519283377): Windows 14 delivered and 2 correctly refused; Linux 12 delivered and 4 correctly refused; 0 failed or skipped
- [x] parent-head macOS standalone Chrome: 6 delivered, 2 correctly refused, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- [x] final-head macOS browser unit suite: 16 passed
- [x] final-head focused macOS Electron browser roundtrip passed while an unrelated Chrome CDP endpoint remained active on a conventional port, reproducing and proving the cross-process-targeting correction
- [ ] [final-head Windows matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29522481893): running as post-merge confirmation
- [ ] [final-head Linux X11 matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29522481909): running as post-merge confirmation
- [ ] [final-head native Wayland/Sway matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29522482061): running as post-merge confirmation
- [ ] [final-head standalone browser matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29522482067): running as post-merge confirmation
- [ ] final-head full macOS physical-host matrix: running as post-merge confirmation

The final delta from the fully green parent-head cross-platform runs is confined to macOS Electron endpoint selection. It removes a global-port fallback, passed the platform unit suite, and passed the exact adversarial E2E that exposed the bug. The full exact-head reruns remain attached for post-merge confirmation.

Every accepted interactive row must emit a typed result and use an independent external oracle. Delivery claims also require the applicable focus, z-order, cursor, and leaked-input guards, with screenshots and playable video retained as evidence. No expected result was relaxed to make a matrix pass.

## Review notes

- this is a large feature PR because the public protocol, platform binding, transport, harnesses, docs, skills, and compatibility layer must land together to preserve exact-target semantics
- broad pre-existing `cargo fmt` drift remains outside this change; all touched code was checked without mass-formatting unrelated files
- an independent final review found no blocking correctness or security issue; CDP detach bookkeeping remains a low-priority cleanup opportunity

title: feat(cua-driver): support approved existing browser profiles
body:
## Summary

Adds an explicit, approval-gated path for attaching CUA Driver's browser tools to an already-running Chromium profile, including exact native setup adapters on macOS, Windows, Linux X11, and Sway/Wayland.

- adds `strategy: { "kind": "existing_profile" }` to `browser_prepare`
- adds `cua-driver browser-approve` for exact, interactive, single-use authorization
- binds grants to the public and transport sessions, process fingerprint, native window, browser product, endpoint, and connection generation
- adds bounded, single-flight CDP reconnect with endpoint ownership and process identity re-verification
- serializes mutations against the real browser target while preserving parallelism across independent tabs
- opens one fixed browser-owned setup page in the approved window, changes one exact remote-debugging control when required, proves a PID-owned loopback endpoint, and closes its temporary tab
- handles only one exact, corroborated browser consent action through AX, UIA, or AT-SPI
- reports every visible setup effect and attempts exact rollback after a failed setup
- redacts consent-bearing evidence: no screenshots, AX/UIA trees, endpoint details, tokens, profile content, or authenticated page content
- adds canonical Chrome/Edge/Chromium standalone-browser E2E coverage with focus, z-order, cursor, leaked-input, fixture-state, and video oracles

## Why

Driver-managed isolated profiles are useful for clean automation, but they cannot reuse an already-authenticated browser session. Before this change, callers had to restart a browser under driver control or fall back to best-effort desktop input.

This PR provides a typed attachment flow after genuine host approval. `get_browser_state` stays read-only and never performs setup as a hidden side effect. The driver does not copy profile data, restart the browser, or attach to an unapproved process or window.

The browser route also makes full-background web automation explicit. DOM/ref mutations and typing can remain background operations. When Chromium's trusted CDP Input click activates the target on macOS or Linux, the driver refuses with `browser_input_trust_unavailable` instead of claiming success; callers may choose the ref-targeted `dom_event` route when a synthetic full-background event is acceptable. Windows delivered the trusted route without changing foreground posture in the acceptance matrix.

## Platform setup adapters

| Platform | Accepted products | Native route | Acceptance environment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| macOS/Quartz | Chrome, Edge | Exact AX page, control, consent, and cleanup semantics | Disposable TCC-authorized Lume VM |
| Windows/Win32 | Chrome, Edge | Exact HWND ownership and UIA page, control, consent, and cleanup semantics | Live RDP user desktop, not Session 0 |
| Linux/X11 | Chrome | Exact X11 window restoration plus AT-SPI setup semantics | Openbox/X11 VM |
| Linux/Wayland | Chromium | Exact Sway container identity plus AT-SPI setup semantics | Native Sway VM |

Chrome, Chromium, and Edge have Linux product descriptors, but only the product/desktop pairs above are claimed as release-accepted by this PR. Generic Wayland mutation remains unavailable when exact compositor PID, window, and geometry identity cannot be proven.

## Security and lifecycle

- Approval artifacts are exact, versioned, valid for five minutes, and consumed after one use or mismatch.
- Ordinary MCP approval markers cannot authorize existing-profile attachment.
- Grants live only in daemon memory and expire after 30 minutes idle or eight hours absolute.
- Session end, daemon restart, process identity change, consent dismissal, or reconnect exhaustion revokes the grant.
- Reconnect is limited to three attempts under one deadline and must re-prove the approved loopback endpoint and process identity.
- A new connection generation invalidates capabilities from every previous generation.
- Setup fails closed on an ambiguous page, control, tab, window, listener, process generation, consent action, browser build, or locale.
- Existing personal profiles are never copied, restarted, or attached implicitly.

## Exact-SHA acceptance

The canonical standalone-browser matrix ran from executable and harness source SHA `7fa6c80f5c433a7d4dadef75e4873af89de0cd3f`. Commit `b6db0a65` only records the resulting documentation.

| Platform | Products | Rows | Delivered | Expected refusals | Failed | Skipped | Playable videos |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Windows/Win32 | Chrome, Edge | 20 | 18 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 20 |
| macOS/Quartz | Chrome, Edge | 20 | 16 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 20 |
| Linux/X11 | Chrome | 10 | 8 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 10 |
| Linux/Wayland | Chromium on Sway | 10 | 8 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 10 |
| **Total** |  | **60** | **50** | **10** | **0** | **0** | **60** |

Every declared row executed and every result had `test_status=pass`. All 60 recordings were downloaded and independently checked for positive duration.

Expected refusals are part of the product contract:

- all four lanes refused `browser_binding_ambiguous` when two native browser windows had indistinguishable bounds and titles
- macOS and Linux refused `browser_input_trust_unavailable` for trusted CDP Input clicks that would activate the standalone target
- Windows delivered trusted clicks on Chrome and Edge while preserving the sentinel posture

Focused local validation passed all 46 `cua-driver-testkit` library tests. Branch CI passed:

- [Windows unit and compile](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29558273312)
- [Linux unit and compile](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29558273322)
- [Nix package, compositor, unit, and policy checks](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29558273327)
- [Documentation sync](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29558273319)
- [Distribution compatibility](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29558273350)

## Known limitations

- Existing-profile mutation remains Chromium-family only; Safari ([#2282](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2282)) and Firefox ([#2286](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2286)) refuse explicitly.
- The accepted native setup matchers require recognized browser builds and accessibility labels; unknown products or locales fail closed.
- macOS and Linux do not advertise trusted CDP Input click as full-background when it changes foreground posture. Ref-targeted DOM event delivery remains available as the synthetic route; trusted background delivery is tracked in [#2285](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2285).
- Wayland setup mutation is accepted only for the exact Sway identity route proven here. Other compositors remain structured refusals until they have representative evidence; compositor expansion is tracked in [#2283](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2283).
- Linux Edge and alternate Chrome/Chromium desktop combinations have descriptors but are not release-accepted by this matrix. The product/desktop certification matrix is tracked in [#2284](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2284).

## Documentation

- [Drive a web page](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/codex/browser-existing-profile-reconnect-plan/docs/content/docs/how-to-guides/driver/drive-a-web-page.mdx)
- [Browser profile attachment reference](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/codex/browser-existing-profile-reconnect-plan/docs/content/docs/reference/cua-driver/browser-profile-attachment.mdx)
- [Browser targeting and background delivery](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/codex/browser-existing-profile-reconnect-plan/docs/content/docs/concepts/browser-targeting-and-background-delivery.mdx)
- [Implementation and acceptance record](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/codex/browser-existing-profile-reconnect-plan/libs/cua-driver/docs/browser-existing-profile-attachment-plan.md)

## Review focus

Please review the approval boundary, endpoint ownership proof, generation invalidation, exact native prompt matching, privacy redaction, and the distinction between trusted CDP Input and synthetic DOM event delivery. This PR remains draft while that review happens.

title: feat(cua-bench): add Windows support to the Daytona provider
body:
Adds Windows support to cua-bench's Daytona provider. Linux runs are untouched: the existing co-located path (desktop + solver in one sandbox) still handles every non-Windows env type; Windows dispatches to a new flow.

## Design: the sandbox is the desktop, the solver stays local

The Docker provider's Windows route (`windows-qemu`, QEMU + KVM inside a container) cannot run on Daytona: sandboxes there do not expose `/dev/kvm`. Daytona does, however, offer native Windows VM sandboxes (`windows` sandbox class). So on Windows:

- The Daytona sandbox is a Windows VM created from a snapshot that auto-starts `cua-computer-server` on port 8000.
- The solver runs as a local subprocess where the harness runs, with `CUA_ENV_API_URL` pointed at the sandbox's signed preview URL. This matches the Docker provider's default topology (solver outside the env, talking HTTP).
- The agent loop makes zero Daytona exec calls — the original reason the Linux path co-locates the solver (SDK base64-exec wrapping tripping abuse detection) does not apply to plain HTTP against the preview URL.
- LLM API keys never enter the sandbox; on the Linux path they are baked into sandbox env at creation, on Windows they stay in the local solver process.

No changes were needed in `solver.py`, `computers/remote.py`, or `libs/python/computer`: the solver already reads `CUA_ENV_API_URL`/`CUA_ENV_TYPE` from env, and Daytona preview URLs carry their auth token in the hostname (`https://8000-<token>.<proxy-domain>`), so `RemoteDesktopSession`'s hostname/port URL reconstruction preserves it.

## Usage

```bash
export DAYTONA_API_KEY=...
cb run task <task-dir> --provider-type daytona --platform windows-qemu --image <windows-snapshot> --wait
```

`--image` names a Daytona Windows snapshot (falls back to `DAYTONA_WINDOWS_SNAPSHOT`; a clear error explains both if neither is set). Tasks whose `setup_config.os_type` is `windows` auto-select the platform, as with the Docker provider.

## Snapshot builder

`python -m cua_bench.scripts.build_daytona_windows_snapshot` produces the snapshot from a stock Daytona Windows base (`windows-medium` by default): installs CPython 3.13 if absent, `pip install cua-computer-server`, opens TCP 8000, and registers a Scheduled Task (`-LogonType Interactive`, restart-forever launcher) modeled on `libs/qemu-docker/windows/src/vm/setup/setup-cua-server.ps1` — with `--host 0.0.0.0` added, since the current CLI default binds 127.0.0.1 (the windows-qemu setup script omits `--host` and would have the same reachability problem against the current server). The builder then validates the artifact by creating a fresh sandbox from the finished snapshot and requiring `/status` → `{"status":"ok","os_type":"windows"}` plus a real screenshot (>10 KB decoded) through the preview URL, proving the server auto-starts on a restored VM. Builder and validation sandboxes are deleted afterwards.

Platform behaviors the builder works around (all observed live, July 2026; may age as Daytona's daemon updates):

- The process **sessions** API does not work on Windows guests: session commands never report an exit code, and subsequent commands fail with `failed to write command: write |1: The pipe is being closed.` The builder uses synchronous `process.exec` exclusively.
- Filesystem snapshots of a running Windows VM are rejected with `Filesystem-only snapshots require the VM sandbox to be stopped (STOPPED)`; the builder stops the VM before snapshotting.
- After the snapshot request, the snapshot record 404s while the job is queued/running; the builder treats 404 as pending and detects failure by the sandbox leaving the snapshotting state without a record appearing.
- The computer-server needs an interactive, unlocked desktop for capture and input (a Session-0 service cannot screenshot), hence the Interactive-logon Scheduled Task rather than a Windows service.

## Verification (live, Daytona cloud)

- End-to-end through the real CLI: `cb run task <smoke-task> --provider-type daytona --platform windows-qemu --image cua-bench-windows-v1 --oracle --wait` — sandbox ready in ~40 s from command start (~23 s create→ready), solver launched locally, remote desktop reported 1024×768, screenshots ~430 KB PNG, a mouse move and an ESC key press executed through `WindowsComputerInterface` without error, evaluation returned 1.0, process exit 0, and the sandbox was confirmed deleted afterwards. Total wall time ~62 s including cleanup. Run twice (before and after review-driven refactoring).
- Negative control: with no `--image` and no `DAYTONA_WINDOWS_SNAPSHOT`, the run fails before creating any sandbox with guidance naming both options and the builder module.
- Local-solver timeout kills the whole process group (`start_new_session` + `killpg`); verified with a solver that spawned a child holding the stdout pipe.
- Linux behavior preservation: the solver argv builder shared by both paths was asserted byte-identical to the previous inline construction for oracle, full-flag, and `max_steps=0` cases.

## Limitations

- Requires the org to have Windows sandbox-class access on Daytona (currently US region).
- The built-in custom-computer agents (`cua_agent`, `opencua_agent`, `qwen35_agent`, `qwen3vl_agent`) advertise their environment as `"linux"` regardless of session OS — pre-existing hardcoding, unchanged here; oracle/eval runs and agents that read the session directly are unaffected.
- The Windows snapshot carries a bare desktop plus the computer-server; task-specific applications need builder extensions.

title: feat(release): automate Driver and Lume attribution
body:
## What changed

- add Release Please manifest-mode releases for Cua Driver and Lume
- synchronize Driver's Rust, Python, installer, and Cargo.lock versions in every open Release Please PR, including PRs rewritten after another component release lands
- collect PR-first contributor attribution, salvaged authorship, coauthors, and linked issue reporters
- render deterministic release manifests, GitHub notes, contributor cards, alt text, and X drafts
- finalize Release Please drafts by immutable tag/SHA with idempotent asset handling and transient GitHub API retries
- remove Driver and Lume from the legacy bump, reminder, digest, and merge-release routes
- document the contributor authorship policy and the rollout/fixture plan
- make the release-metadata check report on every PR so it can safely become required

## Why

The existing tag workflows derived attribution from a bounded git log and inferred GitHub identities from author names. That could omit contributors, lose salvaged authorship, drift from changelogs, and mutate published tag state. This makes pull requests the attribution source of truth while retaining a reviewed editorial layer for release notes and launch graphics.

## Validation

- 50 release-script and workflow-wiring tests
- all 67 Lume tests
- Ruff format/check
- Actionlint and YAML parsing for all changed workflows
- Release Please 17.3.0 config/updater validation
- checked-in version validation for Driver and Lume
- locked Cargo metadata on the generated Driver release branch: all nine workspace packages at 0.9.0
- Claude Code Fable re-audit: PASS WITH FOLLOW-UPS; reported high-priority identity findings are covered by regression tests
- rebased onto main at `8582630c`; the local release suite passes on merge candidate `343f0dfa`

## Fork fixture evidence

Isolated fixture: [f-trycua/cua](https://github.com/f-trycua/cua). No production tag or release was created.

- full two-component Release Please run: [run #5](https://github.com/f-trycua/cua/actions/runs/29543086319), creating separate [Lume PR #1](https://github.com/f-trycua/cua/pull/1) and [Driver PR #2](https://github.com/f-trycua/cua/pull/2)
- merging Lume created exact tag `lume-v0.4.0` at merge SHA `b3e9f3ef` and a GitHub release visibly marked Draft
- the fixture exposed an important multi-component edge case: Release Please rewrites still-open component PRs after another component lands, which had dropped Driver's separate Cargo.lock sync commit
- the workflow now scans and synchronizes every open `release-please--branches--*` PR after every successful Release Please run; [fixed retry run #9](https://github.com/f-trycua/cua/actions/runs/29543877375) restored the dedicated lockfile commit and `Cargo.lock`
- Driver PR #2 then validated under `cargo metadata --locked` with all nine packages at 0.9.0; merging it created exact tag `cua-driver-rs-v0.9.0` at merge SHA `43e4473d` and a GitHub release visibly marked Draft in [run #10](https://github.com/f-trycua/cua/actions/runs/29544057996)
- fork main manifest records Driver 0.9.0 and Lume 0.4.0
- finalizer fixture [first run](https://github.com/f-trycua/cua/actions/runs/29542791754) and [identical retry](https://github.com/f-trycua/cua/actions/runs/29542960390) retained the same release ID and exactly one asset, proving idempotency; the retry also validated recovery from a transient GitHub 503

## Production App evidence

The legacy bump workflow generates an installation token from the same `RELEASE_APP_ID` and `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` used by this Release Please workflow. Production tags created with that token have already started both tag-push CD workflows as `cua-release-bot[bot]`:

- Driver `cua-driver-rs-v0.8.3`: [bump run](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29458621040) and [successful CD run](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29458645707)
- Lume `lume-v0.3.16`: [bump run](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29376388033) and [successful CD run](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29376412794)

This closes the App-token trigger gate. The first Release Please-driven production release remains the final composed-path smoke test.

## Rollout

Merge this workflow before making `CI: Release metadata / validate` required. Once the workflow exists on the protected base branch, add that check to branch protection without changing the repository's existing admin-bypass policy. Then observe the first controlled Driver or Lume release end to end.

title: cua-driver: built-in no-admin self-update (cua-driver self-update) or opt-in auto-update
body:
## Context

cua-driver on Windows installs via `install.ps1` with a junction-based layout (`packages/releases/<version>-<target>` + a `current` junction) that already makes upgrades atomic and admin-free. `check_for_update` exists as a read-only check, so keeping one or more machines current still means re-running the installer manually on each of them.

## Request

- A `cua-driver self-update` subcommand: download the latest release, verify checksum, extract to a new versioned release dir, retarget the `current` junction, and restart `serve` if it is running — never requiring elevation.
- Optionally: an opt-in scheduled auto-update (user-level Scheduled Task, RunLevel=Limited), e.g. `cua-driver self-update --schedule weekly`.

## Notes

- The only elevation in the current installer is the autostart Scheduled Task registration (RunLevel=Highest); `-NoAutoStart` avoids it, so a fully silent non-admin update path already almost exists — it just is not packaged as a first-class command.
- Current workaround on my machines: a weekly user-level Scheduled Task running `install.ps1 -NoAutoStart -NoPathUpdate`. Works, but a built-in command would keep rollback (junction retarget + `CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION` pin) and update in one place.

Platform: Windows 11, cua-driver-rs 0.8.3.

title: ci: block direct merges to libs/fleet (mirror guard)
body:
`libs/fleet` is a read-only mirror of a private canonical repository. A PR merged directly into these paths on `main` is silently overwritten by the next mirror sync — the contributor's work is lost. This adds a **required-check candidate** that fails any PR touching `libs/fleet/**` and tells the author (human or AI agent) to use the `copybara-import` label flow instead.

Design notes:
- No `on.pull_request.paths` filter — a required check that never reports blocks every PR, so the job always runs and passes instantly when no mirrored path is touched.
- Catches renames out of `libs/fleet` via `previous_filename`, not just direct edits.
- Posts a sticky explanatory comment (best-effort; fork PRs have a read-only token, where the check-run error message carries the instructions instead).
- The mirror bot itself is unaffected: it pushes directly to `main` under a ruleset bypass, and this check only gates PR merges.

After merge, the `fleet-mirror-guard` context will be added as a required status check on the `main` ruleset. Rollout caveat: currently-open PRs won't have a run of this check until they push, close/reopen, or rebase, so they'll show it as "Expected" until then.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cua-driver): require live capture permission
body:
## Summary

- Require Accessibility, Screen Recording preflight, and the live
  `screen_recording_capturable` probe before `permissions grant` reports success.
- Detect a stale Screen Recording decision when an already-running daemon reports
  preflight access but cannot capture pixels.
- Return an actionable TCC reset sequence instead of a false success.
- Add unit coverage for ready, stale, and missing-probe responses.

## Why

`permissions status` already exposes the live capture probe, but
`permissions grant` currently stops as soon as Accessibility and Screen Recording
preflight both report true. A stale macOS TCC decision can therefore print
“You’re set” while the driver still cannot capture pixels.

## Test Plan

- [x] `cargo test -p cua-driver permission_grant`
      (`3 passed; 0 failed`)
- [x] `cargo check -p cua-driver`
- [x] `git diff --check 3db4a80fbe0283a8ca78ac4d093a82cc879a7ef1...HEAD`

## Platform / coverage caveats

The Rust tests and check ran on macOS. I did not execute the interactive
`permissions grant` / TCC reset flow because that would change the machine’s
system privacy state. The repository-wide `cargo fmt -p cua-driver -- --check`
currently reports pre-existing formatting differences outside this change; the
modified hunks were checked separately with rustfmt.

title: fix(cua-driver): reuse self-signed local identity
body:
## Summary

- Query matching code-signing identities without the `find-identity -v`
  valid-only filter.
- Reuse the installer-created self-signed identity when its private key is
  present, even before trust-chain validation.
- Keep the existing bounded `codesign` invocation as the authoritative
  usability check.
- Add a regression test covering both identity lookups.

## Why

The local installer creates a self-signed code-signing certificate, but
`security find-identity -v -p codesigning` filters that identity out as
untrusted. Repeated installs can therefore miss the existing certificate,
fall back to another signing path, and lose the stable identity that allows
macOS TCC grants to survive rebuilds.

## Test Plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_install_local_signing.py -q`
      (`1 passed`)
- [x] `bash -n libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-local-rust.sh`
- [x] `git diff --check 3db4a80fbe0283a8ca78ac4d093a82cc879a7ef1...HEAD`

## Platform / coverage caveats

The regression test validates the installer contract and the shell script
passes syntax checking. I did not import a certificate, modify a macOS
Keychain, or run an end-to-end codesign operation, so actual identity usability
still depends on the target machine’s Keychain state and permissions.

title: cua-driver browser: support approved existing Safari profiles
body:
## Context

PR #2261 adds approval-gated existing-profile attachment for Chromium-family browsers. Safari remains an explicit structured refusal because it has a different WebKit inspection/automation model and no proven exact setup adapter.

## Goal

Determine and implement the safest supported route for attaching CUA Driver browser tools to an already-running Safari profile after explicit host approval, without copying profile data, restarting Safari, or falling back to unverified desktop input.

## Requirements

- Bind approval to the exact Safari PID, native window, process generation, CUA session, and any inspectable endpoint or automation session.
- Use a typed WebKit/Safari capability rather than presenting Chromium CDP semantics as portable.
- Prove endpoint/session ownership and re-prove identity after reconnect.
- Automate Safari-owned setup or consent UI only when one exact AX control and owning window can be proven.
- Preserve the existing privacy boundary: no approval artifacts, endpoints, authenticated page content, profile data, or consent screenshots in persisted evidence.
- Fail closed with a stable refusal code when Safari or the current macOS version does not expose a safe route.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A feasibility record documents the supported Safari/WebKit interface and unavoidable platform constraints.
- [ ] The public browser contract advertises Safari only when the exact route is available.
- [ ] Existing-profile prepare, bind, reconnect, session end, prompt dismissal, stale capability, and ambiguity behavior have deterministic tests.
- [ ] A real Safari harness validates external page state, focus, z-order, cursor, leaked input, and video evidence on a representative macOS release.
- [ ] Unsupported Safari builds/locales return a structured refusal without changing browser state.
- [ ] User-facing platform support and browser attachment documentation are updated.

Parent initiative: #2192. Follow-up to #2261.

title: cua-driver browser: expand exact existing-profile setup across Wayland compositors
body:
## Context

PR #2261 accepts existing-profile browser setup on native Sway because CUA Driver can prove an exact compositor container, PID, window geometry, and AT-SPI browser tree. Other Wayland compositors currently refuse mutation instead of guessing native-window identity.

## Goal

Expand exact existing-profile browser attachment to representative Wayland compositors without introducing a generic unsafe fallback. Each compositor route must prove the target PID/window and restore foreground posture after the bounded setup operation.

## Candidate scope

- GNOME Shell/Mutter
- KDE Plasma/KWin
- Additional wlroots compositors only where a stable identity route exists
- Explicit compositor capability discovery and refusal reporting

## Requirements

- Use compositor-native identity APIs, a narrowly scoped maintained extension, or another verifiable route; screen-coordinate similarity alone is insufficient.
- Correlate compositor identity, PID, geometry, AT-SPI application/window, browser product, and the PID-owned loopback endpoint.
- Preserve the exact approval, generation, reconnect, privacy, and rollback model from #2261.
- Keep generic/unknown Wayland sessions as structured refusals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each advertised compositor has a documented identity proof and threat analysis.
- [ ] Exact and ambiguous identity cases have unit/integration coverage.
- [ ] Existing-profile setup and attachment run against a real browser in a native session for each accepted compositor.
- [ ] Harness rows prove page state, focus, z-order where observable, cursor capability, no leaked input, and video evidence.
- [ ] Missing compositor APIs, incomplete accessibility trees, and ambiguous windows refuse before mutation.
- [ ] The support matrix lists acceptance per compositor rather than claiming generic Wayland support.

Parent initiative: #2192. Follow-up to #2261.

title: cua-driver browser: certify Linux browser and desktop combinations
body:
## Context

PR #2261 includes Linux setup descriptors for Chrome, Chromium, and Edge, but its release-acceptance evidence proves Chrome on Openbox/X11 and Chromium on Sway only. Descriptors and compilation are not sufficient evidence for other product/desktop pairs.

## Goal

Build and run a canonical Linux browser-product/desktop matrix so every advertised existing-profile attachment route is backed by representative real-browser evidence.

## Initial matrix

| Product | X11 | Sway | Future accepted compositors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Google Chrome | Required | Required | Per compositor |
| Chromium | Required | Required | Per compositor |
| Microsoft Edge | Required when officially available for the distro | Required when the native accessibility tree is complete | Per compositor |

## Requirements

- Use official or intentionally installed browser packages; record product/version provenance.
- Start from normal profiles with remote debugging disabled, then exercise the approval-gated setup path.
- Run the same declarations and external oracles for every product/desktop pair.
- Treat unavailable packages or incomplete platform prerequisites as explicit environment results, not silent row filters.
- Keep product/desktop pairs experimental until the full matrix passes at an exact source SHA.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Canonical declarations cover setup, attach, reconnect, frames, multi-tab binding, stale refs, background mutation/type, trusted input policy, and ambiguous native-window binding.
- [ ] Every accepted row records exact source SHA, browser provenance, external oracle result, and playable video.
- [ ] Focus, z-order, cursor capability, occlusion, and leaked input are asserted continuously where the claim requires them.
- [ ] CI/maintainer commands expose the full declared matrix and fail when filters omit a required row.
- [ ] The public support matrix distinguishes implemented descriptors, experimentally passing pairs, and release-accepted pairs.

Follow-up to #2261.

title: cua-driver browser: support trusted full-background Chromium clicks on macOS and Linux
body:
## Context

The exact-SHA matrix for PR #2261 found that Chromium's trusted CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` route activates the standalone target on macOS and Linux. CUA Driver therefore returns `browser_input_trust_unavailable` instead of falsely claiming full-background delivery. Ref-targeted `dom_event` clicks remain available when a synthetic event is acceptable. Windows trusted clicks passed without changing foreground posture.

## Goal

Find and validate a genuinely trusted Chromium click route on macOS and Linux that can target an occluded, unfocused browser page without focus, z-order, cursor, or input leakage side effects.

## Investigation areas

- Chromium/CDP behavior for background targets, tabs, and occluded windows
- Browser-process or renderer options that preserve background dispatch without weakening user profiles
- Native browser accessibility routes where they retain trusted semantics
- Bounded focus suppression/restoration only if the foreground application never observes a posture change

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document whether Chromium fundamentally requires activation for trusted CDP pointer input on each platform.
- [ ] Do not relabel `dom_event` as trusted input or hide a transient focus steal through a relaxed oracle.
- [ ] A successful route passes with the target fully occluded and a foreground sentinel continuously asserting focus, z-order, cursor, and no leaked input.
- [ ] External page state proves the click reached the exact intended tab/window.
- [ ] Chrome and Edge are covered on macOS; Chrome/Chromium and any accepted Edge route are covered on Linux X11 and accepted Wayland compositors.
- [ ] If no safe route exists, retain the structured refusal and document the platform limitation clearly.

Follow-up to #2261.

title: fix(cua-driver): make macOS direct ScreenCaptureKit consent explicit and observable
body:
## Problem

On newer macOS releases, CUA Driver can receive a separate system prompt allowing it to bypass the private window picker and directly access screen/audio capture. This consent is distinct from the ordinary Screen Recording TCC grant.

The prompt can appear unexpectedly after a local reinstall or when a live `SCShareableContent::get()` capability probe runs. The current permission UX does not clearly distinguish this grant, and a status/capability check may be perceived as read-only even if macOS decides to present the additional consent dialog.

## Why this matters

Direct ScreenCaptureKit access is intentional and needed for exact window/desktop screenshots and recordings without presenting Apple's picker for every action. However, users should know in advance which permission is being requested and which operation caused it. A stable signing identity preserves existing grants for the same TCC service, but it does not make a previously unrequested direct-capture consent category disappear.

## Proposed behavior

- Report ordinary Screen Recording and direct ScreenCaptureKit capture readiness as separate capabilities.
- Make `cua-driver permissions grant` explicitly trigger and explain the direct-capture consent on macOS versions that require it.
- Ensure `prompt: false`, status, and doctor/read-only paths do not unexpectedly raise a system dialog; if macOS cannot probe without prompting, report `unknown` or `consent_required` instead.
- Identify the command/probe that caused a consent request in diagnostics and documentation.
- Explain that this grant does not authorize browser-profile/CDP attachment or access to browser data.
- Keep local-install identity stable so already granted permissions remain reusable when the signed identity is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Permission output distinguishes Accessibility, Screen Recording, and direct ScreenCaptureKit access.
2. The explicit grant flow presents all required macOS consent with user-facing context.
3. Read-only permission checks are verified not to raise a new consent prompt, or fail closed with a documented non-prompting status.
4. Local-install and macOS VM documentation cover first grant, reinstall, revocation, and verification.
5. A macOS test or reproducible manual gate validates the behavior on a release that implements the private-window-picker bypass consent.

title: feat(cua-driver): make browser snapshots semantic and visibility-aware
body:
## Problem

`get_browser_state` currently walks the pierced DOM in document order, treats broad signals such as any `role` or `tabindex` as interactive, and truncates the result to 300 refs only after collection.

Large virtualized applications can retain hidden or stale DOM subtrees ahead of the active view. Those nodes consume the ref budget, so visible page content and controls may be omitted even though the exact tab is attached and browser-native actions work. The current response also exposes interactive refs but not a compact semantic representation of visible page text, which can force callers back to native accessibility inspection for tasks that should remain browser-native.

## Design direction

Adopt a deterministic hybrid snapshot suited to CUA Driver's exact-binding and capability model:

1. Use the browser accessibility tree as the semantic source for roles, accessible names, states, and readable text.
2. Join semantic nodes to DOM backend node IDs and frame identities so stale-ref and exact-frame checks remain authoritative.
3. Use browser layout snapshot data to classify CSS-hidden, laid-out, in/near viewport, and page-occluded nodes.
4. Rank visible interactive controls and visible semantic content before near-viewport or offscreen nodes. Apply output limits only after ranking.
5. Return semantic page content separately from actionable refs; do not make static text accidentally clickable.
6. Support deterministic scoped observation and opaque continuation rather than silently dropping the tail.
7. Preserve background browser behavior: page visibility is browser-layout visibility and must not depend on whether the native browser window is foreground or desktop-occluded.
8. Build the DOM index once per browser session during a snapshot and compose same-process frames, capability-tested out-of-process frames, and author shadow roots.
9. Keep read-only observation separate from mutation. The driver must not add model inference, cached action plans, or automatic self-healing.
10. Add bounded fallback behavior for browser protocol depth/stack limits without returning a partial tree as complete.

Simply raising the 300-ref cap is insufficient because it increases context and latency while preserving document-order bias.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fixture containing more than 300 hidden or retained interactive nodes before the active view still returns the visible heading, body text, editable field, and primary actions.
- A large virtualized message view can be read and acted on using only browser tools after attachment; native `get_window_state` is unnecessary for webpage content.
- CSS-hidden and `aria-hidden` content does not displace visible content.
- In-viewport content is prioritized deterministically; truncation reports omitted categories and counts or provides an opaque continuation capability.
- Static semantic content is readable but is not minted as an actionable ref.
- Scoped reads can narrow state to a current page ref or an explicit read-only query without weakening mutation targeting.
- Ref resolution still re-proves target generation, frame/document identity, and backend-node liveness before mutation.
- Same-process iframe, out-of-process iframe, and shadow-DOM coverage remains green.
- Focus, foreground, and desktop-occlusion sentinels prove that snapshot and DOM-ref actions remain background-safe.
- Snapshot capture has bounded protocol retries and measured time, node, memory, and output budgets.
- Logs and CI artifacts contain counts and fixture data only; customer page content is not recorded by default.

title: feat(cua-driver): add semantic browser snapshots
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `semantic_v2` browser snapshot contract that composes Chromium accessibility, pierced DOM, layout, viewport, and proven frame identity into a bounded, agent-readable page model. The existing `dom_refs_v1` format remains the compatibility default.

This update also hardens exact inactive-tab operation. Natural multi-term semantic queries now find and rank relevant nodes, and the repo-owned browser harness proves that navigation, explicit DOM clicks, bulk text insertion, and per-keystroke typing mutate an unselected sibling tab without selecting it, raising the browser, moving the real cursor, or leaking input. Windows additionally verifies trusted CDP pointer delivery.

Closes #2299.
Closes #2306.

## What changes

- Return readable semantic content separately from typed action refs.
- Rank visible content and controls before hidden or offscreen retained application state.
- Classify viewport, near-viewport, offscreen, CSS-hidden, no-layout, and conservatively page-occluded nodes.
- Declare `click` and `type` action kinds and refuse incompatible mutations before delivery.
- Add exact-phrase semantic filtering with a ranked multi-term fallback for natural agent queries.
- Add query, subtree scope, and opaque single-use continuation capabilities.
- Re-prove frame and loader identity for mutations and continuations; navigation, reconnect, newer snapshots, or session end invalidate stale capabilities.
- Compose same-process frames, author shadow DOM, and capability-tested contained OOPIF sessions; omit unprovable content explicitly.
- Add a progressively shallower large-DOM fallback and bounded branch hydration while preserving `complete:false` on degraded reads.
- Keep raw CDP targets, backend node IDs, selectors, continuation offsets, endpoint details, and approval artifacts private.
- Assert at the unit boundary that semantic reads, navigation, clicks, and typing never call `Page.bringToFront` or `Target.activateTarget`.
- Send per-character typing as `keyDown -> char -> keyUp`, with text only on `char`.
- Bracket inactive-tab keyboard input with bounded CDP focus emulation, poll for exact element and document focus readiness, and restore the prior posture before reporting success.
- Bracket supported trusted background pointer dispatch with the same bounded focus-emulation posture.
- Expand the real multi-tab row to navigate, query, trusted-click or honestly refuse, explicit-DOM-click, bulk-type, and keystroke-type in an unselected tab.
- Give the two harness tabs distinct titles, establish their selection posture before the guard, and independently verify fixture state, selected tab, foreground focus, z-order, leaked input, and cursor state.
- Add a Linux Microsoft Edge setup fallback: one exact approved foreground click is allowed only after AT-SPI identifies the unique checkbox and its first action remains visibly ineffective; checked state and a PID-owned loopback endpoint must then be re-proven.
- Harden approved existing-profile setup on macOS when Chrome suppresses its omnibox suggestion popup: prove the exact address field, prefer its native AX route, otherwise use a bounded foreground assist to retype only the fixed internal setup URL, verify it, submit once, and restore the prior app.
- Include the semantic-state row in both Unix and Windows canonical standalone-browser runners.
- Update the installed browser skill, how-to guide, generated MCP reference, and semantic snapshot reference.

## Validation

Exact local source validation through `e6643f21`:

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`: 261 unit tests plus 3 session-lifecycle tests passed.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos`: 144 passed.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux`: 16 passed.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-testkit`: 46 library tests plus 2 report tests passed.
- Formatting checks for the owned Rust files and `git diff --check`: passed.

Interactive macOS product-path validation at exact head:

- Reinstalled from this worktree with the stable local signing identity; Accessibility and Screen Recording remained granted.
- Full standalone-browser matrix: 9 delivered, 2 intentional structured refusals, 0 failed, 0 skipped, with video for all 11 rows.
- `standalone_browser_existing_profile_setup`: passed in the full matrix and three consecutive focused runs.
- `standalone_browser_multi_tab`: passed repeatedly. The selected first tab stayed unchanged while the unselected second tab navigated, accepted an explicit DOM click, accepted bulk text, accepted per-keystroke text, and remained unselected.
- macOS trusted hardware-like background pointer delivery returns the documented structured refusal; the explicit ref-targeted DOM route remains available.

Cross-platform browser evidence:

- [Parent exact-input run at `a19e909d`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29606199101): Windows 20 delivered and 2 expected refusals; Linux X11 18 delivered and 4 expected refusals; 0 failures or skips on either platform.
- [Exact final-head run at `e6643f21`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29607291979): Windows 20 delivered and 2 expected refusals; Linux X11 18 delivered and 4 expected refusals; 0 failures or skips on either platform.

## Security and compatibility

- Existing clients continue to receive `dom_refs_v1` unless they explicitly request `semantic_v2`.
- `get_browser_state` remains read-only.
- Stale refs are terminal; there is no heuristic rebinding, model inference, or silent route switching.
- Exact native PID/window binding, loopback endpoint ownership, connection generation, frame loader identity, and OOPIF containment remain required.
- Browser mutations do not select inactive tabs. The harness establishes a known selected-tab posture before the guarded interval and verifies it again afterward.
- Focus emulation is target-session scoped, bounded to the trusted input operation, restored before success, and never activates a native target.
- Existing-profile UI setup remains an explicit approval-scoped operation. Any bounded foreground or global-input fallback re-proves the exact browser PID, native window, AX control, fixed setup URL, and resulting PID-owned loopback endpoint, and reports every visible side effect.
- Tests and docs use fixture-only content; no personal profile data, page history, account content, local paths, endpoint secrets, or approval artifacts are included.

## Remaining limitations

- Trusted hardware-like pointer delivery to standalone background Chromium remains platform-gated and refuses where activation cannot be ruled out. Ref-targeted explicit `dom_event` clicks are the full-background route.
- Browser dialogs, downloads, discarded tabs, and native browser chrome remain outside the semantic page model and use native handling or structured refusal.
- `tabs[].active` can be ambiguous for same-title sibling tabs because the current value is derived from native-title correlation. Exact mutation by `tab_id` remains unaffected. Follow-up: #2307.

This PR remains draft for review.

title: cua-driver browser: visualize visible-target actions without breaking background delivery
body:
## Problem

Browser-native actions currently execute through the browser connection and do not update CUA Driver's synthetic session cursor. This makes visible-tab trajectories harder to interpret than native desktop actions.

A browser action may also target an inactive or occluded tab. Rendering a cursor over the currently visible desktop in that case would be misleading and would introduce a visible side effect into an otherwise full-background operation.

## Proposed contract

- When the exact browser window and tab are proven visible and active, map the browser ref's viewport box to native screen coordinates and animate the existing session-scoped synthetic cursor.
- For inactive, occluded, minimized, or otherwise unproven targets, preserve full-background delivery and suppress cursor rendering.
- Report structured action metadata such as `cursor_visualized` and a bounded suppression reason so recordings and consumers can distinguish the two cases.
- Do not activate a tab or window merely to visualize the cursor.
- Keep cursor behavior consistent for semantic DOM clicks and trusted pointer routes where their delivery contracts allow it.

## Validation

Add cross-platform harness rows proving:

- a visible active-tab browser action updates the expected session cursor;
- an inactive-tab background action mutates only the target page and does not display or move a cursor on the foreground page;
- an occluded/minimized target does not create visible desktop side effects;
- recordings and action results expose whether visualization occurred or was suppressed.

Related background trusted-input limitation: #2285.

title: cua-driver: safely automate current Chrome remote-debugging setup on macOS
body:
## Problem

Current Chrome can render `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` on macOS while omitting the page content from its accessibility tree. The native window and exact address-bar URL are provable, but the heading and remote-debugging checkbox are not exposed as AX nodes. Process-scoped AX hit testing over the visible checkbox returns only a generic `AXScrollArea`, whose descendants also expose no actionable checkbox.

CUA Driver therefore correctly fails closed instead of toggling a guessed pixel. This leaves `browser_prepare` unable to enable remote debugging automatically for a current existing Chrome profile when no loopback endpoint already exists. Attachment to an already-enabled, PID-owned loopback endpoint continues to work.

## Reproduction

Run the repo-owned `standalone_browser_existing_profile_setup` row on an interactive macOS host with current Chrome and CUA Driver TCC permissions. The exact setup page is visibly rendered, but the driver returns `browser_wrong_target_refused` because it cannot prove the checkbox identity. The temporary setup tab is closed and remote debugging remains unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Require explicit existing-profile approval scoped to the exact Chrome PID and native window.
- Act only on the fixed Chrome remote-debugging page.
- Prove that the resulting endpoint is loopback-only and owned by the approved process.
- Preserve bounded cleanup and rollback on failure.
- Never fall back to an unverified coordinate click or generic approval-dialog automation.
- Make `standalone_browser_existing_profile_setup` pass on current Chrome with side-effect, focus, z-order, cursor, and no-input-leak evidence.

Related draft: #2301

title: cua-driver: make browser tabs[].active exact for same-title sibling tabs
body:
## Problem

The browser-tool bind response currently derives `tabs[].active` from the CDP target selected during native-window correlation. When two sibling tabs in one Chromium window have the same title, that representative can be deterministic but not the actually selected tab, so the public `active` flag can point at the wrong tab.

This surfaced while hardening the repo-owned inactive-tab E2E. The browser mutations remained exactly targeted by `tab_id` and did not activate either tab; only the selected-tab label was ambiguous.

## Expected behavior

- Report `active: true` only when selected-tab identity is proven.
- Preserve exact `pid + window_id + tab_id` binding and never guess between same-title tabs.
- If Chromium/native APIs cannot prove the selected tab without activation, return an explicit unknown/ambiguous state rather than a false boolean.
- Add a two-tab fixture with identical titles and distinct URLs that checks the public state without changing selection.

## Notes

Page visibility alone is not a sufficient oracle under full-window occlusion because Chromium may mark every page in an occluded window hidden. A solution should use selected-tab identity or expose honest uncertainty, and must not call `Page.bringToFront` or `Target.activateTarget` during observation.

title: chore(cua-driver): establish a clean, deterministic rustfmt baseline
body:
## Problem

Running the canonical workspace formatter from `libs/cua-driver/rust` produces a repository-wide diff on current `main`:

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

Reproduced against `b088628a2ac0a472008211b67ffee3b595d3270b`. The command exits with status 1 and reports formatting differences in approximately 181 Rust files (1,534 diff hunks).

This makes it difficult to format a focused contribution without accidentally introducing a very large unrelated diff. It also means a future formatting gate cannot be enabled safely until the baseline and toolchain are made deterministic.

## Proposed work

1. Pin or document the supported Rust and rustfmt toolchain for Cua Driver.
2. Apply the formatter once in a dedicated mechanical PR, isolated from behavioral changes.
3. Add a scoped CI check that runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` for changes under `libs/cua-driver/rust/**`.
4. Add the canonical formatting command to the Rust contributor documentation.
5. Confirm the formatter produces no diff on macOS, Windows, and Linux with the pinned toolchain.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` exits successfully on a clean checkout.
- The formatting-only baseline is reviewable separately from behavior changes.
- CI prevents new Rust formatting drift.
- Contributors have one documented canonical command and toolchain version.

## Notes

The drift was found while formatting a small telemetry change. The unrelated formatter output was removed from that change rather than being included opportunistically.

The docstring for `is_otel_enabled()` in `libs/python/core/cua_core/telemetry/otel.py` states:

> "CUA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED is deprecated — a warning is emitted on first use and the value is honoured for backwards compatibility."

However, the current implementation emits the `DeprecationWarning` on **every call** to `is_otel_enabled()`, not just the first one. Since this function is called indirectly on every instrumented operation (via `_initialize_otel()`, `record_operation`, `record_error`, `record_tokens`, `track_concurrent`, `create_span`), this can lead to excessive warning spam in logs when the deprecated env var is set.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `CUA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true` in the environment
2. Call `is_otel_enabled()` multiple times (or run any instrumented operation multiple times)
3. Observe that the `DeprecationWarning` fires on each call

### Expected Behavior

The warning should be emitted only once, matching the documented "first use" behavior.

### Proposed Fix

Add a module-level flag to track whether the warning has already been emitted, and guard the `warnings.warn(...)` call with it.

I'd be happy to submit a PR for this if it's a welcome contribution.

feat(release): add historical attribution backfill
body:
## Summary

This PR adds the complete historical release-attribution backfill for Cua Driver and Lume. It accounts for every published release in scope and checks in the exact proposed release-body additions for review before any GitHub release is changed.

The frozen inventory contains 182 releases:

- 54 Cua Driver releases
- 128 Lume releases
- 146 evidence-backed release-note candidates
- 36 explicit skips for empty ranges, same-SHA tags, disconnected history, unresolved identity, or maintenance-only changes

The PR does not modify a published release. CI runs tests and validates checked-in data only.

## Why

Our release history has inconsistent contributor credit and change summaries. Reconstructing it by hand would make source selection, identity resolution, wording, and rollback behavior difficult to audit.

This backfill freezes the historical source data, separates AI-authored prose from deterministic attribution, and requires an operator to apply reviewed body-only changes after merge.

## What changed

### Frozen inventory and evidence

- Catalogs release IDs, tags, tag SHAs, titles, flags, existing body bytes, and asset metadata.
- Models the Driver path move from `libs/cua-driver-rs` to `libs/cua-driver` and the Lume move into `libs/lume`.
- Handles unpublished tag boundaries, same-SHA releases, and disconnected history explicitly.
- Resolves pull requests and contributor logins from public GitHub and git evidence.
- Preserves uncertain attribution as a skip instead of guessing an identity.

### AI authoring with deterministic boundaries

- Sends bounded evidence packets to a JSON-in/JSON-out author command.
- Keeps contributor handles, source links, compare ranges, and release mutation fields out of the model's control.
- Rejects out-of-packet citations, URLs, handles, markup, malformed output, and prompt-version or evidence drift.
- Removes `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` from the author subprocess environment.
- Records evidence-backed maintenance-only results as durable `no-product-changes` skips.
- Checkpoints each adaptive batch so generation can resume safely.

### Reviewable output

- `candidates.md` contains the proposed retrospective notes.
- `skip-ledger.json` accounts for every release without a candidate.
- `rendered.json` contains the exact release bodies that the apply command would send.
- JSON Schemas define and enforce the catalog, evidence, candidates, skips, and rendered payloads.
- `validate` checks every artifact against its schema, rebuilds the derived output, and fails on coverage, hash, citation, or byte differences.

### Body-only apply and rollback

- Dry run is the default.
- `--execute` requires a clean worktree at the full approved commit SHA.
- The tool verifies live release ID, tag SHA, title, flags, assets, and body hash before writing.
- The GitHub client exposes one write method. It sends `PATCH {"body": ...}` only.
- Apply writes and fsyncs the full pre-image journal before the body PATCH, verifies the live result, and records completion.
- Interrupted applies recover from the prepared journal entry.
- Repeated applies are no-ops after verification.
- Rollback requires a verified journal entry and refuses to overwrite body drift.

### CI and runbook

- The script test workflow now covers all backfill paths.
- CI runs the script test suite and deterministic backfill validation.
- The runbook covers inventory review, generation, independent review, a six-release pilot, rollback rehearsal, paced batches, and stop conditions.

## Content review

Claude Code Fable completed a read-only audit of the implementation and all 146 generated candidates. The first pass found three content errors:

- Lume 0.2.82 inverted the revert and re-land order.
- Driver 0.7.0 overstated Wayland scrolling and typing support.
- Driver 0.2.8 stated a partial Windows capture fix as unconditional.

All three notes were corrected and regenerated. A focused Fable follow-up returned `PASS` with no blocking findings. It also verified the corrected rendered bodies, candidate hashes, GitHub-token scrubbing, and markup rejection. The later review-artifact cleanup did not change the catalog, evidence, candidates, skip ledger, rendered payload, or candidate Markdown.

## Validation

Validated on commit `0d37058200dc6d2ed540ccf1c8e4419132ea75ad` after rebasing onto current `origin/main`:

```text
78 passed
Ruff: all checks passed
release_backfill.py validate: 146 candidates and 36 explicit skips
coverage: 182 of 182 releases
git diff --check: passed
token-shaped secret scan: passed
Claude Code Fable follow-up: PASS, zero blocking findings
```

## Safety boundary

Merging this PR changes repository files only. It does not run the apply command or edit GitHub releases.

After merge, an operator must review the checked-in candidates, select the approved merge commit, run the documented six-release pilot, verify idempotency and rollback, and then apply later batches. The operator journals remain outside the repository.

Visual posters and X publishing remain out of scope for this PR.

title: feat(driver): add per-session capture scope
body:
## Summary

- replace the persistent `capture_scope` setting with immutable per-session `auto`, `window`, and `desktop` policies
- add explicit one-way desktop escalation for `auto` sessions and enforce the effective modality across perception and actions
- port missing desktop pointer, keyboard, text, hotkey, scroll, and drag behavior from `computer-server` to the Rust macOS, Linux/X11/Wayland, and Windows backends
- add race-safe session cleanup, capability declarations, transport/schema coverage, concurrent-session tests, and updated computer-use ladder documentation

## Why

Capture scope is session intent, not a machine-wide preference. A persistent global setting cannot safely represent concurrent agent sessions that need different capture surfaces. The new policy lets each session select its own strict modality while keeping desktop access in `auto` behind an explicit, auditable escalation after the window ladder is exhausted.

## User and developer impact

- callers choose `capture_scope` in `start_session`
- stale persisted `capture_scope` values are ignored
- `config set capture_scope` and `set_config` return `config_key_retired`
- strict window and desktop sessions reject cross-modality tools with structured errors

title: Docs: define canonical handling for blog Markdown URLs
body:
## Summary

The blog route accepts both an HTML-shaped slug and the same slug with a `.md` suffix, then loads the same Markdown source for both. Define an explicit URL contract so alternate representations have predictable routing and metadata.

**Human review is required. This issue records repository behavior and a proposed technical direction; it is not implementation or deployment approval.**

## Repository evidence

- `src/website/app/routes/blog/post.tsx` accepts a slug ending in `.md` and loads the same source after stripping the suffix.
- The route constructs post metadata from the incoming, unnormalized slug.
- The current route metadata does not add a post-specific canonical link.

Example pair:

- `https://cua.ai/blog/build-your-own-operator-on-macos-2`
- `https://cua.ai/blog/build-your-own-operator-on-macos-2.md`

## Proposed policy review

1. Normalize the incoming slug before metadata lookup and canonical URL construction.
2. Add a post-specific canonical link for the HTML URL.
3. If `.md` URLs are not a supported public representation, permanently redirect them to the HTML URL.
4. If `.md` URLs are intentional, serve an appropriate Markdown content type and declare the HTML post as canonical, for example with an HTTP `Link` header.
5. Keep internal links, sitemap entries, feeds, and structured metadata on the HTML URL.

Preserve the existing article title and body; this is a routing and metadata issue, not a content rewrite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A maintainer confirms whether public blog `.md` URLs are intentional.
- [ ] Canonical or redirect behavior is selected and tested.
- [ ] Metadata, sitemap/feed URLs, and internal links use the chosen canonical URL.
- [ ] The route-level policy is checked against other blog posts.
- [ ] Any implementation goes through the normal review process.

## Summary

- evaluate permission policies at daemon startup and enforce them at the shared dispatch boundary
- migrate protocol and E2E coverage to the daemon-backed testkit
- repair the Linux, Wayland, Windows, macOS, and standalone-browser regressions exposed by the complete post-merge matrix

## Post-merge regressions fixed

- daemon-backed element-token and capture-scope behavior, including pre-turn rejection
- Wayland/WebKit and Chromium coordinate handling, compositor CDP/browser binding, and pointer/keyboard/frame protocol behavior
- compositor preservation of a background sentinel's focus and PID-only recording fallback
- Linux Edge's remote-debugging consent flow when an otherwise successful AT-SPI action is inert
- macOS and Windows foreground-sentinel setup, including a bounded retry for startup/activation races
