title: [RFC]: Cua Driver SDK-owned runtime and optional services
body:
## Primary area

Cua Driver

## Summary

Make the typed `CuaDriver` SDK and its owned native runtime the default application boundary. Keep private workers and authenticated long-lived services as explicit optional topologies. This RFC supersedes #2447 while retaining its typed SDK, generated binding, private native core, versioned C ABI, and downstream-adapter decisions.

## Motivation and current state

The daemon originally provided useful lifecycle ownership, stable platform identity, shared state, and crash isolation. Requiring that topology for every integration now adds process, socket, version, reconnect, and delegation complexity to applications that already own their automation lifecycle.

The SDK can now construct the native runtime in the importing process. The architecture needs a focused decision about who owns that state, how permission modes are isolated, when MCP can own a runtime, and when a worker or service is still the right boundary.

## Goals

- Make direct SDK creation the documented default.
- Start with one direct runtime per process.
- Put different permission modes in separate runtime-owner processes.
- Keep standalone macOS MCP under the stable CuaDriver.app identity.
- Preserve one typed contract and one authorization path across topologies.
- Define lifecycle, platform, service-authentication, and rollback gates.

## Non-goals

- Remove daemon or service support.
- Support multiple direct runtimes in one process in the first milestone.
- Treat in-process objects as a security boundary against their host.
- Let an agent select or widen its permission mode.
- Change the active protected-consent coverage tracked by #2385.

## Proposal

Applications use `CuaDriver.create(options)` and own one stateful runtime until shutdown. Hosts that need process isolation use a private, non-reattachable worker. Deployments that intentionally serve external clients use an authenticated service.

MCP owns a runtime directly on Windows, Linux, and embedded macOS paths. Standalone installed MCP on macOS continues through CuaDriver.app so TCC grants retain a stable responsible identity. Gateways with mixed permission modes use separate runtime-owner processes, with unrestricted mode requiring explicit launch-time acknowledgement.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep the shared daemon as the default for every integration.
- Delegate mixed permission modes through sessions in one shared daemon.
- Remove every daemon and worker topology.
- Make desktop actions stateless.
- Maintain separate SDK and transport contracts.

The detailed RFC explains why none is the right universal default.

## Compatibility and migration

The rollout is additive. Canonical authorization and a single-runtime guard land first, followed by the direct SDK default, platform-aware MCP ownership, private workers, and authenticated service cleanup. `CuaDriver.connect()` remains available while compatibility use is measured. Each phase can return to service-default documentation without weakening authorization.

## Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Trusted host code selects immutable runtime authorization. Agent-visible arguments, session IDs, environment metadata, and reconnect requests cannot widen it. Different trust levels use separate processes. Service endpoints authenticate peers before accepting runtime work.

Telemetry is limited to topology, versions, generation, permission mode, policy digests, counts, and structured lifecycle outcomes. It excludes screenshots, accessibility trees, typed text, clipboard data, cookies, browser storage, page content, file contents, protected-consent responses, and serializable authority values.

## Validation and acceptance evidence

- Contract parity across Rust, Python, TypeScript, MCP, worker, and service paths.
- Authorization, configuration-precedence, lifecycle, and generation tests.
- macOS TCC attribution and main-thread overlay tests.
- Windows interactive-session and UIAccess boundary tests.
- Linux display, compositor, and Wayland portal-scope tests.
- Service peer-authentication and remote-principal tests.
- Browser and CDP bindings remain generation-scoped.

## Unresolved questions

- Which platform callbacks need an explicit process coordinator?
- What protocol should the private worker use?
- Which daemon administrative tools still need typed SDK replacements?
- What measured usage should precede a future `connect()` deprecation RFC?
- Does any current consumer require mixed permission modes in one shared service after separate workers ship?

## RFC document pull request

#2550

## Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and required evidence, not only an implementation preference.

title: docs: supersede RFC 2447 with SDK-owned runtime RFC
body:
## Summary

- add RFC 2549, making the typed SDK-owned runtime the default application boundary
- make authorization portable as a runtime ceiling plus immutable session contexts
- preserve released behavior through a compatibility session for existing CLI, MCP, daemon, Rust, Python, and TypeScript callers
- require trusted host creation and authenticated action binding before advertising mixed permission modes in one runtime
- retain separate runtime-owner processes as the safe fallback and private workers and authenticated services as explicit optional topologies
- start with one direct runtime per process
- preserve the standalone macOS CuaDriver.app identity while allowing direct ownership for embedded hosts
- keep gRPC, MCP, HTTP, local sockets, and environment forwarding outside the transport-free native runtime and public SDK contract
- coordinate generated remote Driver connections with #2513 without creating a second desktop-control vocabulary
- mark RFC 2447 as superseded while carrying forward its typed SDK, generated binding, native core, and versioned C ABI decisions
- add a diagram-driven north-star note for the target topology and migration path

## Why

RFC 2447 combined the typed SDK contract, ABI direction, runtime ownership, MCP topology, permission-mode isolation, and platform lifecycle into one broad proposal. RFC 2549 keeps the contract decisions that have proven useful and replaces the less focused runtime and process-topology guidance with explicit ownership, lifecycle, platform, authentication, migration, and acceptance gates.

The permission contract is deliberately separated from the process topology. Effective authority is the intersection of an immutable runtime ceiling, an immutable session context, managed policy, and user policy. A model-visible tool argument, public session ID, MCP metadata field, or reconnect token is never authority.

Discussion: #2549
Supersedes: #2447
Related remote-connection proposal: #2513
Canonical authorization prerequisite: #2542
Portable session-authorization foundation: #2545

## Compatibility promise

This refactor is not allowed to disrupt current CLI, MCP, Rust, Python, or TypeScript users. Existing commands, defaults, flags, sockets, platform identity, exit codes, schemas, constructors, typed methods, package exports, result envelopes, structured errors, and lifecycle behavior are explicit release gates.

Released callers that do not use a future trusted host session API inherit a compatibility session with today's behavior and require no source changes. The host-only session factory is additive. Mixed modes are exposed only on topologies whose session-to-action binding passes substitution, replay, expiry, revocation, generation, and reconnect tests.

Browser-use improvements may continue shipping through the current CLI and daemon topology. Canonical dispatch authorization (#2542) and the portable session-authorization foundation (#2545) can land before the larger SDK-owned-runtime refactor; direct SDK ownership, private workers, remote connections, and service cleanup do not block the browser release.

## Security and disclosure review

The public issue, RFC, north-star note, and staged diff were scanned for credentials, private paths, private user or partner context, sensitive screenshots, raw session material, and vulnerability details. The proposal states target security requirements without publishing implementation-state vulnerability claims.

## Validation

- `npm --prefix docs run docs:check-hygiene`
- `npm --prefix docs run docs:check-links`
- `npm --prefix docs run docs:check`
- Markdown whitespace checks for the new and modified RFC files
- staged-file sensitive-content scan
- independent Claude Code Fable architecture review, followed by a blocker-closure review with a ready verdict

title: docs: document monorepo component release resolution
body:
## Summary

- document that Cua's components have independent release streams
- prohibit using GitHub's repository-wide `Latest` badge or `/releases/latest` as component release evidence
- require agents to inspect canonical installers, baked-version precedence, component tag prefixes, and exact release assets
- record Cua Driver's `cua-driver-rs-v*` resolution behavior

## Why

The repository-wide GitHub release badge does not determine what the monorepo's component installers deliver. Release-status claims must reflect the component-specific distribution path users actually invoke.

## Validation

- inspected the Unix and Windows Cua Driver installers on current `origin/main`
- confirmed baked-version precedence and the prefix-filtered GitHub Releases API fallback
- ran `git diff --check`

title: feat(cua-driver): implement SDK-owned runtime RFC

title: Windows installer loses executable-path quotes when enabling autostart for profiles containing spaces
body:
## Summary

On Windows, the cua-driver installer fails to register autostart when the user profile path contains a space, such as `C:\Users\First Last`.

This also blocks callers such as `hermes update` on an Administrator PowerShell window until the user presses Enter.

## Environment

- Windows 11
- cua-driver 0.12.6
- Installer launched from a non-elevated PowerShell session
- Default autostart enabled

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Windows account whose profile path contains a space.
2. From a non-elevated PowerShell session, run the official Windows installer.
3. Approve the UAC request.
4. Observe the elevated PowerShell error.

## Actual result

The elevated process receives an unquoted command similar to:

```powershell
& C:\Users\First Last\...\cua-driver.exe autostart enable
```

PowerShell treats `C:\Users\First` as the command and reports `CommandNotFoundException`.

The installer then waits at:

```text
cua-driver autostart enable failed; press Enter to close
```

The driver files are installed, but `cua-driver autostart status` reports `not-registered`.

## Expected result

The scheduled task should be registered regardless of spaces in the Windows profile path, and a non-interactive caller should not be blocked by a failure prompt.

## Root cause

`Register-CuaDriverAutostart` builds a quoted PowerShell command in `$elevCmd`, then passes it through `Start-Process -ArgumentList`:

https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1#L580-L584

PowerShell documents that `Start-Process` joins ArgumentList values and does not automatically retain outer quotes:

https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/start-process#-argumentlist

## Tested fix direction

Elevating the installed executable directly avoids the second PowerShell command-string boundary:

```powershell
$proc = Start-Process `
    -FilePath $InstalledBinary `
    -ArgumentList @("autostart", "enable") `
    -Verb RunAs `
    -Wait `
    -PassThru `
    -ErrorAction Stop

if ($proc.ExitCode -ne 0) {
    throw "cua-driver autostart enable failed (exit $($proc.ExitCode))"
}
```

This was tested with an executable path containing spaces. Registration returned exit code 0, the `cua-driver-serve` task was created at `RunLevel=Highest`, and `cua-driver status` confirmed the daemon was running.

## Related report

Hermes Agent has the same user-visible failure tracked at:

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/60808

title: fix(cua-driver): declare WinRects support for GNOME Shell 49 and 50
body:
## Problem

`libs/cua-driver/wayland-helper/winrects@cua/metadata.json` declares
`shell-version: ["45","46","47","48"]`, so GNOME Shell 49 and 50 refuse to load
the helper.

Without the helper, cua-driver has no target-addressable activation adapter on
GNOME and — correctly — refuses foreground dispatch:

```
wayland_backend: The RemoteDesktop portal is reachable, but this compositor has
no verified target-activation adapter (foreign-toplevel=false, screencopy=false,
ext-image-copy=false, ext-output-source=false, virtual-pointer=false,
wl_shm=true). Portal/libei input is global and would otherwise affect whichever
window is focused, potentially the wrong application, so cua-driver refuses
foreground dispatch.
```

That makes Linux input effectively unavailable on current Ubuntu — 26.04 LTS
ships GNOME Shell 50.1.

## Change

Metadata only: `shell-version` gains `"49"` and `"50"`. No code change.

## Verification

The extension was installed **unmodified** (only this metadata line differs) on
Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland session, with cua-driver 0.12.6.
The full D-Bus surface was exercised:

| Method | Result on Shell 50.1 |
|---|---|
| load | `gnome-extensions info winrects@cua` -> `State: ACTIVE` |
| `GetVersion` | `u 4` |
| `GetRects` | frame + buffer origins, `focused`, `stacking`, `minimized` per window |
| `Capture` | valid PNG via the Shell screenshot API (correct signature, ~1.1 MB base64) |
| `Activate` | activates the target; `bring_to_front` then returns success where it previously failed with the message above |

End-to-end input, which is what the helper exists for:

```
bring_to_front -> type_text -> press_key Return
```

into a **native GTK4 Wayland** `zenity --entry` returned exactly the typed
string via zenity's stdout, layout-correct on a German QWERTZ keymap
(`Y`/`Z` not transposed, `_` correct).

## Note on 49

50.1 is the version actually tested. 49 is included because the APIs the
extension uses are unchanged across 48-50 — the ESM `Extension` class,
`global.get_window_actors`, `global.display.sort_windows_by_stacking`,
`Meta.Window.get_buffer_rect`, `Shell.Screenshot`,
`Main.layoutManager.addTopChrome`, `Gio.DBusExportedObject` — and a gap between
48 and 50 would be arbitrary. Happy to drop `"49"` if you would rather only
declare versions with a test run behind them.

title: feat(cua-driver): support multiple direct runtimes per process
body:
## Summary

Allow a trusted application process to own more than one direct `CuaDriver` runtime safely.

Today `CuaDriver.create()` / `create_configured()` acquire the process-wide `DIRECT_RUNTIME_ACTIVE` guard. A second runtime returns:

```text
runtime_already_exists: one direct Cua Driver runtime is already active in this process
```

This was the intentional first milestone in [RFC 2549](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/rfcs/2549-cua-driver-sdk-owned-runtime.md): keep one runtime owner until every mutable process-global facility is either runtime-scoped or explicitly coordinated.

## Why this matters

One runtime can already host multiple authorization sessions, including sessions with different allowed modes beneath its ceiling. Multiple runtime objects are still useful for trusted application hosts that need independent lifecycle and resource ownership—for example, separately owned application components or independent private runtime pools—without forcing every runtime into a child process.

This must not be presented as desktop virtualization or a same-process security boundary. The runtimes still control the same physical interactive desktop, and arbitrary code in the host process can inspect or interfere with all of them.

## Required design work

Audit and remove the process-global ownership assumptions that make a second runtime unsafe, including at least:

- session and authorization registries;
- grants, browser/profile bindings, recordings, and resource handles;
- cursor and overlay ownership;
- configuration and policy hooks;
- capture/input backends and platform event-loop state;
- macOS main-thread/TCC responsibility behavior;
- Windows interactive-session and Linux display/AT-SPI coordination.

Each runtime must have an opaque generation. Session IDs, grants, browser references, element handles, recording ownership, and teardown must remain bound to that generation.

Facilities that are inherently OS- or process-global should use an explicit process coordinator rather than silently sharing mutable state.

## Compatibility

- Preserve existing `CuaDriver.create()`, `create_configured()`, `connect()`, CLI, and MCP contracts.
- One-runtime applications should observe no behavioral change.
- Private workers remain the recommended boundary for crash isolation or different trust domains.
- Multiple runtimes in one process remain a coordination feature, not a security boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two direct runtimes can be created concurrently in one process on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
- [ ] Each runtime has a distinct generation and independent shutdown lifecycle.
- [ ] Shutting down or dropping runtime A does not revoke, stop, or corrupt runtime B.
- [ ] Runtime A and B may have different immutable authorization ceilings.
- [ ] Sessions cannot exchange manifests, grants, browser bindings, element handles, recordings, or authority across runtimes.
- [ ] Expiry and revocation in one runtime do not affect the other.
- [ ] Attempts to use cross-runtime or stale-generation references fail closed with structured errors.
- [ ] Concurrent access to the one physical desktop has documented coordination semantics and deterministic tests.
- [ ] Existing single-runtime SDK, CLI, MCP, daemon, and private-worker tests remain green.
- [ ] Representative GUI E2E covers lifecycle isolation on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

## Non-goals

- Treating same-process runtimes as mutually distrusting sandboxes.
- Giving each runtime a separate physical or virtual desktop.
- Removing private-worker or service topologies.
- Allowing agent-visible inputs to construct runtimes or select authorization ceilings.

title: docs(cua-driver): recommend bounded mode for unattended browser use
body:
## Summary

Make bounded mode the recommended Cua Driver configuration for unattended browser use that needs an existing logged-in profile. Reserve unrestricted / `--dangerously-bypass-approvals` for explicitly accepted high-risk environments such as disposable test machines.

The current [Drive a web page](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/docs/content/docs/how-to-guides/driver/drive-a-web-page.mdx) guide demonstrates existing-profile attachment by launching the daemon with:

```bash
cua-driver serve \
  --permission-mode unrestricted \
  --dangerously-bypass-approvals
```

That example is useful as an escape hatch, but its placement can make unrestricted mode look like the normal way to obtain autonomous browser use.

## Recommended documentation hierarchy

Document browser authorization as a clear safety ladder:

1. **Isolated profile + standard mode** for tasks that do not need the user's authenticated browser state.
2. **Existing profile + standard mode** when a certified protected host can collect the initial runtime approval.
3. **Existing profile + bounded mode** for unattended work: the trusted launcher approves one immutable manifest naming the exact browser PID/window, allowed typed browser tools, origins, duration, and idle timeout.
4. **Unrestricted mode** only after explicit launch-time risk acceptance, primarily for disposable or externally isolated environments.

Bounded mode should be described as the preferred alternative to “YOLO” for autonomous browser sessions, not as a synonym for unrestricted operation.

## Required changes

- [ ] Update the browser how-to so unrestricted mode is no longer the primary existing-profile example.
- [ ] Add a complete, copyable bounded session-policy YAML example using the current schema.
- [ ] Show the matching trusted-launch command:

  ```bash
  cua-driver serve \
    --permission-mode bounded \
    --session-policy /trusted/browser-session.yaml \
    --approve-session-policy
  ```

- [ ] Explain how to discover and bind the exact browser `pid` and `window_id` without suggesting that the agent may approve its own manifest.
- [ ] Demonstrate origin-scoped typed browser tools and explain that raw desktop/page tools cannot be allowed in an origin-scoped manifest because they bypass the typed browser-origin adapter.
- [ ] Explain `allow`, `deny`, `ask`, and undeclared behavior. Be explicit that `ask` currently refuses unattended dispatch rather than opening a runtime prompt.
- [ ] State expiry and idle-timeout behavior and what requires a new trusted approval.
- [ ] Keep an unrestricted example in a clearly labeled escape-hatch section with the prompt-injection and authenticated-session risks next to it.
- [ ] Apply the same recommendation consistently across CLI, MCP launcher configuration, and SDK-hosting examples where those surfaces are documented.
- [ ] Link the browser guide to the permission-mode reference and profile-attachment threat model.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user can copy the bounded manifest and launch command, then run a typed browser session restricted to the declared browser identity and origins.
- No primary browser-use quickstart tells users to enable unrestricted mode merely to avoid repeated approval prompts.
- The guide clearly distinguishes interactive `standard`, unattended `bounded`, and explicitly unsafe `unrestricted` behavior.
- Examples match the generated/current tool names and are covered by a docs test, checked fixture, or executable smoke test so schema drift fails CI.
- Documentation remains truthful about current enforcement: broader protected prompts for consequential actions are tracked separately in #2385.

## Related

- #2385 — expand active permission-mode enforcement beyond existing-profile attachment
- #2381 — umbrella permission-mode and bounded-autonomy tracker

title: fix(cua-driver): pick the AT-SPI action by name, not by position
body:
## Problem

On Linux, an AT-SPI element click used `do_action(0)`. Position is not meaning: a GTK4 text view advertises `buffer.delete-line` as action zero, so a routine click could delete a document line while reporting an ordinary click.

## Change

- Select only a named activation action such as `click`, `activate`, `press`, or `toggle`.
- Normalize punctuation and case before matching.
- Preserve the original AT-SPI index when one action-name lookup fails, so the selected name can never address a different action.
- Apply the same safe selection to element-index, window-coordinate, and screen-coordinate click paths.
- Return an error when no safe activation exists, allowing the existing pixel fallback to run instead of reporting a false click.

## Validation

- Added regression coverage for destructive GTK4 editing actions, Chromium activation names, punctuation normalization, and sparse action-name results.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo check -p platform-linux --locked`
- Linux CI and exact Wayland certification are required before merge.

Found while driving a GNOME Wayland desktop with Cua Driver. Companion to #2573.

body:
## Summary

- allow a trusted process to own multiple direct Cua Driver runtimes
- bind sessions, grants, browser references, element tokens, cursor state, recordings, and teardown to an opaque runtime generation
- coordinate inherently process-global desktop input and platform facilities without treating same-process runtimes as a security boundary

- No biometric requirement is introduced; the embedding host chooses its protected renderer.
- Provider identity and grants remain runtime-scoped, including with multiple direct runtimes.

title: bug(cua-driver)(Windows): cannot capture Edge/Chrome — UIA BoundingRectangle empty
body:
**Describe the bug**
`capture(app="Microsoft Edge")` returns "no on-screen window matched" even though the Edge window is visible on screen and `list_apps` correctly lists it.

**Environment**
- cua-driver 0.7.1 on Windows 10 (build 26200)
- Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based)
- `hermes computer-use doctor` — all checks pass

**Root Cause Analysis**

The Edge window's UIA `BoundingRectangle` is `Empty` (0,0,0,0), while Win32 `GetWindowRect` correctly reports the real position:

```
UIA Properties for Edge window (PID 11404):
  IsEnabled:         True
  IsOffscreen:       False
  ControlType:       ControlType.Window
  FrameworkId:       Win32
  NativeWindowHandle: 0x11076A (valid)
  ClassName:         Chrome_WidgetWin_1
  BoundingRectangle: EMPTY          ← THE BUG

Win32 GetWindowRect(hWnd):
  Rect = (200, 52, 1400, 852)       ← correct position
```

`list_apps` returns the window but `capture(app=...)` fails because cua-driver uses UIA BoundingRectangle to determine if a window is "on screen" and to get its bounds. When BoundingRectangle is empty, the window is treated as off-screen.

**Why Edge's UIA BoundingRectangle is empty**

Edge (Chromium) renders via DirectComposition with an off-screen D3D intermediate window:

```
Chrome_WidgetWin_1 (Root, UIA Bounds = Empty)
  └─ Intermediate D3D Window (UIA Bounds = -31992, -32000, 1184, 792)
```

The "Intermediate D3D Window" is placed at extreme negative coordinates for off-screen rendering. This appears to confuse the parent Chrome_WidgetWin_1's UIA BoundingRectangle computation.

**Suggested fix**

When `BoundingRectangle.IsEmpty` is true but `IsOffscreen` is false and `NativeWindowHandle` is valid, fall back to Win32 `GetWindowRect(NativeWindowHandle)` to get the real window bounds. This would also fix potential issues with other Chromium-based applications (Chrome, Brave, Electron apps using D3D rendering).

**Workaround (for users)**
None currently. The window is completely unreachable via cua-driver on Windows.

title: v0.12.5 and v0.12.6 darwin tarballs are missing cua-cursor-theme (install.sh aborts)
body:
## Bug

Running the official macOS install command from the v0.12.5 / v0.12.6 release notes:

```
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh)"
```

fails immediately after extracting the `darwin-universal.tar.gz` asset:

```
note: installing cua-driver via the Rust implementation.
==> using baked release: cua-driver-rs-v0.12.6
==> downloading https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/download/cua-driver-rs-v0.12.6/cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal.tar.gz
==> extracting
error: expected cua-cursor-theme in tarball but didn't find it
```

The same failure reproduces with the `v0.12.5` tag (replacing the URL/VERSION in the install command).

## Expected

`install.sh` should complete, leaving `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` installed and `cua-driver` on PATH.

## Actual

`install.sh` aborts. The user is left on the previously-installed version (e.g. 0.7.1). No CuaDriver.app gets replaced.

## Environment

- macOS 26.4.1 (arm64)
- Tried both v0.12.5 and v0.12.6 darwin-universal tarballs.

## Investigation

### 1. The tarball is missing the file

`tar -tzf` on the published asset:

```
cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal/
cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal/cua_driver_abi.h
cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal/cua_driver_node_runtime.node
cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal/cua-driver
cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal/CuaDriver.app/Contents/_CodeSignature/CodeResources
cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal/CuaDriver.app/Contents/CodeResources
cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal/CuaDriver.app/Contents/Info.plist
cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver   ← only the driver, no cursor-theme
cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal/CuaDriver.app/Contents/Resources/AppIcon.icns
cua-driver-rs-0.12.6-darwin-universal/libcua_driver_sdk.dylib
```

Both the top-level `cua-cursor-theme` binary **and** the `CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-cursor-theme` copy are absent. The v0.12.5 tarball has the same shape (only `cua-driver`, no `cua-cursor-theme`).

The Linux and Windows tarballs may also be affected — I only verified macOS.

### 2. The CD workflow `expects` to ship it

Looking at `.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml`:

- Line 145 (`Package` step for Linux): `cp "target/${TARGET}/release/cua-cursor-theme" "release/${STAGE}/"`
- Line 383–385 (`Create universal binary (lipo)` for macOS): declares `THEME_ARM64` and `THEME_X86` and runs
  `lipo -create "$THEME_ARM64" "$THEME_X86" -output release/universal/cua-cursor-theme`
- Line 444: `cp release/universal/cua-cursor-theme release/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-cursor-theme`
- Line 471: `cp release/universal/cua-cursor-theme "release/${STAGE}/"` in the macOS `Package` loop

So the workflow stages `cua-cursor-theme` at three macOS locations (universal dir, `CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/`, per-arch tarball root) and codesigns it at line ~404. The fact that none of them appear in the published artifact points to one of:

1. The `cursor-theme-cli` crate failed to build for the macOS targets during the `cargo build` step — subsequent `cp` calls silently skipped because the source didn't exist.
2. Something between `release/universal/` and the final `tar` excluded it.

### 3. The cursor-theme binary is a real product artifact

`cua-cursor-theme` is its own crate (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cursor-theme-cli/Cargo.toml`). It's referenced from `rust/crates/cua-driver/src/main.rs` (both `.exe` and unix names). So it's not optional infrastructure — it's part of the driver runtime.

## Suggested fix

Once the root cause is identified, two plausible remedies:

1. Add a CI guard that runs `test -f release/universal/cua-cursor-theme` (and `CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-cursor-theme`) before invoking `tar`, and fails the workflow otherwise.
2. Make `install.sh` warn instead of abort when `cua-cursor-theme` is missing, since the CLI can fall back to the system cursor theme (current behaviour on older releases).

## Workaround until fixed

Stay on the last installed version (`cua-driver --version` still reports it). The driver keeps working — the only thing missing after a manual copy from the tarball would be the bespoke cursor theme.

## Cross-references

- v0.12.5 release: https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.12.5
- v0.12.6 release: https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.12.6
- CD workflow: `.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml`
- Install script: `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh`

body:
## Summary

The representative GNOME/Mutter Wayland E2E lane repeats three failures that prevent a clean certification run even though the rest of the native and standalone-browser coverage succeeds:

1. `linux-electron-child-window-ax-background` changes the foreground window while establishing/verifying a background AX action.

- GNOME/Mutter Wayland user session
- AT-SPI plus the release `portal-input`/libei path
- source-built Cua Driver `0.12.6`

CUA_E2E_HARNESS_FILTER=electron \
  scripts/ci/linux/run-rust-e2e-desktop.sh gnome

  scripts/ci/run-rust-standalone-browser-e2e.sh

title: fix(cua-driver): distrust web keystroke AX read-back
body:
## Problem

On macOS, foreground pixel `type_text` can report a Chromium web editor as confirmed when that verdict comes only from `AXValue`. The renderer may still have ignored the input, so the key-event paths need the same `AXWebArea` distrust already applied to AX writes.

## Change

- Treat AXValue-only read-back from `ax`, `key_events`, and `key_events_fg` as untrusted inside web content.
- Return `verified: false` and `effect: unverifiable` while preserving the existing `page` or first pixel-rung escalation.
- Do not recommend the pixel rung again after a pixel-focus attempt has already run.
- Keep native browser chrome outside `AXWebArea` eligible for trusted read-back.
- Add exhaustive policy tests and a macOS standalone-Chromium row that checks the protocol result and DOM independently.

## Tests

title: fix(cua-driver): restore v0.12.5 and v0.12.6 installs
body:
Fixes #2592.

## What broke

The installer on `main` expects every release archive to contain `cua-cursor-theme`.

That file did not exist when v0.12.5 and v0.12.6 were published. The official install command therefore downloads either release, extracts it, and then stops with this error:

```
error: expected cua-cursor-theme in tarball but didn't find it
```

## What changed

The macOS, Linux, and Windows installers now allow `cua-cursor-theme` to be absent when installing v0.12.6 or older.

Starting with v0.12.7, the file is required. If a new release omits it, installation still stops instead of hiding a broken release.

The release jobs already prevent that mistake: they build the cursor-theme program, copy it into each package, and name it explicitly when creating each archive.

## Verification

- installed the published v0.12.6 macOS archive into a temporary app location; installation completed and `cua-driver --version` reported v0.12.6
- verified the temporary macOS app signature, bundle ID, and version
- installed the published v0.12.6 Windows archive in the Windows sandbox; installation completed and `cua-driver.exe --version` reported v0.12.6
- changed the test threshold to v0.12.6 on both systems and confirmed that the same missing file caused installation to stop
- ran 31 release tests, the shell syntax check, and `git diff --check`

No release or tag was created.

title: fix(cua-driver): declare browser chrome capture coverage
body:
Fixes #2589.

## Root cause

`get_window_state` captures one native window surface. On macOS and Windows, Chromium can composite browser-owned permission UI outside that surface, so a window snapshot cannot prove browser chrome is absent. Linux X11 does not have this gap for the tested notification prompt: its window capture contains the same permission surface as the desktop crop.

## What changed

- Add an additive `capture_coverage.browser_chrome.status: "not_observable_in_window_scope"` capability signal for standalone Chromium browsers on macOS and Windows only.
- Keep the signal conditional: callers continue in window scope until a verified window action is ineffective.
- Return the executable recovery order: `escalate_session(reason="foreground_ineffective")`, fresh `get_desktop_state`, explicit desktop-scoped action if needed, then fresh desktop verification.
- Keep Electron and CEF apps out of the browser classifier.
- Do not emit the signal on Linux, where the certified X11 capture includes the tested browser-owned surface.
- Keep browser-owned permission UI separate from page JavaScript dialogs handled by `browser_dialog`.
- Add a sanitized Chrome/Edge/Chromium fixture and platform-specific pixel assertions.

## Evidence

The prior exact-source interactive run is https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/30279875965 at `03a3f14b830d23434baf5e221e72bae93b60bb04`.

- Linux/X11 Chrome: desktop and window each changed 20,179 pixels. Linux is not affected by this reproduced case.
- Windows Chrome: desktop changed 20,471 pixels; window changed 7,613. The window contains only the address-bar chip while the desktop contains the actionable Allow/Block surface.
- Windows Edge: desktop changed 17,930 pixels; window changed 6,048. The window omits the expanded permission surface visible in the desktop crop.

The earlier 4× comparison incorrectly classified both Windows rows. The regression now requires at least a 2× desktop-to-window difference on affected platforms and asserts material window observability on Linux.

## Validation

Current source: `8a762ec17`, rebased onto `faa0e1e1d`.

Local checks:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core window_inspection --lib`
- `cargo check -p cua-driver --test standalone_browser_behavior_test`
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --test session_capture_scope_test`
- `bash -n scripts/ci/run-rust-standalone-browser-e2e.sh`

The rebase conflicts in the Linux and Windows standalone-browser test lists were resolved by retaining current main's `standalone_browser_type_replace` row and adding this PR's permission row once.

A macOS-to-Windows cross-target check remains blocked locally because the MSVC C sysroot is unavailable. Hosted Windows and Linux interactive lanes will validate the pushed source.

The local macOS interactive row is not claimed: the dedicated local app still needs Accessibility and Screen Recording approval. Those security settings were not changed without explicit user approval.

## Privacy

The routine coverage signal contains fixed capability and recovery codes only. It does not contain prompt text, origin text, button labels, choices, or a claim that a prompt is present.

title: fix(cua-driver): carry full 32-bit snapshot generation in element tokens
body:
## Summary

`element_token` truncated a monotonic 32-bit snapshot generation to 16 bits. The truncated id repeats every 65,536 process-global snapshots. In a long-lived daemon, a repeated id can still exist in another runtime and pid lane, allowing a stale token to resolve to the wrong snapshot instead of failing.

## Change

- Keep the complete 32-bit snapshot generation.
- Render the full value as eight lowercase hexadecimal digits.
- Correct the module contract and collision rationale.

Example:

```text
s00010001:3
```

Tokens remain opaque, process-local, and snapshot-scoped, so widening the prefix does not change a persisted client contract.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core element_token --locked`: 20 passed
- Full Rust and generated-contract CI are required before merge.

This is split from #2210 so the hardening change can be reviewed independently.

title: chore(lume): stop mutating the repository-wide GitHub Latest release
body:
## Problem

The Lume release workflow publishes normal component releases but also passes `--make-latest` to `.github/scripts/github_release.py`.

This repository contains independent release streams such as `lume-v*` and `cua-driver-rs-v*`. A repository-wide GitHub "Latest" pointer cannot accurately represent all of them. Making every Lume release globally latest is therefore misleading for users and unsafe for any generic consumer that assumes `/releases/latest` identifies its own component.

Lume does not need this pointer for its normal install path:

- `libs/lume/scripts/install.sh` prefers the exact `LUME_BAKED_VERSION` updated by Release Please.
- `LUME_VERSION` provides an explicit version override.
- The API fallback scans releases and filters `lume-v*` tags.

## Proposed change

- Continue publishing Lume releases as normal non-prerelease releases.
- Stop passing `--make-latest` from `.github/workflows/cd-swift-lume.yml`.
- Keep installer resolution component-scoped and version-pinned.
- Audit and remove the unused `LATEST_RELEASE_URL` constant if it is no longer referenced.
- Update workflow comments or release documentation that imply the repository-wide Latest pointer is authoritative.

## Acceptance criteria

- A Lume release is published with `prerelease: false` and `make_latest: false`.
- The release contains the expected notarized assets and metadata.
- The baked-version install path still resolves the exact `lume-v*` tag.
- The explicit `LUME_VERSION` override still works.
- The component-scoped fallback still selects the highest valid Lume version without relying on `/releases/latest`.
- Tests confirm that publishing Lume does not change the repository-wide GitHub Latest pointer.

## Context

This is release hygiene for a monorepo with independent component tags. It is separate from changing how any component installer chooses versions.

title: cua-driver: prefer foreground delivery in refusal guidance
body:
## Problem

Some `background_unavailable` refusals tell an agent to call `bring_to_front` and then retry with `delivery_mode:"foreground"`.

That guidance conflicts with the intended action ladder:

- retry the action directly with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` when action-scoped activation is acceptable
- reserve `bring_to_front` for the narrower case where a focus-proxy surface must remain persistently foreground across interactions

The current wording encourages an unnecessary extra tool call, changes foreground posture for longer than needed, and makes integrators treat persistent activation as a normal escalation rung.

## Reproduction

1. Target a Windows WPF keystroke or a Linux target with no focus-free input backend.
2. Request the action with `delivery_mode:"background"`.
3. Observe a structured `background_unavailable` refusal whose remediation begins with `bring_to_front`.

The behavior is reproducible on current `main` after #2616.

## Expected

The primary remediation should be:

> Retry this action with `delivery_mode:"foreground"`.

`bring_to_front` should appear only as an additional suggestion when the target is a known focus-proxy surface that needs persistent activation, such as a remote desktop client.

## Relevant locations

- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/input/delivery.rs`
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/input/delivery.rs`
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/WINDOWS.md`
- generated MCP tool descriptions and public delivery documentation

This complements #2206, which tracks the action-scoped foreground contract itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generic `background_unavailable` errors recommend direct foreground delivery first.
- [ ] Generic refusal text does not make `bring_to_front` part of the normal action ladder.
- [ ] Persistent activation guidance remains available for documented focus-proxy cases.
- [ ] Windows and Linux unit tests assert the revised remediation.
- [ ] Generated tool descriptions and public docs use the same terminology.

title: Cua Driver daemon exits during sustained Linux Python SDK sessions
body:
## Summary

A release-pinned Cua Driver daemon can exit during a sustained Linux GUI session, after which the release-matched Python SDK reports a Unix-socket connection refusal. This reproduced on two independent disposable Ubuntu x86_64 VMs.

## Environment

- Cua Driver: `0.12.6` (`cua-driver-rs-v0.12.6`)
- Python SDK: release-matched `0.12.6` native library
- Guest: Ubuntu x86_64, X11, AT-SPI available
- Daemon: one fresh process per session, explicit Unix socket, unrestricted startup permission mode
- Startup checks: `cua-driver doctor`, version, socket probe, and initial Python SDK smoke call all passed

## Reproduction pattern

1. Start a fresh daemon with an explicit Unix socket.
2. Connect through `CuaDriver.connect(...)` from the release-matched Python SDK.
3. Start one session.
4. Run a serial loop of fresh window inventory/snapshot calls and grounded GUI actions.
5. Continue for a long-running workload (roughly 60–80 observe/action cycles).

The failure occurred independently after approximately 76 cycles and 63 cycles. Both sessions started from fresh daemon processes with different PIDs.

## Actual behavior

A subsequent `list_windows` call fails with:

```text
cua_driver._native.DriverError.Transport:
socket_path='<explicit socket>',
reason='connect to <explicit socket>: Connection refused (os error 111)'
```

The SDK caller and native library were still present and executable. The failure was the daemon/socket endpoint, not a missing SDK installation. Retrying the RPC cannot recover because the process is no longer accepting connections.

## Expected behavior

The daemon should remain available for the lifetime of a valid long-running session. If an internal failure occurs, it should preserve an actionable exit/crash report instead of leaving callers with only a generic socket refusal.

## Impact

Long-running GUI workflows are invalidated late in execution, after model/API cost and many successful actions. Freshening the daemon before each workload reduces cross-workload accumulation but does not prevent the within-session exit.

## Suggested investigation / acceptance criteria

- Preserve daemon stderr, exit status, and panic/crash diagnostics for this path.
- Add a Linux stress test that runs at least 100 serial Python SDK inventory/snapshot/action cycles against one fresh daemon.
- Confirm the daemon remains alive and the session can end cleanly.
- If a fatal internal error is injected, return or persist a structured diagnostic that distinguishes daemon exit from a transient transport failure.

title: cua-driver (macOS): AX actions on non-frontmost apps silently no-op — the `AXEnabled` guard from #1386 is missing in the Rust port
body:
## Summary

`perform_ax_action` dispatches `AXUIElementPerformAction` without checking `AXEnabled`. When the target app is not frontmost, macOS returns `kAXErrorSuccess` but nothing happens, so the driver reports `✅ Performed AXPress/AXPick on [N] ...` for an action that did not occur.

This is the same "ghost click" failure that #1386 diagnosed and fixed in the Swift implementation:

> Chrome's `commandDispatch` marks Developer submenu items as `AXEnabled = false` when the app is not frontmost. `AXUIElementPerformAction` returns `.success` regardless, so clicks silently no-op — the agent sees ✅ but nothing changes.

The fix there was "check `AXEnabled` before dispatching any AX action; bail with a clear `❌` error". That guard did not carry over into `crates/platform-macos`.

It is not Chrome-specific — it reproduces on stock TextEdit menus.

## Environment

- `cua-driver-rs` 0.12.6 (`darwin-universal`, `CuaDriver.app`)
- macOS 27.0 (Darwin 27.0.0), Apple Silicon
- Accessibility + Screen Recording + direct capture all granted to `com.trycua.driver`

## Reproduction

1. Open TextEdit with any document. Leave another app frontmost.
2. `get_window_state(pid, window_id)` → note the index of `AXMenuItem "Zoom"` under `AXMenuBarItem "Window"`.
3. `list_windows(pid)` → record the document window's `bounds`.
4. `click(pid, window_id, element_index=<Zoom>)`.
5. `list_windows(pid)` → bounds are unchanged.

Every variant reports success and changes nothing:

| Call | Result | Window bounds |
|---|---|---|
| `click(element_index)` | `✅ Performed AXPress on [310] AXMenuItem "Zoom".` | unchanged |
| open parent menu first, then click child | both `✅` | unchanged |
| `click(action:"pick")` | `✅ Performed AXPick on [310] AXMenuItem "Zoom".` | unchanged |
| `click(scope:"desktop", action:"pick")` | `✅` | unchanged |
| `click(scope:"desktop")` | `✅` | unchanged |
| `click(delivery_mode:"foreground", action:"pick")` | `✅` | unchanged |
| `click(action:"show_menu")` | `AXShowMenu returned -25200` | unchanged |

`structuredContent` is `{"effect":"unverifiable","path":"ax","verified":false}` throughout — correct, but the `✅ Performed ...` text still asserts the action happened.

**With an explicit `bring_to_front(pid)` first, the same `pick` works:** bounds go `656x422` → `1512x949`.

Control: Peekaboo 3.9.8 `menu click --app TextEdit --path "Window > Zoom"` works without fronting (`656x422` → `2238x1266`), so the menu item itself is not a no-op.

## Root cause

`crates/platform-macos/src/input/ax_actions.rs`:

```rust
pub fn perform_ax_action(element_ptr: usize, action: &str) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let ax_action = map_action(action);
    let err = unsafe { perform_action(element_ptr as AXUIElementRef, ax_action) };

    if err == kAXErrorSuccess {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        anyhow::bail!("AXUIElementPerformAction({action}) failed with error {err}")
    }
}
```

No `AXEnabled` check. The attribute is already collected one layer up — `crates/platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs:425`:

```rust
enabled: copy_bool_attr(element, "AXEnabled"),
```

and carried on `ControlState`/node as `enabled: Option<bool>`, so the data needed for the #1386 guard is present at snapshot time; only the check at dispatch time is missing.

## Suggested fix

1. In `perform_ax_action` (or its caller, where the cached node with `enabled` is in scope), bail when `enabled == Some(false)` with a message naming the cause and suggesting `bring_to_front`, matching #1386's behaviour.
2. Consider why `delivery_mode:"foreground"` does not make this work while an explicit `bring_to_front` does — per its own docs it should "briefly front the window, act, let transient UI settle, then restore". If fronting happens after the element is resolved, or is restored before the AX action lands, menus will keep failing in the mode that is supposed to handle exactly this.
3. Optional: soften the `✅ Performed <action> on [N] <role>` wording for `verified:false` results so it states what was dispatched rather than what was achieved.

Related: #2022 (Linux/X11 pixel click silently ignored), #2574 (AT-SPI action picked by position rather than name), #1895 (scroll should prefer AX actions).

title: fix(cua-driver): prefer direct foreground retry guidance
body:
## Problem

Generic `background_unavailable` responses on Windows and Linux recommended `bring_to_front` before a foreground retry. That turns a one-action escalation into persistent activation and encourages an unnecessary tool call.

## Change

- make the primary remediation `Retry this action with delivery_mode:"foreground".`
- cover both Windows refusal builders and every Linux refusal reason
- reserve `bring_to_front` guidance for known focus-proxy workflows
- align MCP descriptions and platform docs, including the current best-effort Windows restore timing

## Tests

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: fix(cua-driver): verify set_value writes with an AXValue read-back
body:
## Summary

`set_value` treated a successful AX write as proof that the value reached the application. Chromium, WebKit, and Electron can echo an accessibility write even when the renderer did not accept it, so that could produce a false `verified: true`.

## Change

- Read AXValue before and after the write.
- Trust a matching read-back only on native surfaces.
- Downgrade AXWebArea results to unverified and provide the appropriate browser or pixel escalation.
- Return the standard structured action contract: `path`, `verified`, `effect`, and optional `escalation`.
- Use the unverified message marker instead of a success checkmark when confirmation is unavailable.
- Compare values numerically only for numeric controls, using a bounded relative tolerance.
- Preserve the original before-value when verifying the slider stepping fallback.

The AXPopUpButton path remains unverified because it selects a menu item instead of writing AXValue directly.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p platform-macos --locked`: 193 passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- Live macOS native and web-surface checks are required before merge.

This is split from #2210 so the verification change can be reviewed independently.

title: fix(cua-driver): prefer foreground delivery in refusal guidance
body:
## Summary

- make direct `delivery_mode:"foreground"` retry the primary remediation for Windows and Linux background refusals
- reserve `bring_to_front` for persistent focus-proxy sessions such as RDP
- add native-platform assertions and align the Windows skill and public delivery docs
- execute the pure Windows delivery tests in CI instead of only compiling them

## Root cause

The refusal guidance conflated action-scoped foreground delivery with persistent activation. That encouraged an extra tool call and left the target foreground longer than necessary.

## User impact

Agents now retry only the refused action in foreground mode. The driver activates the target for that action and restores the prior foreground. Persistent activation remains available for surfaces that truly require it across multiple calls.

## Validation

title: feat(cua-driver): browser_type can replace a field's content, not only append
body:
## Summary

`browser_type` previously inserted only at the current selection. A caller
could not safely set or clear a field that already contained text, so retries
could silently duplicate the value.

This change adds optional `replace: true` behavior:

- select the complete editable value immediately before delivery;
- type through the normal `beforeinput` and `input` event path;
- clear a selected value when `text` is empty;
- refuse replacement when a safe complete selection cannot be proven;
- report `replace` and `replaced_chars` in the result.

The existing append behavior remains unchanged when `replace` is absent or
false.

## Safety and correctness

- Replacement supports text inputs, textareas, and contenteditable elements.
- Unsupported input types fail closed with `browser_action_unavailable`.
- Unicode character counts use Unicode scalar values instead of UTF-16 code
  units.
- In inactive or occluded Chromium tabs, temporary focus emulation keeps the
  select-and-deliver sequence bound to the exact ref without selecting the tab.
- Selection, editability, focus ownership, binding, and ref freshness are
  revalidated before delivery.

## Documentation

- Updated the browser skill guide.
- Updated the public browser how-to.
- Regenerated the MCP tool reference from the canonical schema.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --locked`
- standalone browser test target compiled on macOS
- repository CI across Linux, macOS, Windows, generated contracts, docs, and
  policy checks
- exact-source standalone browser behavior matrix on macOS, including append,
  replace with `insert_text`, replace with `keystrokes`, empty-text clearing,
  unsupported-type refusal, and value preservation after refusal

The standalone browser test is also listed explicitly in both the Unix and
Windows E2E runners so it cannot be silently omitted from release
certification.

title: feat(cua-driver): animate drag as a continuous point-to-point gesture
body:
## Problem

The agent cursor currently represents `drag` with the same general movement treatment used for ordinary pointer travel. During a real drag, this does not clearly communicate the gesture from source to destination or distinguish press, hold, travel, and release.

## Desired behavior

Render a drag as one continuous point-to-point gesture driven by the real action arguments:

1. Move to the source point.
2. Enter the drag state when the button is pressed.
3. Keep the drag treatment active while the overlay follows the dispatched path from `from_x/from_y` to `to_x/to_y`.
4. Show a subtle release or drop response at the destination.
5. Return to idle only after the real action completes.

The animation should use `duration_ms` and `steps` where available so the overlay stays synchronized with the dispatched gesture instead of playing a separate generic glide.

## Requirements

- Preserve the drag semantic icon throughout the held movement.
- Avoid a generic move animation or visual teleport between the source and destination.
- Compose correctly with background/foreground, AX/pixel, browser/desktop, and session-color treatments.
- Support left, right, and middle-button drag variants without requiring separate themes.
- Respect reduced-motion mode with an understandable low-motion fallback.
- Keep the behavior consistent across macOS, Windows, and Linux renderers.
- Keep custom cursor themes compatible through the existing semantic drag state rather than adding a required new icon.

## Acceptance criteria

- A real `drag` action visibly traverses the complete source-to-destination path while the drag state remains active.
- Press, travel, and release phases are ordered and synchronized with native input delivery.
- The action gallery includes a deterministic point-to-point drag preview.
- Automated tests cover interpolation, lifecycle ordering, reduced motion, and modifier composition.
- Cross-platform video or visual evidence confirms the result on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

title: COSMIC: cua-driver advertises ScreenReaderEnabled and launches Orca
body:
## Bug description

On Pop!_OS COSMIC, starting `cua-driver serve` sets `org.a11y.Status.ScreenReaderEnabled=true`. COSMIC treats that property as an explicit request to start the screen reader and launches `/usr/bin/orca`, which in turn socket-activates Speech Dispatcher.

This is the same class of bug fixed for GNOME in #2010 / `8114e17`, but the current desktop guard recognizes only `GNOME`. Since `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=COSMIC`, COSMIC falls through to `AdvertiseMode::All` and still advertises a screen reader.

## Environment

- OS: Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS
- Desktop: COSMIC
- Session: Wayland with XWayland (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`, `DISPLAY=:1`)
- `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=COSMIC`
- cua-driver: `0.12.6` (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`)
- Hermes Agent using cua-driver over MCP

## Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure the screen-reader flags are off:

   ```bash
   gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-reader-enabled

   gdbus call --session \
     --dest org.a11y.Bus \
     --object-path /org/a11y/bus \
     --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get \
     org.a11y.Status ScreenReaderEnabled
   ```

   Both reported `false` in this session.

2. Start the daemon normally:

   ```bash
   cua-driver serve
   ```

3. Observe COSMIC launch Orca and Speech Dispatcher immediately.

## Actual behavior

The journal shows the daemon and Orca starting in the same second:

```text
14:29:56  cua-driver serve started
14:29:57  cosmic-session[2520]: starting process ' WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 DISPLAY=:1 XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland GTK_MODULES=gail:atk-bridge QT_ACCESSIBILITY=1 ... /usr/bin/orca '
14:29:57  systemd[2474]: Started speech-dispatcher.service - Common interface to speech synthesizers.
14:29:57  speech-dispatcher[116448]: Speech Dispatcher 0.12.0-rc2 starting
```

There was no `hotkey`, `press_key`, or other input action preceding the launch; merely starting `cua-driver serve` reproduced it.

## Expected behavior

Starting cua-driver should enable generic AT-SPI inspection without claiming that a screen reader is active or launching Orca.

## Root cause

The current desktop default in [`platform-linux/src/a11y.rs`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/a11y.rs) special-cases only GNOME:

```rust
let is_gnome = desktop.is_some_and(|desktop| {
    desktop
        .split([':', ';'])
        .any(|part| part.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case("gnome"))
});
if is_gnome {
    AdvertiseMode::IsEnabledOnly
} else {
    AdvertiseMode::All
}
```

For `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=COSMIC`, this selects `AdvertiseMode::All`, which writes `ScreenReaderEnabled=true`.

COSMIC explicitly monitors that property and starts Orca when it becomes true: [`cosmic-session/src/a11y.rs`](https://github.com/pop-os/cosmic-session/blob/master/src/a11y.rs).

## Verified workaround

Starting the daemon with:

```bash
CUA_DRIVER_RS_A11Y_ADVERTISE_MODE=is_enabled_only cua-driver serve
```

produces the desired state:

```text
IsEnabled=(<true>,)
ScreenReaderEnabled=(<false>,)
```

With that mode:

- Orca does not start.
- Speech Dispatcher does not start.
- `hermes computer-use doctor` still reports both AT-SPI inspection and screen capture as functional.
- A live Computer Use MCP call completes without a new Orca launch event.

## Suggested fix

Treat COSMIC like GNOME for the default advertisement mode, and add a regression test:

```rust
#[test]
fn cosmic_default_does_not_claim_a_screen_reader() {
    assert_eq!(
        advertise_mode_from(false, None, Some("COSMIC")),
        AdvertiseMode::IsEnabledOnly
    );
}
```

A broader safety improvement may be to default unknown desktops to `IsEnabledOnly`, requiring an explicit `CUA_DRIVER_RS_A11Y_ADVERTISE_MODE=all` where `ScreenReaderEnabled` is genuinely necessary. The minimal fix is adding COSMIC to the existing non-screen-reader guard.

title: fix(cua-driver): avoid leaking XInput masters without uinput
body:
## Summary

- require read/write access to `/dev/uinput` before selecting the Linux real-pointer path
- acquire the uinput device before mutating the XInput hierarchy
- cover the capability gate with a focused Linux unit test

## Root cause

`ensure_master_pointer` called `XIAddMaster` before opening `/dev/uinput`. When `/dev/uinput` was inaccessible, every native input attempt created a new XInput master pair and returned before recording it for cleanup. Sustained sessions accumulated abandoned masters until Xorg terminated the daemon connection with `BadAlloc`.

## User impact

Linux X11 sessions now fall back without mutating the XInput hierarchy when real-pointer injection cannot be initialized, instead of failing late after many otherwise successful actions.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- native Linux focused test at exact head SHA `a4e884b1137cd2fce0d5226d33dd93c548443787`: 1 passed
- Azure Debian 13 x86_64 VM, Xorg 21.1.16 with dummy video driver (not Xvfb), `/dev/uinput` absent
- exact-SHA daemon binary SHA-256: `79017c6e72196ac8c29289746ded3ac7605dd4e4d55c33ca9966f00aaaf2200d`
- 120 serial background right-click actions completed in one window-scoped session
- daemon PID `22751` remained alive at every 20-action checkpoint and final `list_windows` succeeded
- XInput master pointer count stayed at 1 before, throughout, and after the run
- zero `BadAlloc`, uinput, MPX-fallback, or permission-denied log entries
- daemon, target app, window manager, and Xorg were stopped cleanly after evidence capture

Fixes #2618

title: fix(lume): distinguish running VMs from resize recovery
body:
## Summary

- classify resize-guard contention using the resize transaction marker as the authoritative signal
- report a running VM when the guard is busy without a marker instead of prescribing an impossible rollback
- keep the interrupted-resize recovery error when a transaction marker is present
- use operation-neutral wording for the existing `vmRunning` error because delete, clone, and push now use it

## Root cause

A running VM intentionally holds the resize guard for its lifetime. Controller operations treated every failed guard acquisition as an interrupted resize, even though the separate resize marker is what records an armed transaction. This sent users who had never resized the VM into a rollback loop.

## Validation

- exact head SHA `56944cffcdeb0756391797f4a58b787cb8ca64cf`
- source-built Lume 0.4.0 binary SHA-256 `1a6c028a01ad397694f61f71175162f5d651d84653358e7a1de6b432facd9b21`

- VM remained running and SSH-available after the refusal; Cua Driver captured before/after Screen Sharing state and ended its isolated proof session

title: fix(cua-bench): share platform image resolution
body:
## What

- Add one shared registry for CUA-Bench's built-in platform configuration.
- Use it from the CLI, local environment provider, two-container runner, interactive
  runner, and Daytona runner.
- Preserve explicit Docker image overrides while keeping QEMU guest-disk names
  separate from the host container image.
- Bind the XFCE `computer_server` to `0.0.0.0` so its published Docker port is
  reachable.

## Why

A real KiCad task exposed two independent failures before task execution:

1. CUA-Bench had three platform maps that disagreed. The CLI and local provider
   resolved `linux-docker` to `trycua/cua-xfce:latest`, while `TaskRunner` resolved it
   to the unavailable `nikri/kicad-snorkel:20260316b` image.
2. After selecting the public XFCE image, its Computer API still could not be reached
   through Docker. The current `computer_server` defaults to `127.0.0.1` and requires
   `--host 0.0.0.0` for external access.

This meant `cb run task ... --platform linux-docker` could not reach task setup even
though the repository already contained a suitable public KiCad image.

## How

- Move the built-in definitions to `cua_bench.platforms`.
- Resolve a platform's container image through `resolve_container_image()` at every
  runner boundary.
- For `linux-docker`, let an explicit image URI replace the built-in default.
- For QEMU platforms, continue treating the supplied image name as the guest disk
  identity and use the platform's configured host image.
- Start the XFCE Computer API with `--host 0.0.0.0`.

Unknown platforms and inaccessible explicit images still fail explicitly. There is no
fallback to a different image.

## Validation

Automated checks:

- `uv run --directory libs/cua-bench ruff check cua_bench`
- `uv run --directory libs/cua-bench pytest cua_bench/tests -q`: **140 passed**
- `bash -n libs/xfce/src/scripts/start-computer-server.sh`
- `git diff --check`

Live positive control:

- Ran `cua-bench-kicad/55f2eefb` through the real two-container
  `cb run task --oracle --wait` path.
- Task setup completed and captured a 222,131-byte screenshot.
- The declared oracle completed.
- Native netlist evaluation passed components, nets, and net names, returning **1.0**.
- The trace was persisted and the task containers and network were cleaned up.

The published `trycua/cua-xfce:latest` manifest is currently amd64-only, so the Apple
Silicon validation used `linux/amd64`. Multi-architecture publication is a separate
packaging concern from the resolver and API binding fixes in this PR.

title: fix(cua-driver): bind macOS state and actions to requested windows
body:
## Summary

- bind macOS AX state, screenshots, and action caches to the requested CGWindowID
- refuse stale and foreign-owner window ids instead of returning a healthy-looking unrelated tree
- preserve truthful AX state when screenshot geometry cannot be proven
- isolate resize and element-token state by `(pid, window_id)`
- recognize AppKit Open/Save panels as dialog scopes so their snapshots do not inherit the application menu bar

## Why

A requested macOS window could previously fall through to unrelated application AX roots, including the menu bar, or pair a child-panel tree with parent-window pixels. That made stale ids and Open/Save panels look actionable while coordinates and element caches belonged to a different surface.

## Exact macOS validation

Certified at head `1cd83749d50e5a472b5e26f5ce0ee25236e8f467` in a fresh logged-in Tahoe VM:

- exact release build was installed into the signed test app; source and embedded executable had identical pre-sign SHA-256 `f48d58bd136025021574013e8e6093bb22abe728ebdcc18aa4f21b689fc2573e`
- daemon reported its own `com.trycua.driver.local` identity with Accessibility and Screen Recording both granted
- normal TextEdit window: 586x488 coherent capture, `screenshot_scale=1`, `screenshot_frame_valid=true`, application menu retained
- AppKit Open panel: 880x448 coherent capture, root `AXWindow` id `open-panel`, 66 scoped elements, no `AXMenuBar`
- a foreign System Settings window id returned `window_owner_pid_mismatch` with the actual owner and exact retry pid
- a fabricated id returned `window_id_not_found`
- two same-PID TextEdit windows remained isolated: writing `WINDOW_4244_ONLY` to one was AX-confirmed while the other retained `ladderladderladder`
- `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` — 238 passed
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test protocol_tools_call_test get_window_state_returns_both_with_opt_out` — passed
- `cargo build --locked --release -p cua-driver` — passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed

Closes #2237.

title: fix(cua-bench): wire resolve_container_image into LocalEnvironmentProvider
body:
`LocalEnvironmentProvider.start()` accepted an `image_name` override but always ran `config["image"]` for `linux-docker`, making the override a no-op even though `resolve_container_image()` was introduced in this same PR.

## Changes

- **`local_environment.py`**
  - Import `resolve_container_image` from `cua_bench.platforms`
  - Replace `docker_image = config["image"]` with `docker_image = resolve_container_image(platform, image_name)` in `start()`
  - Thread the resolved image through to `_build_docker_cmd()` as an explicit parameter instead of re-deriving from `config["image"]` inside that method
  - Initialize `image_path = None` before the `image_marker` guard to prevent `UnboundLocalError` on `linux-docker` (no marker → variable never assigned)

- **`tests/test_task_runner.py`**
  - Fix indentation bug introduced in PR #2644: the `assert` verifying the resolved image was placed at module level outside the async function, causing `NameError` at collection time

With these changes, passing an explicit image URI to `LocalEnvironmentProvider.start()` on `linux-docker` now selects that image, consistent with the behavior already wired into `TaskRunner`:

```python
env_info = await provider.start("linux-docker", image_name="ghcr.io/my-org/custom-xfce:latest")
# Previously always launched trycua/cua-xfce:latest; now launches the override
```

title: Install script fails: baked version 0.13.0 does not exist on GitHub Releases (404)
body:
## Bug

The install script on `main` ([`_install-rust.sh` line 515](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh#L515)) has `CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION="0.13.0"` (set by `x-release-please-version`), but there is no `cua-driver-rs-v0.13.0` release on GitHub Releases. The latest published release is `cua-driver-rs-v0.12.6`.

This causes the default install command to fail with a **404**:

```
$ /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh)"
note: installing cua-driver via the Rust implementation.
==> using baked release: cua-driver-rs-v0.13.0
==> downloading https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/download/cua-driver-rs-v0.13.0/cua-driver-rs-0.13.0-darwin-universal.tar.gz
curl: (56) The requested URL returned error: 404
error: download failed; try CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION=<version> to pin a specific release
```

## Root Cause

It appears that release-please bumped the version in `_install-rust.sh` to `0.13.0` on `main`, but the corresponding release was never created (or the release workflow failed / was skipped). The baked version on `main` now points at a non-existent release.

## Workaround

Pin the version manually:

```bash
CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION=0.12.6 /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh)"
```

## Expected Behavior

The default install command should either:
1. Download a release that actually exists, or
2. Fall back to the GitHub Releases API to find the latest published release when the baked version returns a 404 (instead of hard-failing)

## Environment

title: test(cua-driver): make macOS release certification hermetic across reruns
body:
## Problem

The macOS release-certification runner can inherit worker state that makes an exact-SHA rerun less reliable than the first run.

Observed failure modes during 0.13.0 certification:

- stale Rust target artifacts caused duplicate Swift bridge symbols until the cache was isolated
- the status probe used a short-circuiting `grep -q` pipeline under `pipefail`, which could close stdout early and trigger a broken-pipe panic in the CLI
- a restored standard daemon could remain active when a targeted retry expected the disposable unrestricted daemon
- an Electron foreground drag fixture missed its drop once, then passed on repeated isolated retries

The product behavior remained correct, but the runner required manual state isolation and targeted retries to establish that.

## Expected

An exact-SHA macOS release-certification run should:

1. use a run-owned build/cache namespace, or validate and clean only incompatible artifacts
2. probe daemon status without closing the producer pipe early
3. own daemon startup, socket selection, permission mode, watchdog, and restoration for the whole run
4. support a documented single-cell retry that preserves exact source and daemon identity
5. distinguish a fixture timing miss from a persistent product failure in its report

## Acceptance criteria

- Two consecutive runs from the same exact SHA do not depend on prior worker build state.
- Status checks cannot cause broken-pipe panics.
- Targeted retries start and verify the required daemon mode automatically.
- The final report records initial failure and retry evidence without turning a real persistent failure into a pass.
- The runner still restores the normal worker daemon after success or failure.

title: Codex routes explicit cua-driver request to built-in computer-use skill
body:
## Summary

In a Codex session on macOS, an explicit request to use `cua-driver` was initially routed to the bundled Codex `computer-use` skill (`node_repl + sky`) instead of the available `mcp__cua_driver` tools.

This report is primarily a heads-up about discoverability and tool-routing behavior in Codex integrations.

## Reproduction

1. Have both the bundled Codex computer-use integration and the cua-driver MCP available.
2. Ask Codex: `using cua-driver can u open whatsapp ...`
3. Codex matches the prominently listed `computer-use:computer-use` skill.
4. The skill instructs Codex to use `node_repl` and the Sky runtime for all computer interactions.
5. Codex begins that workflow without first discovering or selecting the deferred `mcp__cua_driver` tools.
6. After the user explicitly corrects it, Codex searches for and finds the cua-driver MCP namespace.

## Expected behavior

An explicit mention of the tool name `cua-driver` should route directly to the cua-driver MCP integration, ahead of a generic computer-use capability match.

## Observed surface-level cause

There is a discoverability asymmetry in the Codex tool surface:

- `computer-use:computer-use` is visible as an installed skill and directly matches local Mac app control.
- Its `SKILL.md` mandates `node_repl + sky` for computer-use actions.
- cua-driver is available as a deferred MCP tool that must first be found through tool search.
- No cua-driver skill was visible in the Codex skill catalog for this session.
- The cua-driver MCP metadata says to prefer its detailed skill when one is loaded, but that skill was not loaded or advertised.

The explicit user request should still have won, so this is not necessarily a cua-driver runtime bug. It may be addressable through integration metadata and packaging.

## Suggestions

- Ship or advertise a Codex-compatible cua-driver skill so it appears alongside other computer-use skills.
- Add strong trigger language for exact mentions such as `cua-driver`, `mcp__cua_driver`, and `use CUA driver`.
- Document that users or harnesses should prioritize the exact named integration over generic computer-use skills.
- If possible, test Codex coexistence with its bundled computer-use skill to catch routing collisions.

## Environment

- Host: macOS
- Harness: Codex
- cua-driver exposed through MCP deferred tool discovery
- Date observed: 2026-07-29

Happy to provide additional metadata if there is a preferred integration diagnostic to capture.

title: fix(cua-driver): avoid false foreground-click failure after Edge chrome action succeeds
body:
## Summary

A desktop-scope foreground click on Microsoft Edge's browser-owned notification indicator can successfully open the permission panel and still return an error:

> The foreground click did not activate its target window.

This makes the action result contradict the externally visible effect.

## Reproduction

1. Launch Edge with a fresh profile on the `windows-latest` hosted runner.
2. Trigger `Notification.requestPermission()` from the page.
3. Escalate the window session to desktop observation.
4. Click the changed browser-chrome indicator with `scope: "desktop"`.
5. Observe the permission panel open, while the `click` result has `isError: true`.

The exact-tag standalone-browser workflow reproduced this on two independent attempts at `3cf5cc1bd701d7c41d823cf995740dc7678200a0`:

- https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/30465760684
- https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/30465760684/attempts/2

Both reports had 31 delivered cases, 2 expected refusals, and this single failed Edge case. Chrome's equivalent permission-control case passed, and every other Edge case passed.

## Evidence

The recorded behavior shows the Edge “Notifications blocked” panel open after the click. The failure is emitted afterward by the foreground root-window equality check in `platform-windows/src/input/mouse.rs`, so delivery succeeded but verification reported an error.

## Expected

A foreground click that visibly opens the targeted transient browser-chrome surface should not be returned as a failed action. The post-click activation check should account for browser-owned transient surfaces or otherwise verify delivery without producing a false-negative result.

title: fix(cua-driver): accept owned foreground windows after clicks
body:
## What changed

- compare the foreground window and click target by Win32 root-owner activation family after a foreground click
- accept browser-owned transient windows, such as Edge's permission panel, when they belong to the clicked browser
- retain the failure for missing or unrelated foreground windows
- add focused Windows regression coverage for same-root, owned-transient, unrelated, and missing-foreground cases

## Root cause

The click was delivered and Edge opened its browser-owned permission panel, but the postcondition compared `GA_ROOT` handles. Owned transient browser chrome can have a different root handle from the browser window even though both are in the same activation family, producing a false delivery error.

## Impact

Successful foreground clicks that open browser-owned transient chrome no longer report a false activation failure. Clicks that leave an unrelated window foreground still fail closed.

## Checks

- `git diff --check`
