title: fix(cua-driver): allow UIA ValuePattern type_text on Chromium when el…
body:
…ement_index is provided

When element_index is supplied, the type_text tool already has a working UIA ValuePattern.SetValue path that handles Chromium/Electron background text input correctly. However, the would_be_silently_dropped() pre-check unconditionally refuses all Chromium background TextInput events, blocking the UIA path before it can be reached.

Add elem_idx.is_none() guard so indexed elements bypass the Chromium pre-check and reach the UIA ValuePattern code path.

title: lume: standardize CLI logging and progress rendering (pull output is unreadable)
body:
## Summary `lume`'s terminal output is noisy and visually broken. Log lines and in-place progress bars are written by different code paths that both own the terminal, so they overwrite each other, leave stray padding, and re-print stale frames. On top of that, a lot of internal debug detail (raw config JSON, the full manifest layer list) is emitted at `INFO`. We should standardize on a single logging/reporting layer for lume that owns the terminal, with proper levels and a progress renderer that coexists with log lines. ## Repro ``` lume pull macos-tahoe-cua:latest ``` ## What it looks like today
Actual output from lume pull macos-tahoe-cua:latest (trimmed) ``` [2026-08-05T10:11:32Z] INFO: Downloading OCI-compliant layers [2026-08-05T10:11:32Z] INFO: Downloading config layer (sha256:56fd425ee0ab…) [░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░] 0% | Current: 1.6 KB/s | Avg: 1.6 KB/s | Peak: 1.6 KB/s | ETA: 3915:56:40 [2026-08-05T10:11:32Z] INFO: Downloading nvram layer (sha256:67825595efad…) [░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░] 0% | Current: 20.1 MB/s | Avg: 13.4 MB/s | Peak: 20.1 MB/s | ETA: 34:09 [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Config layer raw JSON: { "hardwareModel" : "YnBsaXN0MDDTAQIDBAQFXxAZRGF0YVJlcHJlc2VudGF0aW9uVmVyc2lvbl8QD1BsYXRmb3JtVmVyc2lvbl8QEk1pbmltdW1TdXBwb3J0ZWRPUxACowYHBxANEAAIDys9UlRYWgAAAAAAAAEBAAAAAAAAAAgAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAABc", ... } [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Manifest layers: application/vnd.trycua.lume.nvram.v1 size=33579164, application/vnd.trycua.lume.disk.v1 size=868083, ... (≈300 more entries on one line) [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Manifest config mediaType: application/vnd.trycua.lume.config.v1+json [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Decoded LumeOCIConfig: os=macOS hardwareModel=YnBsaXN0MDDTAQIDBAQF... [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Wrote config.json [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Saved nvram.bin [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Chunked disk: 300 parts, total uncompressed size: 161061273600 disk layer disk layer 1: Pull complete disk layer 3: Pull complete disk layedisk layer 1: Pull complete disk layer 2: Pull complete disk layer 1 disk layer 1 disk layer disk layer 1: Pull complete disk layer 2: Pull complete disk layer 3: Pull complete disk layer 4: Pull complete disk layer 5: Pull complete disk layer 6: Pull complete disk layer 7: Pull complete disk layer 8: Pull complete disk layer 9: Pull complete disk layer 1: Downloading [░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░] 0.0 B/248.0 MB disk layer 1: Downloading [░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░] 0.0 B/448.1 MB disk layer 1: Downloading [░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░] 0.0 B/464.8 MB 9/300 done | 238.4 MB/21.5 GB | 19s ```
## Concrete problems 1. **Log lines and progress bars fight over the terminal.** An `INFO:` line is appended directly onto the end of a progress-bar line (`... ETA: 34:09 [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: ...`). Nothing coordinates the two writers. 2. **Stray padding and torn frames.** Long runs of spaces and truncated text (`disk layedisk layer 1: Pull complete`, `disk layer 1` with no suffix) — the result of `\r` overwrites with a shorter string and no clear-to-end-of-line. 3. **Completed-layer list is re-rendered repeatedly**, so `disk layer 1: Pull complete` shows up many times in scrollback instead of once. 4. **Layer identity is wrong/confusing.** Three concurrent downloads are all labelled `disk layer 1` with three different sizes (248.0 MB / 448.1 MB / 464.8 MB). Layer numbering appears to be per-worker rather than a stable identifier. 5. **Debug internals at INFO level.** The raw config JSON blob, the ~300-entry manifest layer list, `Decoded LumeOCIConfig`, `Wrote config.json`, `Saved nvram.bin` are implementation detail. Nobody running `lume pull` needs them; they bury the two lines that actually matter. 6. **Nonsense ETA from a single sample.** `ETA: 3915:56:40` on the config layer, computed off a 1.6 KB/s first reading. 7. **Timestamps on every line in an interactive session.** `[2026-08-05T10:11:32Z] INFO:` per line is server-log formatting on a foreground CLI. Useful when piped to a file, noise on a TTY. 8. **Two different progress-bar styles in the same run** — the top-level `[░░░] 0% | Current: … | Avg: … | Peak: … | ETA: …` bar vs. the per-layer `[░░░] 0.0 B/248.0 MB` bar vs. the `9/300 done | 238.4 MB/21.5 GB | 19s` summary line. No shared renderer. ## Proposal **One reporting layer that owns stdout.** All user-facing output — log lines and progress — goes through a single component. Progress lives in a pinned region at the bottom of the screen; log lines scroll above it; the region is cleared (`\r` + erase-to-EOL, or a proper ANSI region) and redrawn on every update. This removes problems 1–3 by construction. **Levels, applied honestly.** - `INFO` (default): what the user asked for and its outcome — image being pulled, total size, progress, done/failed. - `DEBUG`: manifest contents, config JSON, per-file writes, decoded structs. Everything in problem 5 moves here. - `WARN`/`ERROR`: unchanged, to stderr. **Stable layer identity.** Label layers by short digest (`a3f1c9d2`) or a stable index assigned from the manifest, not a per-worker counter. Rendering should look closer to `docker pull`: one line per in-flight layer with a fixed identity, plus an aggregate line. **TTY vs. non-TTY.** On a TTY: no timestamps, no level prefix for `INFO`, colors, live progress. When not a TTY (piped, CI, `lume serve` logs): no ANSI, timestamps + level on every line, periodic progress lines instead of in-place redraws. **Suppress ETA until it's meaningful** — needs a minimum number of samples / elapsed time, and should use a smoothed rate rather than the instantaneous one. ### Sketch of the target output ``` Pulling macos-tahoe-cua:latest Manifest: 300 layers, 21.5 GB compressed / 150 GB on disk a3f1c9d2 ██████████████████░░░░░░░ 412 MB / 464 MB 58 MB/s 7b20e4f1 ████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 180 MB / 448 MB 61 MB/s ee91c507 ██░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 28 MB / 248 MB 44 MB/s 9/300 layers · 238 MB / 21.5 GB · 163 MB/s · ETA 2m 10s ``` ## Scope Applies to every lume command that prints progress or logs, not just `pull` — `push`, `run`, `create`, `clone`, `serve`. The point is to fix this once in a shared reporting layer rather than per-command.

title: fix(cua-driver): direct capture grant is unobservable — `permissions status` always reports "not checked"
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver permissions grant` claims it requested **and verified** direct capture ("✅ … Accessibility, Screen Recording, and direct capture access"), but no direct-capture consent dialog was observed, and `cua-driver permissions status` run immediately afterwards still reports:

```
Direct Capture:     ❓ not checked (status is read-only; run `cua-driver-local permissions grant`)
```

So there is no way to observe that direct capture was ever actually granted. `grant` says yes; `status` can never say anything but "not checked". Running `grant` again produces the same claim, so re-running is not a way to confirm either.

## Reproduction

```console
$ /Users/francesco/.local/bin/cua-driver-local permissions grant
Launching CuaDriverLocal to request permissions.
A dialog for CuaDriverLocal will appear — approve Accessibility and Screen Recording in System Settings, then this command continues.

Accessibility and Screen Recording are granted.
macOS may now ask CuaDriverLocal to bypass the system private window picker and directly access your screen and audio. …
Choose Allow to request and verify direct capture now…

✅ CuaDriverLocal has Accessibility, Screen Recording, and direct capture access. You're set.

$ /Users/francesco/.local/bin/cua-driver-local permissions status
Accessibility:    ✅ granted
Screen Recording: ✅ granted
Direct Capture:     ❓ not checked (status is read-only; run `cua-driver-local permissions grant`)
Source: driver-daemon
```

Host: macOS, local install (`com.trycua.driver.local` identity), daemon running under the driver's own identity (`Source: driver-daemon`).

## Why this happens (code)

- `permission_status_request()` sends `check_permissions` with `prompt:false, probe_direct_capture:false` — `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:2594`.
- `check_permissions` short-circuits to `(None, "not_checked", None)` whenever `!should_prompt` — `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/check_permissions.rs:322-337`.
- The CLI then prints the `None` branch — `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:2560-2565`.

That read-only behaviour is deliberate (`SCShareableContent::get()` can itself raise Tahoe's picker-bypass consent, so a status call must not run it). The gap is that **the successful probe result from `grant` is never persisted**, so nothing can report it later. `screen_recording_capturable` is computed and thrown away on every call; there is no cache, no marker file, no daemon-held last-verified state.

## Expected behavior

Either:

1. `permissions grant` records the verified direct-capture outcome (timestamp + identity) and `permissions status` reports it as e.g. `✅ verified (2026-08-05, by permissions grant)` — still without running a probe itself; or
2. `permissions grant` stops claiming "direct capture access" as verified when the result cannot subsequently be observed, and says exactly what it did.

Option 1 is preferable — otherwise the only user-visible signal is a claim that no later command can corroborate.

## Secondary question: was the consent actually triggered?

No dialog appeared during `grant` on this machine, yet `grant` reported direct capture verified. Two indistinguishable explanations, and the current output does not disambiguate:

- the consent was already granted earlier (probe returned `ready` without a prompt) — fine; or
- the probe never raised the consent, and consent will instead be deferred to the first real recording — which is exactly the failure mode tracked in #2443.

`grant` should distinguish "consent already present" from "consent newly requested and approved" in its output, so this is not guesswork.

## Related

- #2443 — probe reports `ready` while Tahoe consent is still deferred to the first recording (adjacent, but that one is about the probe's truthfulness; this one is about the status surface never being able to report a result at all).
- #2296 / #2407 — made the direct ScreenCaptureKit consent explicit and observable.

title: cua-driver: adopt ActionEffect/effect_from_value_readback — browser hardcodes effect: "unverifiable"
body:
## Summary

`ActionEffect` already models the distinction the driver needs, and a classifier for it already exists — but adoption is near zero, and the browser stack bypasses both with a hardcoded string literal. The result is that successful actions, silent misses, and complete no-ops are all reported identically as `effect: "unverifiable"`.

## What already exists

`cua-driver-core/src/action_record.rs:9`

```rust
pub enum ActionEffect { Confirmed, Partial, Unverifiable, SuspectedNoop, Refused }
```

`cua-driver-core/src/action_record.rs:20` — `effect_from_value_readback(confirmed, changed, readback_available)`, whose doc comment already states the correct rule:

> "A missing readback never confirms success, while a readable unchanged value is stronger evidence of a no-op than of an unknown outcome."

`SuspectedNoop` is exactly the value that distinguishes *"I looked and nothing moved"* from *"I didn't look."*

## Current adoption

| Location | `effect_from_value_readback` | `ActionEffect::` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `platform-macos` | 1 file (`tools/set_window_frame.rs`) | 6 |
| `platform-windows` | 1 file (`tools/impl_.rs`) | 1 |
| `platform-linux` | 1 file (`tools/impl_.rs`) | 1 |
| `cua-driver-core/src/browser/` | **0** | **0** |

The browser path emits a literal instead — `cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:1157`:

```rust
"effect": "unverifiable",
```

Reproduce:
```
grep -rn "ActionEffect\|effect_from_value_readback" --include="*.rs" cua-driver-core/src/browser/   # empty
```

## Measured consequence

In one session on macOS, five `browser_click` calls all returned `effect: "unverifiable"`:

- 3 changed page state (verified out-of-band via `aria-pressed` / `aria-selected` / URL change)
- 1 delivered a genuinely trusted click that missed its target entirely and changed nothing
- 1 `browser_pointer` scroll was a complete no-op (hidden tab, no compositor)

The field did not discriminate success from total failure in any case. Every outcome was only distinguishable by inspecting page state out of band.

## Proposed change

Route browser actions through the existing classifier rather than a literal, and widen adoption on the desktop side.

For a ref-targeted click the driver already resolves a `backendNodeId`, so a bounded before/after vector on the target node is cheap:

- ARIA state: `aria-pressed`, `aria-selected`, `aria-checked`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-current`, `disabled`
- Form state: `checked`, `value`
- The node's own `innerText` (bounded length)
- Document level: `location.href`, `document.activeElement` identity

Poll to a bounded deadline (~400ms, early-exit on first delta) and report the delta plus `observed_after_ms`:

```json
{"effect": "confirmed",
 "observed": {"aria-pressed": ["false", "true"], "innerText": ["378", "379"]},
 "observed_after_ms": 180}
```

## Design constraints (learned the hard way)

**Do not diff the whole document.** A media page mutates continuously; a generic `MutationObserver` returns "changed" for a click that did nothing. A confident false positive is worse than today's honest shrug.

**Do not use accessible names as postconditions.** On YouTube a like button's `aria-label` still read `"...come hanno fatto 378 altre persone"` *after* the like registered; the truth was only in `aria-pressed="true"` and the rendered count `378`→`379`. Comparing accessible names would report failure on a successful action — the false-negative mirror of the current problem.

**Do not add a flag to enable verification.** Make it the default behavior.

**Do not add a caller-supplied `expect` API yet.** Desktop callers have `verify_state` / `ObservationProvider` (`cua-driver-core/src/expectation.rs:48`); the browser stack has no equivalent (`grep -rn "verify_state\|ObservationProvider" cua-driver-core/src/browser/` is empty). Tempting to mirror it, but the automatic vector would have caught every observed case — add the explicit API only if something real escapes it.

## Risk to document

`SuspectedNoop` is **not** "failed". An action can legitimately do something the vector cannot observe (a fetch with no immediate DOM effect, a change inside a child frame). If the docs do not say this plainly, agents will treat it as hard failure and retry destructively.

This changes the action-result contract (`docs/action-result-contract.md`), so it needs the values documented, a CHANGELOG entry, and tests pinning each value — callers may already branch on `effect`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace the hardcoded literal in `browser/tools.rs:1157` with the classifier
- [ ] Implement the bounded before/after vector for ref-targeted browser clicks
- [ ] Widen `effect_from_value_readback` adoption across desktop tools on all three OSs
- [ ] Document that `SuspectedNoop` is not failure
- [ ] Tests pinning each `ActionEffect` value; CHANGELOG + contract doc update

Context: `libs/cua-driver/docs/cross-platform-verification-audit.md` (F1, F5, F6). Related: #2882.

title: cua-driver: Linux browser actions render no agent cursor (visualize_browser_action unimplemented)
body:
## Summary

`visualize_browser_action` is not implemented in `platform-linux`, so it falls through to the empty default in the `BrowserPlatform` trait. Browser tool calls on Linux therefore place no agent cursor over the browser and render no badge — the agent is invisible during browser automation, with no refusal, warning, or log.

## Evidence

Trait default (a no-op body) — `cua-driver-core/src/browser/platform.rs:234`:

```rust
async fn visualize_browser_action(&self, _action: BrowserVisualAction) {}
```

Implementations:

- macOS: `platform-macos/src/browser/platform.rs:403` ✅
- Windows: `platform-windows/src/browser_platform.rs:814` ✅
- Linux: **none** — `grep -c "visualize_browser_action" platform-linux/src/browser_platform.rs` → `0`

The badge rendering itself is fine and platform-independent: an audit of all 180 combinations (12 actions x 3 deliveries x 5 targets) in the shared `cursor-overlay` crate shows every glyph drawing correctly, including the browser globe, on both light and dark backgrounds. The gap is purely that Linux never places the cursor.

## The broader problem

`BrowserPlatform` mixes required and defaulted methods. A platform that does not override a defaulted method silently gets no-op behavior, and nothing distinguishes "deliberately accepts the default" from "nobody implemented this yet."

Full audit of all 15 methods:

| Method | Default? | macOS | Windows | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `standalone_trusted_input_background_limitation` | yes | yes | **default** | yes |
| `visualize_browser_action` | yes | yes | yes | **default (no-op)** |
| `discover_spawned_endpoint` | yes | **default** | yes | **default** |
| all 12 others | — | yes | yes | yes |

The other two rows are likely intentional (Windows genuinely has no trusted-input limitation; the `discover_spawned_endpoint` default preserves ordinary exact-pid ownership) — but that is inference, not something the code states.

## Proposed change

1. Implement `visualize_browser_action` for Linux, or have it refuse visibly rather than silently no-op.
2. Make deliberate non-implementation explicit so this class of gap cannot recur silently — e.g. require each platform to declare the set of defaults it accepts, and assert that set in a test. A gap that must be declared is a gap someone reviews.

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement Linux `visualize_browser_action` (X11 + Wayland), or refuse visibly
- [ ] Verify the agent cursor + badge appear over the browser on Linux
- [ ] Add an explicit per-platform declaration of accepted trait defaults, asserted in a test
- [ ] Confirm whether the `discover_spawned_endpoint` defaults on macOS/Linux are intentional

Context: `libs/cua-driver/docs/cross-platform-verification-audit.md` (F2).

title: cua-driver: close out and generalize the macOS modality-ladder audit to Windows and Linux
body:
## Summary

`CUA_DRIVER_MODALITY_LADDER_AUDIT.md` (2026-06-28) identified a systemic false-success pattern across macOS desktop tools and prescribed a fix. It has no status tracking, so it is not possible to tell from the document which items shipped — and the same question was never asked for Windows or Linux at all.

## Background

That audit's root finding:

> A primary path returns a "success" status code, the tool reports success **without confirming the effect**, and there is no automatic escalation to the next rung.

Its prescribed fix: *"read back a post-condition, and treat *unverifiable* as *not-success* → escalate, surfacing the delivering path."*

P0 items listed: `type_text`, `click` (pixel), `drag`, `scroll`, `get_window_state`. P1 items include `set_value`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `click` (AX), `type_text_chars`, `press_key`, `hotkey`, `get_desktop_state`, `zoom`, `page`, `launch_app`.

## Why this needs closing out

Adoption numbers for the shared classifier suggest the prescribed pattern was not broadly applied — `effect_from_value_readback` appears in exactly one file per platform (see #2883). But the audit has no outcome column, so "is the false-success pattern fixed?" cannot be answered without re-reading every tool.

Note this is an open question, not an assertion of regression: the P0/P1 items were **not** individually re-verified against current code during the 2026-08-05 audit.

Separately, the ladder question has never been asked for Windows or Linux. Their tool code lives in single files (`platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`, 10,096 lines; `platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`, 7,809 lines), so a per-tool pass there is a materially different amount of work than on macOS — worth scoping before committing.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add an outcome column to the June audit (shipped / not shipped / no longer applicable) per P0 and P1 item
- [ ] Re-verify the five P0 items against current macOS code
- [ ] Run the equivalent per-tool ladder pass for Windows
- [ ] Run the equivalent per-tool ladder pass for Linux
- [ ] Supersede or archive the June document once cross-platform coverage exists

Context: `libs/cua-driver/docs/cross-platform-verification-audit.md` (F9).

title: ci(cua-driver): run distro checks after publication
body:
## Summary

- stop starting released-binary distro compatibility from the private candidate tag
- dispatch the standalone distro matrix from the Cua Driver finalizer only after it verifies the release and every staged asset are public
- scope `actions: write` to the finalizer job and pass the exact published version to the dispatch
- retain a one-minute retry window only for public CDN propagation
- add release-wiring regressions for the trigger and dispatch ordering

## Root cause

Tag candidate creation and distro compatibility started concurrently, but the release process intentionally keeps tag artifacts in a private draft until post-certification publication. The distro workflow therefore polled a public URL that could not exist during its 15-minute window.

GitHub also suppresses ordinary workflow-triggering events created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so this uses an explicit `workflow_dispatch` after publication instead of relying on `release.published`.

Fixes #2896.

## Validation

- `python3 .github/scripts/tests/test_cua_driver_release_wiring.py` (36 passed)
- full `.github/scripts/tests` suite with Python 3.13 and test dependencies (75 passed)
- `actionlint` on the distro workflow
- `actionlint` on the release workflow with its two pre-existing diagnostics excluded (`macos-26` runner catalog and SC2129)
- Prettier check on the distro workflow
- YAML parse checks for both workflows
- `git diff --check`

The active release tag and draft were not changed.

title: Linux: get_desktop_state capture fails with X11 GetImage BadMatch on WSLg (Xwayland, dual RANDR outputs)
body:
## Summary
On WSL2 with WSLg, `get_desktop_state` (and any full-root capture) fails with an X11 protocol error. Reproduced on cua-driver 0.17.0 AND 0.18.0 (linux x86_64).

## Environment
- WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04, WSLg (Weston compositor + Xwayland)
- DISPLAY=:0, WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0
- X screen: 3840x1080, two RANDR outputs side by side:
  - rdp-0 connected 1920x1080+0+0
  - rdp-2 connected 1920x1080+1920+0

## Repro
```
echo '{"screenshot_out_file":"/tmp/shot.png"}' | cua-driver call get_desktop_state
```

## Actual result
```
Capture error: X11 error X11Error { error_kind: Match, error_code: 8, sequence: 2, bad_value: 1080, minor_opcode: 0, major_opcode: 73, extension_name: None, request_name: Some("GetImage") }
```
No PNG is written. Identical error on both 0.17.0 and 0.18.0.

## Analysis
`bad_value: 1080` on a core `GetImage` (opcode 73) request suggests the capture path computes an out-of-bounds region for the second RANDR output — consistent with the second output's offset being computed as y=1080 (vertical stacking) instead of x=+1920 (the actual horizontal layout reported by RANDR). Root window is 3840x1080 per xdpyinfo/xrandr, so a correct full-root GetImage(0,0,3840,1080) would be in bounds.

Also note: `cua-driver doctor` reports `screen_capture_capability: X11 reachable; screen capture path is functional` — a false green in this environment.

Wayland backend (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`) does not help: WSLg's Weston does not expose wlr-screencopy, so capture falls back to the same X11 path and fails identically.

## Expected
Full-desktop capture works on WSLg Xwayland multi-output layouts (or doctor flags the unsupported layout honestly).

## Summary

- treat OpenShell as the standard outer runtime and policy boundary for unattended agents while keeping Cua authorization and live GUI target proof mandatory

Generic text input requires the caller to possess plaintext before Cua Driver can act. This proposal adds a release capability: trusted host code selects and scopes credentials, while the agent can only discover matches for a verified target and request delivery with a fresh handle bound to that exact browser, document, and field context.

The design reuses OpenShell for sandbox, network, MCP admission, workload identity seams, credential-driver storage, and outer security events. It reuses OAuth, SPIFFE, sender-constrained tokens, WebAuthn, OCSF, and non-exportable-operation patterns where they apply. Cua-specific work is limited to binding one secret release to a freshly verified live GUI password field and delivering it without exposing the value to the agent.

title: docs(rfcs): add RFC 2969 for compact-by-default agent payloads
body:
RFC document for [#2969](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2969), following `rfcs/0000-template.md` and the structure of RFC 2447 and RFC 2549. Status is `review`.

## What it proposes

Making Cua Driver's agent-facing payloads compact by default, so a small local model can drive the same contract a frontier model drives. **Net new tool parameters, CLI flags, and environment variables: zero.** The method is to change defaults and keep the opt-ups that already ship.

**Tier 1 — unconditional, no negotiation needed.** Each item removes payload no caller wanted, or repairs a defect a caller of any size can hit:

1. Collapse `semantic_v2` ref clusters that share one accessible name, bounded so a cluster is never collapsed to zero.
2. Canonicalize the shared schema fragments and trim tool descriptions to the installable skill files that already exist for long-form guidance.
3. Apply the operator's existing `deny.tools` policy to `tools/list` — reusing an intent already declared, not adding a knob.
4. Declare the missing `element_token` pattern.
5. Lead `browser_prepare` success text with the outcome instead of the non-effect assurance.
6. Converge the cross-platform `max_elements`/`max_depth` drift; default `include_screenshot` to `false`.

**Tier 2 — capability negotiation**, kept narrow and placed at MCP `initialize`, which Cua Driver already parses and discards. The only axis that qualifies today is whether the client can accept images at all. A per-call argument is rejected explicitly: it charges every model a decision on every call to fix a default that should simply be better.

## Measured evidence

Captured on 2026-08-07, macOS 26.5.2 / Apple M5 Max, `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-mtp-q8_0` via Ollama 0.32.5 and opencode 1.18.14, against `cua-driver` 0.19.0.

A live `tools/list` capture (`cua-driver mcp` fed `initialize` + `tools/list` over stdin) measures **126,461 bytes across 54 tools**, roughly 34k tokens:

| Component | Bytes |
| --- | ---: |
| Input schemas | 48,051 (12,304 of them byte-identical repeats) |
| Descriptions | 35,771 |
| Output schemas | 24,714 |
| Annotations / risk / capabilities | 11,488 |

First inference of every session costs 2m41s–2m44s, essentially all prompt-eval over that prefix; cached afterwards, subsequent steps 3–80s. `session` alone ships three different descriptions (243 B × 13 tools, 128 B × 7, 17 B × 6). `get_browser_state` `semantic_v2` on a YouTube results page returned 113 nodes for ~25 videos — four refs per result sharing one name, three of them wrong to click.

## Honesty notes

- The observed local-model failures were **not** context overflow. They were fabricated `snapshot_id`/`element_token` handles and a successful `browser_prepare` read as a refusal — legibility problems, which is why the fixes are unconditional rather than negotiated.
- **Budget negotiation is deferred, not rejected**, and the RFC says so plainly: `semantic_v2` already pages at 300 nodes and `get_window_state` already caps elements, so an overflow would have surfaced as a non-zero `omitted.budget`, which was not observed. The document states the specific evidence that would justify revisiting it.
- Dropping `outputSchema` would recover 24,714 bytes and is rejected — it was added deliberately in `dc6f32cd4` so strict clients stop replacing refusal messages with schema errors, which is one of the failure modes this RFC exists to prevent.
- `get_desktop_state`'s full-resolution capture is deliberate (desktop-scope coordinates are read from it) and is explicitly out of scope.
- Filtering `tools/list` by policy is stated as presentational only; enforcement stays at the native registry boundary, and an implementation that makes listing load-bearing for authorization is called out as incorrect.
- The one change with real blast radius — flipping `include_screenshot` to `false` — is separated into its own slice with its own release note, announcement window, and an unresolved question about whether it should wait for image-capability negotiation.

## Prior art cited, not re-proposed

The RFC surveys and cites what already ships: `get_window_state`'s `max_elements` / `max_depth` / `query` / `include_screenshot` / `screenshot_out_file`, `get_browser_state`'s `snapshot_format` / `scope_ref` / `query` / `continuation`, the 300-node budget and `omitted` accounting, the parent-only `remove_redundant_static_text` rule, the `tool_schema.rs` drift gate (and why its `structural()` reducer's prose-stripping is what let three `session` descriptions coexist), permission policies, the short `initialize` `instructions` plus out-of-band skill files, and `initialize_metadata`'s parsed-then-discarded client capability flags.

title: docs(cua-driver): add local-model setup guide
body:
## What

`libs/cua-driver/docs/run-with-a-local-model.md` — end-to-end guide for driving Cua Driver from a model running entirely on the local machine (Ollama + opencode + Qwen 3.6 on Apple Silicon).

Every number in it was measured on an M5 Max / 128 GB during a full day of dogfooding, not estimated. Where a figure is cited, it came from a run.

## Why it's organised around traps

Each of these fails *silently* — you get a plausible-looking result and no error:

**Build choice is counter-intuitive.** Three builds of the same model:

| Tag | Backend | Precision | Warm tok/s | Vision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.6:35b` | llama.cpp | 4-bit | 43 | ✅ |
| `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-mxfp8` | MLX | 8-bit | 30–34 | ❌ silently broken |
| `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-mtp-q8_0` | llama.cpp | 8-bit | 37–39 | ✅ |

The MLX 8-bit build is the *slowest* of the three (MXFP8 doubles bytes-per-token, costing more than the backend saves), and it drops images without erroring — a solid red PNG comes back as "White". `ollama show` reports `vision` for it regardless, because that flag comes from the model card rather than the runtime. The guide therefore treats the capability flag as untrustworthy and gives a red-PNG control test, plus a manifest check for a `projector` layer you can run *before* committing to a 38 GB download.

**`OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE` is easy to set and not have work.** The daemon runs under launchd, which doesn't inherit your shell environment — so `export` in `~/.zshrc` is invisible to it. And `brew services restart` regenerates the plist from the formula, discarding the edit. The guide documents the `launchctl bootout`/`bootstrap` reload instead, and shows both the log line and the `ollama ps` output that prove it took, because otherwise you silently keep the 5-minute default and eat a reload mid-agent-loop.

**The first inference looks like a hang.** It costs 2–3 minutes prompt-evaluating the ~54-tool schema prefix before emitting a token (measured 2m41s and 2m44s on separate runs; cached afterwards, subsequent steps 3–80 s). The guide gives two commands to distinguish it from a genuine hang.

## Also covered

Memory sizing per unified-memory tier, macOS permission attribution (`cua-driver permissions grant` vs. granting from a shell), the `--auto` flag required for non-interactive opencode runs, a troubleshooting table, and an appendix on verifying which backend actually loaded (`--mlx-engine` vs `llama-server --mmproj`).

## Verification

Every command block in the guide was executed on the target machine. The vision test, the manifest probe, the runner-directory listing, and the keep-alive verification all run as written and produce the output shown.

## Placement

Filed under `libs/cua-driver/docs/` alongside the other engineering guides. If you'd rather it render on the site, it should move to `docs/content/docs/how-to-guides/driver/` as `.mdx` — happy to relocate, it's Diátaxis how-to shaped either way.

title: bug(cua-driver): first keyboard/text action leaves the agent cursor off-screen or idle-hidden
body:
## Summary

A declared session whose first visible action is `press_key` or untargeted `type_text` can deliver the input and enter the correct `key` / `text` semantic animation state while the agent cursor remains impossible to render: `get_agent_cursor_state` still reports `position: null`.

The same code path can leave an already-positioned cursor hidden after `idle_hide_ms`, because a non-spatial `BeginAction` changes the semantic animation without re-revealing the cursor.

Observed on macOS 26.6.1 (arm64) with Cua Driver 0.19.2. I audited the current source at `bfe50bdd016985fe5f598e8334779266a0a5c271`.

## Sanitized reproduction

Use any ordinary on-screen window with a focused text field. The live reproduction used a generic Electron search field and the literal probe text below; no application or user data is required.

```sh
cua-driver start_session \
  '{"session":"cursor-keyboard-first-action","capture_scope":"auto"}'

cua-driver get_agent_cursor_state \
  '{"session":"cursor-keyboard-first-action"}'
# enabled=true, position=null

cua-driver press_key \
  '{"session":"cursor-keyboard-first-action","pid":<PID>,"window_id":<WINDOW_ID>,"key":"/","delivery_mode":"background"}'

cua-driver get_agent_cursor_state \
  '{"session":"cursor-keyboard-first-action"}'
# requested_action="key", resolved_action="key", position=null

cua-driver type_text \
  '{"session":"cursor-keyboard-first-action","pid":<PID>,"window_id":<WINDOW_ID>,"text":"cursor-visibility-probe","delivery_mode":"background","delay_ms":1}'

cua-driver get_agent_cursor_state \
  '{"session":"cursor-keyboard-first-action"}'
# requested_action="text", resolved_action="text", position=null
```

In the live run, both actions changed the target UI as expected. Fresh window state confirmed the probe text, while the cursor state remained positionless and therefore off-screen.

## Expected

- The first keyboard or text action in a declared session should provide visible agent-cursor feedback.
- A non-spatial action after the idle fade should re-reveal an already-positioned cursor for the duration of its semantic cue.
- Element-addressed `press_key` / `hotkey` should use the resolved element geometry when available, matching the existing element-addressed `type_text` behavior.
- The physical pointer, focus, and foreground posture must remain unchanged.

## Actual

- The input lands.
- Cursor semantics advance to `key` or `text`.
- A fresh session stays at `position: null`, so no overlay can appear.
- A previously faded cursor can remain at `idle_alpha = 0` because the semantic action does not reset the idle timer or alpha.

## Source findings

- `cua-driver-contract/src/cursor.rs` correctly classifies `press_key` / `hotkey` as `Key` and `type_text` as `Text`.
- `cua-driver-core/src/cursor_events.rs` emits `BeginAction` / `EndAction`.
- `cursor-overlay/src/render_state.rs` handles `BeginAction` by calling `visual.begin(...)`, but it does not seed an on-screen position or reset `idle_secs` / `idle_alpha`.
- The native external-visibility checks require an enabled cursor with an on-screen position and nonzero idle alpha.
- The macOS `press_key` path does not animate to an addressed AX element. The macOS `type_text` path animates only when an explicit element target resolves; the already-focused path does not.

The render-state portion is shared, so the bug appears cross-platform, although the live reproduction above is macOS-only.

## Suggested direction

1. On a non-spatial action, re-reveal an already-positioned cursor by resetting the idle timer/alpha.
2. When the session has never acquired a position, seed the cursor at a provable target: focused element center when available, otherwise a documented safe fallback such as the target window center or current hardware-pointer position.
3. Move element-addressed `press_key` / `hotkey` to the resolved element center before dispatch, as element-addressed `type_text` already does.
4. Add shared render-state coverage plus native macOS, Windows, X11, and Wayland E2E coverage for first-action keyboard/text visibility and post-idle reveal.

Related but distinct:

- #2879 tracks the missing cross-platform first-action pixel/recording oracle.
- #1945 tracks following focus changes during typing after the cursor is already visible.

title: fix(cua-driver): render cursors across macos displays
body:
## summary

- replace cursor-coordinate sentinels with explicit shared placement state
- create one macos cursor surface per connected display
- render each surface in global coordinates with its own backing scale
- rebuild surfaces after display changes and reject stale frames

## implementation

cursor visibility and first placement no longer infer state from coordinate signs. the shared cursor state now carries `placed`, and macos, windows, x11, and wayland use it consistently. negative coordinates are therefore ordinary display coordinates rather than hidden-state markers.

macos keeps one shared cursor state and render worker, while appkit owns one transparent surface per display. cursor artwork is rendered into every display it intersects, so seam crossings do not clip the pointer. only displays with current or previous pixels are rendered, which also clears the old display after movement.

placement is explicit instead of encoded as a coordinate. theme-derived paint bounds select intersecting displays without rendering every display for custom themes. the session badge remains on the cursor's anchor display, and target-relative z-order applies to every surface carrying cursor pixels.

rebasing onto main preserves the current display-mode backing-scale calculation from [#3328](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3328) for every display.

candidate: `d27f6a89d8aeef0f56363ee9bb60bbc565912b1e`

## validation

- `cargo test -p cursor-overlay --locked` — 44 passed
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib --locked` — 352 passed, 2 environment-mutating/native-display tests ignored
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib --locked` — 16 host-available tests passed
- `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib --locked` — 42 host-available tests passed

- `cargo check -p platform-windows --locked`

- exact-candidate github ci passed, including linux and nix rust unit tests, windows compile/tests, cross-platform rustfmt, portable contract parity, generated bindings, docs, and release metadata.

## remaining validation gap

the exact candidate still needs the canonical cross-platform desktop e2e matrix. macos coverage must include left, upper, mixed-scale, cross-display, and hotplug layouts.

title: Add opt-in per-session visibility scope confinement
body:
## Summary

Wires up the (previously dead) per-session visibility-scope confinement primitive in `cua-driver-core/src/visibility_scope.rs`. A confined session's `list_apps`/`list_windows`/`get_desktop_state` now enumerate only the processes it itself launched — filtered at the source, before any summary line or count is built, so the counts/arrays/lines a confined session sees all describe the same smaller world rather than a redacted-after-the-fact one. `get_desktop_state` refuses entirely for a confined session, since a full-display screenshot cannot be scoped (the pixels of every other app come with it).

## Wiring

- `bind_session(session_id, [])` is now called at `start_session`, establishing an initially-empty scope.
- `extend_session(session_id, pid)` is now called after each successful `launch_app`, so "what a session launches, it may see."
- Both call sites live in `cua-driver-core/src/session.rs` and `cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs`.

## Opt-in gating

Confinement is gated behind a new daemon-startup environment variable, `CUA_DRIVER_VISIBILITY_SCOPE_ENABLED`, resolved once via `visibility_scope::enabled()` — the same pattern `authorization.rs` already uses for `CUA_DRIVER_PERMISSION_MODE`. It is **never** read from a tool argument or transport field, matching the confinement-integrity property the module's own doc comments already required (reserved `_session_id` transport mirrors must never mint or resolve a scope).

**Default behavior is unchanged.** With the env var unset — the default for every existing caller — `enabled()` is `false`, `bind_session`/`extend_session` are never invoked, `scope_for_args` always resolves `None`, and every enumeration path runs exactly as it did before this change. This is exercised by a dedicated test (`the_feature_is_off_unless_a_trusted_operator_opts_the_daemon_in`) plus the full existing `visibility_scope` unit test suite.

## Testing

- `cargo check -p cua-driver-core -p platform-windows -p cua-driver -p cua-driver-sdk` — clean (worked around a pre-existing local MSVC Spectre-libs gap on this machine by building with the `stable-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` toolchain).
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` — 486 passed, including all 8 `visibility_scope` tests. The 2 failing tests in this suite (`session_manifest::...reject_filesystem_roots`, `tool::...bounded_observation_uses_only_the_manifest_without_a_protected_host`) are pre-existing environment-specific failures, reproduced identically on an unmodified checkout of this branch's base commit — unrelated to this change.
- `platform-linux`/`platform-macos` changes were applied with careful line-by-line context verification against current `main` (this repo moves fast; local dev checkout had drifted) but could not be locally cross-compiled on this Windows dev machine (no Linux/macOS toolchain available) — recommend CI confirms.

title: Linux driver reliability fixes + Windows window_center perf improvement
body:
## Summary

Five independent reliability fixes, each addressing a real observed failure mode:

- **AT-SPI editable-picking ambiguity** (`platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs`): `pick_editable`'s third rung used to be "the first editable anywhere" by tree order. In Geany the first editable is the toolbar search entry, several nodes above the document. Whenever nothing reported focus — which happens constantly on a shared desktop whenever another process holds X input focus — text meant for the document silently landed in that search box instead, and the write was reported as confirmed. The rung now only fires when there is exactly *one* editable candidate; with more than one and no focus signal to disambiguate, it refuses rather than guesses, falling through to real key events at wherever focus actually is.

- **Foreground `type_text` no longer silently downgrades to AT-SPI for native toolkits** (`platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`): the foreground path used to be gated on `is_chromium_embedder || is_webkitgtk_embedder`, on the theory that native toolkits have a "verifiable" AT-SPI path below. That path is not verifiable, and for native GTK it picked the wrong widget often enough (the same Geany toolbar-search-entry issue) to invalidate roughly half of all such calls in a calibration campaign — while still reporting `verified: true`. An explicit foreground request now gets real key events for every toolkit, not just web embedders.

- **Capture-subprocess hang fix** (`platform-linux/src/capture.rs`): the capture helper now enforces a 5s timeout with SIGKILL and reads stdout on a background thread instead of blocking synchronously, so a wedged capture subprocess can no longer hang the calling tool indefinitely.

- **Keysym normalization** (`platform-linux/src/input/mod.rs`): both spellings of keysyms like `Page_Down` and `pagedown` are now accepted, instead of only one canonical form.

- **Overlay/cursor-recording gap fix** (`platform-linux/src/overlay.rs`): Linux never emitted the tap event that the Windows overlay already emits on click dispatch, so `cursor.jsonl` was empty on every Linux recording ever made. Linux now emits the same tap.

- **Windows `window_center()` perf fix** (`platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`): `ScrollTool`'s no-explicit-target path used to resolve a window's center by calling `list_windows(Some(pid))` and searching every window the process owns. Measured against a WinForms app this cost ~2.5s per call, making a foreground scroll feel like it had been ignored. The HWND is already known at that call site, so `window_center(hwnd)` now reads its rect directly via `DwmGetWindowAttribute`/`GetWindowRect` — 27ms once resolved directly.

## Testing

- `cargo check -p platform-windows -p cua-driver -p cua-driver-sdk` — clean (worked around a pre-existing local MSVC Spectre-libs gap by building with the `stable-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` toolchain).
- `platform-linux` changes were applied with careful line-by-line context verification against current `main` (this repo moves fast; the local dev checkout this work started from had drifted meaningfully from origin/main — several related fixes, e.g. foreground XTest clicks for modified clicks, were found already shipped upstream and were **not** re-applied to avoid duplicating/conflicting with existing work) but could not be locally cross-compiled on this Windows dev machine — no Linux C toolchain available for the `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` target. Recommend CI confirms the Linux build.

title: [Bug]: Screenshot coordinate frames do not match the input frame under Wayland fractional scaling
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On a Wayland session with fractional display scaling, the coordinate frame of the screenshots returned by `get_desktop_state` and `get_window_state` does not match the coordinate frame that the input tools (`click`, `move_cursor`, …) consume. Any `px` action grounded on a driver screenshot therefore misses its target by exactly the scale factor, and `get_window_state` returns an image of the wrong region of the screen entirely.

### Reproduction

Environment: GNOME/Wayland, single 3840×2160 monitor, GNOME display scale **150%** → logical desktop 2560×1440. `cua-driver` 0.19.3, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`.

1. Confirm the scale factor is fractional:

   ```bash
   gdbus call --session --dest org.gnome.Mutter.DisplayConfig \
     --object-path /org/gnome/Mutter/DisplayConfig \
     --method org.gnome.Mutter.DisplayConfig.GetCurrentState
   # → [(0, 0, 1.5, uint32 0, true, [('HDMI-1', 'AUS', 'PG32UCDM', ...)], ...)]
   ```

2. Observe that the three geometry-reporting tools disagree:

   ```bash
   cua-driver get_screen_size '{}'
   # → {"width": 5120, "height": 2880, "scale_factor": 1.0}      # XWayland root

   cua-driver get_desktop_state '{"session":"s","screenshot_out_file":"/tmp/d.png"}'
   # → {"screen_width": 3840, "screen_height": 2160, "scale_factor": 1.0,
   #    "screenshot_width": 3840, "screenshot_height": 2160}      # native pixels
   ```

   None of the three reports the logical frame (2560×1440) that input actually uses.

3. Launch a target with a small, unambiguous hit area:

   ```bash
   cua-driver launch_app '{"name":"gnome-calculator","session":"s"}'
   # → windows[0].bounds = {x: 1100, y: 428, width: 360, height: 616}
   ```

   These bounds are **logical points**. In `/tmp/d.png` (native pixels) the window
   actually occupies (1650, 642)–(2190, 1566), i.e. `bounds × 1.5`.

4. Locate the `7` key in `/tmp/d.png`. It sits at native pixel ≈ (1714, 1300).
   Click there in desktop scope, per the documented contract that desktop actions
   use "screen-absolute coordinates from that exact full-display image":

   ```bash
   cua-driver click '{"session":"s","scope":"desktop","x":1714,"y":1300}'
   # → {"effect":"unverifiable","route":"global_input"}
   ```

   Nothing is entered in the calculator; the click lands ~1.5× further down/right
   (in this case below the window, raising the app behind it).

5. Click the same key using its **logical** coordinate (native ÷ 1.5):

   ```bash
   cua-driver click '{"session":"s","scope":"desktop","x":1143,"y":867}'
   ```

   The `7` key is pressed. Input is in the logical frame; the screenshot is not.

6. Now request the window screenshot:

   ```bash
   cua-driver get_window_state '{"pid":<pid>,"window_id":<wid>,"screenshot_out_file":"/tmp/w.png"}'
   # → {"screenshot_width": 360, "screenshot_height": 616}
   ```

   `/tmp/w.png` does not contain the calculator at all. It contains the content of
   an unrelated part of the desktop.

Reproduces 100% of the time. Setting the display scale to 100% makes all of it disappear.

### Expected behavior

A pixel coordinate read off a screenshot returned by the driver should be directly usable as an `x,y` argument to the driver's own input tools, without the caller having to know or apply the compositor's scale factor.

Concretely:

- `get_desktop_state`'s image and the coordinates accepted by `scope:"desktop"` actions should be in the same frame (either both logical, or both native with input scaling accordingly).
- `get_window_state`'s image should show the requested window.
- `get_screen_size` should report the logical screen size and the real scale factor.

### Actual behavior

Three different coordinate frames are mixed, and only the input path is self-consistent:

| Frame | Size here | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Logical points | 2560×1440 | **all input** (`click`, `move_cursor`, `drag`, px `type_text`), `list_windows` bounds, AT-SPI element bounds |
| Native pixels | 3840×2160 | the `get_desktop_state` screenshot |
| XWayland root | 5120×2880 | `get_screen_size` |

1. **`get_desktop_state` — image is native, input is logical.** Coordinates read off the image are off by the scale factor. The tool's own description states "Captures the entire display (root window) as native-size PNG so screen-absolute pixel coordinates land exactly", which does not hold when scale ≠ 1. It also returns `scale_factor: 1.0`, so a caller has no in-band signal that a conversion is needed.

2. **`get_window_state` — wrong region, not merely wrong zoom.** The window screenshot appears to crop the *native* full-display capture using the window's *logical* bounds. The result is a crop at the wrong origin and the wrong size — a different part of the screen, not a rescaled view of the window. It is returned with `screenshot_width/height` equal to the logical window size, so the response looks well-formed and is silently wrong.

3. **`get_screen_size` — reports the XWayland root** (logical × 2 under mutter's `xwayland-native-scaling`) together with `scale_factor: 1.0`, so it matches neither the input frame nor the screenshot frame.

Because the failures are silent (`effect: "unverifiable"`, plausible-looking dimensions), an agent following the documented snapshot → ground → act loop reports success on actions that landed nowhere.

### Environment

- Cua component and version: `cua-driver` 0.19.3 (x86_64-linux), installed via the release channel
- Operating system and architecture: Ubuntu, GNOME (`XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=ubuntu:GNOME`), `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`, x86_64
- Window system: Wayland (`wayland-0`) + XWayland (`:0`), `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`
- Display: single HDMI-1, 3840×2160 native, GNOME scale **1.5** → logical 2560×1440; mutter `experimental-features = ['scale-monitor-framebuffer', 'xwayland-native-scaling']`
- Application under test: `gnome-calculator` (GTK4)

`cua-driver doctor`:

```
[ok  ] binary: cua-driver 0.19.3 (x86_64-linux)
[ok  ] display server: Wayland+XWayland (WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0, DISPLAY=:0)
[warn] X11 connection: no top-level windows returned (possible disconnected or inaccessible X11 display)
[ok  ] AT-SPI: org.a11y.Bus reachable via session bus
```

### Evidence

**Input frame is logical, confirmed both in desktop scope and window scope.**

- Desktop scope: click at native (1714, 1300) → no effect. Click at logical (1143, 867) → the `7` key is pressed; the AT-SPI tree confirms the display text box changes, and the agent-cursor overlay is drawn on the `7` key.
- Window scope: `click({pid, window_id, x: 316, y: 390})` — window-local **logical** coordinates — pressed the `mod` key exactly, giving display text `"¹7mod"`. So window-local px input is correct; only the window *screenshot* is wrong.

**`get_window_state` returns a crop at logical bounds taken from the native image.** Comparing the driver's `/tmp/w.png` against two candidate regions of the same full-display capture (mean per-pixel absolute difference, RGB):

```
mean | driver_window_png − desktop.crop(bounds)        |  =  9.75   # native crop at LOGICAL bounds
mean | driver_window_png − desktop.crop(bounds × 1.5)  |  = 60.63   # the actual window region
```

The driver's output matches the wrong crop nearly exactly, and does not match the correct region. (The residual 9.75 is live content changing between the two captures.)

**Deriving the window view manually produces the correct image**, which suggests the fix is localized to how the crop rectangle is scaled:

```python
S = 1.5                                   # mutter logical-monitor scale
bx, by, bw, bh = 1150, 478, 360, 616      # list_windows bounds (logical)
crop = desktop.crop((bx*S, by*S, (bx+bw)*S, (by+bh)*S))   # correct native region
crop = crop.resize((bw, bh))              # back to logical == the input frame
```

Coordinates read off that resized crop are directly usable as window-local `x,y` and land correctly. End-to-end check: `9` located at window-local (180, 439) → desktop logical (1330, 917) → `click({scope:"desktop", x:1330, y:917})` → calculator display reads `9`.

### Workaround and additional context

Callers can compensate by probing the scale factor themselves and dividing every screenshot-derived coordinate by it, and by rebuilding window views from a `get_desktop_state` capture using the crop-and-resize shown above rather than trusting `get_window_state`'s image. That requires each caller to know the compositor's scale, which the driver does not report anywhere (`scale_factor` is `1.0` in every response observed here).

A few notes that may help narrow the suspected area:

- `element_index` / AT-SPI actions are unaffected — they never go through a pixel frame.
- `list_windows` bounds and AT-SPI element bounds are already in the logical (input) frame and are consistent with input.
- On GNOME, window screenshots also appear to be crops of a full-display capture rather than per-surface captures, so an occluding window bleeds into the returned window image even after the crop rectangle is corrected. That may be a separate issue; mentioning it only because it surfaced while isolating this one.
- Reporting `scale_factor` truthfully in `get_desktop_state` / `get_window_state` / `get_screen_size` would let callers detect and compensate for this even before the frames are unified.

title: fix(security): refresh Fleet dependency graphs
body:
## Problem

Fleet's public dependency alerts are spread across several stale drafts and direct Dependabot branches. This PR updates the current generated mirror in one import candidate so the changes can move through the canonical Fleet repository instead of being merged into paths that the next mirror sync would overwrite.

There are no application-source changes in this PR. The only non-dependency file is the contributor identity mapping requested by CI for the salvaged work.

## What changed

- Updated the backend's Go dependency set, including pgx, JWT, OPA, OpenTelemetry, x/crypto, x/net, gRPC, x/text, and compress.
- Raised the backend build image and all three changed Go modules to the patched Go 1.25.12 standard library.
- Updated the RBAC test module's x/net and OAuth dependencies.
- Updated the current Terraform provider's x/crypto, x/net, gRPC, and related Go dependencies.
- Updated the Fleet web graph to React Router 7.18, Vite 6.4.3, PostCSS 8.5.23, and Babel 7.29.6.
- Updated the JavaScript SDK generator to 13.12.2 and pinned js-yaml 4.3.1 in both committed lock formats.
- Updated the browser binding example to Vite 6.4.3 with patched nanoid and PostCSS resolutions.

Salvaged from #2274, #2275, #2276, and #2277. The shared dependency work remains credited to @0xjohnnydev in the commit trailer.

This also supersedes the narrower direct dependency PRs #2422, #2518, #2535, #2536, #2537, #2538, #2539, #2540, #2546, #2582, #2583, #2584, and #3050 once the canonical import is accepted.

## Definition of Done

- [x] **The current Fleet dependency graphs resolve outside the public alert ranges.** Backend, RBAC tests, Terraform provider, Fleet web, JavaScript SDK, and browser binding locks select the patched versions.
- [x] **The updated Go dependency sets have no known reachable vulnerabilities.** `govulncheck` reports none when run with the Go 1.25.12 toolchain; backend, RBAC, and provider scans also report no vulnerable imported package or required module.
- [x] **The updated JavaScript locks audit clean.** Fleet web, both JavaScript SDK lock formats, and the browser binding lock report no known advisories.
- [x] **The package-level validation available in the mirror passes.** Backend and RBAC tests pass, the Terraform provider root package builds, and the JavaScript SDK typecheck and tests pass.
- [ ] **A maintainer reviews and merges the imported change in the canonical Fleet repository.** This public PR must not merge directly.
- [ ] **The mirror bot lands the canonical change on CUA `main`.** This PR should then collapse to an empty diff and close.
- [ ] **GitHub confirms alert closure on `main`.** An import draft cannot prove final alert closure.

## Mirror limits

- The public mirror does not contain the backend's local `pkg/featureflags` module. Backend validation used the corresponding module from the freshly fetched canonical Cloud checkout; it was not added to this PR.
- Full Fleet web and browser-binding builds stop because this mirror does not contain the generated `ts/index.web` binding.
- The full Terraform-provider test command also needs canonical-only CRD and native binding artifacts. Its root package builds, and its complete dependency graph passes `govulncheck`.

## Import path

`libs/fleet` is read-only in this repository. The `copybara-import` label is required so this change is reviewed and merged upstream, then returned by the mirror bot. Do not merge this PR directly.

title: chore(deps): bump fastmcp from 2.14.7 to 3.2.0 in /docs/scripts/docs-mcp-server
body:
Bumps [fastmcp](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp) from 2.14.7 to 3.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from fastmcp's releases.

v3.2.0: Show Don't Tool

FastMCP 3.2 is the Apps release. The 3.0 architecture gave you providers and transforms; 3.1 shipped Code Mode for tool discovery. 3.2 puts a face on it: your tools can now return interactive UIs — charts, dashboards, forms, maps — rendered right inside the conversation.

FastMCPApp

FastMCPApp is a new provider class for building interactive applications inside MCP. It separates the tools the LLM sees (@app.ui()) from the backend tools the UI calls (@app.tool()), manages visibility automatically, and gives tool references stable identifiers that survive namespace transforms and server composition — without requiring host cooperation.

from fastmcp import FastMCP, FastMCPApp
from prefab_ui.actions.mcp import CallTool
from prefab_ui.components import Column, Form, Input, Button, ForEach, Text

app = FastMCPApp("Contacts")


@​app.tool()
def save_contact(name: str, email: str) -> list[dict]:
db.append({"name": name, "email": email})
return list(db)


@​app.ui()
def contact_manager() -> PrefabApp:
with PrefabApp(state={"contacts": list(db)}) as view:
with Column(gap=4):
ForEach("contacts", lambda c: Text(c.name))
with Form(on_submit=CallTool("save_contact")):
Input(name="name", required=True)
Input(name="email", required=True)
Button("Save")
return view


mcp = FastMCP("Server", providers=[app])

The UI is built with Prefab, a Python component library that compiles to interactive UIs. You write Python; the user sees charts, tables, forms, and dashboards. FastMCP handles the MCP Apps protocol machinery — renderer resources, CSP configuration, structured content serialization — so you don't have to.

For simpler cases where you just want to visualize data without server interaction, set app=True on any tool and return Prefab components directly:

@mcp.tool(app=True)
def revenue_chart(year: int) -> PrefabApp:
    with PrefabApp() as app:
        BarChart(data=revenue_data, series=[ChartSeries(data_key="revenue")])
    return app

Built-in Providers

Five ready-made providers you add with a single add_provider() call:

  • FileUpload — drag-and-drop file upload with session-scoped storage

FastMCP 3.4.6 backports trusted-proxy support for SSRF-protected OAuth metadata and JWKS fetches. Deployments can now route these requests through a mandated corporate proxy while preserving custom CA certificates; FastMCP refuses the fetch when no proxy is configured instead of risking an unprotected direct request.

title: fix(cua-driver): make Linux browser prepare language independent
body:
## What this fixes

On Linux, `browser_prepare` located and acted on the browser consent / authorization prompt by **matching English UI strings** ("Allow", "Cancel", …). On a host whose locale is not English, those strings do not appear, so:

- the consent prompt was never identified, or the wrong control was matched;
- `browser_prepare` either timed out or acted on the wrong element.

This change removes the language assumption and replaces it with structural, language-independent identification:

- **Consent actions are bound to the native alert** rather than discovered by label text, so the prompt is located by structure/window relationship, not by wording.
- Where several actionable controls remain, a `select_language_independent_allow` discriminator picks the allow action from geometry and enabled-state instead of text equality.
- Adds redacted diagnostics so a failed consent match reports *why* without leaking page content.
- Proves the Linux browser setup destination before acting on it, and extends script/label coverage in tests.

This is the Linux counterpart of the already-merged Windows change (#3135); macOS is tracked separately.

## Why it matters to other users

We drive long-running desktop GUI applications through agents as part of a digital content creation (DCC) pipeline, running on hosts with **non-English locales**. In that setting the browser consent prompt is rendered in the host language, so any English-text matching fails outright — this is not an occasional flake but a deterministic blocker for every non-English user.

More generally, matching native UI by localized string is fragile across browser versions and locales; binding to the native alert structure is stable under both.

## Scope

- 4 files under `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/`.
- Linux backend only. No public API change, no dependency change.

## Verification

- `cargo check -p platform-linux`: clean (only pre-existing dead-code warnings in `overlay.rs`, untouched by this change).
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`: 23 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- Rebased onto current `main`; one semantic conflict with newer upstream label-matching code resolved in favour of the language-independent selector.

Note on platform coverage: the Linux crate compiles and its unit tests run on the development host used here. The integration test `kwin_helper_contract` is `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`-gated, so its coverage **relies on** the repository's CI lane; workflow runs for pull requests from forks start only after a maintainer approves them, so that lane has not reported on this change yet.

title: [Bug]: macOS browser setup and consent depend on English AX titles
body:
## Primary area

Cua Driver

Exact-window browser preparation should support any UI language without translation tables. The action must be proven by the approved PID/window, native-versus-renderer boundary, exact internal URL, AX role/action, unique topology, focus, geometry, and post-state.

Localized AX titles cause valid setup or consent surfaces to be missed. Suggestion text also embeds an English accessibility suffix.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep named CLI sessions and include X11 overlay in screenshots
body: ## Summary - One-shot `cua-driver call` (and `cua-driver-local call`) always minted a disposable transport `cli-{uuid}` and sent `session_end` after the response. That reaped every public session owned by that transport, so the agent cursor overlay disappeared immediately. A following `get_agent_cursor_state` with the same public `session` returned "session has ended". A held MCP connection kept the overlay because its transport stayed alive. - X11 `get_desktop_state` captured the root via ImageMagick `import -window root` or `XGetImage` on root. The overlay is a shaped override-redirect window (`Cua.AgentCursorOverlay.*`). Root reads cannot see those pixels (daemon log: "root reads cannot see this window's own pixels"), so PNG screenshots omitted the cursor even while picom composited it into x11vnc/noVNC. ## What changed - **Named CLI sessions keep the overlay.** If JSON args include a non-empty `session` string, that public name is the daemon transport id and the CLI does **not** send `session_end`. Later `call` invocations with the same `session` continue that overlay. `end_session` still tears it down. Calls without `session` still mint `cli-{uuid}` and `session_end` it (security / one-shot cleanup unchanged). - **X11 desktop screenshots include the mapped overlay.** After the root capture, the screenshot path finds mapped `Cua.AgentCursorOverlay.*` windows, reads their shaped pixmap, and blends those premultiplied pixels onto the root buffer. Disabled or unmapped overlays leave the root capture unchanged. Root-only `XGetImage` is no longer the final capture when the overlay is shown. ## Grok Bot / Xvfb reproduction Observed on a Grok Bot Linux VM (Debian 13, Xvfb `:2`, picom, no root): 1. `cua-driver call move_cursor '{"session":"demo","x":...,"y":...}'` painted the overlay, then tore it down on the synchronous `session_end` of `cli-{uuid}`. `get_agent_cursor_state` with `{"session":"demo"}` then failed with "session has ended". The same sequence over a held MCP connection kept the overlay. 2. `get_desktop_state` / root `XGetImage` omitted the cursor while the x11vnc/noVNC view (picom-composited) showed it. ## Related work No linked GitHub issue. Aligns CLI with the already-documented public session label ("repeat a short public session on every call"). Not a new SDK/MCP contract; no RFC. ## Compatibility and risk - User-visible: named `cua-driver call` sessions now persist until `end_session` or idle TTL, matching MCP/SDK. Unnamed one-shot calls are unchanged. - X11 screenshots may now include overlay pixels when the overlay is mapped. macOS/Windows capture is unchanged. - Rollback: revert this commit. ## Validation - `cargo test -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver named_cli_session unnamed_cli_call blank_or_non_string_session` - `cargo test -p platform-linux capture::` (19 passed, 1 ignored live XShm test) - Known gap: no live Xvfb overlay-in-screenshot run in this environment. Compositing is covered by focused unit tests (empty/unmapped tiles, opaque and translucent blend, ARGB zpixmap alpha). Linux CI X11 overlay click-through remains the live overlay gate. ## Contributor and release checks - [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff. - [x] This change does not require an RFC (documented session-label contract; CLI now honors it). - [x] Tests and the Xvfb/Grok Bot reproduction are in this description; live screenshot-with-overlay on Xvfb is the remaining CI/maintainer gap. - [x] Title is a Conventional Commit for the production fix (`fix(cua-driver): ...`). - [x] No external contribution to attribute. - [x] Release-tracked: user-visible CLI session + X11 screenshot behavior, so this should release.

title: fix(cua-driver): diagnose Linux hosts and refuse dishonest background PX
body: ## Summary - Problem this solves: `cua-driver diagnose` on Linux printed a broken macOS TCC dump, and `doctor` did not warn that Xvfb / missing `/dev/uinput` cannot host background MPX. Background pixel clicks on those hosts fell through to XSendEvent and returned `effect: unverifiable`, which looks like a landed click. - What changed: Linux `diagnose` prints a host section (display server, compositor, uinput, session bus, AT-SPI, background MPX) and explicitly skips macOS TCC/codesign. Linux `doctor` warns on Xvfb/Xtigervnc and missing/inaccessible `/dev/uinput`. When AT-SPI-at-point misses and MPX cannot run, background PX/scroll/drag returns structured `background_unavailable` so the caller retries with `delivery_mode: foreground`. ## Reproduction (Grok Bot Linux VM) Debian 13, user `box`, no root: - Display: `Xvfb :2 -screen 0 1280x800x24` plus `x11vnc`. `xfwm4 --compositor=off` and `picom --backend xrender`. - `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` unset, `/run/user/1000` does not exist, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` unset in the agent shell, no systemd user (`systemctl` missing), no `xfce4-session`. - `/dev/uinput` does not exist. - `at-spi2-core` not installed; `at-spi-bus-launcher` absent; `org.a11y.Bus` ServiceUnknown. `get_window_state` returns `degraded: true` with that reason. - Before this change, `doctor` warned AT-SPI only. It did not warn about Xvfb or missing uinput. - `diagnose` was macOS-shaped (TCC, `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, `~/Library/.../TCC.db`, LaunchAgents) and needed `sqlite3`. - Background PX on Chromium cannot use MPX; AT-SPI-at-point is dead; remaining rungs were XSendEvent (unreliable on Chrome) or `delivery_mode: foreground`. Clicks often returned `effect: unverifiable`. ## Related work No linked intake issue. Small, self-contained fix from maintainer-selected Cloud Agent work. RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission, or cross-component contract change): not required. The `background_unavailable` / `delivery_mode: foreground` contract is unchanged; the driver now emits it when the host cannot land background PX. ## Compatibility and risk - User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux `doctor`/`diagnose` output changes. Background PX/scroll/drag on Xvfb or no-uinput hosts now refuse with `code: background_unavailable` instead of a quiet unverifiable success. Foreground delivery and AT-SPI-at-point are unchanged. macOS diagnose is unchanged. - Risk and rollback: revert this commit. GTK3 harness already expected this refusal when MPX is unavailable (except left-click AT-SPI). ## Validation - Focused tests and checks: - `cargo test -p platform-linux --locked --lib` filters: `diagnostics::`, `background_pixel_refuses`, `no_mpx_pointer`, `real_pointer_capabilities` - `cargo test -p cua-driver --locked --bin cua-driver` filters: `doctor::`, `diagnose_linux` - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - Manual or platform evidence: unit tests inject the Grok Bot facts (Xvfb `:2`, missing uinput, unset `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, no `/run/user/1000/bus`, AT-SPI down). Full desktop E2E matrix not rerun; this is probe/honesty logic, not a harness-app behavior change on real Xorg. - Known gaps or CI still required: ordinary PR CI (`CI: Release metadata`, Linux Rust unit/compile). Doctor does not apt-install `at-spi2-core`. ## Contributor and release checks - [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff. - [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above. - [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained. - [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change. - [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included. - [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.

title: docs(rfcs): define OAuth and MCP gateway boundary
body:
## Summary

- define Cua Driver's standard, transport-neutral MCP boundary
- place OAuth, DCR, TLS, tunnels, and provider adapters in a separate optional gateway
- keep one canonical Driver tool inventory and require trusted local approval for remote desktop access

## Why

PR #2063 demonstrates demand from remote MCP clients that require OAuth and HTTPS. Keeping the public OAuth edge inside `cua-driver` would couple the desktop runtime to token storage, tunnel operations, and client-specific compatibility rules.

This RFC moves those responsibilities to a separately owned gateway while keeping Driver as the final authorization point.

Refs #3197.

Salvaged from #2063. The RFC and commit preserve `outdog-hwh`'s design credit; later implementations must preserve authorship for any material code they adapt.

## Validation

- `prettier --check rfcs/3197-oauth-mcp-gateway-boundary.md`
- RFC template-section and placeholder scan
- `git diff --check`
- repository-relative target check for every linked source and RFC file

## Review focus

- ownership and packaging of the gateway
- the minimum authenticated Driver connection-lease contract
- trusted local approval ownership on each platform
- first supported OAuth and MCP transport profiles
- DCR, token lifetime, revocation, storage, and tunnel policy

This is a draft decision document. It does not authorize implementation until the RFC is accepted.

title: fix(cua-driver): route foreground typing into Screen Sharing canvases
body:
## Problem

`type_text` cannot deliver foreground keyboard input to an exact Apple Screen Sharing window whose content is exposed as `AXSharedScreen`.

## Reproduction

Environment:

- macOS host
- Cua Driver `0.19.4-nightly.20260812.31613035038`
- Apple Screen Sharing connected to a local disposable VNC target
- multiple Screen Sharing windows present

Steps:

1. Resolve the Screen Sharing PID and exact connected window with `launch_app` / `list_windows`.
2. Snapshot that exact window. Its content is an `AXSharedScreen`; the response reports `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` for the PID keyboard route.
3. A foreground pixel click against the exact PID/window returns:

   `effect: unverifiable`, `route: global_input`

4. Attempt foreground pixel-addressed typing against the same exact PID/window:

   `type_text({pid, window_id, x, y, text, delivery_mode: "foreground"})`

Actual result:

`type_text failed: exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery`

The text is not delivered to the remote canvas.

## Expected

Foreground delivery should temporarily focus the exact Screen Sharing connection window, route text into its shared-screen canvas, and restore the prior foreground app. If this surface cannot be supported safely, the driver should return a specific pre-dispatch capability error that identifies Screen Sharing / `AXSharedScreen`, instead of the generic exact-window focus failure.

## Notes

The exact-window binding matters because several Screen Sharing windows may share one PID. No remote address, credentials, screenshots, or private task data are required to reproduce.
