title: launch_app steals focus on GNOME/X11 despite active:false reply
body:
## Environment
- cua-driver 0.20.0 (linux-x86_64), Ubuntu 22.04.5, GNOME Shell 42.9, X11

## Summary
`launch_app` on GNOME/X11 gives the newly launched window keyboard focus, even though the response reports `"active": false`. For co-work ("no-foreground") workflows this is disruptive: launching an app while the user is typing steals their focus.

## Reproduction (2026-08-18)
- Active window: user's terminal (verified via `xdotool getactivewindow`).
- `launch_app {"name": "gnome-calculator"}` → response `"active": false`, but the calculator window received keyboard focus (user observed focus switch; verified active window changed).
- Input-delivery tools correctly avoid focus changes (background `click` verified: digits landed in an unfocused calculator while focus and cursor stayed in the user's window) — only `launch_app` has the problem.

## Suspicion
The daemon spawns the process without a startup-notification (SN) timestamp, so the WM applies its default new-window focus policy. Passing a SN sequence with a stale/zero timestamp (or setting `_NET_WM_USER_TIME` to 0 on the launched window) would make GNOME keep focus with the user's window.

## Suggestion
A `--no-focus`/`background: true` option on `launch_app`, or SN timestamp handling. Thanks — the rest of the input model is exemplary for co-work use.

title: feat(cua-driver): support Helium profile attachment on Linux and macOS
body:
Fixes #3252

Helium was classified as an unknown browser, so authorized existing-profile attachment failed before endpoint discovery. This change recognizes Helium as a Chromium-family standalone browser on Linux and macOS and resolves its default profile directory.

## Behavior

- Linux: recognize the exact Helium executable basename and resolve `~/.config/net.imput.helium`.
- macOS: recognize `net.imput.helium`, classify the main process as a standalone consumer, and resolve `~/Library/Application Support/net.imput.helium`.
- Preserve existing-profile grants, exact PID/window binding, loopback ownership, and fresh endpoint reproof. Helium requires its own PID-owned `DevToolsActivePort`; its generic `/json/version` fallback remains disabled.
- Linux packed command lines retain normal NUL-delimited parsing whenever available. A recovered profile candidate must be corroborated by a live SingletonSocket held by the exact process tree; ordinary path/URL text and ambient working directories cannot prove a profile.
- Automatic setup without an existing endpoint remains an explicit refusal. Windows Helium recognition is outside this change and is documented as unsupported.

## Regression and E2E coverage

The existing reviewer-requested Linux parser, role, and kernel socket ownership regressions are retained. macOS adds product identity and default-profile coverage.

The standalone Rust harness accepts `CUA_E2E_BROWSER_PRODUCTS=helium`, discovers Linux/macOS installations, launches disposable profiles with spaces in their paths, and obtains the browser-written endpoint using port zero. It tests actual attachment, missing-endpoint refusal while the real listener remains alive, no-endpoint setup refusal, and isolated launch selected by the exact Helium PID. Existing application, focus, z-order, cursor, and leaked-input oracles remain enforced.

The Linux standalone CI lane includes Chrome and a pinned Helium 0.18.1.1 package verified against its SHA-256 digest. The macOS hosted browser lane opts into Helium alongside Chrome/Edge, installs a pinned architecture-specific 0.18.1.1 image with a verified SHA-256 digest, and attests the Helium code-signing identifier/team.

## Validation

Final candidate: `7e4d924bdcaef2e770eb02b378e239757aa447fc` (based on upstream `0f29c142d`).

Linux/Windows product and browser-harness certification uses `05285d04809da09dbb3ac73386817d814c9e604c`. The final diff adds only a pinned macOS Helium installation and opt-in hosted browser selection in `.github/workflows/e2e-rust-macos.yml` and `scripts/ci/macos/run-hosted-rust-e2e.sh`; Linux/Windows code and environments are unchanged. The affected macOS matrix is dispatched anew on the final candidate.

Local focused evidence:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Linux platform tests with Wayland variables unset: 587 unit tests and 8 integration tests pass; desktop-only rows remain ignored in this unit invocation.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --locked`: 771 unit tests and all invoked integration tests pass.
- Strict browser-product selection: pass.
- Live Helium in a disposable Xvfb/Openbox X11 desktop: authorized existing-profile attachment, missing-active-port refusal, unavailable-setup refusal, and exact-product isolated launch pass.
- Docs hygiene, internal links, production build, and Cua Driver generated-reference drift checks pass.
- Complete local standalone Helium suite at `05285d048`: **23 cells pass: 16 delivered, 7 expected refusals, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. The canonical report validator accepts all required video and trajectory evidence. Environment: disposable Xvfb/Openbox X11; CDP reports Chromium `152.0.7977.64`.
- [Linux unit CI](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36723419678), [Windows unit CI](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36723424688), and [macOS unit CI](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36724747367): pass. The macOS run includes the final isolated-launch test adjustment.

- [Linux complete desktop matrix](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36723696716)
- [Windows complete desktop matrix](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36723701276)

- On this Niri/Wayland host, the upstream overlay test `unreported_arrival_releases_the_waiter_after_the_cap` fails; unsetting Wayland variables makes the entire platform suite pass. The overlay file is unchanged from upstream.

title: feat(cua-driver): capture embedded startup diagnostics
body:
## Summary

- Add opt-in stderr capture to `EmbeddedCuaDriverHost` and expose bounded startup diagnostics through generated Python and TypeScript bindings.
- Retain the final 65,536 stderr bytes, report truncation only when bytes were discarded, and preserve the child exit code when known.
- Give each startup its own diagnostics capture so stale stderr tasks cannot modify a later generation.
- Make one managed child own the process, liveness pipe, stderr pump, and shutdown timeout.
- Preserve existing stderr inheritance and constructor defaults, export `EmbeddedDriverDiagnostics` from Python, and document the sensitivity of raw stderr.

Refs #3278.

## Design

Each startup creates one shared diagnostics capture. The host retains it as the latest result, while the stderr pump writes directly to that same capture. A successful startup clears it by reference identity. An old pump only retains its detached capture and therefore cannot reach diagnostics from a newer startup.

The managed child provides one cleanup path for graceful shutdown, forced termination, stderr draining, and exit-status recording. This removes generation fields and comparisons from diagnostics, the fixed 250 ms startup shutdown path, and the former standalone append, clear, finish, and terminate helpers.

## Diff scope

The committed generated bindings account for 203 added lines. Focused tests account for 139 added lines. The handwritten Rust runtime change is 293 additions and 57 removals, or 236 net lines. The ownership refactor removed 43 net handwritten lines from the earlier candidate. No unrelated product files are included.

## Validation

Local validation:

- `cargo check -p cua-driver-sdk --lib --locked`: passed
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-sdk --lib --locked`: 53 passed
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --test embedded_host_sdk_mcp_test --locked`: 6 passed
- `node libs/cua-driver/scripts/generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check`: passed
- Python generated-options and public diagnostics import tests: 2 passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

All required pull request checks pass across macOS, Linux, and Windows. The first Nix YAML policy run failed while downloading from `cache.nixos.org`; its rerun passed without a code change.

No desktop E2E certification is claimed because this change affects SDK-owned startup lifecycle rather than desktop interaction behavior.

## Current-main refresh, 3 Nov

- Merged current `main` without rewriting earlier commits. Conflicts were limited to test fixtures and generated TypeScript: main's new `isolated_driver_host` helper and the private-worker fixture now pass `capture_stderr: false`, and the UniFFI bindings were regenerated (`--check` passes).
- Replaced the stderr pump's `loop`/`let else` with `while let` to satisfy clippy on the pinned toolchain. Behavior is unchanged: stop on read error or EOF.
- The scoped repository checks pass on macOS: `cargo fmt` and `cargo test --locked` for `cua-driver` and `cua-driver-sdk`, which includes the six embedded-host tests and 110 SDK tests. The UniFFI generated bindings check passes. The Python UniFFI loader tests and the TypeScript typecheck and tests pass with `CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1`. Without that variable, the two "own the runtime in process" tests take the CuaDriver.app daemon path from #5090 on a Mac that has the app installed. The PR does not touch that path.
- Linux and Windows CI cover the remaining platforms.

Size limit: the managed-child ownership refactor and bounded capture form one lifecycle change; splitting them would leave the stderr pump without a single owner.

## Summary

Promotes the playground's movement parameters into a shared, repository-owned movement spec, so the gallery and the production platform overlays consume one source of truth for cursor motion.

- **Shared spec** (`assets/motion.default.json`, schema `cua.cursor-motion/1`): embedded at compile time via `include_str!` and parsed once. `MotionConfig::default()`, the Windows/Linux spring derivation, the macOS reference settle constants, and the thrice-duplicated `CLICK_OFFSET` all now derive from this single file. The per-platform `spring_settle` sections are explicit (macOS `k=400, c=17, overshoot=0.8`; Windows/Linux derived `spring*400 / spring*20`, overshoot 0.5) — behavior-preserving, not unified.
- **Strict checked-in contract**: parsing validates the exact schema, typed `fixed`/`derived` platform modes, finite production bounds, and speed-floor cross-fields. An invalid embedded asset fails fast with no shadow defaults.
- **Parity gates**: a double-entry test pins the embedded spec against an independent Rust literal (`reference_defaults()`), and a thrown-away harness proved trajectories bit-identical to the pre-change build on both platform tick paths before being discarded.
- **Gallery manifest v2**: the exporter records the exact movement contract it rendered (effective values, spring mode, overridden fields), so an overridden recording can never be mistaken for production defaults.
- **Movement lab UI** (dev-only): six sliders bounded to production ranges rebuild the preview through the production renderer; state echoes from the server so UI and file never drift.
- **Dev server**: one whitelisted loopback POST endpoint writes the override to a fixed ignored path; payload size-capped, origin-checked, and sanitized (unknown fields/non-finite/out-of-range rejected).
- **Promotion workflow**: `cursor-gallery.sh promote-motion` merges a tuned override into the shared spec with a value-only canonical diff, re-validating hand-edited files through the same sanitizer and the exporter's cross-field rule (floors ≤ effective peak). Parity tests gate the promotion.

## Decision record

An advisory architecture review (Claude Code Fable, read-only plan mode) recommended the JSON-spec + `include_str!` + parse-once-static approach, per-platform spring-settle sections instead of unification, a single whitelisted dev endpoint, and promotion with contract tests. The implemented design follows it. Full advisory archived in the linked card.

## Validation

Local, at candidate SHA `a5690ed2f`:

- `cargo test -p cursor-overlay --lib` — 49 passed (incl. spec parity and rejection tests)
- `cargo test -p cursor-overlay --example export_gallery_frames --features theme-authoring` — 11 passed
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s libs/cua-driver/tools/cursor-gallery -p "test_*.py"` — 16 passed
- `cargo fmt --check`, `bash -n`, `node --check` clean; `platform-macos/windows/linux` `cargo check` clean
- Loopback e2e: POST override → rebuild → manifest echoes `overridden_fields` + effective values
- Trajectory parity: bit-identical pre/post refactor on both tick paths (throwaway harness, not committed)

Platform evidence at exact candidate SHA `a5690ed2f` (workflow_dispatch with requested SHA; the resolve job pinned `CUA_E2E_SOURCE_SHA` and every downstream job fetched this commit):

- **Linux X11 — exact-candidate recert** ([run 32519842962](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32519842962)): success — all 6 jobs (install-local.sh smoke, shared Electron + Tauri, capture and desktop scope, GTK3 + GTK4 native harnesses, matrix summary); this run's head SHA is `a5690ed2f` directly, pinning the interactive X11 gate to the exact candidate.
- **Linux X11 — companion recert** ([run 32517328710](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32517328710)): success — all 6 jobs, confirming the same gate.
- **Standalone browsers at `a5690ed2f`** ([run 32519839892](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32519839892) + companion [run 32517331028](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32517331028)): both runs conclusive. Linux X11/chrome succeeded in both. Windows chrome+edge failed with the pre-existing attestation defect — decisive: the test `standalone_browser_prepare_isolated` panicked at `standalone_browser_behavior_test.rs:2229` (`left: String("refused")` / `right: "ok"`), structured `code: browser_route_unavailable`, message `no vendor-signed protected Chromium executable is available for isolated launch`, identical on Chrome and Edge — a runner-environment attestation gap, not a movement-spec regression; tracked separately on the Windows triage card.

Pre-hardening platform diagnostics at SHA `5ebe5f012`:

- **Windows** ([run 32509120689](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32509120689)): success — native WPF + WinUI3 + WebView2, capture + desktop scope, shared Electron + Tauri, installer + update smoke, matrix summary

- **Standalone browsers** ([run 32512934295](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32512934295)): Linux X11/chrome success. Windows chrome+edge failed with `browser_route_unavailable: no vendor-signed protected Chromium executable is available for isolated launch` — a runner-environment issue pre-existing on `main` (the last 7 main runs of this workflow failed identically), not caused by this change.

## Interactive playground evidence

Real Movement Lab interaction was verified at exact candidate `a5690ed2f` through an exactly bound, driver-owned Chrome window using Cua Driver's snapshot-before/action/fresh-snapshot-after loop:

- A real pointer drag changed `peak_speed` from `900` to `2000`. macOS correctly refused the background gesture; the explicit foreground fallback delivered it with input route `global_input`.
- The page moved from `ready` to `building`, then returned to `ready` after rebuilding through the production Rust renderer.
- Gallery manifest v2 echoed effective `peak_speed: 2000` with `overridden_fields: ["peak_speed"]`; all other effective fields remained at production defaults.
- All 3,000 generated movement frames retained transparent canvas margin: zero frames touched an image edge and the minimum margin was 56 pixels.
- The rendered Reset control rebuilt the preview to production defaults (`peak_speed: 900`, no overridden fields) and removed the fixed override file.
- Browser binding quality was `exact`, endpoint access was `driver_owned`, mutation was allowed, and the slider gesture's successful input trust class was native foreground `global_input` after the platform-declared background refusal.

## Pending requested platform evidence

This pull request remains draft and the following user-requested exact-candidate rows remain gates for the active validation goal:

title: test(cua-driver): normalize Windows browser trust posture
body:
## What this fixes

The canonical standalone-browser workflow failed the isolated-launch cells on GitHub-hosted Windows even though Chrome and Edge were vendor-signed. The runner token is elevated and can write beneath `Program Files`, while production Cua Driver intentionally refuses pid-free isolated launch from any browser tree writable by its current token.

## Root cause

This was an environment-parity defect in the E2E harness, not a product trust defect. Weakening the production check would have broadened the isolated-launch trust boundary.

## Change

Before the Windows browser matrix runs, the disposable hosted runner now adds non-inherited deny rules for the exact write/modify rights that Cua Driver probes on the installed Chrome/Edge executable and every ancestor through the relevant `Program Files` root.

This preserves the real product contract during certification:

- the candidate browser remains readable and executable;
- the current test token cannot modify the browser installation chain;
- vendor Authenticode verification remains mandatory and unchanged;
- no production Cua Driver code changes;
- Linux behavior is unchanged.

The ACL changes are confined to the ephemeral GitHub-hosted runner, which is discarded after the job.

title: Cua Driver: native open-panel sheet is observable but cannot be AX-targeted in window scope
body:
## Environment

- macOS
- Cua Driver `0.21.1-nightly.20260822.32551728570`
- Window-scoped session with unrestricted driver permissions

## Reproduction

1. Open a native macOS app window through Cua Driver.
2. Trigger an `NSOpenPanel` sheet from that window.
3. Snapshot the app main window. The AX tree includes an `AXSheet` and actionable descendants such as sidebar cells and the search field.
4. Act on a fresh descendant `element_token`.
5. Separately list windows and snapshot the CG window titled `Open`.

## Expected

A fresh AX token returned beneath the main-window snapshot can be acted on, or the sheet has an exact independently targetable window identity.

## Actual

- The main-window snapshot returns the sheet descendants, but actions refuse with `element_outside_target_window`, saying the element cannot be proven to belong to the main window.
- The separately listed `Open` window snapshots as `ax_unresolved`; its screenshot is available, but both AX and background pixel routes are refused.
- Re-snapshotting does not resolve either state.
- Window-local foreground pixel delivery can report `unverifiable` without changing the sheet.
- A desktop-scope click at the same visible control succeeds.

This leaves a native sheet visible and semantically described but unusable through the normal window ladder. No sensitive file names, paths, or screenshots are included.

feat(cua-driver): add target-bound credential delivery
body:
## Intent

Implement the provider-neutral, target-bound credential delivery architecture proposed in RFC #2942. This stays draft until the RFC is accepted and the exact candidate passes the required security and Fleet evidence.

## Implemented

- make recording projections explicit for every currently advertised mutable tool and fail closed for unknown mutations while recording
- redact text, value, URL, path, clipboard, file, and download inputs before retention; visible typing labels no longer echo caller content
- classify only live semantic-v2 DOM-backed `input[type=password]` nodes as secure password fields
- omit password values, masks, and lengths from semantic output; AX-protected fields are redacted even when DOM evidence is unavailable, without becoming eligible for delivery
- add an internal provider-neutral broker with target-first discovery, opaque fresh handles, exact runtime/session/process/endpoint/tab/frame/document/origin/ref binding, expiry, single use, release limits, revocation, and cancellation
- add a distinct internal R3 `secret_release` authorization adapter: Standard denies, Bounded requires an exact version-three credential binding and origin scope, and optional manifests narrow Unrestricted
- bind authorization permits to the handle, binding, provider, exact browser target, permission mode, manifest, and policy hashes, then revalidate inside the release critical section
- reject already-ended sessions and suspended runtimes, wire terminal runtime suspension to broker revocation, and require provider-side cancellation checks before prompts, unlocks, IPC, reads, or fills
- remove consumed/revoked/expired handles from active retention, retain only bounded content-free tombstones, enforce a per-session active-handle quota, and avoid partial discovery minting
- keep bootstrap credentials in a separate internal store abstraction and keep secret-bearing values non-debuggable, non-serializable, and zeroizing
- keep the foundation out of public tools, contracts, MCP, CLI, ABI, UniFFI, and generated SDKs until the secure route is certified

## Security properties covered by tests

- discovery exposes only safe descriptors and never invokes a provider
- target, field, cross-runtime, and cross-broker handle replay are refused
- release reservations are atomic and provider failure consumes the handle
- session, binding, provider, and runtime revocation cancel in-flight releases and reject late plans
- cancellation tombstones prevent a provider effect even when cancellation arrives before release
- drop and post-return revocation cancel exactly once; every release-plan variant has a revocation-gated accessor
- capacity failure mints no partial batch, per-session quotas prevent cross-session starvation, and expiry/revocation releases active capacity
- provider errors collapse to fixed enums and secret/bootstrap payloads have fixed bounds
- password fixtures prove positive eligibility, negative near-misses, and redaction-only AX protection

## Validation so far

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --locked` (612 unit tests, 2 contract parity tests, 3 lifecycle tests, and doc tests)
- focused broker suite: 21 passed
- focused `secret_release` authorization/manifest suite: 2 passed
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets --locked` completes with the repository's existing warning set
- independent adversarial architecture review completed; confirmed findings were addressed in the current head
- changed-file scan found no credentials, bootstrap values, private service metadata, or prohibited competitor references; only synthetic test locators and canaries are present

## Remaining gates

- fresh verified-target minting inside `BrowserEngine` and target-first broker discovery
- exact-node guarded CDP delivery with boolean-only event evidence and no plaintext fallback
- Windows/Linux bootstrap stores and dedicated automation-vault provider
- atomic public contract, ABI, UniFFI, Python, TypeScript, CLI, and MCP exposure
- source-built exact-candidate Linux and Windows Cua Cloud Fleet certification, including synthetic-secret retention scans and deterministic claim/pool cleanup

Refs #2942
RFC: #2943

title: feat(cua-driver): add target-scoped post-action rediscovery
body:
## why

[#2238](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2238) describes a stale-target failure: an action starts against window a, opens a sheet, dialog, popover, or Open/Save panel b, and leaves the caller bound to a. later snapshots and actions then target the blocked parent instead of the new interaction surface.

cua-driver already noticed some new macos windows, but its global detector could not prove that a desktop change belonged to the action. it also kept the result in diagnostic prose, so callers received neither a stable window address nor a machine-readable rebind instruction.

this pr resolves the structured-rediscovery part of the issue. after an action opens a target-owned surface, the result identifies the observed candidates and recommends `rebind`. when exactly one candidate is owner-verified, the result includes its `(pid, window_id)` so the caller can take a fresh window-scoped snapshot without activating or raising it.

## design

### retained from cua-driver

this keeps cua-driver's native action routes, focus-suppression leases, shared `ActionExecutionRecord`, closed `ActionResult`, and harness-owned escalation policy. it also retains the useful contract work from [#2746](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2746): typed `window_change` metadata, an explicit `rebind` escalation, and generated rust, python, typescript, and manifest bindings.

it removes the unsafe parts of the old path: the desktop-global `WindowChangeDetector`, seven per-tool diagnostic suffix mutations, the dead observation-skip hook, topology transport through legacy json, and window changes as evidence that an actuator succeeded.

### adapted from pi-computer-use

this adapts the target-root observation model from `injaneity/pi-computer-use` commit `022a280a377065c95736cc15f684bf1fad46479e`:

- snapshot the addressed process's accessibility roots before dispatch;
- run the native actuator;
- use a cheap target-window signature only to end a 400 ms wait early;
- run the authoritative accessibility diff once, with bounded catch-up when the signal beats the tree; and
- rebind directly when the AX diff yields one owner-verified logical root, and fail closed when several roots appear.

the persistent ax-observer ring is intentionally not copied because the source commit established that sheet creation emits no reliable notification; it adds lifecycle state without improving correctness here. cua-driver instead merges `AXSheets` with `AXChildren`, keeps its focus-suppression lease across dispatch and observation, and resolves owners only after the authoritative ax diff. unresolved appeared roots retry WindowServer ownership independently; an incomplete owner set can return known candidates but never an exact target.

### combined result

```text
macos action decorator
  → target-process ax snapshot
  → native actuator
  → target-process ax diff
  → windowserver ownership proof
  → shared candidate resolver
  → typed action record
  → closed action result
```

observation and action accounting remain separate. a surface change can add `window_change` and `escalation`, but it cannot promote `effect` to `confirmed`; confirmation still requires value readback. ambiguous candidates are returned without an invented exact target and can be correlated with one fresh `list_windows` call.

## issue coverage

this pr covers the structured rebind rung from [#2238](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2238):

- return stable candidate pids, window ids, titles, app names, and foreground-change state;
- recommend `rebind`, with an exact target only when ownership and modal/focused state make it unambiguous;
- preserve the human's foreground app, z-order, cursor position, and input isolation; and
- add the canonical TextEdit Open-panel case, then re-address the returned panel window.

it does not implement the issue's later privacy-sensitive desktop-frame fallback or inert-resnapshot backstop. those remain separate because this structured path recovers without widening capture scope. this pr therefore uses `Refs`, not an issue-closing keyword.

## diff shape

the runtime production diff is `+899/-829` (net `+70`). the new 411-line observer replaces the deleted 530-line global detector, while affected macos tool files remove 203 lines and add 79. most apparent growth is required generated contract output: `+1103/-157` across the manifest and python/typescript bindings.

## logical-root correction

host investigation found that AppKit can expose two Open-panel WindowServer records: an AX-addressable same-process TextEdit proxy and an AX-empty XPC duplicate. `pi-computer-use` keeps the target-scoped AX identity rather than requiring the foreign service pid. this branch now does the same: it preserves the appeared AX root's exact WindowServer identity, removes internal modal/focus eligibility state, and rebinds whenever exactly one owner-verified logical root appears. ambiguity still omits the exact target.

on the host probe, the returned TextEdit proxy exposed 62 Open-panel AX elements; the XPC duplicate exposed none. a direct exact-head action returned `escalation.target: rebind`, the proxy `(pid, window_id)`, and a successful fresh scoped snapshot without changing the foreground app.

## compatibility and validation

macos emits the new optional topology. windows and linux emit none rather than substituting a global heuristic. generated sdk consumers gain optional `window_change` plus the `rebind` and `surface_changed` enum values.

local validation passed:

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-contract --lib` — 33 passed
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` — 587 passed at rebased head `f5ea38210932db1389c199bc768891a21b9782e0`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` — 338 passed, 2 ignored at the same sha
- pre-rebase direct host TextEdit Open-panel probe at `a2d513b93ac6122ad4dd8639e3e1ec7c88bca5cf` — one typed rebind to an AX-addressable logical root with 62 elements and unchanged foreground
- pre-rebase complete local macos contributor matrix on an integration of `a2d513b93ac6122ad4dd8639e3e1ec7c88bca5cf` with [#2907](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2907) — 140 of 158 cells passed; `macos-textedit-open-panel-background-rebind` passed all five declared oracles. the 18 unrelated failures were host input-isolation, cursor, desktop-coordinate, and video-finalization failures, so this is diagnostic evidence rather than canonical acceptance
- contract and uniffi generation checks
- typescript build and python binding compile check
- rustfmt, shell syntax, and diff checks

before this pull request is ready, the final candidate still needs the canonical macos Lume matrix. the local host can run the complete matrix when the foreground-sentinel fix in [#2907](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2907) is included, but its active desktop is not an acceptance environment: cursor movement, global-coordinate delivery, and concurrent recordings caused unrelated failures. maintainers must also confirm whether this additive public contract requires a separate rfc.

Salvaged from [#2746](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2746).

Refs [#2238](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2238).


## stacked scheduling follow-up

The stacked draft [#3391](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3391) replaces duplicate native action admission with one scheduler and canonical lease plan, ensuring this pull request's before/action/after decorator remains inside the same desktop action lease. It does not add another observation owner or change the public tool contract.







## canonical macos lume evidence — 2026-09-04

- tested source: `b131ca4f8e22650a8ed992df228f659b93eb9640` (the current PR head, not a merge commit).
- command: `libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/macos-lume/run-all.sh`, full unfiltered matrix; no retry or single-cell selector.
- run id: `20260904T181935Z-11114`.
- environment: disposable public `macos-tahoe-cua:26.5.2` worker, macOS 26.5.2 build 25F84, SIP disabled, stable local certificate, app-owned grants seeded with the repository helper, and a logged-in guest Terminal session.
- results: **158/158 passed**, including 150 delivered actions and 8 expected refusals; 0 failed and 0 skipped.
- `macos-textedit-open-panel-background-rebind`: passed AX state, focus, z-order, cursor, and no-leaked-input checks.
- `failures.json`: `failure_count=0`, `preflight_failed=false`, `report_failed=false`, no failed lanes or video failures.
- daemon verified restored to standard mode; worker stopped and retained.
- evidence retrieved to the maintainer host: `~/workspaces/cua-pr-3373-b131ca4f/artifacts/cua-driver/vm/lume_192.168.64.2/20260904T184538Z/` (local evidence, not a public download link).
- standalone installed Chrome/Edge matrix was **not** run.

This certifies only the SHA above. The requested rebase and review fixes remain outstanding; this evidence must not be presented as certification of a later candidate.

title: [Feature]: get_window_state structured elements should expose action names across platforms

Cua Driver

### User problem

The Linux, macOS, and Windows accessibility walkers in cua-driver already collect action names during `get_window_state`, but  the structured `elements` array omits them. body:
## Problem

Agent View currently duplicates presentation across AppKit, Win32, X11, and Wayland. That makes visual parity and interaction behavior expensive to maintain even though session and exact-target state are already platform-neutral.

Refs #3438.

## Current slice

- Add a cross-platform Tauri companion with a borderless, resizable session/target UI.
- Match the approved platform treatments: clear acrylic on macOS, light Mica on Windows 11, and a smoky desktop shell on Linux.
- Reconcile cards in place and decode replacement screenshots before swapping them, preventing blank-card and host-desktop flashes.
- Use the host wallpaper as an explicit bounded backdrop, with opaque fallbacks when discovery or decoding fails.
- Stream private presentation commands over child-process stdin/stdout; no port is opened.
- Preserve exact target ordering, browser-tab/native-container suppression, session tabs, active-target highlighting, and the synthetic cursor.
- Make Cua Driver prefer the sibling companion and retain the native renderer as a temporary migration fallback.
- Build and stage the companion from the macOS/Linux and Windows local installers.
- Preserve the existing default-off behavior and all CLI/MCP/SDK contracts.

Current visual candidate: `a6a82d2d9c6e8b33259c9c3b0e744bb28e8bfc47`.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo test --locked -p pip-preview` (44 passed)
- [x] `cargo check --locked -p cua-driver`

title: fix(cua-driver): preserve physical pixels in embedded Windows SDK
body:
## Summary

- Initialize Cua-owned Windows threads with Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness without changing the importing application's process-wide DPI setting or caller thread.
- Fail closed at the actual execution boundary, including blocking workers created after successful runtime startup, rather than only recording initialization errors.
- Propagate DPI failures to ABI callers as `RuntimeUnavailable`, preserve resource teardown, and add late-thread regression coverage.

Refs #3449.

## Problem

The standalone executable declares PMv2 awareness in its manifest, but an embedded SDK runs inside an arbitrary host process. The original reproduction used a DPI-unaware Node host on a `2560x1600` display at 150% scaling: the embedded driver reported and captured `1707x1067 @ 1.0`, containing the upper-left physical region, while the standalone daemon captured the complete desktop.

The previous revision initialized Tokio threads but only consumed initialization failures during startup. A later blocking-pool thread could fail DPI setup and still enter native work. Startup probes cannot establish the invariant for future threads.

## Implementation

- Keep a sticky failure state owned by the ABI executor. Every Tokio worker/blocking-thread initializer contributes to that state; later submissions reject a failed executor.
- Gate native blocking closures on their actual execution thread, before calling the work body. Windows backend task submissions use the shared guarded entry points instead of adding checks independently to individual tools.
- Check async operations on every poll and again before accepting their result. This covers worker migration and prevents an optional screenshot fallback from swallowing an initialization error and reporting ABI success.
- Dedicated Windows threads use the same initializer and inherit the submitting thread's owner when one exists. An overlay started during synchronous host-side registry creation instead gets an independent owner; its failure stops the overlay body but does not poison the ABI executor. Single-flight cleanup guards are captured before dispatch so refusal still releases them.
- Guard native window/display capture entry points as well, including calls from recording hooks outside the platform task wrapper.
- Keep shutdown and resource finalization available after failure. Do not retry capture/input automatically, alter coordinate conversion, or change the public tool/ABI schema.

An executor failure is terminal for GUI admission within that executor. This is not transactional cancellation of work already in progress and does not undo input that was issued before a failure.

## Tests

Passed locally on Windows using the GNU Rust toolchain with cached dependencies and `--offline`:

- SDK suite: **46 unit tests and 2 integration tests passed**.
- Windows platform library test target compiled successfully.
- Host-started independent owner and submitting-thread owner inheritance tests: **2 passed**.
- Existing UIA and UWP bounded-worker recovery tests: **2 passed**.
- Existing AppsFolder single-flight timeout/recovery test: **1 passed**.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `git diff --check`.

The added regressions hold the existing blocking worker to force pool growth after startup, inject a late DPI failure, and assert that:

- the guarded native work body is not executed;
- direct display/window capture entry points refuse the failed thread;
- ABI completion returns `RuntimeUnavailable` with no success payload, even if the inner operation swallows the worker error;
- later admission fails, while cleanup completion remains available;
- failure on a dedicated child thread prevents both its work body and the next async continuation;
- healthy late blocking workers and dedicated child threads use PMv2.

The existing real embedded-ABI regression also passes: it checks `get_screen_size`, desktop PNG dimensions and scale, and verifies that the deliberately DPI-unaware host thread remains unchanged. These local results do not substitute for the official input/GUI matrix.


## Maintainer validation — September 6, 2026

The [Windows MSVC workflow](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/33479754606) passed, including all **47 SDK unit tests**, unaware-host regular/trusted ABI capture, late-thread failure handling, and trusted-call cancellation. Its PR merge checkout `3aceac01c8dba4f9dd5d1d08dda6101a78caf7b4` has an identical Git tree to candidate `1a4165a4b47546a86a0bb450cd7581be821128ce`.

The complete [Linux canonical run](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34056686843) passed at that exact candidate SHA: **129 desktop cases** (87 delivered, 42 expected capability refusals), zero failures/skips, plus the installer smoke. Environment records and all per-case videos were retained.

The [Windows canonical run](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34056685900) passed installer, shared (84 cases), and capture (9 cases) lanes, but its native lane has **one failure among 43 cases**: `windows-webview2-left-click-px-background` left the fixture counter at 2 instead of 3. The recorded target is centered on Increment. Desktop UIA enumeration exceeded 2 seconds, returned, and entered a 30-second recovery cooldown before the click. The click fell back to PostMessage; the shared UIA gate also covers point hit-testing. This evidence does not yet attribute the failure to DPI coordinates. A single [native-only repeat](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34057872092) at the unchanged SHA reproduced the same failure: 42/43 cases passed, with a ready environment and the same PostMessage fallback during UIA cooldown. This is a reproducible native gate failure, not a passing retry; both runs are retained. Causation by the DPI changes is not established.

Server 2025 at 100%/150% scaling remains outstanding. Existing requested reviews are not cleared. No merge or release is requested.

title: perf(cua-driver): extend configurable pacing to mouse, WebKit settle, and type_text default
body:
Companion to #3489 (keyboard key gap): the remaining hardcoded input pacing constants on macOS move behind read-once `CUA_DRIVER_RS_*` env overrides. **Every default is unchanged — zero out-of-the-box behavior change.**

| Constant | Sites | Knob | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| mouseMoved-primer settle 12ms | 3 (left, right, scroll primer) | `CUA_DRIVER_RS_MOUSE_PRIMER_MS` | 12 |
| click down→up gap 28ms | 3 (warp path, pid path, right-click) | `CUA_DRIVER_RS_CLICK_GAP_MS` | 28 |
| multi-click pair gap 80ms | 3 | `CUA_DRIVER_RS_MULTI_CLICK_GAP_MS` | 80 |
| WebKit DOM-focus settle 800ms | 1 (`click.rs`) | `CUA_DRIVER_RS_WEBKIT_SETTLE_MS` | 800 |
| `type_text` default `delay_ms` 30 | 2 (`type_text.rs`) | `CUA_DRIVER_RS_TYPE_TEXT_DELAY_MS` | 30 (per-call `delay_ms` still wins) |

All knobs share one `ms_from`/`env_ms` helper in a new `input/pacing.rs`, read once per process, with the parse-and-fallback contract unit-tested (`ms_from_parses_and_falls_back`). The 40-100ms warp/settle sleeps on the foreground path are deliberately untouched — those pace cursor restore and AppKit event consumption, not the click itself.

Evidence that tighter pacing holds up where deployments choose it (Swift driver this Rust tree mirrors, measured live against Safari): primer 4ms + click gap 8ms delivered focus-correct clicks with a typed marker read back through an independent AX referee, and inter-character delay 0 with a 2ms key gap typed 136/136 characters exactly.

title: perf(cua-driver): memoize the installed-app scan behind a root-mtime key
body:
## Problem

`list_all_apps` re-walks five app directories and re-reads every bundle's `Info.plist` on **every call** — hundreds of file reads for an answer that changes only when something is installed or removed. Measured against the 0.16 binary under adversarial load (6 CPU spinners, fresh connection per request): `list_apps` p50 **1.2–2.6 s**, dominated by this scan.

## Change

`scan_installed_apps` is memoized behind a two-part key:

- **Root mtimes** — adding or removing a `.app` bundle touches its parent directory, so an install/uninstall invalidates the cache instantly.
- **30s TTL** — per-bundle `last_used` timestamps (filesystem mtime heuristic) can change without any root directory noticing; the TTL bounds that drift.

An unreadable root keys as `None`, and two `None`s compare equal — a permanently missing root (e.g. no `~/Applications`) still caches instead of rescanning forever. Running apps are untouched: `list_running_apps` still runs live on every call, and running entries are still backfilled from the (now cached) installed scan.

The freshness contract (`installed_cache_is_fresh`) is a pure function with a unit test covering: matching key within TTL → serve; changed mtime, appearing/disappearing root, or expired TTL → rescan.

## Numbers

With the equivalent mtime-keyed cache in the Swift driver this Rust tree mirrors, the same adversarial bench answered `list_apps` in **~15–23 ms** (vs 1.2–2.6 s), with correctness checked against `NSWorkspace` ground truth (21/21 running apps, all bundle ids present).

`cargo test -p platform-macos` — 353 passed. `cargo fmt` applied.

title: perf(cua-driver): run health checks concurrently
body:
## Problem

`HealthReportTool::invoke` awaits each provider check in sequence, so a full report pays the **sum** of every probe's latency — and the slow probes (capture, AX, subprocess-backed checks) dominate. The checks are independent probes; nothing about the report depends on execution order.

## Change

The loop becomes `futures_util::future::join_all` (already a dependency of `cua-driver-core`) over the same per-name closure:

- All check futures are polled **within the same task** — no extra threads, and no new `Send`/`Sync` requirements on `HealthCheckProvider` implementations.
- `join_all` returns results in input order, so the report keeps its canonical check order (pinned by the existing fixture test, still green).
- Skip-filter behavior unchanged: filtered names still yield their skip entries in place.

A provider whose checks must not overlap can still serialize internally, but none of the in-tree providers do — each check is a self-contained probe.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos` — green, including `invoke_full_run_produces_macos_check_set` (canonical order) and the core fixture suite.
- In the Swift driver this Rust tree mirrors, the same change (task group with order-preserving slots) took a warm quiet `health_report` from ~43ms to ~0.4ms; the report's floor becomes the slowest single probe instead of the sum of all probes.

title: uninstall-local.sh reports success while app-bundle daemon and release markers remain
body:
## Summary

`uninstall-local.sh` can print a successful uninstall while a daemon launched from `/Applications/CuaDriverLocal.app` is still running and local release-marker files remain.

The script stops processes launched through the CLI symlink or the package-current executable, but it does not stop the app-bundle executable before deleting the bundle. Its local-home cleanup list also omits `.release_installed` marker files.

## Reproduction

1. Install the local macOS build using the repository's local installer.
2. Start the daemon through the app bundle:

   ```bash
   /Applications/CuaDriverLocal.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver-local serve --dangerously-bypass-approvals
   ```

3. Run the repository's `uninstall-local.sh`.
4. Inspect the local daemon processes and the local product home.

## Expected behavior

The uninstaller should stop every process owned by the local installation before removing its executable, remove all installer-owned marker files, and report success only after the local installation is inactive and its owned state is gone.

## Actual behavior

- The app bundle is removed, but the daemon launched from the app-bundle executable remains running.
- `.release_installed` remains under the local product home, so the directory is preserved.
- The script still prints `cua-driver-local uninstalled`.

## Root cause in the current script

- The process-stop loop checks only the CLI symlink and `$HOME/.cua-driver-local/packages/current/cua-driver-local`; it omits `/Applications/CuaDriverLocal.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver-local`.
- The known-file cleanup list omits `.release_installed`.
- No final verification checks for a remaining local daemon before reporting success.

## Suggested fix

- Stop the exact app-bundle executable path before removing the app.
- Include all installer-owned release markers in the bounded cleanup list.
- Add a final local-identity process check and fail or warn if a daemon remains.

This is distinct from #3191, which addressed the release Unix uninstaller rather than the local macOS app-bundle path.

Confirmed with local package version `0.23.1`; the same omissions remain on current `origin/main` at `72fe7fff6e2d84863585f7164d9663367e8fa465`.

title: fix(cua-cli): preflight credential storage before device login
body:
## Summary

Detect unavailable or explicitly disabled credential storage before starting device authorization. This is a narrow login correction: it does not change identity providers, token scopes, credential precedence, or CLI-to-SDK handoff.

- Perform a read-only check of the configured store before discovery or browser launch. Do not write a probe credential, parse stale data, or select a fallback backend.
- Reject the null backend, whose writes silently discard tokens.
- Keep later save failures actionable and sanitize keyring/OS errors.
- Isolate command tests from the host keychain and add CLI unit CI for Python 3.12/3.13.

## Validation

- CLI suite: 201 passed on Python 3.13.15; five coroutine warnings from unrelated image-command tests.
- Focused Ruff, Black, isort, and whitespace checks.
- Synthetic tests cover unavailable/disabled storage, empty/corrupt old contents, pre-network refusal, later write failure, and credential redaction.

A read check does not prove later writability. No real login is required for these tests. Native platform keyring integration remains a separate manual smoke.

## Review and rollback

Requested implementation scope is the pre-login storage diagnostic. Draft for maintainer review; do not merge automatically. Revert this commit to restore the previous login sequence. No migration, plaintext fallback, package upgrade, or deployment is included.

title: fix(cua-sandbox): explain supported Fleet credential routes

Explain the actual credential routes when the Fleet SDK has no usable token or complete client-credential pair. This changes the early error only; it does not implement a new CLI-to-SDK handoff.

- Name `FLEETS_TOKEN` and `cua.configure(fleet_token=...)` alongside client credentials.
- Identify missing client-credential field names without printing values.
- Explain that this SDK path does not read the separate session stored by `cua auth login`, and that `CUA_API_KEY` is not a Fleet credential.

- Only synthetic credentials used; no network or credential-store access in the new tests.

## Boundaries

No token audience, refresh policy, environment precedence, legacy/custom endpoint routing or permissions change. A static token still has its existing lifetime; this does not resolve #3127. Existing credential-acquisition documentation remains in #3556 rather than being duplicated here. A unified session handoff would require a separate accepted auth contract.

Draft for review, no merge or release authorized. Revert the diagnostic/tests to roll back; no migration or persistent state change.

title: fix(cua-sandbox): reject unauthorized readiness responses
body:
## Summary

Reject HTTP 401/403 during the Fleet guest-service readiness probe instead of reporting the service ready. Previously the `200 <= status < 500` condition accepted those authorization failures.

- Raise an actionable `PermissionError` after an unauthorized/forbidden readiness response.
- Do not print guest/proxy response bodies or retry a terminal access denial in this layer.
- Preserve existing reachable-service behavior for other statuses, including 404 compatibility, and the existing 5xx readiness retry.

## Validation

- Both 401/403 regressions failed against unchanged production code (`DID NOT RAISE`) and pass with this correction.
- 85 Fleet client, transport and configuration tests passed on Python 3.13.15, including resource cleanup on provisioning failure.
- New tests cover 200/204/404 compatibility, 503-to-200 retry, terminal-denial call count and response-body redaction.
- Ruff, Black, isort and whitespace checks passed.

## Limits and related work

This is a reproduced unit-level readiness defect, not a diagnosis or fix for historical 502s, tenant permissions or billing. No live workload or pool was created. Existing cleanup-convergence work remains in #3367 and is not duplicated. This PR and #3582 touch the same client/test files in separate scopes; rebase and rerun the targeted suites after either lands.

Draft for SDK maintainer review; no merge or release authorized. Verify the selected hosted path with an authorized test account before release. Revert this commit to restore prior status handling; no migration or production state change.

title: build(cua-driver): eliminate duplicate macOS Swift bridge symbols
body:
## Problem

Successful macOS Cua Driver builds and focused tests emit repeated duplicate Swift bridge symbol warnings, obscuring actual failures and test summaries. Recorded independently during build/test work on July 20 and August 21, with an additional incidental report on September 7, 2026.

## Investigation

Current main still locks `screencapturekit 6.0.1` and `apple-cf 0.9.3`. Both published Swift packages declare a target named `CoreMediaBridge`. Upstream confirmed that their `AudioBufferBridge` and `AudioBufferListRaw` Swift metadata symbols collide when both object files are linked.

The exact upstream fix already exists: https://github.com/doom-fish/screencapturekit-rs/pull/159 (merged July 18). It renames screencapturekit's private Swift module while preserving its C exports. Preserve that contribution rather than independently reimplementing it.

The fix postdates the published 6.x releases. A dependency update must therefore assess API migration and runtime implications rather than assume a patch-level lockfile refresh is sufficient.

Related Cua evidence: https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2356 records the same warning, but is not a linker-fix workstream. No dedicated active Cua fix was found in searches for duplicate Swift symbols, CoreMediaBridge, apple_cf, and linker warnings.

## Acceptance evidence

- Retain baseline native link output identifying the duplicate Swift symbols.
- Show the same link succeeds without those warnings after the change, while unrelated warnings remain visible.
- Add a focused regression check for the duplicate module/symbol boundary.
- If updating capture dependencies changes production code or behavior, run affected native capture/recording coverage and the required exact-candidate desktop certification before readiness.
- Document Windows/Linux impact explicitly; the colliding Swift bridges are macOS dependencies.

Fresh native reproduction and candidate validation are still pending. Source inspection and upstream evidence are not being presented as a completed local build.

title: fix(agent): execute computer tool calls that arrive as function calls
body:
Fixes #3614.

## Problem

When the configured model does not match `computer-use-preview`, the OpenAI loop hands it the computer tool as a **plain function** (`_map_computer_tool_to_openai(use_native_tool=False)`). The model then answers with a `function_call` named `computer` instead of a `computer_call`.

The dispatch loop had no execution path for that item. `function_call` went straight to `_get_tool()`, which only searches caller-registered tools, so `"computer"` was never found:

```python
if item_type == "function_call":
    await self._on_function_call_start(item)
    function = self._get_tool(item.get("name"))
    if not function:
        raise ToolError(f"Function {item.get('name')} not found")
```

The `ToolError` is caught and fed back to the model, which concludes the tool is unavailable and stops — an accurate report of what happened. As the issue notes, this means the function-calling harness has never actually been able to execute a computer action; only literal `computer-use-preview` models worked, and for models where `computer_use_preview` is rejected by the API this is a hard blocker rather than a degraded path.

## Change

A `computer` function call now runs the same action semantics as a native `computer_call`.

- The shared execution — method lookup, argument validation, telemetry, terminate detection, post-action screenshot — moved into `_execute_computer_action`, which both item types call, so the two paths cannot drift.
- **Both argument spellings are accepted**: the flat schema the function tool advertises (`{"action": "click", "x": 12, "y": 34}`) and the native action dict (`{"type": "click", ...}`), which `replace_failed_computer_calls_with_function_calls` re-emits when a computer_call is retried as a function_call.
- **Flat drag coordinates** (`start_x`/`start_y`/`end_x`/`end_y`) map onto the handler protocol's `path`.
- **Null and non-applicable fields are dropped.** The function tool advertises one flat parameter object shared by every action, so fields belonging to other actions are noise by construction — the trace in the issue shows a `keypress` carrying `status: "success"`. Native `computer_call` items are untouched by this: their action dict is already per-action.
- The reply is a **`function_call_output`**, because the model holds the function tool and not `computer_use_preview`; a `computer_call_output` would not be a valid input item for it. That output carries text only, so the post-action screenshot rides in its own user message.
- `ImageRetentionCallback` now recognizes those captures, so `only_n_most_recent_images` keeps working on this path. It trims only the image message: the `function_call` / `function_call_output` pair is text and has to stay paired.
- A caller-registered tool named `computer` still wins. The built-in semantics are the fallback, not an override.

Malformed arguments, a missing `action`, and an unknown action are reported to the model as tool errors rather than raising.

## Validation

```
CUA_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false uv run pytest libs/python/agent/tests -q   # 62 passed
uv run ruff check libs/python/agent                                    # All checks passed
uv run ruff format ...                                                 # clean
```

`libs/python/agent/tests/test_computer_function_call.py` is new: 13 tests over flat and native argument shapes, field filtering, drag mapping, terminate, screenshot delivery, custom-tool precedence, the three error paths, and retention. Verified against unmodified `main` (stashing only the two source files): **11 fail, 2 pass** — the two that pass are the deliberate no-change guards, `test_native_computer_call_path_is_unchanged` and `test_a_registered_tool_named_computer_still_wins`.

## Known gaps

- No live API call was made from here; the tests drive `_handle_item` against a fake computer handler. The issue already carries the live evidence that the model emits well-formed `function_call` items against this exact schema.
- Only the dispatch gap is addressed. `OperatorNormalizerCallback` still normalizes hallucinated action spellings for `computer_call` items only; extending it to function-call items is a separate change.

title: Anthropic computer-use loop: no tool-version mapping for Claude Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 (falls back to retired computer_20241022)
body:
## Summary
`cua_agent/loops/anthropic.py`'s `MODEL_TOOL_MAPPING` table (used by `_get_tool_config_for_model`) has regex patterns for Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.6, Claude 4, Claude 3.7, and Claude 3.5, but none for the new Claude 5 family (e.g. `claude-sonnet-5`). Since none of the patterns match, model lookups for Sonnet 5 silently fall through to the final default:

```python
# Default to Claude 3.5 configuration
return {"tool_version": "computer_20241022", "beta_flag": "computer-use-2024-10-22"}
```

`computer_20241022` has since been fully retired by the Anthropic API — it is not in the list of tool tags the API currently accepts. Every request built with this fallback fails outright:

```
litellm.BadRequestError: AnthropicException - {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"tools.0: Input tag 'computer_20241022' found using 'type' does not match any of the expected tags: 'bash_20250124', 'browser_toolset_20260801', 'code_execution_20250522', 'code_execution_20250825', 'code_execution_20260120', 'code_execution_20260521', 'computer_toolset_20260801', 'custom', 'memory_20250818', 'text_editor_20250124', 'text_editor_20250429', 'text_editor_20250728', 'tool_search_tool_bm25', 'tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119', 'tool_search_tool_regex', 'tool_search_tool_regex_20251119', 'web_fetch_20250910', 'web_fetch_20260209', 'web_fetch_20260309', 'web_fetch_20260318', 'web_search_20250305', 'web_search_20260209', 'web_search_20260318'"}}
```

## Repro
```python
from cua_agent.loops.anthropic import _get_tool_config_for_model
_get_tool_config_for_model("claude-sonnet-5")
# {'tool_version': 'computer_20241022', 'beta_flag': 'computer-use-2024-10-22'}  <- wrong, and now rejected server-side
```
Confirmed live: running the ComputerAgent loop end-to-end against `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5" (via litellm) with a real E2B sandbox fails on every retry with the 400 above. Reproduced on `cua-agent` 0.8.3 (currently installed) and confirmed the same fallback logic is still present in the latest published 0.8.4.

## Suggested fix
Add a `MODEL_TOOL_MAPPING` entry for the Claude 5 family (`claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-5`, etc.) pointing at whatever tool version/beta flag Anthropic expects for that generation (from the accepted-tags list above, looks like `computer_toolset_20260801` is the current computer-use tag, though I don't have Anthropic's docs confirmation of the exact beta flag name to pair with it).

## Environment
- cua-agent: 0.8.3 (also checked 0.8.4 source on PyPI — same gap)
- Called via gl-computer-use (GDP-ADMIN/gl-sdk), which wraps cua-agent's ComputerAgent as its default automation backend.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep strict local signing noninteractive
body:
## Summary

Strict macOS source installs could find an older signing identity in the user's
login Keychain and unexpectedly open a password dialog during unattended tests.
The test then appeared stuck, and the dialog did not make it clear that local
code signing—not the website—caused the prompt.

This PR makes strict local signing noninteractive by default and gives clearer
instructions when a user deliberately chooses a keychain that may prompt.

## What changes

- Do not select the login Keychain automatically during strict source signing.
- Prefer the dedicated Cua Driver development keychain when it is available.
- Continue to support an explicitly selected signing identity and keychain.
- When the login Keychain was selected explicitly, explain that any prompt is
  for local-build signing and should not be approved for an unrelated key.
- Stop waiting for keychain-backed signing after 20 seconds.
- In normal non-strict installs, preserve the existing ad-hoc signing fallback.
  In strict installs, report an error before replacing the working app.
- Limit setup guidance to the dedicated development identity rather than
  changing permissions for every key in a keychain.

This does not teach the agent to enter passwords or approve system dialogs.

## Validation

Nineteen focused policy tests cover automatic keychain selection, explicit
login-keychain guidance, timeouts, strict and non-strict results, ad-hoc
fallback, signing requirements, and preservation of the installed signed app.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Keep unattended strict signing noninteractive by default.
- [x] Prefer a dedicated, reusable local-development keychain.
- [x] Preserve explicitly configured signing identities and keychains.
- [x] Bound unexpected authorization waits to 20 seconds.
- [x] Leave the installed app unchanged when strict signing cannot finish.
- [x] Scope keychain authorization guidance to the intended identity.
- [ ] Exercise the real macOS first-use and stale-key dialogs.
- [ ] Receive maintainer review for the installer behavior.

title: feat(cua-driver): add explicit window-only recording
body:
## Scope

Refs #3644. Implements the accepted window-video increment in `rfcs/3644-window-recording.md`; it does not close the broader recorder ownership/concurrency issue or duplicate #3632's trajectory attribution work.

The implementation and focused native macOS diagnostics pass at `98485717048e0b52ad1ea7e96cd551faf0909c3c`. This PR remains a draft for review and complete affected-platform certification. No merge or release is requested.

## Implementation

- Add `target: {kind: "window", pid, window_id}` to `start_recording`, requiring `record_video: true`, and equivalent `recording start DIR --video --pid PID --window-id WINDOW_ID` CLI flags.
- Validate before authorization and recorder mutation; attest the exact window for observation grants. Reject invalid/ambiguous targets and refuse unsupported backends without display or trajectory fallback.
- Write only `recording.mp4` and bounded `session.json` metadata in window mode. Suppress trajectory turns, global cursor logs, system cursor, separate agent overlay windows, audio, and microphone capture. The live input-safety overlay remains enabled.
- Use macOS 15+ ScreenCaptureKit's desktop-independent window filter, dual PID checks, fixed encoder geometry, callback-backed live state and finalization, and explicit termination on resize, scale change, close/minimize, or lost shareability. Track each native API's dimensions separately because WindowServer and ScreenCaptureKit can report different bounds.
- Keep singleton busy protection and existing daemon-wide manual stop. After automatic termination, `stop_recording` or owner teardown joins/releases the retained recorder. No-target legacy replacement behavior stays unchanged.
- Update skills and generated CLI/MCP references. Add a synthetic native test and fixture covering exact-window isolation, lifecycle, finalized MP4s, and repeated descriptor counts.

## Validation at the candidate SHA

Source and installed Local version: **0.24.0**. The source-built Local app passed strict certificate-backed signature verification and runtime source-SHA readback. Accessibility, Screen Recording, and native capture were verified on the explicitly authorized macOS host. The separate released 0.23.2 executable and its existing daemon were preserved.

- Native `exact_window_recording_isolation_and_lifecycle`: **passed all seven cases**: manual stop, two repeat recordings, minimize, close, resize, and owner disconnect. Each produced a finalized, fully decoded H.264 MP4 with no audio and exactly two recording artifacts.
- All seven recordings excluded the adjacent and occluding red sibling window while retaining the animated target. Every decoded frame passed the color-isolation oracle; frame counts matched `ffprobe`, timestamps increased, and full-brightness changing content spanned at least 1.5 seconds. Representative final-candidate frames were visually inspected.
- Movement preserved recording. Start and explicit stop/disconnect preserved the foreground PID, fixture window order, key window, and physical cursor. Wrong-PID and busy requests were rejected. Descriptor counts were 11 before native warm-up and 12 after each of the seven recordings, with no repeated growth.
- Native environment: macOS 26.6.1 build 25G76, backing scale 1, Rust 1.97.1, Swift 6.3.3, FFmpeg/FFprobe 8.1.2. A 321-by-241-point fixture produced 322-by-242-pixel video, rounding up to even encoder dimensions.
- Separate installed-CLI smoke: `recording start ... --video --pid ... --window-id ...` survived the start command's exit; `recording stop` finalized a 21.47-second H.264 MP4. All 72 decoded frame timestamps strictly increased. Before/after Driver snapshots matched the synthetic target, with no trajectory or cursor-log artifacts.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`: **617 passed**.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos window_video_tests --lib`: **7 passed**.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver cli::tests::recording_`: **7 passed**.
- Non-GUI `window_recording_macos_test` checks: **2 passed**; the native case was separately executed with explicit host opt-in, as reported above.
- Release build, signed installation through `install-local.sh --release --require-stable-signing`, Swift fixture compilation, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, and `npx tsx scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver.ts --check`: passed.
- Independent integrated and focused native-geometry/test reviews completed; findings were corrected with regression coverage. Build output contains duplicate CoreMedia Swift-symbol dependency and existing dead-code warnings; successful exit is not a warning-free claim.

The fixture README contains reproducible setup, host opt-in and isolation requirements, and artifact expectations. These focused host diagnostics do not replace canonical desktop certification. Use the live PR checks for CI status at this SHA.

## Remaining proof and limitations

- Before a later ready/merge action, the maintainer must review the native evidence and run the canonical complete affected-platform matrix at the exact candidate SHA. This draft does not claim that certification.
- Native capture was exercised at scale 1 only. Retina, live scale changes, display reconfiguration, cross-process occlusion, session ownership races, permission revocation, and encoder failure recovery remain unverified by this focused lane. Shared tests cover scale arithmetic and scale-change policy.
- Windows, X11, and Wayland explicitly return `window_recording_unsupported`; this increment adds no native window-video implementation for them.
- Closing and minimizing can change native bounds before disappearance. The tested macOS animations reported `window_resized` as the first observed stop reason; the test separately confirmed close/minimize and successful finalization. A bounded terminal source fade is accepted only for those cases, without weakening foreign-color rejection.
- Shareable-content queries have a two-second deadline and recording callbacks have ten-second deadlines. The pinned `screencapturekit` 6.0.1 synchronous attach/start/stop/detach calls have no cancellation API and can still hang. This is not a hard end-to-end timeout guarantee.
- Browser chrome inside the selected window is included. Cursor compositing, tab-only capture, dynamic resizing, and independent concurrent recorders are out of scope.

title: fix(cua-driver): bind semantic snapshots to one document
body:
## Summary

Cua Driver can turn the current web page into a structured snapshot that an
agent can read and act on. Before this change, the page could navigate while a
snapshot was being assembled, leaving the text, action references, or optional
screenshot tied to different page versions.

This PR keeps the complete `semantic_v2` snapshot operation tied to one browser
tab and one set of page documents. If the main page or a collected embedded
frame changes during the operation, the Driver refuses the result instead of
publishing stale references.

## What changes

- Collect semantic content and an optional screenshot through the same browser
  connection while holding the existing per-tab operation lock.
- Check the main document and every collected embedded-frame document before
  and after collection.
- Publish only while the original session, browser target, tab, and connection
  are still current.
- Consume a continuation token only when the replacement page is successfully
  published. Two concurrent users of one token have exactly one winner.
- Include the frame and document identity in scoped references, preventing a
  matching node number from another frame from being accepted by mistake.
- Remove cancelled browser requests from the pending-response table.
- Limit embedded-frame collection to 16 frames and eight seconds, with a
  separate bounded cleanup step.

The older `dom_refs_v1` response format is unchanged.

## Validation

Deterministic tests cover navigation during first-page and continuation
collection, screenshot failure, cancellation, concurrent continuation use,
replaced targets, frame-number collisions, stale embedded frames, and bounded
cleanup. The full 625-test core suite passed after the shared frame-lifetime
change; the final cleanup-bound adjustment also passed its focused test.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Refuse a snapshot when a collected document is replaced.
- [x] Keep the screenshot and semantic data in one tab operation.
- [x] Preserve continuation tokens after cancellation or capture failure.
- [x] Allow only one successful use of a continuation token.
- [x] Bind scoped references to the exact frame and document.
- [x] Bound embedded-frame collection and cleanup.
- [ ] Run the supported installed-browser matrix at this exact commit.
- [ ] Receive maintainer review for the snapshot-lifetime contract.

Refs #3136

title: feat(cua-driver): prototype Android background runtime and device-owned agent
body:
Android has no local Cua Driver backend. This draft adds an experimental Android 17 runtime, host/phone CLI, typed Kotlin SDK, and an Android-owned visual agent that operates selected real apps in a background virtual workspace while the main display remains usable.

Host commands use `cua-driver --device SERIAL`; authorized on-device shell commands use `cua-driver --local`. There is no `android` verb. Without an Android selector, existing desktop dispatch is unchanged. The experimental contract is separate from the stable desktop platform enum and ToolRegistry.

### Runtime and SDK

- One virtual display per leased session; allowlisted apps get owned tasks on that display. Repeated app switches preserve task identity and issue fresh target generations. A task already running outside the session is refused, including `singleTask` activities; it is never adopted from display 0.
- PNG snapshots, downscaled previews, and snapshot-bound taps/swipes. Static capture requests a genuine new producer frame by replacing the capture surface; five-second producer-frame and input-token limits remain enforced.
- Signing-identity-checked app provider/Binder transport and peer-checked shell sockets, caller/session ownership, bounded gestures, mutation deduplication, lease renewal, and cleanup of every owned task plus the virtual display. Input API acceptance remains `effect: unverifiable` and `actual_delivery: unknown` until application evidence is inspected.
- Coroutine SDK preserves request/runtime identities and distinguishes refusal, uncertainty, and cancellation. The foreground service owns renewal and preview across Activity recreation/backgrounding, exposes Stop, and handles cleanup/restart ordering. Process death falls back to lease expiry.

### Device-owned visual agent

The debug controller runs the snapshot → model decision → fresh-frame verification → SDK action loop on Android. It owns session renewal, app switching, preview, Stop and cleanup. Decisions are bounded to 40 steps/10 minutes; uncertain input stops the run. After slow inference, only exact decoded-pixel and target/display/runtime/geometry matches may bind a decision to a new input handle. Bounded extra captures accommodate blinking caret phases without masking pixels or weakening freshness.

Inference uses a loopback-only, authenticated host relay and the host's existing Claude Code authentication. The model has no shell, file, browser, Driver or MCP tools; its sole permitted formatter produces a strict action. Disconnect cancels and reaps the request's subprocess. The formatter can revise its proposal at most twice within one inference request. Earlier proposals have no side effects; only the final response is validated against the strict schema, allowlist and coordinate bounds and must equal the last formatter input. Other tools, excess proposals, invalid final responses and policy errors are refused. There is no automatic inference retry or retry of uncertain driver input.

This is a device-owned agent loop with host-relayed inference, not offline on-device inference or a system-UID app. The runtime is an explicitly authorized shell-UID helper. Raw screenshots and model evidence remain local and outside Git.

### Validation

- 42 JVM tests across runtime, SDK and demo; all four Android lint tasks pass. All APKs build, and installed APK versions/digests match the verified source builds.
- 35 relay tests cover strict final-action/tool admission, bounded formatter revisions, invalid final responses, the deadline, socket cancellation, subprocess cleanup and admission of the next request.
- Android 17/API 37 Google APIs ARM64 emulator: repeated switching between unmodified OpenCalc 3.2.1 and Tasks.org 15.10 preserves task IDs, uses one nonzero display, rejects stale handles, refreshes static frames, preserves main-display focus and destroys both tasks on Stop.
- Existing fixture smoke passes, including simultaneous synthetic display-0 text and virtual-display input, phone-local CLI, geometry/swipe/PNG, SDK preview, refusals, deduplication and lease cleanup. These checks do not establish physical-phone or human IME isolation.
- Native Stop during model inference cancels the relay request and cleans the workspace; a subsequent run is admitted. Earlier lifecycle verification covers Activity recreation, 65 seconds of service-owned background preview/renewal, notification Stop and process-death cleanup.
- Actual model-driven two-app run on candidate `0d8de736829970dc5bb6d016944a8be021ef72b2`: a 129-second continuous capture records 15 model decisions and 14 renewals. Independent image inspection confirms OpenCalc result 42, the matching snack-pack task checked/struck through in Tasks.org, and the venue task left unchecked. Synthetic main-display text/focus survives; both tasks and the virtual display are removed. The real CLI exercises formatter revisions successfully. A prior single-app run also computed 42. Recordings and model evidence remain local; model-declared `done` alone is not treated as task proof.

### Scope and remaining gates

Phase 1 local experiment; keep draft. Accessibility/semantic text, raw keys and human IME isolation, ordinary app/Termux UIDs, physical-phone/vendor-image qualification, general application coverage, streaming, stable API/authorization integration and Fleet work remain open. No Fleet changes or deployment are included. Full desktop certification remains a readiness/merge gate; Android fixtures and recordings do not replace it.

Setup, SDK examples, real-app provenance links, and reproducible harness commands: [Android README](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/feat/cua-driver-android-local/libs/cua-driver/android/README.md).

Refs #3673

title: feat(cua-driver-bench): import public benchmark runtime and tooling
body:
## Summary

- import an allowlisted Cua Driver Bench snapshot into the public monorepo without its private Git history
- add the `cua-bench-runtime` package and collision-free `cua_bench_runtime` / `cdb` names
- add schemas, synthetic conformance material, profiles, calibration, and Jainish Patel's automated driver-comparison runner
- add Diátaxis documentation, CODEOWNERS, documentation-link coverage, and Python 3.11–3.13 CI

## Public boundary

This PR excludes executable benchmark tasks, private manifests, task fixtures, hidden evaluators, expected-state definitions, oracles, datasets, releases, results, traces, screenshots, and evidence.

The public runtime contains generic protected-execution apparatus, but no task-specific protected mediator. An authorized task pack or prepared seed must provide the task application, launch contract, and mediator. CDB task IDs appear only as opaque selectors in the comparison runner; the public runtime and tests contain no held-out target or end-state values.

The comparison runner requires an explicit `--tasks-root`; it does not search private or machine-specific locations.

## Source and attribution

Source snapshot: `trycua/cua-driver-bench@a820570ae02844d3615e784dfc366df16183701c`

The automated driver-comparison runner is adapted from `trycua/cua-driver-bench#58`, authored by Jainish Patel. The import commit preserves his credit with both `Salvaged from trycua/cua-driver-bench#58` and a GitHub-linked `Co-authored-by` trailer.

See `benchmarks/cua-driver-bench/PROVENANCE.md` and the public-boundary ADR for the complete import policy.

## Validation

Validated on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13:

- repository schema suite: valid
- runtime: 388 tests and 307 subtests passed per Python version
- synthetic runtime conformance: passed per Python version
- documentation links: passed per Python version
