title: Windows recorder intermittently reports failed FFmpeg finalization during native E2E preflight
body:
## Verified failure

The production stop_recording operation reports failed FFmpeg finalization during Windows native preflight. The harness correctly stops before native behavior rows. This predates #3706/#3704:

- Main bd4c10020cd7cac07c0d19b0f53ba4b007fbcb15 failed: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34306620850/job/102324572423
- The identical main SHA later passed the native lane: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34307741070/job/102327857162
- Stack candidate 603d50e6bc76d5cb0538f827b536c4d21f47c6ae failed with the same signature: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34499846099/job/102947618595

The recorder backend, recording manager, preflight test, and FFmpeg setup script are byte-identical across baseline and failing candidate. Both failures used FFmpeg 9.0.1 through the Chocolatey shim. Retained MP4s are nonempty and have moov boxes, but that does not override the failed finalization contract or prove valid recordings.

## Unknown cause

FfmpegVideoBackend::stop ignores stdin write/flush errors and collapses a nonzero child exit or its three-second shutdown timeout into finalized=false. The retained stderr tail is empty. We cannot distinguish a recorder bug, shim/process behavior, or environmental timing from these logs alone. Do not attribute this to Session 0 or weaken the video gate.

## Selected investigation

Maintainer requested attribution and root-cause diagnosis. Run a bounded diagnostic on a GitHub-hosted interactive Windows runner, preserving every result. Compare identical FFmpeg arguments and production shutdown timing via the Chocolatey shim versus the underlying executable, recording stdin errors, exit status, shutdown elapsed time, and forced termination. If needed, follow with product-boundary instrumentation. This is diagnostic evidence, not certification or retry-to-green.

Acceptance: identify the failing shutdown path with observable evidence, then scope a focused regression/fix without mixing it into the macOS consent or overlay changes. Track readiness impact on #3704 and #3706.

title: Roll back opened tunnels when a multi-port acquisition fails
body:
Users forwarding multiple ports through one await or async context retain earlier successful port forwards when a later acquisition fails. Callers receive no TunnelInfo result with which to close those resources. SSH listeners remain until broader transport teardown, while ADB forwarding rules require explicit removal. The shared interface affects every resource-owning tunnel transport.

At `libs/python/cua-sandbox/cua_sandbox/interfaces/tunnel.py:69`:

_TunnelContext._open opens each port sequentially and appends each successful TunnelInfo to self._infos at lines 68-71, without an exception cleanup path. __aenter__ directly awaits _open at line 82. If the second forward_tunnel raises, context entry never completes and __aexit__ is not called, so the first tunnel is never closed. The plain-await path at line 65 has the same failure. Actual resource owners exist: transport/adb.py:222 allocates an ADB forward and line 230 removes it only through close_tunnel; transport/ssh.py:119 starts a listener and line 132 stops it through close_tunnel. Root cause: partial acquisition cleanup is deferred to an exit method that cannot run after failed entry.

## Proposed fix

Add rollback around the acquisition loop in interfaces/tunnel.py. On failure or cancellation, attempt to close every handle acquired by that attempt, clear successfully released handles and their closers, and re-raise the original acquisition exception. Do not let one cleanup failure prevent attempts to release the remaining handles. Add tests/test_tunnel.py with fake-transport regression cases for async-with, plain await, cancellation after one successful acquisition, and successful acquisition/exit. Keep existing backend allocation behavior unchanged.

## How to see it

Unexecuted deterministic test plan: use a fake transport whose first forward_tunnel returns TunnelInfo('localhost', 45001, 9222) and whose second call raises RuntimeError('second forward failed'). Record close_tunnel calls. Execute async with Tunnel(fake).forward(9222, 8080) under pytest.raises and assert the body never runs and the first TunnelInfo is closed exactly once. Current trace leaves the close-call list empty; after rollback it contains the first handle. Parameterize the same test for plain await. Add a cancellation case that cancels while the second acquisition awaits an event, after the first handle has been recorded; require cleanup and propagation of CancelledError. No sockets, commands, ADB process, or remote sandbox are necessary.

If this looks right I can push `fix/sandbox-tunnel-acquisition-cleanup` on `anxkhn/cua` instead of opening a pull request first.

title: Report directory entries accurately when list_dir returns names
body:
Remote Sandbox directory traversal and file browsers using FileEntry.is_dir misclassify every directory returned by GenericFileHandler. Code that recurses only into directories skips subtrees, while code that downloads entries classified as files tries to read directories. Entries returned with explicit metadata are not affected.

At `libs/python/cua-sandbox/cua_sandbox/interfaces/files.py:66`:

Files.list converts every string item to `FileEntry(name=item, path=f"{path.rstrip('/')}/{item}", is_dir=False)`. This is the normal server response, not a hypothetical legacy shape: computer_server/handlers/generic.py:318 returns a files array of p.name for both p.is_file() and p.is_dir(). Thus a real subdirectory is always exposed as is_dir=False by the Sandbox SDK. Files.is_dir already implements the directory_exists operation at files.py:51, and the server implements it at generic.py:290. Root cause: treating absent metadata in a name-only listing as a definitive file classification.

## Proposed fix

In Files.list, resolve is_dir for name-only entries through the existing remote Files.is_dir operation instead of hardcoding False. Keep the dictionary-entry fast path and the current wire protocol unchanged. Add tests/test_files.py with mixed file/directory listings, empty listings, trailing separators, and metadata-bearing entries. Do not add a new server response format or infer remote file types from the local host filesystem.

## How to see it

Unexecuted focused regression plan: use a fake transport returning {'success': True, 'files': ['subdir', 'note.txt']} for list_dir('/work'), and returning exists=True only for directory_exists('/work/subdir'). Await Files(fake).list('/work'). Expect subdir.is_dir=True and note.txt.is_dir=False. Current code never requests directory metadata and returns False for both. Add a trailing-slash case and retain coverage for an empty listing and dictionary entries that already include is_dir, verifying the latter do not incur metadata lookups. These fixtures follow the actual GenericFileHandler listing and directory_exists response contracts.

If this looks right I can push `fix/sandbox-directory-entry-types` on `anxkhn/cua` instead of opening a pull request first.

title: [Bug]: macOS window-scoped snapshots list the application's menu bar rows, but every action on them is refused with `element_outside_target_window`
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`get_window_state` on macOS deliberately keeps the application's `AXMenuBar` in a window snapshot (it is the first step of the documented two-snapshot menu flow), but the background-input gate requires an addressed element to prove ancestry to the requested window. A menu bar cannot: it is process-scoped, carries no CGWindowID, and its `AXParent` chain reaches `AXApplication` without passing an `AXWindow`. Every menu row the snapshot surfaces is therefore refused, and the refusal's advice ("take a fresh snapshot and re-address it") can never be satisfied.

### Reproduction

1. Open TextEdit with one document window; note `pid` and `window_id`.
2. `get_window_state` with `include_accessibility_tree: true`; find the `AXMenuBarItem` row titled "Format" (it is listed with `actions: ["AXPress"]` and an `element_token`).
3. `click` that `element_token` against the same `pid`/`window_id` with `delivery_mode: "background"`.
4. Take a fresh snapshot as the refusal suggests and repeat step 3 with the new token.

### Expected behavior

The semantic AX action (`AXPress`) on a menu bar item that belongs to the requested window's own process is admitted; the menu opens. Window-aimed routes (routed pointer, process keyboard) may still refuse, since a stamped pointer event cannot be aimed at a row that lives outside every window. When an element does belong to a different window, the refusal should name that window so the caller can re-target it.

### Actual behavior

Both attempts return `code: "element_outside_target_window"` with the re-snapshot advice, for every `AXMenuBarItem` the snapshot advertises as actionable. `invoke_menu` works because it resolves the path itself. The refusal also never says which window the element does belong to.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.0 (`cua-driver-rs-v0.28.0`, e7e141ae)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1, arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: TextEdit (any AppKit app)

### Evidence

`platform-macos/src/ax/window_scope.rs` keeps `AXMenuBar` in the top-level candidate set for window snapshots ("dropping AXMenuBar here would remove" the two-snapshot menu flow) while `cua-driver-core/src/background_input.rs::decide_background_input` admits only `ElementAncestry::ProvenDescendant` of the requested window. `platform-macos/src/ax/exact_target.rs::element_window_id` resolves ancestry through `AXWindow` / `_AXUIElementGetWindow`, which a menu bar never satisfies, so `gather_background_facts` classifies every menu row as `Unproven` and the gate refuses it.

### Workaround and additional context

Use `invoke_menu` with the full path. Related: #2645 (bound state and actions to the requested window; the gate this hits), #2788 (`invoke_menu` exact focus), #3301 (RFC on coordinate-free menu-extra invocation, a different surface), #3351 / #3353 (the same class of refusal for sheets, handled separately).

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

- Problem this solves: every menu-bar row a macOS window snapshot surfaced was refused as outside the target window, with advice to re-snapshot that could never be satisfied (#3792).
- What changed: a semantic action on the application's own menu bar is admitted when the addressed window is where the process directs its input, refused with `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` naming the focused window otherwise, and reported `unverifiable` after dispatch.

<details><summary>Mechanism and measurements</summary>

- `ElementAncestry::ProvenAppMenu` in `cua-driver-core/src/background_input.rs` proves the fact that does exist: the element ascends to the requested process's own `AXMenuBar`. `decide_background_input` admits it for `AxSemantic` only.
- Review round 1 (f-trycua, 2026-09-13): admission needed the focused-window guard the process-scoped keyboard route already implied. `process_directs_input_at_target` is now one predicate shared by both routes; the keyboard route gains the same focused-window escape, so a two-window process no longer refuses when the requested window is the proven focused one. Facts carry the focused window id from `ax::bindings::focused_window_id_of_pid`, the reader `bring_to_front` and `invoke_menu` already trust; unreadable focus fails closed.
- Sheet remediation: `ax::exact_target::foreign_window_ancestry` verifies acquirability against the layer-0 listing; a sheet resolves to an id that listing cannot return, so `ElementAncestry::OutsideUnacquirableSurface` names the condition and points at the presenting window, with no id.
- The `ProvenAppMenu` refusal arm has its own advice instead of sharing `Unproven`'s "re-observe" text; no gate change.
- Gate matrix: two same-app windows with the addressed one not focused (refused, reason names the focused window), focused (admitted), single-window process (admitted), the keyboard route on a proven focused window, the listing lookup behind the sheet refusal.

The released driver refuses the same press with `element_outside_target_window`.
- Non-goal: window-aimed routes still require window ancestry; a menu action is never reported confirmed. Foreign-window refusals name a CGWindowID only when `list_windows` can serve it; a sheet names the condition and the presenting window instead.

**Rebased onto main `c5ee191c0`.** #4144 moved the harness case into `crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/`; it is selected by `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh` in the same commit. #4116 deleted `scroll::tests::exact_target_refusal_prevents_ax_reveal`, which this PR had only adapted to the new `OutsideTargetWindow` fields, so that edit is gone. title: [Bug]: macOS fullscreen app exposes agent cursor during background computer use
body:
## Bug description

When a user is focused on a fullscreen macOS app, Cua Driver background computer-use actions against another app are not visually isolated. A floating agent cursor appears over the foreground fullscreen app, and it is unclear whether the action is actually being delivered to the intended background target.

In the observed use case, the background target is the Notch app.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS, open an app in fullscreen mode and keep it focused.
2. Use Cua Driver to perform a computer-use action against another app in the background (for example, click a control in the Notch app).
3. Observe the fullscreen app and the target app's resulting state.

## Expected behavior

- Computer-use actions are delivered to the intended background app without changing the user's current fullscreen app or Space.
- The agent cursor does not float over or interfere visually with the foreground fullscreen app.
- The driver provides a reliable indication that the background action succeeded or failed.

## Actual behavior

- A floating agent cursor appears on top of the foreground fullscreen app.
- It is ambiguous whether the click is delivered successfully to the intended background target.

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- Foreground state: another app focused in fullscreen mode
- Background target in the observed case: Notch app

## Acceptance criteria

- Background actions remain correctly routed while an unrelated fullscreen app is focused.
- The agent cursor overlay does not appear over the unrelated fullscreen app.
- Action results can be verified without switching focus or Spaces.

title: [Bug]: generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs resolves the SDK library under `rust/target/release`, ignoring CARGO_TARGET_DIR
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs` builds `cua-driver-sdk` with cargo and then passes a hand-built path under `rust/target/release` as `--library` to both generators. Cargo honours `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, the script does not, so whenever a contributor or CI builds with a target directory outside the tree the script either fails with `missing built SDK library` or, worse, silently generates bindings from whatever stale library still sits in `rust/target/release`.

The second case is the dangerous one: it produces bindings that do not correspond to the branch being built, and `--check` then reports them as up to date.

### Reproduction

1. `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/some-target`
2. `node libs/cua-driver/scripts/generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check`
3. Repeat with a `rust/target/release/libcua_driver_sdk.dylib` left behind by an earlier build of a different branch.

### Expected behavior

The script resolves the library from the same target directory cargo just used (`cargo metadata --format-version 1 | jq -r .target_directory`, or `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`), and fails loudly if the file it finds was not produced by the build it just ran.

### Actual behavior

Step 2 aborts with `missing built SDK library …/rust/target/release/…` although the build succeeded. Step 3 completes and reports the bindings as current, having generated them from the other branch's library. We hit exactly this while preparing per-PR branches in separate worktrees with private target directories: the script consumed a sibling worktree's binary.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `libs/cua-driver/scripts/generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs` at `31c2184f8`
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1, arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: n/a

### Evidence

`generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs::nativeLibraryPath` composes the path from `rustRoot` plus `target/release`, and the `existsSync` guard after the cargo build only proves that *some* library exists there.

### Workaround and additional context

Unset `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` for this script and delete `rust/target` afterwards, which is what we do per PR branch today.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: test(cua-driver): guard Hyprland element-reveal output coordinates
body:
Refs #3554.

The issue reported that a Hyprland AT-SPI action could place the agent cursor outside the target window, with window-local accessibility bounds behaving as output-space coordinates. Checked against current `main` with the issue's scenario: the reveal path already resolves proven output coordinates, but nothing guarded that contract. This adds the live regression.

## What changed

- `hyprland_element_reveal_test.rs` (live, `#[ignore]`, Hyprland-only): moves the agent cursor to a neutral point, locates the overlay's debug square (`CUA_OVERLAY_DEBUG=1`) in a driver desktop capture, performs a background element click by token, and asserts the revealed cursor lands on the element's absolute frame center (within the cursor-artwork anchor tolerance, 32 points) and inside the target window. It requires the fixture window to sit away from the output origin, so a window-local leak cannot pass.
- `McpDriver::spawn_named_with_overlay_and_env` (testkit, additive): overlay-enabled spawn with child-scoped environment, mirroring the existing `RawDriver::spawn_with_overlay_and_env`.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` — 440 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-testkit --lib` — 106 passed, 0 failed when the test process is in the CI-shaped X11 session (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE` unset/x11). Note: on a live Wayland session one pre-existing assertion on `main` fails (`native_case_builders_encode_delivery_and_oracle_contracts` hard-codes the `Cursor` oracle for every display server) — #3466 carries that fix and is not part of this branch.
- Live on Hyprland 0.56 with a single output at a non-zero global origin and scale 1.8 (so raw-pixel mapping is genuinely exercised): `cargo test -p cua-driver --test hyprland_element_reveal_test -- --ignored` — 1 passed, 0 failed.
- Measured on the same run: the click resolved the element's frame center `(3830.5, 1581.0)` exactly as reported by the snapshot, and the overlay's debug square landed within ~15 points of it (the artwork anchor offset) — not near the output origin, and inside the target window.

title: fix(cua-driver): correct keyboard delivery and outcome reporting
body:
Refs #3473 and #3657. Salvaged from #3658.

## Scope

Preserve Ben Kamholtz’s Enter/Return terminal-gate fix and reference update via `cherry-pick -x` of 78875a32 and c2ca6f1c; Francesco Bonacci’s coauthor credit remains intact. Keep the earlier XTest hotkey reporting correction. Source #3658 stays open pending landing disposition.

The maintainer clarified that completing the red-case phase does not require native certification and explicitly selected the tech-spec handoff. **Red-case characterization is complete for this slice; the design proposal is ready for review. No typed-producer implementation or further production fix has started.** Native execution gaps and intentional reds remain explicit; this is not merge-ready.

### Revised vertical-slice proposal awaiting review

At the maintainer's request, the additive accounting-layer proposal is superseded by a deletion-led design: separate compatibility-preserving entry parsers feed one keyboard executor per platform; native backend transactions own retained targets, focus and input lifetimes and return immutable typed outcomes. No shared mutable progress tracker, universal keyboard planner, phantom search transport or duplicate recorded/unrecorded actuator implementations.

Separate preparation failure from attempted dispatch failure. Source review shows that Wayland may try another backend after a post-input error, and the XAML scan may continue to another matching control after Invoke/Toggle failure. These are source-verified risks, not new native fault reproductions. No-replay, owned cleanup and Wayland focus restoration are proposed as explicit behavior-changing red-to-green slices, not hidden refactors. XAML no-transient-focus-steal still needs a verified mechanism or an explicit capability decision; an after-the-fact restore is not sufficient.

Keep ActionExecutionRecord as the canonical outcome, but distinguish refused routes, execution facts and genuinely unknown worker outcomes rather than inventing an actuator for refusals. The core crate is unpublished; this internal representation change requires workspace caller migration and cross-action projection regression coverage. Successful SDK/MCP schemas and existing error envelopes remain unchanged. Recording/debug readers must explicitly support transport-less refusals and unknown outcomes without reinterpreting historical artifacts as proof of delivery.

Remove keyboard-only legacy payloads/inference after producer migration; preserve unrelated compatibility. The proposal includes a scoped inventory of structural deletions, FFI ownership improvements, schema/parser opportunities, test/CI cleanup and deferred optimizations. Preserve Enter/Return provenance, native route exceptions, admission timing, existing protocol count units and independent test oracles. No implementation or additional native test runs have started.

## Implemented coverage

- Real producer invocation before dispatch reconstruction on Linux, Windows and macOS. Implemented cases cover foreground/background routes, unchanged-value versus genuine AX readback, target closure, duplicate modifiers, and focus preservation/restoration using a separate native sentinel and global key probes. Implemented is not synonymous with natively observed: macOS positive producer cases remain permission-blocked below.
- Public dispatch: malformed/unknown input and token refusals, authorization targets, real multi-window ambiguity, admitted-action serialization, queued cancellation, and deterministic cancellation after native key/modifier down. The latter observes the existing in-flight sequence finish and release; it does **not** certify cancelled-worker drain/readiness before completion or redesign it.
- Real X11 connection-loss injection after independently received key/modifier down, retaining missing-record failures and checking that input is not replayed.
- Real xterm PTYs: aliases/case, modified-key and hotkey bypass, no-PTY fallback, actual transport and delivery. An XI2 observer and managed focus sentinel distinguish consumed PTY input from XTest and transient foreground activation. Positive XTest controls validate the observer.
- Native GTK terminal with a real owned PTY and real snapshot-bound accessible entry: bare Return takes the PTY shortcut; valid element-targeted press_key/hotkey reach the exact GTK entry, preserve modifiers and do not duplicate delivery.
- Shared SDK/native harness: stale/conflicting targets, runtime isolation and retirement; shared/desktop outcome schemas, truthful route/mode/effect, absent invented evidence/counts, and recording/public parity. An accepted independently observed action must not be described as `delivery_failed` merely because its effect is `unverifiable`.

## Exact 58a1b2531d0eaad1ba490cf6780eb143672340df evidence

Linux focused native keyboard suite: **48 cases, 35 pass / 13 intentional reporting reds**, no fixture failure:

- 8 real producer results omit execution records after observed input.
- 2 public post-input native errors omit execution records after observed key/modifier down.
- F5 uses XTest but reports `synthetic_events`; a PTY write is recorded as `LinuxXSendEvent`; a focus-free PTY write requested as foreground reports foreground.

Additional Linux validation: platform unit tests **448 pass / 15 ignored** (ignored native cases were run explicitly above); core **628 pass**; SDK **93 pass serially**; testkit **106 pass**; session/snapshot/dispatch integrations **13 pass**; shared native harness compiles. Formatting and diff checks pass.

Retained diagnostics are not replaced with favorable results:

- Default parallel SDK execution failed a process-global hook-count assertion (4 versus baseline 0) and eight poisoned-lock cascades. The documented serial native-harness setting passed 93/93; the parallel isolation issue remains unfixed and separately logged.
- An unmanaged root-focus canary was invalid: a no-driver control reproduced focus reclamation. Its replacement is a real managed sentinel with stricter transient-focus and raw-key observation; the original failures remain retained.
- Native terminal host construction initially used mismatched runtime/cache scopes. The fixture now follows the SDK’s immutable context and `with_runtime_scope` construction contract; no token validation changed.

Local evidence is retained under `artifacts/keyboard-completion/` in the isolated Linux checkout and transferred verbatim to the maintainer host. SHA-256 of the transferred evidence archive: `aa01565add94f57712ec1d167fca5ea941210372660089adc2ad7cef6e28f370`.

## Completed canonical runs at 58a1b2531d0eaad1ba490cf6780eb143672340df

| Environment | Desktop rows passing, including expected refusals | Failed rows | Classification |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [Linux X11](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34893920047) | 126 | 5 | Foreground press_key reports synthetic instead of global input |
| [Windows](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34893922524) | 134 | 4 | Observed press_key actions incorrectly advertise delivery_failed |
| [Sway](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34893925305) | 122 | 8 | Foreground press_key/hotkey report synthetic instead of global input |
| macOS Lume `20260914T204105Z-0cf607e5` | 155 | 9 | Six background hotkey failure-advice errors; three pixel press_key route/mode errors |

Failed rows are not complete evidence passes: reporting assertions stop later checks. Raw logs and recordings remain retained. Windows strict GUI preflight, capture/native framework lanes, and installer smoke passed. macOS producer diagnostics separately report **2 pass / 7 permission-blocked**; daemon authorization does not authorize the Cargo test executable, and no grants were changed.

[Cua compositor](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34893927797) does not qualify keyboard behavior: native/capture fail ready-window/AX/screenshot preflight; shared stops earlier because the Nix environment lacks `gnome-keyring-daemon`. These are not keyboard reporting reds. Real Hyprland execution is also unqualified; its unit/mock workflow is not native evidence.

## Focused continuation and exact-diff accounting

Current published head: `b4e5f6f54b34534378fc0a343cffd948e535d7f8`.

**Latest runnable batches are fully classified, with no fixture failures at 9acad90:** [Windows](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34936998965) **5 pass / 10 missing-record reds**; [native Sway](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34937001391) **5 missing-record reds**, including independently confirmed hotkey focus loss. These are intentional product-red tests, not passing acceptance. macOS positive producer execution and the previously documented compositor environments remain blocked/unqualified. These are native-validation gaps, not blockers to completing the red-case phase or reviewing the tech spec.

The final b4e5f6f delta only wires the existing Sway producer group into the normal native/all session tail, preserving earlier failures and not rerunning diagnostics recursively. Six shell control-flow cases passed against the actual dispatch block with external command stubs; shell syntax/diff checks passed. Native product/test bodies remain those tested at 9acad90. No unrelated matrix rerun.

### Latest canonical macOS run

Maintainer-authorized Lume run `20260915T064932Z-46ba3173` tested the exact current b4e5f6f head after waiting for another workstream's lock to clear. **146 delivered / 9 expected refusals / 9 failed** (155 passing desktop rows). The failures remain six background hotkey `delivery_failed` advice errors and three pixel press_key foreground-request route/mode errors. Failed rows do not establish their later oracle assertions. Strict preflight and report validation passed; no video failures.

Direct producer suite: **2 pass / 10 Accessibility-blocked**. The installed app's daemon reports Accessibility and Screen Recording granted, while the distinct Cargo test executable reports no Accessibility permission. The VM therefore does not qualify the positive producer, AX-retention or closure cases. No grants were changed and no failed tests were retried.

Evidence collected and worker stop confirmed. The standard-daemon restoration trap reported no error or deferred restoration; this failed run has no separate post-run daemon-status attestation. Clone source `cua-driver-browser-baseline-20260908-chrome152` is worker-derived from #2907/#3373, not an immutable certified seed. Standalone-browser was outside scope and not run. Local evidence is retained at `/Users/administrator/.local/share/cua-lume-e2e/runs/20260915T064932Z-46ba3173/`; that path is not a public download link. PR head remained unchanged after execution.

### Latest focused batches

- [Windows fbb0c79 keyboard](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34931831446): **5 pass / 8 missing-record reds**, no fixture failures; strengthened retained UIA PID/name checks and native input observations passed before reporting assertions.
- [Windows fbb0c79 native lane](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34931833408): **39 delivered / 4 expected refusals / 0 failed**, including eight WinUI3 rows after fixture changes. The attempted harness filter did not limit the native script. This is not a full shared/capture/desktop certification; subsequent keyboard-xaml diagnostics build only their fixture and skip the native matrix.
- The initial XAML diagnostic had **1 physical-control pass / 3 fixture failures** from an incorrectly scoped focus probe. Those failures are retained; the established desktop probe is now shared instead of duplicated.
- [XAML d5abd2b](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34935387410): **1 pass / 3 product-red cases**. Invoke/Toggle callbacks occurred once with no native key replay, but native foreground PID/HWND observation shows the target app has taken foreground from the sentinel, and producer records are absent. This is verified focus loss, not merely a probe error. A no-matching-accelerator refusal also lacks a producer record. The focus behavior has not been fixed or silently excluded.
- Five native-Wayland GTK producer cases compiled at ffdc9dc; their first run stopped on a GTK/GDK namespace mismatch before input. Both namespaces were pinned to version 3 at 9afeb22. Original fixture failures and the later misplaced post-hotkey probe are retained. At 9acad90 all five reach intended reporting reds after independent receipt or observed refusal. Both press_key variants restore the sentinel; hotkey leaves the target foreground (Sway IPC PID10911, expected sentinel PID10946). Source review confirms hotkey calls an activating helper without the restoring wrapper used by press_key. No production focus fix.
- Two Windows tests simulate partial acceptance at the external SendInput boundary. At 632303a the API accepted one event and returned the expected short-count error, but app receipt timed out; those failures are retained and not counted as delivered input. At 9acad90 the test-only syscall boundary waits for independent receipt before returning the real short count to the unchanged producer error path. Both cases now observe key/modifier down, owned key-up cleanup, global release, no replay and restored-focus recovery, then fail solely on missing execution records. This is controlled syscall-boundary partial acceptance, not spontaneous OS failure or product-owned cleanup.
- macOS producer compilation and **94 testkit unit tests** passed at fbb0c79. Positive macOS producers remain blocked as documented below; no grant changed.

### Earlier focused evidence

Linux at a721db4: queued lifecycle/terminal-element group **9/9 pass**; full focused native group **50 cases, 37 pass / 13 reporting reds**, no fixture failures. Adding hotkey target loss at 118f338 produced **11 producer cases, 2 pass / 9 missing-record reds**. e10f9ad retained complete ToolResult diagnostics and its native-producer-only filter produced **1 pass / 9 reds** (registry ambiguity remained covered at 118f338). Combined with unchanged integrations this is **51 cases, 37 pass / 14 reporting reds by explicit delta accounting**, not a single exact-head run. The remote launcher returned transport status 255 after one completed run; original logs and exited processes were recovered without rerunning or replacing the evidence.

[Windows e10f9ad](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34927957630): **5 pass / 6 missing-record reds**, no fixture failures. Hotkey target loss observed real Ctrl down and window closure; the producer still returned legacy success without a record. Closure need not force an OS error; the Linux connection-loss cases remain separate actual post-input error coverage.

[Windows 46ac840](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34929689654): **5 pass / 8 missing-record reds**, no fixture failures. Two new tests pause immediately before the real UIA SetFocus boundary, clear the owning snapshot cache, successfully query the retained native handle's PID, require a reused token to be refused, then release and independently observe a single completed key/chord in the original field. These ownership/input assertions passed before the final missing-record assertion failed. The hooks are test-only and do not mock native results. The bounded barrier's release/abandonment unit test passed.

macOS 46ac840 producer suite: **2 pass / 10 permission-blocked**. This includes the new hotkey closure and two AX retained-target cases; none of those positive cases reached native input. The changed Swift fixture compiled and its real invalid-input and ambiguity cases passed. No grants were changed.

[Windows keyboard-only diagnostics](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34900062224) at `75f473d2b2f6de443784df62b8d97f819134a286`: **5 pass / 5 missing-record reds**, no fixture failures. The corrected oracle observes both root-window and text-field messages. Background receipts were root-window PostMessage sequences, with modifier flags zero; they establish message receipt, not a confirmed application shortcut. Foreground receipts and sentinel F6 probes establish sequence completion and focus restoration. Modifier-only hotkeys are explicitly rejected before input; the earlier compatibility assumption was wrong.

That commit was amended only to correct the agent commit identity as `4bd6cbcc799e76be303fba27f50e118b19ad97af`; Git tree hashes are identical. Subsequent heads add the observed queued-token cases, hotkey target-loss cases and native-retention tests above. The keyboard-only workflow no longer publishes a desktop matrix summary. This continuation changes tests, fixtures and cfg(test)-only native-boundary pauses, not production behavior; the prior full desktop runs are not presented as exact-head certification.

The original Windows 58a1b25 observer timeouts and incorrect modifier-only assertion remain retained, alongside the corrected diagnostic run.

## Historical evidence and remaining limits

The pre-salvage 059b36521 terminal fixture delivered Enter but timed out on Return; salvaged code delivered both and case variants. The mixed-source Cargo-cache run is invalid and retained. No permissions or credentials were repaired.

At c47e75ed, [Windows native diagnostics](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34880967983) passed native framework tests, then five producer record cases failed after receipt. The sixth revealed a test assumption: Windows retains first-character key-name compatibility; new tests observe that behavior rather than silently changing parsing. [Linux SDK diagnostics](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34880965059) passed live foreign-runtime rejection, then hit an incorrect retired-token expectation; retirement correctly reports `stale_element_token`.

Remaining work includes maintainer disposition of the newly observed XAML and Wayland hotkey focus loss and resolving or explicitly bounding unavailable native environments. The new runnable Wayland and Windows partial-acceptance batches are now classified; original fixture failures remain retained separately. Queue-time token retirement is not proof of retained native handles after admission; the Windows ownership assertions above now independently cover post-admission cache clearing, while corresponding macOS execution remains blocked. Permission-blocked macOS cases and compositor setup failures remain outstanding for native qualification. Historical green runs do not certify this head. **The red-case phase is complete and the typed-producer tech-spec proposal is ready for review; implementation, green acceptance and native qualification are not complete. This draft remains unmerged.**

title: fix(cua-driver): hide agent cursor for background actions on another Space
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a Cua Driver background computer-use action against an app on another Space paints the floating agent cursor over the user's current (e.g. fullscreen) app, and it is unclear the action is isolated. Fixes #3801.
- What changed: window-targeted actions (click, double-click, right-click, drag, scroll, type_text, set_value) now route cursor display through one helper that hides the agent cursor when a background delivery targets a window not painted on the current Space. The show/hide decision lives in portable `cua-driver-core`; Space resolution and a sticky per-cursor paint flag live in the macOS overlay. Delivery, focus suppression, pacing, and result reporting are unchanged — the cursor is display-only telemetry.

## Related work

Fixes #3801

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required — no tool schema, MCP, protocol, or CLI change; behavior delta is confined to an off-Space background paint path.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: user-visible only when a background action targets an off-Space window (cursor stays hidden instead of floating over the foreground app). Same-Space background, foreground, desktop-scope, and explicit move_cursor behavior unchanged. No API/CLI/MCP change; Windows/Linux overlays untouched.
- Risk and rollback: low — suppression requires positive off-Space evidence and fails visible on unknown state; any later positioning command unhides. Rollback: revert.

title: fix(cua-driver): unify Wayland screenshot and input frames under fractional scaling
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves:
  On a Wayland session with fractional display scaling (e.g. GNOME at 150%), the coordinate frame of the screenshots returned by `get_desktop_state` and `get_window_state` did not match the frame the input tools consume. Any `px` action grounded on a driver screenshot missed its target by exactly the scale factor, and `get_window_state` returned an image of the wrong region entirely. `get_screen_size` additionally reported the XWayland root geometry with `scale_factor: 1.0`, matching neither frame.
- What changed:
  The driver now resolves the compositor-logical frame from `zxdg_output_manager_v1` (the same protocol the overlay already consumes) on single-output layouts and unifies all three tools around it: `get_desktop_state` feeds the logical frame to the existing capture normalizer so the PNG is downscaled into the input frame with a truthful scale factor; `get_window_state` maps the logical crop rect through the capture buffer's own backing scale and resizes back to logical dims; `get_screen_size` reports the logical size with the real backing scale. When no single logical output is advertised (older compositors, multi-output fractional layouts), each tool keeps its previous frame and logs the fallback at debug level.

## Related work

Refs #3061 (the crop-and-resize direction follows the approach demonstrated in the issue report).

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): N/A — bug fix restoring the documented screenshot-to-action contract; no contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  Screenshot pixel dimensions and `scale_factor` values change on single-output fractional-scale Wayland desktops (they now match the input frame, as documented). Scale-1.0 desktops, X11 sessions, and Hyprland sessions are byte-for-byte unchanged: at scale 1.0 the new crop path delegates to the legacy 1:1 crop, and the X11/Hyprland branches are untouched.
- Risk and rollback:
  Low. Every new lookup fails closed to the exact legacy frame (multi-output and missing-protocol cases keep prior behavior), guarded by a 5s probe cache shared across the three call sites. Roll back by reverting these two files.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` — 454 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored (11 new: 1.5x frame fixtures for the desktop normalizer, logical-output/scale unit guards, scale-aware crop discrimination showing the legacy 1:1 crop returns the wrong region, unit-scale equivalence, degenerate-input and negative-origin guards, fail-closed query without a compositor). `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Manual or platform evidence:
  Headless unit coverage only. No live GNOME fractional-scale session was available in this environment, and the canonical Linux desktop harness (`scripts/ci/linux/run-rust-e2e.sh`) requires a GUI session, so it was not run here.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  Live GNOME 150% confirmation on the exact candidate SHA (`get_screen_size` logical + scale, desktop PNG dims, window-crop region) plus the Linux Rust unit/compile lane and the canonical desktop E2E matrix before merge. Multi-output fractional layouts remain on the legacy frame (documented limitation).

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.

title: fix(lume): keep the login keychain usable after automatic setup
body:
Lume's automatic macOS setup must encode a NUL-terminated password before writing the automatic-login password file. Padding after encoding can prevent the normal account password from unlocking the login keychain. This change pads the UTF-8 plaintext before XOR encoding and always includes a terminator, including at exact 12-byte boundaries.

Both setup paths now use byte counts. The shell path previously counted Unicode characters: a 12-byte fixture password produced an 18-byte buffer, while the Swift path produced the expected 24 bytes. The follow-up aligns those paths and adds boundary coverage to CI. Commands and public APIs are unchanged.

Validation of candidate `b0408db3e969345a2ca3394599e3ea41a8e0b638`:

- All 143 Swift tests passed.
- The setup-script regression tests passed across eight ASCII lengths and five UTF-8 boundary fixtures; four non-ASCII cases failed before the follow-up.
- Shell syntax, CI workflow syntax/wiring, and diff checks passed.
- In a disposable macOS Tahoe 26.5.2 VM, the Swift helper compiled from the candidate source and the shell encoder produced identical bytes for a Unicode fixture password. A fresh test account logged in automatically, its normal password unlocked the login keychain, and no renamed replacement keychain appeared across two boots. The second boot's keychain was already unlocked before the manual unlock check.

The VM check exercises generated password bytes with a fresh account. It does not replace a complete fresh `lume create` or unattended-install run. The prior PR head's six-boot report remains historical evidence; those six boots were not repeated for this follow-up. Existing images whose login keychains were already replaced still need a clean rebuild.

Visual follow-up: the fixture reached first-login Setup Assistant on a subsequent boot; optional screens were completed manually. At the user's request, the synthetic account and existing login-keychain password were then changed to a normal ASCII fixture. Keychain Access accepted that password in the actual GUI and displayed an unlocked login keychain. This confirms GUI authentication after the explicit password change. It does not establish original Unicode GUI authentication, a fresh unattended installation, or unattended desktop readiness.

title: fix(cua-driver): name the state behind a macOS press or click refusal
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: A macOS refusal did not say which window held focus or why a control was disabled, so agents retried the wrong route.
- What changed: a disabled control is refused with `code: element_disabled` and one cause; only a window that is not key adds `escalation: {target: foreground, reason: route_unavailable}`. Before: one uncoded text in every state. `press_key` names the window holding focus. Detail fields are documented macOS-only (`MACOS.md`), not typed contract.

<details><summary>Mechanism and measurements</summary>

Sheet refusal. `with_foreground_hid_activation` reached its bail only when `focused_window_id_of_pid` reported a window other than the target, so the id was in hand and thrown away. `ax::bindings::focused_window_of_pid` returns the focused window's id and role in the one native round-trip the id already cost. The bail is a typed `ForegroundActivationRefused`; its `Display` names both windows (`window 11151, a sheet attached to 11139, holds keyboard focus - snapshot that window_id and press its own buttons`, measured on Calendar), and `press_key`'s refusal publishes `target_window_id`, `focused_window_id` and `focused_window_relation`. An unknown focus holder leaves the old payload plus `target_window_id`.

Disabled control. `ensure_ax_action_enabled` answered every disabled element with one literal naming `delivery_mode:"foreground"` and `bring_to_front`. Measured in Chrome and Notes across four states, the text was byte-identical, and in the plain state both routes were already taken; on the foreground rung the check runs inside `with_foreground_assist`, so the window was already in front. It was right only for a control disabled until its window is key (Notes' toolbar search field), and even there it carried no code. `perform_ax_click` now builds `ElementDisabled` from the element's role and label, the process's front window on the target's display (`bring_to_front::process_front_window_on_display`, the resolution #3785 uses) and the process's key-window state, and `cause()` picks one arm:

1. a menu item tracks the application's applicability: no route;
2. the process's own window drawn in front: `obscured_by: {window_id, title}`, dismiss or address it;
3. background delivery and the window not key (`key_window: {is_key, app_frontmost, focused_window_id}`): the foreground escalation;
4. otherwise the application disabled it: no route.

Prose and payload branch on the same `cause()`, so a reply cannot name a route its escalation withholds. The escalation uses existing contract values only, as #4009 accepted. `ax_actions` keeps only `ax_element_enabled`; the unused `perform_ax_action` and its re-export go with the literal.

Tests. `harness_appkit_key_window_control_refusal_names_the_foreground_rung` (new; selected by `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh`): the AppKit fixture gains a button enabled only while its window is key; the cell snapshots it, presses it in the background behind the foreground sentinel and asserts `code`, `escalation` and `key_window`, then presses it with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` and reads `key_only_pressed=1` back. Unit tests pin the arms the fixture does not reach: key window (no route, prose names neither taken route), another window holding focus (escalation), own window in front outranks the key-window fact, menu item, foreground rung in force. Press_key: the sheet and unidentified-holder payloads.

Before-proof and mutations. The new cell run with a driver built from `origin/main` `0f29c142d` fails at the code assertion (`tool_invocation_failed` with main's literal, not `element_disabled`). Moving the key-window arm above the owned-window arm, dropping the foreground-rung filter and dropping the menu arm fail `the_apps_own_window_in_front_outranks_the_key_window_fact`, `the_foreground_rung_is_not_offered_once_it_is_in_force` and `a_disabled_menu_item_names_no_route`.

title: macOS invoke_menu presses a submenu-bearing final segment and discards the labels it just enumerated
body:
## What happens

`invoke_menu` presses whatever its final path segment resolves to, and a menu item that bears a submenu advertises `AXPress` like any other:

```rust
fn choose_action(actions: &[String], final_segment: bool) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let supports = |name: &str| actions.iter().any(|action| action == name);
    let order: &[&str] = if final_segment {
        &["AXPress", "AXPick", "AXConfirm"]
    } else {
        &["AXPress", "AXPick", "AXShowMenu", "AXOpen"]
    };
    order.iter().copied().find(|action| supports(action))
}
```

So `invoke_menu(["Format", "Font"])` presses `Font`. That press cannot invoke a command — there is none — it opens the submenu and leaves the application tracking an open menu. The reply nevertheless says:

> Resolved the live native menu path and dispatched its final accessibility action; verify the command's semantic effect from fresh state.

A caller cannot tell that from a real dispatch, and there is no way to ask what is inside a submenu, so the caller has to guess the next segment. Two consequences we hit in practice:

**A wrong guess returns nothing to correct it.** The refusal names the index and stops:

```
await win.menu(["File", "New Contact"], …)
→ CuaError: invoke_menu: path segment 1 was not found
```

The labels that *are* at that level are known to the driver at the moment it refuses — `resolve_exact_prefix` just enumerated them to decide there was no exact match — and they are discarded. In the bench run above both harness runs then fell back to blind pixel clicks at the toolbar, typed into whatever had focus, and did not complete the task.

**Callers read menus out of `get_window_state` instead, which is expensive.** Because the menu tree is reachable through the ordinary AX walk, a consumer that needs menu labels asks for the window tree and parses the rendered menu bar out of it. On Contacts that observation is 68.7 kB / 530 lines, of which lines 413-530 are the entire menu bar with every submenu expanded (`Apple ▸ Recent Items`, `Card ▸ Add Field ▸ …`); the consumer's 50 kB cap then elided lines 264-454 — the contact rows, the card pane and the whole `AXToolbar`. The menu listing displaced the window content the caller actually asked about.

For the "the press did not invoke the command" half, a related live case: Chrome's `View ▸ Developer ▸ Allow JavaScript from Apple Events`. `AXPress` on `Developer` (tried three times) left the toggle unchanged; opening `View ▸ Developer` and then walking the open submenu with real key events (`key code 125` ×5, `key code 36`) did flip it.

## Where (`8cb8f6d2b`)

- `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/invoke_menu.rs`, `choose_action` — `final_segment: true` offers `AXPress` first, with nothing asking whether the target bears a submenu.
- same file, `invoke_path` — presses at every depth including the last, then reports the success text above.
- same file, `resolve_exact_prefix` — has the sibling titles in hand when it returns `path segment {depth} is ambiguous` / `was not found`, and drops them.

## Expected

- A final segment that bears a submenu is listed, not pressed: the items macOS actually has under it, in order, each with the title a path segment can address and whether it opens a further submenu.
- A segment resolution failure names which segment failed and the items at that level, so a caller that guessed a label wrong can correct it from the refusal.
- A leaf segment keeps pressing exactly as it does today.

That makes the menu reachable without the window-tree detour, and it removes the class of reply that claims a command was dispatched when a submenu was opened.

I have this implemented and unit-tested on a branch and can open a PR referencing this issue. Shape there: `{status: "listed", resolved_path, items: [{title, enabled?, has_submenu, shortcut?}]}` on the listing path and `refusal.failed_segment` / `refusal.items` under the existing `menu_path_unavailable` code — no contract types change, since this tool's structured payloads are already free-form. The listing resolves against the closed menu tree first and only falls back to the press walk for lazily populated menus, so listing opens nothing on screen.

title: feat(cua-driver): add OpenJev decision model adapter
body:
## TL;DR

Re-cut per maintainer review: this PR is now **OpenJev backend only** on current `main`'s accepted decision architecture. The old parallel `jev_backends` layer, browser-runner routing changes, TypeSafe configuration changes, and backend telemetry are gone.

Candidate: `48c9fc770674f57ca40466b9f7e006150456a183` on base `9545a3d17b44b587b593d59090dc140740876a6e`.

## Change

Adds Python + TypeScript OpenJev System One adapters for `jev-use`.

- Python implements the existing `DecisionModel` / `DecisionRequest` seam and returns `ModelScores`.
- Both languages consume the existing validated `cua.jev_choice_request_v1|v2` shape; a v2 request is sent directly as the System One `state`.
- The provider can only score caller-supplied IDs. It does not construct Driver actions or own retry/routing policy.
- The remote contract is `POST /v1/systemone` with one `choice` question over the immutable candidate criteria.

### Transport boundary

Configuration is intentionally explicit:

- `OPENJEV_BASE_URL` — required remote base or full `/v1/systemone` endpoint;
- `OPENJEV_API_KEY` — optional;
- `OPENJEV_MODEL` — defaults to `openjev`;
- `OPENJEV_TIMEOUT_MS` — bounded to 100–60000 ms.

Safety properties retained from the earlier #3961 investigation:

- API keys are sent only over HTTPS;
- URL-embedded credentials are rejected;
- query/fragment-bearing base URLs are rejected;
- redirects are not followed;
- response reads are capped at 256 KiB;
- timeout / transport / malformed-response failures are bounded errors;
- no provider error causes action replay in this adapter.

The existing Python `choose()` validator remains the final authority for exact candidate-set equality, finite probability mass, unique argmax and selected ID. The TypeScript mirror enforces the same score invariants before returning.

## Scope deliberately removed

Per the review on this PR:

- no replacement `jev_backends` abstraction;
- no Driver changes;
- no visual-routing changes;
- no browser runner provider selection in this slice;
- no content-free `backend` event field in this slice;
- no S1 duplication;
- no TypeSafe base/model/timeout change yet.

Browser provider parity + backend receipts are tracked separately in https://github.com/kvnloo/cua/issues/78.

## Invocation surface

The backend is now selectable through the existing Python decision CLI:

`python/choose_decision.py --model openjev`

and through `verify_decision_cli.py --model openjev`. This is still only the bounded decision interface; browser/native runner provider routing remains the separate follow-up.

## Validation status

Exact head `48c9fc770674f57ca40466b9f7e006150456a183`, from `libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use`:

- `uv run --frozen python -m unittest python/tests/test_openjev_model.py` — 15 tests OK
- `uv run --frozen python -m unittest discover -s python/tests` — 226 tests OK, 1 skipped
- `npm test` — 113 pass
- `npm run typecheck` — pass

The added loopback rows use the real HTTP transport. Valid selection, unknown candidate ID, HTTP 503, malformed body, redirect, and oversized response each made exactly one request to `/v1/systemone`. The redirect target was not fetched. 503 and malformed responses are bounded transport errors; an unknown ID becomes `kind: "error"` / `reason: "model_error"` and dispatches no action.

The PR is ready for re-review after the maintainer-requested re-cut. Browser provider parity and backend receipts remain https://github.com/kvnloo/cua/issues/78.

## Related work

Refs #3915.

- Maintainer re-cut request: https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3961#pullrequestreview-5345901372
- downstream execution packet: https://github.com/kvnloo/cua/issues/77
- browser provider follow-up: https://github.com/kvnloo/cua/issues/78



## 2026-10-01 current-main refresh

Rebuilt the backend-only slice directly on current upstream `9545a3d17b44b587b593d59090dc140740876a6e` as exact head `48c9fc770674f57ca40466b9f7e006150456a183`. The PR is one commit / seven files with the same intended OpenJev-only delta. Exact-head fork validation is `kvnloo/cua#88`; its checks are queued, so the earlier green evidence remains historical rather than a claim about this head.

## Credit / provenance

- @f-trycua opened #3915 proposing a mockable TypeSafe Jev decision-loop example for Cua Driver. This PR implements that requested integration surface and extends it with the adapter/evidence work described above.


## 2026-10-16 supported CLI acceptance update (supersedes earlier head pins)

Current exact head: `6ece26927ab4c532af8fb459c2de6434a8339aa0`, fast-forward test/docs-only extension of `97cd02c2`. The adapter implementation and existing contributor history are unchanged.

Fresh Python 3.14.8 focused suite: `python -m unittest discover -s python/tests -p test_openjev_model.py -v` — **19 tests PASS**, including eight real subprocess/loopback-HTTP CLI scenarios (exact v2 state/criteria, valid choice, five response failures without retry, and two pre-transport refusals). [Exact evidence, scope and CI handoff](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3961#issuecomment-6217323201).

This is decision-boundary proof only: no Driver, external service, browser/native effect, speedup, TypeScript rerun or full-suite claim. Current-head [jev-use CI](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/38913473901) is `action_required`, not executed green; maintainer re-review remains required. The older tests/timing in this body remain historical at their named SHAs.

title: fix(cua-driver): a background left click must land where it is aimed
body:
Clicking anything in a background session did nothing, in an app whose event
loop resolves a button event at the pointer position it last *saw* rather than
at the coordinate the event carries — while every layer reported success.

The click was posted, and it was delivered. It was applied at the **wrong
place**, because neither background left-click path established that position
first:

* `interactive.rs` posted the Down with no move primer at all, no settle, and a
  zero-millisecond gap to the Up.
* `click_at_xy_chromium` posted a primer at the target and then an **off-screen**
  primer down/up at `(-1,-1)` followed by a 100 ms settle — precisely long
  enough for such an app to adopt `(-1,-1)` as the pointer position. The real
  down/up 1 ms later then resolved off the window.

The background **right** click already worked, which is the control: it does
primer → 12 ms → down → 28 ms → up, and posts no off-screen pair.

## How the mechanism was established

Two measurements on a live guest, not inference:

* a background down+drag drew a box-select rectangle **anchored at the previous
  interaction's coordinate** while its end matched the drag exactly; and
* the identical click that did nothing cold **succeeded once two standalone move
  events had settled the pointer first**, with no other change.

## The change

Prime the position before a background Down and give the target a frame to adopt
it; never let the Up follow the Down inside one pass of the target's event loop;
and re-aim at the target after the Chromium primer pair rather than leaving the
cached pointer off-screen.

The off-screen primer is **kept** — Chromium needs it to open the user-activation
gate at a coordinate that cannot hit a DOM element — so this costs one extra
event and one frame while leaving that gate open.

## Evidence

Same probe, same coordinate, `background_only` policy, read back from the target
application's own rendering rather than from any ack:

```
before: click the "Modeling" tab -> workspace stays Sculpting
after:  click the "Modeling" tab -> workspace is Modeling,
        mode changes Sculpt Mode -> Edit Mode (82% of pixels redrawn)
```

The `interactive_input` path likewise switches workspace on a click. Chromium
still accepts background clicks afterwards: a click on the omnibox focuses it
and opens its suggestion dropdown.

## Not covered

No controlled before/after for the Chromium path — only that it still works. The
change lengthens its target Down→Up gap from 1 ms to 28 ms, well inside the
double-click interval, but that is reasoning rather than measurement.

Linux/X11 was not exercised: it refuses a `background_only` interactive-input
lease outright, so this exact failure cannot arise there, though XTest's
pointer-warp semantics were not measured.

title: [Bug]: browser_click cannot activate any element that opens a JS dialog — trusted refuses, dom_event deadlocks in Runtime.callFunctionOn, then browser_dialog cannot reach the tab
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On a driver-owned isolated browser, no `browser_click` route can click an element whose handler opens a page-owned JavaScript dialog. `trusted` refuses, `dom_event` deadlocks for 20s inside `Runtime.callFunctionOn`, and afterwards `browser_dialog` cannot reach the tab at all because `Page.enable` also times out. A sibling button that opens no dialog works through the same route in 1.4s.

### Reproduction

`repro_browser_dialog.py` in the gist below is self-contained: it serves its own fixture, launches a throwaway host Chrome, lets `browser_prepare` spawn an isolated driver-owned browser, and clicks both buttons.

```html
<button id="quiet" onclick="window.__quiet=true">no dialog</button>
<button id="asks"  onclick="window.__asked = confirm('Delete?')">opens confirm()</button>
```

1. `browser_prepare` with `allow_launch: true` and `profile: {mode: isolated_new}`
2. `get_browser_state` to bind, then `browser_navigate` to the fixture
3. `browser_click` the `quiet` button with `input_route: "dom_event"`
4. `browser_click` the `asks` button with the default `trusted` route
5. `browser_click` the `asks` button with `input_route: "dom_event"`
6. `browser_dialog` with `action: "inspect"`

### Expected behavior

At least one route can activate a control that opens a dialog, so that `browser_dialog` can then inspect and resolve it. That tool exists for exactly this case — its description covers "a page-owned JavaScript alert, confirm, prompt, or beforeunload dialog" — but there is currently no way to reach the state where it applies.

### Actual behavior

```
control: no dialog, dom_event      1439 ms  {"delivery":{"mode":"background"},"effect":"unverifiable","escalation":{"reason":"effect_unconfirmed","target":"page"},"route":"dom"}
confirm(), trusted                   62 ms  {"effect":"refused","escalation":{"reason":"route_unavailable","target":"page"},"route":"trusted_input"}
confirm(), dom_event              21268 ms  {"_raw":"DOM click failed: CDP Runtime.callFunctionOn timed out after 20s"}
browser_dialog inspect                      {"refusal":{"code":"browser_action_unavailable","message":"the exact tab does not expose JavaScript dialog events: CDP Page.enable timed out after …"}}
```

Step by step:

- `trusted` refuses, which matches its documented posture: "It refuses rather than foregrounding a standalone browser." Not a defect by itself, but it leaves `dom_event` as the only background option.
- `dom_event` dispatches `el.click()` through `Runtime.callFunctionOn`. `confirm()` blocks the JS frame that call is awaiting, so the CDP response never arrives and the driver gives up after 20s.
- The blocked frame then wedges the rest of the tab's CDP session: the follow-up `Page.enable` from `browser_dialog` also times out, so the dialog is not merely absent, it is unreachable.

The control isolates the cause: the same route, same tab, same snapshot, on the sibling button that opens no dialog returns in 1439 ms.

### Environment

```
Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.2 (aarch64-macos), installed via cua.ai/driver/install.sh
Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.0.0 (Darwin 27.0.0), arm64, Apple M5
Browser: Google Chrome 153.0.8010.50, driver-owned isolated_new profile via browser_prepare
Permission mode: standard; Accessibility + Screen Recording granted; daemon started with `open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve`
```

### Evidence

https://gist.github.com/0xsline/e1bf3d91aaa9857612bf0dc1f63e97ae

The script exits 0 only when all four observations hold: the control is not refused, `trusted` is refused, the `dom_event` reply contains a timeout, and `browser_dialog` cannot report a present dialog.

### Workaround and additional context

None found for a driver-owned standalone browser. Attaching to a foregrounded existing profile may let the `trusted` route through, but that changes the permission posture and was not the configuration under test.

A fix probably does not need the response at all: `el.click()` is fire-and-forget, so dispatching it without awaiting the `Runtime.callFunctionOn` result, or racing the dispatch against `Page.javascriptDialogOpening`, would let the dialog surface while the handler stays blocked, which is the state `browser_dialog` is designed to resolve. Enabling `Page` events before the click rather than on first `browser_dialog` call would also avoid the second timeout.

This is a different failure from the adjacent open issues. #2953 is `dom_event` reporting success after a no-op; here the call reports an explicit timeout. #2811 was `dom_event` silently no-opping on trust-gated controls; here the handler does run, and running it is precisely what wedges the session. #2882 tracks re-validating the two routes across platforms, which this data point feeds but does not duplicate.

The closest precedent is #1936, "Linux: get_window_state and type_text hang (no timeout) on modal dialogs", fixed in #1938. This is the same hazard on the browser surface: a modal blocks the transport the driver is waiting on. The browser side already degrades better than that one did — the timeout is bounded and the daemon and page both survive — but the operation still cannot complete.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(sandbox): preserve configured HTTP command timeouts
body:
## Summary

Commands without a server-side timeout pass `timeout=None` to HTTPX, which disables the configured client timeout. Reuse the client timeout so stalled commands stop as configured. Keep the existing server timeout plus 10 seconds of read headroom.

Fixes #3769. Restores the default-timeout behavior intended by #1355.

## Compatibility and risk

No public API or retry policy change; no RFC needed. Calls that previously waited indefinitely now honor the configured timeout. This is a Sandbox patch fix.

## Validation

- Added five request-timeout cases. Three failed before the fix; all five pass after it.
- HTTP retry and computer-server transport tests: 16 passed.
- Black, isort, Ruff, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Broader Sandbox run: 640 passed, 63 skipped, four unrelated failures (three stale Fleet version assertions and one live registry image-format check). Desktop and VM integration files were excluded. All four failures also reproduce on unchanged main (`83f142c4290a`).
- Independent loopback checks: `send()` and `get_screen_size()` each raised `httpx.ReadTimeout` after about 0.2 seconds with a 0.2-second timeout; the server received one request in each case.
- Validated commit: `8c7f80389b6e793cc8b6f4d7037c56d85a2c00b5`. Release-title and version checks pass locally; contributor-attribution and release-reminder checks pass on GitHub.
- Pull request CI, including release metadata, is waiting for maintainer approval to run.

title: fix(sandbox): match computer-server WebSocket envelopes
body:
## Summary

WebSocket commands put arguments at the wrong JSON level, and successful replies lose their fields. File reads fail, screenshots are empty, and screen-size calls raise `KeyError`.

Send nested `params`, keep top-level reply fields, and use the existing screenshot and screen-size helpers. Preserve legacy responses and JPEG conversion, and raise explicit server errors consistently.

## Related work

Fixes #3771. Thanks to the reporter for the problem description and reproduction outline.

## Compatibility and risk

Restores the existing computer-server protocol; no public signature or server changes. Authentication and reconnect behavior are unchanged. No RFC is needed for this bug fix. Reverting the commit restores the previous client behavior.

## Validation

- Fresh before/after check against current main `9bbfa7dd3e27ca7f1861ede70aaca390174493f9`: the same 26 WebSocket tests produce 17 failures / 9 passes before, and 26 passes at this PR head. Includes empty or missing error details.
- Focused WebSocket, HTTP retry, shared response, and SSE suites: 45 passed.

title: docs(cua-driver): typecheck SDK cleanup examples
body:
## Summary

Two desktop-embedding TypeScript examples call `uniffiDestroy()` on `CuaDriverLike`, which fails with TS2339. Narrowing with `CuaDriver.instanceOf()` makes the examples compile while preserving their cleanup order.

Add a check that extracts six example scenarios directly from the SDK README and three maintained documentation pages, then typechecks them against the current SDK. It runs through `npm run typecheck` and a dedicated Linux workflow on relevant SDK or documentation changes, without loading a native library. The already-correct in-process examples are covered too.

## Related work

Fixes #3677.

RFC: not required; documentation and compile-time regression coverage only.

## Compatibility and risk

No runtime, public API, protocol, permissions or platform behavior changes. The check uses strict TypeScript with NodeNext/ES2022, rejects missing or empty selected examples, and accepts LF/CRLF documentation. Rollback is a revert of this PR.

## Validation

Candidate `5a4c71af0d62f6bf166c4f82759e75d3f8d87840`, validated on Ubuntu 24.04.4 ARM64, Node 22.23.2 and the locked TypeScript 5.9.3:

- Before the documentation fix, the new check reported TS2339 for both embedding examples.
- `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `npm run build`, and `npm run typecheck` in `libs/cua-driver/typescript` passed.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm docs:check-hygiene`, `pnpm docs:check-links`, and `pnpm build` in `docs` passed; links reported zero errors and the build generated 158 pages.
- Prettier 3.6.2 passed for the changed JavaScript, package manifest and workflow. MDX is ignored by the repository's Prettier configuration and passed the owning documentation checks.
- The built preview served both changed pages under `/docs/` with HTTP 200 and the guarded cleanup present.
- Independent review passed: unsafe-cleanup mutations in all six selected scenarios fail, missing/empty examples fail, and CRLF content passes.

Native lifecycle and desktop behavior were not exercised; no native code changes. Upstream workflows currently report `action_required` before jobs start (for example, [the documentation typecheck run](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/35466757263)); maintainer approval is needed for the fork workflows. title: fix(cua-driver): fail closed on unloadable policy and harden gates
body:
## Summary

Hardens Cua Driver's permission-policy enforcement and a set of higher-severity
findings surfaced by a focused code review of the driver. All changes are in
`libs/cua-driver/rust` and are covered by unit or integration tests.

## Changes

### Permission policy (highest severity)
- `is_tool_listable()` previously swallowed a policy load error and advertised
  every tool (fail-open). It now **fails closed** and logs the fault, so an
  unloadable policy can never present tools the daemon cannot authorize.
  (`cua-driver-core/src/policy.rs`)
- A configured-but-missing policy path was already fatal in
  `PolicyEngine::load`; the README claimed otherwise ("unset **or** points to a
  path that does not exist ... no policy enforcement"). The README now states
  the real contract: unset disables enforcement, a missing/failing configured
  path is a hard startup error.
- New `CUA_DRIVER_REQUIRE_POLICY=1` refuses startup unless at least one policy
  layer is configured.
- `DaemonMetadata.policy_mode` (`enforced` | `disabled` | `error`) is now
  returned in the daemon metadata handshake as an additive field (older peers
  ignore it).
- The README policy example no longer references removed/nonexistent tools
  (`screenshot`, `shell_execute`, `file_delete`) and uses real tools.

### Revoke reporting
- `SdkAdapter::end_session` returned `Ok` whenever the transport succeeded,
  even when the `end_session` tool result was `isError: true`. It now inspects
  the tool result, so `revoke_authorization` cannot claim a successful revoke
  for a session that was not ended.

### ABI / gates
- Added a dedicated C-linkage test for `cua_driver_is_available_v1`,
  `cua_driver_metadata_json_v1`, and `cua_driver_list_tools_json_v1` that
  asserts their documented null-handle status.
- `default_capabilities_for` now logs a warning when a tool has no capability
  mapping (with `health_report` listed explicitly as intentionally
  capability-free).
- `schema_consistency_test.rs` no longer silently passes when the driver binary
  was not built: it panics under `CUA_DRIVER_REQUIRE_BINARY=1` or `CI`, and
  prints a loud warning on a local skip.

## Scope note: session tombstones decoupled

An earlier revision of this pull request also capped `ENDED_SESSIONS` at 4096
entries with oldest-first eviction. Review raised that this weakens a
security/lifecycle invariant: the end-of-session tombstone is the durable
authority behind every resurrection guard (`tool.rs`, `capture_scope.rs`,
`recording.rs`), so evicting an entry makes `is_session_ended()` return `false`
and lets a stray late action recreate session-owned state.

That change is **removed from this pull request** (reverted in `14d8db12`).
Bounded tombstone growth is being handled as a dedicated lifecycle change that
prunes only at a proof boundary — for example after the owning transport is
irreversibly gone — or by requiring an active lifecycle record for
non-`start_session` calls, with a regression test that forces pruning and
proves an evicted id is still refused. Keeping the policy, revoke, ABI, and
gate hardening here keeps this PR focused on the fail-closed behavior it
documents.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` — 630 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-sdk --lib availability_and_introspection_symbols_are_exported_with_c_linkage` — passed.
- `cargo check -p cua-driver --tests` — clean (no new warnings).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- New integration tests (Linux/Windows lanes) cover both fail-closed startup
  guards for direct MCP.

## Release note

`fix(cua-driver)`: patch release. The behavior changes are: unloadable policy
now fails closed, `CUA_DRIVER_REQUIRE_POLICY` and `policy_mode` are new, and
`revoke_authorization` no longer over-reports success.

title: Fix/3981 permissions status daemon running liveness
body:
## What

`run_permissions_status` was reporting `daemon_running: false` whenever direct permissions were pending or unreadable — even when the daemon socket was actively listening. This caused the CLI remediation output to erroneously suggest starting the daemon when it was already running.

This fix evaluates socket liveness via `is_daemon_listening` and propagates it accurately in both the JSON and human-readable outputs, independently of the permissions-check result.

## Why

Issue #3981: `permissions status` is used by agents and scripts to decide whether to run `lume start`. A false `daemon_running: false` causes unnecessary restarts and masks the real problem (a missing permission grant), leading to misleading remediation loops.

## Changes

- **`cli.rs`** (`run_permissions_status`): Decouples `daemon_running` from the permissions outcome — socket liveness is now checked independently and reported accurately in all output modes.

## Testing

`cargo check` passes. Existing `cua-driver` CI suite green.

title: fix(mcp-server): return session stats without blocking the event loop
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: the `get_session_stats` MCP tool (an `async def` in `mcp_server/server.py`) calls the synchronous `SessionManager.get_session_stats()` on the server's running event loop. That method scheduled a coroutine on the same loop with `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(..., loop)` and then blocked on `.result()`. The loop thread is the one blocked, so the coroutine never runs and the call never returns. Calling the tool freezes the whole MCP server.
- What changed: `get_session_stats()` now builds the stats dict directly. The body has no `await`, so on the event loop it already reads a consistent snapshot without taking `_session_lock`. The return shape is unchanged.

## Related work

No existing issue or pull request covers this. Searched issues/PRs for `get_session_stats`, `session_manager`, `run_coroutine_threadsafe`.

Refs #
