fix(cua-bench): preserve quoted keyboard action literals
body:
## Summary

Parsing `repr(TypeAction(text="line one\nline two"))` currently produces literal backslash-n characters instead of a newline. Mixed quotes can truncate text, Windows paths gain extra backslashes, and hotkeys containing commas or closing brackets fail to round-trip.

Match complete string/list literals and decode them with `ast.literal_eval`. Require the complete action to match so trailing commands or unexpected fields do not get silently discarded. This covers the repr parser and the snake-case `type(...)` form.

## Related work

Self-contained correctness fix; no linked issue. Searched active PRs for competing parser work.

## Compatibility and risk

The existing action classes, function signatures and serialized fields remain compatible. Escapes now follow the Python literal syntax already used by action reprs; malformed input raises ValueError rather than being partially accepted.

## Validation

- Reproduced 19 failures on the unmodified parser before implementing the fix.
- Focused parser suite: 55 passed, covering multiline text, Windows paths, mixed quotes, punctuation keys, empty/string hotkey lists and malformed literals.
- Python 3.12, full offline cua-bench suite on candidate `2d33c8d`: **343 passed, 2 skipped**.
- Black, isort, Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing CI collects the new cases.

- Local release-title validation and `validate_release_versions.py --product all` passed.
- GitHub `contributor-attribution` and `release-reminder` checks passed.
- Other upstream workflows, including `CI: cua-bench` and `CI: Release metadata`, are `action_required` and await a maintainer's approval to run fork workflows.

title: fix(cua-bench): apply configuration for the selected agent
body:
## Summary

If `.cua/config.yaml` selects `first` and the CLI selects `--agent second`, configuration lookup still loads first's registered import path. The resulting namespace names second but can execute first's class. Registered defaults also lose to lower-priority config.yaml values despite the documented precedence.

Resolve the winning agent before looking up its registration, clear an inherited import when switching agents, and merge the existing layers in their documented order: CLI > environment > registered agent defaults > agent config > project defaults. A registration without an import path preserves the explicit configured import for the same agent.

## Related work

Self-contained correctness fix; no linked issue. Searched active PRs for ConfigLoader/agent-selection work.

## Compatibility and risk

No flags, schema fields or function signatures are added. Configurations relying on the reversed precedence now follow the documented order. Explicit CLI import paths remain highest priority.

## Validation

- Six new regression cases failed against the original loader.
- Focused config/discovery suite: 13 passed, including the real CLI configuration application helper and YAML-backed selection/precedence cases.
- Python 3.12, full offline cua-bench suite on candidate `65b7ec52`: **327 passed, 2 skipped**.
- Black, isort, Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing CI collects the new cases.

title: fix(cua-bench): resolve Harbor task links from their cache directory
body:
## Summary

A Harbor dataset fetched with `CUA_BENCH_REGISTRY_CACHE=cache` creates a task symlink whose target repeats the relative cache path. The pinned checkout succeeds, but `tasks/hello/main.py` cannot be opened. Re-resolving that cached dataset can then raise FileExistsError.

Create each link relative to its containing tasks directory. Repair dangling task symlinks left by the previous behavior before recreating them.

## Related work

Self-contained correctness fix; no linked issue. Searched active PRs for relative registry-cache work.

## Compatibility and risk

The registry format and pinned checkout behavior are retained. Existing valid links remain in use; repair removes only a dangling symlink at the selected task link. Dataset files and checkouts are preserved.

## Validation

- All three relative-cache cases failed against the original implementation. A separate regression also reproduced the stale-link FileExistsError before adding repair.
- Harbor/registry suite: 16 passed.
- Fixtures fetch a real temporary git repository via file://, check source contents, cover paths with spaces and an explicit relative root, then disable git to prove offline cache reuse.
- Python 3.12, full offline cua-bench suite on candidate `9e9f0e72`: **324 passed, 2 skipped**.
- Black, isort, Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.
- Native Windows symlink behavior was not exercised in this Linux environment.

- Local release-title validation and `validate_release_versions.py --product all` passed.
- GitHub `contributor-attribution` and `release-reminder` checks passed.
- Other upstream workflows, including `CI: cua-bench` and `CI: Release metadata`, are `action_required` and await a maintainer's approval to run fork workflows.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Focused change; the description matches the diff.
- [x] Corrects existing behavior without introducing a public contract; no RFC needed.
- [x] Regression tests are collected by the existing cua-bench CI workflow.

title: fix(cua-bench): save trace image paths relative to the dataset
body:
## Summary

`Tracing.save_to_disk(..., save_pngs=True, image_dir=...)` records only the image directory's basename. With `image_dir="trace/assets/screenshots"`, the exported row incorrectly points to `screenshots/<hash>.png`; using a sibling/shared directory breaks the reference too.

Store PNG references relative to the trace dataset directory, preserving the full directory relationship. Keep portable forward-slash paths, with an absolute-path fallback when Windows cannot express a relative path across drives.

## Related work

Self-contained correctness fix; no linked issue. Checked active export/artifact PRs for overlapping implementation.

## Compatibility and risk

The exported schema stays the same. The default `imgs/<hash>.png` form is retained. Custom image-directory references now resolve to the files that were actually written; sibling-directory references include the necessary parent components.

## Validation

- Nine custom-directory cases failed on the original exporter; all three default-directory controls passed.
- PNG sidecar and existing export-schema suites: 14 passed.
- Twelve real save/load cases cover PIL images, PNG bytes and bytearrays across default, nested, sibling and relative directories. Each exported reference is opened and its pixels compared with the original.
- Python 3.12, full offline cua-bench suite on candidate `d4b74caa`: **332 passed, 2 skipped**.
- Black, isort, Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.

title: fix(images): release-macos.sh logs in to ghcr, guards disk and drops push caches
body:
These fix rough edges found in the first end-to-end run of `scripts/images/release-macos.sh` (cua-spacesd 0.5.3, macOS 26-slim and 26):

- **Registry login:** the script never logged crane and oras in, so `annotate.sh`, the doctor-report attach and `verify` relied on whatever `~/.docker` held. The run only worked because I had pre-logged-in a scratch `DOCKER_CONFIG`. It now logs both in to ghcr.io with the gh token under an isolated `DOCKER_CONFIG=$WORK/docker`.
- **Push caches:** `lume push` keeps a ~23 GB `.lume_oci_push_cache` inside each VM directory. Slim's was also cloned into the full VM, and neither was deleted, so the run sat about 50 GB above what it needed. On this Mac (~265 GB free) that hit the 200 GB floor during the slim push. Each tier's cache is now dropped as soon as its pin is verified, before the full tier clones slim.
- **Disk guard:** the run refuses to start below `MIN_FREE_GB + 60` (default 260 GB) and checks again before each build and push. Below the floor it stops cleanly, and a rerun resumes.
- **Local ledger:** with `RECORD_LEDGER=false`, the pins' doctor verdicts are now written to `$WORK/ledger`, so `check-docs-image-refs.py --ledger` can confirm the macOS refs.

Tested with `bash -n`, `shellcheck -S warning` and `--dry-run`, which shows the order: publish, drop cache, record, then the next tier. The cache deletion and local-ledger steps are exactly what I ran by hand during the 0.5.3 run.

Other notes from the run, not changed here:
- **Keychain check on resume:** a rerun repeats the keychain check, booting a fresh clone each time. That's harmless and takes about 20 seconds.
- **Input-gate build directory:** the gate builds its cargo test into the checkout's `libs/cua/target` unless `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is set (about 9 GB).

title: fix(cua-driver): find driver releases beyond the first page of monorepo releases
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `cua-driver update` fails with "Could not reach GitHub" when no tag for the selected channel is among the 40 newest monorepo releases. The check read a single page, and every lookup failure printed that one line. Since the Oct 3 cua-spaces, cua-spacesd, and cua-sdk releases, the nightly channel has no tag on that page.
- What changed: the check pages through the listing, 40 releases per request, and stops at the first page with a matching tag or after five pages. `cua-driver update` now prints why a lookup failed. A request failure keeps the "Could not reach GitHub" line and adds a `Reason:` line. A lookup that finds no release for the channel prints `Could not find a <channel> release: no <prefix>* release in the <n> most recent GitHub releases.`

## Related work

Fixes #4598

#2116 edits the same fetch function to add a token header. The two changes will conflict textually but not in behavior.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. Only failure-path message text changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - `cua-driver update` text output changes on failure only, as described above. Exit codes are unchanged. The Windows update E2E retries on the "Could not reach GitHub" line, which request failures still print.
  - The `error` string in `check-update --json` and the `check_for_update` MCP tool is reworded for the no-release case. The JSON shape is unchanged, and the cache fallback is unchanged.
  - A check makes one request when page 1 has a matching tag, as before, and up to five when it does not. Each request keeps the 4 second timeout, so the background banner check can now take up to 20 seconds on its own thread in the worst case.
  - The page size stays at 40. A 100-release page is about 5 MB and took 1.7 s from my machine, which is too close to the timeout.
  - Stopping at the first matching page assumes the listing puts a channel's newest release first. A backport tagged after a higher version can break that if a page boundary falls between the two. The single-page check had the same limit inside its page. A comment on `find_latest_release` states the assumption.
- Risk and rollback: the change is confined to the release lookup and its error message. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver --locked` on macOS arm64: exit 0, no failures, 305 unit tests including the five new `release_lookup_*` tests.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - Mutation check of the new tests: capping the lookup at one page fails four of them, ignoring a short page fails `release_lookup_ends_at_a_short_page`, and reading past a matching page fails `release_lookup_reads_past_a_page_without_matching_tags`.
- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 27.2 arm64, debug build of this branch, isolated `HOME`, live GitHub API, 2026-10-04):
  - stable channel: `Already up to date.`
  - nightly channel: `New version available: 0.30.5-nightly.20260929.36522098176`, found on page 2. The released 0.30.5 nightly binary fails in the same environment.
  - request failure through a dead proxy: the "Could not reach GitHub" line, then `Reason: HTTP error: io: Connection refused`, exit 1.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - The no-release message was not produced against live GitHub because both channels currently resolve. Its text is covered by `release_lookup_gives_up_after_the_page_cap`.
  - Not run on Windows or Linux. The change has no platform-specific code.
  - The desktop E2E matrix was not run. No input, capture, or desktop behavior changed.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.

title: chore: remove the libs/fleet mirror and the cua-fleet crate
body:
Cua Cloud (Fleets) shuts down on Fri 16 Oct 2026, 17:00 PT. This removes the Fleets code that was mirrored into this repo under `libs/fleet`, and everything that built against it. **Draft: do not merge.**

## What is removed
- `libs/fleet` (the Copybara mirror: Go backend, web console, `cyclops-sdk` Rust crates, language bindings, Terraform provider) and `.github/workflows/fleet-mirror-guard.yml`, plus the CODEOWNERS entry.
- The `cua-fleet` crate. The local helpers it held (sidecars, local image builds) move into `cua-sandbox-core` (`build`, `sidecar` modules) unchanged in behaviour.
- `libs/typescript/fleet` (`@trycua/fleet` was built from `libs/fleet`) with `cd-ts-fleet.yml`, `ci-ts-fleet.yml` and its release wiring. Published versions are untouched.
- Workflows that built or ran `libs/fleet` / `cua-fleet` code: `infra-fleets-wif-smoke.yml`, `nightly-image-doctor.yml`, the Go Terraform smoke, the Fleet docs generator, the `fleet`/`fleet-env`/`cua-sandbox` e2e lanes and the fake Fleet test fixture.

## Behaviour after this change
- `on="cloud"` creates, `cloud:<name>` refs, `Cua.fleet()` pool/claim/image calls, `cua fleet …`, `cua image ls|info|rm|create` and `cua auth keys …` fail at once with "Cua Cloud has closed: … Run sandboxes locally, on a machine you run, or in your own cloud account (on=aws|gcp|modal)". The CLI exits with code 4.
- The SDK's FFI shape is unchanged (same objects, records and methods), so existing callers get that message, not a missing symbol. Bindings are regenerated for the doc text only.
- Records of earlier cloud sandboxes and Spaces stay listed; using them says Cua Cloud has closed, and `delete` removes the record.
- `cua auth whoami` shows the identity from the account token and no longer lists Fleet namespaces.

## What keeps working
- The Spaces apps' billing status (`GET /api/billing/status`) and the existing Cua Volume `cloud` backend still call the same endpoints with the same base URL (`CUA_FLEET_BASE_URL`, default `https://run.cua.ai`) and the same credentials (signed-in session, `FLEETS_TOKEN`, or `CUA_CLIENT_ID`/`CUA_CLIENT_SECRET`). They now go through a small client in `cua-auth` (`account`) instead of the Fleet SDK. `Cua.fleet().billingStatus()` keeps working for the SwiftUI app.

## Tests
- `libs/cua`: `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, the web-feature clippy, the wasm32 build, `cargo fmt`, and `cargo test` for cua-auth, cua-sandbox-core, cua-spaces, cua-daemon, cua-sdk, cua-cli, cua-spaces-ext, cua-spaces-ffi, cua-spaces-app-core, cua-spaces-cli and cua-volume.
- Spaces app (Tauri): `cargo test --lib --test commands`; openkoalabot sample and the spaces-e2e and SDK e2e crates check and clippy clean.
- Python binding tests; bindings drift check; docs generators (`--check` for cua-cli, cua-sdk, python, TS, cua-rust, sandbox, spaces) and docs structure, link and image-ref checks; `check-lockfiles` for every Cargo and pnpm lockfile.

title: [Bug]: macOS Lume bring_to_front test loses its SwiftUI occluder before prior-app recovery
body:
## Summary

On the canonical Lume lane, `exact_secondary_window_is_verified_and_prior_app_can_recover_focus` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/bring_to_front_macos_test.rs:351`) fails at its final step:

```
prior app recovery failed: bring_to_front: no running application for pid <occluder> (process not found or exited).
```

The SwiftUI occluder is launched with `open -n -g`. It maps an ordinary window, accepts `AXRaise` through System Events, and the exact secondary-window activation and its frontmost, AX key-window and z-order oracles all pass. By the recovery call, the occluder process has gone. It leaves no crash report and no runningboard termination record. The other two `bring_to_front` tests pass. The hosted macOS lane passes this test.

## Occurrences

Same disposable `macos-tahoe-cua:26.5.2` worker (25F84, SIP off), with `--test-threads=1` as the runner invokes it:

| Source | Run | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `b00cb46d5` (#4601) | `20261004T112135Z-95348` | pass |
| `7ff69de17` | `20261004T113152Z-35288` | fail |
| `c7e684b41` | `20261004T134131Z-1402` | fail |
| `c7e684b41` (after a VM reboot) | `20261004T141421Z-39361` | fail |

In the last two runs, every other part of the gate passes, including all 173 typed rows. This test is the only thing keeping the Lume gate from a clean pass on `main`.

## Notes

- The SwiftUI harness exits only through its Exit button (`NSApp.terminate`). Nothing in the test presses it.
- `launch_occluder` takes the first new pid of the harness executable after `open -n`. If LaunchServices briefly creates a handoff process, or another instance of the harness is relaunched, that pid may not be the long-lived app. This is unproven.
- Possible directions: resolve the occluder through `NSRunningApplication` and the bundle URL, and re-resolve before recovery; or launch the occluder in the test's job and own its lifetime.

title: fix(cua-driver): count focus in a window's inline rename field as focus on that window
body:
## Summary

This PR was narrowed to the focus fix only; keeping Finder in front when the field is opened from behind another app follows as a separate PR once this one lands, and that one will close #4615.

- Problem this solves: with Finder in front, renaming a file through foreground keys on its window (the route #4483's `file_name_needs_rename` refusal points to) never commits. Return opens the rename field, `hotkey` cmd+a and `type_text` reach it, and the final Return is refused: `press_key delivery failed: exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery`. While the field has the focus, Finder reports no `AXFocusedWindow`, so foreground HID delivery re-keys the window and then cannot see it focused. The same happens after `invoke_menu ["File", "Rename"]`.
- What changed: the rename field is an `AXTextField` in its own small WindowServer window whose WindowServer parent is the Finder window; its AX parent is the application and it has no `AXWindow`, so the parent record (`SLSWindowIteratorGetParentID`, read by the new `window_parent_id` in `input/skylight.rs`) is the only link back. When the target app reports **no** focused window and its focused element is such a text field of the target window (`inline_editor_open` in `ax/bindings.rs`), `with_foreground_hid_activation` treats the target window as focused and delivers without re-keying it. A reported focused window is used as before, so a sibling window that holds focus still gets today's handling. Reads use 0.2 s timeouts. The decision is a pure `is_inline_editor` with unit tests.

## Related work

Refs #4615, #4469, #4483. Part (b) (Finder kept in front when the field is opened from behind another app) builds on this.

RFC: not required (no contract, schema, tool-list or result text change).

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. In a logged-in macOS session, create a folder with `draft.txt` and `other.txt` and open it in Finder; open two more Finder windows (Documents, Downloads) so background keys are refused `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity`. Bring the folder window to front (`bring_to_front`). `list_windows` gives Finder's `<pid>` and the folder window's `<window_id>`; `get_window_state` on it and `click` the `draft.txt` name cell's `element_token`.
2. On the folder window, each with `delivery_mode: "foreground"`:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "key": "return", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "keys": ["cmd", "a"], "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "text": "final.txt", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "key": "return", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   ```
   (`press_key`, `hotkey`, `type_text`, `press_key`).
3. On main the field opens and keeps the typed name, and the last call is refused:
   ```json
   {"isError": true, "text": "press_key delivery failed: exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery"}
   ```
   The folder still holds `draft.txt`. Same with `invoke_menu ["File", "Rename"]` in place of the first Return.

On this branch the last Return is delivered and the folder lists `final.txt`.

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM, Apple Silicon, Finder list view, three Finder windows, Finder relaunched clean and a fresh fixture per run, one MCP connection per run; disk read with `os.listdir` after every call, front app and Finder's focused element polled every 20 ms outside cua-driver. 3 runs per row on each build.

| Case | main ed22ad958 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Keyboard route, Finder in front | **0 of 3** renamed, final Return refused | **3 of 3** renamed |
| Menu route (File > Rename), Finder in front | **0 of 3** renamed, final Return refused | **3 of 3** renamed |
| Keyboard route, TextEdit in front (part (b)'s case) | 0 of 3, every call success | 0 of 3, unchanged (not claimed here) |
| Menu route, TextEdit in front (part (b)'s case) | 0 of 3, every call success | 0 of 3, unchanged |
| Foreground `press_key down` on Finder, TextEdit in front (no field) | TextEdit front again, 3 of 3 (1.15-1.17 s) | same, 3 of 3 (1.17-1.20 s) |
| File > Get Info on Finder, TextEdit in front (no field) | TextEdit front again, 3 of 3 (0.37-0.48 s) | same, 3 of 3 (0.39-0.40 s) |
| Foreground click on a Finder item, TextEdit in front | TextEdit front again, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Foreground `press_key right` on TextEdit, Finder in front | Finder front again, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Foreground `press_key x` on TextEdit's text area by `element_token`, Finder in front | typed, Finder front again, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |

Clip (29 s): main first, then this branch, same layout (Finder left, the MCP calls top right, `ls` of the folder bottom right). Finder is in front. On main the final foreground Return is refused ("exact target window did not become focused") and the folder keeps `draft.txt`; on this branch it is delivered and the folder shows `final.txt`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a09bf87-b977-47b6-9700-3b158fb55a63

## Compatibility and risk

- Scope: foreground HID delivery (`with_foreground_hid_activation`) when the target app reports no focused window. The fallback needs a focused `AXTextField` whose own WindowServer window is a child of exactly the requested window; anything else (another window's child, a field in the window itself, an unreadable role, a failed parent lookup) keeps today's behavior.
- Not Finder-specific: any app whose inline editor has this shape benefits; the proof is structural.
- Cost: one focused-element read and one WindowServer query, only when the app reports no focused window.
- Rollback: revert the commit.

## Validation

- Unit tests (`ax/bindings.rs`): a focused text field in a child window of the target is an inline editor; a field in the window itself, a button in the child, a field in another window's child, an unrelated window, an unknown window, an unreadable role and a failed parent lookup are not.
- Checks: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (457 passed, 6 ignored, run in the VM), `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test contract_parity`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` (up to date), `scripts/check-no-em-dash.sh`, `git diff --check`; no clippy warnings in the touched files.
- Known gaps: no AppKit harness e2e (no fixture opens a child-window editor). `get_window_state` still does not list Finder's rename field (it hangs off the application element), so `set_value` on it is not reachable; typing works.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. (Not applicable: releasing `fix`.)

title: ci(release): regenerate files that record the version on cua-sdk release PRs
body:
A cua-sdk Release Please PR bumps only the SDK's version files (\`VERSION\`, pyproject, \`__init__\`, \`package.json\` and its lock). Everything that copies the version kept the old one. After the release merged, main drifted and later PRs went red. It happened for both 0.3.0 (#4539) and 0.3.1 (#4591, #4593).

**What this adds**
- \`.github/workflows/release-sync-generated-files.yml\`, which runs on pushes to \`release-please--branches--main--components--*\`. Today only the cua-sdk job runs. The other components keep their existing sync step in \`release-please.yml\`.
- \`.github/scripts/sync_sdk_release_files.py\`, which runs the commands the drift checks print:
  - \`runner.ts --library\` for every generator that records the SDK version (cua-sdk, cua-sdk-python, cua-sdk-ts, cua-rust, cua-cli, fleet, sandbox);
  - the two hand-written facts that \`test_fleet_docs_version_facts\` checks;
  - \`uv lock --upgrade-package cua\` for each uv.lock whose \`cua\` is the checkout (editable or directory source);
  - \`npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts\` for each package-lock.json that links \`libs/cua/typescript\`. The SDK's own lock is skipped because Release Please bumps it.
  - Nothing else is upgraded. \`--list\` shows the selection: 6 uv locks and 3 npm locks.
- It commits only if something changed and pushes fast-forward with the release GitHub App (\`RELEASE_APP_ID\` / \`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY\`), so the PR's checks re-run.
- A push of the job's own commit is skipped. A run is cancelled when Release Please pushes again.
- The regeneration runs from a checkout with \`persist-credentials: false\`, with no lifecycle scripts. The App token is minted only after the regeneration, for the push.
- Setup mirrors the Check Docs rows for these generators: protoc, Rust 1.97.1, the rustdoc nightly, uv and the docs and TS SDK installs.

**Verified**
- Simulated a 0.3.2 release branch locally by bumping the files Release Please bumps, then ran the script. The diff was 143 files, all of them version-only.
- After that: all 7 generators pass \`--check\`, \`test_fleet_docs_version_facts\` passes, and every uv lock passes \`uv lock --check\`.
- New tests in \`.github/scripts/tests/test_sync_sdk_release_files.py\` (9 tests, passing) cover lock selection, idempotent fact rewriting, loud failure when a fact is missing, the trigger, the loop guard, the token ordering and commit-only-on-change.
- actionlint is clean, both as CI runs it and with shellcheck on for the new file.

Not merged here: this is a workflow change, so a maintainer merges it.

title: fix(cua-driver): return from a dom_event click when its handler opens a dialog
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on a driver-owned isolated browser, no `browser_click` route could activate an element whose handler opens a page-owned JavaScript dialog. `trusted` refuses by design. `dom_event` dispatched `this.click()` through `Runtime.callFunctionOn` and awaited the reply, but `confirm()` blocks the JS frame that call is waiting on, so the click sat through the 20 s call timeout. The blocked frame then also wedged the follow-up `browser_dialog`, whose own `Page.enable` timed out, so the dialog was unreachable rather than merely unresolved.
- What changed: before a `dom_event` click goes out, Page events are enabled on the tab session and the dialog session is registered, the same way `browser_dialog` does it. The click is then raced against the `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` event. When a dialog opens, the call returns at once with `status: "ok"`, `effect: "unverifiable"`, and a `dialog` block (`present`, `kind`, `dialog_id`) whose id `browser_dialog` accepts directly; the summary names the id as well. The reply to the click, which only arrives once the dialog is resolved, is dropped harmlessly. A `browser_click` sent while a dialog is already open is refused with `browser_action_unavailable` before any frame revalidation, so it no longer waits out `Page.getFrameTree` against the blocked renderer. A quiet click returns `dialog: {present: false}` and is otherwise unchanged.

## Related work

Fixes #3982

RFC: not required. No new tool, parameter, or refusal code. The dialog block is an addition to the existing `browser_click` payload, and the `ActionResult` envelope is unchanged (its summary carries the dialog id).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: shared CDP code in `cua-driver-core`, same on macOS, Linux, and Windows. `Page.enable` is already in the reviewed existing-profile command set. A `dom_event` click now sends one `Page.enable` on first use per tab; later calls see the registered session and skip it.
- Risk and rollback: if `Page.enable` fails, the click proceeds exactly as before. The race polls dialog state every 25 ms and otherwise waits for the reply as today, so a click that opens no dialog has the same timing. Revert the two fix commits to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --locked` (three new mock-CDP cases in `v2_tests.rs`: a click whose reply never arrives but whose dialog event does, a quiet click, and a click while a dialog is open; the mock gained a reply mode that emits events and never answers), `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test --locked`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Manual or platform evidence: macOS 26, Apple Silicon, Google Chrome launched by `browser_prepare` (`allow_launch: true`, `isolated_new`) through `cua-driver mcp --direct` built from `9f1b7bd01`, against the two-button fixture from the report (a quiet button and one whose handler calls `confirm('Delete?')` and writes the outcome into the page):

  | Step | Before (report, 0.28.2) | After |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | quiet button, dom_event | ok, 1439 ms | ok, 64 ms, page shows "quiet clicked" |
  | confirm button, trusted | refused | refused `browser_input_trust_unavailable` (unchanged) |
  | confirm button, dom_event | timeout after 21268 ms | ok in 61 ms, summary names `dialog-1`, `dialog.present: true` |
  | second dom_event click while open | n/a | refused `browser_action_unavailable` in 98 ms |
  | `browser_dialog inspect` | Page.enable timed out | "confirm dialog is open", 35 ms |
  | `browser_dialog accept dialog-1` | unreachable | accepted; page shows "confirm accepted" |
  | click again, then `dismiss dialog-2` | unreachable | dismissed; page shows "confirm dismissed" |

title: fix(cua-driver): say when a refused Catalyst menu item leaves its menu open
body:
## Summary

This PR was narrowed to the refusal note only; the structural proof that admits these items in the background follows as a separate PR once this one lands, and that one will close #4619.

- Problem this solves: in a Mac Catalyst app, a background `click` on a pop-up menu item is refused `element_outside_target_window` with the advice to take a fresh `get_window_state` snapshot, while the menu stays open. Following that advice is refused again, and the next background click on the window then only closes the menu while reporting success. The refusal does not say that the menu is still open, or that the foreground route (which picks the item) exists.
- What changed: when the refused element is an `AXMenuItem` whose `AXMenu` has no readable `AXParent` (the shape of a Catalyst pop-up's menu, which is its own WindowServer window and names no window) and a menu window of the app (WindowServer layer 101, the helper from #4484) is on screen, the refusal now says so and recommends `delivery_mode: "foreground"`, in the reason text and in `escalation.recommended`:

  ```
  click: Background input refused (element_outside_target_window): the addressed element could not be proven to belong to window <id>; take a fresh get_window_state snapshot and re-address it. It is an item of a menu that names no window, and a menu of this app is still on screen; click this item with delivery_mode "foreground" to pick it
  ```

  Admission is unchanged: every action that was refused is still refused.

## Related work

Refs #4619. Part (b), the structural proof that admits these items for semantic AX actions, builds on this. Related: #3792 / #3793 (menu bar rows), #4507 (sheets), #4484.

RFC: not required (one sentence appended to an existing refusal and an existing `escalation.recommended` value).

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. Launch a Catalyst app with a `UIButton` pop-up (`showsMenuAsPrimaryAction`; items Never, Daily, Weekly, Monthly; Daily chosen) and a Save button, in the background. `list_windows` gives `<pid>` and `<window_id>`.
2. `get_window_state` on that window, then `click` the pop-up by its token. A layer-101 window of the app appears.
3. `get_window_state` again, then `click` the "Weekly" `AXMenuItem` by its token.
4. On main: refused `element_outside_target_window`, `escalation.recommended: "get_window_state"`, nothing about the open menu; a fresh snapshot and retry is refused the same way. On this branch: the same refusal with the sentence above and `escalation.recommended: "foreground"`. `click` on the same token with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` picks Weekly (unchanged, works on main too).

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM, Apple Silicon, the lab's CatalystProfile app relaunched clean each run, one MCP connection per run. App state read outside cua-driver (the app's own state file, WindowServer's window list). 3 runs per row on each build.

| Case | main b0a634813 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Background click pop-up, then background click "Weekly" | refused, recommends `get_window_state`, menu left open, 3 of 3; retry refused the same way | refused, **says the menu is open and recommends `foreground`**, 3 of 3 (retry likewise); app state unchanged (Daily) |
| Then background click Save | "Performed AXPress", nothing saved (it only closed the menu), 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 (admission unchanged) |
| Menu opened outside cua, background click "Weekly" | refused, no note, 3 of 3 | refused with the note, 3 of 3 |
| `scroll` by the item's token (a pointer route) while its menu is open | refused, no note, 3 of 3 | refused with the note, 3 of 3 |
| Following the note: `click` "Weekly" with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` | picks Weekly (Oct 4 main f83bd7a5c, 3 of 3; unchanged code path) | picks Weekly, menu closed, 3 of 3 |
| Control: AppKit pop-up in TextEdit's Save sheet, click it, click "Unicode (UTF-16)" | picked, 3 of 3 | picked, 3 of 3 |
| Control: TextEdit menu bar row by token (#3792) | refused, no note, no menu left, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Control: element token of one TextEdit window clicked with the other window's id | refused `conflicting_element_target`, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Control: `invoke_menu ["File","Nope"]` (#4484) | refused, no menu left, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |

Clip (30 s): main first, then this branch, same layout (CatalystProfile left, the MCP calls right). On main the background click on "Weekly" is refused with only the fresh-snapshot advice, a retry is refused the same way, and the menu stays open. On this branch the refusal says the menu is still open and recommends foreground; following it picks Weekly.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/93acb948-3dad-4c38-bd06-88a141299233

## Compatibility and risk

- Scope: only refusals with code `element_outside_target_window` for an `AXMenuItem` whose `AXMenu` has no readable parent, while a layer-101 window of the same pid is on screen. Other refusals are unchanged.
- The recommended route is the existing foreground element path, which is not exact-target gated; the note does not prove the item belongs to the window, it states what is on screen.
- Rollback: revert the commit.

## Validation

- Unit test `only_items_of_a_menu_with_no_parent_qualify` (`ax/exact_target.rs`): the measured Catalyst shape qualifies; an AppKit pop-up's menu (parent is the button), a menu under the application, the menu itself, a non-item and an unreadable role do not.
- Checks: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (481 passed, 6 ignored, run in the VM), `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test contract_parity`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` (up to date), `scripts/check-no-em-dash.sh`, `git diff --check`; no clippy warnings in the touched files.

title: Daemon spawns agent harness on host instead of in sandbox (ENOENT on /home/cua/.cua/tools)
body:
## Bug

`cua agent tell` (daemon mode) fails to start any harness with:

```
[error] could not start the agent: spawn /home/cua/.cua/tools/pi/0.87.1/node_modules/pi-acp/dist/index.js ENOENT
```

## Root cause

The daemon installs harness tools correctly **inside the sandbox** at `/home/cua/.cua/tools/` (verified: files exist, are executable, and run manually via `cua do shell`).

But when spawning the agent, the daemon uses Node `child_process.spawn()` with the **sandbox-internal path** on the **host**. The Mac host has no `/home/cua/` (`/home` is a symlink to the read-only system volume), so spawn fails with ENOENT.

The daemon process runs as the Mac user with `HOME=/Users/rook`, yet constructs the hardcoded sandbox path `/home/cua/.cua/tools` instead of either:
1. Spawning via the sandbox exec API (like `--embedded` mode does), or
2. Using a host-accessible tools path

## Workaround

`cua agent run --embedded` works correctly — the harness spawns, connects to the model, and uses sandbox MCP tools. Only daemon-mode (`tell` / persistent agents) is broken.

## Repro

1. `cua agent create combo --harness pi --in local:chrome-space --model <model> --base-url <url>`
2. `cua agent tell combo "test"`
3. Observe ENOENT in `cua agent logs`

## Environment

- cua 0.3.1 (CLI), cua-spacesd 0.5.0 (daemon)
- Mac host (arm64), Linux sandbox (gVisor, ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04)
- Happens with pi and opencode harnesses

title: [Bug]: set_window_frame and invoke_menu can't find an off-Space window that get_window_state resolves
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `get_window_state` resolves an AppKit window on another Space through the off-Space probe from #4068 and #4085, but `set_window_frame` and `invoke_menu` can't find that same window. They look it up with `copy_ax_windows`, which has nothing for an app whose windows are all off the current Space.

### Reproduction

1. Open a TextEdit document on a desktop Space, then switch to another Space (here a fullscreen app), so TextEdit has no window on the current Space.
2. `get_window_state` on the TextEdit window.
3. `set_window_frame` on it, same size, moved 40 pt.
4. `invoke_menu` on it with `["Edit", "Select All"]`.

### Expected behavior

`set_window_frame` and `invoke_menu` act on the window `get_window_state` just resolved, or refuse with an off-Space reason.

### Actual behavior

```text
list_windows:     window 34189, space_ids [6], on_current_space false (current Space 1239)
get_window_state: exact_window matched, 169 elements, AXWindow frame 656x422 at 218,84
set_window_frame: exit 1, "set_window_frame: window_id 34189 belongs to pid 34255 in WindowServer but has no matching AXWindow"
invoke_menu:      refused, menu_path_unavailable, "invoke_menu: target accessibility window is unavailable"
```

With the window on the current Space, both tools find it. (Stage Manager is on here, so `set_window_frame` then reported `suspected_noop` for a window in the strip; that part is separate.)

### Environment

Cua Driver 0.33.3 release app, called through `cua-driver call`. macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple silicon, Stage Manager on. TextEdit.

### Evidence

`get_window_state` gets the window through `copy_ax_windows_including`, which adds the probe:
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/2b3e4e548c6d27f918f5367f84c094151aa10c8f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs#L346

`set_window_frame` and `invoke_menu` use `copy_ax_windows`:
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/2b3e4e548c6d27f918f5367f84c094151aa10c8f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/set_window_frame.rs#L208
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/2b3e4e548c6d27f918f5367f84c094151aa10c8f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/invoke_menu.rs#L319

### Workaround and additional context

Bring the window onto the current Space first. Refs #3458.

Not the helper-window case from #4525: #4534 drops AX-less helper windows from `list_windows` and keeps windows on another Space. This one is titled, sits on Space 6 and `get_window_state` resolves it with 169 elements.

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): release a background Command chord's base key without Command
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, one background `hotkey` with Command to a Mac Catalyst app fires the app's key command over and over. A `UIKeyCommand` for cmd+shift+[ (the kind Messages uses to switch conversations) fired about 125 times in 3 s from one call, and keeps firing until some other key event reaches the app. An event tap on the app sees exactly one key-down and one key-up, so the driver sends the chord once; the problem is the key-up. It carries the Command flag, the app drops it, and UIKit treats the key as still held.
- What changed: the background PID-routed key press (`keyboard::press_key`, used by background `hotkey` and `press_key`) now sends its key-up without Command. The key-down is unchanged and keeps every modifier, so menus and key commands still match it. Other modifiers (Shift, Option, Control, fn) stay on both halves. The foreground menu-shortcut helpers (`hotkey_no_auth`, `press_key_no_auth`) and the global HID paths are not touched. The pair of events is built by a small `pid_key_press` function so the sequence is unit-tested.

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. Build a tiny Catalyst probe whose window shows how often its cmd+shift+[ key command fired (source and build command below), and open it.
2. Bring another app to the front (Finder), so the probe is in the background.
3. `list_windows` gives the probe's `<pid>` and `<window_id>`. Send one background chord:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "keys": ["cmd", "shift", "["]}
   ```
4. Wait 3 s and read the probe's label (on screen, or the `counts` element's value in `get_window_state`).

On main, the call returns success and the label reads `fired=125 began=1 ended=0`, still climbing. On this branch it reads `fired=1 began=1 ended=1`.

<details><summary>Probe source (main.swift) and build</summary>

```swift
import UIKit

final class ProbeController: UIViewController {
    var fired = 0, began = 0, ended = 0
    let label = UILabel()
    override func viewDidLoad() {
        super.viewDidLoad()
        view.backgroundColor = .systemBackground
        label.accessibilityIdentifier = "counts"
        label.frame = CGRect(x: 20, y: 40, width: 600, height: 80)
        view.addSubview(label)
        render()
    }
    override var canBecomeFirstResponder: Bool { true }
    override func viewDidAppear(_ animated: Bool) { super.viewDidAppear(animated); becomeFirstResponder() }
    override var keyCommands: [UIKeyCommand]? {
        let command = UIKeyCommand(input: "[", modifierFlags: [.command, .shift], action: #selector(onCommand))
        command.wantsPriorityOverSystemBehavior = true
        return [command]
    }
    @objc func onCommand() { fired += 1; render() }
    override func pressesBegan(_ presses: Set<UIPress>, with event: UIPressesEvent?) {
        if presses.contains(where: { $0.key?.keyCode == .keyboardOpenBracket }) { began += 1; render() }
        super.pressesBegan(presses, with: event)
    }
    override func pressesEnded(_ presses: Set<UIPress>, with event: UIPressesEvent?) {
        if presses.contains(where: { $0.key?.keyCode == .keyboardOpenBracket }) { ended += 1; render() }
        super.pressesEnded(presses, with: event)
    }
    func render() { label.text = "fired=\(fired) began=\(began) ended=\(ended)"; label.accessibilityValue = label.text }
}

final class AppDelegate: UIResponder, UIApplicationDelegate {
    var window: UIWindow?
    func application(_ application: UIApplication,
                     didFinishLaunchingWithOptions options: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any]?) -> Bool {
        window = UIWindow(frame: CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 640, height: 240))
        window?.rootViewController = ProbeController()
        window?.makeKeyAndVisible()
        return true
    }
}

UIApplicationMain(CommandLine.argc, CommandLine.unsafeArgv, nil, NSStringFromClass(AppDelegate.self))
```

```sh
APP=~/CatalystKeys.app; SDK=$(xcrun --show-sdk-path); mkdir -p $APP/Contents/MacOS
swiftc -O -target "$(uname -m)-apple-ios17.0-macabi" -sdk "$SDK" \
  -F "$SDK/System/iOSSupport/System/Library/Frameworks" -L "$SDK/System/iOSSupport/usr/lib/swift" \
  -Xlinker -rpath -Xlinker /System/iOSSupport/usr/lib/swift main.swift -o $APP/Contents/MacOS/CatalystKeys
cat > $APP/Contents/Info.plist <<'PLIST'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
<key>CFBundleIdentifier</key><string>dev.example.catalystkeys</string>
<key>CFBundleExecutable</key><string>CatalystKeys</string>
<key>CFBundlePackageType</key><string>APPL</string>
<key>CFBundleSupportedPlatforms</key><array><string>MacOSX</string></array>
<key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key><string>14.0</string>
<key>UIDeviceFamily</key><array><integer>2</integer></array>
</dict></plist>
PLIST
codesign -s - -f $APP && open $APP
```
</details>

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM (Apple Silicon). Probe relaunched for every run, Finder or Terminal frontmost, one `hotkey` call per run. Counts are the probe's own; key events come from a listen-only event tap on the probe's process (`CGEvent.tapCreateForPid`).

| Case | main b0a634813 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Background cmd+shift+[ to the probe: key command firings in 3 s | **125-126**, `began 1 ended 0`, 3 of 3 | **1**, `began 1 ended 1`, 3 of 3 |
| Key events the probe received | 1 key-down, 1 key-up with flags cmd+shift | 1 key-down, 1 key-up with flags shift |
| Foreground cmd+shift+[ (`delivery_mode: "foreground"`, control, path unchanged) | 125-126, key-up cmd+shift, 3 of 3 | 124-125, key-up cmd+shift, 3 of 3 (unchanged; see gaps) |
| Background cmd+shift+right into a TextEdit note (control) | selects to the line end (11 chars), 3 of 3 | selects to the line end (11 chars), 3 of 3 |

Clip (27 s): main first, then this branch, same layout. Left: a variant of the probe that shows every firing (a big counter that flashes on each one, plus a log row per firing). Right: the MCP call and the event tap. On main the counter and log run away from one chord (114 rows and still climbing 10 s later); on this branch they stop at 1. The focus moves to the runaway versus the single firing and to the key-up flags (cmd+shift versus shift), ending on a side-by-side frame.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bad503c2-7722-421d-ada0-25e2744c7f04

## Related work

No existing issue. Refs none.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. No schema, contract or binding change; only the flags on one synthesized event.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS background `hotkey` and `press_key` with Command. The key-down is identical; only the key-up loses Command. Linux and Windows are untouched.
- Risk and rollback: a background consumer that reads Command from the key-up rather than the key-down would see it missing. AppKit text handling (the TextEdit control) and UIKit key commands act on the key-down. Rollback is reverting the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - Unit test `pid_key_press_releases_the_base_key_without_command` (`keyboard.rs`): cmd+shift releases with shift only; all four modifiers release without Command; a chord without Command keeps its flags on both halves.
  - `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (481 passed, 6 ignored, run in the VM), `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test contract_parity`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` (up to date), `scripts/check-no-em-dash.sh`, `git diff --check`.
- Manual or platform evidence: the table and clip above.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - The foreground menu-shortcut rung (`hotkey` with `delivery_mode: "foreground"`, `hotkey_no_auth`) has the same symptom on Catalyst apps (125 firings on both builds). It is left as it is here: that path exists so AppKit menu key equivalents dispatch, and changing its key-up needs its own check across AppKit menus. I can follow up separately.
  - No harness e2e row: the AppKit harness fixture has no Catalyst key command; the probe above is the oracle.

title: fix(cua-driver): focus the exact sibling window for macOS foreground input
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS a foreground click into a Finder window is refused whenever another Finder window is key and Finder is in front. `click` with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` and the target's `window_id` returns `isError: true`, `click failed: foreground HID delivery to window <id> was not possible: exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery`, and nothing happens. Foreground HID delivery asks SkyLight to make the exact window key (`make_exact_window_key`) and then requires AX to report it focused; in that state Finder ignores those key-window records and keeps its current key window, so the check fails every time. The same refusal applies to every foreground input that goes through this helper (double and right clicks, drags, focused-field keys).
- What changed: when the records alone did not focus the window, `with_foreground_hid_activation` now runs the exact AX window raise that `bring_to_front` already uses (`raise_exact_ax_window`: AXRaise, AXMain and AXFocused on that one window, never the app's other windows) and waits for focus once more before refusing. The focus proof is unchanged: input is still only posted after AX reports the exact window focused. The driver's own windows keep today's refusal (AppKit orders windows on the main thread only). The helper stays where it is; it becomes `pub(crate)`, and so does the `bring_to_front` module. Only the would-refuse path changes; when the records work, nothing extra runs.

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. Open two Finder windows side by side, the second one key, and keep Finder in front:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p ~/r2click ~/r2clickfront && touch ~/r2click/a.txt ~/r2click/b.txt ~/r2clickfront/c.txt
   open ~/r2click && sleep 1 && open ~/r2clickfront
   ```
   (Move r2clickfront so it does not cover r2click; `set_window_frame` works.)
2. `list_windows` gives Finder's `<pid>` and r2click's `<window_id>`. `get_window_state` on r2click (with its screenshot) gives a.txt's frame; take its centre `x,y` in screenshot pixels.
3. Click it in the foreground:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "x": <x>, "y": <y>, "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   ```

On main step 3 returns the refusal above, r2clickfront stays key and nothing is selected in r2click. On this branch it returns `<check mark> Posted click at screen-point ... (foreground: exact window activated, ...)`, r2click becomes key and a.txt is selected.

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM (Apple Silicon). Key window and selection read by a separate AX probe (`AXFocusedWindow`, `AXSelected`); 3 runs per row on each build.

| Case | main b0a634813 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Finder in front, r2clickfront key, foreground click a.txt in r2click (windows apart) | **refused**, 3 of 3 (1.88-1.91 s); key stays r2clickfront; nothing selected | **posted**, 3 of 3 (2.06-2.09 s); key r2click; a.txt selected |
| Same, r2clickfront overlapping r2click | **refused**, 3 of 3 | **posted**, 3 of 3; a.txt selected |
| Control: TextEdit in front, two Finder windows | posted, a.txt selected, 3 of 3 (1.20-1.26 s) | same, 3 of 3 (1.22-1.26 s) |
| Control: one Finder window behind TextEdit | posted, a.txt selected, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Control: background click, two Finder windows | AX press via hit-test, key unchanged, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Control (#4551 case): TextEdit Open panel with its Go to Folder sheet focused, foreground Return aimed at the Open window | refused, sheet stays, 3 of 3 | refused, sheet stays, 3 of 3 |
| Same panel and sheet, foreground key "z" aimed at the note.txt window | refused, 3 of 3 | delivered to note.txt (`zx`), sheet stays open, 3 of 3 |

The last row is the one behavior change outside Finder: a foreground key aimed at a sibling document while another window of the app holds focus now reaches the requested window, as it does when the key-window records work.

Clip (26 s): main first, then this branch, same layout (both Finder windows left, the MCP calls right), with the focus moving to the result and on the key window and selection, ending on a side-by-side frame.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e0e1998-67f3-4b96-9564-0803377c4e3c

## Related work

No existing issue or PR covers the refusal. Related: #3574 (open issue, foreground `type_text` reaching a sibling window, a different helper that this does not touch), #3923 (open, adds the focused window's id to this refusal's text; partly superseded by #4821, which now names the window holding focus in the refusal), #4821 (merged: retries the activation once before this fallback; on its own that retry does not focus the Finder window in the rows above, so main still refuses), #3863 (draft, exact key window for foreground shortcuts on the menu path).

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. No schema, contract, or result text change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS foreground input through `with_foreground_hid_activation` (window-scoped foreground `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `drag`, and focused-field `press_key`, `hotkey`, `type_text`). Calls that were refused because the window never became focused can now succeed when an AX raise focuses it.
- Risk and rollback: on that path the target window is also raised in z-order (AXRaise), as `bring_to_front` does. A call that still cannot focus the window is refused as before, about 0.4 s later (one more focus wait). Rollback is reverting the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: no new unit test (the change is one boolean condition calling an existing helper; the behavior is covered by the VM rows above). `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (480 passed, 6 ignored, run in the VM), `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test contract_parity`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` (up to date), `scripts/check-no-em-dash.sh`, `git diff --check`.
- Manual or platform evidence: the table and clip above.
- Known gaps or CI still required: Finder and TextEdit only; `with_foreground_assist` (the foreground rung for scroll and some `type_text` paths, which proceeds without the focus proof) is unchanged; no harness e2e row.

title: fix(spaces-macos): run the app's daemon as its launchd agent so it keeps Local Network access
body:
A user reported that after quitting Cua Spaces while the daemon kept running, creating a Space failed with "No route to host": the daemon had lost Local Network access to the macOS VMs on vmnet (192.168.64.x).

## Cause

The app started its daemon as a child process: `DaemonSupervisor.start` runs `cua daemon start` with `Process`, which spawns the daemon with `Command::spawn` (`libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/lib.rs`, `daemon_start`). macOS attributes a child's Local Network access to its responsible process, which for the daemon was the app process. On this Mac, `responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid` on the installed daemon returns the app's pid. Once the app quits, the daemon's access no longer comes from a running app.

## Fix

The daemon now runs as the app's launchd agent, which Apple documents as the way to tie a helper to the app's Local Network permission whether or not the app runs ([TN3179](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3179-understanding-local-network-privacy)).

- `Support/com.trycua.spaces.daemon.plist` is copied to `Contents/Library/LaunchAgents/`. It runs `Contents/MacOS/cua daemon start --foreground --loopback 127.0.0.1:0` and is set to `RunAtLoad false` and `KeepAlive false`, so it starts only when asked and `cua daemon stop` keeps it stopped.
- `DaemonSupervisor` registers the agent with `SMAppService.agent(plistName:)` and passes its label to `cua daemon start` in `CUA_DAEMON_LAUNCHD_LABEL`.
- With that label set, `cua daemon start` uses `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<uid>/<label>` and waits for the job's pid in the discovery file. It no longer spawns the daemon itself (`cua-cli/src/daemon_launchd.rs`).
- `cua daemon start` started by something other than the app also uses the agent when it is loaded. That covers a terminal, an MCP server, and the relay host's `cua-spacesd` LaunchAgent. The start must use default arguments and this user's own home (no `CUA_HOME`, and `HOME` is the account's), and the `cua` must not be inside another app's bundle. Before, such a daemon got its access from whoever started it. A LaunchAgent is responsible for itself and has no grant, so its daemon got "No route to host".
- In these cases the daemon is still spawned as a child, as before:
  - the agent is missing, or the user turned it off in Login Items (`requiresApproval`);
  - registering it fails, or `launchctl` fails;
  - the start uses `--socket`, `--state-dir` or a different `--loopback`;
  - another executable runs the daemon;
  - the app runs with its own `HOME` or `CUA_*` settings (tests, development runs).

  The spawned daemon does not inherit the label, so a `cua daemon start` inside it cannot restart the agent's job.

The first registration shows macOS's "Background item added" notice for Cua Spaces.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p cua-cli --lib daemon_launchd`: tests for when the label is used, parsing the `launchctl print` pid, and the launchd target. `cargo clippy -p cua-cli --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
- `apps/cua-spaces-macos/scripts/test.sh --filter DaemonSupervisorTests`: 9 tests pass. The new ones cover registering the agent, the fallbacks (not registered, approval needed, missing, register fails, own `HOME`/`CUA_HOME`), the label reaching `cua daemon start`, and the bundled plist matching what the CLI would spawn.
- On a Mac, using a debug `cua-spaces-cli` with a throwaway `HOME`/`CUA_HOME` and a test launchd job:
  - With the label, `cua daemon start` started the daemon through launchd. Its parent pid was 1, it was its own responsible process, and the job showed `state = running` with the same pid.
  - A second start was a no-op, and `cua daemon stop` left the job not running.
  - An unknown label logged the reason and fell back to the spawn. With no label, the spawn ran as before.
- The installed app's `cua` (Developer ID, `com.trycua.cua`), spawned with responsibility disclaimed, could not reach a vmnet VM: its TCP connect failed. Spawned plainly from a shell, the same connect went through. So the binary has no Local Network grant of its own, and any daemon that answers for itself fails.
- A harness of small C programs measured how responsibility works on macOS 26.6 (Darwin 25.6):
  - A self-responsible ad hoc binary with no grant got exactly `connect: No route to host` to a vmnet VM. This is the user's error.
  - Children spawned by a granted parent kept access after the parent exited, so I could not reproduce the loss itself on this Mac.

Not verified here: that macOS applies the app's grant to the SMAppService agent. That needs a Developer ID-signed build. Ad hoc test jobs with `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` were not given another app's grant.

title: cua-driver (macOS): every window screenshot leaks its full-resolution pixel buffer in the serve process
body:
### Summary

On macOS, every window screenshot taken by `cua-driver serve --embedded` leaves one full-resolution pixel buffer allocated in the driver process. The buffers are never released: not after the call returns, not after `end_session`, and not after the MCP client disconnects. Memory grows by `width × height × 4` bytes per capture until the driver is restarted.

### Environment

- cua-driver-rs 0.28.3 (universal macOS binary from the GitHub release), embedded via `@trycua/cua-driver` 0.28.3 (`EmbeddedCuaDriverHost`, `permissionMode: Unrestricted`)
- macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple silicon, built-in 3024×1964 Retina display
- Client: `cua-driver mcp --embedded --socket …` over stdio

I have not run a newer release, but the macOS capture path (`crates/platform-macos/src/capture.rs`, `capture_window_from_plan` → `SCScreenshotManager::capture_image` → `rgba_data`) and the `screencapturekit = 8.0.1` pin look unchanged between `cua-driver-rs-v0.28.3` and `main`.

### Reproduction

1. Start an embedded host and connect an MCP client.
2. `start_session`, then call `get_window_state` with a screenshot (the default) on any window, N times.
3. Inspect the `serve` process: `vmmap <pid> | grep '^MALLOC_LARGE '`.
4. `end_session`, close the client, wait, and inspect again.

### Observed

Each capture adds one `MALLOC_LARGE` region the size of the window's backing pixels, in `DefaultPurgeableMallocZone`:

- A 1800×1130 pt window at 2× adds 32.1 MB per capture.
- A 920×436 pt Finder window at 2× adds about 6.8 MB per capture. Four captures: `MALLOC_LARGE` went from 875.2 MB to 903.8 MB (27 → 33 regions; a 22 MB region also came and went with unrelated calls).
- `get_window_state` with `include_screenshot: false` adds nothing.
- After `end_session` and after closing the client, the capture regions are all still there.

A driver that had served agent sessions for about an hour held 22 such regions (19 × 32.1 MB, 3 × 54.1 MB) and had a 1.1 GB physical footprint:

```
MALLOC ZONE                              VIRTUAL  RESIDENT  ALLOCATION COUNT  BYTES ALLOCATED
DefaultPurgeableMallocZone_0x10f270000    772.6M    772.6M                22           772.3M
DefaultMallocZone_0x106e54000             124.6M     84.6M             85647            54.2M
```

The returned image is downscaled (1567×984 here), but the retained buffers are native resolution.

### Expected

The native-resolution pixels are released once the PNG/JPEG for the response has been encoded, or at the latest when the session that captured them ends.

### Notes

The buffers sit in the purgeable malloc zone rather than the default zone, which suggests CoreGraphics-owned image data (the `CGImage` returned by `SCScreenshotManager`, or data copied from its provider) that is never released, rather than a Rust-side `Vec`. I have not traced it further than that, so the leak may be in the `screencapturekit` crate's bridge rather than in the driver itself.

title: fix(cua-driver): say how to recover from an unapproved browser profile
body:
## What

`browser_consent_required` refusals now say how to get past them.

- **`get_browser_state` on a person's own Chrome or Edge window.** The message used to say the profile "requires explicit existing-profile approval". It now names both routes:
  - `browser_prepare` with `strategy: existing_profile`, which needs the runtime grant;
  - `browser_prepare` with `allow_launch` and `profile: {mode: "isolated_new"}`, which needs no grant.
- **`browser_prepare` with `strategy: existing_profile` on a standard runtime without the grant.** The message now says that a running daemon cannot gain the grant and must be restarted.
- **Machine-readable recovery.** Both refusals now carry `detail.recovery`:
  - `grant_restart_command` is the platform's restart command with `--grant existing-profile`. It is `null` on embedded runtimes, because the host owns the launch there.
  - `isolated_alternative` holds the exact `browser_prepare` arguments for the isolated route.
- **Docs.** The browsers guide now shows the restart command. It also says what a person sees during existing-profile setup on each new session: the browser comes to the front, a setup tab opens, and Chrome asks "Allow remote debugging?". It names the two refusals to retry once when setup is interrupted.

The existing fields `reason`, `supported_strategies` and `next_action` are unchanged, so this is additive.

## Why

I reproduced this on macOS 26 with Chrome 154, using a throwaway `--user-data-dir` and the quickstart's default daemon. The first refusal an agent got didn't say that a restart was needed, or that an isolated profile needed no grant. With the grant, 2 of 5 attaches on 0.28.2 failed on a busy desktop:
- once with `browser_wrong_target_refused`, because the window lost focus before the setup URL was committed;
- once with `browser_reconnect_exhausted`.

On 0.33.4, 4 of 4 succeeded, taking about 6-7 s each. Each new session repeated the visible setup.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::`: 188 passed, including the new `existing_profile_recovery_names_the_grant_restart_and_the_isolated_route` and extended assertions in `existing_profile_requires_runtime_authorization` and `standalone_consumer_refuses_existing_profile_approval_without_preparing`.
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Live: I ran a debug `cua-driver serve` against the throwaway Chrome, and both refusals returned the new `detail.recovery`.

title: ci: sign Windows binaries without the signing action's dependency cache
body:
`azure/artifact-signing-action` v2.0.0 fails whenever it restores its own cached `ArtifactSigning` PowerShell module:

```
Cache hit for: ArtifactSigning-0.1.8
Invoke-ArtifactSigning: The term 'Invoke-ArtifactSigning' is not recognized as a name of a cmdlet
```

A first run (cache miss) installs the module, signs and saves the cache; any later run that restores it fails. cua-sdk 0.3.1, 0.4.0 and 0.4.1 each failed this way and only passed after the cache entry was deleted.

This sets `cache-dependencies: false` (an input the action already has) on all five uses: `cd-cua-sdk.yml`, `cd-cua-spaces.yml` (2), `cd-cua-spacesd.yml` and `cd-rust-cua-driver.yml`. Costs a module download per signing job, about a minute.

title: fix(cua-driver): sweep orphaned isolated_new browser profiles
body:
## Problem

`browser_prepare` with `profile.mode=isolated_new` creates `~/Library/Application Support/CuaDriver/BrowserProfiles/isolated-<uuid>` (Linux: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/cua-driver/browser-profiles`) and is meant to delete it when the session ends. The deletion only happens in `ManagedBrowser::drop`, i.e. in daemon memory. If the daemon is killed, crashes, is restarted or exits without dropping the engine before the session ends, nothing ever removes the directory. Anything the agent signed into stays on disk, unencrypted from the driver's point of view.

Found on a dogfooding Mac: three `isolated-*` profiles dated 16 Aug, 17 Aug and 8 Sep had survived (two with a stale Chrome `SingletonLock` pointing at a dead pid, which matches a daemon killed mid-session). They held cookies for sites the agents had visited.

## Fix

Before creating a new profile, `prepare_profile` now sweeps orphans (`sweep_orphaned_isolated_profiles`). A directory is removed only if all of these hold:

- the name starts with `isolated-`;
- it carries this driver's marker with `mode=isolated_new` (named profiles and unmarked directories are never touched);
- the marker is at least 1 hour old, so a profile another daemon just created is safe;
- Chrome's `SingletonLock` does not point at a live process.

Unix only (macOS and Linux). Windows has no `SingletonLock`, so it is left as before.

## Tests

- New unit test `sweep_removes_only_stale_unowned_isolated_new_profiles`: covers an orphan, a live-lock profile, a dead-lock profile, an `isolated_named` profile with an `isolated-` name, a normal named profile, an unmarked directory, and the age gate.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::prepare`: 21 passed. `cargo clippy` is clean for the changed file.

Not merging; for review.
