Refs #4947 for the separate Windows right-click modifier fix. That change is
absent from this PR.

title: feat(cua-driver): report is_password for Windows text-entry elements
body:
## What

Windows UI Automation exposes a password box as an ordinary `Edit` control with the `IsPassword` property set. `get_window_state` never read that property, so a caller had no way to tell a password field from a plain text field. macOS and Linux already convey it through the role (`securetextfield` / `passwordtext`).

This reads `UIA_IsPasswordPropertyId` in the node cache request and surfaces it:

- **Structured elements** carry `is_password`: `true` for a password field, `false` for an element that accepts text (`set_value` / `text` actions) and is not one, and absent when unknown or not applicable (non-text elements, the MSAA fallback). Buttons and menus stay unchanged, and a consumer can still tell "not a password field" from "unknown".
- **The Markdown row** (the default `tree_format`) marks a password field with `password`, for example `[1] Edit "Password" [id=pwBox password actions=[set_value]]`.
- **A password field's value is never echoed.** Providers are expected to blank `Value` for password fields, but UIA does not enforce it, so the value is dropped before it can reach `value`, the label fallback or the Markdown row.
- **`WindowElement`** gains an optional `is_password` field. The contract manifest and the UniFFI Python/TypeScript bindings are regenerated.
- The Windows `get_window_state` description mentions the field.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cua-contract-gen -- all --check`, `cua-driver-abi-header -- --check`
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-contract`, `-p cua-driver-sdk` (99 + 1 + 2 passed), `-p cua-driver-core --test contract_parity`
- `node scripts/generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` (Ubuntu 24.04 with the CI apt packages, Rust 1.97.1)
- Windows release build. `platform-windows` tests on Windows 11: 276 passed, 0 failed (new tests cover emission, the text-entry filter, the Markdown marker and value redaction).
- Live check on Windows 11 against a WinForms window with a plain `TextBox` and a `UseSystemPasswordChar` `TextBox`, read through `get_window_state` from a loopback MCP-over-HTTP client:
  - password box: `is_password: true`, Markdown `password`; plain box: `is_password: false`;
  - the password box's contents are absent from the response, while the plain box's value is present;
  - the released 0.34.1 binary reports the field absent on both boxes.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop worker and embedded processes launching Orca on GNOME
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on GNOME, the driver's private-worker and embedded daemon processes set `ScreenReaderEnabled` on the session's accessibility bus, and the desktop responds by launching the Orca screen reader. #2010 fixed this for `cua-driver serve` by checking the desktop name, but these processes start with a filtered environment that dropped the desktop name, so the check could not work. The same filter dropped every variable that turns the advertisement off.
- What changed: the filter now passes `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP`, `DESKTOP_SESSION`, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_DISABLE_A11Y_ADVERTISE`, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_A11Y_ADVERTISE_MODE`, and `NO_AT_BRIDGE` to worker and embedded processes. The accessibility module exports the names it reads, and a test checks each one against the filter. The worker and embedded-host tests now set `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1`, so their child processes stay off the developer's accessibility bus entirely; the opt-in desktop test keeps the listener and disables only the advertisement.

## Related work

Fixes #4963

This restores the behavior #2010 established and widens an internal environment allowlist by six names; SDK hosts gain the ability to pass those names as overrides.

Related: #2010, #2630, #2703 (closed; the same symptom for `serve` on GNOME, COSMIC, and Cinnamon). #2915 (open) questions whether advertising `ScreenReaderEnabled` should remain at all; this change is independent of that outcome.

Open pull requests #3490 and #4733 add other names to the same `matches!` list, so a trivial conflict is possible. #4903 (the fix for #4894) works in the same accessibility startup area but shares no file with this change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - Linux: worker and embedded processes on GNOME and COSMIC no longer claim a screen reader, and on Cinnamon no longer advertise at all, matching `cua-driver serve`. Hosts can now pass the three controls. A worker or embedded process whose parent has `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1` now skips accessibility setup, as `serve` does in that environment.
  - On desktops other than those three, behavior is unchanged: the default was and remains the full advertisement.
  - macOS and Windows: no effect. The names are not read there.
  - The allowlist is a trust boundary, so each addition matters: the six names carry a desktop name or an on/off choice, and none can redirect the process to another bus or load code. `AT_SPI_BUS_ADDRESS` is still dropped, and a test asserts it.
- Risk and rollback: low. Reverting the commit restores the previous filter.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (Ubuntu 26.04, x86_64, Rust 1.97.1):
  - Two new unit tests in `cua-driver-sdk/src/embedded.rs`: all six names reach the child environment, inherited or as host overrides; and every name in `platform_linux::a11y::ADVERTISE_ENVIRONMENT` passes the allowlist.
  - Mutation checks: removing `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `DESKTOP_SESSION`, `NO_AT_BRIDGE`, or `CUA_DRIVER_RS_A11Y_ADVERTISE_MODE` from the allowlist fails the new tests.
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver-sdk --locked`: exit 0; 4 test targets, 104 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver --locked`: exit 0; 28 test targets, 400 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.
  - `cargo test -p platform-linux --locked --lib a11y::`: 7 passed.
  - After the fixtures moved to `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1`: `cargo test -p cua-driver --locked --test private_worker_test --test embedded_host_sdk_mcp_test` passed (9 tests, 1 ignored). While it ran, every sampled worker and embedded process had `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1` and no connection to the AT-SPI socket.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- Manual or platform evidence (GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland, Orca 50.2, screen reader off beforehand):
  - Without the fix, on `main` at `e32127764`, one private-worker test and one embedded-host test, each started with all three values off: the child process had no `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`; `ScreenReaderEnabled` and the GNOME screen-reader setting became `true` 9 s and 11 s after the test started; `orca.service` began starting in that same second and stayed on after the test ended. These control runs were made after this PR was opened and are detailed on the issue.
  - With the fix, the same two tests, each run with the test's disable switch temporarily removed so the child had to rely on desktop detection: `ScreenReaderEnabled` and the GNOME setting stayed `false` throughout, and `orca.service` did not start. No sample of the child's environment lacked `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`.
  - With the fix, the two full crate runs above: the journal shows 10 `orca.service` starts for the day before the runs and 10 after. Before the fix, one full run of the crate started it three times.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - `private_worker_inherits_the_interactive_linux_display_scope` runs only with `CUA_REQUIRE_GUI=1`. I did not set it, so the separate environment that test now uses was compiled but not exercised.
  - The two full crate runs above were made before the fixtures moved from the disable switch to `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1`; afterward I reran only the two affected test binaries.
  - In the "with the fix" single-test runs, the process sampler matched by command-line pattern and also matched its own shell, which carries the desktop name. The statement about the child's environment therefore rests on no sample lacking the variable; the same sampler did show such samples on the unfixed code. I have not re-measured it with an exact process match.
  - COSMIC and Cinnamon were not tested; they rely on the same variable reaching the child.
  - macOS and Windows were not built locally.
  - The full `platform-linux` suite was not run locally; only its `a11y` tests. Parts of that suite need a display.
  - `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` does not pass on `main` for `platform-linux` on this toolchain (seven findings in `input/mod.rs`, `tools/impl_.rs`, and `wayland/`). None is in a file this PR touches, and clippy reports nothing for the changed files.
  - Tests that start a plain `serve` daemon still advertise by design, including `ScreenReaderEnabled` on desktops other than GNOME, COSMIC, and Cinnamon. This PR does not change that.
  - The desktop E2E matrix was not run; no input delivery or capture behavior changes.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. (Not applicable: this is a releasing `fix`.)

title: [Bug]: macOS: Chromium silently drops the background press_key path that 0.34.x describes as "Chromium-safe" — the unverifiable result carries no target-aware hint
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On stable 0.34.x, `press_key`'s description calls the default background path
"the auth-message path (Chromium-safe)" (`press_key.rs:187`, identical in
`cua-driver-rs-v0.34.0` and `cua-driver-rs-v0.34.1`). Yet on Chrome 155 /
macOS 26.6, a background `press_key "return"` aimed at Chrome's own omnibox
is silently dropped — no navigation, with a bare `effect:"unverifiable"`
result and no target-aware hint distinguishing this drop from the ordinary
no-delivery-oracle case. The ask: confirm the class, and either extend the
repository's existing unverifiable-advice pattern to `press_key`/`hotkey` on
targets that resolve to a Chromium-browser bundle, or rule that this belongs
in the #4009 ActionResult RFC.

### Reproduction

A self-contained script (attached, together with its two `srv/` pages) drives
an isolated Chrome instance — own `--user-data-dir`, no user data touched —
with two local pages whose titles (`REPRO-BEFORE` / `REPRO-AFTER`) serve as
navigation markers. Result route gloss: background → `synthetic_events`,
foreground → `global_input`, AX `type_text` → `accessibility`.

- **Phase A (cooperative case — Chrome frontmost throughout):** AX `type_text`
  fills the omnibox (`confirmed`); background `return` is refused with
  `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` — presumably because the transient
  "Sign In to Chrome?" bubble counts as a sibling keyboard destination (the
  bubble is visible in the Phase A screenshot and gone by Phase B, in step
  with the refusal; both runs refused identically); foreground + element
  `return` does not navigate.
- **Phase B (real-session case — Finder frontmost, asserted via `lsappinfo`
  immediately before the phase):** AX `type_text` still lands (`confirmed`)
  while Chrome is NOT frontmost; background `return` posts
  `effect:"unverifiable"` (route `synthetic_events`) and the page does not
  navigate — the silent drop; a foreground `return` without an element
  commits whatever the omnibox buffer holds (see the matrix and run-to-run
  notes); foreground + element then produces no further change.

Observed output (run 2; each printed verdict is derived only from the saved
raw JSON; the full capture ships inside the run's artifact directory):

```
driver: cua-driver 0.34.0 | chrome: Google Chrome 155.0.8059.39  | os: 26.6.2
target: pid=16861 window=55239 title='REPRO-BEFORE'
omnibox token: s00000672:3
a1_type: effect=confirmed route=accessibility
a2_return_bg: REFUSED same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity (effect=refused)
     title after A2: 'REPRO-BEFORE'
a3_return_fg_elem: effect=unverifiable route=global_input
     title after A3: 'REPRO-BEFORE'
-- reset done; title now: 'REPRO-BEFORE' (omnibox buffer may hold concatenated text: inserts append) --
-- Phase B precondition: frontmost bundle='com.apple.finder' (not Chrome) --
b1_type: effect=confirmed route=accessibility
b2_return_bg: effect=unverifiable route=synthetic_events
     title after B2: 'REPRO-BEFORE'
b3_return_fg: effect=unverifiable route=global_input
     title after B3: 'Error response'
b4_return_fg_elem: effect=unverifiable route=global_input
     title after B4: 'Error response'
```

Step → outcome matrix (run 2; screenshots attached):

| step | call | structured result | page outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | AX `type_text` (frontmost) | `confirmed`, `accessibility` | omnibox shows the target URL — the insert replaced the click-selected page URL (`a1_after_type.png`) |
| A2 | `press_key return` (background) | `refused`, `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity`, `escalation.recommended="accessibility"` | nothing posted (state-dependent; see Phase A note) |
| A3 | `press_key return` (foreground + element) | `unverifiable`, `global_input` | no navigation |
| B1 | AX `type_text` (Chrome NOT frontmost) | `confirmed`, `accessibility` | text visible in the omnibox while unfocused (`b1_after_ax_type_unfocused.png`); the insert appends to whatever the buffer holds |
| B2 | `press_key return` (background) | `unverifiable`, `synthetic_events` | **no navigation — silent drop** (`b2_after_bg_return.png`, title unchanged) |
| B3 | `press_key return` (foreground, no element) | `unverifiable`, `global_input` | commits whatever the buffer holds: here the stale concatenated URL `localhost:8123/repro-after.htmllocalhost:8123/repro-before.html` → 404 (`b3_after_fg_no_element.png`). The committed URL matched only part of the AX-visible buffer — B1's screenshot shows a third appended segment the commit dropped |
| B4 | `press_key return` (foreground + element) | `unverifiable`, `global_input` | produced no further change (already at the 404) |

Run-to-run: the script's final revision ran end-to-end twice (run 1, run 2;
the attached file differs from it only in header comments) with identical
effect/route/refusal-code results on every narrated step, yet different page
outcomes. In run 2 (quoted above) the reset `return` delivered nothing —
run 2's B1/B2 screenshots show the reset's insert still sitting uncommitted
in the buffer — and B3 then committed the two oldest of the buffer's three
concatenated segments → 404. In run 1, the refused A2 left the omnibox in
edit mode with its popup open (visible in run 1's post-A2 screenshot), and
the reset foreground + element `return` — a delivered key — committed the
popup's URL instead of the typed text (the page ended on `REPRO-AFTER`); B3
and B4 then delivered nothing. The reset Return's own result also differed
between the runs (`confirmed` in run 1, where it committed the wrong URL;
`unverifiable` in run 2, where it delivered nothing). None of these
deviations from intent is visible in the structured results. Across all 10 captured runs —
spanning every revision of the script, the final one attached (it produced
both runs) — the background Return never navigated, and the
foreground-without-element Return committed the stale buffer 6 times and
delivered nothing 4 times: the outcome tracks invisible omnibox state, while
the structured result reads `unverifiable` in every case.

### Expected behavior

Either (a) the background path actually reaches Chromium as its description
promises, or (b) when the target resolves to a Chromium-browser bundle
(`is_chromium_identity` already exists — note it matches Chromium-family
browsers, not Electron apps) and a background key result is `unverifiable`,
the result carries a target-aware hint in the same shape refusals already
use. A refused result carries `escalation.recommended` (e.g. the
`same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` refusal recommends `accessibility`); an
`unverifiable` Chromium background key could carry, say,
`escalation.recommended="foreground"` with a reason naming the
`chromium_background_drop_suspected` class — letting a caller recover in one
step instead of screenshot-diffing.

### Actual behavior

`effect:"unverifiable"` with route `synthetic_events` and no
target-class information; the dropped background Return is
indistinguishable from the no-delivery-oracle case, and the only way to
notice is page inspection.

### Environment

- cua-driver **0.34.0** (system daemon); **0.34.1 is equally affected** —
  `git diff cua-driver-rs-v0.34.0 cua-driver-rs-v0.34.1` over
  `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/press_key.rs`,
  `.../input/keyboard.rs`, `.../tools/hotkey.rs`, `.../tools/type_text.rs`
  is empty, and the "Chromium-safe" string is present in both releases.
- macOS 26.6.2 arm64; Google Chrome 155.0.8059.39 (isolated profile).
- Source references pinned at `9579e5616`; the transport
  (`post_keyboard_event` → `SLEventPostToPid`, `input/keyboard.rs:642`) is
  byte-identical across v0.34.0, v0.34.1, and `9579e5616`, so the class is
  expected to persist on main — happy to re-run the repro against a nightly
  build to confirm.

### Evidence

- Attached (run 2): per-call raw JSON, screenshots, and a `run_manifest.tsv`
  step log. The same artifacts exist for run 1 and for the earlier script
  revisions' runs (JSONs and screenshots; the manifest/transcript pairing
  starts with the previous revision) — available on request.
- `b1_after_ax_type_unfocused.png` (run 2) — AX-inserted text visible in the
  omnibox while Chrome is not frontmost: the AX/HID asymmetry that makes the
  composed "type, then press Return" workflow fail.
- `b3_after_fg_no_element.png` (run 2) — the committed concatenated URL and
  the resulting 404.

### Workaround and additional context

No workaround exists in the result itself (the drop leaves no signal to act
on): today a caller recovers only by re-calling with
`delivery_mode:"foreground"` or by inspecting the page. The ask is for the
result to carry that recovery. Relation to recent upstream work (all verified
at `9579e5616`):

- The repository already attaches advice to `unverifiable` results where the
  miss is class-provable: `type_text` attaches
  `escalation.recommended="foreground"` to unverifiable background inserts
  (`tools/type_text.rs:547-553`), and #4977's `move_cursor` ships the
  class-aware `BACKGROUND_HOVER_NOTE` on unverifiable hover results — a
  per-call-unprovable platform-class statement, the exact pattern proposed
  here. The gap is `press_key`/`hotkey`: neither attaches any hint to an
  `unverifiable` result (`press_key`'s tests assert this,
  `tools/press_key.rs:510-528`; `hotkey`'s `delivered_structured` likewise).
- Relation to #4982: removing that hint was right — it fired on results that
  already carried positive delivery evidence (an opened window); in
  #4649/#4982's own words, "Delivery is no evidence of a miss". The hint
  proposed here is different in the property that motivated removing #4982's
  hint: it fires only on results with **no** delivery evidence (no oracle
  fired), only when the target class is bundle-proven, and it names a drop
  class rather than asserting a miss. If even that is too strong, guidance
  toward the #4009 ActionResult RFC is welcome — happy to fold it there or
  implement it as a small diagnostics-only change with unit tests on the
  pure helpers.
- #4856 (main only, not in any stable release) already covers the AX side of
  this scenario: `is_chromium_identity` (`tools/type_text.rs:296`), the
  Chromium-native-field note (:768) and the `browser_field_needs_keystrokes`
  refusal (:786) — and upstream's own comment states the class flatly:
  "Return, background or foreground, does not submit it, and background
  keystrokes never reach the browser" (`tools/type_text.rs:291-293`). The
  real-world session that surfaced this report (a failed `type_text` into a
  Chromium field followed by an undelivered Return) ran 0.34.0, which
  predates #4856. What #4856 does not cover is the keyboard half: at main,
  `press_key`'s rewritten description no longer claims Chromium-safety, while
  `hotkey`'s still does (`tools/hotkey.rs:40`); and v0.34.0's own description
  paired the Chromium-safe claim with "remains effect:\"unverifiable\"
  without implying delivery failure or recommending foreground"
  (`tools/press_key.rs:195` @ v0.34.0) — the shipped behavior matches the
  second promise while contradicting the first, and the second promise is
  exactly what strands the caller.
- Prior art: #4243 (background clicks silently no-op on React controls in
  Chrome — the click analogue of this report), #4241 (the
  `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` refusal on Chrome), #3389 (Electron
  `type_text` background unverifiable — inverse sign: text lands but the
  result reports unverifiable), #2285 (trusted background Chromium clicks
  workstream), #4919 (background `type_text`/`press_key` dropped for iPhone
  Mirroring targets — same symptom, different class: a version regression,
  not a renderer drop), #4986/#4711 (browser tools already refuse this class
  on macOS — supporting direction), #4833 (the Linux compositor lane shows
  the same background-key/effect-oracle gap — cross-platform family), #4723
  (the ✅-on-`unverifiable` summary glyph — same result-honesty family),
  #3068 (foreground focus verification —
  not at issue here), #1753 (`type_text` focus lineage).

Related, out of scope for this issue: `type_text`'s confirmed result reports
only counts (`delivered_count` in the 0.34.0 payload; `requested_chars`/
`delivered_chars` on main) — never the resulting field value or its length,
so append-vs-replace concatenation is invisible without a screenshot. The
AXValue read-back evidently holds the value; reporting it (or its length)
would have surfaced both anomalies in this repro. That belongs with
#2883/#4009 rather than here.

Happy to implement the target-aware hint (or its #4009 variant) as a PR with
unit tests on the pure helpers, and to run the repro against a nightly build
on request.

**Artifacts** — attached on the fork branch [`issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop`](https://github.com/xronocode/cua/tree/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop) (evidence-only, no code changes):

- [`repro_chromium_background_key_drop.sh`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xronocode/cua/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop/repro_chromium_background_key_drop.sh) + [`srv/repro-before.html`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xronocode/cua/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop/srv/repro-before.html) / [`srv/repro-after.html`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xronocode/cua/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop/srv/repro-after.html)
- run 2: per-call raw JSONs, [`run_manifest.tsv`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xronocode/cua/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop/runs/v7mx/run_manifest.tsv), literal transcript [`run_output.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xronocode/cua/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop/runs/v7mx/run_output.txt)
- key screenshots: [`a1_after_type.png`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xronocode/cua/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop/runs/v7mx/a1_after_type.png), [`b2_after_bg_return.png`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xronocode/cua/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop/runs/v7mx/b2_after_bg_return.png), [`b4_final.png`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xronocode/cua/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop/runs/v7mx/b4_final.png), run 1's post-A2 popup state: [`VGF3/a2_after_return.png`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xronocode/cua/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop/runs/VGF3/a2_after_return.png)

AX-inserted text visible while Chrome is NOT frontmost (B1):

![b1 — AX text landed while unfocused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xronocode/cua/issue-evidence/chromium-key-drop/runs/v7mx/b1_after_ax_type_unfocused.png)

title: ci: restore Rust caches from main instead of saving per-PR
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: 680 of 756 `ci-cua-sdk` jobs checked last week rebuilt Rust from scratch and ran about twice as long, because each PR job saves its own 0.7-2.7 GB rust-cache entry and evicts main's within minutes.
- What changed: Rust caches save only from `main`, as the `ci-rust-*` and cua-driver workflows already do, so PRs restore a warm cache. PR-only workflows stop saving too; they rarely hit today. At a 60-90% hit rate that returns roughly 65k-104k job-minutes a week from `ci-cua-sdk` alone.

## Related work

Refs: N/A, no tracking issue.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): Not required, CI-only.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: None.
- Risk and rollback: Low. A PR that changes `Cargo.lock` builds cold until it merges; revert to undo.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: actionlint 1.7.12 (`-shellcheck= -pyflakes=`) is clean, and zizmor findings are unchanged.
- Manual or platform evidence: N/A.

title: fix(cua-driver): bound Windows semantic click provider calls
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: an element-token UIA click on a classic WinForms button that calls `ShowDialog` leaves the MCP response pending until the modal closes, even after the application handler has run.
- What changed: run the existing Invoke / Toggle / SelectionItem / ExpandCollapse sequence under the existing four-second UIA deadline and process-wide single-flight gate. The worker keeps its permit, retained element, and COM apartment until the provider returns. Cancellation checks guard subsequent provider calls. Timeout, busy, and unavailable outcomes stop before coordinate fallback; completed misses retain the existing fallback behavior.
- Timeout reports an unknown effect (`unverifiable`); busy reports that this click was not started (`refused`). Neither recommends replaying an uncertain activation.
- Compatibility with current main: retain the new focused-document UIA entry point, and supply a producer-owned no-replay hint so the shared recovery annotator cannot turn these deadline errors into foreground retry advice.
- The Windows regression now declares a typed case and links its continuous video, trajectory, and protocol log before scenario execution, including assertion/panic outcomes. A separate MCP session on the same daemon probes the intentionally blocked provider; the recording owner retains normal pre/post-action accessibility evidence without injecting recorder UIA walks into the deadline measurement.

## Related work

Fixes #5012. Scope and acceptance evidence were recorded in [the issue](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/5012#issuecomment-6128137903), following the maintainer's invitation.

Refs #3623 / #3671 for the existing point-based no-replay boundary. #3171 / #4885 concern evidence after successful semantic dispatch; this PR addresses the pending response and does not supersede that work.

RFC: not required for this bounded Windows bug fix. It reuses existing deadline, admission, error code, and ActionResult types, with no schema, permission, or cross-component contract changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows element-token semantic clicks now return a bounded error when the provider remains blocked. Foreground SendInput, pixel clicks, Chromium's coordinate-first route, right-clicks, multi-clicks, and normal completed-miss fallbacks retain their existing routing. Other platforms are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: COM calls cannot safely be cancelled once entered. A timed-out provider deliberately retains the shared UIA permit until it returns, so further UIA operations may report busy; Win32 read-only enumeration and explicit foreground modal dismissal remain usable. Revert this PR to restore the old waiting behavior. The test proves a modal operation may already have taken effect at timeout; it does not infer success or non-delivery from the error alone.

## Review and validation (2026-10-29)

Rebased onto latest main `df2af4f410aa66e898e9e758bb63afda1bb33c55`. Candidate: `8cdd68683af09808524631b0565dfda91c23ff7a`. The existing contributor commits and authorship are preserved; the previous merge commit is flattened and its no-replay recovery fix is explicitly retained.

Review covered all 12 changed files and the surrounding click routing, retained-element lifetime, COM cleanup, single-flight cancellation, recovery annotation, fixture, and recording integration:
- Resolved the click-route conflict while preserving main's minimized-snapshot coordinate validation and existing Chromium routing.
- Preserved main's focused-document UIA entry point and the producer-owned no-replay hint from the old merge resolution.
- Guarded pattern QueryInterface calls with the existing cancellation check, so a lookup returning after timeout does not enter another COM call.
- Added the modal fixture to the native runner's existing required-fixture preflight.
- Kept test scope bounded: only added public no-replay hint assertions to the existing modal scenario; no new test suite, matrix, product switch, dependency, or defensive framework.

Validation on Windows x64 with repository-pinned Rust 1.97.1; Cargo commands used `--release --locked`:
- Complete `platform-windows`, `cua-driver-core`, and `cua-driver-testkit` owners: **1,524 passed / 3 existing ignored / 0 failed**. Windows unit owner: 310 passed; core unit owner: 1,075 passed. One initial source-text invariant failed on CRLF checkout bytes; rerunning with its two source inputs restored to canonical Git LF bytes passed, with no committed source or assertion change.
- Complete `protocol_element_token_test`, `protocol_schema_test`, and `schema_consistency_test`: **8 passed**.
- E2E inventory and gate-path suites: **35 passed**.
- Changed Rust crate formatting, diff whitespace, and Windows runner PowerShell syntax passed.
- Rebuilt driver and reporter; complete recorded `semantic_click_deadline_windows_test` binary: **1 passed**. Modal response **4,006 ms**, `timeout/unverifiable`; blocked retry **1 ms**, `busy/refused`. Existing 6 s / 1 s limits retained. Public no-replay hints and observation-only next calls passed.
- Fixture journal: `opened=1, closed=1, normal=2, toggled=1, selected=1, expanded=1, fallback=1, mouse_down=0`. No duplicate activation; modal dismissal releases the permit and ordinary semantic/fallback paths recover.
- Finalized video, trajectory, and protocol evidence passed both the canonical runner's verbatim `Test-E2eRecordings` and rebuilt `cua-e2e-report --require-video`. This is scoped local regression evidence, not complete desktop certification.
- Runtime SHA256: `b5fdeb48af9317cad85c732e6e7425a583ab287cc4495362051f866281bf48b1`.

Maintainer approval remains necessary for fork CI and complete final desktop certification at this new candidate. Existing Ready state is preserved in response to the maintainer's rebase request; no claim that the full cross-platform matrix or pending CI has passed. The Windows interactive workflow uses `e2e-rust-windows.yml`, full candidate SHA, `lane=all`. No DTW pin, dependency declaration, or release artifact changes.

title: fix(cua-driver): release session labels when their owner transport closes
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: every `cua-driver mcp` process is its own transport on the shared daemon. When one exits, `end_sessions_for_owner` records its sessions as ended and owned by the closed transport, and every admission path then refuses everyone else for the rest of the daemon's life. Public session labels are short model-chosen names (`calc`, `te`), so a later, unrelated MCP process that picks the same label gets `session has ended` on every call, and the suggested recovery fails too: `start_session` returns `session is not available to this transport`. Agents waste calls inventing new labels; in a local benchmark this hit almost every run after the first.
- What changed: closed transports are recorded; a labelled session whose owner transport has closed is released, and another transport's next ordinary call or `start_session` starts a fresh session once the old session's cleanup has finished. This reuses the path that already recreates an idle-expired unnamed session (#4283). `recreates_on_next_call` now takes the real caller transport, and the daemon's early refusal (`SdkAdapter::is_session_ended`) passes it, so the early check and core admission agree.
- Unchanged protections: an explicit `end_session` stays terminal for a still-connected owner until it calls `start_session`; a label held by a live transport stays unavailable to others; a late call from the closed transport itself is refused; a transport's own unnamed session id is never released; revoke-all still fails closed.

## Related work

Refs #3329
Related: #3146 (one-shot CLI transports ending named sessions)

RFC: this changes when an ended labelled session can be reused by another transport. It stays inside the existing lease/lifecycle design and keeps the refusals above, but if maintainers consider it a lifecycle-contract change I'm happy to move it through the RFC process; opening as a draft for that reason.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: a label previously owned by a now-closed MCP process becomes usable by other transports instead of being permanently refused. No schema change.
- Risk and rollback: the closed-transport set grows like the existing ended-session list (#4993) and is cleared on runtime shutdown. Revert the commit to restore the old behavior.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core` (958 unit + integration) and `cargo test -p cua-driver` pass; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean. New tests: `session::tests::a_closed_transport_releases_its_labels_to_other_transports` and `serve::gate_tests::a_closed_transports_session_labels_are_reusable` (real daemon socket, two transports). Disabling the release, removing the "not the closed owner" check, or removing the "not its own unnamed id" check each makes them fail.
- Manual or platform evidence: separate binary + scratch daemon over MCP stdio. On `main`, transport B using label `calc` after A closed gets `session has ended…` and `start_session` gets `session is not available to this transport`. With this branch, B reuses `calc` and a label A had explicitly ended before closing; A's own explicit end still refuses A while connected; B's explicit end refuses B until `start_session`; C is refused `calc` while B holds it.
- Known gaps or CI still required: macOS only locally; Windows/Linux CI. `cargo clippy` not run (component not installed for the pinned toolchain).

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [ ] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

title: install.ps1: Windows PowerShell 5.1 aborts after a successful cosign verification (NativeCommandError on 'Verified OK')
body:
### Primary area

Build, packaging, or release

### Summary

On Windows PowerShell 5.1, `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1` aborts right after a **successful** Sigstore check whenever `cosign` is on PATH. cosign prints `Verified OK` to stderr; the script runs it with `*> $null` under `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`, and PowerShell 5.1 turns that redirected native stderr line into a terminating `NativeCommandError`. The install stops before anything is staged, so having cosign installed makes the installer unusable on stock Windows PowerShell (the same happens with `-RequireSignature`).

### Reproduction

1. Windows 11 with the built-in Windows PowerShell 5.1 (no pwsh 7).
2. Install cosign and make it resolvable as `cosign` (for example `winget install Sigstore.Cosign`, then expose it as `cosign.exe`, since winget names the shim `cosign-windows-amd64`).
3. Run the installer, e.g. `$env:CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION = "0.34.1"; powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install.ps1` (also reproduced with `-RequireSignature`).

### Expected behavior

`cosign verify-blob` exits 0, the script logs `verified the Sigstore signature of ...zip`, and the install continues.

### Actual behavior

The SHA256 check passes, then the cosign call raises a terminating error and the installer exits. Nothing is installed; the existing release, junctions and autostart task are left untouched.

### Environment

- cua-driver-rs 0.34.1, `install.ps1` from `main` (the same code is at line ~1308: `& $cosign verify-blob ... $zipPath *> $null`, with `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` at line 115)
- Windows 11 (10.0.26300), x86_64
- Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100
- cosign v3.1.3 (winget `Sigstore.Cosign`)
- Observed when the installer was launched over OpenSSH from an elevated session. My understanding is that this is PowerShell 5.1's general handling of redirected native stderr under `Stop`, so I expect a console run to behave the same, but I only reproduced it over SSH.

### Evidence

```
==> verified cua-driver-rs-0.34.1-windows-x86_64.zip against SHA256SUMS
powershell : cosign.exe : Verified OK
    + CategoryInfo          : NotSpecified: (cosign.exe : Verified OK:String) [], RemoteException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : NativeCommandError
At ...\install.ps1:1305 char:13
+             & $cosign verify-blob --bundle $bundlePath `
    + CategoryInfo          : NotSpecified: (Verified OK:String) [], RemoteException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : NativeCommandError
```

The signature itself is valid: running the same `cosign verify-blob --bundle ... --certificate-identity https://github.com/trycua/cua/.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml@refs/tags/cua-driver-rs-v0.34.1 --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com <zip>` via `cmd /c` prints `Verified OK` and exits 0.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: verify the zip manually with cosign, then run the installer with cosign removed from that process's PATH (it still checks SHA256SUMS and Authenticode); afterwards compare the installed `cua-driver.exe` / `cua-driver-uia.exe` hashes with the verified zip.

Possible fix: relax the error preference just around the native call and rely on `$LASTEXITCODE`, e.g.

```powershell
$prevEap = $ErrorActionPreference
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
try {
    & $cosign verify-blob --bundle $bundlePath `
        --certificate-identity $identity `
        --certificate-oidc-issuer $CosignOidcIssuer $zipPath 2>&1 | Out-Null
} finally { $ErrorActionPreference = $prevEap }
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { ... }
```

(or invoke it through `cmd /c` / `Start-Process -Wait -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardError`).

Related nit: winget exposes cosign as `cosign-windows-amd64`, so `Get-Command cosign` does not find a winget install unless the user adds a `cosign.exe` alias.

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep install.ps1 from aborting after a successful cosign check
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows PowerShell 5.1, `install.ps1` aborts right after a successful Sigstore check whenever cosign is on PATH (and therefore always with `-RequireSignature`). cosign prints `Verified OK` on stderr; the script runs it under `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`, and 5.1 turns that redirected native stderr into a terminating `NativeCommandError`. Nothing gets installed.
- What changed: the `cosign verify-blob` call moves into a small `Invoke-CosignVerifyBlob` helper that relaxes the error preference for that one call (function-local) and returns cosign's exit code. It seeds `$global:LASTEXITCODE` with a failure and treats an exception as one, so a cosign that cannot start fails closed instead of returning a stale exit code (review follow-up). The caller still refuses to install on a non-zero exit, so a bad signature is rejected exactly as before. A Windows PowerShell regression test covers both outcomes and runs in the `ci-test-scripts` Windows job, which already uses `shell: powershell`.

## Related work

Fixes #5058

RFC: not needed (no public contract change).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only. Installs with cosign present now succeed on Windows PowerShell 5.1 instead of aborting. No change for pwsh 7, for installs without cosign, or for the shell installer.
- Risk and rollback: the helper only changes how cosign's output and errors are handled; the pass/fail decision is still cosign's exit code. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/install-cosign-verify-windows-regression.ps1`. It asserts that the single `verify-blob` call lives in the helper, that a stand-in cosign writing `Verified OK` to stderr and exiting 0 returns 0 without throwing under `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` (and does not leak the relaxed preference), that a failing stand-in returns non-zero, and that with `$global:LASTEXITCODE = 0` a cosign that does not exist still returns non-zero without throwing. On Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100 it passes against this branch and fails against `main`.
- Manual or platform evidence (Windows 11 10.0.26300, Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100, cosign v3.1.3, run over OpenSSH from an elevated session; isolated `CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME` / `CUA_DRIVER_RS_INSTALL_DIR`, `-RequireSignature -NoAutoStart -NoPathUpdate`, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION=0.34.1`):
  - `main`: `verified ... against SHA256SUMS`, then `NativeCommandError`, exit 1, nothing installed.
  - this branch: `verified ... against SHA256SUMS`, `verified the Sigstore signature of cua-driver-rs-0.34.1-windows-x86_64.zip`, `verified the Authenticode signatures of the staged executables`, `cua-driver-rs 0.34.1 installed.`, exit 0.
  - After the review fix (8bc83d1): the regression passes and the same isolated signed install still succeeds. On 5.1, 3ddb898 threw (rather than returning a stale `0`) for a missing cosign and for a non-executable one; this commit returns `1` for both.
  - The old call pattern alone (`& <cosign stand-in> verify-blob x *> $null` under `Stop`) throws `NativeCommandError` on 5.1.
- Known gaps or CI still required: I reproduced and verified over SSH only, not from an interactive console window, and not on pwsh 7. The negative path (signature mismatch) is covered by the stand-in in the regression test, not by a tampered real release. The new CI step has not run yet.

title: feat(lume): support owned GHCR preparation work roots
body:
## Summary

Lume image pulls can optionally use a caller-supplied preparation work root for GHCR legacy and OCI images. The work-root tuple is carried through the CLI, controller, and HTTP pull paths; selected staging, layer downloads, reassembly, decompression, and final assembly use an operation-owned layout, while GCS rejects the option explicitly.

The change keeps ordinary pulls on their existing publication and cache paths. In owned mode, partial tuples, unsafe root/destination overlap, invalid digest path components, and unsupported cross-volume final publication are rejected; verified layers and the final VM directory are committed atomically where the owned contract requires it. Background pull status and cancellation use an operation token, and conflicting operation identities return 409.

## Scope and compatibility

- GHCR legacy and OCI preparation paths are in scope.
- The option is opt-in; callers that omit the tuple retain the ordinary pull path.
- The work-root, scope, and operation identifiers must be supplied together.
- GCS pulls reject an owned work root with a clear error.
- Existing cache naming and legacy assembly behavior remain compatible, including synthetic test fixtures.
- Provider lifecycle, VM lifecycle, resource leasing, and runtime qualification are outside this change.

## HTTP behavior

`POST /lume/pull` and `POST /lume/pull/start` accept `preparationWorkRoot`, `preparationScopeID`, and `preparationOperationID`. Background starts return an `operationToken`; `GET /lume/vms/:name` includes it while a cancellable pull is active; `POST /lume/pull/cancel` requires the token and waits for cleanup. Conflicting active operation identities return 409, and the synchronous pull documentation describes the same conflict response.

## Verification

At current upstream `main` plus this branch:

- `swift build` — passed.
- `swift test` — **215 passed, 0 failures, 0 unexpected issues**.
- `swift test --filter PreparationPlacementTests` — 14 passed.
- `swift test --filter PullProgressTests` — 21 passed.
- `swift test --filter LegacyDiskAssemblyTests` — all 4 parameter combinations passed.
- `swift test --filter CommandDocExtractorTests` — 5 passed.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

The complete source suite and focused placement/streaming/legacy/documentation tests are green. Runtime qualification remains separate: no public Lume server pull, credentialed CLI against a real registry, loopback registry, provider or VM/image/network operation, cross-process lock run, Foundation callback memory/backpressure measurement, process-loss/reboot recovery, or APFS durability run has been performed.

## Acceptance criteria

- Complete Swift suite passes with zero failures.
- Existing legacy and synthetic cache fixtures retain distinct path-safe cache identifiers.
- CLI command documentation lists all Pull options exposed by ArgumentParser.
- API documentation lists all response status codes, including synchronous 409 conflicts.
- Focused placement, streaming, digest, cleanup, and operation-token tests remain green.

title: feat(cua): report agent run and Space create status to the terminal (OSC 7501)
body:
## Problem

`cua agent run -f`, `cua agent send -f`, `cua agent logs -f` and `cua spaces create` can run for minutes. A terminal that supports OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol, rev 0.4) can show whether a tab is working, done or failed, but `cua` reported nothing, so the only signal was the text scrolling past.

## Before / after

Before: plain text only (the agent log lines, the `\r` progress line for `spaces create`).

After, only when stderr is a terminal and `--json` is off:
- `cua agent run -f` / `send -f` / `logs -f`: `working` after the first page of events is read, unless that page already ended the turn, and whenever a turn starts; `done` when the turn ends (`end_turn` or no stop reason, whatever text the event carries); `idle` when the turn is cancelled or the run goes idle; `error` for other stop reasons, `error` events, the agent exiting mid-turn, or the run being `failed`/`crashed`. The message is `<harness> <run_id>: <what happened>`. At most one report per page of events, and only when the state changes. Plain `cua agent logs` (no `-f`) stays silent.
- `cua spaces create` of one Space (the same gate as its step lines; `--count` above 1 shows neither): `working` with `progress=0-100` and the same text as the step line; `done` with the same `Created <id> (<name>[, on <host>])` line the CLI prints; `error` with the error text.
- Ctrl-C (the create cancel, the second Ctrl-C after it, and Ctrl-C during an agent follow that reports) writes `state=clear` if anything was reported, so no stale record is left behind. After the clear nothing more is reported, so progress from creates still being cleaned up cannot bring `working` back. `done`/`error` at a normal exit are kept, as the spec intends.

Every report is `ESC ] 7501 ; state=<s>[:progress=N]:app=cua:msg=<base64> ESC \` on the root record. Control characters in the message become spaces, and the message is trimmed and cut to 2048 bytes on a char boundary, so the whole sequence stays under 4096 bytes. There is no feature detection query: an unsupported terminal ignores the sequence.

## Tests

- `util::secret_tests::program_status_reports_are_osc_7501`: exact bytes for `working`, `working:progress=42`, progress clamped to 100, and progress dropped for `done`.
- `util::secret_tests::program_status_messages_fit_the_limits`: 3000×`é` decodes to 1024×`é` (2048 B of valid UTF-8) and the report is ≤4096 B; `"a\x1bb\u{85}c\n"` decodes to `"a b c"`.
- `util::secret_tests::program_status_is_not_reported_after_it_is_cleared`: a clear with no prior report writes nothing; after report, report, clear, only those three write, and a later report or clear does not.
- `agent_cmd::tests::turn_events_and_run_statuses_map_to_program_states`: covers end_turn, no stop reason, cancelled, max_tokens, error, exited after done (state unchanged), exited while working, crashed, idle, and unrelated events or an `unknown` status (state unchanged).
- `agent_cmd::tests::turn_end_text_is_not_a_stop_reason`: a `turn_ended` with no stop reason and text `All done.` is `done`; `max_tokens` with text is still `error (max_tokens)`.

These 5 tests don't exist on main (filtering for them there runs 0 tests). They pass at head. `cargo fmt -p cua-cli -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p cua-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. `cargo test -p cua-cli` passes.

Terminal check, using a scratch test that calls `program_status(Working, Some(42), "Installing updates")`, then `clear_program_status()`, then `program_status(Working, Some(43), "late")`, run with `--nocapture`:
- run under `script` (stderr is a pty): `033 ] 7 5 0 1 ; s t a t e = w o r k i n g : p r o g r e s s = 4 2 : a p p = c u a : m s g = S W 5 z d G F s b G l u Z y B 1 c G R h d G V z 033 \ 033 ] 7 5 0 1 ; s t a t e = c l e a r 033 \` and nothing after the clear (before the clear suppression, a third `state=working:progress=43` record followed)
- stderr redirected to a file or a pipe: 0 bytes.

Linear: CUA-1573, CUA-3446

title: feat(spaces): right-click menus in the New UI (CUA-1639)
body:
**Held for feature freeze. Don't merge until the freeze lifts.**

Right-clicking a Space tile in the New UI showed the web view's own menu ("Copy Image"). Now Spaces and machines have menus of their own. The Mac app and Electron draw them natively, and they work from the keyboard.

Linear: CUA-1639 (part A: the shared plumbing, Space tiles and rows, machines. Part B, which covers Agents, Keyvault items and Notifications, stacks on this branch).

## What changes for users
- **Space tile or row:** Open, Turn on / Turn off… / Restart…, Teleport an app…, Send file…, Share…, Copy Name, Copy ID, Delete Space… (or Remove… / Remove from List). An item appears only when the Space's page would offer it, by the same rules: the core's detail actions and power button. Turn off, Restart and Delete ask first.
- **Machine row:** Open, New Space on This Machine…, Copy Name, and Remove… where the machine's detail has Remove.
- **Everywhere else:** the web view's own menu is gone. Text fields and selected text keep the system menu (Cut/Copy/Paste). Links that leave the app get Open Link / Copy Link. Electron now also gets Cut/Copy/Paste in text fields, which it never had.
- **Keyboard:** Shift+F10 or the context-menu key on a focused tile or row opens the menu.

## How
- `useContextMenu(items)` and `<ContextMenuHost />` in `apps/cua-spaces-web/src/components/context-menu.tsx`. Each item has a stable action id (`space.stop`, `machine.copyName`, …), and choosing one runs the existing action. Destructive items carry a `confirm`.
- New bridge method `window.showContextMenu {items, x, y}` answers `{id | null}`. It's in the web contract (shapes, coverage), Swift (`WebUIBridge+ContextMenu.swift`, NSMenu) and Electron (`src/context-menu.ts`, `Menu.popup`). When an item has `copy`, the host writes that text to the clipboard itself.
- The demo, Tauri, and an older app that answers `unimplemented` all fall back to a menu drawn in the page.
- Not included: **Rename** for a Space, because neither the core nor the hosts have a rename for Spaces. **Revoke** stays in Settings > Devices, since the Machines page doesn't offer it today.

## Tests
- web (vitest): `components/__tests__/context-menu.test.tsx` covers the native path, the confirmation, keyboard, the in-page fallback, default-menu suppression, and the menus on the real Spaces and Machines pages with the wasm core.
- Electron: `test/context-menu.test.ts` (request checks, the template, zoom, Cut/Copy/Paste) and a `bridge-native` case.
- Swift: `WebUIHostTests.thePagesContextMenusAreNative` and a `BridgeContractTests` case.

## Verified on a signed build
I tested signed, notarized CI builds of this branch (CD run 38642709685, version 0.9.0-ctxmenu.1, nothing published) on a spare test Mac.
- **Mac app, New UI:** right-clicking a Space tile opens the native NSMenu with Open, Turn off…, Restart…, Teleport an app…, Send file…, Copy Name, Copy ID and Delete Space…. Choosing Copy ID put the Space's id on the clipboard. Right-clicking a machine row shows Open, New Space on This Machine… and Copy Name, and Copy Name copied "This Mac". A Space row in a machine's detail, here a suspended one, shows Teleport greyed out, the same rule as its page. Right-clicking a blank area, a sidebar link or the Space page shows no menu. The Filter field keeps the system menu (Cut/Copy/Paste…). "Copy Image" never appeared.
- **Electron:** the same native menus on the Space tile and the machine row, and Copy ID copied the id. The Filter field gets Undo/Redo/Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All. A blank area shows no menu.
- One test-harness quirk: a *synthetic background* right-click (posted straight to the process) opened the Mac menu twice. A real HID right-click opens exactly one menu, and choosing an item or pressing Escape closes it.

title: feat(spaces): right-click menus for Agents and Keyvault items (CUA-1639)
body:
Part B of CUA-1639. It is stacked on #5197 (part A: the context-menu plumbing plus Space and Machine menus) and targets that branch.

**For users:** right-clicking an agent, a run or a Keyvault item in the New UI (Mac app and Electron) now shows a menu of that item's actions instead of the web view's default menu.

### Menus
- **Agents** (list rows and the detail header): Open, Pause/Resume (the core's label, as on the detail's button), Stop (only while a run is running), Copy Name, and Remove… with a confirmation. The agent's home stays in Cua Volume.
- **Runs** (Recent runs): Open, and Stop while the run is running.
- **Keyvault items:** Copy Name (the item's name, never a value, and hidden while names are hidden), Unlock… or Lock (as the row's lock button does), and Delete…. Delete asks first the same way the batch bar's Delete does: the page's dialog in the demo, the host's own alert in the Mac app and Electron. Labels are fixed words and never contain item names or values.
- **Everything else** (Settings images and icons, the checklist, the palette): part A's host already cancels the web view's default menu outside text fields and selected text, so these show no menu. Text fields keep Cut/Copy/Paste.

### Bridge
Adds `agents.remove` (`persistent_agent_remove`) and `agents.stop` (`agent_stop`, `{spaceId, runId}`). The daemon already had both tools. This change wires them into the web contract (protocol, shapes, `bridge-shapes.json`, coverage), the Mac app host (`WebUIBridge.agents`), Electron (`PersistentAgents.remove/stopRun`) and the demo host. Tauri reports them as unsupported, because its tool allow-list creates and deletes nothing. No change to part A's plumbing.

### Decisions
- No **Edit** for Keyvault items, because no edit action for an item exists in the core or the bridge.
- No **copy of a secret's value**, because the UI only ever has the redacted list.
- **Notifications** (Open, Mark as Read, Open Space) wait for #5196 (CUA-1636), which adds expandable rows and `notifications.markRead`. #5196 has merged. The commit is ready and goes in after the retarget. Mark as Unread and Dismiss are left out because the daemon can only mark entries read.

### Tests
- Web vitest: `src/__tests__/context-menus-pages.test.tsx` covers the menus on the real Agents page and Keyvault list (wasm core, demo host): items by state, Open selects, Stop calls `agents.stop`, Remove and Delete run only after confirming, Copy Name copies the name, and labels never name the item. The full suite passes locally (567 tests).
- Electron: `test/agents.test.ts` covers `agents.remove` and `agents.stop` through the host (the tools' args, the list read again, failed, bad_args, unsupported). The full suite passes locally (548 tests).
- Swift: `WebUIHostTests.agentsRemoveAndStopRunTheDaemonsTools` and the unsupported/bad_args cases. `WebUIHostTests`, `BridgeContractTests` and `AgentsPagesTests` pass locally.

### Verified on a signed build
CI build `0.9.1-ctxmenus.b1` (Developer ID signed and notarized; this branch plus #5196 plus the notifications commit), on a spare test Mac, in both the Mac app's New UI and Electron:
- Agents: the row's native menu shows Open, Pause, Copy Name and Remove…. The detail header shows the same menu without Open. Remove… asks first, then removes the agent (it's gone from the page and from `cua agent persistent`).
- Notifications: Open, Mark as Read (unread only) and Copy Text. Mark as Read and Open both work.
- Right-clicking an icon on the Keyvault page shows no menu. The test Mac has no Keyvault, so the item menu is covered by the web tests only.

### Before merge
Once #5197 merges: retarget to main, add the notifications commit, rerun CI, then squash-merge.

title: fix(spaces): list the Spaces on your other machines with their live state (CUA-1638, CUA-1637)
body:
Fixes CUA-1638 and CUA-1637.

**For users:**
- The Spaces on a Mac that has "Provide Spaces" on now show on every other device signed in to the same account, labelled "on <machine>". This covers its own Linux and macOS Spaces, not only the ones other devices created there.
- Each Space shows what it is actually doing:
  - Starting while it boots or joins the relay. Before, it showed Stopped (CUA-1637).
  - Running or Stopped.
  - Failed, with the reason.
  - When its machine is offline, it says so.
- You can open, start and stop these Spaces from the other device.
- The same list is used everywhere: the Mac app (classic and New UI), Electron, the menu bar and notch counts, and `cua sandbox ls`.

- **Machines page:** each computer is listed once, under its computer name. Reinstalls, sign-ins and host setups used to leave the same Mac behind as several rows: "This Mac", "Dillons-MacBook-Pro-2.local" and "Dillon's MacBook Pro (2)" for one laptop.

### Causes
- **Spaces missing (CUA-1638):** a Space got a relay entry only when another device created it through the relay. Spaces made on the providing machine itself were never put on the relay, and nothing else listed them.
- **"Stopped" while starting (CUA-1637):** the relay only says whether a Space's connection is up right now. Every app turned "not connected" into Stopped, so a Space that was being created, booting or joining the relay read Stopped. The machine running it knew the real state, but nothing asked it.

### What changes
- **The providing machine publishes its own Spaces** (`HostSpacesServer::publish_own`, run by `cua daemon` every 20 s):
  - It runs while "Provide Spaces" is on and the machine is signed in.
  - Each Space made on the machine gets a relay entry under the machine. The entry id comes from the machine id and the Space id, so a Space is published once. Only the owner can see it.
  - A running Space's driver is attached to its entry. A stopped Space is attached when it is started, from any device.
  - These Spaces count as provided Spaces, so the existing remote start, stop and delete work for them. They do not count toward the machine's `max_spaces` limit.
  - Turning "Provide Spaces" off takes them off the relay again. A refused registration, such as the account's relay machine limit, is retried every 2 minutes instead of on every pass.
- **The host reports state:** each Space in `GetHostSpaces` now carries `state` (running, starting, suspended, stopped or failed) and `state_reason`, read from its runtime.
- **One roster in the core** (`cua-spaces/src/pool_roster.rs`):
  - `Spaces::list_all` asks each of the account's machines that provides Spaces for its listing. It does this through the relay, at most every 5 s per machine, with a 4 s budget each. A machine that doesn't answer is left alone for 30 s.
  - `Spaces::list` gives each Space on another machine that machine's state, in `power_state` plus `state_reason`. The daemon's `ListSpaces`, the SDK's `SpaceInfo` and the apps' rows carry it.
- **Apps:**
  - The app core maps `starting` to Starting (Provisioning), and `failed` to "Failed · <reason>" with Start offered. A row whose machine is offline says why.
  - The Swift and Electron shells pass the reason through, and skip their 4 s probe for Spaces their machine says are starting, failed or off.
  - The New UI bridge keeps these states.
- **CLI:** `cua sandbox ls` also lists the Spaces on your other machines, as "on <machine>" with their state (JSON: `location: relay`, `machine`, `state`, `reason`).

- **One computer per row** (app core `machines::merge`):
  - A machine and a device are paired by their computer name, however it is spelled ("Dillon's MacBook Pro (2)" and "Dillons-MacBook-Pro-2.local").
  - A stale identity folds into the one live row of that computer. Stale means offline and, for a device, not seen for a day.
  - A machine named after its hostname takes its device's computer name.
  - A host whose relay entry still has the hostname an older setup gave it renames it once to its computer name (`label_own_machine`, an owner `PATCH`). A name the owner chose is kept.
  - Two computers that share a name, or that are both in use, stay apart.
- **Steadier states:**
  - While its runtimes are slow to list (cloning or booting a VM), a host answers with its last listing, and lists a Space it is turning on as starting.
  - A client keeps a machine's last answer when one read fails.
  - Spaces whose driver can't join the relay are not published.
  - Every Space the host provides on the relay is attached again after its driver loses the relay, for example after a daemon restart.

### Compatibility
- **No relay change.** This uses `POST /v1/machines` with `host` and `GET /v1/machines`, which the current prod relay already serves.
- **Old clients** keep working. They already list relay Spaces that have a `host`, so they also see the published Spaces, with their old connected-or-Stopped status.
- **Old hosts** list no states. Their Spaces read as they did before.
- **Live states need the new cua-spacesd on the providing machine.** cua-spacesd forwards the host's listing typed, and an older one drops the new fields. This PR changes a cua-spacesd test so its next release carries them. Publishing needs only the new `cua` daemon.
- **CUA-1527:** Spaces are still never machines, since they have a `host` and a `space-` id. On the providing machine each published Space is listed once, as its local Space.
- Fields added to protos: `HostSpace.state` = 12, `HostSpace.state_reason` = 13, `cua.daemon.v1.Space.state_reason` = 21. Field 8 of `GetHostSpacesResponse` and field 10 of `CreateHostSpaceRequest` stay free for CUA-1635.

### With CUA-1635
A create still running on another machine reads Starting with the step it is on, such as "Downloading the image, 41%…". This comes from the machine's `creating` listing (#5198), keyed by the Space's relay entry. This PR reuses those fields and adds none of its own.

### Tests
- **`cua-spaces` `tests/host_spaces.rs`**, `spaces_made_on_a_providing_machine_list_on_other_devices_with_their_state`. It runs against the fake relay, a fake runtime and a second device's `Spaces`, and checks:
  - publishing happens once, and only when signed in;
  - the host lists each Space once and its limit is untouched;
  - the other device lists the Spaces "on Mac mini (spare)", Running and Suspended;
  - a Space started from the other device reads Starting, then Running;
  - a Space stopped from the other device reads Stopped;
  - with the host offline, the Spaces say why;
  - with "Provide Spaces" off, they leave the relay.
- **`cua-spaces` `pool_roster` unit tests:** state mapping, including a create still running there, and which machines are asked.
- **App core:** `a_space_on_another_machine_reads_its_machines_state`.
- **cua-spacesd-server:** the host's states reach the caller through the driver.

title: ci: PR runs restore Rust caches but never save them
body:
Part of CUA-1653 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-1653).

**Problem.** The repo's Actions cache is capped at 10 GB but holds about 18.9 GB. GitHub evicts the least recently used entries, so entries live about 10 minutes. 24 of the 30 live entries were Rust caches saved by PR runs, and other PRs can't restore those. In the last runs I sampled, only 7 of about 41 rust-cache restores in PR jobs found anything. Examples of cold builds:
- SwiftUI app job: "Cache not found", then a 34 min cold `cargo build --release -p cua-spaces-ffi` (run 38638558590).
- In #5186's dry run, a native cache saved at 20:06 was gone by 20:35 for the same key.

**Change.**
- Every `Swatinem/rust-cache` step in PR-triggered and reusable workflows: `save-if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}` (38 steps, 24 files). Steps that already had a `save-if` are unchanged. Main, schedule and dispatch runs still save, and PRs restore main's cache.
- `ci-cua-spaces.yml` and `ci-openkoalabot-example-tauri.yml` (2.4 GB entries): `actions/cache` is split into restore, plus a save step that runs only outside PRs.
- `ci-cua-spaces-macos`, `ci-test-python` and `ci-cua-spaces-web` never ran on main, so PRs had nothing to restore. Each gets a daily scheduled run, which saves the cache and also checks main itself.

No tests, jobs or required checks are removed. CD workflows are not touched (`cd-cua-spaces.yml` belongs to #5186).

**Follow-up for a repo admin (billing):** raise the cache limit above 10 GB (Settings → Actions → Caches). Main-only caches still add up to well over 10 GB.

Before/after timings will be added once main has saved its caches.

title: fix(cua-driver): send key identity with browser_type keystrokes
body:
Fixes #5212

## What changes for users

Agents can now press Enter in a search or combobox field in a background browser tab (`browser_type` with `mode: "keystrokes"` and `"\n"`), and pages that check `keyCode`/`code` see real key identities.

## Change

`browser_type` keystrokes sent `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` with only `key`, so Chromium delivered `code: ""` and `keyCode: 0`. The new `KeyStroke` helper adds `code`, `windowsVirtualKeyCode` and `nativeVirtualKeyCode` for Enter, space, ASCII letters and digits on keyDown, char and keyUp. Other characters keep the previous key-only shape.

## Testing

- `keystrokes_use_char_events_for_text_delivery` now asserts `KeyA`/65 and `Enter`/13 on every phase.
- New `keystroke_identity_covers_enter_space_letters_and_digits` unit test.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::` (209 passed) and `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -D warnings`.
- Manual: against a hidden tab in Chrome 155 on macOS 26.6.1, the old event shape logged `kd:Enter//0` and didn't submit; the new shape logged `kd:Enter/Enter/13` and submitted.

title: ci(spaces-tauri): macOS/Windows bundles only when the app changes

Part of CUA-1653 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-1653).

The Tauri app (apps/cua-spaces) isn't shipped: `cd-cua-spaces.yml` has it disabled. But `CI: Cua Spaces` built its macOS and Windows installer bundles on every PR that touched `libs/cua/**`. title: fix(spaces): Back after a refused window drop shows the whole app picker (CUA-1671)
body:
Fixes CUA-1671.

**What changes for users:** drag a window onto a Space, and if its app can't be teleported (for example TextEdit), Back now shows the full app picker, the same as the Space's "Teleport an app" button. Before, it showed an empty "No apps match." list. This works in the New UI (Mac app and Electron) and in the classic Mac UI.

**Why:** a drop opens the sheet straight at the dropped app and never reads the app list (catalog). Back then landed on a picker with no catalog loaded.

- Core (`teleport/flow.rs`): Back from an app's options or error always leads to the full picker. If the catalog hasn't been read yet, it goes to the loading step, and the picker appears once the list arrives, with the same selection as a fresh picker. A drop clears the search.
- React store (`bridge/teleport.ts`): Back onto the loading step reads the catalog. A failed read is retried; before, it could hang on "Loading apps…".
- SwiftUI (`TeleportModel.swift`): the same read on Back.
- Tests:
  - core: `back_from_a_dropped_app_shows_the_whole_grid`;
  - web: two tests with the wasm core (a refused drop then Back; a catalog read that fails then succeeds on retry);
  - Swift: `backFromADroppedAppShowsTheWholeGrid`.

title: fix(spaces): window-drag detection survives a slow first drag (CUA-1670)
body:
Fixes CUA-1670.

**What changes for users:** dragging a window onto a Space tile, or onto the notch, keeps working after the first drag, in both the Mac app and Electron. Before, the first drag (often the one that raises macOS's screen-capture consent) could switch off drag detection for the rest of the session.

**Why:** the macOS event tap called the app's listener on the tap's own thread. In Electron that call waits for the JS thread, which was busy capturing the ghost image while the consent prompt was up. In the Mac app, the dragged window's app was matched against the catalog on that same thread. macOS switches off a tap whose callback is slow. We ignored the "tap disabled" event, and the "never start a second tracker" guard kept the dead tap in place.

- `cua-teleport` (`ux/window_macos.rs`, `ux/window.rs`):
  - The tap thread only works out the drag and queues events. A separate thread runs the listener and the app lookup, coalescing stale moves.
  - A disabled tap is re-enabled. If it keeps dying, or stops on its own, the tracker ends with a `stopped` event and `is_running()` turns false.
  - Mouse-down remembers up to 4 windows under the cursor, skipping fully transparent ones.
- Electron (`notch/model.ts`) and the Mac app (`NotchController.swift`) drop a stopped tracker and start a fresh one on the next readiness check, activation or toggle, or within 2 s.
- Logging: `[cua] window drag:` lines on stderr (tap up, failed, disabled and re-enabled, stopped). With `CUA_SPACES_NOTCH_DEBUG=1`, the windows under the cursor at mouse-down are logged too.
- Tests: Rust (6 new: re-enable, give up, coalescing, slow listener never blocks the tap, invisible window on top), Electron (stopped tracker restarts, late stop from an old tracker ignored), Swift (stopped tracker restarts).

title: fix(cua): split the rest of create runtime errors and explain the macOS VM limit (CUA-1356)
body:
Refs CUA-1356.

## Why
`runtime` is still the top failed-create kind: 67 `cua_sandbox_created` errors in the last 7 days (non-CI). Every one comes from a CLI build that predates the fixes already on main: 0.4.1 (5 Oct), or 0.2.0 (one Windows install, 14 errors). Rough split:

title: fix(spaces): Set up installs and checks cua-driver before saying done (CUA-1797)
body:
## What was wrong

In Cua Spaces (macOS, 0.9.x), Settings → **Background computer use** → **Set up** (and the same card in the first-run "AI agents" step) reported "Claude Code: done … cua-driver configured" while cua-driver wasn't on the machine. Agents then failed to start the server: `/mcp` → `ENOENT: Executable not found in $PATH: cua-driver`.

## Root cause

- **Nothing installed cua-driver.** cua-driver isn't bundled with Cua Spaces. On macOS it is its own signed app (`/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, the identity that gets Accessibility and Screen Recording), installed by `cua.ai/driver/install.sh`. The `cua.ai/install.sh` "cua-driver" item runs that installer and then `cua agents setup --cua-driver`. The app's Set up ran only the second half.
- **A bare `cua-driver` command was written.** `McpServer::driver_for` looks for cua-driver on the PATH and in `~/.local/bin`. When it found nothing, it fell back to the bare name `cua-driver`, and `setup_cua_driver` wrote that into every agent's MCP config. GUI agents like VS Code and Claude Desktop don't get the shell PATH, so a bare name fails even when the binary exists somewhere.
- **"Done" was never checked.** A row was "done" as soon as the config file was written. Nothing checked that the command exists or that `cua-driver mcp` answers.
- **Not a code regression.** This behaviour dates from the SDK merge (#4397); the Settings card (#4893) put it in front of more people. On machines that still had the legacy `/usr/local/bin/cua-driver` link from older cua-driver installers, the PATH lookup found it and wrote an absolute path, so Set up appeared to work there. Without that link it wrote the bare name.

## Fix

- **`cua-agent-setup`: new `driver` module.**
  - `locate` finds cua-driver: on the PATH, in `~/.local/bin`, then inside `CuaDriver.app`.
  - `check` runs `cua-driver mcp` and sends an MCP `initialize`; it passes only on a valid answer.
  - `install` downloads cua-driver's release installer (`cua.ai/driver/install.sh`, or `install.ps1` on Windows) and runs it. That installer verifies the archive against `SHA256SUMS` and checks the `CuaDriver.app` signature. Its output goes to `~/.cua/logs/cua-driver-install.log`.
  - `ensure` uses an existing cua-driver that passes `check`, and otherwise installs one and checks it again.
- **`AgentSetup::setup_cua_driver`.** The MCP server is written only by absolute path, and only after `check` passes. Otherwise each agent's `cua-driver` row fails with the reason, and its config is left unchanged. Re-running Set up repairs entries that point at a missing binary: the entry is updated to the checked absolute path.
- **SDK `AgentSetup.setup_cua_driver`** (the Set up button in the SwiftUI and Electron apps) calls `ensure` first, so it installs cua-driver when it's missing or broken. A failed row says how to fix it: "Set up again to retry, or install it with: …".
- **UI.** The SwiftUI first-run view now shows each failure reason under the agent's row; before, it was only in a tooltip. The shared web card (used by both the Mac app and Electron) wraps the reason instead of truncating it.
- **`cua agents setup --cua-driver`** no longer writes a bare entry. When cua-driver is missing it fails with the reason and prints the install one-liner, as before.

## Verification

All runs used a real `Cua Spaces.app` (release build of this repo) on a spare macOS 26 Mac. Each run had a throwaway `HOME` containing Claude Code 2.1.301, a Copilot CLI dir and a VS Code user dir. `CUA_AGENT_APP_DIRS` pointed into that home, so the Mac's own `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` didn't count as installed. I drove the app with cua-driver.

1. **main (9737d6f), reproduced.** First-run AI agents → **Set up** showed "Claude Code: done / … / VS Code (Copilot agent mode): done". `~/.claude.json` and VS Code `mcp.json` got `"command": "cua-driver"`. `cua-driver mcp` in a shell → `command not found`. `claude mcp list` → `cua-driver: cua-driver mcp - ✘ Failed to connect — ENOENT: Executable not found in $PATH: "cua-driver"`.
2. **This branch, identical steps.** Set up ran cua-driver's installer (cua-driver-rs 0.35.4: SHA256SUMS verified; the existing Accessibility and Screen Recording grants were kept). The rows said "done", and both configs got `"command": "<home>/.local/bin/cua-driver"`. `cua-driver mcp` answered `initialize` from a fresh shell. `claude mcp list` → `cua-driver: … - ✔ Connected`.
3. **Repair.** I ran this branch against the home that main had broken, using Settings → Background computer use → **Set up** in the web UI. The Claude Code and VS Code entries changed from `cua-driver` to the absolute path, and `claude mcp list` → `✔ Connected`.
4. **Failure path.** I made the install impossible: a directory sits where the `cua-driver` link goes. The rows read "Claude Code: failed", followed by "the cua-driver installer finished, but no cua-driver was found. Set up again to retry, or install it with: …". No `cua-driver` MCP entry was written.
5. **Neighbouring flows didn't change.** The cua MCP server and cua skills were written the same on main and on this branch, and `cua: … mcp - ✔ Connected` both times. The `cua agents` CLI tests pass.

Tests: `cargo test -p cua-agent-setup` covers these cases:
- a missing driver fails and leaves the config untouched;
- a driver that never answers MCP fails;
- a bare entry is repaired to an absolute path;
- the binary inside `CuaDriver.app` is found.

`cargo test -p cua-cli --test agents_login` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` pass on the changed crates.

## Not verified / known limits

- **Not run:** the Windows install path (`install.ps1` via PowerShell), Linux, and the Electron app. Electron uses the same SDK call and web card.
- **Running sessions are interrupted.** cua-driver's installer stops a running cua-driver daemon while it swaps the app, so agent sessions using cua-driver drop during Set up.
- **Fresh machines still need permissions.** Set up doesn't ask for Accessibility or Screen Recording; cua-driver asks the first time it's used. On an upgrade, the installer keeps the existing grants.
- **First-run heading is unchanged.** The heading still reads "Your AI agents are set up" when a row failed. That copy wasn't changed.
