title: fix(cua-driver): keep trusting GNOME Shell and KWin after an update replaces their binary
body:
Salvaged from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5329

## Why
A distro update replaces `/usr/bin/gnome-shell` or `/usr/bin/kwin_wayland` while the compositor keeps running. `/proc/<pid>/exe` then reads `<path> (deleted)`, the old check called `fs::metadata` on that string and failed, and the driver stopped trusting the session's own Shell or KWin until the user logged out.

## What changed
- `proc_fs::running_executable` judges the running image. It opens `/proc/<pid>/exe` with `O_PATH`, rechecks the process instance, and drops the ` (deleted)` suffix only when the image has no links left. It accepts a replaced image only from the driver's mount namespace and from a mount the driver can see.
- `is_trusted_gnome_shell` and `is_trusted_kwin` both use `RunningExecutable::is_system_program`, which keeps the existing rule (matching `comm` and file name, root-owned, not group- or world-writable).
- The test fixtures now copy `sh` instead of `sleep`. Nix's multi-call coreutils `sleep` renames its `comm` to `sleep`, and that broke `Nix / Rust unit tests`.

## Scope
Linux helper trust only: `platform-linux/src/proc_fs.rs`, `wayland/shell_helper.rs` and `wayland/kwin_helper.rs`. Discovery, transport and the other `/proc/<pid>/exe` readers are unchanged.

## Blast Radius
GNOME and KDE Wayland sessions. A compositor whose binary was not replaced takes the same path as before, with an added dev/inode match between the path and the running image. A replaced image from another mount namespace, or one reached through a mount the driver can't see, is still refused (covered by the namespace and private-mount tests).

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, plus `cargo test -p platform-linux --all-targets` (918 lib tests passed). I ran the test suite once with a `sleep` that renames its `comm`, like Nix's, ahead on PATH, and once with `sh` as a bash symlink. I ran the replaced-program and namespace tests both unprivileged and as root, so the namespace cases ran instead of skipping.
- `verify-cua-driver` X11 lane (`verify-linux.sh x11`): 2 delivered, 0 failed, evidence check passed after cleanup.
- `runner.ts --library cua-driver --check`: the Linux reference is up to date. The earlier `Reference / cua-driver / linux` failure was a runner "The server is busy" error, not drift.

title: fix(cua-driver): invoke a menu for a window behind the user's window without raising it on macOS
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `invoke_menu` for a window of the **frontmost** app that is **not its key window** raised and focused that window. `invoke()` sends every frontmost-app call through `focus_exact_window` (SkyLight make-key, `AXRaise`/`AXMain`/`AXFocused`), opens the menu on screen through `invoke_path`, then restores the prior key window. The user is working in that app, so their window loses key for the call, the raised window covers it for a moment, and their typing can land in the open menu. A background agent hits this whenever it runs a menu command in another window of the app the user is in (a second document, terminal or browser window), directly or through `run_steps`' menu-bar click route (`menu_bar_route`), which calls `invoke_menu`.
- What changed: that one case now uses the same mechanism keys already use for a window behind the user's window (`key_scope` → `enter_exact_window_key`): the target becomes the app's key window through the in-app key-window record (no raise, no activation, no pointer), the item is pressed through the existing background route without opening its menu (`run_in_background`), and the scope hands key back to the user's window. If the window cannot be confirmed key that way, the call is refused with the existing `window_not_key` code, escalation `bring_to_front`, and nothing is invoked (pressing it with the user's window still key would run the command there). A background app and the frontmost app's key window keep their current routes. When the app's key window (`AXFocusedWindow`) cannot be read, the route falls back to its on-screen window order: the app's frontmost window on screen is the user's own window and keeps the old path (raising it changes nothing); any other window, and every window when no frontmost window can be found, is refused with `window_not_key` before any key-window record is posted. One per-process mutation lease covers the route decision, the key change, the press and the hand-back. Results and refusals on this route say where the window was, not that the app is in the background (`MenuRequest` words them per route, as `placement()` does); the core recovery hint for a disabled `invoke_menu` item now says its window is behind the user's window, which holds on both routes.

## Related work

Refs #3780 (the exact-window readiness wait this path uses), Refs #4955 (the background menu route and key-focus guard this reuses).

I found no issue or pull request for this case (searched `invoke_menu`, focus, raise, frontmost, `focus_exact_window`). Found while building a background voice agent that runs tasks in the user's apps.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required, I believe: no schema, parameter or new refusal code; one macOS route changes for one placement.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. A call that used to raise another window of the frontmost app now presses the item without raising it, or is refused with `window_not_key` when the key-window record cannot be confirmed (e.g. where focus without raise is unavailable) or when the app's key window cannot be read and the target is not its frontmost window on screen. Callers that want the old raise can call `bring_to_front` first, as the existing `background_unavailable` guidance already says. `MACOS.md` (the driver's skill) now describes the three placements.
- Risk and rollback: an app whose menu command runs after the AX press returns (a deferred perform) could run it after key went back to the user's window; I did not see this for menu items, which AppKit performs within the press, but I could not test it live (below). Since d52ec6ebe (#5520, salvaged from #5514), the press on this route also requires `AXFocusedWindow` and `AXMainWindow` to be the target; if the key-window record does not move `AXMainWindow`, this route refuses with `window_not_key` instead of pressing (not checked on a desktop). `invoke_menu` now holds the pid's mutation lease through the old path too, so same-pid background actions wait for it. Rollback is reverting the PR.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (rustc 1.97.1, the pin; branch updated by merging main at 87ffb67bf): `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core` → all pass: `platform-macos` unit 643 passed, 7 ignored (636 on that main), `cursor_hook_registry` 2 passed, `embedded_menu_restore` skipped itself (it needs `--run-gui`); `cua-driver-core` unit 1080 passed, 1 ignored, and 45 tests passed across its 16 integration test binaries; each crate's doc-tests 0 passed, 1 ignored; `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test` → 2 passed, 1 ignored; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core --lib --tests` reports nothing in the touched files (5 warnings elsewhere). Tests in `tools::invoke_menu::tests` cover the route decision (`menu_route`: background, behind the user's window, the key window, and an unreadable key window with the target in front, another window in front, or no front window), each refusal's code and escalation, the texts on each route, and the reuse of a held mutation lease. Breaking each rule (old path for any unknown key window, no front-window rule, background wording on the behind route, no held-lease check) fails a test.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. Reproducing it means making an app frontmost on a machine someone is using; I did not run the Lume harness.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the fork's `pull_request` workflows are waiting for maintainer approval, so no CI beyond CLA, contributor attribution and release reminder has run on this branch. Not run here (deterministic but outside these two crates, or desktop-bound): `cua-driver` `status_pid_file_cli_test`, the hermetic `cua-driver-e2e` tests, `embedded_menu_restore --run-gui`, and the desktop E2E matrix that `AGENTS.md` asks for on the candidate SHA before the PR is ready. The one that matters most is a desktop run (Lume) of `invoke_menu` on a second window of a frontmost TextEdit or Terminal, checking that the user's window keeps key and order, that `AXMainWindow` follows the key-window record so the press is not refused, and that the command lands in the target window.

title: fix(cua-driver): stamp window-local point on background click routes
body:
## Behavior

Background (pid-routed) mouse clicks on macOS were silently dropped for targets whose controls hit-test the physical cursor position. Root cause: the background click route received the target's window-local point but discarded it (`chromium_click_route_plan` stamped the *screen* point into `CGEventSetWindowLocation` for every event). AppKit's `NSWindow.sendEvent` hit-tests in **window-local** space, so a screen-space point lands outside the window and the event never reaches the control.

Measured invariant (ablation matrix, 16/16 clean runs, pointer byte-identical, host macOS 26): `CGEventSetWindowLocation` carrying the **window-local** point is the single necessary-and-sufficient component of background pid-post delivery; subtype, command-flag, fields 91/92, and the screen-space point are inert.

## Changes
- `chromium_click_route_plan` now stamps the window-local point on the public transport (SkyLight route itself unchanged).
- Transport selection by target class: Chromium-identity targets keep the SkyLight route byte-identical (they require it); plain targets take the public pid-post transport, which now stamps correctly.
- Focused unit tests for both selections and the route-plan stamp; doc comments state the invariant.
- New example `background_window_local_click.rs` used for the live transport probes.

## Validation
- `cargo build`; `cargo test -p platform-macos input::mouse` — 25 passed, including the new selection tests.
- Live matrix (macOS 26B5112a, dual display; pointer byte-identical + frontmost preserved on every run):
  - plain AppKit NSButton: public window-local **DELIVERED** ×2; SkyLight screen-point **DROPPED** ×2.
  - Chromium-class target (Brave, throwaway `--user-data-dir`, `file://` fixture button, AX read-back): SkyLight route through the new selection **DELIVERED** ×2; route attribution proven via `is_chromium_identity`.

## Known gaps
- The public transport is the fallback while the SkyLight SPI resolves, so the fixed public stamp is not exercised by the daemon's default path for Chromium-class targets on current macOS; for plain targets the new selection routes to it directly (live-verified).
- `cargo clippy` not run (clippy unavailable for the pinned toolchain 1.97.1 in our environment).
- Platform-scoped: `platform-macos` adapter only; other platform adapters untouched (per the cross-platform contract, this behavior change is macOS-specific and recorded as such).

Agent-assisted contribution: the opener has run the stated checks and can explain every hunk.

title: fix(cua-driver): name the AXWindows read error in ax_window_unresolved
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: when an app answers the `AXWindows` attribute with an error (`kAXErrorCannotComplete` while it is busy or showing a sheet, `kAXErrorAPIDisabled`, a messaging timeout), `copy_ax_windows` returns an empty list and `get_window_state` degrades with:

  ```
  ax_window_unresolved: window_id 3549 exists and is owned by pid 56350, but none of the
  0 AXWindow element(s) under that pid reports this CGWindowID. The tree is returned EMPTY ...
  ```

  That sentence blames the window for a read that never happened. The agent's natural next move is to re-snapshot the same window, while the app is not answering accessibility at all; the right move (wait, or dismiss the sheet) is not visible from the output.

- What changed: the `AXError` from the `AXWindows` read travels with the window-scope decision into `WindowScope::AxUnresolved`, and the degraded reason names it:

  ```
  ax_window_unresolved: window_id 3549 exists and is owned by pid 56350, but reading that
  pid's AXWindows failed with AXError -25204 (kAXErrorCannotComplete). The tree is returned EMPTY ...
  ```

  A clean read that lists no matching window keeps the existing wording. No field is added or renamed; only the `degraded_reason` text changes, and only in the error case.

How it threads through:

```
copy_ax_windows_or_error(app)            -> Result<Vec<AXUIElementRef>, AXError>
copy_ax_windows_including_or_error(..)   -> (Vec<AXUIElementRef>, Option<AXError>)
decide_window_scope(.., ax_windows_error, ..)
WindowScope::AxUnresolved { ax_window_count, ax_windows_error }
Degradation::AxWindowUnresolved { ax_window_count, ax_windows_error }
ax_window_unresolved_reason(window_id, pid, ax_window_count, ax_windows_error)
```

`copy_ax_windows` keeps its signature (`unwrap_or_default` over the new fallible read) so the other callers are untouched.

## Related work

Refs the `ax_window_unresolved` degradation introduced for Qt and Electron windows that do not publish their CGWindowID.

RFC: not required, no contract change (`degraded_reason` is free text).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Output changes only in the `degraded_reason` string, and only when `AXWindows` returned an error.
- Risk and rollback: low. The error branch produces exactly the empty list it produced before; only the explanation differs. Revert the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `an_ax_windows_read_error_survives_the_scope_decision` (`ax/window_scope.rs`) and `an_ax_windows_read_error_is_named_instead_of_a_zero_window_count` (`tools/get_window_state.rs`, through `degradation_for`), plus the existing `window_scope` and `get_window_state` tests updated for the new variant shape. `cargo test -p cua-driver-platform-macos`: 615 passed locally (macOS 15, Apple Silicon). `cargo fmt` and `clippy -D warnings` clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: the "none of the 0 AXWindow element(s)" sentence showed up on 0.34.1 for FreeCAD, Slack and Chess windows that visibly existed; on current `main` I still get `ax_window_unresolved` on Chrome while its consent sheet or omnibox popup is up, and on a Slack window parked on another space. I could not force an `AXError` on demand for an after receipt (a Chrome `alert()` keeps answering `AXWindows`), so the wording is covered by the unit test; a clean read on the same windows keeps the existing text on this branch.
- Known gaps or CI still required: macOS hosted E2E.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep browser refusal codes through protected scope attestation
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: browser refusals lose their code on the way out. Every browser tool proves its target before dispatch through `Tool::protected_resource_scope`. That hook returns `Result<_, String>`, so `browser_protected_resource_scope` flattens the `BrowserRefusal` it gets from `attest_protected_tab` to its message, and the authorization layer re-labels the string with whichever generic code fits the call site: `authorization_host_failed` for observations, `protected_resource_scope_invalid` for actions. A stale `target_id`, a browser process that exited, and a CDP `Page.getFrameTree` timeout on a hung page all come back under those two codes, with the real reason only in prose. A client that branches on `refusal.code` (rebind on `browser_binding_stale`, back off on a timeout) cannot, and has to grep the message.

  On the 0.36.0 release binary, with a `target_id` the daemon does not hold:

  ```
  $ cua-driver call get_browser_state '{"target_id":"bt-4f1c…","tab_id":"tab-9a2b…"}'
  { "refusal": { "code": "authorization_host_failed",
                 "message": "confirmation provider failed: target bt-4f1c… is not a live binding in this session — re-run get_browser_state with pid + window_id" } }

  $ cua-driver call browser_click '{"target_id":"bt-4f1c…","tab_id":"tab-9a2b…","ref":"p1:3"}'
  { "refusal": { "code": "protected_resource_scope_invalid",
                 "message": "target bt-4f1c… is not a live binding in this session — re-run get_browser_state with pid + window_id" } }
  ```

  The store minted `browser_binding_stale` for both; neither caller sees it.

- What changed: the hook gets a small error type that carries an optional code next to the message. `From<String>` keeps every existing `?` and `.ok_or_else(..)` site unchanged; `From<BrowserRefusal>` lets the browser attestation hand its code through. The authorization layer uses the carried code when there is one and falls back to today's generic codes otherwise, so non-browser attestations (process identity on `kill_app`, window identity on the desktop tools) answer exactly as before.

  ```rust
  pub struct ProtectedResourceScopeError {
      pub code: Option<&'static str>,
      pub message: String,
  }
  ```

  ```diff
   async fn protected_resource_scope(...) -> Result<Option<Value>, ProtectedResourceScopeError> {
  -    attest_protected_tab(..).await.map_err(|error| error.message)?;
  +    attest_protected_tab(..).await?;
  ```

  ```diff
  -    .map_err(|message| protected_scope_refusal(&message))?
  +    .map_err(|error| protected_scope_error_refusal(&error))?
   // protected_scope_error_refusal: error.code.unwrap_or("protected_resource_scope_invalid")
  ```

  ```diff
   ConsentError::Provider(_) => "authorization_host_failed",
  +ConsentError::ProtectedScope(error) => error.code.unwrap_or("authorization_host_failed"),
  ```

  Same two calls after:

  ```
  $ cua-driver call get_browser_state '{"target_id":"bt-4f1c…","tab_id":"tab-9a2b…"}'
  { "refusal": { "code": "browser_binding_stale",
                 "message": "target bt-4f1c… is not a live binding in this session — re-run get_browser_state with pid + window_id" } }

  $ cua-driver call browser_click '{"target_id":"bt-4f1c…","tab_id":"tab-9a2b…","ref":"p1:3"}'
  { "refusal": { "code": "browser_binding_stale",
                 "message": "target bt-4f1c… is not a live binding in this session — re-run get_browser_state with pid + window_id" } }
  ```

## Related work

Refs #4618 (dialog click), which also surfaces as a `Page.getFrameTree` timeout and today lands under the same two generic codes.

RFC: not required. No new code is introduced; codes the browser layer already mints (`browser_binding_stale` for an unknown or drifted binding, `browser_route_unavailable` for a `Page.getFrameTree` timeout, `browser_consent_revoked`, `browser_tab_not_found`) reach the caller instead of being overwritten. Callers matching on the two generic codes for browser tools will now see the specific one.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: all platforms, browser tools only. `refusal.code` becomes specific where it was generic. `refusal.message` keeps the browser layer's text; on the observation path it loses the `confirmation provider failed:` prefix that came with the generic code. Non-browser tools are unaffected (their attestations return plain strings, which still map to the old codes).
- Risk and rollback: low. The type change is mechanical and the compiler walked every implementor (core, macOS, Windows, Linux). Revert the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `a_stale_binding_keeps_its_refusal_code_through_scope_attestation` (`browser/v2_tests.rs`) registers the real browser tools in a `ToolRegistry` and invokes `get_browser_state` and `browser_click` on an unknown target; both answer `browser_binding_stale`. `a_plain_string_scope_error_keeps_the_generic_refusal_codes` (`tool.rs`) shows a plain-string scope error still gives `authorization_host_failed` and `protected_resource_scope_invalid`. `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`: 997 passed; `cargo check` for the macOS platform crate clean; `cargo fmt` and `clippy -D warnings` clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: receipts above, release binary vs this branch, macOS 15 Apple Silicon. `kill_app` on a foreign pid still answers `foreign_process_termination_denied` on this branch (non-browser attestation unchanged).
- Known gaps or CI still required: the Windows and Linux platform crates were updated by reading the compiler errors on macOS (`error.message` where a `String` was expected); I could not build them here, so their CI lanes are the check.

title: [Bug]: Windows skill path + urls example opens selected browser and default browser separately
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver / Documentation (Windows browser launch guidance)

### Summary

The Windows skill recommends `launch_app({path: "...msedge.exe", urls: [...]})` for opening a URL in a selected browser. On a machine whose default browser is Chrome, this starts Edge and opens the URL in Chrome, producing two browser windows rather than navigating the selected browser. The tool schema and implementation describe different semantics from the skill.

### Reproduction

1. On Windows, install both Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome, with Chrome as the default browser.
2. Through the persistent MCP connection, call:

```json
{
  "path": "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft\\Edge\\Application\\msedge.exe",
  "urls": ["https://example.com/"]
}
```

3. Inspect both browser windows and their process command lines.

The observed report used `https://news.ycombinator.com/` instead of `https://example.com/`.

### Expected behavior

Following the Windows skill's documented selected-browser navigation example should open the requested URL in Edge without also opening the default browser. The guidance, tool schema, and actual launch behavior should agree.

If `urls` intentionally always uses the default browser, please correct the skill to use the supported selected-process argument mechanism (`additional_arguments`) and explicitly warn against combining an app target with `urls` for selected-browser navigation.

### Actual behavior

- Edge starts, but the returned window remains on its existing/start page.
- Chrome starts with the requested URL.
- The MCP result reports the Edge process/window, without identifying the separate default-browser launch. An agent can therefore conclude incorrectly that it only opened Edge.

This was observed from a single `launch_app` call, before any subsequent browser setup or retry.

### Environment

- Windows 11, x86_64.
- Cua Driver 0.34.1, embedded direct stdio MCP (`mcp --direct --embedded`), via an Agent Plugin launcher that forwards this call unchanged.
- Installed browsers: Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome; Chrome is the default browser.
- The same launch code was inspected in `cua-driver-rs-v0.36.0` and current `main` (`075add55cf938f4e351b74539efa18d4976696ae`). This is source confirmation; I have not rerun the reproduction against the 0.36.0 binary.

### Evidence

The original MCP transcript records the selected Edge executable plus the URL in `urls`. Its result identifies Edge and a window titled `Google - ... - Microsoft Edge`. Process inspection shows Chrome starting at the time of that call with `--single-argument https://news.ycombinator.com/`. The Edge launch command line contains the driver's Chromium background flags but not that URL.

The source explains this behavior:

- [Windows skill, selected-browser omnibox navigation example](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/075add55cf938f4e351b74539efa18d4976696ae/libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/WINDOWS.md#L186-L197) recommends `path + urls` and the analogous AUMID form.
- [Windows tool schema](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-driver-rs-v0.36.0/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs#L2246-L2256) describes `urls` as opening in the default browser, while `additional_arguments` is passed to the selected process.
- [URL fan-out implementation](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-driver-rs-v0.36.0/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs#L2712-L2742) opens every URL separately through the shell when an app target was supplied. `first_unopened_shell_url_index(true)` returns 0.
- The same Windows skill's [file/URL-to-app mapping](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/075add55cf938f4e351b74539efa18d4976696ae/libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/WINDOWS.md#L352) uses `args`, whereas this tool schema declares `additional_arguments`; please align that example as part of correcting the selected-app launch guidance.

### Workaround and additional context

For the default browser, use `launch_app` with `urls` only. For a specific executable, the current schema provides `additional_arguments` for passing the URL to that executable instead of opening it through the default-browser association. The latter follows the inspected source; it has not yet been independently verified in this report's environment.

This report concerns selected-browser URL routing and its inconsistent documentation, not `browser_prepare`'s separate isolated-profile behavior.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: ci(spaces): reuse a prior run's native artifacts on a cache miss
body:
Refs #5224 — revised after #5299's review: the fallback now pins and verifies
the artifact it reuses instead of trusting a name match.

cd-cua-spaces keys each compiled native layer by the git tree hash of its
inputs, so a dry run of a commit should warm the release run of the same
commit. Every run still misses: the repository's Actions cache sits over its
10 GB cap, so a save is evicted long before an ~80-minute run finishes, and
dry runs on a feature branch save neither their caches nor their dependency
cache anywhere the tag run can see.

The jobs already upload the layer as `electron-native-<label>` /
`macos-rust-<arch>` artifacts on every run. On a cache miss we look up the
newest non-expired artifact a prior run of the same commit uploaded
(head_sha == GITHUB_SHA, excluding the current run), then pin its artifact
id, sha256 digest and producing run id. The zip is fetched by pinned artifact
id and the sha256 is verified before a byte lands in the tree — an artifact
without a digest, or one that fails verification, is refused and we build
normally. Any failure in the lookup, download, verification, or check —
including a partial download, which is removed — falls through to a normal
build. The artifact path also crosses the branch-to-tag cache-scope wall the
cache itself can't.

permissions: contents: read + actions: read on the three native jobs —
the artifact API needs actions: read, and job-level permissions replace the
workflow-wide contents: write, so contents: read is restated for checkout.

Validated: actionlint clean; the lookup run live against the repo's artifact
list (same-sha prior-run artifacts exist, pin and select correctly); the
restore run-block exercised verbatim against stubbed gh across digest-match,
digest-mismatch and download-failure paths. The path itself can't run until
the next cd-cua-spaces run; every failure mode degrades to today's rebuild.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep browser tools in the background (no tab activation)
body:
Fixes #5397

## What changed for users

Cua Driver no longer switches the tab you are looking at in Chrome when an agent works in another tab in the background. If an agent really needs to switch tabs, it has to ask for foreground delivery, and the result says the tab changed.

## Root cause

The typed browser tools were already background-safe. `get_browser_state`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_click` and `browser_type` reach an unselected tab by `tab_id` over CDP. They never call `Target.activateTarget` or `Page.bringToFront`, and no CDP call made in the background selected a tab or raised Chrome (results below).

The tab switching came from the native fallback. When the typed route was unavailable, for example because `get_browser_state` asked for `browser_prepare` or `browser_prepare` refused in the background, agents fell back to `get_window_state`. Chrome's accessibility tree only shows the selected tab's page, so to reach another tab the agent pressed that tab in the tab strip, or opened a URL with `launch_app`. Both change the tab the user sees. The driver allowed the background press and did not report it. The `browser_prepare` refusal and the `not_rendered` hint also told agents to select the tab.

## Fix

- On macOS, a background `click` (element token or pixel) on an unselected tab in a Chromium tab strip now refuses before sending anything, with `browser_tab_switch_refused`. The refusal points to `get_browser_state` and the typed tools with the tab's `tab_id`. Page widgets with `role="tab"` (inside the `AXWebArea`), the already selected tab, and tabs whose selection state is unknown are not affected.
- A click with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` still selects the tab. Its summary now ends with "This selected another browser tab, so the tab the user sees changed.", and the legacy payload carries `side_effects.selected_browser_tab: true`.
- `run_steps` does not auto-retry this refusal in the foreground, because it does not recommend foreground.
- The `browser_prepare` background refusal, the `not_rendered` snapshot hint and `BROWSER.md` now say that the native route only sees the selected tab, and that selecting another tab needs the user's agreement.

Windows and Linux are unchanged. Their native click paths do not have this guard yet.

## Tests

- Unit tests for the tab-strip decision and the foreground report (`platform-macos`, `browser_tab_strip`).
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (619 passed) and `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib browser` (240 passed).

## Live results (macOS, Chrome 155, separate throwaway profiles)

Tab A was selected and Finder was frontmost before each step. The oracle read each tab's `document.visibilityState` over CDP and the frontmost app with `lsappinfo`.

| Step on tab B | Released 0.35.2 | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background AX click on tab B in the tab strip (`run_steps` click by role and name) | **Tab B became selected**, reported as plain success | Refused with `browser_tab_switch_refused`, tab A still selected |
| `get_browser_state` bind and snapshot, `browser_navigate`, `browser_click` (`dom_event`), `browser_type` | Tab A stayed selected, Finder stayed in front, and the actions took effect in B | Same |
| `browser_click` (trusted) | Refused, as before | Clicked in B, tab A stayed selected |

Raw CDP against a hidden tab didn't select it or raise Chrome either. The calls tested were `Runtime.evaluate`, `DOM.getDocument`, `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, `Page.captureScreenshot`, trusted mouse clicks under focus emulation (including on a `<select>` and a handler that calls `window.focus()`), `Input.insertText` and key events, `DOM.focus` and `Page.navigate`.

`Page.startScreencast` does not make a hidden tab render in Chrome 155, so it is not a way around `not_rendered`.

## Still foreground-only

- Rendering a background tab Chrome has never painted (`not_rendered`) still needs the user to select it.
- Attaching to the user's own Chrome on the same Space still shows Chrome's "Allow remote debugging?" prompt in front, so `browser_prepare` refuses in the background unless `delivery_mode:"foreground"` is used.
- `launch_app` with a URL in a running browser opens a new selected tab. It is now documented, not blocked.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cua-driver): Windows list_windows omits the driver's own overlay windows
body:
On Windows, `list_windows` now omits the driver's own windows, such as the full-screen agent-cursor overlay.

**Why.** The overlay is a top-level window of the driver's own process, so `list_windows` returned it like an app window. macOS already drops the driver's own pid (#4916), and the docs say the overlay is omitted. Windows now does the same, before `z_index` is assigned, so `z_index` stays contiguous. The tool description now says the overlay is omitted.

**Testing.**
- A unit test checks that the driver's windows are dropped and that `z_index` stays contiguous.
- On a Windows test VM with the overlay on, `list_windows` returned 6 windows before (one was the overlay) and 5 after, with contiguous `z_index`.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes on this branch. On windows-2025, with this change and our other pending driver fixes on current main, `cargo clippy -p platform-windows --all-targets` reports the same 44 findings as main (none new), and `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib` passes (284 passed, 0 failed).

title: fix(cua-driver): keep install.ps1 from aborting after a successful cosign check (re-authored #5245)
body:
Windows PowerShell 5.1 turns a native command's redirected stderr into error records. install.ps1 runs with `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`, and cosign prints `Verified OK` on stderr. So with cosign on PATH, or with `-RequireSignature`, a signature that verified still aborted the install with NativeCommandError before anything was staged.

`Assert-ReleaseZipIntegrity` now relaxes the error preference to `Continue` for the cosign call only (save, try, finally restore) and still decides on `$LASTEXITCODE`, so a failed verification is still refused. The Windows installer harness imports the real function and runs it against two `cosign.cmd` stand-ins. One prints `Verified OK` to stderr and exits 0, and it must reach the Sigstore success step. The other fails, and it must be refused without logging success.

Salvaged from #5245 (originally #5061 by @sly321-pixel). Fixes #5058.

Proof:
- On this head, `windows-uninstall` in CI: Test Scripts runs `install-common-windows-regression.ps1` under `powershell.EXE` (5.1) and prints "Windows installer cosign check accepted a verified zip and refused an unverified one."
- Locally under PowerShell 7 on macOS, the extracted `Assert-ReleaseZipIntegrity` accepts a cosign stand-in that writes to stderr and exits 0, and refuses one that exits 1. Both PowerShell files parse cleanly.
- All PR checks are green on this head.

title: fix(cua-driver): stamp the window-local point on macOS 27 background clicks
body:
## Behavior change

On macOS 27 and later, background pixel left-clicks (`click` / `double_click` with `x, y`, the `synthetic_events` route) stamp `CGEventSetWindowLocation` with the window-local point instead of the screen point. Earlier macOS releases keep the screen point, unchanged.

## Why

On macOS 27.0.1 (26A434) WindowServer hands the stamp to the target as its window-local point. With the screen point stamped, every background pixel click landed shifted by the window's origin:

- A plain AppKit probe window at screen (600, 429), 400×600, was clicked at capture (200, 400), which is local point (100, 200). `NSApplication.sendEvent` logged `locationInWindow = (700, -29)`, `cgEvent.location = (700, 629)`, `windowNumber` = the probe. That is `(screen_x, height - screen_y)`, outside the view, so `mouseDown` never fired.
- A GPUI app (no AX tree, so every click takes this route) with its window at (0, 39) hit the row 39 pt below the target. After the window was moved to (100, 300), clicks missed it entirely.
- Chrome Canary (fresh profile, page logging `mousedown` client coordinates; double-click to force the pixel route): with the screen-point stamp no event arrived. With the window-local stamp it logged `client=200,200`, exactly the target.

With the window-local stamp, all three hit exactly. The titled AppKit window got (100, 168) in view coordinates, which is the target minus the 32 pt title bar, as expected.

## Scope and gaps

- The macOS ≤ 26 path is untouched because I could not test it there. `capture_bound_background_route_preserves_nonzero_origin_hit` still pins the screen-point plan for those releases.
- `drag_at_xy` also stamps the screen point (`step.point`), so it probably has the same problem on macOS 27. It is not changed or verified here.
- The version check reads `kern.osproductversion` once (`sw_vers_product_version`, which is now `pub(crate)`).

## Validation

- Ran `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 614 passed, including the new `macos_27_route_stamps_the_window_local_point`.
- Live test on macOS 27.0.1 with a locally built driver in embedded mode: AppKit plain window, AppKit full-size-content window, Chrome Canary and a GPUI app. Each was tried with both stamps.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-macos -- -D warnings` reports pre-existing lints only, in `reveal_scroll.rs`, `click.rs` and `document_edit.rs`. None are in the changed files.

title: fix(cua-driver): verify existing-profile CDP readiness
body:
## Summary

- `browser_prepare(existing_profile)` currently treats a completed WebSocket handshake as readiness, even when the socket cannot complete a CDP command.
- Probe with the already-allowed, read-only `Target.getTargets` before either the initial claim or the one permitted retry can report success. Discard the response.
- Release only the preparing generation on probe error or cancellation. Preserve peer-held shared connections; a later claim redials when the failed probe was the last holder.
- Add four regressions through `BrowserPrepareTool`, using loopback TCP/WebSockets and scripted CDP responses.

## Related work

Fixes #5446.

Retains the consent/retry behavior from #3288 and shared-socket ownership from #5115. This is a small, currently unselected bug-fix contribution submitted for maintainer review.

Adapted from [loonghao's original liveness commit](https://github.com/loonghao/cua/commit/c8be5551dd262d886fca08528792aa6995460dcb) and the shared-generation correction in [loonghao/cua#7](https://github.com/loonghao/cua/pull/7). The landing commit is a new adaptation: it preserves source links, original author/date metadata in its message, and the original author's coauthor credit. It adds cancellation cleanup and stronger public-seam tests.

## Compatibility and risk

- No new public request parameters, response shapes, refusal codes, consent authority, endpoint scope, or CDP methods.
- Healthy preparation adds one read-only CDP round trip. The current consent observation and CDP timeout policies remain unchanged.
- A silent socket can be refused by the existing consent path before the CDP timeout. A peer-held socket is intentionally retained, so a retry does not always imply a new physical connection.
- Cleanup here covers the pending probe's socket hold. General whole-prepare grant cancellation and cancellation cleanup of the CDP pending-response map are outside this change.
- Rollback is a revert of this focused patch.

## Validation

Base: `trycua/cua@5df19ea9`. Published head: `8194ada2`. The published tree exactly matches the locally tested candidate tree `3e067822f87a26c9a58fe9c6c578ba0e5fcbc3c0`.

- Removing the pending-probe cleanup makes the cancellation regression fail.
- Reverting only the retry callsite to plain `claim_existing` makes the accepted-consent retry regression fail with false success.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::`: 229 passed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --test '*'`: 28 passed across 13 integration binaries.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed on Rust 1.97.1.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib`: 989 passed, 13 failed, 1 ignored. The same 13 perception-worker tests fail on untouched official `5df19ea9` (985 passed, 13 failed, 1 ignored), because this cloud kernel does not provide the required Landlock containment. The failing-test sets are identical; this is not a clean full-suite pass.
- Exact-head hosted CLA, contributor-attribution, and release-reminder checks pass. The 19 code/test workflows are `action_required`, awaiting maintainer approval for this fork; for example [quick feedback](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/39181568653) and [Windows unit tests](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/39181568673).

These tests use real loopback transport but simulated platform/CDP behavior. No real Chrome/Edge, Windows UIA, or desktop acceptance is claimed. Hosted code/test CI and maintainer/native review remain pending; this PR stays draft.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop re-sending input that may already have landed
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On Linux, an AT-SPI `EditableText` write or `doAction` can be sent and then fail with an error reply, or not answer within its budget, after the application has already acted on it. The driver often treated that as "nothing delivered". Within the same call it moved on to the next route: `SetTextContents` after a failed `InsertText`, a second write after `GrabFocus`, the same index re-resolved in a fresh walk, another hit-test tier, key events, or a pointer click. Or it returned a result that invites sending again: `background_unavailable` with `escalation.recommended: "foreground"` and `Retry this action with delivery_mode:"foreground"` (element-token `type_text` on Wayland, the background pixel click on Wayland and X11), `element_bounds_unavailable` with "no input was sent" (an X11 foreground element click on an element without usable bounds), or a `menu_path_unavailable` refusal from `invoke_menu`. That last one also happened when nothing failed: `invoke_menu` waited on the last menu item's action with no bound of its own, and a GTK item whose command opens a dialog answers only once the dialog closes, so the call ran into the 25 s operation timeout. A cleanup step sent after the input could also replace its outcome: a failed synthetic FocusOut in the Qt5 workaround turned a delivered write into an X11 error, after which the next route wrote the text again, and a failed Escape after a `set_value` combo-box pick turned the pick into an error. The browser consent and remote-debugging setup flows turned an action that may have acted into a refusal before reading the UI back, so a checkbox toggle that may have landed was never recorded for rollback. `run_steps` with `foreground_fallback: true` replays results that carry the foreground hint; it also replayed a token click's `ax_timeout` on Wayland and the Windows UIA pixel click whose provider failed or timed out (`effect: "unverifiable"`; its own text asks the caller to inspect state first). Either way, text could be typed twice or a control clicked twice. Separately, Hyprland isolated background input that stopped after two or more acknowledged keys or wheel packets was reported as `refused` with its delivered count removed, which reads as "nothing was sent".
- What changed:
  - Linux: an `EditableText` write that fails or times out after it was sent, and a `doAction` that gets an error reply, are marked as possibly landed where the request is sent. Every caller checks that mark before any fallback or refusal of its own, the X11 foreground click on an element without usable bounds included.
  - Such a call ends in an error with `effect: "unverifiable"` and `delivery: {"mode": "unknown"}`, the action-result shape the Hyprland foreground click already returns when its AT-SPI outcome is unknown. It has no `background_unavailable` code, no `suggestion`, no `refusal` and no `escalation`, and its text asks the caller to read the target back before sending again. Refusals raised before anything is sent keep their codes and the foreground hint.
  - A `doAction` that does not answer counts as dispatched in every at-point hit-test tier, the passive fallback (a label) included, so the full-walk tier never runs after it. Only a declined action falls through.
  - `invoke_menu` bounds the last menu item's action like every other action. If it does not answer, the call succeeds with `effect: "unverifiable"` and says so; an error reply ends in the unknown-outcome error; only a declined action is still refused.
  - The browser consent and remote-debugging setup flows count an action that may have acted as sent and read the UI back, as they already do after an accepted one.
  - A cleanup step that fails after the input was sent no longer replaces the input's outcome. A failed FocusOut in the Qt5 workaround, or a failed Escape after a `set_value` combo pick, becomes a warning sentence at the end of the result text. A successful write or pick stays a success, and the dispatcher's action-result projection carries that text as `summary`, so the warning reaches `structuredContent` only there, with no `warning` key. The one error result that can carry the warning is a Qt5 workaround write that may have landed: it stays the unknown-outcome error above, and its `structuredContent` also has a `warning` key. A combo pick that fails is reported as before, without the warning.
  - A token click's `ax_timeout` keeps its code and `effect: "unknown"` and drops its escalation. Its text asks for a screenshot before any retry.
  - `run_steps` replays a step with `foreground_fallback` only when the failed result shows nothing was delivered: no `effect` or one of `refused`, `none` and macOS `no_drop`, and no `delivery`. Any other effect, `suspected_noop` and values the rule does not know included, is not replayed.
  - Hyprland isolated background input interrupted after N ≥ 2 acknowledged keys or packets reports `effect: "partial"` with `delivery.delivered_count: N`, as a single key and every foreground count already did.
  - Unchanged: a `doAction` that never answers is still reported as dispatched with `effect: "unverifiable"`.

## Related work

No issue is filed for this. Refs #5431: its description lists these results as a known gap in the driver, and its `WORKFLOW.md` rule says that on Linux/Wayland `background_unavailable` can follow an AT-SPI write or action that already ran, and that Hyprland isolated input can report `refused` after delivering part of a text. With this change both clauses describe the old behavior; whichever of the two merges second should update them. The rule itself (fresh state before re-sending) still holds.

Interaction with the other open pull requests:

- #5430 (keep GNOME element actions inside the requested window): eight textual conflicts. Three are in `tools/impl_.rs`: the Hyprland foreground token write, and two in the `set_value` keyboard fallback, which #5430 moves to its token element. Two are in `atspi/mod.rs`, where #5430 replaces `perform_action_in` and `type_into_editable_at`; three are in the browser consent and setup flows, where #5430 switches to `perform_action_walked`. Two rules must carry over, and whichever pull request lands second adds them. #5430's `TokenElement::act` re-resolves the index after the observed object fails when `may_reresolve` is set; it must instead return the error when that error reports input that may have landed. Its browser consent and setup calls (`perform_action_walked`) need the same read-back wrapper as the calls they replace.
- #5431 is stacked on #5430 and conflicts the same way, in addition to the docs clauses above.
- #5429 and #5370 change other files and merge cleanly with this branch.

RFC: not needed in my reading. `rfcs/README.md` does not require an RFC for small bug fixes, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` lets a small, self-contained fix go straight to a focused pull request. These are bug fixes on error paths: tool schemas, descriptions and refusal codes are unchanged, and the new results use existing action-result values. Success results gain no field: when a cleanup step fails after a successful write or pick, the warning is a sentence in the result text, which success results already carry as `summary`. The one added key is `warning` on the error result of a Qt5 workaround write that may have landed when its FocusOut also failed; the dispatcher neither projects nor validates error results against the action-result contract. Clients do get different results on these paths:

- A Linux AT-SPI write or action that failed after it was sent: an error with `effect: "unverifiable"` and `delivery: {"mode": "unknown"}`, instead of `background_unavailable` with the foreground hint, `element_bounds_unavailable` with `effect: "none"`, or a `menu_path_unavailable` refusal. The call no longer tries a second route.
- `invoke_menu` whose last action does not answer in time: a success with `effect: "unverifiable"` after a few seconds, instead of a `menu_path_unavailable` refusal after 25 s.
- A token click's `ax_timeout`: no `escalation`.
- Hyprland isolated input interrupted after two or more keys or packets: `effect: "partial"` with `delivered_count`, instead of `refused`.
- `type_text` through the Qt5 workaround and `set_value` on a combo box, when the cleanup step fails after the write or pick: the write's or pick's own result instead of an error. On success the warning is the last sentence of `summary`. A Qt5 write that may have landed returns the unknown-outcome error above, with a `warning` key in its `structuredContent`.
- The browser remote-debugging consent and setup flows: the UI readback decides, instead of an immediate refusal.
- `run_steps` with `foreground_fallback`: no replay of a failed step whose result does not show that nothing was delivered.

If maintainers read any of this as a contract change, I will open an RFC before this goes further.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux changes, plus one shared `run_steps` rule; the result changes are listed under RFC above. On X11 the pointer or key-event fallback no longer runs after such a failure. `run_steps` on Windows no longer replays the UIA pixel click whose provider failed or timed out. Every other foreground-hinted error result on macOS and Windows has `effect` `refused` or `no_drop`, or no `effect` at all, so their replay is unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: The marking is conservative. An error reply after which the toolkit in fact did nothing now reports an unknown outcome instead of trying another route, so the caller re-reads state before deciding. In the browser setup flows the readback that follows an accepted action now also follows such a failure, with the same deadline and fallbacks. Reverting the commits restores the previous behavior.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `atspi::native::input_dispatch_tests` serves a fake `org.a11y.atspi.EditableText`, `org.a11y.atspi.Action` and passive `label` accessibles on a private `dbus-daemon`, skipping when it is absent, like the shell helper transport test. An `InsertText` that raises, or that does not answer within the budget, reaches the field once and is reported as possibly landed; a declined insert still falls back to `SetTextContents`; a `doAction` error reply is reported as possibly landed. A passive label whose action does not answer, is accepted, or raises is a hit (or the possibly-landed error), and the full-walk tier never runs; a declined one falls through to it. The last menu action is never refused unless declined.
  - `atspi_input_that_may_have_landed_is_reported_without_a_retry_hint`: the text, click, menu and `ax_timeout` results carry no `background_unavailable` code, refusal, suggestion or escalation, and the text, click and menu results equal their public action result.
  - `a_boundless_foreground_click_whose_action_may_have_landed_is_not_refused`, `a_failed_focus_out_never_hides_a_write_that_was_sent` (delivered and possibly-landed writes with a failing FocusOut), `a_failed_popup_close_never_turns_a_pick_into_an_error` and `an_action_that_may_have_acted_is_read_back_not_refused`.
  - `isolated_hyprland_refused_partial_and_unknown_outcomes_stay_distinct` gains a background text interrupted after three keys: `partial` with `delivered_count: 3`.
  - `a_step_whose_input_may_have_landed_is_never_replayed`: `run_steps` with `foreground_fallback` sends each step once whose result reports `unverifiable`, `unknown`, `partial`, `suspected_noop`, an unknown effect, or a refusal with a `delivery` record, and still replays a step refused before sending, including macOS `no_drop`.
  - Negative controls: putting the previous rule back into each owning function, or breaking each new guard, makes its test fail (14 controls; each test run exits 101).
  - CI parity at `8c31dc9b1`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes. `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p platform-linux --all-targets --locked` passes (1702 passed, 31 ignored). The full Linux CI line `cargo test -p cua-driver -p cua-driver-e2e -p cua-driver-contract -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver-testkit -p cursor-overlay -p cursor-theme-cli -p platform-linux --all-targets --locked --no-fail-fast` gives 2482 passed and 126 ignored, with `platform-linux` 667 and `cua-driver-core` 999 library tests passing. Three tests fail locally in the two perception binaries (`perception_cli_test`, `perception_capture_loop_test`): their fixture worker links as a static PIE and this machine has no static glibc (`unable to find library -lc`). The CLI one fails the same way at the base commit.
  - `cargo check -p cua-driver --features portal-input --locked` passes.
- Manual or platform evidence: a release build with `portal-input` ran read-only on GNOME Shell 50 under Wayland (Fedora 44): `--version`, `doctor`, `serve`, `list_windows` and `stop`. No input was sent, so the changed paths were not exercised on a live desktop; the fake-bus tests exercise the AT-SPI calls.
- Known gaps or CI still required: The marker checks at the tool call sites, in `atspi/mod.rs` and in the browser flows are one-line guards on tested helpers. They have no hermetic test of their own, because reaching them needs a live AT-SPI tree. The desktop E2E matrix was not run. The 12 s deadline around a foreground X11 action still reports `foreground_timeout` with `effect: "none"`; every bounded phase inside it ends sooner, so it fires only when the X server or the blocking pool stalls, and its text asks for a screenshot first. Out of scope and unchanged: the `set_value` value writes and keyboard fallback (they replace the whole value, so a repeat does not duplicate text), combo-box option picks that fail, AT-SPI scroll, and Hyprland's unknown-dispatch result, which keeps the `background_unavailable` code with `effect` and `delivery` stating the outcome and no hint.

title: cua-driver (macOS): drag-and-drop in native apps without taking the user's pointer
body:
**Problem:** native AppKit drag-and-drop is tracked by macOS with the real pointer, so a background drag currently refuses ("drop did not land"). Tasks that need a native drag can't be completed in the background.

**Proposal:** investigate background options (accessibility-driven moves where the app supports them, synthesized dragging sessions, app-specific APIs). Where no background route exists, see the companion issue for a permitted, brief foreground fallback.

**Done when:** there is either a working background route for common native drag cases with tests, or a documented, tested decision to use the foreground fallback.

title: ci: pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs, enforce it, add lefthook pre-push guard
body:
## What changed

- Every external GitHub Action in `.github/workflows` and `.github/actions` is now pinned to a full commit SHA, with the old tag kept as a trailing comment (`uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`). That is 347 references in 86 files. The SHAs are the ones the repo already used for `checkout`, `setup-node`, `setup-python`, `rust-toolchain` and the rest; the only new lookup was `actions/github-script@v7`.
- `.github/scripts/check_actions_pinned.sh` fails when an external action is not SHA-pinned. `ci-lint-workflows` runs it on every workflow change, so new unpinned refs can't land.
- `.github/dependabot.yml` opens one grouped PR a month to bump the pinned SHAs and their comments.

- Optional lefthook pre-push hook (`lefthook.yml`, `scripts/hooks/pre-push-guard.sh`). Before a push leaves the machine it refuses: a push to `main` on trycua/cua; history whose root commit is not cua's (another repo's history); a push of more than 300 new commits (`CUA_ALLOW_LARGE_PUSH=1` overrides); likely secrets in the new commits (gitleaks, high-confidence provider rules only); tailnet hostnames in added lines; and any unpinned Action. Install with `brew install lefthook gitleaks && scripts/hooks/install.sh`, not `lefthook install`: the script never writes into a global `core.hooksPath` (where `lefthook install --force` would overwrite the shared push guards). With a hooksPath set it adds a pre-push hook to the repo's own hooks directory, which the shared dispatcher chains to, and runs lefthook with `--no-auto-install`. Documented in CONTRIBUTING.

## Why

A tag can be moved by whoever controls the action's repo, and the workflows here run with release and signing secrets. Pinning removes that supply-chain path. This is part of the GitHub org hardening after the 13 Oct leak (CUA-1886). `trycua/cloud` was already fully pinned.

## User impact

None. Workflows run the same code as before.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep browser attestation off the renderer while a dialog is open
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `browser_dialog` cannot reach a tab that has a JavaScript dialog open. Every browser tool proves the tab's live top-level origin before it runs, and that proof asked the renderer for `Page.getFrameTree`. A page-owned `alert`, `confirm` or `prompt` blocks the renderer, so the one tool meant to resolve the dialog waited out the 20 s CDP deadline and refused:

  ```
  $ echo '{"target_id":"bt-…","tab_id":"tab-…","action":"inspect"}' | cua-driver call browser_dialog
  { "refusal": { "code": "authorization_host_failed",
      "message": "confirmation provider failed: could not prove the live top-level browser document: CDP Page.getFrameTree timed out after 20s" } }
    took 20.4s
  ```

  A second problem sits behind it. Chromium reports a dialog only to CDP sessions that enabled the Page domain *before* the dialog opened. Only `browser_dialog` itself enabled it, so a dialog raised by a trusted click, a timer or the person was invisible to the driver even once the proof got out of the way.

- What changed:

  1. While a dialog is known to be open on the tab, the origin proof reads the browser process's own record of the target instead of asking the blocked renderer. `Target.getTargetInfo` answers while a dialog is up, and the document cannot navigate until the dialog is handled, so the record is current. The method joins the existing-profile allowlist (read-only, same data as `Target.getTargets`).

     ```rust
     let (method, params, session, pointer) = if conn.dialog_state(cdp_target_id).is_some() {
         ("Target.getTargetInfo", json!({ "targetId": cdp_target_id }), None, "/targetInfo/url")
     } else {
         ("Page.getFrameTree", json!({}), Some(cdp_session), "/frameTree/frame/url")
     };
     ```

  2. The first session attached to a tab enables Page events on behalf of every later caller (tab sessions stay attached for the life of the connection). The enable has a 2 s deadline so a renderer already blocked by an unseen dialog cannot stall the attach; `browser_dialog` keeps its own enable as the retry for that case.

     ```
     browser_click / browser_type / get_browser_state snapshot / browser_dialog
       └─ revalidate_for_mutation
            └─ attach(tab)  ──►  Target.attachToTarget
                                 Page.enable (once per tab, 2 s cap)   <- new
     page opens confirm()  ──►  Page.javascriptDialogOpening  journaled for the tab
     browser_dialog        ──►  attestation via Target.getTargetInfo  <- new
                                Page.handleJavaScriptDialog
     ```

  Observable behavior: after any tool has touched the tab, a dialog opened by the page is inspected and resolved in under a second instead of refusing after 20 s.

## Related work

Refs #3982, which asked for Page events to be enabled before the click rather than on the first `browser_dialog` call. #4618 handles the other half of that issue (returning from a `dom_event` click whose handler opens a dialog); the two are independent and compose, since the dialog tool's own enable is skipped when a session already subscribed.

RFC: not required, no contract change. One read-only method added to the existing-profile allowlist.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: none in the API. Every tab attach now sends one extra `Page.enable` the first time a tab is touched on a connection. Embedded hosts without the Page domain answer it with an error, which is ignored.
- Risk and rollback: the attestation source changes only while a dialog is journaled for the tab. Revert the commit to restore the previous path.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`: 1075 passed (224 in `browser::`)
  - `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --tests`, `cargo fmt --check`: clean (pre-existing warnings only)
  - New test `an_open_dialog_moves_the_origin_proof_off_the_blocked_renderer` (`v2_tests.rs`): with a dialog journaled, the protected-scope attestation for `browser_click` proves the origin through `Target.getTargetInfo`, never asks `Page.getFrameTree`, and two tool calls produce exactly one `Page.enable`. Fails on main with `could not prove the live top-level browser document: CDP Page.getFrameTree failed`.

- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 15.8, Chrome with a throwaway profile, embedded daemon with `--grant existing-profile`, page with `setTimeout(() => alert("hello from the page"), 9000)`; `browser_prepare` + `get_browser_state`, one `browser_dialog inspect` before the alert so a tab session exists, then `inspect` and `accept` after it opens):

  | step | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `browser_dialog inspect`, alert open | `Page.getFrameTree timed out after 20s`, 20.4 s | `{"present": true, "kind": "alert", "dialog_id": "dialog-1"}`, 0.7 s |
  | `browser_dialog accept` | `Page.getFrameTree timed out after 20s`, 20.4 s | `{"action": "accept", "status": "ok"}`, 0.8 s |

  <details><summary>Receipt on this branch</summary>

  ```
  --- before the alert: browser_dialog inspect (first attach)
  { "present": false, "status": "ok", ... }   took 0.8s
  --- alert open: browser_dialog inspect
  { "dialog_id": "dialog-1", "kind": "alert", "present": true, "status": "ok", ... }   took 0.7s
  --- alert open: browser_dialog accept
  { "action": "accept", "dialog_id": "dialog-1", "kind": "alert", "status": "ok", ... }   took 0.8s
  ```
  </details>

- Known gaps or CI still required: a dialog that opens before *any* tool has attached to the tab (bind alone does not attach) is still unreachable: Chromium will not report it to a session that enables Page afterwards, so the enable times out (2 s) and the proof still waits on `Page.getFrameTree` (20 s), measured at 22.4 s on this branch versus 20.4 s on main. Closing that requires subscribing at bind time, which means attaching a session to the tab from `get_browser_state`; I left that out of this change since it touches the observation-only posture of the bind and is better decided by the maintainers. Browser e2e lanes still need to run on the maintainers' runners.

title: fix(cua-driver): list bound tabs in the order the browser reports them
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `get_browser_state` in bind mode lists the tabs of the bound window in `HashMap` iteration order. Six binds of the same untouched four-tab window on main:

  ```
  $ echo '{"pid":25494,"window_id":6964,"session":"s"}' | cua-driver call get_browser_state   # x6
  tabs: [four, one*, two, three]
  tabs: [three, one*, two, four]
  tabs: [three, four, two, one*]
  tabs: [one*, two, three, four]
  tabs: [one*, three, two, four]
  tabs: [two, three, one*, four]
  ```

  A caller that picks "the second tab" or diffs two binds gets a different answer each time, and nothing in the output says which order is the tab strip.

- What changed: the bound target keeps its tabs in an `IndexMap`, so the record preserves the order `Target.getTargets` returned them and the bind output lists them that way every time. Same six binds on this branch:

  ```
  tabs: [one*, two, three, four]   (x6, matches the tab strip)
  ```

  ```diff
  -    pub tabs: HashMap<String, TabRecord>,
  +    pub tabs: IndexMap<String, TabRecord>,
  ```

  Tab ids are still minted per bind, which is deliberate (they are session capabilities), so this only fixes the order, not identity across binds.

## Related work

No open issue or PR covers this. `indexmap` is already in the lockfile through `cursor-overlay`; this adds it as a direct dependency of `cua-driver-core`.

RFC: not required, no contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: the `tabs` array of a bind keeps the same shape; only its order becomes deterministic. No new field, no id change.
- Risk and rollback: type swap with identical lookup API; every `tabs.get`/`get_mut` site compiles unchanged. Revert the commit to go back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`: 1075 passed (224 in `browser::`)
  - `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --tests`, `cargo fmt --check`: clean on the touched files
  - New test `bound_tabs_keep_the_browser_order_across_binds` (`v2_tests.rs`): a window with five page targets binds twice and lists them in `Target.getTargets` order both times, the selected one first. On main it fails with
    ```
    left:  ["https://fixture.test/", "https://tab4.test/", "https://tab5.test/", "https://tab2.test/", "https://tab3.test/"]
    right: ["https://fixture.test/", "https://tab2.test/", "https://tab3.test/", "https://tab4.test/", "https://tab5.test/"]
    ```

title: feat(cua-driver): add a niri compositor adapter for Linux Wayland
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on niri, cua-driver could take screenshots and list windows, but every pointer, keyboard and focus action refused with `foreground_unavailable`. Window capture came back 0x0, and a 1.5 scale read as 1.0.
- What changed: a niri adapter in `platform-linux/src/wayland/niri/`, held to the Sway row's contract in `action-support.md`, and a nested niri lane in the Linux Wayland E2E matrix.

On niri 25.08 and later:

- Windows are found, activated and focused through niri IPC, after checking that the IPC socket belongs to the compositor serving `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`.
- Floating windows get window capture and window-coordinate input once the layout has been quiet for 1 s.
- Tiled windows (niri's default) have no position in IPC (niri-wm/niri#4369), so window-coordinate input on them refuses and points to `get_desktop_state`. Desktop-scope input uses the latest desktop screenshot and refuses after niri reports a layout or focus change.
- Typing uses niri's own keymap. Characters the layout lacks go on spare keys of a temporary keymap, restored afterwards. No wtype.
- Input and capture refuse while logind reports the session locked.

The adapter talks to `$NIRI_SOCKET` directly, with deadlines, instead of using the `niri-ipc` crate, which pins one niri version. There is no shared compositor trait yet.

The diff is +15k/-1k across 50 files; about 4,200 added lines are the E2E lane, harness and CI.

## Related work

Refs #3735

RFC: none; @f-trycua asked for a draft PR in #3735, with @injaneity reviewing. The only schema change is click `count` gaining `maximum: 3`, which the routes already enforced.

## Compatibility and risk

Changes outside niri:

- `cua-driver-core` `tool.rs`: the desktop lock becomes an owned `DesktopLease`. A Linux input worker that outlives its call keeps it until it stops, so the next action can't overlap leftover input. A waiter gives up after 12 s with `input_busy`. A worker that never returns, because the compositor or X server stopped answering, keeps later actions refusing until the driver restarts. macOS and Windows take and drop the lease where they took and dropped the lock.
- Every Linux worker that sends Wayland or X11 input runs under `spawn_blocking_bounded` with its call's budget. Most had no time limit before; a structural test fails on a new unbounded one.
- A held mouse button is released or tracked through cancellation, panics and failed releases.
- Click `count` is clamped to 1 to 3 and drag steps to 1 to 200, on X11 too. The Wayland drag path uses i64, so extreme coordinates no longer overflow on Sway or Hyprland.
- Compositor peer attestation moved from `hyprland.rs` to `compositor_peer.rs` without behaviour changes.
- zbus gains `blocking-api`, and `xkbcommon` 0.9 is no longer optional.
- The Wayland E2E runner gives each session its own session bus and keyring, unsets inherited compositor sockets, and bounds startup and cleanup.

Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

Fork CI passed on every Linux, macOS and Windows workflow before the rebase onto current `main`; this PR's CI covers the head. On the niri and Sway lanes, all 132 declared outcomes held (84 deliveries and 48 exact refusals on niri). Locally, `platform-linux` unit tests pass except upstream's Xvfb test, which needs Xvfb.

The niri lane runs niri's winit backend in a headless `cage` (`nix develop .#cua-driver-niri-e2e`) with one 1920x1080 output, floating windows, a US keymap and animations off. Tiled windows, the `us,de` keymap, the lock check and the drag rules are covered by unit tests and nested smokes.

I also ran it on my own niri 26.04 desktop (2560x1440, `focus-follows-mouse` on) against GTK 3, kitty and Chromium, twice, the second time at this head. Text arrived exactly, no click hit the wrong window, and the refusals matched. The first run found three bugs and the second found the `€` one; all are fixed here.

### Limits

- No background input: niri has no per-window capture protocol and no RemoteDesktop/libei.
- IPC reports where a window will be, not where an animation draws it. Animations longer than 1 s can misplace a click; niri's defaults are shorter.
- Overlapping floating windows refuse the affected point, since IPC has no stacking order. Bars and notifications aren't in IPC and can take a click drawn over a window.
- niri scrolls its view without an event for `center-column` and similar actions. The 60 s screenshot age limit bounds that.
- At desktop scope, a double click or drag that starts on an unfocused tiled window stops after the first press, which moves focus.
- With `focus-follows-mouse`, a desktop-scope click on an unfocused window refuses before its press; a new `get_desktop_state` and a second click work.
- With several outputs, window capture and pointer input refuse.
- With client-side decorations, GTK 3 and Chromium windows publish no element frames. Element actions still work.
- Browser identity routes are refused on niri until a browser threat matrix runs there.
- The generated `click.mdx` and Linux MCP spec still lack the click `count` maximum; `cd-cua-driver-docs.yml` regenerates them.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

title: feat(cua-driver): experimental held-pointer route for background native drag-and-drop on macOS
body:
Refs #5477 (MB-09). Draft, experimental, off by default. Do not merge before the decision in "Open question".

## What changes for users
With `CUA_DRIVER_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_DND=1` in the daemon environment, a background `drag` can finish native macOS drag-and-drop (list reordering, moving a file between windows, dragging an object onto a drop zone) without moving the pointer or raising the window. Without the flag nothing changes: same `background_unavailable` refusal, or the brief foreground step from #5481.

## Why the current route fails
A drag-and-drop session ends as soon as the window server reports the hardware button as up. Window-routed events don't change that state (inside the target `NSEvent.pressedMouseButtons` is 0 during a posted drag), so the session cancels about 0.6 s after it starts.

## The route
1. Detect the session as today (drag image window appears).
2. Put a transparent, non-activating shield window under the pointer, then post one hardware `leftMouseDown` at the stationary pointer. The shield takes the press, so the app under the pointer never sees a click.
3. Keep posting the pid-routed drags to the drop point, plus a short settle there.
4. Post the hardware `leftMouseUp` first, then the window-routed up at the drop point (the other order never ends the session).
5. If the pointer moved during the gesture, return an error instead of reporting a drop. If the hold can't be made (no AppKit main loop, button already down), fall back to the existing refusal or foreground step.

## Evidence (macOS 26.5.2 VM, DragLab test app)
- NSTableView reorder, in-app object to drop zone, and Finder file to another app's drop zone all dropped at the requested point; pointer and frontmost app unchanged. Plain canvas drags are untouched.
- Flag off: same refusal as before. User moves the pointer mid-gesture: error, no drop.
- Findings, candidates ruled out (AX drag attributes, global events, pasteboard routes) and limits: the internal findings doc (shared separately).
- Unit tests added for the held gesture order (engage once, settle, hardware release before the window up), no-session and failed-engage cases, and the result shapes.

## Open question
The route posts two hardware events (a down and an up, absorbed by the shield). The bench harness counts `hid_events`, so a scored background run may flag them. Needs a decision before it is used in scoring. Also untested on macOS versions other than 26.5.2, and only AppKit sources and destinations.
