title: Detect Windows optional features without elevation
body:
Problem: Windows VM preflight inferred Windows Hypervisor Platform state from a DLL, and desktop runtime advice could not identify disabled Windows features.

Before: an installed but stopped Docker Desktop always offered Start Docker Desktop, even when Virtual Machine Platform was disabled.

After: read-only filtered Win32_OptionalFeature queries detect feature states; desktop facts also include EditionID. Installed Docker users with disabled VMP or WSL can open Windows Features with restart guidance. WHP alone does not replace Docker advice, absent features remain unknown, and no advice recommends Hyper-V. VM preflight checks WHP once per report with a five-second subprocess bound.

Merged origin/main: preflight now keeps main's `gather_waiting` (local-network patience) and the macOS container virtualization gap, and passes the once-per-report WHP result through `gather_with_virtualization`. The spaces bridge keeps main's `createNetworks`/`runtimeOf` imports alongside the PR's runtime fix action validation.

Tests:
- WindowsSystem regressions for Home, feature parsing and refresh, query failures, action effects, installation/restart precedence, and bridge action validation.
- Rust parser/preflight coverage for enabled, disabled, unknown and container behavior.
- The scoped repository checks pass on the head below: cargo fmt, clippy with warnings denied, and tests for cua-vmm.
- cua-spaces-desktop: `tsc --noEmit` passes and the full vitest suite passes, including windows-runtime and bridge-registry tests.
- The PowerShell CIM query itself runs only on Windows and is covered by Windows CI, not by these checks.

title: feat(telemetry): split create-failure runtime into runtime_kind sub-kinds (CUA-2091)
body:
Linear: CUA-2091 (related to CUA-2061). For review by @ddupont808. No auto-merge.

## What changes for users and customers

When a Space fails to start on someone's computer, the error now says what to do next in plain words (for example "The Linux engine that Cua sets up on this Mac did not start. Quit Cua and open it again..."), and we can see which cause is behind the biggest failure class.

## Why

`runtime` is 35% of Space create errors (110 of 312 over 7 days) and cannot be ranked. Most of it comes from versions before the shared classifier (0.9.4 and older); this adds a real split for what still falls through today.

## Change

- `runtime` stays the parent `error_kind` (dashboards keep working). New `runtime_kind` property on `cua_space_create` (v4), `cua_sandbox_created` (v3) and `cua_host_space_provided` (v3). It is `none` for any other `error_kind`.
- Shared code in `cua-create-failure`: `create_failure_kind` returns `runtime.<sub-kind>` for a `Runtime` error no other rule names; `cua-telemetry` reads it back into `error_kind=runtime` plus `runtime_kind`, validated against the schema. Every client (app, SDK, host daemon) goes through the same path. No FFI or generated bindings change.
- Kind codes only: no message, path, user name or machine name leaves the process (tested).
- Two text rules moved to existing top-level kinds: Docker Desktop on Windows (named pipe missing) is `runtime_not_running`, and "operation not permitted" is `runtime_permission`.
- `user_text` gives a plain, actionable sentence per kind, and the app's failure text uses it. A `runtime` error nothing names keeps the SDK text.
- Docs updated: `telemetry-error-kinds.mdx`, `telemetry-events.mdx`. No PostHog insight or dashboard definitions live in this repo, so none changed.

## New `runtime_kind` values

`linux_runtime_start_failed`, `linux_runtime_not_ready`, `gvisor_unavailable`, `runtime_download_failed`, `runtime_path_too_long`, `memory_limit`, `unsupported_hardware`, `open_file_limit`, `lume_outdated`, `lume_unreachable`, `vm_stopped_early`, `qemu_start_failed`, `image_arch_mismatch`, `container_start_failed`, `container_engine_error`, `unclassified`.

Image pull, disk full, boot timeout, hypervisor, Docker not running, port in use, guest service never answered and permissions already have their own top-level `error_kind` words (`image_pull_*`, `insufficient_disk`, `vm_boot_timeout`, `virtualization_unavailable`, `runtime_not_running`, `port_in_use`, `services_unreachable`, `runtime_permission`); they are unchanged.

## Tests

One test per classifier pattern in `cua-create-failure`, schema and privacy tests in `cua-telemetry`, app-core tests for the text and the emitted variant. `cargo test` for create-failure, telemetry, spaces-app-core, sdk telemetry and host_spaces pass; clippy clean. Windows-host and headless-Mac preflight files untouched.

title: [Bug]: Recordings through cua-spacesd's driver on Linux have no screenshots, state or video
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

A trajectory recording started through `cua-spacesd`'s driver (its `/mcp`, or a Space's `call_tool`) on Linux writes only `action.json`. Every turn's screenshots are `capture_hook_unavailable`, its state is `capture_failed`, and `record_video: true` fails with `no video backend registered for this platform`. The standalone `cua-driver` 0.38.0, run on the same guest, records all three.

### Reproduction

1. Create a Linux Space (`cua spaces create linux --on aws`) and install `ffmpeg` and `mousepad` with apt.
2. Through the Space's driver, call `start_session {session: "s"}`, then `start_recording {output_dir: "/home/cua/traj", record_video: true, session: "s"}`.
3. Call `launch_app {name: "mousepad", additional_arguments: ["/home/cua/notes.txt"]}`, then `get_window_state`, then `type_text` into the text view's element token, then `get_window_state` and `stop_recording`.
4. Inspect `/home/cua/traj`.
5. Repeat steps 2–4 with the release `cua-driver` 0.38.0 binary (`cua-driver mcp`, stdio) on the same guest.

It happens on every run.

### Expected behavior

What the `start_recording` reference describes: per turn, `before.png`/`after.png` and `before_state.json`/`after_state.json`, plus `recording.mp4` when ffmpeg is on `PATH`.

### Actual behavior

Through `cua-spacesd` 0.6.0 (shipped in the image) and 0.7.0 (the release binary, served on loopback on the same guest):

- `start_recording` returns `⚠️ Video capture failed (per-turn JSON+screenshot still running): no video backend registered for this platform`, with ffmpeg 6.1.1 on `PATH`.
- Each turn folder holds only `action.json` and `evidence.json`. On the `type_text` turn, before and after are both:
  ```json
  {"screenshot": {"status": "unavailable", "classification": "capture_hook_unavailable"},
   "state": {"status": "unavailable", "classification": "capture_failed"}}
  ```
- `get_window_state` in the same session returns a screenshot and the AT-SPI tree, so capture and AT-SPI work in that process.

Through `cua-driver` 0.38.0, with the same guest, app and steps: both turns record `captured` screenshots, the `type_text` turn records `captured` state, and `recording.mp4` is written (115,741 bytes).

Cause: the recording hooks (`set_screenshot_fn`, `set_click_marker_fn`, `set_budgeted_ax_snapshot_fn`, `set_element_bounds_fn`, `set_video_backend_factory`) are installed only by `cua-driver-sdk`'s `build_registry`, through `configure_{macos,windows,linux}_runtime` ([runtime.rs:557-705](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/9bf7e51adb66545aea0a0d7eb8900c879d2a55bf/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-sdk/src/runtime.rs#L557-L705)). `cua-spacesd` builds its registries with `platform_*::register_tools*` directly and never installs them:

- `platform_tools()` ([cua-spacesd/src/main.rs:593-607](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/9bf7e51adb66545aea0a0d7eb8900c879d2a55bf/libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd/src/main.rs#L593-L607));
- `platform_registry()` ([cua-spacesd-desktop/src/lib.rs:2392, 2410, 2428](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/9bf7e51adb66545aea0a0d7eb8900c879d2a55bf/libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/lib.rs#L2428)).

The unset defaults produce exactly the strings above: [recording.rs:1093](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/9bf7e51adb66545aea0a0d7eb8900c879d2a55bf/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/recording.rs#L1093), [313](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/9bf7e51adb66545aea0a0d7eb8900c879d2a55bf/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/recording.rs#L313) with [1184](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/9bf7e51adb66545aea0a0d7eb8900c879d2a55bf/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/recording.rs#L1184), and [video.rs:63](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/9bf7e51adb66545aea0a0d7eb8900c879d2a55bf/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/video.rs#L63). The macOS and Windows arms of both functions take the same path; only Linux was run. `main` (9bf7e51) is unchanged from `cua-spacesd-v0.7.0` in these files.

### Environment

- `cua-spacesd` 0.6.0 (the `linux` image) and 0.7.0 (`cua-spacesd-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`), both reporting `cua_driver_version` 0.38.0; `cua-driver` 0.38.0 (`cua-driver-rs-0.38.0-linux-arm64-binary.tar.gz`); `cua` CLI 0.7.0
- Ubuntu 24.04.5 aarch64 (AWS t4g.medium Space), XFCE on Xvfb `:1`, AT-SPI
- Mousepad 0.6.1 (GTK3), ffmpeg 6.1.1-3ubuntu5

### Evidence

The `evidence.json` excerpt and the `start_recording` text above.

### Workaround and additional context

Run the standalone `cua-driver` in the guest for recordings, or save `get_window_state` screenshots from the client. A fix would install the same platform hooks in `cua-spacesd` before it builds a registry, for example by having it build through, or call, the SDK's runtime configuration.

title: [Feature]: Cua Driver (macOS): let scripting-backed background actions refuse instead of raising the Automation prompt when nobody can answer it
body:
**Primary area:** Cua Driver

**User problem**

Suppose Cua Driver has no Automation consent for an app. A background `invoke_menu ["File","Save"]` on a TextEdit document then sends an Apple Event that raises "“CuaDriver” wants access to control “TextEdit”". Per #5057 and `MACOS.md`, a background `hotkey cmd+s` and `set_value` on a Finder name cell take the same route. In an unattended run (a VM, CI, or an agent working while the user is away), nobody answers the prompt, and then:

- The call blocks for 30 s. It then returns `background_unavailable` with `automation_timeout: the app did not answer within 30 s (a macOS Automation prompt may be waiting for the user)`.
- The prompt stays on screen as the front app (`lsappinfo front` reads `UserNotificationCenter`) until tccd gives up at 120 s. **Allow** is its default button.
- The timeout is not kept as a denial. The next background Save raises the prompt again and blocks for another 30 s. This happened on 2 of 2 attempts. TCC holds `kTCCServiceAppleEvents|com.trycua.driver|com.apple.TextEdit|auth_value 0|auth_reason 9`, re-stamped at each timeout, yet the driver does not treat that row as denied.

The driver reads the permission without asking before it sends (`AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget(..., 0)`, `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/apple_events.rs:74-95`). It refuses only on denied or not-running (`:182-198`), so the caller has no way to get a refusal instead of a prompt.

**Desired outcome**

An opt-in for unattended use (a `serve` flag or config key) under which these routes send nothing when Automation consent for the target app has not been given. The call then refuses at once with a distinct code that names the app and the System Settings pane. The current prompt-on-first-use behavior can stay the default.

**Current workaround**

- Approve the prompt once per target app in the image before running unattended.
- Or bring the app to the front first: with TextEdit in front, `invoke_menu ["File","Save"]` went through AX and saved, with no Apple Event and no prompt.

**Affected components and platforms**

Cua Driver on macOS, 0.38.0 (`cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0`). `main` at `4ecb58e` is unchanged in these files. The routes that send events are `save_document` (`apple_events.rs:367-379`, called from `tools/invoke_menu.rs:852`), the background key-equivalent Save in `hotkey` (`MACOS.md:94-101`), and `finder_rename` (`apple_events.rs:251`). Only `invoke_menu` Save in TextEdit was run.

Tested on a macOS 26.5.2 (25F84) arm64 VM with the release CuaDriver.app. Accessibility and Screen Recording were granted; no Automation was granted.

Reproduction:
1. Open a `.txt` file with `launch_app {"bundle_id":"com.apple.TextEdit","urls":[...]}`, keep another app in front, and `type_text` into the text area.
2. Call `invoke_menu {"pid":…,"window_id":…,"path":["File","Save"]}`.
3. Leave the prompt unanswered, then repeat steps 1–2 after it closes.

tccd log, twice per run:
```
Prompting for access to indirect object TextEdit by CuaDriver
AccessRequestIndirect: prompt timed out after 120 seconds
```

**Alternatives and prior art**

#5057 introduced the scripting routes and states that macOS "shows its consent prompt once, on the first save or rename". In an unattended session the prompt is never answered, so it recurs on every call.

**Implementation ideas**

In `ensure_permitted` (`apple_events.rs:182-198`), return a refusal for `NeedsConsent` when the opt-in is set.

**Checks**

- [x] I searched existing issues, RFCs and active pull requests.
- [x] This request describes one problem and its desired outcome.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data and sensitive screenshots.

title: perf(cua-driver): capture PiP frames off the request path
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: with the experimental PiP preview on, every action tool captured and PNG-encoded the action's window before it returned its result. In a debug build that held each result back 2.2 s for a 1332x1049 window and 0.5 s for a 640x558 window (Astro Gold 6.7.6, from the daemon's phase timings). For a menu command that was most of a 2.3 to 3.0 s call.
- What changed: the frame is captured on its own thread after the result is returned. One capture runs at a time. An action that finishes while a capture is still running gets no frame of its own; the next action after that capture ends gets one. With PiP off (no PiP backend registered), nothing changes.

## Related work

No issue filed. I found no open PR that changes when the PiP frame is captured.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. No tool, schema, or result change. Only the timing of the PiP preview frame changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - Only with the experimental PiP preview on. Tool results return without waiting for the capture.
  - The preview frame now shows the window a moment after the result returns, not just before. Under fast consecutive actions, some actions get no preview frame.
  - The code is in `cua-driver-core`, so it applies on every platform with a PiP backend.
- Risk and rollback: at most one capture thread is alive at a time; a busy flag is cleared when the thread ends and when the thread fails to spawn. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (macOS 27.2 arm64, from `libs/cua-driver/rust`):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo build -p cua-driver --locked`: ok.
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core`: 1125 passed, 2 ignored.
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test`: 2 passed, 1 ignored.
- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 27.2 arm64, debug build, Astro Gold 6.7.6, PiP on, another app frontmost):
  - The capture this PR moves off the request path cost 2.2 s per action on the 1332x1049 main window and 0.5 s on a 640x558 window.
  - On a prototype branch that also carried #5770 (background menus) and #5771 (pop-ups and dialog fields), `invoke_menu` calls went from 2.3 to 3.0 s down to 0.44 to 0.45 s, and a background `click` on a dialog button from 1.55 s to 1.25 s. Those totals mix this change with the others, so I only claim the capture cost above for this PR.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - No unit test drives the background capture. It needs a registered PiP backend and a live window.
  - Not timed on a release build: on this macOS beta, release-profile proc-macro dylibs fail to load, so only debug builds run here.
  - Not run on Windows or Linux.
  - `cargo clippy` was not run: clippy is not installed for the pinned 1.97.1 toolchain on this machine.

title: fix(cua-driver): run background menu commands that need the key window
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: background `invoke_menu` on macOS refused two kinds of commands that work once the right window is key.
  - An item AppKit disables while its app is inactive was refused. TextEdit's Edit > Paste is one: AppKit validates menu items against its own key window, and only when their menu opens, and the background route never opened one. A background `cmd+v` `hotkey` takes the same menu route; it fell through to key events, reported "Pressed", and nothing was pasted.
  - With a second window of the app key (another document or a panel), a command bound to the main window was refused `window_not_key` with advice to use the foreground. In Astro Gold 6.7.6 with a listing window key, View > Interpretations and a chart's Edit Chart... item were refused this way, although both run in the background once the main window is key. The key window was named only in free text.
- What changed:
  - Before a background menu command, the driver makes the requested window the app's key window inside the app, through the key scope `hotkey` already uses: no activation, no raise, confirmed before the command runs. It skips this when the window already is the app's focused and main window. It leaves the window key afterwards, as a click on it would; handing key back cost another round of records (about 0.3 s) for no change the user sees.
  - A `window_not_key` refusal names the app's key window as `key_window_id` in structured output, and its text says to retry an app-wide command (View, Window, Help) in the background bound to that window. The foreground stays the advice for a command about the requested window's own document.
  - An item that is disabled only because the app is inactive: the app receives the activation record and the make-key pair for the window, the menu levels above the item are opened so AppKit re-validates it, the item is pressed, any menu left open is closed, and the app receives the defocus record. A menu opens only for an item that would otherwise be refused. An item that stays disabled is refused as before and its menu is closed.
  - When a key scope ends and the app's key window has moved to a window the action opened (a dialog), that window keeps key, so the next action lands there. This applies to every key scope that hands key back: `hotkey`, `press_key`, and `type_text` with `window_id`.
  - The macOS skill text for background `invoke_menu` describes the new behavior.

## Related work

No issue filed.

#4651 (Ed-Key) keeps the requested window key within its app after a menu command on the route used when the app is frontmost. This PR does the same on the background route and also makes the window key before the command. The two touch different branches of `invoke` in `invoke_menu.rs`.

#5380 (skap3214) handles a window of the frontmost app that is not its key window: it makes that window key with `enter_exact_window_key`, presses the item through the background route, and hands key back to the user's window. This PR handles an app in the background, where nothing of the user's is in that app, so the window stays key. Both PRs edit `invoke` in `invoke_menu.rs` and `skylight.rs`, so expect a textual conflict; the behaviors do not overlap.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): I don't think one is needed, but it is a judgment call. The tool's behavior and result text change: a background call that was refused now runs, and a still-disabled item briefly shows its menu. `window_not_key` refusals gain an optional `key_window_id` field in structured output. The refusal code, its escalation, the tool schema, and the versioned SDK contract in `libs/cua-driver/contract` are unchanged. I read the new field as an additive detail on an existing refusal. If maintainers count new structured fields as an MCP contract change, I can drop `key_window_id` and keep the text.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - macOS only, background `invoke_menu`, and `hotkey` combos that route through it.
  - After the call, the requested window is the app's key window. The user's front app and the window order do not change (checked on TextEdit).
  - For an item disabled only by inactivity, its menu is drawn over the user's screen while it is pressed: 125 to 130 ms on TextEdit.
  - Until the defocus record is posted, the app believes it is active. The call posts it right after the press.
  - A key scope that ends with a newly opened window key leaves that window key instead of handing key back.
- Risk and rollback: the new decisions are small functions with unit tests (`key_moved_to_new_window`, the `key_window_id` refusal). Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (macOS 27.2 arm64, from `libs/cua-driver/rust`):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo build -p cua-driver --locked`: ok.
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos`: 638 passed, 7 ignored (lib), plus 2 passed in the integration test binary. Includes the new `a_window_the_action_opened_keeps_key_when_the_scope_ends` and `unbound_menu_names_the_key_window_for_a_background_retry`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test`: 2 passed, 1 ignored.
  - After the skill text change: `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core`: 1125 passed, 2 ignored. `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test mcp_config_skills_cli_test`: 10 passed.
- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 27.2 arm64, debug build, another app frontmost the whole time):
  - TextEdit: Edit > Paste through `invoke_menu` and `cmd+v` through `hotkey` both paste. The menu is on screen 125 to 130 ms. An item that stays disabled is refused and its menu closes. The front app and window order do not change.
  - Astro Gold 6.7.6, `invoke_menu` View > Interpretations bound to the main window with a listing window key: before (cua-driver 0.37.0) `window_not_key` with advice to use the foreground; after, invoked in the background.
  - Astro Gold 6.7.6, a chart's Edit Chart... bound to the main window: before `window_not_key`; after, the Edit Chart dialog opened in the background.
  - `invoke_menu` call time (debug build): 2.3 to 3.0 s before, 0.44 to 0.45 s after. Most of the old time was the PiP frame capture, which #5769 moves off the request path; this PR removes the key scope's hand-back round.
  - This evidence comes from a prototype branch that also carried #5768 (cursor), #5769 (PiP capture), and #5771 (pop-ups and dialog fields).
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - The canonical desktop E2E harness was not run, and no harness fixture has a menu item disabled while its app is inactive.
  - Not run on Windows or Linux. The change is in the macOS adapter only.
  - `cargo clippy` was not run: clippy is not installed for the pinned 1.97.1 toolchain on this machine.
  - The skill copy under `libs/cua/skills/cua-driver/` already differs from the canonical skill on main, so I left it for the usual sync.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

title: fix(cua-driver): close background pop-ups and commit dialog text fields
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: three background problems on macOS, all seen driving Astro Gold 6.7.6 with another app frontmost.
  - `click` on an AppKit pop-up button opened its menu and left it over the user's front app until a later call chose an item: 36 s of agent think time in one run. The result listed no options, because they were read from the pop-up's direct children and an AppKit pop-up's only child is its `AXMenu`.
  - `set_value` on a dialog text field read back the new value, but the dialog's commit button used the old one (Edit Chart > Calculate kept the old date). An `AXValue` write never ends AppKit's field-editor session, so the control's bound value is not updated. An `AXConfirm`, a programmatic focus change, and an `AXSelectedText` write all left the old date too. Only typed keys followed by Tab committed it, and only when the typed text differed from the text the field held when editing began.
  - `click` on a toolbar button that opens a popover ("Select Date") reported "Performed AXPress" and nothing appeared.
- What changed:
  - In the background, `click` on a pop-up button reads the options from its `AXMenu`, closes the menu in the same call, and lists the options with a pointer to `set_value`, which already selects in one call. If the menu could not be closed, the result says so and asks for Escape before other input. In the foreground the menu stays open as before, and the options are now listed there too. The tool description says this; the macOS MCP snapshot, its reference page, and the macOS skill text follow.
  - After a write that changed a single-line `AXTextField` of a native app (not secure, at most 200 characters, no line breaks or tabs), `set_value` makes the field's window key in its app (no activation, no raise), puts the old text back, focuses the field, and checks that it is the app's focused element. Only then does it select all, type the value as pid-routed key events, and press Tab. If the field cannot be focused, no key is sent and the new value is written back. The result says what was done and asks the caller to check the dependent result from fresh state. Structured output gains `committed` (true or false), present only when this step was attempted.
    - Only a native app's own field gets this step, the AppKit case it was built for (SwiftUI's text fields are AppKit-backed and count). A field in web content (Chromium, Electron, WebKit) is recognized by an `AXWebArea` ancestor, the same walk `type_text` uses; a field whose walk does not reach its window counts as web content. Any field of a browser, its address bar included, is recognized by the driver's existing browser check (Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera, Thorium, Safari), because the address bar sits outside the web area. Those fields keep the plain `AXValue` write with no focus change, typing, or Tab, and report no `committed`.
  - A background `AXPress` on an `AXButton` or `AXMenuButton` compares the app's on-screen windows at every layer before the press and after the click's existing window-change wait. The result names the windows that opened or closed, or says none did and names routes that work instead (a menu command or its dialog, or the foreground). The window-change detector only counted layer-0 windows, so a popover or pop-up menu was invisible to it. The popover itself is still not shown: a transient popover needs the app active, and once shown it would sit over the user's window like the pop-up menus above.

## Related work

No issue filed.

#5129 (merged) fixed background pop-ups and context menus that closed straight away on macOS: the key-focus guard's own steal made AppKit end menu tracking, so an agent could not pick an item. This PR still changes the background pop-up `click`. Left open, the menu sat over the user's front app for the agent's whole think time (36 s measured on Astro Gold), and the click listed no options, because an AppKit pop-up's only child is its `AXMenu`. A background `click` now reads the options from that `AXMenu` and closes the menu in the same call. What #5129 fixed still holds: the front window keeps key status while a menu is open, `set_value` still opens the menu, presses the item and closes it in one call, and context menus from `right_click` stay open and are unchanged. The release gate `harness_appkit_popup_click_keeps_front_key_focus_background` now clicks the pop-up, checks that the result lists Research and that a fresh snapshot shows no open menu item, then selects Research with `set_value`.

#3858 (will-bogusz, draft) solves the same `set_value` problem more broadly. It types the value into native single-line fields and reports a typed `committed` verdict (`committed`, `not_committed`, `unproven`) on `ActionResult`, under RFC #4009 and contract 0.9.0. This PR keeps the `AXValue` write, adds the retype-and-Tab step after it, and reports a plain boolean `committed` in `set_value`'s structured output, outside the versioned contract. If #3858 lands first, the `set_value` part here should be dropped or rebased onto it. I can split it into its own PR if that helps review.

#4620 (Ed-Key) adds a note when a refused Catalyst menu item leaves its menu open. Same theme as the pop-up change here, no shared code. #3858, #3897, and #3886 also edit `set_value.rs` or `click.rs`, so expect textual conflicts.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): this needs a maintainer call for one part. The `click` and button-press changes only change behavior and result text. The new `committed` field in `set_value`'s structured output is additive and outside the versioned SDK contract, but its name and meaning overlap the typed `committed` verdict that RFC #4009 defines. I am fine renaming it, dropping it in favor of #4009, or waiting for #3858.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - macOS only.
  - A background `click` on a pop-up no longer leaves its menu open. A caller that clicked the pop-up and then an `AXMenuItem` in the background now has to use `set_value`. The foreground route is unchanged.
  - `set_value` on a native app's single-line text field now sends key events to the app, and focus ends on the next control (Tab). Browsers and web content are unchanged. Typing takes about 30 ms per character, up to 6 s at the 200-character cap. An app that reacts to typed text or Tab (autocomplete) sees those events. Secure fields are skipped. Every field in a recognized browser's process keeps the plain write, not only its address bar. Another browser's own address bar would count as native. If a step fails, the AX write stays and the result says to use `type_text` and `press_key` with tab.
  - A background button press adds one window-list read after the existing wait, and a line to the result.
- Risk and rollback: the new decisions have unit tests (`press_window_note`, `popup_click_note`). Revert the commits to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (macOS 27.2 arm64, from `libs/cua-driver/rust`):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo build -p cua-driver --locked`: ok.
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos`: 642 passed, 7 ignored (lib), plus 2 passed in the integration test binary. Includes the new `a_background_button_press_reports_which_app_windows_opened_or_closed`, `a_background_popup_click_says_its_menu_was_closed`, and the commit-step gate tests: `a_native_app_text_field_is_committed_after_a_changed_write`, `browser_and_web_content_fields_keep_the_plain_write` (no retype, no note, no `committed` field), `only_a_changed_single_line_text_field_is_considered`, and `an_attempted_commit_is_reported`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test`: 2 passed, 1 ignored.
  - After the skill text change: `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core`: 1125 passed, 2 ignored. `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test mcp_config_skills_cli_test`: 10 passed.
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-e2e --no-run`: every test target compiles, including the updated `harness_appkit_test`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-e2e`: 37 passed, 91 ignored (the desktop cases are ignored by default).
  - Release-gate cases updated in `harness_appkit_test.rs`: `harness_appkit_popup_click_keeps_front_key_focus_background` as described under Related work. `harness_appkit_element_foreground_press_key_commits_edit` and `harness_appkit_px_background_press_key_reports_honest_delivery_truth` now type their text with `type_text` instead of `set_value`. `set_value` now ends a text field's edit with Tab, which commits it: the first case asserts `committed=none` before Return, and in the second the commit would run the fixture's command before Return, so its oracle would no longer prove Return. The background case now also checks that the command has not run before Return. #3858 makes the same setup change to the foreground case.
  - Generated reference: the docs generator needs a release build, which does not link on this macOS beta. I applied the one changed sentence to `cua-driver-mcp-macos.json` and `click-and-type.mdx`, then compared the snapshot with `cua-driver dump-docs --type all` from the debug build of this branch: every tool's name, description, flags, and input schema match.
- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 27.2 arm64, debug build, Astro Gold 6.7.6, another app frontmost the whole time):
  - `click` on the Dynamic Listings job pop-up: before (cua-driver 0.37.0) the menu stayed over the user's window 36 s and no options were listed; after, the options are listed and the menu is on screen 73 to 107 ms, closed in the same call.
  - `set_value` on the Edit Chart date, then Calculate: before, the chart kept the old date; after, the chart took the new date, one day forward and back again.
  - `click` on "Select Date": before, "Performed AXPress" only; after, the same press plus "No window, sheet, popover or menu of the app appeared or closed" and the routes that work.
  - A press that closes a dialog is reported as closing it.
  - Background `click` time (debug build): job pop-up 2.0 s before, 1.3 s after; Calculate 1.55 s before, 1.25 s after. These totals include the PiP capture change in #5769.

title: fix(cua-driver): don't move Windows windows off their virtual desktop
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, a background action on a window parked on another Task View desktop (Win+Ctrl+D) moves that window onto the desktop the user is viewing, where it stays cloaked (invisible). #5711 describes it.
- What changed: `NoActivateGuard` sets and clears `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` on the target's top-level window. Clearing it makes Explorer re-register the taskbar button, and Explorer files the window under the current desktop. The guard now asks `IVirtualDesktopManager::IsWindowOnCurrentVirtualDesktop` first and skips the style change for a window on another desktop. If the shell can't answer (no Explorer, COM failure), it keeps the existing behavior. Every caller goes through `arm`, so all 11 call sites (click, drag, press_key, type_text, set_value, scroll, multi-invoke) get the fix.

Not affected: windows with `WS_EX_APPWINDOW`. That style keeps their taskbar button under `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE`, so nothing re-registers. Plain Win32 apps such as charmap don't set it, which is why the issue reproduces with them.

## Related work

Fixes #5711

Related: #4068 made background input work on windows in other macOS Spaces.

RFC: not required (no contract change).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: background input no longer moves windows between Task View desktops. On a window on another desktop, the driver no longer applies `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` during the action. Such a window is cloaked. `post_click_on` and `inject_click_screen` still restore the user's foreground afterwards, and the `fg_bypass` comment notes that `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` never stopped an explicit self-`SetForegroundWindow` anyway. Measured below with a target that calls `SetForegroundWindow(self)` on mouse-down.
- Cost: one in-process COM call per `arm`. Click latency was unchanged in the run below (142 ms before, 145 ms after, debug build).
- Risk and rollback: one condition in `NoActivateGuard::arm` plus a helper. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - New `#[ignore]` test `input::inject::task_view_desktop_tests::guard_leaves_a_window_on_another_task_view_desktop_where_it_is`. It creates its own window, moves it to a second Task View desktop with the public `MoveWindowToDesktop`, holds and releases the guard, and asserts the window is still on that desktop. It then moves the window back and asserts the guard still applies on the current desktop. No public API creates a Task View desktop, so the test needs one prepared first (Win+Ctrl+D, then Win+Ctrl+Left) and is ignored by default, like the Credential Manager test in `history.rs`.
    - With the fix: passed 3/3 runs.
    - Mutation check (guard condition reverted): failed 3/3 runs with `the guard took the window off its desktop`.
    - Explorer reports the new desktop from `GetWindowDesktopId` before it finishes the move, and a style change in that window doesn't reproduce the bug, so the test settles before arming.
  - `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib`: 304 passed. `diagnostics::tests::ui_automation_available_succeeds_in_test_runner` failed with "UI Automation desktop enumeration exceeded 4000ms". It fails the same way on unmodified `main` on this machine, so it is a host-state issue.
  - `cargo fmt -p platform-windows -- --check` clean. `cargo clippy -p platform-windows --lib --tests` reports nothing in the changed file.
- Manual or platform evidence: Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200, debug `cua-driver serve` with an isolated home, `get_window_state` followed by a background pixel `click` (route `synthetic_events`, "Posted click to pid …"). The target was a WinForms window without `WS_EX_APPWINDOW` that moves itself to a second Task View desktop and reports its desktop, cloak state, and received mouse-downs.

  | | `main` (27d8da9fd) | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | target desktop after click | moved to the user's desktop, still cloaked | stayed on its desktop |
  | click reached the target | yes (1 mouse-down) | yes (1 mouse-down) |
  | target that calls `SetForegroundWindow(self)` on mouse-down | moved | stayed; user's desktop and foreground unchanged |

- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - The canonical Windows desktop E2E matrix has not been run on this branch.
  - My local Visual Studio lacks the Spectre-mitigated libraries `regorus` requires, so local builds patched `msvc_spectre_libs` with a no-op crate and ran without `--locked`. CI builds the stock dependency.
  - Not exercised: windows pinned to all desktops, and the `element_token`, keyboard, and scroll routes end to end. They go through the same `arm`.

title: fix(cua-driver): initialize recording hooks for embedded platform registries
body:
## Problem
Spacesd constructs platform registries directly, but recording screenshots, application state, click markers and video were initialized only by the SDK. Recordings therefore reported missing capture hooks and video backends.

## Before / after
- Install existing recording callbacks alongside each native registry's recording setup, so SDK and embedded registries share one initialization path.
- Remove duplicate SDK initialization while preserving conditional Linux desktop preparation.
- Select the Linux video backend when recording starts, including after nested Wayland session creation.
- Preserve process-wide first-writer-wins behavior. The supplied embedding inventory identifies no supported custom installer whose ordering changes; the Windows UIA host also gains recording support without capture at construction.
- Correct recording initialization documentation.

## Tests
- Add separate-process Linux registration tests for both constructors, checking video backend availability and recorded screenshot evidence without a display.
- Add nested-session video selection coverage and an isolated spacesd fallback regression.
- Extend Linux desktop conformance with GTK text input, captured screenshot/state evidence, PNG decoding and finalized MP4 inspection. Its existing remote-target harness also permits testing a daemon with desktop services disabled.
- All focused Cargo commands were bounded by `timeout 120s`. The initial pre-fix run could not resolve crates.io. Post-fix offline runs could not resolve cached dependencies (`cap-fs-ext` in the driver workspace; `clipboard-rs` in spacesd), so no test compiled or executed and failing-before/passing-after remains unverified.
- Rustfmt and `git diff --check` pass.

Native macOS/Windows compilation and execution, Xvfb conformance, and remote fallback execution remain unverified in this environment. Existing SDK recording tests were not run under the builder restriction to changed tests only.

## Fix rounds

- Updated the fallback recording regression to send a valid set_config field through service authorization and isolate saved configuration in a temporary home. The focused test reproduced the empty-request refusal before the change and passes afterward; cargo fmt check passes.
- Updated the shared Linux recording regression harness to send a reviewed `max_image_dimension` field instead of an empty `set_config` request. Both constructor tests pass when rebuilt against cached platform libraries; the original test reproduced the authorization refusal. Platform formatting and diff whitespace checks pass.

## Merge with main

- Merged main. It had renamed the Linux Wayland factory to `WaylandVideoBackendFactory` (now GNOME helper, wf-recorder or portal ScreenCast), so the Linux capture-start selector calls that factory.
- macOS registers the snapshot store directly, as main does, and then calls `recording_hooks::install()`. The SDK keeps main's musl gating for Linux desktop preparation.
- The spacesd fallback regression is gated to non-headless Linux builds, because the static headless build has no platform tools.
- Added the MIT SPDX header to the four new Linux recording test files.
- The image gates have no ffmpeg, so the GTK recording conformance test requires an active video and a finalized MP4 only when the target has ffmpeg. Without ffmpeg it still requires a registered video backend, screenshots and state.
- The scoped repository checks pass for cua-driver-core, cua-driver-sdk, platform-linux (host build), cua-spacesd and cua-spacesd-desktop. platform-macos fmt and tests pass, and a throwaway macOS test confirmed `register_tools()` alone installs the video backend. Windows, Linux desktop and Xvfb execution were not run.

Closes #5760

title: cua sandbox launch --local fails on ARM64 hosts: runtime resolves ubuntu:24.04 to trycua/cua-xfce:latest, which publishes no arm64 build
body:
**What happened**

On an ARM64 host, `cua sandbox launch --local ubuntu:24.04` fails before any container is created. The cua-sandbox local Docker runtime resolves `ubuntu:24.04` to `trycua/cua-xfce:latest`, and Docker refuses the image because `trycua/cua-xfce:latest` publishes no linux/arm64 build.

**Environment**

- Host: Lenovo Yoga, Windows 11 on ARM64 (NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X)
- WSL2: Ubuntu 24.04, aarch64
- Docker Engine 29.9.1 (linux/arm64, native in WSL2)
- Python 3.12.3 venv
- cua 0.7.0, cua-cli 0.1.15, cua-sandbox 0.1.28, cua-computer 0.5.19

**Reproduction**

```
cua sandbox launch --local ubuntu:24.04 --name gen2-settle
```

Result (exit code 1):

```
RuntimeError("docker run failed: Unable to find image 'trycua/cua-xfce:latest' locally
docker: Error response from daemon: no matching manifest for linux/arm64/v8 in the manifest list entries: no match for platform in manifest: not found
...")
```

(raised from cua_sandbox/runtime/docker.py)

**Registry evidence**

`trycua/cua-xfce:latest` publishes no arm64 build: its manifest index contains linux/amd64 (sha256:0ac954ee…) plus an unknown/unknown attestation entry only. By contrast, `trycua/cua-ubuntu:latest` and `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04` both publish linux/arm64, and arm64 containers run fine on this host (the ghcr.io image was pulled and verified: linux/arm64, 4,395,581,727 bytes, digest sha256:d0f845852b717aca5f3692fbe244e724500847f22400f2f672c505623ed542bf).

**Related**

- #3254 (closed) covers an Apple Silicon failure with a different image in the path.
- #353 concerns cua-ubuntu arm64; that image has since gained an arm64 build.

title: fix(cua-driver): match flatpak apps on the a11y bus and click elements in native Wayland windows
body:
Two Linux fixes found while driving a GNOME 50 Wayland desktop (Ubuntu 26.04) with cua-driver 0.38.0.

**1. Flatpak apps resolve to an empty, degraded window**

Sandboxed flatpak apps reach the AT-SPI bus through their instance's `xdg-dbus-proxy`, so `GetConnectionUnixProcessID` returns the proxy's pid, not the app's. `pid_of` then never matches the window's pid and `get_window_state` falls back to window metadata only ("AT-SPI was unavailable…").

`pid_of` now maps an `xdg-dbus-proxy` pid to the sandboxed app: read `instance-id` from `/proc/<proxy>/root/.flatpak-info`, the inner bwrap pid from `/run/user/<uid>/.flatpak/<instance>/bwrapinfo.json` (`child-pid`), and take that process's first child. Non-proxy pids are unchanged.

Result with flatpak Telegram (`org.telegram.desktop`): 1 degraded element → 350–424 elements.

**2. Element clicks fail on native Wayland toplevels**

With Wayland input enabled, an element click on a native Wayland window (no X11 xid) went down the X11 routes and failed. It now uses the same portal pointer path as coordinate clicks (`with_target_foreground` + `click_focused`) at the element's screen centre. Background delivery isn't possible there, so it returns an explicit error asking for `delivery_mode: "foreground"`.

Verified: click on Telegram's Search field by element, typed text appeared, Escape cleared it.

`cargo check -p platform-linux` passes on current main.

title: fix(lume): keep a Linux VM's machine identifier so suspend can resume it
body:
## What

`lume suspend` never resumes a Linux VM. A saved state restores only into a VM with the machine identifier it was saved with, and Linux VMs get a new `VZGenericPlatformConfiguration` identifier on every run. So the next run's `restoreMachineState` fails with "invalid argument", `restoreOrBoot` boots the VM instead, and its memory is lost.

Each Linux VM now keeps one `VZGenericMachineIdentifier` in `machine-identifier` beside its disk. It's created on first use and reused on every run. A clone gets its own identifier, unless it keeps the source's saved state (`includeSavedState`), which is bound to the source's identifier.

## Reproduced and fixed

On an Apple M5 running macOS 27, with an Ubuntu 26.04 arm64 guest under `lume serve`, I ran run → `POST /lume/vms/<vm>/suspend` → run:
- **Before:** `ERROR: Could not restore the saved state; booting the VM instead … VZErrorDomain Code=12 "…failed to restore with error “invalid argument”"`, and the guest's `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` changed.
- **After:** `INFO: VM resumed from its saved state … ms=1278`, and the same `boot_id`.

## Tests

`tests/LinuxMachineIdentifierTests.swift` checks that the identifier is stable and valid, that an unreadable one is replaced, and that a clone gets its own unless it keeps the saved state. `swift test --no-parallel`: 246 tests pass.

## Two further ideas

We run a fork of Lume 0.5.3 that saves and restores VMs held by `lume run` processes (no `lume serve`). Two pieces of it might interest you; happy to send PRs if they fit:
- **Bind the saved state to the disk it was saved against.** Record the disk's size and mtime, plus a generation counter bumped at every start. A run then never restores memory onto a disk something else booted in the meantime (say an older Lume, or a manual `lume run` after a downgrade).
- **A signal that suspends a VM held by its own `lume run` process.** This works for VMs not started through `lume serve`.

title: feat(spaces): cua sync — make a folder in a Space match a folder here, sending only what changed
body:
CUA-2190

**What changes for users:** `cua sync ./my-repo builder:/src/my-repo` makes a folder in a Space hold what a folder on this computer holds now, and a second sync sends only what changed. It is also available as `cua spaces sync`, MCP `space_sync` and `Spaces.sync`. This is the step an agent needs before it builds or tests its worktree on another machine; today that means hand-rolled rsync or tarballs.

**How it works:**
- **Like git:** files `.gitignore` (and `.git/info/exclude`) leave out stay behind, and so does `.git`. `--no-gitignore`, `--include-git` and `--exclude PATTERN` change that.
- **The host side** hashes the folder (SHA-256), with a size/mtime cache under the cua home, so an unchanged file is not read again.
- **The Space side** keeps a manifest of what the last sync put there (`<dest>/.cua-sync.json`). New and changed files travel as one gzipped tar through the file service, are unpacked with the time of the sync, and are then deleted from `/tmp`.
- **Builds stay correct:** a changed file gets the time of the sync, so cargo, make and tsc rebuild exactly the changed files. An unchanged file keeps its time.
- **Deletes:** files the last sync put there and that are gone here are deleted (`--no-delete` keeps them). Nothing else in the destination is touched, such as a `target/` or `node_modules/`.
- Linux and macOS Spaces. A Windows Space is refused with a message for now.

**Verified:**
- Unit tests in `cua-spaces/src/sync.rs`:
  - the walk honours .gitignore (nested ones too), .git, `--include-git` and excludes;
  - the plan sends only changed and new files and deletes only synced files;
  - the hash cache, and the tar's contents.
- End to end, on a real build: `cua` was built from this branch and run in a Linux VM Space against a real cua-spacesd, on a 10,364-file checkout of this repository:
  1. First sync: all 10,364 files, 226 MiB over the wire, in 28.6 s.
  2. Sync again with nothing changed: 0 sent, in 0.4 s.
  3. One file edited and one deleted: 1 sent (7.4 KB over the wire) and 1 deleted, in 0.4 s. The edited file matches. The deleted file is gone. The destination's own `target/` is untouched, and the gitignored `target/` was not sent. The unchanged file kept its time, and the edited file has the time of the sync.
- `cargo clippy -p cua-spaces -p cua-spaces-contract -p cua-sdk -p cua-cli --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings` is clean. Regenerated: the contract manifest, bindings (including the Electron binding) and the CLI/SDK reference (a new "Sync a folder" page).

title: perf(cua-driver): read each AX node in one batched round trip
body:
## Summary

The macOS tree walker reads every node attribute by attribute: AXRole, AXTitle, AXValue, AXPlaceholderValue, AXDescription, AXIdentifier, AXHelp, AXEnabled, AXPosition, AXSize, AXValueDescription, AXMinValue, AXMaxValue, AXSelected and AXChildren are each one Mach round trip that the target app answers on its main thread.

This reads them with one `AXUIElementCopyMultipleAttributeValues` call per node (new `ax/batch.rs`) and converts the reply with the same rules as the single-read helpers (`copy_string_attr`, `copy_stringish_attr`, `copy_bool_attr`, `copy_number_attr`, `element_screen_rect`, `copy_children`), so `tree_markdown` and `elements` are unchanged. Action names and `AXValue` settability stay separate reads.

- If an app refuses the batch, the node falls back to the single reads.
- If the app does not answer in time (`kAXErrorCannotComplete`), the node is treated as unreadable instead of waiting out the 2 s messaging timeout once per attribute.

Refs #1757. That draft batches the same attributes on a much older walker. This version is rebased onto the current walker (menu collapsing, control state, web-content marker, value-settable rows). If maintainers would rather land it through #1757, I'm happy to close this one.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1, about 1,400 WindowServer windows open. Daemon run as `CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1 cua-driver serve --socket …`, driven by a stdio MCP client through `cua-driver mcp --socket …`. Walk phase from timing marks around `walk_tree_budgeted` in `get_window_state`, median of 15:

| window | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Calculator (36 indexed rows) | 117–145 ms | 56–61 ms |
| TextEdit document | 128–144 ms | 69–85 ms |

Those runs were under machine load (load average about 10). On an idle machine the walk went from 47–51 ms to 16–19 ms, combined with the window-lookup change in the companion PR.

## Validation

- Live A/B on the same windows: `tree_markdown`, `elements` (minus tokens) and the structured key set are byte-identical to main for Calculator and a TextEdit document.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 639 passed. One unrelated port-discovery test (`owned_discovery_prefers_profile_endpoint_over_inherited_listener`) failed once and passed on three reruns.
- `cargo fmt` passes. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets` adds no new warnings.

title: perf(cua-driver): look up one window by id instead of enumerating all
body:
## Summary

`get_window_state` and every background action resolve the target window several times per call: owner pre-flight, bounds, title, Space membership, capture identity and the keyboard-sibling count in `gather_background_facts`. Each lookup called `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` for every window in the session. On a busy Mac that is about 1,400 windows and 10–15 ms per enumeration. `window_on_current_space_by_id` also queried SkyLight for the Spaces of each of those windows, about 30 ms.

This PR:

- Adds `windows::describe_window(id)`, which describes one window with `CGWindowListCreateDescriptionFromArray`. A window below the normal level is checked against the `kCGWindowListExcludeDesktopElements` enumeration, so a lookup lists exactly what that enumeration lists. The desktop-element set (wallpaper, backstop, desktop icons, underbelly) does not follow one level rule, so it is not guessed.
- Switches `resolve_window_owner`, `window_bounds_by_id`, `window_space_view_by_id` / `window_on_current_space_by_id` (Spaces read for that one window), the capture identity check, the `window_title` / `app_name` lookup in `get_window_state`, and the focus-failure hint to it.
- Makes `gather_background_facts` describe only the AX-mapped sibling windows its keyboard-ambiguity count can match, lazily, instead of enumerating all windows.
- Makes `list_running_apps`, which only reads owner pids, enumerate without the per-window Space queries.

Refs #4534 and #4940. #4940 scopes the Space queries for pid listings; this PR covers lookups by window id.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1, about 1,400 windows. Embedded daemon plus a stdio MCP client, p50/p90 of 12 calls, two rounds:

| call | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| get_window_state, tree only (Calculator) | 129–134 / 141 ms | 67 / 72–76 ms |
| get_window_state, tree + screenshot (Calculator) | 183–188 ms | 79–83 ms |
| get_window_state, tree only (TextEdit) | 139–141 ms | 75–76 ms |
| get_window_state, tree + screenshot (TextEdit) | 242–244 ms | 130–133 ms |

Per-phase marks on Calculator: owner pre-flight 13.4 → 0.4 ms, title lookup 12.6 → 0.3 ms, Space lookup 16.4 → 0.2 ms, tree-only snapshot bounds 13.0 → 0.4 ms, background facts 26.9 → 13.9 ms. The table and these marks were measured before the sibling-row and app-list commits, so the branch head is faster still.

## Validation

- New ignored live test `windows::tests::single_window_lookups_match_the_enumerations`. For every window in the session (1,397 here, including 22 desktop elements), it checks that `describe_window`, `window_space_view_by_id` and `resolve_window_owner` match the enumerations they replace. Run with `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib single_window_lookups -- --ignored`. It passes.
- `get_window_state` output (tree, elements, key set) is identical to main for Calculator and TextEdit.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` passes (`exact_target` included). `cargo fmt` passes. `cargo clippy` adds no new warnings.

title: perf(cua-driver): identify apps without spawning ps or listing every process
body:
## Summary

- `apps::get_app_name_for_pid` spawned `ps -p <pid> -o comm=` on every call, and `get_window_state` called it twice per read through `chromium_browser_window`.
- `ElectronJs::is_electron` runs before every background click, `type_text`, scroll, hotkey and `set_value`. It listed every running app (about 35 ms with roughly 950 processes) to find the pid's name, then spawned `ps` for the executable path.

This PR:

- The `comm` column is the process's argv[0]. `process_command` reads it with `sysctl(KERN_PROCARGS2)`, which the kernel answers for the user's own processes (every app the driver targets). It falls back to the setuid `ps` only when the kernel withholds the arguments.
- `get_window_state` asks once per read.
- `is_electron` checks the executable first. It lists the running apps only when the pid's own bundle name could lead to an Electron bundle. Both checks still run whenever either could be true, so the answer is unchanged.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1:

- `is_electron` over all 948 running pids: old and new agree on every pid (4 Electron). Total time drops from 33.8 s to 1.06 s, about 35 ms to 1.1 ms per call.

title: fix(cua-driver): run screencapture by absolute path and let hosts turn it off
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: when ScreenCaptureKit cannot capture a window, the macOS driver falls back to `screencapture -l <id> -x -o`, started by name through the inherited `PATH`. `/usr/sbin/screencapture` is entitled to record audio and macOS checks its privacy access against the host app, so in an embedded host it can raise a Microphone prompt attributed to the host and take focus during background control (#5938).
- What changed: `screencapture` now runs only from `/usr/sbin/screencapture`, for both the window fallback and the display capture. A host can set `CUA_DRIVER_DISABLE_SCREENCAPTURE=1` so the driver never starts the tool: a failed native window capture then returns the native error, and every whole-display capture (the agent desktop capture without a cursor overlay, recording before/after snapshots, picture-in-picture frames) goes through ScreenCaptureKit with nothing excluded, the same image `screencapture -x` takes. The embedded SDK passes the variable through its environment allowlist. An embedded driver (`--embedded`), and the SDK's private worker runtime (`__private-worker`, host-owned but launched without `--embedded`), keep `screencapture` off by default, since a host on an SDK whose allowlist predates the variable cannot pass it, and the tool's prompts and its temporary capture file (`${TMPDIR}/cua-driver-rs-capture-<pid>-<uuid>/window.png`, readable by the host's user) land under the host's identity; a host that wants the tool sets `CUA_DRIVER_DISABLE_SCREENCAPTURE=0`, which requires an SDK that allowlists the variable (this PR's; npm `@trycua/cua-driver` 0.37.0 rejects the name whatever its value). Standalone drivers keep it on by default. The in-process runtime (`RuntimeOptions`, the C ABI, the Node addon) is left as is: it runs inside the host app's own process, which can set the variable in its own environment with no allowlist in the way.

## Related work

Refs #5938

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): MCP schemas and the protocol are unchanged, but this does change a default: embedded and SDK-worker runtimes no longer start `screencapture` unless the host allows it. I treated that as part of the #5938 bug fix, since the tool raises unrelated privacy prompts and writes a temporary capture file under the host's identity. I'm happy to open an RFC first if maintainers want the default change reviewed that way.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Embedded hosts change default: when ScreenCaptureKit cannot capture a window, the `screencapture` shell fallback is refused (the in-memory SkyLight route may still succeed) unless the host sets `CUA_DRIVER_DISABLE_SCREENCAPTURE=0`. Standalone drivers that do not set the variable keep the same fallbacks, except that a different `screencapture` earlier on `PATH` is no longer used. With the variable set, a window ScreenCaptureKit cannot capture returns an error instead of a `screencapture` image; the off-Space SkyLight route is unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: small and local to `platform-macos/src/capture.rs` and the SDK allowlist; revert the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (macOS 27.2 arm64, from `libs/cua-driver/rust`):
  - `cargo fmt -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-sdk --check`: pass.
  - `cargo test -q -p platform-macos --lib`: 639 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored.
  - `TMPDIR=/tmp cargo test -q -p cua-driver-sdk --lib`: 109 passed, 0 failed.
  - `capture::tests::an_embedded_driver_keeps_screencapture_off_unless_the_host_allows_it` failed with the embedded default ignored and passes with it; `cargo test -q -p platform-macos --lib` at the new head: 640 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored.
  - `capture::tests::a_host_owned_runtime_gets_the_embedded_default` failed against a no-op marker and passes once the private worker's marker is set; at head `60f13a9642`: `cargo test -q -p platform-macos --lib` 641 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored; `cargo check -q -p cua-driver` passes.
  - New tests `capture::tests::screencapture_runs_only_from_its_absolute_path`, `capture::tests::a_host_can_turn_screencapture_off` and `embedded::tests::disable_screencapture_env_propagates`. With the previous behavior restored (relative `screencapture`, no allowlist entry) the absolute-path and allowlist tests fail.
- Manual or platform evidence: none yet for the TCC prompt itself; it is being verified live with a host app built from this change.
- Known gaps or CI still required: `cargo clippy -D warnings` on this toolchain reports 5 errors in files this change does not touch (`ax/reveal_scroll.rs`, `tools/click.rs`, `document_edit.rs`), reported in #5943. Repository CI still required.

title: fix(cua-driver): report Windows toggle and expand/collapse state on elements
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, `get_window_state` elements cannot express three UI Automation states. An indeterminate checkbox has no state (`read_cached_selected` maps only On/Off), expand/collapse state is never read, and toggle state shares `selected` with `SelectionItem.IsSelected` (#5939).
- What changed: Windows elements now carry `toggle_state` (`"on"` / `"off"` / `"mixed"`) and `expanded` (bool) when UIA reports them, read from the already-cached TogglePattern and ExpandCollapsePattern (`ExpandCollapseExpandCollapseStateProperty` is added to the cache request; PartiallyExpanded counts as expanded, LeafNode reports nothing). Tree rows show the same states as `toggle=…` and `expanded=…` attributes, so an incremental read (`since`) reports a state-only change, such as ticking a checkbox, as a change. `selected` keeps its current meaning.

## Related work

Refs #5939

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission, or cross-component contract change): none. This adds optional output fields to Windows `get_window_state` and two row attributes; nothing existing changes meaning. If you consider additive MCP output fields RFC-worthy, say so and I'll open one, or keep this as a draft until then.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only. New optional structured fields and row attributes; existing fields, `selected` included, are unchanged. The typed contract (`WindowElement` in `cua-driver-contract`) does not list the new fields yet, so typed SDK results ignore them while raw/MCP output carries them; adding them to the contract plus regenerating the bindings is a natural follow-up I kept out to keep this PR to the Windows walk. `toggle_state` is a string so the contract can carry it as a `snake_case` enum.
- Risk and rollback: reads stay inside the existing cached walk (no new live COM calls). Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `get_window_state_actions_tests.rs` covers `toggle_state` for on/off/mixed, `expanded` for both values, both omitted when unknown, and a tree row that changes when only the toggle or expanded state changes.
- Manual or platform evidence: the same change, on top of `cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0`, passed `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib` on Windows 11 x64 (287 passed, 1 ignored) and the Windows/macOS/Linux release builds plus a 0.37.0 protocol-compatibility check in GOAT's fork of the driver (goat-si/cua-driver#6). On this `main` I applied it by hand (the import list differs) and ran `rustfmt`; I have not built this exact branch.

title: fix(cua-driver): get_screen_size reads the GNOME Wayland monitor layout from Mutter
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on a GNOME Wayland session without an X11 `DISPLAY`, `get_screen_size` fails ("`$DISPLAY` variable not set"). Consent scopes whole-desktop and unfiltered listing calls to that geometry (`cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs`), so `list_windows {app}` and similar calls are refused with "confirmation provider failed: display identity could not be read". An embedded host on native GNOME Wayland cannot list or act on any window.
- What changed: `get_screen_size` reads GNOME's monitor layout from `org.gnome.Mutter.DisplayConfig.GetCurrentState` when the driver runs on Wayland without `DISPLAY`. The answer is content-free (logical-monitor positions, scale, transform, current mode) and has the Hyprland path's shape: frame size, largest scale, and per-monitor `frame_x`/`frame_y`. Like Hyprland's IPC check, the unique D-Bus connection that owns the name must be the `SO_PEERCRED` peer of the `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` socket, and the layout is read from that unique connection, so a handover of the well-known name cannot substitute another process. An inherited `WAYLAND_SOCKET` is refused, and the socket connect is non-blocking and bounded on the calling thread. Any refusal keeps today's error.

## Related work

Refs #1922 (scope comment: https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/1922#issuecomment-6395031516)

RFC: not required in our reading. No public API, schema or permission changes; the tool returns data it could not return before on this platform.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: only GNOME Wayland without `DISPLAY`. There, `get_screen_size` now succeeds, and consent-scoped listing calls work. X11, Hyprland, and other compositors (KDE, other wlroots) are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: any failure (no Mutter, attestation mismatch, timeout, odd layout) falls through to the previous X11 read and its error. Reverting restores today's behavior.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib mutter_display` on this branch (`main` at 9f910eae0): 10 passed. They cover the frame math (layout mode, scale, rotation, offsets, unusable layouts), reading from the attested owner when the name moves, refusal of an inherited `WAYLAND_SOCKET`, a non-blocking connect that leaves nothing behind on a full backlog, a `WAYLAND_SOCKET` found in the start environment, and NUL paths refused.
- Manual or platform evidence: in an isolated headless GNOME 46 Wayland session without XWayland, `cua-driver mcp` → `get_screen_size` returned "Desktop frame: 1600x1000 points @ 1x … Meta-0 1600x1000 on, at (0,0)", matching `GetCurrentState`. 0.37.0 in the same session returned "`$DISPLAY` variable not set and no value was provided explicitly". (Measured on our fork build, which carries the identical commit.)
- Known gaps or CI still required: real seat GNOME and multi-monitor hardware not tested. Forged-owner attestation is covered by unit tests, not live (needs a second compositor). KDE is not covered.

**Known limits.** The check refuses a `WAYLAND_SOCKET` the process started with, read from `/proc/self/environ` because `wayland-client` unsets it on use. Once a connection has consumed the socket, every connection the driver opens later with `connect_to_env` (listing, capture, pointer sessions, virtual keyboard) goes to `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, the compositor this attests; connections it keeps open (the overlay, a held drag) stay where they were opened, which is why a socket the process started with is refused outright. Code running inside the process that sets `WAYLAND_SOCKET` after start, or rewrites the start environment (`PR_SET_MM_MAP`), is outside this check: such code could ask Mutter itself.

## Contributor and release checks
