title: macOS 27.2: APNs/BAA failure persists from macOS 27.0.1
body:
### macOS compatibility status

The APNs/BAA failure previously observed in a macOS 27.0.1 VM also occurs in a freshly installed macOS **27.2 (26B123)** VM. Updating to 27.2 has therefore not resolved this macOS problem in our test.

### Test setup

Tested on **2026-10-30**, with both host and guest running macOS **27.2 (26B123)**.

The guest was freshly installed and Setup Assistant was completed manually with a local account, without signing into an Apple Account. APNs was checked with:

```sh
/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ApplePushService.framework/apsctl status
/usr/bin/log show --last 10m --process apsd --info --debug --style compact
```

### Observed result

The production connection remained disconnected in two status samples several minutes apart:

```text
connection environment: production
   connection status: No
```

The `apsd` log contains the same SEP key-generation and BAA certificate failure chain seen in the earlier macOS 27.0.1 test:

```text
unable to generate key: error e00002e2(-536870174)
SecKeyCreateRandomKey_ios failed: ... Code=-25308 "Failed to generate keypair"
APSBAAClientIdentityProvider failed to obtain a BAA cert
underlying identity provider has identity to connect? NO
told not to connect!
```

Two consecutive attempts produced this error chain at **10:35:33 UTC**. The later status sample at **10:40:51 UTC** still showed no production connection.

Related reports of the same APNs/BAA error pattern: [Apple Developer Forums thread 840500](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/840500).

This confirms persistence of the APNs/BAA failure in this 27.2 test.

title: fix(cua-cli): load saved token for consented local host
body:
## Summary

`cua do switch host` registers a direct sandbox, but without an explicit token it never loads the local host service's `host/env-token`. Later actions consequently reach the right service without its bearer token and fail authentication.

Add a final credential fallback for the sandbox named `host`, only when its endpoint exactly matches the configured local host URL and the existing host-consent marker is present. Read the token when resolving the connection, trim surrounding whitespace, and ignore missing or empty files. Already-selected hosts benefit without being registered again.

## Related work

Fixes #6154.

No RFC: this repairs credential loading for the existing consented host target. It adds no CLI flags, protocol fields, or permission grants.

## Compatibility and risk

- Remembered direct credentials, registry credentials, and `CUA_ENV_TOKEN` retain their existing precedence. `--token` and `CUA_HOST_ENV_TOKEN` continue to work through host selection.
- The automatic fallback does not apply to an unrelated endpoint, another sandbox name, or a host whose consent marker has been removed. The local token is not copied into the direct-credential store or printed.
- This changes CLI credential resolution only; it does not change host setup, authentication enforcement, desktop input, or the SDK protocol. Rollback is a revert of this commit.

## Validation

From `libs/cua`, using the repository-pinned Rust 1.97.1 on macOS arm64:

- Before the production change, `host_target_uses_its_saved_token_after_consent` failed on the screenshot action with `unauthenticated: unauthenticated: bad token (Unauthenticated)` from the mock service.
- `cargo test --locked --offline -p cua-cli --lib --test sandbox_do -- --test-threads=2`: 298 unit tests and 16 integration tests passed; one existing host-runtime probe remained ignored.
- Regression coverage includes saved-token loading with a trailing newline, consent enforcement and removal, explicit-token precedence, a custom endpoint, and a different sandbox at the local endpoint. Tests run the real CLI against loopback mocks with temporary homes; they do not use the developer's desktop or credentials.
- `cargo clippy --locked --offline -p cua-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `bash scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast`: SPDX headers and CLI formatting passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The signed Cua Spaces app from the report was not exercised. Linux/Windows execution and upstream CI remain pending. The macOS test builds emit the same SDK unwind-table linker warning seen before the production change; Clippy passes without suppression.

title: fix(cua-sdk): report unsupported remote health checks accurately
body:
## Summary

`Spaces::machine_health` treats every `DiagnoseHost` `Unimplemented` response as proof that the remote computer runs an older Cua. The current Windows host returns the same status for its unsupported daemon transport, so the CLI and Spaces UI recommend an update that does not resolve the problem.

Report that the computer does not support remote health checks and suggest running `cua doctor --machine this` on that computer. Keep the existing error kind, timeout, ownership checks, successful response, and other RPC error handling unchanged.

## Related work

Fixes #6212.

No RFC: this corrects misleading diagnostic text within an existing error path; it adds no API, protocol, permission, or platform capability.

## Compatibility and risk

- Shared client-side handling applies to both an unsupported Windows transport and an older server missing the RPC. Neither status alone establishes that an update supplies the feature.
- The `host_capability_missing` tag remains unchanged. No host settings or transport behavior change.
- This does not implement remote Windows health checking. Reverting the message change restores the previous diagnostic.

## Validation

On macOS arm64 with the repository-pinned Rust 1.97.1:

- Added three public-API integration tests through the existing loopback fake relay and gRPC host. They cover the Windows `Unimplemented` message, an unknown RPC, successful health responses, permission denial, and connection failure.
- Before the fix, the new unsupported-health test failed on the old update advice; the two control tests passed.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-spaces --test host_spaces -- --test-threads=4`: **44 passed**, including a rerun on candidate `12bf9f2f9ad67d447bc35338e4df9e540044fa85`.

The full crate run was **not clean**, and no full-suite or CI pass is claimed:

- `providers::a_space_that_fails_to_start_leaves_no_instance` expected one deletion but observed two. It failed identically after restoring all production source to upstream `78cbbecab6e1803d25b9cf093070e7e41bbb4c4d`; it is left unchanged.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop the video startup probe skewing recording times
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: with `record_video: true`, turn times start after the video backend's 1.5 s startup probe. An action logged at 3.0 s can appear at about 4.5 s in `recording.mp4`, and `recording render` inherits the offset. The probe also shortens ffmpeg's reported `duration_ms`.
- What changed: read the session's wall-clock start next to its monotonic anchor before starting video, so turns share the zero already used by `cursor.jsonl`. Start ffmpeg's duration clock before spawning the encoder. Both startup probes stay.

## Related work

Refs #6210

RFC: not required. This restores the existing timing contract without changing fields, schemas, traits, or public APIs.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: wf-recorder and ffmpeg turn offsets include their startup probe; `started_at_monotonic_ms` moves earlier accordingly. Remove any manual 1.5 s compensation. ffmpeg duration metadata now includes the probe.
- Risk and rollback: backend setup latency remains between the shared anchor and the first video frame. ScreenCaptureKit has no probe and now includes capture setup time in its turn clock, which may make turns lead the video. This requires macOS evidence. Both production changes are individual clock moves and revert independently. Wall-clock steps remain an existing risk.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the new `turn_times_count_from_before_the_video_backend_starts` failed before its fix with `turn start 0 ms`; the existing timestamp test passed. After the session fix both timestamp tests passed. The new `stop_recording_duration_includes_the_ffmpeg_startup_probe` then failed before its fix with `duration_ms 0`; both existing shutdown error tests passed.
- Complete core owner: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --locked` reports 1,142 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored across all 18 unit/integration/doc-test groups, including both new regressions and manifest start-time preservation. The runtime lost its command session handle before the shell saved the exit code; the complete log ends at the successful doc-test footer, and no test process remains.
- Protocol owners: `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_media_test --test protocol_schema_test --locked` exits 0; schema tests pass 4/4. The media binary runs 0 tests because its whole-file cfg selects only macOS/Windows, so media protocol coverage is unverified on Linux. An unchanged dependency, `nom v1.2.4`, emits a future-Rust incompatibility warning.
- Final affected tests: after the review correction, both focused test binaries pass 5/5 (exit 0). Only test cfg/module organization and subsequent whitespace/comment cleanup changed after the wider runs; production sources are unchanged. Independent read-only review accepted the correction with no remaining actionable findings.
- Local checks: `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --base a9902d272655b65180fa713a8b1f2f1c1935e70b` exits 0; SPDX headers, scoped cargo fmt, and all-targets clippy with `-D warnings` pass. Windows clippy is skipped because cargo-xwin is absent. `git diff --check` passes.

title: [Feature]: keep typed secrets out of `action.json`
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

With recording on, `action.json` stores tool arguments as sent, so a password typed through `type_text` lands in the recording in plain text. `recording_args_for` (`cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs:6367`) already redacts `clipboard_write` text and `browser_dialog`'s `prompt_text`, but not `type_text`, `browser_type` or `set_value`.

### Desired outcome

A caller can type a secret during a recording without its value reaching the recording's files. The turn still shows that text was typed and where.

### Current workaround

After `stop_recording` we replace known values in every text file of the recording folder. The plain text stays on disk until then.

### Affected components and platforms

`recording_args_for`, the text tools, and `replay_trajectory`, which re-invokes each turn's call and can't type a redacted value. Every platform.

### Alternatives and prior art

Always redact typed text, like `clipboard_write`. Simple, but it breaks replay and hides ordinary typing when debugging.

### Implementation ideas

- Per call: `sensitive: true` on the text tools.
- Per session: secret values given to `start_recording` and replaced across the turn's text files.

We need the per-session shape, because the caller knows the values and the agent doing the typing may not mark them. Both change a public tool schema. Does this need an RFC?

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for existing issues, RFCs, and active pull requests.
- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: fix(sdk): keep Keyvault payloads consistent when a batch commit fails
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `Vault::upsert_items` writes payloads, then commits the sealed index, then advances the external generation anchor. One cleanup closure handled every failure, which caused two problems:
  - If the anchor write failed after the index had landed, the closure deleted the new payload files. The committed index still listed those items, and `read_payload` returned `NotFound`.
  - If the index write itself failed after an existing item's record had been overwritten, the old index was left pointing at the new record, so the item failed its digest check. Before this change that failure appeared after reopening; `update_meta` also adopted the draft in memory before the write.
- What changed:
  - `save_meta` is split into `write_meta`, which seals the next generation and adopts it in memory only after the write lands, and `record_generation`, which advances the anchor.
  - `upsert_items` stages every record it replaces as a hard link, so nothing is copied. A failure before the commit point removes created files and renames the staged records back, which needs no free space; a restore that still fails is reported, not ignored. A failure after the commit keeps every payload the index references and still returns the error.
  - A record that is already missing counts as nothing to restore, so an upsert can repair an indexed item whose file is gone (review follow-up).

## Related work

Small, self-contained fix; no existing issue or PR found.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: none on success. On these failure paths, the vault now stays readable, matching either the previous committed state or the new one.
- Risk and rollback: the change is local to `cua-keyvault` `store.rs`. Revert to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `upsert_keeps_committed_payloads_when_the_anchor_write_fails`: with the anchor directory removed, a mixed update-and-create batch keeps every indexed item readable, in memory and after reopening.
  - `upsert_restores_overwritten_records_when_the_index_write_fails` (unix): with the vault root read-only and `items/` writable, the existing item keeps its old payload and no new file remains.
  - `upsert_repairs_an_indexed_item_whose_record_is_missing`: an indexed item with a deleted file is repaired by the next upsert, and no staged backup remains after an ordinary update.
  - Each test fails when its fix is reverted, the link restore is made a no-op, or staged-link cleanup is skipped (mutation-checked).
  - On this branch: `cargo test -p cua-keyvault` passed 168 tests across all targets. `cargo clippy -p cua-keyvault --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: a hermetic synthetic probe confirmed the original fault-path observations before the fix.
- Known gaps or CI still required: none known.

title: fix(sandbox): preserve registry identity for QEMU image layers
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on the local QEMU path, `NativeQEMURuntime._image_ref` returned `vm:<ref>` for a registry image only when the image had no build work. A registry image with layers, env or files fell through to `create_session_disk`, which lost the pinned registry identity. `NativeRuntime` already applies VM layers after boot through cua-spacesd and refuses when the image has no spacesd (`_require_spacesd_for_layers`), so those images should keep `vm:<ref>`.
- What changed: a registry image without an explicit disk now always resolves to `vm:<ref>`, and its layers are applied after boot by the existing owner. When layers are applied after boot, `NativeRuntime.start` waits for readiness probes only after the layers have run, because a layer may install the service a probe waits for (review follow-up). Explicit disks and non-registry images are unchanged.

## Related work

Small, self-contained fix; no existing issue or PR found.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: local QEMU sandboxes created from a registry image with layers boot the pinned registry disk and receive their layers after boot, instead of a locally rebuilt session disk.

title: ci: stop PR-scoped cache saves, cap the gate timeout, and measure it
body:
Stops pull requests from writing PR-scoped Rust caches in the E2E matrices, and caps the CI gate at three hours instead of six.

CUA-3211

## What changes

- `.github/workflows/e2e-rust-linux.yml`, `.github/workflows/e2e-rust-windows.yml`: the nine `save-if` guards read `github.ref_type == 'branch'`, which is also true on `pull_request`, so they never gated a PR save. The single `Swatinem/rust-cache` call honours `save-if` itself and was writing PR-scoped entries. It now saves only on `main` or a `workflow_dispatch`. The eight `.github/actions/rust-cache` sites now read `github.event_name != 'pull_request' && ...`. That action already decides `save` itself and only drops a save on the literal `"false"`, so for those eight the change states the intent rather than changing behaviour. Every guard keeps `needs.source.outputs.sha == github.sha`, so a dispatch that certifies an older commit cannot seed main's scope.
- `.github/workflows/ci-gate.yml`: `timeout-minutes` 360 to 180. The gate's longest run on main is well under that, so a wedged gate now releases the required check after three hours.
- Tests: `test_ci_gate_workflow.py` now expects 180. New `test_cache_saves_never_write_pull_request_scope_but_keep_dispatches` on Linux and Windows. It checks only the `save-if:` lines, so `setup-node`'s `cache:` inputs are untouched.

## Not changed

- `ci-gate` `sleep 120`: run creation can still fan out near the end of that window, and `test_gate_catches_a_failing_run_that_appears_inside_the_window` covers it.
- `poll_interval()`: `test_gate_poll_schedule_backs_off_and_stays_within_the_api_budget` pins the schedule.
- `concurrency:` on `ci-release-metadata.yml`: a cancelled call fails the required `validate` check (`test_installer_compatibility_never_cancels_a_superseded_caller`).

## Proof

The scoped repository checks pass on the merged head (`.github/scripts/tests`, em-dash check).

CI on this head is the proof for the workflow change. Every guarded job in the release gate's Linux and Windows E2E legs and in the Rust Linux interactive run logs `save-if: false`. The in-repo rust-cache plan prints `save=false`. After the run, the `refs/pull/6260/merge` cache scope holds only the two `setup-node` npm entries and no Rust or sccache entry. All required checks pass, including `ci-gate`.

title: [Bug]: Hyprland 0.57.0 — unused specialWorkspace omits id, j/monitors fails to parse, list_windows always returns []
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Hyprland 0.57.0 every `list_windows` call returns `{"windows": []}` because the driver cannot deserialize `hyprctl -j monitors`. Hyprland 0.57.0 serializes an unused `specialWorkspace` as `{"address":"","type":"","name":""}` with no `id`, and `struct Workspace { id: i64 }` requires it. One failed `j/monitors` parse empties the whole window inventory. Reproduces on `0.33.4`, `0.38.0` and the `2026-11-01` nightly.

### Reproduction

1. Hyprland 0.57.0, native Wayland session, driver started with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`.
2. Open two or three toplevels. Native Wayland and XWayland windows are affected the same way.
3. `cua-driver call list_windows --json`.

Observed on every call, not intermittent. `cua-driver call get_desktop_state` still returns a valid PNG from the same session, so capture is unaffected.

### Expected behavior

`list_windows` returns the visible toplevels with their bounds, as reported working on Hyprland 0.56.2 in #3247.

### Actual behavior

```json
{ "windows": [] }
```

Daemon log, once per call:

```
WARN platform_linux::wayland: Hyprland window enumeration unavailable: invalid Hyprland IPC JSON: missing field `id` at line 25 column 5
```

`hyprctl -j monitors` on 0.57.0 omits the key for an unused special workspace, and line 25 column 5 of that payload is the closing brace of this object:

```json
"specialWorkspace": {
    "address": "",
    "type": "",
    "name": ""
},
```

`activeWorkspace` and client workspaces still carry `id`, so only an unused special workspace breaks the parse.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `cua-driver` `0.33.4-2` (omarchy repo), `cua-driver` `0.38.0` (`cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0` release tarball), `cua-driver` `0.38.1-nightly.20261101.41272696578`. All three reproduce.

Operating system and architecture: Omarchy 4.0.6 / Arch Linux x86_64, Hyprland `0.57.0-1`, hyprutils `0.14.3-1`, one output `2048x1115` at scale `1.25`.

Application/browser/window system: native Wayland toplevels plus one XWayland (`kitty`) window. Affected identically.

### Evidence

The log line and the `hyprctl` fragment above. Adding `#[serde(default)]` to `Workspace.id` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/hyprland.rs` and building `0.38.0` locally makes the same session return all three windows with correct bounds, `get_window_state` return a window capture at `1019x1115`, and the AT-SPI walk return 250 nodes.

`Workspace.id` is only read to build the visible-workspace set, via `active_workspace.id` and `special_workspace.id` in `list_windows`, so an absent id on an unused special workspace cannot select a wrong workspace. `Option<i64>` would work as well.

### Workaround and additional context

This matters beyond the empty list, because discovery-only is the recommended route on 0.57.0: #6232 asks for the v3 input route on 0.57.0 and suggests building the plugin without it, and #5751 collects 0.57.0 requalification rows. On 0.57.0 discovery is broken too, so that route currently yields no windows at all.

Local workaround: patch `Workspace.id` with `#[serde(default)]` and rebuild.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): list windows when Hyprland omits a workspace id
body:
## Why

On Hyprland 0.57.0, `list_windows` returns `[]` for every app. `0.57.0` serializes an unused `specialWorkspace` as `{"address":"","type":"","name":""}`, without the `id` field every earlier release sends, and `struct Workspace { id: i64 }` required it. One failed `j/monitors` parse empties the whole window inventory, so discovery fails before any window identity, AT-SPI, or input path can run.

Fixes #6267

Refs #6232, #5751. Discovery-only is the 0.57.0 workaround suggested in #6232, and #5751 tracks 0.57.0 requalification. Both assume a driver that can list windows on 0.57.0, which this restores.

RFC: none required. This adds no contract, permission, or cross-component change; it restores behavior the driver already documents for a compositor it already supports. If you read 0.57.0 support itself as a compatibility change, say so and I will stop and file an RFC instead.

## What changed

`Workspace.id` is now `#[serde(default)]`, so an absent id reads as `0`, which the visible-workspace filter already treats as "not a live workspace". A reply that does report an id still decides visibility exactly as before, so windows on a special workspace are not hidden. The visible-set computation moved out of `list_windows` into `active_workspaces` so the reply parse and the resulting visible set are asserted together, which is the strongest boundary reachable without adding an injector to shipped code.

One file: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/hyprland.rs`.

## Scope

- In: the `j/monitors` parse on the Hyprland adapter, plus one unit test covering a reply with and without the field.
- Out: window identity, AT-SPI correlation, input, and every other compositor.
- `#3448` also touches this adapter, but only `wayland/mod.rs`, not this parse, so the two do not overlap.

## Tradeoffs

If Hyprland ever omitted `id` for the *active* workspace, that workspace would read as `0` and be dropped from the visible set, hiding its windows. Hyprland reports the active workspace id in every release observed, and the tolerance only applies to a field that is absent. Rollback is reverting one line plus the extraction.

No `no-release` label is applied: this is a `fix` with a real release entry, not a non-releasing change.

## Blast Radius

Linux/Wayland/Hyprland only. Replies that carry `id` are unchanged. Replies that omit it now parse instead of failing. No API, CLI, or MCP surface change, and no other platform adapter is touched.

## Verification

- Focused tests: `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib wayland::hyprland` passes on this branch, including the new `monitor_reply_accepts_a_special_workspace_without_an_id`.
- `cargo fmt -p platform-linux --check` clean. SPDX header check clean.
- Platform evidence, Hyprland `0.57.0-1` (Omarchy 4.0.6, Arch x86_64, one 2048x1115 output at scale 1.25), release build from this branch, same session, same daemon flags (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`):
  - this branch: `list_windows` returns 3 toplevels with correct bounds, no warnings in the daemon log;
  - upstream `main` rebuilt from the same checkout with this commit reverted: `{"windows": []}` and `WARN platform_linux::wayland: Hyprland window enumeration unavailable: invalid Hyprland IPC JSON: missing field \`id\` at line 25 column 5`.
- Known gap: `scripts/ci/prepush.sh` reports the clippy step failing with 9 pre-existing lints in files this change does not touch (`input/mod.rs`, `get_window_state.rs`, `launch_app.rs`, `press_key.rs`, `wayland/mod.rs`, and the older `SCALED_OUTPUTS` constant in `hyprland.rs`). The identical list appears on unmodified `main` under the pinned `1.97.1` toolchain with `-D warnings`, so this change adds no lint. The Windows clippy step was skipped here (`cargo-xwin` not installed); CI covers it.
- Known gap: the crate-wide `cargo test -p platform-linux` has three failing tests on this host (`input::admission_tests::a_drag_abandoned_after_its_press_still_releases_the_button` and `input::own_dialog_tests::focus_restore_leaves_focus_on_a_dialog_the_app_opened` need `xvfb`; `overlay::tests::unreported_arrival_releases_the_waiter_after_the_cap` asserts on a timing floor). All three fail identically on unmodified `main`, so the suite's baseline is unchanged by this patch.

title: fix(cua-driver): suppress macOS foreground focus steal during isolated browser launch
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On macOS, `browser_prepare` with `mode: "isolated"` and `posture: "background"` spawns standalone Chromium directly via `std::process::Command` (`BrowserPlatform::spawn_isolated_browser` previously fell through to the default unguarded spawn). Even with `--no-startup-window` and background posture, Chromium calls `NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps:)` inside `applicationDidFinishLaunching`, briefly stealing foreground activation and key focus from the user's active window during cold start.
- What changed: `MacOsBrowserPlatform::spawn_isolated_browser` now wraps the child spawn in `FocusStealPreventer::begin_suppression` (`BrowserPrepare.isolated.pre` -> `BrowserPrepare.isolated.post`) paired with a bounded (`<= 2.8 s`) `watch_self_activation` SkyLight key-focus/z-order guard that stops immediately if the child process exits early, followed by `restore_front_app_if_browser_front`.

## Related work

Refs #6270

or cross-component contract change): Not required (internal macOS platform fix preserving existing `browser_prepare` background-posture contract; no schema, CLI, SDK, or permission changes).

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only; zero API, CLI, MCP, or SDK contract changes. Cold isolated browser launches keep the user's frontmost window active and key.
- Risk and rollback: Bounded to the initial 2.8 s cold-launch window of driver-spawned isolated browsers (and canceled immediately on child exit/drop), so normal user focus changes afterward are unaffected. Revert this single-file change in `platform-macos/src/browser/platform.rs` to roll back.

title: perf(cua-driver): poll AXWebArea stabilization instead of sleeping 500ms on Chromium AX wake
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On macOS, `ax::enablement::await_web_content` unconditionally slept for `CHROMIUM_SETTLE_SECONDS` (`500 ms`) after detecting a populated `AXWebArea` and re-asserting `AXEnhancedUserInterface` / `AXManualAccessibility`, even when Chromium's accessibility subtree had already finished materializing within `50–100 ms`.
- What changed: `probe_web_content` now samples a bounded `AXWebArea` descendant count (`WEB_AREA_SETTLE_SAMPLE_CAP = 128`, depth `4`), and `await_web_content` polls in `50 ms` slices (`CHROMIUM_SETTLE_POLL_SECONDS`) up to the existing `500 ms` ceiling (`CHROMIUM_SETTLE_MAX_SECONDS`), returning early once two consecutive slices observe the same non-zero descendant count.

## Related work

title: feat(cua-driver): add macOS AX root_element_token subtree walk, include_menubar, and pre-seeded regions
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On dense native and Electron macOS windows (`1,000+` AX nodes across split panes, sidebars, toolbars, and detail tables), the depth-first `max_elements` walk can exhaust its budget inside the first large pane before sibling panes are even discovered, forcing agents into full-window `full_output: true` walks (`~15 s` of cross-process AX IPC) to reach or re-verify controls in later regions. In addition, `query` / `full_output` walks previously expanded `AXMenuBar` unconditionally even when callers only wanted in-window content.
- What changed:
  - **Pre-seeded `regions` and `surfaces` (macOS)**: Before the depth-first walk truncates at `max_elements`, `ax::tree` performs a shallow top-level scan of landmark containers (`AXSplitGroup`, `AXScrollArea`, `AXToolbar`, `AXTabGroup`, `AXOutline`, `AXTable`, `AXSheet`, `AXPopover`, etc.), publishing `structuredContent.regions[]` (each carrying an addressable `region_token` of the form `<snapshot_id>:r<N>`, bounds, role, label, and `child_count_hint`) plus window-level `structuredContent.surfaces` (`window`, `sheet`, `popover`, `menubar`) even when the element walk truncates early.
  - **`root_element_token` subtree walk (`get_window_state`)**: Accepts an element token (`<snapshot_id>:<row>`) or region token (`<snapshot_id>:r<N>`) from a live snapshot of the same `(pid, window_id)` and walks only that container's AX subtree while preserving window-level status `AXStaticText` siblings for post-action verification. Refuses fail-closed without evicting the existing live snapshot on `invalid_element_token`, `stale_element_token` (including `current_snapshots`), `conflicting_element_target`, or `detached_root_element`, and returns an explicit `root_element_token_unsupported` refusal on Linux and Windows.
  - **`include_menubar` (`get_window_state`)**: Optional boolean (default `true`, preserving existing behavior); setting `include_menubar: false` skips `AXMenuBar` traversal completely on macOS.
  - **`ViewKey` isolation & MCP reference docs**: Tracks `subtree_scope` and `include_menubar` in `ViewKey` so `since: "latest"` never cross-diffs a scoped subtree read against a full-window baseline, and regenerates the MCP tool reference and macOS/Linux/Windows registry snapshots.

## Related work

Refs #6270

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): Additive optional MCP tool parameters (`root_element_token`, `include_menubar`) and additive `structuredContent` metadata (`regions`, `surfaces`) on `get_window_state`; the portable `GetWindowStateInput` UniFFI/Python/TypeScript/C-ABI contract (`SchemaMode::PortableSubset`) is unchanged. Happy to add a companion `docs/rfcs/` document if maintainers would like one for the new optional MCP parameters before merge.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - Default `get_window_state` behavior when `root_element_token` and `include_menubar` are omitted is preserved on all platforms; macOS responses gain additive `structuredContent.regions` and `structuredContent.surfaces` arrays when landmarks/surfaces are present.
  - Linux and Windows accept `include_menubar` without error and fail closed with `root_element_token_unsupported` if `root_element_token` is supplied.
  - `SnapshotPayload` adds default-implemented `region_len()` (`0`) and `retain_region()` (`None`) methods, keeping non-macOS `SnapshotStore` payloads source-compatible.
- Risk and rollback: Refusal paths in `SnapshotStore::resolve_root_token` and `GetWindowStateTool` run before snapshot publication so an invalid, stale, cross-window, or detached `root_element_token` never clobbers the caller's live snapshot. Revert this commit to roll back cleanly.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast` (`SPDX headers`, `generated docs are current`, `cargo fmt`)
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib` (`1110 passed; 0 failed`, including `element_token::tests::region_and_element_root_tokens_round_trip` and `snapshot_store::tests::resolve_root_token_handles_elements_regions_and_preserves_snapshot_on_refusal`)
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib ax::` (`63 passed; 0 failed`) and `tools::get_window_state` (schema and view option tests)
  - `CUA_TEST_REQUIRE_DRIVER_BIN=1 cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test schema_consistency_test --test compatibility_contract_test` (`pass`)
  - `node docs/node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs --test scripts/docs-generators/runner.test.ts scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver.test.ts scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver-platform.test.ts scripts/docs-generators/prose-style.test.ts scripts/docs-generators/reference-quality.test.ts` (`45 pass; 0 fail`)
- Manual or platform evidence: Benchmarked on macOS against a 4-region, `1,500`-row native AppKit split-view harness where pane 4 sits past the default `max_elements` walk budget:
  - Full-window fallback (`full_output: true`, `max_elements: 2000`): `15,998.2 ms` (`observe + click + verify`)

title: fix(spaces): enforce the notch helper line limit before appending
body:
## Summary

The notch helper promises to drop lines longer than 32 MiB. The check currently covers only the unfinished buffer. If a newline arrives in the same chunk as the whole line, or as the bytes that take it over the limit, the oversized line reaches the decoder.

Check the remaining byte allowance before appending each segment, including the one before a newline. Drop the whole oversized line and continue with the next one. Lines exactly at the limit still pass, and one chunk may contain several valid lines.

## Related work

Small, self-contained fix; no linked issue. No RFC is needed: this enforces the existing `NotchProtocol.maxLine` contract without changing the wire format.

## Compatibility and risk

Only the macOS notch helper changes. The main risk is discarding a valid line at the boundary or losing the next message after a rejection; both have regression coverage. The two-file change can be reverted on its own.

## Validation

Checked commit: `dc7f3a43a1f1f3ba9229e52bc19c9bf6a4319b98`.

- `libs/spaces-notch-swift/scripts/test.sh`: all 21 tests passed. New regressions fail against the original implementation for complete oversized lines and lines whose final chunk crosses the limit. Exact-limit, fragmented-input and recovery controls pass.
- `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast --base origin/main`: applicable SPDX check passed.
- `swift build --package-path libs/spaces-notch-swift -c release --product CuaSpacesNotch` and the built helper's `--selftest`: passed.
- Sent an oversized JSON quit line to the optimized helper's stdin, then hello and quit. It dropped the oversized record, answered hello and exited 0 without stderr. A separate hello exactly at 32 MiB also passed.
- Local platform: macOS 26.5.1, arm64, Apple Swift 6.3.2; the package uses Swift 5 language mode.

The visible Electron app was not exercised. These checks cover the splitter's public interface and the real helper process.

As of November 3, 2026, this PR is ready for review. The CLA is signed and the contributor-attribution check passed. Codex's automated review completed on the checked commit with no findings; no human review has been submitted. GitHub CI is still held for maintainer workflow approval (`action_required`), including the release-metadata and macOS test workflows. Those workflows have not run.

title: fix(spaces): preserve newer typing across repeated notch search echoes
body:
## Summary

The notch helper can replace newer typing with an older search echo. Type "a", then "ab", and let the host send "a" twice while other notch state changes. The first echo is skipped. The second is treated as a host replacement, so the search goes back to "a".

Remember the last text received from the core. Another state carrying that text does not consume another acknowledgement. New host text still acknowledges typing or replaces it, and a closed panel's empty query clears pending typing even when the previous host text was already empty.

## Related work

Small, self-contained fix; no linked issue. No RFC is needed: the existing search events and state messages keep their wire format and meaning.

## Compatibility and risk

Only the macOS notch helper changes. Host clears must keep working, including Escape while open and closing after a pending backspace to empty. title: fix(cua-driver): refuse unsafe background input for UTM
body:
## 개요
- UTM guest console에서 background text 입력이 A 키 반복으로 변형되는 경로를 안전하게 거절합니다.
- 공개 버그 #6296의 재현 경로를 대상으로 하며, 서명된 배포 앱이나 VM 설정은 바꾸지 않습니다.

## 문제 배경
Cua Driver의 PID-routed Unicode text 이벤트는 keycode 0과 Unicode payload를 함께 보냅니다. UTM은 payload 대신 physical key transition을 guest에 전달할 수 있어, 정상 문자열이 반복된 a로 오염됩니다. 이 경로를 성공으로 보고하면 자동화가 잘못된 명령을 실행할 위험이 있습니다.

## 무엇을 바꿨는가
- platform-macos keyboard: com.utmapp.UTM을 input forwarder로 exact-match 분류했습니다.
- type_text와 modifier hotkey: background route를 UTM_REQUIRES_FOREGROUND_HID로 fail-closed 처리하고 명시적 foreground HID/window_id만 안내합니다.
- 기존 Screen Sharing의 SCREEN_SHARING_REQUIRES_FOREGROUND_HID 계약은 유지하도록 회귀 테스트를 추가했습니다.

## 검증
- cargo test -p platform-macos --lib: 638 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored
- cargo +1.97.1 clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings: 통과
- cargo +1.97.1 build -p cua-driver: 통과
- scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast: 통과
- read-only Codex 구현 검토는 실행했지만 이 환경의 runner가 최종 출력을 보존하지 않아, 이 Draft PR에서 독립 리뷰를 다시 받아야 합니다.

Refs #6296. 이 변경은 손상되는 background 경로를 거절할 뿐 foreground 자동화를 넓히지 않습니다.

title: feat(spaces): Secure Spaces, child Spaces, conformance, space jobs and the macOS developer-tools image, behind experiments
body:
This puts the next set of Spaces features on main behind experiment switches, with the fixes that need no switch already merged earlier (QEMU monitor on a private socket, microVM restart, Containerization pulls).

## What changes when nobody turns anything on

Nothing a user can see. The new commands and flags are hidden from `--help` and refuse with how to enable them. Spaces keep the open network they have today. Persisted fields are additive and optional.

## Secure Spaces and experiments (off by default)

- `cua experiments list|enable|disable`; switches live in `<CUA_HOME>/experiments/`, or `CUA_EXPERIMENTS=secure-spaces,-child-spaces` per process.
- With `secure-spaces` on: network presets, host-side enforcement, per-tree networks, `cua network`. A Space made before the switch keeps running; restarting a stopped one is refused with the two ways forward (turn it off, or copy files out and recreate).

## Child Spaces (off by default)

Spaces can create child Spaces under a tree budget, and keep commands running as services. Switch: `child-spaces`.

## Runtime conformance

A registry of runtime behaviors, a generated docs page, and a live driver (`libs/cua/scripts/conformance/run.py`). No behavior change.

## Settings, Advanced, Labs

Rows for the two experiments appear only once an experiment is already on. Hidden otherwise, so no UI change for anyone by default.

## Space jobs

Run a job in a Space and read its result, through the Spaces tools and the SDK (`space_jobs`). Additive tools; the tool count and contract are regenerated.

## macOS developer-tools image

The macOS Space with Xcode as a tier (`ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26-xcode`), built locally as the fallback when it is not published. The Xcode build only runs on the manual dispatch path, not on pull requests.

## Also in this update

- The interim guest-side guard that drops inbound IPv4 options in Linux VM images (CVE-2026-98432), from its own branch.
- cua-vmm now embeds committed copies of the macOS recipe files (`libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/recipe/`), so the Rust build reads only `libs/cua`. A test fails when a copy falls behind; refresh with `scripts/images/sync-cua-vmm-recipe.sh`.
- The doctor no longer reports the child-Space tools as a mismatch between `/mcp` and ListTools (they are the MCP server's alone).
- User-facing strings in this change say "computers".
- The CLI Spaces page and the Spaces tools reference are split to stay under the docs page limits.

## Known limits

- With secure-spaces on, macOS microVMs, QEMU on macOS and Windows, macOS VMs, Apple's Containerization and your own cloud refuse or start without network rather than open.
- A QEMU VM started by this build keeps its monitor on a private socket; stop QEMU VMs with this build before going back to an older one.

## Checks run locally

prepush with bindings (all pass except the two items below), regenerated contract, bindings and docs, `buf breaking`, gitleaks, nextest for the touched crates and the spacesd workspace, web check (186 files, 1293 tests), Windows clippy for the touched crates.

- Windows clippy of the whole `libs/cua` workspace fails in the opus C build of `cua-media-codec` (an untouched crate) on this machine; the touched crates pass.
- nextest failures are the ones that also fail on main on a Mac: qemu `live_tpm_vm_refusals`, `providers`, the `scale` tests, a mesh timing test, and the TCP probe in `a_failing_health_check_restarts_a_service`.
- The old-build-then-new-build run over one isolated home and the replica chaos run passed on the earlier stack (secure spaces, child Spaces); they were not repeated on this final head.

## Needs a maintainer

None of the commits here edits a workflow file (the push token cannot).

## CI state at 92fbcbae5

Every check passes except `release` in "CD: Image omarchy" (and `ci-gate`, which fails only because of it). No macOS job timed out.

The Omarchy doctor fails on the display fixture ("grid not located", `input.click`, `input.drag`, `input.scroll`, `screenshot.fixture_pixel`); the build and the 14 e2e checks pass. The same image job is red on unrelated branches: `ci/omarchy-edge-watch` (run 41536122372, same doctor failure), `chore/remove-fleet-mentions` (run 41502099729, an Omarchy mirror signature file over pacman's size limit) and the Hyprland pin and requalify branches. This change only adds `nftables` and the IPv4 options guard unit to that image.

**What changes for users:** the Omarchy Space image boots to a clean desktop again (no Hyprland config-error bar), and its windows behave as before, so the image can be published.

**Cause.** The image build pins Hyprland to 0.56.2-4 because `cua-hyprland-plugin` requires that exact version (#6326). Omarchy edge's config package (`omarchy-dev`) has no older versions to pin, and it moved from r7437.g7f4b1dd (last green image, 30 Oct) to r7561.ga69b19f, which targets Hyprland 0.57 and sets `misc.bell_sound`. title: fix(cua-driver): qualify the Hyprland plugin for Hyprland 0.57.0 (CUA-3107)
body:
Cua's Hyprland plugin now builds against Hyprland 0.57.0, so the Omarchy image can follow Omarchy edge again instead of staying on 0.56.2.

Refs CUA-3107 (and CUA-3105, #6326, #6328).

## What changed
- Ported the input code to the 0.57 plugin headers. The plugin API version is now 0.2. Only three things the plugin uses changed:
  - Window state moved behind `CWindow::backend()`: `m_isX11` is now `backend().isX11()`, `getPID()` is now `backend().pid()`, and `m_isMapped` is private (use `mapped()`).
  - `CInputManager::m_exclusiveLSes` is now `m_exclusiveKeyboardLSes`. It still counts as a grab, so behavior is unchanged.
  - The hyprctl command API is the Socket1 one, which the plugin already supported.
- `src/hyprland_compat.hpp` holds these shims, selected by CMake (`CUA_HYPRLAND_WINDOW_BACKEND_API`). 0.56.2 still builds.
- Input builds are accepted for 0.56.2 and 0.57.0 (was 0.56.2 only). The Arch recipe defaults to 0.57.0 headers.
- Omarchy image: right after the package install, the build now fails early if the installed `hyprland` differs from the version `cua-hyprland-plugin` pins.

Checked by diffing the Hyprland v0.56.2 and v0.57.0 headers for every symbol the plugin uses. Nothing was compiled on the authoring host; CI is the qualification (below).

## Relation to #6326 and #6328
Both are still open and are not touched here. #6326 (archive pin) is still right while the packaged plugin pins 0.56.2. #6328 (drop `bell_sound` below 0.57) turns itself off once the image has Hyprland 0.57, so it can be closed after the follow-ups below.

## Needs after merge (follow-ups)
1. Cut a cua-hyprland-plugin release from this source.
2. Update Omarchy's AUR/package entry to that release, rebuilt against `hyprland=0.57.0-1`. The image installs Omarchy's packaged plugin, so it only moves to 0.57 after this.
3. Re-run the image build and doctor lanes, then close #6328 if it is still open.
4. The native release kit (`packaging/release`, the 0.56.2-1 profile) is a separate certified bundle and is not changed here.

## Requalification
Run through CI with workflow_dispatch on this branch: Hyprland plugin requalify, Omarchy image build (no publish) and the image doctor.

title: feat(cua-driver): fast path with act-time target guards, behind a default-off flag (CUA-3102)
body:
Linear: CUA-3102

Adds the Cua Driver "fast path" behind a new `fast_path` setting, which is **off by default**. With it on, the agent can act on the elements it already read, without taking a fresh full snapshot first. Before each action the driver checks that the target is still the one the agent saw, and it refuses when the target changed.

**For users:** with the setting off, nothing changes. With `set_config {"fast_path": "guard"}` (or `on`), a click on something that moved, changed or disappeared since the last read is refused with `target_changed` and a pointer to fresh state, instead of landing on the wrong thing.

### What's in it
- `cua-driver-core::fast_path` holds the platform-free checks, all std-only and unit-tested:
  - AX fingerprint check: gone, relabelled, role changed, moved, resized, hit mismatch.
  - Pixel check for sparse or no-tree targets: a read-time crop compared with two act-time crops 50 ms apart, an animation settle budget, and a template match for pure shifts, with cursor masking and a wider tolerance for remote desktops.
  - Window guards, per-target classification, and the changed-region finder.
- Modes:
  - `off` (default): no checks.
  - `shadow`: checks run and report `would_refuse`, but never refuse.
  - `guard`: refuses on a mismatch.
  - `on`: guard, plus direct actions return a `since:latest` delta in the same result, and `since:` re-reads are tree-only unless the tree is sparse.
- The setting works on macOS, Linux and Windows through `set_config`/`get_config` (env `CUA_DRIVER_FAST_PATH`). The act-time guards are wired for macOS `click` only so far (token and pixel paths).

### Tests
- Unit tests for each guard reason and the tolerance edges.
- A randomized race over 1,000 iterations per delivery mode (move, swap, remove, row reuse, cover): zero wrong-target actions, zero static false refusals.
- A canvas target that moves or is redrawn, a no-tree window, 1,000 blinking-caret clicks, and a remote-desktop stream with noise and an in-content cursor.

### Flag-off safety
With `fast_path` off, every new entry point returns before doing any work. The only visible changes are the new `fast_path` key in the `set_config` schema and in `get_config`/`set_config` output.

### Not yet
- Guards for the other action tools (`double_click`, `drag`, `type_text`…) and for Windows and Linux.
- A per-call `verify_target` override (implemented in core, not exposed in schemas yet).
- A source-rect window capture for cheaper act-time crops (today each crop captures the whole window).
- Change crops in sparse-target results.

title: feat(cua-driver): keep typed secrets out of recordings
body:
Closes #6250. Linear: CUA-3110.

**What changes for users:** you can type a password during a recording without it landing in the recording's files. Pass it to `start_recording` in `redact_values`, and every turn shows `[redacted]` in its place.

## Changes

- `start_recording` takes an optional `redact_values` (1 to 64 non-empty strings). The values are held in memory only, never written, and cleared on stop or restart. Validation errors name the position, never the value.
- Each turn's `action.json` (arguments, result summary, action truth) and `before_state.json` / `after_state.json` / `app_state.json` are scrubbed. JSON state is scrubbed structurally, so an escaped character can't hide a value. Longer values are replaced first.
- A turn whose arguments lost a value is marked `"redacted": true`. `replay_trajectory` refuses it instead of typing the placeholder.
- Screenshots and video are not altered (the OS masks secure fields). The docs and tool description say so.
- The generated MCP reference gains the new row.

This takes the per-session shape from the issue: the caller knows the values even when the typing agent doesn't. It adds one optional field and changes no existing behaviour.

## Tests

- `redact_values_never_reach_turn_files` walks every file a turn writes and checks that no value appears, raw or JSON-escaped. It also checks the `redacted` mark and that stopping forgets the values.
- Separate tests cover longest-first replacement, schema validation that never echoes a value, and the replay refusal.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib -- recording redact`: all pass except `turn_capture_brackets_action_and_preserves_post_action_aliases`. That test fails the same way on unmodified `main` when run alongside the module (shared capture hooks) and passes alone.

title: [Bug]: `cua join` always fails with `internal: secret name "space-member.mem_…"` and uses up the join code
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### Summary

`cua join <code>` accepts the code and then fails with `cua: internal: secret name "space-member.mem_…"`. It never saves the member credential, so the computer does not join the Space. The code is used up, and a retry with the same code fails with "This code doesn't work".

### Reproduction

1. In Cua Spaces, open a Space and choose Add an agent to get a "Join my Cua Space" link.
2. On a signed-in computer, run `cua join <code>`.
3. Run `cua join <code>` again.
4. Run `cua thread read`.

This happened every time: 2 of 2 attempts, each with a new code.

### Expected behavior

`cua join` saves the member credential and the computer joins the Space. After that, `cua thread join`, `cua thread inbox` and `cua thread post` work.

### Actual behavior

Step 2:

```
$ cua join F64G-3ED7 --json
cua: internal: secret name "space-member.mem_652cf79a39be44a7"
exit=1
```

Step 3:

```
This code doesn't work: it was used, cancelled or has expired, or it is for a Space on another computer. Ask for a new link in Add an agent.
exit=4
```

Step 4:

```
cua: not found: this computer hasn't joined a Space; run cua join <code> first
```

An empty `~/.cua/threads/local-<space>/` directory was created anyway.

### Environment

- Cua component and version: cua CLI 0.10.0 (`cua-sdk-v0.10.0`), daemon 0.10.0, Cua Spaces app 0.19.3 (both the latest release)
- Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2, arm64
- Credential store: default (`CUA_CREDENTIAL_STORE` not set); keyvault unlocked; signed in (`cua auth status` OK)

### Evidence

The member ID in the error is `mem_652cf79a39be44a7`. The first attempt failed the same way with `mem_6f122a4c2f479a08`.

The cause seems to be a mismatch between the secret name the join command builds and the names the credential store accepts:

- `libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/member_cmd.rs`:
  ```rust
  fn secret_name(member_id: &str) -> String {
      format!("space-member.{member_id}")
  }
  ```
  `save_secret(&secret_name(&m.member_id), …)` is called on join (around line 409).
- `libs/cua/crates/cua-auth/src/lib.rs`, `Store::secret_path` (around line 803):
  ```rust
  if name.is_empty() || !name.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_lowercase() || b == b'-') {
      return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(format!("secret name {name:?}")));
  }
  ```

`write_secret_text`, `load_secret` and `clear_secret` call `secret_path(name)` before they branch on the store type. The check therefore applies to the Keychain store and to the file store. `space-member.mem_<hex>` contains `.`, `_` and digits, so the check rejects every member ID that the server issues. The same code is in the `cua-sdk-v0.10.0` tag and on `main`. I did not find a test in `member_cmd.rs` that uses a real member ID.

### Workaround and additional context

I don't know of a workaround. Possible fixes:

- Make `secret_name` produce a name that `secret_path` accepts, for example by encoding the member ID into `[a-z-]`.
- Make `secret_path` accept digits, `_` and `.`, and keep the rejection of path separators and `..`.

`cua join` should also save the credential before it uses up the code, or let the code be retried after a local failure. Then a failure like this one would not use up the invite.

title: fix(cua-driver): deliver deep CDP replies instead of timing out
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `get_browser_state` takes 20 s and returns an incomplete `semantic_v2` snapshot, or refuses in `dom_refs_v1`, on any page deeper than about 63 elements. A full-depth `DOM.getDocument` reply nests two JSON levels per DOM level, so ordinary pages exceed serde_json's default 128-level recursion limit. ChatGPT's home and conversation pages render 69 levels deep (reply nesting 143). `read_loop` silently dropped every frame it could not parse, so the caller waited out the 20 s `CALL_TIMEOUT` even though Chromium had answered in about 20 ms.
- What changed:
  - The CDP reader parses frames with serde_json's recursion limit replaced by an explicit 512-level bound. Chromium refuses to serialize replies past its 300-level CBOR stack limit, so every reply it sends is accepted, while parser recursion and stack use stay bounded.
  - A reply that still cannot be decoded now fails its own call immediately, matched by the leading `id` Chromium writes first, and the socket stays usable. No reply is dropped into a timeout any more.
  - Chromium's own refusal for pages deeper than about 150 elements (`Failed to convert response to JSON: CBOR: stack limit exceeded`) now takes the existing bounded-depth fallback instead of failing the snapshot.

## Related work

Refs #6299 and #6307. Those fix reply *size* above the 16 MiB WebSocket frame limit in the connection config. This fixes reply *nesting depth* in frame decoding. The two changes are independent and touch different lines.

RFC: not required. No public API, protocol field, MCP schema or permission changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: deep pages snapshot in milliseconds instead of 20 s. `semantic_v2` returns complete trees where it used to fall back. `dom_refs_v1` succeeds where it used to refuse. Applies to every platform adapter that uses the shared CDP client.
- Risk: frames are now scanned once for nesting before parsing, a linear pass over bytes. The 512-level bound keeps recursive parsing and `Value` drops within default thread stacks; the cap is exercised in a debug-build test.
- Rollback: revert the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests: `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::` passes, 239 tests on `main` and 251 on the host integration build. New tests:
  - deep replies at 300 levels and at the cap are delivered without waiting for `CALL_TIMEOUT`;
  - a reply above the cap fails its call immediately with a decode error, and the next call on the same socket succeeds;
  - Chromium's verbatim CBOR stack-limit refusal takes the bounded fallback.
- With the production change reverted, both new reader tests fail.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Real browser, Linux X11, Chrome 156.0.8078.79, existing-profile attachment, same tabs, same session flow. Release build before and after:

| Page | Format | Before | After |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| chatgpt.com home (DOM depth 69) | semantic_v2 | 20,326 ms, incomplete | 587 ms |
| chatgpt.com home | dom_refs_v1 | 20,013 ms, refused (`DOM.getDocument timed out after 20s`) | 27 ms |
| example.com with a 64-deep `div` chain | semantic_v2 | 20,017 ms, incomplete | 16 ms, complete |
| example.com with a 64-deep `div` chain | dom_refs_v1 | 20,013 ms, refused | 13 ms |

  The ChatGPT `semantic_v2` result after the fix is incomplete only because the page has more nodes than the 300-node budget; it returns a continuation.
- Over 13 days of production use on this host, 78 successful snapshots each paid the 20 s timeout, nearly all on ChatGPT pages.
- Known gaps: macOS and Windows adapters were not run live; they share the changed reader. CI and the desktop/browser matrix are still required.

title: [Bug]: `open_space_viewer` / `show_space_pip` fail with "Cua Spaces app isn't running" while CuaSpacesMac is running; `spaces-control.json` is never written
body:
### Primary area

Other

### Summary

The Cua Spaces app process (`CuaSpacesMac`) is running, but it never writes `~/.cua/spaces-control.json`. The MCP tools that draw on the user's desktop (`open_space_viewer`, `show_space_pip`) therefore fail with `operator_display is not available on this host`. The error says the app isn't running, which is wrong: the process is up and the daemon works.

## Related problems seen in the same session

1. **`create_space` blocks with no progress.** The MCP call was aborted after 1800 s of silence ("sent no response or progress") while the image pull was still running (269/300 layers). The pull progress only appeared in `~/.cua/vmm/lume/serve.log`. Progress notifications, or an async create, would avoid this.
2. **Local Network permission error.** While the Space was running, the daemon logged `re-attach still failing ... Local Network access is not available ... No route to host` for `192.168.64.5:3211`, and every guest-agent tool returned `this Space's image runs no cua-spacesd`. `nc -z 192.168.64.5 3211` from a normal shell succeeded, so the route was fine and only the app was blocked. The error message misleads: `list_spaces` still advertised `desktop_stream`, and the tool errors blamed the image rather than the permission. Toggling Cua Spaces in Privacy & Security → Local Network and turning Tailscale off did not help. Only the `AllowedEthernetLocalNetworkAddresses` / `AllowedWiFiLocalNetworkAddresses` workaround from the log, plus a reboot, did.
3. **`cua-driver` MCP server fails to start** (see below).




### Reproduction

1. Install Cua Spaces and connect the `cua` MCP server.
2. Call `create_space(image="macos", on="local")`. The first run pulls the 22.5 GB base image and takes about 30 minutes.
3. Call `open_space_viewer(space="local:space-666b491caf")`.

### Expected behavior

Either the app writes `spaces-control.json` at launch, or the tool error names the real cause (for example "the app has no window open yet") and says how to fix it.

### Actual behavior

```
error: operator_display is not available on this host: the Cua Spaces app isn't running
(no control server at /Users/davidmcgregor/.cua/spaces-control.json: No such file or directory (os error 2))
```

- `pgrep` shows `/Applications/Cua Spaces.app/Contents/MacOS/CuaSpacesMac` and the `--service-helper` process.
- `ls ~/.cua | grep control` shows only `host/mesh-control.sock`, never `spaces-control.json`.
- Quitting and relaunching the app (`osascript -e 'quit app "Cua Spaces"'`, then `open -a "Cua Spaces"`) did not create the file.
- After a Mac reboot the file was missing again, and `start_space` was needed because the Space was Stopped.
- `daemon.log` and `log show` have no line about the control server.

### Environment

- macOS 27.2 (arm64), MacBook Pro
- Cua Spaces app 0.19.3, `cua` CLI 0.10.0 (cua-spacesd 0.10.0 on the host; 0.7.0 in the guest)
- Space: `local:space-666b491caf`, image `ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26` (Lume 0.6.0, built-in), created with `create_space(image="macos", on="local")`
- Tailscale was installed and running during part of the test

### Evidence

## `cua-driver` not on `$PATH`

`~/.claude.json` has `{"type": "stdio", "command": "cua-driver", "args": ["mcp"]}`. Claude Code reports `Failed to connect: Executable not found in $PATH: "cua-driver"`.

The binary does exist at `/Applications/Cua Spaces.app/Contents/Helpers/cua-driver`, and only `~/.local/bin/cua` is on `$PATH`. The installer or docs could either symlink `cua-driver` next to `cua` or document the full path.

## Search of existing issues

No match for `spaces-control.json`, `open_space_viewer` or `operator_display`. Related but different: #4823 (viewer "Open when ready" button), #5795 (guest freezes when the volume host goes away).

### Workaround and additional context

_No response_

title: fix(spaces-macos): serve the loopback control server so open_space_viewer works
body:
Refs #6339

## Problem

The Swift app (`apps/cua-spaces-macos`) never writes `~/.cua/spaces-control.json`. Only the Tauri app (`apps/cua-spaces/src-tauri/src/control.rs`) serves the control protocol that `cua_spaces::operator::ControlServerDisplay` calls. So `open_space_viewer` and `show_space_pip` fail with "the Cua Spaces app isn't running" while `CuaSpacesMac` is running.

## Change

- `SpacesControlServer` (new): listens on `127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>`, writes `{port, token}` to `<cua home>/spaces-control.json` (mode 0600, atomic rename), requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and removes the file on quit.
- `POST /viewer/open` resolves the Space (id, short id or name) and opens its page in the main window, as the notch does.
- `/pip/pin`, `/pip/unpin` and `/window/stream` answer `501` with a clear message. Known gap: the app doesn't present those natively through this path yet.
- The cua home follows `CUA_HOME`, then the bundle's `CuaHome` (Cua Spaces Local), then `~/.cua`. A bundle of another channel with no usable home writes nothing. `HelperService.homeDirectory` is the shared piece, split out of `specPath`.
- Not started in an offscreen run.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter "SpacesControlServerTests|HelperServiceTests"`: 15 tests pass. The new suite runs a real server on a real port and checks the file mode, the bearer check (401), unknown Space (404), missing field (400), the 501 routes, and file removal on stop.
- Not yet verified: an end-to-end run of the MCP `open_space_viewer` tool against a built app bundle. I'd like a maintainer or a second pair of eyes on that.
- The full `swift test` suite and the desktop E2E matrix were not run.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop the X11 agent cursor splitting in two while it moves
body:
Fixes CUA-3120. Part of CUA-3103 (new cursor on Windows and Linux).

**For users:** on Linux X11 desktops the agent cursor no longer splits into two pieces while it moves.

## Root cause

The X11 overlay is one full-screen window. Every frame it set a new bounding shape and then uploaded the cursor's pixels as separate requests.

- **With a compositing manager** (picom on the XFCE desktop where the bug was recorded), the manager learns the new shape and the new pixels from separate events, and fetches the shape asynchronously. A composited frame could pair one frame's shape with another frame's pixels, so the arrow showed as two offset pieces.
- **Without one**, pixels the cursor left kept our paint until the window under them answered its Expose, so the previous frame's arrow stayed on screen beside the new one.

## Fix

- **Compositing manager present:** the overlay stops reshaping. The bounding shape stays the whole window, and alpha does the hiding. Each frame clears the rects the last frame drew to transparent and copies the new tiles in. The window sets `_NET_WM_BYPASS_COMPOSITOR=2`, so no manager unredirects it. This path runs only on a 32-bit ARGB window.
- **No compositing manager:** the overlay paints the save-under of the frame on screen back over the pixels it vacates, and only then shrinks the shape. The window underneath then repaints pixels that already look right.
- **Both:** frames are uploaded into offscreen pixmaps first and presented in one short server grab, so no client can read half a frame. The grab holds only small requests, flushed together with the ungrab.

## Tests

Two live X11 regressions (`#[ignore]`, run in CI under `xvfb-run`) paint 600 to 6,000 frames of an alternating-colour square while a second connection reads the root. Every read must show exactly one whole square.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| No compositor, a window that never answers Expose | 927 of 928 reads torn | 0 |
| picom | 43 of 861 reads torn | 0 |

CI installs `picom` for the second run. I re-recorded the same XFCE script with the main build and with this build, under picom: main splits the arrow during moves, and this build shows one whole arrow in every frame.

title: fix(cua-driver): draw the GNOME helper cursor's tip on the click point
body:
Fixes CUA-3121. Part of CUA-3103.

**For users:** on GNOME the agent cursor's tip now sits exactly on the point it clicks.

## Root cause

The GNOME Shell helper (`winrects@cua`) places its cursor actor with its centre on the cursor point. The repaint then mapped the canvas centre (64, 64) to that centre instead of the arrow's tip (55, 30). At 42/128 scale that is 2.95 px left and 11.16 px up, which matches the "about 3 px left and 11 px above" seen in the recording. The pose stream already sends the tip; its test asserts that the last sample equals the target.

## Fix

- The repaint maps the tip (`TIP_X`, `TIP_Y`) to the actor centre.
- The click squish now scales about the tip, like the Rust renderer, so a press no longer moves the point.
- A click the helper plays by itself (`ClickPulse`) no longer draws click marks. Marks show only when cua-driver asks for them (`cursor.marks`). This was the sparkle seen at the tip with marks off.
- The helper is bumped to v12, so a fixed helper can be told apart. The pose API minimum stays 11.

## Tests

- `scripts/tests/test_wayland_helper_cursor_paint.mjs` (run by pytest) paints the helper into a recording Cairo context. It asserts that the tip lands on the point at rest, while travelling (point plus float), on arrival, mid-squish and on clicks. It also asserts that the arrow and halo keep one colour from rest to arrival, and that self-played clicks draw no marks. On main it fails with the tip at (297.05, 188.84) for (300, 200).
- I re-recorded the GNOME 46 Wayland script on a VM: with helper v12 the click point (green cross) lands on the tip.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the GNOME agent cursor in its session colour
body:
Fixes CUA-3126. Part of CUA-3103. Found next to CUA-3121.

**For users:** on GNOME the agent cursor keeps one colour. Before, it flashed other colours as it moved and just before clicks.

## Root cause

Every CLI call first sends a few cursor commands (an empty label, an idle cue and a system cue) under its own per-call session, then the named session's commands. Platforms with one cursor per session never draw that per-call cursor, because it is never placed. The GNOME Shell helper draws a single cursor, and `SharedCursorSurface` gave it to whichever session sent any command, so each call recoloured the arrow and halo. A D-Bus capture of the helper during one `demo` session showed five different `SetCursorColor` values; with this change it shows one.

## Fix

- `SharedCursorSurface::on_command` takes a `places` flag. Only a move, snap or click can take the shared cursor or claim an empty one. Labels and cues from another session leave it alone, which matches what a per-session renderer shows.
- When a session takes the cursor over, the helper gets its label and cue replayed, because what it sent before it owned the cursor never reached the helper.

## Tests

- `the_helper_cursor_keeps_its_colour_from_rest_through_travel_to_arrival` plays a rest, per-call burst, travel and arrival script. It asserts that the helper only ever gets the named session's arrow colour and one halo colour, with one takeover.
- `taking_the_helper_cursor_over_replays_the_owners_label` and `only_a_placing_command_takes_the_shared_surface` cover the takeover rules.

title: fix(cua-relay): mint a new service token on a 401 and refresh at half-life (CUA-2959)
body:
Fixes CUA-2959.

**What changes for users:** nothing visible. Team and plan checks on the hosted relay no longer hit a steady trickle of refused lookups, so the relay stops falling back to cached plans, and the error alert reflects real failures only.

## Root cause

The relay already calls the Spaces API with its own client-credentials token (`cua-relay-svc`). It never forwards user or machine tokens. The 401s were the API refusing that service token as **expired**:

- The token issuer's clock ran about 60 s behind the API's. The issuer stamps `exp` from its own clock, and the API checks it against its own clock with 30 s of leeway.
- The relay used each 300 s token for 270 s (`expires_in - 30`). With 60 s of skew, the token looked expired to the API for the last second or so of each 270 s window. Production logs show the refusals at exactly 270 s intervals.
- On a 401 the relay retried with the **same** cached token. Every lookup in that second failed, and every attempt counted in `cua_relay_org_api_errors_total`. Reconnect bursts made those seconds busier.

## Fix (standard OAuth client pattern)

- Replace the service token at **half its lifetime** (150 s for 300 s tokens). That tolerates minutes of skew between issuer and API.
- On a 401, **mint a new token once and resend**. Concurrent refusals mint a single token. Only a 401 to a freshly minted token is an error (`TOKEN_REFUSED`), and plan lookups don't retry it further, so a misconfigured secret can't fan out into 6x token mints.
- New counters: `cua_relay_org_service_token_fetches_total`, `_errors_total` and `_refused_total` (recovered refusals). `cua_relay_org_api_errors_total` now counts only real failures. `fail_closed` behaviour is unchanged.
- New `cua_relay_auth_rejections_total{route,reason}`: the relay's own 401s to its callers. Revoked, rotated or deleted machines and devices still reconnecting (`unknown_machine_token`, `ticket_revoked`) are counted there as expected outcomes, apart from Spaces API errors.

## Tests

- `a_refused_cached_token_is_replaced_and_not_an_api_error`: the API refuses token 1 and accepts token 2. The call succeeds with 0 API errors and 1 recovered refusal.
- `a_refused_fresh_token_is_one_api_error_and_final`: every token is refused. That gives exactly 2 mints, 2 API hits and 1 error, and the plan lookup adds no retries.
- `concurrent_refusals_mint_one_new_token`
- `service_tokens_are_replaced_at_half_their_lifetime`
- `revoked_machines_are_counted_apart_by_reason` and `every_reason_and_route_has_its_own_slot`

`cargo test -p cua-relay --features hosted` passes, and clippy is clean with and without `hosted`.

The clock drift itself is being fixed separately in our infrastructure. This change makes the relay correct under any realistic skew.

title: fix(cua-cli): encode member credential names for storage
body:
## Summary

`cua join` saves a returned member key as `space-member.<member_id>`, but the credential store accepts only lowercase ASCII letters and hyphens. The dot, underscore and digits make every server-issued member ID fail validation after the join code has been redeemed.

Encode each member-ID byte as two lowercase letters under the `space-member-` prefix. The existing shared helper supplies the name for saving, loading and removing credentials, and preserves distinctions between IDs rather than stripping punctuation or folding case. Update the module documentation to match.

## Related work

Refs #6334, reported by @DoWhileGeek.

No RFC is required: this repairs an internal credential-name mismatch without changing CLI arguments, protocol fields or the credential store's accepted names.

## Compatibility and risk

The member ID and key remain unchanged. Previously generated names could not pass the store's validation, so this change does not need to migrate successfully stored credentials from that format.

This fixes the deterministic local naming failure. Already consumed join codes still need replacing. General retryability or atomicity when redemption succeeds but a later vault/disk write fails is outside this patch.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the new regression failed with the reported `InvalidArgument("secret name \"space-member.mem_…\"")` error.
- After the fix, it passes against the file store and test-keychain backend. It covers independent save/load round trips for server-shaped, punctuation-distinct and case-distinct IDs, removal, repeated removal and preservation of another member's key.
- `cargo test --locked --offline -p cua-cli -p cua-auth --lib -- --test-threads=4`: 307 CLI tests and 57 authentication tests passed; one existing host-runtime probe remained ignored.
- `cargo test --locked --offline -p cua-cli --test auth -- --test-threads=4`: eight integration tests passed.
- `cargo clippy --locked --offline -p cua-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Workspace formatting, fast pre-push checks, release-title syntax validation and `git diff --check`: passed.

Tests used the repository's pinned Rust 1.97.1 and isolated temporary homes. This does not claim a live signed-app join, real OS keychain exercise or Linux/Windows execution. The test builds emitted the existing SDK unwind-table linker warning, also seen before the production change.

Draft pending upstream CI, including the release-metadata gate. No upstream CI result is claimed.

title: fix(cua-driver): avoid terminating client stdio MCP servers and duplicate PATH on Linux (#6335)
body:
Fixes #6335

### Problem
1. On Linux, `_install-common.sh` executed `pkill -x cua-driver` as a blanket backstop after stopping the systemd unit. This terminated:
   - Client-owned `cua-driver mcp` stdio processes mid-session.
   - The calling `cua-driver update --apply` process itself (exiting with status 143 / SIGTERM).
   - Unrelated processes from other users or test harnesses.
2. In `_install-rust.sh`, repeated or timer-based runs without `$BIN_DIR` in the caller's `$PATH` appended duplicate `export PATH=...` entries to shell rc files.

### Solution
1. **Scope Linux daemon shutdown (`_install-common.sh`)**:
   - Removed blanket `pkill -x cua-driver` on Linux.
   - Preserves running client stdio MCP sessions across the atomic symlink flip (`packages/current`) so active sessions continue executing smoothly on their existing held inode.
   - Protects the updater PID (`$$`) and parent PID (`$PPID`).
   - Targets only unmanaged `serve` background daemons owned by the current user.
   - Scoped `show_cua_driver_daemon_survivors` on Linux to unmanaged `serve` daemons to eliminate false survivor warnings for active client stdio sessions.
2. **De-duplicate shell RC modifications (`_install-rust.sh`)**:
   - Added an idempotency check (`! grep -Fq "$BIN_DIR" "$SHELL_RC"`) before appending `export PATH="..."`.
3. **Tests**:
   - Added `test_installer_swap_step_skips_blanket_pkill_on_linux` in `test_uninstall_stops_daemons_from_other_copies.py`.

### Validation
- Validated shell syntax with `bash -n` on `_install-common.sh` and `_install-rust.sh`.
- Ran helper drift tests: `test_uninstall_copy_of_each_shared_helper_has_not_drifted` (5/5 passed).
- Simulated PATH idempotency across 3 consecutive runs (single export entry retained).

title: feat(spaces): ask first, CI runners, TCP shares, secure networks and the phone app, behind experiments
body:
## What this adds

Five features that were developed separately and are merged here once, in this order. Each new surface is behind its own experiment (off by default, turned on with `cua experiments enable <name>` or Settings, Advanced, Labs), except the About page change.

| Experiment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ask-first` | An agent asks you on a card before anything leaves its Space, starting with a push to GitHub. Connections lists GitHub; thread cards show the request. |
| `ci-runners` | GitHub Actions jobs run in a fresh Space each, on your computers: `cua ci`, the CI Runners page, and the `cua-ci` crate. |
| `tcp-shares` | Share a raw TCP service in a Space (a game server) at a public address, with the relay edge and `cua share --tcp`. |
| `secure-spaces`, `child-spaces` | The secure default network for a Space (exit-through, hotspot, mesh paths, Volume isolation, clipboard gate), the agent home image (slim Linux plus the cua CLI), and the child-Space conformance case. The two experiments already exist; this adds the network and sharing UI behind them. |
| `mobile` | The Cua Spaces phone app: the daemon serves a phone's tools (start a task, tool rows, changes and diffs, approval scopes) and reports events for push alerts; relay phone endpoints and `cua-spacesd phone`. |
| (none) | About, Reset welcome: a second button on the About page that starts the welcome again (`session.resetOnboarding`). |

## Merge notes

- Order: ask-first, ci-runners, onboarding-reset, secure-spaces and tcp-shares, mobile. The CVE guard already on main was skipped.
- All of them add one experiment to the same registration files (gate, app core, FFI, telemetry schema, web bridge, desktop, macOS). The result keeps every entry; `Experiment::ALL` has 10 entries and `Gate::ALL` has 6, with `mobile` last.
- The generated files were regenerated, not merged by hand: UniFFI bindings (Swift and TypeScript), `bridge-shapes.json`, the parity golden `experiments.json`, and the CLI, Spaces and protocol references.
- The phone's agent home now uses `ghcr.io/trycua/agent-home:24.04` (the image catalog entry) instead of an image tag that is not in the catalog. That image is not published yet, so a phone task needs the image publish first.
- Wording: computers (not machines or devices) in the new text; no middle dots in UI text.

## Checks

- `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast` pieces: SPDX headers, actionlint, cargo fmt, lockfiles (five lock files bumped to the current version), image refs, web typecheck and tests (1361 passed), Electron shell typecheck and tests (561 passed).
