title: docs(cua-driver): explain declarative hl.plugin.load in Hyprland Lua configs
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: The plugin README warns against adding a `plugin =` line until the module has been checked, but Omarchy uses Hyprland's Lua configuration, where autoloading is a call to `hl.plugin.load()`. The README does not say how those calls behave. The obvious guard, skipping the call when `hl.get_loaded_plugins()` already lists `cua-hyprland-plugin`, hangs the compositor at every login.
- What changed: A paragraph in "Load, inspect, and unload" explains that `hl.plugin.load()` is a declaration and shows the unconditional call. It explains why a guard on the loaded state never settles, and notes that conditions which do not change between evaluations (such as the ABI check) and modules loaded with `hyprctl plugin load` are unaffected.

## Related work

None. I searched issues and pull requests (`hyprland startup`, `hang`, `autoload`, `uwsm`, `hl.plugin.load`, `cua-hyprland-plugin`) and found nothing covering this. This is a small, self-contained documentation fix.

RFC: not required (documentation only).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: documentation only; no code, protocol, or package change.
- Risk and rollback: none beyond the wording; revert the commit.
- Release metadata: the README is under `libs/cua-driver/`, which `CI: Release metadata` treats as release-tracked, so this `docs(...)` title needs the `no-release` label. I can't add labels from a fork; please apply it if you agree this is non-releasing.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `prettier@3.6.2 --check` with the repository's `.prettierrc.yaml` passes on the changed README.
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - Setup: Omarchy 4.0.6, Hyprland 0.56.2-4 (`efb50993`), Lua configuration, NVIDIA RTX 3060, SDDM autologin through uwsm. The plugin was built from the `cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0` source with `CUA_HYPRLAND_INPUT=ON` and installed under `~/.local/lib/cua/hyprland`.
  - With the guarded load, every session start stalled: `wayland-session-waitenv` timed out waiting for `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, and SDDM fell back to the greeter. Reproduced 3 of 3 times.
  - A core dump taken 12 s into a stalled start shows `CCompositor::initManagers` → `CConfigManager::handlePluginLoads` → `reload` → `postConfigReload` → `handlePluginLoads`, repeated 544 times, with the full Lua configuration re-evaluated at each level.
  - The v0.56.2 source matches this. `hlPluginLoad` only appends to `m_registeredPlugins`, and `reload()` clears that list. `CPluginSystem::updateConfigPlugins` unloads config-loaded plugins that are no longer listed and sets `changed`, and `handlePluginLoads` then calls `reload()` again.
  - With the call made on every evaluation (keeping only the ABI check), the session started in about 1 s. `hyprctl -j cua:status` reported `"configured": true` and `"transport": {"ready": true}`.
- Known gaps or CI still required: verified only with Hyprland 0.56.2's Lua configuration. The existing `plugin =` guidance for legacy configurations is unchanged.

**Off (the default):** setup is the one from #6323. It opens on first launch, and the "Finish setting up" button, the Claude Code detection and the check for Macs that can't run virtual machines are unchanged.

**On** (`spaces_new_onboarding`, this device only; it also turns on the new Home it ends on):
- Preparing starts at launch: a Linux Space for Claude Code, then the agent in it. Progress is saved after each step, so a quit resumes where it was. A dropped connection is retried by itself, and a failure that won't clear shows Try again.
- Setup has no "Try it" screen. The last screen's button, "Open Cua", ends on Home with the prompt box and the suggestions.

- Downloads of the Linux runtime tools, its disk and Apple's container package resume from the bytes already downloaded instead of starting over, and are checked end to end (`cua-vmm` `fetch.rs`).
- `cua-image` can unpack zstd layers.

title: fix(cua-driver): record KDE Wayland desktops through the portal ScreenCast
body:
## Why

https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4034 by factory-ain3sh adds Wayland video recording through the xdg-desktop-portal ScreenCast for compositors without wlr-screencopy (KDE/KWin), behind the optional `portal-capture` feature. Its fork CI never ran, because every `pull_request` workflow is waiting on approval. This PR keeps its commits unchanged and adds fixes on top, plus a merge of main.

On a live Mutter + PipeWire session, two failure paths did not behave as #4034 describes. Separately, `portal-capture` builds linked libpipewire, so `cua-driver` and `libcua_driver_sdk.so` (which the Python SDK loads) failed to load at all on a host without PipeWire, not just when recording.

## What changed

- **libpipewire is loaded at runtime.** The capture calls its 16 `pw_*` functions through a table that libloading resolves when a portal recording starts. Each entry's type is checked at compile time against pipewire-sys. `run_frame_stream` uses raw libpipewire calls instead of the `pipewire` crate, which only links. pipewire-sys stays for types and constants, and libspa for pods (header-only). Without the library, the binary and the SDK load and every other tool works. A portal video recording reports `portal ScreenCast video needs the PipeWire client library, and libpipewire-0.3.so.0 could not be loaded (...). Install it (libpipewire-0.3-0 on Debian and Ubuntu, pipewire-libs on Fedora, libpipewire on Arch) and start the recording again.` in `last_error`, before any consent dialog opens. A failed load is not cached, so installing PipeWire works without a restart.
- `ScreencastSession::open` bounds session setup (CreateSession, SelectSources) and `OpenPipeWireRemote` with `PORTAL_CALL_TIMEOUT`. Before, a portal that never answered parked `PortalVideoBackend::start` indefinitely.
- `run_frame_stream` watches the PipeWire registry and ends the capture with the stream-loss error when the cast node is removed. Before, the pacer kept duplicating the last frame, so a revoked share recorded a frozen tail and `stop()` reported success.
- CI and packaging:
  - The installer-compat and branded-installer checks keep their runtime package lists without libpipewire. They now fail if the installed `cua-driver` lists it as NEEDED.
  - The Nix package adds PipeWire back to the RUNPATH, because the fixup keeps only linked libraries. Its build fails if `cua-driver` links libpipewire.
  - The release build comment says libpipewire is not part of the distro floor.

## Scope

Covers the portal video route that https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4034 adds, which builds only with `portal-capture`. Release builds don't enable that feature. The published nightly needs only libX11, libXi and libxkbcommon beyond libc, so the installer package lists were already right for it and stay as they are. Turning `portal-capture` on for releases is https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6340, open in https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2004. With this change it no longer adds a load-time dependency.

The recorder mutex held across the portal consent wait is fixed separately in https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6376, stacked on this branch.

## Tradeoffs

- **Trampoline symbols instead of a table:** exported `pw_*` trampolines would keep the old call sites but export `pw_*` from the SDK cdylib, where they would clash with a host process that loads the real libpipewire.
- **pipewire-rs:** it has no runtime-loading option (pipewire-sys links through system-deps), so keeping it means keeping the link.

## Blast radius

Linux builds with `portal-capture` (Nix and local builds) on Wayland compositors without wlr-screencopy. GNOME with the trusted Shell helper still takes its route, and wlroots still uses wf-recorder. Default and release builds compile none of this code. The FFI rewrite keeps the old event set and teardown order. The loop is now quit only after the callback's `RefCell` borrow ends. The old closures quit it while borrowed, so a re-entrant dispatch could panic across the C boundary.

## Verification

All runs below are at the head in the `verify:` line, on a Debian 13 arm64 host with libpipewire 1.4.2, using a release build with `portal-capture`.

- `readelf -d` on `cua-driver` and `libcua_driver_sdk.so` lists libX11, libXi, libxkbcommon, libgcc_s, libm and libc, with no libpipewire. `ldd` shows no pipewire line, and neither file imports a `pw_*` symbol. Before, both listed `libpipewire-0.3.so.0` and imported 20 `pw_*` symbols.
- Without libpipewire (bubblewrap binding `/dev/null` over the library file, inside a headless Mutter Wayland session):
  - `cua-driver --version` exits 0, and `serve` starts with libpipewire not mapped.
  - `list_windows` returns the session's windows.
  - The Python SDK imports, lists 64 tools and runs `list_windows`.
  - `start_recording` with `record_video: true`, from both the CLI and the SDK, returns the install message above in `last_error`.
- With libpipewire present:
  - `run_frame_stream` recorded a real Mutter ScreenCast PipeWire node into a 1280x800 mp4. In 5 s it wrote 48 frames, and ffprobe counts 48.
  - With the node removed at 3 s, the capture ended with "the compositor removed the source" and 26 frames.
  - The release daemon maps libpipewire only once `start_recording` begins, then reaches the portal consent wait.
- The scoped repository checks pass. `platform-linux` tests pass with `--features portal-input,portal-capture` (935) and without `portal-capture` (922). Clippy `-D warnings` reports the same locations as before this change, none in the changed files. A unit test reads the test binary's NEEDED entries with the capture code kept live. It turns red when `run_frame_stream` calls a `pw_*` function directly.

Not run: a full KDE consent-to-cast round trip. KWin's screencast plugin needs OpenGL compositing, and the test host has no DRM device. The host's xdg-desktop-portal-gnome crashes when Share is pressed. Nix was not built here, so the RUNPATH and NEEDED checks in `package.nix` run first in CI. Windows and macOS platform checks could not run here, and this change touches neither.

Review: a second review found nothing blocking. Fixed the re-entrant loop quit and the NEEDED test that could pass on dead code. Dismissed: the `errno` text on a NULL return (pipewire-rs gave no detail at all), and a test for the uncached failed load (the soname is fixed, so the test would need a seam that exists only for itself).

Size: over the production-line target because it carries https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4034 whole, and the libpipewire table replaces the `pipewire` crate's wrappers with direct calls.

title: fix(spaces): keep prereleases off the Stable Sparkle feed (CUA-3131)

For users: nothing changes. Macs on Stable keep getting stable updates only. If a future prerelease ever lands in the appcast without its channel, the release now fails before the feed goes live.

title: [Bug]: [Cua Spaces macOS] Selecting 'This Mac' in Home composer navigates to 'This Space isn't here'
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### Summary

In Cua Spaces for macOS (0.10.1 / build 0.19.4.128), selecting 'This Mac' in the Home prompt composer and sending a message immediately redirects to `/spaces/relay:<machineId>` and displays "This Space isn't here — It may have been deleted, or it runs on a machine this app can't see."

### Reproduction

1. Set up the local Mac as a host (`cua host setup --share both`, `mode: "relay"`, `share_desktop: true`).
2. Open Cua Spaces.app (0.10.1) and go to the Home tab.
3. Enter a prompt (e.g., `hi`), pick an agent (e.g., `OpenCode` or `Codex`), select `in This Mac` in the location picker, and click Send.

### Expected behavior

Selecting 'This Mac' in the Home prompt bar and sending a message should navigate to a valid, interactive Space view for This Mac and start the agent conversation.

### Actual behavior

The router navigates to `/spaces/relay:<machineId>`, which is not present in `spaces.list` because `app_without_this_relay_machine` strips the local machine's `relay:<machineId>` entry and `app_with_this_machine` replaces it with a synthetic entry with `id: "this-mac"`. As a result, `/spaces/$spaceId` (`spaces.find(t => t.id === spaceId)`) returns `undefined` and renders "This Space isn't here".

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: Cua Spaces.app 0.10.1 (build 0.19.4.128), cua CLI / cua-spacesd 0.10.1
Operating system and architecture: macOS (arm64)
Application/browser/window system/image: Cua Spaces native macOS app (WKWebView)

### Evidence

1. In `use-agent-attempts` / `ask-first`, selecting `This Mac` (`where = { kind: "this-mac" }`) maps to `{ kind: "host" }` and resolves the Space ID from `host.status`:
```js
function hostSpaceId(e) {
  if (!e?.configured || !e.sharing || e.shareDesktop === false) return null;
  if (e.mode === "relay" && e.machineId) return `relay:${e.machineId}`;
  if (e.mode === "direct" && e.directUrl)
    try { return `direct:${new URL(e.directUrl).host}`; } catch { return null; }
  return null;
}
```
2. `startAttempt` then calls `onSpace("relay:<machineId>")`, navigating to `/spaces/relay:<machineId>`.
3. Meanwhile, `libcua_sdk.dylib` (`app_without_this_relay_machine` + `app_with_this_machine`) removes `relay:<this_machine_id>` from `spaces.list` and inserts `id: "this-mac"` instead.
4. Additionally, `updateTask(id, { spaceId: o, onHost: true })` sets `spaceId` before `thread.members` / `agents.start` completes, so if `agents.start` throws, the `catch` block (`getTask(id)?.spaceId || onNoSpace?.()`) skips `onNoSpace()`.

### Workaround and additional context

Add the local `cua-spacesd` daemon (`127.0.0.1:3211`) as a direct Space (`cua spaces add 127.0.0.1:3211 --token $(cat ~/.cua/host/env-token) --name local-mac`) and select `local-mac` (`direct:127.0.0.1:3211`) instead of `This Mac` in the Home location picker.

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(ci): quarantine the linux-kvm concurrent flake, fix the TCC seed lock and the Windows portmap pick
body:
Two known CI flakes were blocking the Spaces port PRs. This handles both without hiding real failures.

**linux-kvm (concurrent)** (CUA-3132). With four creates at once on a hosted runner, one create sometimes gets `registry: Not authorized` from ghcr on a public manifest, and others miss the 10 s spacesd connect window. Only the concurrent shape gets one more run, and only when every failure line matches one of those two signatures. Any other failure, or a second failure, still fails the job. The retry is reported in the job summary and as a warning. The root cause stays open on CUA-3132.

**macOS hosted E2E TCC seed** (CUA-3133). tccd keeps TCC.db open, so the seeder's bare `sqlite3` calls could fail at once with `database is locked`. Every TCC.db access now waits up to 30 s for the lock, and the seed transaction is `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. This fixes the cause, so it needs no quarantine.

**cua-spacesd Windows test `volume_portmap::serves_over_tcp_and_udp`**. On some Windows runners, `Portmap::start(0)` failed all 32 picks with `PermissionDenied` (os error 10013). The runner excludes a block of UDP ports, and Windows hands out TCP ports in order, so every TCP-first pick landed in that block. Picks now alternate between TCP-first and UDP-first, and refused ports stay bound so the same number isn't handed out again. The fixed-port path (production, port 111) is unchanged.

All three are listed in `.github/workflows/FLAKY.md`.

Tests: the new `test_macos_lume_runner.py` cases hold a write lock and check that the seed invocation waits for it (22 passed). I ran the retry step locally against the real failure log with a stubbed `cargo` in four cases: a known flake that then passes (green), a known flake twice (red), the sequential shape (red, no retry), and an unknown failure (red, no retry).

Refs CUA-3098.

Before: about 22-27 min. - **Image doctor with the driver and daemon under test:** the three binaries (CLI, spacesd, driver) are built in parallel jobs and the doctor jobs download them, instead of building in sequence. Before: about 21 min. - **Nix Rust unit tests:** the derivation no longer does a separate 15 minute release build that the tests never used. Before: about 26-33 min. title: ci: scope ci-gate with the crate and package graph (CUA-3134)
body: Part 1 of the faster-CI plan (CUA-3134): `ci-gate` now waits only for the checks a change can affect, using the real crate and package graph. **What changes for contributors:** a change to a shared crate (`cua-proto`, `cua-driver-core`, `cua-driver-contract`, `cua-sandbox-core`) or to one workspace's `Cargo.lock` / `pnpm-lock.yaml` no longer waits for every workflow. It waits for the areas of the packages that depend on it. Replayed over the last 287 merged PRs, the share that waited for everything drops from 42% to 25%. Most of the rest touch `.github/**`, which still waits for everything by design. **How:** - New `.github/scripts/ci_graph.py` reads every `Cargo.toml`, `package.json` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: path deps (including `workspace = true` and `target.*` tables) and `workspace:` / `link:` / `file:` deps. A test checks the Cargo edges against `cargo metadata` for the three main workspaces. - `ci_gate_scope.py`: a file in a package affects that package and its transitive dependents. A workspace file affects every member. `libs/cua/proto/**` is an input of `cua-proto`. Each affected package adds its directory's area. Anything unmapped still waits for everything. - `shared` shrinks to `.github/**`, root files, `**/uv.lock` (the Python graph isn't modelled yet), `scripts/ci/**`, `flake.nix` and `nix/**`. - The graph caught a gap: `cua-spacesd` links `cua-relay`, so a relay change now waits for the `spacesd` area too. Before, it skipped it. - `scripts/docs-generators/**` and `libs/spaces-{app,notch}-swift/**` are now mapped. They caused 21 of the wait-for-everything PRs. **Bypass guard:** the gate checks out the map and both scripts from the **base commit**. The PR's manifests are read only to add edges the PR introduces (union of base and head). A PR can't narrow its own gate by editing the selector, and any `.github/**` change waits for everything. The gate workflow file itself still comes from the PR, as with any `pull_request` check, so it stays behind code-owner review. Main pushes, nightly and manual runs are unchanged: every workflow runs in full on its own triggers. Unaffected workflows still start when their `paths:` match; the gate just doesn't wait for them. `ci-gate` is the only required check. Tests: `test_ci_gate_scope.py` (shared crates, workspace files, PR-added edges, unmapped dependents, `workspace = true` and `target` tables, the base-commit checkout, and `cargo metadata` parity) and `test_ci_gate_workflow.py`: 286 passed. title: ci: quarantine known flaky jobs in ci-gate and scan reruns nightly (CUA-3134)
body: Part 2 of the faster-CI plan (CUA-3134): known flaky jobs get one automatic rerun and stop failing the merge check, and a nightly scan files an issue for every new flake. **What changes for contributors:** if a PR's only failures are a known flake (for example `linux-kvm (concurrent)` hitting the ghcr `Not authorized` race), `ci-gate` reruns those jobs once by itself. If they fail again the same way, the gate passes with a "quarantined flake" warning instead of sending you round again. Any other failure still blocks. **How:** - `.github/flaky/quarantine.json` (the existing list, now also for jobs) takes `job` entries: a check-name glob, a workflow-name glob, a **`signature`** regex that must appear in the failed job's log, an owner, an issue and an expiry. The signature means only the known failure is forgiven, never a new one in the same job. Validation needs the signature and keeps the existing 90-day cap. An expired entry still fails `CI: flaky quarantine`. - `ci-gate`: when every failed job of a run matches an entry and its log has the signature, the gate calls `rerun-failed-jobs` once and waits again. A repeat failure is reported as quarantined, not blocking. This needs `actions: write`. Fork PRs have a read-only token, so they get the report without the rerun. - The gate reads the list and `flaky.py` from the **base commit**, as the selector in #6369 does, so a PR can't quarantine its own failure. - New nightly `Flaky job scan` (`flaky-detect.yml`): finds jobs that failed and then passed on a rerun of the same commit across all workflows in the last 26 hours, and opens or updates one `flaky` GitHub issue per job (existing `file-issues` path). - Seeded with today's two flakes, both expiring 10 Nov (7 days): - `linux-kvm (concurrent)`: ghcr auth and spacesd connect timeout (CUA-3132) - `macOS * mock E2E` in `CI: jev-use`: `database is locked` during TCC seeding (CUA-3133) **Coordination with #6365:** that PR fixes the TCC lock at its root and adds an in-workflow retry for `linux-kvm (concurrent)`. This PR doesn't touch those files. Once #6365 lands and stays green, drop the CUA-3133 entry, or let it expire. The `FLAKY.md` change here only adds a section above the table, so it doesn't conflict with #6365's new rows. Stacked on #6369 (both edit `ci-gate.yml`). The diff shrinks to this change once #6369 merges. Tests: `test_flaky.py` (job entry validation, `gate-check` matching including signature misses, partial matches, expired entries and wrong workflows, and `detect` on rerun attempts) and `test_ci_gate_workflow.py` (rerun once then pass, repeat failure passes as quarantined, an unquarantined failure fails, list read from base). 310 passed. title: fix(cua-driver): release the recorder lock while video capture waits for consent
body: Stacked on https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6361. The base is that PR's branch, `onigiri/salvage-4034`, so this diff is one commit on top of its head `77a7f296d`. Once #6361 lands, retarget this to main. ## Why `RecordingSession::start_with_state_budget` held the recorder mutex across `video::start_video`. On the portal ScreenCast route added in #6361, that call blocks until the user answers the consent dialog, which can take up to 60 s. Every other recording call on the daemon queued behind it, including `get_recording_state`, `stop_recording`, session-end teardown and per-turn capture. This change makes the start a state of the recorder, so it no longer has to hold the lock while it waits. ## What changed - `RecordingInner.enabled: bool` becomes `phase: Idle | Starting | Cancelling | Recording`. A start claims the recorder as `Starting` under the lock (generation, owner and output dir), then releases the lock while the video backend and cursor sampler start. It commits only if the phase is still `Starting`. - While a start is `Starting`, a second start is refused with "a recording is already starting". `stop_recording`, or the owning session's end, moves it to `Cancelling` right away. The start then stops whatever backend it got, returns an error and frees the recorder. New starts are refused until that happens, so two backends never write to the same `recording.mp4` or `cursor.jsonl`. - `get_recording_state` and the start and stop responses gain a `starting` field, and the text line reads `recording: starting output_dir=...` during the wait. ## Scope This covers the core recorder start path only. The portal and PipeWire code from #6361 is untouched. Cancelling does not close the pending portal dialog. The start keeps waiting for the dialog to be answered or for the portal timeout, then discards the result. Left open: `StartRecordingTool::invoke` still calls the blocking start inside an async fn, which ties up one tokio worker for the duration of the dialog. That was true before this change as well. ## Tradeoffs - **Second start: refuse or queue.** It is refused rather than queued or allowed to supersede the pending start. Superseding would leave two consent dialogs open at once, and queueing would bring back the wait this PR removes. - **Phase field or a second mutex.** A start mutex would also have removed the stall. It would add a second piece of hidden state, though, and a stop still could not cancel a start waiting on consent. ## Blast radius The change applies to every platform's recorder. Only backends that block in `start` behave differently, such as the portal consent wait. Fast backends such as ffmpeg/x11grab go through `Starting` within one call, so their start, stop and turn behavior is unchanged. A previous recording is still stopped under the lock before the new claim, as before. `RecordingState` gains a public `starting` field, and the JSON gains a `starting` key. Both changes are additive. ## Verification - Live, on a headless Mutter + PipeWire + xdg-desktop-portal session with nobody answering the ScreenCast consent dialog: `get_recording_state` during the wait took 57.2 s at #6361's head, the same stall the #6361 review found. With this change it takes 0.050 s (0.028 s idle) and reports `starting: true`. A second `start_recording` is refused in 0.032 s. `stop_recording` returns in 0.027 s. The pending start then fails with "cancelled", and the recorder is idle afterwards. - `tests/recording_start_consent.rs` uses a video backend that blocks in `start`. Its tests fail at #6361's head because `current_state` blocks past the 2 s limit. Deleting the cancel refusal, the `Starting` to `Cancelling` move, or the commit-time cancel check each turns at least two of the four tests red. - The scoped repository checks pass for `cua-driver-core`, `cua-driver-sdk` and `platform-linux`. Clippy reports nothing in the touched files. Windows and macOS platform checks could not run here. Review: the cold review found nothing blocking. Fixed from it: concurrent backends after a cancel (the new `Cancelling` phase), the previous recording now stopped under the lock again, a cancel message that no longer blames only `stop_recording`, and tests for the session-end cancel and the refusal after a cancel. Not fixed: a panic inside a backend's `start` leaves the recorder in `Starting` until a `stop_recording`. Before this change the same panic poisoned the mutex for good. verify: PASS at 82e46a078b99c540331cb8ce29ad64a6a52934fc risk: standard --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? title: fix(spaces): reach macOS VMs over vsock, not Local Network or VPN routes (CUA-3139)
body: Refs CUA-3139. **For users:** once this ships in Lume, cua-spacesd and the macOS images, a macOS Space on your Mac starts even if Cua Spaces has no Local Network permission or a full-tunnel VPN is on. ## Root cause `local_network` is the top Space start failure: 45 of 159 (28%), all macOS VMs on a Mac. The Spaces app's daemon, via `cua-vmm`'s Lume backend, dials the guest's cua-spacesd at its `192.168.64.x` address on Apple's shared VM network. macOS Local Network privacy blocks that connect for each responsible app (`local_network_denied`), and a VPN can route the network into its tunnel (`local_network_vpn`). Both happen in `waiting_for_services`, and the app's preflight catches some of them in `preparing`. ## Fix This follows the pattern the macOS microVM backend (cua-vz) already uses. Published ports become host loopback ports, carried over the VM's virtio socket. Loopback and vsock are outside Local Network privacy and VPN routing. - **lume:** a run with `forwards: [ports]` adds a `VZVirtioSocketDevice`. It binds `127.0.0.1:0` for each port and relays each connection over vsock to the guest agent, using the microVM init's `{"op":"forward","port":N}` protocol. `GET` reports `vsock: true`, and adds `forwards` once the agent answers a ping. A saved state keeps a marker that says whether it has the device, so an older warm state still resumes, just without forwards. - **cua-spacesd:** inside a macOS VM (`kern.hv_vmm_present`), a vsock agent on port 1024 answers `ping` and `forward`, then connects to the guest's own loopback port. On a real Mac, or a VM without the device, the listen fails and nothing starts. - **cua-vmm:** macOS runs ask for forwards for their published ports, including restarts and warm-state prep. The start waits on the vsock path and the VM address together, and once the agent answers it hands out `127.0.0.1:` endpoints. Reattaching by name follows Lume's report. If the VM address has no route, the start fails only when vsock doesn't come up within 30 s. An older Lume or image keeps today's IP path. Each piece is inert alone, and every mix of old and new parts falls back to the IP path. ## Tests - lume `swift test`: 249 pass, 6 new. They cover the forward relay, the no-agent close, the agent-ready report, the protocol lines, the saved-state device rule and the directory records. - cua-spacesd `vsock_agent`: ping, refusal, a two-way forward including early bytes, and a closed port. - cua-vmm: unit tests for loopback endpoints and run bodies, plus a hermetic `lume_vsock` test where the VM address never answers and the start succeeds over vsock. The existing Lume integration tests pass. The qemu TPM tests fail locally on main too; that comes from the local environment and is unrelated to this change. ## Still to do 1. **Rollout:** this takes effect after a cua-spacesd release, then a macOS image rebuild with that build, then a Lume release and its bundled-Lume pin, then an app release. No release in this PR. 2. **The app preflight** (`cua-spaces-app-core/src/local_network.rs`) still explains or fails before a create. That covers 8 of the 25 denied cases, in `preparing`. Once the agent image is the default, it should proceed and leave the decision to the daemon, which then fails only if both paths do. 3. **Other connects by IP:** SSH env sync and the hostname update (`lume ssh`) and Lume's `sshAvailable` check still use the VM address. Move them to a forwarded port 22 next. 4. **Warm states** saved before this change resume without the device until the next warm prep remakes them. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? title: Remove VMs and containers that failed Space creates left (CUA-3139)
body: Part of CUA-3139 (host_capacity Space start failures). For users: if an earlier failed create left a hidden VM or container holding your machine's memory, Cua now removes it on its own within about 15 minutes, so new Spaces can start again. Independent of #6378, which stops new failed creates from leaving instances. This PR cleans up the instances earlier versions left. It works with or without #6378. What the daemon does at start (first pass after 30 s) and then every 5 minutes: - It lists the instances each local runtime holds as Cua's own: QEMU VMs (instances only, no bases or checkpoints), microVMs, containers with Cua's label, Apple Containerization containers Cua created, and macOS VMs Cua recorded as its own. It never boots or installs a runtime to do this. Warm-pool members are skipped. - It removes an instance only when all of these hold: - its name is in the form a Space create generates (`space-` plus 10 hex digits); - no Space record in the home mentions it. This covers the registry, credentials, metadata, lifetimes, direct hosts, Spaces provided to other machines, creates in flight, child Spaces, durable and pool records, prewarm settings, warm-pool records and ephemeral leases. The check is a plain text match, so a record of any shape keeps the instance; - it has stayed unclaimed for 10 minutes since this daemon first saw it. - Before deleting, it reads the records again. It deletes only on the runtime that listed the instance, then removes the instance's sandbox record and lease so its size stops counting as reserved. - If any runtime that is up fails to answer, or any record can't be read, the pass deletes nothing and the 10-minute clock starts over. - An instance Cua can't prove it made (any other name) is kept and logged once. Each removal is logged with its id, runtime and age, and no paths. - `CUA_SPACE_ORPHAN_SWEEP=0` turns the sweep off. What it leaves alone: instances a create gave a custom name and that never got a Space record, because Cua can't prove a failed create made them. The existing VM guard already ends running QEMU VMs that have no record. Containers and macOS VMs with custom names are kept and logged. Tests cover: a known Space is kept (any record shape), an unmarked or foreign instance is kept, an instance younger than the grace period is kept, an orphan older than the grace period is removed, a failed runtime listing or an unreadable record deletes nothing, a removal frees the instance's reservation (its sandbox record), and a Space registered during the grace period is kept. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? title: ci: add bin/ci to run the affected CI checks locally before push (CUA-3134)
body:
Refs CUA-3134 (faster CI, plan C, part 1).

**What changes for contributors and agents:** run `bin/ci` before you push. It runs the CI checks your change can break, in parallel, and prints the exact fix command for each failure, so most red CI rounds turn into one local run. `bin/ci --fix` applies the safe fixers.

## What it does

`bin/ci` reads `git diff origin/main...HEAD` (plus uncommitted files) and runs only the checks those files affect:

- rustfmt; clippy `-D warnings` on changed crates and their in-workspace dependents; the changed crates' unit tests (with an empty `HOME`, like a fresh runner)
- each workspace's Windows CI lane, cross-compiled with `cargo xwin` on the package list read from the workflow
- lockfiles in every nested workspace (`scripts/ci/check-lockfiles.sh`)
- generated files: cua SDK and Cua Driver UniFFI bindings, Electron and SwiftUI app bindings, Spaces contract manifest and control fixtures, Cua Driver contract
- generated reference docs (the docs runner's own `--changed-files-file` routing), docs code-block dispositions, image refs, docs image refs
- Python isort/black/ruff (same paths as CI), web typecheck, tests and the design lint, actionlint, SPDX headers

Modes: default (affected), `--quick` (no builds, seconds), `--full`, `--list`, `--only`. A check whose tool is missing is reported as skipped, never passed. It uses the pinned Rust toolchain through rustup even when Homebrew `cargo` comes first on `PATH`.

**One source of truth:** every mirrored command names the workflow text it copies, and the Windows lanes are parsed from the workflows. `bin/ci --verify-sync` fails when a workflow stops running one of them; **CI: Test Scripts** now runs it with the new unit tests. `scripts/ci/prepush.sh` forwards to `bin/ci`.

**Opt-in hook:** `bin/ci --install-hook` adds a `pre-push` hook that keeps and chains any existing one and composes with a global `core.hooksPath` dispatcher that chains to repository hooks. Skip once with `CUA_SKIP_LOCAL_CI=1`.

**Optional sign-off:** `bin/ci --signoff` sets a `local-ci` commit status after a green, clean, nothing-skipped run. Not required by `ci-gate`.

## Run time (Mac mini, M-series)

- Checks that build nothing (fmt, lockfiles, Python, docs, image refs, actionlint, SPDX): 10 to 20 s; `bin/ci --quick` runs only these.
- Rust builds dominate the rest. Warm: the Windows lane 1.5 min, contract fixtures under 20 s. Cold (empty target dir): clippy on 13 crates about 8 min, a release build for driver bindings about 4 min, tests 10 to 15 min.

## Replayed against today's failing commits

| PR | CI failure | bin/ci |
|---|---|---|
| #6318 | rustfmt (`cua-image`), black (`conftest.py` after a `uv.lock` bump), stale SDK bindings | caught all three, 13 s; `--fix` repaired fmt and black |
| #6332 | rustfmt (`cua-driver-contract`), stale `_native_contract.py` | caught both (bindings via a release build, 3m40s cold) |
| #6355 | Windows dead code / unused import in `cua-spaces`, stale control fixture, stale Spaces reference | caught all three: same three rustc errors as CI (Windows lane 1m31s warm), fixture 3m22s cold, reference 0.8 s |
| #6358 | nested `Cargo.lock` drift (3 workspaces) | caught, 10 s, with the three `cargo update` fixes |
| #6360 | docs code block without disposition, image ref outside the catalog | caught both, under 30 s |

Not caught: the #6360 `upgrade_from_070` test (time-dependent flake in a crate the PR did not touch) and the #6355 Windows-only socket permission test (needs a real Windows host).

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/ci/tests` (routing, graph, fix parsing, xwin classification, hook install/chain/skip, workflow sync)
- [x] `bin/ci --verify-sync`
- [x] Real push through the global dispatcher into a scratch bare repo: hook blocks on failure, `CUA_SKIP_LOCAL_CI=1` passes
- [x] `bin/ci` on this branch: green in 17 s

title: ci(e2e-cua-sdk): per-job compiler caches, warmed nightly (CUA-3134)
body:
Part of CUA-3134 (faster CI, plan C follow-up). After #6368 the E2E: cua SDK workflow is on the ci-gate critical path: its build jobs take 15 to 23 min before the 6-min test shards start.

**Why the builds were slow.** All four Rust build jobs used the `libs-cua` sccache family, which `ci-cua-sdk.yml` saves on main with its own unit kinds. Measured on the probe PRs: release SDK 0.2% hits, Rust test binaries 3.6%, static daemon plus fixtures 4.1%, debug CLI 58%. The reference-image job compiled cua-spacesd cold inside a container (about 15 of its 18 min). This workflow does not run on main pushes, so nothing ever saved these shapes.

**Change**

- The nightly `live` job restores the CLI family but no longer saves, so it cannot overwrite an entry with its own mix.

**What users see:** nothing directly. PRs that touch the SDK or spacesd get their CI result sooner.

After merge, one manual run of this workflow on main seeds the caches; then the probe PRs are measured again.

title: fix(cua-relay): the per-token computer limit holds when joins race
body:
The relay could let one token have more computers online than its limit when joins arrived together. This showed up as `reconnect_storm::machines_past_the_token_limit_keep_trying_and_take_a_freed_place` failing with "9 online, wanted 8", on main and on PRs, including #6355 and #6365.

**Cause.** The limit is checked before the WebSocket upgrade, and again after the insert. The second check ranked the new session by its `generation`, which is assigned at upgrade time. Take a join that upgraded earlier but was inserted later. It ranked among the oldest sessions, so it stayed, and the token went over its limit.

**Fix.** Under the same lock as the insert, count the token's other computers. A join that would go past the limit is not inserted, so it is refused and retries. The sessions already online keep their places, and a session that replaces the same computer id is still allowed.

Tests: `cua-relay` lib (163 passed) and `--test reconnect_storm` (3 passed), run locally.

Refs CUA-3098.

title: [Bug]: Linux QEMU Space boots with egress policy but guest control resets (suspected pasta loopback forwarding mismatch)
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### Summary

On Linux, a retained QEMU Space boots after applying a supported egress policy, but `cua sb exec` cannot reach its `cua-spacesd` endpoint: both the initial attempt and one readiness recheck fail with connection-reset/broken-pipe errors. The recorded QEMU listener and the documented pasta forwarding destination appear inconsistent, but that explanation has **not** been experimentally established as the cause.

### Reproduction

Observed sequence on one retained Ubuntu VM, not a fresh-image minimal reproducer:

1. Use the official standalone `cua` CLI 0.10.1 and an existing stopped `local:<name>` QEMU VM. Set `CUA_HOME` to its retained store and `--state-dir` to **`$CUA_HOME/sandboxes`**, not `$CUA_HOME`. A read-only `sb info` confirms the same stopped QEMU VM.
2. Apply a nonempty policy with `cua --embedded --state-dir "$CUA_HOME/sandboxes" spaces egress "$SPACE" ...`. In this observation, the policy denied host/on-link destinations, private/shared/loopback/link-local/reserved IPv4 ranges and all IPv6, with an allow exception for the virtual DNS resolver `10.0.2.3/32`. Host-specific addresses are omitted here. The policy command exited 0, and stored policy matched before starting.
3. Start that retained VM with `cua --embedded --state-dir "$CUA_HOME/sandboxes" sb resume "$SPACE"`. QEMU and pasta start; QEMU runs in a different network namespace from the host. QEMU's recorded arguments retain `restrict=on`.
4. Attempt guest diagnostics, then make one readiness recheck. The recheck used:

   ```sh
   cua --embedded --state-dir "$CUA_HOME/sandboxes" sb exec "$SPACE" -- \
     'id; uname -r; cat /etc/os-release; printf "\nBrowser processes\n"; pgrep -a chromium'
   ```

   `$SPACE` and `$CUA_HOME` above replace the local VM name and private storage path. Telemetry was disabled with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1 CUA_TELEMETRY=0`.

Both guest-control attempts failed during this single boot. No successful guest command output was returned. This was not tested repeatedly or with a new image.

### Expected behavior

The supported namespaced QEMU route should preserve host-to-guest control connectivity while enforcing the configured egress policy, or return a specific compatibility/readiness error rather than a connection reset at the forwarded endpoint.

### Actual behavior

The structured readiness-recheck receipt returned exit code **5**, empty stdout, and the following stderr. Only the sandbox name is substituted:

```text
cua: cua-spacesd is not available: cua-spacesd is not available in sandbox <name>: nothing answered at http://127.0.0.1:44069/ (it may still be starting; retry in a few seconds): gRPC: transport error (stream closed because of a broken pipe); gRPC-Web: client error (SendRequest) (Connection reset by peer (os error 104))
```

Retained serial output reports Ubuntu/service/media readiness around 17:17:01 UTC; the failing recheck was recorded at 17:17:26 UTC. Those messages do not establish that the forwarded control endpoint was ready, but this was not only an immediate first-boot probe.

### Environment

- Host: Arch Linux x86_64; kernel `7.2.11-arch1-1`.
- Official standalone CLI: `cua 0.10.1`, release [`cua-sdk-v0.10.1`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-sdk-v0.10.1). Download digest checked against official release metadata; installed binaries matched the archive.
- Host packages: `qemu-system-x86 11.1.3-1`; `passt 2026_10_02.cba3570-1` (`pasta`).
- Retained guest: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, QEMU/KVM, 2 vCPUs, 4096 MiB. Serial output identifies guest `cua-spacesd 0.6.0`.
- Guest-image/CLI compatibility has not been established. The version difference is a separate possible contributor, not proof of incompatibility.
- Local embedded mode, not the remote relay/mesh route. No host directory sharing was requested.

### Evidence

**Specific forwarding hypothesis:**

1. The installed passt manual documents `--host-lo-to-ns-lo` as follows:

   > If specified, connections to a host loopback address forwarded with -t or -u will be delivered to the same loopback address in the namespace. Without this option such connections are forwarded to the namespace's public address.

2. Official 0.10.1 [`netns_pasta_args`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.10.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/qemu/mod.rs#L2071-L2104) builds `-t 127.0.0.1/<port>:<port>` arguments and omits `--host-lo-to-ns-lo`.
3. The recorded QEMU host-forwarding listener for the failed endpoint binds `127.0.0.1:44069` **inside that separate namespace**.
4. The same omission was observed at the corresponding launcher site in inspected upstream commit [`ab9e814984610e042352f3095d0f58da42d03abd`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ab9e814984610e042352f3095d0f58da42d03abd/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/qemu/mod.rs).

This suggests pasta could deliver the connection to the namespace public address while QEMU listens on namespace loopback. **No isolated reproducer, flag-change trial, or effective live-listener readback was performed, so this is a source/documentation-supported hypothesis, not a proven root cause or tested fix.**

Separately, read-only effective-rule inspection with `nsenter --target <qemu-pid> --user --net iptables-save` failed with `nsenter: setgroups failed: Operation not permitted`. It was not retried with different flags or privilege. That inspection failure does not itself explain the control reset, and stored policy/namespace separation are not claimed as runtime proof of effective filtering.

### Workaround and additional context

No working workaround was established. After the failed control attempts, the task-started VM was stopped through `cua spaces stop`; QEMU and pasta exited and the disk was retained. No launcher patch, widened bind address, additional privilege, guest replacement or service restart was attempted.

Could maintainers confirm the intended pasta destination mapping for the loopback-bound QEMU forwards with this passt version, and whether this retained guest-server version is supported by CLI 0.10.1?

Duplicate search covered open/closed issues and PRs for `pasta`, `passt`, `host-lo-to-ns-lo`, `netns`, QEMU forwarding, connection resets and broken pipes. Related but not established duplicates:

- #3537: another listener/probe address mismatch, but in the older Windows QEMU container path.
- #6041: fresh remote mesh/relay connection setup failures, not this local namespace route.
- #6308: merged restart/token/readiness fixes; does not change the pasta forwarding construction cited above.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: test(spaces): add a Linux verification skill that drives a Space like a user
body:
Adds `.cursor/skills/verify-cua-spaces`, a project-local skill that verifies Cua Spaces on Linux by driving a Space the way a user does, with retained evidence. It sits next to `verify-cua-driver`.

## What it does

`scripts/spaces-desk.sh` starts a throwaway Space: Xvfb on a free display, a private session bus, PipeWire + WirePlumber + pipewire-pulse, openbox, the `cua-spacesd-x11-pad` input-echo fixture, and a source-built cua-spacesd on a free loopback port with a fresh token. It then registers that cua-spacesd with `cua spaces add` in an isolated cua home. "Ready" means `/health` answers, `SystemService/Health` reports every component serving, the Space is registered, and the pad is up.

- **Drive:** `cua` verbs run through a wrapper that writes transcripts. `viewer` opens a `cua sb view` link in headless Chromium, waits for `data-status=streaming` and a decoded frame, then clicks and types and requires the pad's own event journal to show the click and the keys. `index` checks the `cua viewer` index page. The MCP recipe pipes JSON-RPC to `cua mcp --embedded`.
- **Doctor:** this is read-only. It checks recorded pids, confirms the port belongs to our pid, reads caps, confirms the registration, and runs `cua-spacesd doctor --target`.
- **Cleanup:** it kills only the pids it recorded and keeps the evidence under `artifacts/cua-spaces/verify/run-*` (gitignored).
- **Feature map:** five journeys. Register and list; the viewer (stream, input, audio, no sound server, index); `cua do`; `cua spacesd` files and exec; MCP.

## Proof

I ran the skill end to end at this head: build, `up`, `doctor` (exit 0, 44 passed, 3 expected warnings), `viewer desktop` PASS (H.264 frame 1280x800, audio packets decoded, click at pad 958,579, keys "ok"), `do switch`, `index`, and `down`. No recorded pid survived, and the evidence directory remained after cleanup. Earlier runs on the same build drove every journey in the map. Two journeys fail on current main, and the map records them under Gotchas without weakening the checks:

- On a fresh cua home, a Space registered only with `cua spaces add` is missing from `cua sb ls` and from the `cua viewer` index, and `cua sb view <name>` cannot find it.
- With no reachable sound server, the viewer fails with `audio: pa_simple_new(@DEFAULT_MONITOR@): Connection refused` and shows no picture.

Both are fixed in separate PRs.

The scoped repository checks: the em-dash check passes on the changed Markdown. No crate or Python project is touched.

Unverified: the Tauri, Electron and SwiftUI apps, macOS and Windows cua-spacesd, Wayland, Space creation (container or VM runtimes), sign-in and the relay, QUIC and GPU encoders. The skill lists these. The stand-in is a host desktop, not an image: `/run/cua/env-token` and the image manifest are absent, so the doctor's image checks do not apply.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): stream the picture when the desktop audio cannot start
body:
Problem: when a Linux Space has no reachable sound server (no PipeWire or PulseAudio, or the server has stopped), the HTML5 viewer shows "audio: audio: pa_simple_new(@DEFAULT_MONITOR@): Connection refused" and a Reconnect button, with no picture. title: fix(cua-daemon): name the holder's pid when a second daemon is refused on Windows
body:
`instance_lock_tests::a_second_daemon_for_the_same_home_is_refused` fails on every `rust (windows-latest)` run of "CI: cua SDK" on main: `left: None, right: Some(<pid>)` at `cua-daemon/src/lib.rs:1147`.

On Unix the instance lock is advisory, so a refused second daemon can still read the holder's pid from `daemon.lock`. On Windows `LockFileEx` is mandatory, so reading the locked file fails and the refusal message can't name the holder's pid. On Windows the holder now writes its pid to a separate `daemon.lock.pid` file, and the refused daemon reads it from there. Unix behaviour stays the same: the pid is still written to and read from the lock file itself.

On Windows a holder that exits leaves `daemon.lock.pid` behind. The next daemon only reads that file after its lock attempt fails, and by then a live holder has overwritten it. A stale pid could only appear if the holder had not yet written its pid when the refusal was built.

Proof:
- Scoped repository checks for `cua-daemon` on macOS: fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`) and tests pass.
- Not verified locally: Windows. The `rust (windows-latest)` job on this PR is the Windows check. The `cua-spaces-cluster` pool failures in the same job are fixed in a separate PR.

title: feat(agentenv-cua): AgentEnv plugin for macOS VMs (lume provider, cua-driver macOS driver)
body:
## What changed for users

Anyone with an Apple-silicon Mac can start running AgentEnv computer tasks on macOS VMs, with cua-driver as the driver. This is the first step toward Cua Driver Bench running on AgentEnv on macOS, the way it already runs on Linux.

## What's in it

A new AgentEnv plugin, `libs/python/agentenv-cua`:

- **`lume` sandbox provider.**
  - Each sandbox is a macOS VM cloned from a pinned lume image and booted headless.
  - The boot settings (driver and app settings, and the control token) are shared into the guest read-only, the way a Linux disk reads its NoCloud seed.
  - A reset re-clones under the same name and MAC address, so the URL stays the same.
  - It refuses to start a third macOS VM on one Mac, which Apple's license doesn't allow.
- **cua-driver 0.38.0 macOS driver.**
  - The daemon runs from `CuaDriver.app`, whose bundle holds the TCC grants.
  - cua-driver's MCP tools and skill pack are forwarded. `computer/v1` goes through desktop-scope calls. `computer-exec` and the data plane work on macOS.
  - Ready checks cover the pinned executable, the pinned tool list (`mcp.json`, pinned per OS) and the Accessibility and Screen Recording grants, including a capture that works.
- **`image/`**: builds the macOS bench image from `ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26` (`build.sh` on the host, `provision.sh` in the guest).
- **`smoke/conformance_smoke.py`**: boots one VM and runs AgentEnv's computer conformance probe against the driver.

## Status: draft

- Offline tests pass: 20 tests, with a fake lume and no daemon. `agent-env plugin check` reports the `lume` provider active on agentenv-framework 0.9.1425.
- Not yet run on a macOS VM. `mcp.json` for macOS is generated on the VM by `image/build.sh`, then committed here.
- **Depends on AgentEnv core.** Core accepts only `os.type = "linux"` computers in `container` or `disk` form. A macOS computer needs `os.type = "macos"` and a prebuilt VM-image form, which we're coordinating with the AgentEnv maintainers. Until then, `install.macos` in `env.toml` is documentation and `provision.sh` does the install.
- **Next in this PR:** the agent-desktop, browser-use macOS harness and Codex computer use drivers, and the bench's macOS apps (BenchLab, the sentinel, the shared tasks' apps) as computer apps.

## How to test

```bash
cd libs/python/agentenv-cua
pip install -e '.[test]' && pytest
agent-env plugin check
# on a Mac with lume and a free VM slot:
image/build.sh --base-image ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26-<pin> --name agentenv-macos-bench
python smoke/conformance_smoke.py --base agentenv-macos-bench
```

Refs CUA-3179, CUA-3180 (parent CUA-3161)

title: [Feature]: Default egress policy for local Spaces (block private networks), and egress options on create_space
body:
### Primary area

CLI / local runtime (macOS)

### Summary

On macOS, local Linux Spaces (gVisor containers in the built-in Colima/Lima runtime) can reach the host's LAN, the host's Tailscale tailnet (100.64.0.0/10), and services bound to the host's loopback (through Lima's user-mode gateway, 192.168.5.2). For agents running unattended, I want "internet yes, private networks no" as the default for every Space, without patching the runtime VM myself.

`cua spaces egress` and `--egress-deny` look like the right tool, but I couldn't get them to work on this setup, and there's no way to make a policy the default.

### What I tried (cua 0.10.1, macOS 27.2, Apple Silicon, built-in Linux runtime, gVisor)

1. `cua spaces create ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim --name egtest --egress-deny 10.0.0.0/8 --egress-deny 172.16.0.0/12 --egress-deny 192.168.0.0/16 --egress-deny 100.64.0.0/10 --egress-deny 169.254.0.0/16`
   Created. Private destinations were blocked, but so was the internet: the guest's resolver is `192.168.5.1`, which is inside `192.168.0.0/16`, so DNS failed.
2. The same, plus `--egress-allow 192.168.5.1`:
   `cua: unsupported: An egress policy (the vmm runtime started the sandbox without enforcing it) is not supported for local Spaces`
   The Space was left in `missing` state. `cua spaces egress --help` says gVisor containers take a policy, so I'm not sure which result is the intended one on macOS.

### Requests

1. **A default egress policy** for new Spaces, in `~/.cua/config.toml` (for example `cua config set default.egress private`), applied to every create path: CLI, `create_space` and `sandbox_create` over MCP, and `agent_start`.
2. **A `private` preset** that blocks RFC 1918, CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10), link-local, ULA (fc00::/7), multicast and the runtime's host gateway, while automatically allowing the runtime's own DNS resolver (DNS only, not every port on it).
3. **Egress options on the MCP tools** (`create_space`, `sandbox_create`), so an orchestrating agent can't create an unrestricted Space by accident.
4. **Supported on macOS's built-in Linux runtime**, or a clear error at create time if not.
5. **Hotspot respects the policy**, or requires the user's confirmation when a policy is set, since `hotspot_start` shares the host's network.

### Workaround I'm using

An `iptables` `DOCKER-USER` rule set inside the runtime VM, run by a systemd unit after `docker.service`. It works and survives VM restarts, but Cua rewrites the colima/lima config on every start, and a runtime reinstall or update would silently remove it. A supported setting would replace it.

title: feat(agentenv-cua): other macOS arms' drivers and the bench's macOS apps (stacked on #6405)
body:
Stacked on #6405 (base `feat/agentenv-macos-plugin`). Part of the Cua x Scale post on AgentEnv on macOS. Refs CUA-3161, CUA-3182, CUA-3183.

**What changes for users:** `agentenv-cua` now carries the other three bench arms' macOS drivers (agent-desktop, the browser-use macOS harness, Codex Computer Use) and the bench's macOS apps (BenchLab, the sentinel, cdb-s02 to s04), so the same agent, tasks and grader run on macOS VMs with each arm's own tools.

## Drivers (`macos-drivers` bundle)

All used by Claude Code with Sonnet 5.5, so only the tool layer changes. Each has a pinned version, ready checks that fail with a reason, a pinned tool manifest, and offline tests with fakes.

| Driver | Wraps | Pin | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-desktop` | vercel-labs/agent-desktop, Apache-2.0, a CLI with no MCP server | 1.0.2 (archive and executable sha256) | 32, one per snapshot, action, app and wait command (`tools.json`); its own skill as the instructions |
| `macos-harness` | browser-use/macos-harness, MIT | 0.2.1 (PyPI wheel sha256, skill sha256) | its eleven (`tools.json`, written by `pin_manifest.py` from the harness's own table); a read's screenshot returned as an image |
| `codex-cu` | the `cua_repl` MCP server of OpenAI's unified-computer-use plugin | ChatGPT app 26.930.51102 (zip and executable sha256), `mcp.json` | `js`, `js_reset`, computer surface only |

- **Sky needs a ChatGPT login inside the VM.** It is an explicit precondition. The ready check "ChatGPT login" runs `codex login status` every time and fails with the instruction until it holds. The app and any credential stay out of the repo and out of a public image (`provision-arms.sh --arms ...,codex-cu` is for a private image only).
- **Neutral `computer_*` helper** (`macos_computer.py`: `screencapture` plus Quartz events). AgentEnv wants the seven operations from every driver, and no arm owns this one. An env hides it from its agent with `[tools]`.
- **Ready checks:** pinned executable or version; the wrapped commands or tool list against the pin (drift is named); TCC grants, re-checked after every reset.

## macOS app envs (`macos-apps` bundle)

Ported from the public Bench v2 in `libs/cua-driver-bench`, pinned to one commit by URL and sha256 (`files.json`).

- `benchlab`: builds `BenchLab.app` from its three Swift sources with the bench's own flags (`mode`, `seed`; data `~/.benchlab`).
- `bench-sentinel`: builds `BenchSentinel.app` (`condition`: foreground witness or the background "User activity" window at the bench's frame; log `~/.bench-sentinel/sentinel.jsonl`). The `sentinel-macos` artifact arms and disarms it around the agent.
- `cdb-s02` to `cdb-s04`: each task's windows opened per its `platform/launch.macos.json`, placed at the bench's bounds, workspace built by the task's own `reset/setup.py` and checked by `reset/verify.py`.

## Also

- `image/build-arms.sh`, `provision-arms.sh` and `install_app.py` add the arms and apps to a built image. They are new files, so they don't touch the base PR's image scripts.
- Both bundles are registered as `agent_env.bundles` entry points; `agent-env plugin check` passes (13 contributions in effect).
- The repo's `.gitignore` skips every `artifacts/` folder, so it gets one negation for this bundle's, and the wheel force-includes it.

## Tests

120 offline tests pass (`pytest`), ruff clean on the new files. Also checked on a Mac: BenchLab and BenchSentinel compile with `build_app.sh`; each driver's tool list matches the real tool (agent-desktop's `--help`, the installed harness's tool table, the shipped `cua_repl` server's `tools/list`).

## Needs a macOS VM to verify (not done here)

- Each wrapped CLI answering under the image's TCC rows (seeded by path in `provision-arms.sh`), including the neutral helper's `screencapture` grant.
- The Codex login and plugin install, then `js` through `cua_repl` in a VM.
- The apps building, opening and settling at their bounds (placement uses Cua Driver's `set_window_frame`), the LibreOffice and GnuCash installs, Chrome for Testing reading its managed policies, and the sentinel arming.
- `install.macos` is still not accepted by core, so the new envs carry no install table; the app envs name placeholder `computer`/`driver` ids until the macOS computer lands (core or the plugin stopgap).
- The Electron DevTools-opening hook the Linux port logs for the GUI-only check isn't ported (it is not in the public Bench v2 code).

title: fix(spaces): a sign-in during the first run never fails silently (CUA-3144)
body:
**For users:** if signing in during the first run doesn't finish, the screen now says why and offers Try again or a code to type on any browser or phone, instead of quietly showing "Sign in" again.

Fixes [CUA-3144](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3144/sign-in-during-onboarding-sometimes-fails-silently-with-no-error-ellie).

## Root causes

1. **The first run's "Add your other computers" screen had no failed state.** The first run draws no sidebar, so the sign-in footer and its toast (#5708) never showed there. A failure just made "Sign in" come back.
2. **The browser page said "You're signed in" before the session was saved.** A locked keychain or a denied prompt looked like success in the browser while the app failed.
3. **A stopped or replaced browser sign-in kept its loopback listener** open for up to 10 minutes.

I checked these and ruled them out: a callback reaching an earlier listener (each attempt has its own ephemeral port and state; a wrong-state tab already gets the "out of date" page), and the port being in use (port 0 by default; a fixed port that is taken already falls back to a code).

## Fix

- **First run (`cua-spaces-app-core` `first_run`, web bridge):**
  - While the browser is open, the screen shows "Use a code instead". During a code sign-in it shows the code and "Open the page".
  - Every failure reason shows as "Sign-in didn't finish" with its plain reason and **Try again**. "Use a code instead" appears where a code helps.
  - The page reads the sign-in again when the window is back in front.
  - The parity flow and golden gain these cases.
- **`cua-auth`:**
  - `Session::finish_login` saves the session before the callback page answers. A new "Sign-in couldn't be saved" page replaces the false success.
  - `LoginCanceller` stops a sign-in and closes its listener, or ends its code polling.
- **SDK:** an `Auth` keeps at most the newest attempt and the one before it, since that attempt's tab may still finish. It stops the rest once one signs in. An attempt stopped because another one signed in ends signed in, not failed, so no false failure toast. There is no change to the exported API, so the bindings stay as they are.
- **CLI:** `cua auth login` uses `finish_login` too.
- **Telemetry (#6377 pattern):** `cua_onboarding_step` v4 gains `failed_step` (`reach_service`, `confirm_in_browser`, `exchange_code`, `save_session`, `cancelled`, `unknown`). It comes from the fixed `error_kind` only, never text, and respects the usage-data switch. The docs are updated.

## Tests

- `cua-auth` flows: an unsaved session shows the "couldn't be saved" page (HTTP 500), never "signed in". A saved one is on disk before the page answers. A stopped sign-in closes its port, and a stopped code sign-in stops polling. An earlier tab still signs in after a retry.
- `cua-auth` callback page: the unsaved page never reads as signed in.
- SDK: a retry keeps one earlier attempt, and a sign-in stops the rest.
- `first_run`: every `SignInFailure` shows on the screen with words, Try again, and a code where it helps. The waiting states are covered, and the new fields read from the page's JSON.
- Telemetry: the `failed_step` vocabulary (`privacy.rs`). App core: each reason sends its step, and nothing is sent while usage data is off.
- Web: the first run shows the failure and Try again, "Use a code instead" starts a code sign-in, and focus re-reads the session.

`bin/ci --quick` is green locally. Heavy builds and tests run in CI.

title: fix(spaces): three first-run fixes for the new setup (CUA-3193)
body:
**For users:** the new setup (Labs, "Try the new setup") now finishes getting your first computer ready instead of stopping on "Preparing stopped: config.image: string". A Mac that can't run Spaces itself now says so in plain words with an "Add a computer" button, not "local runtime: ...". And Home only offers coding agents that are on your computer: with none, it says "Install Claude Code" instead of @claude.

Ships in 0.20.1. Linear: CUA-3193.

## What changed

- **"Preparing stopped: config.image: string".** Preparing started the first Space before this computer's offers were read. The create went out with no image, and the host refused it with its internal argument check. Preparing now waits for the offers and creates from the wizard's own Linux offer (`homeCreateRequest`). With no Linux offer, or a blocked one, it stops in plain words. (`cua-spaces-web`)
- **Raw "local runtime:" text.** `plain_error` drops the SDK's error tags (`local runtime: `, `[local] `) and starts the sentence with a capital. This fixes the "can't run Spaces" message (#6323), and every failed create row that showed the tag. Preparing now passes its failure through the create's own wording. A refusal from the app's own check (for example, a Mac that can't run virtual computers) stops at once instead of waiting to try again. When this computer can't run Spaces, the button is "Add a computer", which opens Add a computer. (`cua-spaces-app-core`, `cua-spaces-web`)
- **@claude without Claude Code.** Home's "Who does it" lists only the agents the agent setup found on this computer. That detection already skips files Cua wrote itself (#6323). A pick or a most-used agent that isn't on this computer is not offered either. With no agent, the picker offers "Install Claude Code" and Start stays off. The new setup prepares the first installed agent, and no agent when none is installed. There is no built-in agent to offer today, so the fallback is the install link. (`cua-spaces-web`)

## Tests

- `lib/prepare/__tests__/home-request.test.ts`: no offer or a blocked offer never sends a create without an image; on the real core, the request is the wizard's Linux offer.
- `apps/cua-spaces-desktop/test/bridge-native.test.ts`: the new setup's create, from the core's offers, through the Electron host's real `spaces.create`. The old request is still refused with `bad_args`.

title: ci(release-please): tag only the merged release PR's own component
body:
Fixes CUA-3198 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3198).

**For users:** releasing one component can no longer tag new versions of unrelated packages.

## Cause

When #6350 (cua-spaces 0.20.0) merged, Release Please also tagged 13 other components `v0.20.0`. Nothing was published.

Just before the merge, the PR body was edited: a "What changes for users" section went above Release Please's `## [0.20.0](...)` heading. Release Please 17.3.0 reads a single-component body only when its notes block *starts* with that heading (`COMPARE_REGEX` has no multiline flag). So the body parsed to zero releases. `BaseStrategy.buildRelease` then used the PR title's version for every configured component. The run log shows `Failed to parse releases` and `Creating 15 releases for pull #6350`.

The config was not the cause: `separate-pull-requests` is already `true`, and there is no `linked-versions`, plugin or shared `release-as`.

## Fix

- `release-please.yml`: a new step runs before Release Please tags anything. It runs the pinned engine (`Manifest.buildReleases`, offline) on each merged `autorelease: pending` PR. If the PR would tag another component and moving the version heading back to the top is enough, the step does that and keeps every line of the body. Otherwise it fails before any tag exists.
- `ci-release-metadata.yml`: the same check runs on every open, edit and push of a release PR.
- `release_please_tagging_preview.cjs`, run by `CI: Test Scripts`: for every configured component, a pristine release PR tags only that component. The real #6350 body tags extra components until it is repaired, and then tags only `cua-spaces-v0.20.0`. A mutation check (guard always passes) makes this test fail.
- `AGENTS.md`: put added notes below the version heading.

`bin/ci --quick` passes, and so do the related `.github/scripts/tests` and every engine preview.

title: fix(ci): key the Spaces Rust slice on the bench files cua-cli embeds
body:
The producer `CI: Cua Spaces SwiftUI Rust slice (producer)` has failed on every main run since #6128: its verify step finds that the build read four bench READMEs the cache key does not hash.

Root cause: cua-cli's `embed!` macro does `include_str!(concat!("../../../bench/", $p))`. The scanner in `spaces_rust_slice_inputs.py` could not resolve the macro variable, so it dropped the read. The base hash drops libs/cua Markdown, which left the embedded READMEs out of the key.

Fix (in the scanner, so the guard keeps deriving inputs from code):
- A `concat!` with a macro variable now resolves to the directory of its literal prefix, so `libs/cua/bench` becomes an extra input (all tracked bench files, Markdown included).
- A `concat!` without `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` now resolves relative to the including file, the way rustc does.
- Tests: a scanner case for the macro form, and `libs/cua/bench` added to the expected inputs.

The workflow `paths` already cover `libs/cua/**`, so no trigger change is needed. The key changes once, so the next main run rebuilds.

Proof: `cargo build --locked --release -p cua-spaces-ffi -p cua-spaces-cli --target aarch64-apple-darwin`, then `spaces_rust_slice_inputs.py verify` on that target dir. Before the fix it reports the same four READMEs as CI. After the fix it prints "The slice cache key covers every tracked file the build read." The scoped repository checks pass. The x86_64 slice was not built.

title: fix(cua-daemon): list Spaces added by address in the sandbox list
body:
Problem: a Space registered by address with `cua spaces add 127.0.0.1:3211 --name studio` shows up in `cua spaces ls` but is missing from `cua sb ls` ("No sandboxes found."), and the `cua viewer` index page says "No sandboxes". `cua sb view studio` and `cua do switch studio` both fail with `not found: sandbox studio`. title: [Bug]: Agent cursor keeps the old page's pixels after a navigation in linux:24.04-slim (xfwm4 not compositing)
body:
### Primary area

Containers or images

### Summary

In `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim`, xfwm4 runs with no active compositor, so the Linux agent cursor overlay uses its software save-under path. When the page under a resting agent cursor changes, the cursor's footprint keeps the old pixels in the viewer stream until the cursor moves or fades (15 s idle).

### Reproduction

1. Start `ghcr.io/trycua/linux@sha256:3bb6e503da0a90dd38cd88d664308f45f7af4661fe89f81e758c3927b6efb156` (`24.04-slim-20261024-38df3cd`) and open the spacesd viewer (`/viewer/`).
2. On the driver MCP endpoint (`/mcp`, `X-Cua-Agent-Session: test`), call `launch_app` with `launch_path: /usr/bin/chromium` and a `data:text/html` page with a red background and large white text.
3. `get_window_state` on the Chromium window with `include_screenshot: true`, then `run_steps` with one `click` at x/y on the page, `delivery_mode: "foreground"`.
4. In the same window, `run_steps` with `hotkey ["ctrl","l"]`, `type_text` with a `data:` URL for a plain blue page, and `press_key Return`. Do not move the cursor.
5. Look at the agent cursor in the viewer.

It happens every time.

### Expected behavior

The cursor's glow and outline sit over the new blue page.

### Actual behavior

The cursor's footprint still shows red and white pixels from the old page, about 7 s after the navigation. The rest of the window is blue. `get_desktop_state` screenshots are clean, since they exclude the overlay. This matches the known limitation documented in `platform-linux/src/overlay.rs` ("whatever ends up under a resting cursor ... stays as it was at the last paint until the cursor moves or fades"). Here that limitation is reached in the stock image, during ordinary browser navigation.

The compositor appears to be off even though xfconf says it is on:

- `xfconf-query -c xfwm4 -p /general/use_compositing` returns `true` in a fresh container, and `/usr/share/xfwm4/defaults` has `use_compositing=true`. Yet the ghosting happens.
- After `xfconf-query ... -s false`, then `-s true` (or `xfwm4 --compositor=on --replace`), the stale pixels no longer appear. xfwm4 logs `Unsupported GL renderer (llvmpipe ...)` on start.
- Side effect: when compositing starts mid-session, the bottom xfce4-panel moves to the top-left of the screen.

I do not know why xfwm4 starts without compositing here.

### Environment

- Cua: image `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim-20261024-38df3cd`, index digest `sha256:3bb6e503da0a90dd38cd88d664308f45f7af4661fe89f81e758c3927b6efb156` (cua-driver and spacesd from that build)
- Host: macOS on Apple silicon, OrbStack, linux/arm64 image
- Container options (a hardened template, not the default run): `cap_drop: ALL` plus `CHOWN`, `FOWNER`, `SETGID`, `SETUID`; `no-new-privileges`; read-only root filesystem with tmpfs on `/tmp`, `/run` and `/var/log`; 1.5 GB memory; 1 CPU; `CUA_DRIVER_DISABLE_RUN_SCRIPT=1`; `CUA_ENV_QUIC_PORT=0`. Not yet tried with the default `docker run`.
- Display: Xvfb `:1` 1280x800x24, xfce4-session, xfwm4, Chromium.

### Evidence

Viewer frames before and after toggling the compositor (crops around the agent cursor) can be attached on request. `get_agent_cursor_state` during the repro: `enabled: true`, theme `cua.default`, effects `glow`, `ripple` and `squish` on, `idle_hide_ms: 15000`.

### Workaround and additional context

- Toggling `use_compositing` off and on as the desktop user (with `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/cua-desktop/bus`) removes the ghosting, at the cost of the panel jump above.
- Related: #2955 (overlay never painted on xorgxrdp without a compositor, closed).

title: fix(cua-driver): stop unit tests mutating the process environment
body:
The cua-driver unit test binary crashed with SIGSEGV on the Linux runner (seen twice on #6376), and a few of its tests, plus some in cua-driver-core, fail now and then. This PR fixes the causes.

## Root cause

Tests in the `cua-driver` binary called `std::env::set_var` / `remove_var` from parallel test threads. Each module guarded them with its own lock (telemetry, version_check plus release_source, extension_manager, responsibility/bundle with none at all), so the locks never excluded each other. Rust's env lock only covers readers that go through `std::env`. On glibc older than 2.41 (the ubuntu-24.04 runner ships 2.39), `setenv` replaces and frees the `environ` array, while libc readers walk it with no lock. Two of those readers run in this binary: the resolver inside `getaddrinfo`, and libX11's `XOpenDisplay`.

The resolver is reached because telemetry tests that strip `DO_NOT_TRACK`/`CUA_TELEMETRY` let another test's capture spawn a real PostHog POST. That puts `getaddrinfo` on a detached thread while the version_check and telemetry tests keep rewriting the environment. On glibc 2.41 `setenv` never frees a live array, which is why hundreds of runs on a 2.41 machine never crashed.

## Fix

- New `env_vars` module: `var_os` / `var` read the process env, except that a unit test can override names for its own thread with `Overrides`. `Overrides::apply` passes the same overrides to child processes the test spawns. The production reads that these tests exercise (telemetry, version_check, release_channel, release_source token, extension_manager home/catalog, macOS disclaim flag, Windows truthy env) use it. `cua_driver_core::embedded_mode`'s rule is split out as `is_embedded_sentinel` so telemetry can apply it to an overridden value.
- No test in the `cua-driver` binary calls `set_var` / `remove_var` now. The only remaining callers are CLI startup paths that run before any threads exist.
- Telemetry delivery returns an error under `cfg(test)`, so no unit test reaches the network whatever the runner's opt-out variables say.
- The telemetry tests keep one shared lock, because they also share process-wide statics (pending sends, session aggregates). A poisoned lock no longer cascades into a dozen unrelated failures.

Smaller flakes found by the same stress runs, and by CI on main over the last week:

- `updater::tests::ownership_*` (Nix CI run 41689174991 on main): the fake `pacman` script is written, then spawned. A fork from a parallel test can still hold its write descriptor, so `spawn` fails with ETXTBSY and is counted as "not owned". `pacman_owns_path` now retries on `ExecutableFileBusy`.
- `telemetry::tests::lifecycle_markers_are_written_only_after_each_2xx` (and the retry test): a child forked by another test briefly holds a copy of the lifecycle lock descriptor, so the non-blocking lock reports busy and the poster never runs. These tests now retry until the poster runs.
- `batch_tools::tests::{every_step_but_the_last_is_paced_as_a_batched_step, observation_inherits_the_window_and_stays_bounded}` (Nix CI runs 40716480281 and 41033310787 on main): text-input admission is a process-wide per-pid lock, and three tests typed into pid 42 at once, so one got `input_busy`. Each now uses its own pid.

## Proof

The SIGSEGV was reproduced on unpatched main by emulating glibc 2.39's `setenv` memory behaviour (move and free the array on insert) through an `LD_PRELOAD` shim. A second shim widens the unlocked `environ` walk at `getaddrinfo`. The same shims ran against both binaries, with `CUA_TELEMETRY=0 DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, `DISPLAY` unset as in CI, `--test-threads=64`, filter `telemetry:: mcp_http:: serve:: sdk_adapter:: version_check:: release_source:: env_vars::`:

| binary | runs | pass | SIGSEGV | test failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 30 | 10 | 12 | 8 |
| this PR | 30 | 30 | 0 | 0 |

The full binary with no shims:

| binary | threads | runs | pass | failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 4 | 40 | 38 | 2 |
| this PR | 4 | 40 | 40 | 0 |
| main | 64 | 20 | 19 | 1 |
| this PR | 64 | 20 | 20 | 0 |

Targeted runs at 64 threads, 100 iterations each: `updater::` 99/100 on main, 100/100 here. `cua-driver-core` `batch_tools::tests::` 93/100 on main (all `input_busy` for pid 42), 100/100 here.

Also checked on this branch: zero `setenv`/`unsetenv` calls in a full run of the `cua-driver` unit binary, and zero `getaddrinfo` calls in 5 full runs at 64 threads with the telemetry opt-out variables removed. On main, the first count was 160 calls in a single-threaded run, and `getaddrinfo` reached `eu.i.posthog.com` in every 64-thread run.

The scoped repository checks pass: fmt and test for `cua-driver` and `cua-driver-core`. Clippy with `-D warnings` reports only lints that already exist on main in files this PR does not touch (platform-linux, `fast_path/pixel_guard.rs`).

Could not run here: the macOS and Windows builds. The cfg-gated edits in `responsibility.rs` (macOS) and `bundle.rs` (Windows) rely on the CI macOS and Windows unit jobs.

Size: the `env_vars` module, about 50 production lines, accounts for most of the production additions. The rest of the diff is tests.
