title: [Bug]: cua-driver no longer starts on Ubuntu 20.04 since #6209 (libxkbcommon V_1.0.0 not found)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Since the niri adapter (#6209), the Linux `cua-driver` binary and `libcua_driver_sdk.so` require libxkbcommon 1.0, so they no longer load on stock Ubuntu 20.04, which ships libxkbcommon 0.10.0. Stable 0.38.0 and the 2026-10-29 nightly start there; the 2026-11-04 nightly exits at load. No stable release includes #6209 yet (the installer's baked version is still 0.38.0), so the next stable release would be the first to drop Ubuntu 20.04.

### Reproduction

1. Download and unpack the 2026-11-04 nightly:
   ```sh
   curl -fsSLO https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/download/nightly-cua-driver-rs-v0.38.1-nightly.20261104.41772590265/cua-driver-rs-0.38.1-nightly.20261104.41772590265-linux-x86_64-binary.tar.gz
   tar -xzf cua-driver-rs-0.38.1-nightly.20261104.41772590265-linux-x86_64-binary.tar.gz
   ```
2. Run it in a stock Ubuntu 20.04 container with the X11 and xkb runtime libraries:
   ```sh
   docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/a:ro" ubuntu:20.04 sh -c 'apt-get update -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq libx11-6 libxi6 libxtst6 libxext6 libxkbcommon0 >/dev/null && /a/cua-driver --version'
   ```

It fails on every run.

### Expected behavior

`cua-driver --version` prints the version and exits 0, as stable 0.38.0 (`cua-driver 0.38.0`) and the 2026-10-29 nightly (`cua-driver 0.38.1-nightly.20261029.40817551945`) do in the same container.

### Actual behavior

The dynamic loader rejects the binary before it runs, and the container exits with code 1:

```text
/a/cua-driver: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libxkbcommon.so.0: version `V_1.0.0' not found (required by /a/cua-driver)
```

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: Cua Driver `0.38.1-nightly.20261104.41772590265` (built from `e58d2eddd`). Last good: `0.38.1-nightly.20261029.40817551945` (built from `a6a2713a`) and stable `0.38.0`.
Operating system and architecture: Ubuntu 20.04 (`ubuntu:20.04` image, `libxkbcommon0` 0.10.0-1, `libc6` 2.31-0ubuntu9.17), x86_64
Application/browser/window system/image: none; the loader fails before any display connection

### Evidence

`readelf -V` on the 2026-11-04 `cua-driver` and `libcua_driver_sdk.so` lists libxkbcommon versions `V_0.5.0`, `V_0.6.0`, and `V_1.0.0`. `cua-driver` from the 2026-10-29 nightly and from 0.38.0 lists only `V_0.5.0`. The `V_1.0.0` imports, from `nm -D --undefined-only`:

```text
U xkb_keymap_key_get_mods_for_level@V_1.0.0
U xkb_utf32_to_keysym@V_1.0.0
```

Both come from `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/niri/keyboard.rs`, which #6209 added: `xkb::utf32_to_keysym` in `text_sym` (line 166) and `Keymap::key_get_mods_for_level` in `level_mods` (line 327). #6209 (`33a57bb0a`) is an ancestor of the 2026-11-04 nightly's commit and not of the 2026-10-29 one.

The same 2026-11-04 binary on other stock images, with the same five runtime packages or the matching RPMs:

| Image | libxkbcommon | glibc | `cua-driver --version` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ubuntu:20.04` | 0.10.0 | 2.31 | `V_1.0.0` not found |
| `ubuntu:22.04` | 1.4.0 | 2.35 | starts |
| `debian:11` | 1.0.3 | 2.31 | starts |
| `rockylinux:9` | 1.0.3 | 2.34 | starts |
| `rockylinux:8` | 0.9.1 | 2.28 | `V_1.0.0`, `GLIBC_2.29`, and `GLIBC_2.30` not found (0.38.0 already fails there on glibc; see #3930) |

Ubuntu 20.04 is the one image that goes from working to broken. Its glibc 2.31 meets the release build's glibc floor, so libxkbcommon is the only blocker there.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: pin the last good stable release with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION=0.38.0 /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"`.

Regression range: the 2026-10-29 nightly (`a6a2713a`) is good, the 2026-11-04 nightly (`e58d2eddd`) is bad, and #6209 added both imports.

Suggested fix: resolve the two functions at run time (`dlsym` against the libxkbcommon the process already loads) and have the niri keyboard path report itself unavailable when they are missing, the same way #6361 loads libpipewire at run time. That keeps the single portable binary starting on Ubuntu 20.04. It also removes the libxkbcommon half of the EL8 and Debian 10 problem @heshamkhaledd described on #3930.

If you would rather set the floor at Ubuntu 22.04 (20.04 left standard support in May 2025), #6340 updates the release build comment and the Linux computer-use blog post to say Debian 11+, Ubuntu 22.04+, and RHEL/Rocky 9+. The comment on `main` still claims Ubuntu 20.04+ and RHEL/Rocky 8+.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-compat): name root to a guest agent that switches users itself
body:
The nightly cua-compat E2B runs on QEMU Spaces fail because root's commands and file writes run as the guest agent's own user, `cua`, not as root. E2B's default user `user` is therefore never created.

CUA-3258

## Root cause

The Linux image runs cua-spacesd as `cua` (uid 1000) with `CAP_SETUID`, `CAP_SETGID` and `CAP_KILL` (`process.run_as` mode `capabilities`). `Drivers::of` reports any agent that switches users itself as driver `root`. `as_user(driver, user)` then checked `user == driver` first, so a request for `root` went out with no user and ran as `cua`. `Writer::begin` likewise wrote root's files without `run_as`. The results:

- `ensure_default_user` ran `useradd` as `cua`. It failed, leaving only a `compat: creating user user:` warning in the gateway log, so later requests got `invalid username: 'user'` and `error looking up user 'user'`.
- `run_root` was sent to `/home/user`, which did not exist.
- `files_write_root_only_dir` got a 403.

The bug came in with #5778, which added both the compat layer and the capability-mode agent. It stayed hidden because every earlier nightly of these workflows stopped at the wasm build. The 4 Nov run at 33db0d554 was the first to reach the SDK cases.

## Change

- `as_user` always names the user, root included, for an agent that switches users itself.
- `Writer::begin` sets `run_as: root` on direct writes through such an agent.
- An agent whose user cannot be read (no `id`, for example on Windows) used to be reported as `root`, and with this change would also be told `root`. It now gets an empty driver instead: root work runs as the agent without a user, other users are named, and nothing goes through `sudo`, the same as before.

## Proof

- A new gateway test, `a_root_command_names_root_to_an_agent_that_switches_users`, checks that a root E2B command reaches the mock agent with `user: "root"`. It failed before the fix (`left: ""`, `right: "root"`).
- `files_round_trip_and_signed_urls` now checks that a root upload is owned by root. It failed without the `run_as` change (`Some("mock")` instead of `Some("root")`).
- A `guest.rs` unit case covers `as_user("root", "root")` and the unnamed driver. It failed before the fix.
- The cua-spacesd `process_run_as` tests run the real agent as an unprivileged user with exactly these capabilities. All 3 pass, including `sh(Some("root"), "id -u") == "0"`, which is the switch this change now asks for.

verify: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test (with the testing feature) on cua-compat, plus the cua-spacesd process_run_as tests run as root, as the scoped repository checks. Skipped: the QEMU/KVM E2E (`tests/compat/run_space.sh e2b --kind vm`), because this host has no Docker to build the Linux image. The nightly "E2E: cua-compat on Spaces" run will show the end result. Windows and macOS guests were not run.

title: spaces-desktop: handle update-download failures instead of reporting them as crashes
body:
Linear: CUA-3304

Fixes Sentry issue CUA-SPACES-DESKTOP-D (empty-message Error from electron-updater `NsisUpdater.executeDownload`, Windows 10, 0.20.0-beta.1).

**Root cause (best reading; electron-updater source is not in the checkout):** with `autoDownload = true`, `checkForUpdates()` returns a `downloadPromise` that `check()` never awaited or caught. When the download failed, `failed()` ran from the "error" event, but the rejection of that dangling promise was unhandled, so Sentry's global handler reported it as a crash.

**Change**
- `check()` now attaches a catch to `result.downloadPromise`; a handled failure routes to `failed()` once (the existing `reported` flag).
- New `describeUpdateError` builds a never-empty reason: message, error code, HTTP status and URL host (no path or query). It is used for the log line, the state message and the dialog.
- Real crashes are untouched: Sentry init and global handlers are unchanged; only this updater rejection is caught.
- Breadcrumbs are disabled in this app by design, so the reason goes to the console and the About state rather than a new Sentry event.
- Unit tests for `describeUpdateError`.

For users: a failed update download no longer triggers a crash report, and the error shown says why.

title: feat(spaces): pick up where you left off in the first run (CUA-3319)
body:
Part of CUA-3319 (under CUA-3193): the first-run storyboard's step 4, "Pick up where you left off", and step 5, the chat opening in Home.

**For users:** if you already use Claude Code, Codex or Hermes, setup now ends by offering your recent chats on this computer. **Continue in Cua** opens one in Home with what was said so far, and you carry on from there. Nothing runs until you send the next message.

## What changed

- **`cua-agent-threads`** (new crate, every OS). A read-only lister and reader for each agent's own store:
  - Claude Code: `projects/<slug>/<id>.jsonl`.
  - Codex: `sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` plus `session_index.jsonl`. Only interactive chats are listed, as `codex resume` does.
  - Hermes: `state.db`, opened read-only, with columns discovered per version.

  Records, columns and lines it doesn't know are skipped. Listing reads only the head and tail of each file, because sessions can run to hundreds of MB. History keeps the newest 200 messages, each cut to 8 KiB, with no tool calls, tool output, thinking or injected preambles. Tested on made-up fixtures.
- **`agent_threads` and `agent_thread_read`** are new person-only daemon tools. No MCP server lists or runs them, and the daemon answers only this computer's own user: relay callers, Space agents and an agent's own process are refused. A list row holds only the title (or the first prompt, cut to 80 characters), the folder and the time.
- **`agent_start` takes `resume_session` and `resume_context`.**
  - The runner reloads the agent's own session over ACP, with `session/resume` or `session/load` (the same path a restarted run uses). claude-agent-acp, codex-acp and hermes-acp all advertise this.
  - If the session can't be reloaded, the first prompt carries the earlier conversation instead.
  - `resume_session` can't be combined with `home` or with durable runs.
- **Bridge:** new `agents.recentThreads` and `agents.threadHistory` ops on the SwiftUI and Electron hosts. The hosts return the tool's JSON untouched, and `ops/agent-threads.ts` maps it. Tauri is unsupported. Also added: demo data (`?demo=nochats` for the empty case), shapes, and `agents.start` now passes `cwd`, `resumeSession` and `resumeContext` through.
- **Web UI** (behind the new-setup Labs flag; only the Ready section and the Home thread):
  - **Ready screen:** a "Pick up where you left off" section in the setup's last step, hidden when there are no chats. Each row has the agent mark, title, folder, time and **Continue in Cua**, with the line "Your chats stay on this Mac until you pick one."
  - **Home task:** the continued chat opens as a Home task. Only a reference to the chat is stored, on this device, and nothing is posted to a Space thread. The page shows "Earlier on this Mac", the message box and **Continue on: This Mac**. The account's other computers are listed but can't be picked yet.
- Spaces reference docs regenerated. A person-only tool's Approval row now says it isn't an MCP permission.

## Privacy defaults

- Only titles, folders and times are listed.
- Nothing leaves this computer until the user picks a chat.
- An imported thread is private to the user.

These are the defaults Francesco approved; his final OK is still pending.

## Follow-ups

- CUA-3331: continue on another computer. This needs the one session file moved there, the agent installed there, the chat's folder (including uncommitted work), and `agent_threads` answering the owner over the relay.
- The parallel phase-1 onboarding PR (screens 1 to 6) can move `<PickUpWhereYouLeftOff>` into its Ready screen. The component takes only `onContinue`.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p cua-agent-threads`: 18 tests on fixtures.
- `cua-spaces-contract`, plus the new `cua-spaces-ext` tool tests, the `cua-agents` resume tests, and the `cua-spaces` start-options tests.
- Runner: `node --test runner/test/` (75 tests, including 3 new resume cases against the mock ACP agent).
- Web: new bridge and UI tests, plus coverage, contract shapes and design lint. Typecheck is clean.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): drain refused /files upload bodies so the reply is not reset
body:
Fixes #6426. CUA-3234

`cua-spacesd::fs_run_as::acting_as_a_different_user_switches_identity` failed on macOS with `ConnectionReset` while reading a response in its raw HTTP helper. The culprit is the last request in `exercise()`, a PUT whose `ru=` is swapped. The `/files` handler refuses it with 403 before reading the body. hyper then closes the socket with the body bytes still unread, and the kernel answers with a TCP reset that can arrive before the 403 is read. Any client that uploads to a signed URL that is refused (bad signature, expired, missing parent, helper refusal) can hit the same thing.

Fix: after `/files` has its response, it reads and discards whatever is left of the request body, up to 8 MiB or 5 s. When the client sent `Expect: 100-continue`, it skips this step. Draining would make hyper send `100 Continue` and pull in a body the client was holding back.

Plan and proof:
- New test `files_extended::a_refused_upload_is_answered_without_resetting_the_connection`. It sends five 1 MiB PUTs to a tampered signed URL and requires a 403 for each, then sends one `Expect: 100-continue` PUT and requires a 403 with no `100 Continue` in front of it.
- Without the drain, the test failed 3 of 3 runs with a broken pipe or reset. With the drain but no `Expect` skip, the reply was `100 Continue` and then `403`. With the full fix it passed every run.
- The flaky test's own request, repeated 2,000 times in a loop (a local-only change, not committed), reset on every run before the fix and never after it.
- `fs_run_as` and `files_extended` each passed 20 of 20 repeated runs at this head.

title: ci: quick stage first in Actions, local-ci gate for agent PRs
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: agents can skip local CI, and a broken PR burns heavy runner minutes (Actions minutes are at 100% this month) before a one-minute lint failure shows.
- What changed:
  - **Layer 2, quick stage first.** New `ci-quick.yml` runs `bin/ci --quick` (formatting, lockfiles, headers, workflow lint; no builds, no installs). 45 heavy workflows (Rust, macOS/Swift, Nix, containers, SDK, e2e) start with a `quick` job that calls it, and their jobs wait for it. Jobs use `!failure() && !cancelled()`, so push, nightly and manual runs still work. It also runs on its own on every PR, so the gate sees a quick failure even when no heavy workflow starts. A failed `quick` fails its run; skipped jobs are not read as passed. Path selector, sharding and caches are untouched.
  - **Layer 3, `local-ci` for agent PRs.** `ci-gate` checks for a successful `local-ci` status on the head commit (set by `bin/ci --signoff`) for PRs from `cua-agents[bot]`, labelled `agent`, or opened from an `agent/` branch of this repo. Community PRs are unaffected. Missing: "Run bin/ci and bin/ci --signoff on this head commit."
  - **Report-only first.** The gate warns and passes until the repository variable `REQUIRE_LOCAL_CI` is set to `true`. We flip it once our shared machine for running `bin/ci` is verified.
  - PR template checklist line, AGENTS.md and docs/contributing/CI.md (hook, quick stage, local-ci gate, how signoff authenticates), tests for the gate and the wiring.
- User-visible effect: a PR that fails a cheap check now stops in about a minute; agent PRs get a visible reminder to run and sign off `bin/ci`.

## Related work

Refs CUA-3338, CUA-3134.

RFC: not required (CI only).

## Compatibility and risk

- Risk: each wired workflow runs a small `quick` job (about a minute on ubuntu), so a green PR pays that once per heavy workflow, against macOS minutes saved on a red one. Rollback: revert, or remove `needs: quick`.
- New heavy workflows need `quick` and `needs` too (documented in CI.md; a test checks the wiring).

## Validation

- `bin/ci --quick`, `bin/ci --fix`, `bin/ci --verify-sync` and actionlint are clean. `.github/scripts/tests` pass except failures that also occur on main (Python 3.9 collection errors, `test_sync_sdk_release_locks`).
- Scoped `bin/ci` on a remote Linux host, then `bin/ci --signoff` semantics for the head commit.
- Known gap: the quick job's real CI run is first seen on this PR.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`)

title: cua-relay: stable probe contract header (x-cua-relay-route)
body:
For users: no change. Monitoring stops depending on the wording of the relay's refusals, so a copy or mode change can't open a false "degraded" incident on the status page again.

## What

Every response of `/healthz` (on every listener, including the probe port and STUN-only pods), `/readyz` and the client route (`/m/<id>/...`, host mode, anything forwarded to a computer) now carries `x-cua-relay-route` with one fixed value:

`ok`, `not-ready`, `forwarded`, `refused-auth`, `refused-denied`, `refused-limit`, `refused`, `offline`, `error`, `relay`

- It follows the existing `x-cua-relay-*` header convention (`x-cua-relay-error` on plan refusals). It adds no body change and no new route.
- It's set in one place for the client route, from the relay's own status (the `RelayStatus` extension the connection metrics already use). gRPC refusals sent as HTTP 200 carry the marker of the relay's real status.
- A computer can't spoof it: `harden_response` overwrites whatever a computer sends under that name with `forwarded`.
- An edge or load-balancer error page carries no marker, so probes still tell the relay apart from the edge.

## Why

INC-27 (4 Nov): turning phone support on changed the 401 body on `/m/<nil-uuid>/healthz` from "... spacesd credential" to "... accepts cua.ai account tokens". The blackbox probe and the status-page checker matched the old text and paged, although users weren't affected.

## Contract test

`tests/probe_contract.rs` runs the matrix {phone support off/on} x {admin token unset/set} x {account sign-in off/on}:
- `/healthz` returns 204 + `ok`, and `/readyz` returns `ok` / `not-ready`, matching its status.
- An anonymous unknown id returns 401 + `refused-auth` for `healthz`, `health` and the gRPC health path. A gRPC-Web call returns 200 with grpc-status 16 + `refused-auth`. The test also asserts that the body text varies across modes, which is the point of the contract.
- A computer's own answer returns `forwarded` (exactly one header, the computer's spoof attempt replaced), and an unconnected id returns 502 + `offline`.
- The probe port (`handover::serve_health`) returns `ok`.

A unit test pins the wire values.

Documented in the crate README under "State and monitoring" as the probe contract.

## Follow-up

trycua/cloud switches the blackbox `spaces_relay_client_route` module and the status checker to status + header, keeping the text fallback until this relay is live in prod.

title: feat(spaces): warm pools, a prepared Linux Space and agent harnesses ready in about one second (behind the warm-pools experiment)
body:
## What this does

A new experiment, `warm-pools`, off by default (`cua experiments enable warm-pools`, or Settings, Advanced, Labs, Warm start). With it on, the cua daemon keeps one Linux Space ready on this computer, with Codex, Hermes, Claude Code and OpenCode already installed. Create from Home takes it in about 0.1 s and the agent session opens about a second later, instead of a cold start that installs the app first.

- Keeps at most one warm Space. It is hidden from every list. It is given back after two hours without a Create, and by the existing memory pressure, reclaim and cap rules. The first one ignores `pool.memory_percent` but not the free-memory floor.
- It is prepared once (the apps installed, one throwaway session opened and closed per app so their files are read), and its filesystem is saved. Later Spaces boot from that saved copy, so a refill takes about 2 s instead of an install. The saved copy survives a daemon restart and is found again (a Space is ready 5 s after the app starts).
- The next Space is started the moment one is taken. A Create that finds none ready waits for the one that is starting only when its refill time is known and under 30 s; the first Space after an install is never waited for.
- While the experiment is on, the first Linux Space of Ask first is made from the Linux slim tier (`ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim`, about 0.5 GB to download), which is what the daemon keeps ready. Off, the first Linux offer is unchanged. Both sides assert the reference.
- Agent starts are faster for everyone (not behind the flag, behavior preserving): a start with its tools already installed skips the install script (3.3 s of a 5.5 s start), and a warm delivery to a running agent is one status read and one guest write, with the credential hash reused for 5 s. With the flag on, each step of a join is also written to `phases.jsonl` in the persistent folder of the Cua home.
- Per-harness differences are data in cua-agents (`Harness::placeholder`: what lets a session open without a real credential), not code per harness.
- Runtime conformance gets a `warm` case and per-runtime `claim` and `prepare` capabilities; the live driver gets a `row_warm`. Only containers can answer before they are claimed, so only they are prepared ahead; every other runtime claims a bare Space and installs after the claim, as today.
- Telemetry fix: persistent agents keep the harness id as typed, so `codex` and `claude` (and ids in another case) reported `other` (5217 events from 46 installs in 14 days). They now count as the harness they name. No schema change.
- Docs: a Warm start guide, the experiments table, and the runtime conformance table.

## Measured

Mac with 36 GB, Cua's built-in Linux runtime (gVisor), Linux slim tier. Ten Creates in a row, three seconds apart, each followed by starting the app and waiting for a session that accepts a message. Medians, in milliseconds, from pressing Create (`warm-pools` on, against off with the image already pulled):

| Harness | Warm | Warm range | Cold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | 897 | 801 to 1025 | 14 415 |
| Claude Code | 1 116 | 960 to 1657 | 21 426 |
| OpenCode | 1 800 | 1762 to 3828 | 19 570 |
| Hermes | 2 793 | 2725 to 5208 | 45 754 |

Of the warm time, the claim is about 0.1 s and the rest is the app's own session start (Hermes spends about 1 s importing Python, OpenCode about 1.5 s starting). That cannot be done before the Space has the user's credentials. The host was shared with other work (load 4 to 14), so expect about 30 percent noise.

Run again on the code rebased onto current main (host busier): Codex 859, Hermes 3794, Claude Code 2032, OpenCode 1802, all ten Creates of each warm.

Other numbers: the first Create after a fresh install took 69.5 s (runtime and image fetched, app installed); the first warm Space is ready about 2 to 4 minutes after the app starts (10 to 80 s install, 66 to 113 s to save, 10 s boot) and 5 s after a restart. The saved copy takes about 5.7 GB of the runtime's disk (slim is 1.8 GB unpacked); a waiting Space holds about 200 MB of memory.

## It never makes a Create fail

Every path out of the warm one is the ordinary cold create, and each is logged with its reason: no ready Space and none starting, the starting one did not arrive in 30 s, the claim failed, the claimed Space did not take its token, the preparation failed (the Space is claimed bare and the app installs after the claim), the saved filesystem no longer starts (the next one is prepared from scratch). A runtime without claims refuses a pool as before.

## Not verified

- Live runs were on the built-in gVisor container runtime only. QEMU, microVM and Containerization claims are declared in the conformance table and unit tested; the live `row_warm` driver was not run on them.
- On arm64 gVisor, memory checkpoints are unavailable (pointer authentication), so the fork is the saved filesystem plus a 2 s boot, not a memory restore.
- The slim tier still needs the `cua` CLI baked in and a cua-spacesd with the spawn channel to host an ask-first agent that makes child Spaces; no image is built here.
- Several `bin/ci` lanes are red on main independent of this change (the web lanes under `pnpm install`, the Tauri app, the mobile core fixtures, the driver lints, `cua-vmm` `live_tpm_vm_refusals`, `cua-spaces` scale tests).
- Not tested: a Windows or Linux host (the pool and the saved filesystem use the container engine, which they share with macOS).

title: test(cua-daemon): give the density burst tests a vCPU limit that fits the burst
body:
Fixes the two burst-admission failures in the nightly `CI: VM density` job (CUA-3272).

**Root cause.** `burst()` in `crates/cua-daemon/tests/qemu_density.rs` starts 24 VMs of 2 vCPUs, plus a 2 vCPU world VM in fork mode. It then asserts that none is refused while real memory has room. The test kept the default 8x vCPU overcommit. On the 4-CPU KVM runner that allows 32 vCPUs, which is 16 VMs, or 15 beside the world VM. All 12 scheduled runs since the test landed (25 Oct to 4 Nov) failed the same way: 16 up and 8 refused for cold, 15 up and 9 refused for fork. Every refusal names the VM CPU limit and none names memory. This is a test sizing bug. It is not a runner regression, and admission behaves as designed, because 48 vCPUs on 4 CPUs is past the configured overcommit.

**Change.** The burst's `DensityConfig` now sets `vcpu_overcommit` to `max(8, ceil(2 * (n + 1) / host_cpus))`. With that, only the memory admission, the thing under test, can refuse a VM. The integer ceiling keeps `floor(cpus * overcommit)` at or above the burst for any `CUA_VMM_TEST_BURST` and CPU count. The diff is test-only and adds no production lines.

**Proof.**
- Reproduced on a 4-CPU KVM host with the published Linux disk on the old test: a cold burst of 20 had 4 refused, each with "its VMs have 32 vCPUs on 4 CPUs (vcpu_overcommit 8x allows 32)".
- With the fix, the same burst had 0 refused. Most of its VMs then missed the ready timeout, because that host cannot boot 20 guests at once. So that run proves the refusals are gone, not that the test passes end to end.
- `density::decide` driven directly with the runner's shape (4 CPUs, 16 GB, 2 vCPU / 2 GiB VMs) refuses the 17th VM under the old config and admits up to 24 measured VMs under the new one.
- The scoped repository checks passed: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-daemon --tests -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p cua-daemon --test qemu_density` (it compiles, and its tests are ignored without QEMU).
- Skipped: a full 24-VM burst on an amd64 KVM runner. It runs on the next nightly, or on this PR with the `ci:vm-density` label.

**Not fixed here, so the nightly can still be red.**
- Once the bursts are admitted, the next assertion compares counted memory with real Pss, allowing a gap of 8% + 128 MiB. Recomputed from the same 12 runs, fork fails it every time: the checkpoint RAM file counts as fully resident while the VMs map much less of it. Cold misses it by a small margin in about half the runs. That is an accounting question for `cua-vmm` and needs its own change.
- The density bench guard fails on `vm_private_p50_mb` against a baseline recorded on a 2-CPU, 8 GB runner. The job now runs on 4 CPUs and 16 GB, and ramps past 9 VMs on some nights. That needs a re-measured baseline.

title: fix(cua-mesh): hung-up clients, connection bursts and UDP flows no longer hold descriptors (CUA-2159)
body:
Follow-up to the CUA-2159 fix (a daemon leaking a loopback socket per mesh probe to a silent machine). The serialized-dial and `Forward::drop` causes are already on main; this closes the paths that still held descriptors. Found by running each path in a process that counts its own descriptors.

## Leaks that remained (cua-mesh `node.rs`)

1. **A client that hangs up while its stream is still being dialled.** The accepted loopback socket was held until the dial gave up (up to `connect_timeout`, 20 s). Probes that give up sooner than that (the daemon's, 8 s) left one socket each behind a silent peer, and a long-lived forward kept the backlog. The forward now watches the client and ends the connection when it closes. Measured: 40 probes, 21 descriptors before, 63 after (one per probe); now flat.
2. **No bound on connections per forward.** A burst past what the peer can answer piled up sockets. A forward now serves at most 256 connections at once and closes the rest on accept. Measured: 800 simultaneous clients opened 802 descriptors on the forward's side; now bounded at 256.
3. **UDP flows outlived the forward.** Dropping a `Forward` aborted its UDP task, but the per-flow reader tasks (which hold the forward's local UDP socket) ran on for their 180 s idle timeout. They now end with the forward. The UDP receive loop also backs off on a socket error instead of spinning.

Paths checked and already clean: silent online peer, listed-offline peer, refused and left-the-mesh dials (closed on the early return), cancelled dial (the connect future is dropped with the task), IPv4 and IPv6 (the forward binds loopback v4; UDP uses the mesh's v6 virtual network, no OS socket).

## Tests

`cua-mesh/tests/forward_fds_hangup.rs` counts this process's descriptors (`/dev/fd`, so macOS and Linux; the file is `cfg(unix)`) across hang-up probes, a connection burst and forwards that carried datagrams. Each assertion was checked against the old code: the hang-up check fails with 63 vs 21, the burst check with 802 extra descriptors, and the UDP check fails when the readers are detached from the forward.

title: fix(spaces-web): let the dialog's focus frame pass before checking a typed resource value
body:
Deflakes `parity.spec.ts > parity flows > create-resources [electron]`. The fix is in the test.

CUA-3255
CUA-3369
Closes #6364

## Root cause

`checkNewSpace` puts each wizard state on screen with `showWizard` and checks it right away. Several create-resources states in a row have a typed value open, a `[data-value-input]` field with `autoFocus` whose `onBlur` sends `commit-resource`.

When a state closes the focused field, Base UI's dialog (`restoreFocus: "popup"`) focuses the popup again on the next animation frame. If the test shows the next typed-value state before that frame runs, the restore takes focus from the new field. The field's blur commits the value, so the field the check waits for is replaced by the slider's number. The CI trace from run 41616557174 shows exactly this: memory drawn as the committed "6 GB" button while the check waits for the typing field with "6".

## Change

After each `showWizard`, the check waits one animation frame. The dialog's restore was requested earlier in that same task, so it runs no later than that frame. The next state can't be shown until the restore has run.

## Proof

Electron shell built as `pnpm parity:electron` builds it, on macOS arm64:

- Repeats of create-resources with 4 workers, `requestAnimationFrame` in the page delayed by a temporary probe (not committed), 20 runs per delay:

| frame delay | main | this change |
|---|---|---|
| 30 ms | 20 of 20 pass | not run |
| 50 ms | 10 of 20 fail | 20 of 20 pass |
| 100 ms | 8 of 20 fail | 20 of 20 pass |
| 150 ms | 6 of 20 fail | 20 of 20 pass |
| 400 ms | not run | 20 of 20 pass |

  On main, every failure was a missing typed-value field (`data-value-input` for disk, cpus or memory), the same failure CI reports. With the change, the head after merging main passed 20 of 20 at each of 50, 100 and 150 ms.
- Without the delay, 20 background CPU-burning processes and 6 workers gave 120 of 120 passes both on main and with the change. So that much load alone didn't reproduce the CI assertion here.
- The full `parity.spec.ts` passes on the Electron shell (35 passed, 15 skipped by design) and in the browser host (35 passed, 15 skipped). create-resources passed 30 of 30 repeats in the browser.

Under heavier load (40 busy processes, 10 workers), main failed some runs with `Tearing down "page" exceeded the test timeout`. That failure comes from closing the Electron shell, not from this race, and this change doesn't address it.

Scoped repository checks: `pnpm typecheck` in apps/cua-spaces-web, plus the parity spec on the Electron shell (macOS arm64) and in the browser host. Not run: the CI job's Linux Electron under xvfb.

title: fix(ci): cua-auth tests never ran on GitHub; fix the broken flows tests (CUA-3363)
body:
Fixes the three cua-auth `flows` tests that merged broken with #6408 (CUA-3144), and the CI gap that let them merge. Tracked in CUA-3363; related CUA-3144, CUA-3134.

For users: nothing changes. This keeps the silent sign-in fix (#6408) covered by tests that actually run.

## Tests
- The three browser sign-in tests sent `code=c`, but the fake issuer only accepts `code-1`. They now send `code-1`.
- `an_earlier_tab_still_signs_in_after_a_retry` also failed once the code was right: the fake issuer kept one PKCE challenge, so the retry's `/auth` overwrote the first tab's. It now keeps one per redirect URI, like a real issuer.
- They cover #6408: the page says "Sign-in couldn't be saved" (500) and never "You're signed in" when the app can't save; the page answers 200 only after the session is on disk; an issuer failure gives "Sign-in didn't finish" (new test). The focus-return re-read is app-side and stays covered by the vitest suites in `apps/cua-spaces-web`.

## Why GitHub CI missed it
Not the path selector (`libs/cua/**` runs `ci-cua-sdk.yml`) and not the shards or quarantine. The `rust-linux` job lists its crates by hand with `-p`, and cua-auth was never in the list, so its tests never ran on GitHub. 14 other crates with tests were missing the same way (cua-bindgen, cua-connections, cua-crash, cua-create-failure, cua-disk, cua-home, cua-hotspot, cua-machine-seal, cua-mock-llm, cua-push, cua-repo-cache, cua-share, cua-snapshot-sync, cua-spaces-contract, cua-spaces-transcript).

## Fix
- Add them to the nextest `-p` list (sharded 1/3 to 3/3). They pass on macOS (g17-4); Linux is proven by this PR's own CI.
- New `.github/scripts/tests/test_ci_cua_workspace_tests.py`: every `libs/cua` crate with tests must be named with `-p` on a `cargo test` or `nextest` step, or be in an explained exception list (cua-keyvault, cua-image, cua-host, cua-ci, cua-replica-lab). It also checks that a cua-auth change reaches `ci-cua-sdk.yml`.
- Adding the crates exposed one more hidden failure: `cua-connections` `generated_files_are_current`. #6313 reworded the generated connections doc to "computer" by hand; the generator still said "machine". The generator now says "computer".

title: fix(cua-mesh): a failed dial no longer answers for a peer that came online since
body:
A failed mesh dial no longer answers for a peer that the map has listed online since it failed. That stale cached failure made `mesh_gang::gang_ports_open_only_to_the_accounts_machines_while_a_job_holds_them` fail at line 242 on loaded runners.

CUA-3264
CUA-3370
Closes #6425

## Root cause

When the runner is under load, machine B's first network map can arrive about 10 ms before host A's mesh node connects to the relay, so A shows up in the map as offline. The test's first `open` (the expected refusal at line 238) dials A while it is listed offline. That dial takes the 1.5 s offline timeout and fails. `Mesh::connection` then holds that failure for `FAILED_DIAL_HOLD` (5 s). By line 242 the map lists A online, but `open_stream` still got the held `ada-host-a001 is offline` error without dialing.

The hold is there so callers stuck behind a dead peer fail fast. It should not outlive the map state it was recorded under.

## Change

- `cua-mesh` `node.rs`: a timed-out dial records whether the map listed the peer online. `recent_failure` returns the held error only while the peer's current `online` flag still matches. A peer that changes state gets one fresh dial, capped by the usual timeout and serialised by the per-peer gate.
- `cua-mesh` `tests/mesh.rs`: new `a_machine_back_online_is_dialed_again_at_once`. A machine goes offline, a dial to it times out, the same machine comes back online inside the hold, and the next stream must reach it. Without the fix it fails with `Unreachable("mesh unreachable: m is offline")`.
- `mesh_gang.rs`: `in_map` now waits until A is online, so the refusal at line 238 comes from the host's port check rather than from a dial to an offline peer.

## Proof

- Before, on origin/main: 8 of 30 runs of the mesh_gang test failed at line 242 with 20 busy processes on the host. With no load, 5 of 5 passed. An instrumented run showed `a.online=false` in B's first map and `open_stream: ada-host-a001 is offline` at line 242, even though the map listed A online by then.
- After, with the fix only: 60 of 60 runs passed under 30 busy processes. With the test change as well: 60 of 60 passed under the same load.
- The new cua-mesh test fails without the `node.rs` change and passes with it.

title: fix(cua-compat): wait for cua-spacesd when a gateway creates a Space
body:
## Why

The nightly Daytona-on-Spaces job (run 41780436926) fails `computer.keyboard`, `computer.display_and_windows`, `computer.accessibility` and `api.resize_applies_on_a_real_guest` with `capability missing: ... does not support spacesd`. The job creates every sandbox from `vm:<path>/disk.img`. A disk path isn't a canonical image reference, so `expects_spacesd` returned false. The create then added no wait for port 3211 and probed cua-spacesd only once. A VM whose cua-spacesd hadn't started yet was registered as a Space without one, and the gateway cached that connection. Every compat call goes to cua-spacesd, so the gateway now says so on create.

## What changed

- `CuaBackend::create_once` sets `spacesd: Some(true)` on the `Spaces.create` path. The create now waits for the guest's cua-spacesd whatever the image string looks like.
- New `cua-spaces` test: a `vm:` disk-image Space created with `spacesd: true` whose cua-spacesd answers 3 s late comes back connected to it.

## Scope

Covers compat creates from an image with outbound network. Checkpoint forks, the Sandboxes API branch (no network, layers, pools) and `host:` placements each take their own path and are unchanged. Injection is unchanged, since it only checks `spacesd != Some(false)`.

## Blast Radius

Every E2B, Daytona and Modal gateway create from an image. A non-canonical image that really runs no cua-spacesd and gets nothing injected used to come up as a Space that failed on every call. It now fails at create, after the readiness budget.

## Verification

- The new test passes with the fix. With `spacesd: None`, as before the fix, it fails with `assertion failed: space.has_spacesd()`, the same state the nightly hit.
- The test drives `cua-spaces` directly, so it doesn't pin the one-line compat change. The nightly E2E is the end-to-end proof, and QEMU disk images can't be built here.
- The scoped repository checks: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and tests for `cua-compat` and `cua-spaces` pass. The exception is three `host_jobs` tests, which fail identically on main because this machine offers no container kind.

CUA-3273
CUA-3374

title: [Bug]: user/pass for clipboard are hardcoded in source code
body:
### Primary area

Lume

### Summary

The clipboard watcher (copy & paste) feature in Lume returns error:

ERROR: Native clipboard copy failed error=The operation couldn’t be completed. (NIOCore.ChannelError error 9.) vm=<vm_name>

The reason is that the clipboard watcher uses SSH. The username / password for the SSH connection are hard-coded in the source code as "lume"/"lume". (at libs/lume/src/Clipboard/ClipboardWatcher.swift, lines 578–579)

If the guest OS does not have an account with these credentiuals, then, the copy/paste fails. 

Suggested fix: turn the username/password into variables that the user can set. 

Suggested syntax:

lume run <VM_name> --clipboard-user username --clipboard-pass password
(where username and password are the credentials to the account on the guest OS)

### Reproduction

Run a lume VM.
In the guest OS, press either "command + C" or "command + V".
No copy or paste action will occur. 
Check the terminal on the host OS, and see the error message in the terminal.

### Expected behavior

Copy and paste function works. 

### Actual behavior

No copy or paste occurs, and, error message appears in terminal. 

### Environment

Lume v 0.6.1
Host: macbook pro, running macos 26.6.2
Guest: macos running 26.6.2

### Evidence

ERROR: Native clipboard copy failed error=The operation couldn’t be completed. (NIOCore.ChannelError error 9.) vm=<vm_name>

### Workaround and additional context

A (very bad) workaround is for the user to change the credentials of their guest macOS to "lume/lume". This is insecure because then any attacker knows their password!

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse with 'did not verify' when cosign cannot start in install.ps1
body:
CUA-3286, CUA-3422

When cosign is on PATH but cannot be started, `install.ps1` stopped with PowerShell's raw "Program 'cosign' failed to run" error instead of the installer's "did not verify" refusal. The zip was still not installed, but the message did not say why.

Root cause: a program that cannot start makes `&` throw `ApplicationFailedException`, so `$LASTEXITCODE` is never set and the refusal branch is skipped. Now the call sets `$verified` only from a zero exit code, and a throw lands in a `catch`. Both paths end in the same refusal, which adds "(cosign could not start)" for the start failure.

Stacks on https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5417, which is still open and edits the same cosign block. Until it lands this diff includes its two commits. Merge it after #5417. Once #5417 is on main, a merge of main leaves only this change.

Test: `install-common-windows-regression.ps1` adds a case with a 4-byte `cosign.exe` that Windows cannot start. It asserts the refusal names the start failure. On #5417's head the raw error escapes and this assertion fails.

Proof: I ran `Assert-ReleaseZipIntegrity` under pwsh 7.6.9 on macOS with a stand-in cosign. Exit 1 gives "did not verify". Exit 0 logs the success step. A non-executable cosign gives "did not verify ... (cosign could not start)". On #5417's head the same start failure gives the raw `ApplicationFailedException`. Both changed scripts parse with no errors. The Windows regression script, and Windows PowerShell 5.1, need Windows and did not run in the scoped repository checks. title: fix(cua-driver): force embedded mode in the SDK in-process loader tests
body:
CUA-3256. Follow-up from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3281.

## Problem

Since https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5090, `CuaDriver.create()` on macOS prefers the CuaDriver.app daemon. The SDK loader tests `test_generated_python_sdk_can_own_the_runtime_in_process` and `generated Node SDK can own the runtime in process` assert the in-process runtime, so on a Mac with CuaDriver.app running they got a daemon-backed driver and failed (`DriverExecutionMode.DAEMON != EMBEDDED`, and `executionMode()` 1 !== 0) unless `CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1` was set.

## Change

Both tests now ask for the in-process runtime themselves through the public option: `CuaDriver.create(embedded=True)` in Python and `CuaDriver.create({ embedded: true })` in TypeScript. On Linux and Windows the tests take the same constructor as before, because `create()` is always in-process there. Rust gets the same `DriverOptions` (`claude_code_compatibility = false`) either way.

## Proof

On macOS arm64, with CuaDriver.app installed and `serve` running, `CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED` unset, and the SDK built in release and staged with `stage-uniffi-library.mjs`:

- On main, both tests fail with a daemon-mode driver.
- On this branch, both pass. The full TypeScript suite (`node --test test/*.test.mjs`) passes 16 of 16, `npm run typecheck` passes, and the full Python suite under pytest (Python 3.11) has 44 passed and 3 skipped. The skips are `test_wrapper.py` cases that need a bundled wheel binary.

title: fix(spaces): a computer keeps one identity when re-enabled, renamed or removed (CUA-3316, CUA-3315)
body:
Fixes CUA-3316 (duplicate and unremovable computers) and CUA-3315 (a renamed computer shows offline).

## Root causes

- **Account switch minted a new id (confirmed in code, fixed).** When an account signed back in and the relay refused the saved registration, `switch_account` silently fell through to a random computer id, leaving the old row on the relay. The saved registration was also looked up only by the token's `sub`. Now the saved id is always reused (also looked up by email), a refusal is reported with its reason, and only an account with no saved registration gets a new id.
- **Removal could leave a ghost with nothing to retry it from (confirmed with a real relay, fixed).** `remove` deleted local state even when the relay delete failed. Now every registration is written to a pending list beside the machine id (not under the removed directory), deleted with the computer's token, falling back to the owner's account when the token is refused or missing, and retried on status and on setup. Setting up again reuses the same id and never deletes the live row.
- **Ghosts could not be removed from the app (confirmed, fixed).** `forget_relay_machine` refused any computer the relay lists as connected. It now checks that the computer answers a fresh connection; one that does not (stale presence) is removed. A computer that answers is still taken off from that computer. Cloud Spaces keep their own rule.
- **Rename updated only the relay (confirmed, fixed).** The Machines-page rename patched the relay and this computer's host config, but not the saved directory, the `relay:` registry record, or the address-added host entries that "Run on" matches by name, so the old name came back as a second, offline host. One function, `adopt_machine_name`, now updates every copy by machine id, used by both the Machines rename and the Space rename.
- Not reproduced: duplicates from a plain off/on (the id is kept in `<home>/spacesd/id`); relay-side rename does not affect presence.

## Tests

- cua-host: `turning_remote_access_off_and_on_keeps_one_computer`, `a_removal_the_relay_missed_is_remembered_and_finished`, `a_refused_computer_token_falls_back_to_the_owner_on_remove`, `setting_up_again_after_a_missed_removal_reuses_the_row`, `switching_accounts_reuses_each_registration_and_never_mints_a_new_id`, `the_saved_registration_is_found_by_email_when_the_account_id_is_not_the_subject`.
- cua-spaces (`tests/computer_identity.rs`, fake relay, no network or dialogs): ghost removal vs live computer, offline removal, rename keeps id and Online in this and another computer's lists and in a restarted app, Space rename path, registry and host-entry rename, no offline duplicate in "Run on".
- Also run against a real cua-relay with real cua-spacesd processes (matrix in the Linear issues).

## Not verified

Windows and Linux fresh computers, the packaged apps, and a relay with phone support on. The Machines page still pairs a computer with its own device by name when the hostname is unknown; a rename can split them (follow-up).

title: feat(spaces): every running Space of a signed-in computer shows on your account and phone
body:
## What

A Space made on a computer that was signed in and sharing never reached the phone: only an explicit `relay_register` (or a first share) put a local Space on the relay, and the phone lists the account's relay rows. Now every running local Space whose cua-spacesd can join the relay is listed on the owner's account by itself, and taken off again when it stops, is deleted, opts out, the setting goes off, the computer stops sharing, or the owner signs out.

## How

- `Spaces::publish_to_relay` (cua-spaces `share/publish.rs`) is one idempotent pass over the Spaces registry and the recorded sandbox power state, so it does not depend on which path made the Space (app, `cua spaces create`, SDKs, MCP, agent children, jobs, compat shims) or on the runtime kind (macOS VM, QEMU VM, container, microVM). Spaces that existed before the upgrade are listed once running. It reuses `relay_register`, so the access is the same owner-only registration: no new secrets, nothing stored beyond the existing attached-Spaces file (plus an `auto` flag), and a Space the owner shared with others stays as shared when it stops.
- The daemon runs the pass on create, start and stop and every 15 seconds.
- Switch: `relay.spaces` / `CUA_RELAY_SPACES` (default on), alongside the existing sharing state (a host that stopped sharing or is paused signed out lists nothing). Opt out one Space with `cua spaces create --no-relay` (label `cua.relay=off` on any path, `Spaces::set_on_relay`); a child follows its parent. `cua spaces ls` says which Spaces stay off.
- Not listed by the pass: Spaces added by address, Spaces a computer provides (already on the relay under their host), Spaces in the owner's own cloud, Spaces with no network.
- A Space listed this way shows once on its own computer, not again as its relay machine.
- Attached Spaces are recorded under a lock (Spaces attaching side by side overwrote each other).

## Tests

- `cua-spaces/tests/relay_publish.rs`: macOS VM, QEMU VM, container and microVM listed, unlisted on stop, listed again, removed on delete; direct address, `--no-relay`, label and child of an opted-out parent stay off; a Space that predates the setting; the switch; sign-out and sign-in; host stopped sharing; shared Space kept; provided Space not listed twice; owner-only rows.
- `cua-daemon/tests/relay_spaces.rs`: the real daemon loop against the local fake relay in a temp home, create to listed, stop, start, delete.

## Cost to the relay, and bursts

Creating a Space never waits for or calls the relay. Listing runs in the daemon, off the create path, and is built for a shared relay:

- Nothing changed here means no call. The relay is asked once in about five minutes (jittered) whether listed Spaces are still online; idle passes make zero requests.
- A pass reads the directory once, then registers or removes at most 24 Spaces, 4 calls at a time, without polling for them to come online (the next pass sees them). The rest carry over to the next pass (4 s), so 200 Spaces take about 9 passes.
- A Space younger than 5 s is not listed, so one made and deleted at once never reaches the relay; while Spaces are still being made (newest under 3 s old) the pass leaves the relay alone, for at most a minute, so a burst of creates has the machine to itself.
- When the relay fails (429, 5xx, not reached) calls stop for 5 s doubling to 5 min, jittered, never less than its `Retry-After`; creating goes on, listing resumes when the pause ends. Passes are jittered (+-20%) so computers do not align.
- Registered Spaces are not registered again while they dial in (90 s grace).

Measured against the local fake relay (200 Spaces, 16 creates at a time, relay at 20 ms per call):

| | without listing | with listing |
|---|---|---|
| time to create 200 Spaces | 13.1 to 14.0 s | 13.0 to 13.7 s |
| relay requests for the 200 | 0 | 209 (200 registrations + 9 directory reads) |
| most calls in flight | | 2 to 4 (cap 4) |
| requests by 20 further idle passes | | 0 |

A relay outage costs one to four requests, then none until the pause ends; 30 creates during it were as fast as before and the process's open sockets stayed flat (50 passes).

Per Space on the relay (from the code; the fake relay does not model streams): one outbound WebSocket carrying a yamux connection (held while the Space runs), a heartbeat stream opened every 5 s (12 a minute; it closes at once, so it does not count against `CUA_RELAY_MAX_GLOBAL_STREAMS`, which counts client streams), one registration request when listed and one removal when unlisted, and, unless `CUA_MESH=off` in the Space, a mesh node that also joins the relay. Client streams (a phone opening a Space) are the only thing that counts against the global cap, and only while open. At 256 Spaces on one computer that is 256 held sockets and about 51 heartbeats a second. Proposed next step (not in this change): Spaces of a computer ride that computer's one relay connection (the host registers them with `host` set and opens local streams to each Space's spacesd), turning N held sockets into 1; and the in-Space mesh node stays off for relay-attached Spaces.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): keep the doctor's token out of the probes it spawns
body:
Fixes CUA-3305: the red main run of "CI: Image doctor with the driver and daemon under test" (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/41812171866, main at c29740b37).

## What failed

The only failing row in `doctor.txt` was `auth.token_leak: token visible in argv of no process, environment of pid 1653 (cua-driver)`. Every `expect.*` row, including both sha256 rows, passed.

## Why

- The doctor runs `cua-driver doctor --json` through `sys::run_local` (`driver.standalone` and `build.identity`), with the doctor's own environment, `CUA_ENV_TOKEN` included.
- cua-driver runs finite commands in a child of itself and hands telemetry to detached workers. Those workers inherit the environment and can outlive the probe.
- `auth.token_leak` runs later, scans every process environment, and skips only processes whose command line contains `cua-spacesd`. A worker that is still alive at that moment fails the check. In the failing run, supervisord reaped pid 1653 (exit 0) at the same second the doctor finished.

## Flake or regression

This is a flake from a latent race, not a regression from #5524.
- #5524 (https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5524) changes only cua-driver browser CDP files.
- The next main push (3271e514e) passed, as did 40 of the last 41 push runs. That one run is the only failure.

## Fix

- `run_local` removes the token variables in `SCRUBBED_ENV`, the list the process spawner already strips from every child.
- `run_local_keeping_token` keeps them. It is used only for the two `cua-spacesd --print-config` runs (`meta.print_config`, `compat.env`), which must resolve the token the way the service did.
- `SCRUBBED_ENV` gains `CUA_GUESTD_TOKEN`. cua-spacesd promotes that interim spelling to `CUA_ENV_TOKEN`, so it carries the same secret.

## Proof

- **Repro.** A real cua-spacesd ran with a token, plus a stand-in `cua-driver` on PATH that leaves a detached child behind, as the telemetry worker does. Before the fix: `[fail] auth.token_leak: ... environment of pid 2213757 (sleep), pid 2213759 (sleep)`. After the fix: `[ok] auth.token_leak`, and the children were still alive with no token in their environment. Same result with the token given as `CUA_GUESTD_TOKEN`.
- **Unit test.** `probes_do_not_inherit_the_token` asserts that each scrubbed variable is unset for a probe and kept by `run_local_keeping_token`. It goes red with the scrub disabled.

title: fix(cua-driver): tell apps how many wheel clicks a Hyprland scroll was
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Hyprland, the `scroll` tool says it worked, but Zed doesn't move. The plugin tells the app "this is a mouse wheel" but never says how many wheel clicks it was, and Zed ignores wheel scrolls without that number.
- What changed: the plugin now sends the click count with every scroll, in both background and foreground input. The driver already sends 10 units per click, so 3 clicks is 30 units. The older form of the count is used for apps on an older version of the pointer protocol. The existing scroll event is still sent as before.

## Related work

I found no open issue or PR for this. I can open an issue if you'd like one.

RFC: not needed. No tool, API or protocol change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User impact: scrolling starts working in apps that need the click count. The tool's inputs don't change.
- Risk: an app that already scrolled correctly now also gets the click count. I only tested Zed, so other apps, including the ones in your qualification set, still need checking.
- Rollback: revert this one commit.

## Validation

- Tests and checks: on this commit, the plugin builds with input enabled against Hyprland 0.56.2, all 20 plugin tests pass, and `bin/ci` passes. No existing test covers this and I didn't add one.
- Manual check: I logged what Zed receives on Omarchy (Hyprland 0.56.2). Scrolling 5 clicks now arrives as `axis_value120(0, 600)` followed by `axis(..., 50)`, and Zed's Settings page moved. Before the fix there was only the `axis` event, and nothing moved.
- Known gaps:
  - That manual check used release 0.33.2 with Omarchy's patch plus this fix, not this exact `main` build.
  - It used foreground input only, because Zed refuses background input in my setup. The background change is the same fix but hasn't been run.
  - The older click-count form hasn't been run either.
  - `bin/ci` passes, but `bin/ci --signoff` fails with `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`, likely because I have no write access to this repo. A maintainer may need to handle that step.

This PR was written with an AI coding agent.

title: feat(spaces): the new prompt box with a model and an optional repo
body:
## What changes

Home's box is now the first prompt of a chat app. The old row ("Describe the job in your own words ... @claude in New Space") is replaced by the job on top and one row under it:

- **Agent menu.** The groups are the coding apps the person has connected: Codex, Hermes, Claude Code and OpenCode first, the others only once one of their accounts works. Under each app are its accounts (sign-ins and keys, by the names the connector data already shows, such as a Claude Max sign-in or "work Max") as rows to pick; picking one picks the app and the account. An app with no account has a "Sign in" row. The chevron on an app's header opens that app's sign-ins in place: which is the default, make default, rename, remove and add. The model is a quiet "Model" line at the bottom of the menu, shown only for an account that offers a choice. The chip in the box shows only the app ("Claude Code"); the account is the ticked row inside the menu. An account reads as `ada@example.com (Max)` (identifier, plan when known), the name the person gave it, `ChatGPT` when no email is known, or `API Key (*abcd)`; the label is the app core's, shared by the web, SwiftUI and Electron hosts.
- **What is remembered.** The account is the app's own choice, kept by the host (`agentKeys.use`, beside the keys), so a run uses the one shown and it survives relaunch; the app and the model are kept on this computer. The app has no general preferences store in the bridge. A remembered account that is no longer saved is never used: the app's own choice, else its first account, stands in; with nothing remembered the first connected app in the menu's order is used.
- **Run side.** Claude Code and Codex can now be told which credential to use (they were fixed to one sign-in), under the app's setup id whichever of it and the harness id a caller has. Another Claude sign-in can be added beside the first (a pasted token with a name), and any saved key or sign-in can be renamed (`agent_keys.rename`, `agentKeys.rename`, through the web, SwiftUI and Electron hosts).
- **Core.** `connectors.agents` (`AgentsView`, `AgentGroup`, `AgentAccount`, `AgentRef`) in the app core with parity flows and goldens; the words are the core's and have no middle dot or "device".
- **Optional repo chip.** "Add a repo" takes a link (repo, issue, pull request, folder, or ssh) or `owner/name`, refuses what is not a repo, keeps the five used lately, and shows the repo as a chip with a way to remove it. The repo goes into the job's message as one plain line (`Repo: <url>`), so the agent starts by getting it.
- **Where it runs.** Without the Child Spaces experiment it stays as a quiet picker in the same row (a new computer, This Mac, or a running Space). With Ask first and Child Spaces both on, there is no where row at all (see the next section).
- **The model reaches the agent.** The picked model rides with the agent when it joins the Space (`thread.agentAdd` now carries `model`, `standby` and `brief` through the web, macOS and desktop bridges; adding the same member again updates it), and with `agents.start` on the run path and the first-run preparing path.

## The agent's Home Space (Ask first and Child Spaces on)

With both existing experiments on, the empty box shows only the model and the repo chip. The job goes to the agent's Home Space instead:

- A normal Space page on the existing slim Linux image, `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim`, made on the first request and reused by the next ones (one per agent; "Let the agent decide, in a new Home" asks for a fresh one), with the spawn capability on and no new image family. The Home is tagged "Home" in the Spaces list and found again by its `cua.home` label on a new computer.
- The agent makes the Spaces the job needs (Linux, Windows or macOS), inside the tree's budget, on the person's own computers when asked in plain words. Nothing to pick.
- A place is named with `@` in the text; the "..." button then appears with the agent's choice, a new computer, This Mac, your computers and your running Spaces. An `@mention` of a Space or computer (or "on my Mac") is the grant, so no card asks. Picking from the menu also keeps a quiet "in <place>" note.
- An agent's request for an ability (list all Spaces, use a computer) is a standard approval card in the Home's thread; allowing it is remembered per agent and written where the daemon reads it, so it takes effect in the running Home at once.
- Home keeps the agent's Home warm, and one quiet line under the box says "Agent ready", "Starting agent" or "Reconnect needed".

What it adds, by layer:

- Web: the child Spaces store (`spaces.tree`, `children.set`, `budget.*`, `services.*`), `lib/agent-home`, the Home tag, the ability approval card, the demo (`?demo=agent-home`).
- Daemon: `children/home.rs`, the three abilities as this host enforces them (list Spaces, spawn a child, use a computer) from the Home's `cua.home.*` labels and a grants file only the app writes; listing granted Spaces and refusing a computer the person has not allowed, in words the agent can act on.
- SwiftUI and Electron hosts: the tree, children, budget and services operations, the Home grants file, and the create's `children` and `labels`.

## Depends on the slim image change

The Home only works end to end once the slim image carries the `cua` CLI and a spawn-capable `cua-spacesd` (a separate image change; this one touches no image recipe). Until then the Home Space is created and takes the job, but an agent in it cannot run `cua spaces create`. The coding apps are installed on first run as in any Space.

## What was already here

The daemon side (`brief` and `briefed_run` on persistent agent records, `model` and `standby` on the agent-add input) and the preparing driver's `model` and `repo` fields were already on main, so this change is the web UI, the bridge argument mapping, the demo adapter and the macOS pass-through only. Sign-in and the guided first run are untouched.

## Tests

- New: `ask-box.test.tsx` (the default app and account, groups and Sign in rows, pick and remember across a reload, the sign-ins page with default, rename and remove, the model line, Enter and Shift+Enter, nothing signed in, repo add, refuse, keep, remove, repo line in the posted message, wording guard), `ask-first-model.test.ts` (remembered account gone, fallbacks), `ask-first-repo.test.ts`; Rust tests for `agents_view`, the choice of account for Claude Code and Codex, adding another Claude sign-in and rename, and the `connectors.agents` parity flows.
- Updated for the new box (tests that need Claude Code remember it as the last pick): `ask-first-in-space`, `ask-first-start-failed`, `home-agents`, `onboarding-lands-on-home`, `warming-home-hidden`.
- Removed `home-agent-picker.test.tsx`: it tested the installed-apps "Who does it" menu and "Install Claude Code", which the model-driven box replaces.
- New: `agent-home-box.test.tsx` (no where row until `@`, the job goes to the Home on the slim image with the spawn capability, the model on standby and the briefing), `lib/agent-home` tests, child store and Home label tests, Rust tests for the abilities (`children::tests`), desktop and Swift tests for the grants file and create extras.
- `bin/ci` (rustfmt, web typecheck, design lint, tests and bridge contract, SPDX, image refs), desktop typecheck and tests, and clippy on `cua-daemon` pass.

## Not in this change

- The Children sheet on the Space page (budget and kept commands UI) and the secure network panels: the store and operations are here, the sheet is not needed by the box.
- The headless image tier and any image recipe.
- The Swift code and its tests compile, but the Swift tests were not run here (they need the native SDK library).

Screenshots for review (simulated accounts: three Claude, one Codex, none for Hermes or OpenCode) are in the owner's shots folder; real-run screenshots are still to be taken before merge.

title: fix(cua-daemon): wait for the lock after release in the instance-lock test
body:
CUA-3334

`instance_lock_tests::a_second_daemon_for_the_same_home_is_refused` fails on `rust (macos-26)` on main. It panics at the last step, the re-acquire after `drop(first)`, with `InstanceHeld { pid: Some(<test pid>) }`. The refusal assertions themselves pass.

Cause: other tests in the same binary spawn child processes. A child forked while `first` holds the lock inherits a copy of the descriptor, and the `flock` stays held until that child's exec closes the copy (std opens files `O_CLOEXEC`). If the child is still between fork and exec when the test drops its handle, an immediate `try_lock` (`Duration::ZERO`) finds the lock still held. Real daemons don't hit this because they acquire with a wait. The lock code isn't wrong. The test just leaves no room for that window.

Fix: re-acquire with a 5 s wait, which is what a restarting daemon does. Test-only change.

Repro on macOS arm64: with four threads spawning `/usr/bin/true` in a loop inside the test, main fails the test 5/20 runs and this branch fails it 0/20. A standalone drop-then-`try_lock` loop with concurrent spawns hits the held lock often on immediate re-acquire, and never once it waits.

title: fix(cua-driver): detect Hyprland input internals instead of pinning 0.56.2
body:
## Why

The Hyprland plugin's input route refuses to configure on anything but Hyprland 0.56.2 (`Input is pinned to Hyprland 0.56.2`, `libs/cua-driver/hyprland-plugin/CMakeLists.txt:250`). That pin is why the Hyprland nightly goes red now that Arch ships 0.57.1. This salvages https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6253 by @chrisohearn, merged onto current main with the contributor's commits kept. It drops the pin and compile-checks the window and layer-surface internals that input reads, so it doesn't swap in a pin to 0.57.0.

CUA-3320. Refs https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/5751, https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6253.

## What changed

- `cua_detect_hyprland_window_api` (in `cmake/DetectHyprlandAPI.cmake`) picks the 0.57 window-backend API (`mapped()`, `backend().isX11()/pid()`, `m_exclusiveKeyboardLSes`) or the legacy one (`m_isMapped`, `m_isX11`, `getPID()`, `m_exclusiveLSes`). Any other result fails configuration.
- `input_experiment.cpp` reads those four internals through small helpers chosen by `CUA_HYPRLAND_WINDOW_BACKEND_API`.
- The `tests/cmake-api` mock headers cover the backend, legacy and unsupported tiers, plus a repeat of backend to show the tier is re-probed rather than read from cache. Those headers ship in the release source bundle, and the release test runs `cmake_api` from the bundle.

## Scope

Covers the configure gate and the input reads. Release packaging keeps its exact 0.56.2 pins (`packaging/release/*`), and `CUA_HYPRLAND_EXPECTED_VERSION` acceptance builds still refuse a different header version. Updating the Omarchy package is out of scope.

## Blast Radius

Only Hyprland plugin builds with `CUA_HYPRLAND_INPUT` or `CUA_HYPRLAND_TEST_INPUT` are affected. On 0.56.2 the helpers compile to the old expressions. On 0.57, Hyprland's own `surfaceLogicalBox()` returns nothing for windows that don't accept input (an inactive group tab, or a window behind a fullscreen one), so input to those windows is refused instead of delivered. That fails safe.

## Verification

All runs used the nightly's production options (`CUA_HYPRLAND_INPUT=ON`, Release, g++, `-Werror`, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`) in an Arch Linux ARM aarch64 root with real Hyprland headers:
- Main with Hyprland 0.57.1 (`hyprland 0.57.1-1`): configure fails with `Input is pinned to Hyprland 0.56.2`, which reproduces the nightly failure.
- This branch with 0.57.1: configure selects "window-backend input API", `cua-hyprland-plugin.so` builds, CTest passes 20/20, and every undefined symbol in the module resolves against the `Hyprland` binary or its libraries. Reconfiguring a 0.56.2 build directory against 0.57.1 headers re-probes and picks the backend tier.
- This branch with 0.56.2 (`hyprland 0.56.2-4` headers): configure selects "legacy window input API", the build passes, CTest passes 20/20, and the module's `.text` is byte-identical to main's 0.56.2 build.

The CI unit job's steps also pass: the clang mock suite (20/20), requalify unit tests, release contract tests (133), and the `tests/` Python suite. If the backend and legacy tiers are swapped in the detector, `cua_hyprland_cmake_api_test` fails with `Expected window_backend (1), found 0`.

Size: production lines are within limits.

Review notes: one reviewer finding is dismissed. It flagged `Co-Authored-By` trailers on the three contributor commits, but those commits are the outside contributor's and are kept unchanged. Two minor findings are left for follow-ups: no CI job builds the legacy input tier, and the probe checks member names but not the exact `std::vector<PHLLSREF>` type.

title: fix(cua-volume): a store being created by a clone is no longer taken for removed
body:
CUA-3276

On Windows, `vfs::tests::a_concurrent_remote_write_becomes_a_visible_conflict_copy` failed once on main (07460674e, 3 Nov) with `NotFound("the store ...\shared was removed")` on the test's first write. It passed in every other Windows run of CI: cua SDK on main since 28 Oct (54 runs). So it is an intermittent race, not a Windows delete or rename problem.

Cause: `FsBackend::ensure_root` checked `root.is_dir()` before it read the shared `seen` flag. In that test two `FsBackend` clones share one store that doesn't exist yet: the feed heartbeat from `spawn()` and the session's first `put`. If caller A sees no directory, then caller B creates it and sets `seen`, A reads `seen == true` and reports the store as removed. The fix reads `seen` before the directory check. `seen` is only set once the directory exists, so a missing directory with `seen` already set still means the store was removed (`a_removed_store_is_not_brought_back_by_a_later_write` still passes).

The new test `fs::tests::concurrent_first_writes_all_create_the_store` races 16 clones on a fresh store. It failed 3 of 3 runs on the old order (on macOS) and passes with the fix.

The six `volume_e2e` failures in the issue are no longer on main. That binary now has one test, and it passed on Windows in every run checked.
