title: Spaces: one list of your computers, and the new first run and Home by default (CUA-3551)
body:
> **Do not merge yet.** The Linux run passed (6 Nov, on this branch's web UI and app code). This lands once the macOS and Windows runs pass too; auto-merge is queued only then.

Linear: CUA-3551

## What changes for people

Machines and Spaces are now one list, called **Computers**. It shows every computer you added, with the Spaces made on each one underneath. The separate Machines page is gone, and Cua Driver is now a setting on This Mac's page instead of its own sidebar item.

Everyone now gets the new first run and opens on the new Home, on macOS, Windows and Linux. The "Try the new Home" and "Try the new setup" switches leave Labs.

## What's in it

1. **One view.** The list of your computers and their Spaces (the tree from #6508 and #6546) is the only view of `/spaces`, with no Labs switch. The old grid and the Machines page are deleted, along with their route, the `nav.machines` command (⌘2) and the code that only they used. Agents is now ⌘2 and Keyvault ⌘3, in the web UI and the Mac menu.
   - Clicking a computer opens its own page at `/spaces/computer/<id>`. That page holds the switches, issues, Spaces (with their disk size on This Mac), New Space here, Details, trust, recent access, Rename and Remove. Clouds have their own page at `/spaces/cloud/<id>`.
   - Everything else the Machines page had now sits around the list: computers waiting to be added (with the count on the sidebar item), the clouds and Connect a cloud, "Also signed in" for sign-ins that aren't computers, Remove old computers on the offline row, the low-disk warning, the page tip and the upsell line.
   - The list also gained a few things the grid used to show: New Space in the header, the step and progress of a Space being made (on this computer or another), Pin to notch, and the Home tag. "Reaching N computers…" now shows while computers are still answering.
   - **Old links still work.** `/machines`, `/machines?add=1` and `/machines?join=<code>&relay=…` (including `cua://add` links from older apps) open the list with Add a computer open. `/machines?machine=<id>` opens that computer's page. `/settings/devices` opens This Mac's page. `/driver` and `/driver?machine=<id>` open Cua Driver under the right computer. The Electron and Mac shells now route deep links, notifications and Add a computer to the new addresses directly.
2. **Cua Driver under This Mac.** It's a "Cua Driver" row on This Mac's page that opens `/spaces/computer/this-mac/driver`, with a back link to This Mac. As before, it shows only where this Cua Spaces carries the driver. The command palette still finds it by name.
3. **One word.** The copy now says "computer" everywhere and keeps "Space" for the separate computers Cua makes. This covers the nav, page titles, empty states, onboarding, the palette, the Add a computer sheet, Settings, and the core strings these pages show (the computer page, trust and approvals, the host switches, the checklist, the tips and the "This computer" label on Linux). Parity goldens are regenerated. Cloud sizes ("Largest machine") are left alone, since they describe cloud machines.
4. **`spaces_tree` is gone.** The flag only ever existed in the web app: there was no Rust, FFI, Swift, Electron or telemetry mirror to remove. I deleted it from `flags.ts`, the bridge exports and the Labs list, and a stored override is cleared on start (`RETIRED_FLAGS`). Home's tree-based "in" picker, which only ran behind this flag, is removed too. Home keeps the This Mac picker from #6580, so it doesn't change for anyone. The default Space stays in Settings and in the list, because MCP and CLI tasks still use it. The FFI and Swift bindings were regenerated with the repo generators and came out unchanged.

5. **The new first run and the new Home are the defaults** (0.21.1). `spaces_ask_first_home` and `spaces_new_onboarding` are deleted with their off paths, as `upsell_cards` was in #6547.
   - Old settings still load: a stored override of either flag, or of `spaces_tree`, is cleared on start. `flags.ts` now only holds that clean-up.
   - The old first run page and its bridge hook (`useFirstRun`) are deleted, with their unit tests and the two e2e specs for its screens. The app core's `firstRun.*` view code stays for now: Settings still uses its CLI view, and removing the rest is a follow-up.
   - Home is first in the nav and `/` opens it. "Ask before a task uses This computer" moves from Labs to a Home group in Settings, Advanced.
   - The new first run sends the onboarding funnel events the old one sent (start, each screen viewed, skipped, finished), on the existing schema. Without this, the funnel would have gone dark.
   - The first Linux Space is prepared after a first run only when that run happened on this install. Someone who set up with an older app and updates doesn't get a Space they didn't ask for.
   - The Mac-only steps (permissions, Cua Driver) stay Mac-only in the new first run, as before. Electron gets the same defaults, because they live in the shared web UI.
6. **Layout shift.** Turning the new Home on by default made the parity layout-shift check measure it for the first time. Home now draws once its lists have loaded (at most 0.8 s), so the welcome no longer turns into the lists and the agents no longer push the Spaces down (0.13 to 0.0004). In Settings, General, the default Space group moves to the end of the tab, so its late arrival moves nothing (0.107 to 0.03).

title: ci(rust): build Linux tests once, run in 3 shards (CUA-3560, audit cut 5)
body:
Cut 5 of the 5 Nov CI audit.

For users: Rust PR checks finish sooner, so Rust changes merge sooner.

- **Build once, run in shards.** New `rust linux build` job runs `cargo nextest archive` once (and compiles the test binaries the cargo test steps of shards 1 and 2 use, so the shared sccache entry has every unit). The three `rust linux shard N/3` jobs download the archive and run `cargo nextest run --archive-file ... --partition hash:N/3`. The same package list is archived and the same partitions run, so coverage is the same. Before, each shard compiled and linked all 176 test binaries (11 to 19 min) for 2 to 5 min of tests. Shards only restore the cache; the build job saves it.
- **Model checks to nightly.** `pool_protocol_is_safe` (254 s), `mutation_no_epoch_check_breaks_single_writer` (112 s) and `finding_stale_holder_cancels_current_attempt` (62 s) are filtered out on PR runs only. They still run on every push to main, in this workflow's nightly schedule, on a PR with `ci:full`, and on the macOS and Windows legs. A failed nightly run opens or updates one issue (`.github/actions/nightly-issue`, identical file in the other cut PRs).
- **Linker and debug info.** x86_64 Linux already links with rust-lld (rustc's default since 1.90; the toolchain is pinned at 1.97.1), so no mold or apt lld. CI test builds already set `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0`, lighter than `line-tables-only` (which `libs/cua/Cargo.toml` keeps for local builds), and keeps the archive small. macOS and Windows keep their linkers: not safe to swap without a run on each OS.
- Tests updated: the workspace-coverage test now reads the archive command's `-p` list; new tests pin the build-once wiring and the filter.

Needs a first CI run to confirm: archive size, the download time, and that the tests that look for built binaries or paths work from the archive (nextest remaps the workspace to the same path). The filter was checked against nextest locally.

Expected saving: 8 to 12 min on about 35% of PRs; about 3k Linux min/week.

Part 2 of CI audit cut 3 (Linear CUA-3562). title: ci: scope relay e2e (docker) to the relay, shard it, retry timing flakes (CUA-3558 #6)
body:
Cut #6 of the CI audit (Linear CUA-3558).

**What changes for contributors:** PRs that do not touch the relay or its dependencies no longer wait for `relay e2e (docker)`. When it does run, it finishes sooner and fails less.

**Scope (uses the package graph to start the job).** `ci_component_scope.py relay-e2e` loads `ci_graph.py` and starts the lane only if a changed file is in the dependency closure of `cua-relay`, `cua-spacesd`, `cua-spacesd-server`, `-socks`, `-teleport` and `tests/teleport-e2e` (macOS and Windows platform crates excluded, the lane is Linux). Pushes, release PRs, shared inputs (lockfiles, workflows, scope scripts) and unknown spacesd files fail closed and run it. So `cua-driver`, `cua-driver-e2e`, `cua-oidc` and similar changes skip it, while `cua-driver-core` or `cua-mesh` changes still run it, because the closure says they affect the build.

**Shards.** One parallel job per shard: `core`, `hosted`, `teleport`, `tunnel`. The old job ran them in sequence (core lane 28 to 34 min, relay lane 3 to 5 min). Reuse by tree still works per shard.

**Why it failed 32% of the time.** In the 40 most recent failing runs of this workflow, all 18 failures of this job were in the `linux-core-tests.sh` step, and every one was a timing test: `reconnect_storm` (4), `churn_bounded`, `share_links`, `pending_deletions`, `conformance::a_failing_health_check_restarts_a_service`, and `mesh_gang` (6, same assertion for four PRs in a row, then gone). This was the only Linux test lane that ran plain `cargo test` with no retry; the ubuntu `test` job and every other lane use nextest with the CI profile (one retry, flaky reporting). The shards now run under nextest with that profile, copy the JUnit files out, and report through `flaky.py`, so a test that passes only on the retry shows in the weekly flaky issue instead of failing the PR.

**Not done:** the compile still happens once per shard (no shared build cache between jobs). Cut #5 (build once with `cargo nextest archive`) would remove that.

Expected saving: wall time on the PRs that run it drops from about 34 min to about 22 to 25 min (the longest shard), and the lane is skipped on driver-only and other out-of-closure PRs. Linux minutes per run go up (four compiles); fewer runs bring the total down.

Tests: `.github/scripts/tests/test_ci_component_scope.py` (new relay cases), actionlint, `bin/ci --quick`.

Refs CUA-3558

title: fix(cua-cli): bound process start and Space lookup so a silent relay stream fails instead of hanging
body:
CUA-3541

`cua do shell` could hang forever when a relay stream went silent. Nothing put a deadline on the process start (the client waited for `ProcessStart` with no bound) or on finding and dialing the Space. Now both are bounded, and a silent link fails with a timeout error.

**Change**

- `cua-spacesd-client`: `start` waits at most `PROCESS_START_DEADLINE` (30s) for the first message on `StartProcess`, then returns `Error::Timeout`. The deadline is the new `ConnectOptions::start_timeout`, so tests and callers can change it. It covers the start only: once the process has started, the existing keepalive liveness check and the command's own timeout apply as before. This covers `run` and `spawn`, so `cua do shell`, `cua sb exec` and the interactive PTY path are all bounded.
- `cua-cli`: `env_of` limits the relay Space lookup (resolve plus the bounded `RELAY_START_WAIT` retry) and the `space_for` lookup to `SPACE_LOOKUP_DEADLINE` (60s). After that it returns `timed out: <space> did not answer within 60s; check that it is online: cua spaces ls`. The 60s budget is longer than `RELAY_START_WAIT` (30s), so a Space that is still starting still says so first.
- Mock spacesd: a new `silent_start` flag accepts `StartProcess` and never answers.
- Docs: the generated `cua-spacesd-client` Rust reference now lists `start_timeout` and `PROCESS_START_DEADLINE`.

**Tests**

- `a_silent_start_times_out` (native gRPC and gRPC-Web): `run` and `spawn` against a silent start both return `Error::Timeout`, and the next start that does get a reply finishes normally. With the deadline taken out, the test hangs until the per-test watchdog fails it.
- `a_space_lookup_that_never_answers_times_out_with_its_name`: a lookup that never resolves gives a `Timeout` naming the Space, and an error that arrives in time is passed through unchanged.

**Proof**

The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `cua-spacesd-client` (with `testing`) and `cua-cli`, run with the stack size CI uses. The cua-rust reference check is clean. All passed. The verify-cua-spaces journey only runs on Linux and was not run.

**Why `ci-gate` ended 26 min after the last check at p90.** It is not mainly a polling interval. Measured from the workflow runs of each PR's last commit, the gate finishes a median 1.9 min and p90 2.3 min after the last other workflow (n=266). The audit's 26 min came from reading check runs through the GraphQL rollup, which truncates at 80 contexts and so missed the real last check. The median 1.9 min is poll lag: the gate needed two identical listings, each up to 60 s apart. The long tail is the `local-ci` sign-off wait (2 PRs this week: 41 and 76 min), bounded at 75 min, and it will grow now that every PR needs the sign-off.
- Fix: once every run is complete, the confirming listing happens after 10 s, not a full poll interval. Expect the median 1.9 min to drop to about 0.5 min.
- The sign-off wait polls every 15 s instead of 60 s (same 75 min bound).
- What is not fixed here: the sign-off queue on the Mac runner. The report now shows it separately each week.

**Heads up.** `GET /repos/trycua/cua/actions/artifacts` answers 500 on this repository, even with `per_page=5`. `flaky.py digest` uses that call, so the weekly flaky issue may be failing silently. The new report avoids it by walking each workflow's runs.

title: feat(cua-driver-bench): Windows port of the BenchLab tasks
body:
Linear: CUA-3563

**What changes for users:** Cua Driver Bench can now run all ten Bench v2 tasks on Windows, so results for a computer-use tool on Windows sit next to its macOS and Linux results with the same seeds, checkers and "user undisturbed" rules.

## What's in it

The seven BenchLab tasks (MB-09 to MB-11, IR-01 to IR-04) ran on macOS and Linux only. This adds a Windows port that mirrors the Linux port:

- `windows/benchlab.py`: the seven modes in wxPython, so every control is a native Win32 control (Button, Edit, ComboBox, CheckBox, list view, tooltip) that UI Automation exposes. It uses `probes/_common/benchlab_common.py` unchanged, so seeds, the state file, the event log and the checkers are identical across OSes.
- `windows/sentinel.py`: the "User activity" window and its log, in the Linux sentinel's format, read by `swift/summarize_sentinel.py` unchanged. It measures all eight A22 criteria: foreground and key focus, windows raised over the user window, lost or redirected typing, real pointer movement, clipboard changes, virtual desktop switches, dialogs on the user's app, and activation changes.
- `windows/guard.py`: the GUI-only guard on Windows. A shell, console or script host (PowerShell, cmd, Windows Terminal, wscript/cscript, mshta, WSL) started in the desktop session outside the runner's own processes, or one in front, fails and stops the trial. Tool inputs are also scanned for PowerShell, cmd and script-host commands, on top of the existing patterns.
- `launch/windows_session.py`: runs one trial end to end. It renders the brief, starts BenchLab and the sentinel, arms the sentinel, runs the agent with the guard watching, then runs the checker and writes `row.json`. `windows/oracle.py` solves each task through the GUI with real input; it is used for validation only.
- `probes/*/launch.windows.json`, and the manifest now lists Windows for all ten tasks. The README's generated table and the Windows notes are updated.
- Tests: `tests/test_windows_tools.py` runs on any OS and covers guard rules, brief, descriptors, parity of modes and events with the Linux port, and that a Windows-shaped sentinel log measures all eight criteria. `tests/test_windows_desktop.py` runs on a Windows desktop. A new CI job, `windows-desktop`, runs both on `windows-latest`.

Where Windows behaves differently is written up in the README ("Windows (the BenchLab tasks)"). In short:

- MB-09 uses a native list-view drag.
- MB-10 and MB-11 stay foreground-only, because hover and tooltips follow the real pointer on Windows too.
- BenchLab's dialogs open without activation when BenchLab is behind, so the app never raises itself over the user's window.

## Validation

On a Windows 11 VM, through the real launcher:

- The scripted oracle passes the checker of all seven tasks, with no GUI-only violation.
- A no-op agent fails the checker, and the sentinel reports all eight criteria held.
- A deliberate disturbance (focus steal, raise, pointer move, clipboard) is flagged on key focus, window raised, typing, pointer, clipboard and activation.
- One full Claude Code trial per setup (IR-02, background) ran end to end.

Locally: `pytest tests probes/tests swift/tests` (354 passed) and `tools/taskset.py check` both pass, and ruff 0.14.10 is clean.

No results are published here.

title: fix(spaces): one clean reply when an agent answers in a thread
body:
## Why

"@claude hi" posted a messy first reply: the agent's narration before its tool call ("I'll check the thread and respond. Let me get the tool schemas first.") glued to its answer with no space, a "woke up and joined" line, and a "New" divider.

## What

- Runner events of a turn are split at tool calls. The reply a thread gets (and the live row preview, and the finished notification) is only the text after the last tool call; a turn that ends right after a tool call posts its last non-empty text. Segments are never glued: `cua agent run` / `logs` still get the whole transcript, with segments separated by a blank line.
- Prompt: the home brief and the thread framing are a short rule set (final text is the one reply, nothing before a tool, greetings and answerable questions get one or two sentences and no tools, never list abilities unless asked). The ability list stays, behind "when asked or when a job needs it". The framing no longer names the thread tools, so a plain reply does not send the model looking for their schemas.
- Thread rows: "woke up and joined" is not drawn between a person's message and the agent's reply (kept for a task another agent gave); the "New" divider is not drawn for an agent's answer to the reader's own message.

## Evidence

- New `agent_one_reply` test (in-process spacesd mock, temp cua home, runner events as files). On main it posts `I'll check the thread and respond. Let me get the tool schemas first.Hi! I'm ready to help. ...`; now `Hi! I'm ready to help. What would you like me to do?`.
- Unit tests for `final_reply` / `summarize`, thread fold tests, agent-home prompt test.
- Screenshots (before/after) are in the PR thread: real web UI, thread data from the test run.

## Not covered

Whether Claude Code defers the thread tools behind ToolSearch is decided by the harness (tool count), not this repo; the framing change removes the prompt that sent the model to look for them.

title: feat(spaces): Network picker with an "Also allow" list (localhost and local network are siblings)
body:
Draft for review (UI change).

## What
In a Space's Network setting, "Allow this computer's localhost" and "Allow my local network" were radio buttons, so one looked like a superset of the other (the web ranked local network above localhost). They are siblings: each is Internet only plus one extra.

Now: the base is Internet only, No network or Custom, and under Internet only an "Also allow" list has two independent checkboxes:

- Services on this computer (with its warning and the ports field)
- Other devices on my network (with its warning)

Both can be ticked. The Details row reads "Internet only", "Internet and this computer's services", "Internet and your local network" or "Internet, this computer's services and your local network" (full text on hover when the column truncates it). A child Space can only tick an extra its parent has.

Screenshots (real web UI, demo mode, before and after): `~/projects/.cua-work/netpicker-shots/` on the author's Mac (before-*.png, after-*.png). They are not attached here.

## Model
The policy could not express both extras any other way: Custom allows cannot open the host's loopback (only the localhost preset does), so this adds one preset, `localhost+lan` (`NetworkPreset::LocalhostLan`). `localhost` and `lan` keep their meaning.

- Preset is a string on the wire (proto, SDK, MCP, settings files, saved Spaces), so no proto fields change and old files and clients keep working; `buf breaking` has nothing to flag (comments only).
- `localhost+lan` takes the ports of `localhost` (`cua network set --network localhost+lan:5432,3000`, `localhost+lan:all`; `lan+localhost` is accepted).
- Children: the meet keeps each extra only when both sides have it (localhost+lan under lan is lan; under localhost, localhost; ports intersect, and if none are shared the local network stays). Agents (MCP) still cannot open either extra.
- The web, Electron and SwiftUI word parsers take the new word. Generated bindings and docs are regenerated.

## Tests
- Rust (cua-vmm, cua-spaces): rules for both extras together, validation, words and JSON round trip including old settings files, summary and widenings, intersections both ways, VM port forwarding, agent refusal, the existing property tests now cover the new preset. `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean.
- Web vitest: picker with nothing, one box, both, No network/Custom hiding the list, child ceiling; summaries; ceiling and word functions. Full web suite passes; typecheck and design lint clean.
- Desktop and SwiftUI parser tests added; not run here (no Electron/Swift build).

Not run locally: the heavy generator checks (docs reference for cua-rust and cua-cli, Electron `--check-bindings`, Swift app binding), the hand-edited CLI and SDK reference pages, and Swift tests; CI will say.

Based on the "Internet only" label fix in #6605 (this branch contains it; it drops out when that merges).

title: [Bug]: cua-driver skill fails Agent Skills frontmatter validation
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

The cua-driver skill fails Agent Skills reference validation because its frontmatter contains an unexpected top-level `version` field.

### Reproduction

1. Get `libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/SKILL.md` from the Cua repository and save it as `cua-driver/SKILL.md`.
2. Run `uvx --from 'git+https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills.git#subdirectory=skills-ref' skills-ref validate cua-driver`.

### Expected behavior

The skill passes frontmatter validation against the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification).

### Actual behavior

```text
Validation failed for cua-driver:
  - Unexpected fields in frontmatter: version. Only ['allowed-tools', 'compatibility', 'description', 'license', 'metadata', 'name'] are allowed.
```

### Environment

Cua Driver 0.38.0 on macOS 27.0 (arm64). Also reproduced with the skill from Cua `main` at commit `81f3e1bb`, version 0.39.0, and `skills-ref` at commit `83021e2be457a9b6679148719c1f6074f0ad975e`.

The field is in [`rust/Skills/cua-driver/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/81f3e1bb/libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/SKILL.md#L4). The installed skill also caused my skill frontmatter check to fail.

### Workaround and additional context

Moving the version into `metadata` made my local frontmatter check pass. The release version checker currently looks for a top-level `version` line.

title: fix(spaces): a new message and an agent's tool calls no longer wait on a slow Space
body:
## What

A message posted to a new home reached its agent 40 to 80 s late, and Claude Code's first token came 31 s after the turn started.

Causes (measured in the Local app):
- The app posts the message in another process than the daemon's supervisor, so the in-process wake never fired. The supervisor pass itself took 30 to 60 s (sequential calls into old Spaces that do not answer), and a new member's setup, standby start, dispatch and the agent's bridge (MCP tool list, answered only at pass time, hence the 31 s) all waited on it.

## Change

- A dispatcher task looks twice a second (and on a wake): settles a new member's setup, starts its standby run, hands queued tasks to members, and reads each live session on its own task (every quarter second while the agent talks to its bridge).
- A Space that does not answer holds up only its own agent.
- Logs for standby starts and for a task waiting behind a serving member.

## Numbers (real Local app, `Hi` in a new home, warm Space claimed)

Before: delivered 39 to 79 s, session_ready +1 s, first_token +31 s. After: delivered 0.3 s, session_ready 1.95 s, first_token 4.1 s, turn_ended 4.2 s.

## Test

Existing `a_posted_task_wakes_the_supervisor_without_waiting_for_the_poll` (60 s poll) still passes by design; the cross-process path was verified in the app.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): wait for each VideoToolbox frame on macOS so encoder surfaces do not pile up
body:
On macOS, a stream whose VideoToolbox session encodes slower than ScreenCaptureKit captures queues frames inside VideoToolbox. This happens on a large display, or when several sessions share the media engine. Each queued frame holds its own encoder surface. The daemon's footprint grows with that backlog, and the viewer falls behind by the same amount.

The cause is in `macos_h264.rs`. The one-slot mailbox only drops frames that have not been submitted yet. `VTCompressionSessionEncodeFrame` returns before the frame is encoded, so the worker kept handing VideoToolbox more frames than it could finish.

The fix calls `VTCompressionSessionCompleteFrames` after each frame, which the `cua-media-codec` VideoToolbox backend already does. The mailbox now drops the frames the encoder can't keep up with, as it was meant to, and each session holds one set of encoder surfaces.

Measured on a Mac mini with a virtual 5K display and full-screen motion, streaming over QUIC:

- Sessions now hold one set of encoder surfaces each, where before they built up a large backlog of them. The daemon's footprint drops several-fold once two or more sessions run at once.
- Frame rate per session is unchanged.
- Capture-to-receive latency per session drops to a fraction of what it was.
- A single session on a 1080p display was already fine and does not change.

Test: `videotoolbox_emits_each_frame_before_the_next_is_submitted` encodes three frames and requires each one's output before the next is submitted. It fails without the fix.

CUA-3327

title: fix(cua-driver-bench): Windows cua-driver process counted as a window raise
body:
Bench v2 Windows port: the sentinel summarizer scored cua-driver's own agent-cursor overlay as `window_raised`, against the documented rule in METHOD.md (the driver's own windows are logged but not counted against the user-undisturbed criteria).

title: fix(cua-driver-core): gate YAML capability-manifest tests on the yaml feature
body:
CUA-3504

## Problem

`cargo test -p cua-driver-core --no-default-features` failed 16 tests in `authorization`, `batch_tools`, `consent`, `session_authorization` and `tool::runtime_isolation_tests`. Each one builds a capability manifest from YAML through `session_manifest::load_manifest`. Without the `yaml` feature that function returns "capability manifest support requires the yaml feature", so the tests panicked while setting up.

## Change

These tests exercise manifest behaviour that a build without `yaml` cannot reach. They are now gated with `#[cfg(feature = "yaml")]`, the same gate `session_manifest`'s own tests already use. The gate also covers the YAML helpers they use (`bounded_context`, `manifest_context`, `manifest_with_allowed_tool`, `authorization_context_with_manifest`) and the `std::io::Write` imports that only those helpers need, so there are no new unused-code warnings. The change is test-only and production code is untouched.

## Proof

The scoped repository checks for `cua-driver-core`, run with default features and with `--no-default-features`:
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test`

Library tests: 1116 passed under `--no-default-features` (16 failed before this change) and 1179 passed with default features. Every integration test target passes in both configurations.

title: fix(auth): the Local channel never touches the login Keychain
body:
Stacked on #6587 (base `localkeys`); retarget to main once it merges.

Cua Spaces Local is signed ad hoc, so macOS sees every rebuild as a new app and asks for Keychain access on each launch. Local now never reads or writes the login Keychain:

- `CuaChannel::uses_login_keychain` (false for Local) is the one gate.
- `Store::from_env` (cua-auth): Local is always the 0600 file store, even with `CUA_CREDENTIAL_STORE=keychain`.
- `vault_fallback_applies`: Local never reads the vault's copy of a named secret (the device key under `ai.cua.session.local`), the read that prompted on a Local launch with an item left by an earlier build.
- Daemon Keyvault (cua-spaces-ext): Local builds it without the OS protector, so opening an existing vault no longer reads or writes the `Cua Keyvault Generation` Keychain item named by the vault id.

Stable and Nightly behavior is unchanged. Tests: Local never calls an injected vault read, Stable still does, and the store choice and fallback rules for Stable are asserted.

## What this does for readers

Publishes the driver arm adapters used in the Cua Driver Bench v2 release runs, so anyone can rerun every arm with the public runner.

- **Vercel agent-desktop 1.2.0**: a small MCP adapter (one tool per CLI command) with the vendor's own skill text as server instructions (Apache-2.0, notice included). Arm `cc-agent-desktop`.

- **Codex computer use**: a stdio filter between Claude Code and OpenAI's computer-use plugin (adds the sandbox metadata, answers the per-app approval prompt for allow-listed apps only, answers `server/discover`, flattens the Windows `js` schema). It is OpenAI's plugin with Claude choosing the actions, not OpenAI's own agent.

The runner gets the two new arms (not in the default set), tool classes for the analysis, a preflight check, and pin entries. README, METHOD and RUNNER say, per arm: what it is, exact versions, install steps, how to run on macOS, Linux and Windows, and the limits. For Codex the docs state that readers need the ChatGPT desktop app with Computer Use enabled (Settings > Computer use > Any App) and their own ChatGPT account with Work or Codex access; no credentials are shipped; it is not available on Linux yet and runs foreground only on Windows (links included).

Only the generic adapter and config code is included: no rig, host or machine plumbing.

## Tests

New `tests/test_vendor_adapters.py` (17 tests: tool-to-argv mapping, command parsing and refusals, round trips against fake binaries, the filter's four behaviours, arm registration and MCP config). title: feat(cua-driver-bench): run the BenchLab tasks on Hyprland (Wayland), e.g. Omarchy
body:
Refs CUA-3573.

**What this means for users:** Cua Driver Bench v2 can now measure computer-use drivers on a Wayland Linux desktop (Hyprland, such as Omarchy), including whether they leave the person using the computer undisturbed.

## What changes

A Hyprland port of the BenchLab trial, next to the Linux/X11 and Windows ports:

- `hyprland/sentinel.py`: the "User activity" witness as a native Wayland GTK3 window. The eight A22 criteria come from Hyprland's IPC socket (active window, stacking order of `clients`, top and overlay layer surfaces, `cursorpos`, active and special workspaces, full-screen windows, a second window of the sentinel's process), `wl-paste --watch` (data-control) for the clipboard, and GTK events for key focus and leaked keys, clicks and scrolls. Compositor reads run off the GTK thread.
- `hyprland/guard.py`: the GUI-only guard. Terminal emulators started outside the runner's tree, or a terminal or Omarchy TUI window active for three samples, fail the trial; tool inputs are scanned for `hyprctl`, compositor `exec`, uwsm and Omarchy launchers, and terminal names.
- `launch/hyprland_session.py` + `hyprland/bench.lua`: one trial (brief, BenchLab, sentinel, guard, checker, `row.json`), with floating frames placed through IPC, 1920x1080 so the shared frames fit, and window rules so BenchLab's windows never take focus on open and its dialogs open over BenchLab instead of over the user window (the macOS sheet / Windows dialog behaviour).
- `hyprland/oracle.py`: solves each task through the GUI with real input (a uinput pointer and keyboard), to validate the port.
- `probes/*/launch.hyprland.json`, README section "Linux on Hyprland", `tests/test_hyprland_tools.py`.

BenchLab itself (`linux/benchlab.py`), the seeds, the checkers and `summarize_sentinel.py` are unchanged.

## Validation

On the Omarchy edge image (Hyprland 0.56.2, GTK 3.24.52): the oracle passes all seven checkers; doing nothing fails all seven and leaves the user undisturbed; a deliberate focus change, raise, pointer move, clipboard change, keystroke and workspace switch are each caught. `pytest tests probes/tests swift/tests` passes (364 passed) and `tools/taskset.py check` is ok.

title: feat(cua): Windows 11 on Apple silicon built locally, ISO downloaded automatically (QEMU+HVF); Windows 10, Server 2019 and 2025 from an ISO
body:
## What this does

A Windows 11 Space works on an Apple silicon Mac with no manual step. In New Space (or `cua sb create windows:11`), choose Windows 11: cua downloads the ARM64 ISO from Microsoft, installs Windows unattended under QEMU with HVF (native speed; Windows 11 on ARM runs x64 apps), installs cua-spacesd, seals the disk as a base image, and boots the Space. Every later Space is a copy-on-write clone that answers in about 40 seconds. The same machinery builds `windows:2025`, `windows:2019` and `windows:10` (x64) from Microsoft's evaluation ISOs or your own (`--iso`); a Windows PC builds through WSL2 with KVM. `windows` / `windows:2022` stays the published Server 2022 containerDisk. Design and verification status: `docs/windows-images.md`.

This branch also carries the 9 dogfooding commits of `fix/winlike-windows-builder-whpx` (Python builder).

## Verified (Mac Studio, Apple silicon, macOS 26.6, QEMU 10.2 with HVF)

From the CLI and in the real Cua Spaces Local app, built from this branch:

* **Nothing to a Windows 11 desktop, unattended.** ISO download from Microsoft (8.5 GB, checked against Microsoft's published SHA-256, 7 min), install, cua-spacesd, seal, first boot. With the ISO cached: 8 to 9 minutes from Create to Running.
* **The second create is a clone**: cua-spacesd answers 36 s (CLI) and 36 s / 40 s (app; the second ran while the first was up) after Create.
* **Cua Spaces works in the guest**: screenshot, `exec` (cmd.exe), `cua do click/type/key` through cua-spacesd (Notepad opened from the Start menu and typed into); in the app the Space is listed like any other, with its desktop streaming, window list and "Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 on This Mac".
* **Progress in plain words**, read in the app: "Downloading Windows (first time only)... 1.5 of 7.9 GB, 14 MB/s, about 8 min", "Installing Windows (first time only)..." with a bar that moves (32% a minute in), "Booting Windows...", Running.
* **Cancel** (`cua spaces cancel`, the call the app's Cancel makes) stops the install VM and its TPM within seconds and releases the build lock.
* **`--runtime auto`** picks QEMU with HVF for ARM64 Windows on Apple silicon (unit test `auto::tests` and the real runs). x64 Windows there is refused in plain words, in the dialog, `cua sb create` and `cua spaces create`.
* Tests: `cua-image` 162, `cua-spaces-app-core` 891, `cua-spaces` windows guard, `cua-daemon` 204 (one timing test flaked once and passed on re-run), `cua-cli` 378, `cua-vmm` qemu/auto/cloudinit/fetch/preflight (1 failure, `qemu::tests::live_tpm_vm_refusals`, which also fails on the base commit on macOS: an egress policy the runtime refuses). Clippy `-D warnings` clean on the 8 crates, on macOS.

Screenshots (real, from the app on the test Mac) are in the Linear issue linked below; they are not attached here because the GitHub API cannot upload images.

## NOT verified

* An interrupted ISO download resuming for real (unit tested with a fake server; a real retry hit Microsoft's rate limit, see below).
* **Windows 10, Server 2019, Server 2025 (x64) builds and the Evaluation Center scraping**: no x64 host; answer file, ISO resolution and runtime selection are unit tested only.
* **The Windows PC path (WSL2/KVM, WHPX)**: unit tested only. The WSL install driver now waits for the guest to power itself off and presses Enter for the first 14 s only; no Windows PC has run it. Running a UEFI Windows guest from the Rust QEMU runtime on a Windows PC still uses WHPX, which hangs in OVMF on current QEMU (known gap, unchanged).
* **No native ARM64 cua-spacesd exists** (releases carry only x86_64 Windows). The guest tries the native asset first and falls back to the x64 build, which Windows 11 on ARM runs under its own emulation; that is what was verified. A release job for `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` is a follow-up.
* The ARM64 display is `ramfb` at 800x600 (virtio-win has an ARM64 `viogpudo`; not done).
* **No ISO-path field in the New Space dialog** (an `isoPath` needs the create request, the SDK options and the bindings changed). Windows 11 on a Mac needs none; `cua sb create windows:11 --iso <path>` registers one.
* Microsoft limits how many download links one network gets in a short time ("Sentinel marked this request as rejected"). It happened after about eight link requests in a day of testing; the create then fails with that cause in words and `--iso` as the way out.

## Questions for the owner

1. **Licence (not decided here).** Microsoft publishes no ARM64 Windows 11 evaluation ISO. For ARM64, cua uses the same account-free service the "Download Windows 11" pages use (the page's edition id, then a link on `software.download.prss.microsoft.com`, checked against the SHA-256 the page publishes; cua never bundles, mirrors or republishes an ISO). That is Microsoft's **consumer media, installed as Windows 11 Pro unactivated** (the answer file uses the public generic Pro key, which activates nothing): it runs with a watermark and limited personalisation until a licence is added. Is that acceptable as the default, or should ARM64 ask for `--iso` or a licence step first? The CLI prints it before the first build.
2. **Software emulation (decided, with the reason; say if you disagree).** x64 Windows on an Apple silicon Mac (and ARM64 Windows on an x64 computer) could only run in software emulation (TCG). That is refused by default, in plain words, before anything is downloaded: it takes hours to install and is too slow for an agent's screenshot and click loop. The message names the way out (on a Mac use `windows:11`) and `CUA_ALLOW_SOFTWARE_EMULATION=1` accepts the slowness (12 hours allowed for the install). One message serves `--runtime auto` (`auto::select`), the QEMU runtime and the build.

## What changed since the Windows-PC-only draft

* **ISO**: Microsoft's download service for ARM64, checksum-checked, resumable, with bytes, rate and time left.
* **Build**: cua-spacesd installed the way the published Windows image does it (scheduled task in the desktop session, bootstrap mode, token directory), the newest cua-spacesd release with a Windows build, then **sealing** (no token or per-machine state) and power-off; the host waits for the power-off. The install VM is stopped at once when the create is cancelled. Enter is pressed only while the screen shows "Press any key to boot from CD": a blind timer reached Setup's Cancel button twice in real runs.
* **Runtime**: ARM64 Windows boots on the generic edk2 firmware when no Secure Boot pair exists (Homebrew's QEMU ships none; Setup's checks are bypassed); swtpm is installed with Homebrew on demand.
* **Create path**: a local Windows build resolves to an image that declares cua-spacesd (`create` returned immediately before), `--kind` defaults to a VM, the catalog's guest OS is used (without it the Space booted as Linux: no TPM, wrong display and disk), and the install VM's own boot reports no longer push the app's progress bar past the install.
* **New Space**: Windows is offered on Apple silicon and picks Windows 11; Server and Windows 10 there are refused with the reason (wizard and Spaces create guard). Row labels: "Downloading Windows (first time only)", "Installing Windows (first time only)".
* **Fixes found on the way**: Windows guests refused the host's telemetry setting; `cua sb exec` ran `/bin/sh` in Windows guests (now `cmd.exe`); `qemu_builder.py` used `_plat` before importing it; the catalog's four local builds are in the `distro` group (the `canonical` group is generated from canonical.rs); docs generator accepts `local_build`; FFI, Swift and Electron bindings regenerated.

## Update 2026-11-12: merged with main, Mac gate removed end to end, verified on a second Mac

* **Merged main** (451 commits) and fixed what the merge broke: feature gates in `cua-vmm` and `cua-sdk`, the `CreateAction` parent field, Swift tests and the bridge for the new fix action (`choose-windows-iso`, link fields; this was the red SwiftUI lane), formatting.
* **No more "coming soon" on a Mac.** The Windows tile reads "Windows" and is selectable on a Mac that has a build for it (Windows 11 on Apple silicon). It is greyed out with its reason only when the processor is unknown; a Mac without QEMU gets "Needs QEMU: ..." with Continue waiting; x64 images keep the "Choose Windows 11" reason. The refusal in `spaces.rs` is renamed (`WINDOWS_EMULATION_ONLY`); goldens regenerated with `UPDATE_PARITY=1`; the Electron wizard test and the Swift tests follow.
* **Bug found by running it:** main now always puts non-Linux QEMU guests behind the secure network gateway, and its DHCP offer carried an empty DNS search list (option 119), which Windows refuses (error 0xD, stays on 169.254). No Windows guest had a network, so the first-logon script could not fetch cua-spacesd. The gateway no longer sends the option without search domains (unit test included).
* **End to end on a spare Apple silicon Mac** (macOS 26.6, QEMU 11.1, HVF, Cua Spaces Local built from this branch): New Space, Windows (tile enabled, Windows 11), Create: the ISO downloaded from Microsoft with its SHA-256 checked, Windows 11 installed unattended, the Space reached Running, `cua sb exec` answered through cua-spacesd (`Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.26300.9457]`), the guest had 10.0.2.15 and internet. Not verified: Windows 10, Server (x64 only), a Windows PC, resuming an interrupted download.
* **Security review findings, fixed:** `cua-spacesd.exe` is run only if it matches the SHA-256 the release publishes beside it (a missing or different one fails the install); virtio-win is pinned to release 0.1.302-1 by its versioned URL and SHA-256 (a mismatch deletes the file and fails the create; the Python builder too); the consumer ISO link must be https on a Microsoft domain. `docs/windows-images.md` lists every download and its check, says the x64 evaluation ISOs (no published hash) rely on TLS, and notes the passwordless administrator (as in the published image).
* **Also fixed:** `cua-sdk` did not compile without its `spaces` feature (also on main: `bin/ci`'s per-crate clippy of `cua-compat-cmd` fails there); the dead-code lints that exposed are allowed for that reduced feature set; a telemetry test lacked the new `parent` field.
* **Re-verified after those changes** on the spare Mac (a fresh Windows 11 Space: the guest log shows the cua-spacesd SHA-256 matching the published one, the Space reached Running, `cua sb exec` answered, the guest had internet).

title: fix(spaces): say why a warm-pool refill waits, and end the agents of a deleted Space
body:
Fixes CUA-3579. Follow-up to #6619 (independent of it; touches different code).

**Warm pool.** The pool decided silently (debug level) not to refill. Reproduced in the real Local app: with seven Spaces running in the 4 CPU / 6 GiB runtime VM the daemon removed the idle member ("memory is short") and deferred the refill, because free memory fell under the 1 GiB floor:

```
warm pool: memory is short; removing a member member=cua-pool-ff03...
warm pool: refill deferred shape=a2d1... reason=not enough free memory: 5044 MiB of 5910 MiB in use by running Spaces, a member needs about 200 MiB and 1024 MiB stay free (pool holds 0 of its 5910 MiB share)
```

So the next new home had no warm Space. Now:
- a deferred refill says why, with the numbers, once per reason and again every 2 minutes (capacity wanted elsewhere, busy CPUs, memory, repeated start failures);
- a shape that failed three starts in a row is tried again after 5 minutes instead of never;
- the refill is retried every pool tick (2 s), so it starts as soon as a Space is deleted: in the app, deleting a home started the new member 2 s later.
The memory floor is kept on purpose: the pool does not take memory from running homes.

**Deleted Spaces and persistent agents.** `Spaces::delete` now tells extensions (`space_deleted`); the persistent-agent extension removes the agents that lived in the Space as `agent rm` does (run stopped, open tasks failed, routines and standby sessions dropped; the home stays in the Cua Volume). Agents of a cloud Space released on pause and durable members are kept. The supervisor also marks agents whose local Space is not registered (deleted behind its back) `gone` after 20 s: paused, unsupervised, no more log lines; `agent rm` still forgets them, `agent ls` shows `gone`.

**Tests.** `pool::` unit tests (memory deferral and recovery, never above the pool size, failure cool-down) and `tests/deleted_space_agents.rs` (delete removes agents and schedules, other Spaces untouched, gone reconciliation with grace, rm still works).

**In the app** (merged build with #6619): three homes back to back all claimed a warm Space (56-353 ms), delivered 261-465 ms, first token 4.3-5.1 s; the pool refilled 1.9-2.8 s after each claim. Deleting homes removed their agents at once.

title: test(agentic): prompt tests v1: plain-English goals, hard checks, record and replay
body:
Prompt tests v1 ([CUA-3570](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3570)). A prompt test is a plain-English goal ("add a second computer, then remove it"). An agent carries it out by driving the real Cua Spaces app through Cua Driver. Hard checks decide pass or fail; the model never does.

**What changes for users:** regressions like the ghost row after Remove, a PC that stays offline after setup, staging taking over a production host, a Windows Firewall prompt during setup, or a computer that never shows as offline get caught every night, before a release.

Design note: `docs/rfcs/prompt-tests.md`.

## What's here

- **Specs:** `tests/agentic/<area>/<name>.yaml`, with `name`, `os`, `setup` (build, canary account, hosts), `prompt`, `budget` and `expect`. `bin/agentic-e2e validate` checks them; an unknown key is an error.
- **Runner:** `bin/agentic-e2e run`. It installs the build, starts Cua Driver, sets up the hosts (each one is its own Cua home), signs the canary account in with the device code flow (staging realm only), runs the agent, runs the checks and writes `report.md` with screenshots, the video and every tool call. Then it tears everything down and takes every computer and device the run added off the account.
- **Agent:** Claude Code in headless mode. The model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) and the harness version are pinned in `tests/agentic/config.yaml`. Its only tools are Cua Driver's, through a pass-through MCP server that logs every call, enforces the step budget and starts Cua Driver's `start_recording` on the agent's own session.
- **Checks:** `relay` and `cli` take jq predicates. `ui` asserts on the accessibility tree (`contains`, `absent`, `row`), held for `hold_s` or reached within `within_s`, optionally timed from an event such as `power_off:2`. `no_dialogs` watches every window title from install to the last check. `file`.
- **Record and replay:** a passing `--record` run saves the turn files that `start_recording` writes, plus a `portable.json` that maps pids, windows and element tokens onto the live app. `--mode auto` replays them and runs live if the replay breaks.
- **Workflow:** `e2e-agentic.yml`. Nightly live runs on `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` (macOS gets a lane once a test lists it). `workflow_call` is ready for the release gate. On PRs it validates the specs and runs the unit tests. A nightly failure opens or updates one issue.
- **Tests:** five, written from the 5 Nov Windows and Linux bugs (CUA-3512, CUA-3513, CUA-3515, CUA-3525 and the offline flip).

## Live results (5 Nov, Linux test VM, nightly build 0.21.0-nightly.20261105.16)

| Test | Result | Why |
|---|---|---|
| offline-flips-fast | **Pass** (live $0.46, then replay $0) | The details showed Offline 1 s after the power-off; the relay agreed. The trajectory is committed, and its replay passed on a fresh machine with no model. |
| add-remove-no-ghost | **Fail** (2 runs, $0.71 / $0.74) | The agent added the computer with a pairing code and turned it off. The Machines page kept it "Online" with a Running Space for 5+ minutes, while the same page's Issues box said it was offline and the relay had it offline. Remove stayed disabled, so the ghost-row step never ran. |
| remove-readd-rejoins | **Fail** (2 runs, $0.42 / $0.46) | Same as above: the app kept the computer "Online" after power-off, so "Remove from account" stayed disabled ("It's online"). |
| staging-prod-isolation | **Blocked** | The staging canary account reached the relay's 64-device cap mid-session. Every fresh sign-in enrolls a device, and the runner didn't revoke them yet (fixed here: teardown revokes each host's device). No new computer can join until stale devices are revoked. Also, on a reused VM, default homes map to isolated ones, so this test only reproduces CUA-3512 fully on a fresh CI runner. |
| no-firewall-prompt (Windows) | **Blocked** | The repo secrets below are missing, so it can't run on `windows-latest`. Our Windows test VM was in use by the benchmark runs all session. |

Also seen: on Linux, a **"Choose password for new keyring"** dialog appeared while using the app (now on the watched-dialogs list), and the Machines list rows expose no online or offline text in the accessibility tree (status is a coloured dot only).

## Secrets to add

`CUA_E2E_CANARY_USERNAME` and `CUA_E2E_CANARY_PASSWORD` (the staging canary account). `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` already exists. Without them, the nightly job fails with the names of the missing secrets.

## Not in v1

macOS tests (hosted macOS needs Cua Driver TCC seeding), PR replay (v2), the release gate wiring (after the secrets and a green week), and pid, window and token mapping inside `replay_trajectory` itself.

## Plan

`is_physical_desktop_action` in `cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs` decides which tools take the process-wide desktop lane (`requires_desktop_coordination`). It was a hand-kept list beside the contract's `ACTION_RESULT_TOOLS`, and it had already drifted: `type_text_chars` and `invoke_menu` return the shared action result but were missing, so they ran outside the lane alongside other native input.

title: feat(cua-driver-bench): shared-desktop tasks PA-01 (parallel agents) and UM-01 (mouse user)
body:
**What this means for users:** Cua Driver Bench can now measure two things people run into when agents share a computer: whether several agents can work at once in their own copies of an app without stepping on each other, and whether a person can keep using their mouse while an agent works in the background.

Stacked on #6630 (Hyprland port); GitHub retargets it to `main` when that merges.

## Design note

[`automated-eval/macos_bench/SHARED-DESKTOP.md`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/feat/driver-bench-parallel-and-mouse-user/libs/cua-driver-bench/automated-eval/macos_bench/SHARED-DESKTOP.md): why the tasks matter, exact starting states, sub-tasks, seeds, checkers, scoring, budgets, how they relate to the eight undisturbed criteria, platform notes (macOS, Windows, Linux X11, Hyprland) and threats to validity. Both tasks are deterministic and checker-graded, like every v2 task. They sit in a new `shared_desktop` category and are selected by id or `--task-set shared-desktop`; they are not added to the ten registered v2 tasks (a dated amendment registers them before the first scored trial).

## The tasks

| Task | Starting state | Agent(s) | Checker pass | Full pass adds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **PA-01** parallel agents | N copies of BenchLab (`desk` mode) in a fixed 5 x 2 grid; labels, codes and shelves from the seed (N = 10; also 4, and 1 for the speed-up baseline) | N agents started at the same moment, one per copy, each told its copy by title and grid position | every copy: right code, right shelf, one Submit, no letter of another copy's code (code letters are unique per copy, so cross-talk is attributable), Submit within the shared 360 s budget | background: the eight undisturbed criteria |
| **UM-01** the user's mouse keeps working | one copy partly under the "User activity" window, whose user moves and clicks the real pointer on a seeded path over eight dots | one agent, background only | the copy's checks | the pointer never displaced from the user's script (3 px), every user click landed on its dot, no agent input in the user window, plus the other undisturbed criteria |

PA-01 also reports copies passed, cross-talk, makespan, throughput (copies per minute) and the speed-up over N = 1 for the same run index. A driver without multi-session support may serialise the agents; its copies count if they are correct within the budget.

On macOS and Windows the mouse user tags its own events (`kCGEventSourceUserData`, `dwExtraInfo`) and a listen-only tap or low-level hook counts any other pointer event; on X11 and Hyprland the sentinel compares the observed pointer with its own script 40 times a second.

## What changes

- BenchLab `desk` mode on macOS (`swift/BenchLabShared.swift`), Linux GTK (X11 and Wayland) and Windows (wxPython).
- `--mouse-user SCRIPT` in every sentinel (macOS, X11, Hyprland, Windows); `summarize_sentinel` reports `mouse_user` and puts the displacement in `pointer_max_deviation_px`; `bench_v2` scores the pointer and input criteria against the mouse user.
- N concurrent agents: `run_bench.py` (macOS, Linux X11), `launch/windows_session.py` and `launch/hyprland_session.py` (`--instances`, `{instance}` and `{title}` in the agent command). Any agent's GUI-only violation ends all of them.
- Checkers `probes/PA-01/evaluate.py` and `probes/UM-01/evaluate.py`; shared derivations in `benchlab_common.py`; runner helpers in `shared_desktop.py`.
- `tools/analyze_v2.py`: PA-01 per N (all copies passed, cross-talk, makespan, throughput, speed-up) and UM-01 (checker pass, full pass, displacement, lost clicks); `--session-rows` reads Windows and Hyprland `row.json`.
- Manifest entries, README table, `TASKS.md`, a pointer in `METHOD.md`, launch descriptors for Windows and Hyprland, TCC grants for the macOS sentinel (Accessibility, Input Monitoring).
- `tools/validate_shared.py`: a model-free real-desktop validation on macOS (accessibility-only oracles, deliberate cross-talk, pointer displacement, covered canvas).

## Testing

- `probes/tests/test_shared_desktop.py`: derivations; scripted oracles pass for N = 1, 4 and 10; a no-op fails; cross-talk (full code or a single foreign letter), a double Submit, a late Submit, a missing copy (harness error), pointer displacement, foreign pointer events, a lost click and an agent click in the user window are all caught; the analysis tables render.
- `tests/test_shared_desktop_runner.py`: `run_attempt` for PA-01 with faked agents (all N start together, each gets its own copy's brief; cross-talk fails the trial; one agent's violation ends all agents).
- Linux (CI `linux-desktop`, Xvfb) and Windows (CI `windows-desktop`) desktop tests drive the new mode and the mouse user on a real display.
- Local: harness suite 414 passed, `tools/taskset.py check`, fairness tests, Swift build, `ruff` clean.

Real-desktop validation on macOS and Hyprland, and the scored re-measure, follow separately.

title: feat(cua-driver-bench): pi-hosted arms for the four Cua Driver setups
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: the bench can drive its four Cua Driver setups only through Claude Code (`cc-*`) or the Codex app server. Comparing another agent host on the same setups had no arm to run.
- What changed: four arms, `pi-cua-driver`, `pi-cua-driver-main`, `pi-cua-driver-main-skill` and `pi-cua-driver-script`. Each reuses its `cc-*` twin's driver build and daemon, MCP entry, skill directory, system prompt, brief, turn cap and wall-time limit. Only the host changes, to `pi --mode json` with a configurable provider and model (`CDB_PI_PROVIDER`, `CDB_PI_MODEL`, `CDB_PI_THINKING`).
  - Tool surface: `read`, `tool_search` and the `cua` server with deferred exposure, the counterpart of Claude Code's `Skill, Read, ToolSearch` with only `mcp__cua` allowed. A small extension (`pi_gate.ts`) limits `read` to the skill's `SKILL.md`, matching the `cc-*` arms where every `Read` is denied. The same extension enforces `max_turns` inside the host, aborting the next turn before its model request. Codemode, shell and file tools, other extensions and context files are off.
  - `pi_arms.Translator` turns the host's JSON events into the stream the GUI-only guard, `claude_events.summarize` and `classify_failure` already read. A tool outside the surface maps to a forbidden built-in, so it ends the trial as a violation. A run that exits nonzero or without settling leaves no result and is retried as a harness failure, never scored.
  - The host's per-trial state, including a symlink to the operator's login, lives in a temporary directory outside the run directory. Only its `mcp.json` and `settings.json` are kept with the trial.
  - Preflight runs a one-turn init check per arm and checks the declared tools, the skill and the model that answered. Linux and macOS both run these arms. `check_run_evidence.py` requires `driver.log` for them, as it does for the `cc-*` arms.

Size: over the production-line target because the host adapter (event translation, process control, preflight) is a new module like `codex_native.py`; the `run_bench.py` changes are wiring.

## Related work

Refs CUA-3543

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: new `--arms` choices only. A run without `pi-*` arms takes the same paths as before. The Codex and Claude Code source-arm lookups now share one `SOURCE_ARM` table, with the same entries.
- Risk and rollback: bench harness only, no release-tracked package. Revert the PR to remove the arms.

title: fix(cua-driver): bound browser_dialog Page.enable retry by the dialog subscription deadline
body:
CUA-3439

`browser_dialog` retries the tab's `Page.enable` dialog subscription when the attach-time subscribe did not take. That retry used the full CDP call timeout (`CALL_TIMEOUT`, 20 s), while the attach-time subscribe in `engine.rs` uses the short `DIALOG_SUBSCRIPTION_TIMEOUT` (2 s). A renderer already blocked by an unseen dialog never answers `Page.enable`, so `browser_dialog` hung for the long deadline before refusing.

Change:
- `engine.rs`: expose `DIALOG_SUBSCRIPTION_TIMEOUT` to the crate.
- `tools.rs`: the `browser_dialog` re-subscribe calls `call_with_timeout(..., DIALOG_SUBSCRIPTION_TIMEOUT)`. The refusal and unregister behaviour on failure are unchanged.

Proof:
- New test `browser_dialog_resubscribe_uses_the_short_dialog_deadline`: the mock tab never answers `Page.enable`. `browser_dialog inspect` must return within two short deadlines (one for the attach subscribe, one for the retry) plus slack, record the retry, and refuse with `browser_action_unavailable`. Against the old `tools.rs` the test fails because it waits out the call timeout.
- The scoped repository checks: fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`, all targets) and the full test suite for `cua-driver-core`.

title: perf(spaces): a new home is warm as soon as the person's agents are prepared
body:
A new home is cold for minutes after an update because the warm member waits for every app and a filesystem save, and the saved filesystem is thrown away too easily. This makes a home warm as soon as the person's own agents are prepared.

Root cause of the cold first message (owner log): the shape hash changed with the new build, so there was no saved filesystem: prepare of all 8 harnesses took 125 s, then the save 102 s, and the member was claimable only 241 s after launch. Separately the cache budget (8.2 GiB) is smaller than base image plus the full filesystem (7.5 GiB), so budget eviction removed it again minutes after it was saved.

- The member waits only for the first apps (Claude Code, then the agents and recent runs from persistent/agents.json and phases.jsonl, at most 3). It never waits for a save.
- The filesystem with every app is built beside the pool by a member nobody can claim (first layer saved at once, then the rest), because saving a member that can be claimed would capture a claim's data.
- The saved filesystem is keyed by backend, image, platform and the apps (at their pinned versions), in an index next to the pool records. A network preset, size or build change no longer discards it, and a superset is reused. An app outside the saved set installs in the Space as before.
- The newest two prepared filesystems stay under a small cache budget (cua-disk).
- Logs: `member ready ... claimable_after_start_s`, `prepared filesystem reused (tag, covers, wanted)`, `no prepared filesystem to reuse (reason)`, `the prepared filesystem has every app`.

Measured in the real Local app (4 CPU, 6 GiB VM), claude-code home:
- No saved filesystem at all: member claimable 21 s after it starts (boot 2 s, prepare 19 s), against 241 s. First layer saved at +69 s, all 8 apps at +270 s, in the background.
- Member from the first layer: ready in 2.6 s. After a relaunch, a refill from the full filesystem: ready in 2.4 s (`covers=8 wanted=8`), no preparing; the GC kept it at 60 s.
- A home 60 s after relaunch: delivered 430 ms, first_token 4.5 s.

Tests: pool unit tests (first-layer claimability and background build, reuse under another network preset and size, pin mismatch re-prepares, superset reuse), ordering of the first apps, GC keeps the newest prepared images. Based on #6632 (same file); base it on main once that merges.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse clicks fast while a detached session's dialog blocks the tab
body:
CUA-3438. Follow-up to #6514 (CUA-3307), now merged; this PR targets `main`.

#6514 drops a tab's dialog record when the session that saw the dialog open gets a `Target.detachedFromTarget`. If something outside the driver detaches that session while the dialog is still showing, the page stays blocked but the driver has no record. `browser_click` then stops refusing as dialog-present, and its frame revalidation waits out the 20 s call timeout.

**Chromium behaviour** (checked against the installed Chrome with a scripted CDP probe):
- Once the session that saw `javascriptDialogOpening` detaches, every newer session gets `-32602 No dialog is showing` from `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog`. Its `Page.enable` and `Runtime.evaluate` never reply.
- A navigation started from another session closes the dialog and sends `Page.javascriptDialogClosed` to the session that is waiting on `Page.enable`, and then `Page.enable` replies.

**Change** (`cua-driver-core` browser module)
- CDP reader: on `Target.detachedFromTarget`, keep the dialog record and mark it `detached` instead of dropping it. The session mapping is still dropped, so the next attach subscribes a fresh session, and a close event on that session clears the record.
- `browser_click`: the existing dialog-present refusal now covers a detached dialog. It fails fast and says the driver cannot resolve the dialog. The dialog block carries `resolvable: false`.
- `browser_dialog`: inspect reports `resolvable`. Accept or dismiss on a detached dialog refuses with the same detail and does not send `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog`. That call would only return `No dialog is showing`, and #6514 would then clear a record for a page that is still blocked.
- Tab attach: a detached record no longer skips the dialog subscription. If the new session's bounded `Page.enable` replies, the renderer is no longer blocked, so the stale record is cleared (generation-checked). This covers a dialog that closed while no session was listening.

**Tests**
- `cdp_ws::tests::a_detached_dialog_session_marks_its_dialog_unresolvable` (replaces `a_detached_dialog_session_drops_its_dialog_record`): the record survives the detach as `detached`, and a new subscriber's close event clears it.
- `v2_tests::a_dialog_whose_session_detached_refuses_clicks_without_waiting`: after the detach, a coordinate click refuses with `resolvable: false` well inside the call timeout and dispatches no input. Inspect reports `resolvable: false`, and dismiss refuses without calling Chromium. Fails without the reader change.
- `v2_tests::a_detached_dialog_that_closed_unseen_stops_blocking_clicks`: when the new session's `Page.enable` answers, the click dispatches. Fails without the attach-time clear.

title: fix(cua-driver): move the skill version under metadata.version
body:
## Why

The cua-driver skill fails Agent Skills validation because `version` is a top-level frontmatter field. Moving it under `metadata` fixes validation, but the bundled copy in `libs/cua` and the `cua agents` skill reader also have to follow. Otherwise the skill would report the cua package version in place of its own.

Salvaged from #6615. The first commit is Joseph Mearman's, cherry-picked with his authorship kept.

Fixes #6614

## What changed

- The canonical cua-driver SKILL.md keeps its version as `metadata.version`. The release-please extra file, release version validation, the ClawHub workflow and the release-channel test now read it there.
- The bundled copy `libs/cua/skills/cua-driver/SKILL.md` moves its version the same way. `cua-agent-setup`'s `front_matter` now reads `metadata.version` and ignores a top-level or more deeply nested `version`.
- The cua-driver MCP frontmatter test now asserts `metadata.version`. It failed on #6615's head.

## Scope

Covers the version field and its readers. It does not resync the rest of the bundled cua-driver skill. That copy already differs from the canonical docs on main, and `scripts/sync-skills.sh --check` fails there before this change too. Resyncing it belongs in its own PR.

## Blast Radius

Release automation for cua-driver (release-please, version validation, ClawHub publish) and `cua agents` skill listing. release-please's generic updater matches the `x-release-please-version` marker, not the indentation, and the scoped checks confirm it bumps the indented line. The MCP `skill://cua-driver` frontmatter now shows the version under `metadata`. No consumer in this repo reads the top-level field.

## Verification

- `cua-agent-setup` and `cua-driver-core` fmt, clippy and tests pass. A new test that the bundled cua-driver skill reports its own version fails against main's bundled copy and passes here.
- The driver release version validation, release-channel and release-wiring tests pass, and `agentskills validate` passes on both skill copies.

title: ci(cua-spaces): rebuild an existing tag from main (rebuild_tag dispatch)
body:
## What

Adds the driver's rebuild-existing-tag path (#6606, #6613) to `cd-cua-spaces.yml`, so `cua-spaces-v0.21.0` can ship without moving or deleting the tag. Its tag-push run died in `refuse-beta` (fixed by #6635) and never published.

Users: nothing changes yet. Latest and cua.ai/download still serve 0.20.0 until the rebuild publishes 0.21.0.

## How

- New dispatch inputs `rebuild_tag` and `rebuild_sha`. Run from main.
- The first job validates the request: dispatch from main, stable `cua-spaces-vX.Y.Z` tag, full SHA equal to what the tag resolves to, **refuses if the release is already published** (never duplicates), and refuses `electron_dry_run`, `sparkle_electron`, `skip_staging_gate` and `platforms`, so every gate behaves as on a tag push.
- `RELEASE_REF`, `RELEASE_REF_NAME`, `RELEASE_SHA` replace `GITHUB_REF`, `GITHUB_REF_NAME` and `GITHUB_SHA` in shell steps. Build and verify jobs check out `rebuild_sha`; publishing and gate tooling stay on main.
- The "source SHA must equal github.sha" equivalents: the staging smoke request and gate and the promote check use `RELEASE_SHA`, the tagged commit. The Spaces workflow has no hosted-E2E SHA check like the driver's, so no reusable-workflow flag was needed.
- Signing, notarization (`REQUIRE_SIGNING`), the existing-draft-or-create step, staging gate, verify-release, installer-manifest, site-follows-release and the staged rollout all key on the same tag-run condition.
- Sigstore: the keyless identity of a rebuild is the workflow at `refs/heads/main`, not the tag. `install.sh` and `install.ps1` now accept that identity for the app next to the tag identity (exact match, no regexp; the CLI is unchanged). Without this, installs with cosign present would fail on a rebuilt release.

## Tests

`test_cua_spaces_rebuild_wiring.py` (contract), an installer test for the main identity and its refusal of any other, and updated existing wiring assertions. `bin/ci --quick --fix` is clean.

## Dispatch

```
gh workflow run cd-cua-spaces.yml -R trycua/cua --ref main -f rebuild_tag=cua-spaces-v0.21.0 -f rebuild_sha=66d5edd6ac84750d1172dede4c21f37a828145ba
```

title: fix(cua-spaces): retire interrupted-create journals whose sandbox is gone
body:
CUA-3505

After a daemon restart, `recover_interrupted_creates` reports every local create whose recovery failed as "local attempt retained" and keeps its journal in `home/creating/`, so that the sandbox can be inspected. Once that sandbox is gone (removed by hand, or never started because the process died while resolving the image), nothing ever removed the journal. Every restart reported the same records again, and chaos runs left dozens.

Recovery now retires such a journal with `RecoveryOutcome::NothingLeft` (its stale `.cancel` marker goes with it). This happens only when all of the following hold:

- nothing is registered under its id,
- no sandbox state file records the name,
- the local runtime answers `NotFound` (new `Sandboxes::local_name_gone`).

If any of these fails, including an engine that is down, an unconfigured local runtime, or a borrowed sandbox that still exists, the journal stays as it did before. Nothing is deleted except the journal. The change keeps the "retain evidence, no speculative cleanup" rule from a597517d8: a journal is removed only after the runtime confirms there is nothing left to inspect.

The issue is filed under cua-compat, but the journals and the recovery live in cua-spaces (`creating.rs`, `Spaces::recover_interrupted_creates`). cua-compat has no code that writes `home/creating`.

Tests:
- `tests/providers.rs` `an_interrupted_local_create_is_registered_or_preserved`: the "early" journal (no sandbox was ever started) is now retired as `NothingLeft`. "cut", where the runtime holds an unrecorded instance, is still retained.
- `tests/cancel.rs` `a_cancel_after_a_restart_undoes_the_journal`: after a retained, cancel-marked sandbox is removed, the next recovery retires its journal and marker. The borrowed one, whose sandbox still exists, stays retained, and no sandbox gets deleted.

risk: standard

follow-ups:
- `mesh::tests::a_space_on_a_mesh_the_relay_turned_off_reconnects` in cua-spaces is flaky ("the cut is explained" panic, 1 of 3 runs alone). It is unrelated to this change.
- A journal whose sandbox still exists is still reported on every restart. Getting rid of those needs an explicit cleanup verb, or a policy on how long retained attempts are kept.

title: ci(cua-driver): fail fast and retry apt in standalone browser E2E
body:
The 0.39.0 rebuild (run 42145808031) was cancelled: the Linux X11 standalone browser E2E job hit its 60 min timeout because the apt install step hung for 53 min. Rebuild dispatches already have their own concurrency key (#6613), so that was not the cause.

Adds apt retries and timeouts plus a 12 min step timeout so a bad mirror fails fast instead of eating the job budget.

Plain words: release gates stop failing on a flaky package mirror.

title: fix(cua-driver): lock the daemon socket so a racing launch cannot orphan a daemon
body:
## Why
Two `cua-driver serve` launches on one socket could both pass the liveness probe. The second unlinked the first's socket and bound its own, so the first kept running unreachable, and on exit it deleted the live daemon's pid file. Fixes CUA-3432.

## What changed
- The standalone Unix daemon takes an exclusive non-blocking lock on `<socket>.lock` before it clears a stale socket, and holds it for the life of `run_serve`. The kernel releases it on exit or crash.
- A launch that loses the race exits with the existing "already running … Run `cua-driver stop` first." message.
- Unit test: a second claim fails while the first is held, the bound socket survives, and the claim succeeds once the first is dropped.

## Scope
Covers standalone daemons on macOS and Linux. Embedded mode keeps its host-owned no-unlink rule and takes no lock. Windows named pipes are unchanged. The `.lock` file stays behind after exit on purpose, since an unheld lock file is harmless.

## Blast Radius
Every standalone `serve` start goes through the new lock. A lone launch works as before, and a stale socket left by a crashed daemon is still cleared, because a dead process holds no lock.

## Verification
- Repro script launching two `serve` processes on one socket at once: before the fix, both stayed alive and the pid file named only one of them. After it, 3 of 3 runs left one live daemon, and the other exited with "already running". `status` reported the survivor's pid and `stop` removed the socket and pid file.
- The scoped repository checks: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo test -p cua-driver` pass.
- macOS Lume focused cell `macos-wkwebview-left-click-ax-background-typed-sdk` passed at the head.

title: fix(cua-driver): cover the desktop lane for invoke_menu and type_text_chars on Linux
body:
CUA-3585

## Plan

https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6638 put `invoke_menu` and `type_text_chars` on the process-wide desktop lane, but the only proof was a unit test of `is_physical_desktop_action`. This adds the Linux desktop E2E for that contract to the existing GTK3 native harness, which the canonical Linux lane already runs (`scripts/ci/linux/run-rust-e2e.sh`, native suite, `harness_gtk3_test -- --ignored`).

- Two cells: `linux-gtk3-invoke-menu-desktop-lane-ax-foreground` and `linux-gtk3-type-text-chars-desktop-lane-ax-foreground`.
- A second MCP client on the same daemon starts a 3 s foreground drag across the slider. Once a read-only snapshot shows the slider moving, with more than half the drag left, the first client sends `invoke_menu` (`Window > Arrange > Left`) or `type_text_chars` into `txt-input`.
- The GTK3 fixture counts the slider's button-1 press and release and records `effect_during_drag=<menu|text>` when the menu activation or entry change lands while the button is held. The cells require the tool's effect, exactly one press and release, `effect_during_drag=none`, and a drag that reached its end.
- No production code changes.

## Proof

- With this diff, X11 (Xvfb, openbox, picom, AT-SPI) passes both new cells, and the native suite of the canonical runner passes `harness_gtk3_test` 39/39. `cua-e2e-report --require-video` over those results reports both new rows Delivered / Pass with playable recordings.
- Mutation check: removing `invoke_menu` from `is_physical_desktop_action` fails the invoke_menu cell. Removing `type_text`, the name dispatch resolves `type_text_chars` to, fails the type_text_chars cell. Both failures say "took effect while the drag held the slider".
- The capture suite, the other GTK3 fixture user, passes capture-contract, desktop-scope and x11-unpublished-pid.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check` and clippy for `cua-driver-e2e --test harness_gtk3_test` report nothing in the touched file.
- Not run: native Wayland/Sway (no compositor on the host), the GTK4 cells (no GTK4 PyGObject on the host), perception-capture-loop (no arm64 archive published), the macOS and Windows lanes. `cargo clippy -p platform-linux -- -D warnings` fails on main already, with five lints this diff does not touch.

The oracle assumes the second request reaches the daemon within the 1.5 s of drag still left when it is sent. A stall longer than that would let a lane regression pass that run, but it cannot fail a correct driver.
