title: fix(cua-driver): keep the Windows daemon pid file owned by the running daemon
body:
## Why
A standalone Windows daemon creates its named pipe without reserving the name, so a second `cua-driver serve` that passes the liveness probe at the same moment serves beside the first. Both write the shared pid file, and whichever exits first deletes it while the other is still running. This is the Windows half of the ownership rule from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6652. Fixes CUA-3599.

## What changed
- A daemon removes its pid file on exit only while the file still holds its own pid. This applies on Unix and Windows.
- A standalone Windows daemon holds an exclusive lock for its pipe name from before the pid write until after cleanup. A launch that loses the race exits with the existing "already running … Run `cua-driver stop` first." message. The lock file is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cua-driver-pipe-locks\<sha256 of the uppercased pipe name>.lock`, so case variants of one name share a lock and long names still fit.
- Unit tests: a second claim fails while the first is held, a waiting claim succeeds once the holder releases, and exit keeps a pid file that names another process.

## Scope
Covers standalone Windows daemons and pid-file removal on every platform. Embedded Windows daemons already reserve their host-chosen pipe name with `first_pipe_instance(true)`, so they take no lock. The Unix socket lock stays in #6652, and the two diffs merge cleanly. One gap remains: when daemons on different sockets share a pid file, the read-then-remove step can still race with a write from the other daemon. Main deleted that file unconditionally, so the window is narrower than before and is left for a follow-up.

## Tradeoffs
I kept the standalone pipe on `first_pipe_instance(false)` instead of reserving the name the way embedded mode does. `stop` returns once the listening instance is gone, and connected instances can keep the name alive a little longer, so a reserving relaunch right after `stop` would fail. The lock waits up to 2 s for a stopping daemon instead.

## Blast Radius
Every standalone Windows `serve` start now takes the lock. A lone launch behaves as before. A crashed daemon holds no lock, because the OS releases it with the handle. On Unix the only change is the pid-file ownership check on exit.

## Verification
- Repro on macOS with two daemons on different sockets sharing one pid file, then stopping the first. On main the pid file was gone and `status` for the live daemon reported `pid: unknown (no pid file)`. On this branch the file still held the live daemon's pid, `status` reported it, and the file was removed when that daemon stopped.
- The scoped repository checks on macOS pass: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, the `serve::` unit tests and `status_pid_file_cli_test`.
- Windows build and tests did not run here, so the Windows CI lane is the first compile of the Windows path.

title: fix(cua-driver-bench): Windows guard treats a driver's own helper shell like macOS (disclosed rule)
body:
Follow-up to #6633 (Windows multi-app tasks). Refs CUA-3563.

**What changes for users:** the Windows GUI-only guard now treats setups the same way the macOS guard does. A shell that a driver's own binary starts for itself no longer ends the trial. The rule is stated in METHOD.md, so it is a disclosed scoring rule, not a silent change.

**The rule, the same for every setup.** `launch/windows_session.py --tool-exe <exe>` (repeatable). A shell or script host whose parent process is one of these binaries is logged in the row as `gui_only.tool_helpers`, and it is not a violation. The four Windows setups pass their own binaries:
- `cua-driver.exe`
- `agent-desktop-win32-x64.exe`
- `windows-harness.exe`
- `codex-computer-use.exe`

Interpreters that run code the agent supplied (`python.exe` for a harness's `exec`, `node.exe` for a JavaScript REPL) are never on the list, so a shell the agent starts that way still counts.

**Why.** The macOS guard flags only named side-door apps ("a process named Script Editor, Automator, iTerm2 or Shortcuts exists") and tool inputs that contain code that runs outside the GUI. A driver's own helper processes were never violations there. On Windows, Cua Driver starts PowerShell in `get_browser_state` / `browser_prepare` to read browser processes; this was reproduced, and the parent process is `cua-driver.exe`. The stricter Windows guard stopped 7 of its 10 CDB-G04 trials for that, even though no tool input asked for a shell. Those trials were rerun with the same seeds.

**Effect on earlier results, checked for all four setups.** Every Windows row with a process violation was audited: run1 browser-use MB-11 r0/r2/r3 and every browser-use multi-app violation. In each case the shell followed a tool input in which the agent itself asked for PowerShell or a subprocess (`subprocess.run(["powershell", ...])`, `win.script(...)`), so its parent is an interpreter and the verdict is unchanged. Codex computer use and agent-desktop had no process violations.

Also in this PR:
- **METHOD.md:** the Windows release scope now covers all ten tasks, with app versions and the Windows driver list including Codex computer use.
- **README:**
  - The approval names Codex computer use uses on Windows. LibreOffice is `soffice.bin`; without it on the allowlist, every Calc approval is declined.
  - The `--tool-exe` note in the Windows guard description.

Tests: `pytest tests probes/tests swift/tests` (402 passed, plus a new unit test for the helper rule), `tools/taskset.py check` ok.

title: ci(cua-driver-bench): stop Linux headless contracts job timing out on slow apt mirror
body:
The `Linux headless desktop contracts (no model)` job was cancelled at its 10 min `timeout-minutes` on several recent PRs, which turned `ci-gate` red until a manual rerun. The cancelled attempts were all stuck in `Install desktop dependencies`: the Azure Ubuntu mirror was throttled and `apt-get` fetched small packages at one every 5-60 s. The tests take about 2.5 min, and every rerun passed.

Changes in `.github/workflows/ci-cua-driver-bench.yml`:
- Job timeout 10 -> 25 min.
- The apt install gets its own 15 min step cap, `Acquire::Retries` and HTTP timeouts, and up to 3 attempts of 5 min each, so a stalled download is aborted and retried.
- The pytest step gets an 8 min cap, so a real hang fails fast and names its step.

For users: CI on bench PRs no longer goes red from mirror slowness, so no manual rerun is needed.

Not merged, awaiting review.

title: fix(cua-driver): find a macOS app by any name it ships, without guessing
body:
## Why

`launch_app` by name only found an exact `<name>.app` directly inside six folders, although its schema takes the display name. @AlexFalher's https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6560 matches every name a bundle ships (file name, `CFBundleDisplayName`, `CFBundleName` and their localizations), one folder down included. This PR keeps that commit as authored and fixes four defects review found at 7bbb033f.

Salvaged from #6560. Linear: CUA-3539.

## What changed

- **Copies of one bundle id:** `apps/names.rs` no longer merges them into the first path with every copy's names. Each copy stays a candidate (`NamedApp.id`), and a top tie among copies of one id goes to the first copy. A name only a second install ships now launches that install.
- **No pre-ranking guess:** `locate_by_name` dropped the `<name>.app` fast path and the Finder special case. It takes an absolute `.app` path, then a bundle id LaunchServices knows, then ranks all names (`locate_in`). A file name another app also displays is refused as `APP_NAME_AMBIGUOUS`.
- **Base and Finder:** `Base` localizations count as unlocalized names. `/System/Library/CoreServices/Finder.app` is scanned as a single-bundle root (the rest of CoreServices is agents and helpers). The scan visits each bundle path once, because `/Applications/Utilities` is both a root and one folder down.
- **No second resolution:** `launch_located` / `launch_with_urls_located` take the resolved `AppLocator`. The tool no longer turns it into a string and looks it up again, so a bundle-id locator cannot turn into a filename match.

## Scope

macOS name lookup for `launch_app` only. Windows and Linux lookup are unchanged. `list_apps` still does not list apps one folder down.

## Blast Radius

Name-based `launch_app` on macOS. Bundle ids, absolute paths and exact file names resolve as before, unless another app displays the same name, which is now refused. Each name lookup scans the roots and reads bundle plists, where before the scan ran only on a miss.

## Verification

- New unit tests for each finding. The `names.rs` tests fail on 7bbb033f and pass here. The scoped repository checks (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cua-driver-core` and `platform-macos` lib tests) pass.
- `launch_app` over MCP on macOS 26 with a release build: `Chess`, `Échecs` (composed and decomposed), `com.apple.Chess`, `Calculator.app`, `Finder` and an absolute bundle path launch the expected bundle id. `Ma` returns `APP_NAME_AMBIGUOUS` with suggestions, and `ess` returns `APP_NOT_INSTALLED` with suggestions.

Size: the name scan and ranking are one new feature from #6560 that can't land in parts, so production lines exceed the add<=200 target.

title: fix(cua-driver): clear Rust 1.97 clippy lints in platform-linux
body:
## Why
On main, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver -- -D warnings` fails on five Rust 1.97 lints in `platform-linux`. CUA-3603

## What changed
- `get_window_state`: `max_elements` is a plain `usize`. It used to be wrapped in `Some` and unwrapped again. The AT-SPI walker still receives `Some(max_elements)`, and the view key gets the same value.
- `input`: X11 button press and release events go to `send_event` by value. Neither event is used after the call.
- `send_drag_xtest_desktop_with_modifiers` and `wayland::drag_desktop` get `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`, like the existing `libei_drag` allowance.

## Scope
Only the five lints named in CUA-3603. Behavior does not change. `--all-targets` still reports four lints in test code (`launch_app.rs`, `press_key.rs`, `wayland/hyprland.rs`, and an unused import in an `input/mod.rs` test module). They are left for a follow-up.

## Blast Radius
Linux driver only. Changing `max_elements` and passing the events by value does not change any value the code sees. The attributes change nothing at runtime.

## Verification
The scoped repository checks: `cargo clippy -p cua-driver -- -D warnings` failed on main with these five errors and passes on this branch. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` pass. The verify-cua-driver X11 lane passes.

title: fix(cua-driver): press a shortcut's key where the keyboard layout types it on macOS
body:
## Why

On a non-US Mac, every macOS chord path pressed letters, digits and symbols at fixed US key positions, so on AZERTY `hotkey cmd+a` pressed the key that types `q` and quit the app. This salvages https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6556 by @AlexFalher, which resolves a chord's key from the current layout with `UCKeyTranslate`. It also fixes one regression that change would have caused. Apple Screen Sharing forwards key positions to a guest whose layout the host cannot read, so reading the host layout there would press the AZERTY A key (US Q) for `cmd+a` on a US guest.

Refs CUA-3604. Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6556. The contributor's commit and authorship are kept as is.

## What changed

- The contributor's commit (`2c13ba9a8`): `chord_key_code` and `current_layout` in `platform-macos/src/input/keyboard.rs` press a single printable character on the key that types it with the chord's modifiers held: the Command layer, the Control layer or the plain layer. Named keys, and characters the layer has no key for, keep the US position.
- Ours: every chord path now resolves its key through `target_key_code(pid)`, which keeps US positions when the target is Screen Sharing. That matches the existing Screen Sharing text path (`physical_key_for_char`). `press_key_bare_global` takes the target pid, and desktop-scope `press_key_global` uses the frontmost pid. `layout_key_code` is deleted so no path can skip the rule.

## Scope

macOS chord key selection only: `press_key`, `hotkey`, their no-auth, global and bare-global variants. Typed text, the viewer keystroke path, Windows and Linux are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

US-layout hosts behave as before. On non-US hosts, chords to ordinary apps land on the layout's key. Chords to Screen Sharing keep the pre-change US positions, which assumes a US guest, the same assumption its text path already makes. Clients that remap keys for the layout themselves would now place them twice.

Size: over the net production budget because the layout reader (`UCKeyTranslate` FFI over three modifier layers) is one indivisible unit from the contributor's change.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks on `platform-macos`: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --lib` pass, plus the ignored host-layout test. The new `screen_sharing_chords_keep_us_positions` test pins the US position for Screen Sharing.
- macOS Lume full matrix at the head: results are in the `verified` comment.
- Not run: a live Screen Sharing cross-layout repro, since this host was at its two-VM limit. Windows and Linux CI were not run locally.

title: bench: park the real pointer before every trial (Amendment 24)
body:
Part of the Cua Driver Bench v2 protocol work (`libs/cua-driver-bench`).

## What changed for users
A pointer left resting over BenchLab by an earlier task could make macOS activate BenchLab when it showed a background sheet, which changed the interruption (IR) results under every tool. The harness now puts the real pointer at a fixed point before each trial, so every setup starts from the same state.

## Change
- Before every trial, move the real pointer to (1000, 12), outside every registered window frame (user window, BenchLab, witness) and every task-pack window. Read the position back and record it in the trial row as `pointer_parked`. A park that does not land within 3 px fails the trial setup (a harness error, never scored).
- macOS: through the recorder daemon. Linux X11: `xdotool`. Hyprland and Windows session launchers: dispatcher / `SetCursorPos`, with the same read-back check. A platform with no supported way raises instead of pretending.
- `--park-pointer` is now on by default (`--no-park-pointer` turns it off).
- `METHOD.md`: dated Amendment 24 with the disclosure sentence.

## Tests
- Park point is outside every registered frame and every window in the task pack launch descriptors.
- Park record accepts a landed read-back and rejects a missed or missing one.
- `run_bench.park_pointer` returns the record on success and raises on a miss or on an unsupported platform.
- Existing suite: 351 passed, 52 skipped.

Not exercised on live Hyprland or Windows desktops here; there a failed park is visible as a harness error rather than a silent skip.

title: fix(installers): accept a rebuilt Cua Spaces release only with a signed claim for its tag
body:
Narrows the trust widened in #6649. Before this, the installers accepted any build signed by `cd-cua-spaces.yml@refs/heads/main`. Now a rebuilt Cua Spaces release verifies only with a signed claim that names the tag being installed.

**What changes for users:** nothing for normal releases (tag identity, unchanged). A rebuilt release still installs, but only if its run signed a tag claim.

## Why a claim

A Sigstore certificate for a `workflow_dispatch` from main carries the workflow ref (`refs/heads/main`), the main commit SHA and the trigger. The tag being rebuilt is only a dispatch input, so no certificate field or cosign flag can encode it. `--certificate-github-workflow-ref/-trigger/-sha` alone would still pass any main-branch dispatch.

So the rebuild run also signs `rebuild-claim.txt`: a `tag cua-spaces-vX.Y.Z` line and the sha256 of every signed asset, with its own bundle, uploaded next to the assets (kept out of the manifest). The claim comes from a run that passed the `rebuild_tag` guard (tag must resolve to `rebuild_sha`, release unpublished).

## Installer check (install.sh, install.ps1)

For the app, accept either:
1. the tag identity (`...@refs/tags/cua-spaces-v<version>`), as before; or
2. the main identity, verified with `--certificate-github-workflow-repository`, `--certificate-github-workflow-ref refs/heads/main` and `--certificate-github-workflow-trigger workflow_dispatch`, plus a claim that verifies under the same pins, names `cua-spaces-v<version>` and lists this file's sha256 under its name.

A missing claim, a claim for another tag, or a claim without the artifact's hash fails with "cosign signature check failed". The CLI identity is unchanged.

## Tests

- `scripts/install/tests/run.sh`: 144 pass (new: no claim aborts, claim accepted with the pinned flags, other-tag claim aborts, wrong-sha claim aborts).
- Pester: added tests (identity helpers, claim verification). Pester/pwsh is not installed here, so they were NOT run locally; CI is the first run.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix`: green.
- Not tested against real signatures: no 0.21.0 rebuild run or signatures exist yet.

## Ordering for the 0.21.0 rebuild

The claim is produced by the workflow in this PR. The 0.21.0 dispatch must run from a main that includes this PR. A rebuild dispatched from the current main signs no claim, and installers with cosign installed would reject it. I did not touch the in-flight release. After the run, verify with real bundles: `cosign verify-blob` on the claim and an asset using the flags above.

title: fix(cua-driver): find localized Chrome setup controls without English names
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `browser_prepare` with `strategy.kind = existing_profile` refuses on a non-English Chrome before it does anything. Run on main with Chrome's UI language set to zh-Hans, the hosted macOS browser lane fails like this:

  ```
  refused (browser_wrong_target_refused): the approved Google Chrome window has no exact New Tab button
  ```

  Setup finds three native controls by their English accessible names: `New Tab`, `Close` and `Address and search bar`. Chrome 156 in zh-Hans names them `新标签页`, `关闭` and `地址和搜索栏`. The `chrome://inspect` page stays English, and #4590 covers the localized consent sheet, so these three controls are what still stops setup.
- What changed: the English match stays and is tried first. When it finds nothing, the control is identified by structure, with no translation table. Every count other than exactly one still refuses.
  - **New tab:** the one native pressable `AXButton` outside every tab that spans the topmost row of native tabs (their top and height). Horizontal position is not used: Chrome overlaps the control with the last tab. The topmost row matters because Translate's bubble, which a non-English Chrome opens on English pages, has its own native tabs below the toolbar.
  - **The new tab's close control (cleanup):** the one native pressable button inside the tab that the existing before/after diff proved new.
  - **Address field:** the window's one native *pressable* text field, the field `unique_omnibox` presses. Chrome also exposes an unnamed native text field that cannot be pressed. The five setup-URL checks now share this identity instead of repeating the English-label predicate, so a find bar holding the setup URL never counts as the address field, in any language.

## Related work

Refs #3139

#4393 by @AidenNovak proposed the same structural approach. Its author closed it without review, noting that it still needed an E2E run on a non-English Chrome. This PR carries that design forward with that E2E evidence, plus the two cases the E2E run exposed: the Translate bubble and the unpressable native field. The commit credits @AidenNovak as co-author. #5304 / #5343 changed the same file (the initial native walk) and do not overlap with these lines.

RFC: not needed. There is no public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol or permission change.

## Compatibility and risk

- Impact: macOS only. Existing-profile setup now works on a localized Chrome instead of refusing. An English Chrome matches the English names first, exactly as before. The one change for English is that the address-field checks are stricter: an extra native field holding the setup URL no longer counts. Windows and Linux are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: the fallbacks run only when no English name matches, and each one refuses unless exactly one candidate fits. A layout the rules do not expect, such as vertical tabs, refuses with the existing codes. To roll back, revert the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `bin/ci` at this commit runs 9 affected checks (rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `platform-macos` unit tests, SPDX, image refs, generated reference, UniFFI bindings), and all 9 pass. `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib -- browser::` passes 95 tests.
  - Four new tests fail on main (6e7e939d5) and pass here: `new_tab_button_selects_the_localized_control_spanning_the_tab_strip` (a zh-Hans tab strip with frames measured on Chrome 156 / macOS 26.6), `new_tab_cleanup_selects_the_one_localized_button_inside_the_new_tab`, `localized_omnibox_is_the_one_native_text_field` and `a_find_bar_holding_the_setup_url_is_not_the_address_field`.
  - The other new tests pin the guards. I removed each guard in turn, and each removal fails a test:
    - pressable-only counting → `a_hidden_unpressable_native_field_leaves_the_localized_address_field`
    - uniqueness of the address field → `a_find_bar_holding_the_setup_url_is_not_the_address_field`
    - topmost tab row → `structural_new_tab_button_ignores_a_tabbed_bubble_below_the_strip`
    - outside-a-tab → `structural_new_tab_button_requires_every_condition`
- Platform evidence: hosted macOS lane (`scripts/ci/macos/run-hosted-rust-e2e.sh`, `macos-26`, Chrome 156) on a fork, with Chrome's UI language set per row via `defaults write com.google.Chrome AppleLanguages`:

  | Source | Cases | Chrome UI zh-Hans | Chrome UI en |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | main 6e7e939d5 | existing-profile cases | setup refused: `no exact New Tab button` | pass |
  | this PR c4e5aeca3 | full standalone lane, Chrome + Edge | every case passes except `native_omnibox_select_all` (test-side English lookup, see Known gaps) | 40/40 pass (38 delivered, 2 expected refusals) |

  Runs: main <https://github.com/YiTaiiiiii/cua/actions/runs/42216932418>, this PR <https://github.com/YiTaiiiiii/cua/actions/runs/42216937134> (evidence, including per-case recordings, is attached to each run).

  On an earlier revision, the lane found two cases that the unit tests had missed. Setup's cleanup refused while Translate's bubble was open, and the unpressable native field kept the address field from being unique. Both are fixed above and covered by tests.
- Review: an independent review with Codex (GPT-6 Astra, `gpt-6.1-sol`) found that the first revision let a find bar stand in for the address field. That is fixed and tested here.
- Known gaps:
  - Only Google Chrome was run localized (zh-Hans). Edge uses the same rules and ran in English.
  - Other locales, including RTL, were not run. No rule uses horizontal position.
  - Vertical tabs and tab groups were not tested. The fallback refuses rather than guesses.
  - `standalone_browser_native_omnibox_select_all` fails on a zh-Hans Chrome on main as well, because the test itself looks for `Address and search bar` (`native_omnibox` in the E2E file). This PR leaves the test unchanged.
  - If a new tab were pinned between the press and the read, its close control would be hidden. If that tab also showed a mute toggle, cleanup would press the mute toggle instead. A tab that was not closed leaves no other effect.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. (N/A: releasing `fix`.)
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`) (bin/ci passed at c4e5aeca3: 9 checks; signing off needs write access to trycua/cua)

title: fix(ci): publish Cua Driver SDKs when post-publish bookkeeping fails
body:
Cua Driver 0.39.0 shipped without its Python and npm SDK packages.

Cause: the SDK workflow only runs when the CD run concludes success. The post-publish installer-bump job failed (it ran `gh pr checks` before checks registered, so every bump PR closed at once: #6676, #6679). That marked the CD run failed and skipped the SDKs.

Fix: the SDK workflow also runs on a failed CD run (the published-release check still gates publishing), and the bump job waits for checks to register.

User impact: SDK users can install 0.39.0 once the packages are published.

Anyone can provision an Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE desktop (`ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04` or plain Ubuntu) and rerun any of the ten tasks with either driver, with the same limits as the report.

title: fix(ci): don't fail the release-gate report when a post-merge push runs no lanes
body:
## What
The "E2E: Cua Driver release gate" run on main goes red on every push that touches no gated path, even though no lane ran.

## Cause
Since #6600, a push to main runs `decide`, which sets `run=false` when the pushed files touch no gated paths. Every lane is then `skipped`. The `nightly-report` job still ran (`mode == post-merge`) and counted each skipped lane as a failed lane, so it opened or updated the "release gate failing on main" issue (#6648) and exited 1. Runs 42220089490, 42222872653 and 42225476391 all show `decide: run=false ... push without gated paths`, all lanes skipped, and only `nightly report` failing. `E2E gate / result` already handles `run != true` and passed.

## Fix
`nightly-report` now runs only when `decide.outputs.run == 'true'`. A skipped push neither reports nor closes the tracking issue; real full runs behave as before.

## User effect
A red gate on main blocks cua-driver releases. Pushes with no gated change no longer turn it red falsely. Real lane failures still do.

Note: runs from earlier today with `run=true` (e.g. the 06:20Z schedule run) may be genuine lane failures; this PR does not touch those.

title: ci(cua-driver): queue auto-merge on installer bump PRs instead of closing them
body:
Release bump PRs were closed within a second, five times in a row (#6679 to #6685). The PRs were already created with the GitHub App token. The real cause: `gh pr checks --required` returns 'no checks reported' until the required checks register, so the job read that as a failed merge and closed the PR.

Fix: queue `gh pr merge --auto --squash` (repo auto-merge is on) and stop; never close on a missing-checks race. Same-repo PRs still need the local-ci sign-off before they merge.

User impact: the public installer version advances on its own after a driver release.

title: fix(cua-driver): re-read AXEnabled after foreground activation on macOS
body:
## Why

A foreground `double_click`, middle `click` or `type_text` with an element token into a background app skips the early `AXEnabled` read so activation can enable the control first (#6503). Nothing read it again afterwards. A control that stayed disabled was double-clicked or typed into, and no `element_disabled` refusal came back. Fixes CUA-3635.

## What changed

- Each of those foreground paths now re-reads `AXEnabled` after activation and right before input. A disabled control gets the structured `element_disabled` refusal. The new `element_disabled_error` in `tools/mod.rs` maps the error.
- Foreground AX `double_click` and unmodified foreground middle click never activated the app, so a read there would still come before activation. Both now front the exact window, act and restore, the same as `click`'s foreground AX path (`with_foreground_assist`).
- New macOS E2E cell `harness_appkit_disabled_control_is_refused_in_foreground_from_the_background`. The AppKit harness with a disabled checkbox sits behind the foreground sentinel. Foreground `double_click`, middle `click` and `type_text` must each return `element_disabled`, and the checkbox must stay unchanged.

## Scope

macOS only. It covers the three tools that skip the early read. `right_click` and `set_value` always read early. `click`'s main AX path already reads inside `perform_ax_click` after activation. No fixture control is enabled only while its app is active, so the activation-enables-it case is covered by the code path, not by an E2E cell.

## Tradeoffs

The cold verifier flagged that `with_foreground_assist` still runs its body when fronting is unavailable or focus never settles. A control that needs activation could then be refused. Not changed: that result is a refusal with no input sent, so it fails closed, and `click`'s existing foreground AX path behaves the same way.

## Blast Radius

Foreground element-token `double_click` and middle click now briefly front the target window and restore the previous app, as foreground `click` already does. Background delivery is unchanged.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test --lib` for `platform-macos` and `cua-driver-e2e` (675 unit tests pass).
- macOS Lume full matrix at 5fb094c07482f2c9444dfbeb6eacbc35b767bb0e: 179 delivered, 5 refused, 0 failed. The new cell `macos-appkit-disabled-control-foreground-ax-foreground` and the existing `macos-appkit-disabled-control-press-ax-background` both pass.

title: fix(spaces-macos): Cua Driver runs on every Mac, not only one set up for sharing (CUA-3638)
body:
Fixes CUA-3638 (release blocker for 0.21.1).

**For users:** Cua Driver now runs on every Mac with Cua Spaces. It no longer depends on the Mac being shared, signed in, or signed in to the account it was first set up with. When it can't start, the Cua Driver page says why.

## Root cause

In 0.21.0, Cua Driver for this Mac's coding agents ran only as a child of the host service, cua-spacesd (`libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd/src/main.rs:973`, `embedded_driver::spawn`). That service runs only while this Mac is set up for sharing under the signed-in account (`~/.cua/helper/service.json`). When there is no host service, there is no driver and no `~/.cua/run/`. That happens when:

- the person signs out, or signs in with another account (`pause_signed_out` uninstalls the service, `libs/cua/crates/cua-host/src/host.rs:2472`);
- the relay won't register this Mac yet ("add computers from a computer you already added, or with a pairing code" for a second Mac on an account);
- host setup fails for any other reason.

Set up then skipped starting the driver without a word (`WebUIBridge+Driver.swift`, `.needsSetUp`), so Test now said only "Cua Driver isn't running".

We reproduced this on a macOS test VM with the prod canary account and 0.21.0. The Mac was set up under another account, so sharing was paused. "Share With This Account" failed with the relay 403 above, and the page showed "Something went wrong".

## Fix

- **Cua Driver gets its own login item**: `com.trycua.spaces.driver`, which runs `CuaSpacesMac --driver-helper run` (`DriverLauncher`, `DriverSupervisor`).
  - The app registers and starts it at launch, and again on Set up, Repair and switching agents back on.
  - It keeps `cua-driver serve --embedded` running as its child, with the same arguments as the SDK's embedded host. Cua Spaces stays the responsible app, so the driver uses Cua Spaces' Accessibility and Screen Recording.
  - It restarts the driver with a backoff from 1 s up to 60 s, and clears a dead driver's socket the way the SDK does.
  - It follows the pause switch and start requests, restarts onto an update, and stops when the app is removed.
  - Sharing, sign-in and the signed-in account play no part.
- **No second driver from the host service.** It starts cua-spacesd with `CUA_SPACESD_EMBEDDED_DRIVER=0`. This needs no cua-spacesd release.
- **The real error is shown.** The login item writes `<CuaHome>/run/cua-driver.status.json` with its state and last error: the exit code plus the driver's last log line, from `<CuaHome>/logs/cua-driver.log`. The page and Test now show that reason, or that macOS is holding the item back in Login Items, instead of "set up this Mac".
- **Plain words for the relay refusal.** It now reads "Add this Mac from another computer" instead of "Something went wrong".
- `build-app.sh`, `build-release.sh`, `check-local-bundle.sh` and the VM check script know about the new login item. Local builds get `com.trycua.spaces.local.driver`.

## Tests

`DriverSupervisorTests` covers:

- a driver that won't start reports its exit code and last log line, and is retried;
- a missing binary is reported;
- a stand-in driver starts, is restarted after a kill, and stops;
- after a SIGKILL leaves its socket behind, the driver still comes back;
- stale-socket handling, the pause, the backoff, and the arguments and environment.

`EmbeddedDriverTests` covers the start steps and channel labels. `HostSetupFailureTests` covers the relay refusal. All of these pass locally (`scripts/test.sh --filter ...`).

## Verified on a macOS VM

Setup: the 0.21.0 bundle with this build's executable, ad hoc signed. The Mac was set up under another account with sharing paused, and Cua Spaces was then signed out.

- The driver login item starts at app launch and `~/.cua/run/` appears. The driver's parent is `CuaSpacesMac --driver-helper run`.
- The agent route answers. A SIGKILLed driver is back within seconds.
- The page shows "Working on this Mac. Last test passed just now."
- With the socket path broken, the page shows "Cua Driver didn't start: … is in the way (not a socket)". It recovers once the path is fixed.

title: fix(hyprland-plugin): keep background popups and drags off the user's seat
body:
## What changes for users

On Hyprland (Omarchy), when an agent works in a background app and that app opens a menu or a combo-box list, the user's keyboard no longer jumps to that popup. Before, the window the user was typing in silently lost keyboard focus until the popup closed, and whatever they typed meanwhile was lost. A drag-and-drop a background app starts is now cancelled instead of following the user's mouse and dropping on their next click.

## Root cause

Hyprland 0.56 and 0.57 ignore the seat and serial in `xdg_popup.grab` and `wl_data_device.start_drag`: every grabbing popup takes the user's seat (keyboard focus moves to the popup until it closes), and every drag runs on the user's pointer (ending it re-sends the user's keyboard focus). An accessibility action that presses a combo box in a background GTK app, or a click from one of the plugin's agent seats, is enough to trigger it. Hyprland's active window does not change, so window-level checks miss it; the user's window gets a `wl_keyboard.leave`.

The agent cursor overlay (`cua-agent-cursor` layer) was a coincidence, not the cause: it maps on the agent's first pointer action, which was the combo-box press. Mapping the overlay alone, repeatedly, never moved keyboard focus.

## Fix

The input build of the plugin hooks both requests (`CXDGShellProtocol::addOrStartGrab`, `CWLDataDeviceProtocol::initiateDrag`) and grants them only to the client that holds the user's keyboard or pointer focus, which every popup and drag the user starts does (clicked app, focused app, clicked panel). Anything else:

- popup: maps and works normally, without the grab;
- drag: the source gets `wl_data_source.cancelled` at once.

`cua:status` reports `user_seat_guard`, `popup_grabs_withheld` and `drags_withheld`. The decision is a small header (`src/user_seat_policy.hpp`) with its own unit test; the new files are added to the release bundle allowlist.

## Testing

- `ctest` (mock Hyprland, plugin hooks off): all 19 tests pass, including the new `user_seat_policy_test` and the lifetime test checking the guard is installed, reported and removed.
- Built against Hyprland 0.56.2 headers and loaded in an Omarchy edge VM:
  - Repro: a user typing continuously into one window while cua-driver presses a GTK combo box in a background window. Before: the user's window lost keyboard focus until the menu closed and keys were dropped (every run). After: no focus change, no keys lost; the combo box still opens and its item can be chosen.
  - Real-agent runs on the same task with continuous typing: no keys lost (see the PR comment for the run count).
  - A background drag in a GTK drag-and-drop list: before, it took the user's pointer and re-sent their keyboard focus; after, it is cancelled and the user is untouched.
- `packaging/release` unit tests: same 5 failures as on `main` (workflow-text assertions), none new.

Background drag-and-drop through the agent seats (reordering a GTK list from the background) still needs plugin support and is tracked separately.

Refs CUA-3582. Follow-up: CUA-3652.

title: fix(cua-driver): admit any native Wayland app to Hyprland background input
body:
## What changes for users

On Hyprland (Omarchy), cua-driver's background pointer and key input now works in ordinary apps, not only in two exact package versions. An agent can click, scroll, drag and type into a GTK 3, GTK 4 or Qt 6 app in the background, including its dialogs, while the user keeps working in another window. Before, every app other than LibreOffice Calc `26.2.5-3` and Inkscape `1.4.4-6` was refused with `background_unavailable (client_not_qualified)`.

## Why it was an allowlist

`hyprland_compatibility.rs` was the initial qualification scope from the isolated-input RFC (#3550): only Calc and Inkscape had been proven end to end, so everything else refused until "qualified". It was not a record of failures. The agent seats (`Cua-Agent`, `Cua-Agent-2`) are ordinary `wl_seat` globals; any client that binds them receives their input the same way, and the plugin already refuses a client that has no pointer or keyboard on the lane seat (`client_not_bound`) before sending anything.

Checking real clients on Omarchy edge (Hyprland 0.56.2):

| Client | Binds the agent seats | Background pointer (click, drag) | Background keys |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GTK 3 | yes | delivered | delivered |
| GTK 4 | yes | delivered | delivered |
| Qt 6 (Qt Quick) | yes | delivered | dropped by Qt: keys go only to Qt's active window |
| Chromium (Ozone) | only the first `wl_seat` | `client_not_bound` | `client_not_bound` |
| XWayland | n/a | refused | refused |

## Change

- Admission is now a capability check on the live target: the compositor must report the exact `(pid, window)` as a native Wayland client (`client_xwayland` / `client_unattested` otherwise) and the process must be alive. The plugin keeps its dispatch-time checks, including `client_not_bound`.
- A short quirk list covers toolkits that bind the seat but drop its input. It has one entry, with the failure it reproduces: Qt 6 (`libQt6Gui` mapped) refuses background keys with `client_drops_background_keys`; its pointer input still goes through.
- Refusals whose reason starts with `client_` carry a hint naming the alternatives (element tokens, the browser tools, or `delivery_mode:"foreground"`).
- The GTK3 e2e harness now expects delivery, not refusal, for background pointer and key rows when the agent seats are present, and records the new `linux_hyprland_isolated_input` route.
- Docs (platform support, Linux skill, plugin README and protocol notes, test-harness guide) describe the new admission.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` for the admission module and the refusal hint (7 tests, Linux).
- `cargo check -p cua-driver-e2e --test harness_gtk3_test`.
- On an Omarchy edge VM with the plugin enabled, a source build of this branch:
  - probe apps per toolkit (table above): GTK 3/4 got the click, typed text and a full press/motion/release drag; Qt 6 got click and drag, keys refused; Chromium refused with `client_not_bound`. The user's focused window stayed active in every case.
  - the BenchLab tasks on Omarchy with a real agent: background pixel clicks on the app's separate permission and save dialogs now land.

A drag that the app turns into drag-and-drop (reordering a GTK list) still cannot complete in the background: Hyprland runs every drag-and-drop on the user's seat. The companion plugin PR #6705 cancels such drags instead of letting them take the user's pointer; doing drag-and-drop on the agent seats is tracked separately.

Refs CUA-3583. Related: #6705, CUA-3652.

title: fix(spaces): start never pulls a moved image, pending first message for a new home, pet-name default names
body:
## What the owner saw

Home said "agent ready", then a new Space sat in Starting while a 556 MB image downloaded, and only then did the agent install and run. His "@claude hi" did not show in the thread until the Space was up. New Spaces were named `home-hi-iy4` and `space-a572d9e2af`.

## Root cause

Creates resolve the image tag to a digest on every start, and the warm pool's shape key and prepared filesystem are keyed by that digest. When the registry moved the tag, the next create resolved the new digest, missed the warm member of the old one and pulled the image itself. The kept-warm Space only caught up some time later. "Agent ready" came from the old home's member and knew nothing about this.

## Changes

- Core (cua-daemon): a request whose shape is kept warm no longer moves to a newer digest when the registry changes. Creates keep the current image, the new one is pulled and a warm member of it is prepared in the background beside the old member (source `warm-pools-next`), and creates switch only once that member is ready. A start never has to pull. First-ever use, with no warm member yet, still has to pull; that case is unchanged.
- Web: a message typed for a new home shows in its thread at once with the existing pending treatment ("only you can see this", sends when ready), and the pending copy goes away when the real message is posted.
- Default names: one generator in `cua-spaces-contract` (`names.rs`, 100+ adjectives and animals), used by the SDK, CLI, MCP `create_space`, the new-Space wizard and Home. A taken name retries another pair; a short suffix is the last resort. Names given explicitly and existing Spaces are unchanged. The web has a generated copy of the lists with a drift test.

## Tests

- Rust: `hold_refresh` decision test (daemon), names format, list sanity, collision and suffix tests, wizard and parity goldens, home name test.
- Web: `pet-name.test.ts`, `queued.test.ts` (pending shows, survives the create, drops once posted).

## Real run

Built and ran Cua Spaces Local from this branch with its own home directory. The new-Space wizard shows the generated name (`noble-llama`). I could not take the pending-message screenshot in that isolated build: signing in to an agent needs the Keychain, which an ad hoc build cannot use and which I did not touch. The digest hold is covered by the unit test, not by a real registry move.

Note: #6631 also touches `wizard.rs` (different region).

title: fix(spaces): explain a refused new computer and offer a code from another computer
body:
Fixes CUA-3653. Sibling 0.21.1 fix to #6704.

**For users:** on a new Mac signed in to an account that already has other computers, "Share With This Account" now says **"Confirm it's you"**: *"To add this Mac to your account, enter a code from a computer you already added. On that computer, open Cua Spaces, go to Machines and click Add machine."* A **Use a code from another computer** button opens Enter a code. Before this, the app showed only "Couldn't set up this Mac for access".

The relay still refuses a new computer that has no proof it belongs to the owner (S5, #6355). This PR only gets that refusal's reason to the person.

## What changed

- **Relay:** the S5 refusal (`POST /v1/machines`, 403) now sends a stable `code: new_computer_needs_proof` alongside its existing reason, using a new `coded_error` helper. The rule itself is unchanged.
- **cua-host:** a 403 keeps the relay's code in the error text (`relay: <reason> [code: <code>]`), and `cua_host::refusal_code` reads it back. The code has to travel inside the message because the SDK error is flat across the FFI. A relay without this PR is recognised by the wording of its refusal, so 0.21.1 works against the current prod relay.
- **Pairing code on a paused Mac:** `cua host setup --pair` used to resume the old account's registration on a Mac paused for another account. It now moves the Mac to the account that made the code (`Host::rejoin_with_code`, the same path a sign-in switch uses).
- **Bridges:** the macOS (`WebUIBridge.reply`) and desktop (`reply`) bridges pass `kind` and `refusalCode` to the page with every host failure, so later refusals can get their own screens too.
- **Web UI:** `FailureView` shows the needs-proof state as the existing grouped card, with a neutral shield icon and a plain title (no coloured stripe). Its button opens Enter a code, wired on Machines, the setup form, Settings > Advanced and the new first run. When a code joins, the failure clears.

## Not included

There is no in-app "Sign in again with two-step verification" action. The app has no step-up sign-in today (no `acr_values` or `prompt` in the client sign-in), and building one is out of scope, so only the code action ships.

## Tests

- Relay: `a_new_computer_from_a_token_alone_is_refused_with_a_code`
- cua-host: `a_refusal_keeps_the_relays_code` (including an old relay), `a_pairing_code_moves_a_paused_computer_to_the_codes_account`

title: [Bug]: Wayland type_text and press_key fail with foreground_unavailable on generic wlroots (labwc) while click and hotkey succeed
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On generic wlroots Wayland compositors (`labwc`) that expose `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` and `zwp_virtual_keyboard_manager_v1` without a compositor-specific IPC adapter, `type_text(pid, window_id, text)` and `press_key(pid, window_id, key)` unconditionally fail with `foreground_unavailable`, even though `hotkey`, `click`, and `scroll` succeed on the exact same `(pid, window_id)` target.

### Reproduction

1. Run `cua-driver` inside a generic wlroots Wayland session (`labwc`, e.g., `linuxserver/chromium` container with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/config/.XDG` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`).
2. Call `list_windows` to obtain the target window's `pid` (e.g., `707`) and `window_id` (e.g., `4278190080`).
3. Call `hotkey` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080, "keys": ["ctrl", "l"]}`) or `click` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080, "x": 300, "y": 82}`) -> both succeed.
4. Call `type_text` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080, "text": "https://example.com"}`) or `press_key` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080, "key": "Return"}`).

### Expected behavior

`type_text` and `press_key` should activate/verify the target window via `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1::activate(&seat)` (just like `hotkey` and `RestoreMode::LeaveFocused` pointer gestures do) and inject the keystrokes via `zwp_virtual_keyboard_v1`.

### Actual behavior

Both `type_text` and `press_key` refuse with:
```json
{
  "code": "foreground_unavailable",
  "message": "foreground_unavailable: no trusted Wayland compositor adapter can confirm exact target window 4278190080 for pid 707; no global keyboard input was sent"
}
```

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `cua-driver 0.38.1-nightly.20261105.41967274244` (commit `b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a`)
Operating system and architecture: Linux (`aarch64`, Ubuntu/Debian container)
Application/browser/window system/image: `linuxserver/chromium` (Selkies WebRTC + `labwc 0.9.7`, exposing `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` v3, `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` v1, `zwp_virtual_keyboard_manager_v1` v1, `zwlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1` v2)

### Evidence

Root cause verified in source (`b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a`):
- `type_text` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/type_text.rs:621-634, 705-720`) and `press_key` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/press_key.rs:418-436`) invoke `interaction::with_target_foreground(pid, window_id, RestoreMode::RestorePrevious, ...)`.
- In `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/interaction/mod.rs:75-138`:
  - `RestoreMode::LeaveFocused` (lines 75-84, used by `click`/`scroll`) calls `crate::wayland::activate_window_for_input_target(window_id, Some(pid))`, which activates the target via `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1::activate(&seat)` and verifies `toplevel.activated == true` (`wayland/mod.rs:1982-2043`).
  - `RestoreMode::RestorePrevious` (lines 85-138, used by `type_text`/`press_key`) only checks `niri::is_session()`, `sway_ipc::window_for_id()`, `kwin_helper::trusted_window_for_id()`, and `shell_helper::trusted_window_for_id()`, then falls through to line 136 and fails with `foreground_unavailable`.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: Pass an explicit AT-SPI `element_token` to `type_text`, or use `hotkey` for single keys.
Suggested fix: In `interaction::with_target_foreground` (`interaction/mod.rs:85-138`), when no compositor-specific IPC adapter matches but `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` is available, snapshot the previously `activated` `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1` before calling `wayland::activate_window_for_input_target(window_id, Some(pid))` and re-activate it on `RestoreFocusGuard::drop` (or fall back to `activate_window_for_input_target(window_id, Some(pid))`).

title: [Bug]: Linux browser_platform is_only_exact_native_window returns None on generic Wayland, preventing cardinality upgrade and refusing browser_* mutations
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On generic Wayland compositors (`labwc`) without a compositor-specific IPC adapter, `LinuxBrowserPlatform::is_only_exact_native_window` falls through and returns `Ok(None)`. This prevents `cardinality_exact_candidate` from upgrading a single-window Chromium session from `Heuristic` to `Exact` binding, causing all `browser_*` mutations (`browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_navigate`, etc.) to refuse with `browser_wrong_target_refused`.

### Reproduction

1. Launch a single Chromium window with `--remote-debugging-port=9222` inside a generic Wayland session (`labwc`, e.g., `linuxserver/chromium` container where only 1 browser window exists in the entire session).
2. Call `get_browser_state` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080}`) -> returns `"binding_quality": "heuristic"`, `"mutation_allowed": false`.
3. Call any browser mutation tool such as `browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, or `browser_type` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080, ...}`).

### Expected behavior

When there is only 1 browser window owned by `pid` (and only 1 CDP window representative with an exact title match), `cardinality_exact_candidate` (`cua-driver-core/src/browser/binding.rs:66-92`) should upgrade the binding to `BindingQuality::Exact` (`CorrelationMethod::Cardinality`, `mutation_allowed: true`) so `browser_*` mutations succeed in single-window generic Wayland sessions.

### Actual behavior

`get_browser_state` reports `"binding_quality": "heuristic"` (`"mutation_allowed": false`), and every `browser_*` mutation refuses with:
```json
{
  "code": "browser_wrong_target_refused",
  "message": "browser_wrong_target_refused: window 4278190080 is bound to CDP target ... only heuristically; refusing mutation because exact window-to-tab identity is not proven"
}
```

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `cua-driver 0.38.1-nightly.20261105.41967274244` (commit `b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a`)
Operating system and architecture: Linux (`aarch64`, Ubuntu/Debian container)
Application/browser/window system/image: Chromium in `linuxserver/chromium` (`labwc 0.9.7`, exposing `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` v3 and `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` v1, with AT-SPI enabled)

### Evidence

Root cause verified in source (`b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a`):
- `BrowserEngine::resolve_binding` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/engine.rs:1376-1388`) calls `self.platform.is_only_exact_native_window(pid, window_id)` and passes the result to `cardinality_exact_candidate` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/binding.rs:66-92`), which requires `is_only_exact_native_window == Some(true)` (line 71).
- However, in `LinuxBrowserPlatform::is_only_exact_native_window` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/browser_platform.rs:753-827`), after checking X11, Hyprland, Sway, GNOME Shell helper, and `wayland::is_inject_mode()`, generic Wayland sessions fall through to line 817 and return `Ok(None)`.

### Workaround and additional context

Suggested fix:
In `LinuxBrowserPlatform::is_only_exact_native_window` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/browser_platform.rs:795-817`), when `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` / `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` is active and `wayland::list_windows_dispatch(Some(pid_u32))` confirms that `pid` owns only 1 native window matching `window_id` (especially when total foreign-toplevel count for the app/session is 1), return `Ok(Some(true)` so `cardinality_exact_candidate` can upgrade single-window browser sessions to `Exact`.

title: ci(cua-driver): fix Hyprland release-contract tests failing with RELEASE_REF unbound
body:
Five tests in `libs/cua-driver/hyprland-plugin/packaging/release` failed on main (and on every PR, e.g. #6705, #6706) with `RELEASE_REF: unbound variable`.

**Cause:** #6606 (rebuild_tag dispatch) made the plugin-source job read `RELEASE_REF` (workflow-level env) and changed its `if:`/`ref:` expressions. The tests extract that step and run it in bash without `RELEASE_REF`, and still asserted the old expressions. The workflow is correct; the tests were stale.

**Fix:** tests set `RELEASE_REF` as the workflow does, and the text contracts assert the current `if:`/`ref:` expressions. No tests skipped or removed; full suite 133/133 pass locally.

Plain words: no user-facing change; unblocks CI on all PRs.

title: [Feature]: Support labwc.sock IPC in LinuxServer.io / Selkies Wayland containers for attested window geometry, PID, and capture
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

`linuxserver/*` GUI containers (such as `linuxserver/chromium`, powered by Selkies WebRTC + `labwc`) are among the most popular Docker desktop environments for running `cua-driver` and browser/GUI agents.

Today, because upstream `labwc 0.9.7` only exposes `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` (v3) and `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` (v1) (neither of which carries `(x, y, width, height)` or `pid`) and does not yet implement `ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1`:
1. `list_windows` returns `bounds: {x: 0, y: 0, width: 0, height: 0}` on `labwc`.
2. `get_window_state(include_screenshot=true)` fails with `surface_identity_unproven: Wayland capture cannot prove pixels belong to window ...: no compositor-attested window geometry is available` (`wayland/mod.rs:1202-1233`).
3. `zoom`, `mouse_button_down`, `mouse_button_up`, and `drag` fail downstream with `screenshot_context_missing: no_screenshot`.

### Desired outcome

Add a compositor IPC adapter for `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/labwc.sock` (shipped in Selkies / LinuxServer `labwc` images) in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/`, attested via `compositor_peer::peer_pid` (`SO_PEERCRED`) just like `sway_ipc.rs` and `niri/ipc.rs`.

With this adapter active:
- `list_windows` reports compositor-attested `(x, y, width, height)`, `pid`, `focused`, and `!minimized` visibility on `labwc`.
- `get_window_state(include_screenshot=true)` can prove single-window / unoccluded crop geometry via `zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1` + `labwc.sock` geometry without failing with `surface_identity_unproven`.
- `with_target_foreground` and `LinuxBrowserPlatform` gain compositor-attested PID, focus readback, and window bounds.

### Current workaround

Currently users in `linuxserver/*` / Selkies containers must either force apps onto Xwayland (`--ozone-platform=x11`, which can conflict with Selkies fullscreen/maximized window management rules) or avoid per-window screenshots (`include_screenshot=false` / full-desktop `get_desktop_state`).

### Affected components and platforms

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/` (`mod.rs`, `compositor_peer.rs`, new `labwc_ipc.rs`), `interaction/mod.rs`, `browser_platform.rs`.

### Alternatives and prior art

Related to #5327 (Wayland compositor support tracking). Upstream `labwc` does not yet implement `ext-image-copy-capture-v1` toplevel capture (`ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1`), whereas Selkies / LinuxServer containers already ship `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/labwc.sock` out of the box.

### Implementation ideas

Verified in `linuxserver/chromium` (`labwc 0.9.7-dirty`, Selkies build):
The `labwc` compositor process (the exact same PID that owns `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/$WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, verifiable via `SO_PEERCRED` in `compositor_peer::peer_pid`) listens on the Unix domain stream socket `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/labwc.sock` (`src/ipc.c`).

Supported commands over `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/labwc.sock`:
- `GET_WINDOWS\n` -> returns JSON array:
  ```json
  [
    {
      "pid": 707,
      "x": 0,
      "y": 0,
      "width": 1457,
      "height": 827,
      "title": "New Tab - Chromium",
      "app_id": "chromium",
      "minimized": false,
      "fullscreen": false,
      "maximized": true,
      "tiled": false,
      "focused": true
    }
  ]
  ```
- `GET_WINDOW_BY_PID <pid>\n` -> returns single JSON object or `null`.
- `GET_FOCUSED_WINDOW\n` -> returns single JSON object or `null`.

Because `labwc` in Selkies does not expose window creation order in `GET_WINDOWS`, `labwc.sock` records can be correlated with `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` / `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` handles via `(app_id, title, focused, minimized, maximized, fullscreen)` (and exact cardinality when a process owns a single window).

title: fix(hyprland-plugin): accept AltGr layouts for foreground typing
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: Hyprland foreground typing refuses `us(altgr-intl)` and layouts built on it, even though they type the same as US on every key the driver presses.
- What changed: the whole-keymap check now skips Right Alt and the ISO `KEY_102ND` key, the only two keys where `us(altgr-intl)` differs from US. The driver never presses either one, and `foreground_chord_failure` still refuses a chord that does. `us(intl)` is still refused, since its dead keys change normal typing.

## Related work

Refs #3968, which made the same check accept Omarchy's default options.

RFC: not needed. No contract, permission, or protocol change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: foreground typing works on AltGr international layouts on Hyprland, where it used to refuse. Nothing changes for layouts that already passed.
- Risk and rollback: low. The up-front check now ignores 2 keys the driver never sends, and the per-chord check still covers them. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `keymap_equivalence_test` accepts `us(altgr-intl)` and still refuses `us(intl)`. `keyboard_layout_test` checks that `foreground_chord_failure` refuses both skipped keys under `us(altgr-intl)`. All 20 plugin tests pass against Hyprland 0.57.1 with `CUA_HYPRLAND_REQUIRE_XKBCOMMON=1`, and `bin/ci` passes locally.
- Manual or platform evidence: on Hyprland 0.57.1 with a custom layout built on `us(altgr-intl)`, foreground `type_text` of ``Hello World 1234567890 -=[]\;',./`~!@#$%^&*()_+{}|:"<>?`` plus Enter into a zenity entry returned exactly that text, and the plugin's dispatch count rose to match.
- Known gaps or CI still required: tested on one machine with one layout. This comes from a fork, so the sign-off is the `CI: Quick` run.

title: bin/ci: run on Windows (Git for Windows' bash, never WSL's)
body:
## What

`bin/ci` now runs on Windows (PowerShell, cmd or Git Bash): `python bin\ci --quick`, then `python bin\ci --signoff` after pushing. The sign-off format is unchanged (the status description ends with `(win32)`).

## Why it did not work

- The checks are bash. A bare `bash` on Windows is usually `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe`, which is **WSL**: the first Windows run executed checks inside the user's Linux distribution. `bin/ci` now finds Git for Windows' bash next to `git` (`CUA_CI_BASH` overrides) and never uses `bash` from `PATH`.
- Windows read files in the ANSI code page (the repo is UTF-8): `bin/ci` re-runs itself in UTF-8 mode.
- The checks call `python3`, which Windows does not have (or has as a Store stub): a `python3` shim for the check's `PATH`.
- Paths: `package_of` and `spdx-headers.py` compared `\` paths with `/` exemption lists.
- Process cleanup used `killpg`/`SIGKILL` (now `taskkill`), `du` was assumed, a log being rewritten by a nested run could not be deleted, and the docs router quoted a Windows path for cmd.exe.
- The tests of `bin/ci` itself ran hook scripts directly and used a bare `bash`.

## Verified on Windows 11 (PowerShell 5.1 and Git Bash, Python 3.13)

`python bin\ci --quick`: SPDX headers, image refs, docs image refs (needs `crane`), bin/ci tests and workflow sync all pass. Not run here: Mac/Linux (the POSIX paths are unchanged apart from `bash -c` replacing `shell=True, executable=/bin/bash`), `--full` and the cargo checks.

title: ci(cua-driver): run platform-linux all-targets clippy with -D warnings
body:
CUA-3650

## Why
#6695 (CUA-3613) cleared the platform-linux test-target clippy lints by hand, but no CI job runs clippy on the cua-driver workspace, so new lints there go unnoticed. This adds `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings` to the Linux unit job.

## What changed
- `.github/workflows/ci-rust-linux.yml` `unit` job: the toolchain step installs the `clippy` component, and a new step runs the command above in `libs/cua-driver/rust` before the tests.

## Scope
platform-linux only, all targets, default features. Other cua-driver crates, feature combinations and `bin/ci` are out of scope.

## Blast Radius
PRs touching the workflow's existing paths (which include `crates/platform-linux/**`) now fail the Linux unit job on any platform-linux clippy warning. The Linux build dependencies are already installed by then, and clippy shares the job's rust-cache.

## Verification
- On macOS, the scoped repository checks ran `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and it passed. That build skips the Linux-cfg code, so this PR's own `Rust Linux unit and compile` run is the Linux proof.

title: Cua Spaces Local on Windows: install-local.ps1 and uninstall-local.ps1
body:
## What

`apps/cua-spaces-desktop/scripts/install-local.ps1` builds this checkout on Windows and installs it as **Cua Spaces Local** next to a released Cua Spaces, so a branch (a new UI, the `windows:*` images) can be dogfooded without touching the app in use. It is the Windows counterpart of `apps/cua-spaces-macos/scripts/install-local.sh`; `uninstall-local.ps1` removes it. Unsigned, no installer, no update feed.

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File apps\cua-spaces-desktop\scripts\install-local.ps1
```

Flags: `-Release` (release Electron fuses), `-NoLaunch`, `-Prefix DIR`, `-SkipRustBuild`, `-SkipWebBuild`, `-NoIntegration` (no Start Menu/PATH/scheme), `-NormalPriority` (builds run at BelowNormal by default). Prerequisites (Rust+MSVC Build Tools, CMake, Node 22+, pnpm, wasm32 target, wasm-bindgen-cli) are checked up front in one message.

## How it isolates Local

- The Electron shell gets a channel (`src/channel.ts`): Local when `CUA_CHANNEL=local` or the executable is `Cua Spaces Local.exe`. Local pins `CUA_CHANNEL=local` and `CUA_HOME=%USERPROFILE%\.cua-local` before the native layer loads, and has its own AppUserModelID (`ai.cua.spaces.desktop.local`), user data folder, Run entry, registry key, window title and `cua-local://` scheme. Stable's names are unchanged (tests).
- `packaging/electron-builder.local.cjs`: dir build, own app id and product name, no `app-update.yml`.
- Installs only: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Cua Spaces Local\` (with `bin\cua-local.exe`, a copy of the bundled `cua.exe`; the CLI is Local by its name), a user-PATH entry for that `bin`, a Start Menu shortcut carrying the AUMID, and `HKCU\Software\Classes\cua-local`.
- Staged build, verified (`cua-local --version`, native layer, web UI, no update feed), then swapped; the old copy is put back if the swap fails. It refuses a `-Prefix` that is, holds or is inside anything the released app owns, and any folder at the Local path without its `.cua-spaces-local.json` marker; only processes running from the Local folder are stopped. The user PATH is read and written as stored (no `%VAR%` expansion).
- The pinned pnpm (11.x) is installed into `.local-tools` when the PC's pnpm is another major (pnpm 10 cannot read the lockfile).

## Verified on Windows 11 (PowerShell 5.1)

Ran the script for real (twice: fresh install, then an in-place reinstall from this branch's worktree): web UI and native layer built, staged copy verified, app launched with the title "Cua Spaces Local" at normal priority, `cua-local --version` prints `cua 0.10.1`, the app's daemon runs from the Local folder, state in `%USERPROFILE%\.cua-local` and `%APPDATA%\Cua Spaces Local`, `cua-local://` and PATH entries registered, the released `%USERPROFILE%\.cua` and its `cua` PATH entry untouched. `scripts/tests/install-local.tests.ps1` (path/refusal/PATH/version checks, names match `src/channel.ts`, the builder config and `CuaChannel::Local`) and `test/channel.test.ts` pass; the desktop suite has the same 12 Windows-only failures as `main` (packaging file modes, nsh CRLF, updater, browser tests) and nothing new. `bin/ci --quick` checks (SPDX, image refs, docs image refs, bin/ci tests, desktop typecheck) pass on Windows with the port from #6719; `local-ci` is signed off.

Not verified: PowerShell 7 (not installed here; the script avoids 5.1-only and 7-only syntax), arm64, `-Release` fuses, `-Prefix` on another drive, an uninstall run on the real install (only its pure parts are tested), sign-in (staging) and creating a Space from the Local app.

## Notes

- Stacked on #6719 (bin/ci on Windows); the first two commits are that PR's and drop out when it merges.
- Dogfooding the `windows:*` images (local ISO build via WSL2/KVM) needs the branch of #6631 checked out: this PR is based on `main`. That branch also needs a small fix (not part of this PR): `AppSandboxImage` in `cua-spaces-ffi` lacks the new `local_build` field, so the Spaces app library does not compile there (E0063); the TypeScript binding needs regenerating and `libs/spaces-app-swift` needs regenerating on a Mac.
- The unattended-access host service (`cua host setup`) still downloads the pinned `cua-spacesd`, which does not know the Local ports.

title: [Bug]: Wayland type_text shells out to wtype on wlroots, corrupting >=14 distinct chars (evdev 14/28) and non-BMP Unicode/Emoji
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On wlroots Wayland compositors (`labwc`, `sway`, `hyprland`), `wayland::type_into` (`wayland/mod.rs:2769-2785`) only uses the built-in XKB keymap planner on `niri` and still shells out to external `wtype` on all other compositors. This causes two reproducible bugs in Chromium/Electron and Wayland apps: (1) non-BMP Unicode characters (Emoji > U+FFFF) are truncated to 16-bit keysyms or dropped, and (2) strings with >=14 distinct characters map to evdev keycode 14 (Backspace) and 28 (Enter), deleting characters or prematurely submitting forms.

### Reproduction

1. Run `cua-driver` inside a wlroots Wayland session (`labwc` or `sway`) with Chromium focused.
2. Call `type_text` with non-BMP Emoji: `{"scope": "desktop", "delivery_mode": "foreground", "text": "Hello 🚀😀🎉"}`.
3. Call `type_text` with a string containing >=14 distinct characters into a Chromium input field: `{"scope": "desktop", "delivery_mode": "foreground", "text": "abcdefghijklmnop0123456789!@"}`.

### Expected behavior

1. Non-BMP Unicode characters (Emoji such as `🚀😀🎉`) should be delivered intact without 16-bit keysym truncation.
2. Strings with >=14 distinct characters should be typed without triggering `Backspace` (evdev 14) or `Enter` (evdev 28) in Chromium/Electron.

### Actual behavior

1. Non-BMP Emoji characters (`> U+FFFF`) are either dropped by `wtype` or truncated to 16-bit keysyms by Chromium.
2. Because `wtype` assigns the n-th distinct character of a call to `evdev code n`, the 14th distinct character triggers `Backspace` (deleting the previous character) and the 28th triggers `Enter`.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver v0.40.2 (commit dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c)
Operating system and architecture: Linux (aarch64 / x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04 container)
Application/browser/window system/image: Chromium on wlroots Wayland (labwc 0.9.7 / sway, zwp_virtual_keyboard_manager_v1)

### Evidence

Verified in `v0.40.2` source (`dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c`):
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/mod.rs:2774-2782`:
  ```rust
  if niri::is_session() {
      return niri::keyboard::type_text(window.or_else(niri_expected_window), text);
  }
  let result = wtype_output(&["-k", "Shift_L", "--", text]);
  ```
- Meanwhile, `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/niri/keyboard.rs:6-28` explicitly documents both `wtype` defects:
  - Lines 6-10: *"A tool like `wtype` instead numbers the n-th distinct character of a call as evdev code n, and Chromium and Electron take the DOM `code` from the evdev code: a punctuation mark on code 1 (Escape) is dropped, one on code 14 (Backspace) deletes the character before it, and one on code 28 (Enter) can submit a form."*
  - Lines 24-27: *"Text outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as most emoji, goes out as its Unicode keysym like any other character, as `wtype` sends it. Chromium cuts a keysym's character to 16 bits, so it types a wrong character there whatever the input route."*

### Workaround and additional context

Suggested fix:
1. Generalize the `CHROMIUM_CODES` + `BORROWABLE` (`F13..=F24`) XKB keymap planner in `wayland/niri/keyboard.rs` so all `zwp_virtual_keyboard_v1` compositors (`labwc`, `sway`, `hyprland`, `niri`) use the native Rust virtual-keyboard keymap planner instead of shelling out to `wtype`.
2. When `text` contains non-BMP characters (`c as u32 > 0xFFFF`, such as Emoji) on Wayland, deliver the non-BMP segment via AT-SPI `EditableText` or a transient clipboard paste (`wl-copy` + `Ctrl+V` with prior clipboard restoration) so Chromium/Electron receives the full UTF-8 code points intact.

title: [Feature]: Support parallel_mouse_drag on wlroots Wayland via zwlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1 without requiring CUA_INJECT_SOCKET
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On standard wlroots Wayland compositors (`labwc`, `sway`, `hyprland`) that expose `zwlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1`, calling `parallel_mouse_drag` unconditionally refuses with:
`parallel_mouse_drag requires the cua-compositor inject socket on Wayland (set CUA_INJECT_SOCKET to the cua-compositor control socket), or run the target under X11.`
This prevents agents running in standard Wayland sessions from executing multi-pointer drag gestures (`parallel_mouse_drag`).

### Desired outcome

When `wayland::is_wayland()` is true and `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` is not set, `parallel_mouse_drag` should drive concurrent `ZwlrVirtualPointerV1` virtual pointers via `zwlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1` (reusing the multi-cursor architecture in `wayland/persistent_vptr.rs` and `wayland::window_local_to_output`), rather than immediately bailing out.

### Current workaround

Currently users on standard wlroots Wayland must either fall back to sequential single-pointer `drag` calls or run a custom `cua-compositor` with `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET`.

### Affected components and platforms

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/parallel_mouse_drag.rs` (`invoke`, lines 136-148), `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/persistent_vptr.rs`, `wayland/mod.rs`.

### Alternatives and prior art

X11 MPX (`send_parallel_virtual_pointer_drags`) only works on X11, and `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` is only available in custom `cua-compositor` builds.

### Implementation ideas

In `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/persistent_vptr.rs`, the owner thread already manages a `HashMap<String, ActivePointer>` where each `cursor_id` binds its own independent `ZwlrVirtualPointerV1` instance on the Wayland connection.
In `parallel_mouse_drag.rs:142-148`, instead of returning an error on native Wayland, translate each drag item's waypoints via `wayland::window_local_to_output`, bind a per-item `ZwlrVirtualPointerV1`, press all buttons, step through the interpolated motion frames in lockstep across all virtual pointers, and release all buttons.

title: fix(spaces): New Space Continue did nothing for a Windows image on a Windows PC
body:
## Problem
In Cua Spaces Local on Windows, New Space > Windows > image `ghcr.io/trycua/windows:11` (any Windows image), pressing Continue did nothing: no error, no progress.

## Root cause
`wizard.reduce` (the `Next` action) decided whether Continue is allowed with `view(&s, env)`, which is the view *as a Mac* (`view_on(.., SpaceOs::Macos)`). On a Mac a Windows image is "coming soon" (`windows_soon`), so `can_continue` was false and `Next` was a silent no-op, while the view the person sees (`wizard.view` with `hostOs: "windows"`) showed Continue enabled. Reduce and view disagreed about the host system. Also affects `microvm_support`-dependent checks. Present on main; independent of the windows image aliases in #6631 (which only add the `windows:11` presets).

## Fix
- `wizard::reduce_on(state, action, env, os)`; `reduce` stays as the Mac default (Swift/FFI callers unchanged), like `view`/`view_on`.
- `wizard.reduce` dispatch accepts `hostOs`; `wizardReduce` in the web bridge and the desktop `NewSpaceWizard` pass `hostOs()` on every reduce call.

## Tests
- Rust: `continue_advances_a_windows_image_on_a_windows_pc` (Windows host advances, Mac host stays on step 0). `cargo test -p cua-spaces-app-core --lib wizard`: 58 passed.
- Vitest: `NewSpaceWizard.test.tsx` "go on to the next step on a Windows PC when Continue is enabled" (not run locally: needs the wasm core build; run in CI).

## Verified in the real app
Before: installed Cua Spaces Local, New Space > Windows > `ghcr.io/trycua/windows:11`, Continue clicked (UIA invoke): stays on "Choose a system". After rebuilding with `scripts/install-local.ps1` (from #install-local branch + this commit) and repeating: Continue goes to Resources (4 cores / 8 GB, "Virtual machine").

## Notes / dependencies
- Runtime requirements are already surfaced by the wizard (e.g. Linux shows "This PC cannot run container Spaces: ... missing: a running container engine"; Windows VM needs QEMU ready). The managed runtimes and disk-space checks are being done in the separate runtime PR; not duplicated here.
- Seen, not fixed here: on the Resources step the fact reads "Available 49 GB on this Mac" on a Windows PC.
- `bin/ci --quick` here: rustfmt, web typecheck, design lint, image refs ok; the SPDX check fails only on files this PR does not touch (cua-spacesd-html5 assets, cua-driver-bench taskpack).

title: [Feature]: Support set_window_frame on labwc / wlroots Wayland via compositor IPC and wlr-foreign-toplevel state requests
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On `labwc` and generic wlroots Wayland sessions (such as `linuxserver/*` / Selkies desktop containers), calling `set_window_frame` always fails with:
`set_window_frame: this Wayland compositor exposes no protocol that permits a client to set another top-level window's geometry`
(`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/set_window_frame.rs:31-35`).

### Desired outcome

Allow `set_window_frame` to succeed on `labwc` / wlroots Wayland sessions by:
1. Supporting compositor IPC geometry commands when `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/labwc.sock` (see #6714) is available, or Xwayland `configure_window` when the target surface is an Xwayland window.
2. Supporting `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1::set_maximized` / `unset_maximized` / `set_fullscreen` when requested bounds match the output dimensions.

### Current workaround

Currently callers must skip `set_window_frame` on `labwc` or rely on pre-configured `rc.xml` window rules.

### Affected components and platforms

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/set_window_frame.rs`, `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/mod.rs`.

### Alternatives and prior art

Related to #6714 (`labwc.sock` IPC support) and #5327 (Wayland compositor support tracking).

### Implementation ideas

In `tools/set_window_frame.rs` and `wayland/mod.rs`:
1. Route `labwc` sessions through `labwc_ipc` (when supported) or check if the requested `(x, y, width, height)` matches the primary output geometry from `get_screen_size`.
2. When the requested frame matches the output size (or when `labwc.sock` confirms the window is already maximized at those exact bounds), apply `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1::set_maximized` and verify the resulting geometry via `labwc.sock`.
