title: [Feature]: Implement cua-driver autostart subcommand on Linux (systemd --user unit and XDG/container service detection)
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### User problem

Running `cua-driver autostart status` (or `enable` / `disable` / `kick`) on Linux currently fails with exit code 1:
`cua-driver autostart is currently Windows-only`
(`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/autostart.rs:16-19`). This is the only CLI subcommand out of all 28 `cua-driver` CLI commands that fails on Linux.

### Desired outcome

Implement `cua-driver autostart {status|enable|disable|kick}` on Linux:
1. On systemd desktop sessions (`systemctl --user`), manage `~/.config/systemd/user/cua-driver-serve.service`.
2. On non-systemd / container desktop environments (such as s6-overlay / XDG autostart containers where `cua-driver serve` is managed by init or `~/.config/autostart/cua-driver.desktop`), allow `cua-driver autostart status` to detect the active daemon / XDG autostart entry and return `registered (running)` (exit 0) instead of failing with a Windows-only error.

### Current workaround

Users currently have to manually create systemd user units, XDG `.desktop` files, or container s6 init scripts, and `cua-driver autostart status` still exits with code 1.

### Affected components and platforms

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/autostart.rs` (`#[cfg(target_os = "linux")] mod platform`).

### Alternatives and prior art

`scripts/install-local.sh --autostart` handles initial install-time setup, but the `cua-driver autostart` CLI subcommand itself remains stubbed out on Linux.

### Implementation ideas

Add a `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")] mod platform` implementation in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/autostart.rs`:
- `enable()`: write `~/.config/systemd/user/cua-driver-serve.service` (if `systemctl --user` is available) or `~/.config/autostart/cua-driver-serve.desktop` as fallback.
- `status()`: check `systemctl --user is-enabled/is-active cua-driver-serve.service`, `~/.config/autostart/cua-driver-serve.desktop`, or `/etc/xdg/autostart` / running daemon status, returning `Status::RegisteredRunning`, `Status::RegisteredIdle`, or `Status::NotRegistered`.

title: [Bug]: _install-rust.sh leaves CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION at 0.38.0 and omits cua-cursor-theme symlink on macOS
body:
### Primary area

Build, packaging, or release

### Summary

The published installer `https://cua.ai/driver/_install-rust.sh` (and `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:671` on `main` / `v0.40.2`) still hardcodes `CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION="0.38.0"`, causing `--channel stable` installs to install stale v0.38.0 instead of the latest stable release (v0.40.2). In addition, on macOS it only symlinks `~/.local/bin/cua-driver` (`_install-rust.sh:1435`) and omits `~/.local/bin/cua-cursor-theme`.

### Reproduction

1. Run the official stable installer on macOS:
   `curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh | bash`
2. Check the installed version:
   `cua-driver --version`
3. Run `cua-driver cursor-theme list --json` when `/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS` is not in `PATH` (only `~/.local/bin` is in `PATH`).

### Expected behavior

1. The stable installer should install the latest published stable release (`cua-driver 0.40.2`).
2. `cua-driver cursor-theme list --json` should locate `cua-cursor-theme` via symlink in `~/.local/bin` or by resolving `realpath` of the `cua-driver` executable.

### Actual behavior

1. The installer logs `using baked release: cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0` and installs `0.38.0` instead of `0.40.2`.
2. `cua-driver cursor-theme` fails with `No such file or directory (os error 2)` unless `~/.local/bin/cua-cursor-theme` is manually symlinked to `/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-cursor-theme`.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver v0.40.2 (commit dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2 (arm64, Apple Silicon)
Application/browser/window system/image: Official installer script `_install-rust.sh`

### Evidence

Verified in `v0.40.2` source (`dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c`):
- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:670-672`:
  ```bash
  # ~~~ BAKED_VERSION: auto-updated after release publication — do not edit ~~~
  CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION="0.38.0" # published-installer-version
  # ~~~ END_BAKED_VERSION ~~~
  ```
- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:1435` only symlinks `cua-driver`:
  ```bash
  ln -sf "$APP_BINARY" "$BIN_LINK"
  ```

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround:
1. Strip `CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION` before piping to bash so the installer falls back to GitHub Releases API resolution:
   `curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/_install-rust.sh | sed 's/^CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION=.*/CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION=""/' | bash -s -- --channel stable`
2. Manually symlink `ln -sf /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-cursor-theme ~/.local/bin/cua-cursor-theme`.

title: [Bug]: browser_download hardcodes a 30-second timeout with no configurable timeout_ms parameter
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`browser_download` hardcodes `const DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30)` (`browser/download.rs:32`) with no configurable `timeout_ms` parameter in its input schema. Any approved download that takes longer than 30 seconds fails with `browser_action_unavailable: the approved browser download did not complete within 30 seconds` (and attempts `remove_proven_partial`), even while the browser is actively downloading.

### Reproduction

1. Start `cua-driver serve --permission-mode unrestricted --dangerously-bypass-approvals`.
2. Attach to or prepare a Chromium window via `browser_prepare` and `get_browser_state`.
3. Trigger a large file download (>30s over the current network) via `browser_download` with a valid `ref` and `destination_root`.

### Expected behavior

`browser_download` should accept an optional `timeout_ms` parameter (or track active download byte progress before timing out) so large legitimate downloads can complete without failing at a fixed 30s wall-clock cutoff.

### Actual behavior

After 30 seconds, `browser_download` returns:
`browser_action_unavailable: the approved browser download did not complete within 30 seconds`
even though `.crdownload` is actively growing in `destination_root`.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver v0.40.2 (commit dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2 (arm64, Apple Silicon)
Application/browser/window system/image: Google Chrome / Chromium CDP via `browser_download`

### Evidence

Verified in `v0.40.2` source (`dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c`):
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/download.rs:32`:
  ```rust
  const DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
  ```
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/download.rs:498-503`:
  ```rust
  remove_proven_partial(&destination_root, observed_guid.as_deref());
  BrowserRefusal::new(
      BrowserRefusalCode::BrowserActionUnavailable,
      "the approved browser download did not complete within 30 seconds",
  )
  .to_tool_result()
  ```

### Workaround and additional context

Suggested fix: Add an optional `timeout_ms` parameter to `browser_download` (e.g., default 30000ms, max 600000ms) or extend the deadline while `Browser.downloadProgress` events report `receivedBytes` increasing.

title: [Bug]: get_window_state / get_desktop_state omit capture_id and parse_visual_regions only returns a count in MCP text content
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### Summary

Over MCP, `get_window_state` and `get_desktop_state` omit `capture_id` from their `content[0].text` summary header, and `parse_visual_regions` (`perception_tools.rs:162`) returns only `"Parsed N visual regions"` in `content[0].text` while placing `capture_id` and `regions` exclusively in `structuredContent`. MCP hosts/agents that only forward `content[].text` to the model (such as Antigravity) cannot read `capture_id` or the parsed visual regions.

### Reproduction

1. With `cua-perception` installed, call `get_window_state` or `get_desktop_state` over `cua-driver mcp` stdio.
2. Inspect `result.content[0].text`: observe `window_id=112507 pid=24388 size=460x816 elements=34 snapshot_id=s00000001` (no `capture_id=...`).
3. Call `parse_visual_regions` with the `capture_id` from `structuredContent`.
4. Inspect `result.content[0].text`: observe it contains only `"Parsed 5 visual regions"` with no region bounds, kinds, labels, or text.

### Expected behavior

1. `get_window_state` and `get_desktop_state` text headers should include `capture_id=<id>` alongside `snapshot_id=<id>` when a capture is registered.
2. `parse_visual_regions` text content should include a compact Markdown/text listing of the parsed regions (id, kind, bounds, confidence, text/label) in addition to `structuredContent`, similar to #4719.

### Actual behavior

1. `get_window_state` and `get_desktop_state` omit `capture_id` from `content[].text`.
2. `parse_visual_regions` returns only `"Parsed N visual regions"` in `content[0].text`, making the tool unusable in MCP clients that do not expose `structuredContent` to the LLM.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver v0.40.2 (commit dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c) + cua-perception 0.2.1
Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2 (arm64, Apple Silicon)
Application/browser/window system/image: MCP stdio (`cua-driver mcp`) with Antigravity vs Codex

### Evidence

Verified in `v0.40.2` source (`dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c`):
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/perception_tools.rs:161-163`:
  ```rust
  let structured = serde_json::to_value(&output).expect("visual output serializes");
  ToolResult::text(format!("Parsed {} visual regions", output.regions.len()))
      .with_structured(structured)
  ```
- Raw MCP wire response:
  `content: [{"text": "Parsed 5 visual regions", "type": "text"}]`

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround for text-only MCP hosts: Use `run_script` (`const st = await app.getState(); return st.capture_id;`) to read `capture_id`, or shell out to `cua-driver call parse_visual_regions`.
Related issue: #4719 (`list_windows` MCP text content is only a count; window rows exist only in `structuredContent`).

title: [Feature]: Implement cua-driver autostart subcommand on macOS (LaunchAgent enable/disable/status/kick)
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### User problem

On macOS, running `cua-driver autostart status|enable|disable|kick` exits with an error stating that `cua-driver autostart is currently Windows-only` and points users to `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.sh --autostart` (which is only present in a source checkout, not in binary installations). Users and agent setups have to manually author and manage `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.trycua.cua-driver.plist`.

### Desired outcome

`cua-driver autostart enable|disable|status|kick` (including `--json`) should natively manage `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.trycua.cua-driver.plist` on macOS (`launchctl bootstrap` / `bootout` / `kickstart` / `print` in `gui/$(id -u)`), preserving `/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver serve` bundle attribution (`com.trycua.driver`) and optional startup flags.

### Current workaround

Manually write `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.trycua.cua-driver.plist` with `RunAtLoad` and `KeepAlive` and run `launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.trycua.cua-driver.plist`.

### Affected components and platforms

`cua-driver` CLI (`autostart` subcommand) on macOS (`launchd` user `LaunchAgents`).

### Alternatives and prior art

title: fix(spaces): every agent message is appended to the thread, child Spaces work from inside a Space, and child agents show in the chat
body:
## What

Three fixes for what an agent does in a Space thread.

### 1. Every message an agent posts is appended
The thread held one reply per task, glued from the turn's text and posted when the turn ended. In a real thread this dropped messages: an agent said "Creating the macOS space...", its turn ended, a background job failed, the agent woke on its own and explained, and that explanation arrived after the task was closed and was never posted. A streaming "live" line was also replaced by the final reply.

Now each stretch of agent text between tool calls is its own thread entry, appended in order as it is written (`Persistent::post_said`, `cua_agents::subagents::said`). Nothing is replaced, glued or dropped:
- text that arrives after the turn ended is posted after 1.5 s without growth;
- posts are idempotent (a restart or a re-read never repeats one);
- the agent can `thread_reply` under a task it already closed (appended, the task keeps its state), and a reply it already posted word for word is not added twice (a restarted bridge runs old calls again);
- a turn that said nothing still ends with `Finished.`, and a failed turn always says why;
- the "working" row stays status UI; it shows the message being written until it lands as an entry.

The ugly first message is handled in what the agent is told: the thread framing, the `thread_reply` tool text and the home brief now say that everything written between tool calls is posted in order, to say in one short sentence what it will do before a long job, not to repeat itself or narrate starting up (the app shows that), and how to make a child computer. A task is quoted once when an agent says several things under it (web and phone).

### 2. Child Spaces from inside a Space
Reproduced with a real agent in a Linux home Space. Causes:
- the Space's MCP tools `create_space`, `delete_space`, `space_bash` and the other child-Space tools had no reviewed risk classification, so the MCP server refused every call ("no reviewed risk classification"). They are classified now, with a test that every tool the Space adds is.
- `cua sb create` inside a Space failed with a bare "unsupported". It now says to use `cua spaces create IMAGE --name NAME`, `cua sb exec NAME`, `cua spaces delete --force NAME`.
- A child macOS or VM computer needs `cua-netgw` next to `cua`; the Local build never bundled it and the refusal quoted a build script. `install-local.sh` now builds and bundles it when Go is installed. A full disk or a missing gateway reaches the agent in words for the person (what is missing, that retrying will not help), not `cua cache prune`.
- Verified in a Local build: an agent's `cua spaces create linux`, `cua sb exec`, then `cua spaces delete --force` from inside a home Space work.

### 3. Child agents in the chat, desktop and phone
Core: events carry `parent_tool_id`; `cua_agents::subagents::fold` derives each subagent (task, running/done/failed, steps, result). The thread records one note when a subagent starts and one when it ends, and one for each child Space made while the agent works; the live row carries the running ones. Web and phone fold a subagent's notes into one quiet row (title, state, steps, result behind a disclosure) and show a child Space as a row with an Open link. The CLI log indents a subagent's steps.

## Evidence
- Real Claude in a Local build with a separate home: a narrated multi-step turn gave seven separate, ordered messages; a subagent turn gave the start note, a finished note with its result and the agent's use of it.
- Tests: `agent_all_messages.rs` (8: order, no duplicates, a message after the turn ended, late `thread_reply`, the same reply run twice, a silent turn, subagent notes and the live row), `subagents.rs` (7), `children/api.rs` (3), a spacesd test that every child-Space tool is classified, web and phone fold tests.
- `durable_member_wiring` has two failures that are the same on `origin/main`.

Not verified: the phone layout was checked by tests only; a child macOS computer was not run (disk).

title: fix(spaces-mobile): send the registered one-slash OAuth redirect
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: Sign-in on the Cua Spaces phone app fails. The cua.ai sign-in sheet shows "Invalid parameter: redirect_uri" and the user cannot sign in. The app sends `redirect_uri=ai.cua.spaces://oauth/callback` (two slashes), because `expo-auth-session`'s `makeRedirectUri({ scheme, path })` always puts `//` after a custom scheme. The `cua-spaces-mobile` client accepts exactly `ai.cua.spaces:/oauth/callback` (one slash), as `apps/cua-spaces-mobile/docs/SETUP.md` and `src/auth/config.ts` already say.
- What changed: The app builds the redirect from the configured scheme and path with one slash (`ai.cua.spaces:/oauth/callback`) and sends that same value in the authorization request and in the code exchange. The scheme in `app.json` (`ai.cua.spaces`) is unchanged, so the callback still opens the app.

## Related work

No issue. Before opening this, I searched open and closed issues and pull requests (`redirect_uri`, `oauth/callback`, `makeRedirectUri`, `spaces-mobile` sign-in). I also checked `src/auth/session.ts` in the 82 open pull requests created since 1 Nov 2026. None of them changes the redirect, and `main` at 39ae68a still sends two slashes.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): Not required. This is an app-internal bug fix.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Phone sign-in against `auth.cua.ai` works again. There are no API, CLI, MCP, protocol or permission changes. A staging or custom issuer (`EXPO_PUBLIC_CUA_OIDC_ISSUER`) must register the same one-slash redirect, which `docs/SETUP.md` already requires.
- Risk and rollback: Low. The change is one line in `src/auth/session.ts` plus one test. To roll back, revert this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - New `__tests__/session-signin.test.ts` drives `session.signIn()` through a mocked `expo-auth-session`. It checks that the `AuthRequest` and `exchangeCodeAsync` both get `ai.cua.spaces:/oauth/callback`.
    - Before the fix (current `main`), it fails:
      ```
      -   "redirectUri": "ai.cua.spaces:/oauth/callback",
      +   "redirectUri": "ai.cua.spaces://oauth/callback",
      ```
    - After the fix, it passes.
  - `pnpm typecheck` passes.
  - `pnpm test` (all of `apps/cua-spaces-mobile`): 32 suites passed, 1 skipped; 179 tests passed, 1 skipped.
  - `bin/ci` and `bin/ci --quick` pass (SPDX headers, image refs).
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - Provider check (6 Nov 2026, reproducible without an account). This sends the authorization request the app sends (client `cua-spaces-mobile`, PKCE S256) and changes only the redirect:
    ```sh
    for r in 'ai.cua.spaces://oauth/callback' 'ai.cua.spaces:/oauth/callback'; do
      enc=$(python3 -c 'import sys,urllib.parse;print(urllib.parse.quote(sys.argv[1],safe=""))' "$r")
      curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$r -> HTTP %{http_code}\n" \
        "https://auth.cua.ai/realms/cyclops-cs/protocol/openid-connect/auth?client_id=cua-spaces-mobile&redirect_uri=$enc&response_type=code&scope=openid&state=probe&code_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeKt8URWbuGjSaR2YsKk&code_challenge_method=S256"
    done
    ```
    - Before (two slashes): HTTP 400, page "Sign-in didn't finish" with "Invalid parameter: redirect_uri".
    - After (one slash): HTTP 200, the "Sign in to Cua Spaces" login form.
  - iPhone (6 Nov 2026): I installed a build of `apps/cua-spaces-mobile` from `main` on a physical iPhone.
    - Before: "Sign in" opened the sign-in sheet, and it showed "Invalid parameter: redirect_uri".
    - After, with this change: sign-in finished, the app returned from the sheet, and the phone enrolled and listed its computers.
    - That device build also carried unrelated local patches (a custom relay setting). Those patches are not part of this pull request.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - No GitHub workflow runs the `apps/cua-spaces-mobile` Jest suite (`spaces-mobile` in `.github/ci-areas.json` maps only to docs links and license checks), so the tests above are local runs.
  - Android was not tested on a device. It uses the same `ai.cua.spaces` scheme from `app.json`.
  - `pnpm proto:check` reports drift in `host_pb.ts` and `tunnel_pb.ts`. The same drift is on unmodified `main`, and this change does not touch protos.

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

title: fix(spaces): say This PC (not This Mac) for the current computer on Windows
body:
## What
The Cua Spaces UI called the current computer "This Mac" / "on this Mac" / "your Mac" on Windows (Agents page "On This Mac", resource warnings, Settings, nudges, CLI columns...). It now says "This PC" on Windows, "This machine" on Linux (the existing convention in `host-os.ts`, `SpaceOs::this_machine`), and keeps "This Mac" on macOS.

## How (driven by the host OS the shell reports, no UA sniffing)
- **Core answers, one place:** `apps/cua-spaces-web/src/bridge/host-words.ts` words every string of an app-core answer for `hostOs()` (Electron's `process.platform`) where `wasmCore.call` hands it to the page. Only the phrases that mean this computer ("This Mac", "this Mac", "your Mac") are replaced. Text about macOS itself (Lume, Keychain, Finder, Xcode, Intel, Touch ID, Apple), "Mac mini" and other Macs are left alone. Display only: nothing is written back, so a Mac user's stored names are untouched and a Windows user's stored "This Mac" displays as "This PC".
- **Web strings that were hardcoded:** Agents page and empty state, empty home, Driver page, Settings quick set-up error, resources (low-disk warning, "uses about X on ..."), add-computer sheet name, first-run default place, the this-computer desktop chat error, the "can't make a Space" toast: now use `thisComputerLabel()/thisComputerText()` (host-labels).
- **Desktop shell:** the Space-ready notification says "this PC" on Windows (was "this machine").
- **CLI/Rust:** `cua_spaces::resources::words::Host` (Mac/Pc/Other); the low-disk warning, `cua host status` "This PC" block and the `DISK ON THIS PC` column follow the system the binary runs on (`warning_on`, `header_on`, `this_mac_lines_on` take the host; the old functions use `Host::current()`). The clap help no longer names "THIS MAC".

## Choices
Linux says "This machine" (what `SpaceOs::this_machine` and `THIS_MACHINE` already use), not "This computer".
Left on purpose: macOS-only copy (Keychain, Lume, teleport, Local Network, notch, SwiftUI app), demo adapters and fixtures, JSON/API keys and ids (`thisMac`, `this-mac`). `cua-vmm` `auto.rs` wording ("this Mac's own container engine") is owned by the managed-runtime PR; `storage.rs` volume naming is in #6724.

## Tests
- Vitest: `bridge/__tests__/host-words.test.ts` (mac/windows/linux, exclusions, key/immutability, through the real wasm core with `navigator.platform` Mac/Win32/Linux); desktop `space-ready.test.ts` (win32/linux). Full web suite: green except pre-existing Windows-only failures (CRLF in `bridge-shapes.json`) and a load-sensitive timing test that passes alone.
- Rust: `resources::words` tests for all three hosts (these run on Linux CI: `cua-spaces` lib tests do not compile on Windows), `cua-cli` `resources_view` tests (5 pass here) for Mac and PC.
- `bin/ci --quick`: all pass except SPDX headers, which fail the same way on a clean main checkout (see #6724).

Verified visually in the running Cua Spaces Local on Windows (screenshots in the PR thread).

title: [Bug]: Cua Volume on a bucket without versioning (Cloudflare R2) reads old cached bytes after another machine rewrites a file
body:
### Primary area

Other (Cua Volume, libs/cua/crates/cua-volume)

### Summary

When Cua Volume uses an S3-compatible bucket that has no object versioning (Cloudflare R2), a machine that has read a file once keeps serving those old bytes from its block cache after another machine rewrites the file. On macOS the mount shows the new size, but the content is the old bytes followed by zero bytes, so the file looks empty or damaged. `cua volume cat` on the same machine shows the correct content.

### Reproduction

1. Point two machines at one R2 bucket: `cua volume config set --backend s3 --endpoint https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com --region auto --bucket <bucket>`, keys through `cua volume config set-keys`. R2 does not offer bucket versioning.
2. On machine A (Linux): `python3 -c "import sys;sys.stdout.write('version-1 '*20)" | cua volume put public/t/a.txt -` (200 bytes).
3. On machine B (macOS), read it through the mount once: `xxd ~/"Cua Volume"/public/t/a.txt`. This fills B's block cache.
4. On machine A: write a longer version to the same path: `'version-2 '*60` (600 bytes).
5. On machine B, after the change feed delivers the change (10 s, and again 45 s later), read through the mount again, and with `cua volume cat public/t/a.txt`.

It happens every time.

### Expected behavior

The mount on machine B shows the new content (600 bytes of `version-2 `), the same as `cua volume cat`.

### Actual behavior

The mount on machine B stayed wrong at both 10 s and 45 s after each write. `cua volume cat` on machine B was correct every time.

```
v1  200 bytes  first read on B, correct: md5 8f7fabf6d6daba897e17413f8d9cf0b3

v2  600 bytes  correct md5 5f5f50e76a422d98b1dbad3ae49242d6 (cat on B matches)
    mount on B: size 600, md5 1d9885a1ca9523e930b3a870e50d809e
    00000000: 7665 7273 696f 6e2d 3120 7665 7273 696f  version-1 versio
    00000250: 0000 0000 0000 0000                      ........

v3   30 bytes  correct md5 7a0b303c1aec057b4b15b00be803f833 (cat on B matches)
    mount on B: size 30, md5 cb3d2ef45cf6844a04c812b7e3941503
    00000000: 7665 7273 696f 6e2d 3120 7665 7273 696f  version-1 versio
    00000010: 6e2d 3120 7665 7273 696f 6e2d 3120       n-1 version-1
```

The v2 md5 is exactly the 200 bytes of v1 plus 400 zero bytes. The v3 md5 is exactly the first 30 bytes of v1.

Other cases I measured:

- **Same-size rewrite (200 to 200 bytes):** the mount on B kept the old content (md5 `1e8999e2d8e621aeaa43446054613807`, `cat` gives `59bebf3bce5b31aa18fccaf1817b36f5`). The size does not change and there are no zero bytes, so nothing shows the file is wrong.
- **Write through machine A's FUSE mount instead of `cua volume put`:** same result on B (size 600, md5 `fc91e232f3b989b0e697d8ea7249fe9b`, which is the old 200 bytes plus 400 zero bytes).
- **Controls, both correct on B:** a file B had not read before the rewrite, and a file whose first version was 0 bytes.
- **macOS page cache:** a read on B with `F_NOCACHE` returned the same old bytes, so this does not look like the NFS client's cache.
- **The machine that wrote the file (Linux FUSE mount, machine A), so this does not need a second machine:** 35 s after `put` of a 600-byte rewrite, `stat` gave 600 and a read returned the old 200 bytes. Reads right after each `put` failed with `Input/output error`, and the first version read correctly at 35 s.

Version ids:

- `cua volume put` prints an id for each write: `7e5e4dca1a08e5c8a28bc8bf2310fac2` (v1), `7e5e4dc9d8c6e300b5a22caec87667a6` (v2), `7e5e4dc9044ccefc1690321de773542d` (v3).
- `cua volume history` fails: `NotImplemented: ListObjectVersions not implemented`.
- `cua volume cat --version <id>` with an id from `put` fails: `NotImplemented: versionId not implemented`.

### Environment

- Cua Spaces 0.22.0 (`cua` 0.10.1, `cua-spacesd` 0.12.1) on macOS arm64 (Volume mounted over the localhost NFS server) and on Linux cua-spaces 0.21.0 (`cua` 0.10.1, `cua-spacesd` 0.12.2), aarch64, Ubuntu 24.04 (Volume mounted over FUSE).
- cua-volume is unchanged from cua-spaces-v0.21.0 through cua-spaces-v0.21.1 and main (39ae68a).
- Store: Cloudflare R2 (`--region auto`), no bucket versioning.

### Evidence

Unit test that reproduces it without a bucket: a test backend over `FsBackend` that returns empty version ids (as `S3Backend::head` appears to on R2, `out.version_id().unwrap_or_default()`) and reports `remote() = true`, two devices on it with their own block caches and change feeds. Device A writes `{"v":1}`, device B reads it through its `Vfs`, A writes a longer version, B waits for the new size, then reads. On main it fails:

```
assertion `left == right` failed: the Mac read stale cached bytes
  left: "{\"v\":1}"
 right: "{\"v\":2,\"name\":\"Ada\",\"model\":\"opus\"}"
```

Why, as far as I can tell from the code:

- `cache::block_id` keys a block by backend identity, key, version and block index.
- On R2 a `put` returns a version id, but `Vfs::read` takes its version from `head`, and the reads behave as if that id is `""` (I did not capture the `head` response directly). So every content of a key gets the same block ids.
- `Vfs::read` pins the new object (`head`: new size), then `Streamer::read` hits the old block in `BlockCache::read`. It returns the old bytes. The read of the rest returns nothing with `eof = false`, and the macOS NFS client fills the rest of the file size with zeros. A shorter rewrite returns the old bytes cut to the new size.
- `Vfs::ensure_dirty` copies the current content through the same path, so an in-place edit on B can also write the stale bytes back to the bucket.
- The `Input/output error` right after a `put` looks like the same missing versioning by a different path: the writer pins the id from `put` (`PIN_TTL` is 30 s), and R2 refuses a read with that id. The empty-id fix below would not cover it.

### Workaround and additional context

- Workaround: a bucket with versioning on (AWS S3, MinIO). I found none for R2.
- The app's Settings > Storage refuses a bucket with versioning off (`versioning_off`), but `cua volume config set --backend s3` accepts it without a warning, and `versioning_help` describes R2 as working without history.
- Possible fix (I can open a PR): when a version id is empty or `"null"`, `Streamer::read` reads the range from the store instead of the block cache. A fuller fix could key such blocks by etag and fetch them with `If-Match`.
- I searched open and closed issues and pull requests (Volume, R2, NFS, empty, truncate, stale, cache, sync) and found no report of this. Related but different: #6321 / #6322, #6238, #5795.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep idle-end launch ownership only until a terminal end
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: after the 5-minute idle sweep, `kill_app` refused a process the same session label had launched, with `foreign_process_termination_denied`. #6553 fixed that by keeping a session's launch records across an idle end. Review of #6553 found three ways the kept records could outlive or erase their lifecycle. This PR ships #6553 with those three fixed.
- What changed:
  - An idle end leaves a session dormant, not finished. Every later terminal end runs the end hooks again with its own reason and drops the records: `end_session`, transport teardown and revocation. Before this, teardown and revocation listed only live sessions and skipped idled ones. A terminal end also overrides an idle end that is still waiting on an in-flight dispatch.
  - Each isolated browser keeps its launch fingerprint. Browser ownership is re-proved against the live process, not the pid alone. Reaping the browser removes only its own record, so a later `launch_app` that reused the pid keeps its record.
  - Revival is refused while an end's cleanup is still pending. This covers `start_session` and the next-call recreation of an unnamed session. So an end's cleanup can no longer erase the launches of the episode that revived it. An idle cleanup pass that a terminal end overtakes also runs the terminal hooks. Capture-scope clearing now happens inside that tracked cleanup.

## Related work

Salvaged from #6553 (AlexFalher). Their commit is cherry-picked with `-x` and keeps its author. The follow-up commits are separate.

Refs CUA-3651

RFC: not required. No SDK, CLI, MCP or protocol change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: a session idled out and restarted with the same label can kill what it launched. Ending it, closing its transport or revoking it afterwards drops that ownership. Shared core, so macOS, Windows and Linux behave the same.
- Risk and rollback: this touches the session-end state machine (end hooks, revival admission). A revival that races an unfinished end now gets the existing `session cleanup is incomplete` refusal and must retry. Before this, it could succeed early. Rollback is a revert.
- Size: production lines exceed the target because the end-hook rerun and the revival barrier both have to change in `session.rs`.

## Validation

- Focused tests: seven regression tests cover terminal ends after an idle end, browser pid reuse, end/revival races and a deferred idle end. Each one fails on the code before its fix and passes after.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `cua-driver-core`, `platform-macos`, `cua-driver-sdk` and `cua-driver`, plus `cargo check --workspace --tests`.
- macOS: the Lume guest full matrix passed at the PR head (183 cells).
- Known gaps: Linux and Windows platform tests and desktop E2E did not run here. They are left to CI.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep polling macOS grants after the permissions gate times out
body:
## Why

CUA-3664. If Accessibility or Screen Recording was not granted within the macOS permissions gate's 10-minute deadline, the daemon stayed gated until it was restarted. `wait_for_grants` returned an error at the deadline, `main.rs` cleared the pending flag only when the gate passed, and stderr told the user to restart the daemon. Now a timed-out gate keeps polling in the background, so a later grant opens tool calls in the running daemon.

## What changed

- `serve::settle_permission_gate` now owns the pending flag after the gate. A pass clears it right away. A timeout starts a `cua-permissions-poll` thread that clears it once the wait succeeds. `main.rs` makes one call to it.
- `GateOpts::after_timeout()` returns the options for that wait: no deadline, a fresh helper-process probe every 5s, and a status line every 5 minutes.
- The timeout message no longer tells the user to restart. It says tool calls stay gated while the daemon keeps checking.

## Scope

Covers only the macOS serve gate after its deadline. The daemon still never runs a TCC preflight in its own process. Each poll uses the short-lived helper probe, as before. Moving the gate check into `SdkAdapter::invoke_raw` (the MCP bypass) is a separate ticket.

## Blast Radius

Affects only macOS `serve` launches that hit the gate deadline. Those launches used to stay gated until restarted. Now they keep one more thread that starts a probe child process every 5s until both grants arrive. The opt-out, embedded and already-granted paths return `Ok`, so they never start the thread.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks for `platform-macos` and `cua-driver` passed on macOS: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings` on all targets, and the full test suites.
- New tests: `wait_after_timeout_picks_up_a_late_grant` drives the wait with an injected probe, and `a_late_grant_reopens_tool_calls_without_a_restart` covers the pass, never-granted and late-grant paths through the pending-response check. Two mutations turn the second test red: dropping the clear in the poll thread, and restoring the old terminal timeout.
- Not run: the macOS Lume lane, because another run held the Lume lock, and a real post-timeout TCC grant in a guest. Linux and Windows are not affected.

title: Windows: Cua Spaces manages its own container runtime (WSL 2 distribution with Docker)
body:
Cua Spaces on Windows now owns its container engine, the way the macOS app and Docker Desktop do: when no engine is reachable, the first Linux Space provisions and starts a Cua-managed one. Nothing to install first, no "install Docker Desktop".

Before: onboarding showed "This PC cannot run container Spaces: container engine: Socket not found: //./pipe/dockerDesktopLinuxEngine; missing: a running container engine" with the Linux option greyed out.

## Design

The macOS built-in runtime (`cua-vmm::managed`, Colima/Lima) gets a Windows backend, `managed_wsl.rs`. Everything above it (Choice/auto, `ManagedContainers`, idle stop, doctor, `runtime.linux` setting, New Space's `managed` backend) is shared, so the UI and `cua` CLI behave as on a Mac.

- **What is provisioned:** a WSL 2 distribution `cua-runtime-<tag>`, imported (`wsl --import`) from a pinned, SHA-256 checked Alpine minirootfs (4 MB). One-time setup installs Docker Engine, socat and iptables from Alpine's repository (about 90 MB). `<tag>` is a digest of the cua home, so a released Cua Spaces and Cua Spaces Local (`~/.cua-local`) get separate distributions, disks and pipes. Disk: `<cua home>\runtimes\linux\wsl`.
- **How it starts:** on demand by the first create (`ensure()`), idempotent (each step is skipped when done; the distribution/engine check is cached for 30 s). A hidden `wsl.exe -d <distro> --exec dockerd` keeps Docker and the distribution alive and outlives the daemon; a restarted daemon re-attaches. Idle stop after the last Linux Space (120 s) terminates only this distribution.
- **How Windows reaches it:** the named pipe `\.\pipe\cua-engine-<tag>`, served by the cua daemon (remote clients rejected, default per-user security); each connection runs `socat` in the distribution against Docker's unix socket. No TCP port. `ContainerRuntime` connects unchanged.
- **Isolation:** never starts, stops, unregisters or edits any other distribution (every `--terminate`/`--unregister` is guarded by the `cua-runtime-` prefix) and never touches Docker Desktop, `~/.cua` of a released install, or `.wslconfig` / the default distribution. The distribution has `automount` and `interop` off, so root in it cannot read Windows files (consequence: Windows folder mounts into a Space are refused with a clear message). Bridge networks use 10.230.0.0/24 and 10.231.0.0/16, away from WSL's 172.x.
- **When it cannot run:** doctor / `cua runtime setup` / New Space say exactly what to turn on: WSL not installed (`wsl --install --no-distribution`, restart), Virtual Machine Platform / WSL feature off, virtualization off in firmware, kernel update needed. New Space shows that reason (and "Open Windows Features") instead of offering the Docker Desktop installer.
- **Disk space:** before setup the existing disk guard (`CUA_DISK_MIN_FREE`, default 5 GiB kept free) is asked about the drive holding the cua home; doctor reports `not enough disk space to set up the built-in Linux runtime: it needs about 2.0 GiB and cua keeps 5.0 GiB free, but only 3.0 GiB is available on F:` before anything downloads.
- **Settings:** `runtime.linux` as on a Mac: `auto` (a working system engine, e.g. Docker Desktop, is used as is; else built-in), `builtin`, `system`.

Differences: from Docker Desktop: no GUI/CLI/Kubernetes, no Windows drive mounts, memory/CPU are WSL's (`.wslconfig`). From macOS: Spaces run under runc (no gVisor yet), and the VM is WSL's, shared with the user's other distributions (Docker's iptables rules live in that shared network namespace).

Independent of #6631 (based on main; that PR's WSL code assumes an existing distribution, this one imports its own). `bin/ci` and `install-local.ps1` come from their own PRs (#6721 etc.); this PR does not depend on them.

## Verified on a Windows 11 PC (WSL 2.6.0, existing Ubuntu/docker-desktop/archlinux distros untouched), isolated `CUA_HOME`

- `cua-local runtime doctor` with no engine: `container notapplicable ... Socket not found: //./pipe/dockerDesktopLinuxEngine` (the screenshot's text) and `managed installable ... set up on first use, about 93 MB`.
- `cua-local sb create alpine:3.20 --runtime runc --no-spacesd -- sleep 3600`: provisioned (download, import, `apk add`, start dockerd) and created in 13.6 s total; `cua-runtime-c3f829a2` appeared in `wsl -l -v`, the default distro stayed Ubuntu.
- `cua-local sb create linux --headless`: pulled the image through the pipe and was ready in 62 s; `sb exec ... uname -srm` printed `Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64`, Ubuntu 24.04; `sb ls` from a new process saw both Spaces (re-attach); both deleted.
- `CUA_DISK_FAKE_AVAILABLE=3GB cua-local runtime doctor` shows the disk refusal above.
- Unit tests (cua-vmm `managed`/`auto`, desktop `local-runtime`), `cargo fmt --check`; the desktop typecheck is clean.

## Known limits

- gVisor is not installed in the distribution yet (runc); checkpoints are filesystem-only.
- Images without cua-spacesd need `cua-spacesd-linux-x86_64` next to `cua` (not built by `install-local.ps1`); the official `linux` image has it.
- microVM runtimes on Windows, a Windows benchmark harness and free-space warnings while running are not in this PR.
- A few pre-existing cua-vmm/cua-cli tests fail on a Windows host for unrelated reasons (no `sh`/`touch`, CRLF checkouts); not changed here.

title: fix(cua-driver): count text typed over a selection as inserted on Windows
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, `type_text` over a selection types the end of the text twice when the replaced value ends the same way. In Notepad holding `hello from cua`, select all then `type_text {"text":"set by cua"}` leaves `set by cua cua`. The tail repair added in #6341 diffs the field before and after: `inserted_segment` strips the common prefix and the common suffix of the two values, so the ` cua` the new text shares with the old one is taken for untouched old text, only `set by` counts as landed, and ` cua` is retyped.
- What changed: when the whole requested text follows the common prefix in the value read back, it is all counted as inserted; the common-suffix strip only runs otherwise, so a genuinely dropped tail over a selection is still retyped.

```diff
     let p = b.iter().zip(a.iter()).take_while(|(x, y)| x == y).count();
+    if a[p..].starts_with(requested) {
+        return requested.iter().collect();
+    }
     let s = b[p..]
```

Seen on the 0.40.2 release binary from a CLI that sets a legacy Edit's value as select all + type:

```
$ cua state -q "Text Editor"
  0 Edit "Text Editor" value='hello from cua'
$ cua set 0 "set by cua"
[set 0 Edit "Text Editor" 'set by cua'] unverifiable: Sent 10 char(s) to pid 6760 via PostMessage (the field changed and now contains the requested text ...)
$ cua state -q "Text Editor"
  0 Edit "Text Editor" value='set by cua cua'
```

## Test

- `tail_retry_tests::text_typed_over_a_selection_that_shares_its_tail_is_complete`: `("hello from cua", "set by cua", "set by cua")` is `Done`; `("hello from cua", "set by", "set by cua")` still retypes ` cua`. The existing four tail-retry tests are unchanged.

title: fix(cua-volume): read current content on a bucket without versioning
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On a bucket without object versioning (Cloudflare R2), a machine that has read a file once keeps serving those bytes after another machine rewrites the file. The mount shows the new size with the old content: padded with zero bytes when the file grew (first noticed as a file that looked empty), cut off when it shrank, and unchanged when the size stayed the same. Reads right after a write on the same machine fail with an I/O error for up to 30 s (`PIN_TTL`). Saving a file through the mount after reading it there can write the stale copy back to the bucket.
- Cause: R2 answers a write with a version id, refuses reads by that id (`versionId not implemented`), and reports no id on HEAD and listings. The block cache keys blocks by version id, so every content of a key shared the empty id. The VFS also pinned the id a write returned, so the next read asked the store for a version it cannot serve.
- What changed:
  - `Streamer::read` reads the range from the store, without the block cache and read-ahead, when the version id is empty or `"null"`. Versioned stores still use the cache.
  - `Vfs::invalidate_key` no longer pins the version id a write returned. The next read pins what the store reports (one HEAD).

## Related work

Fixes #6737

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): Not required. Internal to `cua-volume`; no public API, CLI, MCP or protocol change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Mounts on a bucket without versioning show the current content of files other machines change, and a file reads back right after it is written. On such a bucket, reads no longer use the block cache, so repeated reads of large files go to the store. Versioned stores (AWS S3, MinIO with versioning, the local `fs` store) keep the cache. Old blocks already in a machine's cache under an empty id are never read again; nothing needs clearing.
- Risk and rollback: Low. Two functions change; no public signature changes. The cost on versioned stores is one HEAD on the first read after a local write, instead of reusing the write's version id. To roll back, revert this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - New tests in `vfs.rs` use `NoVersions`, a test backend over `FsBackend` that behaves like R2: a write answers with a fresh version id, reads by version fail with `versionId not implemented`, and HEAD and listings report no id. It is remote, so the block cache is in front of it.
    - `another_devices_rewrite_reads_whole_on_a_bucket_without_versions`: device A writes `{"v":1}`, device B reads it through its `Vfs`, A writes a longer and then a shorter version, B waits for the new size through the change feed and reads. On main it fails:
      ```
      assertion `left == right` failed: the Mac read stale cached bytes
        left: "{\"v\":1}"
       right: "{\"v\":2,\"name\":\"Ada\",\"model\":\"opus\"}"
      ```
    - `a_file_reads_back_right_after_it_is_written_on_a_bucket_without_versions`: a file written through the `Vfs` (create, write, flush), and a file written by a tool call, are read back through the `Vfs` at once. On main it fails with `Backend("versionId not implemented")` (EIO on a mount).
    - Both pass with this change.
  - `cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -p cua-volume`: 99 unit tests and the replica integration tests (20 + 7) pass. The FUSE, macOS NFS and MinIO suites are opt-in and did not run.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-volume --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p cua-volume -- --check` and `scripts/spdx-headers.py --fsl --check` pass.
  - Rerun on macOS arm64 with the pinned Rust 1.97.1 from a clean export of this commit: `cargo test --locked -p cua-volume --lib` passes all 99 unit tests. With only the `stream.rs` change undone, the first test above fails with the assertion shown.
- Manual or platform evidence: The bug is reproduced on two real machines in #6737 (an R2 bucket, Cua Spaces 0.22.0 on macOS arm64 over NFS and 0.21.0 on Linux over FUSE). This change was not yet run on those machines.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - The full run above (integration tests, clippy, fmt, SPDX) used Rust 1.97.0; the repo pins 1.97.1. Only the unit tests were rerun on 1.97.1.
  - `bin/ci` was not run in full: its clippy step builds four more crates that depend on `cua-volume`. No public signature in `cua-volume` changed.
  - Not tested against a live R2 or an unversioned AWS bucket.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse MCP requests before initialize on HTTP and envelope transports
body:
## Why

MCP requires `initialize` before any other request. The opt-in envelope stream and the daemon's HTTP listener both dispatched `tools/call` without it (CUA-3665). The stdio adapters already refuse it through `ProtocolSession`.

## What changed

- `mcp_envelope.rs`: the stream holds a `ProtocolSession`. A request other than `initialize` that comes first gets `-32602` with its id and never reaches tool dispatch or the envelope receiver.
- `mcp_http.rs`: a successful `initialize` mints an `Mcp-Session-Id` header. Every later request with an id must carry a live one. A missing id gets HTTP 400 and an unknown one HTTP 404, the spec's signal to initialize again. Both carry a JSON-RPC `-32600` error with the request id. Notifications still get 202.

## Scope

Covers the two transports named in CUA-3665. Leaves out SSE, `DELETE` session termination, and the per-connection tool-session lifetime on HTTP. stdio and cua-spacesd's `/mcp` already gate on `initialize` and are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

A gate keyed to the TCP connection would have been smaller. But pooled HTTP clients reconnect after initializing, and their next call would have been refused, so the gate is keyed to the MCP session instead. The registry keeps the newest 256 ids. A client whose id falls out gets 404 and initializes again.

## Blast Radius

HTTP clients that never send `initialize`, or drop the `Mcp-Session-Id` header, are now refused. The in-repo carrier (`cua-driver-sdk` `remote_mcp`) initializes first, and nothing else in the repo uses `CUA_DRIVER_RS_MCP_HTTP_PORT`. `ping` before `initialize` is refused, as on stdio.

## Verification

- New tests on both transports refuse `tools/call`, `tools/list` and `cua/driver/v1/open` before `initialize` and serve them after it. On HTTP, the session carries across new connections. With each gate disabled, its test fails.
- Live daemon on macOS, HTTP: no session gives 400, a forged session 404, a notification 202, and `initialize` 200 with the header. A `tools/call` with that id on a new connection gives 200.
- Live `cua-driver mcp --socket` with envelopes on: `tools/call` and `cua/driver/v1/open` before `initialize` get `-32602`, and both succeed after it.

Size: 97 production lines added. The HTTP session registry and its header plumbing account for most of them.

title: ci(spaces): wait for cua.ai's release snapshot instead of failing every release (CUA-3128)
body:
For users: a Cua Spaces release no longer gets a red CD run just because the download page updates a few minutes after the release.

**Problem.** The "cua.ai serves the new release" job failed for 0.21.0 (run 42212057241) and is about to fail for 0.21.1 (run 42267854747). The download links and `/download/info` follow the release at once. But the page's HTML takes its version from trycua/cloud's release snapshot, and that only changes when cloud's snapshot PR merges and the site redeploys. Nothing told cloud that a release had shipped, so the snapshot waited for its half-hourly cron. For 0.21.0, the snapshot PR opened 2 minutes after the 15-minute check gave up, and merged 13 minutes after that.

**Fix.** Before it checks, the job mints the release app token (the same one `request-staging-smoke` uses) and sends the `cua-spaces-released` dispatch that cloud's `update-spaces-release-snapshot.yml` already listens for. It then waits up to 40 minutes, which covers the PR checks, auto-merge and the deploy. The job timeout goes from 20 to 50 minutes. The dispatch is best effort, so the cron is still the fallback.

Refs CUA-3128.

title: fix(spaces): stop the video reporter when the host removes its handler
body:
## Problem

Sentry CUA-SPACES-DESKTOP-3 (`InvalidAccessError`, an unhandled rejection from `VideoSlotReporter.flush`) has been firing since 29 Oct on every channel and nearly every release from 0.17 to 0.21.0 (stable).

## Root cause

In the SwiftUI app, `WebUIWindowController.windowWillClose` calls `removeAllScriptMessageHandlers()`, but the page behind the closed window keeps running. WebKit's `webkit.messageHandlers.cuaVideo.postMessage` returns a promise, and once the handler is removed that promise rejects with `InvalidAccessError`. The reporter's 400 ms poll, ResizeObserver and animation-frame paths kept posting and never looked at the returned promise, so each tick raised an unhandled rejection.

Reproduced in a real WKWebView with a small Swift harness (handler registered, then `removeAllScriptMessageHandlers()` on the live page). Running the real reporter bundle in it:

- before: 3 messages sent while the handler existed, then every poll/frame after removal raised an unhandled rejection (2 after 3 s, 4 after 6 s, still counting);
- after this change: one rejected post, no unhandled rejections, no further posts (poll, frames and observers stopped).

## Fix

- `VideoSlotReporter.send` settles the promise `postMessage` returns (and a synchronous throw). `InvalidAccessError` means the handler is gone for good: the reporter stops its poll, frames and observers and posts nothing more. Any other failure is logged once with `console.warn` and reporting continues.
- `focus` and `surfaces` go through it.
- `VideoHandler.postMessage` is typed as returning `unknown`, which is what WebKit does.

## Tests

Three new vitest cases in `stream-surface.test.tsx`: handler removed (no unhandled rejection, poll and frames stop, one warning), synchronous throw, and a transient failure that keeps reporting. They fail without the change. `bin/ci --quick --fix` passes.

The same cause is filed as CUA-SPACES-DESKTOP-G (the minified frame of a built web UI).

Fixes CUA-SPACES-DESKTOP-3
Fixes CUA-SPACES-DESKTOP-G

title: fix(spaces): survive a process that cannot be inspected; upload nightly dSYMs
body:
## CUA-SPACES-DESKTOP-5 (Electron, Windows)

`executablePath` (used by the daemon supervisor to tell whose daemon is running) called `execFile` inside a promise executor. When spawning throws synchronously, the promise rejects, the supervisor's `pidNow` rejects, and the loop ends in an unhandled rejection (8 events, Windows 10 and 11, 0.17 to 0.19.4). The call is now wrapped: a process that cannot be inspected has no known path. `execFile` is injectable so a test covers the throwing case (`test/daemon-startup.test.ts`).

## Nightly and beta crash reports had no symbols (CUA-SPACES-DESKTOP-2, -H)

`build-app.sh` strips the shipped binaries and keeps their dSYMs, and `cd-cua-spaces.yml` uploads them to Sentry. The nightly path goes through `cd-cua-spaces-build.yml`, which built the same app but never uploaded the dSYMs. Crash reports from nightlies (and any build from that workflow) therefore show system frames only, with the app's own frames unresolved. The macOS build job now runs the same `sentry-upload` step (never fails the build; skipped when the token or DSN is missing).

Not changed: the `strlen` crash reports themselves (two events, no app frame to act on) and the `swift_getObjectType` nightly crash, which need symbols from a build with this change before they can be attributed.

title: feat(spaces): put quiet agent home Spaces to sleep
body:
## What

First slice of "many agent home threads on one Mac come back to idle" (CUA-3661). A Space that a helper made to run a task for you (an agent home) now goes to sleep on its own when nothing is running in it, and wakes when you message its agent.

- New Space setting `cua.sleep` (`never`, `auto`, or a duration), read by `cua_spaces::sleep::Sleep`. A Space with no setting is `never`, so nothing that exists changes. Agent homes made by the ask-first flow are created with `auto`. There is no CLI, SDK or UI for the setting yet; that is the next PR.
- In an `auto` Space an agent run exits after 60 s without a message (it was 30 min). An explicit `idle_exit_secs` and `standby` agents are unchanged. `cua_agents::runs::DEFAULT_IDLE_EXIT_SECS` names the old default.
- The persistent-agent supervisor stops an `auto` Space after it has been quiet for 30 s: no agent has a task or a live run, nothing was started in the guest after boot, and no file was left in the home folder outside the Cua Volume. Anything it cannot read counts as busy, and nothing is killed.
- A message or task for an agent whose Space slept starts the Space first (`Persistent::wake_space`). A home that slept is reused by the next ask-first task instead of making a new one.
- The shared Linux runtime VM already ignored stopped Spaces in `idle_verdict` (only paused ones hold it); this slice makes use of that, and it is the reason the VM now stops after the last home sleeps.

## Measured on a Mac Studio (96 GB), mock provider, isolated home

One home, Claude Code against `cua-mock-llm`, one turn:

| | Today (main) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Space after the turn | running for 8+ min | stopped 116 s after the task was added |
| Linux runtime VM | up for 8+ min | stopped 121 s after the Space stopped |
| Wake: message to reply, Space and VM both stopped | not applicable | 12.8 s |

## Known limits

- A stop loses files a container Space wrote outside the Cua Volume (its root file system is memory-backed). The check above refuses to stop a Space with such files in the home folder; a file elsewhere (for example `/opt`) is not seen. Checkpointing is a later step.
- A harness installed into the Space (`~/.cua`) is cached by the install cache, but the first wake after a stop reinstalls from it; the 12.8 s includes that.
- Only Spaces that have a persistent agent are looked at. Child Spaces and durable or standby agents are left running.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p cua-spaces --lib sleep`, `-p cua-spaces-ext --lib persistent::` (parsing, defaults, probe decision).
- Live: sleep and wake of one home against the mock provider, as in the table.

Tracked in CUA-3661.

title: [Bug]: Foreground pixel actions after an ax_window_unresolved read are refused as "window never read"
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

After `get_window_state` returns `degraded_reason: ax_window_unresolved`, the same response recommends `delivery_mode: "foreground"`. Every window-scope pixel action on that window is then refused with "it has not been read yet", also in the foreground and right after the read.

### Reproduction

1. Open a window the driver cannot match to its AXWindow. For me it was a small untitled System Settings window (260×337), on screen. The driver found 1 AXWindow under the pid, but not this one.
2. `get_window_state({pid, window_id})`
3. `click({pid, window_id, x, y, delivery_mode: "foreground"})` with x,y from that screenshot. `zoom` on the same window fails the same way.

I saw it three times in a row on 31 Oct. Each action used the same session as the read right before it, twice without a label and once with one. A later read was still unresolved.

### Expected behavior

Either the foreground pixel action works as the escalation suggests, or the hint names a route that works and the refusal gives the real reason: no frame is kept after an unresolved read.

### Actual behavior

The read returns `degraded: true`, `element_count: 0`, `screenshot_frame_valid: true` and

```
"escalation": { "recommended": "foreground", "reason": "observation-only: the screenshot in this response IS the requested window, but background input (including px) is refused while its AX surface is unresolved ... Re-snapshot after the app settles, or act with delivery_mode:\"foreground\"." }
```

The click then returns

```
No screenshot of window 18535 in this session: it has not been read yet. Call get_window_state(pid:45829, window_id:18535) and take x,y from that window's own screenshot; pixels read off another window's screenshot do not apply to it.
{ "code": "screenshot_context_missing", "reason": "window_never_read", "pid": 45829, "window_id": 18535 }
```

Doing what the message says gives the same result again.

### Environment

- Cua component and version: cua-driver-rs 0.38.0 (Homebrew cask `cuadriver`, darwin-universal), through `cua-driver mcp`
- Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.0, arm64
- Application: System Settings

### Evidence

The source at cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0 (85e2b13) shows the cause. main has the same code today.

- `get_window_state.rs` removes the window's snapshot when the scope did not match: https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85e2b1318bd77ccf3cfa88ccdf875a4bb7eaed19/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs#L377-L379
- It publishes a new snapshot, and with it the pixel frame, only for `scope_matched && !observation_only`: https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85e2b1318bd77ccf3cfa88ccdf875a4bb7eaed19/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs#L579-L592
- In the same case it recommends foreground: https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85e2b1318bd77ccf3cfa88ccdf875a4bb7eaed19/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs#L781-L788
- `snapshot_store.rs` answers `window_never_read` when the window has no snapshot: https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85e2b1318bd77ccf3cfa88ccdf875a4bb7eaed19/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/snapshot_store.rs#L444-L463
- `click.rs` needs that frame for every x,y click, whatever the delivery mode: https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85e2b1318bd77ccf3cfa88ccdf875a4bb7eaed19/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs#L1031-L1035

So I think the refusal itself is intended, since AX-unresolved is observation-only. Only the hint and the error reason don't match it.

### Workaround and additional context

Calling `get_desktop_state` and then `click` with `scope: "desktop"`, its `capture_id` and `delivery_mode: "foreground"` reached the window. After two such clicks it was gone. `press_key escape` in the foreground on the same window was accepted, but the window stayed.

Related: #3458 (its point 4 is the same foreground escalation, for off-Space windows) and #4138 (the same misleading `screenshot_context_missing` on Sway, closed).

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep a macOS sheet's own id for focus and snapshot scope
body:
## Why

Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6551 by @AlexFalher, whose commit is kept as is. With a sheet open (Finder's Go to Folder, a Save sheet), keys to the window were refused as `window_not_key`, and a request naming the sheet's own id was refused. That PR fixed it by collapsing the sheet into its parent window. Review found two problems with that approach. Keys addressed to the sheet's id could not pass focus confirmation, because the focused-window read reported the parent id. A snapshot scoped to the sheet also walked the parent window's controls. This branch keeps both ids: a sheet answers to its own id and to its parent's.

CUA-3655

## What changed

- `AxWindowId { own, root }` replaces the single collapsed id. `focused_window_id_of_pid`, `KeyFocus` and the element-ancestry checks use `is(id)`, so a focused sheet confirms keys addressed to the sheet or to its parent. A focused parent does not confirm a request addressed to its sheet, and sibling windows are still refused.
- `get_window_state` on a sheet's id walks only the sheet. Parent-window controls, the menu bar and other top-level sheets stay out. Element ancestry follows `AXParent` while the window has a sheet, because AppKit reports a sheet control's `AXWindow` as the parent.
- Unit tests cover sheet-addressed and parent-addressed requests for key focus, ancestry and scope. The AppKit fixture gains a sheet-input mode, and a new macOS e2e row types and presses keys through both ids and checks the sheet snapshot holds only the sheet.

## Scope

macOS `platform-macos` only. `bring_to_front` keeps main's exact-window contract, so a parent behind a modal sheet is still not reported as brought to front (`modal_sheet_never_yields_false_parent_success`). The remote Save panel's own window belongs to the panel service and is still refused under the app's pid. Windows and Linux have no sheets of this kind and are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

#6551 also made `bring_to_front` accept the parent with the sheet in front. That contradicts the existing e2e contract that a modal sheet never yields a false parent success, so this branch restores main's behavior there.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS focused-window and element-window comparison moves from `==` to `is(id)`. For an ordinary window `own == root`, so behavior is unchanged. A sheet now widens only to its own parent window, and only when AX proves that parent.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings` and the `platform-macos` and `cua-driver-core` unit tests pass.
- The macOS Lume full matrix ran at the head. Results are in the verification comment.

Size limit: production code is over budget because every focused-window caller moves to the two-id type in the same change, and the sheet scope needs its own walk.

title: ci(spaces): hand the SwiftUI Rust slice over as an artifact, save its cache right after the build
body:
## Problem

The Cua Spaces nightly fails about every other run, about 1.5 hours in, in `Build / SwiftUI Rust (arm64)` and `(x86_64)`: "The SwiftUI Rust slice is not in the Actions cache although the producer stage just ran". Re-running only the failed jobs does not help; a full re-dispatch often passes.

## Root cause

It is not cache eviction. The slice was never saved.

- The slice action used `actions/cache@v4`, which saves in its post-job phase. Post steps run in reverse order, so `Swatinem/rust-cache` (declared after it) runs its post step first.
- When the dependency cache is not an exact hit, rust-cache saves and first cleans `libs/cua/target`, which deletes `libcua_spaces_ffi.dylib` and `cua-spaces-cli`. The slice cache's post step then logs `Path Validation Error: Path(s) specified in the action for caching do(es) not exist, hence no cache is being saved.`
- When the dependency cache is an exact hit (`Cache hit for: v0-rust-swiftui-rust-...`), rust-cache neither saves nor cleans and the slice is saved (`Cache saved with key: swiftui-rust-v3-...`). That is why runs alternate.
- Evidence: run 42286152225 (arm64 post phase at 22:00:46 saves the 817 MB rust-cache, then "Path Validation Error", and the consumer starts 22:00:56 and misses); run 42157751639 shows the same warning in both producers (which is why rerun-failed cannot help); run 42208940384 shows `Cache saved with key: swiftui-rust-v3-...` in both.

## Fix

- `spaces-rust-slice` action: restore with `actions/cache/restore` and save with an explicit `actions/cache/save` right after the build and checks (`continue-on-error`), so the save no longer depends on post-step order. This also fixes the release build (`cd-cua-spaces.yml`) and the main producer, which use the same action and key (`swiftui-rust-v3` is defined only there).
- Producer (`ci-cua-spaces-rust-slice.yml`) uploads the slice as the workflow artifact `swiftui-rust-slice-<arch>`.
- Shadow/nightly build (`cd-cua-spaces-build.yml`, `macos-rust`) downloads that artifact from the same run; the cache restore is only the fallback, and it still never compiles a second copy.
- Tests updated for the new contract.

## Testing

Contract tests under `.github/scripts/tests` pass locally. The build workflow only runs on main (its Plan job and signing are main-only), so the artifact download is exercised by the next nightly after merge; the producer workflow runs on this PR and exercises the restore, build, save and upload steps.

title: feat(cua-driver): step-by-step permission guide and Screen Recording entry fix (CUA-3660)
body:
**What changes for users:** a newcomer setting up Cua Driver on a Mac now gets a small "Set up Cua Driver" window that takes them through the two macOS switches one at a time, in plain words. Cua Driver now shows up in the Screen Recording list by itself, so nobody has to add it with "+". `cua-driver permissions status` gives a real answer even when Cua Driver isn't running.

Part of [CUA-3660](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3660) (plan item 2: permission guide in CuaDriver.app).

## Root cause: Cua Driver missing from the Screen Recording list

Every request path asked macOS for both permissions back to back: the startup helper (`--cua-internal-permission-probe-request`), the `permissions grant` app host and `check_permissions` called `AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions(prompt)` and then `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` immediately, from short-lived processes that exited right after. With both CLI and app asking, up to four requests went out at once.

macOS shows one privacy prompt at a time. With the Accessibility prompt up, the Screen Recording request was dropped, and because the requesting process exited at once, nothing recorded it either. Cua Driver therefore never appeared under Screen & System Audio Recording, and the person had to click "+", find the app and turn it on, which matches the onboarding audit (fresh macOS 26.4).

Fix:
- **One request at a time, Accessibility first.** `request_next_missing` asks only for the first missing permission. Screen Recording is asked for only once Accessibility is on: by the guide window, by the terminal wait loop, or by `permissions grant` when Cua Driver was already running. Each is asked once.
- **Register reliably.** `request_screen_recording` now calls `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess` and then queries ScreenCaptureKit's shareable content, which goes through the same Screen Recording check and lists the app even if the prompt isn't shown. It waits up to 5 s for that query before the helper exits. It never captures a frame, so it doesn't raise the separate "screenshots without a picker" consent.
- The requests still come from processes attributed to the Cua Driver app: the bundled service's helper child, or the app launched through LaunchServices.

## The guide window

Before, the guide was an opt-in panel (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_PERMISSIONS_PANEL=1`) that listed both permissions with "AX RPC / accessibility tree" copy. It is now on by default for the bundled app (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_PERMISSIONS_PANEL=0` turns it off; bare binaries and headless runs keep the terminal text):

- **Step 1 of 2: Let Cua Driver use your mouse and keyboard** (Accessibility), then **Step 2 of 2: Let Cua Driver see your screen** (Screen Recording). Each step has one sentence on why, "In System Settings, turn on the switch next to Cua Driver.", an **Open System Settings** button for that pane, and a live "Waiting for the switch to turn on…" line, checked every second.
- **Drag tile fallback:** "If Cua Driver isn't in the list, drag this into it:" over a plain card with the app's own icon. Dragging it puts the app on the pasteboard the way dragging it from Finder does. This follows the Cua Spaces guide.
- **Moves on by itself:** when a switch turns on, it shows the next step, asks macOS for Screen Recording and opens that pane.
- **Quit & Reopen:** step 2 says to click Quit & Reopen if macOS asks. A short-lived note (15 min, 0600, per app bundle) remembers the `serve` arguments. When macOS starts the app again with no arguments, it comes back as the same service and shows the finished state. Approval-bypass flags are never replayed.
- Ends with **"All set. Cua Driver can now use this Mac."** and closes itself after about 2 s. "Not Now" or closing the window keeps waiting quietly in the background, as before.
- Native AppKit through `objc2::msg_send!` (rounded push buttons, a small spinner, SF Symbols, a floating panel at the top right so it doesn't cover System Settings). No coloured edge stripes, no italic headline accents. The tile uses the bundle's existing app icon. The Cua logo is unchanged.

Logic lives in a new AppKit-free `permissions/guide.rs` (`GuideMachine`, copy, resume note) so it can be unit tested. The panel and the terminal wait loop both drive it.

Screenshots of the window (run with the new `permission_guide_preview` example, which asks macOS for nothing): step 1 shows "Step 1 of 2", the bold title, the reason in grey, the switch instruction, a spinner with "Waiting for the switch to turn on…", a blue "Open System Settings" button, the drag hint, and the bordered "Cua Driver" tile with the app icon and a hand "Drag" glyph, with "Not Now" at the bottom right. Step 2 has the same layout plus the Quit & Reopen note. The finished state is a green check with "All set. Cua Driver can now use this Mac." and "You can close System Settings." It closed itself as expected.

## `permissions status`

When the service isn't running (or can't answer yet), it now starts the installed app briefly in the background through LaunchServices with a new read-only host flag (`--status-only`), reads the app's own status, and exits. The honesty guarantee is unchanged: the answer is used only when its attribution is `driver-daemon`, never the terminal's. If no reliable answer is possible, it gives exactly one next step: install the app if it's missing, otherwise run `cua-driver permissions grant`. The JSON keeps the no-booleans `unknown` shape for that case and adds `next_step`.

## Plain words

The guide, terminal banner, wait-loop lines, `permissions status`, `permissions grant` and the `--help` lines no longer say TCC, AX, accessibility tree or daemon, and they write "Cua Driver" in prose. The CLI reference abstracts, the quickstart line about prompts, and the troubleshooting row are updated to match.

title: fix(cua-driver): restore the prior X11 foreground after foreground type_text
body:
CUA-3663

The Linux `delivery_mode` docs say a foreground action activates the target, injects, then restores the prior active window. On X11, `with_x11_foreground` activated the target and left it active, so foreground `type_text` took the user's focus and kept it.

## Change

- `with_x11_foreground` takes a `RestoreMode`. `RestorePrevious` holds the foreground transaction, snapshots the X11 focus before activation, and gives the focus back after the body, also when activation or the body failed. It refuses when the prior focus cannot be read.
- `type_text` foreground (all four X11 routes) and the X11 branch of `with_target_foreground` use `RestorePrevious`. Pointer and key tools pass `LeaveFocused` and behave as before: restoring would close a menu the click opened, or move focus away from the widget a following `type_text` needs.
- The restore reuses the background focus guard with the same-app rule off. The target pid is still passed, so a new popup without `_NET_WM_PID` counts as a held grab. The guard compares the exact saved focus: a cleared active window or a None/PointerRoot core focus counts as moved. The call fails when focus moved and did not come back (unless the body closed the prior window) and when the display cannot be opened to restore.
- The focus guard skips the driver's own agent-cursor overlay, which it recognises by XID. Before this change it counted as a grabbing popup.
- New ignored e2e test `x11_foreground_restore_linux_test`, wired into the X11 lane of `scripts/ci/linux/run-rust-e2e.sh`. It maps a prior window and a target, calls `type_text` foreground through cua-driver, and checks that the target received the key presses and that `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW` returned to the prior window.

## Proof

The scoped repository checks: cargo fmt check, clippy with `-D warnings` for platform-linux and cua-driver-e2e, platform-linux tests, a release build of cua-driver, the new e2e test under Xvfb + openbox, and the verify-cua-driver X11 lane. A two-window GTK repro through cua-driver also passed: after foreground `type_text` the prior window was active again, and the text landed in the target. Wayland, macOS and Windows lanes did not run.

Size: about 150 production lines added; the restore needs a new transaction path plus a `RestoreMode` argument at every existing `with_x11_foreground` call site.
