title: feat(cua-driver): capture the KWin desktop through ScreenShot2 behind kwin-capture
body:
Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6451 by @astrovm. Their commits are kept unchanged under their own authorship. On top are one merge and three commits of ours. Linear: CUA-3711.

**Stacked on https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6820.** #6451 carries #6450's window-capture work, and #6820 is our salvage of #6450. This branch is #6820's head (`996968175c`) with #6451 merged in, so until #6820 merges, this diff also shows all of #6820. Merge #6820 first. After that, this PR's own change is the four files under `wayland/` and `docs/kwin-window-capture.md` listed below.

## Why

#6451 makes a KWin desktop screenshot call ScreenShot2 `CaptureWorkspace` before the Screenshot portal, so there is no consent dialog and no portal request to wait on. Review found two problems. First, ScreenShot2 never asks the portal, and the tier ran for every KWin session, so a screenshot Deny saved in the portal no longer stopped a desktop capture. Second, the new route had no automated coverage. Review also asked whether a multi-output workspace image shares a frame with window records and input.

## What changed

- The tier runs only when `kwin_access::allowed()` says yes. That is the `cua-driver kwin-capture` switch #6820 adds for window capture. It is off by default, `on` keeps a saved portal Deny in force, and only `on --override-portal-deny` bypasses that Deny. When the tier is off or KWin refuses, the cascade continues to wlroots, ext-image-copy and the portal as before.
- Frame: with `native-resolution` false, KWin captures `Workspace::geometry()`. That is the union of the outputs' logical rectangles at one pixel per logical pixel, the same bounding box `kwin_layout::frame_of` reads from xdg-output (main's #6821). `get_desktop_state` already rebases KWin window records and desktop input onto that frame. A new test pins the rebase on a layout with an output at negative coordinates, a 1x output, a 2x output and a 1.25x output.
- Tests for the route. The gate gets a unit test. `CaptureWorkspace` runs against a fake ScreenShot2 on a private `dbus-daemon`, which checks the requested options, the pixel decoding and the refusal of a non-raw reply. `capture_workspace` is split so the exchange can be tested without the trusted-compositor owner check. The docs say the tier follows the switch, and a broken `#permissions` link now points at the section that exists.

## Scope

Covers the KWin desktop-capture tier in `screenshot_display_dispatch`, plus its docs. It does not change window capture, the switch itself (#6820), or the GNOME, Hyprland, niri or wlroots tiers.

## Blast Radius

Only KWin sessions that turned `kwin-capture` on reach the new tier. Every other session gets exactly main's desktop cascade. With the switch on, desktop screenshots skip the portal dialog, and a saved portal Deny still keeps them on the portal path.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean. Clippy with `-D warnings` is clean for `platform-linux` and `cua-driver` on aarch64 Linux (cross-built), and for `cua-driver` and `platform-macos` on macOS. The `platform-linux` lib tests ran on a Debian aarch64 host: 976 passed, 0 failed. Each new test failed under a matching mutation (gate dropped, `native-resolution` flipped, raw check dropped).
- Live, on nested KWin 6.3.6 with a single virtual output, the driver ran in five states: off, on, on with a saved portal Deny, `--override-portal-deny`, and off again. At this head KWin was asked only in the on and override states (3 of 3 runs pass). The binary from before this change asked KWin in all five states, Deny included (3 of 7 checks fail).
- Not run: this host's KWin has no OpenGL, so it exports no ScreenShot2 object and no live workspace image was captured. The multi-output, scaled and negative-origin frame is covered by the unit test and by reading KWin's source, not by a live capture. Also not run: `kwin_logical_frame_test` and `kwin_native_capture_test` (they need native KWin with GL), the verify-cua-driver X11 and Wayland lanes, and Windows. The macOS lane doesn't apply because no macOS code changed.

Size: the PR carries #6820 and the contributor's feature in full. Our own commits add about 45 production lines (the gate and the `workspace_image` split).

title: perf(cua-driver): batch type_text key events on Windows and Linux
body:
Brings the macOS `type_text` speedup from #6884 to Windows and Linux X11. `type_text` on those platforms now sends text in batches by default instead of pacing every character.

Refs CUA-3763.

**What changed**
- `delay_ms` now defaults to 0. A positive value keeps one paced key per character.
- Shared contract in `cua-driver-core::type_pacing`: the default, the 0-200 clamp, a chunk planner (batches of up to 16 UTF-16 units, a surrogate pair is never split, Return and Tab stay real key presses) and the 30 ms tail pace.
- Windows, background (`WM_CHAR`): posts a batch, waits for the target to pump, then lets it drain (2 ms per unit). Tab is now a real key press like Return. The existing read-back retypes a dropped tail, now paced at 30 ms.
- Windows, foreground (`SendInput`, `KEYEVENTF_UNICODE`): one `SendInput` per batch with a single drain sentinel, still confirmed as read before the next batch. A positive `delay_ms` now also applies here. UIA ValuePattern (with `element_token`) is unchanged: it is atomic, so `delay_ms` does not apply.
- Linux X11 (XTest and XSendEvent): no per-key pause, and a server round trip every 16 keys. The virtual-keyboard (uinput) route drops its per-step pause and still confirms the last key. `type_text` accepts `delay_ms`.
- Linux Wayland routes (wtype, libei, KWin, Hyprland, niri) already send a whole string or are acknowledgement-paced, so they are unchanged, except that a positive `delay_ms` now sends one character per call.
- Secure fields and IME paths are unchanged: no new routes, only the pacing of existing ones.

**Numbers** (GitHub-hosted runners, 78 characters, p50 of 9 runs; the same bench file runs before and after)

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Windows `WM_CHAR` into an EDIT control (before = `delay_ms` 30, the old default) | 2683 ms | 163 ms |
| Linux X11 XTest (Xvfb) | 789 ms | 0.9 ms |
| Linux X11 XSendEvent (Xvfb) | 790 ms | 1.1 ms |

Linux numbers measure delivery into the X server; they do not include how fast a real toolkit reads the keys. The Windows run confirmed all 78 characters landed in order.

**Tests**
- Core planner: limits, surrogate pairs, keys as their own chunks, full coverage (7 tests, pass).
- Windows: unit tests for Tab, batches and key events pass on a Windows runner; the cross-compiled `cargo xwin` check and clippy are clean. New ignored desktop tests: `bench_post_type_text` (the numbers above) and a Tab-between-batches test.
- Linux: `TypePacing` unit tests pass. New X11 tests: batches deliver every key in order, `delay_ms` paces each key, XSendEvent batches. `text_delivers_distinct_unmapped_keysyms_on_both_paths` now runs paced, because it reads each borrowed keycode's keysym while the key is still borrowed.
- Benchmarks: `platform-linux/tests/type_text_bench_x11.rs`, and `bench_post_type_text` in `platform-windows/src/input/keyboard.rs`.

**Still running, not in this PR:** one more Linux X11 run of the full `key_input_x11` file on this exact head. Its output lands in the log of the latest run on branch `tmp/type-text-bench-3763` (`gh run list --repo trycua/cua --branch tmp/type-text-bench-3763`, job `linux (after)`, step `Detail`). That branch gets deleted once it is read.

**Risks**
- A Windows target slower than 2 ms per character can still hold queued characters after the call returns. The read-back retype only repairs a proven prefix and does not duplicate text, but a target that stalls mid-drain could be mis-read. The uinput and XSendEvent routes have no read-back, so a client that drops fast keys is not repaired.
- Tab on Windows is now a real key press: in a dialog it moves focus instead of inserting a tab.
- The generated tool reference for `delay_ms` changed and may need regenerating in CI.
- Not run: the Linux uinput and Wayland routes (no test host), and the Windows foreground `SendInput` path (needs an interactive desktop).

title: feat(cua-driver): expose macOS search field identity attributes
body:
Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6857 by @lidge-jun, whose commit is kept unchanged with its authorship. Linear: CUA-3754.

## Why

macOS `get_window_state` elements expose only a merged `label` and `value`. A search field named only by `AXPlaceholderValue` therefore looks the same as a composer whose typed text happens to read like a search hint. #6857 adds raw `title`, `description`, `placeholder` and `subrole` keys. Review found that its `AXSubrole` read, plus an `AXPlaceholderValue` read even when `AXValue` is set, ran for every visited node. That includes display-only rows the public `elements` array never shows. Each is a synchronous AX request that spends the walk's time budget. Since #6878, main reads each node in one batched `AXUIElementCopyMultipleAttributeValues` call. `AXSubrole` now joins that batch, and the gate still applies on the per-attribute fallback path used by apps that refuse the batch.

## What changed

- `AXNode` gains `placeholder` and `subrole`, and `element_entry` emits trimmed `title`, `description`, `placeholder` and `subrole` (the #6857 commit).
- `NodeAttr::Subrole` joins the batched node read in `ax/batch.rs`. `read_identity_attrs` in `ax/tree.rs` gates which identity values each node keeps and, on the fallback path, which ones it requests. Indexed nodes read both. Display-only nodes read `AXPlaceholderValue` only as the empty-`AXValue` fallback that main already uses, and never read `AXSubrole`.
- Unit tests check which attributes each kind of node reads, alongside the #6857 schema-conformance and identity tests.

## Scope

Only the macOS walker and `get_window_state` element entries. The label and value fallbacks behave as on main, and no AX request is added for a node that main skipped. Production lines are about +60/-10, within the size limit.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS `get_window_state` and `verify_state` element gains up to four optional keys, which pass the advertised output schema (`search_field_identities_survive_protocol_conformance`). Display-only rows in `verify_state`'s observation array carry `placeholder` only when it is also their value, and never carry `subrole`.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `platform-macos` all pass.
- The macOS Lume full matrix from the verify-cua-driver skill ran at fb68c90e. All cells passed, and the worker was stopped by hand after the wrapper's own stop step failed.
- Instrumented walks of a synthetic AppKit window that is mostly static labels with a few search fields. Before main's batching, #6857 alone read `AXSubrole` and `AXPlaceholderValue` on every node, and with the gate both were read only on the indexed fields. After merging main, the batch answers every node and the walk makes no single-attribute identity reads.

title: microVMs on Windows: QEMU on the Windows Hypervisor Platform, with checkpoints, forks and warm pools
body:
## What

microVM Spaces on Windows: QEMU on the Windows Hypervisor Platform (hardware acceleration only, never TCG), managed like the macOS runtime.

- WHPX detected without elevation (`WHvGetCapability`); one UAC prompt runs `dism /enable-feature HypervisorPlatform` when missing; QEMU installed with winget; pinned kernel; static guest init shipped with the app (TCP link with a per-VM key, since Windows QEMU has no vsock).
- Doctor and New Space say what is missing; the MicroVM option is enabled on Windows hosts; disk-space guard.
- Lifecycle: create, exec, stop (ACPI power-off), start, delete, pause/resume (QMP over an AF_UNIX socket).
- Checkpoint, fork and warm pool, disk-only: WHPX blocks QEMU migration, so no memory snapshots. Scratch disk is a qcow2 over a shared read-only template; a pool member is booted and paused and claimed by hard links.
- Network: QEMU user networking enforces no rules, so a Windows microVM is `NoNetworkOnly` (no network unless the user picks No protection).

## Benchmarks (same harness as cua.ai/compare, `libs/cua/bench/microvm-fork-windows`)

| Row | Mac p50 | Windows p50 |
|---|---|---|
| checkpoint | 650 ms | 308 ms |
| restore | 610 ms | 3970 ms |
| fork of running | 1160 ms | 4052 ms |
| fan-out (4) | 1460 ms | 5202 ms |
| create from warm pool | - | 360 ms |
| memory per fork | 1620 MiB | 684 MiB |

Restore, fork and fan-out stay slower because WHPX cannot save VM memory; details and iteration log in `RESULTS.md`.

## Verification

Unit tests and clippy `-D warnings` for cua-vmm, cua-daemon, cua-spaces-app-core. Verified end to end through the CLI and daemon on this PC (create, exec, stop, start, checkpoint, fork, pool claim). Pre-existing Windows-only test failures (CRLF goldens, exec, qemu args) are unrelated. Real-app GUI verification: pending.

title: test(cua-relay): fix flaky TCP share test (port handed to two parallel tests)
body:
Fixes the flaky `an_edge_carries_tcp_shares_for_its_token_only_and_checks_hosts_and_allowlists` seen in the relay e2e job on #6775 (assert `left: 1, right: 0` on the wrong-host dial).

Cause: five tests in `share_links.rs` pick a port by binding port 0 and dropping it, and the relay binds it later. Parallel tests in one process can get the same port. The second share's listener then fails to bind, and its dial lands in the other test's echo share, so the "dropped" connection reads an echoed byte. Fix: a `free_port()` helper that never hands out the same port twice in the process. No relay code change.

Verification: not reproducible on macOS (0/300 under load before, 0/100 after); the diagnosis comes from reading the code and the CI failure. Users: no change.

title: docs(skills): verify skills drop fixed Spaces gotchas, add the macOS app lane, and scope FAILs to the diff
body:
## Why
A retro over the last two weeks of verify runs on the relay Mac mini and the Linux VM found three problems. The two verify skills told sessions things that are no longer true. The macOS app had no lane, so every first-run session worked out isolation and cleanup again from scratch. And some FAIL verdicts named no defect in the diff. This PR deletes the stale steps first and then adds only what runs kept rediscovering.

## What changed
- **verify-cua-spaces.**
  - Removes four gotchas about bugs fixed by https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6400 and https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6414. On this base, a fresh cua home lists the added Space in `sb ls`, `do switch verify` exits 0, `index` passes, and the viewer streams and takes input with no sound server.
  - Adds `macos-app.md`, a lane for the SwiftUI app's first run. It covers the Local channel and the installed app, pressing by `element_token` instead of pixels, finding system prompt windows, bringing the app to the front before judging the inline viewer, and a cleanup that unregisters the Local driver login item that `uninstall-local.sh` leaves loaded.
- **verify-cua-driver.**
  - The CI proof job passes now, so the "pending" status and the historical offline attempts go.
  - Adds the two Linux host fixes runs kept rediscovering: a writable `/dev/shm`, and `CUA_AT_SPI_BUS_LAUNCHER` on Debian.
  - Adds a compositor-specific lane note and a Verdict section. A FAIL needs a base rerun, and a merge-first dependency is named as one.
  - `macos-lume.md` says what can run focused on main, since `appkit-cells.tsv` isn't there yet. It also covers the disk floor and lock that block runs, and the lume 0.5.3 `stop` bug that marks passing runs incomplete.

## Scope
Docs under `.cursor/skills/verify-cua-driver` and `.cursor/skills/verify-cua-spaces` only. It changes no scripts and no product code. The product bugs these runs found (the Local Network gate, the covered-window viewer message, `uninstall-local.sh` and the driver item, `type_text` into a VZ guest) are separate fixes.

## Tradeoffs
- The macOS app lane is a page of rules, not a script. A helper that re-bundles a DMG as Local would duplicate `build-app.sh --channel local`.
- The page also doesn't add a fixture oracle. Its proof is a screenshot plus an accessibility read and the app's own state.

## Evidence
- Pixel clicks missed a Safari sheet and a web-view menu row on the host while `element_token` presses worked. This was first logged as guest-only.
- The inline viewer's "No picture arrived … 20 seconds" reproduced only while another app covered the window, which matches `setPaused` in `WebUIVideoSurfaces.swift`.
- `sfltool dumpbtm` blocked for hours in one cleanup, so the lane checks login items with `launchctl` instead.
- `/dev/shm` blocked the X11 lane in two VM runs. #6836's verifier failed only on merge order.
- These follow the usual GUI test guidance: prefer user-facing accessibility locators over coordinates, keep each test's state isolated, and fix non-determinism rather than retrying it ([Playwright best practices](https://playwright.dev/docs/best-practices), [Fowler on non-deterministic tests](https://martinfowler.com/articles/nonDeterminism.html)). Local Network state is per user and can't be reset before macOS 27.2 ([TN3179](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3179-understanding-local-network-privacy)).

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci` on the affected files, `test_e2e_rust_linux_workflow.py`, `bash -n` on the skills' scripts, relative links under `.cursor/skills`, and `verify-macos.sh doctor`.
- The verify-cua-spaces lane ran on this base on Linux: build, up, doctor, `sb ls`, `do switch verify`, index, the viewer with no sound server, then down. Evidence survived cleanup.
- Not run: the macOS app lane itself, because another session on this Mac has Cua Spaces Local installed and the bundle id is shared. Also not run: the driver's Linux, Wayland and KWin lanes, and Windows.

title: ci(cua-driver): clippy the whole workspace on Linux and trigger on every member
body:
## Why

Linux CI ran clippy only on `platform-linux`, so code that is dead only on Linux could get past every platform's CI. @astrovm's commit (from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6847, authorship kept) switches the step to `--workspace`. The workflow's path filters still listed only some members, so a PR touching only `cua-driver-bindgen`, `cua-perception`, `cursor-theme-cli` or the other missing members skipped the new check.

The same gap let https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6882, a `platform-macos`-only change, break a `cua-driver-core` source pin that only Linux unit runs. Main has failed `Rust Linux unit and compile` since then. This PR repins that test so the job is green again.

## What changed

- `ci-rust-linux.yml` runs `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (astrovm).

title: perf(cua-driver): overlap the web focus wait with the window watch and detect WebKit focus (CUA-3763)
body:
Stacked on #6889 (base is its branch; it retargets to main when #6889 merges).

Plain words: clicking a web text field in Safari should return sooner, and typing right after the click still lands in the field.

## What was slow

Reading the click path, an AX press on a web text field ends with two waits that ran one after the other:

1. The window watch (new window or focus steal), which always waits its 300 ms report window.
2. The web focus wait from #6889, capped at 800 ms, and counted from before the window watch.

The focus wait checked only `AXFocused` on the field. WebKit does not reliably set that attribute on a web field, but it does publish the field as the app's `AXFocusedUIElement`. If `AXFocused` never reads true, every press waits the full cap, which fits the measured p50 of 0.89 to 0.92 s (about 0.8 s cap plus about 0.1 s of resolve, AX reads and dispatch) in the #6889 comment.

## Changes

- The focus check is now true when the field reports `AXFocused` or is the app's `AXFocusedUIElement`, so the wait ends when the page really has focus.
- The focus wait runs together with the window watch instead of after it. The click returns after the slower of the two, and the cap counts from the press.
- `CUA_DRIVER_CLICK_TRACE=1` prints a timing line to stderr for each phase of the element click path (token resolve, background gate, fast-path guard, Chromium select check, element center, cursor glide, selection probe, AX reads, mouse primer, `AXPerformAction`, ancestor read, overlay, window watch plus focus wait). Off by default.

The correctness rule is unchanged: the wait still ends only on observed focus (or the cap), so typing after the click lands in the field.

## Not measured yet

The numbers above are from reading the code and the #6889 measurements, not from a new run. The macOS test VM was reclaimed for another test before I could take the 20 clicks on 3 pages, and the g17-4 Apple VM slots are both in use. Before merging, run the #6889 harness (20 clicks per page, type after the click, read the field back) on this build with `CUA_DRIVER_CLICK_TRACE=1` and confirm the per-phase lines show the focus wait ending in tens of milliseconds. If `web_focus` still runs to the cap in Safari, the trace shows which phase holds the time.

Tracked in CUA-3763.

title: fix(cua-driver): an AX press on a web textarea now takes DOM focus (CUA-3763)
body:
A Cua Driver click on a `<textarea>` search box in Safari never focused it, so the text typed next went to the previously focused field (in Safari, the address bar). Linear: CUA-3763. Found while measuring #6901.

**Old bug, not a regression.** I built Cua Driver at the commit before #6878, the commit before #6889 and current main, and ran 20 click+type cycles on a textarea in Safari (macOS 26.4 VM) on each. All three landed 0/20.

**Cause.** `AXPress` on a WebKit `AXTextArea` takes the press without moving DOM focus (text inputs do focus). The driver then waited out the whole settle cap for a focus that never came.

**Fix.** After the press the driver watches `AXFocused`. If the field does not report focus within 40 ms, it writes `AXFocused=true` (up to 4 times, 60 ms apart) while it keeps polling. A write made while WebKit is still handling the press is dropped, which is why the first request waits. A field that focuses itself returns as soon as focus is stable, as before. `CUA_DRIVER_WEBKIT_SETTLE_MS=0` still skips the wait; an enabled wait keeps at least 250 ms so the requests run even when the window watch used up the cap.

| Textarea, 20 click+type cycles in Safari | Landed in the field | Click call p50 (incl. CLI round trip) |
|---|---|---|
| Before #6878 | 0/20 | about 1.4 s |
| Before #6889 | 0/20 | about 1.4 s |
| Current main | 0/20 | about 1.4 s |
| This PR | 20/20 | about 0.97 s |

For users: clicking a search box or comment box on a web page now puts the cursor in it, so the next typing goes there.

Unit tests cover the request timing (`focus_request_due`); `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib web_focus_settle` passes. `bin/ci --quick --fix` is green.

title: macOS: 64 sandboxd approval workers stalled during Finder/iCloud operations
body:
During CuaDriver-driven Finder work on macOS, the shared macOS approval service became exhausted and unrelated background file opens on an external APFS SSD stalled. CuaDriver is the observed requesting client; this report does not establish a Cua implementation defect.

Could you help identify which native calls in Finder launch/window/session inspection can trigger File Provider approval, and whether outstanding operations can be coalesced or paused after a failure?

## Environment

- Apple silicon Mac mini, macOS 26.7, build 25G229.
- Standalone CuaDriver 0.22.1, official signed `com.trycua.driver` app.
- The original process's logged arm64 UUID matches the installed executable: `D5A2FC14-6D8B-35B4-8CA5-3C82F2F4A9AF`.
- Current installed signatures verify. A newer CuaDriver release has not been tested against this incident.

## Observed incident, November 5 UTC

1. CuaDriver `launch_app` asked Finder to open a folder under `~/Library/Mobile Documents/.Trash/`. The result was `LAUNCH_FAILED`.
2. Finder window/session inspection continued. Within approximately four minutes, sandboxd logged 64 indirect File Provider authorization requests whose subject was `com.trycua.driver`. The retained provider strings identify the CloudDocs family but are truncated.
3. All 64 unique logged request thread IDs match all 64 blocked approval workers in two later sandboxd samples and an independent historical stackshot. Each thread has one approval start and no later approval start in the retained log window. This was not a transcript showing 64 explicit launch retries.
4. Both samples report `Dispatch Thread Soft Limit: 64 reached` and show every approval worker waiting on a semaphore in the File Provider authorization branch. An independent background file-open trace waits for sandboxd approval.
5. A later historical capture shows replacement CuaDriver and TCC processes while the same sandboxd instance still holds those 64 waits. This was not a controlled restart experiment. Reboot subsequently restored access.

We could not map individual approvals to specific Cua tools, establish whether a consent prompt appeared at onset, or recover the original dispatch queue's pending blocks.

## Possible callback starvation in the macOS approval path

Static inspection used the binaries matching the historical images:

- sandboxd arm64e UUID: `05B82BBA-F239-3C69-8D4F-CA1F7398FF4A`.
- TCC library UUID: `3BC4BFE7-2666-3BA0-BEEB-550EBB717692`.

The inspected sandboxd creates its concurrent approval queue targeting the default global dispatch queue. In the File Provider branch it calls `TCCAccessRequestIndirectWithOptions`, then waits with `DISPATCH_TIME_FOREVER` for its semaphore-signaling completion.

The matching TCC library defaults to dispatching final completions onto that same global pool. Its success and XPC-error response branches both have this asynchronous completion path. sandboxd's inspected options omit the private sync-callback option. The configured constrained-worker limit was 64.

This suggests a circular dependency once all workers are occupied. It does not prove an original reply was delivered or queued; an absent semaphore signal is not proof that the TCC daemon never replied. The initial reason approvals remained pending is still unknown.

## Bounded scheduling experiment, not a full incident reproduction

A disposable process called the matching TCC library with empty identity dictionaries that fail local validation and preflight enabled. It supplied no user file path, real client identity, or provider account and did not run Cua or exhaust the live sandboxd service.

The fixture deliberately occupied a concurrent queue targeting the default global pool before submitting callbacks. It explicitly sets the private sync-callback option to false for async tests; native sandboxd omits that option. One run of each configuration produced:

| Configuration | Callbacks about 300 ms after submission, before manual release | Callbacks after releasing the test's waits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 worker, async callback | 1/1 | 1/1 |
| 63 workers, async callback | 63/63 | 63/63 |
| 64 workers, async callback | 0/64 | 64/64 |
| 64 workers, sync-callback control | 64/64 | 64/64 |

Every process exited successfully, with no group timeout and no allowed authorization result. The fixture has watchdog deadlines and manually releases only its own waits. It does not demonstrate an infinite wait, a valid File Provider consent transaction, or a Cua-specific bug. The historical incident's persistence across hours and the static no-timeout wait are separate evidence.

The probe uses an undocumented private API/ABI on this exact build. The sync option is a diagnostic control, not a suggested supported fix. No system binary, privacy grant, SIP setting or mount policy was changed for the experiment.

## What would help

- Identify which native operations beneath the observed Cua workflow could generate these requests.
- Determine whether Cua can avoid unnecessary protected-file probes or coalesce/pause outstanding operations after an access failure.
- Advise whether this should be routed to Apple with additional targeted evidence.

The full original consent sequence has not been reproduced in a disposable macOS installation. Raw captures and private provider/account details are not attached. A sanitized process-local probe can be supplied if useful.

title: ci: require before/after UI screenshots (desktop and mobile) with an automated render
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: UI pull requests reach review with no picture of what changed, at either size.
- What changed: UI pull requests now carry before/after screenshots at desktop (1440x900) and mobile (390x844), from demo data only. A workflow renders the screens for you, a template section and rules say where the evidence goes, and a check flags a UI PR whose description has none.

For users and customers: nothing. This changes how we review.

## What it adds

1. **`CI: PR screenshots` workflow** (`.github/workflows/ci-pr-screenshots.yml`). Runs only when a PR touches `apps/cua-spaces-web/**`, `apps/cua-spaces-desktop/src/**`, or the app-core onboarding, first-run, sign-in, nudges and checklist files.
   - Builds spaces-web and renders first run (welcome, add this computer and sign in), Home, Computers and Settings, plus any route named in a `Screenshot routes: /a, /b` line of the description. It does this at both sizes for the PR head and for its merge-base, as two parallel jobs.
   - Uploads each side as a workflow artifact (30-day retention) and posts one sticky comment. The comment says, per screen and size, whether the rendering changed, and links both artifacts.
   - Caches pnpm, the Playwright browser and the Rust build (sccache), and does not run when no UI path changed. It is not a required check, and `ci-gate` ignores it.
2. **PR template:** a "Screenshots (before/after)" section with a desktop and mobile table.
3. **Check** (`UI pull requests include screenshots`, last job of the same workflow): passes when the description has at least two images labelled desktop and mobile, or `Screenshots: not needed - <reason>`. HTML comments are ignored, so the template's own text does not count. It runs the base branch's copy of the checker, so a PR cannot loosen it. It fails (red, not required) when evidence is missing.
4. **Rules:** a "Show UI Changes" section in `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md` (a UI PR without evidence can be closed) and a matching section in `AGENTS.md`: before/after at both sizes, demo data only, never commit PR-only images.

## Decisions

- **Image hosting.** Images are not committed anywhere in the repository history, and not stored on a branch. They live in workflow artifacts. GitHub cannot embed an artifact in a comment, so the sticky comment shows a change summary and links, and the author embeds the images that matter in the description (GitHub uploads them as attachments). A host outside the repo that could embed images inline needs a bucket and credentials we do not have yet; if we add one, only the report step changes.
- **Forks.** Fork PRs skip rendering: the read-only fork token cannot comment, and whether fork PRs run our CI at all is still open (decision 5a299b9c). The description check still runs for forks and only reads the description.
- **Demo data only.** The script uses the demo adapter and a fresh, signed-out demo for first run. It never touches a real account, host or chat.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **SwiftUI.** The macOS app cannot render on Linux. Cover it later on the macOS lane with swift-snapshot-testing: snapshot the key SwiftUI views at the same two sizes against checked-in reference images, and attach the diffs to the same sticky comment.
- **Preview builds.** T3 Code has a label-triggered `desktop-macos-preview.yml` (label `preview:mac`) that builds an installable preview for a PR. A similar `preview:mac` label would cover what screenshots cannot show.
- Make the check required once it has run cleanly for a few weeks.

## Validation

- `bin/ci --quick --fix`: 8 passed, 2 skipped (actionlint, workflow lint, SPDX, typecheck included).
- Ran `scripts/pr-screenshots.mjs` locally against a production build: 10 of 10 screenshots (5 screens at 2 sizes) in 14 seconds. The sticky-comment builder was run locally, and the description check has unit tests.
- The workflow itself runs here for the first time. This PR carries a throwaway visible change (`Skip for now` gets a suffix on the first-run screen) so the comment has something to show. A revert commit follows once that run has posted its comment.
- Expected workflow time: a cold run is about 6 to 8 minutes, dominated by the Rust wasm build; with warm sccache and pnpm caches, about 3 to 4. Both sides run in parallel. This is an estimate to confirm on the first runs.

Screenshots: not needed - this PR changes CI, templates and docs only; its throwaway commit exists to exercise the workflow.

title: ci: preview:mac label builds an installable Cua Spaces app from a PR
body:
A maintainer can now add the `preview:mac` label to a pull request and get an installable Cua Spaces macOS app built from its head commit, with the download linked in one PR comment. For you: try any PR without a local build.

## How it works

- Triggers on `labeled` (`preview:mac`) and on `synchronize` while the label is present. One concurrency group per PR cancels the build in flight. Other labels get their own group, so they can't cancel or replace a build.
- Builds the same way as a local dogfood build: `install-local.sh --release --no-launch --prefix ...`, which gives "Cua Spaces Local" next to the released app. Then it sets `CuaEnv=prod` and re-signs ad hoc.
- Runs the Swift and Electron binding checks before the build. Uses corepack for pnpm (root pins 9.0.4, spaces-web and the Electron shell pin 11.20.0), a clean SwiftPM `.build`, and the existing `macos-26` runner, `rust-cache` (sccache, restore only), `wasm-bindgen` and `swiftpm-resolve` actions.
- Uploads the zip as an artifact (14 days) and keeps one sticky comment (commit SHA, download link, how to open it).

## Security

- Runs only when `head.repo.full_name == github.repository`; fork PRs never build (fork CI decision 5a299b9c stays open).
- No signing or notarization secrets. The build job has `contents: read`; only the two small comment jobs have `pull-requests: write`, and they check out nothing.
- Adding a label needs triage access; pushing needs write access.

## Also changed

- `ci-gate` now ignores this workflow in its wait list (and its test), so a 30 to 90 minute preview build can't delay or fail a merge.
- Documented in `docs/contributing/CI.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`, each in its own section so it won't conflict with the UI-screenshot rule another PR adds.

I'm testing it on this PR by adding the label. Not set to auto-merge: please review the new CI.

title: fix(spaces): Ready lists only the picked agent's chats, and shows at once (CUA-3774)
body:
Fixes [CUA-3774](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3774).

**For people:** after you pick Claude Code in setup, "Pick up where you left off" shows only your Claude Code chats, and the "Claude Code can now use this Mac" screen shows as soon as Cua is in Claude Code's settings.

## Wrong chats
The Ready screen called `agents.recentThreads` without the picked agent, so the daemon's `agent_threads` listed Claude Code, Codex and Hermes chats.
- The page now passes the picked agent. The daemon (`cua-agent-threads`, shared by macOS, Windows and Linux) reads only that agent's store. The Swift host forwards `agents`, and Electron maps it through `AGENT_THREADS_TOOLS`.
- The page also drops other agents' rows if an older daemon ignores `agents`.
- Agents whose chats Cua doesn't read (Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Goose) hide the section without asking the daemon.

## Slow after picking
Continue waited for `agents.connect {signIn: true}` and then an extra `agents.setup`. Copying Claude Code's sign-in runs `claude -p` to refresh a sign-in that has expired. That took 2.4 to 2.8 s on a dev Mac and is capped at 30 s. Writing Cua's skills and MCP entry alone takes about 0.2 s.
- Continue now waits only for Cua's tools (`signIn: false`). The connect result's `tools_ok` says whether they were added. The sign-in copy then runs in the background.
- The chats are requested when Continue is pressed and cached per host and agent for 30 s. Ready shows them at once, or two plain grey placeholder rows while they load (no spinner).
- `cua-agent-threads`:
  - Codex's `YYYY/MM/DD` folders are read newest first, and reading stops a week of folders after enough chats are found.
  - The file name is checked before any stat, so archived `.jsonl.zst` sessions are skipped.
  - Several agents' stores are read in parallel.
  - `recent_cached` keeps a listing for 30 s.

Timings for `recent` with limit 4:

| Store | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Synthetic: 12k Claude and 7.3k Codex sessions, Codex only | 20 ms | 0.6 ms |
| Synthetic, all agents | 47 ms | 26 ms |
| Real store on a dev Mac, all agents | 1.44 s cold, 160 ms warm | 130 ms (Claude only) |

## Tests
- Rust: Claude only, Codex only, both, none; Codex reads only its newest days but still finds a chat resumed within the week; the cached listing.
- Web: Ready with Claude only, Codex only, both; placeholder then hidden when empty; no ask for agents whose chats Cua can't read; the list fetched during connect is reused. The route test checks the connect order: tools first, sign-in after Ready.
- Electron host: `agents` is forwarded.
- Also run: the full web suite (226 files, 1574 tests), `cua-agent-threads` tests and clippy, the `cua-spaces-ext` `agent_threads` tests, and `bin/ci --quick --fix`.
- No FFI change.

The welcome screen is unchanged.

title: [Bug]: Deleting an ordinary runc sandbox creates and retains cua-runsc-helper
body:
### Primary area

Containers or images

### Summary

Deleting a successfully created local runc sandbox starts and leaves `cua-runsc-helper` running even when Secure Spaces is off and no checkpoint or warm-start workflow was used. The sandbox disappears from both Cua and Docker, but deletion adds an engine-global helper that did not exist before.

### Reproduction

Prerequisites: the released CLI baseline below, a working local Docker engine, and no pre-existing `cua-runsc-helper`. Use a disposable sandbox name and a new Cua state directory; run with no concurrent Cua work against the same engine. These are the executed desktop-image steps, not a claimed minimal reproducer.

```sh
export CUA_HOME="$(mktemp -d)"
export CUA_EXPERIMENTS=-secure-spaces
export CUA_SECURE_DEFAULT=0
cua --embedded experiments list --json
# secure-spaces has on:false

docker inspect cua-runsc-helper
# No such object

cua --embedded sb create linux --tier slim --on local --kind container \
  --runtime runc --name cua-helper-lifecycle-repro --cpu 2 --memory 2GB \
  --wait desktop --ready-timeout 120 --json

docker inspect cua-runsc-helper
# Still no such object

cua --embedded sb rm -f cua-helper-lifecycle-repro
cua --embedded sb ls --json
# []
docker inspect cua-helper-lifecycle-repro
# No such object

docker inspect cua-runsc-helper --format \
  '{{json .State.Running}} {{json .Config.Image}} {{json .HostConfig.Privileged}} {{json .HostConfig.PidMode}} {{json .HostConfig.NetworkMode}}'
docker inspect cua-runsc-helper --format '{{json .Mounts}}'
```

### Expected behavior

Deleting an ordinary runc sandbox that never needed the helper should remove that sandbox without creating a new, persistent helper as a cleanup side effect. Existing shared helpers needed by other sandboxes should remain intact. The merged Secure Spaces change promises no visible change when experiments are off, and the egress guide scopes the new network behavior to the enabled experiment.

### Actual behavior

Creation and deletion both exited 0 in one fresh local attempt. No helper existed before creation or immediately before deletion. After deletion returned and a fresh Cua list was empty, Docker showed the new helper still running:

```text
true "cua-vmm/helper:1" true "host" "none"
```

The bind mounts were `/` to `/host` with `RW:true`, and `/usr` to `/usr` with `RW:false`. The helper carried `ai.cua.kind=helper` and `ai.cua.managed=true`. These are Docker engine filesystem mounts; this observation does not establish exposure of macOS files, an attacker path, or a security vulnerability. This report concerns unnecessary helper creation and retention.

### Environment

- Executed: PyPI `cua` and `cua-cli` 0.14.0 in a fresh isolated uv environment; macOS 27.2 arm64; Docker Desktop 4.98.0, Engine 29.9.2, runc 1.5.2.
- Sandbox image: `ghcr.io/trycua/linux@sha256:6d932b2572fdd5fd5f1c1193da91b70654c6ad5dc7eeba7334844609c38bc69a`, selected through `linux --tier slim`.
- Release source: `cua-sdk-v0.14.0`, commit `f92ce98b450ec855205e38391d99917be8e2a280`.
- Current `main` inspected at `79cbba588355059a382ab4165043090578b90317`; its three container source files cited below are byte-identical to the release. A main-branch binary was not built or run.

### Evidence

- Expected source: [merged Secure Spaces introduction](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6306), “What changes when nobody turns anything on”; [egress guide](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.14.0/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/guides/egress.mdx#L6), experiment-off applicability.
- Failure source: the executed before/create/delete/after comparison above; [container deletion](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.14.0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/container/mod.rs#L1940-L1977), [unpolice](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.14.0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/container/egress.rs#L918-L938), [engine_sh](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.14.0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/container/egress.rs#L389-L396), and [helper creation](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.14.0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/container/snapshot.rs#L409-L484).
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

The deletion path calls `unpolice(name)`. Its resolver-file removal is guarded by name validity, without requiring a retained egress policy or an existing resolver file; it calls `engine_sh`, which ensures the helper. The helper configuration uses runc, privileged mode, the host PID namespace, no network, and the mounts observed above.

### Workaround and additional context

The observed workaround was to remove the newly created helper with `docker rm -f cua-runsc-helper` after confirming it was absent from the baseline and no concurrent Cua work needed it. The probe's task-owned helper and images were removed, and final Docker container and image ID sets matched their baselines. Do not remove a pre-existing shared helper blindly.

#### Restoration check

Repeat the same create/delete sequence with experiments off and no initial helper. Creation should still reach desktop readiness, deletion should still remove the sandbox, and the helper should remain absent after deletion. Also preserve legitimate cleanup for a sandbox with network policy and preserve any pre-existing shared helper in use; avoiding this side effect must not skip required cleanup or remove another sandbox's resources.

#### Impact assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: A successful ordinary sandbox deletion leaves a new engine-global running utility with privileged mode and a writable engine-root mount, requiring cleanup outside the empty Cua sandbox list; no attacker boundary or data exposure was established.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: In the isolated run, removing the newly created helper and task-owned images restored the original engine inventories; this requires checking ownership and concurrent use before manual removal.

title: [Bug]: macOS arm64 PyPI install cannot inject spacesd into plain images
body:
### Primary area

Build, packaging, or release

### Summary

A fresh macOS arm64 PyPI installation cannot create a local container from a plain OCI image with the default spacesd behavior. The documented HTTP-server example fails before a container is created because the static Linux guest helper is unavailable; the same image and command work with `--no-spacesd`.

### Reproduction

1. On the environment below, install `cua` in a fresh Python virtual environment with its dependencies. Leave `CUA_SPACESD_STATIC` unset and use an empty `CUA_HOME` so an independently installed helper cannot mask the result.
2. Run `cua runtime doctor --embedded` with Docker reachable.
3. Run the following command. This was executed once with default injection, once with the opt-out control, and once with a separately supplied static helper.

```sh
cua sb create python:3.12-slim --on local --embedded --runtime runc \
  --name injection-probe --service web=8000 --wait http:web/ \
  --ready-timeout 30 -- python -m http.server 8000
```

4. Repeat with `--no-spacesd` added before `--`, using another sandbox name. For the successful control, run `cua sb url CONTROL_NAME web --embedded` and request the returned loopback URL.

### Expected behavior

The local-runtimes guide's “What differs locally” section says any OCI image on containers and microVMs gets a static cua-spacesd when it lacks one, so exec, files and ports work. It includes `python:3.12-slim` and does not exclude macOS PyPI installs. The CLI's create help makes the same default-injection promise. A fresh installation on this supported local container backend should run the documented plain-image command with injection enabled.

### Actual behavior

The default create exits 1 before creating a container:

```text
cua: local runtime: [local] the static cua-spacesd is not available: an image without cua-spacesd gets one injected, a static Linux build that ships next to `cua` as cua-spacesd-linux-aarch64; set CUA_SPACESD_STATIC to its path, or create the Space with spacesd=false to run the image as it is
```

Doctor reports the container backend `ok` and `spacesd-static error` with the same missing-helper explanation, and exits 1. The setup dry-run lists other runtimes but no plan to provide that static helper. The opt-out control exits 0, reaches `ready` as a local runc container, and a real HTTP request returns 200. Container inventories before and after the failing create are unchanged.

A second discriminating control supplies the official matching Linux arm64 static helper through `CUA_SPACESD_STATIC` and leaves injection enabled. The same create then exits 0, serves HTTP 200, and `cua sb exec` returns the requested `helper-injection-ok` marker. Docker inspection shows `/.cua/bin/cua-spacesd supervise --on-exit exit -- python -m http.server 8000` as the container entry point. This establishes that the measured macOS container path can inject and run the guest helper when it is available.

### Environment

- Fresh PyPI install: `cua==0.14.0` and its dependency `cua-cli==0.14.0`; Python 3.15.2; macOS 27.2 arm64.
- Docker Desktop 4.98.0, Engine 29.9.2, runc 1.5.2; native Linux arm64 guest image.
- Additional control: official `cua-spacesd-v0.12.7` asset `cua-spacesd-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`, verified against its published SHA-256 file.
- Published component release: `cua-sdk-v0.14.0`, commit `f92ce98b450ec855205e38391d99917be8e2a280`.
- Current main inspected: `79cbba588355059a382ab4165043090578b90317`. The relevant wheel builder, console wrapper and release workflow match the release tag. Main was inspected in source, not compiled or executed.

### Evidence

- Expected source: [local-runtimes guide at the inspected main revision](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/79cbba588355059a382ab4165043090578b90317/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/guides/local-runtimes.mdx#L86-L94), plus the installed create help's `--no-spacesd` description and HTTP-server example.
- Failure source: the fresh-install create command and doctor output quoted above; `importlib.metadata.distribution(...).files` contains no `spacesd` entry for either installed distribution.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

The [wheel builder](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/79cbba588355059a382ab4165043090578b90317/libs/cua/python/build_wheel.py#L111-L123) stages the helper only for Linux and rejects `--spacesd` for other wheel platforms. The [release wheel job](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/79cbba588355059a382ab4165043090578b90317/.github/workflows/cd-cua-sdk.yml#L434-L442) likewise supplies it only for Linux. This is an explicit packaging rule, but the user-facing local container promise has no corresponding platform exception.

The [local create path](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/79cbba588355059a382ab4165043090578b90317/libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon/src/local.rs#L2172-L2179) requires the helper when injection is selected. That selection includes the container backend without a macOS exclusion.

### Restoration check

Repeat the failing command from a fresh macOS arm64 PyPI installation, with empty Cua state, no separately provisioned helper and no opt-out. It should create the container, serve HTTP 200, and expose the injected spacesd functionality promised for plain OCI images. Keep the opt-out case working as a control. The current failure occurs before either HTTP readiness or spacesd capability verification can run.

### Workaround and additional context

`--no-spacesd` is a verified service-only bypass, but it intentionally drops the injected spacesd capabilities. A workaround preserving injection was also verified: download the official matching static Linux arm64 helper, check its published SHA-256, and set `CUA_SPACESD_STATIC` to that file before running the command. This extra provisioning is absent from the quickstart. The report does not claim all missing platform helpers are bugs and does not establish behavior on Intel macOS or Windows. No security impact is alleged.

### References

[The wheel-split PR](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5852) documents Linux-only helper packaging; it does not describe a macOS plain-image exception or a macOS setup path. This report concerns the resulting default-injection failure, not the intentional absence of a console entry point in the `cua-cli` carrier package.

### Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The documented plain-image local create fails on the measured macOS arm64 PyPI installation before creating a container; this is bounded to images needing injection, rather than every sandbox workflow.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: Supplying the checksum-verified official matching static helper through `CUA_SPACESD_STATIC` lets the same create inject spacesd, return HTTP 200, and run the exec marker. The separate opt-out control also serves HTTP but does not preserve spacesd capabilities.

title: [Bug]: Documentation: provider-key storage guide retains the legacy service and omits Local file storage
body:
### Primary area

Documentation

### Summary

The Connect your agent guide describes an obsolete provider-key Keychain service and says file-backed development builds cannot save provider keys without naming the supported Local-channel exception. This is a documentation mismatch; no loss, exposure, or agent-run failure is claimed.

### Reproduction

1. Open the hosted [Connect your agent guide](https://cua.ai/docs/spaces/guides/connect-your-agent.md), section “Where the keys are kept”. It names `run.cua.ai` and says file-backed unsigned development builds cannot save agent keys.
2. Compare the [Authenticate guide](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-cli/guides/authentication.md), which describes the current `ai.cua.session` service and migration of older secrets.
3. With the released CLI binary, use two separate disposable directories as `HOME` and `CUA_HOME`, set `CUA_CREDENTIAL_STORE=file` and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, and run the command below once with `CUA_CHANNEL=stable` and once with `CUA_CHANNEL=local`. The input is synthetic, not a usable provider key; do not run `keys check`.

```sh
printf '%s\n' 'synthetic-doc-probe-0000' | cua --embedded --json agent keys set anthropic
```

4. Inspect whether `<CUA_HOME>/agent-keys` exists and its permissions. Inspect the provider-key store call path cited below for the service name; no real Keychain access is needed.

### Expected behavior

The guide names the service used for provider keys, distinguishes Stable from the Local development channel, and preserves the warning that Local's file is unencrypted. It continues to explain that Stable file-backed builds cannot save provider keys. Session file storage alone must not be presented as equivalent to provider-key storage.

### Actual behavior

The hosted guide and checked-out source documentation still name the legacy service, although provider keys use the same current service as the session. In the isolated CLI probe, Stable file-backed storage exited 2 and created no provider-key file. Local exited 0, reported `available: true` and an `insecure` warning, created `agent-keys` with mode 0600, and stored the synthetic fixture there. The warning says the keys are stored unencrypted and should not be real production secrets. The guide's blanket development-build statement omits this channel distinction.

### Environment

- Current source snapshot: trycua/cua `main` at `79cbba588355059a382ab4165043090578b90317`.
- Latest published CLI/SDK inspected: `cua-sdk-v0.14.0`, tag commit `f92ce98b450ec855205e38391d99917be8e2a280`. Executed `cua 0.14.0` from its checksum-verified official darwin-arm64 CLI archive with isolated homes and embedded execution.
- Latest published Spaces app source inspected: `cua-spaces-v0.22.3`, tag commit `01f60c48bdabe40e6c23a8069872f5f1d9da9ad3`. The app was not launched.
- CLI probe platform: macOS, arm64. Linux and Windows execution and real vault migration were not tested.

### Evidence

- Expected source: `libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/agents/keys.rs` lines 1–11 and 560–589 (`AgentKeys::new_for`); `libs/cua/crates/cua-home/src/channel.rs` lines 263–268 and 480–489; `libs/cua/crates/cua-auth/src/lib.rs` lines 1019–1033 and 1688–1690. The same storage contracts are present at both inspected release tags.
- Failure source: `docs/content/docs/spaces/guides/connect-your-agent.mdx` lines 344–369 and the hosted guide in step 1.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

hosted wording and isolated released-CLI results were read directly. Service selection is source evidence, not a real-vault test.

`AgentKeys` saves the named secret `agent-keys` through `Store::save_secret`; vault storage selects `keyring_service()` with account `cua-cli.agent-keys`, so provider keys do not retain a separate `run.cua.ai` service. `AgentKeys::new_for` permits file storage only when `CuaChannel::allows_insecure_dev_store()` is true, which is Local only. The existing unit tests `a_file_store_keeps_no_keys` and `the_local_channel_keeps_keys_in_a_private_file_and_says_so` were inspected, not executed here.

### Workaround and additional context

Restoration check: passing when the hosted section and source page describe the current service and Local-only unencrypted file-store exception. The same isolated CLI comparison remains a control: Stable refuses file storage, Local stores the synthetic key with mode 0600 and the warning. Correcting the guide requires no expansion of Stable storage permissions or removal of the development warning. Reading workaround: use the authentication guide for the current service and the Local CLI warning for the actual storage behavior.

### References

- [Service migration implementation, PR #5436](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5436): includes agent keys among migrated secrets; closed historical implementation, not an open documentation duplicate.
- [Local development storage implementation, PR #6587](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6587): preserves Stable refusal while adding Local file storage; closed historical implementation.

### Triage assessment

- Impact level: P3
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: Incorrect storage wording can confuse inspection and development setup; observed product behavior includes its warning and no consequential runtime failure is established.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The authentication guide identifies the service, and the released CLI's Local warning identifies the actual store. Stable's existing environment-based route remains described by the provider-key guide.

title: [Bug]: Documentation: space-kinds states VZ always refuses egress policies without the experiment qualifier
body:
### Primary area

Documentation

### Summary

The Space kinds page says egress policies are refused on `vz` microVMs without qualifying the Secure Spaces setting. Its linked network guide describes VZ gateway enforcement with Secure Spaces enabled, and inspected source implements those two modes. This report concerns missing documentation scope, not a demonstrated enforcement failure.

### Reproduction

1. Open the hosted [Space kinds page](https://cua.ai/docs/spaces/concepts/space-kinds.md), section “MicroVM runtimes”. It groups `vz` and Containerization as refusing egress policies, without an experiment qualifier.
2. Follow its egress link to [A Space's network](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-sdk/guides/egress.md). The introduction explicitly scopes the page to Secure Spaces, off until enabled with `cua experiments enable secure-spaces`; “Rules by name” and “Trees” include VZ microVMs behind the Cua network gateway.
3. Inspect the mode selector, egress support selector and VZ launch path cited below in current source and the published CLI/SDK tag. These source checks were performed; no VM was started and no packet-enforcement test was run.

### Expected behavior

The space-kinds statement distinguishes refusal while Secure Spaces is off from gateway enforcement while it is on. It retains the separate Containerization limitation and does not imply that the experiment is enabled by default.

### Actual behavior

Both hosted pages retain this different wording. The Space kinds statement is unqualified, although `egress::support` uses `legacy_support_on(Vz, "macos")` only in Legacy mode and otherwise selects host enforcement at the Cua gateway. The VZ launch path selects gvproxy in Legacy mode and the gateway in Secure mode, writing its rules before launch. Source supports the linked network guide's experiment scope; it does not support unconditional refusal covering that scope.

### Environment

- Current source snapshot: trycua/cua `main` at `79cbba588355059a382ab4165043090578b90317`.
- Latest published CLI/SDK source inspected: `cua-sdk-v0.14.0`, tag commit `f92ce98b450ec855205e38391d99917be8e2a280`.
- Applicable documented condition: macOS VZ microVM, Secure Spaces enabled versus disabled. Runtime VZ startup and actual network enforcement were not tested. No settings were changed.

### Evidence

- Expected source: `libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/network.rs` lines 943–968 (experiment/override mode selection), `libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/egress.rs` lines 744–813 (mode-sensitive support), and `libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/microvm/mod.rs` lines 1823–1842 and 1863–1866 (gateway selection and rules). The same mode split is present in the published CLI/SDK tag.
- Failure source: `docs/content/docs/spaces/concepts/space-kinds.mdx` lines 64–65 states refusal without scope, while `docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/guides/egress.mdx` lines 6, 73–88 and 98 describe the enabled experiment. Hosted copies in steps 1–2 show the same distinction.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

the documentation mismatch was read directly, with source used to establish the missing condition.

The observable failure is documentation wording. A successful docs fetch is not treated as runtime proof. The source's control is Legacy mode: it still returns `Unsupported` for a nonempty VZ egress policy, so deleting the refusal statement without retaining the default-mode limitation would also be incomplete.

### Workaround and additional context

Restoration check: passing when reading the space-kinds statement and following its egress link gives a consistent answer for both modes: VZ refuses policies with Secure Spaces off and uses the host gateway with it on, subject to runtime prerequisites. Containerization's limitation stays distinct. No code or network-boundary change is requested. Reading workaround: use the linked network guide's explicit Secure Spaces scope to distinguish the two modes.

### References

- [VZ gateway implementation history, PR #6071](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6071): closed with work moving elsewhere; historical context, not proof that current source lacks implementation.
- [Open experiment graduation work, PR #6775](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6775): proposes changing the default experiment scope. This report describes current main and the published tag, not that unmerged change.

### Triage assessment

- Impact level: P3
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The runtime-choice page omits a setting that changes its stated capability. This establishes wording inconsistency only; no failed sandbox workflow or enforcement was observed.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The linked network guide explicitly names the experiment and includes VZ gateway behavior, so a reader can resolve the scope there today.

title: feat(cua-driver): nudge to batch after the second action, with a ready run_steps call
body:
Linear: CUA-3763

## What changes for users

Agents using Cua Driver chain their actions into one `run_steps` call sooner, so a task takes fewer model turns. The driver now tells an agent after its second single action, not the third, and the hint carries a call it can send as is.

## What the recorded runs show

I read the public Scale AgentEnv dataset (`calls.parquet`, macOS, Cua Driver 0.38, 270 trials, 6,476 tool calls) with the new `rust/scripts/measure-batching.py`.

| Model | Calls that are `run_steps` or `run_script` | Actions inside a batch | Actions per batch | Calls one batch would save |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sonnet 5.5 | 15.4% | 62% | 3.4 | 604 of 2,200 (27.5%) |
| Haiku 5.5 | 9.8% | 50% | 3.4 | 791 of 2,570 (30.8%) |
| Opus 5.5 | 42.1% | 90% | 2.8 | 180 of 1,706 (10.6%) |
| All three | 20.2% | 69% | 3.1 | 1,575 of 6,476 (24.3%) |

A "group" is a run of single actions (click, type, key, set value, scroll, drag, menu) with an optional `get_window_state` right after. If every group of two or more calls became one `run_steps` call with `observe:{}`, the call count would drop by the last column. The common shape is act, read, act, read: 1,182 of the 2,262 `get_window_state` calls came straight after a single action.

## Changes

- **Nudge on the second direct action** (`batch_nudge.rs`). It was the third. The hint now says why (`observe:{}` returns what changed, so no separate read) and includes a ready call, `run_steps({pid:..,window_id:..,steps:[...],observe:{}})`, for the window the action targeted. It is still advice only, never on an error, and never inside a batch.
- **`click`, `type_text` and `press_key` point at `run_steps`** in their descriptions: one line, through the existing `get_guide` hint seam. They are 95% of single actions in the runs above.
- **Server instructions and `SKILL.md`** say to batch the actions you know and never follow a batch with a separate read.
- **Tool-list size is unchanged.** The three pointers (about 230 characters) are paid for by trimming repeated prose in the `run_steps` description (about 275 characters). The server instructions keep their word count; a test caps it at 200.
- **Tests:** the nudge tracker and dispatch tests cover the new threshold and the ready call; the description-hint test covers the three tools. `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` passes (1,220 tests).

## Not measured yet

There are no live before/after numbers. The live A/B (same model, `main` against this branch, three tasks on a macOS VM) did not run. The test VM's display is black until a VNC click and then shows the lock screen. The plan does not let an agent type the VM password to unlock it, so the test build could not be granted Accessibility. Both driver binaries are built and the runner is written, so the run can start as soon as a VM with a usable screen is free.

Until that run shows no pass-rate loss, this PR has no auto-merge queued. The hint only reaches agents that make two single calls in a row, so I expect little risk to pass rate, but that is not measured.

title: [Bug]: default installer selects CLI 0.10.1 despite published 0.14.0
body:
### Primary area

Build, packaging, or release

### Summary

The official Unix installer selects CLI 0.10.1 by default even though the stable component release already provides CLI 0.14.0 for the same platform. The rolling manifest's CLI entries still point to the older release, so a fresh install using the advertised latest selection misses newer CLI releases.

### Reproduction

1. Download the official installer as data: `curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/install.sh -o install.sh`.
2. Run `sh install.sh --cli-only --yes --dry-run --no-onboarding --no-modify-path` with an empty isolated HOME and no existing target binary. This exercises the default version selection without installing anything.
3. Repeat with `--version 0.14.0` added as a control.
4. Compare the download URLs printed by the two runs with the CLI entries in the rolling manifest and the component release assets identified below.

Both dry runs were executed on the environment below and exited 0. No actual installer execution without `--dry-run` was performed.

### Expected behavior

The default selection should resolve the newest published stable CLI artifact available for the platform. The installer documents `--version VERSION` as an override with "default: latest". The installer README's Release manifest section says SDK publication moves the rolling CLI version; the stable SDK workflow publishes the release before updating that feed.

### Actual behavior

The default dry run selected:

```text
[dry-run] download https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/download/cua-sdk-v0.10.1/cua-cli-0.10.1-darwin-arm64.tar.gz (sha256 cc2006e99bf701f7a91fecdead676f693734150fded0ab838cd0d6ab18936203)
```

The pinned control selected the newer artifact. Its checksum agreed with both the component release's `checksums.txt` and pinned manifest; extracting that archive in isolation and running only `cua --version` printed `cua 0.14.0` and exited 0. The published component release is neither a draft nor a prerelease. The default rolling manifest reports `versions.cli = "0.10.1"`, and all six CLI platform entries report that same version.

This report concerns fresh-install version selection. The installer's existing-newer-binary guard was not triggered because the isolated target did not exist; no downgrade of an existing installation was tested or claimed. The underlying reason the feed has not advanced is unknown.

### Environment

- Tested selection: official live `install.sh`, byte-identical to `scripts/install/install.sh` at current `main` commit `f365b53b0a14c3995b0a00d2ae63f204ead7d531`.
- Platform: macOS arm64, using `/bin/sh` and isolated HOME, CUA_HOME and install prefix; telemetry disabled.
- Rolling CLI baseline: 0.10.1; latest published non-prerelease `cua-sdk-v*` baseline inspected: 0.14.0.

### Evidence

- Expected source: [installer README, Release manifest](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/f365b53b0a14c3995b0a00d2ae63f204ead7d531/scripts/install/README.md#release-manifest), the installer's help, and [stable SDK feed update](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/f365b53b0a14c3995b0a00d2ae63f204ead7d531/.github/workflows/cd-cua-sdk.yml#L797-L818).
- Failure source: executed dry-run download line above and [live rolling manifest](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/download/cua-install-latest/release-artifacts.json); the [stable component release](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-sdk-v0.14.0) supplies the newer executable.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

Source tracing confirms `load_manifest()` uses `cua-install-latest` when neither a version nor a custom manifest URL is provided, and `download()` selects the platform's artifact from that manifest. The dry run uses those same selection paths and stops before artifact download or target installation.

### Restoration check

Repeat the default dry run against the live installer and rolling feed: it should select the newest published stable CLI artifact for the tested platform. Verify that the selected archive exists and its checksum and executable version agree. Keep the explicit-version control resolving its requested release; do not substitute GitHub's repository-wide Latest badge for the component release stream.

### Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: Fresh users following the advertised latest installer receive a selection for an older CLI even though a newer stable executable exists for the same platform. No failure of specific newer CLI functionality or population frequency was measured.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The explicit-version control resolves the current release, and its checksum-verified archive executes with the expected version. A full pinned installation was not run; the existing-newer-binary guard also preserves newer binaries already at the target.

### Workaround and additional context

Use an explicit version to select the current component release. This report is distinct from the Driver installer baked-version problem: it concerns the `cua` CLI rolling JSON feed. The report does not diagnose the release-workflow failure.

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.

title: fix(cua-driver): query macOS keyboard layout on the main queue
body:
## Summary

Background TextEdit `type_text` on macOS 27.3 (Apple Silicon) could terminate cua-driver 0.41.2 with `SIGTRAP`. The reduced stack was `dispatch_assert_queue → TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource → target_layout → press_key → document_edit::send_net_zero_edit → ensure_marked_after_ax_write → type_text_blocking`, on a `tokio-rt-worker`.

Move Carbon keyboard-layout lookup onto the existing bounded main-queue bridge. On a bridge error, return `None`; never retry Carbon directly on the worker. Add a regression test that requests the layout from a worker while the harness does not service the main queue, expecting `None` rather than a process abort.

## Related work

Small, self-contained bug fix submitted directly under the contribution guide. Searches for the Carbon function and keyboard-layout crashes found no existing issue/PR. Reproduction notes and the original patch are at https://github.com/RockENZO/cua-macos-background-input-fix.

No RFC: this changes internal macOS thread affinity without changing a public API, permission boundary, or cross-component contract. Agent-assisted contribution by RockENZO.

## Compatibility and risk

- Only the macOS layout lookup changes. The existing bridge executes inline on the main thread and queues off-main requests with a two-second timeout.
- A timeout returns the existing absent-layout fallback; it does not guarantee atomic failure of the entire input operation or preservation of every layout. Repeated timeout latency has not been benchmarked.
- Background save refusal, intermittent off-Space window resolution, and multi-agent concurrency are outside this fix.
- Rollback: revert this commit.

## Validation

- Current main base: `066f837d6e9a84483d02076dcd8a3ea5f67fe29c`; patch applies, `git diff --check` and the changed file's rustfmt check pass.
- Prior verification of the same fix on tag `cua-driver-rs-v0.41.2` (`86b5ea2d403017d224bb7a1057f1841668b0a68c`), with Homebrew Rust 1.99.1: locked cua-driver debug build passed; focused regression passed (1 passed, 0 failed, 690 filtered out, about 2.01 seconds).
- Recorded manual verification on that tagged build, November 8, 2026: Chinese/English/digits/newline inserted into background TextEdit and read back without a crash; foreground app and cursor unchanged immediately before/after. These manual checks were not rerun on this PR's main-based commit.
- Regression scope: safe timeout without a draining main queue. Successful main-queue execution is covered only by the recorded manual test; queue-resumption cancellation is not independently tested here.
- `python3 bin/ci --quick` was attempted but stopped because this host has Homebrew Rust 1.99.1 while upstream pins 1.97.1. No green `bin/ci` or local-ci signoff is claimed. Current-commit native tests and canonical E2E remain outstanding; this PR stays draft pending validation/review.

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] No external contribution is included beyond existing upstream code.

title: fix(cua-driver): report macOS opened-window identity per action
body:
## Why

macOS click and press_key results report opened windows only in their text suffix (#6853). This salvages https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6854 by @lidge-jun (JUN), whose commit is kept as authored. It publishes structured `new_windows` and fixes two problems in that patch. A late window from the previous action's detached tail turned the current AX click's `suspected_noop` into `unverifiable` and dropped its pixel escalation. Windows from this action and the previous one were also merged into one list.

## What changed

- AX click, pixel click and confirmed or unverifiable press_key results carry `new_windows: [{window_id, pid, title}]` (the Linux shape) for windows this action opened. Windows the previous action's detached tail saw go in a separate `earlier_new_windows`. Each key is omitted when its list is empty.
- The AX click result is built in `ax_click_structured`. Only this action's `new_windows` lifts `suspected_noop`, and `escalation` stays tied to that effect.
- Regression tests cover the attribution split and the click effect. Each test was checked by reintroducing the old behavior, and it fails.

## Scope

macOS `platform-macos` only: `click.rs`, `press_key.rs`, `window_change_detector.rs`. The text suffix and the observation deadline are unchanged. Linux and Windows results are untouched.

## Blast Radius

Structured-result consumers of macOS click and press_key get two optional keys. An AX click that opens a window now reports `unverifiable` instead of `suspected_noop`, as the original PR intended. A previous action's late window no longer changes the current click's effect.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --lib` for `platform-macos` all pass on macOS arm64. Linux and Windows platform crates were not built.

Credit: @lidge-jun wrote the original change in https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6854.

CUA-3770

Size: within the production limits, so no size-limit reason is needed.

title: fix(cua-driver): read the keyboard layout on the main queue so press_key cannot trap on macOS 26 (CUA-3763)
body:
Linear: CUA-3763

## What changed for users
On macOS 26 and later, pressing a key through Cua Driver could kill the driver's background service. Key presses now read the keyboard layout on the system's main thread, so the service stays up.

## Evidence
During an overnight Bench run on macOS 26.5.2 the daemon died repeatedly with `EXC_BREAKPOINT` / `SIGTRAP`. Every crash report has the same trigger thread:

`_dispatch_assert_queue_fail` < `TSMGetInputSourceProperty` < `TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource` < `keyboard::target_layout` < `keyboard::press_key` (a tokio blocking-pool thread).

The code came in with #6659 (layout-aware shortcut keys), so it is in 0.41.3 and main but not in 0.38.0. The Text Input Sources calls assert that they run on the main dispatch queue.

## Fix
`current_layout()` runs on the main dispatch queue (`dispatch_async_f` to `_dispatch_main_q`, same pattern as `cursor::overlay`) and waits up to 2 s. If the main queue is not serviced, the wait times out and the key code comes from the fixed ANSI map, as before #6659. On the main thread it runs inline.

## Not yet verified
- A single `press_key` with `cmd+a` from the CLI did NOT crash in a quick test on the release build, so the exact trigger (first TSM use on a worker thread, a particular key or modifier set) is not pinned down. The Bench has run its first trials on a build of this branch without a crash (more results follow in the overnight run).
- Needs a macOS-hosted test that calls `press_key` from a worker thread on macOS 26; the quick CI skips the platform-macos unit tests.

Not queued for auto-merge.

title: test(cua-driver): cover trusted_session_call on the socket while permissions are pending
body:
## Why

CUA-3698, a follow-up from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6802. The existing `trusted_session_call_waits_for_the_permission_gate` test calls the bound session directly, so nothing covers the `trusted_session_call` socket arm. That arm binds only for an embedded-mode peer whose pid is the daemon's parent, which an in-process server can't produce.

## What changed

- New test `serve::permission_gate_tests::socket_trusted_session_call_waits_for_the_permission_gate`. It re-runs the test binary as an embedded child daemon (`CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1`), so the test process is the daemon's parent. It then binds a trusted session over the Unix socket.
- While the gate is pending, `trusted_session_call` returns a `permissions_pending` refusal. After the parent tells the child (over stdin) to open the gate, the same call runs the probe tool. The child asserts that the tool ran exactly once.
- A drop guard kills and reaps the child on any failure, and every wait has a deadline.

## Scope

Test-only, in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/serve.rs`, gated on `cfg(unix)`. No production code changes. The Windows named-pipe trusted arm is not covered.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --bin cua-driver` (396 passed) for `cua-driver` on macOS.
- Making `permissions_pending_refusal` in `cua-driver-sdk/src/runtime.rs` return `None` fails the new test at the pending assertion (`left: None, right: Some("permissions_pending")`) and leaves no child process behind. Restoring it makes the test pass.
- Linux and Windows did not run here. The test is `cfg(unix)` and should also run on Linux CI.
