title: Spaces first run asks for Local Network on Macs that run macOS Spaces; status line says when a computer has something to fix (CUA-3854)
body: Closes CUA-3854. **For users:** a Mac set up to run Spaces now asks for Local Network during setup, right next to the other two permissions. Its first macOS Space just starts, and the "Local Network access is off" issue no longer turns up later on the computer's page. A computer that is online but has something to fix now says so ("Online, 1 thing to fix") with an amber dot, instead of "Online" next to a red dot. ## Why it showed up The old first run asked for Local Network: its permissions page called `host.status { localNetwork: true }`, and the Mac app answered with a `local-network` row. The new first run (#6593) kept Screen Recording and Accessibility but dropped that row. A new Mac only found out later, when the daemon's machine check failed and the computer page showed the issue. ## What changed - **First run, permissions step (`first-run-new.tsx`, `bridge/local-network.ts`, `components/app-permissions.tsx`).** On a Mac that runs macOS Spaces (set up with Spaces, Apple silicon: the same rule the Mac app already uses for the row), the step shows a third row, "Run macOS Spaces on this Mac". The note under the rows says why just before macOS asks. **Allow** calls `host.openSettings` with the Local Network pane, which the Mac app already turns into a connect from the background service (cua-spacesd's daemon). That connect is what makes macOS show its own prompt, using the app's `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`. The row then shows the answer live: "Waiting for your answer", then **On**. If the person says no, the row reads **Off**, the button becomes **Open Settings**, and it opens the same Local Network pane the issue card uses. **Later** still never blocks the run. On other Macs and computers the step is unchanged. - **No prompt before the explanation.** macOS asks on the first local connect, so reading the row must not check it. `host.status` takes a new `localNetworkCheck` argument (default: same as `localNetwork`, so older callers behave the same). The first run lists the row with `localNetworkCheck: false` until Allow is pressed, then checks on every read (also after a relaunch: `cua.localNetwork.askedAtMs`). Pressing Allow also sets the native gate's `localNetworkExplained` flag, so creating the first macOS Space doesn't explain it a second time. - **Status line (`machines_health::status_with_issues`, `computer-page.tsx`).** A computer that is online with warn or fail issues says "Online, 1 thing to fix" / "Online, N things to fix". The dot is amber for any issue; red never sits next to "Online". Notes and other statuses are unchanged. The parity golden `machines.json` is updated to match. - Demo adapter: `host.status` lists `local-network` for a Mac set up with Spaces, and Allow plays macOS's prompt being answered. ## Decisions - **Onboarding, not right before the first macOS Space** (Francesco's preference). The row only shows on a Mac that will run macOS Spaces, so nobody else is asked. Asking during setup means the first macOS Space just starts. The native pre-create gate (`LocalNetworkGate`) stays as the safety net for anyone who pressed Later. - **Asked from the daemon, not from an NWBrowser/NWConnection in the app.** macOS decides Local Network per process. The process that has to reach the VMs is the background service, and the app's own connect can pass while the service stays blocked. So the check and the prompt go through the daemon's machine check (`machine.local_network`), the same check that raises the issue card. That way, "On" in setup means the issue card can't appear. - **`NSBonjourServices` is not added.** Info.plist already has `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` (checked in the installed Local build too). Nothing in the app browses Bonjour: it connects by address. `NSBonjourServices` only matters for Bonjour browsing, so adding one would declare a service we don't use. ## Screenshots (demo data) Permissions step, desktop: before / after / after Allow Permissions step, narrow: before / after / waiting for macOS's answer / allowed Computer page, desktop: before / after Computer page, narrow: before / after ## Tests - `first-run-local-network.test.tsx` (new): the third row and its words; Allow; waiting, On and Off; Open Settings after a no; no row on Macs that don't run macOS Spaces; the hook lists without checking before Allow and checks after (also after a relaunch). - `machines_health::online_with_issues_says_so`; parity goldens updated; `cargo test -p cua-spaces-app-core` passes. - Web: typecheck plus first-run, computers-page and permissions suites pass. - **Not yet verified:** the real macOS prompt on a fresh user in a macOS VM. Both Apple VM slots on the test host were held by other running VMs, so nothing was started. This is tracked on CUA-3854. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: CI: ci-gate reruns itself after a green rerun; PRs run only the lanes they touch (CUA-3856)
body:
Linear: [CUA-3856](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3856)

**For contributors:** rerunning a failed job is now enough. `ci-gate` turns green by itself once everything is green. A PR also stops running the slow suites for code it doesn't touch.

### Problem

- **A green rerun left ci-gate red.** `ci-gate` is one long job that waits for every other workflow on the PR head, then gives one verdict. When a job failed, the gate failed. Rerunning only that job never re-ran the gate, so PRs sat red for hours until someone also reran the gate.
- **PRs ran checks for lanes they don't touch.** `.github/ci-areas.json` (path → area → workflows, plus the package graph in `ci_graph.py`) already decided which runs the gate *waits* for. But every workflow still *ran* on its own coarse `paths:` filter. For example, any `libs/cua/**` change ran `CI: Test Python` (21 min), both openkoalabot example suites (13–14 min each), and so on. #6992 (a copy pass across Swift, Rust and web) ran 94 check runs.

### Chosen pattern

1. **Gate recheck: `workflow_run: completed`, the standard pattern.** `ci-gate-recheck.yml` listens to every workflow the gate waits for, and to `status` (the `local-ci` sign-off). It calls `.github/scripts/ci_gate_recheck.py`, which reruns the newest `ci-gate` run for that SHA only when all of these hold:
   - the trigger is green;
   - that gate run failed (or timed out) *before* the green result arrived;
   - the SHA is still the head of an open PR;
   - the PR has no hold label.

   The rerun is the gate's own run, so the check name `ci-gate`, its event, branch protection and auto-merge are unchanged. The gate recomputes from scratch, so it is never greener than its own evaluation. A sync test fails if the workflow list misses a workflow the gate waits for.
2. **One decision, used twice.** The existing map and `ci_gate_scope.py` stay the single source of truth.
   - A new `--workflow <file>` mode answers "does this workflow need to run?" with the same function the gate uses to decide what to ignore.
   - The shared `quick` stage (`ci-quick.yml`, already the first job of the 38 heavy workflows) gets a `scope` job. It reads the selector, the map and the base manifests from the **base commit** (a PR can't narrow itself; any `.github/**` change runs everything), diffs base..head with git (no API budget), and outputs `skip`.
   - Every job in those workflows now `needs: quick` and adds `needs.quick.outputs.skip != 'true'`. A job that only waited through another job could still start under `!cancelled()`, so every job gets the check, not just the root jobs.
   - Skipped by scope means the gate doesn't wait for it, so it counts as passing. If the scope job fails, the caller's run fails, so the gate **fails closed**.
3. **Package-level narrowing (the Nx/Turborepo "affected" model).** A new `narrow` block in the map names the packages a suite builds. The package graph adds their dependency closure, so a suite runs only when one of those packages, or something it depends on, changed. It starts with three suites, each verified against what it builds:
   - `ci-test-python`: cua-sdk and cua-cli, plus the Python paths.
   - `ci-openkoalabot-example-tauri`: its workspace and UI.
   - `ci-openkoalabot-example-samples`: cua-sdk, @trycua/cua and the Swift paths.
4. **Merge queue: run the lanes the queued PRs touch, behind a switch.**
   - `merge_group:` is on every workflow with the quick stage, and the scope there is `merge_group.base_sha..head_sha`. That is the union of the queued PRs on the merged result: as safe as a PR run, and much cheaper than "run everything" for copy PRs.
   - The repository variable `CI_QUEUE_RUNS` (default off) keeps queue runs skipped. With it off, the gate in the queue re-reads the PR's own results, as it does today. With it on, the gate judges each workflow by its queue run where one ran, and by the PR run otherwise.
   - In a merge_group run, `github.event_name` isn't `pull_request`, so touched lanes run their main-push jobs too. That is intended: the queue is pre-main.

### Alternatives considered

- **Synthetic `ci-gate` check run posted from a `workflow_run` job.** Rejected: it creates a second check suite with the same name, and the result depends on which suite branch protection reads. Rerunning the gate's own run keeps a single source.
- **`dorny/paths-filter` per workflow, or a second map (`ci-scope.yml`).** Rejected: that would be two maps, and we already have a map plus a package graph with tests. A second source of truth would drift.
- **Generating `paths:` from the map.** Rejected: globs can't express package-graph dependents, and `merge_group` ignores `paths:`.
- **Running everything in the merge queue.** Rejected as the default: it costs 30–60 min per entry for every PR, including copy PRs.
- **Rewriting every `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` to include merge_group.** Tried, then dropped: about 210 expressions and 16 tests churned for a path that's off by default.

### Where the logic lives

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `.github/ci-areas.json` | Map, plus the new `narrow` block. Read from the base commit. |
| `.github/scripts/ci_gate_scope.py` | Rules 1–8, `--workflow` mode. |
| `.github/workflows/ci-quick.yml` | `scope` job and `skip` output. |
| `.github/workflows/ci-gate.yml` | Queue-run reading, behind `CI_QUEUE_RUNS`. |
| `.github/workflows/ci-gate-recheck.yml` and `.github/scripts/ci_gate_recheck.py` | Rerun the gate when a result turns green. |
| `docs/contributing/CI.md` | Contributor docs. |

### Measured (from real runs and the selector on real file lists)

**Web-only PR** (#6971 / #6965, `apps/cua-spaces-web` only):
- Before: 38–64 check runs (26–39 not skipped), about 15 min. Most of that is the web lane itself (`CI: Cua Spaces web UI and Electron shell`, 14 min).
- After: the same, about 15 min. Web-only PRs were already scoped by `paths:`. Only the samples suite now skips its jobs (it was about 1 min).

**#6992 file list** (Swift, Rust app-core and web together; it is not web-only):
- Before: 94 check runs. Wall time is bounded by `CI: cua SDK` (46 min, which legitimately lints `cua-spaces-ffi` and `cua-spaces-cli`).
- After: `CI: Test Python` (21 min), the openkoalabot Tauri suite (14 min) and the samples suite (13 min) skip their jobs. That saves about 48 runner-min. Wall time is unchanged until `CI: cua SDK` gets per-package test selection.
- The web subset of #6992 runs only the `spaces-web` lane.

**`libs/cua` Rust diff** (`cua-sdk`): still runs the Rust lane (`ci-cua-sdk`, `ci-test-python`, `ci-rust-*` as mapped).

**Stuck-red PRs:** after this, rerunning the failed job is enough. The gate reruns itself within seconds of the green completion.

### Risks and follow-ups

- **Scope job overhead:** about 15–20 s extra per heavy workflow per push (an ubuntu runner, no paid runners).
- **Recheck noise:** recheck runs on every completion of the about 100 listed workflows, including main pushes (skipped at the job level), which adds noise in the Actions list. The API cost is about 3 calls per green PR completion.
- **Queue switch:** turn on `CI_QUEUE_RUNS` only after one canary queue entry is green. Scripts that read `EVENT=pull_request` treat merge_group as non-PR, which fails closed to their full lanes.
- **Not yet covered:** about 60 light, path-filtered workflows without the quick stage have no `merge_group` trigger. In the queue they keep their PR result. Give them the stage, then add `merge_group`.
- **Remaining wall-time lever for cross-lane PRs:** per-package test selection inside `CI: cua SDK` (`nextest -p` over the affected set), as `ci_component_scope.py` already does for the driver.

### Testing

- `bin/ci --quick --fix`: green (actionlint, larger-runner guard, workflow sync).
- `.github/scripts/tests`: 1839 passed. New tests:
  - recheck decisions;
  - a sync test that the recheck lists every workflow the gate waits for;
  - narrowing on real paths, the web-only scope and `--workflow` output;
  - every heavy job reads the scope;
  - queue-run reading in the gate, on and off.
- The tests that pinned exact `needs:`/`if:` text were updated for the added `quick` need. A transformer checked the new wiring: each job's needs = old needs + `quick`, and no other key changed.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop cua-driver test from failing Linux and Windows on macOS grants
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux and Windows, `cua-driver test` always failed at step one. It read the macOS `accessibility` and `screen_recording` flags from `check_permissions`, which Linux and Windows don't report, so it said Cua Driver "can't use your mouse and keyboard" and "can't see your screen" and told the user to turn on Accessibility and Screen Recording.
- What changed: the test checks those grants only where the OS has them (macOS). Elsewhere it goes straight to the screen read and pointer steps, which are the real proof, and a failure there points to `cua-driver doctor` instead of `cua-driver permissions grant`, which is macOS only. The `cua-driver test` help says which platforms check permissions.

## Related work

Fixes #6998

RFC: not needed. No contract changes; `cua-driver test` keeps its steps, output and exit codes on macOS.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux and Windows `cua-driver test` (also run at the end of install) now passes when the driver works. Its JSON has no `accessibility` or `screen_recording` steps there. macOS is unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: a Linux or Windows install that can't read the screen still fails at `screen_read`. Revert to restore the old steps.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new `selftest` tests use what Linux `check_permissions` really returns. They failed on main with the same output users see and pass with the fix. `cargo test -p cua-driver`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver --all-targets -D warnings` (Linux, in a container), and `bin/ci --quick` pass. The help text matches `cua-driver dump-docs --type cli` from this build.
- Manual or platform evidence: on KDE Plasma 6.6.6 Wayland (Ubuntu 26.04), 0.44.0 prints the two macOS failures. This build prints `Cua Driver read your screen`, `Cua Driver moved its own pointer` and exits 0.
- Known gaps or CI still required: Windows not run by hand. It takes the same path as Linux, and CI's Windows lanes build it.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. Not applicable: this is a user-visible fix.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`). `bin/ci --quick` passes. A fork's sign-off is `CI: Quick`.

Prepared with an AI coding agent, and I ran the checks on my own machine.

title: fix(cua-driver): report the KWin capture switch as it is in the installer and health report
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: after `cua-driver kwin-capture on`, the installer still logged `KWin window capture is off` on every KWin machine, and `health_report` still said capture goes through the portal. Neither looked at the switch.
- What changed: `kwin_access` exposes one status (the switch, a portal Deny that keeps it off, and what the desktop entry names) that `kwin-capture status` now prints from.
  - The installer asks the installed driver for `kwin-capture status`. When the switch is on, it logs that status. Otherwise it logs the same off hint as before.
  - With the switch on, `health_report` names KWin ScreenShot2 as the first capture tier, matching `screenshot_display_dispatch`. When the desktop entry names another executable, it says KWin 6.7 and older refuse this one and to run `cua-driver kwin-capture on` again. With the switch off, the report is unchanged.

## Related work

Fixes #6999

RFC: not needed. No contract changes; `kwin-capture status` output is unchanged.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux on KWin only. One installer log line and the `screen_capture_capability` message change. Nothing is granted, written or switched.
- Risk and rollback: if the installed driver can't answer, the installer prints the old off hint. Revert to restore the old lines.

## Validation

It fails on main because the off hint is printed, and passes here. `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`, clippy `-D warnings` for `platform-linux` (with and without `portal-input`) and `cua-driver`, the installer integrity tests (all in containers), and `bin/ci --quick` pass.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop Windows stub registry panicking off Windows
body:
## Why
CUA-3314. On any non-Windows host, `platform_windows::tools::build_registry` panicked at `ToolDef::from_contract` with "portable subset contracts cannot replace live runtime schemas". The stub `InvokeMenuTool` went through `contract_stub_tool!`, which uses that canonical-schema bridge, but the `invoke_menu` contract is a portable subset. The Linux stubs had the same bug and #4715 fixed it there; the Windows stubs never got that fix.

## What changed
- The Windows `invoke_menu` stub builds its `ToolDef` by copying the contract fields, the same way the native Windows tool and the Linux stub do. `from_contract` keeps its assertion.
- `tests/stub_menu_registry.rs` (non-Windows only) builds the registry in standard and compat modes and checks the menu definition against the contract. It is the same test as the Linux one.
- The Linux CI test step now runs `-p platform-windows`, so this crate's off-Windows tests run in CI.

## Scope
Covers the Windows stub registry on non-Windows hosts. The native Windows registry and `from_contract` are unchanged.

## Blast Radius
Only non-Windows builds of `platform-windows` reach the stub. The CI step adds one more crate to an existing `cargo test` run.

## Verification
- At the base commit, the new test fails in both modes with the panic above. At head it passes.
- On macOS, the scoped repository checks pass: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-windows --all-targets -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p platform-windows --all-targets`.
- Windows and Linux builds could not run here. The Linux job covers the new CI step.

title: fix(spaces): a job shows as one row in the child Spaces list, wherever it runs
body:
A job is one row in the child Spaces list, wherever it runs. Without this, a job on another computer (for example an MLX job on a Mac) shows no child row at all, because the app only listed Space records on this computer.

- The daemon already writes `spawn/job-rows.json` from the run ledger and the pool's own answer (one row per run: name, GPU, host, state, gang size, error). The app reads it with the Space tree and lists each job under the Space that submitted it: pet name, JOB tag, GPU or OS icon, host as a quiet detail, state from the run (queued, starting, running, failed). Finished or canceled runs leave the list.
- The app's startup backend (`PendingSpacesBackend`) answered an empty tree, so child rows, budgets and kept services never reached the live app. It now forwards them. This was verified in the real app during an MLX run on a Mac: one row, `JOB`, `on mac-m2max`, Running.
- App core row fields (`jobName`, `jobGpu`, `jobRun`), bridge contracts and shapes, regenerated bindings, fixtures, and tests (job nodes for another host, a gang, a failed run, a missing or broken ledger; the backend forwarding).

Independent of #6799: built from main plus #7006 (merged), with this PR's own commits only (the two web conflicts were hand-resolved).

User impact: low. A list that was missing rows now shows them. Nothing changes for Spaces that are not jobs.

Local checks: web and desktop typecheck, job and bridge tests, clippy, rustfmt, SPDX, design lint. Not clean locally on Windows, same as main: the desktop packaging/uninstall tests, the Linux-only checks, one load-timing test that passes alone, the `onboarding_reset` golden (line endings), and the bindings comparison (line endings); CI on Linux is the judge for those.

title: Spaces web: i18n infrastructure, OS language from the host, Language setting (CUA-3886)
body: Part of [CUA-3886](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3886): Cua Spaces in the computer's language. **For users:** nothing changes yet. This sets up the plumbing, so the next PRs can move screens into the catalog and add languages. ## What this adds - **i18n in `apps/cua-spaces-web`:** i18next, react-i18next and ICU messages. There's one catalog file per area under `src/i18n/locales//`, and keys follow `area.screen.element`. English is bundled. Each other language loads as its own chunk before the first render that needs it, so no English flashes first. - **Language detection:** the saved choice comes first. Next come the system's preferred languages from the host: - SwiftUI: `cuaHost.languages` = `Locale.preferredLanguages`. - Electron (macOS and Windows): `cuaDesktop.languages` = `app.getPreferredSystemLanguages()`. - Browser and demo: `navigator.languages`. If none of those match, the app uses English. `zh-CN` maps to `zh-Hans`, and `zh-TW` is never shown Simplified Chinese. - **Draft languages** (machine translations not yet reviewed) appear in the switcher as "Preview". They're never picked automatically from the OS. - **Settings → General → Language:** "System (…)" plus each language in its own name, and it switches live. The row stays hidden while only English ships, so the English UI is unchanged. - **Pseudo-localization:** add `?lang=pseudo` to the URL. Strings that aren't extracted stay plain English, and the about 40% padding exposes clipping. - **CI guards (vitest):** - `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` checks the paths listed in `localized.ts`. It covers JSX text, visible attributes and props (`title`, `aria-label`, `label`, `description`, …) and toast titles. The list grows with each extraction PR. - `catalog.test.ts` checks that English is valid ICU, every key the code uses exists, and every shipped language has every key with the same variables. - **Core `Msg` codes** (`message.rs`) now resolve through the catalog. `lib/messages.ts` no longer has its own English table. - **CJK:** system CJK fonts and `word-break: auto-phrase`, plus `` that follows the language. Docs: `apps/cua-spaces-web/src/i18n/README.md`. ## Screenshots Settings → General, demo data. Before and after are identical in English because the row is hidden while only English ships. The pseudo view shows the Language row and the extracted strings. | | Before | After | Pseudo (`?lang=pseudo`) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Desktop (1440) | | | | | Narrow (760) | | | | ## Checks - `bin/ci --quick`: green (web and desktop typecheck, design lint, lockfiles, headers). - `vitest run` in `apps/cua-spaces-web`: 161 files passed. Next PRs: extract the shell (sidebar, top bar, command palette), Home, Computers and Settings. title: fix(spaces): hold back an agent's narration of its own process in the thread
body:
## What
A stretch of an agent's words after its opening line that begins a plan ("Let me look at it...", "I'll check...", "Now I'm writing...") is not posted to the thread. Closing messages and the opening line are untouched; the app's own "working for Ns" line shows the agent is busy.

## Why
Observed in a recorded run: "Got the logo. Let me look at it and see which packages exist for rasterizing." The brief says no narration, the model still does it before tool calls. A rule in prose does not hold; this is the structural filter (`is_process_narration`), with a unit test of what is held and what is not.

## Risk and rollback
A final message that happens to start with "I'll ..." after the first stretch would be held; the closing messages we write start with what the person has. Revert alone.

title: feat(cua-driver): formally-verify-cua-driver skill and TLA+ models for the driver's state machines
body:
## Why

The driver's riskiest code is a set of small state machines. They cover element tokens, the session lifecycle, permission admission, the macOS foreground restore, recording, Windows typing, daemon shutdown and the invoke_menu cancel. Their bugs only show up under one particular interleaving, and the repo had just two TLA+ models (recording, Windows typing) and nothing that ran them. This PR adds a project skill that checks every one of these machines with TLC in one command.

## What changed

- `.cursor/skills/formally-verify-cua-driver/`: `SKILL.md` maps each model to the functions it mirrors, its rules in plain words, and the harm when a rule breaks. It also covers how to run the models, how to tell a real bug from a modelling error, and the sync commit. `scripts/check-models.sh` runs every config in `models.tsv` against its expected result.
- Every spec lives in the skill's `models/` directory: new `token`, `session`, `admission`, `serve_drain`, `foreground_restore` and `invoke_menu_cancel`, plus the two loose models, which move there. Each has a config for main, one variant per guard that must fail, and a fixed variant for each open finding.
- `windows_typing.tla` now describes batched text (#6892) and a foreground lost before the first batch.

Old to new paths (every invariant and config is kept, and all of them run):

| Old (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/`) | New (`.cursor/skills/formally-verify-cua-driver/`) |
| --- | --- |
| `cua-driver-core/models/recording.tla`, `recording{,_restart,_dirfail,_idle}.cfg` | `models/recording.tla`, the same four configs (RC1-RC5) |
| `platform-windows/models/windows_typing.tla`, `windows_typing{,_always}.cfg` | `models/windows_typing.tla`, the same two configs (TypeOK, NoLateKeystroke, NoSteal, GivesWindowBack) |

The two doc comments that named the old paths (`cua-driver-core/tests/recording_restart.rs`, `platform-windows/src/typing_turn.rs`) now name the new ones. Nothing else in docs or CI referred to them.

## Scope

Models, configs, the skill, and two doc comments. No product code changes. The four open findings below are reported, not fixed:

- `session.cfg` SE5. An explicit end that saw no call in flight releases the records lock. A new call can then be admitted before `mark_session_ended` removes the record, so cleanup runs under a live call.
- `foreground_restore.cfg` FR1. `with_foreground_assist` restores the saved front app unconditionally, which undoes an app switch you made during the turn.
- `invoke_menu_cancel.cfg` MC2. The background menu worker holds neither the desktop lane nor the pid lease after its caller is dropped. The next action can run during the AX press.
- `serve_drain_windows.cfg` SD1/SD2. The Windows loop drops the pipe lock before `sdk.shutdown` and never joins its connections or releases proxy sessions.

Not covered: Linux desktop identity and the foreground table, more than one session per model, real time, and the unattached Windows typing path.

## Blast Radius

Agents and reviewers who touch the covered files. Nothing builds or ships from these files.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`, including both SPDX checks) pass, as does `cargo fmt --check` on the two touched Rust files.
- `check-models.sh` gives the expected result on all 23 rows. It exits 2 when a filter selects no row, and 1 when a row differs from `models.tsv`.
- I ran the skill once on a scratch change that deleted the idle re-check in `mark_session_ended`, and the session row failed as it should. With the change reverted, every row matched again. Every invariant in a passing config fails under a one-line mutation of its model or in a variant row.

title: fix(cua-driver): an end defers behind a call admitted after it decided
body:
## Why

`end_session_with_reason` checks `in_flight` under the records lock, releases the lock, and then calls `mark_session_ended`, which removes the record without checking again. A call admitted in that gap loses its session mid-action: cleanup (cursor, recording, grants, snapshots) runs under it, and its guard drop finds no record. The TLA+ session model in https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7035 finds this in 5 steps (`session.cfg`, rule SE5).

## What changed

- `mark_session_ended` checks `in_flight` under the same lock that removes the record. If a call is in flight, the end is recorded as that call's `pending_end`, and the call's guard drop finishes it with the same reason. A terminal reason still overrides a pending idle end.
- New test `an_end_waits_for_a_call_admitted_after_it_decided`. It admits a call in the gap and checks that no cleanup runs until the call ends, then that the end completes with `Explicit`.

## Scope

Only `cua-driver-core/src/session.rs`. The idle sweep already re-checks under this lock (#6773), and this applies the same rule to every end. `fire_session_end` now defers behind a call in flight too. Its callers are tests and the legacy reaper, and the reaper already tolerates a deferred end.

## Blast Radius

Every session end. An end that races a call now finishes when that call returns, not under it. `end_session` already reports "Session is ending after its in-flight action completes" for that case.

## Verification

- The new test fails at the base commit (the session ends under the live call) and passes with the fix.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` (1229 passed) and `cargo test -p cua-driver-sdk` pass.
- TLC: `session_fixed.cfg` (both re-checks) holds every rule.

title: fix(cua-driver): an invoke_menu worker keeps its pid lease and the desktop lane until it returns
body:
## Why

A background `invoke_menu` presses the item on a blocking worker that outlives a dropped call (#6953). The per-pid mutation lease and the desktop lane belonged to the dropped call future. When that future went away, both were freed while the worker could still be inside `AXPerformAction`, and the next desktop action on that pid ran beside the press. The TLA+ model in https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7035 (`invoke_menu_cancel.cfg`, rule MC2) finds it in 4 steps.

## What changed

- `run_admitted` takes an `Arc` share of the pid's `BackgroundMutationLease` and moves it, together with `DesktopLease::current()`, into the worker closure. `bring_to_front`'s worker has done the same since #6980. When the call is dropped, the lane marks the worker stale, and the next action waits for it, or gets `input_busy` after the lane's 12 s stale wait.
- New test `a_dropped_call_keeps_the_pid_until_its_worker_returns`. The test drops a call while its worker is parked and checks that the next acquirer of the pid's lease waits until the worker returns.

## Scope

Only the background route in `platform-macos/src/tools/invoke_menu.rs`, which the background `hotkey` key-equivalent route shares. The foreground route already runs inline under the call.

## Blast Radius

Live calls behave as before. After a cancel, the next action on the same pid, or the next desktop action, waits for the worker's AX call. That call is bounded by the 2 s AX messaging timeout plus up to 600 ms of enablement polling.

## Verification

- The new test fails at the base commit (the next action gets the lease while the worker runs) and passes with the fix.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (722 passed) all pass.
- TLC: `invoke_menu_cancel_fixed.cfg` (worker keeps both leases) holds MC1 and MC2.
- Skipped: the verify-cua-driver macOS Lume lane. Its doctor refused to start a guest for lack of free disk on this host.

title: fix(cua-driver): wait for a foreground-activated macOS control to report enabled
body:
Why the 0.44.1 and 0.44.2 releases stayed drafts: the release gate's hosted macOS native lane failed twice (including the retry) on `harness_appkit_foreground_from_the_background_rereads_enablement_after_activation`: `refusing AXPress: the target reports AXEnabled=false`. Signing, notarization, packaging and every other lane passed. It is not the Windows signing-list problem from #7038.

Cause: the AXEnabled re-read after a foreground activation ran as soon as the window reported focus, before the app had handled its activation. A control that is enabled only while its app is active still read disabled, and the call was refused. Push CI skips the hosted macOS lane, so only releases hit it.

Fix: foreground click, middle click, double_click and type_text re-read AXEnabled for up to 750 ms before refusing. A control that stays disabled is still refused as `element_disabled`, after the settle window. Background paths are unchanged.

For users: foreground actions on controls that an app enables on activation no longer fail intermittently.

Verification: the release gate is re-run on 0.44.2 after this merges.

title: fix(cua-driver): report the KWin capture switch and desktop entry as KWin reads them
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: after `cua-driver kwin-capture on`, the installer still logged `KWin window capture is off` on every KWin machine, and `health_report` still said capture went through the portal. With the switch on, the health report also passed cleanly when the desktop entry was missing, and `kwin-capture status` flagged any entry whose text differed from the template, such as one with an edited `Name`, as naming another executable.
- What changed:
  - From #7010 by @astrovm: `kwin_access::status()` is shared by `kwin-capture status`, the installer and `health_report`. The installer prints the real status when the switch is on, and `health_report` names KWin ScreenShot2 as the first capture tier.
  - An existing desktop entry is now judged by what KWin reads from it: the `Exec` program, compared to this executable with symlinks resolved, and the window-management and ScreenShot2 grants. Edits to `Name` or comments keep the grant. An entry for this executable that lacks one of those grants gets its own state.
  - With the switch on, `health_report` adds "run `cua-driver kwin-capture on` again" for a missing entry, another executable's entry, or an entry without the capture grants. Only a current entry reports no problem.

Salvaged from #7010. Linear: CUA-3890.

## Related work

Fixes #6999

RFC: not needed. No contract changes. `kwin-capture status` prints one new line, for an entry that names this executable without the capture grants.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux on KWin only. One installer log line, the `screen_capture_capability` message, and one possible `kwin-capture status` line change. Nothing is granted, written or switched.
- Risk and rollback: the status and health output are read-only diagnostics. If the installed driver can't answer, the installer prints the old off hint. Revert to restore the old lines.

risk: standard

Size: production lines run over the add/net guideline because the contributor's shared status plus the entry parser and health states fix one user-visible diagnosis, and splitting them would ship a health report that still passes a missing entry.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `health_report` tests for the current, missing, other-executable, ungranted, and edited-but-granting entry, and `kwin_access` tests for `Name`/comment edits, interface order, a dropped keystate, another or unquoted program, a symlink to this executable, and keys outside `[Desktop Entry]`. Breaking each behavior (whole-text compare, a missing entry that passes, no symlink resolution) turns one of these red. The scoped repository checks pass on Linux: rustfmt, `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`, and clippy `-D warnings` for `platform-linux` (with and without `portal-input`) and `cua-driver`. They also pass on macOS, along with `bin/ci --quick`.
- Manual or platform evidence: @astrovm's run on KDE Plasma 6.6.6 Wayland is in #7010.
- Known gaps or CI still required: no KWin session was run for the salvage commit. Desktop E2E (X11, Wayland, KWin) and Windows were not run. On a host with a real `kwin_wayland`, the installer integrity test `grants_nothing_on_kwin[False]` fails on main too, since its PATH keeps `/usr/bin`.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. Not applicable: this is a user-visible fix.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`)

title: feat(agents): official sign-in on each computer, stop copying sign-ins by default (CUA-3907)
body: Fixes [CUA-3907](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3907). **For users:** Cua no longer copies your Claude Code or ChatGPT sign-in to your other computers. When Claude Code or Codex on another computer isn't signed in, its message offers **Sign in to Codex on Mac mini**. You open the link on your phone or computer, sign in with ChatGPT or Claude, and the message is sent again. It's the providers' own sign-in, so the sign-in stays on that computer and Cua never holds it. Teams can still use an API key. **Why:** In 2026 Anthropic limited Claude subscription sign-ins to Claude Code itself (the January block, the February terms wording, the April cut-off for third-party harnesses). Moving that sign-in between machines is the grey zone. Now each install signs itself in. ## What changes - **Each computer signs itself in** (`cua_agents::remote_login`, `Agents::sign_in`). The agent's own login runs detached on the target computer: `codex login --device-auth` (codex-cli 0.164) or `claude auth login --claudeai` (Claude Code 2.1.318, which prints a link and waits for "Paste code here if prompted"). Cua reads only the link and code it prints. States: not signed in, signing in, signed in, failed (in plain words) and expired (a sign-in is there but the provider refused it). - **New person-only MCP tool `agent_sign_in`** `{space, agent, action: status|start|code|cancel, code?, after_refusal?}`. No MCP server lists it for agents. The contract, manifest and generated reference are updated. - **No copying by default.** `run_env`, `env_from_host` and `connection_plan` no longer deliver `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or `CODEX_AUTH_JSON` to any run, and Claude Code's login is not re-read at run start. A copied sign-in chosen as an app's account gives nothing, never another credential in its place. API keys go as before. - **Opt-in kept** (not removed). **Settings, Connections, On another computer, "Copy my sign-in to my other computers"** is off by default (`agent_keys.copy_sign_in`, `copy_sign_in` in the keys report). I kept it so people who used #6136 can turn it back on knowingly. Removing it would have silently deleted their stored copies. - **Apps:** `agents.computerSignIn` and `agentKeys.copySignIn` across the web bridge, SwiftUI and Electron hosts. Tauri reports `agents.computerSignIn` as unsupported, like the other person-only tools. The new `ComputerSignIn` sits in the thread's failure note on any computer that isn't This Mac. Docs are updated. ## Existing users who copied a sign-in (changes #6136's default) - Their saved copies stay in Keyvault but are no longer sent to new runs. - Runs that are already going keep the environment they started with, so nothing is stopped mid-job. - Their next run on a computer with no sign-in of its own gets the official sign-in prompt. - This Mac is unchanged: it uses the sign-in it already has. ## Persistence The sign-in lives in the computer's own `~/.codex/auth.json`, `~/.claude/.credentials.json` or Keychain, never on the Cua Volume. The Volume's secret scanner refuses credentials, and syncing a refresh token would mean Cua holds it again. Computers and local Spaces keep their disk, so they ask once. A cloud Space that is made again from its image asks again. ## Screenshots (demo data) | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Thread, desktop | | | | Signing in, desktop | (none) | | | Settings, desktop | | | | Thread, mobile | | | | Signing in, mobile | (none) | | | Settings, mobile | (none) | | On mobile, the floating desktop player is hidden in the screenshots. It covers the thread at phone width both before and after this change. ## Tests - **Rust:** `remote_login` covers each state (not signed in, signing in for Codex and Claude, signed in, failed, expired, cancel). An end-to-end test runs the real scripts with a stand-in `claude` that takes a pasted code. Another test checks that no sign-in reaches any harness by any route by default, and that one does once the person opts in. Results: `cua-agents` 95 passed; `cua-spaces` 501 passed; contract 23 passed; clippy `-D warnings` is clean on the three crates. - **Real CLIs:** an ignored test (`the_real_agents_show_their_sign_in_link`) ran the installed `codex` 0.164 and `claude` 2.1.318 through the same guest scripts in a throwaway home. It passed: Codex showed `https://auth.openai.com/codex/device` and a 10-character code, Claude showed its authorize link and asked for the pasted code, and both stopped cleanly on cancel. - **Web:** 232 files and 1629 tests passed, including the updated failure-card tests (which click Sign in, see the link, then use an API key) and the bridge state tests. **Desktop:** 80 files passed. `bin/ci --quick` is green. - **Not run:** a live sign-in inside a real Linux Space or VM with a real account. Follow-ups are tracked on CUA-3907. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(platform-macos): spawn owned-discovery fixture with only its named listeners
body:
## Why

CUA-3336. `owned_discovery_prefers_profile_endpoint_over_inherited_listener` and its five sibling owned-discovery tests flake under parallel runs. On main, 22 of 60 parallel runs of the `browser::` filter failed. The fixture forks a `/bin/sh` child that should own exactly three loopback listeners, then asserts that `lsof` reports exactly those three ports. It fails in two ways:

- **Extra port.** `std::process::Command` forks, and the fixture's `pre_exec` clears CLOEXEC on the three listeners. A socket another test thread has just created, but not yet marked CLOEXEC, crosses that fork, so `lsof` sees a fourth port.
- **No ports.** The forked child crashes in `libSystem_atfork_child` → `_notify_fork_child` ("os_once_t is corrupt", "crashed on child side of fork pre-exec" in the crash report) while `guarded_attach_flag_follows_live_guards` runs on another thread. It dies of SIGKILL before `lsof` runs.

## What changed

- The fixture spawns its child with `posix_spawn` and `POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT`. The child inherits only stdin (a pipe whose writer the test holds), `/dev/null` stdout/stderr, and the three listeners named through `posix_spawn_file_actions_addinherit_np`. The `libc` crate does not bind that function, so the test declares it locally.
- No fork, so no atfork handlers run in the child.

## Scope

Test fixture only, in `assert_owned_discovery_profile_case`. The asserted port list is unchanged: the child must still own exactly the three named listeners. Production discovery code is untouched.

## Verification

- At this head, 60 of 60 parallel `browser::` runs pass, 100 of 100 runs of the owned-discovery tests next to `guarded_attach_flag_follows_live_guards` pass, and 10 of 10 full `platform-macos` lib runs pass (721 tests each). No new fork crash reports appeared.
- Mutations: leaving out one listener's inherit fails on the first run (2 ports reported, 3 expected). Dropping `POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT` brings back the extra-port failure in 5 of 30 parallel runs.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and the lib tests for `platform-macos`, on macOS arm64.

title: test(agent): check predict_click's edge clicks through predict_click itself
body:
CUA-3768. Draft: the first rewrite from the test audit, shown as a sample before anything else in the audit moves. Please do not merge until the audit is reviewed.

The zero-coordinate tests for `predict_click` (#1515) ran a copy of the coordinate check, not `predict_click`, and grepped `anthropic.py` for the fix's exact spelling. So a regression that kept the spelling but dropped a zero x passed all six, and an equivalent rewrite of the check (`None not in (x, y)`) failed one.

This replaces them with tests that call `AnthropicHostedToolsConfig.predict_click` with liteLLM's reply stubbed, and read only what it returns: an edge click at x=0, y=0 or both comes back as given, a normal click comes back, and a reply with no click predicts nothing.

Checked by mutation on `cua_agent/loops/anthropic.py`:

title: [Bug]: Chromium radio buttons, select options and scroll into view fail by element on KDE Wayland
body:
### Primary area Cua Driver ### Summary On KDE Plasma Wayland, three Chromium page controls can't be used by element, even though Chromium exposes an AT-SPI action for each that works with no focus: 1. Clicking a radio button by `element_token` fails with `background_unavailable`. 2. A `Alpha
``` 1. `get_window_state` on the window. Rows: `radio button "Alpha" [actions=[check,…]]`, `check box "Gamma" [actions=[check,…]]`, `combo box [actions=[open,…]]`, `button "Press"`, `button "Far"`. 2. `click` by token on the check box and the button: both work. 3. `click` by token on the radio button. 4. `click` the combo box, then `click` with `role:"menu item", name:"Two"`. 5. `set_value` on the combo box with `"Two"`. 6. `scroll` by token on `button "Far"`. ### Expected behavior The radio is checked, option "Two" is selected and "Far" scrolls into view, all without focus, the same way the check box and button clicks already work. ### Actual behavior - Step 3: `Background delivery is not available: the requested target has no focus-free input backend; the remaining input route can only deliver to the globally focused widget.` - Step 4: the combo box opens, then `no menu item "Two" in window …`. - Step 5: `no_value_route: cached element exposes neither EditableText nor Value; the keyboard fallback needs an X11 session.` - Step 6: the same `background_unavailable` error as step 3. ### Environment Ubuntu 26.04.1, KWin 6.6.6 (Wayland), cua-driver 0.44.0, Google Chrome 157.0.8103.38. Code read at main `f2068eb68`. ### Evidence Calling AT-SPI directly (Python `gi.repository.Atspi`) on the same page, with the window unfocused, works for all three: - radio button "Beta": `do_action(0)` (`check`) returns true, and the radio reports `CHECKED`. - menu item "Two" (a child of the combo box's `menu`): `do_action(0)` (`select`) selects it. - button "Far": `Component.scroll_to(TOP_EDGE)` moves it from y=3911 to y=716. Cause of 3: `activation_index` in `platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs` accepts Chromium's `check`/`uncheck` only when the role is `check box` (`CHECKBOX_ACTIVATION_VERBS`). A radio button exposes only `check`, finds no activation, and falls through to the KWin input refusal in `tools/click.rs`. `select` isn't in `ACTIVATION_VERBS` for any role. ### Workaround and additional context Direct AT-SPI calls from a script, as above. Prepared with an AI coding agent, and I ran the checks on my own machine. title: [Feature]: Existing-profile setup for Brave

title: [Feature]: Verified foreground input on KDE Plasma Wayland
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On KDE Plasma Wayland there's no way to send keyboard or pointer input to a window, even in the foreground. `delivery_mode: "foreground"` refuses with `foreground_unavailable: this Wayland compositor does not expose a verified, target-addressable activation adapter for window …`, even with `cua-driver kwin-capture on`. So anything that needs real input fails: keyboard-only widgets (for example drag-and-drop with the keyboard), canvases and pointer drags.

`bring_to_front` on the same window works: KWin activates it. The refusal is deliberate (`refuse_kwin_input` in `wayland/mod.rs`): portal/libei input goes to whatever holds focus when it lands, so activating first doesn't bind the input to that window. `health_report` says the same: "KDE foreground input remains unavailable until a target-addressable KWin activation adapter is installed."

### Desired outcome

Foreground input works on KWin, with the same guarantee as other compositors: it either reaches the named window or is refused.

### Current workaround

Outside cua-driver: activate the window with a KWin script (`workspace.activeWindow = w`, loaded with `org.kde.kwin.Scripting.loadScript`), then send keys with `ydotool`. It works, but nothing checks that focus didn't move in between.

### Affected components and platforms

`platform-linux` Wayland input on KWin (KDE Plasma 6.6.6 tested).

### Alternatives and prior art

The GNOME path uses a Shell helper as its activation adapter.

### Implementation ideas

A KWin activation adapter that verifies: activate the window through KWin (`kwin_capture::activate` already does this for `bring_to_front`), confirm through KWin that it is `workspace.activeWindow`, send the libei input, then confirm it's still the active window and report `unverifiable` if it changed. This changes when the driver lets input through, so if you'd rather handle it as an RFC, I'm happy to move it there.

Prepared with an AI coding agent, and I ran the checks on my own machine.

Prettier fails on the 7 app-harness test files from #6473 because nothing enforces Prettier in `apps/cua-spaces-web`, not because those files drifted. title: test(cua-spaces-web): poll for the drawn report in expectDrawn instead of sleeping 400 ms
body:
## Why

`expectDrawn` in the popup stream spec slept a fixed 400 ms before it read the popup's box and the viewer's video report. On an idle machine that wastes time on every popup. Under load it is too short, and the single box read can catch the popup mid-animation. This is a follow-up to https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6469.

## What changed

- `expectDrawn` polls until the popup's box is the same in two samples in a row and the latest report matches it. The report must keep the same rect, stay visible, be interactive unless the popup is a modal, be occluded only under a modal, have a hole under a non-modal popup that covers the picture, and have no holes under a modal.
- It checks the same conditions as before, now together in one poll with the 5 s limit. `over` comes from the final settled box.

## Scope

Only `apps/cua-spaces-web/e2e/space-popups-stream.spec.ts`. No product code changed. The other `waitForTimeout` calls in the e2e specs and scripts are left alone.

## Verification

- Under parallel load (`--repeat-each=30 --workers=16`, plus 10 CPU burners on a 10-core host, two rounds per side): the old spec passed 44/60, mostly by hitting the 30 s test timeout. The new spec passed 59/60. Its one failure was the page load assertion (`[data-stream-surface]` visible) that runs before `expectDrawn` is ever called.
- With lighter load (`--repeat-each=20 --workers=10`, 4 burners), both versions passed 20/20.
- The scoped repository checks in apps/cua-spaces-web: `pnpm typecheck`, vitest (1626 passed, 1 skipped), and the full browser parity suite (49 passed, 17 skipped). The Electron parity host and the Linux verify-cua-spaces lane did not run.

title: fix(cua-driver): pick Chromium radios, options and scroll by element on Linux
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux, Chromium pages had controls the driver couldn't use by element in the background. A radio or list option click fell through to the global-input route (refused on KDE Wayland), `set_value` on a `<select>` failed with `no_value_route`, and `scroll` on a control with no scroll action of its own was refused.
- What changed:
  - Radio buttons: Chromium's `check` action now counts as their click, as it already did for check boxes.
  - List and menu options: Chromium's `select` action now counts as their click. Only option roles get it.
  - `<select>`: Chromium's combo box has no `Selection`, and `SelectChild` on its menu does nothing. `set_value` now fires the option's own `select` action and confirms the option reports SELECTED. Reading the combo's value returns that option's name instead of `￼`.
  - `scroll` on an element with no scroll action or Value now scrolls the nearest ancestor that has one, like a mouse wheel over the element would.

## Related work

Fixes #7052

RFC: not needed. No new tool or parameter: existing calls succeed where they were refused.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: these calls now work in the background on Chromium-family browsers on Linux (X11 and Wayland). Other toolkits keep their current routes: the new verbs only apply to the roles above, and the `<select>` fallback only fires an option's `select` action.
- Risk and rollback: a scroll on a non-scrolling control now moves its scrollable ancestor instead of refusing. Each part is separate and can be reverted on its own.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - Unit tests for the role-gated verbs (radio `check`, option `select`, and that other roles don't get them) and for the ancestor walk.
  - `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`: 998 passed.
  - `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -D warnings` and `bin/ci --quick` are green.
- Manual or platform evidence: KDE Plasma 6.6.6 Wayland, Chrome with `--force-renderer-accessibility`, a test page with a radio group, a check box, a `<select>`, a list box and buttons below the fold. Each result read back over AT-SPI:

  | Call | Before (0.44.0) | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | `click` on radio **Beta** | refused (`background_unavailable`) | Beta CHECKED |
  | `set_value` `<select>` to "Three" | `no_value_route` | `confirmed`, Three SELECTED |
  | `set_value` `<select>` to "Purple" | `no_value_route` | `option_not_found`, nothing changed |
  | `click` on list box item **Blue** | refused (`background_unavailable`) | Blue SELECTED |
  | `scroll` down on button **Press** | refused | page scrolled about 1,470 px |

- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - Not run on X11. The code path is the same AT-SPI route.
  - Radio, list item and scroll clicks report `unverifiable`, the same as check box clicks today.

title: Linux X11: desktop type_text types under a latched modifier, so a sticky Ctrl turns text into shortcuts
body:
## Problem

On X11, `type_text` with `scope: "desktop"` (no pid) types through `send_type_text_xtest_paced` (`platform-linux/src/input/mod.rs`, line 3829 on 609e5f7f9). It presses plain XTest keycodes and does not look at the keyboard's modifier state. A modifier the user has latched (StickyKeys) or locked stays in effect, so each typed key reaches the focused app as a shortcut. With Ctrl latched, `type_text "c"` arrives as Ctrl+C: nothing is typed, the latch is spent, and the call still reports success.

The background MPX path already clears this state: `input/mod.rs:1347` calls `XkbLockModifiers` and `XkbLatchModifiers` on the virtual master when it finds a locked or latched modifier. Since #6827, the KWin libei route reads held and latched modifiers and refuses the text. The X11 XTest route does neither.

## Reproduction

X11 session (Ubuntu 24.04, Xfce, gedit), on a build based on 0.43.1. The XTest typing loop on main 609e5f7f9 has no modifier handling either.

1. `xkbset sticky -twokey -latchlock`
2. Focus a text editor with an empty document.
3. Press and release Ctrl once (`xdotool key Control_L`). The XKB state now reads `mods=0x04 latched=0x04`.
4. Call `type_text {"text": "c", "scope": "desktop"}`.

Expected: `c` in the document.
Actual: the result is `Typed text into the focused desktop application.`, the document stays empty, and the XKB state afterwards shows `latched=0x00`, because the latch was spent on Ctrl+C. Running step 4 again with no latch types `c`.

## Possible fix

Before it types, the XTest route could clear latched and locked modifiers on the core keyboard (`XkbLatchModifiers(dpy, XkbUseCoreKbd, mask, 0)`, `XkbLockModifiers`) and restore the locks afterwards, as the MPX path does. A modifier that is physically held cannot be cleared that way. For that case it could either send a fake key-up first, like `xdotool --clearmodifiers`, or refuse the text, like the libei route. I can send a PR for whichever you prefer.

title: fix(cua-driver): Windows type_text's tail repair and read-back leave text that replaced a selection
body:
## Problem

The PostMessage tail repair compares the field before and after typing by removing their common prefix and suffix (`inserted_segment`). When the typed text replaced a selection and shares its end with that selection, the shared characters are taken out of the insert. What remains looks like a strict prefix of the requested text, so the repair types the remainder again:

| selected | typed | result |
|---|---|---|
| `c` | `abc` | `abcc` |
| `10` | `110` | `11010` |
| `c` | `cc` | `ccc` |

#6741 reported the select-all case (`hello from cua` → `set by cua cua`) and was closed without a merge. This change covers that case and the cases above.

The read-back verdict has two smaller gaps:
- It matches the requested text against the raw value. An Edit control stores Enter as CRLF, so multi-line text never matches and is reported as not landed.
- A value that did not change is reported as a firm drop, although typing over an identical selection gives the same reading.

## Change

- `typed_over(before, after, typed)` is true when `after` is a prefix of `before`, then the whole typed text, then a suffix of `before`, with the prefix and suffix not overlapping in `before`. It compares with newlines normalized. When it is true, the tail repair returns `Done`. A tail the target really dropped is still retyped.
- The read-back counts `typed_over` as observed, so text with line breaks matches.
- An unchanged value gets its own unverifiable result (`verify: "unchanged"`): the text was dropped, or it replaced an identical selection. A changed value that does not contain the text keeps the foreground escalation, now with `verify: "missing"`.

## Test

- `tail_retry_tests::text_that_replaced_a_selection_ending_like_it_is_not_retyped`
- `post_message_readback_tests::text_typed_over_a_selection_is_observed_and_an_unchanged_value_is_not`, which includes `post_message_readback_observed(Some(""), Some("a\r\nb"), "a\nb")`
- The existing tail-retry and read-back tests are unchanged.

On main, without this change, both new checks fail on windows-2025:

```
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: Retype("c")
 right: Done
```

```
assertion failed: post_message_readback_observed(Some(""), Some("a\r\nb"), "a\nb")
```

## Checks

- [x] `bin/ci --quick`: 3 passed, 1 skipped (Rust checks: no cargo on that machine).
- [x] On a windows-2025 runner: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the platform-windows lib tests (322 passed).
- [ ] No rerun on a Windows desktop against main.

title: test(cua-driver): wait for the spawned process's environment before reading it in the NO_AT_BRIDGE test
body:
Fixes #6987.

## Problem

`an_empty_walk_reads_the_reason_from_the_real_process` spawns `sleep` with `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1` and reads `/proc/<pid>/environ` right away. `Command::spawn` returns once the child calls `execve`, and the read can land before the kernel has set up the new image's environment. The read then comes back empty and the test fails with `left: None`.

Since #6987 was filed, it failed on the first attempt of 2 of 2 Linux CI runs on a 0.45.1-based branch today (`cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib` on ubuntu-24.04), and both passed on re-run:

panicked at crates/platform-linux/src/atspi/mod.rs:1180:9:
  left: None
test result: FAILED. 1006 passed; 1 failed; 11 ignored
```

- https://github.com/loomhand/cua/actions/runs/42544514589/attempts/1
- https://github.com/loomhand/cua/actions/runs/42546422597/attempts/1

## Change

Test only. The `Sleeper` helper waits, up to 2 s, until `/proc/<pid>/environ` is non-empty before the test reads it. The code under test is unchanged.

title: feat(cua-driver): bind KDE foreground input to the target window
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on KDE Wayland, KWin sends each input event to whatever window has focus when it processes that event. The driver could activate the target, then focus could move (a notification, the user, another app), and the rest of the keys or clicks would land in the wrong application. So foreground input on KWin was refused (#7054).
- What changed:
  - The KWin helper (protocol 2) gets an input gate. While it's armed, a KWin input filter lets this driver's libei events reach only the target window or its transients (dialogs, menus). Anything that would reach another window is held back. KWin decides per event, after it resolves focus and before any window sees the event, so there's no check-then-send gap.
  - The gate only covers devices of the libei client that armed it (named `cua-driver <pid>`). Other input tools are untouched. It is released on `DisarmInput` or when the arming D-Bus connection closes, so a crashed driver can't leave it armed.
  - The driver arms the gate around each KWin input call (`click`, `scroll`, `drag`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey`). It activates the target inside the gate, confirms keyboard focus, sends the input, then gives focus back to the window that had it.
  - If the gate held anything back, the call fails with `input_interrupted` and says how many events stopped. Those events reached no other window.
  - While the gate is armed, the non-libei routes (wlroots virtual pointer and keyboard, `wtype`) stand down, since the gate can't see them.
  - While the gate is armed, text goes only as key presses. KWin 6.8 hands `ei_text` strings to the input method without passing any input filter, so the gate can't see them. Text the layout has no key for is refused.
  - `type_text` and `press_key` replies on Wayland now name the route that really sent the keys (`libei`, `niri's keyboard`, `Wayland virtual-keyboard`, `cua-compositor`). They always said "virtual-keyboard", even when KDE used libei.
  - The helper now builds on Debian 13 (KWin 6.3) and Fedora 45 (KWin 6.8) too: it finds ECM and epoxy itself, and keeps the plugin in the build tree on older ECM (it was written to `/kwin/...`).
  - `cua-driver kwin-capture on` now also loads the helper, when it is installed, and sets its `kwinrc` entry so KWin starts it with every session. Before, the helper had to be loaded by hand with `qdbus6` after every login. `off` undoes both, and `status` says whether the helper is installed, loaded and set to start.
  - New `kwin-target-helper/install.sh` builds the helper against the machine's KWin, installs it, and runs `kwin-capture on`.
  - Without helper protocol 2, KWin input stays refused, as before, and the refusal now names `cua-driver kwin-capture on`. Background input on KWin stays refused.

```
driver ──ArmInput(target)──▶ KWin helper
driver ──libei key/click──▶ KWin: resolve focus ─▶ gate: focus is target? ── yes ─▶ target window
                                                                         └─ no ──▶ held back (counted)
driver ──DisarmInput──▶ {passed, dropped} ─▶ dropped > 0 ⇒ input_interrupted
```

## Related work

Fixes #7054

RFC: not needed. No new tool or parameter. The helper's D-Bus API grows by three methods (`ArmInput`, `GetInputGate`, `DisarmInput`) plus `GetFocus`, and protocol 1 callers keep working.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: foreground input to KWin windows now works when the helper is installed, `cua-driver kwin-capture on` has run, and the driver has libei input. Users with an older helper get the same refusal as today, with a message that names protocol 2.
- On KWin 6.8, text a layout can't type now gets refused when bound to a window, instead of going through `ei_text`. Before this PR, all KWin foreground input was refused, so nothing that worked before stops working.
- `kwin-capture on` now writes one entry to `kwinrc` (`cua_kwin_target_helperEnabled=true` under `[Plugins]`), through `kwriteconfig6`, and only when KWin lists the helper as installed. `kwin-capture off` removes it.
- The helper is still built on the user's machine: KWin loads only a plugin built for its own version, so it needs a rebuild after a KWin upgrade. `status` then reads "installed but not loaded".
- What the gate does not stop: KWin moves the pointer and updates modifier state before input filters run, so a held-back event can still move the cursor or leave a modifier pressed in KWin's state. It never reaches another window. This is written down in the helper README.
- Risk and rollback: the helper change is a KWin effect plugin. A bug there runs inside KWin. The gate filter only reads focus and returns early when not armed. Reverting this PR goes back to refusing KWin input.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - New opt-in kit `libs/cua-driver/kwin-target-helper/tests/run.sh [cua-driver]`, with `DISTRO=debian13` or `DISTRO=fedora45`. It installs the helper with `install.sh`, runs headless KWin in a container, and opens two test windows, A and B, that log every key and click they get. With a driver, it turns the helper on through `kwin-capture on`, restarts KWin, and checks that the helper comes back by itself and that `off` clears the `kwinrc` entry.
  - Gate suite, raw libei clients, 10 / 10: target focused, other window focused, no gate armed, foreign client, focus moved mid-input, click aimed at B, click on A, client with no device, caller disconnect.
  - Driver suite, the real `cua-driver mcp`, 6 / 6:

    | Case | Result |
    |---|---|
    | `type_text` into A while B is active | A gets `hi`, B nothing, B active again |
    | Pixel `click` on A while B is active | A gets the click, B nothing |
    | Focus stolen every 0.3s during slow typing | `input_interrupted`, KWin held back 18 events, B got no keys |
    | `press_key` Return into A while B is active | A gets Return, B nothing |
    | Background `click` on a KWin window | refused, nothing sent |
    | Helper unloaded | `foreground_unavailable`, nothing sent |

  - Results per distro, with one driver built on Debian 13:

    | Image | KWin | Gate suite | Driver suite |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | Debian 13 | 6.3.6 | 10 / 10 | 6 / 6 |
    | Ubuntu 26.04 | 6.6.6 | 10 / 10 | 6 / 6 |
    | Fedora 45 | 6.8.2 | 10 / 10 | 6 / 6 |

  - Fedora 45 caught a real bypass: before the `ei_text` change, driver case 3 sent 19 of 20 keys to window B while the gate was armed, and reported success.
  - Stable across 3 repeat runs on Ubuntu plus 2 runs of the in-repo kit.
  - Mutation checks: a gate that never holds anything back fails gate cases 2, 6, 7 and driver case 3. Dropping the `ei_text` rule fails `text_bound_to_a_window_goes_as_keys_never_through_ei_text`. A `kwin-capture on` that skips the `kwinrc` entry fails the restart check, and an `off` that keeps it fails the last check.
  - `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib --features portal-input,portal-capture`: 1077 passed.
  - `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -D warnings`, with and without those features, and `bin/ci --quick` are green.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - Real Plasma 6.6.6 session (Kubuntu 26.04, helper installed system-wide and loaded with `loadEffect`): the driver suite passes 6 / 6, with focus theft refused after KWin held back 19 events.
  - Not run on a real Plasma 6.8 session; Fedora 45 is headless only.
  - That real session ran before the `kwin-capture on` change. The `kwinrc` start was checked on headless KWin restarts on all three images, not across a real Plasma login.
  - The kit needs `/dev/dri` for window capture and is not wired into CI.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`)

Prepared with an AI coding agent, and I ran the checks on my own machine.

title: `cua_auth::Credentials` Debug output exposes access, refresh, and ID tokens
body:
## Summary

`Credentials` derives `Debug` and stores `access_token`, `refresh_token`, and
`id_token` as plain fields. Its ordinary `{:?}` output prints all three token
values verbatim, and serde serialization emits them as well.

## Affected code

- Repository: `trycua/cua`
- Commit: `eb679b9e021146c5d948e58b8422e6b0589cf3b1`
- File: `libs/cua/crates/cua-auth/src/lib.rs:134`

## Expected behavior

Debug/serialization of a credential-bearing type should redact token values or
exclude them from the ordinary representation.

## Actual behavior

A probe linked against the real `cua-auth` crate printed:

```text
Debug: Credentials { access_token: "ACCESS_TOKEN_VERIFY_1_9f3a",
  refresh_token: Some("REFRESH_TOKEN_VERIFY_1_7c2b"),
  expires_at: "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z", token_type: "Bearer",
  scope: Some("openid profile offline_access"),
  id_token: Some("ID_TOKEN_VERIFY_1_a1b2") }
access token in Debug:  true
refresh token in Debug: true
id token in Debug:      true
```

Serde also emitted all three values.

## Impact

Any diagnostic, error, or trace that formats `Credentials` with `{:?}` or
serializes it writes reusable bearer credentials to logs.

## Suggested fix

Implement a redacting `Debug` for `Credentials`, or wrap the token fields in a
secret type whose `Debug` is `"***"`; keep serialization explicit for the
credential store only.

title: fix(ci): release gate ignores the PR-only quick job when it is skipped
body:
## Why
The post-merge release gate on main (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/42544993683) went red with every lane green: `release-gate lanes not green: quick=skipped`. This is a gate bug, not a driver break. #7008 added the PR-only `quick` job to the `needs` of `result` and `nightly-report`. On push, schedule and dispatch runs `quick` is always `skipped`, and both jq filters counted that as a failed lane.

## What changed
- `result` treats a skipped `quick` as expected outside `pull_request` and `merge_group` events.
- `nightly-report` leaves a skipped `quick` out of the failed-lane list, the same way it already treats `macos-pr`.
- The nightly report tests now include `quick: skipped` in their fixture, as a real full run reports it, and also run the `result` step script.

## Scope
Only `.github/workflows/e2e-cua-driver-release-gate.yml` and its test. The other workflows that list `quick` in `needs` already accept skipped jobs in their filters.

## Blast Radius
Full release-gate runs on main. A real lane that is skipped, cancelled or failed still fails both jobs, and the tests cover each of those cases.

## Verification
- With the new tests and the old workflow, six tests fail: the two green-nightly cases, the flaky-evidence case, and the three full-run `result` cases. With the fix, the release-gate test files pass, and so does the whole `.github/scripts/tests` suite.
- actionlint on the workflow is clean.

CUA-3937
Fixes #7068

title: fix(spaces): run Prettier on the Cua Spaces apps again
body:
## Why

#7057 (CUA-3358) added `apps/cua-spaces-web/`, `apps/cua-spaces-desktop/` and `apps/cua-spaces-mobile/` to `.prettierignore` to avoid a 746-file reformat, so Prettier stopped checking these apps. This turns it back on for all four JS Spaces apps, including `apps/cua-spaces`, and CI now checks them.

## What changed

- Each app has a `.prettierrc.yaml` in its own style: double quotes, `trailingComma: all`, `printWidth` 160 (120 for `apps/cua-spaces`). `.prettierignore` drops the three app directories and keeps only committed generated files whose generators compare output byte for byte: the UniFFI bindings, `routeTree.gen.ts`, `bridge/generated/`, `bridge-shapes.json`, `pet-names.generated.ts`, the synced Connect-ES types and the Swift-written `mac-host-settings-*.json` fixtures. `tauri.conf.json` and the mobile core fixtures use the `json-stringify` parser, which matches how Release Please and their generators write them.
- New `spaces-prettier` check in `bin/ci --quick`, so `CI: Quick` runs it. It runs `prettier@3.6.2 --check` (the pre-commit hook's version) on changed files in those apps and fails, rather than skips, when the tool is missing on the runner. `bin/ci --fix` repairs it.
- One mechanical `prettier --write` over 667 files (+15,964/-4,651). This also normalises `apps/cua-spaces` to double quotes: 15 of its files were mostly single-quoted. 84 files are left unformatted for now, and each is formatted the next time it changes, which is why the check covers changed files. Six existing `design-ok:` comments moved next to the lines they exempt, and `overlay.test.ts` now matches the Backdrop element across lines instead of on one line.

## Scope

Formatting config, the CI check and the reformat. No lint rule is disabled and no `eslint-disable` or `prettier-ignore` is added. `apps/cua-spaces-macos` (Swift) is unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

- No config matches the existing code. These apps were never formatted, so every config rewrites most files. Double quotes with width 160 rewrites the fewest lines among the configs measured: about 20k changed lines, against about 63k for width 100 and 110k for the root single-quote config. The root config would also flip every string in about 1,360 files.
- The check runs on changed files, not the whole tree, so the 84 files left out do not block unrelated PRs.

## Blast Radius

Pre-commit and format-on-save now format these apps with their own config instead of skipping them. 31 open PRs touch files that were reformatted, and most of them will need a merge of main (`bin/ci --fix` reformats their side). Behaviour does not change: a Babel AST comparison of the 643 reformatted JS/TS files, with comments compared too, finds no difference except `overlay.test.ts`, and the reformatted JSON files parse to the same values.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`, the `bin/ci` unit tests, `bin/ci --verify-sync`) pass. The new check fails on an edited single-quoted file and on a new unformatted file, and `--fix` repairs both.
- `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass in all four apps. `pnpm proto:check` in `apps/cua-spaces-mobile` reports the same three drifted files on main as on this branch, and this PR leaves those files alone.
- Not run here: the Linux Spaces desktop journey and the Linux and Windows platform builds.

Size: the production diff is the mechanical reformat. The hand-written part is 8 config, CI and doc files (+78/-7).

Follows #7057, CUA-3358.

title: fix(cua-driver): route macOS element-token middle clicks to the target window
body:
CUA-3797, follow-up to https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6947.

An element-token middle click never reached an AppKit control. The element path in `click` posted through `middle_click_at_xy`, which stamps no window-local point and no window id. AppKit hit-tests that stamp, so the `otherMouseDown` never arrived, in background and in foreground delivery. The pixel middle click and the double_click AX fallback already use the window-routed primitive and do reach the control. AppKit buttons do take middle clicks. The driver was not routing this one.

## Change

- `platform-macos` `click`, `button: "middle"` with `element_token`: translate the element center by the window's bounds and post through `middle_click_at_xy_with_window_local`, like the pixel path. If the bounds can't be resolved it errors and sends nothing. The foreground-with-modifiers branch is unchanged, since it posts at the HID tap.
- AppKit fixture: the active-only button reports `active_only=middle_click` on `otherMouseDown` while it is enabled.
- `macos-appkit-activation-enablement-ax-foreground` gains a success row. A foreground element-token middle click on the active-only button from behind another app must land. The refusal row on the always-disabled checkbox stays.

## Proof

Repro on the host with a minimal AppKit window holding one NSButton that logs `otherMouseDown`: at the base, element-token middle clicks in foreground and in background delivery logged nothing. Pixel middle clicks at the same point logged `middle_down`/`middle_up`. With the fix, element-token middle clicks logged `middle_down`/`middle_up` in foreground, in background, and in foreground with the app starting behind Finder.

The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-e2e --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`, and a `swiftc` compile of the AppKit fixture. Full macOS Lume guest matrix at the head through the verify-cua-driver skill: 179 delivered, 5 refused, 0 failed. In the new row the fixture records `active_only=middle_click` after the call. Two earlier full runs at this head each failed only `macos-appkit-invoke-menu-ax-foreground`: a background-disabled menu item got invoked. That cell is not touched here. It failed the same way at three earlier heads of #6947, and the base run on main passed it, so it reads as intermittent.

Not run: Linux and Windows lanes (macOS-only change), standalone browsers, SIP-on permission flow.
