title: ci: stop using pull_request_target before GitHub's 2 Dec enforcement
body:
Linear: CUA-3966

## Why
GitHub is blocking `pull_request_target` by default on public repositories from 2 Dec 2026, unless an Actions policy explicitly allows it. A scheduled brownout on 9 Nov (16:03 to 18:00 UTC) already blocked every `pull_request_target` run (`startup_failure`), which made `ci-gate` fail on every PR. We chose to stop using the event rather than add an allowlist policy (an allowlist blocks every event not listed, which is a footgun for new workflows).

## What changed
- **contributor-attribution** (required check): now `pull_request`, read-only token, no secrets. It only calls GET endpoints, so a fork's read-only token is enough. It checks out the tip of the base branch (not the merge commit) to run the validator, so PR code never runs. The check name `contributor-attribution` is unchanged, so the ruleset and `ci-gate` keep working.
- **release-pr-auto-merge**: now `pull_request`; the job only runs for same-repo `release-please--branches--*` PRs and is skipped for forks. The script still comes from the default branch; push and 30-minute sweep are unchanged.
- **ci-release-reminder**: now `pull_request`; skipped for fork PRs (a fork token cannot comment).
- **CLA**: split. The `cla.yml` `collect` job (pull_request, no permissions, no secrets) uploads only the PR number as an artifact. New `cla-report.yml` (`workflow_run`, runs from the default branch, never checks out PR code) validates the number as an integer, reads everything else from the API, sets the informational `cla` status and posts or updates the "please sign" comment (new `cla_pr_report.py`, with tests). The `issue_comment` job (`recheck` / sign phrase) is unchanged and now also refreshes the status and comment.
- **ci-gate / recheck / weekly report**: read `pull_request` runs only. `workflow_run` runs are not waited on; the gate keeps ignoring `cla.yml`. A new test fails if any workflow uses `pull_request_target`.

## Security model
No PR code runs with secrets or a write token. Fork PRs get a read-only token in every `pull_request` job. Privileged jobs (`cla-report`, the `issue_comment` job) run from the default branch and treat the artifact as untrusted data.

## Behaviour to know
- A first-time fork contributor's `contributor-attribution` and `cla` runs now wait for a maintainer to approve the workflow run, like the rest of CI (ci-gate already needed that). Previously they ran without approval.
- Fork PRs no longer get the release reminder.
- `cla-report.yml` starts working once this is on main (workflow_run workflows load from the default branch).

## Checks
actionlint on the changed workflows, `bin/ci --quick --fix`, and the gate, recheck, weekly-report and new tests pass.

title: fix(cua-driver): pace the Linux virtual keyboard and unplug it when keys stay unread
body:
Salvaged from #7076 by @CMGS. Supersedes #7076. The stacked follow-up #7146, the salvage of #7079, is merged into this branch, so this PR carries both.

## Why

Since #6892, background `type_text` on X11 through the virtual master keyboard (`path=mpx_uinput`) writes the whole text to the uinput device at once. A keys-only uinput device gets a 64-event evdev buffer, so an X server short of CPU loses most of the text and the call still reports success. @CMGS's change sends at most one run of about 8 key transitions before it waits for the server to report them as raw key events, and fails with a count of what was read if the server stalls. This PR keeps that change, fixes what review found around the timeout, and gives the keyboard's state one owner each.

## What changed

- @CMGS's commits, cherry-picked with authorship kept. `confirm_points` splits the text into runs that end with no key held, and the delivery counts the slave's raw key events at each run end. A key on a borrowed keycode gets the paced hold, and borrowed keycodes stay bound until `SPARE_KEYCODE_IDLE` after the last key on them.
- Key repeat. A server that read a key's press and then stalled before its release held the key and repeated it into the target until the release arrived. This also happens on main. The driver writes every key transition itself, so `disable_key_repeat` now turns the server's XKB key repeat off on the keyboard when it is plugged in, and the plug-in fails if that cannot be done.
- One owner for each piece of state:
  - `Keyboard` holds the uinput device with its slave id. A session has a keyboard exactly while it is in the map. `MasterPointerIds.slave_keyboard_id` is gone, so the id can no longer outlive the device.
  - `Delivery` is one call's use of the keyboard. It counts the transitions written and the ones the server read back, and tracks the keys left down. When it drops it releases those keys and unplugs a keyboard that still has unread transitions, on every exit path. The kernel then discards them, so the server never reads them under the restored keymap and the next call never counts them.
  - The warm-up key goes through a `Delivery` too. A new keyboard whose warm-up key the server never reports is no longer kept. Before, the next call counted that key as its own and confirmed two transitions early.
  - `BorrowedKeycodes` owns the remapped keycodes and the time of the last key on them, for the XSendEvent, XTest and virtual keyboard routes.
- `models/virtual_keyboard.tla` models the keyboard's lifecycle, with a statechart in `models/virtual_keyboard.md`. Its five states are unplugged, still listed by the server, warming up, ready and typing.
- The XTest route holds a borrowed key before it releases it. The two Xvfb-spawning restore tests are `#[ignore]` with their own CI step.

## Scope

The X11 key routes: the virtual keyboard (`mpx_uinput`), and the spare-keycode lifetime on the XSendEvent and XTest routes. It does not make delivery to an arbitrarily slow client correct. X11 has no signal that a client has translated a key event, so `SPARE_KEYCODE_IDLE` is a bound, not a guarantee, and `a_client_that_looks_up_after_the_idle_window_reads_no_symbol` pins that limit.

## Tradeoffs

- Key repeat is turned off instead of making the release arrive on time. Nothing the driver does makes a stalled input thread read, and guarding press and release as a pair cannot help once the server has read the press. No tool on this route holds a key down to repeat it.
- Draining the evdev queue before the keymap restore was the other option for unread keys. A stalled server may not read it for seconds. Unplugging discards it at once and costs one hot-plug, only after a failure.
- A stalled server during the warm-up now fails the call instead of typing on a keyboard in an unknown state. The next call plugs in a new one.
- Keycode 248 is the warm-up key and is never borrowed, so a layout has one fewer keycode for unmapped characters.

## Blast Radius

Every background `type_text` and key chord on X11 through `mpx_uinput`, and every X11 `type_text` that borrows a keycode. On success the costs are the per-run wait, the hold on each borrowed key and one idle wait per spare-keycode batch. Text that is all on the layout pays only the per-run wait. A call that ends with unread keys re-plugs the session's keyboard on the next call.

## Verification

- `tests/virtual_keyboard_xorg.rs` (ignored, needs a real Xorg running as the test's user, `/dev/uinput` and libinput hotplug) ptrace-stops Xorg's input thread, so the server still answers requests but reads no input. It has three tests:
  - A key the server reads down but not up. Before the key repeat fix the server repeated the held key more than 20 times in each of 3 runs. At this head it passes 5 of 5 with no repeat.
  - A new keyboard whose warm-up key is never read. It fails before the `Delivery` change and passes at this head.
  - Borrowed keys during a stall, which fails at @CMGS's head with `keys read after their keycode was restored` and passes at this head.
- TLC checks `ReadyIsClean`, `NoRepeat`, `NoKeyAfterRestore` and `CountsOnlyItsOwnKeys` on the model. All hold with the code's three rules on, and each breaks with its rule off.
- On a Debian 13 arm64 guest with Xorg 21.1 (dummy video, libinput), the scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -D warnings`, `xvfb-run cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`, `spare_keycode_restore_tests --ignored` and `key_input_x11 --ignored`.
- The verify-cua-driver X11 lane (`verify-linux.sh x11`) delivered 2 of 2 cells with complete evidence. The Wayland lane does not apply because these routes are X11-only. Not run: the CI-only GNOME/KDE desktop lanes.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep borrowed keycodes bound until 150 ms after a text's last key on them
body:
Salvaged from #7079 by @CMGS. Supersedes #7079. Stacked on #7145, the salvage of #7076. The base is `fix/mpx-keyboard-pacing-7076`. Retarget it to `main` once #7145 merges.

## Why

A character with no key on the layout (CJK, for example) is typed through a borrowed spare keycode, and the keycode is restored after the text. Xlib and Qt look a key up in their own copy of the keymap when they handle it, and reload that copy when the map changes. Since #6892 removed the per-key pause, the restore usually lands before the client handles the keys, and most of a CJK text comes out as `NoSymbol`. @CMGS showed that a `_NET_WM_PING` answer does not prove the lookup happened either. Qt's xcb plugin can answer the ping, reload the keymap and only then handle the keys it set aside.

## What changed

- @CMGS's commit, cherry-picked with authorship kept. A key on a borrowed keycode gets the paced 10 ms hold (`pacing_for`), and the borrowed keycodes stay bound until 150 ms (`SPARE_KEYCODE_IDLE`) after the last such key (`TextClient::release`, and the remap guards on the virtual keyboard route).
- The XTest route paused after the release, so its borrowed keys were never held. It now flushes the press, holds, then releases.
- The two Xvfb-spawning restore tests are `#[ignore]` with their own CI step, so the plain unit test run does not need Xvfb.

## Scope

Covers the spare-keycode lifetime on the XSendEvent, XTest and virtual keyboard routes. It does not make delivery to an arbitrarily slow client correct. X11 has no signal that a client has translated a key event, so 150 ms is a bound, not a guarantee. `SPARE_KEYCODE_IDLE` documents this, and `a_client_that_looks_up_after_the_idle_window_reads_no_symbol` pins it. That test shows a client looking up at 3x the window gets `NoSymbol`.

## Tradeoffs

Leaving borrowed keycodes bound until the next text needs them, or until the session ends, would remove the race for slow clients. But it leaves foreign keysyms in the user's keymap between calls, and every later text that borrows has to rebind under a client that may still be reading the old binding. That is a design choice for maintainers, so it is not in this PR.

## Blast Radius

Every X11 `type_text` that borrows a keycode gets +20 ms per borrowed character and up to 150 ms once per spare-keycode batch. Text that is all on the layout is unchanged. @CMGS's measurements are in #7079.

## Verification

- On a Debian 13 arm64 guest with Xorg 21.1 (dummy video, libinput): `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -D warnings`, `xvfb-run cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` (1008 passed), `spare_keycode_restore_tests --ignored` (3 passed), `key_input_x11 --ignored` (20 passed) and the base's `virtual_keyboard_xorg` (passed). With `SPARE_KEYCODE_IDLE` set to 0, the two restore tests type `???????`. The new XTest hold test measured a 0 ms hold before the fix.
- The verify-cua-driver X11 lane (`verify-linux.sh x11`) delivered 2 of 2 cells with complete evidence. The Wayland lane does not apply because these routes are X11-only. Not run here: the CI-only GNOME/KDE desktop lanes.

title: fix(spaces-desktop): a closed stdout no longer pages Sentry as a fatal
body:
## What

The Electron app (Cua Spaces desktop) reported fatal, message-less `Error` events whenever its stdout or stderr was gone. Sentry issues CUA-SPACES-DESKTOP-T, V, W and X (Windows 0.22.3, an update check) and N, P and Q (Fedora, 14 events in 14 seconds) are all this one cause.

Linear: CUA-3970.

## Cause

A packaged Windows app has no console, and a Linux app can lose its terminal. electron-updater's default logger is `console`. The write to the dead stream fails, the stream emits an `error` event nobody listens for, and that is an uncaught exception. Sentry's own uncaught-exception handler then calls `console.error`, which fails the same way. The message is empty because the crash-report scrub clears all exception messages.

## Changes

- `stdio-guard.ts`: an `error` listener on stdout and stderr that drops write failures (EPIPE, EBADF, EIO, EAGAIN, destroyed stream) and rethrows anything else; console methods that cannot throw; a never-throwing logger given to electron-updater. Installed first thing in the main process.
- `crash-reporting.ts` and `crash-reporting-main.ts`: `beforeSend` drops exactly the stack that runs from a `console.*` call through a stream write. Other errors, including ones that mention EPIPE without that stack, are kept.
- `updater.ts`: a failed update check or download is now a handled, warning-level event. The scrub empties exception messages, so the real reason travels in `extra`, and events group by error code or HTTP status. The state machine is unchanged.

## Tests

- `stdio-guard.test.ts`: the guard, the console wrapper, and the event filter, including the real shapes of T/V (Windows) and P (Linux) and cases it must keep.
- `updater-closed-stdout.test.ts`: an update check with a console that throws on every write still finds the update and reports nothing; a real failure is reported once as a handled warning with its reason.
- `bin/ci`: prettier, SPDX, typecheck, desktop tests pass.

title: fix(ci): a failed sccache download no longer fails the Rust job
body:
## Why

The `rust-cache` action says cargo compiles without sccache when it cannot start, but its "Install sccache" step had no `continue-on-error`. On 9 Nov the release CDN answered the sccache download with HTTP 504, and every Rust job that started then failed before compiling (for example the Rust Windows clippy and shard jobs of #7082 and #7083).

## What changed

- "Install sccache" in `.github/actions/rust-cache/action.yml` may fail. The next step already starts the server only if the binary is there and otherwise warns "sccache did not start; compiling without it".
- A test pins that the install step may fail and that the routing step keeps its fallback.

## Scope

Only the shared Rust cache action. No workflow calls `mozilla-actions/sccache-action` directly. Other release-asset downloads that failed in the same window (actionlint, the Electron zip) are not covered.

## Tradeoffs

Retrying the download was the alternative. The sccache action already retries, and a job that compiles cold is better than a red one.

## Blast Radius

Every Rust CI job. When the download works nothing changes. When it fails the job compiles without the cache, so it is slower, and the log carries the step's error annotation and the existing warning.

## Verification

- The new test fails on main's `action.yml` and passes here.
- The `.github/scripts` test suite passes.
- The runner applies `continue-on-error` to a composite action's embedded steps, main and post, so the sccache action's post step (which failed with "Unable to locate executable file" in the same jobs) no longer fails the job. This was read from the runner source, not exercised with a forced download failure.

title: fix(cua-driver): deliver a background left click on a Chromium control on Linux X11
body:
CUA-1292

## Problem

On Linux X11, a background `click` at a pixel of a Chromium or Electron window that does not have focus was refused with `background_unavailable` before anything was tried. The same click by `element_token` already worked, because it goes through the control's accessibility action. The refusal text also said the window had to be occluded, which is not the condition: an uncovered, unfocused window is refused the same way.

## Change

- A plain left click (one click, no modifiers) at a pixel now runs the accessibility action of the control under that pixel, the route other X11 apps already use. Focus, stacking and the pointer stay where they were. It refuses, with the same code as before, only when no control covers the point.
- Text fields are still refused at a pixel: their accessibility action does not give them focus, so a following `type_text` would go nowhere.
- A web document's own `doDefault` is no longer an at-point target. Chromium answers true to it and the page sees no click, so it would have reported a click that did not happen. This applies to any toolkit that publishes the `document web` role.
- Right, double and modified clicks, typing, keys, scroll and drag are refused as before. Synthetic X11 events sent to the unfocused window still do not reach the page, and no XTest or libei route can aim at a window without moving the real pointer or focus. Wayland is unchanged.
- The refusal now says what it is about (the window lacks input focus) and what does work in the background (a left click on a button, link or other control, by `element_token` or at its pixel).

## Known limit

When the point is over page content that is clickable only through an ancestor (Chromium's `clickAncestor`), the page receives the click on that element, at the element's centre and not at the requested pixel. The result reports the element it hit and `effect: unverifiable`, as for every accessibility click.

## Test plan

- Unit: a `document web` element is never an at-point activation target, deepest hit or not.
- E2E contract: on X11 the Electron `left_click` and `child_window` cells addressed by pixel in the background now expect delivery through the accessibility route, checked by fixture state and the focus, z-order, cursor and leaked-input oracles. `right_click` and `type_text` at a pixel still expect `background_unavailable`.
- Manual, real Chromium under Xvfb with openbox and picom, target window fully covered by a second focused browser window, and again uncovered but unfocused. Before: every pixel click refused. After: the button and link under the pixel receive a DOM click and the active window does not change; a text field, a double click, a right click, the address bar and `type_text` are refused with the new text.

title: fix(spaces): setup's step bars count the steps it really shows (CUA-3973)
body:
Fixes CUA-3973 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3973/spaces-setup-step-indicator-shows-the-wrong-number-of-steps)

## What changes for users

The bars at the bottom of Cua Spaces setup now show exactly the steps you go through, and light the one you're on. On a Mac that's 4: Add this computer, Let Cua Spaces use apps, Which agents do you use?, and Try your first job. If every permission is already on, setup skips the permissions screen, which would ask for nothing, and shows 3 bars. Windows and Linux show 3.

Before, setup always showed 2 bars. On a Mac the permissions screen still lit the first bar, and the last screen (Ready) had no bars at all.

## Root cause

The bars came from their own hand-kept list (`DOT_SCREENS`/`dotFor`). It was separate from the code that decides where setup goes next (`afterSignIn`, the permissions auto-skip, agents → Ready). When the "where your agents work" step was removed on 8 Nov, the bar list was cut to 2 and grouped sign-in and permissions under the first bar. Setup itself still showed 4 or 5 screens.

## The fix

- One list, `RUN_STEPS`, says which steps exist and which screens each covers. `runSteps(facts)` keeps the steps this run shows (the permissions step only on a Mac that still needs a permission). The bars (`stepDots`) and every move to the next step (`nextStepScreen`) read that same list, so they can't drift apart again.
- "Add this computer" is one step: the sign-in screen is the wait after its button. A run saved on the removed "where" step still counts as this step.
- Permissions are read from the first screen on a Mac, so the bar count is right from the start. The answer is saved when the run leaves the first step, so the bars don't change under the person while they turn permissions on. `useLocalNetwork` now reports `loading`, so a Local Network status that hasn't been read yet isn't taken as "not needed".
- The furthest step reached is now saved as a step id (`reachedStep`), not a bar index, because the index moves when a step is left out.

## Steps per path (expected bars)

| Path | Screens | Bars |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh Mac, signed out, no permissions | Welcome → Sign-in → Permissions → Agents → Ready | 4: 1, 1, 2, 3, 4 |
| Fresh Mac, Skip for now | Welcome → Permissions → Agents → Ready | 4: 1, 2, 3, 4 |
| Mac with permissions already on | Welcome → Sign-in → Agents → Ready | 3: 1, 1, 2, 3 |
| Existing account, or this computer already added (Mac) | Welcome → "Adding this Mac" → Permissions (if needed) → Agents → Ready | 4 (or 3 if permissions are on) |
| Windows / Linux | Welcome → Sign-in → Agents → Ready | 3 |

Choose later or Install later on the agents step ends setup on Home without Ready.

## Tests

- `the step dots match the steps setup really shows`: walks every path above with the run's own moves (`nextStepScreen`). On each screen it checks that the number of bars equals the number of steps the walk goes through, and that the lit bar is the step showing. It also checks that every screen belongs to exactly one step. A screen added without a step, or a step the bars count that the run skips, fails here.
- Two route tests on the real page with the wasm core: a Mac that still needs permissions (4 bars, lit 1→2→3→4), and a Mac with every permission on (3 bars; the permissions screen is skipped and the decision is saved).
- I broke the page on purpose to feed the bars fixed facts, and the route test failed as expected.
- Full `cua-spaces-web` vitest suite: 236 files, 1657 tests pass. `bin/ci --quick` is green.

## Screenshots

These come from the web UI's demo mode, with demo data only. Each screen was taken at desktop (1440×900) and mobile (390×844) width, before and after. Bar count per screen on the main Mac path:

| Screen | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Welcome | 2 bars, 1st lit | 4 bars, 1st lit |
| Sign-in | 2 bars, 1st lit | 4 bars, 1st lit |
| Permissions | 2 bars, 1st lit | 4 bars, 2nd lit |
| Agents | 2 bars, 2nd lit | 4 bars, 3rd lit |
| Ready | no bars | 4 bars, 4th lit |

Screenshot images to follow in a comment.

title: fix(spaces): first agent on This Mac after Set up no longer fails to reach it
body: Fixes [CUA-3974](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3974). **For users:** on a fresh install, the first coding agent you start on This Mac right after Set up now starts, instead of stopping with "Couldn't reach that computer". ## Root cause Set up turns on desktop sharing for This Mac, and that restarts its cua-spacesd. The daemon kept its cached connection to the old cua-spacesd. Over the mesh nothing resets that connection, so the first job went down a dead connection. It hung until the HTTP/2 keepalive gave up (20 s + 10 s) and failed with `transport error: http2 error (operation timed out)`. The app showed that as "Couldn't reach that computer. Check it's on". A retry a minute later worked because by then the connection had been replaced. The logs from the affected Mac show the sequence: sharing turned on, cua-spacesd restarted and rejoined the relay, and 7 s later the start failed with that error. The start never reached cua-spacesd's ProcessService. ## Fix - **cua-spaces:** a cached relay connection (or a routed one through that host) is dialed again when the relay directory says the computer connected again since the connection was made. - **cua-spaces:** `agent_start` and `agent_message` first check a cached connection with a short health probe (`Spaces::checked`, 4 s). If it is silent or fails at the transport level, they reconnect. The probe has no side effects, so the start itself is sent only once, on a connection that just answered. - **cua-spaces:** any tool call that fails with a transport error drops the cached connection, so the next call dials again. Hotspots and mounted volumes are kept. - **web:** a job on This Mac waits up to 20 s while This Mac is set up but offline (its sharing service restarting). If This Mac still doesn't answer, the error now says "This Mac didn't answer in time" instead of "Check it's on". - **web (same view):** the This Mac card shows the model or OS instead of repeating its title. "Didn't start" now appears once, in the header; the empty screen says "Nothing ran yet" and drops the duplicate caption bar. ## Tests - `cua-spaces/tests/stale_connection.rs`: a proxy in front of the relay silences the Space's open connections without resetting them, which is what the mesh does when the peer restarts. With the fix turned off, two of the three tests fail (the call hangs); with it, all three pass. - Unit tests: `session_changed`, `hostStatusWhenOnline`, `thisComputerSubtitle`, the This Mac start-error copy, and the updated wasm-core UI test ("Didn't start" shown once). - `bin/ci --quick` is green. ## Screenshots (demo data) Desktop, before and after: Mobile (390 px), before and after: The sidebar doesn't collapse at 390 px on main either. That's out of scope here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux foreground press_key, hotkey and click give the focus back
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux X11, foreground `press_key`, `hotkey` and `click` left the target window active, while `type_text` on X11 and every foreground action on macOS, Windows and Wayland give the focus back to the window that had it. The published `delivery_mode` text already promises the restore. On Wayland, `hotkey` was the one key action that left the target focused. A foreground action that opened a menu failed with "the input was sent, but the prior focus could not be restored: grab_held".
- What changed:
  - X11 and XWayland foreground `press_key`, `hotkey` and `click` restore the previously active window.
  - Wayland `hotkey` runs in the same focus transaction as `press_key`, so it restores too.
  - On X11, a menu or popup the action opened keeps the target focused. The call succeeds, the result carries `focus_outcome: "menu_open"` and `grab_held_by`, and the text says "The target was left focused because a menu is open".
  - The restore watches for a menu that maps a beat after the input instead of reading once, so a late menu is no longer closed. Tooltips, notifications, drag icons and popups of another process do not count as the action's menu.
  - `right_click`, `set_value` and the gestures are unchanged.
  - `action-icon-catalog.md`, `action-support.md` (niri row, Hyprland paragraph) and the Linux skill text now agree with the code.

## Related work

Refs CUA-3767

RFC: not required. The behaviour now matches the published `delivery_mode` contract.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: after a Linux X11 foreground `press_key`, `hotkey` or `click`, the previously active window is active again. A caller that relied on the target staying active must send the next action with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` (each foreground call activates the target itself) or call `bring_to_front`. Toolkits keep the focused widget across the swap: checked live on GTK 3, Qt 6 and Electron. Foreground results gain the optional `focus_outcome` and `grab_held_by` fields.
- Known limit: the Wayland restore cannot see a menu, so a Wayland `hotkey` that opens one now gives the focus back and the menu closes. `press_key` with the same chord already restored the focus. The catalog says so.
- Known limit: on X11 a new popup of the target is read as its menu without probing the keyboard grab. A non-menu popup the target maps during the action keeps the target focused, which is what every foreground key and click did before.
- Risk and rollback: Linux only. Reverting this PR restores the previous table.

risk: standard

Size: over the production-line aim because the menu outcome has to reach every foreground result text (click, key, type).

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the scoped repository checks (format, clippy with warnings denied, `platform-linux` unit tests) pass. `x11_foreground_restore_linux_test` now has seven cases: restore after `type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey` and `click`; a click and a `type_text` whose menu maps late keep the target focused and succeed; a click restores past another process's popup. All seven pass on this branch across repeated runs. Against a driver built from main, six fail and only the `type_text` restore case passes.

title: fix(cua-driver): connect says when an agent uses another Cua Driver
body:
## Why

Cua Spaces' Set up and `cua-driver connect` both register an MCP server named `cua-driver`. `connect` matched an existing server by name only, so an agent that Set up had pointed at the driver inside Cua Spaces was reported as "already connected", as if it used the standalone driver. Spaces already tells the other side of this ("Uses another Cua Driver. Set up switches it to this one."), so `connect` now says the same thing from its side.

## What changed

- `connect` reads the command the existing server launches, for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Factory Droid. When it is another executable, the agent is reported as `other_driver`: "uses another Cua Driver (<command>); left as is", with the server to remove to switch.
- Nothing is written for that agent: no config change, no Droid ratings, no skill pack.
- Codex's `config.toml` is parsed as TOML. A file that is not valid TOML is reported and left unchanged.

## Scope

Covers what `cua-driver connect` reports and writes when a `cua-driver` server already exists. It never replaces the other entry. Out of scope: a `connect` flag that switches the agent over, and any change to Set up in Cua Spaces, which already backs up and replaces a standalone entry when asked.

## Tradeoffs

- Two server names, one per install, would end the collision but load two drivers with the same tools into one agent.
- The rule is "the last tool the person ran decides, and each says what it found". Spaces switches on Set up. `connect` reports and leaves the entry alone, because it also runs unattended from the installer.

## Blast Radius

Anyone who runs `cua-driver connect` or the installer on a machine where an agent's `cua-driver` server launches a different driver. They see the new line where they saw "already connected", and the installer no longer ends with "Ask <agent>" for that agent. An entry that points at this driver, directly or through the `~/.local/bin` link, behaves as before. One new direct dependency, `toml_edit`, which was already in the lockfile.

## Verification

- `connect_other_driver_cli_test` runs the built binary against a config with the entry Set up writes. It fails on the test-only commit (`already_connected`) and passes at the head.
- The built binary in a throwaway home, for all four agents: the new line, `other_driver` in JSON, exit 0, and the home directory byte-identical afterwards. An entry reaching this driver through a symlink still reports "already connected". Six Codex TOML layouts are read correctly.
- The scoped repository checks: rustfmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, the `cua-driver` crate tests, the generated CLI reference check and the installer connect-step tests passed. The macOS Lume lane does not apply to an agent-registration change. Linux and Windows lanes did not run.

Size: over the production-line aim because four agents' config readers each needed the command comparison, and the Codex reader moved from a line scan to a TOML parse.

title: feat(spaces): Home shows your computers as one supercomputer (CUA-3976)
body: Home now shows your computers as one supercomputer: the combined total, one card per computer with its free room and the jobs on it, and **Run something**, which starts Claude Code or Codex on the computer with the most room. Chat stays in each job's own page. Linear: [CUA-3976](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3976/spaces-home-supercomputer-view-option-a). This is option A ("Machine grid"), picked on 10 Nov. **Waiting on a device test before merge.** It's marked ready, but auto-merge is not queued. A separate pass on real Macs comes first. ## What changes for people - **Top:** "3 computers · 40 cores · 96 GB", a line saying how much is free for new jobs, then **Add a computer** and **Run something**. - **One card per computer:** online or offline, a **Free now** bar ("7 of 8 cores · 9 GB"), and the agents working on it. A job opens its Space's thread, or its task page for a job on this computer. A computer's name opens its own page. - **Add a computer:** a large dashed tile. If you only have This Mac, it says in one line why you'd add another. - **Run something:** pick Claude Code or Codex, a project (optional) and a task. **Where** picks the computer with the most room, and you can change it. The job starts without leaving Home and appears on that computer's card. - **Fallback:** if the computer can't be reached when the job starts, the job moves to the next best computer. Home then says "Mac mini couldn't be reached, so "Fix the flaky checkout tests" moved to Linux box." with **Show job**. - **The old composer** (every agent, account and model, plus agent Homes) moves to `/home/ask` and is linked as **More options** in the sheet. ## Design note: placement 1. **Pattern:** spread to the most free room, like Kubernetes' LeastAllocated score and Nomad's spread scheduling. Computers are ranked by free cores, then free memory, then fewest jobs. The computer you're on goes last, and offline or unshared computers are never picked. 2. **Where it lives:** the shared app core, `cua-spaces-app-core::pool` (`pool.summary`, `pool.place`), so every app places a job the same way. The web UI calls it through the core wasm and only gathers inputs and words the result. 3. **Inputs are real host data:** `machines.list` (online, sharing) plus `resources.get` (cores, CPU busy %, memory total and used, per computer). No new daemon API was needed, because computers already publish this summary through their machine record. 4. **Fallback:** `pool.place` takes `picked` and `exclude`. A pick that can't take the job, or a start that fails as unreachable, moves the job to the next best computer and records `movedFrom` on the task. 5. **Alternatives considered:** bin-packing (fill the busiest computer first) leaves headroom for big jobs but slows the computers people are using. Placing in the UI would let apps disagree. Placing in the control plane is the long-term home once jobs are server-side records; today, tasks live on the device. ## What's real and what isn't - **Real:** the computers, online state, cores, memory and free room (from `resources.get`), the jobs per computer (the Agents page's list), the start itself (`useStartTask`), and the This Mac confirm and setup. - **Unknown room:** a computer that sends no numbers (an older app on it) shows "—" and "Free room not known yet". It can still be picked, after the computers that did send numbers. - **Not in this PR:** moving a job that is already running when its computer drops offline. A run can't move between computers today. Fallback happens when the job starts. The offline card says new jobs go elsewhere. - **Without the core wasm**, the stand-ins show only counts and pick the first computer that can take the job. ## Screenshots (demo data) | | Desktop | Mobile | |---|---|---| | Before | | | | After | | | | Run something | | | | Dark | | | ## Tests - **Core:** 13 unit tests in `pool.rs` covering free room, totals, ranking, This Mac last, unknown numbers, a kept pick, an offline pick, an excluded computer, nothing eligible and unshared computers. The full `cua-spaces-app-core` suite passes (918). - **Web:** `lib/pool.test.ts` runs through the real wasm core plus the no-core stand-ins. `__tests__/pool-home.test.tsx` covers: - only This Mac; - 3 computers with one offline; - jobs running on cards; - the Run something flow; - fallback when the computer can't be reached. - **Old composer tests:** now mount `/home/ask`. The onboarding test checks it lands on the new Home. - **Results:** full web suite 238 files and 1675 tests passing. `bin/ci --quick` is green. ## Base and dependencies - Built on `main` at 0f39fa3f63, with #7161 (stale connection to This Mac) and #7159 (onboarding step bars) merged in. The device test then includes both. - While those are open, this diff shows their changes too. I'll rebase onto `main` once they land. ## For the device test - **Build:** check out `feat/spaces-home-machine-grid` and build the apps as usual. The web UI needs the core wasm (`pnpm --dir apps/cua-spaces-web build` builds it). - **No feature flag:** the new Home is the default `/home`. - **Worth checking:** - the Free now numbers against Activity Monitor; - a computer going offline; - Run something on another computer's shared desktop, and on one that doesn't share it (a new Linux Space there); - the This Mac confirm. ## Device test 2 fixes (10 Nov) - **A job no longer waits on a computer that just went away.** Before a job is handed to a Space on another computer, the app asks the SDK whether it can take work now (`Spaces::reach`: the relay's directory, then a health check on the connection, within 8 s). If it can't, the job moves to the next computer `pool.place` picks, and Home shows the "moved to" line. Served as the app method `spaces.reach` (not an MCP tool) through both hosts. - **The task you typed survives This Mac's confirm and "Pick another".** It clears only once the job starts. - **Merged `main`** to resolve the conflicts with #7175 and #6873 (Warm start): `spaces.rs` keeps both live checks; the first-run and warm-start tests expect the pool grid at `/home` and the prompt box at `/home/ask`, plus the one hidden warm home. - **Tests:** `cua-spaces/tests/reach.rs` (incl. a computer switched off after it was picked), three new `pool-home.test.tsx` cases (offline between picking and starting; asked before hand-off; task kept through the confirm), `ask-first.test.ts`, and bridge contract cases in web, Swift and Electron. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(spaces): an offline computer reads offline within seconds, not minutes (CUA-3981)
body:
Fixes CUA-3981 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3981). Found in the device test of #7166.

**What changes for users:** when one of your computers goes offline (its Cua Spaces app quits, it sleeps, it loses the network), the app shows it Offline on Home, on Computers and in Run something's "Where" within seconds, the same as `cua spaces ls`. Before, it stayed Online for 5+ minutes and Run something could pick it.

## Root cause

- Every app shell decides "reachable" by asking the SDK for the Space (`Spaces::space`). `cached_connection` answered with the connection cached from before, without checking the relay. That connection runs over the mesh, which sends no reset when the other side disappears, and the probe sends nothing on it, so it never failed. The row read "Running", so the computer read Online, indefinitely.
- `machines::page_rows` then ORed that with the shell's `presence` map, which comes from a second, slower read of the relay (up to ~30 s old on the Mac app).
- The CLI reads the relay directory directly, so it was right. The relay itself is fine: it drops a computer the moment its tunnel closes (15 s heartbeats, 90 s watchdog for a silent death).

## Fix

The relay stays the one source of presence; the shared core follows it:

- **cua-spaces:** a cached connection to a computer the relay lists offline must answer a health check within 2 s, or it is dropped. A computer that still answers (the LAN mesh) stays usable.
- **cua-spaces:** a computer listed offline that cannot be reached fails with a reason that says so (`cua_spaces_contract::presence::LISTED_OFFLINE`, kept by the dial backoff), instead of "has no cua-spacesd ... needs an image".
- **cua-spaces-app-core:** `machines::page_rows` treats a row whose connect says the relay lists it offline as offline, whatever an older presence read says. Home, Computers and Run something all draw these rows, so there is one rule for every UI.

No relay or control-plane change is needed for this bug.

## Tests

- `cua-spaces/tests/offline_presence.rs`:
  - An app quit without a clean disconnect: the connection goes silent with no reset, and the relay lists the computer offline. The probe fails as offline within seconds, later probes fail at once, and the computer reconnects when it comes back. **This test fails without the fix** (the probe returns the dead cached connection).
  - Offline on the relay but still answering: stays reachable.
- app-core: `a_computer_the_list_found_offline_is_offline_whatever_an_older_presence_says`.
- Ran locally: the new tests, `cua-spaces --lib` (501 passed), and the app-core `machines` tests (58 passed).

Note: #7166 changes the same `cached_connection` function to handle the "reconnected since" case. The two changes are independent, and whichever PR merges second needs a small rebase.

title: fix(spaces): new-user friction from the 10 Nov device test (CUA-3980)
body:
Fixes the first-time-user friction found in the 10 Nov Cua Spaces device test (see the comment on #7166). Linear: [CUA-3980](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3980).

**For users:** a new person now gets through setup with nothing hidden: the permissions step says what's still off and lets you jump to it, Add a computer leads with the usual way, macOS's Local Network question comes during setup (not as Home opens), keycaps stay off the buttons, and computers get a short name instead of a long network address.

## What changed, per item

1. **Permissions step cut off.** On a short window the Local Network row hid under the fade, so the button stayed "Later" with no reason given.
   - Until everything is on, the button reads **Continue without it/them**. Next to it, **Still off: Run macOS Spaces on this Mac** scrolls to that row and focuses its Allow.
   - Any first-run step that runs past the window shows a **More below** button, which scrolls the page.
   - At the default 1200×780 window everything fits.
2. **Email verification page.** This lives in the Keycloak theme in trycua/cloud, so it is fixed there, not in this PR (see Linear).
3. **Add a computer.**
   - The usual way (install Cua Spaces there and sign in, with the link to copy) is shown in full on the first page.
   - The other five ways (Open a link, Scan a QR code, Run a command, Type a code there, Ask an agent there) sit under **Other ways to add it**.
   - The code row was also called "Enter a code". It is now "Type a code there", so "Enter a code" means only a code made on another computer (the footer's "Have a code? Enter it").
   - The agent prompt moved from the first page into its own entry, "Ask an agent there".
4. **Local Network prompt as Home opens.** The Mac app used to show its own explanation dialog when the first run finished.
   - The permissions step now owns this question. Its row already gives the one-line reason ("macOS Spaces run on a small network inside this Mac…").
   - Finishing the first run asks nothing.
   - The question still comes when it's actually needed: the first macOS Space on this Mac, turning on Spaces from other computers, or a join code.
5. **Keycap over "Install later".** The keys were placed for a copy column ending at 544px; the column really ends at 664px. The keys now use the real edge, and any key that would still reach into the column is moved right of it, or left out.
6. **Long hostnames.** The app already used macOS's Computer Name. On hosted Macs that name *is* the full host name (`j17-2.<host>.com`).
   - A name that is really a network host name (no spaces, has dots, not an IP) now registers as its first part (`j17-2`). Real names like "Ada's MacBook Pro" stay as they are.
   - The same rule applies in the cua service (`cua_host` `friendly_name`), the Mac app (`ComputerName`) and the Electron app (`personName`).
   - Renaming already exists on the computer page and in the Computers list.

title: fix(ci): spdx-headers.py leaves vendored cua-driver files alone
body:
## Why

`scripts/spdx-headers.py --apply` wrote `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` and the Cua copyright line on top of any `.rs` or `.swift` file under `libs/cua-driver` that had no SPDX line, including a file that carries another party's copyright or license notice. `--check` reported the same file as missing a header, and `bin/ci --fix` runs `--apply` for that check. The skip for another party's notice existed, but only in `--fsl` mode. It now applies in both modes. (CUA-3443)

## What changed

- `scripts/spdx-headers.py`: a file with another party's notice is listed under "left alone" in the default (MIT) mode too, never stamped and never reported missing.
- The notice detector no longer reads a `copyright` identifier (`COPYRIGHT: &str = ...`, `copyright + 1`) as a notice, so our own files that use the word in code still get their header.
- New `scripts/ci/tests/test_spdx_headers.py` runs `--apply` and `--check` in a temporary repository. `bin/ci` and `ci-test-scripts.yml` run the script tests when `scripts/spdx-headers.py` changes.

## Scope

Covers the header script, its test and the two triggers. No source file gains or loses a header: no file under `libs/cua-driver` is vendored today, so this fixes a latent defect, not a file already stamped wrong. It does not add an SPDX line naming the upstream license to vendored files.

## Tradeoffs

The detector is a line heuristic and errs toward leaving a file alone. A headerless file of ours with the word "copyright" in prose near the top is listed under "left alone" instead of failing `--check`, as it already was in `--fsl` mode. The list is printed on every run.

## Blast Radius

Anyone who runs the SPDX check or its fix. Both `--check` modes print the same output on this branch as on main, so no existing file changes category.

## Verification

- The new test fails against main's script (the vendored fixture is stamped and reported missing) and passes here.
- The scoped repository checks pass: the script unit tests, `spdx-headers.py --check libs/cua-driver`, `spdx-headers.py --fsl --check`, and `bin/ci --verify-sync`.

title: perf(spaces): install-local dev-fast by default, parallel cua-spacesd, --build-only (CUA-3971)
body:
Tracks CUA-3971 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3971).

## What changes for users

Cua Spaces Local builds are fast by default. A rebuild after a version bump drops from 9m27s to 6m36s, a cua-spacesd change from 44s to 28s, and a cold build from 12m43s to 8m16s. Release-grade builds are opt-in with `--release`. CI and the published release builds do not use this script and are unchanged. `--build-only` lets anyone time or check a build without replacing the installed app.

## What I measured

Apple Silicon Mac (32 cores, 96 GB), `install-local.sh --build-only`, each build in a fresh worktree with its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` and its own sccache directory, run one at a time. "Base" is `main` plus `--build-only` and nothing else. All three columns use `--release` (Swift release); the third also passes `--rust-profile dev-fast`. Each scenario ran twice.

| Scenario (wall time) | Base | PR: cua-spacesd built in parallel | PR + `--rust-profile dev-fast` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold build (64e25f3a6) | 763 s / 617 s | 545 s / 581 s | 496 s |
| (a) Version bump 64e25f3a6 to 5486b6246, then a synthetic bump to 0.18.1 | 567 s / 518 s | 472 s / 474 s | 396 s / 395 s |
| (b) No change | 29 s / 27 s | 28 s / 27 s | 28 s / 28 s |
| (c) One-line Swift change | 29 s / 27 s | 29 s / 27 s | 28 s / 28 s |
| (d) One-line Rust change in cua-spacesd | 44 s / 44 s | 46 s / 43 s | 28 s / 27 s |

Version bump: 567 s to 396 s is 30% faster (518 s to 395 s, 24%). The parallel cua-spacesd build takes off 17%, and dev-fast a further 16%. No-change and Swift rebuilds are about 28 s either way, so the profile does not matter there; it decides the Rust rebuilds, so the default is now dev-fast. The absolute numbers differ from the 18-core MacBook runs earlier (1011 s to 623 s for the bump), but the relative gain holds: about 30 to 40% on a version bump.

Where the 6m36s goes: `cargo build --timings` of a bump rebuild shows a 357 s Rust build, of which 287 s is a serial chain (cua-daemon 68 s, cua-sdk 101 s, cua-compat 65 s, cua-cli 69 s, cua-spaces-cli 28 s). Getting under 5 minutes needs that chain broken. The design note is on CUA-3971 (crate split, estimated 4 minutes after a bump). Not part of this PR.

## Changes

- Rust profile now defaults to `dev-fast` (opt-level 1, incremental, no LTO). `--release` still builds everything fully optimised, and `--rust-profile release|dev-fast` picks the profile on its own.
- cua-spacesd now builds beside the library (it has its own workspace and target dir).
- `--build-only`: build, sign and verify, then stop. Nothing is installed, quit or registered.
- One summary line after the build says where the time went (Rust, web UI, app, signing).
- README and the script's usage text describe the new defaults.
- `install-local-test.sh` covers the new flags and defaults (308 checks pass). `bin/ci --quick` is green.

Not changed: sccache is only used when it is installed (it is not on the MacBook); a version bump misses it for workspace crates because the version is in the cache key.

title: feat(cua): show each Space's progress when spaces create makes several
body:
## Problem

`cua spaces create --count N` with N above 1 printed nothing until every create ended, and sent no OSC 7501 report. With one Space it shows each step on stderr and reports it to the terminal (#5155). Follow-up to https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5155.

## Before / after

Before (N=3): no output until the three `Created …` lines.

After, only when stderr is a terminal and `--json` is off:
- stderr keeps one line per Space, rewritten in place with that Space's step (the same words and download line as one Space) and then `Created <id> (<name>)` or `failed: <error>`. Autowrap is off while drawing, so a long line cannot push the others down. Names and errors have control characters replaced.
- OSC 7501 gets a child record per Space, `id=space-<n>` titled with its name (an unnamed one is titled by its id until it is created, then by its name), carrying `working` with `progress` from the step, then `done` or `error`. The root record says `Creating 3 Spaces: 1 created, 1 failed` with `progress` = the share ended, and is sent only when a create starts or ends. This is the spec's "Several records" shape.
- At the end the lines are erased, the per-Space records are cleared, the `Created …` lines print to stdout as before, and the root record is `done` (`Created 3 Spaces`) or `error` (`Created 2 of 3 Spaces: <first error>`).
- Ctrl-C stops the drawing before `Cancelling...` prints and clears every record, as for one Space.
- One Space (`--count 1`) is unchanged.

```
web    Created local:web (web)
web-2  failed: no room on the machine
web-3  Downloading image 1.0 of 2.5 GB · 85 MB/s · less than a minute
```

## Tests

- `util::secret_tests::a_child_record_carries_its_id_and_title`: exact bytes of a child record (`id`, base64 `title`, `progress`).
- `util::parallel_step_tests::several_creates_keep_a_line_each_and_count_overall`: the drawn lines and their padding, an unnamed create taking its id and then its name, the cursor-up redraw, the overall text and percent, and control characters replaced.
- The existing `program_status_*` and `create_step_tests` pass unchanged.

Size: over the production-line target because several creates need their own renderer (per-Space line state, redraw and records), which the single-Space step lines cannot share.

title: [Bug]: macOS set_value says LibreOffice cells "cannot be edited in the background", but keys sent to LibreOffice's process edit them
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

When `set_value` on a LibreOffice Calc cell isn't applied, the error says LibreOffice "drops background pointer input, so its cells cannot be edited in the background". It then tells the agent to bring the window to the front or stop. But keystrokes sent to LibreOffice's process (`hotkey`, `press_key`, `type_text`) do edit the cells while another app stays frontmost. So the message steers agents away from a background route that works.

### Reproduction

1. On macOS, open a Calc workbook in LibreOffice, then make another app frontmost and key.
2. Call `set_value` on a cell's `AXTextField`. It returns `write_not_applied` with the message below.
3. With LibreOffice still in the background, call `run_steps` on its window with these steps: `hotkey` `["ctrl", "home"]`, `press_key` `down` and `right` to reach the cell, `type_text` `"cancelled"`, `press_key` `tab`, and so on.
4. The cells take the values, and the other app stays frontmost throughout.

This was seen in benchmark runs, not a standalone script. One agent took the keyboard route after this message and passed a background trial. Another agent followed the message and stopped in 7 background trials.

### Expected behavior

For Calc cells, the error names the background route that works first: keyboard input to the window (move to the cell, `type_text`, Tab or Return). Only then does it suggest `bring_to_front` or stopping.

### Actual behavior

```
set_value did not take: element [107] still shows its old value after the write. The app accepted the accessibility write but did not apply it, so nothing changed. LibreOffice ignores accessibility value writes and drops background pointer input, so its cells cannot be edited in the background. Editing them needs the window in front: bring_to_front if the user allows it, then type_text into the cell. Otherwise stop and report that the edit is blocked.
```

Structured content: `{"code": "write_not_applied", "path": "ax", "verified": false, "effect": "not_applied"}`. This text is the `vcl` route of `not_applied_result` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/set_value.rs`, and it is unchanged on `main`.

### Environment

- Cua component and version: cua-driver-rs v0.38.0, darwin-arm64 (CuaDriver.app). The message is the same on `main`.
- Operating system and architecture: macOS 26 VM (trycua's `macos:26` image under Lume), Apple Silicon.
- Application: LibreOffice 25.8.7.3 (aarch64), a Calc workbook.

### Evidence

Public trial data, each with its trajectory, a `timeline.json` of every tool call and result, the sentinel's record of the user's frontmost app, and the grade:

- **Keys edit the cells in the background:** [cdb-g02-r4-background](https://huggingface.co/datasets/earakely-scale/CuaDriverBench-AgentEnv/tree/main/runs/macos/cua-driver-sonnet-5-5-2026-11-05/cdb-g02-r4-background), Claude Sonnet 5.5.
  - The message arrives at call 33.
  - The six `run_steps` after it send 14 `hotkey`, 57 `press_key` and 22 `type_text` steps to LibreOffice's process. Their results read like `Pressed ctrl+home on pid 736` and `Inserted 9 char(s) via CGEvent`.
  - The task's workbook check passes. The sentinel shows the user's app frontmost in all 3,440 samples while the trial was armed.
- **The message stops an agent:** [cdb-g02-r1-background](https://huggingface.co/datasets/earakely-scale/CuaDriverBench-AgentEnv/tree/main/runs/macos/cua-driver-gpt-6-1-sol-2026-11-09/cdb-g02-r1-background), GPT-6.1 Sol. It replies BLOCKED and cites the message. The same happened in six more CDB-G02 and CDB-G03 background trials.

### Workaround and additional context

The workaround is keyboard input to the Calc window: arrow keys to the cell, `type_text`, then Tab or Return. In the passing trial one `press_key` was refused with `window_not_key`, so the route isn't flawless, but it carried the edit.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: feat(cua-driver): connect --replace switches an agent from another Cua Driver
body:
## Why

`cua-driver connect` stops when an agent's `cua-driver` server already launches another Cua Driver, such as the one inside Cua Spaces. Until now the only way to switch was the Set up button in Spaces or a hand edit. `--replace` does the switch from the CLI, using the MCP writer Set up already uses (`AgentSetup::configure_mcp`) rather than a second copy of it.

## What changed

- `cua-driver connect --replace` points Claude Code, Codex and Cursor at this binary when they launch another driver. The new statuses are `would_replace` (with `--dry-run`, nothing written) and `replaced`. A second run reports `already_connected`.
- The switch goes through `AgentSetup::configure_mcp_only`. That is the same writer as `configure_mcp` (the agent's own CLI for Claude Code, in-place TOML/JSON edits, a `.cua-backup-*` before the first write, the record in `agent-setup.json`), but it leaves a retired `cua-spaces` entry alone. `configure_mcp` itself is unchanged.
- Without `--replace` nothing changes except the refusal line, which now names `cua-driver connect --replace`. The help, the guide and the generated CLI reference cover the flag.

## Scope

This covers Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. Factory Droid is not in `cua-agent-setup`'s registry, and a Claude Code entry still named `cua-computer-use` would be left beside the new one. Both keep the existing "remove that server and run again" hint.

## Blast Radius

This adds a path dependency from `cua-driver` on `cua-agent-setup` and `cua-home`. Both now declare `rust-version = "1.95"`, which matches the driver's Nix rustc. `flake.nix` adds them, plus the bundled skills `cua-agent-setup` embeds, to the driver's source set, and the `ci-nix-linux` cache key includes their manifests. Plain `connect` follows the same code path as before.

Size: about +180/−15 production lines. One status pair with its help text, plus the build wiring for a new path dependency, takes that many lines.

## Verification

- The unit test `replace_switches_an_agent_that_uses_another_driver_to_this_one` covers dry run, the switch, kept comments and other servers, the kept `cua-spaces` entry, backups and the repeat run. `connect_other_driver_cli_test` runs `--replace --json` against the built binary.
- An isolated-home run of the built binary against Cursor and Codex configs: `connect` and `--replace --dry-run` left the files byte-identical. `--replace` switched both, kept `cua-spaces` and wrote a backup. A repeat reported `already_connected`. The real agent configs were untouched.
- The scoped repository checks and the macOS full Lume lane passed. The verification comment lists exactly what ran.

title: fix(cua-driver): name the AXWindows read error in ax_window_unresolved
body:
Salvaged from #5391

## Why

When an app answers the `AXWindows` attribute with an error (`kAXErrorCannotComplete` while it is busy or showing a sheet, `kAXErrorAPIDisabled`, a messaging timeout), `get_window_state` reports `ax_window_unresolved: ... none of the 0 AXWindow element(s) under that pid reports this CGWindowID`. That sentence blames the window for a read that never happened, so the agent re-snapshots instead of waiting or dismissing the sheet. @abonneth's change carries the `AXError` through the window-scope decision and names it in the reason:

```
ax_window_unresolved: window_id 3549 exists and is owned by pid 56350, but reading that
pid's AXWindows failed with AXError -25204 (kAXErrorCannotComplete). The tree is returned EMPTY ...
```

A clean read that lists no matching window keeps the existing wording.

## What changed

- @abonneth's two commits from #5391, cherry-picked with `-x` onto current main with his authorship kept: `copy_ax_windows_or_error` and `copy_ax_windows_including_or_error` return the read error, `WindowScope::AxUnresolved` and `Degradation::AxWindowUnresolved` carry it, and `ax_window_unresolved_reason` names it using the `kAXError` constants.
- Conflict resolution in `ax/tree.rs`: main's `scope_top_level` now appends attached sheets (#6758). It keeps that logic and takes the new `ax_windows_error` argument.
- Two tests added on main after #5391 branched (`a_sheet_id_walks_only_the_sheet`, `a_locked_screen_explains_an_empty_or_unresolved_tree`) are updated for the new argument and field, folded into the first commit so each commit builds.

## Scope

macOS `platform-macos` only. Only the `degraded_reason` text changes, and only when the `AXWindows` read returned an error. No field is added or renamed. `copy_ax_windows` and `copy_ax_windows_including` keep their signatures for other callers.

## Blast Radius

Agents reading `degraded_reason` for `ax_window_unresolved`. The error branch still returns the same empty tree and the same escalation; only the explanation differs.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks for `platform-macos` (fmt, clippy with warnings denied, the crate's tests, a build of its dependent driver and SDK crates) pass at the head, and the first commit builds alone.
- Mutation checks: dropping the error in `decide_window_scope` or in `degradation_for` turns `an_ax_windows_read_error_survives_the_scope_decision` or `an_ax_windows_read_error_is_named_instead_of_a_zero_window_count` red.
- macOS Lume focused cell `macos-wkwebview-scroll-ax-background` passed at the head. A live `AXError` was not forced on demand, so the new wording is covered by the unit tests.

title: fix(spaces-desktop): Electron shell throws at load, no window opens (parity flows electron red)
body:
The `parity flows (electron)` job has failed on main and on every PR since #7117, and that failure keeps `ci-gate` red.

**Root cause.** #7117 added `"paths": {"*": ["./node_modules/*"]}` to the shell's tsconfig so the bundled web sources resolve their packages from the shell. tsdown reads that tsconfig, and with it the bundler loads each package directory by its `main` (a CommonJS build) and ignores `exports`. `import ICU from "i18next-icu"` then is the module object instead of its default, and the shell's `main.cjs` throws `TypeError: import_commonjs.default is not a constructor` while loading. No window is ever created, so every test times out on `electronApplication.firstWindow`. Reproduced locally by launching the built shell, and the same launch shows the window loading after the fix. The last green run of the job (push 9dfa1dcd5) is the commit before #7117.

**Fix.** tsdown uses a new `tsconfig.build.json` (extends `tsconfig.json`, no `paths`) and finds the shell's packages through `resolve.modules`, which honours `exports`. `tsc` keeps the `paths` mapping for typechecking. The standalone build of the shell without the web app installed (`pnpm build`) still passes.

Checks: `bin/ci` (prettier, typecheck, desktop tests and router contract, image refs) passes; `pnpm build` in `apps/cua-spaces-desktop` passes.

title: fix(cua-vmm): a delete starts no cua-runsc-helper for a resolv.conf it never wrote
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: with the `CUA_SECURE_DEFAULT=0` override, deleting an ordinary runc Space starts
  `cua-runsc-helper` (privileged, `--pid host`, the engine host's `/` mounted read-write) and leaves it running,
  although nothing needed it. Fixes #6917.
- What changed: a delete removes the Space's resolv.conf only when its container mounts one, so it no longer
  starts the helper for a file that was never written. Under the default (Secure Spaces) nothing changes.

## Problem

Since #6775 Secure Spaces is always on, so this now happens only under the `CUA_SECURE_DEFAULT=0` override.
Reproduced on `cua` 0.19.0 from PyPI (macOS, Docker Desktop, engine 29.9.2), runc Space, fresh `CUA_HOME`:

| | before create | after create | after `sb rm -f` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CUA_SECURE_DEFAULT=0` | no helper | no helper | helper running |
| default (Secure Spaces) | no helper | helper running | helper running (expected) |

## Root cause

`unpolice()` always removed the Space's resolv.conf (`container/egress.rs`), through `engine_sh()`, which first
calls `helper.ensure()` and so creates and starts the helper when it isn't running. Under the override
`prepare_resolv()` never writes that file, so the delete started the helper only to `rm -f` nothing, and nothing
stops it afterwards.

## Fix

`unpolice()` takes whether the Space has a resolv.conf and removes it only then. `delete()` already inspects the
container before removing it and now passes `has_resolv_bind(...)`, the check `set_guest_dns()` already uses; when
the inspect fails it removes the file as before. A start that fails passes `egress::secure()`, since its create
wrote one exactly under the secure default. This matches how `unpolice()` already removes nft rules only when a
table was recorded.

## Tests

New opt-in `crates/cua-vmm/tests/container_delete_live.rs` (needs a Docker engine; `--ignored`): under
`Mode::Legacy` a runc Space's start and delete make no helper; under `Mode::Secure` the start writes its resolv.conf
and the delete removes it.

### Before/after

title: fix(cua-driver): post a pointer move before macOS foreground clicks
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a `delivery_mode:"foreground"` pixel click warps the hardware pointer to the target and posts the down/up pair at the HID tap. `CGWarpMouseCursorPosition` posts no mouse event, and the MouseMoved primer in `click_at_xy_desktop_inner` only ran for modified clicks. A view that arms a control on pointer movement never sees the pointer arrive and drops the press. Seen with Blender 5.2.2: a foreground click on the file browser's **Cancel** moves the pointer onto the button, raises and restores Blender, and returns success, but the file browser stays open; clicking again changes nothing. `move_cursor_desktop` already documents the cause ("A warp alone posts no mouse event … hover-revealed controls stay hidden") and follows its warp with a MouseMoved.
- What changed: `click_at_xy_desktop_inner` now posts one MouseMoved at the target before every click, as a physical mouse would, instead of only when modifiers are held. It keeps the existing `mouse_primer_settle` pacing, and with modifiers the move still follows the physical modifier keys. This covers every desktop HID click: window-scoped foreground pixel clicks (left, right, middle, multi-click), desktop-scope clicks, and the cursor-preserving variants. Background routes are unchanged.
- Test oracle: the AppKit pointer oracle (`CUA_APPKIT_POINTER_ORACLE`) now records `moved` events through a tracking area. `harness_appkit_foreground_single_click_has_one_ordered_native_pair` asserts that a `moved` at the target comes before the `down`, and both pointer-oracle rows leave `moved` out when they count the native pair.

## Related work

Refs #2789 (introduced the modifier-only primer)

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required; no contract changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS foreground clicks now deliver one extra MouseMoved at the click point before the press, so hover-armed controls receive the click. No tool schema, response, or permission change. Each foreground click takes about 12 ms longer (`mouse_primer_settle`).
- Risk and rollback: an app that reacts to pointer movement at the target (hover state, tooltip) now sees it just before the press, the same as with a physical mouse. Rollback is reverting this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `bin/ci` (affected mode, 9 checks) passes rustfmt, both SPDX header checks, the Windows cfg grep and image refs. Clippy, the unit tests, the generated reference and the UniFFI bindings check did not run here: each fails before compiling this change, while building `screencapturekit`, `apple-metal` and `apple-cf`, whose Swift `Package.swift` manifests do not link against this machine's Command Line Tools (`PackageDescription.Package.__allocating_init` undefined; CLT 26.6, no Xcode). I rely on `CI: Rust macOS` for clippy and the tests. This change touches no tool schema or bindings, so the two generator checks should not drift. The AppKit fixture sources pass `xcrun swiftc -typecheck -parse-as-library main.swift SnapshotPublication.swift`.
- Manual or platform evidence (before the change, cua-driver 0.36.0 in embedded mode on macOS 26 / Darwin 25.6, Blender 5.2.2): the foreground click on Cancel moved the pointer to the button center and stayed there, Blender was raised for about 0.27 s and the prior app restored, the response was success, and Blender's file-browser state, read from inside Blender, stayed open; a second click behaved the same. In the same run, a foreground click in Blender's text editor (no hover gating) placed the caret, and the VCL-refused-then-foreground click selected cell C5 in LibreOffice Calc.
- Known gaps or CI still required: clippy and the unit tests need CI (see above). The macOS harness lane (`E2E: Rust macOS hosted`) was not run: it needs the installed, TCC-authorized daemon on a disposable desktop, so it needs a maintainer dispatch. I have no after-the-change Blender run.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep one fake WM in the Linux own-dialog focus test
body:
## Problem

`input::own_dialog_tests::focus_restore_leaves_focus_on_a_dialog_the_app_opened` fails now and then in the Linux platform unit tests with an X11 `Access` error from `ChangeWindowAttributes` (#6989).

## Root cause

The test opened a new fake window-manager connection for each of its three cases and selected `SubstructureRedirect` on the root every time. Only one client may hold that selection. The previous fake WM connection was moved into its event thread and dropped when the thread ended, but the X server releases a client's selections only when it processes that disconnect, not when the client closes the socket. Nothing waited for that, so when the server had not handled the old connection's close yet, the next selection got `BadAccess` and the `.check().unwrap()` panicked.

Reproduced by keeping the first fake WM connection open (`ManuallyDrop`) in place of the late disconnect. That fails the same way as CI:

```
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: X11Error(X11Error { error_kind: Access, error_code: 10, sequence: 1, bad_value: 543, minor_opcode: 0, major_opcode: 2, extension_name: None, request_name: Some("ChangeWindowAttributes") })
```

## Fix

Test only. The test now opens one fake WM connection, selects the redirect once, and shares the connection with each case's event thread. Before each case it drains activations still queued from the one before. That way the "closed saved window" case, which counts zero activations, does not see a leftover message from the delayed case. No retry or sleep was added. The product code (`restore_focus_state`, `is_own_dialog`) is unchanged.

Fixes #6989. CUA-3252.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib own_dialog_tests` on Xvfb, repeated in parallel.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings`, rustfmt.
- The Linux X11 lane of the cua-driver verify skill.

title: fix(hyprland-plugin): smoke-test the released Cua Driver in the requalification session (CUA-3992)
body:
Linear: CUA-3992. Refs #4216, CUA-3107.

**What changes for users:** Omarchy and Arch Hyprland users get an answer within hours on whether Cua Driver still works with the plugin on each new Hyprland build, and the check now covers what an agent actually does (list windows, screenshot, click, type), not only the plugin's input protocol.

The requalification workflow from #4910 already detects new Hyprland builds in Arch and Omarchy edge/rc/stable, builds the plugin against each, loads it into a headless Hyprland on vkms, writes `compatibility.json` to the `hyprland-plugin-compat` branch and opens one tracking issue (#5751) on failure. This PR closes the remaining gaps from #4216:

- **Driver smoke.** After the plugin's input smoke, the latest released Cua Driver (the newest published `cua-driver-rs-vX.Y.Z`; every Driver release is marked pre-release, so that flag is not used) serves the same session with native Wayland on. Against a fresh foot window: `list_windows` must show it, `get_window_state` must write a PNG, `click` must put Hyprland's pointer on the window centre, and `type_text` must reach the application (its own output is the oracle). Any failure fails that build's smoke, so the per-version status and the issue reflect it. The driver's calls and replies are kept in `result.json` for debugging.
- **Cadence and trigger.** Detection runs every four hours instead of daily (a run with nothing new stops after the detect job), and a `hyprland-build-published` repository dispatch starts it on demand.
- **Tests and README.** Unit tests for the new helpers; README section updated.

- **rc and stable setup.** Their jobs had failed in setup (the channel's openssl 3.x collides with the base image's `openssl-3`); the container now drops the owning package and retries.
- **Pull requests are dry runs.** A PR run reports the matrix in the summary and fails only on a tooling error. The matrix is a fact about that day's packages (today it is red for reasons outside any PR: see below), and it was keeping every PR that touches this workflow red.

Not in this PR: the unsupported-release handling (#6561) and the Omarchy edge watch (#6330) are separate open PRs and untouched here.

Verification: `bin/ci --quick` green; requalify unit tests pass; the workflow runs on this PR (it forces a full rebuild) and is the evidence for the smoke.

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux background focus guard restores the focus when the delivery fails
body:
CUA-3266

On Linux, a background action ran between a focus snapshot and a restore (`focus_guard::guarded` / `guarded_settled`), but the body's error returned through `?` before the restore ran. When a background combo-box pick in `set_value` opened the popup and the AT-SPI pick then failed (for example "the combo box popup listed no options"), the user's X11 focus stayed wherever the app had moved it. Every other background guarded caller had the same gap: AT-SPI click, `invoke_menu`, keyboard `set_value`, drag and type_text.

The fix: both functions now go through one `restore_after` helper. It runs the body, always restores the snapshot, and only then returns the body's error. The success path is unchanged.

Tests: `a_failed_delivery_still_restores_the_focus_and_returns_its_error` fails on the old body-then-restore order (first commit) and passes after the fix. `a_successful_delivery_restores_once_and_returns_the_report` pins the success path.

Not changed: a popup that holds a keyboard grab is still left in place by the existing `GrabHeld` policy, on the success path and the error path alike.
