title: [Bug]: macOS Mission Control thumbnails show only wallpaper; recover after stopping Cua Driver
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

The Desktop thumbnails at the top of macOS Mission Control showed only wallpaper, even though application windows remained visible on the desktops and in Mission Control's main area. After stopping the Cua Driver daemon, then closing and reopening Mission Control, window previews returned on all six desktops.

This report documents one observed failure and its recovery. The initial trigger and the internal window or compositor behavior responsible are still unknown.

### Reproduction

I do not yet have reliable steps to trigger this from a clean start. The problem was already present before this diagnostic session. The observed sequence was:

1. The Mac had six desktops with applications open, and the Cua Driver daemon was running.
2. Open Mission Control and move the pointer to the top to expand the Desktop thumbnails. Initially, Desktop 2 and 3 showed windows; Desktop 1, 4, 5 and 6 showed only wallpaper.
3. Switch to Desktop 1 and confirm that a Chrome window exists. Reopen Mission Control: all six Desktop thumbnails now show only wallpaper, while Chrome remains visible in the main area.
4. Confirm there are no other active Cua Driver sessions or recordings, end the diagnostic session, and run `cua-driver stop`.
5. Confirm the daemon has exited and CoreGraphics no longer lists any Cua Driver windows.
6. The thumbnails in the already-open Mission Control view do not update immediately. Close and reopen Mission Control: window previews return on all six desktops. The user also visually confirmed recovery.

Cua Driver CLI calls were used during diagnosis to capture the display, open Mission Control, move the pointer and switch desktops. Those diagnostic actions may themselves have affected the state. Recovery was checked without restarting Cua Driver. Restarting the daemon and triggering the failure again has not been tested; recurrence frequency is unknown.

### Expected behavior

Mission Control's Desktop thumbnails continue to show each desktop's application windows while Cua Driver is running and after a session ends.

### Actual behavior

The Desktop thumbnails show only wallpaper. The application windows are still open and usable when switching to those desktops.

Tests during the incident:

| Action | Result after reopening Mission Control |
| --- | --- |
| Quit Raycast alone | No recovery; Raycast was then relaunched |
| Quit Input Source Pro alone | No recovery; Input Source Pro was then relaunched |
| Restart Dock | No recovery |
| End the diagnostic session / hide the agent cursor | No recovery; the display-sized Cua Driver window remained |
| Stop the Cua Driver daemon, then close and reopen Mission Control | Window previews returned on all six desktops |

Raycast, Input Source Pro and the restarted Dock were all running when the previews recovered. The Mac was not rebooted, WindowServer was not terminated, and Dock/Spaces preferences were not deleted.

### Environment

- Incident date: 2026-11-10.
- Cua Driver CLI: `cua-driver 0.46.1`.
- Installed CuaDriver.app: `CFBundleShortVersionString = 0.46.1`, `CFBundleVersion = 0.46.1`.
- CLI sessions connected to an already-running CuaDriver.app daemon; permission mode: `standard`.
- macOS `27.0.1`, build `26A434`, `arm64`.
- Primary display reported during capture: 1920×1080 logical size, 3840×2160 capture size, scale factor 2.
- Six desktops on the user's physical Mac, rather than a unit test in a VM.
- The running daemon's source SHA and executable hash were not captured. The versions above come from the CLI and installed app metadata.

### Evidence

Two screenshots redacted by the reporter are included below. They show the missing Desktop previews and the recovered previews; application content has been obscured.

#### Before: Desktop thumbnails show only wallpaper

The six Desktop thumbnails are blank apart from the wallpaper, while an application window remains visible in the main Mission Control area. Sensitive content has been obscured by the reporter.

![Redacted screenshot before recovery: all six Desktop thumbnails show only wallpaper](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb7f64af-9ec1-49a8-a140-fac879266e3e)

#### After: previews restored

After stopping Cua Driver and closing and reopening Mission Control, application windows are visible in all six Desktop thumbnails. Sensitive content has been obscured by the reporter.

![Redacted screenshot after recovery: application windows appear in all six Desktop thumbnails](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea5f2ca8-7b5a-468f-b3db-521234277f3c)

#### Window metadata

Before any Cua Driver UI actions in this diagnostic session, window metadata was captured using `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionAll, kCGNullWindowID)`. This is an excerpt of the actual fields for the Cua Driver window, with the PID, window ID and unrelated fields omitted:

```json
{
  "kCGWindowOwnerName": "Cua Driver",
  "kCGWindowBounds": {
    "Height": 1080,
    "Width": 1920,
    "X": 0,
    "Y": 0
  },
  "kCGWindowLayer": 0,
  "kCGWindowAlpha": 1,
  "kCGWindowIsOnscreen": true,
  "kCGWindowSharingState": 1
}
```

The same window remained after ending the diagnostic session. There was one Cua Driver window before stopping the daemon and zero afterward, using the same CoreGraphics query and owner filter.

This establishes that a display-sized window existed and disappeared when the daemon stopped. It does not establish whether that window was the agent cursor overlay, another internal window, or the direct cause of the Mission Control failure.

### Workaround and additional context

The recovery that worked in this incident was to confirm no other sessions or recordings were active, end the diagnostic session, stop the daemon, then close and reopen Mission Control. Stopping the daemon interrupts Cua Driver's computer-control service, so this should not be applied while other work is using it.

There is a before/after observation linking daemon shutdown with recovery, but no completed causal reproduction. Please help identify whether an internal window's lifecycle or its interaction with Spaces/Mission Control needs investigation, and which diagnostics without screen content would be useful if this happens again.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: perf(cua): split cua-daemon into cua-daemon-core and the server (CUA-3971)
body:
Cut 1 of 3 for [CUA-3971](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3971) (Spaces Local build under 5 minutes after a version bump; design note and plan are on the issue).

**What changes for users:** nothing. This only makes the Rust build of Cua Spaces Local faster.

## What

`cua-sdk` waited for all of `cua-daemon` (33k lines, about 80 s) although it uses none of the server. The runtime, the typed client, local runtimes, pools, shares, identity and storage move into a new `cua-daemon-core`, and `cua-sdk` depends on that alone. `cua-daemon` keeps the server (server, passthrough, the Spaces/share/host services, child Spaces, the test fixtures) and re-exports the core with `pub use cua_daemon_core::*`.

- Public paths, names and features of `cua-daemon` are unchanged (`cua_daemon::Runtime`, `::client`, `::local`, `::server`, and the `server`/`client`/`spaces`/`byoc`/`aws`/`contrib*`/`test-fixtures` features; the one addition is that `server` now implies `spaces`, which its services always needed: a CLI build without another crate asking for `spaces` did not compile). No caller of `cua-daemon` changed; only `cua-sdk` now names `cua_daemon_core`.
- crates.io: `publish-crates.sh` computes the closure from `cargo metadata`, so `cua-daemon-core` is published with `cua-sdk` automatically. The new crate is in the workspace version marker list, so release-please bumps it with the rest.
- Moved with `git mv`, so history follows. Only visibility changes in the core: a few `pub(crate)` items the server uses became `pub` (`#[doc(hidden)]` modules `convert`, `runtime`, `share_link`, `cloud_sweep`); the two `server`-only trait defaults in `extension` are now unconditional.
- CI path filters, the fmt/clippy/test package lists, the layering guard and the other workspaces' lockfiles follow the new crate.

## Build time (`cargo build --timings`)

`cargo build --profile dev-fast --no-default-features -p cua-spaces-ffi -p cua-spaces-cli` (the `install-local.sh` Rust step) on a 32-core Apple Silicon Mac, all workspace crates rebuilt (the shape of a version bump), third-party dependencies cached.

| | wall | cua-daemon | cua-sdk starts at |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (main 977871e) | 447 s | 82 s, serial before cua-sdk | 172 s |
| after | 363 s | 79 s, in parallel with cua-sdk | 104 s (cua-daemon-core takes 33 s) |

Saves 84 s. The critical path is now cua-spaces, cua-sdk (126 s), cua-compat, cua-cli, cua-spaces-cli; cuts 2 and 3 shorten the rest.

## Tests

- `cargo test --profile dev-fast -p cua-daemon-core -p cua-daemon -p cua-sdk`: all pass (the live suites stay ignored as before).
- `cargo check --all-targets` for `cua-cli`, `cua-spaces-cli`, `cua-spaces-ext`, `cua-spaces-ffi`, `cua-spaces-cluster`, and `cua-daemon` with `byoc,contrib`.

title: fix(cua-driver): rebuild the X11 overlay window when a compositor starts or stops
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: in `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim`, when the page under a resting agent cursor changes, the cursor's footprint keeps showing the old page in the viewer until the cursor moves or fades.
- What changed: the X11 overlay window's visual now tracks the compositor. When a compositing manager starts or stops, the overlay replaces its window with one built for the new state.

The issue reports xfwm4 as not compositing, but it is: xfwm4 owns `_NET_WM_CM_S0`, and a second manual redirect of the root is refused. The real cause is startup order. cua-spacesd's overlay comes up about 0.1 s before xfwm4 claims the selection (3 of 3 cold starts). The overlay sampled "no compositor" once at startup and pinned a 24-bit window with the software save-under path (`software_only`) for the whole session.

Once xfwm4 redirects that window, root reads no longer show what is beneath it. They return the overlay's own composited pixels. `resolve_backdrop` matches those to what it uploaded and keeps serving the stale save-under, which holds the previous page. Restarting cua-spacesd after the desktop is up gave a 32-bit window and no ghost. That confirms the startup sample was the wrong decision.

## Related work

Fixes #6415

CUA-3263

## What changed

- `X11OverlayWindow::create` owns the window and its visual, colormap, readback probe, title, bypass-compositor hint, empty shapes and GC. It records the compositor state it was built for (`built_for_compositor`). `software_only` is gone.
- The existing 1 s compositor poll now triggers a rebuild when the state differs from the window's. The old window is destroyed, and the save-under cache is reset with a resync blank. The rebuild works in both directions. Paint policy and effects capability read the window's state, so they always match its visual.
- New live regression `x11_overlay_follows_a_compositor_that_starts_after_it`, added to `ci-rust-linux.yml`. It starts picom after the overlay, changes the desktop under the resting cursor, and requires no old pixels around it. The overlay tests' `find_named_window` helper now skips a root child destroyed mid-scan. That race failed the capture-exclusion and lifecycle tests intermittently on main too.

## Scope

Linux X11 overlay in `platform-linux` only. Out of scope:
- Wayland.
- Software compositing itself, which is unchanged for desktops that never run a compositor.
- The hardened container template from the issue (read-only root filesystem without a writable `/home`). There xfce4-session exits on `.ICEauthority`, so no window manager runs at all. That is a separate image/config problem, not this bug.

## Tradeoffs

- Creating the overlay lazily on first paint would cover this startup race, but not a compositor that starts or stops later. Rebuilding on the change covers both.
- Waiting at startup for a compositor is a time-based guess and does nothing for desktops without one.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible: under a compositor that starts after the driver, the cursor now gets the composited path, with translucent glow and effects, instead of the opaque software one. On compositor-less servers (xorgxrdp, bare Xvfb) nothing changes: the window is still the root visual with software compositing.
- A compositor change now costs one window replacement and the existing 200 ms blank.
- Rollback: revert the fix commit.

risk: standard

## Validation

- Repro on the image, the issue's steps through `/mcp` on a fresh `24.04-slim` container (arm64), reading the root the way the viewer stream does. With the image's cua-spacesd, 3 of 3 runs left 364 to 370 red pixels in a 60x60 box around the resting cursor on the blue page; the overlay was 24-bit. With cua-spacesd built from this branch, 3 of 3 runs had 0 red and the page showed blue around the cursor; the overlay was 32-bit.
- The new test fails on main 3 of 3 (28 to 30 red pixels) and passes with the fix.
- The `platform-linux` lib tests and the X11 overlay lanes (click-through, lifecycle and RandR, half-presented, half-presented under picom, desktop-capture exclusion) pass under Xvfb, and clippy with `-D warnings` is clean. Full runs are in the verification comment.
- Known gaps: arm64 only, no amd64 run. No Wayland, KDE or GNOME session. macOS and Windows do not apply to this Linux-only file.

title: perf(cua-cli): build cua-compat beside cua-cli, not before it (CUA-3971)
body:
Cut 2 of 3 for [CUA-3971](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3971) (Spaces Local build under 5 minutes after a version bump; design note and plan are on the issue). Independent of cut 1 (#7214); the two add up.

**What changes for users:** nothing. `cua compat`, `cua run --compat` and `--prewarm` behave the same in the MIT `cua` and in the Cua Spaces `cua`; only the Rust build of Cua Spaces Local is faster.

## What

`cua-cli` depended on `cua-compat` (47k lines, about 70 s, the E2B / Daytona / Modal gateway) for `cua compat` and the `--prewarm` image resolver only, so every CLI build waited for the gateway. Now the Cua Spaces `cua` builds the CLI without it and registers the same code through `CliExtension`, the seam teleport and the Keyvault already use. The gateway compiles beside the CLI.

- `cua-compat-cmd` (new, clap and the SDK's `Overlay`): the `cua compat` arguments only, so the CLI can parse the command without the gateway. Help text, flags and output are unchanged.
- `cua-compat::cli` (moved from `cua-cli/src/compat_cmd.rs`, history follows): the command, the job services `cua run --compat` starts in a daemon, and the prewarm image resolver. `run` takes the CLI's `hint` function, so `cua-local` renaming still applies.
- `cua-cli`: new feature `compat`, on by default, so the MIT `cua` (`cargo build -p cua-cli`) is unchanged. With it off, the three entry points go to `CliExtension` (`compat`, `register_compat_job_services`, `compat_prewarm_image`), whose defaults fail closed with the same "ships with Cua Spaces" style message.
- `cua-spaces-cli`: `cua-cli` with `default-features = false`, plus `cua-compat`, and implements the three methods.
- `scripts/check-spaces-build-graph.sh`, run by `ci-cua-compat.yml`: fails when feature unification turns cua-cli's `compat` back on in the Spaces build graph or anything but `cua-spaces-cli` depends on `cua-compat` (checked: it passes here and fails on main).
- Nothing is published from this: `cua-cli`, `cua-compat` and the new crate are `publish = false`; the crates.io closure of `cua-sdk` is unchanged. The new crate is in the release-please version marker list.

## Build time (`cargo build --timings`)

`cargo build --profile dev-fast --no-default-features -p cua-spaces-ffi -p cua-spaces-cli` (the `install-local.sh` Rust step) on a 32-core Apple Silicon Mac, all workspace crates rebuilt (the shape of a version bump), third-party dependencies cached.

| | wall | cua-sdk done | cua-cli done |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (main 977871e) | 447 s | 289 s | 446 s |
| after | 323 s | 237 s | 322 s |

cua-cli now finishes 85 s after cua-sdk instead of 157 s; cua-compat (70 s) runs beside it. Run-to-run noise on this shared host is about 10 percent (cua-sdk itself took 100 s here and 118 s in the baseline), so the structural number is the 72 s the CLI no longer waits. With cut 1 the two add up.

## Tests

- `cargo clippy --locked -D warnings --all-targets` for `cua-compat` (with `testing`), `cua-compat-cmd`, `cua-cli` (default features and `--no-default-features`) and `cua-spaces-cli`: clean.
- `cargo test --profile dev-fast` for `cua-compat-cmd`, `cua-compat` (with `testing`), `cua-cli` and `cua-spaces-cli`: pass, with two exceptions that are not from this change: `cua-compat --test chaos` needs a higher fd limit (`ulimit -n`; passes with it), and `cua-spaces-cli --test drive an_agent_needs_a_grant_for_another_agents_folder` times out in this environment on current main too (same failure on 977871e).
- `cargo tree --no-default-features -p cua-spaces-ffi -p cua-spaces-cli`: `cua-cli` has no `compat` feature and `cua-compat` has the single dependent `cua-spaces-cli`.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix` green.

title: ci: keep AWS OIDC roles out of pull request runs (CUA-4000)
body:
Hardens how workflows get AWS credentials through GitHub OIDC, so pull request runs never hold a token they do not need.

## Changes
- **Remove the Claude Auto Fix workflow.** The AWS role it used only trusts another repository, so the job could not run any more.
- **Scope `id-token: write` to jobs.** The Docs MCP Server and ClawHub workflows no longer grant it at the workflow level. Only the jobs that assume an AWS role ask for it, and those steps already skip `pull_request` events.
- **Add `.github/scripts/tests/test_aws_oidc_fork_safety.py`.** In any workflow with a `pull_request` trigger, it fails if:
  - the workflow grants `id-token: write` at the workflow level;
  - a step that assumes an AWS role can run for a `pull_request` event;
  - a job that assumes a role does not request `id-token` itself.

  It also fails if any workflow on a default-branch-context event (`issue_comment`, `workflow_run`, `pull_request_target`, review and discussion events) assumes an AWS role.

## For users
Nothing changes. CI keeps AWS access to main-branch and protected-environment runs only.

## Testing
- `bin/ci --quick`: green.
- `pytest .github/scripts/tests/test_aws_oidc_fork_safety.py test_ci_gate_*.py test_no_pull_request_target.py`: green.
- The new test fails against the previous workflow files.

title: feat(cua-driver): support tiled niri windows and multi-output capture
body:
## Summary

niri merged [niri-wm/niri#4711](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/pull/4711) after 26.04: `tile_pos_in_workspace_view` is now populated for tiled windows **while they intersect the workspace view** (off-screen tiles keep `None`). Cua's niri adapter still refused every tiled window before reading the field, so window capture and window-coordinate input never reached the new data.

This change:

- Uses `tile_pos_in_workspace_view` when niri reports it for a tiled window, with the same origin math as floating windows (including `window_offset_in_tile` and the output origin).
- Keeps the exact `Tiled` refusal for niri releases that report no tiled position, and reports `NotShowing` for a tiled window outside the view.
- Skips the floating-window `Covered` check for the tiled window itself.
- Makes window capture copy the window's own output, so multi-output layouts work for window capture. Desktop scope and window-coordinate pointer input still require one output, unchanged.
- Pastes text containing characters outside the BMP (emoji) through the clipboard on niri and restores the previous text, because Chromium/Electron truncate a 32-bit keysym to 16 bits. A clipboard holding non-text content is refused rather than clobbered. Refs #6722.
- Updates the niri unit tests and the Linux platform docs.

## Why this is safe on 26.04

Feature detection is by field presence, not a niri version string. On 26.04 every tiled window still reports `None`, so the existing refusal is unchanged. On a release with #4711, a visible tiled window reports `Some`; an off-screen one reports `None` and is refused as not showing.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib wayland::niri` — 97 passed, 0 failed; the keyboard suite is 23/23.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean.
- Full `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` — 1013 passed, 1 unrelated pre-existing timing failure (`overlay::tests::unreported_arrival_releases_the_waiter_after_the_cap`; fails on this host without the overlay waiter).
- Real-host smoke on niri 26.04 (native Wayland, single output): a patched release build captured a floating zenity window (valid 300x226 PNG + AT-SPI tree), and the per-output screencopy selection works.
- Non-BMP live test: set the clipboard to `KEEP-ME`, typed `Hello 😀` into a zenity entry (output correct), then pasted into a second entry and got `KEEP-ME` back — the restore works.

## Notes

- The nested niri CI lane pins niri 26.04, so the tiled branch is covered by unit fixtures, not the live lane. A lane bump to a niri release containing #4711 is the follow-up once that release exists.
- No schema changes.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): remove the agent sandbox even when its setup fails
body:
Fixes CUA-3297.

## What broke

`tests/process_run_as.rs` copies the debug `cua-spacesd` binary (about 1.3G) as root into `$TMPDIR/.tmpXXXX/agent` for each of its three tests. Only `Agent`'s `Drop` removed that directory with root, and `start()` builds the `Agent` only after the server answers. When any root step in `start()` fails (an `install` hitting a full disk, or the agent never coming up), the panic drops only the `tempfile::TempDir`. That runs as the test user and cannot delete the root-owned `agent/` inside, so the copy stays behind.

## Fix

A `Sandbox` guard owns `.tmpXXXX/agent` and removes it as root on drop. It is created before the first root write, and `Agent` holds it. `Agent`'s `Drop` now only kills the agent, then the sandbox goes. The leak happened because cleanup was tied to the running agent instead of the directory. The guard ties it to the directory.

## Proof (Linux arm64, passwordless sudo, `/tmp` a 3.9G tmpfs)

Three parallel 1.37G copies fill that tmpfs, which triggers the failed-setup path on its own. Leftovers are counted with `ls -d /tmp/.tmp*/agent | wc -l` around `CUA_REQUIRE_PRIVILEGED_TESTS=1 cargo test -p cua-spacesd --test process_run_as`:

| run | tests | leftover `.tmp*/agent` before → after |
|---|---|---|
| main, parallel | 3 failed (`install: ... No space left on device`) | 0 → 3 (root-owned, each holding a partial `cua-spacesd`) |
| main, parallel, second run | 3 failed | 3 → 6 |
| this branch, parallel | 3 failed (ENOSPC, the trigger) | 0 → 0 |
| this branch, `--test-threads=1` | 3 passed | 0 → 0 |
| this branch, agent never starts (unreachable `TMPDIR`), serial | 3 failed ("the agent did not start") | 0 → 0 |

The full-tmpfs failure in parallel runs predates this change. It is a separate issue (see follow-up).

## Test plan

- The repro above on a Linux host with sudo, `setpriv` and `useradd`.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p cua-spacesd --test process_run_as -- -D warnings`.
- The e2b-core nightly lane runs this file with `CUA_REQUIRE_PRIVILEGED_TESTS=1`.

body:
## Why
One `Spaces::space` connect read `spaces.json` up to five times: once for the name in `connect_space`, then again in `provided_by_a_host`, the `image_config` lookup in `connect_with`, `refresh_record` and the `remember_reported` check. An app launch connects to every Space at once, so each Space added several full parses of the registry. Now the connect reads the record once and passes it down.

## What changed
- `connect_space` reads the record once and passes `Option<&dpb::Space>` through `connect` and `connect_with` to `provided_by_a_host`, the waking-spacesd check, the image config and `refresh_record`. `connect_when_ready` and `add` each read it once for all their attempts.
- `refresh_record` checks the Space is still registered before it rewrites the record, so a Space removed while its connect ran is not written back. The decision to refresh still comes from the record read before the connect.
- `Registry::spaces_reads()` (doc-hidden) counts reads. `tests/scale.rs` now also connects this machine's 10 registered Spaces, not only the relay ones, and asserts each scenario's connect phase reads `spaces.json` no more than once per Space connected.

## Scope
Covers the `Spaces::space` connect path and the create, fork and recovery connects that go through `connect_when_ready`. A connect that finds the record's handshake facts stale still reads the registry inside `store`/`upsert` to write it. That path is a write, it runs only when a fact changed, and the budget leaves it out. Other registry readers (`list`, `resolve`, `info`) are unchanged.

## Blast Radius
Only `cua-spaces` internals change. The one public addition is the doc-hidden counter. The behavior difference is that `refresh_record` and the relay `remember_reported` branch decide from the record as it was when the connect started instead of re-reading after it. A Space registered while its own connect ran would now get its reported facts remembered instead of its record refreshed. The next connect refreshes it.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p cua-spaces --test scale` fails on the test-only commit (`all_online: 1030 spaces.json reads for 210 connects`) and passes at the head (`registry_reads=210/210`). Adding one extra `registry.get` back into `connect_space` turns it red again (`420 spaces.json reads for 210 connects`).
- The scoped repository checks (rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test -p cua-spaces`, `cargo check` of cua-daemon, cua-sdk and cua-cli, `bin/ci --quick`) pass on macOS except `host_spaces::a_stale_relay_space_is_removed_by_delete_or_relay_unregister`, which fails the same way on unchanged main.
- Linux and Windows platform checks could not run here. CI covers them.

CUA-3333

title: fix(volume): a stalled sync never hangs an agent start or the mount (CUA-4002)
body:
Fixes [CUA-4002](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-4002/cua-volume-a-stalled-sync-hangs-agent-start-and-the-mount-guest).

**For users:** an agent on another computer now starts even when Cua Volume can't sync right now. It says in plain words that it started without its saved files, instead of hanging and showing "guest command failed (None)". Unmounting no longer hangs either.

## Root cause

Every file operation that Cua Volume serves to a mount (NFS on macOS, FUSE on Linux) waited on the store with no deadline. With replication on, the store waits on the other computer, so while sync had stalled each request waited as long as sync did. As a result:

- the guest's NFS client (`soft,timeo=50,deadtimeout=30`) retransmitted and kept folders busy;
- the agent start's `mkdir -p` under the volume was killed at spacesd's 30 s cap, with no exit code and no stderr, so the card read "guest command failed (None)";
- the kernel later declared the mount dead.

On the host, taking the volume for an agent (`volume_for_agent` → `Vfs::set_context` → `flush_all`) held the runtime's volume-table lock while it flushed pending writes through the same stalled store. Every other volume call queued behind it, unmount included, and `detach` flushed with no deadline.

## Fix

- **cua-volume:** each NFS and FUSE request is answered within `OP_DEADLINE` (4 s, below the guest's 5 s `timeo`), or 60 s for an upload on close. The work runs as its own task and isn't cancelled mid-way. A stalled store fails the call with EIO, and the mount stays alive.
- **cua-spaces-ext, volume runtime:** the view switch, flush and release run off the lock, each bounded at 10 s, and unmount steps are bounded at 30 s. A stale detach runs in the background.
- **Agent start:** the home's lease (15 s), taking the volume (20 s) and a probe of the agent's folder (10 s) are all bounded. If Cua Volume isn't ready, a bounded copy of the home is tried. If that also fails, the agent starts in its own folder (`<home>@offline`), and the start posts a plain-words thread note and returns `Delivery.notice`. The record gets `home_offline`, so that run is never saved over the home: a save would otherwise delete the home's files. A held lease (another machine working in the home) still refuses the start.
- **Errors:** a failed guest step says what happened: "didn't finish within 30 s, so it was stopped", the exit code, the signal, or "couldn't run". An agent folder on Cua Volume that doesn't answer gets a sentence that says so.
- **spacesd:** a mount or unmount tool that times out is killed instead of left behind.
- **spacesd mock:** now understands `umask NNN; mkdir -p ...`, so a full persistent start runs against it.

## Tests

- `cua-volume`: `a_stalled_store_fails_each_request_in_time_instead_of_hanging_the_mount` (NFS) and `a_stalled_store_answers_the_guest_in_time` (FUSE stream), both on paused time against a store that never answers.
- `cua-spaces-ext/tests/volume_not_ready_start.rs`: a full agent start against the spacesd mock with a store that refuses every call. It checks that the agent starts in its own folder with the notice, sets `home_offline`, and that `save` touches nothing.
- `cua-agents`: `a_failed_step_says_what_happened_in_plain_words`.
- `cua-volume`, `cua-agents` and `cua-spacesd-client` suites pass; `bin/ci --quick` is green.

## Reproduction (fresh macOS 26.4 virtual machine)

The real `cua-volume` NFS server and `Vfs` ran over a store that stalls on demand, mounted with the exact guest options spacesd uses.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `mkdir -p` under the volume, store stalled | ETIMEDOUT at 7.6 s | EIO at 8.0 s |
| `ls` of a folder, store stalled | 39 s, then ENXIO, and the mount is gone (kernel declared it dead) | EIO at 8.0 s, mount still mounted |
| the agent-start `mkdir` while other programs use the volume | **killed at the 30 s cap** (the field's "guest command failed (None)") | exit 1 with "Input/output error" at 15 s; the start's own 10 s probe catches it first and starts without the volume |
| `umount -f` afterwards | (mount already dropped by the kernel) | 0-2 s |

title: ci: automatic local-ci sign-off on our Mac runner, and auto-revert when main breaks
body:
Linear: [CUA-4001](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-4001/self-driving-merge-flow-automatic-local-ci-sign-off-on-our-mac-runner)

**For users:** pull requests from our own branches now get their `local-ci` sign-off automatically within minutes of every push, instead of waiting hours for someone to start a run. When a change breaks main, it is reverted and reported automatically.

## What changes

1. **`CI: local-ci sign-off`** (`ci-local-signoff.yml`), on every `pull_request` push from a branch of this repository:
   - `bin-ci` runs `bin/ci --quick` on our self-hosted Mac runners (label `cua-local-ci`) with a read-only token and no secrets. It tries up to 3 times when the failure is infra (guard exit 3, vitest worker start timeouts, dropped connections).
   - `sign-off` runs on a GitHub-hosted runner and never checks out PR code. It sets `local-ci` to `success`, or to `failure` on a real check failure (so ci-gate fails at once instead of waiting 75 min). With no verdict (runner lost) it sets nothing.
   - After a success it reruns a `ci-gate` run that already failed while waiting, through the existing `ci_gate_recheck.py` (a status set with the job token does not fire the `status` event).
2. **`CI: local-ci sign-off retry`**: a `workflow_run` listener that reruns a sign-off run that ended without a verdict. At most 3 attempts, only while the commit is still an open PR head with no `local-ci` status.
3. **`ci-gate`**: does not wait for the sign-off workflow's run (its own sign-off steps already wait for the status, with a bound). Otherwise a runner outage would hang the gate.
4. **`CI: main break`** (`ci-main-break.yml` + `main_break.py`) watches the 33 lanes that run on both PRs and pushes to main.
   - On the first failure it reruns the failed jobs once.
   - If they fail again and exactly one commit since the lane's last green main run reaches that lane (by `ci-areas.json`, the same rule ci-gate uses), it opens `revert: <title> (main broken: <lane>)`, labels it `auto-revert`, and runs `gh pr merge --auto --squash`.
   - It also opens one `main-broken` issue per lane and closes it when the lane is green again.
   - Loop guards: it never reverts a revert, opens at most one auto-revert an hour and one per culprit, and does nothing once main is green again.
   - A twice-hourly sweep catches missed events.
5. Host setup for the runner in `.github/runners/local-ci/`, plus docs (`docs/contributing/CI.md`, `AGENTS.md`) and tests.

## Design note

**Pattern.** A standard GitHub Actions self-hosted runner, with the job split by trust: the untrusted part (building and checking PR code) runs on the self-hosted runner with a read-only token. The privileged part (writing the commit status, rerunning the gate) runs on a GitHub-hosted runner that never sees PR code. Main-break is the usual workflow_run "monitor, rerun once, revert the culprit" pattern from mature monorepos. The culprit rule reuses our own area map, so an innocent PR is not reverted on a guess.

**Alternatives considered.**
- *Keep the agent-run `ci-remote-sweep` (ssh to a Mac).* This is what blocked PRs for 2-3 hours: nobody re-runs it when it misses a commit or misreads a flake. It stays as the fallback until this workflow has signed 10 PRs green, and now defers to the workflow.
- *Drop the Mac and accept the existing GitHub-hosted `CI: Quick` run for our branches too.* Cheaper, but the Mac run also installs and runs checks that `--no-install` skips on Linux. Changing what the sign-off means is a policy change, not a reliability fix.
- *`pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` to run the self-hosted job from main's YAML.* This would make the `if:` unforgeable, but it is the classic secret-exposure footgun, and the repository bans `pull_request_target` (`test_no_pull_request_target.py`). The host-side hook gives the same guarantee without it.
- *Ephemeral or JIT runners.* Re-registering per job needs a repository-admin credential stored on the runner machine, which is a bigger risk than a persistent runner that is guarded and cleaned.
- *Revert on any failure.* Rejected because flaky or path-filtered lanes would revert innocent PRs. When the culprit is unclear, the workflow reports and does not revert.

**Security model** (the repository is public; the runner is our machine):
1. The self-hosted job runs only when `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`.
2. A fork can edit that `if:`, so the runner enforces it too. A root-owned `ACTIONS_RUNNER_HOOK_JOB_STARTED` script, outside the runner directory and set in a root-owned LaunchDaemon, refuses before the first step any job that is not `ci-local-signoff.yml` on a `pull_request` whose base and head are both this repository. It reads them from the event payload, which the job cannot alter.
3. The runner has only the label `cua-local-ci` (`--no-default-labels`), so workflows asking for `self-hosted` never land on it.
4. The runner runs as a hidden, password-less, non-admin user with its own group. It is not in `staff`, ssh or screen-sharing, cannot read other users' homes, and holds no GitHub or cloud credentials.
5. The work directory is emptied after every job and at service start.
6. `pull_request` only; the self-hosted job has `contents: read`, no secrets, and `persist-credentials: false`.
7. Fork PRs keep the existing path: a green GitHub-hosted `CI: Quick` run, with "require approval for all external contributors" on.

`main_break.py` uses the release App token only to push the revert branch and open the PR, because a PR opened with the job token would never start CI. The workflow runs only main's own code (`workflow_run`, `schedule`).

## Merge queue (read-only audit)
- The merge queue is on (ruleset `main-merge-queue`: squash, ALLGREEN, up to 5, 60 min check timeout).
- "Require branches to be up to date" is off (`strict_required_status_checks_policy: false`), which is right with a queue.
- `local-ci` is not itself a required check. `ci-gate` enforces it, and in `merge_group` it reads the queued PR's head commit, which is already signed. So the queue needs no sign-off run of its own. `CI_QUEUE_RUNS` is `false`.

## Tests
- `bin/ci --quick` is green.
- `.github/scripts/tests` passes: 1934 passed.
- New tests: `test_ci_local_signoff.py` (workflow shape and runner guard behaviour) and `test_main_break.py` (watch-list sync, culprit rule, loop guards).

title: feat(cua-spacesd): support niri sessions
body:
## Summary

cua-spacesd selected its Wayland backend only on `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE`. On niri it fell back to the X11 backend, which reads rootless Xwayland `:0` and streams black frames ([#6111](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/6111)). niri already implements the `wlr-screencopy` path the backend uses.

This change:

- Treats `NIRI_SOCKET` as a Wayland session too.
- Reads displays from `niri msg --json outputs` (logical bounds, native mode, millihertz refresh, focused output as primary).
- Reads windows from `niri msg --json windows` + `workspaces`, and the focused window from `focused-window`.
- Adds `NiriWindowManager`: focused id via IPC; window actions are left to the driver; `set_bounds` refuses because niri's layout owns geometry.
- Keeps display streaming on the existing screencopy/grim path, which fixes the black stream.
- Refuses **window** streams and layout-managed resize explicitly instead of calling `hyprctl`. Window capture on niri needs a per-toplevel protocol or the driver's desktop-scope path; that is a follow-up.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p cua-spacesd-desktop --lib` — 125 passed, 0 failed.
- New pure parser tests for niri outputs and windows; a live niri test runs `niri msg --json outputs` and asserts a non-zero native display.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.
- Live on niri 26.04: `displays()` returns the real eDP-2 output, so the previous empty-display/X11 fallback path is no longer taken.

## Limitations

- niri window streams (per-window capture) still refuse; use a display stream.
- Background input on niri remains unavailable (compositor limit); the cua-driver tool path reports its own refusal.

title: perf(cua-ci): build cua-ci beside cua-sdk, not after it (CUA-3971)
body:
Step 1 of the CUA-3971 follow-up ([CUA-3971](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3971), Spaces Local build under 5 minutes after a version bump). Stacked on #7214 and #7222: this branch contains both, so until they merge the diff includes them; the change of this PR alone is the `perf(cua-ci)` commits.

**What changes for users:** nothing. It only shortens the Rust build of Cua Spaces Local.

## What

`cua-ci` (the CI runner pool, 15k lines) used `cua-sdk` in one file, `src/sdk.rs` (the `SdkSpaces` implementation of its own `Spaces` seam). That one file made all of `cua-ci` wait for the 28k-line SDK, and `cua-cli` wait for `cua-ci`.

- `SdkSpaces` moves, with `git mv` (history follows), into `cua-cli` as `ci_sdk.rs`. `cua-cli` is its only user. (A first version put it in a new crate; a 360-line crate between `cua-sdk` and `cua-cli` cost 17 s on the build path, so it is a module instead.)
- `cua-ci` no longer depends on `cua-sdk`; it builds beside it.
- `scripts/check-spaces-build-graph.sh` (the guard from #7222) also fails if `cua-ci` gets a `cua-sdk` dependency back.
- No new crates, so crates.io publishing, release-please and the workspace test lists are untouched.
- Also fixes the `crates.io dry run` failure on #7214: `cua-sdk`'s dev-dependency on `cua-daemon` carried a version, which cannot resolve once `cua-daemon` is no longer in the published closure. It is path-only now (pushed to #7214).

## Build time (`cargo build --timings`)

`cargo build --profile dev-fast --no-default-features -p cua-spaces-ffi -p cua-spaces-cli` (the `install-local.sh` Rust step), 32-core Apple Silicon, workspace version bumped so every workspace crate rebuilds, third-party dependencies cached. The host is shared and noisy (load 8 to 13), so read differences under 10 s as noise.

| | wall | cua-ci | cua-cli starts at |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (#7214 + #7222) | 314 s | 22 s, after cua-sdk | 244 s |
| after (first version, with a crate) | 310 s | 9 s, beside cua-sdk | 230 s |

By itself the gain is small. It matters together with the next PR (the SDK stops blocking its neighbours), after which `cua-ci` and `cua-cli` start as soon as the SDK's metadata is ready.

## Tests

- `cargo check --all-targets -p cua-ci -p cua-cli`, clippy `-D warnings` on both, the moved unit test passes.
- `scripts/check-spaces-build-graph.sh` ok; `bin/ci --quick --fix` green.

title: macOS type_text confirms a partial terminal delivery when the scrollback already holds the text
body:
## Summary

On macOS, `type_text` verifies keystroke delivery with `typed_progress` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs`), which returns `Complete` as soon as the read-back `AXValue` contains the requested text. In a terminal emulator (Terminal.app, iTerm2), the `AXValue` is the whole scrollback. If the same text is already on screen from earlier, for example a command being run again, a delivery that lands only in part is reported as verified.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In Terminal.app, run `git status` once, so it is in the scrollback.
2. Call `type_text` in background mode with `text: "git status"` on that window, under conditions where only part of the keys land (a partial delivery is observable on a loaded host; it can be simulated with a read-back of `"...$ git sta"`).
3. The reply reports the text as verified, with `delivered_chars` = 10.

## Expected

The reply is unverified or partial, because the copy of `git status` in the value was there before the call.

## Actual

`after.contains(text)` matches the old copy in the scrollback, so the poll returns `Complete`. A client that presses Return after a verified line then runs the partial command (`git sta`).

## Suggested fix

On the terminal key path only, require more occurrences of `text` in `after` than in `before` when `before` is readable:

```rust
let shown = match before {
    Some(before) if terminal => after.matches(text).count() > before.matches(text).count(),
    _ => after.contains(text),
};
```

Keep `contains()` for the `AXSelectedText` write and for non-terminal keys. There, a selection replaced by the same text leaves the count unchanged, and counting would turn a successful write into `Unchanged` and a second, duplicate key delivery.

If the scrollback drops an old copy just as the new one lands (a `clear`, a trimmed buffer), the count does not grow, so the result is unverified. It is never a false confirm.

Cost: the two `str::matches` counts run only on polls where the value moved (`after != before` is checked first), so a no-echo prompt never counts.

When `before` is unreadable on a terminal, nothing tells an old copy from a new one, so the result should be unverified rather than `contains()`.

A second instance of the same class: kitty's `AXValue` path confirms with `ax_value_insert_landed`, which is `after.contains(text) && before != after`. kitty's value is the text around the cursor, so the same old-copy match can confirm a write there too. It is all-or-nothing, so a partial command is less likely, but the check has the same blind spot.

We carry this fix in a fork with unit tests: a terminal with the text in its scrollback plus a partial delivery is not `Complete`; a fresh delivery and a full new copy are `Complete`; a shrinking value is not `Complete`; and a non-terminal selection replaced by the same text stays `Complete`. Happy to open a PR if that helps.

title: macOS type_text advises a foreground retry for an unconfirmed terminal insert, which types the text twice at a no-echo prompt
body:
Traced against main at 666a8ccab.

## Summary

In `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs`, a background `type_text` whose read-back is `Unverifiable` replies "📨 Sent (unverified) … verify via screenshot, and re-call with delivery_mode:"foreground" if it didn't". The structured result carries `escalation.recommended = "foreground"`. That holds for terminal emulators too. A terminal reading with echo off (`read -s`, `sudo`, `ssh` password prompts) never shows the text, so neither the screen nor a screenshot can confirm it. An agent that follows the advice sends the text a second time.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In Terminal.app, run `read -s pw; echo ${#pw}`.
2. Call `type_text` in background mode on that window with `text: "abc\n"`. The newline makes the read-back `Unverifiable`.
3. The reply says to verify by screenshot and re-call in the foreground. The screenshot shows no text, so following the advice types `abc` again.

## Expected

For a terminal target, an unconfirmed insert says that a terminal may not echo what it reads, so the text must not be typed again, and it recommends no foreground escalation.

## Suggested fix

Choose the note and the escalation from `is_terminal_target`. A terminal gets a "do not type it again" note and no `escalation`; other targets keep today's advice.

title: macOS type_text follows a successful AX write with the same text as keystrokes when the field changed without growing
body:
Traced against main at 666a8ccab.

## Summary

The background AX rung writes `AXSelectedText` and classifies the read-back with `typed_progress`. A write that changed the field without making it longer, and whose value no longer contains the raw text, is classified `Unchanged`, because `typed_progress` counts only length growth. Typical cases are a selection replaced by text the app normalizes, such as smart quotes or autocorrect. The rung then records `AxAttempt::Unchanged` and falls back to CGEvent keystrokes, which type the text a second time after the AX write already landed.

## Reproduction (code level)

`typed_progress(Some("say hello world"), Some("say “hi”"), "\"hi\"")` returns `Unchanged`. This is the read-back of an AX write that replaced the selected `hello world` with `"hi"`, which the app then turned into curly quotes. The AX rung maps `Unchanged` to `AxAttempt::Unchanged` and falls back to CGEvent keystrokes, so the keys type `"hi"` again after the write landed.

## Expected

A successful AX write whose read-back changed is reported unverified and is not followed by keys.

## Suggested fix

Distinguish "the value changed but did not grow" from "the value did not change" (`after != before`). On the AX rung, a changed read-back returns an unverified `Typed` outcome instead of falling through to keystrokes.

title: fix(cua-spaces): the name and stale-relay tests follow pet names and the relay's cascade
body:
## What

Three `cua-spaces` integration tests still expected old behaviour, so `cargo test -p cua-spaces` fails on `main` (and `bin/ci` with it for any change under `libs/cua`):

- `providers`: `a_local_space_is_named_what_it_was_created_as` and `a_space_that_fails_to_start_leaves_no_instance` expected a Space made without a name to be called `space-<hex>`. Since pet names (#6707) it is a friendly name such as `brave-otter`.
- `host_spaces`: `a_stale_relay_space_is_removed_by_delete_or_relay_unregister` deleted a relay entry whose host had left the relay and expected the text "stale entry". The relay now takes a removed host's Spaces with it, so the delete reports the Space as removed.

CI never runs the `providers` and `host_spaces` test binaries (it runs `cua-spaces --lib`, `relay`, `cloud_discovery` and `scale`), which is why they went unnoticed. They fail on every platform, not only on macOS.

title: perf(cua-sdk): build libcua_sdk in its own crate so cua-sdk is rlib-only (CUA-3971)
body:
Step 4 of [CUA-3971](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3971) (Spaces Local build under 5 minutes after a version bump), and the one that matters most. Stacked on #7240, which is stacked on #7214 and #7222: until those merge the diff includes them; this PR alone is the `perf(cua-sdk)` commit and the Cargo.lock refresh.

**What changes for users:** nothing. Same `libcua_sdk` file, same bindings, same Rust paths. Cua Spaces Local builds faster.

## Why

I measured where the build waits. `cua-sdk` was built as `rlib + cdylib + staticlib`. Cargo can start a crate when its dependencies' metadata is ready, before their code generation finishes, but not when the crate has a cdylib or staticlib target: that kind of crate needs every dependency fully built, and its dependents wait for it fully built and linked. So `cua-sdk` started only when `cua-spaces` was completely done, and `cua-cli` and `cua-compat` started only when `cua-sdk` was linked into two libraries nobody in the Local build uses. (Splitting `cua-sdk` by feature would not have helped: the cause is the crate types, not its size.)

## What

- `cua-sdk` is `rlib` only. Source, features, `uniffi.toml`, public paths and crates.io publishing are unchanged.
- New `cua-sdk-native` (unpublished, about 5 lines): library name `cua_sdk`, `cdylib + staticlib`, `pub use cua_sdk::*`, the same features passed through, the macOS `install_name` link argument (moved from `cua-sdk/build.rs`). `libcua_sdk.so/.dylib/.dll/.a` keep their file names and output paths.
- Every command that built `libcua_sdk` now builds `-p cua-sdk-native` (workflows, `build-xcframework.sh`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs`, `stage-uniffi-library.mjs`, docs generators config, example scripts, READMEs). `--example` builds (rollout_bench and friends) and fmt, clippy, test and wasm32 lines stay on `cua-sdk`.
- CI scope: `cua-sdk-native` is added next to `cua-sdk` in the path filters, `ci-areas.json`, `e2e_cua_sdk_scope.py` roots and the Swift samples scope.
- `cua-sdk` and `cua-sdk-native` are both the library `cua_sdk`, and UniFFI finds a library's binding settings by that name. `cua-sdk-native` therefore carries a copy of `uniffi.toml`, and its `build.rs` fails the build if the two differ.

## Checks

- Exports: `nm` shows 1137 `uniffi_cua_sdk_*` symbols and the UniFFI metadata in `libcua_sdk.dylib`; `otool -D` shows `@rpath/libcua_sdk.dylib`.
- `scripts/generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` against the new library: Python, Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript are byte for byte the committed bindings.
- `cargo check --all-targets -p cua-sdk`, `cargo check -p cua-sdk-native` (default and `--features contrib`), clippy `-D warnings` on both.
- `.github/scripts/tests`: all pass. `bin/ci --quick --fix` green.
- Not run here: the release and platform lanes (`cd-cua-sdk.yml` per-target builds, wheels, npm packages, Android/iOS). They only changed `-p cua-sdk` to `-p cua-sdk-native` and a missing library fails loudly; please watch the `ci-cua-sdk` lanes on this PR.
- `cargo check -p cua-sdk --no-default-features` fails (`spaces` module) on main too; unrelated.

## Build time (`cargo build --timings`)

`cargo build --profile dev-fast --no-default-features -p cua-spaces-ffi -p cua-spaces-cli`, 32-core Apple Silicon, workspace version bumped so every workspace crate rebuilds, third-party dependencies cached, shared host (load 10 to 14).

| | wall | cua-sdk | cua-cli starts at |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (#7214 + #7222) | 314 s | starts when cua-spaces ends; cli waits for the link | 244 s |
| this stack | 216 s | starts on cua-spaces metadata | 106 s |

About 100 s off the Rust step (a Local build after a bump was about 5m50 with the earlier cuts; the non-Rust tail is about 40 s, so about 4m15 now). Remaining critical path: `cua-sdk` -> `cua-spaces-ffi` (its own staticlib, needs everything built) -> `cua-spaces-cli`, which depends on `cua_spaces_ffi::media_decode` only for `stream-probe`. The same split applied to `cua-spaces-ffi` would take roughly 10 s more.

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux X11 foreground gestures, right_click and set_value give the focus back
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux X11 and XWayland, a `delivery_mode:"foreground"` `double_click`, `scroll`, `drag`, `right_click` or `set_value` activated the target and left it active. The `delivery_mode` schema text says every foreground action injects, "then restore[s] the prior active window … Matches the macOS / Windows delivery_mode surface". macOS and Windows do restore after these actions, and since #6768 and #7164 so do X11 `type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey` and `click`.
- What changed:
  - The X11/XWayland row of the foreground restore table (`interaction::foreground_policy`) now restores after gestures and after `right_click`/`set_value`. Native Wayland rows are unchanged.
  - A `right_click` that opens a context menu keeps it open. The X11 restore already detects the target's new popup, leaves the target focused, and the result carries `focus_outcome: "menu_open"` with "The target was left focused because a menu is open", as for `click` today.
  - `set_value`'s combo-box keyboard fallback used to open the popup in one foreground transaction, then pick and close it outside it. It now opens, picks and closes inside one transaction, so the restore runs after the popup is gone instead of between the open and the pick.
  - The action-icon catalog footnote and the X11 foreground module doc now say that X11 restores after every foreground action.

## Related work

Refs CUA-3434

RFC: not required. The code now does what the published `delivery_mode` contract already says.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: after an X11 foreground `double_click`, `scroll`, `drag`, `right_click` or `set_value`, the previously active window is active again. A caller that relied on the target staying active should send its next action with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` (each foreground call activates the target itself) or call `bring_to_front`.
- Known limit: on X11, the restore reads any new popup of the target as a menu. A gesture that maps a non-menu popup keeps the target focused, which is what every gesture did before this change.
- Risk and rollback: Linux X11/XWayland only. Reverting this PR restores the previous table.

risk: standard

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the scoped repository checks passed: format, clippy with warnings denied for `platform-linux` and `cua-driver-e2e`, and the `platform-linux` unit tests. The policy-table unit test now pins all six X11/XWayland columns to restore and keeps the Wayland expectations.
- Behaviour test: `x11_foreground_restore_linux_test` gains five cases. `double_click`, `scroll`, `drag` and `right_click` each restore the prior active window, and a `right_click` whose menu maps after the press keeps the target focused and says why. Under Xvfb with openbox, the suite against a driver built from the test-only commit (main behaviour) passed the 7 existing cases and failed the 5 new ones, for example "foreground double_click left the active window on the target instead of the prior window". Against this branch all 12 pass.
- Manual or platform evidence: the verify-cua-driver Linux X11 lane passed both default Electron background cells with complete evidence. The full Electron X11 matrix delivered 25 cells and refused 16 as declared, with complete evidence and no failures. Every foreground cell delivered: AX and PX left, right and double click, scroll, hotkey, press_key, type_text, type_submit and child_window, plus PX drag and AX editor_save.
- Known gaps: no test reaches `set_value`'s combo keyboard fallback. A GTK 3 combo uses the accessibility route. Forced to show as a list, the fallback fails with "the combo box popup listed no options" on main and on this branch alike, so the restructure was checked by review only. Native Wayland compositors, XWayland sessions and Windows were not run.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse input to macOS security and consent prompts
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: nothing in the macOS driver kept input away from the system prompts that grant or refuse access on the user's behalf. Seen downstream: an agent clicked "Allow" on "HoloWork would like to access data from other apps"; a foreground click would have granted it. 0.37.0 also types into an administrator password prompt.
- What changed:
  - A new core module, `security_prompt`, names the macOS processes that draw these prompts (UserNotificationCenter for privacy alerts, SecurityAgent, universalAccessAuthWarn, LocalAuthentication's coreautha, CoreServicesUIAgent for Gatekeeper, CoreLocationAgent), matched by bundle id or executable name, and a refusal, `security_prompt_protected`, with a hint to leave the prompt to the user.
  - The macOS tools refuse before sending any event:
    - a window or element target owned by one of them (every tool that resolves its pid through `target_pid`, plus `drag`, `type_text_chars` and `invoke_menu`);
    - a desktop-target click, drag or scroll whose point a prompt window covers, in any delivery mode;
    - a foreground click, right click, drag or scroll whose screen point a prompt window covers, since those go to whatever window is on top;
    - desktop-scope keys and text while a prompt owner is frontmost.
  - Reading prompts stays allowed, so an agent can tell the user what is being asked.

## Related work

Refs: no upstream issue.

RFC: not required. One new refusal code, `security_prompt_protected`, returned only for input that targets or lands on these prompts.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: input to these prompts is refused; everything else is unchanged.
- Not covered: Windows shows UAC on the secure desktop, which input cannot reach, and does not check Credential UI yet; Linux does not check polkit agents yet. Both are noted in the module.
- Risk and rollback: a legitimate automation of one of these prompts (a test harness clicking a Gatekeeper dialog, say) is now refused. Rollback is a revert of this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: unit tests for the prompt owners and the refusal. `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos --lib` passes (1238 + 726), `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- Live (macOS 26, daemon built from this branch on current main, run from an app bundle): an administrator password prompt (`osascript -e 'do shell script "true" with administrator privileges'`, SecurityAgent, layer 1000). Every input route sent to its exact pid and window was refused with `security_prompt_protected`: `type_text` and `press_key` (background and foreground), `hotkey`, a click on "Cancel" by name (background and foreground). The prompt stayed open and empty; `get_window_state` still read it.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the privacy alert (UserNotificationCenter) itself was not shown live; on the test Mac it is pre-approved by device management. Windows and Linux CI.

title: test(spaces): list a stale Space before its host leaves the relay (CUA-3982)
body:
Fixes CUA-3982. `host_spaces::a_stale_relay_space_is_removed_by_delete_or_relay_unregister` failed on main every run: the delete said `Removed relay:space-00000000000000a2 (disconnected).` where the test expected a stale-entry message.

## Root cause

The test was wrong, not the code, and the host was not a factor. The failure reproduces on any machine.

- #6504 made the relay keep a removed computer's Spaces but detach them: `GET /v1/machines` stops listing them (`Directory::is_detached` in `cua-relay`).
- #6508 copied that into `FakeRelay::list` (`cua-host/src/testing.rs`).
- The test's third case registers a Space, removes its host, then deletes the Space. The client had never listed that Space, so `Spaces::relay_row` finds no row and `Spaces::delete` takes its `None => "Removed {id} (disconnected)."` branch. It never reaches the stale-entry branch in `delete_on_host`.
- `ci-cua-sdk.yml` compiles `--test host_spaces` but never runs it, so CI did not catch this.

The stale-entry branch is still reachable. A device that listed the Space shortly before the host left has the row in its cache and still holds it when the relay stops listing the Space. The test now sets up that state: it lists the Space, removes the host, then deletes. It then checks the stale-entry message and that the relay forgot the record. Before, the test only checked that the Space was absent from the listing, and a detached Space is always absent.

The first two cases (a Space its host does not have, and `relay-unregister`) are unchanged.

## Test plan

- The focused test fails at the base commit with the original message, and passes at this head 3 of 3 times.
- The full `host_spaces` file passes (41 tests).
- Two mutants of `delete_on_host`'s stale-entry branch each turn the test red: one leaves the relay record in place, one changes the message.
- `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` pass for `cua-spaces` tests.

title: ci(gate): fail fast on a failed job so one bad entry cannot hold the merge queue
body:
Linear: CUA-4007 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-4007)

**For users:** a pull request whose own CI already failed now leaves the merge queue within about a minute. The other queued pull requests no longer wait up to an hour behind it.

## What happened

On 10 Nov, #7136 was marked ready for review 3 seconds before it was added to the merge queue, so its `pull_request` lanes ran again. In that run, the `app core (Rust) + FFI mirror gate` job failed at about 15:05Z. Another job, which has a 180-minute timeout, kept the run open. The queue's `ci-gate` judges an entry by the pull request's own runs while `CI_QUEUE_RUNS` is off, and it waits for every run to complete. So it waited, and eight green pull requests sat behind it until GitHub removed #7136 at 16:02Z (`checks_timed_out`, the queue's 60-minute limit). #7133 hit the same limit at 06:05Z the same day. Normal enqueue-to-merge time today was 3 to 5 minutes.

The `local-ci` sign-off was not involved. In the queue, the gate checks the sign-off on the queued pull request's head commit, not on the merge-group commit, so merge-group commits need no sign-off of their own.

## Change

- In the wait step, at most once a minute, the gate reads the commit's check runs (one listing for the PR head, plus one for the queue commit when queue runs are on). If the newest run of a workflow it waits on is still going and already has a `failure` or `timed_out` job, the gate fails at once and names the job.
- A failure that is a quarantined flake (`.github/flaky/quarantine.json`) still waits for the full verdict and its one rerun, as before.
- Completed runs keep the existing verdict logic. Older runs of the same workflow are ignored, as before.
- The gate's token gets `checks: read`.
- `ci-gate-recheck` still reruns the gate if the failed job is later rerun green.
- `docs/contributing/CI.md` describes the new behaviour.

## Tests

- `test_ci_gate_workflow.py`: new cases for today's incident (PR context and queue context), for no failure / a failure in a completed run / a failure in a run the gate does not wait on, for "newest run only", for a quarantined early failure, and for the once-a-minute read budget. 475 gate-related script tests pass locally.
- I checked the jq against #7136's live check runs. It returns exactly the failed FFI mirror job and its run.

title: fix(cua-driver): tell a live macOS app from an exited one in bring_to_front (CUA-3617)
body:
Fixes CUA-3617. Same cause as CUA-3798.

## What broke

`bring_to_front_macos_test` (`exact_secondary_window_is_verified_and_prior_app_can_recover_focus`) failed now and then in the macOS Lume matrix with:

```
prior app recovery failed: bring_to_front: no running application for pid N (process not found or exited).
```

It failed in 15 of 55 recorded full Lume runs, including the runs at a4bdc7a19 and 8e39e4813 and the run on #6659. Several of those SHAs also passed on other runs. The same error showed up in four more runs as the foreground sentinel's first launch attempt in `shared-app-matrix` and `embedded-browser-routes`, where the sentinel's retry hid it.

## Root cause

`bring_to_front` took a nil from `NSRunningApplication::runningApplicationWithProcessIdentifier(pid)` to mean the process had exited. That call reads AppKit's cache of running applications, and the cache can briefly lose a live app. Instrumented guest runs (16 of them) caught it every time:

- the prior app's pid was alive (`kill(pid, 0)`), LaunchServices still had it (`lsappinfo`), and `list_apps` listed it;
- `pgrep` showed exactly one new SwiftUI process, so the pid was the right one;
- repeating the same `bring_to_front` for the same pid succeeded on its first try, 127 to 182 ms later.

So the pid had not died and was not wrong. The AX path was never reached, because the failure happens at the lookup before any activation. The bug is the decision that a cache miss means the process exited.

## Fix

`bring_to_front.rs` now has one lookup, `running_application(pid)`:

- AppKit has the app: use it, as before.
- AppKit has no entry and the kernel has no process: fail at once with `bring_to_front_pid_not_found`, as before.
- AppKit has no entry but the process is alive: poll AppKit for up to 1 s. If AppKit never reports it, fail with a new code, `bring_to_front_pid_not_application`, instead of claiming the process exited.

The foreground `type_text` activation (`activate_exact_window_blocking`) and its handback to the previous app (`reactivate_application`) use the same lookup. All three run on blocking threads, never on an async worker.

Unit tests cover a late AppKit answer, an exited pid (no wait), a live pid AppKit never reports, the kernel oracle on a reaped child, and the tool's refusal for a reaped pid.

## Evidence

Same Lume guest, same harness, the test above run 150 times against each signed `CuaDriverLocal.app` install:

| daemon | pass | fail |
|---|---|---|
| main a4ec97ee94 | 145 | 5, all "no running application for pid" |
| this branch 0834b2d63e | 150 | 0 |

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib tools::bring_to_front::`

title: fix(spaces): a computer's row opens its shared desktop's Space page
body:
## What

Sharing a computer's desktop changed nothing on the Computers page: every machine's desktop is filtered out of the tree, and a computer row always opened the settings-style computer page. A computer row now opens by state:

1. A computer that shares its desktop opens that desktop's Space page (thread layout, Stream, rail).
2. This Mac, set up but not sharing, opens the same page; its stage has "Share this desktop" (and "Stop sharing" once on), the page that already existed for `this-mac`.
3. A computer that cannot share (offline, set up for Spaces only, unreachable, not set up) opens its own page as before.

A computer whose row opens its desktop keeps its own page one step away: "Computer settings" in the row menu.

## Notes

- `TreeNode.opens` carries the choice (`lib/spaces-tree.ts`); the page's `open()` uses it.
- Demo data: `?demo=desktops` now includes a sharing This Mac; `?demo=desktops-off` has This Mac not sharing.
- #7132 question: attached machines are always the Spaces' own `space-<hex>` ids, never a host's `relay:<id>`, so a host's own desktop row is not hidden. Test added in `relay_publish.rs`.

## Tests

`spaces-tree.test.ts` (3 states plus the cannot-share variants), `spaces-tree.test.tsx` (click navigation), the `relay_publish` test above. `first-run-new.test.tsx` "dots count the steps" fails locally on main too; `pick-up.test.tsx` failed once under load and passes alone.

title: ci(release): hourly sweeper for superseded draft releases
body:
## What changed for users
Fewer stale draft releases on trycua/cua; the release canary stops warning about them.

## Why drafts pile up
- Release Please opens an untagged draft per version, and the Spaces CD adds a second, tagged draft. The existing cleanup runs only in the final publish step of a successful run, and only for the exact version.
- A failed or cancelled run (every cd-rust-cua-driver and cd-cua-sdk run on 7-10 Nov failed in a late gate), or a skipped version (Spaces 0.25.x), leaves its drafts forever. The next version makes new ones.

## Fix
Hourly `release-sweep-drafts.yml` (`sweep_draft_releases.py`) deletes a draft only when it is older than 24 h, is superseded by a same-component published release (>= version) or a newer draft, and has no queued, running or last-3h CD run for its tag. Unclassifiable drafts, prereleases and the newest draft per component are kept. Tags and published releases are never touched. Manual runs default to dry run.

Unit tests cover the rules; a dry run against the live repo after the manual cleanup reports nothing left to delete.

title: fix(cua-driver): unblock Cua Driver and cua SDK releases (X11 pixel click, SDK feed checkout, installer bump)
body:
Every cd-rust-cua-driver and cd-cua-sdk run from 7 to 10 Nov failed, so nothing after Cua Driver 0.46.1 published.

**Cua Driver, Linux X11 Chrome release gate.** #7157 made a background pixel click on a Chromium control land through its AT-SPI action on X11, but `standalone_browser_capture_bound_pixel_click_background_refusal` still expected a refusal for a point covered by a button. On X11 the test now asserts delivery (page counter increments, no focus, z-order or input leak) and keeps the refusal for a point no control covers. Wayland and the inject lanes keep the old refusal.

**cua SDK, publish job.** A second sparse checkout into the workspace removed `scripts/install` (and the downloaded `release-artifacts.json`), so "Update the rolling installer manifest" failed on `stamp_installers.py` in every release. The checkout now uses its own path. Test added.

Plain words: this unblocks the next Cua Driver and cua SDK releases.

Not covered here: a separate staging smoke failure on 0.47.2 (transient, cloud repo) and a release PR merged before Release Please refreshed its changelog (0.46.3, 0.47.1).

**Decision (capture contract unchanged).** A refused background click must not spend the one-shot capture: agents retry in the foreground with the same capture, as the old pre-admission refusal allowed. After #7157 the X11 AT-SPI miss refused after admission, which spent it. The driver now previews the capture-bound admission for a Chromium background click (new `CaptureService::preview_action`) and spends the capture only once the click is dispatched; the E2E again asserts that the foreground retry with the same capture lands. The full-walk at-point click also no longer presses a web document (`doDefault` dispatches no DOM click), which had made a miss report success.

title: fix(cua-driver): the macOS cursor overlay no longer takes the front app
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, starting the daemon with the agent cursor overlay made `cua-driver` the frontmost app and took keyboard focus from the window the user was typing in. The overlay set the Accessory activation policy, and AppKit activates an Accessory app as it finishes launching. Embedded hosts saw the front app move to cua-driver about 70 ms after the host reported ready.
- What changed: the overlay now uses the Prohibited activation policy, so the daemon never becomes the active app. The overlay is a click-through window shown with `orderFrontRegardless`, so it never needs activation. A Prohibited app's windows still show, order above other apps' windows, and take clicks.
- Tests: a new E2E, `overlay_daemon_start_leaves_the_front_app_in_front`, starts an overlay daemon and checks that the front app does not change and the daemon registers as BackgroundOnly. The frontmost-app E2E helpers also read `lsappinfo` pids on macOS 27, which prints `pid = 468 …` instead of `"pid"=468`; before this, `front_pid` and `pid_of_app` parsed nothing there.

## Related work

No existing issue for this bug. Related but distinct: #4277 (a background click briefly deactivates the active app).

RFC: not required (no public contract change).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. The daemon no longer steals focus when the overlay starts. Windows, X11 and Wayland are unaffected; this fixes a macOS AppKit activation-policy behavior that has no counterpart there. No API, CLI or MCP change.
- Risk and rollback: low. Two `setActivationPolicy:` values change from 1 to 2. Rollback is a revert of this commit. `permissions/panel.rs` still uses Accessory on purpose, since that panel is a window the user interacts with; it is out of scope here.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `bin/ci --quick` is green and `cargo check -p cua-driver-e2e --tests -p platform-macos` compiles on the current head `e6aaaeb1e` (5 passed; clippy, unit tests, generated reference and UniFFI bindings are skipped by `--quick`).
- Manual or platform evidence: on macOS 27 at `8b5272625` (an earlier head; `e6aaaeb1e` is that commit rebased onto main after #7481 removed the picture-in-picture module, so it drops the `pip/mod.rs` change and keeps the overlay and E2E diffs unchanged; the E2E has not been re-run on the new base), `cargo test -p cua-driver-e2e --test frontmost_app_macos_test -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1` passes both tests (`no_overlay_daemon_reports_the_current_frontmost_app`, `overlay_daemon_start_leaves_the_front_app_in_front`). With the activation policy set back to Accessory on this same base (after the multi-display overlay rewrite in #7458), `overlay_daemon_start_leaves_the_front_app_in_front` fails. Earlier, on the `cua-driver-rs-v0.45.4` base: `overlay_daemon_start_leaves_the_front_app_in_front` fails on shipped 0.45.4 and passes with this change; `no_overlay_daemon_reports_the_current_frontmost_app` passes again with the `lsappinfo` fix. Both run with `cargo test -p cua-driver-e2e --test frontmost_app_macos_test -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`, which the canonical macOS runner already selects.
- Known gaps or CI still required: only the frontmost-app test binary was run locally, not the complete macOS matrix (`libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/macos-lume/run-all.sh`); the macOS, Windows and Wayland E2E workflows need a maintainer dispatch. Full-screen Spaces and macOS versions before 27 are untested.

title: ci(spacesd): pin cargo-nextest and retry its download in the Linux test image
body:
## Why
The spacesd Linux test image installed cargo-nextest from `get.nexte.st/latest` through a pipe with no retry (CUA-3995). A transient fetch failure failed the image build and redded the relay e2e (docker) job, and a new nextest release could change the image without a commit.

## What changed
- `linux-test.Dockerfile` pins cargo-nextest with `ARG NEXTEST_VERSION=0.9.151`, the current release.
- The tarball downloads to a file with `curl --retry 5 --retry-all-errors` and connect and total time limits, then extracts. curl cannot retry a transfer it has already started writing into a pipe.
- The build runs `cargo nextest --version`, so a bad download fails at build time.

## Scope
Only the spacesd Docker test image (used by `linux-core-tests.sh`, `relay-e2e.sh` and `build-linux-e2e-bins.sh`). The `.github/actions/nextest` action, which installs nextest on runners through taiki-e/install-action, is unchanged.

## Blast Radius
The relay e2e (docker) shards in ci-cua-spacesd.yml. A wrong pin would fail the image build loudly, not run tests on a different nextest.

## Verification
- `get.nexte.st/0.9.151/linux` and `/linux-arm` redirect to the x86_64 and aarch64 linux-gnu tarballs of cargo-nextest 0.9.151. Each holds one top-level `cargo-nextest` binary, and both match the release's sha256 files.
- The same curl flags against a failing endpoint retry and then exit non-zero.
- The Docker image build did not run in the scoped repository checks. This PR's CI relay e2e (docker) lane builds it.

CUA-3995

title: feat(spaces): Agents tab starts agents from the Home box, one entry per Space, easy to clear
body:
Four changes to the Agents tab, plus `@` in the prompt box.

## What changes for people

- **New agent** no longer opens a popup. It clears the selection and shows the same prompt box as Home at the bottom of the pane. With no agents at all, the pane shows the same box (the "Who should work for you?" empty state and its buttons are gone).
- **`@` picks a computer.** In the box, `@` lists your computers (this one first, online first, offline greyed with their OS icon), filters as you type, arrows move, Enter or a click picks, Esc closes. The pick becomes the where chip, with an X to undo. With no computers it shows one line.
- **Each agent in each Space is its own entry**, with its own thread. The Space tab strip is gone. Home's "Your agents" lists the same entries, so the counts match.
- **Not started** rows have a Remove (shown on hover and on keyboard focus) and the section has Clear all. Only the run's record on this device is removed.

## Why the list kept refreshing

Every poll pass (about every 5 s) set the "Checking N Spaces" counter to all Spaces, even ones already answered, so the line came and went and moved the list. Each pass also built new chat objects, so the list and the open thread's roster were redrawn. And with no agent yet, "checking" blanked the pane on every pass. Now only a Space that has never answered counts as being checked, and a pass that finds nothing new keeps the same list objects.

## Orphaned runs

A run that never started is removed by itself (its record only) when:

- its Space no longer exists: a real (not `pending:`) Space id that is missing from a loaded, non-empty Spaces list, and the run is more than 2 minutes old; or
- it never started in 7 days.

Started runs, runs being connected, agents and their threads are never touched. An empty or unread Spaces list removes nothing.

## Notes

- The prompt box state moved out of Home into `useAskComposer` (`ask-first/use-ask-composer.tsx`), so Home and the Agents tab draw one box; the `@` logic lives in the shared `AskBox`. `ask-box.tsx` keeps its path.
- Core: `agentList.view` takes `perSpace` (default off, so mobile and its fixtures are unchanged).
- Demo flag `?demo=agent-home` turns child Spaces on in the web demo.

## Checks

`bin/ci` passes. New tests: `at-picker`, `agents-not-started` (remove, clear all, orphans, list stays still) and updated `agents-chat`, `agents-populate`; a Rust test for `perSpace`.
