title: Linux: a background delivery refused before any key is sent still waits out the focus guard's 220 ms settle watch
body:
## Summary

Since #7208, `focus_guard::guarded` restores focus on every exit path (`restore_after`, `platform-linux/src/input/focus_guard.rs`). `guarded` passes `settle_watch = true`, so `restore_guarded` polls every 30 ms until `SETTLE_WATCH` (220 ms) has passed, even when nothing changed.

That is right after a delivery that sent keys, since the target may still open a popup. A delivery refused before it sent anything pays the same 220 ms, though: for example, the virtual-keyboard pid route refusing a text that needs more spare keycodes than the keymap has free ("needs 40 spare keycodes").

## Measured

Linux X11 guest, Xorg with 19 free keycodes. `type_text` on the pid route (path `mpx_uinput`) with 40 distinct CJK characters, same refusal text on both builds, 14 calls each:

| build | refusal time |
|---|---|
| 0.45.1 | 25–82 ms |
| 0.47.2 | 239–310 ms |

The ~220 ms difference matches `SETTLE_WATCH`. Successful pid-route calls take the same time on both builds (935–938 ms), because both already paid the watch on success.

## Suggestion

Skip the settle watch when the body failed before sending any input. The restore itself can stay, so a failure after keys still gives focus back as #7208 intends. One shape: let the body report whether it sent anything (for example an error type for "refused before sending") and pass `settle_watch = false` to the restore in that case.

title: Hermes mcp-config snippet duplicates top-level mcp_servers key
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver mcp-config --client hermes` instructs users to paste its output "under mcp_servers" in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, but emits a fresh top-level `mcp_servers:` key. For an existing Hermes config (the normal case), following the instruction creates duplicate YAML mapping keys and Hermes rejects the config with `DuplicateKeyError`.

## Reproduction

Given an existing config:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  telegram:
    command: telegram-mcp
    args: []
```

The generated fragment is:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  cua-driver:
    command: "/path/to/cua-driver"
    args: ["mcp"]
```

Pasting it below the existing `mcp_servers` mapping creates a second top-level `mcp_servers` key. The current Hermes loader rejects duplicate keys.

## Expected behavior

Either print only the indented `cua-driver:` child entry intended for insertion under the existing mapping, or explicitly instruct users to merge/replace the top-level mapping (and avoid suggesting a raw paste). Add a regression test for Hermes output when the config already contains `mcp_servers`.

## Validation

Observed in the current Rust CLI at `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:2370-2375` and confirmed against Hermes safe YAML loading. No Hermes config was modified during validation.

title: docs: generated reference pages no longer carry a release version (CUA-4021)
body:
Linear: CUA-4021

## What users see
Nothing changes on the docs site except that install lines no longer repeat a version number (`pip install cua`, `npm install @trycua/cua`).

## Problem
A generated reference page carried a `Version: x.y.z` stamp. A PR that regenerated a page before a release and merged after it left main stamped with the old version. The release sync only rewrites the previous version it knows, so it never saw those pages, and "Reference / cua-sdk / linux" and "Check Documentation Sync" failed for everyone (#6819, fixed by hand in #7283; bench in #7252).

## Choice: option (a), drop the stamps
- (b) keeps a moving value in generated output and needs the check to guess which drift is harmless.
- (c) adds a bot to the merge queue to repair a value nobody reads.
- (a) removes the cause. The banner stamp was inside an MDX comment, so no reader saw it. The release version is already shown by the releases page, the changelog and the package registries. There is no single place the docs site could read it from at build time that would justify per-page stamps.

Generated output now depends on no release version:
- No `Version:` line in any generated banner (107 pages).
- The `version` field is no longer written to the `cli-specs/*.json` snapshots (`cliSpecJson`).
- Install-line versions, the Lume "Documented against" line, the sandbox runtime-support versions and the Rust `VERSION` constant value are gone. The Rust tag example reads `cua-sdk-v<version>`.
- `sync_driver_release_docs.py`, `sync_lume_release_docs.py`, `sync_bench_release_docs.py`, their tests and `release_reference_docs.py` are deleted, along with the release-please steps and the sandbox regeneration step. `validate_release_versions.py` no longer reads doc stamps. The SDK and Sandbox syncs stay for hand-written pages, which `test_docs_version_facts.py` still pins.

## Test
`scripts/docs-generators/docs-version-stamp.test.ts`:
- Renders the CLI reference and the Lume reference (pages and spec snapshot) with two different tool versions and requires identical output, so a version bump cannot make an untouched page out of sync.
- Fails if any committed generated page has a `Version:` banner or names the current cua, cua-sandbox or `@trycua/cua` release.
- Fails if a header template takes a version placeholder.

Also updated: `rust-crates.test.ts` (semver constants are elided), the generator tests that asserted a stamp, `test_docs_version_facts.py`, the sync and release wiring tests.

## Coordination
#7250 edits `cua-sdk.ts` (`loadApi`/`loadApis`) and the last line of the Rust header. This PR touches different hunks of both; the Rust header change here is the `tag =` line.

Verified locally: `bin/ci --quick`, 120 generator unit tests, release-script pytest suites, `docs:check` for spaces, sandbox, cua-proto, cua-sdk-python, cua-bench. The cua-driver, lume, cua-cli, cua-sdk and cua-rust generators need native builds and run in CI; their pages only lost the stamp lines.

title: fix(cua-spacesd-doctor): retry input.type once when nothing reached the entry

Plain words: the Windows image check that types into the form fails now and then for no driver reason, which fails the whole cua-spacesd image release (run 42866618402, v0.15.0, after about 13 minutes in the windows image job).

title: [Bug]: macOS pixel clicks write a click-group ID into CGEvent field 58 (the timestamp), crashing Chromium/Electron renderers on navigation
body:
### What happens

On macOS, a pixel click from cua-driver into a Chromium or Electron window crashes the page's renderer whenever the click starts a same-document navigation (a hash or `history.pushState` route change). The renderer exits with SIGTRAP (exit code 5) and the page reloads. Clicks that don't navigate are fine, and `element_index` (AX) presses never crash.

### Cause

CGEvent integer field 58 is the event **timestamp** (`kCGEventTimestamp`'s integer slot), not a free field. `mouse.rs` writes a click-group ID into it:

- `click_at_xy_chromium`, line ~726: `set(58, click_group_id)`, where the ID is `SystemTime::now()…subsec_nanos()` (0 to 999,999,999)
- `post_mouse_event_with_mode`, line ~1610: `set(58, cgid)` for every pixel click with a known window id
- background drags, line ~1025: `set(58, gesture_id)`

The app therefore receives the click with a timestamp 0 to 1 s after boot. Chromium on macOS takes `NSEvent.timestamp` unchecked (`components/input/web_input_event_builders_mac.mm`), and Blink's soft-navigation heuristic then fails `CHECK_GT(context->TimeOrigin(), loader->GetTiming().ReferenceMonotonicTime())` (`soft_navigation_heuristics.cc`), because the click looks older than the page load. Chromium's comment above that check mentions events simulated "with an impossibly small start_time".

### Measured

- Posting a click to a test receiver: field 58 unset gives `timestamp ≈ uptime`. Field 58 = 123456789 gives `timestamp = 0.123456789`. Same with `SLEventPostToPid` and the public `CGEventPostToPid`.
- Minimal Electron 45.2.3 page that pushes `#pN` on click, clicks posted as cua-driver posts them (SkyLight, window id, window-local point):
  - field 58 unset: 5/5 clicks fine
  - field 58 = current uptime: 2/2 fine
  - field 58 = 0.123 s: 4/4 renderer crashes (`render-process-gone`, `exitCode: 5`), and the page saw `event.timeStamp = 0`

### Suggested fix

Don't use field 58 for the click group. Leave the timestamp to the OS, or set it to the current time if a shared value is really needed. If pairing needs an ID, use a field that isn't the timestamp.

Possibly related: #5484.

title: fix(ci): every pull request's sign-off is its CI: Quick run
body:
## Why

`ci-gate` required a `local-ci` commit status for every pull request from a branch of this repository. Our Mac runner sets that status after it runs `bin/ci --quick`. `CI: Quick` runs the same command in GitHub Actions on every pull request, and forks already use it as their sign-off. The Mac runner is one queue, so waiting for it was often the gate's last step. On the commits from 7 to 10 Nov where both ran, the Mac status never failed a commit that `CI: Quick` passed.

## What changed

- `ci-gate.yml`: every pull request's sign-off is a successful `CI: Quick` run on the head commit. Release Please pull requests stay exempt. The gate no longer reads commit statuses.
- `ci-gate-recheck.yml` and `ci_gate_recheck.py`: the `status` trigger is gone. `CI: Quick` is already a `workflow_run` the recheck listens to, so a green `CI: Quick` after a failed gate still reruns the gate.
- Docs: `docs/contributing/CI.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the PR template and one comment in `cd-rust-cua-driver.yml`.

## Scope

Covers the gate's sign-off rule only. Unchanged: the `REQUIRE_LOCAL_CI` switch (name and report-only behavior), `bin/ci --signoff` (it still sets the status, which no required check reads now), the required-check set (`ci-gate`, `validate`, `contributor-attribution`), and the weekly report's `local-ci` attribution, which still describes older pull requests.

## Tradeoffs

- **Policy change. Open as a draft for that decision.** The Mac sign-off was added on purpose (#6465, #6569, #6584). This PR keeps its check set and drops where it runs.
- Fidelity. Both sides run `bin/ci --quick`. On Actions it runs with `--no-install`, so a check that needs a package's `node_modules` (web typecheck, design lint) is skipped there. Every one of those checks also runs in its own package workflow (`CI: Cua Spaces web UI and Electron shell`, `CI: cua-driver contract clients`, `CI: openkoalabot-example`, `CI: Lint TypeScript`). The gate waits for that workflow whenever the area map says the package changed.
- #7238 (open) automates the Mac sign-off instead. The two conflict. If this one lands, #7238's sign-off workflow has nothing to gate.

## Blast Radius

Every pull request's `ci-gate`. Forks see no change. Members' pull requests stop waiting for the Mac status. A rollback reverts this PR.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: the `.github/scripts` test suite, actionlint on every workflow, and `bin/ci --quick`, all green. The gate tests now cover a same-repo pull request and a fork needing the `CI: Quick` run, and a test asserts the gate never reads a commit status.
- Measured on six heads of this PR, each a merge of main. The gate finished within about a minute of the last other workflow every time, because `CI: Quick` had already passed. On the same heads, the Mac status arrived later than the last workflow on three, and was never set on two, which under the old rule means a 75-minute wait and a red gate. The historical replay over 7 to 10 Nov is in the report this PR came from.

Refs CUA-3558, CUA-3856

title: fix(ci): survive GitHub release and artifact hiccups in PR lanes
body:
## Why

From 6 to 10 Nov, most pull request reruns of `E2E: cua SDK`, the Swift sample lanes (`CI: infinite-canvas (Swift)`, `CI: openkoalabot-example`) and `CD: Image linux` had one cause: a pinned tool or artifact fetched from a single host with no second source. GitHub timed out unauthenticated release downloads on 8 and 9 Nov (githubstatus incidents), artifacts were listed before they were served, and proxy.golang.org 404ed a new Go toolchain. A rerun passed every time. #7152 already fixed the sccache case. This PR fixes the rest.

## What changed

- `install-actionlint` caches the binary per version and falls back to `gh release download` with the workflow token. Its download failed the `quick` job most often.
- `astral-sh/setup-uv` goes from v6 to v8.3.2 (all 35 uses, one pinned sha). v8 downloads uv from Astral's mirror first and falls back to GitHub Releases.
- New `download-fresh-artifact` action: `actions/download-artifact` with one retry after 30 s. Used for the 13 downloads in `e2e-cua-sdk.yml` and `cd-image-linux.yml`.
- `install-release-tools.sh` uses the newest Go in the runner's tool cache with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, so `go install oras` never downloads a toolchain. This fixes the same failure as #7271 in the image release jobs.

## Scope

Download paths only. No check is skipped or quarantined, and nothing about what the lanes test changes. Left out on purpose:
- Ubuntu mirror mid-sync 404s inside image Dockerfiles. Rare, and a different code path from `apt-install`, which already retries.
- The 9 Nov 18:12 GitHub Actions incident (runs whose jobs never got a runner).
- One shard failure that was a pull request's own change.

## Tradeoffs

- setup-uv v7 moved to the node24 runtime. All runners here are GitHub-hosted, so this changes nothing. v8 only changed custom `manifest-file`, which no workflow uses.
- The artifact retry adds 30 s only when the first download fails.

## Blast Radius

Every workflow that installs uv (35 steps), the `quick` stage of every heavy workflow, `E2E: cua SDK` shards and `CD: Image linux` image jobs. A cache hit or a first-try success follows the same path as before.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: the `.github/scripts` test suite, actionlint on every workflow, and `bin/ci --quick`, all green.
- New `test_tool_downloads_survive_github_releases_outage.py` fails 6 of 6 at the base and passes at the head. It runs the actionlint install with a failing `curl` (falls back to `gh`) and with a cached binary (no network call).
- The Go selection was run against a stub tool cache: it picks the newest Go with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, and an empty cache falls through to the runner's `go`.
- On five heads of this PR, `CD: Image linux` release jobs ran with the cached Go and no toolchain download, uv came from the Astral mirror, and `E2E: cua SDK` passed on all four heads where it ran to completion (the fifth was cancelled by the next push). Two heads failed on unrelated Windows lanes: `CI: Cua Driver Bench` (guard saw a WSL process) and `CI: jev-use` (one browser main process instead of two). Each passed on the other heads with the same setup-uv pin.

Refs CUA-3558

title: fix(sandbox): forward time_to_start to the local runtime's readiness budget
body:
## Problem
Run 42895898819 (cd-images-spacesd-release, cua-spacesd v0.15.0) failed only in \`bench / verify (amd64)\`, step \`verify/amd64/containerdisk\`: \`cua-spacesd did not answer within 0ns\`. The same job passed in the earlier run (containerdisk ready after 1252 s, no KVM on the runner).

## Cause
\`Sandbox.create/ephemeral(time_to_start=...)\` was only used by the contrib path. The local runtime always sent its 900 s default as \`ready_timeout_ms\`, so \`smoke.py\`'s \`time_to_start=1500\` was ignored. The budget covers the server probe and the cua-spacesd wait; when a slow boot passes the probe near 900 s, the spacesd wait gets about nothing.

## Fix
\`_create\` forwards \`time_to_start\` to SDK-backed runtimes as \`ready_timeout\`; \`NativeRuntime.start\` uses it; the legacy QEMU path drops it. Test: \`test_time_to_start_is_the_sdk_readiness_budget\` (explicit budget reaches the SDK, default stays 900 s).

Plain words: slow local VM boots no longer fail with a spurious spacesd timeout when the caller asked for a longer start time.

Refs LOOPS.md findings table. Not run locally (needs the native cua lib); CI runs it.

title: ci(spaces): cap the app library job at 120 min, time-box cache restores
body:
Cua Spaces app library (built once) sat for 70+ min on #7241 and 60+ min on #7302 and could hold the merge queue for up to 180 min (see #7259).

What the logs show (#7241, attempt 1): the slice cache missed and the Swatinem dependency cache missed too, so the job compiled all 585 crates cold at 4 jobs and was still in cua-spaces-ext after 70 min. The restore steps themselves took 0.5 s and 1.7 s. It is a cold build, not a stalled restore. Last 26 successful runs: median 57 min, p95 about 90, max 93.

Changes
- Job ceiling 180 -> 120 min (above the 93 min worst real build).
- Cache restores in the shared action: SEGMENT_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MINS=4 and continue-on-error, so a stalled download falls through to a miss and a build instead of holding the job.

Not fixed here: the repo holds 56 GB in 155 Actions caches, so the main-only dependency cache gets evicted and PRs then build cold. Needs a separate cache-budget change.

For users: nothing changes; CI jobs that really hang now free the merge queue in 2 h, not 3.

title: [Bug]: Forking a checkpoint from a client fails with "does not create vm Spaces", even for a container checkpoint
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### Summary

Forking a Space from a checkpoint from a client (`create_space` with `image: "checkpoint:<name>"`) fails on a direct host with `no machine can take it: <host> does not create vm Spaces`. It fails the same way for a container (runc) checkpoint as for a QEMU one, and the host does run both kinds. The same fork done on the host with `cua sb fork` works.

### Reproduction

1. Ubuntu 24.04 host with Docker and QEMU: `cua host setup --direct <ip>:3211 --share spaces --name spaces-trial`, then `cua spaces add` it on the client with the printed token.
2. From the client's `cua mcp`, create a container Space on it: `create_space {"on": "host:spaces-trial", "kind": "container", "name": "ct-1"}`. (A QEMU Space created with `cua spaces create linux --kind vm --memory-mb 1536 --on host:spaces-trial` behaves the same.)
3. From the client: `cua sb checkpoint ct-1 cpc-1`. This works.
4. From the client's `cua mcp`: `create_space {"on": "host:spaces-trial", "image": "checkpoint:cpc-1", "name": "ct-1-fork"}`.
5. On the host: `cua sb fork cpc-1 ct-1-fork`.

5 of 5 container checkpoints and 5 of 5 QEMU checkpoints failed at step 4 (and again when restoring under the original name after deleting the source). Step 5 worked 10 of 10, and the fork held the checkpoint's state each time.

### Expected behavior

The fork lands on the host that holds the checkpoint, as it does from the host itself. If client-side fork to a direct host isn't supported, an error that says that.

### Actual behavior

MCP error result, verbatim, for both engines:

```
error: no machine can take it: spaces-trial does not create vm Spaces
```

The host does create VM Spaces: the QEMU Spaces in step 2 were created on it from the same client.

I haven't traced it fully, but `cua-spaces/src/fork_batch.rs` (the only place that builds "no machine can take it") sizes every group member as `kind: "vm"` whatever the checkpoint's engine (`Need { kind: "vm".into(), .. }` in the placement loop, line 432 on 09b38ab66), and `cua-cluster/src/elastic/solve.rs` then rejects any host whose listed kinds don't include that string. So a container checkpoint is placed as a VM, and the direct host's listed kinds apparently don't include `vm` either.

### Environment

cua CLI 0.22.0 (`cua-sdk-v0.22.0`) on the client and host, host daemon cua-spacesd 0.15.0 from `cua host setup`. Host: Ubuntu 24.04 KVM guest, 4 vCPU / 4 GiB, Docker 29.1.3, QEMU from `cua runtime setup qemu`. Client: Ubuntu 24.04, over libvirt NAT, direct mode (no relay, no account). The fork_batch code is unchanged on main 09b38ab66.

### Evidence

Per-step JSON rows from the run (MCP results):

```
{"kind": "container", "i": 1, "step": "fork", "route": "mcp", "ok": false, "note": "error: no machine can take it: spaces-trial does not create vm Spaces"}
{"kind": "container", "i": 1, "step": "restore", "route": "mcp", "ok": false, "note": "error: no machine can take it: spaces-trial does not create vm Spaces"}
{"kind": "vm", "i": 1, "step": "fork", "route": "host", "ok": true, "note": "Sandbox 'vm-1-fork' forked from 'cpv-1' (1.41s)."}
```

### Workaround and additional context

ssh to the host and run `cua sb fork` there. That works but isn't reachable for an agent that only has `cua mcp`.

title: [Bug]: `cua runtime setup runsc` says "already available" when Docker has only runc
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### Summary

`cua runtime setup runsc` answers `Ok: already available` on a Linux host whose Docker has only runc, so gVisor never gets installed and the user is told it is. `cua runtime doctor` on the same machine says runsc is missing and that setup would install it.

### Reproduction

1. Ubuntu 24.04 with `docker.io` (runc only, no runsc).
2. `cua runtime setup runsc --dry-run`
3. `cua runtime setup runsc`
4. `cua runtime doctor`

### Expected behavior

Step 2 shows the runsc install plan the doctor describes, and step 3 runs it (or says it can't run unattended, as the `Unsupported { op: "unattended runsc install (run the plan shown by --dry-run)" }` arm in `setup_with` intends).

### Actual behavior

```
$ cua runtime setup runsc --dry-run
runsc      Ok: already available
$ cua runtime setup runsc
runsc      Ok: already available
$ docker info --format '{{range $k,$v := .Runtimes}}{{$k}} {{end}}'
io.containerd.runc.v2 runc
$ cua runtime doctor
...
container  ok           [NativeLinux] unix:///var/run/docker.sock without runsc: containers run with runc unless runsc is installed; missing: runsc; setup would: install runsc on this Linux host, `runsc install` into /etc/docker/daemon.json and restart dockerd (sudo -n)
```

In `cua-daemon-core/src/local.rs` `setup_with`, the component names `container | runsc | gvisor` all map to `BackendKind::Container` (line 3472 on 09b38ab66), and the step returns `already available` as soon as that backend is ready (lines 3492-3497), which it is whenever Docker is. So runsc never reaches the dry-run plan or the install arm.

### Environment

cua CLI 0.22.0 (`cua-cli-0.22.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` from `cua-sdk-v0.22.0`, checksum verified), in a throwaway privileged `ubuntu:24.04` container running its own `dockerd` (Docker 29.x, runc only), telemetry off. Same code on main 09b38ab66.

### Evidence

Output above, from the 0.22.0 release binary.

### Workaround and additional context

Install runsc and register it with Docker by hand.

title: [Bug]: MCP create_space has no memory_mb or cpus, though its host_capacity error says to create it smaller
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### Summary

The MCP `create_space` tool has no `cpus` or `memory_mb`, so an agent can't create a VM Space smaller than the default, which on a small host means it can't create one at all. Its own `host_capacity` error tells the agent to "create it smaller (cpus, memory_mb)", which it has no way to do.

### Reproduction

1. `cua mcp`, then `tools/list`.
2. Look at `create_space`'s `inputSchema.properties`.

### Expected behavior

`create_space` takes `cpus` and `memory_mb` like `cua spaces create --memory-mb`, `resize_space` and `sandbox_pool_create` already do, so the advice in `host_capacity` can be followed from MCP.

### Actual behavior

On 0.22.0 the schema properties are:

```
["allow","command","count","deny","durable","env","image","instance_type","kind","labels","name","network","on","parent","region","reuse","runtime","services","spacesd","timeout","wait"]
```

`CreateSpace` in `cua-spaces-contract/src/inputs.rs` (and the flattened `SpaceWorkload`) has no size fields on main 09b38ab66 either, while the `host_capacity` entry in `cua-spaces-contract/src/lib.rs` says `fix: "Delete a Space (delete_space), create it smaller (cpus, memory_mb), or create it with on=\"auto\" so another machine takes it."`

Where it bites: on a 4 GiB Ubuntu host, a 2 GiB VM is refused from the CLI with a clear message:

```
host capacity: this host has 2.9 GiB of memory available and keeps 1.0 GiB free for everything else, so 'vm-1', expected to need 2.0 GiB, does not fit; delete a Space, close programs, or create it on another machine (on="auto") ...
```

`cua spaces create linux --kind vm --memory-mb 1536` then worked, but there is no MCP equivalent.

### Environment

cua CLI 0.22.0 (`cua-sdk-v0.22.0`, macOS arm64 binary for the `tools/list` above; linux-x64 client against a cua-spacesd 0.15.0 direct host for the capacity refusal). Host: Ubuntu 24.04 KVM guest, 4 vCPU / 4 GiB.

### Evidence

`tools/list` output above (179 tools; checked again just now against the 0.22.0 release binary).

### Workaround and additional context

Create through the CLI with `--memory-mb`, or create on `auto`.

title: [Docs]: Headless Ubuntu 24.04 Spaces host needs linger, passt and a pasta userns allowance that setup and doctor never mention
body:
### Primary area

Documentation

### Summary

Setting up a headless Ubuntu 24.04 server as a Spaces host over ssh (the "A Linux box or VPS" path in `spaces/guides/bring-your-own-compute.mdx`) runs into a few prerequisites that neither the docs, `cua host setup`, `cua runtime setup` nor `cua runtime doctor` mention. Each one only shows up as an error later, or not at all. Filing them together since they're all the same page and the same doctor.

### Reproduction

Fresh Ubuntu 24.04 server, Docker installed, only the `cua` CLI binaries, reached over ssh:

1. `cua host setup --direct <ip>:3211 --share spaces` (or `--remote`), log out.
2. `cua runtime setup qemu`, `cua runtime doctor`, then create a QEMU Space on it.

### Expected behavior

The Linux host section lists what the host needs, and doctor flags the ones it can check.

### Actual behavior

1. **The host stops when you log out.** Setup installs `cua-spacesd-host.service` as a systemd user unit and doesn't enable linger (nothing in the repo calls `loginctl enable-linger` for it). With `Linger=no`, the user manager and the service stop when the last ssh session ends. The VPS guide says "Setup installs it as a background service, so it comes back after a restart", and `add-a-computer.mdx` says "With systemd, nothing more." The cua-driver operate guide already tells headless users to run `loginctl enable-linger $USER`; the Spaces host needs the same, ideally from setup itself or at least a warning.
2. **QEMU Spaces need passt, which `runtime setup qemu` doesn't install and doctor doesn't check for QEMU.** The apt list in `cua-vmm/src/auto.rs` `QemuPackageManager::packages` has no `passt`. On 0.22.0 doctor only names pasta under firecracker: `qemu installable QEMU not found; missing: qemu-system-x86_64 / qemu-img; ...` vs `firecracker notapplicable microVM Spaces need passt for their network...`. `egress-exit.mdx` does say VMs on Linux need pasta.
3. **Ubuntu 24.04's default AppArmor policy blocks pasta's user namespace.** 24.04 ships `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1`. The only place this appears is the create-time error (`PASTA_USERNS_HINT` in `cua-vmm/src/qemu/mod.rs`). Ubuntu 24.04 is the one Linux `install.mdx` lists as supported, so doctor could check the sysctl or a pasta profile up front.
4. **X libraries on a server without a desktop.** `host setup` stops when `libXi.so.6` and friends are missing; `missing_libraries_message` in `cua-host/src/host.rs` names the apt line, which is fine, but the VPS guide could list `libxi6 libxtst6 libx11-6 libxcb1` next to "install Docker first".
5. **`--direct` isn't in `cua host setup --help`** (`hide = true` in `cua-cli/src/host.rs`), though the help's first line says the host can serve "on a direct ip:port". It's under `cua help advanced`, which the setup help doesn't point to.

### Environment

cua CLI 0.22.0 (`cua-sdk-v0.22.0`), cua-spacesd 0.15.0, Ubuntu 24.04. Code references are from main 09b38ab66.

### Evidence

Doctor lines in item 2 and the help text in item 5 are from the 0.22.0 release binaries (linux-x64 in a throwaway Ubuntu 24.04 container, darwin-arm64). The sysctl value in item 3 is from a stock Ubuntu 24.04.3 server. Items 1 and 4 are from the code and docs named above.

### Workaround and additional context

`loginctl enable-linger $USER`; `apt install passt libxi6 libxtst6 libx11-6 libxcb1`; an AppArmor profile allowing `userns` for `/usr/bin/pasta` (or the sysctl set to 0); `cua help advanced` for `--direct`. With those, container and QEMU Spaces worked end to end.

title: fix(runtime): setup runsc no longer says already available on a runc-only Docker
body:
Fixes #7308

## Root cause
`setup_with` mapped `container | runsc | gvisor` to the container backend and returned `already available` as soon as that backend was ready, which is true whenever Docker answers. runsc is a separate component of it, so on a runc-only engine `cua runtime setup runsc` (and `--dry-run`) never reached the plan or the install, while `cua runtime doctor` said runsc was missing.

## Fix
- `DoctorReport::runsc()` (cua-vmm) is the single answer for gVisor: ready (registered, or provided by the built-in Linux runtime), installable (the doctor's plan), or unavailable (why). Setup uses it, so doctor and setup cannot disagree.
- `setup runsc` / `gvisor` shows the plan under `--dry-run` and runs it for real through the container runtime (`require_gvisor`, no fallback to runc). Without passwordless sudo it reports the error. An engine cua cannot put gVisor into (Docker Desktop, OrbStack) or no engine gives the doctor's reason.
- `setup container` stays `already available` while Docker is ready.

## Same class, checked
| Component | Result |
|---|---|
| runsc / gvisor | found, fixed |
| firecracker / microvm / vz / lume / containerization with no backend on this computer (e.g. firecracker on a Mac) | found, fixed: was `would: ` with an empty plan, or ran an installer; now an error saying it is not available |
| any backend not ready and not provisionable | found, fixed: dry run printed an empty plan and the real run tried an installer anyway; now the doctor's reason in both |
| managed on a host that cannot run it | found, fixed: said Ok "set up when the first Linux Space is created"; now an error |
| firecracker / vz ready with downloads pending (kernel, gvproxy) | found, fixed: said `already available` while the doctor lists downloads; setup now lists and does them |
| qemu installed but held back by KVM access | found, fixed: was reinstalled; now already installed, kvm step follows |
| qemu, lume, managed, containerization with a ready backend | fine |
| CLI (`cua runtime setup`), SDK `local().setup`, daemon RPC | fine: pass-through to `local::setup`; CLI downgrades only non-requested optional errors |
| CLI `cua doctor` `host.gvisor` check | fine: reads the same `container.gvisor` flag |
| app host-setup surfaces | fine: they set up the host service, not runtimes |
| bare `cua runtime setup` skips runsc | left on purpose (restarts dockerd, uses sudo); logged for a decision |
| `cua runtime setup kvm` is an unknown component | not fixed, logged |

## Tests
New unit tests of `setup_with` with fakes: docker with runc only (dry run, real run, sudo failure, `runsc` and `gvisor`), runsc registered, `setup container`, engine that cannot take runsc, no engine, doctor/setup agreement, missing backends, unprovisionable backends, pending microVM downloads, installed qemu.

Not run: the real Linux/Docker `runsc install` (needs a Linux host with dockerd and sudo); it was not run on this Mac. `bin/ci` passed unit tests; its per-crate `clippy -p cua-vmm` lane fails on errors in code this PR does not touch (storage.rs feature gating, an unused `mut`); I did not run it on main, so clippy was run as CI does (`-p cua-sdk -p cua-daemon-core -p cua-daemon -p cua-cli -p cua-vmm --all-targets -D warnings`) and is clean. Windows cross-clippy skipped (audiopus_sys cannot cross-build here).

title: perf(cua-driver): strip symbols and fat LTO for release builds
body:
PyPI rejected the cua-driver 0.47.4 upload with "400 Project size too large" (74 versions, 10.71 GB, about 188 MB per version; run 42927325420).

The workspace had no `[profile.release]`, so the shipped CLI and the UniFFI library (both bundled in every wheel) kept their full symbol tables. This adds `strip = "symbols"`, `lto = "fat"`, `codegen-units = 1`. Same code and behaviour; exported dynamic symbols are unchanged (702 before and after on macOS), `list-tools` and `--version` run.

Measured (macOS arm64, release build, same lockfile):
| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| cua-driver | 40.7 MB | 24.8 MB |
| libcua_driver_sdk.dylib | 31.0 MB | 20.1 MB |
Compressed (what goes in the wheel): about 25.2 MB -> 19.6 MB per slice, roughly -22% on the macOS wheel. Linux and Windows wheels will be measured by the next release (expect similar or smaller gains).

Cost: release builds link about 2x slower (2 min -> 4 min locally for these two crates). Does not shrink the versions already on PyPI; pruning and the limit increase are separate.

For users: smaller downloads and installs of `pip install cua-driver`, and a PyPI project that fills up more slowly.

title: fix(spaces): fork a checkpoint as the kind its engine makes on a direct host
body:
Fixes #7307

## Root cause
Two things together:
1. `fork_batch` placed every fork as `Need { kind: "vm" }`, whatever engine the checkpoint came from. A container checkpoint was asked of the host as a VM.
2. A Linux host's status listed `container` but not `vm`. That list was the job executor's (jobs never run `vm` on Linux, because job members mount host directories QEMU cannot), but the same list is what placement reads for Spaces and forks. So a QEMU checkpoint on a Linux direct host was refused too: `does not create vm Spaces`. (QEMU Spaces created directly with `--on host:` skip this placement, which is why those worked.)

## Changes
- Fork batches take each checkpoint's kind from its engine (the local record, or the holder's listing for a checkpoint held elsewhere), via `kind_of_engine` (now also resolves `qemu-docker`, `containerization`, ...). `create_space image=checkpoint:` passes it directly.
- `cua-cluster` batch placement: a host that holds the checkpoint, or restores its ABI, forks the kind its engine makes, listed or not. A host with neither still has to offer the kind, and the refusal names the real kind.
- A host's status now reports the kinds it creates as Spaces (`JobExecutor::space_offers`); job admission still refuses `vm` on Linux up front.
- `detect_offers` looks for QEMU/Firecracker where the runtime does (`cua_vmm::host::which`, which includes cua's own `bin` where `cua runtime setup qemu` installs it), and a QEMU set up after the daemon started is offered without a restart.
- Host side: a fork via `CreateHostSpace.fork_source` is admitted (CPU/memory/VM accounting) as its checkpoint's kind, not as `auto` (was counted as a container); a caller-named kind that contradicts the engine is refused with a plain message.

## Related checks
Bugs found and fixed: the above (hardcoded `vm` in the fork placement and in the elastic-growth fit check; status kinds missing `vm` also broke `on="auto"` creates of `kind=vm` onto Linux hosts and the relay/cluster coordinator's view; fork admission accounting; QEMU detection by `PATH` only).
Checked and fine: `create_space` from a checkpoint (kind/engine mismatch already refused client-side), restore under the original name (same path), `cua sb fork` / `ForkSandboxBatch` (fills kinds in `fork_batch`), local `fork_local`, host-local fork, the SDK/MCP/CLI routes (all go through `fork_batch` or `create_on_host_from`), `kind_of_runtime`, `placement_of_backend`, `build` (kind chosen from options), elastic growth (only QEMU-ABI checkpoints grow the pool, so `vm` was right there), client's view of host capacity (`HostCapacity` copies the status kinds verbatim).
Not fixed (logged): the local machine's candidate claims container+vm whatever is installed; `detect_offers` is read once at start for Docker; a `kind: vm` job on Linux is now placed and refused at admission instead of "no host can take it".

## Tests
- Reproduced first: `cua-cluster batch::a_holder_forks_its_checkpoints_kind_whatever_it_lists` fails without the fix with `linux does not create vm Spaces`.
- New: `fork_batch::forks_are_placed_as_their_checkpoints_kind` (container checkpoint and QEMU checkpoint on a host that does not list `vm`; refusal names the real kind), `engine_kind_tests`, `fork_kind_tests`, `cua-cluster/tests/node.rs::status_lists_the_kinds_it_creates_as_spaces_and_jobs_refuse_the_rest`.
- `bin/ci`: rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, unit tests (cua-cluster, cua-spaces), contract manifest, generated reference all pass; the Windows cross-clippy lane only warned (could not cross-build `audiopus_sys` here).
- Not run: this is a Mac. Real Docker/QEMU on a Linux direct host (the reporter's setup) were not exercised; the behavior is covered by unit tests with fake hosts.

title: fix(cua-driver): hover background Hyprland apps through the agent seat
body:
## What changes for users

On Hyprland (for example Omarchy), an agent can now hover a background app. `move_cursor` with a window target moves the agent cursor over that point **and** shows the app the pointer there through Cua's own input seat, so hover styles, hover-only buttons and tooltips appear. The user's pointer, keyboard focus and windows do not change.

Before, Linux ignored the window target: it drew the agent cursor at the window-local point as if it were a screen point, sent the app nothing, and replied with a plain "moved". Agents took that as a hover and clicked without the state the task needed.

## Change

**Hyprland plugin (`cua-input-v3`)**
- New background-only operation `HOVER <sequence> <target> <revision> <x> <y>`, capability `32`: pointer enter and motion on the lane's agent seat, no button. The lane keeps passive pointer focus there (the existing passive-focus rules), so the hover stays until the target changes or another lane action moves it.
- `HELLO` advertises `"hover":true`. Foreground selection refuses capability 32, just as background selection refuses `ACTIVATE` (16). A foreground hover would move the user's pointer.
- `InputGrant` admits 32 as a single operation; the grant test covers it and the new invalid masks.
- Protocol notes updated.

**Driver**
- `hyprland_input::Action::Hover`, sent only when the plugin advertised `hover`. An older plugin gets `hover_unsupported` and nothing is sent, not even `TARGET`.
- `move_cursor` (Linux) with `target: {kind: "window", pid, window_id}`:
  - x/y are window screenshot pixels, as for `click`;
  - the agent cursor is pinned above that window and glides to the matching screen point;
  - on Hyprland with background input it hovers through the agent seat;
  - the result says `hover_delivered: true` (with `hover_route`), `false` (with `reason`, and what to use instead: element tokens, the browser tools, or a desktop-scope move only when nobody is using the screen), or `"unknown"` when the dispatch failed after it may have sent input.
- Without a target, `move_cursor` is unchanged (screen coordinates, overlay only).

## Testing

- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` (Linux): new tests for the HOVER packet and bounds, the `hover` advertisement in `HELLO`, the refusal that sends nothing without it, hover never using the foreground route, and the `move_cursor` result for each outcome.
- Plugin `ctest` (mock Hyprland): `input_grant_test` covers capability 32.
- Plugin built against Hyprland 0.56.2 and loaded in an Omarchy edge VM, with a source build of this branch: a window-target `move_cursor` over a background GTK 3 app's hover zone reached the app as pointer enter and motion from the agent seat, and the hover-only controls appeared and stayed until the click. The user's window stayed the active window and the real pointer did not move. With `main`'s `move_cursor`, the same app saw no hover.

Refs CUA-4034 (Linear). Related: #6705, #6706.

title: fix(hyprland-plugin): upstream Omarchy's IME popup guard and text-chord typing check
body:
## What changes for users

Nothing new for Omarchy users today. Omarchy's `cua-hyprland-plugin` package already applies these two fixes as a downstream patch. Moving them into the plugin source lets the package drop that patch at its next rebase, and every other Hyprland install gets them too:

- Hyprland no longer crashes into safe mode when an input method such as fcitx5 exits while Cua's agent seats are present.
- Keyboard layouts with harmless remaps (Caps/Ctrl swap, Compose on Right Alt, Alt/Super swap, Omarchy's non-Latin options) can type in the foreground. Before, they were refused.

## Change

- **IME popup guard** (`src/ime_popup_guard.{hpp,cpp}`). With the agent seats present, fcitx5 registers an input method per `wl_seat`. When it exits, Hyprland 0.56 can keep an input-method popup mapped after its `wl_surface` is gone, then dereference it in `CInputPopup::updateBox` or `CInputPopup::shouldBeRendered`. The guard hooks both, so a popup without a surface is neither placed nor drawn. It is installed and removed with the plugin in every input build, like the user seat guard (#6705). `cua:status` reports `ime_popup_guard`, the field Omarchy's install check already reads. If either exact symbol is missing, the plugin loads without the guard and reports `false`.
- **Typing check** (`typing_keymap_equivalent`). A physical keymap now qualifies for foreground typing when every chord Driver types text with (digits, letters, punctuation, Tab, Return, Space, with and without Shift) passes `foreground_chord_failure` with Num Lock off and on. Before, every key on the keyboard had to match. Remaps of keys text never uses qualify, and the per-chord check still refuses any requested chord they change. A different layout, a dead key, or a remap of Shift or of a text key still refuses.
- The new sources are on the release bundle allowlist. The README and the Omarchy validation note say the downstream patch can be dropped.

## Testing

- `keymap_equivalence_test`: the new admitted and refused layouts and options, plus hand-written key overrides (`Shift` level of a digit, `Return` as Compose, `Tab` as a dead key, a key text never uses).
- `plugin_input_lifetime_test`: the guard is installed with the plugin, reported in status, and removed on unload.
- Full plugin `ctest` against mock Hyprland, plus a module build against Hyprland 0.56.2 headers loaded in an Omarchy edge VM (`cua:status` reports `ime_popup_guard: true`).

This is the same code Omarchy has shipped as `downstream.patch` since 0.33.2-4, adapted to the current source.

Refs CUA-4034 (Linear).

title: ci: keep the Actions cache budget for main's Rust caches
body:
## What

The Actions cache is at 54 GB against a 50 GB limit, so GitHub evicts main's Rust caches and Spaces PRs compile from scratch (60-90 min instead of ~35). PRs already restore without saving; this adds what keeps main's caches from being squeezed out.

- `ci-cache-hygiene.yml` + `.github/scripts/cache_hygiene.py`: on PR close, delete that PR's caches; daily, delete caches of closed PRs, tags and branches older than 2 days, and superseded days of main's sccache and nix families (newest entry per family stays; main's only entry is never deleted). Manual run is a dry run by default. Runs the script from main, never PR code.
- `ci-cache-warm.yml`: daily, dispatches the seeding Rust workflows when none has run green on main for 36 hours, so a quiet weekend does not let the 7-day idle eviction drop them.
- Unit tests for the plan, README note.

Measured on the live repo (dry run): 7 superseded main entries (5.4 GB) plus 3.7 GB of tag-scoped release caches that age out after 2 days. After that main holds about 40 GB of one-entry-per-family caches, still close to the limit; raising the repo cache limit is a separate admin setting (pay-as-you-go, cents per GB).

For users: PR CI starts warm more often, so Spaces PRs build in about 35 minutes instead of 60-90.

Follows the stopgap in #7306.

title: fix(cua-spacesd-doctor): wait for the form's entry focus before typing (replaces the #7290 retry)
body:
Plain words: the Windows image check that types into the form stopped failing the whole cua-spacesd image release at random, because it now waits until the form is really ready for typing instead of retrying after a failure.

## Root cause

The `input.type` doctor check typed as soon as `ActivateWindow` and a click on the Name entry had returned. On the Windows image the form is a PowerShell/WinForms process whose UI thread applies the focus change (and runs slow script-block handlers) after those calls return, so the first keystrokes reach a control that does not hold keyboard focus yet. The driver's report is clean in every case (`Typed 6 character(s)`) because `SendInput` and the drain sentinel both succeed; the loss happens inside the form.

Evidence from `windows / image` doctor logs of `cd-images-spacesd-release`:

| run | result of `input.type` |
| --- | --- |
| 42866618402 (v0.15.0) | fail: entry never changed, the form saw 1 key press (the drain sentinel) |
| 42325506448 | fail: entry read `ctor`, the first two characters (`do`) were lost; no retry would have helped |
| 42313668217, 42337644226, 42394653248, 42415532963, 42614588397, 42684840041, 42842043415, 42895898819 | pass |

The second failure shows the retry-once stopgap from #7290 was incomplete: it only retried when no `entry_changed` arrived, so a partly lost string still failed.

## Fix

- The form fixtures (Windows `form.ps1`, Linux `form.py`) log `widget_focus` records when the Name entry gains or loses keyboard focus and say `focus_events: true` in their `ready` record. The Windows form also makes the entry its active control when shown.
- The doctor waits for that ready signal: the latest `widget_focus` for Name is `focused: true`, then a Backspace probe (harmless on the empty entry) must come back as a key press with the entry focused. That proves focus is in place and the form's thread is draining input. Only then does it type.
- The retry from #7290 is removed. A form without `focus_events` (an older image) falls back to the window-focus check the doctor already did.
- A failure to become ready says which focus records the form logged.

## Tests

Unit tests for the focus-record parsing and the probe matcher (`entry_ready_tests`). `cargo test -p cua-spacesd-doctor --lib` (49 pass) and `clippy -D warnings` are clean on a Mac. The end-to-end proof is the next `windows / image` job; it needs the image workflow to run on this branch.

title: ci: raise the open-files limit before every script that runs cargo test
body:
Plain words: cua-spaces tests no longer fail with "Too many open files" on a Mac that still has the default shell limit of 256.

## Root cause

macOS shells start with a soft open-files limit of 256. The cua-spaces test binaries (`host_spaces`, `scale`, `relay_publish`, the cua-compat chaos suite) open more than that, so on such a Mac they fail for no code reason. `bin/ci` already raised the limit for its own children, but the many scripts that run `cargo test` directly (E2E runners, image gates, the macOS and Linux driver E2E scripts) did not.

## Fix

- Every tracked shell script that runs `cargo test` or `cargo nextest` (27 of them) carries one canonical line after its `set -e...` that raises the soft limit to 10240, never lowers a higher limit, falls back to the hard limit, and cannot abort a `set -e` script. Checked on a Mac whose shell limit is 256: it reads 10240 afterwards.
- The cua-sdk E2E runner (`tests/e2e/cua-sdk/run.py`) raises the limit itself before it starts `cargo test`.
- `bin/ci` already did (`raise_open_file_limit`); a test now pins it.

## Guard

`scripts/ci/tests/test_nofile_limit.py` (runs in `bin/ci` and in CI Test Scripts, which now also triggers on any `*.sh` change):
- fails when a tracked shell script runs `cargo test` / `cargo nextest` without the line, or runs it before the line;
- checks the line itself: 256 becomes 10240, a higher limit is kept, and it survives `set -eu`;
- checks that `bin/ci` and the cua-sdk runner raise 256.

A new script that runs cargo test without the line now fails `bin/ci` and CI with the exact line to paste.

title: [Bug]: Ending a session on Linux X11 crashes every running Qt 6 app (master pointer removal, QTBUG-146876)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, when a cua-driver session that used background input ends, the driver removes its XInput2 master pointer, and every running Qt 6.5+ application segfaults. This is a Qt bug ([QTBUG-146876](https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-146876), open, still in Qt 6.12 per [QTBUG-151420](https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-151420)), but any `XIRemoveMaster` triggers it, so the driver's session teardown kills the user's Qt apps.

### Reproduction

1. X11 desktop with `/dev/uinput` writable by the user, so background input takes the MPX route. Start two PySide6 6.10.1 windows and one PySide6-Essentials 6.8.3 window (any plain `QWidget` with a `QLineEdit` does it), plus a GTK window to act on.
2. One `cua-driver mcp` connection, session `e0`: `get_window_state` on the GTK window, `click` at a blank point of it (`path=mpx_pointer`), `type_text` a few characters (`path=mpx_uinput`). The session adds its `CUA v1.… pointer` master pair.
3. `end_session {"session": "e0"}` → `✅ Session 'e0' ended.`
4. All three Qt processes are gone within a second.

10 of 10 trials on each build. The same happens when the client just exits without `end_session` (stdin closed), when a killed driver's pair is cleaned up by the next `cua-driver serve` at startup, and when a session is left connected but idle.

### Expected behavior

Ending a session leaves the user's other applications running.

### Actual behavior

Qt windows killed per case (each trial: two Qt 6.10.1 windows and one Qt 6.8.3 window):

| Case | 0.46.1 release binary | 0.47.4 (built from 09b38ab66, the release commit) | masters removed |
|---|---|---|---|
| act, then `end_session` | 30 / 30 (10 trials) | 30 / 30 | 1 per trial |
| act, then the client exits (stdin closed) | 30 / 30 | 30 / 30 | 1 per trial |
| `cua-driver mcp` SIGKILLed after acting, then `cua-driver serve` starts and acts | 9 / 9 (3 trials) | 9 / 9 | 2 per trial (startup reaper) |
| act once, stay connected and idle | 3 / 3 (1 trial), dead by the 330 s poll | 3 / 3, same | 1 |
| control: one session acts every trial, never ended | 0 / 30 | 0 / 30 | 0 |
| control: `cua-driver mcp` SIGKILLed, a new `mcp` acts (no reaper) | 0 / 9 | 0 / 9 | 0 |
| control, no Cua: `xinput create-master x` then `xinput remove-master "x pointer"` | 9 / 9 (3 trials) | (same guest, not repeated) | 1 per trial |

Every death lines up with a `master_removed` XI2 hierarchy event. The kernel log shows `general protection fault ... in libQt6XcbQpa.so.6` at offsets `+0x279e4` or `+0x2755c` (or a jump to 0 in the interpreter right after), the same offsets as the plain `xinput remove-master` control.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.46.1 (`cua-driver-rs-0.46.1-linux-x86_64-binary.tar.gz`) and cua-driver 0.47.4 built with their release recipe (`cargo build --locked -p cua-driver --release --features cua-driver/portal-input`) from 09b38ab66 (the `cua-driver-rs-v0.47.4` release commit, current main). Ubuntu 24.04.5 KVM guest, Xorg 21.1.12 (modesetting), mutter 46.2 X11 session, `/dev/uinput` writable, PySide6 6.10.1 and PySide6-Essentials 6.8.3 (bundled Qt), GTK 3.24.41. Telemetry disabled.

### Evidence

Per-trial rows (Qt pids, kernel trap lines, every XI2 hierarchy event in the trial, Cua's replies) are from a scripted MCP client, no model involved. Happy to attach the scripts if useful; the core is just steps 1-3 above.

### Workaround and additional context

Qt 6.5's `QXcbConnection::xi2SetupDevices()` deletes the `QInputDevice`s for devices X no longer lists, but slave devices have their master as QObject parent, so deleting the master deletes the slaves and the loop deletes them again (introduced by qtbase 2a9d93efc6, picked to 6.5.0). Only master removal triggers it: adding a master, reattaching or floating a slave killed 0 of 30 Qt 6.10 and 6.12 windows in our runs, removing one killed 20 of 30. Qt 6.4 and Qt 5.15 are not affected.

In cua-driver the removals are `remove_master_pair` / `remove_master_pointer` in `platform-linux/src/input/mod.rs`, reached from `end_session` (`forget_master_pointer`), idle teardown (in our runs the pair went about five minutes after the last action with the connection still open; I didn't trace which timer, `MPX_IDLE_TTL` is 30 minutes), the popup waiter, the startup `reap_orphaned_master_pointers`, and the no-hotplug failure path in `ensure_master_pointer_for_session`.

#2304 looks like this same crash (`libQt6XcbQpa.so.6.11.1` in the kernel line; its title says the pointer was ephemeral then, so a removal followed every action). #2888 fixed it for KDE Plasma X11 by turning the route off there, but Qt 6.5+ apps on any other X11 desktop still die whenever a pair is removed: it's the client's own device handling, not the window manager (it also happens on a bare Xvfb with no WM).

We hit the same thing in our own tool and fixed it by never removing a master while the X server lives: a session takes a free pair (marked by a property on the master device naming its holder, claimed under `XGrabServer`), adds one only when none is free, and at the end unplugs its uinput slaves, parks the cursor and marks the pair free; pairs whose holder process is dead are taken over instead of removed; and the uinput slave has to show up as an X device before any master is added, so a server without hotplug never gets one. The cost is that pairs stay in `xinput list` until the server exits, as many as the most sessions that used background input at once. In the same kind of run that went from 20/20 Qt windows killed to 0/20. Happy to put up a PR in that shape if you want it.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11: type_text after a refused click on a covered Chromium window reports "Typed 6 characters" but the field stays empty
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, after `click` on a covered Chromium window is refused as `target_occluded`, `type_text` into that window still answers "Typed 6 character(s)… not verified", and the field stays empty, 10 of 10. The keys do reach the page, but no field there has focus because the click that would have focused it never happened, so the text goes nowhere. The reply's hint ("The text was delivered but not read back. Read the field before typing again, or it may be duplicated") points the caller the wrong way.

### Reproduction

1. X11 desktop with `/dev/uinput` writable (MPX route). A Chromium `--app` page with one `<input>` that does not have focus (the page's `document.activeElement` is `BODY`), fully covered by another app's focused window.
2. `get_window_state` on the Chromium window, then `click` at the input's screen point: refused with `target_occluded`, as expected.
3. `type_text {"pid": …, "window_id": …, "text": "M0wzqk"}` in the same session.
4. Read the input's value from the page itself.

### Expected behavior

The caller learns the text did not go into a field: something like a refusal or a not-applied result saying the window has no focused editable element (Chromium exposes its focused element over AT-SPI), or at least a result that does not say "delivered". When the click before it was refused, nothing in that window was focused by the caller.

### Actual behavior

Click, every trial:

```
"code": "target_occluded", "effect": "refused", "covering_title": "FX-USER", "path": "mpx_pointer"
```

type_text, every trial:

```json
{
  "delivery": {"mode": "background"},
  "effect": "unverifiable",
  "hint": "The text was delivered but not read back. Read the field before typing again, or it may be duplicated.",
  "route": "global_input",
  "summary": "Typed 6 character(s) as real key events through a virtual master keyboard (path=mpx_uinput, focus untouched) (delivery_mode=background); not verified — confirm with a screenshot."
}
```

The page logged a `focus` and all six key events, `isTrusted: true`, with `document.activeElement` still `BODY`; the input read back empty in 10 of 10 on each build. Nothing reached the covering window either (0 of 10), so the user was not disturbed.

Contrast, same cell: when the input already had focus before the window was covered, the same calls put the text in 10 of 10 (0.46.1). The GTK and Qt targets landed 3 of 3 each on both builds for the same reason (their entry already had keyboard focus). So `type_text` is right only when the field happened to be focused already, and the reply is identical either way.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.46.1 (release binary) and 0.47.4 built from 09b38ab66 (the `cua-driver-rs-v0.47.4` release commit). Ubuntu 24.04.5 KVM guest, Xorg 21.1.12, mutter 46.2 X11 session, Chrome for Testing 154 as `--app`, covering window GTK 3.24.41. One `cua-driver mcp` stdio connection, scripted client, telemetry off.

### Evidence

Verbatim replies above. Field value and key events come from the page's own log and HTTP state endpoint, not through the driver. Covering window text was checked the same way.

### Workaround and additional context

Callers can read the field back with `get_window_state` and retype, which the hint discourages. Related in spirit: #4997 (macOS Chromium, unverifiable result with no target-aware hint).

title: [Bug]: Linux type_text puts letters into a Qt QIntValidator field and reports confirmed
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux, `type_text` into a Qt `QLineEdit` that has a `QIntValidator` puts letters in the field and reports `effect: "confirmed"`. A user typing the same keys gets nothing. The driver's AT-SPI EditableText write turns into `QLineEdit::setText` on Qt's side, which skips the validator and input mask (and, per Qt's docs, doesn't emit `textEdited`), so the app ends up holding a value its own UI would never allow.

### Reproduction

1. PySide6 window with a few `QLineEdit`s; one has `setValidator(QIntValidator(0, 999999))` and `setAccessibleName("int-field")`. Keyboard focus on another field.
2. `get_window_state` on the window, then `type_text {"pid": …, "window_id": …, "element_token": "<token of int-field>", "text": "AB"}`.
3. Read the field's `text()` from the app itself.
4. Control: focus the window, Tab to int-field, `xdotool type AB`.

### Expected behavior

The field rejects the letters the way it does for the keyboard, and the reply says the text didn't go in.

### Actual behavior

```json
{
  "delivery": {"mode": "background"},
  "effect": "confirmed",
  "evidence": [{"kind": "value_readback"}, {"detail": "element [2] reads back the typed text", "kind": "value_readback"}],
  "route": "accessibility",
  "summary": "Typed 2 character(s) into element [2] (via targeted AT-SPI); it reads back 'AB'."
}
```

The field holds `AB`: 3 of 3 on 0.46.1, 6 of 6 on 0.47.4. The xdotool control leaves the field empty every time. `12` goes in both ways.

On Qt's side, `QAccessibleLineEdit::insertText` (qtbase `src/widgets/accessible/simplewidgets.cpp`) builds the new string and calls `lineEdit()->setText(...)`, and `setText` is documented as not validating. Spin boxes and date edits forward the same call to their line edit. In cua-driver the route is `write_into_editable_acc` / `write_through_editable_proxies` in `platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs` (InsertText, falling back to SetTextContents), tried before any key events.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.46.1 (release binary) and 0.47.4 built from 09b38ab66 (the `cua-driver-rs-v0.47.4` release commit). Ubuntu 24.04.5 KVM guest, Xorg 21.1.12, mutter 46.2 X11 session, PySide6 6.10.1, at-spi2-core 2.52. Scripted MCP client, telemetry off.

### Evidence

Reply above, verbatim. Field state read from the app over its own HTTP endpoint, not through the driver.

### Workaround and additional context

None from the caller's side: the reply says confirmed and the read-back agrees. The same probably applies to `QLineEdit::setInputMask` fields and to any app that only reacts to `textEdited` (search-as-you-type, form dirty flags), but I only measured the validator.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse input to macOS security and consent prompts
body:
Salvaged from #7255

## Why

An agent clicked Allow on "HoloWork would like to access data from other apps", and the macOS driver also typed into an administrator password sheet. Nothing stopped input from reaching the system prompts that grant access on the user's behalf. This lands @AlexFalher's change from #7255 (his commit is first, author kept) and reworks it so every route is covered, the refusal is one authorization adapter, and unrestricted mode can still answer a prompt on a disposable machine.

## What changed

- A new `os_security_prompt` enforcement adapter (R4, unrestricted only) in `authorization.rs` owns the refusal. Standard and bounded mode refuse with `status: refused`, `refusal.code: security_prompt_protected`. The dispatch boundary records the adapter's decision for the call's mode in a reserved argument, which callers cannot set.
- The macOS check sits inside each global HID primitive in `input/mouse.rs` and `input/keyboard.rs`. It runs right before the first cursor warp or event, after any foreground activation. Pointer input is refused when a prompt window is under the point, on any layer. Keys are refused when a prompt owns the front. Pid-addressed routes are refused at the target pid. This covers the two foreground element fallbacks that #7255 missed (modified middle-click, AX selection with modifiers) and foreground keys aimed at another app while a prompt is in front.
- UserNotificationCenter windows count only when they ask for consent. That means a secure field, or a button whose label is one of the system's own consent labels, read from the TCC and NetworkExtension string tables in every language. Crash alerts ("… quit unexpectedly") no longer refuse clicks near them. An alert that cannot be read in full counts as consent.

## Scope

macOS only. The prompt owners are SecurityAgent, UserNotificationCenter (consent alerts only), universalAccessAuthWarn, coreautha, CoreServicesUIAgent and CoreLocationAgent. Reading prompts (window state, screenshots) stays allowed. Windows Credential UI and Linux polkit agents are not checked yet, as #7255 noted. Docs: the permissions guide and the Lume seed steps now say an unattended seed must answer the admin-password dialog from an unrestricted daemon.

## Tradeoffs

- One check inside each HID primitive replaces the dozen tool call sites in #7255, so a new tool route cannot skip it. Window-scoped foreground scroll and drag post to the target pid, not the HID queue, so they are no longer point-checked. The target-pid guard still covers them.
- Matching consent labels from the OS string tables is a heuristic. Every way it can fail (unreadable alert, unlabeled button, missing table) refuses.

## Blast radius

Every macOS input tool, the browser setup assists, and every permission mode. Standard and bounded mode now refuse input that would land on one of these prompts. That is the intended change. A test harness that clicks a Gatekeeper or password dialog has to run unrestricted. Unrestricted behaves as before.

## Verification

- Tests drive every HID primitive and every pid-addressed tool against a prompt fixture, refused and allowed. With any one guard removed, a test fails. Core tests cover the adapter per mode and show a forged decision argument is stripped.
- Read-only probe of the live prompts on a macOS 26 desktop. A SecurityAgent sheet (layer 1000), a universalAccessAuthWarn alert (layer 0) and a "find devices on local networks" consent alert were refused. Crash alerts on the same desktop were not.
- The scoped repository checks and the macOS Lume full matrix passed. The live prompt cases in a Lume guest did not run (details in the verification comment).

title: ci: enable KVM via udev rule and require it for bench verify
body:
## What changed for users
Image releases no longer fail slowly: the osworld bench image verify now boots its VM with hardware acceleration (KVM) on GitHub-hosted amd64 runners, and a missing KVM fails in seconds with the reason, not after 30 minutes.

## Why
`bench / verify (amd64)` in `cd-images-spacesd-release.yml` timed out (1849 s, "cua-spacesd did not answer") even with `time_to_start=1500`. A desktop image under QEMU TCG (software emulation) boots in 900-1300+ s on a hosted runner. The runtime also fell back to TCG silently (a warning only), including when KVM stalled at start.

## Change
- `scripts/images/enable-kvm.sh [--require]`: the documented static udev rule (`99-kvm4all.rules`, reload, trigger), so installing QEMU can't reset `/dev/kvm` to 0660. `--require` errors if KVM is missing.
- `install-release-tools.sh` and all workflows that boot QEMU on hosted Linux (images linux/windows, bench, nightly qemu/build/ready/vmm/fork, vm-density, perf channel, space-egress, e2b-core) use it instead of `chmod 666 /dev/kvm`.
- `cd-bench-images.yml` verify: amd64 runs `enable-kvm.sh --require` and sets `CUA_REQUIRE_KVM=1`.
- `cua-vmm` QEMU runtime: with `CUA_REQUIRE_KVM=1` a same-arch Linux guest never falls back to TCG (neither at accelerator selection nor on the KVM-stall retry); it errors naming `/dev/kvm`. Unit test added.
- `smoke.py`: same preflight for the containerdisk variant.
- `.github/scripts/tests/test_workflow_kvm_policy.py`: no raw `chmod /dev/kvm`; bench verify requires KVM on amd64.

arm64 hosted runners have no KVM and keep the TCG doctor path (`CUA_REQUIRE_KVM` is only set for amd64).

`bin/ci --quick` passes.

title: fix(cua-driver): check the cells a verify-linux.sh run declared
body:
## Why

CUA-4014. `verify-linux.sh` runs `check-evidence.sh` after every run, and the checker hard-coded the two default background left-click labels. Any `CUA_E2E_CELL_FILTER` run then failed with `expected one current recording for linux-electron-left-click-ax-background`, even when its selected cells passed. That covers the foreground-only commands the feature map documents, such as `linux-electron-left-click-px-foreground`. The checker now validates the cells the run declared in `cases.jsonl`.

## What changed

- `check-evidence.sh` reads `cases.jsonl` and checks each declared cell. It needs exactly one current recording, one summary row with the expected outcome (`Delivered` or `Refused`) and `Pass`, and the transcript and fixture journal. Sentinel and desktop-observation evidence with a heartbeat is required only for background cells. The `last_action` marker and the MCP-tool screenshot pair are required only for delivered click cells. If `cases.jsonl` is missing, empty or malformed, the check fails.
- The offline checker regression writes `cases.jsonl` and adds foreground-only, background-refusal and broken-declaration scenarios.
- SKILL.md and execution.md describe what the checker now requires.

## Scope

Covers the Linux verify helper's evidence checker and its offline test. The Rust runner, the report format and the macOS lane are unchanged. The default run still checks both background AX left-click cells to the same standard as before.

## Blast Radius

The checker is used only by the verify skill and by the `verify-skill` CI job. For the default filter it applies the same checks as before. The difference is that the cell list now comes from the run's own declarations instead of a constant.

## Verification

- On main, X11 runs filtered to `linux-electron-left-click-px-foreground`, `linux-electron-right-click-ax-foreground`, `linux-electron-type-text-ax-foreground` and `linux-electron-type-text-ax-background` all failed the evidence check, although every cell passed in `summary.md`. The new checker accepts all four retained evidence directories.
- At this head, the X11 helper exits 0 for `CUA_E2E_CELL_FILTER=linux-electron-left-click-ax-foreground` and for the default filter.
- The scoped repository checks (`test_e2e_rust_linux_workflow.py`) pass. With the base checker in place, the new `foreground` and `refused-background` scenarios fail.

title: fix(cua-driver): on Linux, set_value refuses an option on a combo box that lists none
body:
Fixes CUA-4013.

## Problem

On Linux, `set_value` on a combo box with no accessibility write route opens the combo's popup and picks the option from it. When the popup listed no options, the fallback failed with the untyped error "the combo box popup listed no options". That error surfaced as `tool_invocation_failed`, so an agent could not tell it apart from a driver crash. The no-options path also had no test.

Repro on main: a GTK3 `ComboBoxText` with no items, and `set_value` with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` returns `tool_invocation_failed` ("the combo box popup listed no options").

## Fix

- The AT-SPI option scan (`list_options`) now reports whether every read it made answered.
- `activate_option_ref` returns the new `OptionPick::NoOptions` when the scan answered and found nothing, and `Unavailable` when a read failed or timed out.
- The popup fallback (`pick_listed_option`) waits for options as before. When the wait ends:
  - `NoOptions` becomes the same `option_not_found` refusal (`effect: none`) as an unknown option. The message says the element lists no options.
  - `Unavailable` stays a plain error. A populated popup can be unreadable too, so an unreadable one is never reported as having no such option.
- The popup is still closed in both cases.

## Tests

- Unit tests (`set_value_tests`) cover: an empty popup is refused as `option_not_found` with `effect: none`; an unreadable popup is never `no_such_option`; a popup that lists its options late still gets the pick.
- The fake-bus test `tests/atspi_option_pick.rs` adds an empty combo box (`NoOptions`) and one whose child cannot be read (`Unavailable`). With the scan's completeness ignored, the test fails.
- Live smoke: the GTK3 fixture gains an empty "Empty" combo box. A Linux-only check runs foreground `set_value` on it and requires three things: `option_not_found`, an unchanged label, and a following click by token that still lands, which proves no popup was left behind. With main's binary the check fails with `tool_invocation_failed`. At this head it passes, along with every other row.

body:
## Summary

`create_space` drops CPU and memory requests: its MCP schema has neither field, and the handler leaves both at their defaults. On a small host, an agent can receive `host_capacity` advice to create a smaller Space but cannot request one.

Expose optional `cpus` and `memory_mb` using the existing resource types, and forward them to `SpaceCreate` for single and multi-Space requests. Omitting either setting preserves the current default. Regenerate the tool manifest and Spaces reference.

For example, `create_space(on="host:my-host", image="linux", kind="vm", cpus=1, memory_mb=1536)` can now pass the requested size to the existing creation path.

## Related work

Fixes #7309.

## Compatibility and risk

This restores the resource controls already available to the CLI and underlying creation code. It adds optional MCP inputs without changing defaults, allocation logic, or the wire protocol. The fields follow `resize_space`'s types. No backend refactor or new dependency.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the schema regression fails because `cpus` is missing; the integration regression requests 1 CPU but observes 2 at the runtime.
- Full `cua-spaces` and `cua-spaces-contract` test suites: **755 tests passed** across 37 test binaries/doctest groups, including the new regressions.
- Tests cover CPU-only, memory-only, both, omitted defaults, malformed resource types, and both members of a two-Space request.
- Clippy with `--all-targets -- -D warnings` passed for the affected crates and dependency checks. The two app crates that initially lacked CMake were rechecked successfully together after installing it.
- Generated manifest, control fixture and Spaces reference checks pass.
- Full affected `bin/ci`: **10 passed, 2 failed**. Its initial dependent-Clippy failure was a missing local CMake executable; after installing CMake, both affected app crates passed the retry. The remaining failure is `docs-image-refs`: 12 existing image references lack doctor ledger entries, including `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04`. Image references, the baseline and checker are unchanged by this PR. No green `local-ci` sign-off is claimed. All CLI, Rust and Spaces generated-reference checks passed.

Integration tests reuse the existing fake runtime and loopback mock server. Live VM/cloud provisioning and hosted PR CI have not been run locally.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Focused diff; description matches the final change.
- [x] Small bug fix using existing creation semantics; no new architecture or permission boundary.
- [x] Regression tests and generated documentation included.
- [x] Conventional `fix(spaces)` title describes the production change.
- [x] No external contribution was adapted.
- [x] No `no-release` label requested for this behavior fix.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off.

title: fix(cua-driver): submit a macOS single-line field with its own Return on background type_text
body:
## Problem

On macOS, a background `type_text` of `"netflix.com\n"` into Safari's address bar searched for "netflix.com netflix.com" instead of opening the site. The background route inserts the text through accessibility. The read-back can't confirm a value containing a newline, because the field drops it. So the code fell through and typed the whole string again as keys.

## Fix

When the target is a single-line field (`AXTextField`, `AXSearchField`, `AXComboBox`) and the text is one line plus one trailing Return:

- Insert the line alone with `AXSelectedText` and confirm it through the read-back.
- Send Return as its own key, but only if two checks pass:
  - the read-back equals the value from before the write with its selection replaced by the line, and differs from that earlier value (a no-op write, a field that already held the line, or a partial write does not count), and
  - the written field holds keyboard focus.
- If either check fails, report the line as delivered with `verified: false` and say why Return was not sent. Return is pid-routed, so sending it then could submit a different field.
- If the write changed the field into anything other than the full insert, report it as unverified partial delivery. Do not type the line and Return again as keys.
- Semantic-only keyboard policy keeps the old path, since Return is a synthesized key.

## Test plan

- Unit tests: `single_line_fields_split_off_one_trailing_return` and `submit_needs_a_visible_change_from_the_insert`.
- On a macOS Lume guest, through cua-driver:
  - Fresh Safari, background `type_text "netflix.com\n"` into the address bar's element token. Main doubled the text in most runs. With this change every run opened netflix.com.
  - Background `"abc\n"` into a page `<input>`: unchanged behaviour.

title: fix(cua-vmm): boot cold when a guest cannot take a restored identity; one readiness budget per start
body:
Fixes the `bench / verify (amd64, ubuntu-24.04)` failure in `cd-images-spacesd-release.yml` (`verify/amd64/containerdisk`: `cua-spacesd did not answer within 0ns`). Linear: CUA-4051.

**For users:** cua-spacesd releases can promote the OSWorld bench image again, and a local OSWorld VM (or any image whose agent is not root) starts in seconds instead of hanging for the whole start timeout before booting.

## Root cause

KVM was in use all along (the run that passed on 10 Nov printed `KVM present`), so the slow-TCG theory behind #7342 was not the cause, and a bigger `time_to_start` (#7304) only moved the failure.

The QEMU runtime's warm start was. On a fresh runner every OSWorld smoke:

1. booted a template VM and recorded a golden memory snapshot (about 90 s);
2. restored it and asked the guest to take a new identity: the renewal runs as root through cua-spacesd (`sudo -n sh -c ...`). The OSWorld disk's cua-spacesd runs as `user`, so the renewal failed on every attempt, and `renew` retried until the whole readiness budget (900 s, later 1500 s) was gone;
3. then booted cold with a fresh budget of its own (up in about 15 s), and returned. The SDK's own clock had run out by then, so its cua-spacesd wait got 0 ns: one 200 ms try, which a guest 15 s into its boot loses.

Evidence, from a diagnostic run of the same image and CLI on a hosted runner with the guest console and process list captured:

| | ready | result |
|---|---|---|
| `CUA_QEMU_WARM=0` | 307 s (pull + KVM cold boot; cua-spacesd serving 10 s after kernel start) | pass |
| warm starts on (default) | template 226-317 s, restored VM 317-1819 s (exactly the 1500 s budget), cold boot at 1819 s | `did not answer within 0ns` at 1826 s |

Every failing release run fits the same sum: budget + pull + cold boot (1372 s with 900 s; 1849 s and 1858 s with 1500 s). The one pass (run 42866618402) won the single 200 ms try: its guest had booted 14 s before ready.

## Changes

- **No golden snapshot from a guest that cannot renew its identity.** `GuestIdentity::check_renewable` (cua-spacesd: `[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || sudo -n true` as the agent) runs on the template before the snapshot is written. A guest that cannot is marked cold on disk (`_golden/<key>.cold`, with the reason), so later starts on that host boot cold at once without recording again. A guest that does not answer the question records nothing this time and is asked again next time, so a transient error never marks an image cold.
- **A refused renewal fails fast.** When the guest ran the renewal script and it failed, `renew` gives up after 3 refusals instead of retrying until the deadline. Transport errors still retry until the deadline.
- **One readiness budget per QEMU start.** Counted from when the image is present (as the SDK counts it), shared by the golden recording, the restore and its renewal, a cold boot after a failed restore, and the probes. Before, each phase got the whole `ready_timeout` again.
- **Failures print the guest console.** `scripts/bench-images/smoke.py` copies the serial console and QEMU log of the VM (and of any golden recording) into the evidence while the sandbox starts, and prints their tails on failure. A failed create deletes the VM directory, so these were lost before.

## Tests

- `cua-vmm`: `a_cold_marked_configuration_records_no_golden`, `phases_of_a_start_share_one_readiness_budget`
- `cua-daemon-core`: `a_refused_renewal_is_given_up_without_waiting_out_the_budget`, `the_renewable_command_needs_root_or_passwordless_sudo`
- `scripts/bench-images/test_bench.py`: `ConsoleCapture` (the console outlives the deleted VM and its golden recording)
- Local: `cargo test -p cua-vmm -p cua-daemon-core --lib`, clippy `-D warnings` on 1.97.1 for both crates, `bin/ci --quick` green.
- End to end: `cd-images-spacesd-release.yml` dispatched on this branch (`build=true`); the result is posted below.

Refs #7342, #7304.
