title: test(spaces): fix flaky prewarm grace test (offline provider race)
body:
Fixes the recurring `anUnclaimedPrewarmedStreamIsLetGoAfterItsGrace` failure (seen on #7337: "Expectation failed: (s.stats().count -> 0) == 1", also on the in-job rerun).

Cause: the test prewarmed a stream on `OfflineStreamSourceProvider`, which refuses to open a session. A warm stream whose session fails is let go at once (`statusChanged` -> `dropWarm`), so the stream could vanish before the first expectation. It was never the 800 ms grace; the failing rerun took 0.36 s.

Fix: use a provider that really streams (`SyntheticStreamProvider`, as the neighbouring prewarm test does) and check the registered stream synchronously after `handle`, before any suspension. The grace-expiry assertion is unchanged.

User impact: none (test only).

title: fix(cua-driver/linux): pool XI2 master pairs instead of removing them (Qt 6 crash, #7325)
body:
Fixes #7325. Linear: CUA-4052.

**For users:** on Linux X11, ending a Cua Driver session (or letting it time out, or restarting the driver after a crash) no longer kills the Qt 6 apps you have open.

## Cause

When a session that used background input ended, the driver removed its XInput2 master pointer pair with `XIRemoveMaster`. Qt 6.5+ double-deletes slave devices whenever any master disappears ([QTBUG-146876](https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-146876), still open in 6.12), so every running Qt 6 client on the display segfaulted. All five removal paths triggered it: `end_session`, the idle timeout, the popup waiter, the startup orphan reaper and the no-hotplug failure path.

## Fix

Master pairs now live for the X server's lifetime and are reused, the shape @will-bogusz suggested in the issue:

- A session takes a free pair and adds one only when none is free. The holder is a `_CUA_MPX_HOLDER` device property on the master pointer, written under `XGrabServer` so two driver processes never take the same pair.
- Releasing a pair unplugs the session's uinput slaves, parks its cursor in the bottom-right corner and marks it free. Nothing is removed.
- Pairs whose holder is provably gone (same boot, PID namespace and uid, process dead or PID reused) are taken over. Startup recovery now frees them instead of removing them.
- The uinput slave must show up as an X device before any pair is taken or added, so a server without hotplug never gains one.

The cost: idle `CUA v1.… pointer` pairs stay in `xinput list` until the X server exits. There are as many as the most sessions that used background input at the same time.

## Tests

- New unit tests: holder marks, which pairs can be taken, and a guard that fails if any code in `platform-linux` issues a master removal.
- New ignored real-Xorg test, `tests/mpx_pool_xorg.rs`. Three sessions in a row free and reuse one pair, no `MASTER_REMOVED` hierarchy event fires, and with `CUA_TEST_QT6_PYTHON` set a live PySide6 window survives. GitHub CI only has Xvfb (no uinput hotplug), so this one runs by hand:
  `DISPLAY=:0 CUA_TEST_QT6_PYTHON=<python with PySide6> cargo test -p platform-linux --test mpx_pool_xorg -- --ignored`
- Manual check on Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME on Xorg (mutter 46), PySide6 6.10.1, the issue's steps (click, then `type_text` into a GTK window, then `end_session`, then the client exits):
  - 0.47.8 release: 9 of 9 Qt windows killed, with `general protection fault in libQt6XcbQpa.so.6` in the kernel log.
  - This branch: 0 of 21 killed. Masters stayed at 2 before, during and after each session, and the pair was reused every time.
  - This branch, two live sessions, then one `cua-driver mcp` SIGKILLed, then `cua-driver serve` starts (startup recovery), then a new session: 0 of 3 killed. The dead driver's pair was freed and reused, and no master was removed.

## Follow-up

#2888 turned the background-input route off on KDE Plasma X11 for what looks like this same crash. That gate is unchanged here. Lifting it should get its own check on a KDE X11 machine.

title: [Bug]: existing-profile bind refuses as ambiguous when a same-bounds window has a background tab with the selected tab's title
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`get_browser_state(pid, window_id)` refuses with `browser_binding_ambiguous` (`candidate_count: 2`) for a window whose visible tab title is unique to that window, whenever another Chrome window has the same bounds and merely *contains* a background tab with that title.

In `correlate` (`cua-driver-core/src/browser/binding.rs`), the title tie-break runs over the per-window representatives built by `window_representatives`. That function prefers, for **every** CDP window, any tab whose title matches the *requested* native window's title. So when two windows share bounds, a background tab in the other window that happens to have the same title (a duplicated settings page, a second `New Tab`, the same site open twice) promotes that window into the tie-break. Both representatives then match and the bind is refused, even though only one window is actually displaying that title.

This is easy to hit on a normal daily-driver profile: windows are often the same maximized size on one display, and `New Tab` exists in almost every window. In practice the agent can only bind when the user happens to be looking at a tab whose title is unique across all same-size windows.

### Reproduction

1. Chrome on macOS, attach the existing profile with `browser_prepare` (`strategy: existing_profile`).
2. Open two normal windows with identical bounds (e.g. both 1920×1050 at the same origin on one display).
3. In window A, select tab "Page X". In window B, open a tab also titled "Page X", then select a different tab in B (so B's native title is something else).
4. `get_browser_state({pid, window_id: A})`.

Same result with step 3 replaced by: press ⌘T in window A (selected tab becomes `New Tab`) while window B also has a background `New Tab`.

### Expected behavior

Bind window A exactly. Window B's native title is different, so B cannot be the window currently showing "Page X". Only the selected tab of each window should be able to make that window match the requested title.

### Actual behavior

```
{"refusal":{"code":"browser_binding_ambiguous","detail":{"candidate_count":2},
 "message":"multiple CDP targets match the native window and the title tie-break cannot pick a unique one"}}
```

When window A is switched to a tab whose title exists in no other window, the same call binds with `binding_quality: exact`. So this looks like the tie-break and not a geometry or ownership problem.

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.38.0 (`serve --dangerously-bypass-approvals`), MCP transport
- macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon
- Google Chrome 157.0.8103.39, existing default profile, `DevToolsActivePort` endpoint
- Source read for the analysis: `main` at 8854478

### Evidence

- The refusal shows up only when the two windows' bounds are identical. `list_windows` reports both at `x=1098, y=-1050, 1920×1050`. A third window of a different width is not counted.
- Calling the bind right after ⌘T in window A (selected tab `New Tab`) still gives `candidate_count: 2`.
- I observed the symptoms above on a real profile. The cause described in the summary comes from reading `correlate` / `window_representatives`. I did not build a minimal fixture, so the two-window steps in Reproduction are derived from the code, not recorded.

### Workaround and additional context

Workarounds we use: give the agent its own Chrome window with a distinct size, or bind only while the selected tab's title is unique.

Possible fixes, in case useful:

1. When several CDP windows match by bounds, also take the titles of the *other* native windows of the same pid with the same bounds. A CDP window whose tabs contain another native window's title is better explained by that window. Matching native windows to CDP windows one-to-one by their own titles would settle this case without guessing.
2. Use page visibility as an extra signal: only each window's selected tab reports `document.visibilityState === "visible"` (occlusion can make it `hidden` too, so it would narrow candidates, not prove the match on its own).

Related: #3681 covers the same-bounds ambiguity fixture. This report is about the refusal also happening when the visible titles differ.

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11: scroll on a Qt list reports "Scrolled down 3 ticks" but nothing moves
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, `scroll` on a Qt list answers "Scrolled down 3 ticks" and the list does not move, on Qt 5 and Qt 6, even with the Qt window focused. A real wheel event at the same point scrolls it.

### Reproduction

1. X11 session (Xvfb + openbox here), a PyQt5 or PyQt6 window with a 20-row `QListWidget`, window focused.
2. `get_window_state` on it, then `scroll {"pid": …, "window_id": …, "x": <list center>, "y": <list center>, "direction": "down", "amount": 3}`.
3. Read the list's scroll position from the app.
4. Control: `xdotool mousemove --window <id> x y click --repeat 3 5` at the same point.

Script: [cua_x11_repro.py](https://gist.github.com/will-bogusz/e8696f3238aaa108cf3e7c0b730440dc), `python3 cua_x11_repro.py scroll --qt 5` (or `--qt 6`). It starts its own window and reads the position from the app itself.

### Expected behavior

The list scrolls, or the call says it couldn't.

### Actual behavior

```
{"trial": 0, "active": "cua-repro-qt", "scroll": {"ok": true, "text": "Scrolled down 3 ticks (delivery_mode=background)."}, "list_top_before": 0, "list_top_after_cua": 0, "list_top_after_xdotool_wheel": 9}
```

3 of 3 on Qt 5 and 3 of 3 on Qt 6 with the script. In a larger matrix on the same build: 80 of 80 across focused, unfocused, covered and user-typing windows, Qt 5 and Qt 6, while the xdotool wheel control moved it every time. GTK 3 on the same guest refuses background scroll with an exact refusal, which is fine; Qt gets a success it didn't earn.

[INFERENCE] Qt's xcb plugin takes wheel input from XI2 and probably drops a synthetic core button 4/5 event, so whatever route the background scroll uses here never reaches it.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.47.9 (`cua-driver-rs-0.47.9` linux arm64 release binary; same result on 0.46.1). Ubuntu 22.04.5 aarch64, Xvfb + openbox (no compositor), AT-SPI 2.44, PyQt5 5.15 (Qt 5.15.3), PyQt6 6.3.1 (Qt 6.2.4). Scripted MCP client, telemetry off.

### Evidence

Output above from the script. The list position is read from the app's own scroll bar, not through the driver.

### Workaround and additional context

`delivery_mode: "foreground"`, or scroll through AT-SPI where the list exposes it.

### Submission checks

- [X] This issue describes a single problem.
- [X] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11: hotkey to an unfocused Qt window reports "Pressed ctrl+m" but the shortcut never fires
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, `hotkey ctrl+m` to a Qt window that isn't focused answers "Pressed ctrl+m on pid …" and the window's Ctrl+M action doesn't fire, on Qt 5 and Qt 6. The same call works when the Qt window is focused.

### Reproduction

1. X11 session, a PyQt5 or PyQt6 window with a File menu `QAction` "Mark" bound to Ctrl+M, and another window focused.
2. `hotkey {"pid": …, "window_id": <the Qt window>, "keys": ["ctrl", "m"]}`.
3. Read the action's trigger count from the app.
4. Control: focus the Qt window, same call.

Script: [cua_x11_repro.py](https://gist.github.com/will-bogusz/e8696f3238aaa108cf3e7c0b730440dc), `python3 cua_x11_repro.py hotkey --qt 5` (or `--qt 6`).

### Expected behavior

The shortcut fires, or the call refuses the way it does for GTK 3 in the same spot. Saying "Pressed" while nothing happened is the problem.

### Actual behavior

```
{"trial": 0, "qt_focused": false, "active": "cua-repro-user", "hotkey": {"ok": true, "text": "Pressed ctrl+m on pid 3176 (delivery_mode=background)."}, "mark_before": 0, "mark_after": 0}
{"trial": 0, "qt_focused": true, "active": "cua-repro-qt", "hotkey": {"ok": true, "text": "Pressed ctrl+m on pid 3176 (delivery_mode=background)."}, "mark_before": 0, "mark_after": 1}
```

title: [Bug]: Linux X11: invoke_menu on a background GTK 3 window drops the user's keystrokes in their own window
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, `invoke_menu` on a background GTK 3 window drops a couple of the user's keystrokes in whatever window they're typing in. The menu command runs, the reply says "focus untouched", and the user's text comes out with characters missing.

### Reproduction

1. X11 session, a GTK 3 window with File > Mark (a plain `Gtk.MenuItem`), and a second GTK window focused where the user is typing (here `xdotool type --delay 80` a 43-character sentence).
2. While the user is typing: `invoke_menu {"pid": …, "window_id": <the menu window>, "path": ["File", "Mark"]}`.
3. Compare what the user's window received with what was typed. Control: same trial without the call.

Script: [cua_x11_repro.py](https://gist.github.com/will-bogusz/e8696f3238aaa108cf3e7c0b730440dc), `python3 cua_x11_repro.py menu-keys`.

### Expected behavior

The user's typing is untouched, as "focus untouched" says.

### Actual behavior

```
{"trial": 0, "invoke_menu": {"ok": true, "text": "Resolved the live native menu path and dispatched its final accessibility action (delivery_mode=background, focus untouched); verify the command's semantic effect from fresh state."}, "user_typed": "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", "user_got": "the quick brown fox jumpover the lazy dog", "lost": 2}
{"trial": 0, "invoke_menu": null, "user_typed": "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", "user_got": "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", "lost": 0}
```

The user lost 2 characters in 8 of 8 trials with the call (5 + 3 across two runs), 0 in 8 of 8 controls. A larger matrix on the same build saw the same in 10 of 10 (5 characters in one trial). [INFERENCE] Opening the menu shell to resolve the live path takes a keyboard grab for a moment, and keys typed during it go to the grab.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.47.9 (`cua-driver-rs-0.47.9` linux arm64 release binary; same on 0.46.1). Ubuntu 22.04.5 aarch64, Xvfb + openbox, AT-SPI 2.44, GTK 3.24. Scripted MCP client, telemetry off.

### Evidence

Output above from the script. Text read from the user window's own buffer.

### Workaround and additional context

None from the caller's side; the call can't know the user is typing. Separately, in 2 of 3 trials of the latest run the menu item's `activate` fired twice, 7-16 ms apart, for one `invoke_menu` call. I haven't pinned that down (another fixture with an accelerator on the item counted one per call), so I'm only noting it here.

title: fix(cua-driver): stamp the window-local point on macOS 27 background drags
body:
## Why

On macOS 27, WindowServer hands a pid-routed event's `CGEventSetWindowLocation` stamp to the target as its window-local point. #5492 switched background clicks to the window-local stamp on macOS 27, but `drag_at_xy_background` still stamped every event with the screen point. A background drag inside a window then pressed, moved and released at points offset by the window's origin, so it moved nothing and still reported a posted drag. Refs CUA-4056.

## What changed

- `drag_at_xy_background` takes the window's screen origin and stamps each move, press, drag and release with `point - origin` on macOS 27+ (the same `window_location_is_window_local` gate as the click route), and with the screen point before. The off-screen primer keeps `(-1, -1)`, and a release cut short by a drag-and-drop session is stamped at the point where it stopped.
- The drag tool and `drag_at_xy_observed` pass the origin from the frame they already resolved.

## Scope

macOS background pixel drags only. Foreground HID drags, Electron main-process drags, clicks and scrolls are unchanged. Linux and Windows are untouched.

## Blast radius

Every macOS background `drag`. Before macOS 27 the stamp is the screen point exactly as before, so current releases see no change.

## Verification

- A new unit test pins the macOS 27 stamps of a whole drag plan against a window at a non-zero origin, and checks that the pre-27 stamps stay the screen points. It fails if the stamp goes back to the screen point.
- Not run: no macOS 27 host or image exists, so the macOS 27 path itself has not been exercised live. The macOS 26 Lume run checks that releases before 27 behave as before.

title: fix(cua-driver): release actions at the native arrival under floor cursor timings
body:
## Why

The default cursor timing, `steady` (#5044), makes every agent-cursor move take at least 600 ms, so a person can follow short hops. A direct action waits for the cursor's arrival signal before it sends input, so that floor became a latency floor on every short action with the cursor on. Refs CUA-4054.

## What changed

- The overlay now releases the waiting action when the same move under `native` timing would have arrived. A floor timing (`relaxed`, `steady`, `calm`) still plays the stretched glide to the target, and the cursor finishes during the action.
- A move the floor does not stretch, and every other timing, release at their own arrival as before. The Linux shell helper's pose track carries the same release time.
- `EMBEDDING.md` says what the floor costs.

## Scope

`cursor-overlay`'s arrival signal, shared by macOS, Windows, X11 and Wayland. The motion planner, golden trajectories, timings and the `steady` default are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

- Making `native` the default would also remove the wait, but it undoes the look chosen in #5044.
- Capping a direct call's glide wait at the batch's 120 ms would cut long moves short too. Releasing at the native arrival keeps long moves exactly as they are.

## Blast radius

Direct actions with the agent cursor on and a floor timing. The click can now land while the cursor is still easing in on the last stretch of a short hop. The input point is unchanged.

## Verification

- A new overlay test checks that each floor timing releases a 20 pt hop at the native arrival while the glide still lasts close to its floor, and that long moves and `native` release at their own arrival. It fails when the release goes back to the stretched arrival.
- The scoped repository checks passed for `cursor-overlay` and `platform-macos` (fmt, clippy, unit tests).

title: fix(cua-driver): Windows consent matcher skips other native bubbles
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, attaching to an existing profile whose remote-debugging toggle is already on fails with `the native Chromium consent prompt did not expose exactly three distinct dialog buttons` whenever another native bubble is open in the window, for example Edge's "Translate page?" bubble on a page in another language. The matcher treats every titled native pane as a consent prompt and refuses on the first one that is not shaped like it, before reaching the real prompt. `dismiss` (session cleanup) hits the same check.
- What changed: a native surface counts as the consent prompt only when it carries exactly three Chromium dialog buttons; other bubbles are skipped. Contradictions inside a three-button prompt (focus, geometry, two prompts) still refuse. The `saw_prompt` branch in `handle` could never run (any surface returned before it) and is removed with `native_prompt_surface_present`.

## Related work

None.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only. A prompt with fewer or more than three dialog buttons now times out ("no exact ... prompt appeared") instead of refusing at once; nothing is clicked either way.
- Risk and rollback: low; one function in `browser_consent_ui.rs`.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new `matcher_skips_other_native_bubbles_beside_the_consent_prompt` (fixture from the Edge 156 tree); two expectations move from refusal to `None`. `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib browser_consent_ui`: 19 passed on `windows-11-arm`.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep isolated macOS browsers off the login keychain and stop launch loops
body:
Fixes CUA-4065.

## What changes for users

On macOS, browsers that Cua Driver launches for an agent (`browser_prepare` with an isolated profile) no longer ask for the login keychain, so they never show "… wants to use your confidential information stored in '… Safe Storage' in your keychain". If a launch fails or a security prompt is on screen anyway, Cua Driver stops with a clear error instead of launching more browsers.

## Cause

`isolated_browser_command` in `cua-driver-core/src/browser/prepare.rs` passed `--password-store=basic` on Linux but had no macOS counterpart. Every driver-launched Chromium therefore read the "<Browser> Safe Storage" item from the login keychain. When the launched binary is not on that item's access list (another Chromium build or tool created it), or the keychain is locked, macOS shows a SecurityAgent prompt for each new browser process, and nothing stopped repeated launches from stacking them.

## Changes

1. **Mock keychain for driver-owned profiles (macOS).** Isolated launches add `--use-mock-keychain` (as Playwright does). The launch command is now built only through `driver_owned_browser_command`, which refuses any directory that is not a marked driver-owned profile directly under the driver's profile root. The user's own profile is only ever attached to its running browser (`strategy=existing_profile`); it is never launched or relaunched, so the mock keychain can never make its cookies unreadable. The standalone-browser E2E test launcher gets the same switch for its throwaway profiles.
2. **Launch circuit breaker.** After 3 consecutive failed isolated launches (spawn error, early exit, no DevTools, endpoint mismatch, or a security prompt), `browser_prepare` refuses further launches for an exponential back-off (30 s, doubling to 10 min) with `detail.reason = "isolated_launch_backoff"`, `retry_after_seconds`, and the last failure. One attempt is let through after the back-off; a success resets it.
3. **Keychain prompt guard.** New `BrowserPlatform::security_prompt_open` (macOS: an on-screen SecurityAgent or LocalAuthentication window, i.e. keychain and password prompts; privacy consent and Gatekeeper prompts do not count; it only looks). Before launching, an open prompt refuses the launch (`security_prompt_open`). While waiting for DevTools and once after attestation, a prompt that appears stops the launch, kills that browser, removes its profile, and opens the breaker at once (`security_prompt_appeared`). Cua Driver never clicks, types into, or dismisses the prompt.
4. Docs: the isolated-browser section of the browsers guide explains the keychain behaviour and the new refusal reasons.

## Tests

- `isolated_launch_uses_a_deterministic_clean_profile`: macOS args include `--use-mock-keychain` (Linux still `--password-store=basic`).
- `only_driver_owned_profiles_get_a_launch_command`: unmarked dirs, marked dirs outside the root, and missing dirs are refused; the owned profile gets the switch on macOS.
- `existing_profile_requests_never_launch_a_browser`: every existing-profile request shape leaves the spawn count at 0.
- `an_open_security_prompt_blocks_isolated_launches`, `a_prompt_raised_by_a_launch_stops_it_and_further_launches`: no spawn while a prompt is open; a prompt during launch stops it and an immediate retry is held back.
- Breaker unit tests (threshold, back-off doubling and cap, half-open, reset, prompt opens at once) and a macOS fixture test for `security_prompt_on_screen`.

Local: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::` and `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib security_prompt` on macOS arm64; clippy `-D warnings`; `bin/ci --quick`.

VM check: macOS VM, Google Chrome 154, `browser_prepare` with `isolated_new` 20 times per run; prompts counted from on-screen SecurityAgent windows and `securityd` "displaying keychain prompt" log lines, never answered.

| Run | "Chrome Safe Storage" item | Keychain prompt requests | Launch results |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before (release 0.47.10) | created by Chrome itself | 0 / 20 | 20 ok |
| Before (release 0.47.10) | created by another binary (Chrome not on its access list) | 20 / 20 (one per launch, queued behind each other) | 20 ok, launching continued |
| After (this branch) | created by another binary | 0 / 20; every Chrome has `--use-mock-keychain` | 20 ok |
| After, with 20 old prompts still on screen | created by another binary | 0 new | 2 refused with `security_prompt_open`, no browser started |

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux background invoke_menu never opens a menu, so the user's typing is kept (#7371)
body:
Closes #7371. Linear: CUA-4062.

**For users:** a background `invoke_menu` on Linux no longer eats letters from what you're typing in your own window, and the menu command runs exactly once.

## Cause

`invoke_menu` resolved a path one level at a time: it fired **File**, which pops the GTK menu up, then fired **Mark** inside it. An open GTK, Qt or VCL menu grabs the core keyboard, so while it was open every key the user typed went to the menu. A swallowed space also activated the selected item, which is why **Mark** sometimes ran twice for one call (the second activation noted in the report).

## Fix

- GTK 3 and Qt publish closed menus through AT-SPI, so the final item is already in the first walk. `invoke_menu` now fires that item's own action directly. GTK runs its `activate` and leaves the menus unposted, so no menu opens and nothing grabs the keyboard.
- Background delivery never opens a menu. If an app only publishes the item once its menu is open, or declines a closed item's action, the call refuses with `background_unavailable` and runs nothing. Foreground keeps the level-by-level walk as the fallback after the direct try.

## Before and after

The reporter's `menu-keys` script, GTK 3.24, on Xvfb + openbox and on GNOME Xorg:

| | Characters lost per call | Mark activations per call |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 1-2 in 6 of 6 calls | 2 in 2 of 3 calls on Xvfb |
| After | 0 in 12 of 12 calls | exactly 1 in every call |

Controls without the call lost nothing in both runs, and after background calls the user's own File menu still opens and runs Mark from the keyboard.

## Tests

- `tests/background_menu_xorg.rs` (ignored, needs a real X11 session): a background `invoke_menu` while `xdotool` types into another window. It passes on GNOME Xorg and on Xvfb + openbox with the fix.
- Unit tests for the leaf plan (a command item runs directly; a submenu would open a menu) and for the refusal mapping.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`: 1032 passed.

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux X11 background scroll on Qt moves the list or refuses (#7369)
body:
Closes #7369. Linear: CUA-4062.

**For users:** a background `scroll` on a Qt app on Linux now moves the list by every detent, or says it can't, instead of reporting success while nothing moves.

## Cause

There are two causes, one for each kind of X server.

- **No agent pointer device** (Xvfb, Xtigervnc, or no writable `/dev/uinput`): background scroll fell back to synthetic Button4/5 `XSendEvent`s. Qt reads the wheel only from XI2 scroll valuators and drops those events, so the call said "Scrolled" and nothing moved. GTK was already refused here.
- **Agent pointer available** (real Xorg): Qt re-reads a scroll device's valuators with a synchronous `XIQueryDevice` on a slave switch and on pointer enter. The first detent after the warp was a slave switch. When Qt's re-read ran after later detents had already landed, Qt took the post-scroll value as its baseline and the detents cancelled out. 3 detents down moved the list 0 or 2 detents. Qt's own input log shows the re-read reading the final value.

## Fix

- The background refusal now covers every toolkit that drops synthetic pointer input (GTK, Qt, LibreOffice VCL) when there is no agent pointer. That applies to `scroll`, `right_click`, `double_click` and `drag`. The agent wheel never falls back to `XSendEvent` for those toolkits.
- Before the first detent, the agent pointer makes the slave switch with a one-pixel step and back, confirmed through `XIQueryPointer`. It then waits on a `_NET_WM_PING` round trip, so the app has finished its re-read before any detent lands.
- The X11 result says what was sent and reports `effect: "unverifiable"` instead of "Scrolled".

## Before and after

The reporter's `scroll` script and the new test, with 3 detents down (9 rows expected):

| Setup | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Xvfb + openbox, Qt 6 | "Scrolled", 0 rows (2 of 2) | `background_unavailable`, 0 rows |
| GNOME Xorg, no uinput, Qt 6 | "Scrolled", 0 rows (3 of 3) | `background_unavailable`, 0 rows |
| GNOME Xorg, uinput, Qt 6 | 6, 0, 6 rows | 9 rows, 5 of 5 |
| GNOME Xorg, uinput, Qt 5.15 | 6, 6 rows | 9 rows, 5 of 5 |
| GNOME Xorg, uinput, Qt window inactive | not measured | 9 rows, 3 of 3 |

## Tests

- `tests/background_scroll_xorg.rs` (ignored, needs a real X11 session): scrolls a Qt list with the Qt window active and inactive. The list must move exactly 9 rows, or the call must refuse with no movement. It passes on GNOME Xorg with uinput and on Xvfb + openbox.
- Unit test for the toolkit refusal rule.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`: 1032 passed.

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux X11 background hotkey to an inactive Qt window fires or refuses (#7370)
body:
Closes #7370. Linear: CUA-4062.

**For users:** a background `hotkey` to a Qt window that isn't focused now either fires the shortcut or says it can't, instead of reporting "Pressed" when nothing happened.

## Cause

Qt runs a `QAction` or `QShortcut` shortcut only in its active window. Without the agent's own XI2 master keyboard (Xvfb, Xtigervnc, or no writable `/dev/uinput`), background keys are synthetic `XSendEvent`s. They reach the inactive Qt window and trigger nothing, but the call still answered "Pressed".

## Fix

On GNOME Xorg with Qt 6.4 and 5.15, keys from the agent's own master keyboard do make Qt run the shortcut in an inactive window, so that route stays. Only the synthetic route changes:

- `hotkey` and `press_key` with a ctrl, alt or super chord to an inactive Qt window now return `background_unavailable`. The refusal suggests `invoke_menu` for commands that are in a menu.
- A chord to the active Qt window, plain keys, and shift chords keep working as before.
- If the agent keyboard fails during a call, the chord is reported as failed instead of falling back to the synthetic route.

## Before and after

The reporter's `hotkey` script and the new test, `ctrl+m` to a Qt window whose File > Mark action has Ctrl+M:

| Setup | Qt window not focused, before | Qt window not focused, after | Qt window focused, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Xvfb + openbox, Qt 5 | "Pressed", fired 0 of 1 | `background_unavailable` | fired 1 of 1 |
| GNOME Xorg, no uinput, Qt 6 | "Pressed", fired 0 of 2 | `background_unavailable` | fired 2 of 2 |
| GNOME Xorg, no uinput, Qt 5 | not measured | `background_unavailable` | fired 1 of 1 |
| GNOME Xorg, uinput, Qt 6 and 5 | fired (agent keyboard) | fired once per call | fired once per call |

## Tests

- `tests/background_hotkey_xorg.rs` (ignored, needs a real X11 session): sends the chord with the Qt window inactive and active. Each call must fire the action exactly once, or refuse with no effect, and a chord to the active window must never be refused. It passes on GNOME Xorg with uinput and on Xvfb + openbox.
- Unit tests for the refusal rule.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`: 1032 passed.

title: feat(spaces): setup shows each agent connection step live, connects Cua Driver and sets up This Mac (CUA-4067)
body:
Closes CUA-4067 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-4067). Approved by Francesco on 11 Nov 2026.

**For users:** setup now shows, live, every change Cua makes for each coding agent, and where it makes it. A step that fails says why and can be retried on its own. Agents can use apps on your Mac straight after setup, and this Mac can run jobs straight away. This closes the "Set up This Mac after onboarding" gap.

## What changes

After Continue, step 3 ("Which agents do you use?") turns into a checklist:

1. **This Mac can run your agents' jobs**, shown first when you're signed in. It runs the same steps as Home's Set up (`thisMacSetupSteps`: `addThisComputer`, then the `host.action` steps). Then it waits until `host.status` reports this Mac shared and online (`hostStatusWhenOnline`) before anything else runs. Sharing the desktop restarts cua-spacesd, so no agent row or first job can hit the stale-connection race from #7161. The row keeps the plain explanation: "Shares this Mac's desktop with Cua so jobs can run on it. You can turn this off in Settings." If it fails, the row says why and offers Retry. Home's Set up button is now only the fallback.
2. For each agent:
   - "Added Cua's tools to Claude Code (~/.claude.json)"
   - "Installed Cua's skills for Claude Code (~/.claude/skills)"
   - "Let Claude Code use apps on this Mac (Cua Driver)"
   - "Saving your Claude Code sign-in to Keyvault so jobs on your other computers can use it"

A failed row shows the reason and its own **Retry**, which re-runs only that part. If Screen Recording or Accessibility was skipped in step 2, the Cua Driver row reads "needs your permission" and offers **Allow**, which opens System Settings. The row checks again when the window comes back into focus. Codex's sign-in row offers **Get a code**, which runs Codex's device sign-in made for Cua. Continue waits only until nothing is still running. Ready names only the agents whose tools went in.

### Core (`cua-agent-setup`)
- `ConnectResult.parts`: one `PartResult { part: mcp|skills|driver|sign_in, status: done|needs_permission|skipped|failed, where, line }` per part asked for. If one part fails, the next part still runs.
- `connect_full(..., driver: Option<&DriverTarget>, ...)` and `AgentSetup::connect_driver`. They write the host's `cua-driver` entry through the same backup-aware structural editor and record it in `~/.cua/agent-setup.json`, so Disconnect can remove exactly that entry. They refuse an entry that isn't named for Cua Driver or whose command isn't an existing absolute binary. When the permissions are off, the entry is still written and the part reports `needs_permission`, so it works as soon as they're on.
- Fixed the stale `driver.rs` comment: Cua Spaces for macOS bundles Cua Driver since 0.26.0.

### SDK, hosts, bridge
- `AgentSetup.connect_json(..., driver, driver_permissions_granted)`. All UniFFI bindings are regenerated (Swift, Kotlin, Python, TS, Electron).
- macOS: `agents.connect {driver: true}` passes `DriverConnect.embedded(EmbeddedDriver.current())`. That is the bundled `Cua Spaces.app/Contents/Helpers/cua-driver` with `mcp --embedded --socket … --host-bundle-id …`, never `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`. It also passes whether Screen Recording and Accessibility are granted, and starts the driver's login item when both are on.
- Electron: the app carries no Cua Driver, so the answer has no driver part and the row isn't drawn.
- Bridge contract: `driver?` arg and optional `parts` in the `ConnectResult` shape (`bridge-shapes.json` regenerated). The demo adapter answers per part.

### Home
- "Now bring the rest in" no longer has the "Let agents use apps on this Mac" row, so it isn't asked twice. If a permission is still off, it shows in Home's existing apps card (`AppsOnThisMac`), which is the fallback.

title: fix(cua-driver): Hyprland plugin kit for 0.57 (Omarchy edge)
body:
## What this means for users

Cua Driver background input (typing and clicking into windows you are not using) works again on Omarchy edge, which ships Hyprland 0.57.2. Today Omarchy's `cua-hyprland-plugin 0.33.2-4` pins Hyprland 0.56.2, so on edge it cannot be installed. This PR adds the reviewed profiles and CI that let Omarchy build the plugin for 0.57.2 while stable and RC keep working on 0.56.2.

Linear: https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-4078

## Findings

The plugin source on main already builds and loads on 0.57.x (#6329, #6495, plus the IME popup guard #7320 and agent-seat hover #7319). What was missing was a reviewed kit profile for 0.57 and a way to test the kit on both versions.

## Changes

- Kit profiles accept Hyprland headers 0.56.2 and 0.57.2; the kit recipe takes the expected header version from the profile. Hyprland 0.57.2's pkg-config also lists glib's `glibconfig.h` directory, which the verifier now admits (only while glib2 owns it).
- New profiles, measured in CI on each channel's own packages for the Driver 0.47.8 plugin source: `omarchy-edge-20261111` (Hyprland 0.57.2-1) and `omarchy-stable-20261111` (0.56.2-4).
- New workflow `ci-hyprland-plugin-kit.yml`: builds the kit per channel in an Arch container, runs the package lifecycle (makepkg, install, remove, reinstall, dependency refusal), loads the packaged module into a headless Hyprland and runs the smoke.
- The background smoke now also clicks into a window that does not hold focus (a terminal reports the click), next to the typing check.
- Requalification imports Omarchy's packaging key (fingerprint checked against Omarchy's `omarchy-update-keyring`) with retries.
- Docs updated from 0.56.2-only to 0.56.2 and 0.57.2. The Omarchy image recipe is unchanged on purpose: editing it would rebuild and republish the image, and its 0.56 handling is needed until the new Omarchy package ships.
- The daily requalification already opens or refreshes one `hyprland-requalify` issue (#5751) when a channel's packaged plugin stops installing (`installable:false`) or a build fails; no change needed.

## Evidence (CI, kit workflow, both channels green)

Packaged module, background type and click, primary focus unchanged, released Driver list_windows / screenshot / click / type_text:

- Omarchy edge, Hyprland 0.57.2-1: lifecycle pass, load pass (ABI match), smoke pass.
- Omarchy stable, Hyprland 0.56.2-4: lifecycle pass, load pass, smoke pass.

This is CI evidence, not native certification or Omabot replay.

## Credit

Thanks to @ludagoo (#6266) and @chrisohearn (#6253). Their 0.57 support work is already on main through #6495, and the 0.56.2/0.57 documentation and qualification notes are carried here (Co-authored-by trailers on the commit). Both PRs are left open for maintainers to close.

## Next

A prepared omarchy-pkgs update (PKGBUILD for `0.47.8-2` from this kit, no downstream patch) is held until the kit release asset is published from the merge commit.

title: ci(release): flag an installer feed that lags the newest CLI release
body:
## What

The hourly release pipeline guard now also checks that the installer feed follows the newest stable CLI release. It compares the newest published, non-prerelease `cua-sdk-vX.Y.Z` release with `versions.cli` and the CLI entries in the rolling `cua-install-latest` `release-artifacts.json`. If the feed names an older CLI more than two hours after publication, the guard's tracking issue names both versions.

## Why

#6923 reported that `install.sh` picked CLI 0.10.1 while 0.14.0 was published. Root cause: the last step of `cd-cua-sdk.yml` (`Update the rolling installer manifest`) failed on every release from 0.11.0 to 0.22.0 because a sparse checkout had removed `scripts/install`. #7265 fixed that, and the rolling manifest now lists CLI 0.24.0 for all six platforms (read from the release as data). Nothing flagged the three days in between, so this adds the missing alarm. No installer, URL or CDN publisher changes.

## Test

- `.github/scripts/tests/test_check_cli_feed_follows_release.py` (8 tests with fake release lists and manifests: the #6923 shape, numeric not lexical order, grace window, drafts, prereleases, other tags, stale platform entry).
- Live dry run against trycua/cua: exit 0 (feed current).
- `bin/ci` (actionlint, SPDX, image refs, .github/scripts tests): green.

Refs #6923 (the root cause is already fixed on main; this prevents a repeat).

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux hit test picks the GTK3 overlay drawn on top
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux X11, a foreground element click on a GTK3 button covered by a `Gtk.Overlay` banner pressed the banner. A click on the banner's own button was refused as "owned by" the covered button. The pre-press ownership check (`atspi::native::hit_test::point_ownership`) asks the toolkit's `GetAccessibleAtPoint` who owns the point. ATK's container implementation, used by GTK 2 and 3, returns the *first* child whose extents contain the point. `GtkOverlay` lists its main child first and draws its overlays above it, so the check returned the covered button and the click went through.
- What changed:
  - For GTK 3 and older (`gtk` toolkit, major version below 4, or `gail`), each step of the at-point descent now checks the later siblings of the toolkit's answer. Among those that are showing and whose `Component.Contains` holds for the point, the last one wins, since it is drawn on top. A parent with more than 32 children is not treated as a stack and is left alone. GTK 4, Qt, Chromium and VCL already answer with the topmost child and are unchanged.
  - With that, the covered button is refused with the banner named (`point_owned_by_another_element`), a click on the banner presses the banner, and a click on the button with no banner up still presses it. The background at-point action route (`perform_action_at_point_in`) uses the same descent, so it now actuates the overlay too.
  - The GTK3 harness gains a covered button with an overlay button above it. A new X11 E2E case covers both clicks.

## Related work

Refs #7299 (seen while comparing script-only and default tool modes on the BenchLab interrupt banner).

RFC: none. This is a bug fix in an existing check.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux X11 only, GTK 2 and 3 apps. A foreground element click whose point is covered by a later, showing sibling is now refused with that sibling named, where before it pressed the sibling. A background at-point click on such a point actuates the sibling. Wayland skips the ownership check and is unaffected.
- Risk and rollback: the change rests on GTK3 drawing later overlapping siblings above earlier ones. That holds for `GtkOverlay`, `GtkFixed` and `GtkLayout`. Hidden pages of a `GtkStack` or `GtkNotebook` are not showing, so they are skipped. Each descent step costs a few more AT-SPI calls on parents with 2 to 32 children. Revert the PR to roll back.

risk: standard

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the scoped repository checks (rustfmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, cua-driver-e2e and platform-linux unit tests, generated reference docs, UniFFI bindings). A new unit test pins which toolkits get the sibling check.
- Manual or platform evidence, on a Linux X11 desktop (Xvfb, openbox, picom):
  - The new `harness_gtk3_foreground_click_respects_overlay_stacking` fails with the origin/main driver ("a press on the covered button was sent") and passes with this head.
  - BenchLab `--mode irbanner`, foreground element click on Apply with the banner up: before, the lab logged `banner_action dismiss`. Now the click is refused with owner `button "Dismiss"` and nothing is pressed. A click on Dismiss logs `dismiss`, and Apply with no banner logs `apply`.
  - The whole GTK3 harness file passes except `harness_gtk3_rejects_exited_target_and_recovers_with_fresh_app`, which fails the same way with the origin/main driver (a `kill_app` permission refusal, outside this diff).
  - The verify-cua-driver Linux X11 lane passes.
- Known gaps or CI still required: Wayland lanes, GNOME and KDE sessions, and the Windows and macOS platform crates were not run.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [x] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`)

title: fix(spaces): the Codex sign-in row says what to do (CUA-4089)
body:
Linear: CUA-4089. Follow-up to #7389.

## What changes for users
The Codex row in the agent-connect checklist now tells you what to do. It read "Save a Codex sign-in to Keyvault so jobs on your other computers can use it" beside a "Get a code" button. It now reads "Sign Codex in for your other computers", with the same subline ("Codex signs in with a code made for Cua. Your own sign-in stays as it is.") and the same button. The Claude Code row keeps its wording.

Tests: `first-run-checklist.test.tsx` checks the row title and subline; `first-run-new.test.tsx` checks the rendered row. `bin/ci --quick` is green.

## Claude Code token rotation (no code change needed)
Question: when Cua copies Claude Code's sign-in into Keyvault, does OAuth refresh-token rotation sign one side out? Not as built. `cua-agent-setup` (`signin.rs::claude_import`, `claude_login.rs`) reads Claude Code's own store (Keychain item `Claude Code-credentials`, or `<config dir>/.credentials.json`) read-only and copies the **access token only**, as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. The refresh token is never copied, so jobs on other computers can never spend it. When the copy nears expiry, `AgentKeys::sync_claude_login` re-reads Claude Code's own store (asking Claude Code to refresh itself through `claude -p` if needed); Cua never calls the refresh endpoint. Codex needs its device-code sign-in because its `auth.json` is refreshed by whoever holds it; Claude's copy does not need that. The residual limit is lifetime: a copy lapses when the Mac is off, and the fallback is a pasted `claude setup-token` token (a one-year token with no refresh token, per code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication, "Generate a long-lived token"), already supported by `claude_pasted_token`. Anthropic's docs do not state whether refresh tokens rotate; the code's single-use assumption comes from ccswap and cswap and is the conservative one.

title: fix(cua-vmm): run the engine helper's chroot from PATH and build sandbox overlays on 24.04
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `ubuntu-latest` now runs ubuntu-26.04. Ubuntu 26.04 ships uutils coreutils by default, and two cua-spacesd checks fail there, on main as well as on PRs. (1) `cua sb create` fails with "could not write the resolv.conf of … on the engine's host" with empty stderr, because cua-vmm's engine helper execs `/usr/sbin/chroot`, and uutils installs `chroot` in `/usr/bin`. This breaks every sandbox job: the image doctor, the stale-build check, and every other helper call (resolv.conf, egress rules, checkpoints) on a 26.04 engine host. (2) `watch_and_signals::attribute_changes_are_chmod_and_writes_are_write` expects an inotify attribute event from `touch` of a new file. uutils `touch` creates the file and does not set its times again, so only the create is reported.
- Problem, part 3: the image doctor builds cua-spacesd and cua-driver on `ubuntu-latest` and injects them into `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04`. A 26.04 build needs `GLIBC_2.43` and the image has glibc 2.39, so the injected daemon never starts and the doctor times out.
- What changed: the helper runs `chroot` from `PATH`. Docker's default exec `PATH` includes both `/usr/sbin` and `/usr/bin`, and `/usr` is the engine host's own. The WSL runtime's setup check accepts `chroot` anywhere on `PATH`. The test no longer requires the attribute event on a new file. It still requires the create with no write, the attribute-only event for `touch` and `chmod` of an existing file, and the write for a content write. The three jobs that build binaries for injection into the 24.04 image (sandbox doctor build, driver preflight, nightly contrib doctor) run on `ubuntu-24.04`.

## Related work

Refs #7400 (its cua-spacesd checks fail only for this reason)

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Local container sandboxes now work on engine hosts whose `chroot` is in `/usr/bin` (Ubuntu 25.10 and later with uutils). Nothing changes on hosts with GNU coreutils.
- Risk and rollback: low. To roll back, revert this PR. Pinning every affected workflow to ubuntu-24.04 would also make CI green, but it would leave the sandbox broken for users on newer Ubuntu. So only the jobs whose output must match the 24.04 image are pinned.

risk: standard

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the scoped repository checks for cua-vmm and cua-spacesd-server (rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, cua-vmm unit tests, the watch_and_signals test).
- Manual or platform evidence: on main, the 26.04 push runs of the sandbox doctor and the cua-spacesd suite fail with exactly these two errors. The last 24.04 runs passed.
- PR CI: on 26.04 runners, the image doctor, the stale-build check and the cua-spacesd Linux suite pass. Before these commits they failed with these errors.
- Known gaps: Windows was not run locally.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.

- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

title: macOS 27.2.1: APNs/BAA failure persists in VMs (27.0.1 → 27.2 → 27.2.1)
body:
### macOS compatibility status

The APNs/BAA failure seen in macOS 27.0.1 and 27.2 VMs (#6197) also occurs in a freshly installed macOS **27.2.1 (26B131)** VM. Updating to 27.2.1 has not resolved it in our test.

### Test setup

Tested on **2026-11-12**, with host and guest both on macOS **27.2.1 (26B131)**.

- Lume 0.7.0. The guest was created from Apple's official IPSW with `lume create --ipsw`, not cloned or pulled.
- The guest had 2 vCPU, 8 GB RAM and a 96 GB disk (VirtualMac2,1).
- Setup Assistant was completed manually with a local account. No Apple Account was signed in.

APNs was checked with:

```sh
/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ApplePushService.framework/apsctl status
/usr/bin/log show --last 20m --process apsd --info --debug --style compact
```

### Observed result

The production connection stayed disconnected in two samples taken 5 minutes apart (00:37:00 and 00:42:00 UTC):

```text
connection environment: production
   connection status: No
```

The `apsd` log contains the same SEP key-generation and BAA certificate failure chain as in 27.0.1 and 27.2. It occurred **34 times** between 00:26:57 and 00:41:23 UTC. No connection succeeded in that window:

```text
<sepk:* kid=…>: (apsd) unable to generate key: error e00002e2(-536870174)
SecKeyCreateRandomKey_ios failed: Error Domain=NSOSStatusErrorDomain Code=-25308 "Failed to generate keypair"
(DeviceIdentity) Error Domain=com.apple.MobileActivation.ErrorDomain Code=-1 "Failed to create reference key."
APSBAAClientIdentityProvider failed to obtain a BAA cert
underlying identity provider has identity to connect? NO
told not to connect!
```

macOS 26.6.2 guests on the same host and Lume version connect to APNs normally.

Related: #6197, [Apple Developer Forums thread 840500](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/840500).

title: fix(cua-spacesd): request a keyframe while a viewer waits for one
body:
## Why

An H.264 viewer can end up waiting for a keyframe that nothing asks for. When the ack window overflows, `ViewerShared::try_next` drops the queue and sets `awaiting_keyframe` without asking the encoder for an IDR. A queue overflow in `push_video` does ask, but `request_keyframe_limited` swallows the ask when another request went out in the last second. While the screen keeps changing, idle refresh never fires, so the viewer stays frozen until the next unrelated IDR.

## What changed

- `ViewerShared::tick` (the 100 ms session maintenance) now reports that a keyframe is needed while an H.264 viewer is waiting for one, its ack window is open and it is not closing. The session's existing 1 s rate limit still bounds how often the encoder is asked.
- `MediaSession::request_keyframe_limited` claims its rate-limit slot under the lock, so the maintenance tick and a frame overflow arriving together send one IDR, not two.
- Tests: an ack-window drop gets a keyframe requested, a rate-limited ask is retried while the viewer waits, and concurrent limited asks reach the encoder once.

## Scope

Covers the v2 media plane in `cua-spacesd-session` (`media/viewer.rs`, `media/session.rs`). The legacy `service.rs` path and the stall probe (unchanged, it still fires every 2 s for a stalled acking client) are out of scope.

## Blast Radius

Every H.264 viewer of a Space desktop stream. While a viewer waits, the session asks for at most one IDR per second, the same bound overflow recovery already had. PNG and BGRA streams are unaffected.

## Verification

- The two new viewer tests fail at the tests-only commit and pass at the head, 3 of 3 repeats each. The concurrency test failed 3 of 5 runs without the locking change and passed 5 of 5 with it.
- The scoped repository checks pass: `cua-spacesd-session` unit tests, the `cua-spacesd` test suite including the run-as integration tests, clippy with `-D warnings`, rustfmt, and `bin/ci`'s runnable checks.
- Not run: the Linux Spaces viewer end-to-end lane, `bin/ci`'s heavy lanes (disk guard), and the macOS and Windows native checks.

title: fix(spaces): pass saved custom endpoints to persistent agents
body:
## Summary

A saved OpenAI-compatible endpoint can show Connected in the app while a persistent agent starts without its provider configuration. Hermes then reports that no AI provider is connected. The same startup path drops the saved endpoint for OpenCode and OpenClaw.

Persistent startup now uses the existing saved-connection resolver, passing through the endpoint, model, mapped key and generated Hermes config. Credential refresh checks the same resolved environment so a mapped custom key does not cause repeated restarts. Keyless Hermes connections also skip the auth probe that runs before their generated config is written.

To reproduce, save a custom OpenAI-chat endpoint, select it for one of these agents, start a persistent agent and send a message. The regression tests cover all three agents, with and without a key, plus model overrides and key rotation.

## Reproduction

Hermes shows Connected with a saved custom endpoint selected, then reports that no AI provider is connected when adding an agent to a space

![Hermes shows Connected with a saved custom endpoint selected, then reports that no AI provider is connected when adding an agent to a space](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95f3ad79-1464-4ce5-9969-b51d8bc1501d)

## Related work

Refs #6134, #6170. These added the connection handling reused here. I found no existing issue or PR covering this persistent-startup gap.

RFC: not required. This restores existing connection behavior without changing a public contract.

Explicit endpoint overrides still exclude unrelated saved credentials. No migration or permission change is needed. The change affects provider resolution at persistent startup and credential refresh. Revert these two commits to roll back.

title: fix(ci): retry the actionlint and Electron downloads past a release CDN outage
body:
## Why

On 8 and 9 Nov GitHub's release CDN answered release downloads with HTTP 504, and two downloads failed pull request jobs that a rerun then passed. #7152 fixed the sccache one.

- **actionlint.** `Install actionlint` failed the `quick` job of 63 runs. In the 9 Nov failures curl got six 504s in about ten seconds. The `gh release download` fallback from #7295 is served by the same CDN, so it doesn't help in this outage. The actions cache that skips the download is saved per pull request ref, so a new pull request or one that hadn't run yet still hits the CDN.
- **Electron.** `electron` 44 has no postinstall. The first `require("electron")` downloads the zip from GitHub Releases with a single fetch and no retry. In `CI: Cua Spaces web UI and Electron shell` that first require happened inside the Electron shell's vitest step (8 Nov) and the Electron parity flows (9 Nov), and both failed on `HTTPError: Response code 504 ... electron-v44.9.1-linux-x64.zip` followed by "Electron failed to install correctly".

## What changed

- `install-actionlint`: curl now backs off exponentially (up to six retries, two minutes at most) instead of retrying every 2 s. When both GitHub downloads fail, it builds the pinned version with `go install github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@v<version>`, which comes from proxy.golang.org and does not touch the release CDN. It uses the newest Go in the runner's tool cache, as `install-release-tools.sh` does.
- New `install-electron` action: it restores `@electron/get`'s download cache from actions/cache (one entry per Electron version, OS and arch), then runs Electron's own `install.js` up to four times, waiting 15, 30 and 45 s between attempts. `install.js` still checks the zip against the package's `checksums.json`. A cache hit makes no network call.
- `ci-cua-spaces-web.yml` runs `install-electron` in the `test` job and in the Electron leg of `parity`, before any step loads `electron`.

## Scope

These are retries plus a second source. Nothing soft-fails. Both tools are needed for the check to mean anything (`CUA_CI_REQUIRE_TOOLS` makes `quick` fail, not skip, when actionlint is missing, and the Electron tests need the binary), so `continue-on-error` as #7152 used for sccache would turn an outage into a skipped check. Not covered: electron-builder's own 504s while packaging in `CD: Cua Spaces` and `Nightly: Cua Spaces` on 8 Nov (Electron itself had downloaded in those jobs, and the failing request came afterwards), and the cua-driver release installer's 504s in the release gate.

## Tradeoffs

A long outage now costs at most about two minutes of curl retries plus a `go install` (actionlint), or 90 s of waiting plus four attempts (Electron), before the job fails. Without an outage nothing changes except the cache restore.

## Blast Radius

Every workflow that installs actionlint (`CI: Quick` and the cua-sandbox action lint) and the `test` and Electron `parity` jobs of `CI: Cua Spaces web UI and Electron shell`.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: the `.github/scripts` test suite, actionlint on every workflow, and `bin/ci --quick`. One suite test, `test_cua_driver_installer_integrity.py::test_a_release_install_grants_nothing_on_kwin_and_says_how_to[False]`, fails the same way on main and doesn't touch these files.
- The new tests run the actions' real step scripts against stub tools: retry until success, the four-attempt bound, and the curl, then gh, then go order. The go-proxy case fails against main's `install-actionlint`.
- The Electron step was run against a real `npm install electron@44.9.1`. With no network and an empty cache it made four attempts and failed. With network it installed `dist/electron` and filled the cache. With `dist/` deleted and no network, it installed from the cache.
- The actionlint step was run with curl and gh stubbed to fail and a real Go. It built actionlint v1.7.12 and put it on the path.

Refs CUA-3977

title: fix(cua-driver): accept delivery_mode on invoke_menu so foreground menus work on Linux
body:
Fixes the 0.47.15 release gate failure (run 43136944355, `harness_gtk3_invoke_menu_live_path`). 0.47.16 would fail the same way.

**Cause.** #7386 made Linux background `invoke_menu` refuse instead of opening a menu, keeping foreground as the fallback. #7401 made the GTK3 harness pass `delivery_mode: foreground`, but `invoke_menu`'s closed contract schema had no `delivery_mode`, so the generic schema check refused it: `unknown argument delivery_mode; accepted: path, pid, window_id`. Nobody could request foreground, and the Linux code that handles it was unreachable.

**Design.** `delivery_mode` (`background` default | `foreground`) is added to the portable `InvokeMenuInput` contract, like click/type/hotkey, with the `input.delivery_mode` capability (the contract test requires the two to agree). Linux already consumed it; it no longer has to strip it before parsing. macOS and Windows accept it and keep their current menu behavior (Windows always activates; macOS refuses a background-app item and points to `bring_to_front`). The test is unchanged; the contract was the gap. Regenerated: manifest, Python and TypeScript bindings, reference docs, and the three MCP registry snapshots.

**Verification.** Contract and schema-consistency tests pass on macOS. The Linux GTK3 harness runs in the Linux E2E workflow on this PR (result in a comment below).

For users: callers can now ask for a foreground menu invocation on Linux when background refuses.

After merge a new release (0.47.17) is needed.

title: fix(images): list [omarchy] first in the Omarchy image's pacman.conf
body:
Fixes the failed Omarchy image release (run 43149810809, `omarchy / release`, build/amd64).

What changed for users: the Omarchy image builds again and ships a Hyprland plugin that matches Omarchy's own Hyprland.

Cause: Omarchy's `pacman-edge.conf` lists `[omarchy]` before `[core]`/`[extra]`, so its patched `hyprland 0.57.2-2` wins over Arch's `0.57.2-1`. Fix: put `[omarchy]` first, as Omarchy does. With the plugin pin now derived from Omarchy's Hyprland, no exact-pkgrel pin is needed on our side.

Checked: `bin/ci --quick`. The image build itself runs in the release workflow after merge.

title: test(lume): prove installer resolution never reads the repo-wide Latest release
body:
Fixes #2611

## Why
Most of #2611 is already on main. #3753 removed `--make-latest` from `cd-swift-lume.yml`, and #6578 removed the unused `LATEST_RELEASE_URL` from the Lume installer. Two parts were still open. The installer's version resolution had no behavioural test against a monorepo release list, and the release guide still said Lume's installer "may use the repository-wide latest release as a fallback".

## What changed
- `test_release_channel_installers.py` runs the installer's `get_latest_lume_tag` with `curl` stubbed to serve a release list in which `cua-driver-rs` and `cua-spaces` releases sit next to Lume drafts, a release candidate and competing nightly builds. The tests check three things. The baked version resolves its exact `lume-v*` tag without calling the API. `LUME_VERSION` wins over the baked version. The stable and nightly fallbacks pick the highest published Lume tag in numeric order and only ever request the release list, never `/releases/latest`.
- `docs/component-release-workflow.md` now states that Lume publishes with `make_latest: false` and gives the installer's resolution order per channel.

## Scope
Tests and docs only. The workflow, the installer and the release helper are unchanged. The existing `test_lume_release_publication.py` already asserts that Lume publication sends `prerelease: false` and `make_latest: "false"`, and `test_release_latest_policy.py` fails if any workflow passes `--make-latest`. The "notarized assets" criterion needs a real tagged macOS release, so this PR does not cover it.

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks: the release-channel, Lume publication, Latest-policy, no-Latest-consumer and release-helper tests pass.
- Mutation runs against the installer each turned the new tests red: lexical instead of numeric sort, lexical ordering of the nightly build number, a `releases/latest` lookup in place of the list, and a disabled baked-version branch.
- The full `.github/scripts/tests/` suite has one failure on both main and this branch, a cua-driver KWin hint test (`test_a_release_install_grants_nothing_on_kwin_and_says_how_to[False]`) that sees the host's KWin through `/usr/bin`. It is unrelated to this change.

title: [Bug]: CLI recording start omits record_video, causing cua-driver recording render to fail with "recording.mp4 not found"
body:
### Primary area
CLI

### Summary
`cua-driver recording start <output-dir>` does not pass `record_video: true` to the daemon and provides no `--video` / `--record-video` flag, causing any subsequent `cua-driver recording render <dir> <out.mp4>` to fail with `recording.mp4 not found`.

### Reproduction
1. Start the Cua Driver daemon: `cua-driver serve` (or ensure it is running).
2. Start trajectory recording via CLI: `cua-driver recording start /tmp/my-recording`
3. Execute any actions, then stop recording: `cua-driver recording stop`
4. Try to render the recording to MP4: `cua-driver recording render /tmp/my-recording /tmp/my-recording/output.mp4`

### Expected behavior
The recording should either record the video by default or provide a `--video` / `--record-video` flag in `cua-driver recording start`, allowing `cua-driver recording render` to find `recording.mp4` and render successfully.

### Actual behavior
`cua-driver recording render` immediately exits with code 1 and errors:
```text
Rendering /tmp/my-recording -> /tmp/my-recording/output.mp4
Render failed: load "/tmp/my-recording": recording.mp4 not found at /tmp/my-recording/recording.mp4
```

### Environment
- Cua component and version: `cua-driver 0.47.17` (darwin-universal)
- Operating system and architecture: macOS 26 (Tahoe) arm64 / Apple Silicon
- Application/browser: N/A (Core trajectory recording)

### Evidence
In `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs` (under subcommand `"start"`):
```rust
let req = crate::serve::DaemonRequest {
    method: "call".into(),
    name: Some("start_recording".into()),
    args: Some(serde_json::json!({
        "output_dir": output_dir
    })),
    // ...
};
```
The CLI command only sends `"output_dir"`, omitting `"record_video"`. Since `start_recording` defaults `record_video` to `false`, the daemon never initializes video recording.

Meanwhile, `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/recording_loader.rs` enforces:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum LoadError {
    // ...
    #[error("recording.mp4 not found at {0}")]
    VideoMissing(PathBuf),
}
```
Thus, `render` hard-fails when `recording.mp4` is absent.

### Workaround and additional context
Currently, callers must bypass the CLI and invoke the MCP tool directly with `{"output_dir": "...", "record_video": true}`.

---

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 核心领域
CLI 命令行工具

### 问题概述
`cua-driver recording start <output-dir>` 在向后台守护进程发送请求时未传递 `record_video: true`，且 CLI 没有提供 `--video` 或 `--record-video` 选项，导致后续执行 `cua-driver recording render <dir> <out.mp4>` 时必然抛出 `recording.mp4 not found` 崩溃。

### 复现步骤
1. 启动 daemon：`cua-driver serve`
2. 通过命令行启动录像：`cua-driver recording start /tmp/my-recording`
3. 执行任意操作后停止：`cua-driver recording stop`
4. 尝试渲染视频：`cua-driver recording render /tmp/my-recording /tmp/my-recording/output.mp4`

### 期望表现
CLI 的 `recording start` 应该默认开启录像或提供 `--video` 开关，使得录制完成后具备基础视频，让 `recording render` 顺利完成导出。

### 实际表现
`cua-driver recording render` 直接退出并报错：
`Render failed: load "...": recording.mp4 not found at .../recording.mp4`

### 源码证据
- 在 `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs` 中，处理 `"start"` 时仅硬编码发送了 `output_dir`，未携带 `record_video` 参数。
- 在 `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/recording_loader.rs` 中，渲染器将 `recording.mp4` 作为强校验依赖，缺少则直接报错退出。

</details>

title: [Feature]: Inject Chromium flags (--force-renderer-accessibility / --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows) on macOS background launch
body:
### Primary area
Cua Driver / macOS

### Summary
[Feature]: Support injecting Chromium accessibility and anti-occlusion flags (`--force-renderer-accessibility`, `--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows`) when launching browsers on macOS.

### User problem
When launching Google Chrome or Chromium in the background on macOS (via `launch_app`), macOS often classifies the newly opened background window as non-active / off-space (`on_current_space: false`). In this state, Chromium pauses painting and accessibility tree updates for performance optimization, causing `get_window_state` to observe an empty or stale DOM tree (returning only outer frame controls with the diagnostic message: `This browser window is on another Space. Chromium pauses painting and accessibility updates while its window is not visible...`).

### Desired outcome
Allow `launch_app` or browser preparation routines on macOS to automatically or optionally inject flags such as:
- `--force-renderer-accessibility`
- `--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows`
This ensures Chromium exposes the full web document accessibility tree even when the window is initialized in the background or off-screen.

---

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 核心领域
Cua Driver / macOS 平台

### 问题概述
[功能建议]：支持在 macOS 后台拉起 Chromium 时自动或可选注入无障碍与防遮挡休眠参数（`--force-renderer-accessibility` 与 `--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows`）。

### 用户痛点
在 macOS 下通过 `launch_app` 后台启动 Chrome 时，系统常将窗口判定为非活跃状态。Chromium 会自动暂停页面绘制和无障碍树更新，导致 `get_window_state` 抓不到内部 DOM 元素。

### 期望效果
在启动浏览器时注入上述两个核心参数，防止后台窗口被休眠，使后台自动化依然能够稳定捕获完整的网页 DOM 树。

</details>

title: [Feature]: Support viewport-scoped DOM capture / review mode to avoid full-desktop capture in automated PR reviews
body:
### Primary area
Cua Driver

### Summary
[Feature]: Support a lightweight viewport-scoped DOM capture / PR review mode to avoid full-desktop capture and large artifact sizes.

### User problem
In automated PR reviews and CI workflows (e.g., verifying web UI changes and generating review comments on GitHub), capturing the full 5K Retina desktop produces screenshots exceeding 1.8MB per turn and risks exposing background application windows, notifications, and menu bar items.

### Desired outcome
Provide a viewport/window-scoped capture option (or lightweight review mode) that clips capture output strictly to the targeted browser viewport or content bounds without capturing the surrounding desktop, drastically reducing artifact sizes (down to ~20-30KB) and eliminating privacy exposure.

---

title: fix(lume): refuse writable VM starts when host free space is unsafe
body:
## Why
`lume run` started a writable sparse-disk VM even when the host volume had almost no allocatable space. The guest sees only the image's logical free space, so once the backing file had to grow, guest writes failed and the APFS Data volume broke. Now `runVM` checks host free space before it creates the VM and refuses the start with a clear error.

## What changed
- New `HostDiskSpace.shortfall` (`libs/lume/src/VM/HostDiskSpace.swift`). It groups the writable disks by host volume and needs `min(their logical size, 2 GiB)` free on each volume. Free space comes from `volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage`, the same key the disk resizer uses.
- `LumeController.runVM` runs the check after path validation and before `loadVM`. The check covers the primary disk (or `--disk-path` override) and any additional disks. Mount and USB images attach read-only, so they are left out.
- New `VMError.insufficientHostSpace`. Its message names the volume and the required and available bytes, and says the VM was not started.

## Scope
Covers the start path that `lume run`, `lume serve` and MCP share. It leaves out the issue's other suggestions: a check at clone time (clones are APFS copy-on-write and take no new space until written) and showing host-capacity risk in `get`. It also leaves out `UnattendedInstaller`'s direct `vm.run` during setup.

## Tradeoffs
The 2 GiB reserve is a fixed floor, not the disk's full unallocated size. Requiring the full logical size would block most normal hosts, since a 50 GiB sparse disk would need 50 GiB free. The floor catches the near-full case the issue reports (about 115 MiB free). It does not promise the guest can fill its whole disk. If free space cannot be read, the start goes ahead, the same way the resizer behaves.

## Blast Radius
Any `lume run` on a volume with less than 2 GiB free now fails where it used to start. That is the intended change. Existing tests use 1 KiB disks, so they need only 1 KiB free.

## Verification
- New `libs/lume/tests/HostDiskSpaceTests.swift`. A sparse 50 GiB disk with 115 MiB free is refused, the error names required and available bytes, no virtualization service is created, and config and disk stay unchanged. Starts with the reserve free still succeed, disks on one volume are pooled, and a volume that cannot be read does not block.
- The four pure `HostDiskSpace` tests passed under Swift 6.0 on Linux and failed when the comparison was disabled. The macOS build and the controller-level tests run in the macOS CI job.

Fixes #2767

title: fix(cua-driver): render macOS cursors on every display and remove all action marks
body:
## Summary

On macOS, actions in a window on a secondary display succeed while the synthetic cursor is invisible: the overlay covers only the main display. Create an overlay surface for every active display, render cursor tiles at each display's backing scale, and preserve global coordinates for monitors with negative origins. Rebuild surfaces when the display layout changes, paint cursor artwork across display seams, and keep the session badge on the display containing the cursor anchor. Retain the newer region-based renderer.

Also remove every agent cursor action mark. Whatever the agent does (click, type, press keys, scroll, drag, open a menu), the cursor is always the plain arrow: the shared renderer no longer paints action marks, a move or click no longer starts one, and the macOS focus box around a clicked element and the GNOME helper action cues are gone. The `cursor.marks` setting is retired but still accepted and ignored, so old configs and callers do not error; it no longer appears in `get_config`. Generated reference docs, the guide and the Skills text are updated.

## Related work

Salvaged from #3019: adapts injaneity's display geometry to the current renderer. Contributor credit is preserved in the commit trailer and source.

Refs #5336, #2992. Related partial fixes: #5603 and #5650.

RFC: not required; this corrects cursor presentation without changing SDK, CLI, MCP, input-delivery, or permission contracts.

## Compatibility and risk

- Multi-display surface management is macOS-specific. The mark removal is in the shared renderer and applies to macOS, Windows, X11, and Wayland (the Linux and Windows lanes were not compiled on the Mac that built this). The existing `paint_cursor` entry point retains its behavior except that it never paints action artwork; per-display rendering can suppress duplicate badges.
- Rendering risk includes display-coordinate conversion, mixed scaling, display changes, layer lifetime, and ordering relative to target windows. Replacement surfaces are built before retiring the live set, and disposal runs on AppKit's main queue after queued presentations.
- No changes to the physical pointer or click targeting. Revert the commits to roll back.

## Validation

Current rebased head:
- `bin/ci --quick`: 5 passed, 4 heavy/generated checks skipped as required on this shared host.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Earlier local candidate, before rebasing onto current main:
- macOS platform library suite: 727 passed, 12 opt-in tests ignored.
- Shared cursor library suite after removing the click mark: 154 passed.
- Regression coverage: negative X/Y and lower/right display layouts; 1x/2x tile dimensions; cursor artwork on both sides of a display seam; clearing the departed display; click pixels matching the idle arrow with marks enabled.
- Built and installed with `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.sh`. Verified visible overlay pixels on both connected displays (main 1180×820 at origin; secondary 1512×982 at −117,820) and completed Calculator operations through the standalone CLI.
- Strict Clippy on that candidate encountered an existing Rust 1.98 `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint in unchanged code. The scoped library run passed with that existing lint suppressed.

Pending before readiness:
- Rebased-head unit, Clippy, generated-reference/binding and cross-platform CI checks.
- Canonical cross-platform desktop E2E matrix on the final candidate.
- Physical hotplug/rearrangement and additional mixed-scale monitor layouts. These have not been certified by the two-display smoke test.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The description matches the aggregated final diff.
- [x] No RFC is required for this presentation fix.
- [x] Tests and platform evidence are included; remaining gaps are explicit.
- [x] The title describes the production behavior and triggers a Cua Driver patch release.
- [x] External contributor credit is preserved.
- [x] Required shared-host `bin/ci --quick` passed.
