title: build(deps): bump soupsieve from 2.9.2 to 4.0 in /libs/cua-bench-rl
body:
Bumps [soupsieve](https://github.com/facelessuser/soupsieve) from 2.9.2 to 4.0.
Release notes

Sourced from soupsieve's releases.

4.0

  • BREAK: The contents of an HTML template are no longer treated as part of the document. Selectors do not descend into a template, and elements inside one can't see beyond it, which also applies to pseudo-classes such as :lang(), :disabled, and :default. select and filter will still reach the contents of a template when they are called on the template itself, for example soup.template.select('p'). See the FAQ for more information.
  • BREAK: The contents of an iframe are no longer treated as a separate document, as they are not one in a browser. Elements in an iframe are normal children, so :root does not match them, and :default, :indeterminate, :checked, :dir(), :lang(), and :read-write treat them like any other element. Recent versions of html.parser, lxml, and html5lib all escape the contents of an iframe like a browser does, so this mostly affects XHTML, Python versions that still don't escape such content in their specific html.parser, and elements added to an iframe by hand. :-soup-contains() now also includes the escaped text in an iframe. See the FAQ for more information.
  • NEW: Update :disabled and :enabled to treat option and optgroup elements inside a disabled select as disabled, following a recent HTML specification update.
  • FIX: Fix the subsequent-sibling combinator and :has(~ ...) never matching top level elements of a fragment that has no root element, unless caching was disabled.
  • FIX: :indeterminate now treats a radio button group without a form as extending across the whole document instead of the top level element that contains it, and it no longer ignores radio buttons at the top level.
  • FIX: Fix :default to treat a button with a missing or invalid type, and an input with type="image", as submit buttons.
  • FIX: Fix :in-range and :out-of-range raising TypeError when the document contains an input without a type attribute.
  • FIX: :read-write (and :read-only) now treat contenteditable="plaintext-only" elements as editing hosts and match the editable elements inside an editing host, following the nearest contenteditable state.
  • FIX: :read-write (and :read-only) now ignore contenteditable on non-HTML elements, such as an SVG foreignObject, as the attribute only applies to HTML elements. Such elements inherit the state of their parent.
  • FIX: :checked now only matches the last radio button with a checked attribute in a radio button group, as in a browser, where a group is the radio buttons with the same name and form, including the form attribute. :default still matches all of them, and the contents of a template are unaffected as they are not connected.
  • FIX: :dir() and :defined no longer affect the rest of the selector list they are in. Previously, a selector list that used either of them could not have its combinators cross an iframe, ignored the specified namespaces, and matched nothing in XML, not even the parts that didn't use them. They still do not match in XML, but :not(:dir(ltr)) and :not(:defined) now do.
  • FIX: :default and :indeterminate now honor the form attribute, which can associate a submit button or radio button with a form it is not in, or leave it without a form. It is ignored in a template, as in the HTML specification. Submit buttons outside of a form can now be its default button.
  • FIX: :default, :checked, and :indeterminate now handle a form inside a form like a browser. In HTML, a browser ignores the nested form and takes its end tag for that of the parent, which matters for parsers that keep the nested form, such as html.parser. In XHTML and in a template, nested forms are real forms.
  • FIX: :checked now matches the option that a browser would select. Without multiple, that is only the last option with a selected attribute in a select, and if there are none and the select shows a single option, the first option that is not disabled. :default still only considers the selected attribute.
  • FIX: Fix [attribute!=value] excluding values that only start with the specified value, and in XML documents, type values that contain a newline.
  • FIX: Match the values of every attribute that the HTML specification lists as ASCII case insensitive (rel, method, lang, dir, ...) without ASCII case sensitivity on HTML elements in HTML documents, not just type. Non-HTML elements are matched case sensitively.
  • FIX: :dir() now matches non-HTML elements, such as SVG and MathML, by the direction they inherit from their

title: macOS: LibreOffice aborts on accessibility text inserts (ImpEditEngine::ImpInsertText); build a minimal repro for upstream
body:
Found during the raw-macos-pure bench run (onigiri, 2026-11-13), on scratch branch `exp/raw-macos-pure`.

Writing a LibreOffice Calc cell from the background works by selecting the cell through AX, inserting into the formula bar's input line, and pressing the bar's Accept button. But soffice aborts inside its own accessibility insert path (`ImpEditEngine::ImpInsertText`):

title: fix(cua-driver): run_steps takes its window from element tokens and accepts flat step arguments
body:
`run_steps` rejected two common batch shapes before running anything, and each rejection costs the caller a turn.

- A batch whose steps target elements only by `element_token`, plus `observe`, was refused with "`pid` and `window_id` are required (no step names a window to inherit from)". An element token names its snapshot, and so its window and process. A step with a live token now counts as naming that window at parse time, and at run time it sets the window that `observe` and later steps inherit. A stale or unknown token still fails closed with the same error. The core reaches the snapshot store through a new `ToolRegistry` token-window resolver that each platform installs, so core takes no platform dependency.

title: feat(cua-driver): background native drag-and-drop on macOS under serve --no-overlay
body:
Refs CUA-4064. Supersedes #5546 (the experimental held-pointer prototype), ported onto current main.

## What changes for users

An agent can now reorder a native macOS list, or drag an object onto a drop zone, in a background window. The user's pointer doesn't move, the window isn't raised and the frontmost app doesn't change. Before this change the `drag` tool refused these drags with `background_unavailable` / `drag_and_drop_session`.

## Why it failed under `serve --no-overlay`

The held-pointer route needs a small shield window that it creates on the main queue. With the cursor overlay off, `serve` had its main thread join the serve thread, so nothing ever drained the main queue. The shield was never made, and the drag fell back to the refusal.

## Changes

- **serve:** the main thread runs the AppKit loop as an accessory app with no Dock icon whenever the process has a graphic session, whether or not the overlay or PiP is on. Without a graphic session (SSH, a LaunchDaemon, headless CI) it still just joins, because `NSApplication` aborts there. `main_thread_loop` makes the choice and has unit tests.
- **pointer hold** (from #5546): it now presses only once the shield is on screen under the pointer. `orderFrontRegardless` returns before the window server shows the window, and in testing a press in that gap reached the window under the pointer.
- **drag:** a drop lands in whatever app-level window is on top at the drop point. If another window covers the drop point, the driver doesn't try the hold. It returns the refusal with `drop_point_covered: true`, rather than dropping into the covering window. Click-through system windows (Dock, Notification Center, menu bar) and desktop widgets are ignored.
- **Default on:** `CUA_DRIVER_BACKGROUND_DND=0` turns the route off. `CUA_DRIVER_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_DND=0` also turns it off.
- **Port:** `drag_at_xy_background_held` keeps main's macOS 27 window-local stamp (#7372) through a shared `drag_window_location` helper.
- **Docs:** operate guide, drag tool description and reference, skill `MACOS.md`, action-support matrix.

## How the hold works

1. The driver posts the gesture to the source window as before.
2. When the drag-and-drop session starts, it places a 40 pt, nearly transparent, non-activating panel under the stationary pointer, at shielding level + 1.
3. It posts one hardware `leftMouseDown` there, so the window server sees the button as held.
4. It drives the session with the window-routed drags and settles at the drop point.
5. It posts the hardware `leftMouseUp`, then the window-routed release.

The shield absorbs both hardware events. If the user moves the pointer during the roughly two seconds the hold lasts, the result is an error, not a reported drop.

## Testing

Live test on a macOS 26.5.2 virtual machine. The daemon was the bundled `CuaDriver.app` started by its LaunchAgent as `serve --socket … --dangerously-bypass-approvals --no-overlay`, with no extra environment variables. The test app had an `NSTableView` with drag-to-reorder, in the background, with TextEdit frontmost.

| Case | Before (main) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reorder by drag, drop point uncovered | refused, list unchanged | row 0 moved to row 3, reorder event recorded |
| Same, another window covering the drop point | refused | refused with `drop_point_covered: true`; list and covering window unchanged |
| Pointer position | unchanged | unchanged |
| Frontmost app | TextEdit | TextEdit |
| Window order | unchanged | unchanged |

A separate AppKit test window received `validateDrop` for each row along the path, then the drop (`op=16`, move).

- Unit tests: `main_thread_loop` choice, shield-under-pointer check, drop point covered or uncovered (including system overlays, the shield and the drag image), default-on flag parsing, plus the held gesture tests carried over from #5546.
- `bin/ci --quick` passes (it added one missing SPDX header). The generated-reference check failed locally on a toolchain problem, not on a diff, so GitHub CI checks it.

## Open

- The route posts two hardware events (one down, one up) at the pointer. Nothing visible changes, but tools that count HID events will see them.
- It was tested on macOS 26.5.2 only. The window-server behaviour it relies on is not a documented contract.

Draft: this changes agent-facing default behaviour, so it needs a review before merge.

title: build(deps): bump soupsieve from 2.10 to 4.0
body:
Bumps [soupsieve](https://github.com/facelessuser/soupsieve) from 2.10 to 4.0.
Release notes

Sourced from soupsieve's releases.

4.0

  • BREAK: The contents of an HTML template are no longer treated as part of the document. Selectors do not descend into a template, and elements inside one can't see beyond it, which also applies to pseudo-classes such as :lang(), :disabled, and :default. select and filter will still reach the contents of a template when they are called on the template itself, for example soup.template.select('p'). See the FAQ for more information.
  • BREAK: The contents of an iframe are no longer treated as a separate document, as they are not one in a browser. Elements in an iframe are normal children, so :root does not match them, and :default, :indeterminate, :checked, :dir(), :lang(), and :read-write treat them like any other element. Recent versions of html.parser, lxml, and html5lib all escape the contents of an iframe like a browser does, so this mostly affects XHTML, Python versions that still don't escape such content in their specific html.parser, and elements added to an iframe by hand. :-soup-contains() now also includes the escaped text in an iframe. See the FAQ for more information.
  • NEW: Update :disabled and :enabled to treat option and optgroup elements inside a disabled select as disabled, following a recent HTML specification update.
  • FIX: Fix the subsequent-sibling combinator and :has(~ ...) never matching top level elements of a fragment that has no root element, unless caching was disabled.
  • FIX: :indeterminate now treats a radio button group without a form as extending across the whole document instead of the top level element that contains it, and it no longer ignores radio buttons at the top level.
  • FIX: Fix :default to treat a button with a missing or invalid type, and an input with type="image", as submit buttons.
  • FIX: Fix :in-range and :out-of-range raising TypeError when the document contains an input without a type attribute.
  • FIX: :read-write (and :read-only) now treat contenteditable="plaintext-only" elements as editing hosts and match the editable elements inside an editing host, following the nearest contenteditable state.
  • FIX: :read-write (and :read-only) now ignore contenteditable on non-HTML elements, such as an SVG foreignObject, as the attribute only applies to HTML elements. Such elements inherit the state of their parent.
  • FIX: :checked now only matches the last radio button with a checked attribute in a radio button group, as in a browser, where a group is the radio buttons with the same name and form, including the form attribute. :default still matches all of them, and the contents of a template are unaffected as they are not connected.
  • FIX: :dir() and :defined no longer affect the rest of the selector list they are in. Previously, a selector list that used either of them could not have its combinators cross an iframe, ignored the specified namespaces, and matched nothing in XML, not even the parts that didn't use them. They still do not match in XML, but :not(:dir(ltr)) and :not(:defined) now do.
  • FIX: :default and :indeterminate now honor the form attribute, which can associate a submit button or radio button with a form it is not in, or leave it without a form. It is ignored in a template, as in the HTML specification. Submit buttons outside of a form can now be its default button.
  • FIX: :default, :checked, and :indeterminate now handle a form inside a form like a browser. In HTML, a browser ignores the nested form and takes its end tag for that of the parent, which matters for parsers that keep the nested form, such as html.parser. In XHTML and in a template, nested forms are real forms.
  • FIX: :checked now matches the option that a browser would select. Without multiple, that is only the last option with a selected attribute in a select, and if there are none and the select shows a single option, the first option that is not disabled. :default still only considers the selected attribute.
  • FIX: Fix [attribute!=value] excluding values that only start with the specified value, and in XML documents, type values that contain a newline.
  • FIX: Match the values of every attribute that the HTML specification lists as ASCII case insensitive (rel, method, lang, dir, ...) without ASCII case sensitivity on HTML elements in HTML documents, not just type. Non-HTML elements are matched case sensitively.
  • FIX: :dir() now matches non-HTML elements, such as SVG and MathML, by the direction they inherit from their

title: fix(cua-driver): read hidden Chromium windows as they are now
body:
## What

On macOS, accessibility reads of a hidden or fully covered Chromium/Electron window now show the page as it is, not as it was one action ago.

Chromium sends a page's accessibility changes to the browser process on a rendering pass, and an occluded window gets none. After an action changes the page (an `AXPress`, a value write), every accessibility read of that window keeps returning the tree from before the action, until the page is asked something else. The press itself works, but:

- the read after it shows the old state, so a working press looks like it did nothing;
- the next press appears to apply the previous one (reads are always one action behind);
- `set_value` read-back can report a write as not applied.

Any accessibility request the page receives makes it send its pending changes first. A hit-test is the request with no effect on the page, so before reading a window the driver now hit-tests the window's `AXWebArea` (only for processes that accepted the Chromium accessibility opt-in; native apps are untouched):

- `ax::tree` walks (`get_window_state`, role/name lookups, `verify_state`, `page`) flush each walked window first;
- `set_value` flushes before its before/after `AXValue` reads.

Refs CUA-4064.

## Root cause

Checked live on an Electron app in a background, fully covered window (macOS 26.5). The original suspicion, that role/name lookups pressed a detached DOM node from a cached snapshot, did not hold: lookups already do a fresh read, and the press reaches the live node. It changed the app's state on disk right away. Only the reads lagged:

| step (window covered) | ID field read right after |
| --- | --- |
| press "Boreal" | previous event (stale) |
| press "Aster" | Boreal (one behind) |
| hit-test at the web area, then read | Aster (current) |

With a hit-test before each read, five presses in a row each read back the event just pressed.

## Tests

- Unit: the flush applies only to the process lifetime that accepted the Chromium opt-in (relaunch at a recycled pid and unreadable lifetimes fail closed), and the hit-test point is inside the visible part of the web area.
- Live, Electron app in a fully covered background window, five role/name presses in a row (`run_script`, `click({role, name})`, then a role/name read of the ID field):
  - before: every read showed the event pressed one step earlier;
  - after: every read showed the event just pressed. A list re-render (`Update event`), then a press by role/name, and a `set_value` read-back were current too.

title: fix(cua-driver): set a background popup by type-select instead of opening its menu
body:
Refs CUA-4064. Stacked on #7497 (base branch `fix/bg-popup-set-value-no-raise`); review that one first.

## What changes for users

When an agent sets a popup in an app that sits behind your window, it can now choose the item without the app's window flashing above yours, in the cases where macOS allows it. Where it can't, nothing changes and the agent is told why, as in #7497. An agent can no longer open such a popup's menu (and raise its window) by pressing an arrow key, Space or Return on it.

## What the driver does

**`set_value` on a covered background popup.** Before refusing, the driver tries AppKit type-select:

1. It focuses the closed popup (the route `press_key` with an `element_token` uses: in-app key window, no activation).
2. It types the item's title up to its first space. A space, like Return or an arrow key, would open the menu.
3. It reads the popup back. AppKit applies type-select when typing pauses (about one second).

If the popup shows the item, the result is `effect: "confirmed"` with `popup_route: "type_select"`. If not, the driver gives focus back to the element that had it and returns #7497's `popup_menu_would_raise_window` refusal. The refusal now has a `type_select` field that says why (`app_not_active`, `item_not_chosen`, `popup_not_focused`, `title_starts_with_a_menu_key`). The menu is never opened in either case.

**Limit.** AppKit applies a closed popup's type-select only in an app it counts as active (`NSApp.isActive`, which the app reports as `AXFrontmost`). An app that has stayed in the background is not active, so it receives the keys but ignores them. The driver therefore types only when `AXFrontmost` is true, and otherwise refuses at once, without typing anything.

An app can count itself active while the user's app is frontmost. This happens when the app activated itself, for example to show an alert or sheet that was answered in the background, and the driver then gave the front back to the user's app. That is the common case for a form behind a permission prompt, and type-select works there.

**`press_key` on a covered background popup.** `up`, `down`, `space` or `return`/`enter` with no modifiers, on a closed popup button whose window another app's window covers, is refused with `background_unavailable`, reason `popup_menu_would_raise_window`. The target is the `element_token`, or the window's focused element when there is no token. These keys open the menu, which raises the window. The refusal points at `set_value`, and so does the existing refusal for a background `click` on such a popup. Letters and digits still go through.

Foreground behaviour, uncovered windows and already-open menus are unchanged.

## Testing

Live, on a macOS 26.5 VM, with the daemon started by its LaunchAgent (`serve --no-overlay`). Each test app sat behind a frontmost TextEdit window. A sampler read the frontmost app and the window order every ~2 ms during each call.

| Case | Result | Window raised | Frontmost app changed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `set_value` "Operations" on a native popup, after a permission sheet answered in the background | selected, read back, app state updated | no | no |
| Same popup, `set_value` "Research" | selected | no | no |
| `set_value` on a popup in a never-activated app | refused, `type_select: "app_not_active"`, value unchanged | no | no |
| `press_key down` on a covered popup | refused, value unchanged | no | no |
| `set_value` after `bring_to_front` (foreground) | menu route as before, selected | n/a | n/a |

A small AppKit probe app that logs `keyDown`, key-window state and `NSApp.isActive` confirmed the limit. In a never-activated app the popup became first responder and got every key, but `isKeyWindow` and `isActive` were false and the item never changed. After the app had activated itself once (a sheet, answered in the background), the same keys selected the item one second after the last key. A variant that briefly activated the app itself (no window raise) changed the frontmost app for about 110 ms, and the app resigned before the type-select interval ended, so nothing was selected. That route is not used.

- Unit tests: type-select typing and read-back (whole title, shared prefixes, stopping before a space, a first word that names another item, an app that ignores the keys, a failed key post), which keys open a popup menu, the `press_key` gate (background only, not the pixel form), and the refusal text that points at `set_value`.
- `bin/ci --quick` passes. Clippy (`-D warnings`) and the unit tests of `platform-macos` and `cua-driver-core` pass. The generated cua-driver reference is regenerated, which also brings in #7497's description changes.

## Open

- In the background, type-select only helps an app that counts itself active. A popup in an app that has never been active still needs the user's agreement and `bring_to_front`.
- An app that counts itself active while another app is frontmost is a side effect of how the driver hands the front back after an app activates itself. That is worth its own look; this PR only reads that state.

Draft: this changes agent-facing behaviour, so it needs a review before merge.

## Follow-up: a window the app shows by itself is not the activation's

When the in-app activation records are posted, the popup was refused (`type_select: "activation_showed_windows"`) whenever a new window of the app was on screen afterwards. An app can also put up a window of its own in that moment, for example a banner it shows a fraction of a second after an earlier field set, and it does so whether it is active or not. Setting a text field and then the popup in one `run_steps` hit this intermittently: the banner landed between the window snapshot and the read-back, and the popup was refused although the activation showed nothing.

- Now, when windows appear during the activation, it is undone and they are read again once the app counts itself inactive. A window that goes away with the activation (a panel AppKit shows only in an active app) is still refused. A window that stays is the app's own: it counts as already there, and the activation is tried once more (at most two attempts).
- `run_steps`: a failed step's report keeps the result's structured `reason` and `type_select`, and the step line ends with `(reason: ..., type_select: ...)`, because the bounded message cuts a refusal before it says why.

Testing: reproduced live on a macOS VM with the previous build (text field set, then popup set in one `run_steps`, a covering window in front; refused 13 of 19 fresh launches; debug log `miss=ActivationShowedWindows`; a window poller showed the app's own banner appearing during the call and staying while the app was inactive). Unit tests cover an activation-only panel (refused), a window of the app's own appearing mid-activation (activated on the second try) and both at once (refused), plus the `run_steps` reason note. `platform-macos` and `cua-driver-core` unit tests, clippy `-D warnings` and `bin/ci --quick` pass. The new build itself has not been run live yet.

title: Linux: terminal-buffer text is not readable through get_window_state (AT-SPI Text gated out of value)
body:
## Summary

On Linux, a terminal's buffer text is exposed as an indexed AT-SPI node, but its AT-SPI Text interface content is gated out of the row's `value`. A caller therefore cannot read or verify terminal output through `get_window_state` / `verify_state`.

This is the case raised by nick-inkeep in a comment on the passive-observations RFC (#3903).

## Relation to #7566

#7566 (fixes #2958) publishes display-only rows as `observations`. That covers unindexed text, not this case: the terminal buffer node is indexed, so it stays in `elements`, and its text is still left out of `value`. #7566 does not change that.

## Expected

The terminal buffer's text is readable from the indexed row (or another typed field) within the existing read bounds, so `verify_state` can evaluate a predicate on terminal output.

Found while implementing #7566.

title: test(cua-driver): Windows E2E foreground state leaks between agent-cursor rows, causing input_delivery_stalled
body:
## Problem

In the Windows desktop E2E lane, `keyboard_first_session_places_its_cursor_on_the_target_window` (in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/agent_cursor_showcase_test.rs`) fails when `session_cursor_follows_a_desktop_scope_keyboard_first_action` runs before it in the same test binary. Its foreground `press_key` (`pid` + `window_id`, `delivery_mode:"foreground"`) is refused with `input_delivery_stalled`.

The desktop-scope row launches the native fixture, calls `bring_to_front` on it, settles for 300 ms, sends a desktop-scope `press_key`, ends its session and tears down. The next row then launches its own fixture and sends a window-targeted foreground `press_key`, which stalls. It looks like foreground state from the first row's `bring_to_front` and teardown leaks into the next row. The likeliest causes are a foreground lock or a foreground window that is gone or stale after the fixture exits, so the next foreground swap does not complete.

## Evidence

- New row named so that it ran first: the window-targeted row failed with `input_delivery_stalled` 2 of 2 times (runs 43314467121 and 43326094731).
- Same row at main, without the new row: passed (run 43330261783).
- After renaming the new row so it sorts second: both passed (run 43330244927 and the head run 43349361911).
- Not seen on macOS or Linux X11.

## Current mitigation

#7527 renamed the desktop-scope row so it sorts after the window-targeted row, and the row's doc comment says why. That hides the leak instead of fixing it. Any future row that calls `bring_to_front` and then tears down could break the rows that follow it.

## Expected

Each E2E row on Windows should start from a neutral foreground state no matter which rows ran before it. One way to get there is for teardown to restore or neutralise the foreground after `bring_to_front`, or for the driver's foreground swap to recover when the previous foreground window has gone away. Once that is fixed, the ordering constraint and its comment in `agent_cursor_showcase_test.rs` can go.

## Suggested check

Run the two rows in the bad order on the Windows lane, for example by temporarily renaming the desktop-scope row back so it sorts first, or by running it alone and then the window-targeted row in one binary, and confirm that the window-targeted row passes.

Related: #7527, #3011, and #2206 (the broader foreground-delivery activation and restore contract).

title: fix(cua-driver): declare libxkbcommon ourselves so no linker adds a 1.0 requirement
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: a `cua-driver` or `libcua_driver_sdk.so` built with the mold linker requires libxkbcommon 1.0 to load, so it does not start on distros with libxkbcommon 0.x (for example Ubuntu 20.04, which has 0.10). `the_crate_does_not_require_libxkbcommon_1_0` fails under mold.
- Cause: the `xkbcommon` crate wraps two libxkbcommon 1.0 functions (`xkb_utf32_to_keysym`, `xkb_keymap_key_get_mods_for_level`). The driver never calls the wrappers. GNU ld drops their imports with the dead code. mold keeps every import of a linked object, also when `--gc-sections` drops the code that uses it. mold 2.40.4 and 3.0.0 behave the same, and a 10-line C program shows it too, so this is how mold works, not a mold bug to wait for.
- What changed:
  - New `wayland::xkb` module. It declares only the libxkbcommon 0.5/0.6 calls that typing uses (context, keymap, state, keysym names), with the same names as the crate. `libei.rs`, `niri/keyboard.rs` and `text_keys.rs` only change their `use` line.
  - `Keysym` and `Keycode` come from `xkeysym` 0.2.1 (pure Rust, links nothing; the crate already used it).
  - The `xkbcommon` dependency is removed (4 lockfiles).
  - The two 1.0 functions stay run-time lookups (`text_keys::xkb1`), as before.

## Related work

Refs: none.

RFC: not required (no public contract change).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: none for builds with GNU ld. Builds with mold no longer require libxkbcommon 1.0.
- Risk and rollback: the new FFI matches the crate's wrappers one to one. A revert restores the crate.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - Linked with mold, before: `the_crate_does_not_require_libxkbcommon_1_0` fails (`V_1.0.0` present). After: it passes.
  - `readelf --version-info` on mold builds of `cua-driver` and `libcua_driver_sdk.so`: libxkbcommon `V_0.5.0 V_0.6.0` only.
  - New tests in `wayland::xkb`: keymap queries, state updates, keysym names, and refusals, on a self-contained keymap (no system XKB data).
  - `cargo clippy -D warnings` for platform-linux with and without `portal-input`; platform-linux unit tests; teleport-e2e and spaces-e2e unit tests.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - Local `bin/ci` also fails `overlay::tests::unreported_arrival_releases_the_waiter_after_the_cap` on a desktop session. That is a separate test bug, fixed in PR #7070.
  - The local disk guard stopped `bin/ci` before the generated-reference and UniFFI binding checks. CI runs them.

## Done when

- [x] mold build does not require libxkbcommon 1.0 (readelf, test above)
- [x] clippy clean with and without `portal-input`
- [ ] CI green
- [x] Agent review (GPT Sol, high): one finding, fixed

## Review

- Agent review (GPT Sol, high effort) of `f34c53c`: one finding. `Keymap` claimed `Send` and `Sync`, but libxkbcommon counts keymap references without atomics, so two threads that clone one keymap could free it early. The `xkbcommon` crate had neither impl. Fixed in `a9abbe3`: both impls removed. platform-linux builds with and without `portal-input`, so no call site needed them.
- No findings for FFI signatures and constants (checked against `xkbcommon.h`), wrapper behavior at every call site, symbol versions (only `V_0.5.0`/`V_0.6.0` imported) or feature gating.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`). Fork PR: the sign-off is the **CI: Quick** run.

title: fix(cua-driver): capture the Linux desktop on rootless Xwayland instead of failing with GetImage BadMatch
body:
## Why

`get_desktop_state` failed with `X11Error { error_kind: Match, ..., request_name: Some("GetImage") }` on WSLg, KDE/KWin, Hyprland and gamescope. All four give X11 clients a rootless Xwayland. Its root window holds no pixels, so a core `GetImage` of the root fails with BadMatch while each top-level window is still readable. `bad_value` in the reports is the root window id (konsorsiumai matched `0x4da` to `1242`), not a coordinate, and the failure happens on single-output layouts too. When the root read returns BadMatch, the X11 desktop capture now builds the frame from the windows.

## What changed

- `screenshot_display_bytes_x11`: if the root `GetImage` fails with BadMatch, the capture paints every viewable top-level window, border included, at its screen position from bottom to top, over black. It decodes pixels through the server's pixmap formats and the reply's visual, and blends depth-32 ARGB windows by their alpha. A window that goes away during the capture (BadMatch, BadWindow, BadDrawable) is skipped. Any other read failure is returned as an error. When the root can be read (Xorg, Xvfb), the capture reads it directly as before, now through the same decoder.
- Doctor `screen_capture_capability` on X11 now reads one root pixel instead of only connecting. In the rootless case it says the capture composes X11 windows only and points at `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`.
- `scripts/ci/linux/with-rootless-xwayland.sh` runs a command against headless sway's own rootless Xwayland. `ci-rust-linux.yml` runs the new live test under Xvfb and under that script.

## Scope

This covers the default X11 path (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND` unset) on any Xwayland that refuses root reads. Native Wayland windows are not part of the X screen, so they are missing from this frame and X11 windows under them show through. Desktop input in these sessions goes through X11 and reaches only X11 clients. The Wayland cascade is unchanged. The gamescope-specific capture that reddraggone9 suggested (`gamescope_control` or `gamescope_pipewire`) is not part of this change.

## Tradeoffs

The other option was to send this case to the Wayland cascade. WSLg's Weston has no screencopy and gamescope has no screencopy or portal, so that would still fail on two of the four reported desktops.

## Blast radius

Linux X11 desktop capture (`get_desktop_state`, the desktop capture-id admission check, recording snapshots) and the doctor message. On a server that can read the root, the only change is decoding through the server's pixel format instead of assuming 32-bit BGRX. A reader on Xorg or Xvfb sees the same image.

## Verification

- The new live test `capture::tests::live_desktop_capture_shows_stacked_windows_at_their_screen_position` maps two overlapping windows, one with a border. At the test-only commit, under rootless Xwayland, it fails with the issue's `X11Error { error_kind: Match, ... request_name: Some("GetImage") }`. At the head it passes under both rootless Xwayland and Xvfb.
- I ran a source-built `cua-driver serve` inside the rootless sway session with an `xeyes` window open. `get_desktop_state` wrote a 1280x720 PNG showing the window. Before the fix, the same call returned the issue's error. The doctor line reads "X11 reachable, but the root window cannot be read (rootless Xwayland); desktop capture composes the X11 windows only...".
- The scoped repository checks passed on Linux arm64: platform-linux lib tests, `clippy -D warnings` on platform-linux, and `cargo fmt --check`. The Windows and macOS platform crates are untouched and could not be built on this host. WSLg, KWin, Hyprland and gamescope themselves were not available. The repro uses sway's rootless Xwayland, which refuses root reads the same way.

Fixes #2932

risk: standard

title: cua-driver (Linux): capture native Wayland surfaces on gamescope via gamescope_control or gamescope_pipewire
body:
## Summary
On gamescope (Bazzite / SteamOS-style Gaming Mode), desktop capture can't include native Wayland surfaces. #7580 fixes the X11 `GetImage` BadMatch from #2932 by building the frame from the X11 windows of the rootless Xwayland. That frame holds X11 clients only. The Wayland cascade can't help on gamescope either: its socket (`gamescope-0`) has no `zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1` or `ext_image_copy_capture`, and Gaming Mode sessions run no xdg-desktop-portal.

## Proposal
When `gamescope-0` is present, add a capture path through gamescope's own globals:
- `gamescope_control`: `gamescopectl screenshot /tmp/x.png` uses it and returns the composited frame, native Wayland surfaces included (reported by reddraggone9 in #2932).
- `gamescope_pipewire`: the streaming equivalent.

Either would give a full composited frame on gamescope where the X11 window composition can't.

## Context
- Original report: #2932 (gamescope 3.17.0, Bazzite 44, single 3840x2160 output).
- Fix that ships the X11 window composition and leaves this out of scope: #7580.
- Not built or tested yet. No gamescope session was available when #7580 was verified.

title: cua-driver (Linux): native Wayland windows missing from capture on WSLg with CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1
body:
## Summary
On WSLg, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1` still doesn't capture native Wayland windows. WSLg's Weston exposes no wlroots screencopy, `ext-image-copy-capture-v1` or portal Screenshot, so the Wayland capture cascade (GNOME helper → wlroots screencopy → ext-image-copy-capture-v1 → portal Screenshot → X11) ends in the X11 step.

Since #7580, that X11 step no longer fails with the `GetImage` BadMatch from #2932. When the root read is refused, it builds the frame from the X11 windows. Native Wayland windows aren't on the X screen, though, so they're missing from the frame, and X11 windows under them show through.

## Expected
On WSLg, with the Wayland backend enabled, the desktop capture should include native Wayland windows. At minimum, `cua-driver doctor` and the capture result should say the frame has X11 windows only.

## Context
- Original report: #2932 (WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04, WSLg Weston + Xwayland). The reporter saw that `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1` falls back to the same X11 path.
- #7580 fixes the X11 failure and states this limit in its Scope section.
- Needs a capture source that WSLg's Weston actually offers. Which one is still open. A real WSLg session wasn't available when #7580 was verified.

title: raw-macos bench runtime: set_text doubles text in Electron fields; set_cell docs point to a sheet-tab press that does nothing
body:
Found while reviewing the raw-macos bench runs (onigiri, 2026-11-13), on scratch branch `exp/raw-macos-popups` (`libs/cua-driver-bench/automated-eval/macos_bench/tools/raw_macos/raw_mac.py`). Neither bug is about a macOS capability limit. Both are in the raw runtime's helpers, and both cost the model turns on the LibreOffice + Electron schedule task (CDB-G02).

**1. `raw.set_text` leaves the text in an Electron web field twice.**
`set_text` writes AXValue, waits 0.15 s, and if the read-back doesn't match it focuses the field, posts cmd+a and types the text. In the Daymark Calendar and Signal Quay Chat fields (Electron, web area), it returns `{"route": "typed", "ok": true}`. A later read of the same field shows the value twice (`11:00` becomes `11:0011:00`). Setting the field again, or writing AXValue directly, does not reliably clear it. One write followed by a 2 s wait read back correctly.
Suspected cause, not proven: the AXValue write reaches the page's state late, after the read-back has given up, so the page receives both the write and the typed text.
Expected: one route per web field, or a settle and re-read before reporting `ok`. For reference, the driver's `set_value` does not trust an AXValue echo in a web area (`platform-macos/src/tools/set_value.rs:209-217`).

**2. `raw.set_cell`'s docstring says to switch sheets by pressing the sheet tab, but that press does nothing.**
`raw_mac.py:858-859` says "switch sheets by pressing the sheet's tab (an AXRadioButton) first". In LibreOffice Calc on macOS, AXPress or AXSelected on the tab returns 0, and the sheet stays the same ("Sheet 1 of 2"). The model keeps retrying, then falls back to pixel clicks, which Calc ignores in the background. The command that works is the menu item Sheet ▸ Navigate ▸ To Next Sheet / To Previous Sheet. `raw.menu` can press it without opening a menu, the same way the driver's `invoke_menu` does (`platform-macos/src/tools/invoke_menu.rs:136`).
Expected: the docstring and tool description name `raw.menu(pid, ["Sheet", "Navigate", "To Next Sheet"])`, or `set_cell` takes a `sheet=` argument and switches through that menu itself.

Related: #7552 (the LibreOffice abort in the AX insert path that `set_cell` uses), #7551.

title: fix(cua-driver): make Linux browser prepare language independent
body:
## Why

On a non-English Linux desktop, existing-profile `browser_prepare` with Chromium never gets past setup or consent, because the Linux backend finds the omnibox and the "Allow remote debugging?" prompt by English names. This lands @loonghao's #3138 on current main, the Linux counterpart of #3135, and fixes a defect in it: on that branch the cleanup path pressed **Allow** on the consent prompt when it meant to press Cancel.

Salvaged from #3138

## What changed

- The consent prompt is found by structure: a native `alert` under the browser frame, with one heading, explanatory text and three buttons in one action container. Allow and Cancel come from one read. Chromium orders the row as the extra action ("Turn off in settings"), then Cancel, then Allow. RTL locales mirror it on screen but keep that order. The buttons must sit in one row with Cancel between the other two, and if one is focused it has to be Cancel. Anything else is refused. `dismiss()` now presses Cancel.
- Setup finds the omnibox as the window's one native, actionable, enabled text field, because Chromium localizes its name. When the browser reports exactly one document URI over AT-SPI, that URI decides whether the setup page is showing. `chrome://inspect` stays English in every UI language, so the page heading and checkbox label checks are unchanged.
- `AtspiNode` gains `focused` and `document_uri`, and the URI is read only on document nodes. A consent timeout returns a redacted node snapshot (roles, bounds, focus, no names).

## Scope

Linux backend only (`platform-linux`). It leaves alone the macOS setup (#6664 covers it) and Windows (#3135 already landed). The commit authored by @loonghao is their branch rebased, with only the edits it needed to compile on main. The two commits after it are ours.

## Tradeoffs

Consent identity is structure only, as on Windows. A different native Chromium alert with the same heading, body and three-button row would match. A page `confirm()` does not: Chromium exposes it as a `dialog` with two buttons, and that is refused.

## Blast Radius

Linux existing-profile browser setup and consent, plus every `AtspiNode` initializer (two new fields). Isolated-profile prepare and the other tools are untouched.

## Verification

- Ran Chromium 156 under Xvfb with AT-SPI in en-US, de, ar and ja, and probed the real setup page and consent prompt with the crate's own `walk_tree` and matchers. On this branch all four locales found the omnibox, the setup checkbox, Allow and Cancel (two distinct buttons). On main, de found none of them.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` pass. The new unit tests use the button geometry captured from those four locales, and include a test that Cancel never resolves to Allow when focus moves.
- Windows and macOS platform crates were not built.

title: fix(cua-driver): cover foreground typing into a minimized Screen Sharing window
body:
## Why

#3201 reported that foreground `type_text` into one exact Apple Screen Sharing window (`AXSharedScreen`, several windows sharing one pid) failed with `exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery` on 0.19.4-nightly.20260812. Current main already delivers it. `with_foreground_hid_activation` now raises the exact window through AX and retries once (#4821, #5522), and both landed after that build. Nothing covered this surface, so this PR adds a regression test that fails when those steps are removed.

## What changed

- New desktop E2E `screen_sharing_macos_test.rs`. It serves two local VNC desktops in the test process and connects Screen Sharing to both. It then minimizes the target window, fronts Finder, and calls `type_text` with `pid`, `window_id`, `x,y` and `delivery_mode:"foreground"`. The VNC servers are the oracle: the target desktop gets exactly the typed text, the sibling gets nothing, and Finder holds the front afterwards.
- `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh` runs it next to the TextEdit installed-app rows. Added rows to the E2E README and the test matrix.

## Scope

Test and docs only. No driver code changes. The issue's other request, a specific pre-dispatch refusal for Screen Sharing, is not needed because delivery works. Linux and Windows are not affected.

## Blast Radius

This adds one row to the macOS canonical E2E lane. It needs Screen Sharing, which ships with macOS, and loopback TCP. The test quits Screen Sharing at the end only if the test launched it.

## Verification

- Reproduced in a disposable macOS VM with two Screen Sharing connections to local key-logging VNC servers. On main, foreground typing reached the exact window in each case tried: back window with another app in front, sibling of the key window, minimized, app hidden, full screen on its own Space, and Control Screen toggled off. Each time the other connection got no keys and the previous app kept the front.
- With the AXRaise and retry removed from `with_foreground_hid_activation`, which matches the guard at the time of the issue, typing into a minimized window failed with the issue's exact error string. The new test failed against that build too (`focus pixel-click at (400,300) failed.`).
- The new test passed repeatedly against main's signed local build in the VM. The scoped repository checks also ran: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-e2e --tests -D warnings`, a compile-only `cargo test`, and `bash -n` on the runner script. The full macOS Lume run-all matrix and the Linux and Windows lanes did not run.

Fixes #3201

title: fix(driver): macOS get_window_state hangs when capture_blocked_reason blocks opening ScreenCaptureApprovals.plist
body:
## What happened

On a macOS host, the installed cua-driver daemon (`/Applications/CuaDriver.app`) got stuck inside `get_window_state` and stopped answering.

A process sample showed:

- `capture_consent::capture_blocked_reason` blocked in `open()` on `~/Library/Group Containers/group.com.apple.replayd/ScreenCaptureApprovals.plist`.
- A `type_text` call holding `input_busy` for the Screen Sharing pid while that was stuck, so later input calls queued behind it.
- Host `screencapture` failed at the same time ("could not create image from display"), so the host's screen capture state was already bad.

Seen during a run on our Mac mini host on 2026-11-13. The daemon needed a restart to recover.

## Expected

Reading the screen-capture approvals plist to decide whether capture is blocked should never hang a tool call. If the file can't be opened promptly (or opening it blocks), `capture_blocked_reason` should time out or fall back to "unknown" and let `get_window_state` return, instead of wedging the daemon and every later call.

## Notes

- The blocking `open()` is the part worth fixing; the bad host capture state is the trigger.
- A fix probably wants the plist read off the request path (cached, or with a bounded non-blocking read), plus a test that a blocked read doesn't hang `get_window_state`.

title: [Bug]: launch_app cannot open a Finder folder when serve runs with --no-overlay (main queue never served)
fix(cua-driver): uninstall-local stops app-bundle daemons and removes release markers
body:
`uninstall-local.sh` no longer reports success while a daemon from the local install is still running or its `.release_installed` markers remain.

Before this change, the script only stopped daemons started through the CLI link or `packages/current/cua-driver-local`. On macOS, a daemon started straight from `/Applications/CuaDriverLocal.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver-local` kept running after its bundle was deleted. Also, `.release_installed` (the per-version marker directory the telemetry code writes) was not in the cleanup list, so the local home was never removed. The script then printed `cua-driver-local uninstalled` anyway.

## Changes

- The script now also stops daemons running from the app-bundle executable. It waits for them to exit, sends `-KILL` to any that remain, and exits 1 with an error before deleting anything if a local daemon is still alive. It checks again just before printing success.
- The LaunchAgent and systemd unit files are removed only after every daemon is confirmed stopped. If an uninstall fails, the install is left intact and the uninstall can be rerun.
- Daemon paths are matched literally (regex metacharacters escaped). Matching is limited to the invoking user, because other accounts may run the shared `/Applications` bundle.
- If `pgrep` fails (any exit status other than 1), the script treats it as a surviving daemon, not as "none running".
- `.release_installed` is removed in both `uninstall-local.sh` and `uninstall-local.ps1`.

## Test plan

- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/test_uninstall_local.py` gains these tests:
  - the app-bundle path is stopped (scoped to the user)
  - a surviving daemon or a `pgrep` error stops the uninstall, deletes no files, keeps the LaunchAgent and prints no success line
  - a real process whose argv[0] is a local daemon path, under a home path containing `.`, a space and parentheses, is stopped and the uninstall succeeds
  - the existing removal test now also removes `.release_installed`
- All of these new or extended tests fail against the current main script.
- The scoped repository checks were run on macOS: the local uninstall, elevation and cross-copy daemon-stop suites pass. A real-process check confirmed that macOS `pkill`/`pgrep` accept `-U` together with `-f`.
- Not run: Linux and Windows native lanes. The Windows change adds one name to the list of removed children.

Fixes #3513

title: Hyprland plugin: always-present agent seats break pointer polling in GTK 3 apps (wxWidgets hover previews)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (Hyprland plugin)

### Summary

Another case for the seat-lifetime plan in #4257 (item 2, "an agent seat exists only while a lane is in use"): with the plugin loaded, the always-present agent seats break **pointer polling in GTK 3 apps**, even ones that never bind an agent seat for input.

GTK 3's Wayland backend answers the legacy `gdk_device_manager_get_client_pointer()` with the pointer of the seat that most recently gained pointer capability, which is `Cua-Agent-2`. `gdk_display_get_default_seat()` still returns `Hyprland`. Apps that poll the pointer through the legacy call get the idle agent pointer at `(0,0)`, while mouse events keep arriving from the Hyprland seat with correct coordinates. wxWidgets uses that call for `wxGetMousePosition()` and `wxGetMouseState()` on GTK 3. In PrusaSlicer 2.9.6, the paint-brush sphere is placed by raycasting `wxGetMousePosition()`, so it disappears, while clicking still paints.

### Reproduction

1. Omarchy 4.5.0, Hyprland 0.56.2, `cua-hyprland-plugin` 0.33.2-3 loaded (`hyprctl -j cua:status` shows two lanes, `seat_lifetime: compositor`).
2. Native Wayland wxWidgets/GTK 3 test app that logs the `wxEVT_MOTION` position and `ScreenToClient(wxGetMousePosition())`.
3. Move the normal mouse over it. To exclude agent input, I used a `/dev/uinput` virtual mouse on the normal input path.

### Observed

| Setup | Event position | Polled position |
|---|---|---|
| All three seats visible | (394,351) | (0,0) |
| `Cua-Agent` and `Cua-Agent-2` globals hidden from the test process only | (418,375) | (418,375) |
| XWayland | (450,387) | (450,387) |

No agent session was active; the plugin only had to advertise the seats.

### Expected

Apps outside an agent session see only the user's seat, as planned in #4257, item 2. Until then, documenting this class of side effect (GTK 3 legacy client pointer, so wxWidgets apps' hover and preview features) next to the imv and Zed cases would help users diagnose it.

title: raw-linux bench desktop: find the unlogged process that stalls the AT-SPI bus
body:
Found by the raw-linux pure bench run (branch `exp/raw-linux-pure`, head `57f8ccca1a`). Follows #7529, which covers the timeout fix, not the cause.

**What happens.** In the splice session (run `rlp-r1`, the 22 reruns of CDB-G03, CDB-G02 and MB-09), one app on the bench desktop's AT-SPI bus stopped answering. Its pid was 773, a process the harness did not log, and it stalled in 245 raw calls. The 2 s `Atspi.set_timeout` from #7529 kept those calls short, but the app stayed unresponsive.

**To do.** Find out which process stalls the bus on the bench desktop: log the process name and command line for every pid that hits the AT-SPI timeout, then fix or exclude it at desktop setup. With the timeout in place, any trial that still pays one 2 s read per stuck app will skew the arm's wall time.

title: verify-cua-driver macOS Lume runner: report the host macOS guest limit instead of "worker stopped during boot"
body:
## What happened

On the relay Mac mini (Lume 0.5.3, macOS 26.6.2), 16 of 24 macOS Lume full-lane runs on 2026-11-13 ended `infrastructure_failed` with `worker stopped during boot`. The lume log for each worker shows two different causes behind that one message:

- **Host macOS guest limit (5 runs: 20261113T045324Z-975ee99a, 071830Z-9d542df8, 114430Z-2995cbff, 123247Z-884d85d2, 123633Z-a02172d7).** `lume run --detach` logged `Failed in VM.run ... The number of virtual machines exceeds the limit. The maximum supported number of active virtual machines has been reached.` Other sessions on the host already had two macOS guests running. The runner's `run.lock` serializes only lume-e2e runs, so a guest started outside it still takes one of the two slots. The runner saw `stopped` and reported a boot failure, which reads like a broken seed or guest.
- **False first `stopped` read (11 runs, including the four for #7614).** The runner gave up within about 6 s of the lume log's `VM started successfully`. In 7 of them the log shows `Wrote VNC config to VM via SSH` 16 to 20 s after the start, so the guest was booting normally. That part is #7513.

## Expected

When the host is at its macOS guest limit, the runner reports that as the reason (for example `blocked: host limit of 2 running macOS guests reached`, matching the wording #3958 gave `lume serve`). It reports it before cloning, or waits for a slot, rather than calling it a boot failure. The verify skill's "Blocked before a VM starts" note in `.cursor/skills/verify-cua-driver/macos-lume.md` lists this case next to the disk floor and `run.lock`.

## Done when

- A run started while two macOS guests are active ends with a reason that names the host guest limit, not `worker stopped during boot`.
- `macos-lume.md` documents the limit as a blocked lane.

Related: #7513 (the false `stopped` read), #3880 and #3958 (the same limit through the HTTP API).

title: fix(cua-driver): let Windows ffmpeg finish shutdown and stop shimmed encoders
body:
Fixes #3713

## Cause

The failing preflight's retained recording from https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34499846099 shows what happened. The MP4 is finalized (`ftyp`, `moov`, `mdat`, faststart applied), but it holds 2 frames over 1.83 s. A healthy preflight holds 80 to 120. The cursor sampler kept running for 6.9 s after the last preflight action. So gdigrab stalled on one frame grab, and ffmpeg reads `q` only between frames. Its clean shutdown ran past the 3 s deadline, and `stop` declared failure.

At the deadline `stop` killed the process it had spawned. With Chocolatey that process is the shim, so the real encoder kept running and finalized the file afterwards. That's why a "failed" recording still had a valid `moov`. The shim also meant a timed-out stop could leave an encoder running against the output path.

The diagnostics on #3739 point the same way. Every slow passing shutdown (1205 and 1686 ms) came from a runner's first preflight after the hosted console was minimized. One of them also had a frame gap of a third of a second and only 14 frames. That is the same grab stall, short of the deadline.

## Change

- Give a clean ffmpeg shutdown 10 s instead of 3 s. That stays well under the testkit's 25 s tool-call timeout. A real exit failure still reports at once, and a hung encoder still reports `ffmpeg shutdown timed out`.
- On Windows, spawn ffmpeg suspended in a kill-on-close job object, then resume it, so anything a shim starts is in the job. A timeout terminates the whole job, and dropping the backend kills any leftover.

## Tests

- `stop_recording_waits_for_a_slow_clean_encoder_shutdown`: a fixture encoder takes 4.5 s to finish after `q`, then writes its output. Through the public `start_recording`/`stop_recording`/`get_recording_state` tools, stop succeeds and reports the video. With the old 3 s deadline it fails with `ffmpeg shutdown timed out after 3000 ms`.
- `shutdown_timeout_stops_the_encoder_behind_a_shim` (Windows only, runs in the existing `recording_shutdown_errors` step of the Windows CI): the fixture acts as a shim that starts a child encoder, and the child ignores `q`. After the timeout, the child process must be gone.

## Verification

Ran the scoped repository checks: rustfmt, clippy with `-D warnings` for macOS and cross-checked for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `recording_shutdown_errors` (3 passed on macOS), and the core library's recording tests. The Windows-only shim test and native Windows and Linux X11 desktop E2E could not run on the macOS host. Windows CI runs the shim test.

title: feat(cua-driver): add OpenJev decision model adapter
body:
## Why

jev-use has a `DecisionModel` seam with mock, TypeSafe and loopback S1 backends, but none that reaches a remote OpenJev-compatible System One server. @kvnloo built that backend in #3961, re-cut to the scope the maintainer review asked for. This PR carries those commits unchanged and adds two fixes found in review.

## What changed

- `python/openjev_model.py` and `typescript/openjev_model.ts` (by @kvnloo): an OpenJev `DecisionModel` that sends the validated `cua.jev_choice_request_v1|v2` as System One `state` to `OPENJEV_BASE_URL` and returns scores for the supplied candidate IDs only. `choose_decision.py --model openjev` and `verify_decision_cli.py --model openjev` select it. An API key is sent only over HTTPS. URL credentials, query and fragment are rejected. Redirects are refused, bodies over 256 KiB fail, and failures make exactly one request.
- `decision_models.choose()` no longer replaces an empty `selected_id` with the argmax. A provider that answered `choice: ""` used to get an actionable `selected` result. It now gets `error` / `model_error`.
- The TypeScript transport now reads the response body inside its error classification, so a timeout or reset during the body read is an `OpenJevError` (`timeout` / `http_error`) and no longer a raw error.

## Scope

Covers the OpenJev adapter in Python and TypeScript, its tests, the CLI choice and the `decision-models.md` section. Leaves out browser-runner provider selection, backend receipts in JSONL events, and TypeSafe base URL/model/timeout configuration. No change to Driver or visual routing.

## Blast Radius

Everything is under `libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use`. The `choose()` change affects every decision model. Only a model that returns an empty-string `selected_id` sees different behavior, and no backend in the tree builds one: mock and S1 pass `None`, and TypeSafe passes a validated ID.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks for jev-use (the `ci-jev-use.yml` commands) pass on this head: the full Python unittest suite, `npm test` and `npm run typecheck`. The Linux mock E2E job needs a Linux desktop and was not run here.
- `choose_decision.py --model openjev` was run against a loopback server. A valid answer returns `selected`. A 302 and an oversized body each return an error, and the redirect target gets no request. An API key with an `http://` URL exits before any request.
- Each new regression test fails when its fix is reverted and passes with it.


Salvaged from #3961
Fixes #3915

title: [Bug]: Windows: Cua Spaces app and cua daemon open visible terminal windows for status checks (schtasks, qemu --version, powershell, wsl, nvidia-smi)
body:
### Primary area

Other (the Cua Spaces desktop app, and the `cua` CLI daemon it starts)

### Summary

On Windows, the Cua Spaces app and the `cua daemon` it runs start short-lived console programs (`schtasks`, `qemu-system-x86_64 --version`, `powershell`, `wsl`, `nvidia-smi`) as visible console processes. With Windows Terminal as the default terminal, each one opens a terminal window that appears and closes, repeatedly, while the app is open. It is most noticeable when changing anything in Settings (for example toggling an agent in the Agent menu) or opening Settings or a computer's page.

### Reproduction

1. On Windows 11, with Windows Terminal set as the default terminal application, start Cua Spaces (the app starts `cua.exe daemon start --foreground --loopback 127.0.0.1:0`).
2. Open Settings and toggle any switch (for example an entry under Agent menu), or open Computers > this PC.
3. Terminal windows open and close several times. They keep appearing while those pages are open.

To see which processes are behind them, poll `Win32_Process` for new PIDs and their parents for about 20 seconds (PowerShell, every 150 ms). I ran this with the app open and nobody touching it.

### Expected behavior

No visible windows: diagnostic and status helpers started by the app or the daemon do not create a console window (`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, or `windowsHide: true` for Node `child_process`).

### Actual behavior

In one 20-second window, with no user input:

| Parent | Children started |
|---|---|
| `Cua Spaces.exe` (Electron main process) | `schtasks.exe`, `qemu-system-x86_64.exe --version` (x2), `powershell.exe` (x2), each with its own `conhost.exe 0x4` |
| `cua.exe daemon start --foreground --loopback 127.0.0.1:0` | `wsl.exe`, `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "... Get-CimInstance Win32_OptionalFeature -Filter \"Name='HypervisorPlatform'\" ..."`, `nvidia-smi.exe` |
| `svchost.exe` (DCOM) | `OpenConsole.exe -Embedding` (x2), the Windows Terminal default-terminal handoff, which is what puts the windows on screen |

As a control, a console program started hidden (`Start-Process cmd.exe -ArgumentList '/c timeout /t 4' -WindowStyle Hidden`) on the same machine started no `OpenConsole`/Windows Terminal process and showed no window. So the windows come from these processes being started without a hidden or no-window flag, not from the default-terminal setting by itself.

I do not know which code path in the app issues each call. The parent PIDs above are what I observed.

### Environment

- Cua Spaces app 0.36.10 (Windows, user install under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\cua-spaces`)
- `cua` CLI 0.27.4 (bundled at `resources\native\cua.exe`), `cua-spacesd` 0.15.2 as the host service
- Windows 11 Home, build 26300, x64
- Windows Terminal 1.25.2733.0 set as the default terminal application

### Evidence

Process listing from the 20-second poll (machine-specific IDs omitted):

```
schtasks.exe              <- Cua Spaces.exe
conhost.exe               <- schtasks.exe
qemu-system-x86_64.exe    <- Cua Spaces.exe   :: "C:\Program Files\qemu\qemu-system-x86_64.exe" --version
conhost.exe 0x4           <- qemu-system-x86_64.exe
OpenConsole.exe -Embedding <- svchost.exe
wsl.exe                   <- cua.exe (daemon)
conhost.exe               <- wsl.exe
powershell.exe            <- cua.exe (daemon) :: -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; Get-CimInstance Win32_OptionalFeature -Filter \"Name='HypervisorPlatform'\" | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Insta..."
powershell.exe            <- Cua Spaces.exe
conhost.exe               <- powershell.exe
nvidia-smi.exe            <- cua.exe (daemon)
```

### Workaround and additional context

- Switching the Windows default terminal to "Windows Console Host" should turn the Windows Terminal windows into plain console flashes (untested here). It does not remove them, and it changes the default for every app.
- Staying off the Settings and Computers pages reduces how often it happens.
- Related, but a different component: #3410 (Cua Driver diagnostic helpers without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`) and #5040 (embedded cua-driver daemon console window, closed). This report is about the Cua Spaces app's own child processes and the `cua daemon`'s.
- Possibly related, not confirmed: on the same pages, toggles sometimes flicker between states after a change, as if the page re-renders while these status checks run.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux consent scans skip web content and honor a late confirmed Allow
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux, `browser_prepare` with `strategy: existing_profile` is refused with `browser_wrong_target_refused: Chromium remote-debugging consent did not settle within its bounded attempt (consent attempt deadline expired)` whenever the active tab is a heavy page, even though the driver presses Allow and Chromium accepts the connection (the "Chrome is being controlled by automated test software" bar appears). The consent loop in `platform-linux/src/browser_consent_ui.rs` has a 4 s deadline, walks the whole AT-SPI tree of the window (web content included) on every step, and checks the deadline before looking whether the prompt closed. With Google Maps active one walk took ~2.1 s (577 nodes), so the walk confirming the closed prompt always ended past the deadline. When the deadline expired before the press, the prompt also stayed open after the driver dropped its socket, and later attempts queued behind it.
- What changed:
  - consent walks (`handle`, `trusted_allow_click`, `dismiss`) use a walk that does not descend into web document subtrees. The prompt matcher already ignores anything inside web content (`trusted_prompt_nodes`), so nothing it can match is lost;
  - a performed Allow whose prompt has closed is accepted even when the walk that observed it ended after the deadline, and once Allow was pressed one confirmation walk may start after the deadline. This mirrors the macOS behavior from #5216 on Linux.

## Related work

Refs #5216, #4630

RFC: not required (no public contract change).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux only. Consent scans become faster; a late confirmed Allow now attaches instead of being refused. Refusal paths for an unpressed or dismissed prompt are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: the web-content skip is scoped to consent walks through a task-local set for the duration of one walk (thread flag restored on return and on unwind); every other walk is unchanged. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `rustfmt --check` on the changed files; `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib` in `rust:1.97.1-bookworm` on aarch64: 1064 passed, 2 failed — `input::admission_tests::a_drag_abandoned_after_its_press_still_releases_the_button` and `input::own_dialog_tests::focus_restore_leaves_focus_on_a_dialog_the_app_opened` need Xvfb and fail the same way on a clean `main` in that container. New unit tests cover the scoped skip flag (body scope, nesting, restore after panic).
- Manual or platform evidence: Debian 13 arm64, Xvnc + Xfce, Chromium with user-enabled remote debugging, Google Maps active. The same change applied to v0.38.0: before, 3/3 `browser_prepare` refused at ~5.5 s; after, 3/3 `attached_existing_profile` in 1.9–2.1 s, with the driver's CDP socket dropped before each attempt so every run went through the consent prompt. No prompt left open afterwards.
- Known gaps or CI still required: `bin/ci --signoff` not run locally; hosted CI still required. Opened as a draft until then.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.

title: fix(cua-driver): list no tools when a policy layer fails to load
body:
Salvaged from #4020

## Why

`is_tool_listable` returned `true` when a policy layer failed to load, so `tools/list` could advertise every tool while `authorize_tool_call` refused all of them. `revoke_authorization` also reported `revoked: 1` when `end_session` came back with `isError`, for example after a cleanup hook failed. This lands @Al-aminI's fixes for both from #4020 (his two commits are first, author kept) on current main.

## What changed

- `is_tool_listable` lists nothing when either the managed or the user policy layer failed to load. The decision is in `tool_listable_in`, with unit tests for both layers.
- `SdkAdapter::end_session` returns an error when the tool result has `isError: true`, so a failed end is no longer reported as a revoke. A new test registers a failing cleanup hook and checks the error.
- README: an unset `CUA_DRIVER_POLICY_FILE` means no enforcement, and a set but missing or unloadable path stops startup, which is what the code already did. The deny example names real tools. A direct-MCP test covers the missing-path refusal on Linux and Windows.

## Scope

Left out of #4020 because main already has them or they add a new surface nobody asked for: `CUA_DRIVER_REQUIRE_POLICY`, the `policy_mode` metadata field, the C-linkage symbol test (main imports those symbols through `ffi` and checks the header), the `default_capabilities_for` warning (telemetry calls it with arbitrary names, so it would warn on every unknown tool), and the schema-test skip gate (the testkit already panics on a missing binary under `CUA_TEST_REQUIRE_DRIVER_BIN=1`). The session tombstone cap was already reverted in #4020 and is tracked in #4993.

## Blast radius

Only a process whose policy failed to load sees the listing change, and startup validation normally stops that process first. Revoke callers now get an error instead of `revoked: 1` when the session did not end cleanly.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks passed on macOS: workspace clippy with `-D warnings`, `cua-driver-core` lib tests, the `sdk_adapter` tests and `daemon_required_test`. Each new unit test fails with its fix reverted.
- On macOS, `cua-driver mcp` with `CUA_DRIVER_POLICY_FILE` pointing at a missing file exits 1 with nothing on stdout and stderr `configured permission policy path does not exist`.
- The macOS Lume matrix did not run (the worker VM failed to boot). The Linux and Windows lanes, including the new direct-MCP test, run in CI.

title: cua-driver-sdk: dropping the private-worker shutdown future while it is queued skips the deadline kill
body:
### Summary

`PrivateWorkerClient::shutdown` in `cua-driver-sdk` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-sdk/src/worker.rs`) does not kill the private worker by its shutdown deadline when the caller drops the shutdown future while the shutdown task is still waiting in Tokio's blocking pool.

- On main, `shutdown()` runs `shutdown_sync` through `spawn_blocking`, and the deadline is computed inside `shutdown_sync`. Time spent queued behind a saturated blocking pool is never bounded, whether or not the caller keeps waiting.
- #7646 (salvaged from #3996) adds an off-pool deadline thread, but that thread belongs to the caller's future (`ShutdownDeadline` is dropped with it). If the caller drops the future while the task is queued, the watchdog is cancelled and nothing kills the child until a pool thread picks up the task. #3996's description already scopes this case out.

### Reproduction

At the #7646 head (7fd302e7), with the existing `worker/shutdown_tests.rs` fixtures (`shutdown_timeout` 100 ms, a current-thread runtime with `max_blocking_threads(1)`):

1. Occupy the only blocking thread with a 1.5 s `spawn_blocking` sleep.
2. Spawn an `unread` fixture child and call `client.shutdown()` under `tokio::time::timeout(20 ms, …)`, so the future is dropped while the shutdown task is queued.
3. Poll the child until 400 ms after the call.

Result: the child is still running at 405 ms, four times the 100 ms budget. It exits only once the blocker frees the pool thread.

### Proposed fix

Make deadline cleanup independent of the caller's future. Once shutdown has started, the off-pool deadline thread should own the expiry path: on timeout it gates transmission, aborts the queued task and calls `schedule_cleanup()`. Dropping the future then only stops the caller from waiting and does not cancel the kill.

### Tests

Add a shutdown test that drops (cancels) the shutdown future while the blocking pool is saturated, and asserts the owned child is killed and reaped by the deadline (the same bound `assert_reaped_by` uses), without the queued request being transmitted late.

title: fix(cua-driver): report the macOS keyboard route as window-addressed keys are gated
body:
Fixes #4241

## What was wrong

On macOS, Chrome with one browser window could refuse background `type_text`, `press_key` and `hotkey` with `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity`. The other "windows" were Chrome's helper surfaces: off-screen or 1x1 strips and the omnibox suggestion popup.

On main, the tools themselves no longer refuse in this case:

- #4821 made the keyboard-ambiguity count skip off-screen and near-zero-size siblings. It also counts nothing when accessibility proves the target is the app's key window.
- #5306 gates window-addressed `type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey` and `type_text_chars` as exact-window keys. The driver makes the addressed window key before posting, so a visible sibling such as an open omnibox popup is not ambiguous for these tools.

One surface still said otherwise. The read-only `background_input` section of `get_window_state` judged its `pid_keyboard` route as the generic key class. With the omnibox popup open and the browser window not key, it reported `pid_keyboard: refused, same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` and sent agents to `delivery_mode:"foreground"`, even though the tools would deliver.

## Change

`background_input_capability_report` now takes the keyboard action class from the platform. On macOS, `get_window_state` passes the same `window_keyboard_action(GenericKey)` that the keyboard tools gate on. That is exact-window keys where the key-window transport exists, and the generic class otherwise. The report and the tools now give the same answer. All other guards (minimized or hidden, off-Space, element ancestry, screen locked) still apply to the route.

## Tests

- New `capability_report_judges_pid_keyboard_as_the_tools_gate_it` covers a target with one competing same-pid destination (the open omnibox popup). The route is `available` under exact-window keys, still `refused` with `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` under the generic class, and `minimized_or_hidden_window` once the target is minimized. With the hard-coded generic class restored, the test fails.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` all pass.
- Not run: `platform-macos` could not be built or tested on the Linux host, and no macOS guest was available, so the native Chrome check did not run. Windows checks were not run either. The Linux X11 desktop lane stopped at a build timeout before any cell ran, and Linux does not call this report.

title: cua-driver diagnose (macOS): local builds report the release bundle's install paths and TCC identity
body:
## What's wrong

`cua-driver diagnose` on a local build (`cua-driver-local`, `CuaDriverLocal.app`, bundle id `com.trycua.driver.local`) reports the release install instead of its own. In `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs` at current `main`:

- `diagnose_install_layout_section` hardcodes `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, `~/.local/bin/cua-driver` and `/usr/local/bin/cua-driver`.
- `diagnose_tcc_db_section` queries TCC rows only for `client='com.trycua.driver'` and titles the section with that id.

`crate::bundle` already has the local identity (`is_local_installation()`, `app_bundle_path()`, `bundle_id()`, `cli_name()`), and `diagnose_config_paths_section` already uses it. The install-layout and TCC sections don't. On a host with a local build, the report shows the release bundle's codesign and TCC rows (or none at all), which is the wrong data for a permissions audit of the build that is actually running.

This is the "Related diagnostic gap" noted in #3514. #7626 fixes the PID part of #3514 and leaves `diagnose` unchanged.

## Expected

On a local build, `diagnose` reports `CuaDriverLocal.app`, the `cua-driver-local` CLI paths and the TCC rows for `com.trycua.driver.local`. A release build's output stays unchanged.

## Done when

- The install-layout and TCC-database sections take their paths and bundle id from `crate::bundle`.
- A unit test covers both identities.
