title: fix(cua-driver): pin before AX double-click pulse
body:
## Why

On macOS, the AX `double_click` pointer fallback sent its `ClickPulse` without pinning the cursor to the target window first. Since #4068, `PinAbove` is where the overlay checks whether the target window is on the current Space, so this path skipped that check. A fresh session cursor could paint at an off-Space target's coordinates over the user's current Space, and a cursor pinned to an earlier window kept that window's state. Every other macOS pointer tool already pins before it pulses.

## What changed

- `ax_double_click` sends `PinAbove(wid)` and then `ClickPulse`, through a small `pulse_on_window` helper.
- A unit test applies those commands to a fresh cursor and to one pinned to another window, and checks that both end pinned to the target window. With the pin removed, the test fails.

## Scope

This covers the macOS AX double-click path used when the element has no `AXOpen`, and the foreground fallback after `AXOpen` fails. The pixel double-click already delegates to `click`, which pins. Linux and Windows are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

The change affects only the overlay cursor for AX double-clicks on macOS. Input delivery is unchanged. For a target on the current Space, the only difference is one extra `PinAbove`, the same command `click` sends.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks passed: fmt, clippy and the `platform-macos` double_click and cursor overlay tests, plus `cursor-overlay`'s off-workspace paint test. With `PinAbove` removed from the helper, the new test fails.
- The macOS Lume full lane of the verify-cua-driver skill passed at this head.
- Not run: a real second-Space or fullscreen setup, which the harness cannot script. Linux and Windows checks did not run either, since this change touches only macOS.

Reported in #3886 by @lorenzozanee.

Fixes #3801

The minimum supported version of Python is 3.11.

My thanks to the many people who have contributed to this release. Also thanks to my co-maintainers: Nicki Křížek, Petr Špaček, and Brian Wellington.

This release was published to PyPI using Trusted Publishing.

Changelog

Sourced from dnspython's changelog.

2.9.2

  • A maliciously crafted zone file could use a WKS record to consume excessive memory and CPU, possibly causing the process to exit due to memory exhaustion. Thanks to Jace (GitHub @​manus-use) for discovering and reporting this issue.

2.9.1

  • LOC text parsing now converts the altitude, size, horizontal precision, and vertical precision fields to centimeters exactly, and requires them to be decimal numbers of meters with at most two fractional digits, as RFC 1876 section 3 specifies. They were converted with float(), so 9.29m became 928 cm rather than 929 cm and the text and wire forms of the record disagreed, forms such as 1e3m, 1_000m, +10m, nanm, and infm were accepted, extra fractional digits were silently dropped, and an altitude outside the representable range was accepted and then failed in to_wire() with a non-DNS exception. dns.exception.SyntaxError is now raised for all of these.

  • The resolver now assigns a new random query id to every query.

  • For transports that require a 0 query id, set it in a way that does not break TSIG.

  • dns.message.QueryMessage.resolve_chaining() now caps the minimum TTL of a negative response with no SOA record at 300 seconds (dns.message.NEGATIVE_TTL_WITHOUT_SOA). Previously the TTL was left at its initial value of 2^32 - 1, so a single NXDOMAIN or NODATA response with no SOA, e.g. a spoofed one, stayed in the resolver cache for the life of the process.

  • DNSSEC validation now rejects an RRSIG whose type covered or class does not match the RRset, as RFC 4035 section 5.3.1 requires. This was not checked, so a revoked DNSKEY, which may only validate the DNSKEY RRset, still validated any RRset signed with its private key if the RRSIG claimed to cover DNSKEY.

  • dns.tokenizer.Tokenizer now ends a line at a carriage return, or at a carriage return followed by a line feed, unless the carriage return is in a quoted string. The carriage return of CRLF line ends used to stay in the last token of each line and in the text of a comment, so e.g. dns.zone.from_text() rejected a zone with CRLF line ends.

  • DNSSEC validation no longer uses a DNSKEY with the REVOKE flag set to validate anything other than the DNSKEY RRset. RFC 5011 section 2.1 says a revoked key must not be used for any other purpose, but it was a candidate key like any other, so as long as the revoked key was still published, data signed with its private key, e.g. by whoever compromised it, validated.

... (truncated)

title: cua-driver (macOS): overlay commands are silently dropped when the cursor channel is full, so a PinAbove can be lost before its ClickPulse
body:
Found by reading the code on main at `d6a5c4f9ef`. Not observed in a run.

## What the code does

The macOS cursor overlay takes commands on one bounded channel of 4096 messages ([overlay.rs#L341](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L341)). Every sender uses `try_send` and throws away the result:

- `send_command` ([overlay.rs#L407-L416](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L407-L416)). Its doc comment says it "drops if the channel is full (old commands are less important than new ones)". The code doesn't match the comment: once the queue is full, the **new** command is the one that gets thrown away, and the old ones stay queued.
- `remove_cursor` ([#L449](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L449)) and `revive_cursor` ([#L460](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L460)) do the same.

Nothing is logged when a command is dropped.

The render loop is the only reader ([overlay.rs#L943-L1020](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L943-L1020)). It reads between frames, and it can wait on the main thread inside the loop: `on_appkit` calls `dispatch_sync_f` on the main queue when the display layout changes ([#L976-L985](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L976-L985), [#L835](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L835)). If the main thread is busy, the loop stops reading. Tools keep sending in the meantime. Drags send one `track_pointer_command` per step ([drag.rs#L190](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/drag.rs#L190), [#L437](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/drag.rs#L437)), and several sessions can send at once. When 4096 messages pile up, later commands are dropped until the loop catches up.

## Why PinAbove then ClickPulse is exposed

Several tools send `PinAbove(wid)` and then a `ClickPulse` or `MoveTo` as two separate `try_send` calls:

- double_click AX path: `pulse_on_window` ([double_click.rs#L233-L238](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/double_click.rs#L233-L238)), sent at [#L284-L286](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/double_click.rs#L284-L286)
- right_click ([right_click.rs#L224-L237](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/right_click.rs#L224-L237))
- click ([click.rs#L1227](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs#L1227) then [#L1320](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs#L1320); [#L1432](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs#L1432) then [#L1450](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs#L1450))
- browser ([browser/platform.rs#L944-L962](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/browser/platform.rs#L944-L962))
- PinAbove followed by an `animate_cursor_to` MoveTo in drag, scroll, set_value, move_cursor and cursor_tools

If the channel is full when `PinAbove` is sent and one slot opens before the next command, the pin is dropped and the pulse or move is accepted. The pulse then runs with the previous `pinned_wid` and `pinned_target_off_workspace` ([overlay.rs#L733-L742](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L733-L742)). The z-order then stays tied to the previous window, and the cursor can paint over the current Space for a target that's on another Space. That's the case #3801 / #7659 fixed by sending the pin first. A dropped `MoveTo` from `animate_cursor_to` ([#L570](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L570)) also leaves its arrival waiter with nothing to wait for, and a dropped `Remove` leaves an ended session's cursor in the render map.

## How likely

Low. The queue only fills while the render loop is stalled, which needs a busy main thread and a lot of commands in flight. I haven't seen it happen. Other commands can be dropped the same way. The pin case gets its own section because a dropped pin leaves the overlay in the wrong place without any error.

## Possible directions (not decided)

- Send the pin and the command that follows it as one message, or one batch, so either both are applied or neither is.
- Never drop lifecycle messages (`Remove`, `Revive`, `PinAbove`). For example, block briefly or use a separate unbounded control lane.
- At minimum, log a `TrySendError::Full` and fix the doc comment on `send_command`.

title: [Bug]: get_guide returns its text only in the content block; the structured result has no guide text
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`get_guide` returns the guide's text only in the text content block. Its structured result holds `platform`, `sources`, `topic` and `topics`, with no text. Clients that show `structuredContent` when a tool returns one (Claude Code does), and `cua-driver call`, show the list of sources and never the guide, so the "Guides: `get_guide({topic})`" pointer in the server instructions leads nowhere.

### Reproduction

1. `cua-driver call get_guide '{"topic":"menus"}'`
2. Or call `get_guide` with `{"topic": "menus"}` from Claude Code through `cua-driver mcp`.

### Expected behavior

The guide's text reaches the caller: for example a `text` field in the structured result, or a structured result that is the same information as the text block.

### Actual behavior

Both print only:

```json
{
  "platform": "macOS",
  "sources": [
    { "file": "MACOS.md", "heading": "Navigating native menu bars (AXMenuBar)" },
    { "file": "MACOS.md", "heading": "Menus opened in the background keep the user's keyboard" }
  ],
  "topic": "menus",
  "topics": ["overview", "drag", "browser", "permissions", "batching", "menus"]
}
```

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.44.0, macOS 26.5.2, arm64; Claude Code 2.1 as the MCP client.
- Unchanged in the source at `cua-driver-rs-v0.49.4`: `cua-driver-core/src/guide.rs` builds `ToolResult::text(guide.text).with_structured(json!({ … "sources": sources … }))`.

### Evidence

The output above, from both routes.

### Workaround and additional context

The same files can be read as MCP resources (`skill://cua-driver/MACOS.md` and the others), but whole: `MACOS.md` is 59 KB, where the `menus` topic is two sections of it.

title: [Bug]: macOS get_window_state: a newline in an AX action name splits the tree row
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `get_window_state`'s Markdown tree writes accessibility action names as they are. An action whose name contains newlines splits its row over several lines, and the rows after it read as that element's children.

### Reproduction

1. Open a presentation in Microsoft PowerPoint for Mac (16.115).
2. `get_window_state` on the presentation window (`include_screenshot: false` is enough).

### Expected behavior

One line per element: control characters in an action name (and in `help` and `id`, which are written the same way) are escaped or replaced.

### Actual behavior

The Copilot button has a custom action whose name holds two newlines. The tree begins:

```
- [0] AXWindow "Presentation1" [actions=[raise]]
    - [1] AXButton (Copilot Chat) [help="Copilot Chat (⌃⌘I)" actions=[press,name:expand
target:0x0
selector:(null)]]
      - AXList (Thumbnail Pane)
        - [2] AXList [enabled=false]
          - AXCell (Slide 1 of 1 Slides)
        - AXLayoutArea (Slide Editor Pane, Slide 1 of 1 Slides)
        - AXLayoutArea (Notes Pane)
  - AXTabGroup (ribbon)
```

The thumbnail pane, the slide and the notes pane are siblings of that button in the window, not its children. A `query` read returns the stray fragment as a row of its own: `selector:(null)]]`.

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.44.0, macOS 26.5.2, arm64, through `cua-driver mcp` and `cua-driver call`.
- Unchanged in the source at `cua-driver-rs-v0.49.4`: `platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs` maps each action through `strip_prefix("AX")` and `to_lowercase()` and joins them into `actions=[…]`.

### Evidence

The tree above.

### Workaround and additional context

None needed to keep working, but a reader of the tree (a model) takes the wrong parent for everything under that row.

title: ci(cla): co-author trailers ignore the email-to-login link from the pull request's own commits
body:
The informational `cla` status on #5180 fails and its cla-report comment says "shostako <shostakovich1117@gmail.com> (no GitHub login) has not signed the CLA". That is wrong. shostako signed on #5180 on 22 Oct, and the signature is on the `cla-signatures` branch (`signatures/version1/cla.json`, name `shostako`, id 131621616).

## Why

`unsigned_cla_contributors` in `.github/scripts/release_attribution.py` resolves each `Co-authored-by:` trailer with `resolve_login(config, name, email)` and no linked login. That lookup tries `coauthorOverrides`, then `identityOverrides`, then a public-email user search. shostako's email is in none of them on main, and the search returns 0 users.

The same pull request already links that email to the account. Commit f55737f2 on #5180 is authored by `shostakovich1117@gmail.com`, and the commits API gives `author.login = shostako`. Release attribution uses this link (`pull_commit_email_logins`, the trailer path in `release_attribution.py`). The CLA check does not, so every later commit with a `Co-authored-by: shostako <shostakovich1117@gmail.com>` trailer (9f32989e, 0024154d, f81b6541) is reported as an unknown person.

#5180 also adds the email to `identityOverrides` in `.github/release-attribution-config.json`. That cannot help: `cla-report.yml` and the `cla` job read the config from the default branch, never from the pull request. So a `recheck` reports the same result until #5180 merges.

## Reproduce

At main 724b6e1b4d, call `cla_pr_report.unsigned_for` for #5180 with a read-only client:

- main's config: `['shostako <shostakovich1117@gmail.com> (no GitHub login) has not signed the CLA; sign it on #5180']`
- main's config with the email mapped to `shostako`: `[]`
- `pull_commit_email_logins(client, "trycua/cua", 5180)["shostakovich1117@gmail.com"]`: `shostako`

## Fix

In `unsigned_cla_contributors`, build an email-to-login map from the commits it has already fetched (each commit's `author.login` and `committer.login` with its email). Use it as the linked login for trailer co-authors before the public-email search. Add a test with a co-author trailer whose email only a commit in the same pull request links to a signed login.

Impact: `cla` is informational and the required `contributor-attribution` check passes on #5180. The bug only posts a wrong "please sign" comment and a red status, and it asks a contributor who already signed to sign again.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse macOS background clicks under the app's own popup
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a background pixel click addressed to a window is routed to that window by number. Where the same app draws a popup or menu over it, the click lands on the window underneath. A click aimed at a Chrome omnibox suggestion opened a saved tab group on the bookmarks bar under the dropdown.
- What changed: `click`, `right_click` and `drag` now refuse a background pointer press at a point covered by a popup or menu of the target's own app. The refusal uses the existing `target_occluded` code and names the covering window (`covering_window`, `covering_layer`, `covering_bounds`, `screen_point`). A covering surface is an on-screen, visible window of the same pid, stacked in front of the target, that is untitled or on a layer other than 0. Chrome's omnibox dropdown is an untitled layer-0 window and its tab context menu is a layer-101 window, so both match.

The other half of the issue no longer reproduces on the current release. With Chrome's omnibox dropdown or a tab context menu open, `list_windows` with a `pid` lists the popup window (layers other than 0 have been included since #5162). The main window's `get_window_state` tree also contains the `Omnibox Popup` web area with its suggestion rows, and the open `AXMenu` with its items. So an agent can see the popup. Its pixel click is what went wrong.

## Related work

Fixes #4242

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: a background pixel `click`, `right_click` or `drag` press at a point under the same app's popup now returns `target_occluded` instead of pressing the window underneath. Nothing changes for foreground delivery (the HID tap hits the popup on top), element tokens, points outside the popup, other apps' windows, or titled sibling windows of the same app.
- The `click` check runs after the background AX hit-test. When accessibility places the popup's element in the target window, as Chrome does for omnibox rows, that AX press still runs. Only the routed pointer event, which cannot reach the popup, is refused.
- Risk: an untitled same-app window that WindowServer reports visible but that draws nothing at the point would now refuse a background click there. Such a window has alpha 0 or is smaller than 2 pt; both are excluded. Rollback is reverting this PR.

## Validation

- Unit tests for `surface_over_in` cover an untitled same-app popup over the point, a layer-101 menu, a popup outside the point, a popup behind the target, another app's window, a titled sibling, a missing target, and transparent or 1 pt helper windows.
- Live check against Chrome on macOS. `same_app_surface_over` returned the omnibox dropdown window for a point on a suggestion row and nothing for a point on the page below it. With a tab context menu open, it returned the layer-101 menu window at a point inside the menu and nothing outside it.
- New AppKit cell `harness_appkit_left_click_px_background_refuses_point_under_own_popup`, registered in the macOS native runner. The fixture opens an untitled borderless child window over the receiver's top-left quarter. A background click there must refuse with `target_occluded`, naming the popup, and neither window may record a press. A background middle click outside the popup must reach the receiver.
- Removing either the title/layer filter or the in-front-of-target cut from `surface_over_in` turns a unit test red.
- macOS Lume full matrix at this head, in a disposable guest: passed, including the new cell and every AppKit, Electron, Tauri and WKWebView background pixel-click row.

- Known gaps: Linux and Windows are untouched and were not run. The live Chrome check ran the detection helper against real Chrome windows. The full click tool was not run against Chrome on the host, because the host's driver daemon cannot load a dev build's Accessibility grant.

title: macOS: get_window_state on an app's own popup window (Chrome tab context menu) returns an empty ax_unresolved tree while the main window's tree holds the menu
body:
## What happened

On macOS, a Chrome tab context menu is its own window. In `list_windows` it is an untitled window of Chrome's pid on layer 101. Calling `get_window_state` on that window id returns an empty, degraded tree:

```
"background_input": { "exact_window": { "status": "ax_unresolved", ... },
                      "routes": [ accessibility / window_pointer / pid_keyboard: refused, off_space_or_ax_unresolved ] }
"degraded": true,
"degraded_reason": "ax_window_unresolved: window_id <menu> exists and is owned by pid <chrome>, but none of the 1 AXWindow element(s) under that pid reports this CGWindowID. The tree is returned EMPTY on purpose ..."
"element_count": 0
```

The same menu is in the main window's tree. `get_window_state` on Chrome's main window returns it as an `AXMenu` under that `AXWindow` (for example `AXMenuItem "Close Tabs to the Right"`), with element tokens that can be acted on.

Seen with cua-driver 0.44.0 on macOS 26.6.2 with Chrome while working on #4242.

## Why it matters

#7669 (for #4242) makes a background pixel `click`, `right_click` or `drag` under one of the app's own popups return `target_occluded`, naming the popup window. Its hint tells the agent to "click its item by element_token from get_window_state". An agent that follows that hint and passes the popup's window id (the one the refusal names) gets an empty tree and no route. The only working path is the main window's snapshot, and nothing in either response says so.

## Steps

1. Open Chrome with one tab and right-click the tab to open its context menu.
2. `list_windows` with Chrome's `pid`. The menu is listed as an untitled layer-101 window over the main window.
3. `get_window_state` with that menu's `window_id`: empty tree, `ax_window_unresolved`, every background route refused.
4. `get_window_state` with the main window's `window_id`: the tree contains the open `AXMenu` and its items.

## Expected

One of these:
- `get_window_state` on the popup's window id resolves the popup's AX element (the `AXMenu` that matches the popup window's frame, via the app's native AX hierarchy) and returns it with tokens; or
- the degraded response names the window whose tree holds the popup's elements (here the main window), so the agent knows which `window_id` to snapshot. The `target_occluded` hint should then name that window too.

Either way the result should come from native AX and CGWindowList data, matched deterministically (pid, frame, layer), with no app-specific rules.

## Related

- #4242 / #7669: the click-through fix whose refusal hint leads here.
- #3351: an NSOpenPanel sheet listed as its own window is also `ax_unresolved` while its elements show under the main window.
- #2807: RFC for an explicit application/composite AX scope.

title: feat(cua-driver): read the text of windows missing from the accessibility tree
body:
## Problem

Toolkits that draw their own widgets (GTK on macOS, many Java and canvas UIs) expose only the window frame, its title-bar buttons and the menu bar to accessibility. For GnuCash, `get_window_state` returns 16 rows for an account register: the window, three unnamed title-bar buttons and the menu bar. Nothing in the content is addressable:

- `query` matches nothing ("Checking" returns an empty tree while the account is on screen).
- Every pixel action is `unverifiable`, so an agent reads a full screenshot (or zooms) after each click or key to see whether a cell changed. On a register, one edit costs two or three calls.
- A dialog's unlabeled title-bar close button reads as a plain `AXButton`, so agents pressed it when they meant the dialog's own OK button.

## Change

- **Text rows for opaque windows.** When a window's subtree holds nothing but its title-bar buttons (plus at most two unlabeled containers), `get_window_state` reads the window's screenshot with Apple's Vision framework (on device, no extra permission) and appends the text as tree rows:
  ```
  - OCR "window content is not in the accessibility tree; rows below are text read from this window's screenshot. ..."
    - OCRRow "y=167" = "10/02/2026 @(66,167) | Harbor Lamp Supply @(230,166) | Assets:Checking Account @(493,167) | n @(586,167) | 1,248.60 @(656,167)" ink=3ac5
  ```
  One row per visual line, each fragment with its centre in screenshot pixels (the space pixel actions take).
- **Diff reads see text changes.** Each row's label is its `y`, so `since:"latest"` reports a changed cell as a `~` row. `ink=` fingerprints the row's dark pixels, so a row still shows as changed when the changed glyph was not recognized.
- **`query` filters the OCR rows** like tree rows.
- **Small text.** Screenshots up to 2000 px on the long edge are upsampled 2x before recognition; at 1x Vision skips most one-letter cells (a register's reconcile flag). Language correction is off so codes and amounts are not "corrected".
- **Tree-only reads** (`include_screenshot:false`) capture for the text alone and keep the pixel frame, so clicks taken from the row coordinates resolve.
- **Cold start.** The first recognition after boot loads Vision's models (tens of seconds; a fraction of a second afterwards, in any process). `serve` warms the recognizer in a background thread at start, and a read waits at most 4 s before returning without text (`ocr_status: "starting"` and a one-line OCR row saying so).
- **Title-bar buttons** without a title or description are named by subrole: `AXButton (window close button)`.
- Structured output adds `opaque_content: true` and `ocr_text_rows` for such windows. Windows with real accessibility content are unchanged.

New: `cua_driver_core::opaque_text` (classifier, row grouping, rendering, ink fingerprint; platform-neutral so Windows/Linux can reuse it) and `platform_macos::ocr` (Vision calls).

## Verification

- Unit tests: `opaque_text` (opacity verdicts, grouping, rendering, query filter, ink change on an unread glyph, block placement before a walk note), `ocr` (Vision answers on a blank image, page size and luminance), tree (title-bar button naming).
- Live, macOS 26.5 VM with GnuCash 5: the released driver's tree for an account register has no content rows. The new reader on the same window's screenshots returns every row of the register, including the one-letter reconcile column (`n` in each row). After a click on a reconcile cell, the clicked row's text and `ink=` change and the other data rows are identical, so a `since` read lists that row (plus the row the edit cursor left).
- Rereading unchanged pixels gives identical rows: row bands (and the `y` label) snap to the first and last ink scanline near the recognized boxes, so box jitter between reads does not show up as a change.
- Timing in the VM (Vision on CPU): first recognition after boot about 1.8 s for the whole process; afterwards 0.85 to 1.0 s for an 800x632 window at 2x. On bare metal the very first recognition on a machine took about 54 s (one-time model compile), later ones 0.1 to 0.3 s; the warm-up thread and the 4 s cap cover that case.
- `clippy -D warnings` clean for cua-driver, cua-driver-core and platform-macos; unit tests above green.
- Not yet run end to end through a daemon in the VM: the new build needs its own Accessibility and Screen Recording grants there.

Refs CUA-4064.

title: perf(cua-driver): add guarded completion to jev-use
body:
Salvaged from #4316

Fixes #3963

Thanks to @kvnloo, who wrote this change. Both commits are theirs, unchanged, and keep their authorship.

## Why

#4316 adds an opt-in guarded completion to the `jev-use` browser fixture, so the runner can skip one provider decision when a fresh snapshot re-proves the completion. Its base was cut before #4913, so its native mock E2E lanes (GTK3, AppKit, WPF, WinUI3) failed with `budget_exhausted`, in code the PR doesn't touch. This PR applies the same two commits on current main.

## What changed

- New `--guarded-completion` flag in `python/run.py` and `typescript/run.ts`, with matching `guarded_completion` modules. After the provider picks the fixture's type action, the next step skips the provider only if a fresh snapshot shows the same session, the required token in the field, exactly one `button / Submit` ref that differs from the earlier one, and exactly one matching `browser_click` candidate. Otherwise the provider decides, and the step logs `guarded_completion: {status: "declined", reason}`.
- Accepted steps log `decision_route: "guarded-completion"` and the re-proven facts, with `confidence`/`probabilities` set to `null`. Outcome events no longer carry the `token` value.
- `verify_setup.py` gains `--guarded-completion` and `--guarded-completion-decline`. The decline row adds a duplicate Submit to the fixture after typing. `ci-jev-use.yml` runs both rows on the Linux real-Driver job and audits their summaries.

## Scope

Covers the browser fixture in `libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use` only. Native tasks, the Driver itself and the default runner behavior are unchanged. The change addresses both blockers from the earlier review on #4316: accepted proofs are logged, and every decline is logged with its reason.

## Blast Radius

Only users of the example who pass the new flag see different behavior. `libs/cua-driver/examples/**` is outside the `cua-driver-rs` release package, so no Driver release follows from this.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks pass on this branch: the jev-use Python unit suite, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, the workflow YAML parse, and a search for any reader of the removed outcome `token` field (none).
- On #4316's head, the fork CI's `Linux mock E2E` job ran both new real-Driver rows (guarded route and duplicate-Submit decline) and passed. The native lanes that failed there come from the old base, and this PR's CI reruns them on current main.
- The macOS real-Driver guarded rows were not run locally. Linux and Windows lanes run only in CI.

title: run-rust-e2e-wayland.sh: fall back to /usr/libexec/at-spi-bus-launcher when it is not on PATH
body:
`scripts/ci/linux/run-rust-e2e-wayland.sh` finds the AT-SPI bus launcher at line 259 with:

```bash
ATSPI_LAUNCHER="${CUA_AT_SPI_BUS_LAUNCHER:-$(command -v at-spi-bus-launcher || true)}"
```

Debian and Ubuntu install `at-spi-bus-launcher` in `/usr/libexec`, which is not on `PATH`. On those hosts the lookup comes back empty and the wrapper exits right away with:

```
AT-SPI bus launcher is unavailable: <not found>
```

The run only gets past this when `CUA_AT_SPI_BUS_LAUNCHER=/usr/libexec/at-spi-bus-launcher` is set by hand.

Seen while running the native sway lane for the review of #4236 on a Debian host. With the variable set, the lane ran.

**Fix:** if `CUA_AT_SPI_BUS_LAUNCHER` is unset and `command -v` finds nothing, try `/usr/libexec/at-spi-bus-launcher` (and possibly `/usr/lib/at-spi2-core/at-spi-bus-launcher`) before failing.

title: cua-driver permissions status (non-macOS): unavailable text says to run serve when the daemon is listening but its reply failed
body:
On non-macOS, `cua-driver permissions status` builds its "no reliable status" text in `permission_status_unavailable()` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs`). It always says:

> Couldn't read Cua Driver's permissions: Cua Driver isn't running.
> start it with `cua-driver serve`, then run this again.

The caller already knows `is_listening` (`crate::serve::is_daemon_listening`), and it reports that value as `daemon_running`. Since #4019 that value is accurate. A daemon can be listening while its permissions reply fails, for example when `send_request` errors on a live socket. In that case the JSON says `daemon_running: true`, but the text tells the user to start a daemon that is already running.

Expected: `permission_status_unavailable` takes `is_listening`. When the daemon is listening but did not answer, the reason says the running daemon didn't answer and the next step says something other than `serve`, such as retrying or restarting the daemon.

Test: a failed `send_request` against a listening socket should give text that does not ask the user to `serve`.

Low priority: this only matters on the failed-reply path. Follow-up from the review of #4045, which was superseded by #4019.

title: Confirm on macOS that platform-macos builds and get_window_state reports pid_keyboard available with Chrome's omnibox popup open (#7653)
body:
#7653 (fixes #4241) changed `get_window_state` on macOS so that its `background_input` report judges the `pid_keyboard` route with `window_keyboard_action(GenericKey)`, the same class the keyboard tools gate on. Its own test covers the shared `cua-driver-core` logic. The `platform-macos` side was never built or tested, and the native Chrome case did not run: the PR was made on a Linux host with no macOS guest.

To confirm on macOS:

1. `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` builds and passes on main.
2. In Chrome with one browser window, the omnibox suggestion popup open and the browser window not key, `get_window_state`'s `background_input.pid_keyboard` reads `available`, not `refused` / `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity`. A background `press_key` to that window is delivered.

If either step fails, the macOS half of #7653 needs a fix.

title: macOS scroll: background keystroke fallback still gates as GenericKey and can refuse with same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity in Chrome
body:
On macOS, `scroll`'s keystroke fallback (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/scroll.rs`) posts PageUp/PageDown/arrow keys when a wheel scroll is not used. In background mode it gates the window with `BackgroundAction::GenericKey`, both in `gate_again` and in `gate_background_window_action`.

Since #5306 and #7653, `type_text`, `press_key` and `hotkey` gate window-addressed keys as exact-window keys (`window_keyboard_action(GenericKey)`). The driver makes the addressed window key before posting, so a visible same-pid sibling is not ambiguous. Scroll's fallback still uses the generic class. In Chrome with the omnibox suggestion popup open, a background `scroll` that falls back to keys can still refuse with `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity`, while `press_key` to the same window is delivered.

Switching the gate class alone is not enough. The fallback posts its keys without a key-window scope, so the exact-window class would claim a guarantee that the posting path does not give. A fix should post the fallback keys through the same key-window-scoped transport the keyboard tools use, then gate with `window_keyboard_action(GenericKey)`.

Test: a target with one competing same-pid destination (an open popup) gets past the background gate for scroll's key fallback when the key-window transport exists, and is still refused under the generic class.

Follow-up from #4241 / #7653.

title: test(cua-driver): align native jev-use timing with browser phases
body:
## Why

The browser `jev-use` runners log named timing phases (#4052), but the native runners only logged `observe_ms`, `parse_ms`, `decide_ms` and `act_ms`. So native and browser logs couldn't be compared by field name. This carries @kvnloo's change from #4336 onto current main.

## What changed

- `python/run_native.py` and `typescript/run_native.ts` now also put `semantic_observe_ms`, `visual_observe_ms`, `candidate_build_ms`, `provider_decision_ms`, `decision_ms`, `action_ms` and `total_step_ms` on every step event. They also add `visual_observe_scope: "parse_only"`, because native capture happens inside `get_window_state` and is counted under `semantic_observe_ms`. The existing fields stay as they were.
- `fake_native_driver.py` is a scripted MCP stand-in. With `fixtures/native/timing-contract-v1.json`, it lets the new `test_native_timing.py` and `native_timing.test.ts` pin the Driver call sequence, the alias equalities and the phase nesting in both languages.
- The README documents how each common field maps onto the native boundaries.

## Scope

Only the native example runners, their tests and the README. No routing, candidate, provider, action or oracle changes. The second commit on #4336 is left out. It added `rust/test-apps/harness-gtk3/`, which is a staging copy that `tests/fixtures/build/linux.sh` generates, and its own commit message marks it as not reviewed. Fork-issue references in three comments were removed. The authorship of the remaining commit is kept.

## Blast Radius

Consumers of native `jev-use` JSONL logs get extra keys. No existing key changes.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks pass: the jev-use Python unit tests, the TypeScript tests and the typecheck, with both new timing tests running.
- Mutation: with main's `run_native.py` or `run_native.ts`, the new tests fail. With one extra `get_window_state` call, the call-sequence assertion fails.
- Parity: both runners on both fake scenarios (counter, canvas), at main and at this head. Once the timing fields are stripped, the event logs are identical, and so are the Driver call lists.
- Not run: the live GTK3, AppKit, WPF and WinUI3 lanes.

title: test(cua-driver): pin display-only precedence in verify_state and lookup
body:
## Why

#4335 by @kvnloo set out to prove one rule for passive (display-only) rows: when a selector matches an addressable control, only the controls count, and a display-only row is read only when no control matches and is never an action target. Since #4531 the Driver implements this rule in `evaluate_element` (`expectation.rs`) and in the name lookup `matches` (`batch_tools/locate.rs`). #4335 tested a separate Python/TypeScript model in the jev-use example that nothing calls, and that model returns different answers from the Driver in several cases. This PR carries the idea over as tests on the Driver code itself, covering the parts of the rule that had no test.

## What changed

- `expectation.rs`: a lone display-only row satisfies an existence check, and two display-only rows with one value are `unknown / multi_match`.
- `locate.rs`: name lookup never returns a display-only row (`not_found` when it is the only match) and picks the control when a caption and a control share the name.

## Scope

Tests only. No production code changes. Two parts of the rule already had tests and are left alone: a control wins over its display-only caption (`addressable_match_wins_over_its_display_only_caption`), and display-only web text stays untrusted. The jev-use model files from #4335 are not carried over.

## Tradeoffs

Keeping #4335's model would put a second copy of the rule in the repo, and that copy already differs from the Driver. A complete check with no matches and a value predicate is `unsatisfied` in the model but `unknown / target_missing` in the Driver. The model treats `exists: false` as satisfied, while the Driver rejects it as an invalid predicate. With `exists: true` plus a mismatched value, the model says satisfied and the Driver says unsatisfied. The model also uses passive rows when the actionable walk is incomplete. Testing the Driver avoids keeping two copies in sync.

## Blast Radius

None at runtime: the change is three `#[cfg(test)]` functions in `cua-driver-core`.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks for `cua-driver-core` (`cargo test --lib`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --tests -D warnings`) pass on macOS.
- Each new test goes red under a mutation of the rule it pins: dropping the display-only fallback, removing the multi-match guard, and removing the display-only filter in lookup.

Salvaged from #4335. Thanks to @kvnloo for stating the rule and its cases.

Fixes #3963

title: fix(cua-driver): capture a macOS window with parent or child windows at its own scale
body:
Refs CUA-4064.

## Problem

Pixel clicks on GTK dialogs (GnuCash's Tip of the Day, for example) seemed to miss in background delivery. Event delivery was not the cause: a background click on the same dialog lands when its coordinates are right. The coordinates were wrong because the dialog's screenshot was wrong.

ScreenCaptureKit's single-window filter (`SCContentFilter(desktopIndependentWindow:)`) renders a window together with its AppKit parent and child windows, then fits the group's bounding box, top-left anchored, into the configured output size. The driver sizes that output from the one window's frame, so:

- capturing a GTK dialog (an AppKit child of the window it is transient for) returned the main window plus the dialog, squeezed into the dialog's size (measured: 40%);
- capturing the main window returned it at 80% once the dialog reached past its right edge.

The screenshot frame still validated (the image had the window's size), so every pixel coordinate read off it mapped to the wrong point.

Measured in a macOS 26 VM with GnuCash 5.17: the dialog's capture matched the main window's capture scaled to the dialog's width (mean absolute pixel difference 1.06/255), and `SLSCopyAssociatedWindows` returned `[dialog, main]` for both windows and only itself for an unrelated Finder window.

## Fix

- `skylight::associated_windows(window_id)` wraps `SLSCopyAssociatedWindows` (the window's AppKit parent/child group, itself included; empty if the SPI is missing).
- When the window has relatives, `build_window_capture_plan` sizes the output for the union of the group's on-screen frames and records the window's own rectangle in it; `capture_window_from_plan` crops that rectangle, so the image is the window alone at 1:1.
- Plans for grouped windows are not cached: the plan cache keys on the window's own frame and would miss a parent that moved or a dialog that opened.
- Windows without relatives (almost all) keep the current path unchanged.

## Tests

- New unit tests: group geometry (dialog half outside its parent, parent with a child past its edge, a child inside its parent leaves the size alone) and the RGBA crop.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib capture`: 51 passed. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos -p cua-driver --all-targets -D warnings`: clean. `bin/ci --quick`: green.

Not yet verified end to end through a rebuilt daemon: a new build needs its own Screen Recording grant in the test VM. The capture model (group union fitted into the output size, top-left anchored) was measured live with two layouts using the current release build; the first end-to-end check is a run with the rebuilt driver on a GTK app with a dialog open.

title: fix(cua-driver): use GNOME Mutter's logical frame for capture and input
body:
On a fractionally scaled GNOME Wayland desktop, `get_desktop_state` returned physical pixels while libei input and window bounds are logical. A pixel read off the screenshot therefore missed by the output scale. `get_window_state` returned the window at its resource scale (2 on a 150% output), and `get_screen_size` failed without an X display.

This change reads Mutter's logical layout the way the driver already reads KWin's:

- `wayland/kwin_layout.rs` becomes `wayland/logical_layout.rs`. It recognises GNOME Mutter (announces `gtk_shell1` and no `zwlr_*` globals, so phoc is excluded) besides KWin, and returns the compositor with the frame. KWin's rotated-output distortion handling stays KWin-only.
- `get_screen_size`, `get_desktop_state`, `get_cursor_position` and desktop-scope input share that logical frame on Mutter.
- GNOME helper window captures (`CaptureWindow`, `CaptureWindowPreview`) are resized to the window's logical frame from `GetRects`. The frame is read before and after the capture. A capture that is not the frame at one scale is refused.
- The GNOME row in `action-support.md` records the behaviour.

This is a fresh implementation on current main, built on the KWin logical-frame path from #6821. It does not reuse code from #5604 or #3887. Credit to @lorenzozanee, whose #3848/#3887 diagnosed and first fixed this mismatch, and who filed #3061 with the reproduction this follows.

Supersedes #5604.

Fixes #3061

## Test plan

Live check on a headless GNOME Shell 48 Wayland session with a 3840x2160 virtual monitor, the WinRects helper, and a GTK3 fixture that logs its button presses:

| scale | `get_screen_size` / desktop PNG | window PNG (400x337 window) | desktop click from PNG pixel | window clicks (full, cap 300, cap 500) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.5, this branch | 2560x1440, scale 1.5 | 400x337 | lands on target | all land on target |
| 2, this branch | 1920x1080, scale 2 | 400x337 | lands | all land |
| 1, this branch | 3840x2160, scale 1 | 400x337 | lands | all land |
| 1.5, main | errors / 3840x2160, scale 1.0 | 800x674 | no press | no press |

The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets`, `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`, and `cargo check`/`build` of `cua-driver` with `portal-input,portal-capture`. The verify-cua-driver Linux lanes ran on X11/Openbox and Wayland/Sway.

Not run: KWin (no session available; KWin code paths are only renamed, and their unit tests pass), multi-output GNOME, Windows and macOS (Linux-only change).

title: [Bug]: KWin/GNOME desktop layout probe has no deadline
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

The KWin/GNOME Mutter desktop layout probe (`platform-linux/src/wayland/logical_layout.rs`, `query_on`) waits on two Wayland roundtrips with no deadline. If the compositor accepts the connection but stops answering, `get_desktop_state`, `get_screen_size`, `get_cursor_position` and desktop-scope pointer input block for good, because each of them reads the layout before it acts.

The probe used to run only on KWin. With https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7687 it also runs on GNOME Mutter, so more sessions now take this path. Hyprland and niri give their probes a deadline already. This was first noted in the review of #3887, whose probe had the same gap.

### Reproduction

Found by reading the code. In `query_on`, both `queue.roundtrip(&mut report)` calls block until the compositor answers. A compositor that holds the socket open without replying keeps the tool call waiting with no timeout. A unit test can show it with the module's scripted test compositor (`serve`) if the script stops answering after the registry.

### Expected behavior

The layout read has a deadline, as the niri and Hyprland probes do. When it expires the tool fails with an error naming the compositor and does not fall back to the physical frame.

### Actual behavior

There is no deadline, so the call blocks for as long as the compositor stays silent.

### Environment

Linux Wayland, KWin or GNOME Mutter, cua-driver main.

### Evidence

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/logical_layout.rs`, `query_on`: `queue.roundtrip(...)` twice, with no timeout.

### Workaround and additional context

None. Restart the driver if a call hangs.

title: feat(cua-driver): report what an action changed in a window missing from the accessibility tree
body:
Stacked on #7673 (base: `feat/cua-driver-opaque-window-ocr`).

## Problem

A window whose content is missing from the accessibility tree (GTK on macOS, many Java and canvas UIs) gets its text read by OCR in `get_window_state` (#7673). Every pointer or keyboard action on such a window still returns `effect: "unverifiable"`, so a caller re-reads the window after each action to see what happened, usually as a picture-only read (`include_accessibility_tree:false`), which carried no text rows. Actions that open a dialog need a `list_windows` + `get_window_state` round trip to find it.

## Change

- **Post-action evidence for opaque windows.** `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `drag`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey` and `scroll` (and so each `run_steps` step) are wrapped: when the target window was found opaque by its last read, the window is recaptured after a 250 ms settle, its text is read and diffed against the window's last text read, in that read's pixel frame (same row keying and `ink=` fingerprint as `since:"latest"`). A change is returned as `window_change` evidence and the action is `confirmed`; the summary lists up to 8 changed rows (`y=165: "a | n" -> "a @(232,165) | c @(846,165)"`, with "same text, pixels changed" for ink-only rows). Unchanged rows make it `suspected_noop`. With no earlier read to compare with, a baseline is taken before the action. The reads are bounded (2 s before, 2.5 s after); past that the action returns as before with `ocr_status`.
- **New windows, every app.** The target app's on-screen windows are listed before and after each action; windows that appeared are returned as `new_windows: [{window_id, title, bounds}]` and in the summary. For an action on an opaque window, the new window's text rows (up to 12) are included and the window is treated as opaque until it is read.
- **run_steps.** A step line kept only the first line of the action's text; each ok step now also carries its `window_change` evidence (rows that changed, windows that opened) or notes a `suspected_noop`.
- **Picture-only reads keep the text.** `include_accessibility_tree:false` on a window an earlier read found opaque returns its OCR rows with the image (`display_only:true` still skips them). Every OCR read becomes the next action's baseline.
- **zoom frame check.** zoom already captures the window on every call; it now refuses a region that starts outside the window's latest screenshot frame and names that frame (coordinates taken from a read at another `max_dimension` used to crop the wrong area silently).
- **Guidance.** The OCR header row and MACOS.md say: act by the rows' pixels, and read the action result instead of taking a new screenshot.

New code: `platform-macos/src/tools/action_evidence.rs` (wrapper), `opaque_text::{diff_rows, render_changes}`, `ocr::{known_opaque, remember_rows, read_window_rows}`. No app-specific logic.

## Tests

- `opaque_text`: diff (identical, changed cell, ink-only, added/removed order, cap): 16/16.
- `action_evidence`: new-window diff, sliver filter, effect folding (changed, unchanged, stronger effect kept, unread), summary placement; zoom frame check; run_steps step note (batch_tools 64/64); existing ocr/get_window_state/ax::tree tests: 64/64.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `bin/ci --quick` green.
- Not run live in this PR: latency is bounded by the budgets above (warm Vision reads measured at 0.1-1 s per window for #7673).

Refs CUA-4064

title: perf(cua-driver): acknowledge witnessed intermediate effects in native jev-use
body:
Salvaged from #4368

## Why

The native jev-use runners wait out the full 20-poll oracle window after every action, even when the harness state already shows that action's effect. This salvage keeps @saariuslystoned's change, which ends the wait once an independently witnessed intermediate effect appears. It also fixes one gap found in review.

## What changed

- Counter and choose-size tasks get intermediate-effect predicates. Increment must move the integer `counter` by exactly +1 from the pre-dispatch read. The Large radio must read `size: large`. Whole-task `verified`/`refuted` still wins. A supported effect that never appears returns `intermediate_timeout`, and the runner stops before a dependent mutation. Python and TypeScript both change.
- Review fix: a foreground retry (`ax:…:foreground`, after a background refusal) is now held to the same predicate. Before this, a foreground press that changed nothing fell back to the plain wait and let the runner dispatch again.
- Adds `verify_native_waits.py`, a fake-clock comparison against the old poller, plus unit tests in both languages. The original PR's timing proof doc is not carried over.

## Scope

Only the jev-use example runners. Driver tools, the daemon, fixtures and permissions are unchanged. Save-note, custom tasks, the final declared action, empty step lists and exhausted budgets keep the plain 20-poll wait.

## Tradeoffs

If the final declared action has no witnessed effect, it still returns `continuation` and the runner may act again. Main behaves the same way after every action, and #4368 deliberately left terminal actions on the baseline wait, so stopping there is left for a separate change.

## Verification

- On a macOS host, the scoped repository checks passed: Python unittest discovery, the choice and decision CLIs on the mock model, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, and `verify_native_waits.py`.
- Mutation checks: removing the `:foreground` normalization turns the new foreground test red in both languages, and accepting a +2 counter step turns a predicate test red.
- Not run: the live macOS harness, plus the Linux and Windows lanes, which this host cannot build.

Credit: the intermediate-effect design, predicates, tests and fake-clock script are @saariuslystoned's, in #4368.

title: fix(cua-driver): report a background web press the page ignored
body:
## Why

On macOS a background `click` on some web controls in Chrome did nothing and still returned `effect:"unverifiable"` with no escalation, so an agent could not tell the click had been ignored. A background accessibility press reaches the page as a click, but the document is not focused, so a control that checks `document.hasFocus()` ignores it. `delivery_mode:"foreground"` reaches that control. The click result now says when the page did not react, and points at foreground delivery.

## What changed

- Before a background `AXPress` on web content, `click` reads a digest of the browser window's accessibility tree. It reads the window again until the window changes or a 500 ms settle window ends. If the window never changed, the result is `effect:"suspected_noop"` with `escalation:{target:"foreground", reason:"suspected_noop"}`, plus a note to check the window before retrying.
- The element-token press and the pixel hit-test press both run this check. A partial or failed read, a text input, a press that opens a window, and `post_action_wait:"none"` all keep the old `unverifiable` result. The digest covers page text and geometry, the browser chrome's structure and values, and the window title. It skips focus, because the press can move focus without the page doing anything.
- New standalone-browser row `standalone_browser_background_web_click_noop`. A background click on a focus-gated button reports `suspected_noop` with a foreground escalation and leaves the button inactive. A plain button on the same page stays `unverifiable` with no escalation and still increments its counter.

## Scope

Covers background accessibility presses on web content in macOS browsers and web views, which is case 1 of the issue (the show/hide toggle, by element token or pixel). Cases 2 and 3 (a combobox row and a date-picker cell that close on a background pixel click) change the page, so they still report `unverifiable`. Making background delivery reach those controls is not in this PR. Windows and Linux are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

- `suspected_noop` is evidence, not proof. A press that only copies to the clipboard, or starts a request that takes longer than the settle window to show, reads as unchanged. The escalation reason and the result note both say to check the window before a foreground retry, and the skill's existing rule against blind replays applies.
- A background web press the page ignores now returns up to 500 ms later than before. A press the page handles returns as soon as the change shows. Foreground presses are unchanged.

## Blast radius

Only macOS `click` results on web content in background delivery change. A handled press keeps `unverifiable`, and any doubt in the read keeps `unverifiable`, so the new state appears only when two complete reads match.

## Verification

- Live repro before the fix, on Chrome with the released driver: a background element click on a button whose handler checks `document.hasFocus()` returned `unverifiable`, no escalation, and the page did not change. The same click with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` changed it. Plain `onclick`, `mousedown`, `pointerdown` and `isTrusted` handlers all fired from a background press, which narrowed the cause to document focus.
- The scoped repository checks pass at the head, including clippy with warnings as errors and the `platform-macos` unit tests for the page watch, the digest, the failed-read rule and the click result.
- macOS Lume full matrix at the head: every canonical row and every standalone-browser row passes, including the new one. Its recording shows `suspected_noop` with a foreground escalation on the focus-gated click and `unverifiable` with no escalation on the plain button. Linux and Windows are untouched and were not run.

Fixes #4243

title: [Bug]: Windows type_text on an Electron app's Save dialog file name appends to the preselected name and reports confirmed
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Windows, `type_text` with an `element_token` on the File name box of an Electron app's Save dialog (the common item dialog from `dialog.showSaveDialog`) adds the text after the preselected name and returns `effect: "confirmed"` with `value_readback` evidence. The box then holds `reportC:\Users\dev\Desktop\cua-repro.txt`, not the text that was asked for. The same dialog opened by Notepad takes the PostMessage route and comes out right.

### Reproduction

1. An Electron 38 app calls `dialog.showSaveDialog(win, { defaultPath: path.join(dir, 'report.txt') })`. The dialog opens with `report` in the File name box, selected.
2. `get_window_state` on the dialog window shows `[40] Edit "File name:" value="report"` (inside `[39] ComboBox "File name:"`).
3. `type_text {"element_token": "<snapshot>:40", "text": "C:\\Users\\dev\\Desktop\\cua-repro.txt"}` (background, the default).
4. `get_window_state` on the dialog again.

It happens every time (3 of 3, on two versions).

### Expected behavior

The box holds `C:\Users\dev\Desktop\cua-repro.txt`, or the result does not say `confirmed` when the box holds something else.

### Actual behavior

The result of step 3:

```json
{"delivery":{"mode":"background"},"effect":"confirmed","evidence":[{"detail":"confirmed","kind":"value_readback"}],"route":"accessibility","summary":"✅ Wrote 34 char(s) on pid 5820 via UIA ValuePattern (element_index=[40]; verify: confirmed)."}
```

Step 4 reads `[40] Edit value="reportC:\Users\dev\Desktop\cua-repro.txt"`, and the ComboBox the same. Saving would write a file of that name.

For comparison, the same steps in Notepad's Save as dialog (preselected `Untitled`) on the same machine take a different route and replace the name correctly:

```json
{"delivery":{"mode":"background"},"effect":"unverifiable","route":"synthetic_events","summary":"📨 Sent 34 char(s) to pid 9128 via PostMessage (0ms delay; the field changed and now contains the requested text, but the insertion point is not known). ..."}
```

I don't know why the route differs between the two processes, or why the read-back passed; the read in step 4 is a fresh snapshot of the same element.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver-rs 0.49.9 (release zip, windows-x86_64); also on 0.44.0
Operating system and architecture: Windows 11 26H2 build 26300.9457, x64 (VM)
Application/browser/window system/image: an Electron 38.2.0 app's `dialog.showSaveDialog`; driven through `cua-driver mcp`

### Evidence

The two tool results above, and the fresh `get_window_state` reads. None else available.

### Workaround and additional context

`set_value` on the same Edit (or the ComboBox) replaces the name and reads back correctly. An agent first met this in a test run and caught it only by reading the box again; a run that trusts `confirmed` saves under the wrong name. Not a duplicate of #6531 (web textarea) or #7496 (`set_value` with no app-side notification), as far as I can tell.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

Found using Claude Opus 5.5.

title: macOS: background pixel clicks on Chrome popup rows and date-picker cells close the popup without acting
body:
## Summary

#4243 reported three Chrome controls on macOS that ignore background clicks. #7694 fixes case 1 only: an AXPress the page ignores now returns `suspected_noop` with a foreground escalation instead of a bare `unverifiable`. Cases 2 and 3 are still open, and #7694's `Fixes #4243` will close the original issue, so this one tracks them.

## Cases not covered (from #4243)

2. **Combobox result row:** a background pixel click on a result row in a React search dropdown closes the dropdown without navigating. An AXPress on the result's `AXLink` works.
3. **Date-picker day cell:** a background pixel click on a calendar day closes the picker without selecting the date. Typing the digits into the date field works.

#7694 compares the page before and after the press. In these two cases the page does change, because the popup closes, so the result stays `unverifiable` with no escalation. The click had an effect, just not the one the caller wanted.

## Scope of the evidence

The cases and their workarounds come from the #4243 report. The #7694 work reproduced case 1 live. It did not reproduce cases 2 or 3. It only established that its no-op signal can't catch them, because both clicks change the page.

## Possible direction

Native OS APIs first, with a deterministic wrapper on top:
- When a background pixel click lands inside a popup row or cell that exposes an AX press target (`AXLink`, `AXCell`, `AXButton`), route it through AXPress on that element, as #4243 says works for case 2, instead of synthesizing a pointer event that closes the popup first.
- Where no AX press target exists, set the value through AX on the owning field (case 3's date field), or return a refusal that names the foreground retry, rather than reporting `unverifiable` after the popup closed.

Refs #4243, #7694.

title: cua-driver (Linux): KWin capture decoder test misses distinct pixels across padded rows and low-alpha rounding
body:
## Summary

The KWin window-capture decoder test on main, `screenshot_decoding_handles_padding_alpha_and_invalid_layouts` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/kwin_capture.rs`, covers row padding with a 1×2 image whose pixels are all the same colour. A decoder that duplicated a pixel or a row, or that read the padding bytes as pixels, would still pass. Its premultiplied alpha (85) also divides exactly, so rounding in unpremultiplication goes untested.

## Proposed coverage

@highdeftant wrote a companion test for this in highdeftant/cua@8dd2735dca66e1f11ce4290d1a6486229c05021a ("test(cua-driver): cover padded KWin pixel layouts"). It is not on main. The test:
- decodes a 2×2 image with distinct pixels and 4 bytes of padding per row (stride 12),
- runs for both premultiplied Qt formats, 6 (`ARGB32_Premultiplied`) and 18 (`RGBA8888_Premultiplied`),
- includes a low-alpha pixel (`[1, 2, 3, 7]` → `[36, 73, 109, 7]`) to exercise rounded unpremultiplication, plus opaque and fully transparent pixels,
- adds a short note to `libs/cua-driver/docs/kwin-window-capture.md` that this is hermetic decoder coverage and does not prove live KWin capture.

The KWin capture work landed through #6820, salvaged from #6450 and #4378. This test was not part of it.

## Next step

Ideally @highdeftant opens it as a small test PR. If not, we can carry it over with authorship credited. It is a hermetic unit test, so it needs a Linux build of `platform-linux` and no KWin session.

title: macOS: fresh Chrome keeps its page tree out of AX for over a minute; the driver's 4 s materialize wait and 30 s backoff give up
body:
## Summary

On macOS, a freshly launched Chrome can go more than a minute without exposing its page content through the AX API, even though the driver opts it in. `get_window_state` returns the window with browser chrome only (toolbar buttons, address bar, menu bar) and no web area. The driver's opt-in in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/ax/enablement.rs` waits `MATERIALIZE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (4 s) for web content. If that times out, it tries again only after `MATERIALIZE_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS` (30 s), and at most `MATERIALIZE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (3) times per process lifetime. After that it skips the process for good. An agent that drives a Chrome it has just launched can be left with a page it cannot see.

## Observed

This came up during the #7694 work, in the macOS Lume e2e lane (a disposable macOS guest):
- The test launched a fresh Chrome with a temporary profile and a local fixture page, without `--force-renderer-accessibility`.
- The test polled `get_window_state` on that window for 60 s, enough to cover the driver's 30 s retry. In two separate runs the page's controls never showed up. Each snapshot held about 300 elements, all browser chrome: Back, Forward, Reload, "Address and search bar" with the fixture URL, and the menu bar. None came from the page.
- With `--force-renderer-accessibility` added to the launch, the same test passed in later runs. The Linux standalone-browser rows already launch Chrome this way.

Not established: whether the guest window was on the current Space or occluded, which #7453 describes as another cause of an empty page tree. It is also not known whether a fresh Chrome on a physical Mac takes this long.

## Possible direction

Native OS APIs first, with a deterministic wrapper on top:
- Find out what Chrome needs before it builds its renderer tree after `AXManualAccessibility` is set on a fresh process. The window may have to be visible, the page may have to finish loading, or a later `AXEnhancedUserInterface` or hit-test may be needed. Then make the wait condition depend on that, rather than on a fixed 4 s plus a 30 s backoff.
- When the attempts run out, have `get_window_state` say so: the page tree is absent, the driver stopped retrying, and relaunching with `--force-renderer-accessibility` fixes it. That is better than returning a chrome-only tree with no explanation (compare #7534).
- When the driver launches Chrome itself, pass `--force-renderer-accessibility`, as #7453 proposes.

Refs #7453, #7534, #7694.

title: feat(jev-use): add S1 and backend receipts to the browser runners
body:
Salvaged from #4394

Thanks to @kvnloo, who wrote this change. Their commit is cherry-picked with its authorship kept. A second commit rebuilds it on current main.

## Why

The `jev-use` browser-fixture runners offer only `mock` and `live`, while the native runners also offer `s1`, and no browser JSONL event says which backend made a decision. #4394 adds both. Its base predates guarded completion (#7674), so its runner hunks no longer apply. This PR applies the change on current main.

## What changed

- `python/run.py` and `typescript/run.ts` accept `--provider s1`. S1 receives only the validated `cua.jev_choice_request_v1` from the new `browser_provider` module: goal, capture ID, typed regions, compact history and candidate IDs with descriptions. It never sees action arguments, refs or the verification token. Both runners check `CUA_S1_DECISION_URL` before they reset the fixture or start Driver.
- Every browser step and decision outcome records `backend` (`mock`, `typesafe` for `live`, or `s1`). A guarded-completion step records `null` because no provider ran. A provider error is now always a logged `unknown` outcome with `phase: "provider"`, the backend and the error class, before any action. Before this, it was logged only when guarded completion was on. Otherwise it was an uncaught error.
- `--provider live` is unchanged and still sends the TypeSafe request pinned by the provider-request golden files. #4394 moved `live` onto the bounded request and added a `typesafe` alias. That would have changed the live request without updating the goldens or the README, so this PR leaves both out.

## Scope

Covers the browser-fixture runners in `libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use`, their tests and the README. The native runners, the Driver and OpenJev are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Only users of the example runners are affected. Their JSONL gains a `backend` field. A provider failure that used to exit with a traceback now ends with an `unknown` outcome event and exit code 1. `libs/cua-driver/examples/**` is outside the `cua-driver-rs` release package.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks pass on this branch: the jev-use Python unit suite, `verify_choice_cli.py`, `verify_decision_cli.py --model mock`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `ruff check`. New runner-level tests in both languages cover the backend receipts, the bounded S1 request and the default-off provider failure.
- On #4394's head, two of its new TypeScript tests fail without `CUA_S1_DECISION_URL` and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` set. The tests here need neither.
- The real-Driver browser lanes and the macOS and Windows lanes were not run locally. CI runs them.

title: fix(cua-driver): OCR rows keep lone glyphs and read picture regions of accessible windows
body:
Stacked on #7690 (base `feat/cua-driver-opaque-action-evidence`).

## Lone glyphs in OCR rows

Vision's current text recognizer (`VNRecognizeTextRequest` revision 3) drops a glyph that stands alone in a narrow cell, such as a register's one-letter reconcile flag (`n`/`c`/`y`). This happens at any scale (1x to 4x) and with language correction on or off; `minimumTextHeight` is already 0. On a real register screenshot (14 one-letter cells), revision 3 at 2x read 2 of them; revision 2 at 2x read 11 to 13, depending on the resampling filter. Text that is not a lone glyph reads the same in both revisions.

- `read_page` runs a second, revision-2 pass with its own request handler. Vision answers repeated text requests on one handler (or in one `performRequests` call) from the first result, whatever their revision. Measured warm, the second pass costs about as much as the first (~250 ms at 2x for a 1150x800 window).
- `merge_second_pass` keeps a second-pass fragment only when it overlaps no first-pass box and has a letter or digit. A lone non-ASCII letter is dropped: revision 2 misreads `n` as `П`.
- `mark_unread_ink`: a glyph-sized ink blob in a text row that still has no fragment becomes a `?` cell. A changed glyph then shows as a changed cell, not as a cell that disappears. Rule lines, 1-2 px grid lines, the window edge, blobs larger than a glyph and rows with no word get no placeholder.

Result on that screenshot: all 14 reconcile cells appear (11 read, 3 as `?`), and no other row gains a placeholder.

## Picture regions in accessible windows

`get_window_state` OCRs only windows whose whole content is missing from the tree. A viewer that renders a document as an image inside an otherwise accessible window gave no text at all.

- `picture_region` finds the largest `AXImage`/`AXGroup`/`AXWebArea`/`AXScrollArea`/`AXLayoutArea`/`AXUnknown` element that meets all of these: it covers at least 30% of the window, holds at most 6 text-bearing elements and 12 elements in total, and its text covers at most 15% of it. A cut-short walk is skipped, because a missing subtree would look empty.
- That region alone is OCRed, in screenshot pixels, and rendered with the same row format under its own `OCR` header. The result is the same in `get_window_state` and in `run_script`'s `app.getState()`. Without a requested screenshot, the region is captured at the read's frame and the pixel scale is set the way the opaque-window path sets it. A blank region costs one decode and no recognition.
- Windows whose content the tree describes pay only the geometric check.

## Tests

title: [Bug]: deleting the prepared agent home recreates home-claude-code
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### Summary

Deleting the automatically prepared `home-claude-code` Space does not keep it deleted. The app's Home preparation loop recreates a missing home and can retry after deletion during agent setup, leaving a container even after its persistent agent record has been removed.

### Reproduction

1. Open Cua Spaces after onboarding with Claude Code installed. Allow Home preparation to create `home-claude-code`.
2. Delete that Space while the app remains open, including while its agent setup is still pending.
3. Leave the app open and inspect `cua agent ls`, `cua spaces ls`, and `cua sandbox ls --local`.
4. In the observed incident, the persistent agent was removed but a new `home-claude-code` container was created afterward. A deterministic replay of the real preparation driver and Rust core reproduces the recreation without using real containers or provider calls.

### Expected behavior

An explicit deletion or cancelled create stops Home preparation. No background retry, reconnect, late create/setup response, or app relaunch recreates it. A new explicit request may prepare a new home.

### Actual behavior

`PrepareDriver.checkHome()` dispatches `homeGone`, and `prepare::reduce(Action::HomeGone)` returns `Effect::Create`. The root component also automatically starts any record with `wanted == false`, so merely stopping the current attempt would not persist the decision.

The driver's missing-home check currently requires `readyMs`, so deletion during agent setup is not noticed there. A network failure can then schedule another create.

### Environment

- Cua Spaces macOS app: 0.36.12.
- Bundled CLI and running daemon: 0.27.4. An older connected CLI was updated separately; the incident preceded that update.
- macOS 27.0.1, arm64; local gVisor Linux container.
- Source inspected and replayed at `cfd2e9b1947d9d3a9db477fe414e5682736c831d`.

### Evidence

Redacted daemon log sequence (UTC, 14 November 2026):

```text
09:25:04 persistent agents: removed an agent whose Space was deleted agent=claude space=local:home-claude-code
09:27:16 home-claude-code sandbox metadata: created_at after the removal above
09:27:22 readiness failed; pre-existing sandbox retained sandbox=local:home-claude-code
```

Current-state readback found an empty persistent agent list and a running local `home-claude-code` sandbox absent from the Spaces registry.

Isolated replay of the actual TypeScript driver, Rust JSON dispatcher, and temporary filesystem lifecycle:

```text
Before: {"creates":2,"recreated":true,"wanted":true}
AssertionError: a deleted home must stay deleted
After candidate fix: {"creates":1,"recreated":false,"wanted":false}
```

This proves app-driven recreation. It does not prove a separate daemon deletion race or that Claude continued running inside the orphan. The container's process service refused authentication during read-only inspection.

### Workaround and additional context

Quit the app before removing the orphan with the sandbox CLI. Keep the old app closed until a corrected build is installed. PR #6632 handles persistent-agent cleanup when a Space is deleted; this report concerns the app's separate preparation loop restarting work afterward. PR #6873 made Warm start always on.

I intend to submit a focused fix: stop preparation before single/bulk deletion, removal, or create cancellation; preserve that stop across relaunch; ignore late create/setup callbacks; keep queued messages; permit a new explicit request. Validation will use an isolated driver/core lifecycle replay, type checking, and applicable static checks. Unit tests and Jest will not be run.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.
