title: fix(cua-driver): skip the glide wait for a cursor turned off at runtime
body:
## Why

`set_agent_cursor_enabled {"enabled": false}` hides the cursor but does not stop the wait. On macOS and Windows, `animate_cursor_to_target` checked only the launch-time `cfg.enabled`. A placed cursor that was turned off at runtime still got a `MoveTo`, and every action waited for its arrival (up to the 8 s arrival limit on macOS) before it pressed anything. This is the disabled-cursor delay in #4276.

## What changed

- `RenderStateCore::animates()` in `cursor-overlay` answers "glide and wait?": enabled at launch, not turned off at runtime, and placed.
- The macOS, Windows and Linux `animate_cursor_to_target` all use it. Linux already checked runtime visibility, so its behavior does not change.
- Tests: a shared one shows that a cursor turned off after it was shown no longer animates. A macOS one shows that `animate_cursor_to` registers no arrival waiter for that cursor. Each test fails when its half of the fix is reverted.

## Scope

This covers the runtime-disable wait only. It leaves out the rest of #4308:
- The second-display re-seeding half is already on main. #4305 and the coordinate-independent `placed` flag mean a cursor on a negative-coordinate display is no longer re-seeded. The #4308 thread measured that on the reporter's setup.
- The macOS overlay painting changes are superseded by #5650 and #7458, which paint each display separately.
- Synchronous `SetEnabled` inside `send_command`, motion quiescing, and the Windows dirty-rect change are left out. The tool path needs none of them for this fix, and they change the render threads' state ownership.

## Blast Radius

The change only affects actions on a session whose cursor was turned off at runtime. Those actions now skip the glide and the wait, as they already did for a cursor disabled at launch. An enabled cursor animates exactly as before. Target checks and focus waits elsewhere in the click path are untouched.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks passed: formatting, clippy with warnings denied, `cursor-overlay` tests, and three full runs of the `platform-macos` lib tests.
- The macOS Lume full matrix passed at this head: 190 cells, runner exit 0.
- Not run here: the Windows and Linux platform crates, and the Linux desktop lanes. CI covers those.

Salvaged from #4308

Fixes #4276

title: [Feature]: live timed check for cursor-off click latency on a real second display
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

#7860 and #4308 fix the second-display click delay reported in #4276. On that bug, a click on a second display waited for the agent cursor's glide even after the cursor had been turned off at runtime. Unit and mutation tests cover the code path. They show that a cursor turned off at runtime no longer animates and registers no arrival waiter. No test times a click on a real multi-display layout, so a regression in the timing could ship without any test failing.

### Desired outcome

A repeatable live check that times the click itself on a second display:

1. Use a real second display, or a CGVirtualDisplay inside a Lume guest.
2. Click an element on that display once with the agent cursor on, so the cursor is placed.
3. Turn the cursor off at runtime with `set_agent_cursor_enabled {"enabled": false}`.
4. Time the next element click on the same display.

The check passes when that click no longer waits for the glide. It fails when the click still takes about as long as the glide or the arrival limit.

### Current workaround

Someone has to time clicks by hand on their own multi-display setup.

### Affected components and platforms

cua-driver on macOS: `platform-macos` cursor overlay and `cursor-overlay`. Windows has the same code path and could get the same check where a second display is available.

### Alternatives and prior art

- #4276: the original report.
- #4308 and #7860: the fixes. Their tests cover the logic but not the timing.
- #5336: drawing the cursor on the target display. It is related but does not cover this timing.

### Implementation ideas

Add a cell to the macOS Lume verification lane that creates a CGVirtualDisplay in the guest, opens a fixture window on it, and runs the four steps above. It should record per-click durations and compare the post-disable click against the configured glide duration.

Refs #4276
Refs #7860

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for existing issues, RFCs, and active pull requests.
- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: fix(cua-driver): let users admit apps past Hyprland background input quirks
body:
## Why

Users on Omarchy could not admit an app they had checked themselves for background Hyprland input. Since #6706 the driver admits any native Wayland app. The one app-level refusal left is the toolkit quirk list: Qt 6 apps refuse background keys with `client_drops_background_keys`. Contrawrite, the Qt Quick editor in this issue, hits it. This adds the opt-in the issue asks for, a user-owned list that lifts that refusal for named executables.

## What changed

- `hyprland_compatibility::admit` reads `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cua-driver/hyprland-apps.txt` (absolute paths, one per line, `#` comments). It reads the list only when a quirk would refuse the target, and matches each canonicalised entry against `/proc/<pid>/exe`. On a match it returns `Admission::User`.
- A dispatch admitted this way carries `admission: "user"` in its structured result, and its text and action-record detail say the user qualified the app, not Cua.
- The Linux skill and the platform-support page document the file and its limits.

## Scope

Driver admission only. The list does not lift `client_xwayland`, `client_unattested` or `target_unavailable`, and the plugin's own dispatch checks (`client_not_bound` for Chromium and Electron) still apply. With no file, behaviour is unchanged. The plugin is untouched.

## Tradeoffs

The issue's local patch matched a list against the old `PACKAGES` allowlist, which #6706 removed. A config key in the driver's settings was the alternative. A plain file under the driver's config dir follows the shape the issue proposed and needs no schema change.

## Blast Radius

This only affects background Hyprland input with the production plugin, and only targets that a quirk refuses. When nothing is listed, the result payload on success is unchanged.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` for the Hyprland and admission tests, plus clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`. The new tests cover a listed executable, a symlinked entry, unlisted, relative, commented and missing entries, and the live-target refusals that stay in force. Making the list read as empty turns two of them red.
- A live Hyprland run (a real Qt app taking background keys) did not run here. No Hyprland session was available, and macOS and Windows checks do not apply.

Fixes #4779

title: fix(cua-daemon): re-land the digest-pinned Lume image handling from #6150
body:
Re-lands @Alex-Wengg's #6150 on current main, with their authorship kept as co-author. A fork PR cannot get the local CI sign-off that merging needs, so the reviewed diff is applied here.

Lume pulls macOS images by tag, and the digest only keys the cached base VM. This change makes that handling honest end to end:

- A Lume reference names its digest once (`repo:tag@sha256:...`), even when the input already carried one.
- A digest-only reference is refused with a plain message, because Lume has no tag to pull.
- After a pull, the digest Lume recorded is compared with the one the base is named for. When the tag has moved off a pinned digest, the pulled base is removed instead of being kept under the old digest's name, and the error says what to do. A tag that moved during an unpinned create is a retryable failure.
- A pull Lume refuses outright is an invalid argument, so `on=auto` does not try every other computer with it.

Tests: 649 in `cua-vmm`, 60 in `cua-sandbox-core`, 173 in `cua-image`, 187 in `cua-daemon-core`, 526 in `cua-spaces` and 63 in `cua-daemon` lib tests pass, as do the `lume_pull_digest` and `placement` integration tests. Clippy (including each `cua-vmm` backend alone), rustfmt and the generated references are clean under `bin/ci`.

Closes #6150.

title: cua-driver: live Omarchy check for user-admitted Hyprland apps (Qt 6 background type_text, admission: "user")
body:
## What is owed

#7867 (for #4779) lets a user admit an executable past the Hyprland background-input quirk refusals by listing it in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cua-driver/hyprland-apps.txt`. A user-admitted dispatch reports `admission: "user"`. The PR's unit tests cover the list parsing and the admission decision. A live check on a real Hyprland session did not run, because no Hyprland session was available where the PR was built.

## Check to run on Omarchy (Hyprland, production plugin)

1. Start a Qt 6 app that the quirk list refuses today with `client_drops_background_keys` (for example a Qt Quick editor such as Contrawrite, from #4779).
2. Without the list file, background `type_text` to its window should be refused with `client_drops_background_keys`, as it is on main.
3. Add the app's absolute executable path to `~/.config/cua-driver/hyprland-apps.txt`. Then `list_windows` should list the app, and background `type_text` into a focused-in-app text field (with another window holding user focus) should reach the field. Read the field back from fresh state.
4. The `type_text` structured result should carry `admission: "user"`, and its text should say the user qualified the app, not Cua.
5. Focus should not move: the user's window keeps focus throughout.

Keep the driver output and a screenshot or AX readback of the field as evidence. If step 3 or 4 fails, report it on #7867, or on a new issue if #7867 has merged.

Refs #4779, #7867

title: fix(cua-driver): return a native set_value once its field settles
body:
A native text `set_value` whose read-back already confirmed the value no longer waits out the 300 ms window-change report window. It returns once the field has kept that value for 150 ms with no new window or foreground change seen.

Fixes #4792

## What changed

- `window_change_detector.rs`: `Snapshot::detect_async_until(settled)` ends the report-window poll early when `settled()` holds. A window or foreground change seen first is still reported. The rest of the deadline still runs detached with the focus-steal lease, exactly as after a quiet report window, so protection lasts as long as before and a late window is still reported on the next result.
- `set_value.rs`: for a native AXValue write whose read-back verified, a watcher thread re-reads the field every 25 ms and sets a flag once it has held the read-back value for 150 ms since the write. A different value or an unreadable field, even once, rules settling out, and the result waits the usual report window. The detector's poll only reads the flag, so an app that stops answering accessibility calls cannot stall the window watch or delay its lease.
- Web content (AX echo is not trusted), unverified writes, popups, Calc cells and errors keep the existing wait. Result text and structured fields are unchanged.

This takes the narrow part of the issue, early return on a settled field with the protection window untouched, on the current detector. It does not bring back the owned-supervision receipts from the closed #4776 and #4793.

## Test plan

- Unit tests: `a_settled_action_returns_early_and_keeps_the_detached_watch` (returns before the report window, detached lease still held), `a_window_seen_before_settling_is_still_reported`, and `FieldSettle` cases for a quiet field, a later change, and an unreadable or unknown field.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`, `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test snapshot_dispatch_invariants`, and `bin/ci --quick` pass on macOS arm64.
- Not run: a live macOS Lume before/after `set_value` on an AppKit text field, and the Linux and Windows lanes (this change touches only the macOS adapter).

title: verify-cua-driver: rerun the macOS Lume full lane for #7880 at fcae3c9942 once guest SSH writes are healthy
body:
Follow-up from #7880 (fixes #4802).

The verify-cua-driver macOS Lume full lane has not run to completion at the PR head `fcae3c9942d8ed3b76b96d2b7b845b76e5dcda41`. Both attempts ended as infrastructure failures before any cell was judged:

1. `source transfer failed`: the `tar` stream over SSH into the guest exited non-zero, and no guest evidence was collected.
2. The host-side SSH write that hands the signing-keychain password to the guest runner (`cat > <run dir>/unlock`) hit its 60 second timeout.

Findings on the second failure: the collected `runner.log` shows the guest runner had already read the password from the FIFO and moved on to signing, history setup and the cargo build. So the password arrived, and the host's SSH session did not exit within 60 s. The same signature (the guest consumed it, the host's SSH timed out) appears in two earlier unlock failures on this host on other heads, and alongside a 300 s source-transfer timeout and a 30 s status-poll timeout. Every one is an SSH session to a guest stalling under host load. None is a credential or keychain problem. During the second attempt a 6-CPU, 12 GB benchmark VM was running beside the 4-CPU worker on the 10-core host. The wrapper waits for memory pressure before cloning, but not for CPU load. That correlation is an inference, not a proven cause. Other full-lane runs on the same seed passed between these failures.

To do:
- Rerun the full lane at `fcae3c9942` (or at #7880's head at the time, if it has moved) once the host's guest SSH writes are healthy, and record the result on #7880.
- If the result is green, nothing else is needed for #4802's verification. If a cell fails, run it at the base before blaming the diff.

Refs #7880, #4802.

title: cua-driver/Linux: stop adding --force-renderer-accessibility in launch_app for Chromium apps
body:
Follow-up to #7886.

#7886 makes the Linux AT-SPI walk wake Chromium and Electron processes and wait for the web document to get children, so the page tree shows up on the first snapshot without `--force-renderer-accessibility`. `launch_app` on Linux still appends the flag to every Chromium-family app it starts (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/launch_app.rs`, the `chromium_family_program(prog)` branch).

With #7886 merged, the flag is probably no longer needed there. Dropping it would make apps the driver launches behave the same as apps the user launched, which is the path #7886 tested.

This should be its own PR, because #7886 only checked X11 under Xvfb. Before dropping the flag:

- Check the first `get_window_state` on a `launch_app`-started Chromium and Electron app with no flag, on X11 and on the Wayland compositors (Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, KDE).
- Keep `ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED=1` / `NO_AT_BRIDGE=0`. The accessibility bus still has to be on before the app starts.
- Keep a caller's own `--force-renderer-accessibility` in `additional_arguments` working.

title: cua-driver e2e: run Linux Chromium/Electron fixtures without --force-renderer-accessibility
body:
Follow-up to #7886.

The cua-driver e2e fixtures still start Chromium and Electron with `--force-renderer-accessibility` on Linux:

- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/cross_platform_behavior_test.rs` (Linux Electron host spec)
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-testkit/src/sentinel.rs`
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/standalone_browser_behavior_test.rs`

The Electron fixture's `main.js` and `build.sh` also add or document the flag. Once #7886 is in, the Linux walk gets the page tree without the flag. With the flag set, these suites test a setup most users don't have. Removing it on Linux would let them cover the default path. #7886's own `chromium_tree_wake_linux_test` already runs that path.

This should be a separate PR from #7886 and from the `launch_app` change. Run the affected e2e suites on Linux X11 and Wayland without the flag. Leave the macOS and Windows host specs alone unless they are checked on those platforms.

title: fix(cua-driver): bind window screenshots on the nested cua-compositor
body:
## Why

On the nested cua-compositor, `get_window_state` read the fixture's accessibility tree but every window screenshot failed with `surface_identity_unproven: no compositor-attested window geometry is available`. The only crop sources were Sway IPC and the GNOME helper, and neither exists on that compositor, so all three compositor E2E lanes stopped at preflight. This fix has the compositor attest the window rectangle, and the driver crops the output only when that attestation holds for the whole capture.

## What changed

- `cua_compositor_patch.py` adds a read-only `w <pid>` control query. For the target's process family it returns the scene rectangle in output pixels, the output size and a scene epoch. It refuses with a reason when the target is ambiguous, occluded by a visible toplevel, or on more than one output, a scaled output or a transformed output. Map, unmap, restacking, placement and xdg geometry commits bump the epoch. The query never focuses or raises.
- New `wayland/cua_compositor_capture.rs`. When `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` is set, window capture checks that the window was listed for that process. It then queries the compositor before and after a screencopy, on a Wayland connection whose peer process is the same as the control socket's. It crops only when both replies match, the image is the attested output and the rectangle lies wholly inside it. ID-only callers such as `zoom` must resolve to one listed process.
- `wayland/mod.rs` routes inject-mode window capture there. It also splits the screencopy helper so the capture can reuse the already-attested connection. A refusal keeps the `surface_identity_unproven` code and names the compositor's reason.

## Scope

This covers foreground or unoccluded window capture on cua-compositor. Background capture of an occluded target is still refused (#4827). Cursor rendering (#4828), desktop pointer delivery (#4829) and the GTK3 and Electron effect failures (#4832, #4833, #4834) are separate.

## Tradeoffs

#4826 took the same approach and also matched the window title. This version leaves the title out, because the title is not what proves the pixels belong to the window: the process match, the scene epoch and the same-process sockets do. It also treats a toplevel stacked above the target as occluding only when that toplevel still draws a buffer. wlroots keeps an unmapped toplevel's scene root enabled, so the simpler check would refuse a window that is actually visible.

## Blast Radius

Only sessions with `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` set take the new path. Sway, GNOME, KWin, Hyprland, niri and X11 capture are unchanged. On cua-compositor, a window capture that cannot be proven still fails closed, just as it does today.

## Verification

- Headless cua-compositor built from this patch against wlroots 0.19, driven with the GTK3 fixture. Before the fix, `get_window_state` refused the screenshot with "no compositor-attested window geometry". After it returns a 560x757 PNG of only the fixture window. With a second fixture on top, capture is refused with `target-occluded`. With a window that maps on top and then hides, capture succeeds.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` passes, including eight new tests for the parser, the before/after bracket, bounds, ID-only resolution and same-process binding. `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets` is clean.
- The [cua-compositor E2E lane at this head](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43787393207) passes `e2e_environment_preflight_test` in the shared, native and capture lanes. [At main](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43782695113) all three stopped there. The later cells that fail belong to the issues listed under Scope.

macOS and Windows checks do not apply to this Linux-only change.

Fixes #4825
